Add database indexes for query performance optimization
body:
## Summary

Adds indexes on frequently queried columns (`name`, `filePath`) for all node tables. This should improve query performance for common operations.

**Problem:** KuzuDB performs full table scans when executing queries with WHERE clauses on non-indexed columns. For larger codebases, this creates noticeable latency during:
- Symbol search (`WHERE n.name = 'X'`)
- Blast radius analysis
- Caller/callee lookups
- Any query filtering by name or file path

**Solution:** Create indexes on the columns used in these frequent query patterns.

## Changes

- **`src/core/kuzu/schema.ts`**: Added `INDEX_QUERIES` array with indexes for:
  - File (name, filePath)
  - Function (name, filePath)
  - Class (name, filePath)
  - Interface (name, filePath)
  - Method (name, filePath)
  - CodeElement (name, filePath)
  - Folder (name)

- **`src/core/kuzu/kuzu-adapter.ts`**: Execute `INDEX_QUERIES` during database initialization (step 6)

## Implementation Notes

- Uses `CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS` for idempotency
- Follows existing pattern of gracefully handling "already exists" errors
- Non-breaking change - existing functionality unchanged
- Indexes are created after tables but before any data operations

## Discovery Context

We built a similar KuzuDB-based code knowledge graph tool and found that adding these indexes significantly improved query response times, especially for codebases with thousands of symbols. Thought this might benefit GitNexus users as well!

Add Claude Code GitHub Workflow
body:
## 🤖 Installing Claude Code GitHub App

This PR adds a GitHub Actions workflow that enables Claude Code integration in our repository.

### What is Claude Code?

[Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) is an AI coding agent that can help with:
- Bug fixes and improvements  
- Documentation updates
- Implementing new features
- Code reviews and suggestions
- Writing tests
- And more!

### How it works

Once this PR is merged, we'll be able to interact with Claude by mentioning @claude in a pull request or issue comment.
Once the workflow is triggered, Claude will analyze the comment and surrounding context, and execute on the request in a GitHub action.

### Important Notes

- **This workflow won't take effect until this PR is merged**
- **@claude mentions won't work until after the merge is complete**
- The workflow runs automatically whenever Claude is mentioned in PR or issue comments
- Claude gets access to the entire PR or issue context including files, diffs, and previous comments

### Security

- Our Anthropic API key is securely stored as a GitHub Actions secret
- Only users with write access to the repository can trigger the workflow
- All Claude runs are stored in the GitHub Actions run history
- Claude's default tools are limited to reading/writing files and interacting with our repo by creating comments, branches, and commits.
- We can add more allowed tools by adding them to the workflow file like:

```
allowed_tools: Bash(npm install),Bash(npm run build),Bash(npm run lint),Bash(npm run test)
```

There's more information in the [Claude Code action repo](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code-action).

After merging this PR, let's try mentioning @claude in a comment on any PR to get started!

title: feat: local backend mode for web UI
body:
## Summary

- **Rewrites `gitnexus serve`** to use `LocalBackend` for multi-repo support — the same engine the MCP server uses, now exposed as a REST API
- **Adds local backend connectivity to the web UI** — auto-detects a running `gitnexus serve` instance on localhost:4747, allows browsing and loading any indexed repo
- **New "Local Server" tab** in the DropZone onboarding screen with repo selector, connection status, and per-repo stats
- **Wires the AI chat agent through HTTP in backend mode** — agent tools (Cypher, search, code navigation) route through the backend API, so chat works fully without the WASM DB

## Motivation

Currently the web UI runs entirely in-browser, requiring users to re-upload ZIPs or clone from GitHub to visualize their code. Users who have already indexed repos via `gitnexus analyze` should be able to point the web UI at their local indexes directly — including using the AI chat agent to ask questions about the codebase.

## What Changed

### Server (`gitnexus/`)
- `src/server/api.ts` — Complete rewrite: 10 REST endpoints using `LocalBackend` for multi-repo graph queries, process/cluster listing, file access, and Cypher execution
- Security: binds to `127.0.0.1`, localhost-only CORS, path traversal protection on `/api/file`

### Web UI (`gitnexus-web/`)
- `src/services/backend.ts` — Stateless HTTP client with timeout handling for all backend endpoints
- `src/hooks/useBackend.ts` — React hook managing connection lifecycle, auto-detection, localStorage persistence
- `src/components/BackendRepoSelector.tsx` — Repo cards with stats matching DropZone aesthetic
- `src/components/DropZone.tsx` — Third "Local Server" tab, auto-selects when backend detected
- `src/hooks/useAppState.tsx` — Backend mode state, query routing through HTTP when connected; `initializeAgent` detects backend mode and calls `initializeBackendAgent` on the worker
- `src/workers/ingestion.worker.ts` — New HTTP helper functions (`httpFetchWithTimeout`, `createHttpExecuteQuery`, `createHttpTextSearch`) and `initializeBackendAgent` method that creates the agent with HTTP-backed tool closures
- `src/App.tsx` — Backend repo loading flow, graph construction from server data
- `src/components/SettingsPanel.tsx` — Backend URL configuration with connection indicator
- `src/components/Header.tsx` — Green "Local" badge when in backend mode

### Docs
- Updated `README.md` and `gitnexus/README.md` with local backend mode and AI chat documentation

## Architecture: Backend Agent Initialization

```
Main Thread (useAppState)
  → worker.initializeBackendAgent(config, backendUrl, repo, fileContents, projectName)
  → Worker creates HTTP wrappers (executeQuery, textSearch)
  → Worker calls createGraphRAGAgent() with HTTP wrappers (same factory)
  → chatStream() works unchanged
```

No changes to `agent.ts` or `tools.ts` — the agent factory is function-parameterized, so swapping KuzuDB closures for HTTP closures is transparent.

## How to Test

1. Index a repo: `cd your-repo && npx gitnexus analyze`
2. Start the server: `npx gitnexus serve`
3. Open the web UI: `cd gitnexus-web && npm run dev`
4. The "Local Server" tab should auto-appear showing your indexed repos
5. Click a repo to load its graph and explore
6. Configure an LLM provider in settings, open chat, and ask a question

## Test plan

- [ ] `gitnexus serve` starts and lists all indexed repos at `/api/repos`
- [ ] Web UI auto-detects running backend on page load
- [ ] Clicking a repo in the Local Server tab loads the graph
- [ ] Graph visualization renders correctly with backend-loaded data
- [ ] Cypher queries route through the backend in backend mode
- [ ] Settings panel allows changing the backend URL
- [ ] Header shows "Local" badge when in backend mode
- [ ] AI chat agent initializes in backend mode (tools use HTTP, not WASM DB)
- [ ] Agent Cypher tool executes queries through the backend API
- [ ] Agent search tool works (Cypher CONTAINS-based text search)
- [ ] Agent grep/read tools work (using in-memory fileContents)
- [ ] Graceful degradation when backend is not running (ZIP/GitHub tabs still work)

title: analyze silently modifies user environment (CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, skills, hooks)
body:
## Summary

`gitnexus analyze` does more than index a codebase. It silently writes files into the user's project and modifies global configuration in the user's home directory. This happens automatically with no opt-in, no flag to disable it, and no prior warning.

Specifically, `analyze` currently:

1. **Creates or overwrites `CLAUDE.md`** in the repo root — injecting GitNexus instructions into Claude Code's project config
2. **Creates or overwrites `AGENTS.md`** in the repo root — same content, targeting Cursor/Windsurf/Cline
3. **Installs 4 skill files** into `.claude/skills/gitnexus/` — writing into the project's Claude Code directory
4. **Registers a PreToolUse hook** in `~/.claude/hooks.json` — modifying the user's **global** Claude Code settings to intercept every Grep, Glob, and Bash call

## Why this is a problem

**Overwriting user files.** If a user already has a `CLAUDE.md` with their own project instructions, GitNexus appends its block on first run and replaces it on re-index. The markers (`<!-- gitnexus:start -->` / `<!-- gitnexus:end -->`) manage the section, but users don't expect an indexing tool to touch their agent config files at all.

**Writing into `.claude/`.** Installing skills into `.claude/skills/gitnexus/` puts GitNexus files inside the editor's config directory. Users who version-control or carefully manage their `.claude/` directory now have unexpected files.

**Modifying global settings.** Writing to `~/.claude/hooks.json` is the most invasive action. This is a global config file that affects all projects. A PreToolUse hook that intercepts Grep/Glob/Bash for every project the user works on — not just the indexed one — is a significant side effect of running a per-repo indexing command. If the hook misbehaves or introduces latency, it affects the user's entire Claude Code experience.

**No way to opt out.** There's no `--no-context`, `--no-hooks`, or `--no-skills` flag. The only way to avoid this is to manually undo the changes after every `analyze` run, or to fork the project.

## What we did in our fork

We removed all environment-writing from `analyze`. It now only indexes.

The 4 agent skills (exploring, debugging, impact-analysis, refactoring) were moved to **MCP prompts** served by the MCP server. This delivers the same guided workflows through the protocol itself — no files written to disk. The server went from 2 prompts to 6, and agents get the same experience.

We also added a test suite (unit + integration) including a guard test that reads `analyze.ts` source to prevent these imports from being re-introduced.

## Recommendation

A few options that would fix this for all users:

### Option A: Make it opt-in (minimal change)

Add flags to `analyze`:
- `--with-context` — generate CLAUDE.md / AGENTS.md (off by default)
- `--with-skills` — install skill files (off by default)
- `--with-hooks` — register Claude Code hooks (off by default)
- `--full` — all of the above

Or a separate command: `gitnexus integrate` that does the environment setup as an explicit action.

### Option B: Move skills to MCP prompts (what we did)

The MCP server already runs when an agent connects. Prompts are the standard MCP mechanism for guided workflows. Serving skill content as prompts eliminates the need to write files to disk entirely. Agents that support MCP prompts get the workflows automatically; agents that don't can still use the tools directly.

### Option C: At minimum, warn and confirm

If the current behavior is intentional, at least:
- Print what files will be created/modified before doing it
- Ask for confirmation on first run
- Never modify `~/.claude/hooks.json` without explicit consent — global config changes should require a deliberate action

---

We're happy to contribute a PR if any of these directions are interesting. Previously submitted a PR that went unreviewed, so opening this as an issue for discussion first.

title: ONNX Runtime crashes instead of falling back to CPU when CUDA libs are missing
body:
## Summary

On Linux machines without NVIDIA hardware or CUDA libraries, `gitnexus analyze` with embeddings enabled crashes with an unrecoverable native error instead of falling back to CPU.

## Steps to reproduce

```bash
gitnexus analyze --embeddings   # or without --skip-embeddings on older versions
```

On any Linux machine without `libcublasLt.so.12` installed (no NVIDIA GPU, or CUDA toolkit not present).

## Error

```
/node_modules/onnxruntime-node/dist/backend.js:25
  __classPrivateFieldGet(this, _OnnxruntimeSessionHandler_inferenceSession, "f").loadModel(pathOrBuffer, options);

Error: /onnxruntime_src/onnxruntime/core/session/provider_bridge_ort.cc:1695
  onnxruntime::Provider& onnxruntime::ProviderLibrary::Get()
  [ONNXRuntimeError] : 1 : FAIL : Failed to load library libonnxruntime_providers_cuda.so
  with error: libcublasLt.so.12: cannot open shared object file: No such file or directory
```

Process exits immediately. No fallback occurs.

## Expected behavior

The embedder code in `src/core/embeddings/embedder.ts` already has a fallback path:

```typescript
const devicesToTry: Array<'dml' | 'cuda' | 'cpu' | 'wasm'> = 
  (requestedDevice === 'dml' || requestedDevice === 'cuda') 
    ? [requestedDevice, 'cpu'] 
    : [requestedDevice as 'cpu' | 'wasm'];
```

The intent is clear: try CUDA, catch the error, fall back to CPU. But the error thrown by `onnxruntime-node` during `loadModel` is a native exception that crashes the process before the JS `try/catch` at line 130 can handle it.

## Suggested fix

Detect whether CUDA is actually available before attempting to use it, rather than relying on a try/catch around a native call that may not be catchable:

```typescript
import { existsSync } from 'fs';

function isCudaAvailable(): boolean {
  // Check for CUDA shared library in standard locations
  const cudaPaths = [
    '/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcublasLt.so.12',
    '/usr/local/cuda/lib64/libcublasLt.so.12',
  ];
  return cudaPaths.some(p => existsSync(p));
}

// Then in device selection:
const gpuDevice = isWindows ? 'dml' : (isCudaAvailable() ? 'cuda' : 'cpu');
```

Or more robustly, use `child_process` to probe `nvidia-smi` or check for `/dev/nvidia*` before even attempting CUDA. The key point: don't let a native crash be the fallback detection mechanism.

## Environment

- OS: Kali Linux 6.12.38 (x86_64)
- Node.js: v22.21.1
- gitnexus: 1.2.8
- No NVIDIA GPU / No CUDA toolkit installed

title: Web UI has no way to connect to local gitnexus serve backend
body:
## Summary

`gitnexus serve` starts an HTTP API server on port 4747 with endpoints for querying a local index (`/api/graph`, `/api/repo`, `/api/query`, `/api/search`, `/api/file`). The README describes it as "Start local HTTP server for web UI connection."

But the web UI (`gitnexus-web/`) never calls any of these endpoints. Zero references to `/api/graph`, `/api/repo`, `/api/query`, `/api/search`, or `/api/file` anywhere in the frontend source. The web UI is fully self-contained — it re-indexes from scratch in WebAssembly every time.

## The gap

A user who has already indexed a repo via `gitnexus analyze` (native tree-sitter, native KuzuDB, embeddings) cannot view that index in the web UI. Instead they have to re-index in the browser using WASM, which:

- Is slower than native
- Is limited to ~5k files by browser memory
- Loses the embeddings they already generated
- Duplicates work that was already done

## What would be useful

A "Connect to local server" option in the web UI landing page alongside the existing ZIP drop and GitHub URL options. When selected, it would:

1. Ask for the server URL (default `http://localhost:4747`)
2. Call `GET /api/repo` to verify connection and show index stats
3. Call `GET /api/graph` to load the full graph into Sigma.js
4. Use `POST /api/search` and `POST /api/query` for the search/chat features
5. Use `GET /api/file` for source code viewing

All the backend endpoints already exist and work. The web UI just needs a third ingestion path that reads from the HTTP API instead of indexing locally.

## Current state

The `serve` command is an API with no consumer. The web UI is a frontend with no local backend option. Both work independently but never connect.

title: Web UI git clone broken when accessed via network IP
body:
## Problem

The web UI's git clone proxy detection in `gitnexus-web/src/services/git-clone.ts` uses this check:

```ts
const isDev = typeof window !== 'undefined' && window.location.hostname === 'localhost';
```

This decides whether to use the hosted Vercel proxy (`https://gitnexus.vercel.app/api/proxy`) or the local `/api/proxy` endpoint.

When accessing the dev server via a LAN IP (e.g. `http://192.168.1.80:5173` — common for headless machines, Docker containers, or remote development), `hostname` is `192.168.1.80`, not `localhost`. The check evaluates to `false`, so it falls through to `/api/proxy` — which doesn't exist on Vite's dev server. Result:

```
Remote did not reply using the 'smart' HTTP protocol
```

GitHub URL cloning is completely broken for any non-localhost access.

## Suggested fix

Invert the check — instead of detecting "am I on localhost?", detect "am I on the Vercel deployment?":

```ts
const isDev = typeof window !== 'undefined' && !window.location.hostname.endsWith('.vercel.app');
```

Any non-Vercel host (localhost, LAN IP, Docker hostname, etc.) uses the hosted proxy. Only the actual Vercel deployment uses its own `/api/proxy` endpoint.

## Reproduction

1. Start the web UI dev server with `--host` (or access from another machine)
2. Open `http://<LAN-IP>:5173`
3. Enter a public GitHub repo URL
4. Clone fails with "Remote did not reply using the 'smart' HTTP protocol"

title: Probe for CUDA before attempting GPU embeddings
body:
## Summary

On systems without NVIDIA GPUs (or without CUDA libraries installed), `gitnexus analyze --embeddings` crashes with an uncatchable native error from ONNX Runtime when it tries to initialize the CUDA execution provider.

This adds a lightweight probe before selecting the GPU device:
1. Try running `nvidia-smi` (3s timeout)
2. If that fails, check for `libcublasLt.so.12` in standard paths
3. If neither succeeds, select `cpu` instead of `cuda`

The probe runs once at embedder initialization. Systems with working CUDA get GPU acceleration as before.

### File changed

| `gitnexus/src/core/embeddings/embedder.ts` | Added `isCudaAvailable()` probe, changed device selection (+27/-1 lines) |

title: `context` tool misses callers when function is accessed via re-exported aggregated object property
body:
## Environment

- GitNexus version: 1.2.0

## Description

When a function is not imported directly but accessed through an aggregated object (a common pattern in large JS/TS projects), `gitnexus_context` fails to resolve the caller relationship. This can result in **~95% of actual callers being invisible** to the knowledge graph.

## Reproduction

Given this code structure:

```javascript
// lib/ajax.js — function definition
export function sendAjax(options) { ... }

// lib/index.js — re-exported as property of aggregated object
import { sendAjax } from './ajax';
export const utils = { sendAjax, /* ...other methods */ };

// app/feature/api.js — consumer (this caller is NOT detected)
import { utils } from 'lib';
utils.sendAjax({ url: '/api/data' });
```

Query:

```
gitnexus_context({ name: "sendAjax", file_path: "lib/ajax.js" })
→ incoming.calls: [] (empty — misses the caller in api.js)
```

Expected:

```
→ incoming.calls: [{ name: "api.js", filePath: "app/feature/api.js" }]
```

Meanwhile, a simple `grep "utils.sendAjax"` correctly finds the caller.

## Why This Matters

The "aggregated object re-export" pattern is very common in real-world JS/TS projects:

```javascript
// SDK / utility barrel exports
export const api = { getUser, createOrder, deleteItem };
export const helpers = { formatDate, debounce, throttle };

// Consumers always use:
api.getUser(...)
helpers.formatDate(...)
```

When this pattern is prevalent, the majority of call relationships become invisible, which severely limits the usefulness of `context`, `impact`, and `query` tools.

## Suggested Approach

1. **Object property assignment tracking** — when `const obj = { fn }` or `obj.fn = fn` is detected, create an alias edge: `obj.fn → fn`
2. **Re-export chain resolution** — follow `export { fn }` and `export default { fn }` through barrel files to final consumers
3. **Fallback: user-declared aliases** — allow a config to manually declare alias mappings for cases static analysis cannot resolve:

```yaml
# .gitnexus.yml (hypothetical)
aliases:
  - "utils.sendAjax": "lib/ajax.js:sendAjax"
  - "api.*": "lib/api/*.js:*"
```

title: [Problem] Full re-index required after branch switch or code changes is impractical for large projects
body:
## Problem                                                                                                       
GitNexus marks the index as "stale" when the current HEAD differs from the indexed commit. The only way to resolve this is running `gitnexus analyze`, which performs a **full re-scan** of the entire codebase.            
                                                                                                                      
For large projects (20k+ files, 176k nodes), this is impractical:                                                
- Branch switching → stale → full re-analyze needed                                                              
- Small code changes → stale → full re-analyze needed                                                            
- Analysis takes significant time, making the workflow nearly unusable                                           
                                                                                                                      
There may already be a solution we're not aware of. Opening this issue to clarify the expected workflow for large projects with frequent branch switches.

## Summary

Adds comprehensive **Dart/Flutter** support to GitNexus as the 11th supported language, following the existing 6-layer language support architecture.

- **11 files modified**, 286 insertions — covers all layers: enum registration, parser loading, file extension mapping, tree-sitter queries, import resolution, export detection, framework detection, entry point scoring, and built-in filtering
- **Tested on a real-world Flutter app**: 17,381 nodes, 28,985 edges indexed in 5.1 seconds

| Layer | What was added |
|-------|---------------|
| **Language enum** | `Dart` in `SupportedLanguages` |
| **Parser loading** | `tree-sitter-dart` grammar (main + worker threads) |
| **File extension** | `.dart` → `SupportedLanguages.Dart` |
| **Tree-sitter queries** | Classes, mixins, enums, extensions, type aliases, functions, methods, imports (with `package:` URI), exports, 4 call patterns (direct, method, return, assignment), heritage (extends, implements, with) |
| **Import resolution** | `package:<name>/path.dart` → `lib/path.dart`, relative imports, skip `dart:` SDK |
| **Export detection** | `_` prefix = private, no prefix = public |
| **Framework detection** | Flutter path patterns: `main.dart` (3.0×), pages/screens/views (2.5×), routes (2.5×), presentation (2.0×), widgets (1.5×) |

title: Feat: Add `.gitnexusignore` support for custom path exclusions
body:
### Problem

GitNexus has no way to exclude custom paths from indexing. All filtering is hardcoded in `ignore-service.ts`. Projects containing vendored bundles, generated files, or other artifacts not covered by the built-in defaults end up polluting the knowledge graph with noise — minified symbols, junk call chains, and misleading community detection.

For example, a project with a vendored QuestDB frontend bundle (`qdb.43f98.js`) gets minified class names like `Xr`, `Je`, `Yn` indexed as real symbols, consuming process slots and degrading search relevance.

### Solution

Users can now place a `.gitnexusignore` file at the repo root using standard gitignore syntax:

```
# Vendored QuestDB frontend
backend/docker/questdb/public/

# Large generated files
*.generated.json
```

On the next `gitnexus analyze`, matched paths are excluded from indexing. If no `.gitnexusignore` file exists, behavior is identical to before.

### Implementation

- Adds the [`ignore`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/ignore) npm package (24KB, zero deps) for full gitignore-spec pattern matching
- `loadCustomIgnore(repoPath)` in `ignore-service.ts` reads the file and returns a predicate, or `null` if absent
- `walkRepositoryPaths()` in `filesystem-walker.ts` accepts an optional custom filter applied alongside the existing hardcoded defaults
- `runPipelineFromRepo()` in `pipeline.ts` loads the ignore file at pipeline start and passes it to the walker
- The built-in default ignore lists are **unchanged** — `.gitnexusignore` is additive
- Added a "Custom Ignore Patterns" section to the README with usage examples

### Additional fix

Fixes a pre-existing build error: duplicate `let ftsLoaded` declaration in `kuzu-adapter.ts` (lines 19 and 679) that caused both `tsc` and `tsx`/`esbuild` to fail.

### Testing

Tested on a real 1,730-file monorepo (Go/Python/Rust/TypeScript). With a `.gitnexusignore` excluding one vendored bundle directory:

| Metric | Before | After | Delta |
|--------|--------|-------|-------|
| Nodes | 7,617 | 7,611 | -6 |
| Edges | 19,582 | 18,447 | **-1,135** |
| Clusters | 476 | 487 | +11 |

The large edge reduction (-1,135) reflects removal of noisy relationships from minified code. The cluster count increased because community detection found more coherent groupings without the noise.

Verified via Cypher query that zero files from the ignored path remain in the index.

title: fix(mcp): don't crash server when no repos are indexed
body:
## Summary
- Removes the `process.exit(1)` calls in `mcpCommand` that killed the MCP server when no repositories were found in the registry
- The server now starts gracefully with 0 repos and logs a helpful message to stderr
- Repos indexed after server start are discovered automatically via `refreshRepos()` on each tool call

## Problem
When a user configured `npx -y gitnexus@latest mcp` in their editor **before** running `gitnexus analyze`, the MCP server process died immediately at startup (#91). The editor saw the crash and reported "No indexed repositories found."

The irony was that `LocalBackend.resolveRepo()` already had lazy discovery — it calls `refreshRepos()` on every cache miss. But the two `process.exit(1)` gates in `mcpCommand` killed the server before this mechanism could ever work.

## What changed
**`gitnexus/src/cli/mcp.ts`** — Removed both exit gates:
1. The `listRegisteredRepos()` check + `process.exit(1)` (line 27-37)
2. The `backend.init()` return check + `process.exit(1)` (line 43-46)

The server now starts, and:
- `list_repos` returns `[]` with a helpful message (already handled in `getReposResource`)
- Other tools throw a clear error via `resolveRepo()` (already handled in `createMCPServer`'s error handler)
- Once the user runs `gitnexus analyze`, the next tool call picks up the new repo automatically

## Test plan
- [ ] Start MCP server with 0 indexed repos — should start without crashing
- [ ] Call `list_repos` with 0 repos — should return empty list
- [ ] Call any tool (e.g. `query`) with 0 repos — should return helpful error, not crash
- [ ] Run `gitnexus analyze` in a repo while server is running — next tool call should discover it
- [ ] Start MCP server with existing repos — should work as before

title: Feature Request: Support locally installed AI CLI tools (Gemini CLI, Claude Code, Codex) as LLM providers via their native authentication
body:
## Summary

Currently, GitNexus Web UI's Graph RAG Agent requires users to provide API keys for LLM providers (OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, Azure OpenAI, Ollama, OpenRouter) as defined in `gitnexus-web/src/core/llm/types.ts`. However, many developers already have **locally installed AI CLI tools** — such as **Gemini CLI**, **Claude Code**, and **OpenAI Codex CLI** — that manage their own authentication (OAuth, browser-based login, API key stored in their own config). 

This feature request proposes adding support for using these locally installed CLI tools as LLM backends, so users can leverage their existing authentication without needing to separately obtain and paste API keys into GitNexus.

## Motivation

- **Zero-config LLM access**: Developers using Claude Code, Gemini CLI, or Codex already have authenticated sessions. GitNexus should be able to reuse them.
- - **Aligns with the CLI-first philosophy**: GitNexus already deeply integrates with Claude Code (hooks, skills, MCP). Allowing Claude Code's own auth for the Web UI agent is a natural extension.
- - - **Lowers the barrier to entry**: Not all users have direct API keys. Some use tools via organizational SSO, team subscriptions, or free tiers managed by the CLI tool itself.
- - - - **Privacy**: Reusing local CLI auth avoids storing additional API keys in `localStorage`.
## Proposed Approach

### 1. New provider type in `LLMProvider`

Extend the existing `LLMProvider` union type in `gitnexus-web/src/core/llm/types.ts`:

```typescript
export type LLMProvider = 
  | 'openai' | 'azure-openai' | 'gemini' | 'anthropic' | 'ollama' | 'openrouter'
  | 'claude-code-cli'   // Uses locally installed Claude Code
  | 'gemini-cli'        // Uses locally installed Gemini CLI
  | 'codex-cli';        // Uses locally installed OpenAI Codex CLI
```

### 2. Backend proxy mode via `gitnexus serve`

Since browser-side JavaScript cannot spawn local CLI processes, this feature would work through the **existing `gitnexus serve` bridge mode**:

- When the Web UI connects to a local `gitnexus serve` instance, it can request LLM completions through a new API endpoint (e.g., `POST /api/llm/chat`).
- - The server-side handler detects which CLI tool is available on the system and proxies the request through it.
- - - The CLI tools handle their own authentication — GitNexus just passes the prompt and receives the response.
### 3. CLI tool detection and routing

On the server side (`gitnexus/src/server/`), add a module that:

1. **Detects installed CLI tools** by checking for binaries on `$PATH` (e.g., `claude`, `gemini`, `codex`).
2. 2. **Reads their auth status** (e.g., `claude auth status`, `gemini auth status`) to verify the tool is authenticated.
3. 3. **Proxies chat completions** by spawning the CLI in non-interactive/API mode and streaming the response back to the Web UI.
### 4. Settings UI integration

In `SettingsPanel.tsx`, when a local `gitnexus serve` connection is detected:

- Show a new **"Local CLI Tools"** section with auto-detected available tools.
- - Display authentication status for each detected tool (authenticated / not authenticated).
- - - Allow the user to select which local CLI tool to use as the default provider.
## Example UX Flow

1. User has Claude Code installed and authenticated (`claude auth login` done previously).
2. 2. User runs `gitnexus serve` and opens the Web UI.
3. 3. In Settings, a new section shows: **"Local CLI Tools — Claude Code ✓ authenticated, Gemini CLI ✗ not found, Codex CLI ✓ authenticated"**.
4. 4. User selects "Claude Code" as the provider.
5. 5. The Graph RAG Agent chat now uses Claude Code's auth — no API key needed.
## Implementation Scope

| Component | Changes |
|---|---|
| `gitnexus-web/src/core/llm/types.ts` | Add new CLI provider types to `LLMProvider` union |
| `gitnexus-web/src/core/llm/agent.ts` | Add routing logic for CLI-backed providers (delegate to server) |
| `gitnexus-web/src/components/SettingsPanel.tsx` | UI for selecting detected local CLI tools |
| `gitnexus/src/server/` | New endpoint `POST /api/llm/chat` that proxies requests through local CLI tools |
| `gitnexus/src/cli/` | CLI detection utility (`which claude`, `which gemini`, `which codex`) |

## Compatibility Notes

- This feature only works in **bridge mode** (`gitnexus serve` + Web UI) since the browser cannot spawn local processes.
- - When used via `gitnexus.vercel.app` (pure browser mode), these providers would be hidden/disabled with a note explaining that local server connection is required.
- - - Falls back gracefully to API-key providers if no CLI tools are detected.
## Related Context

- GitNexus already supports Claude Code deeply (MCP, hooks, skills, CLAUDE.md) — this extends that integration to the Web UI's chat agent.
- - The `gitnexus wiki --model <model>` CLI command already supports custom LLM backends, so server-side LLM routing has precedent in the codebase.

feat(ingestion): add AST decorator-based entrypoint hints
body:
## Description

This PR implements AST-based framework hint detection for decorator/annotation-driven entrypoints and wires it into process entrypoint scoring.

Before this change, framework awareness was path-only (e.g. `/controllers/`, `views.py`, `*Controller.java`).  
Now we also detect framework signals from definition text (decorators/annotations/attributes), so entrypoint ranking is less dependent on folder naming conventions.

## What Changed

- Added AST framework detection:
  - `detectFrameworkFromAST(language, definitionText)`
  - File: `gitnexus/src/core/ingestion/framework-detection.ts`
- Extended node properties with AST hint metadata:
  - `astFrameworkMultiplier`
  - `astFrameworkReason`
  - File: `gitnexus/src/core/graph/types.ts`
- Integrated AST detection into parsing (both paths):
  - Sequential parser: `gitnexus/src/core/ingestion/parsing-processor.ts`
  - Worker parser: `gitnexus/src/core/ingestion/workers/parse-worker.ts`
- Applied AST hint multiplier in process entrypoint scoring:
  - File: `gitnexus/src/core/ingestion/process-processor.ts`

## Supported AST Hints (this PR)

- TypeScript/JavaScript: NestJS decorators (`@Controller`, `@Get`, `@Post`, etc.)
- Python: FastAPI / Flask decorators (`@app.get`, `@router.get`, `@app.route`, etc.)
- Java: Spring / JAX-RS annotations (`@RestController`, `@GetMapping`, `@GET`, etc.)
- C#: ASP.NET attributes (`[ApiController]`, `[HttpGet]`, `[HttpPost]`, etc.)
- PHP: Laravel/PHP route patterns (`Route::get`, `#[Route(...)]`, etc.)

## Why Not Full Semantic Decorator Parsing (in this PR)

This PR intentionally uses AST-text pattern hints instead of full framework-specific semantic parsing because:

- **Cross-language cost**: full semantic parsing must be implemented and maintained separately per framework/language.
- **Grammar/version fragility**: strict decorator AST handling is more sensitive to parser/grammar evolution.
- **Performance target**: ingestion is optimized for broad, fast indexing; full semantic extraction would increase complexity and parse overhead.
- **Incremental delivery**: this change provides immediate entrypoint-quality gains with low risk, while keeping room for language-by-language semantic upgrades.

In short: this is a pragmatic step that improves signal now, without overfitting the ingestion pipeline to a few frameworks.

## Scope / Non-Goals

- No full semantic route/decorator model in this PR.
- Detection is currently pattern-based on AST definition text.
- No new CLI flags/options introduced.

## Validation

- `npm run build` passed in `gitnexus/`.
- Spot checks of `detectFrameworkFromAST(...)` returned expected hints for:
  - NestJS (TS)
  - Spring (Java)
  - ASP.NET (C#)

title: fix(web): map API path field to repoPath in fetchRepoInfo
body:
## Problem

When connecting the web UI to a local `gitnexus serve` backend, clicking "Connect" crashes with:

```
Uncaught (in promise) TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'split')
    at App.tsx:138:34
```

**Root cause:** The npm-published backend (`gitnexus@1.3.3`) `GET /api/repo` returns `path`, but `ServerRepoInfo` expects `repoPath`. The `fetchRepoInfo` function passes the raw JSON through without field mapping, so `result.repoInfo.repoPath` is `undefined`, and `App.tsx:138` calls `.split('/')` on it.

## Fix

Use spread operator to preserve all API fields, only overriding `repoPath` with `data.repoPath ?? data.path` for backwards compatibility with both npm `1.3.3` (`path`) and git HEAD (`repoPath`).

## Testing

1. `gitnexus serve` → running on `http://localhost:4747`
2. `cd gitnexus-web && npm run dev` → running on `http://localhost:5173`
3. Enter `http://localhost:4747` in the connection field → graph loads successfully

Supersedes #98. Fixes #92

title: feat(ruby): Add Ruby language support for CLI and web
body: ## Summary - Adds Ruby as the 11th supported language across both CLI (worker + sequential fallback) and web ingestion pipelines - Full tree-sitter parsing with Ruby-specific query patterns for classes, modules, methods, calls, and heritage - Ruby-aware import resolution (`require` / `require_relative`) with proper path handling - Mixin heritage extraction (`include` / `extend` / `prepend`) routed as `IMPLEMENTS` edges - Property extraction from `attr_accessor` / `attr_reader` / `attr_writer` - Entry point scoring for Ruby conventions (service objects, background jobs, CLI executables) - Framework detection for Rake tasks, bin/exe scripts, and extensionless Ruby files - Ruby test file filtering (`_spec.rb`, `_test.rb`, `/spec/`) in MCP impact tool ## What changed **Core parsing (both CLI + web):** - `tree-sitter-queries.ts` — new Ruby query capturing classes, modules, methods, singleton methods, calls, and heritage - `parsing-processor.ts` — Ruby export detection (all symbols public by default) - `utils.ts` — file extension + extensionless filename mapping (`Rakefile`, `Gemfile`, etc.) - `parser-loader.ts` — Ruby WASM grammar registration **Call resolution (both CLI + web):** - `call-processor.ts` — Ruby-specific routing: `require`/`require_relative` skipped (handled by import-processor), `include`/`extend`/`prepend` → `IMPLEMENTS` edges, `attr_*` → `Property` nodes - `import-processor.ts` — Ruby `require`/`require_relative` captured from `@call` nodes (Ruby grammar doesn't produce `@import` captures) **CLI worker thread:** - `parse-worker.ts` — Full Ruby call routing in the worker path (heritage, properties, import-like calls) **Scoring & detection (both CLI + web):** - `entry-point-scoring.ts` — Ruby entry point patterns: `call`, `perform`, `execute` - `framework-detection.ts` — Ruby bin/exe detection, Rake tasks **MCP layer:** - `local-backend.ts` — `isTestFilePath` now filters `_spec.rb`, `_test.rb`, `/spec/` **Config:** - `supported-languages.ts` — `Ruby = 'ruby'` added to enum - `tree-sitter-ruby.wasm` — WASM grammar binary for web ## Design decisions 1. **Ruby calls routed in call-processor, not heritage-processor** — Ruby's tree-sitter grammar captures `include`/`extend`/`prepend` as generic `@call` nodes, not `@heritage`. The routing lives in call-processor since it already iterates `@call` captures. 2. **All mixin types use `trait-impl` → `IMPLEMENTS`** — `include`, `extend`, and `prepend` all add module methods to a class/module. None represent true class inheritance (`EXTENDS`), so all three map to `IMPLEMENTS`. 3. **Ruby imports in import-processor** — `require`/`require_relative` are routed to import-processor (not just filtered as built-ins) so `importMap` gets populated before call resolution, enabling high-confidence (0.9) import-resolved call edges. 4. **Removed `lib/` framework boost** — Every `.rb` file under `lib/` was getting a 1.5x entry point multiplier, which conflicts with `isUtilityFile()`. Removed to avoid scoring contradictions. 5. **Removed `initialize` and `run` from entry points** — `initialize` is a constructor (called implicitly), not an entry point. `run` is too generic and creates false positives. ## Test plan - [x] Run `npx gitnexus analyze` on a Ruby/Rails codebase and verify: - [x] Folders and files - [x] Classes, modules, and methods appear as nodes - [x] `require`/`require_relative` create `IMPORTS` edges - [x] `include`/`extend`/`prepend` create `IMPLEMENTS` edges - [x] `attr_*` create `Property` nodes - [x] Method calls create `CALLS` edges with appropriate confidence - [x] Verify web version produces identical graph structure - [x] Verify `impact({ includeTests: false })` filters Ruby spec files - [x] Verify entry point scoring ranks `call`/`perform`/`execute` methods higher ## Demo - 6,724 edges - 4,331 nodes - 709 clusters Tested with [Fizzy](https://github.com/basecamp/fizzy) **How test it?** ```bash # Build cd gitnexus && npm install && npm run build # Analyze the codebase node gitnexus/dist/cli/index.js analyze --force ../fizzy` # Start the serve npx gitnexus serve # Open the Web UI cd gitnexus-web && npm install && npm run dev ``` **Syntax Highlight at Code inspector**

title: fix(query): rank with task_context and goal signals
body:
## Problem

The `query` tool exposes `task_context` and `goal` as ranking signals, but `LocalBackend.query` only used `query`.
This made the API contract misleading and reduced relevance for intent-heavy tasks.

## What changed

Implemented multi-signal retrieval + ranking in `gitnexus/src/mcp/local/local-backend.ts`:

1. Build retrieval signals from:
   - `query` (weight `1.0`)
   - `goal` (weight `0.75`, when provided)
   - `task_context` (weight `0.45`, when provided)

2. Deduplicate identical signal text (case-insensitive), keeping the strongest weight.

3. Run BM25 + semantic retrieval for each signal.

4. Merge all results with weighted Reciprocal Rank Fusion (wRRF), then continue existing process grouping/ranking flow.

## Why this is safe

- No MCP schema changes.
- No response shape changes (`processes`, `process_symbols`, `definitions` unchanged).
- Backward compatible: if only `query` is provided, behavior remains query-only ranking flow.

## Validation

- Build passes:
  - `cd gitnexus`
  - `npm run build`

## Notes

This fixes a functional gap where `task_context` and `goal` were accepted but ignored.

title: fix: sanitize shell-interpolated parameters to prevent command injection
body:
## Summary

Adds input validation for parameters that are interpolated into shell commands to prevent command injection attacks.

### Changes

**src/mcp/local/local-backend.ts**
- Added regex validation for `params.base_ref` before it's used in `git diff` commands
- Pattern: `^[a-zA-Z0-9._\-~^/]+$`
- Throws descriptive error if validation fails

**src/mcp/staleness.ts**
- Added hex hash validation for `lastCommit` parameter before use in `git log` commands
- Pattern: `^[0-9a-f]{7,40}$`
- Throws descriptive error if validation fails

### Why

Both parameters were previously passed directly to shell commands via template literals without sanitization. A malicious input could execute arbitrary commands on the host system.

### Risk
Low - validation is additive and only rejects malformed inputs. Legitimate git refs and commit hashes always match these patterns.

title: fix: reject write operations in Cypher query endpoints
body:
## Summary

Adds a read-only guard to both the MCP `cypher` tool and the HTTP `/api/query` endpoint.

Queries containing write keywords (`CREATE`, `DELETE`, `SET`, `REMOVE`, `MERGE`, `DROP`, `ALTER`, `DETACH`, `COPY`, `CALL`) are rejected before execution.

## Motivation

The `cypher` tool is exposed to AI assistants and HTTP clients. Without validation, a crafted query could mutate or destroy the knowledge graph. This guard ensures only read-only `MATCH`/`RETURN` queries are permitted.

## Changes

- `gitnexus/src/mcp/local/local-backend.ts`: Added `WRITE_PATTERN` static regex and early rejection in `cypher()` method
- `gitnexus/src/server/api.ts`: Added same pattern check in `/api/query` handler, returns 403

## Risk

Low — only adds a pre-execution check. No changes to query execution or result formatting.

title: fix: add explicit radix to parseInt calls
body:
## Summary

Add explicit radix parameter (`10`) to all `parseInt()` calls that were missing it.

## Problem

Without an explicit radix, `parseInt` defaults to base 10 for decimal strings but can misparse strings with leading zeros as octal in older engines. Additionally, missing the radix parameter violates ESLint's `radix` rule, which exists to prevent subtle numeric parsing bugs.

## Changes

7 `parseInt()` calls updated across 5 files:

| File | Context |
|------|---------|
| `gitnexus/src/core/kuzu/kuzu-adapter.ts` | Step number parsing in edge insertion |
| `gitnexus/src/cli/analyze.ts` | Edge count extraction from warning messages |
| `gitnexus/src/cli/tool.ts` | CLI `--limit` and `--depth` option parsing (2 calls) |
| `gitnexus/src/cli/eval-server.ts` | Port and idle timeout option parsing (2 calls) |
| `gitnexus-web/src/core/kuzu/kuzu-adapter.ts` | Step number parsing (web version) |

## Testing

Pure mechanical change — adds `, 10` to each call. No behavioral difference for valid decimal inputs. Prevents potential misparse of zero-prefixed strings.

title: fix: handle stream errors during CSV writer flush cycles
body:
BufferedCSVWriter registers its error handler only inside finish(). During intermediate addRow/flush cycles, write errors are unhandled — in Node.js this crashes the process. Also, flush() waits on drain but never rejects on error, so the promise hangs indefinitely if a write fails.

Changes:
- Register error handler in constructor to capture errors during all writes
- Check for prior stream errors at start of flush()
- Add error listener alongside drain listener so flush() rejects on failure

title: Fix hook CLI path resolution after gitnexus setup
body:
Fixes #108

When gitnexus setup copies the hook file to ~/.claude/hooks/gitnexus the relative CLI path resolution breaks because the hook is no longer in node_modules/gitnexus.

This fix implements three CLI discovery strategies in order of preference:
1. Use which to find the gitnexus command and resolve from the package root
2. Fall back to relative path from hook location for local development
3. Try global npm root as last resort

The hook now gracefully bails if no CLI can be found instead of crashing with a module not found error.

title: fix: use 1-based ranks in RRF score calculation
body:
## Problem

The RRF (Reciprocal Rank Fusion) formula in local-backend.ts uses 0-based array index directly: 1/(60+i). This gives the rank-0 item a score of 1/60 instead of the correct 1/61.

The same project already has the correct implementation in hybrid-search.ts: 1/(RRF_K+i+1) with the comment "i+1 because rank starts at 1".

## Fix

Changed both RRF loops in local-backend.ts from 1/(60+i) to 1/(60+i+1) to match the standard RRF formula where ranks are 1-indexed.

## Impact

Without this fix, the first item in each result set gets a slightly inflated score (1/60 vs 1/61), which can subtly alter merge ordering when BM25 and semantic search return different top results.

title: TypeError: At least one of max, maxSize, or ttl is required when indexing repos with no parseable files
body:
## Bug Report

**gitnexus version:** 1.3.3  
**lru-cache version:** 11.2.6  
**Node.js version:** 24.0.2  

## Description

Running `gitnexus analyze` crashes with:

```
TypeError: At least one of max, maxSize, or ttl is required
    at createASTCache (dist/core/ingestion/ast-cache.js:5:19)
    at runPipelineFromRepo (dist/core/ingestion/pipeline.js:113:20)
    at async Command.analyzeCommand (dist/cli/analyze.js:166:28)
```

## Root Cause

In `pipeline.js`, the chunk size is computed as:

```js
const maxChunkFiles = chunks.reduce((max, c) => Math.max(max, c.length), 0);
astCache = createASTCache(maxChunkFiles);
```

When no files match (empty repo, all files filtered out, or chunks happen to be empty), `maxChunkFiles` is `0`. This calls `createASTCache(0)`, which passes `max: 0` to `new LRUCache(...)`.

**lru-cache v11 treats `max: 0` as "not provided"** and throws if none of `max`, `maxSize`, or `ttl` are set. This is a breaking behavior change from older versions where `max: 0` was silently accepted.

## Proposed Fix

In `src/core/ingestion/pipeline.ts`, ensure the value passed to `createASTCache` is at least `1`:

```diff
- astCache = createASTCache(maxChunkFiles);
+ astCache = createASTCache(Math.max(1, maxChunkFiles));
```

The same fix applies to the sequential fallback path where `createASTCache(chunkFiles.length)` could also be `0`:

```diff
- astCache = createASTCache(chunkFiles.length);
+ astCache = createASTCache(Math.max(1, chunkFiles.length));
```

title: fix: add symbol-level IMPORTS edges for named imports
body:
#### NOTE: This was fixed by AI and I am by no means a programmer. Please let me know if you have any issues with this.
---
### Problem

The ingestion pipeline only creates **file-to-file** IMPORTS edges. When a file uses a named import like:

```python
from myapp.auth import validate_user
```

The graph only records:

```
auth_controller.py (File) --IMPORTS--> auth.py (File)
```

The specific symbol (`validate_user` function) being imported is lost. This means:

- `impact("validate_user")` can't trace what depends on this function via imports
- `context("validate_user")` doesn't show importing files in its incoming references
- Blast radius analysis falls back to file-level granularity, overstating impact for files that export many symbols

### Solution

Add **symbol-level IMPORTS edges** alongside existing file-level ones by leveraging the `SymbolTable` (already populated during parsing) to resolve named imports to their target nodes.

After this fix, the graph contains both:

```
auth_controller.py (File) --IMPORTS--> auth.py (File)              ← unchanged
auth_controller.py (File) --IMPORTS--> validate_user (Function)     ← NEW
```

### What's affected

| Import pattern | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `from X import foo, bar` (Python) | File → File only | File → File + File → Function/Class |
| `import { foo, bar } from 'X'` (JS/TS) | File → File only | File → File + File → Function/Class |
| `from X import foo as alias` (Python) | File → File only | File → File + File → Function (original name) |
| `import X` (Python bare import) | File → File | No change (correct — no specific symbol imported) |
| `import X from 'Y'` (JS default import) | File → File | No change (default imports don't target named symbols) |
| `from X import *` (Python wildcard) | File → File | No change (wildcard doesn't target specific symbols) |

### Changes

**`src/core/ingestion/workers/parse-worker.ts`**

- Add `extractImportedSymbolNames()` — walks the import AST node to extract named symbols from Python `import_from_statement` and JS/TS `named_imports` nodes
- Attach extracted `symbolNames` array to the `ExtractedImport` interface for the worker data path

**`src/core/ingestion/import-processor.ts`**

- Add `addSymbolImportEdges()` helper in both `processImports` (sequential path) and `processImportsFromExtracted` (worker path)
- For each extracted symbol name, calls `symbolTable.lookupExact(resolvedPath, name)` to find the target Function/Class node
- Creates a high-confidence IMPORTS edge from the source File to the target symbol node
- Accept optional `symbolTable` parameter (no breaking change — undefined falls through gracefully)

**`src/core/ingestion/pipeline.ts`**

- Pass the existing `symbolTable` as a new argument to `processImports()` and `processImportsFromExtracted()`

### Design decisions

- **Additive, not replacing** — file-level edges are preserved. Symbol-level edges are additional. No existing behavior changes.
- **Graceful degradation** — if `symbolTable` is undefined or a symbol isn't found, the code silently skips. No errors for unresolved symbols.
- **Source is File, target is Symbol** — the `sourceId` is the importing File node (not a symbol within it), since Python/JS import statements are module-level, not scoped to a function.
- **Uses `lookupExact` only** — matches symbol by (filePath, name) pair. No fuzzy matching, keeping confidence at 1.0.

### Testing

Verified on a Python LangGraph project (84 nodes). Before: 179 edges (all file-level). After: 179 file-level edges + ~40 new symbol-level IMPORTS edges correctly linking files to the specific Function/Class nodes they import.

Example results from `impact("supervisor")` targeting a Function node:

- **Before**: no upstream edges (function node was unreachable via IMPORTS)
- **After**: `graph.py (File) --IMPORTS--> supervisor (Function)` at depth 1, with correct transitive trace through files that import `graph.py` at depth 2

title: Fix/detect changes hunk mapping
body:
## Summary

This PR upgrades MCP `detect_changes` from file-level detection to hunk-level symbol mapping, and fixes line-side alignment issues that previously caused missed matches.

## What changed

- Switched from `git diff --name-only` to full patch parsing (`--unified=0 --no-color --find-renames --relative`).
- Added robust diff parsing:
  - hunk headers (`@@ -a,b +c,d @@`)
  - quoted/escaped `diff --git` paths (including octal escapes)
  - normalized path handling.
- Replaced file substring matching with exact file-path + line-range overlap matching.
- Added support for change types: `Modified`, `Added`, `Deleted`, `Renamed`.
- Added fallback `UNINDEXED:<file>` nodes when no indexed symbol matches, so file changes are not silently dropped.
- Enriched output with:
  - `summary.changed_hunks`
  - `changed_file_hunks`
  - per-symbol `changed_ranges`, `changed_new_ranges`, `hunk_count`
  - `filePath` in affected process steps.

## Critical fix included

- Symbol matching now prefers **old-side** hunk ranges (`oldRanges`) and keeps `newRanges` for diagnostics.
- This addresses missed detections in scenarios such as:
  - pure deletions
  - insertions near top-of-file followed by edits later (line-shift issue).

## Scope

- 1 file changed: `gitnexus/src/mcp/local/local-backend.ts`
- Branch commits:
  - `2094935` map detect_changes diff hunks to symbols
  - `db91b94` parse quoted diff header paths in detect_changes
  - `e0e9dfd` align detect_changes symbol mapping to old-side hunks

## Validation

- `npm run build` passed.
- Manual smoke checks confirmed expected old/new range behavior for deletion and insertion+modify cases.

## Dear Reviewer
This PR is a substantial behavior change and may include changes you do not want.  （︶^︶）
Please review carefully before merging, especially output-schema expectations and old/new range semantics for downstream consumers.

title: [Feature Request] Integrate Kreuzberg for Enhanced Document Text Recognition
body:
Currently, the workspace has limited capabilities regarding text content recognition and extraction from non-code documents. Users often need to extract text, metadata, or structured information from various file formats (such as PDFs, Office documents, or images) directly within the environment, but the current solution lacks comprehensive format support or performance efficiency.
Describe the solution you'd like
I propose integrating Kreuzberg, a polyglot document intelligence framework with a Rust core, into the code workspace. This integration would enable robust text content recognition and data extraction across a wide variety of file types.
Key Capabilities of Kreuzberg:
Core: High-performance Rust backend.
Format Support: Handles PDFs, Office documents, images, and 76+ other formats.
Extraction: Capable of extracting text, metadata, and structured information.
Polyglot: Designed to work seamlessly across different language environments.
Describe alternatives you've considered
Existing OCR tools: Often limited to images and lack deep structure extraction for Office/PDF files.
Python-based libraries: While flexible, they may introduce heavier dependencies and slower performance compared to a Rust-core solution.
External APIs: Relying on external services introduces latency and privacy concerns; a local integration like Kreuzberg is preferable for a workspace environment.
Potential Implementation Strategy
Dependency Management: Add Kreuzberg as a core dependency (via Cargo if the workspace uses Rust, or via FFI/WASM bindings if the workspace is primarily Electron/JS/TS).
API Exposure: Expose a unified interface (e.g., workspace.document.extractText(file)) that leverages Kreuzberg's engine.
Configuration: Allow users to enable/disable specific parsers based on their needs to optimize resource usage.
Additional Context
Integrating Kreuzberg would significantly boost the workspace's ability to handle RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) pipelines, code context analysis from documentation, and general file indexing.

title: [Bug] Java polymorphic method resolution inaccuracy in call graph (e.g., toResponse overloads)
body:
```markdown
**Title:**  
[Bug] Java call graph merges same-name methods incorrectly (polymorphic resolution missing)

**Description**  
In Java projects, method calls with the same name but from different classes are merged into one node, causing false positives in upstream impact analysis.

**Steps to Reproduce**  
1. Index a Spring Boot project with multiple services having same-named methods (e.g., `toResponse()`).  
2. Run upstream impact on a method like `googleStoreMatch`.  
3. Unrelated methods (e.g., `getStoreInfoListOverview`) appear as callers.

**Evidence**  
- Cypher query:  
```cypher
MATCH (caller:Function)-[:CALLS]->(target:Function {name: 'toResponse'})
WHERE target.class = 'VendorStoreProcessService'
RETURN caller.name, caller.class, count(*) AS call_count
```
Result: `VendorStoreProcessService.toResponse` has **234 callers**, including `getStoreInfoListOverview` (which calls `GetStoreInfoListOverviewService.toResponse`).

- Code example:  
```java
GetStoreInfoListOverviewService service = ...;
service.toResponse(dto);  // Should link to GetStoreInfoListOverviewService.toResponse
// But graph links to VendorStoreProcessService.toResponse
```

**Expected**  
`CALLS` edge should resolve to the correct method based on the receiver's **declared type**, not just method name.

**Actual**  
All same-name methods are merged into one node → wrong upstream counts, inaccurate impact/rename.

**Environment**  
- GitNexus: 1.3.6  
- Language: Java (Spring Boot)  
- Command: `gitnexus analyze . --force --embeddings`  
- Stats: ~8,935 nodes, ~31,787 edges

**Root Cause**  
Tree-sitter Java lacks type-aware resolution for polymorphic calls (only name + signature).

**Suggested Fix**  
1. Track receiver's declared type in resolution phase and disambiguate `CALLS` edges.  
2. Integrate lightweight JavaParser for better symbol/type resolution.  
3. Or create separate nodes per class for same-name methods.

Thanks for the great tool! This fix would greatly improve Java backend accuracy.

title: skip unsupported languages instead of crashing
body:
Running `gitnexus analyze` on a repository containing files in a language whose tree-sitter grammar is unavailable (e.g. Swift when running `git nexus analyze` on [pytorch](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch) repo) crashes with `Error: Unsupported language: swift` instead of skipping the file.


`loadLanguage` throws when a grammar is missing, and several callers (`heritage-processor.ts`, `import-processor.ts`, `call-processor.ts`) don't catch it. The worker-local `setLanguage` in `parse-worker.ts` has the same issue.

The pipeline already warns about unavailable languages upfront, so these files should be silently skipped downstream.

title: wiki command hangs with Ollama local LLM endpoint
body:
## Description

The `npx gitnexus wiki` command hangs indefinitely when using a local Ollama endpoint. The process stops after "Config saved to ~/.gitnexus/config.json" and never progresses to actual LLM calls.

## Environment

- **GitNexus version**: 1.3.6
- **Node**: v25.2.1
- **OS**: macOS (Darwin 24.6.0, Apple Silicon)
- **Ollama**: running locally on `http://localhost:11434`
- **Index**: 7,624 symbols, 15,085 relationships, 262 execution flows

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Index a project: `npx gitnexus analyze` (succeeds)
2. Install Ollama with a standard model (e.g., `llama3.1:8b`)
3. Verify Ollama API works:
   ```bash
   curl -s http://localhost:11434/v1/chat/completions \
     -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
     -d '{"model":"llama3.1:8b","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Say hello"}],"max_tokens":20}'
   # Returns: {"choices":[{"message":{"content":"Hi"}}]} ✅
   ```
4. Run wiki generation:
   ```bash
   npx gitnexus wiki --base-url http://localhost:11434/v1 --model llama3.1:8b --api-key ollama
   ```

## Expected Behavior

Wiki generation should start, showing progress (e.g., percentage) and generating markdown files in `.gitnexus/wiki/`.

## Actual Behavior

Output hangs after:
```
  GitNexus Wiki Generator

  Config saved to ~/.gitnexus/config.json
```

- The `.gitnexus/wiki/` directory is created but remains empty
- No LLM requests are sent (Ollama shows no activity)
- The process must be killed manually
- Tried `--concurrency 1` flag — same result

title: Feature: Markdown as a first-class language for knowledge graph indexing
body:
## Summary

GitNexus currently indexes source code files (Python, JS, TS, etc.) into the knowledge graph but skips markdown files entirely. Repos that are primarily or entirely markdown — documentation repos, knowledge bases, strategy docs, wikis — crash the analyzer (see #135) and produce no graph even when they have rich, structured content worth mapping.

Markdown has real structure that maps naturally to GitNexus's graph model:

- **Headings** → symbols (H1 as top-level, H2-H6 as nested)
- **Cross-references** (links between .md files) → edges (REFERENCES relationship)
- **Document hierarchy** (heading nesting) → CONTAINS relationships
- **Frontmatter** (YAML metadata) → symbol properties
- **Code blocks** → could still be parsed for symbol references
- **Tables of contents / index files** → process-like navigation flows

## Use Case

We run a multi-agent system with several repos that are pure markdown:
- Executive strategy repo (priorities, business model, market position docs)
- Agent memory (structured knowledge entries with frontmatter, cross-references, indexes)
- Rules and skills directories (policy documents, playbooks, templates)

These repos have dozens of interconnected documents with explicit cross-references. Being able to query "what documents reference this concept?" or "what's the blast radius if I restructure this section?" would be as valuable for documentation repos as it is for code repos.

## Proposed Behavior

1. **Treat .md/.mdx files as a supported language** — parse headings, links, frontmatter
2. **Build symbols from headings** — `# Title` becomes a top-level symbol, `## Section` becomes a child
3. **Build edges from links** — `[text](other-file.md)` and `[text](other-file.md#section)` become REFERENCES edges
4. **Detect communities** from link clusters (groups of documents that reference each other heavily)
5. **Build processes** from index/TOC files that define reading order
6. **Graceful handling** when a repo has only markdown — return a valid (possibly sparse) graph instead of crashing (#135)

## Current Behavior

- Markdown-only repos crash with `TypeError: At least one of max, maxSize, or ttl is required` in ast-cache.js (createASTCache called with 0 parseable files)
- Mixed repos index the code but ignore the markdown entirely
- No way to query documentation structure through the graph

## Environment

- GitNexus 1.3.6
- Node.js v20.20.0
- Linux (Ubuntu)

Related: #135 (crash on zero parseable files), #155 (unsupported language handling)

title: Server connect shows cryptic 404 error when no repo is indexed
body:
## Bug

When connecting the web UI to a local gitnexus serve instance that has no indexed repository, the error shown is:

> Server connect failed: Error: Server returned 404: Not Found

This is confusing — users have no idea they need to run gitnexus analyze first.

## Root cause

GET /api/repo already returns a helpful JSON body:


But fetchRepoInfo() in server-connection.ts ignores the JSON body and only reads response.statusText, discarding the actionable message.

## Steps to reproduce
1. Start gitnexus serve in a directory where gitnexus analyze has never been run
2. Open the web UI and enter the server URL
3. See the cryptic error: *Server returned 404: Not Found*

## Expected
The user should see: *Repository not found. Run: gitnexus analyze*

## Fix
Parse the JSON error body on non-ok responses in fetchRepoInfo() and surface it to the user.

## Problem

title: Feature request: cross-lingual query support (--smart flag)
body:
## Problem

GitNexus FTS indexes English code symbols (function names, file names, variable names). However, many development teams discuss code in non-English languages (Chinese, Japanese, Korean, Spanish, etc.).

When a user searches for `"收盘评分链可靠性改进"` (Chinese for "closing score pipeline reliability improvement"), `gitnexus query` returns zero results because FTS cannot match Chinese text against English code symbols.

## Current Workaround

We built a wrapper that uses an LLM to translate non-English topics into English code keywords before passing them to `gitnexus query`:

```
"收盘评分链可靠性改进"
  → LLM → "signal_scorer closing_score reliability pipeline"
  → gitnexus query → relevant code symbols
```

This works well but requires each project to implement its own translation layer.

## Proposed Solution

Add a `--smart` (or `--translate`) flag to `gitnexus query` that automatically detects non-English input and translates it to English code keywords before searching:

```bash
# Current: user must manually translate
gitnexus query -r myrepo "signal_scorer closing_score reliability"

# Proposed: automatic cross-lingual mapping
gitnexus query -r myrepo "收盘评分链可靠性改进" --smart
```

### Design Considerations

1. **LLM provider**: Could use a lightweight local model (e.g., Ollama) or configurable provider (OpenAI/Anthropic/etc.) to avoid hard dependency
2. **Opt-in only**: The `--smart` flag keeps the default behavior unchanged (zero LLM dependency for normal queries)
3. **Caching**: Translation results could be cached to avoid repeated LLM calls for similar topics
4. **Detection**: Could auto-detect non-ASCII-dominant input and suggest using `--smart`

### Alternative: `augment` Extension

Another approach: extend the existing `gitnexus augment` command to handle cross-lingual input, since it is already designed as the "intelligence layer" for platform hooks.

## Use Case

We use GitNexus in multi-agent review board systems where:
- Discussion topics are in Chinese
- Code is in English (Python)
- 3 indexed repos (5185 / 2275 / 298 nodes)
- Automated knowledge pack generation queries GitNexus per topic

The cross-lingual gap is the #1 friction point in our workflow.

## Environment
- GitNexus v1.3.6
- macOS (arm64)
- Repos: Python codebases

title: feat(gitnexus): honor .gitignore/custom ignore profiles in indexing + stale checks
body:
## Summary
- honor `.gitignore` during repository scanning via `git check-ignore`
- add repo-local ignore profile support (`.gitnexusignore`, `.gitnexusignore.<profile>`, `--ignore-file`, `--ignore-profile`)
- make staleness checks ignore-aware by filtering changed files through the same rules
- persist active ignore config in index metadata/registry so status/resources evaluate staleness with the same profile used for indexing
- apply ignore-aware filtering to `detect_changes`
- reindex when ignore-rule files change between indexed commit and `HEAD` (for example `.gitignore` and `.gitnexusignore*`), even if no relevant source files changed
- preserve directory-only custom matcher semantics so patterns like `deploy-v1/` exclude descendants but do not exclude files named `deploy-v1`

## Why
Generated/build artifacts (for example `cdk.out` and `deploy-v1`) can dominate graph results and trigger stale updates even when only ignored paths changed.

Without the staleness + directory-only follow-up fixes, ignore-rule-only commits could be misclassified as up-to-date and custom directory-only patterns could overmatch.

## Validation
- `npm run build`
- `npm test` (all unit tests pass)
- `npx vitest run test/unit/ignore-service.test.ts test/unit/staleness.test.ts test/integration/filesystem-walker.test.ts`

## Notes
- README updated with new analyze options and ignore configuration behavior.

title: Wiki generation fails on large repositories due to context window overflow
body:
# Summary

`npx gitnexus wiki` crashes during the **"Grouping files into modules (LLM)"** step when run on large repositories. The tool attempts to send the entire repository content in a single LLM prompt, which can reach **up to 1.2 million tokens** — far exceeding the 200,000-token limit of Claude models.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Run `npx gitnexus wiki` on a large repository (e.g., a monorepo or a project with many files)
2. Wait for the progress bar to reach ~15% ("Grouping files into modules (LLM)...")
3. Observe the crash

## Actual Behavior

The process exits with an error:

```
LLM Error: LLM API error (400): {
  "error": {
    "message": "litellm.ContextWindowExceededError: litellm.BadRequestError: AnthropicError -
    '{\"type\":\"error\",\"error\":{\"type\":\"invalid_request_error\",
    \"message\":\"prompt is too long: 468935 tokens > 200000 maximum\"},
    \"request_id\":\"req_011CYiZkaqdgRo3B3FojoKbu\"}'\n
    model=claude-sonnet-4-6. context_window_fallbacks=None. fallbacks=None."
  }
}
```

- **Observed prompt size in the reported case:** ~469,000 tokens
- **Estimated worst-case prompt size on very large repos:** up to ~1,200,000 tokens
- **Model context limit:** 200,000 tokens (Claude claude-sonnet-4-6)

## Expected Behavior

The tool should handle large repositories gracefully — either by:
- Chunking the file list and processing it in multiple batches, or
- Pre-filtering files (e.g., respecting `.gitignore`, skipping binaries/lock files/generated files), or
- Providing a configurable file inclusion/exclusion mechanism before the LLM step

## Environment

| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| Tool | `gitnexus` (via `npx gitnexus wiki`) |
| Model | `claude-sonnet-4-6` |
| Error stage | 15% — "Grouping files into modules (LLM)" |

## Suggested Fix

The "Grouping files into modules" step should not attempt to pass the full repository content in one shot. Possible approaches:

1. **Chunked processing** — Split the file list into batches of N files and make multiple LLM calls, merging the module groupings afterward.
2. **File pre-filtering** — Before calling the LLM, strip files that are unlikely to need documentation: lock files (`package-lock.json`, `yarn.lock`), build artifacts, binary files, vendored code, etc.

## Impact

**High** — Wiki generation is completely non-functional for any large or monorepo-scale codebase. This is likely to affect a significant portion of real-world users since large projects are the ones that would benefit most from automated wiki generation.

title: feat: In-Browser Execution via WebContainers and Instant Run
body:
# Pull Request: In-Browser Execution via WebContainers & `gitnexus-bundler` integration

## Overview

📺 **[Watch the Video Demo here](https://youtu.be/hjlBrGLujPA)**

GitNexus currently provides exceptional static code intelligence—allowing users to understand what code does and how it connects through interactive knowledge graphs. 

This PR introduces the missing piece: **Execution**. 

By integrating `@webcontainer/api`, users can now transition from "I understand this code" to "I am running this app" in a single click. Everything runs entirely client-side in the browser, with no external compute servers or local installations required.

## Key Additions

### 1. Instant Run & `gitnexus-bundler` Integration
- Introduced native support for `gitnexus.json` manifests.
- Developers can use the companion [`gitnexus-bundler` CLI](https://www.npmjs.com/package/gitnexus-bundler) to compile their Node.js or full-stack React/Next.js apps into a single, self-contained `.cjs` output.
- When GitNexus detects a `gitnexus.json` pointing to a bundle, it engages **Instant Load Mode**. The bundle is fetched and booted inside the WebContainer in under 5 seconds—completely bypassing the slow, fragile `npm install` and compilation steps inside the browser.
- **UI:** A distinct **"Instant Run ⚡"** button appears in the header for these optimized repositories.

### 2. Universal WebContainer Fallback 
- For standard Node.js repositories without a manifest (but containing a `package.json`), GitNexus provides a standard **"Run App ▶"** button.
- GitNexus automatically mounts the repository tree into the WebContainer and attempts a standard execution sequence (`npm install` followed by `npm run dev`/`start`). While setup takes longer than Instant Run, it offers a seamless best-effort execution environment.

### 3. Integrated Terminal & Preview Panel
- Added a `WebContainerPanel` component that slides in seamlessly from the right.
- Features a secure terminal interface powered by `xterm.js` to display live build logs and server outputs.
- Includes a responsive `iframe` preview panel that automatically binds to and loads the exposed application port (e.g., `8080`) once the server is ready.

### 4. Optional Feature: GitNexus Marketplace
- As a demonstration of this execution capability, we've linked an optional community extension: the [GitNexus Marketplace](https://github.com/GitNexus-Marketplace/gitnexus-marketplace).
- This serves as an open, community-driven registry where users can discover and instantly boot compatible AI tools and applications optimized with `gitnexus-bundler`.
- *(Note: This marketplace integration is entirely opt-in and secondary. The core knowledge graph and indexing pipelines for standard repos remain completely unaffected).*

### 5. Direct URL Loading (Auto-Clone)
- Added routing support to dynamically clone and analyze GitHub repositories straight from the URL path.
- Users can navigate to `localhost:5173/github.com/owner/repo` (or their staging domain) to automatically trigger the cloning sequence without manually pasting URLs.
- Significantly improves onboarding flow when sharing links to specific repositories.

## Value Proposition
This transforms GitNexus from a code visualization platform into an **interactive cloud operating system**. It directly answers the user's next logical question after exploring a knowledge graph: *"Does it actually work?"* By closing the gap between analysis and execution, we remove all friction from testing open-source repositories.

## Technical Details & Review Notes
- **Dependencies Added:** `@webcontainer/api` and `xterm`.
- **Security Headers:** The WebContainer API intrinsically requires COOP/COEP isolation headers (`Cross-Origin-Embedder-Policy: require-corp`, `Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy: same-origin`) to be active on the GitNexus hosting server in order to enable `SharedArrayBuffer`.
- **Component Logic:** Header UI conditionally renders execution buttons strictly based on the presence of `gitnexus.json` or `package.json` in the parsed repository graph. All mounting logic reconstructs flat file arrays into the hierarchical trees required by the WebContainer filesystem.

title: C# files indexed as File/Folder only — no Class, Method, Interface, or Namespace nodes extracted
body:
When indexing a C# (.NET 10) repository with gitnexus analyze, C# source files (.cs) are indexed only as File and Folder nodes. No semantic symbols (Class, Method, Interface, Property, Namespace, Record, etc.) are extracted.

  This makes GitNexus unusable for C# projects — no execution flows, no call graphs, no meaningful clusters.

  Environment

  - GitNexus: 1.3.6
  - OS: Windows 11
  - Repository: Mixed C#/.NET 10 backend + Angular/TypeScript frontend, with git submodules (TypeScript, Go)

  Evidence

  C# files — zero symbol extraction:

  MATCH (n) WHERE n.filePath ENDS WITH '.cs' AND n.filePath STARTS WITH 'src/'
  RETURN labels(n)[0] AS type, count(*)
  -- Result: type = (empty), count = 199

  TypeScript files in the same repo — symbols extracted correctly:

  MATCH (n:Class) WHERE n.filePath CONTAINS 'component'
  RETURN n.name, n.filePath
  -- Result: DashboardComponent, RepositoriesComponent, etc.

  Python files in the same repo — symbols extracted correctly:

  MATCH (n:Class) WHERE n.filePath CONTAINS 'Python'
  RETURN n.name
  -- Result: UserService, BaseEntity, User, AdminUser

  Expected behavior

  C# files should produce Class, Method, Interface, Namespace, Property, Record nodes — same as TypeScript and Python. For example, a file containing public class MyService : IMyService should produce a Class node + an IMPLEMENTS edge.

  Impact

  - Clusters are meaningless for C# code since no symbols exist
  - Execution flows contain zero C# traces — all 300 detected processes come from TypeScript/Python code in the same repo
  - Query/context/impact tools only return File-level matches for C#
  - README lists C# as a supported language

  Bonus request

  A .gitnexusignore or --exclude option would help exclude submodules/ and test data directories that otherwise dominate the index.

title: fix: always force-exit after analyze to avoid KuzuDB destructor crash
body:
## Summary

- `npx gitnexus analyze` crashes under some circumstances with "double free or corruption (out)" or "munmap_chunk(): invalid pointer" on **Node 22+**
- KuzuDB 0.11.3's native `atexit` hooks corrupt the heap during natural process shutdown
- The existing `process.exit(0)` workaround was conditional on `--embeddings` being enabled; without it (the default), the process exits naturally and hits the crash

## Fix

Always call `process.exit(0)` after successful completion, since KuzuDB is always loaded. One-line change (removes the `if (!embeddingSkipped)` guard).

## Root cause analysis

KuzuDB 0.11.3's C++ destructors registered via `atexit` conflict with Node 22's V8 shutdown sequence. Minimal reproducer:

\`\`\`js
const kuzu = require('kuzu');
const db = new kuzu.Database('/tmp/test');
const conn = new kuzu.Connection(db);
await conn.query('CREATE NODE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS T(id STRING, PRIMARY KEY(id))');
await conn.close();
await db.close();
// Process exits naturally → segfault
\`\`\`

This happens regardless of tree-sitter or worker threads — it's purely KuzuDB 0.11.3 + Node 22.

## Test plan

- [x] \`gitnexus analyze --force\` completes cleanly on Node 22.22.0 (exit code 0, no crash)
- [x] Worker pool path works (15.6s vs 50s sequential)
- [x] Verified crash does not occur with \`process.exit(0)\`
- [x] Verified \`embeddingSkipped\` variable is still used in summary output (no unused var)
