title: feat: added skip-agents-md cli flag
body:
## Summary

Adds a new gitnexus analyze --skip-agents-md flag to skip updating the GitNexus-managed sections in AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md, allowing users to preserve manual/custom instructions in the gitnexus sections of those files.

## Motivation / context

Some users maintain custom guidance in AGENTS.md / CLAUDE.md and don’t want gitnexus analyze to rewrite those files' GitNexus blocks on each run. This flag provides an explicit opt-out while keeping the default behavior unchanged. This addresses #510 

## Areas touched

- [x] `gitnexus/` (CLI / core / MCP server)
- [ ] `gitnexus-web/` (Vite / React UI)
- [ ] `.github/` (workflows, actions)
- [ ] `eval/` or other tooling
- [ ] Docs / agent config only (`AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `.cursor/`, `llms.txt`, etc.)

## Scope & constraints

**In scope**

- Add a new CLI flag gitnexus analyze --skip-agents-md.
- When the flag is set, skip updating the GitNexus-managed sections in AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md.
- Plumb the option from CLI → AnalyzeOptions → generateAIContextFiles(...).
- Update docs (README.md, gitnexus/README.md) to mention the new flag.
- Add/adjust unit tests to cover the new behavior and CLI help output.

**Explicitly out of scope / not done here**

- Changing the default behavior of gitnexus analyze (still updates AGENTS.md / CLAUDE.md unless the flag is provided).
- Changing the format/markers/content of the GitNexus inserted blocks.
- Any changes to embeddings, skill generation behavior, indexing pipeline logic, or MCP server behavior.
- Any changes to gitnexus-web.

## Implementation notes

- Implemented as an optional `AIContextOptions` argument to `generateAIContextFiles(...)` (`skipAgentsMd?: boolean`).
- The skip is applied by guarding the existing upsert calls for `AGENTS.md` and `CLAUDE.md` behind `if (!options?.skipAgentsMd)`.
- Commander wiring adds --skip-agents-md and maps it into `AnalyzeOptions.skipAgentsMd`.

## Testing & verification

<!-- What you ran; paste commands. Omit sections that do not apply. -->

- [x] `cd gitnexus && npm test`

- [ ] `cd gitnexus-web && npx tsc -b --noEmit` *(if web changed)*
- [ ] Manual / Playwright E2E *(note environment — see `gitnexus-web/e2e/`)*

If you didn’t actually run npm test / tsc yet, flip those [x] back to [ ] before opening.

## Risk & rollout

- Risk: Low. Behavior change is behind an opt-in flag; default behavior remains unchanged.
- Breaking changes: None intended.
- Rollout: No migration required. Users who want to preserve manual AGENTS.md / CLAUDE.md edits can re-run indexing with:
    - `gitnexus analyze --skip-agents-md`
- Rollback: Revert the flag wiring and the generateAIContextFiles option gate; docs/tests revert cleanly.

title: refactor: split global BUILT_IN_NAMES into per-language noise filters
body:
## Problem

`BUILT_IN_NAMES` in `gitnexus/src/core/ingestion/utils/noise-filter.ts` is a single global `Set` applied to **all languages**. With 14 supported languages, entries accumulate and cause cross-language false positives:

- `push`/`pop` — JS array methods, but also C stack operations and Rust `Vec::push`
- `map`/`filter` — JS/Python/Rust/Swift collection methods, but also meaningful domain names
- `close` — was previously removed for C POSIX (`// NOTE: 'open', 'read', 'write', 'close' removed`), but Dart/Kotlin sections re-add it
- `add` — Java `List.add()`, Python `set.add()`, but also valid domain method names
- `then`/`catch`/`finally` — JS Promise methods added globally, suppress Rust `Result::catch` etc.

Any entry added for one language silently suppresses call graph edges in all other languages.

## Proposed solution

Replace the single `BUILT_IN_NAMES: Set<string>` with a per-language structure:

```typescript
const BUILT_IN_NAMES: Record<SupportedLanguages, ReadonlySet<string>> = {
  [SupportedLanguages.JavaScript]: new Set(['console', 'log', 'setTimeout', ...]),
  [SupportedLanguages.Python]: new Set(['print', 'len', 'range', ...]),
  // ...
};

// Shared entries that are genuinely universal noise
const UNIVERSAL_NOISE = new Set(['toString', 'valueOf', 'hashCode']);

export const isBuiltInOrNoise = (name: string, language: SupportedLanguages): boolean =>
  UNIVERSAL_NOISE.has(name) || BUILT_IN_NAMES[language]?.has(name) || false;
```

This requires updating callers of `isBuiltInOrNoise` to pass the language parameter (currently ~3 call sites in `parse-worker.ts` and `parsing-processor.ts` where language is already available).

## Scope

- Refactor `noise-filter.ts` to per-language sets
- Update `isBuiltInOrNoise` signature to accept `SupportedLanguages`
- Update call sites (`parse-worker.ts`, `parsing-processor.ts`)
- Use `satisfies Record<SupportedLanguages, ...>` for compile-time exhaustiveness
- Move shared entries (truly universal noise like `toString`) to a small universal set

## Context

Raised during review of Dart language support (abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus#204). @magyargergo requested this as a follow-up.

title: fix: close remaining Dart language support gaps
body:
## Summary

Fixes 4 gaps in the Dart language support that were not addressed in PR #204:

- **`extractFunctionName` + `FUNCTION_NODE_TYPES`**: PR #204 moved `@definition.function` onto `function_signature` nodes but never added them to `FUNCTION_NODE_TYPES` or `extractFunctionName`. Without this, `findEnclosingFunctionId` can't resolve Dart function scopes — all CALLS edges from inside Dart functions have no `sourceId`, breaking call attribution.

- **`formal_parameter_list` in `paramListTypes`**: Dart's tree-sitter grammar uses `formal_parameter_list` (not `formal_parameters`). Without adding it to `paramListTypes`, `extractMethodSignature` returns `parameterCount: 0` for every Dart function.

- **Write-access queries**: PR #204 has no `@assignment` patterns for Dart. Without them, no `ACCESSES write` edges are emitted — `obj.field = value` and `this.field = value` are invisible to the graph. Every other language (except C) has these.

- **`initialized_identifier` guard**: `DART_DECLARATION_NODE_TYPES` includes `initialized_identifier` (for comma-separated declarations like `String a, b, c`), but `extractDartDeclaration` only handled `initialized_variable_definition`. Variables after the first comma silently got no type binding because the type lives on the parent node.

Also adds Dart column to the feature matrix in `type-resolution-system.md`.

## Changed files

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `ast-helpers.ts` | Add `function_signature`/`method_signature` to `FUNCTION_NODE_TYPES` and `extractFunctionName`; add `formal_parameter_list` to `paramListTypes` |
| `tree-sitter-queries.ts` | Add 2 write-access query patterns for Dart |
| `type-extractors/dart.ts` | Add `initialized_identifier` guard in `extractDartDeclaration` |
| `type-resolution-system.md` | Add Dart column to feature matrix |

## Test plan

- [x] `tsc --noEmit` passes
- [x] All 4112 tests pass (119 test files, 0 failures)
- [x] No existing language behavior affected (all changes are additive — new `else if` branches, new set entries, new query patterns)

title: perf(web): comprehensive graph rendering and UI performance overhaul
body:
## Summary

- **Progressive node loading**: For graphs >2k nodes, only Folders/Files/Classes visible initially. Functions/Methods/Variables hidden — reveal via Filters tab. Reduces visible nodes from 55k→10k.
- **Edge optimization**: Max 8-15 edges per node, skip structural edges (CONTAINS/DEFINES/IMPORTS) for 5k+, straight lines instead of curves for 5k+. Reduces edges from 186k→15k.
- **Skip O(n²) layout**: For 10k+ nodes, skip ForceAtlas2 entirely — hierarchical positions from graph-adapter are sufficient. Cached positions in sessionStorage for instant reload.
- **Context splitting**: New `CodeRefsContext` isolates AI citation updates so GraphCanvas/FileTree/Header don't re-render during chat streaming.
- **O(1) lookups**: Pre-built `nodeMap`, `nodeIdSet`, `filePathIndex`, `fileNodeIndex` replace all `graph.nodes.find()` O(n) calls in hot paths.
- **Reducer fast-paths**: For 2k+ graphs, skip dimming of non-active nodes — only modify selected/highlighted nodes. Turns O(N) allocations into O(k).
- **Lazy mermaid**: ~480KB loaded on first diagram render via `import('mermaid')` + SVG caching.
- **Sigma tuning**: 30fps animation throttle, color caching, disable hover/edge events for large graphs, adaptive label density.
- **Bundle**: 8 vendor chunks (added vendor-git, vendor-ml, vendor-markdown), debounced search, useTransition for filters, code viewer windowed to ~70 lines.
- **FPS counter**: Live overlay top-right for monitoring.

title: feat: Add Solidity language support
body:
### Area

gitnexus (CLI / core / indexing / MCP server)

### Problem or opportunity

Smart contract codebases are structurally complex in ways that map well to a knowledge graph. Contracts inherit from base contracts (OpenZeppelin's UUPS proxy pattern, for example), modifiers compose like middleware, events act as cross-boundary signals, and import graphs can get deep. This is exactly the kind of code where grep falls short and graph-based analysis would help.

### Proposed solution

Add Solidity as a supported language using the existing `tree-sitter-solidity` grammar.

A mature grammar already exists:
- **Repo:** [JoranHonig/tree-sitter-solidity](https://github.com/JoranHonig/tree-sitter-solidity) (185 stars, MIT, actively maintained)
- **npm:** `tree-sitter-solidity@1.2.13`

The grammar exposes AST node types that map cleanly to GitNexus's symbol model:
- `contract_declaration`, `interface_declaration`, `library_declaration` for top-level definitions
- `function_definition`, `constructor_definition`, `modifier_definition` for callable members
- `event_definition`, `struct_declaration`, `enum_declaration` for type definitions
- `state_variable_declaration` for properties
- `import_directive` for import resolution (`import "./Foo.sol"` and `import {X} from "./Foo.sol"`)
- `inheritance_specifier` for heritage tracking

Following the checklist in `supported-languages.ts`, the integration touches:
1. `supported-languages.ts` - add `Solidity = 'solidity'` to enum
2. `parser-loader.ts` - import and register grammar
3. `languages/solidity.ts` - new `LanguageProvider` with tree-sitter queries
4. `languages/index.ts` - register provider
5. `language-detection.ts` - add `.sol` extension mapping
6. `tree-sitter-queries.ts`, `export-detection.ts`, `import-resolvers/solidity.ts`, `call-routing.ts`, `entry-point-scoring.ts`, `framework-detection.ts`, `type-extractors/solidity.ts`
7. `package.json` - add `tree-sitter-solidity` dependency

**Known blocker:** `tree-sitter-solidity` declares `peerDependencies: { "tree-sitter": "^0.25.0" }` while GitNexus pins tree-sitter at `0.22.4`. An older version of `tree-sitter-solidity` (1.0.x/1.1.x) may still be compatible with 0.22.x, or it could be added as an `optionalDependency` following the Kotlin/Swift pattern.

### Alternatives considered

Follow the COBOL precedent (issue #498) and use a standalone regex processor based on `markdown-processor.ts`. This avoids the tree-sitter version mismatch entirely but would produce a less precise graph for a language with Solidity's level of syntactic structure (nested contracts, multiple inheritance, modifier chains).

### Acceptance criteria

- `.sol` files are parsed and symbols appear in the knowledge graph
- `contract`, `interface`, `library` declarations are indexed as top-level symbols
- `function`, `constructor`, `modifier`, `event` definitions are indexed as members
- Solidity import directives are resolved correctly (both path imports and named imports)
- Inheritance relationships (`is BaseContract, OtherContract`) create heritage edges in the graph
- `query`, `context`, and `impact` return meaningful results for Solidity symbols

### Constraints

- Must not break existing language support if `tree-sitter-solidity` fails to install (use `optionalDependencies` pattern)
- Tree-sitter version compatibility needs to be resolved (0.22.4 vs 0.25.0 peer dep)

### Contribution

- [x] I am willing to open a PR for this

title: feat: WCAG 2.2 AA accessibility detection with wcag_audit tool
body: ## Summary Adds WCAG 2.2 AA accessibility detection to GitNexus using a three-category system modeled after axe-core's zero-false-positive approach: - **Violation** — statically proven issue, zero doubt - **Needs-review** — suspicious pattern, requires human/AI verification with exact file:line context - **Pass** — statically proven accessible Validated on two real Next.js codebases (27K+ and 1.4K JSX elements): **zero false positives in the violation category** across both projects. ## Why this approach (not axe-core integration) GitNexus's value is **code intelligence from static analysis** — understanding relationships, impact, and structure without running the app. Integrating axe-core (runtime DOM testing) would make GitNexus a pass-through data store rather than an intelligent analyzer. Instead, this feature keeps GitNexus's identity: static analysis that provides **pre-filtered targets for AI agents**. When an AI agent needs to fix a11y issues, instead of reading dozens of files (~50K tokens), it queries `wcag_audit` and gets: - Proven violations with exact file:line → fix directly (~2K tokens) - Needs-review items with specific review prompts → targeted verification (~5K tokens per item) - Fix patterns from components in the same codebase that already pass the criterion The needs-review items are not noise — they're **pre-filtered locations** that reduce AI exploration from 27,000 JSX elements to ~300 specific targets. ## What's included **Three-category detection system:** - Violations only when statically provable (e.g., `` with zero alt/aria-label, `

title: perf: content-addressed parse and embedding caches for faster reindexing
body:
## Summary

Cache deterministic per-file operations to reduce reindexing time.

## Motivation / context

When under active development, code changes quickly and the graph gets stale. Reducing reindex time improves DX.

## Areas touched

- [X] `gitnexus/` (CLI / core / MCP server)
- [ ] `gitnexus-web/` (Vite / React UI)
- [ ] `.github/` (workflows, actions)
- [ ] `eval/` or other tooling
- [ ] Docs / agent config only (`AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `.cursor/`, `llms.txt`, etc.)

## Scope & constraints

**In scope**

- Parse cache: content-addressed per-file Tree-sitter results (SHA-256 of file content).
- Embedding cache: content-addressed per-node embedding vectors (SHA-256 of embedding input text).
- Both caches survive `--force` (content-addressed, always safe to reuse).
- Replaces old LadybugDB-based embedding cache (lost on `--force`, keyed by node ID not content).

**Explicitly out of scope / not done here**

- Incremental LadybugDB load

## Implementation notes

- Shared `cache-io.ts` for atomic JSON read/write/delete with version validation
- Parse cache stored in `.gitnexus/parse-cache.json`, embedding cache in `.gitnexus/embedding-cache.json`

title: fix: probe CUDA availability in MCP embedder before requesting it
body:
## Summary

Add CUDA availability probe to the MCP embedder so semantic search works on systems without CUDA.

## Motivation / context

The MCP embedder blindly attempted CUDA initialization on Linux. When CUDA libraries were absent, the failed attempt poisoned ONNX Runtime's native state, causing the CPU fallback to fail with the same CUDA error. This silently disabled all semantic vector search — the `catch` in `semanticSearch()` swallowed the error and returned `[]`, so queries fell back to BM25-only with no visible indication.

The core embedder (`src/core/embeddings/embedder.ts`) already had `isCudaAvailable()` / `hasOrtCudaProvider()` guards that probe for CUDA libraries before requesting them. The MCP embedder was missing these guards.

## Areas touched

- [X] `gitnexus/` (CLI / core / MCP server)
- [ ] `gitnexus-web/` (Vite / React UI)
- [ ] `.github/` (workflows, actions)
- [ ] `eval/` or other tooling
- [ ] Docs / agent config only (`AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `.cursor/`, `llms.txt`, etc.)

## Scope & constraints

**In scope**

- Port `hasOrtCudaProvider()` and `isCudaAvailable()` from the core embedder to the MCP embedder
- Skip CUDA attempt entirely when system lacks required libraries
- Affects both MCP server and CLI `query` command (both use the same MCP embedder)

**Explicitly out of scope / not done here**

- Refactoring to share the CUDA probe between core and MCP embedders

## Implementation notes

- `hasOrtCudaProvider()` resolves `onnxruntime-node` from transformers.js's module scope and checks for `libonnxruntime_providers_cuda.so`
- `isCudaAvailable()` additionally probes `ldconfig -p` and `CUDA_PATH`/`LD_LIBRARY_PATH` for `libcublasLt.so.12`
- Device list construction now skips CUDA when probe returns false, going straight to CPU

## Testing & verification

- [X] `cd gitnexus && npx tsc --noEmit`
- [X] `cd gitnexus && npm test` — 128 files, 4457 tests passed
- [X] Manual: `npx gitnexus query "retry with exponential backoff" -r GitNexus` now prints "Embedding model loaded (cpu)" and returns semantic results (previously returned BM25-only)

## Risk & rollout

- No behavioral change on systems with CUDA — the probe returns true and CUDA is attempted as before
- On systems without CUDA, semantic search now works instead of silently failing
- No migration or config changes needed

## Checklist

- [X] PR body meets repo minimum length

title: feat: unify web and cli ingestion pipeline
body:
## Summary

Complete architectural migration of GitNexus web from a self-contained browser app (WASM LadybugDB, Web Worker, in-browser embeddings) to a thin client backed by the CLI server. Also creates `gitnexus-shared` package for cross-package type unification.

## Architecture

```
BROWSER (gitnexus-web)
├─ OnboardingGuide → auto-detect server → auto-connect → graph explorer
├─ RepoAnalyzer → GitHub URL or Local Folder → SSE progress → graph loads
├─ Header → repo dropdown (switch / re-analyze / delete) + search
├─ CodeReferencesPanel → buffered file reading → scroll to selected line
├─ GraphCanvas + FileTree + NexusAI + StatusBar
└─ BackendClient → all queries via HTTP to localhost:4747

SERVER (gitnexus serve — Express)
├─ GET  /api/heartbeat     SSE liveness (instant disconnect detection)
├─ GET  /api/info           Version, launch context, Node.js version
├─ GET  /api/repos          List indexed repositories
├─ GET  /api/repo           Repo metadata
├─ DELETE /api/repo         Delete repo (index + clone + registry)
├─ GET  /api/graph          Nodes + relationships
├─ GET  /api/file           Read file (supports ?startLine=N&endLine=M)
├─ POST /api/query          Cypher (write-guarded)
├─ POST /api/search         Hybrid search + enrichment
├─ GET  /api/grep           Regex over file contents
├─ POST /api/analyze        SSE progress → child_process (8GB, auto-retry)
├─ POST /api/embed          SSE progress for embedding generation
├─ ALL  /api/mcp            MCP-over-StreamableHTTP
└─ LadybugDB + tree-sitter + FTS

gitnexus-shared (types)
├─ GraphNode, GraphRelationship, NodeLabel, NODE_TABLES
├─ SupportedLanguages (exhaustive Record enforcement)
├─ PipelinePhase, PipelineProgress
└─ getLanguageFromFilename, getSyntaxLanguageFromFilename
```

## What changed

### Onboarding & UX (new)
- **Auto server detection** — polling via setTimeout chain (3s), Page Visibility API pause, SSE heartbeat for instant disconnect detection
- **OnboardingGuide** — step-by-step instructions (copy → run → auto-connect), smart command detection (dev vs prod via `import.meta.env.DEV`)
- **Crossfade transitions** — smooth phase changes (onboarding → success → loading → exploring) with snapshot pattern
- **Server heartbeat** — SSE EventSource with exponential backoff (3 retries), instant server-down detection from exploring view
- **Node.js version** auto-detected from package.json via Vite define (not bundled)

### Repository Analysis (new)
- **AnalyzeOnboarding** — empty-state card when server has zero repos
- **RepoAnalyzer** — GitHub URL + Local Folder tabs with browse button (webkitdirectory)
- **Header repo dropdown** — click project badge to: switch repos, re-analyze with force (live SSE progress), delete repos
- **Delete repos** — `DELETE /api/repo` with repo lock (409 if analyze in flight), cleans index + clone dir + registry
- **Re-analyze** — `POST /api/analyze` with `force: true`, spinning icon + inline progress bar via SSE
- **Auto-select** — after analysis completes, refreshes repo list and connects to the specific repo by name

### Code Inspector (new)
- **Buffered file reading** — `GET /api/file?startLine=N&endLine=M` for partial reads (±50 lines around symbols)
- **Auto scroll to line** — after content loads, scrolls to selected node's startLine with highlight
- **Loading spinner** — shows while fetching source from server

### Server Resilience (new)
- **Worker auto-retry** — up to 2 retries with exponential backoff (1s, 2s) on crash
- **Dev mode fork fix** — resolves tsx ESM hook via `pathToFileURL` for Windows/macOS/Linux
- **Error handling** — friendly messages for EADDRINUSE, global uncaughtException/unhandledRejection handlers
- **backend.init() sequencing** — awaited before SSE complete event, job fails if init fails
- **Repo lock on delete** — prevents deleting while analyze/embed is in flight

### Existing (from earlier commits)
- **Server-side ingestion** — `POST /api/analyze` with SSE progress, `child_process.fork()` with 8GB heap, cancellation, 30-min timeout
- **Unified shared types** — `gitnexus-shared` package with exhaustive `Record<SupportedLanguages, ...>` enforcement
- **Backend-only LadybugDB** — removed WASM from browser, all queries via HTTP
- **Enhanced search** — hybrid/semantic/BM25 modes, server-side enrichment
- **Security** — `isWriteQuery()` guard, CORS fix, `x-powered-by` disabled, `prefers-reduced-motion` CSS

### Accessibility
- `prefers-reduced-motion` global CSS rule (WCAG 2.3.3)
- ARIA: `role="tablist/tab"`, `aria-selected`, `role="status"`, `aria-live="polite"`
- `focus-visible:ring-2` on interactive elements
- `cursor-pointer` on all clickable elements

### Tests
- 11 Playwright e2e tests covering all onboarding flows (mock backend for offline tests)
- Updated `server-connect.spec.ts` for auto-connect flow (no manual Connect button)
- 198 unit tests passing, TypeScript clean across all 3 packages

## Packages removed from web (7)
`@ladybugdb/wasm-core`, `@huggingface/transformers`, `comlink`, `minisearch`, `vite-plugin-wasm`, `vite-plugin-top-level-await`, `vite-plugin-static-copy`

title: fix: resolve tree-sitter peer dependency conflicts breaking MCP server install via npx
body:
## Summary

Fixes #537 — MCP server fails to connect via `npx -y gitnexus@latest mcp` due to tree-sitter peer dependency conflicts.

### Root Cause

`gitnexus@1.4.9` pins `tree-sitter@^0.25.0`, but 9 of 14 bundled language parsers declare peer deps on `^0.21.x` or `^0.22.x`. npm 7+ treats peer dep conflicts as hard errors (ERESOLVE), blocking installation. The `overrides` field in `package.json` only applies when the package is the **root project** — when installed via `npx`, gitnexus is NOT the root, so overrides are silently ignored.

### Fix

Downgrade `tree-sitter` to `^0.21.1` and align all parser versions to their highest `^0.21.x`-compatible releases. This is the only tree-sitter version on npm where all 14 parsers agree without overrides (npm jumps from `0.22.4` → `0.25.0` with no `0.23.x`/`0.24.x` releases).

### Changes

| Package | Before | After | Reason |
|---------|--------|-------|--------|
| tree-sitter | ^0.25.0 | ^0.21.1 | Only version satisfying all parsers |
| tree-sitter-c | ^0.24.1 | 0.23.2 | 0.24.x needs ^0.22.4 |
| tree-sitter-go | ^0.25.0 | ^0.23.0 | 0.25.x needs ^0.25.0 |
| tree-sitter-javascript | ^0.25.0 | ^0.23.0 | 0.25.x needs ^0.25.0 |
| tree-sitter-php | ^0.24.2 | ^0.23.0 | 0.24.x needs ^0.22.4 |
| tree-sitter-python | ^0.25.0 | 0.23.4 | 0.25.x needs ^0.25.0 |
| tree-sitter-rust | ^0.24.0 | 0.23.1 | 0.24.x needs ^0.22.1 |
| tree-sitter-swift | 0.7.1 | ^0.6.0 | 0.7.x needs ^0.22.1 |
| tree-sitter-dart | git#0fc19c3a (ABI 15) | git#80e23c07 (ABI 14) | Last commit with ^0.21.0 peer dep and aligned build toolchain |
| tree-sitter override | ^0.25.0 | removed | No longer needed |

**Unchanged** (already compatible with ^0.21.x): tree-sitter-typescript, tree-sitter-java, tree-sitter-cpp, tree-sitter-c-sharp, tree-sitter-ruby, tree-sitter-kotlin.

### Dart parser note

`tree-sitter-dart` is pinned to GitHub commit `80e23c07b644` (Feb 2025), the last commit where both the peer dep (`^0.21.0`) and build toolchain (`tree-sitter-cli@^0.22.6`) are aligned with tree-sitter@0.21.1. Later commits (through `c1222f5a65ab`, Oct 2025) are still ABI 14 binary-compatible, but their `tree-sitter-cli` was upgraded to `^0.25.10` — since this is a GitHub dep that builds from source, the aligned toolchain is safer.

Features deferred until parser ecosystem catches up to 0.25.x:
- Extension type declarations (#83)
- NativeFinalizer memory leak fix (#88)
- get/set contextual keyword fix (#89)
- Dart 3.10 dot shorthand (#93)

### Verification

- [x] `npm ls tree-sitter` — zero peer dep conflicts
- [x] All tests pass (4325 passed, pre-existing lbug-db env failures only)
- [x] tree-sitter override removed from package.json
- [x] Dart SHA verified against GitHub API (original Copilot SHA was invalid, corrected)

### Pin strategy

- **Exact pins** (`0.23.2`, `0.23.4`, `0.23.1`): tree-sitter-c, tree-sitter-python, tree-sitter-rust — their next patch versions require `^0.22.x`
- **Caret ranges** (`^0.23.x`): all other parsers — safe because subsequent patches stay on `^0.21.x`

title: feat(java): method references, worker overload disambiguation, interface dispatch
body:
### Summary
Tightens Java **CALLS** resolution for method references (`obj::method`), **overload** selection when args are typed variables (not only literals), and **interface dispatch** (extra edges to implementing classes at lower confidence).

### What changed
- **Method references:** Java tree-sitter query treats `method_reference` as a call site; `parseJavaMethodReference` + `extractParsedCallSite` wire into **parse-worker** and **call-processor** (same seed path for both).
- **Worker overloads:** `ExtractedCall.argTypes` is filled during parse (`extractCallArgTypes`); resolution uses `matchCandidatesByArgTypes`. Non-literal args use **TypeEnv** where literals still use `inferJvmLiteralType`.
- **Interface dispatch:** After resolving to the interface method, emit additional **CALLS** to matching methods on **implementing** files (lower confidence than the primary edge).

### Tests / fixtures
New fixtures under `test/fixtures/lang-resolution/` for method references, typed-arg overloads, and interface dispatch; coverage in `java.test.ts`, `call-form.test.ts`, and `call-processor.test.ts`.

**Scope:** `gitnexus/` only (no web UI or workflow changes in this PR).


Earlier for a Java repo -
```
MATCH (m:Method)
WHERE NOT EXISTS {
    MATCH ()-[r:CodeRelation {type: 'CALLS'}]->(m)
}
RETURN m.name, m.filePath, m.startLine
```
gave me 499 functions. Now I am at 384.  Functions with no callers dropped correctly.

Did the same analysis for leaf functions:

```
MATCH (m:Method)
WHERE NOT EXISTS {
    MATCH (m)-[r:CodeRelation {type: 'CALLS'}]->()
}
RETURN m.name, m.filePath, m.startLine
```
earlier gave 434 nodes and now the number is down to 408

body:
## Background (Jeff Dean Review Round 2, Gap 5: Confidence Calibration)

Currently, search results return a score but the agent has no way to distinguish between:
- A 99%-confidence exact symbol match (CamelCase lookup hit)
- A 60%-confidence BM25 fuzzy guess

This matters for agent efficiency: an exact match can be trusted immediately, but a fuzzy guess should be verified with `context()` before committing to a code path.

**Jeff Dean's observation**: "This is analogous to how Google's Knowledge Graph panels differ from blue links — the panel says 'I'm confident this is the answer' while links say 'these might help.'"

## Current State

`HybridSearchResult` in `hybrid-search.ts`:
```typescript
export interface HybridSearchResult {
  filePath: string;
  score: number;
  rank: number;
  sources: ('bm25' | 'semantic')[];
  nodeId?: string;
  name?: string;
  label?: string;
  semanticScore?: number;
}
```

No `confidence` or `matchType` field exists.

## Implementation Spec

### 1. Add `matchType` and `confidence` to `HybridSearchResult`

```typescript
export type MatchType =
  | 'exact_symbol'      // CamelCase/snake_case direct Cypher lookup
  | 'composition'       // Multi-token composition match (Phase 2.5)
  | 'file_name'         // Matched via file name search
  | 'bm25_keyword'      // BM25 full-text search hit
  | 'semantic_vector'   // Vector similarity match
  | 'process_step'      // Process-aware search injection
  | 'header_traversal'  // Found via header→impl traversal
  | 'expansion'         // NL stem expansion hit

export interface HybridSearchResult {
  // ...existing fields...
  matchType?: MatchType;
  confidence?: 'high' | 'medium' | 'low';
}
```

### 2. Tag results during pipeline phases

In `local-backend.ts`, when results are created in each phase, set `matchType`:
- Phase 2.5 (symbol lookup): `matchType: 'exact_symbol'` or `'composition'`, `confidence: 'high'`
- Phase 3 (file name): `matchType: 'file_name'`, `confidence: 'medium'`
- Phase 4 (header): `matchType: 'header_traversal'`, `confidence: 'medium'`
- Phase 4.5 (process): `matchType: 'process_step'`, `confidence: 'medium'`
- BM25: `matchType: 'bm25_keyword'`, `confidence: 'medium'` if score > 10, else `'low'`
- Vector: `matchType: 'semantic_vector'`, `confidence` based on `1-distance` threshold (>0.7 = high, >0.5 = medium, else low)

### 3. Surface in `query` MCP tool response

Add to the formatted output of the `query` tool:
```
[HIGH] exact_symbol — MinervaSnapshotManager → minerva_snapshot_manager.h
[MED]  bm25_keyword — SnapshotOps → snapshot_ops.cc
[LOW]  semantic_vector — BackupManager → backup_manager.py
```

This lets the agent decide:
- **HIGH**: Trust immediately, proceed to `context()` on this symbol
- **MED**: Plausible, verify with `context()` before committing
- **LOW**: Exploratory signal, try a different query if no HIGH results

## Files to Modify
- `gitnexus/src/core/search/hybrid-search.ts` — Add types, set `matchType` in `mergeWithRRF()`
- `gitnexus/src/mcp/local/local-backend.ts` — Set `matchType` and `confidence` in each pipeline phase
- `gitnexus/src/core/graph/types.ts` — Add `MatchType` type if shared

## Validation
- TSC clean (0 errors)
- All existing unit tests pass
- `query` tool output shows `[HIGH/MED/LOW]` confidence tags
- No regression on rca-eval-v2.py scores

## Context

title: [P2] Add Repository Overview MCP Tool (repo_overview)
[P1] Add Per-Phase Timing Instrumentation to Search Pipeline
[P2] Add Temporal Robustness Testing Infrastructure
body:
## Background (Jeff Dean Review Round 2, Gap: Temporal Robustness — F grade)

All eval runs test against a frozen graph snapshot. We never test:
1. Does search quality degrade after incremental reindex (add/remove files)?
2. Do stale embeddings cause false positives?
3. Does the system handle graph schema changes gracefully?

**Jeff Dean**: "Still testing against a frozen snapshot. No test of incremental reindex or stale graph behavior."

## Current State

- Eval runs against a single Neo4j instance with a fixed graph
- No test infrastructure for simulating graph changes
- No regression test for "add 100 files, re-search, same quality?"

## Implementation Spec

### 1. Add `--temporal-test` flag to eval harness

```python
parser.add_argument("--temporal-test", action="store_true",
    help="Run temporal robustness test: mutate graph, re-eval, compare")
```

### 2. Temporal test protocol

```python
def run_temporal_test():
    """
    Protocol:
    1. Run baseline eval (S1-S5) → record pass/fail for each scenario
    2. Inject 100 synthetic nodes (fake files with realistic names and connections)
    3. Re-run eval → compare pass/fail
    4. Remove the 100 synthetic nodes
    5. Re-run eval → should match baseline exactly
    
    Metrics:
    - Degradation rate: % of scenarios that flip PASS→FAIL after injection
    - Recovery rate: % of scenarios that return to baseline after cleanup
    - Noise tolerance: do injected nodes appear as false positives?
    """
```

### 3. Synthetic node injection

```python
def inject_temporal_nodes(n=100):
    """Create n fake nodes with realistic structure."""
    for i in range(n):
        name = f"TemporalTest_{i:03d}"
        path = f"test/temporal/temporal_test_{i:03d}.py"
        cypher("""
            CREATE (n:Class {
                name: $name, filePath: $path,
                content: 'class ' + $name + ': pass',
                description: 'Temporal test node'
            })
        """, {"name": name, "path": path})
    
    # Add some fake edges to existing nodes
    cypher("""
        MATCH (t:Class) WHERE t.name STARTS WITH 'TemporalTest_'
        WITH t LIMIT 20
        MATCH (real:Class) WHERE real.name = 'MinervaServer'
        CREATE (t)-[:CodeRelation {type: 'IMPORTS'}]->(real)
    """)

def cleanup_temporal_nodes():
    """Remove all temporal test nodes and their edges."""
    cypher("""
        MATCH (n) WHERE n.name STARTS WITH 'TemporalTest_'
        DETACH DELETE n
    """)
```

### 4. Report format

```
TEMPORAL ROBUSTNESS TEST
========================
Baseline: 48/50 (96%)
After injection (+100 nodes): 47/50 (94%)  — Degradation: 2%
After cleanup: 48/50 (96%)  — Recovery: 100%

Noise: 0/100 injected nodes appeared in top-10 results for any scenario
```

## Files to Modify
- `.overhaul/qa/rca-eval-v2.py` — Add `--temporal-test` flag and protocol

## Validation
- Temporal test runs end-to-end without Neo4j errors
- Cleanup removes all injected nodes (verify with `MATCH (n) WHERE n.name STARTS WITH 'TemporalTest_' RETURN count(n)`)
- Degradation rate < 5% (target)
- Recovery rate = 100%

## Context
- Jeff Dean Review Round 2: `.overhaul/qa/JEFF_DEAN_REVIEW_ROUND_2.md` (Temporal dimension: F grade)
- Research log: `.overhaul/qa/RESEARCH_LOG.md`

title: Diversity-Aware Re-ranking (MMR) for Ambiguous Queries
body:
## Problem
S7.09-S7.11 eval scenarios show that generic/ambiguous queries (e.g., "config handler", "Init", "error") cluster results in a single subsystem instead of spreading across the codebase. This gives a misleading view of where relevant code lives.

## Root Cause
Current post-ranking only boosts/penalizes based on subsystem match and community membership. There's no mechanism to penalize redundancy (multiple results from the same directory/subsystem).

## Solution: Maximal Marginal Relevance (MMR)
Implemented in `hybrid-search.ts::applyMMRDiversity()`:

1. **Detection**: `isAmbiguousQuery()` returns true for short queries (≤3 words) with no CamelCase/snake_case symbols
2. **MMR Selection**: Greedy selection that maximizes `λ * relevance - (1-λ) * similarity_to_selected`
3. **Similarity metric**: Subsystem overlap ratio (how many already-selected results share the same top-level directory)
4. **Lambda = 0.7**: Relevance-heavy but with meaningful diversity pressure

## Implementation
- `applyMMRDiversity()` in `hybrid-search.ts` — core MMR algorithm
- `isAmbiguousQuery()` in `hybrid-search.ts` — trigger condition
- Applied in `local-backend.ts::query()` after final sort, before confidence computation
- Only activates for ambiguous queries with >5 results

## Expected Impact
- S7.09-S7.11 pass rate should improve from 0/3 to 2-3/3
- No regression on precise queries (MMR is not triggered)

## Validation
```bash
python3 .overhaul/qa/rca-eval-v2.py --selection --hallucination
```

## Status
Already implemented in product code (this round). This issue documents the change.

title: feat: guard clause and guarded call detection
body:
## Summary

- Adds guard clause detection to the ingestion pipeline — enriches Function/Method nodes with `guardClauses` metadata and CALLS edges with `guard` conditions
- New `guard-extractor.ts` module using tree-sitter AST, supporting return-based and throw/raise-based guards
- Confidence-scored guards (1.0/0.7/0.3) with automatic filtering of low-confidence results

## What it detects

| Pattern | Languages | Example | Confidence |
|---------|-----------|---------|------------|
| Return with HTTP status | TS/JS, Python, PHP | `if (!session) return json({...}, { status: 401 })` | 1.0 |
| Throw/raise with exception | TS/JS, Python, Java, C#, Kotlin, PHP | `if (!user) throw new UnauthorizedException()` | 1.0 |
| Negation guard | All | `if (!org) return null` | 0.7 |
| Other early return | All | `if (cached) return cached` | 0.3 (filtered) |
| Guarded calls | All | `if (result.requiresApproval) initializeWorkflow(id)` | N/A |

## Confidence scoring

Guards are scored by evidence strength:
- **1.0** — Has HTTP status code or exception type. Definitely a guard.
- **0.7** — Negation pattern (`!session`, `!org`, `not authenticated`). Likely a guard.
- **0.3** — Other early returns. Filtered out of graph (threshold >= 0.5).

## Schema changes

- `guardClauses STRING` column added to Function and Method node tables
- `guard STRING` column added to CodeRelation table
- No new node types, no new edge types

## Real-world validation (Next.js + Prisma, 30K nodes, 431 route handlers)

| Metric | Count |
|--------|-------|
| Guards with HTTP status (confidence 1.0) | 572 |
| Throw guards (confidence 1.0) | 14 |
| Negation guards (confidence 0.7) | 39 |
| Filtered out (confidence 0.3) | 66 |
| **Stored in graph** | **611** |
| **False positive rate** | **6%** |
| Guarded call edges | 1,357 |

## Known limitations

1. **Heuristic, not CFG-based.** Scans top of function bodies for if-statements with return/throw. Guards after complex logic are missed.
2. **Indirect guards not detected.** Functions that guard via a called function (which throws internally) are invisible — requires inter-procedural analysis.
3. **Callback arrows skipped.** Arrow functions passed as arguments to `.sort()`, `.reduce()`, `.then()` are excluded to prevent false positives.
4. **Status extraction is regex-based.** Looks for `status: NNN` or `status(NNN)`. Custom error classes won't be captured.
5. **Try-block unwrapping is single-level.** Looks inside `try { ... }` for guards (common Next.js pattern). Nested try blocks aren't handled.
6. **Confidence 0.7 may include false positives.** `if (!cachedValue) return fetchFresh()` is caching logic scored 0.7, not an access guard.
7. **Language support varies.** Full TS/JS support. Python/Java/C#/PHP throw detection relies on tree-sitter grammar node types.

## Test plan

- [x] 7 unit tests (return guards, throw guards, mixed, callback filtering)
- [x] Integration test with Next.js-style route handler fixture
- [x] Schema validation tests
- [x] Real-repo validation: 611 guards stored, 6% FP rate

title: feat: workflow/state machine detection — StatusType nodes, TRANSITIONS edges
body:
## Summary

- Detects status/state type definitions and status transition patterns across multiple languages
- New `StatusType` node type with `TRANSITIONS` edges mapping which functions change which statuses
- Supports TypeScript unions/enums, Python Enums, Java enums, plus generic assignment and setter patterns

## What it detects

### Status type definitions

| Pattern | Languages | Example |
|---------|-----------|---------|
| Union types (single + multi-line) | TypeScript | `type GrantStatus = 'DRAFT' \| 'ACTIVE' \| 'COMPLETED'` |
| TS/JS enums | TypeScript/JS | `enum OrderStatus { PENDING = 'pending' }` |
| Python Enum classes | Python | `class OrderStatus(Enum): PENDING = 'pending'` |
| Java enums | Java | `enum Status { PENDING, ACTIVE, COMPLETED }` |

### Status transitions

| Pattern | Scope | Example |
|---------|-------|---------|
| Prisma ORM updates | Prisma | `prisma.grant.update({ data: { status: 'ACTIVE' } })` |
| Transactional updates | Prisma | `tx.step.update({ data: { status: 'approved' } })` |
| Direct assignment | Any language | `order.status = 'shipped'` / `self.status = 'active'` |
| Setter patterns | Any language | `entity.setStatus('approved')` / `obj.set_status('active')` |
| Generic .update() | Any ORM | `entity.update({ status: 'completed' })` |

### Entity-name matching

Transitions matched to StatusType by **entity name first** (e.g., `prisma.grant.update` -> `GrantStatus`), falling back to value-based matching only when entity name doesn't match.

## Schema changes

- New `StatusType` node table: `id, name, filePath, statusValues STRING[], statusKind`
- `TRANSITIONS` added to REL_TYPES
- FROM/TO pairs: File/Function/Method -> StatusType, StatusType -> Community/Process
- COPY query + insert + batch-upsert in lbug-adapter

## Real-world validation (Next.js + Prisma, 30K nodes)

| Metric | Count |
|--------|-------|
| StatusType nodes | 63 |
| Core domain types found (of 7 expected) | **7/7** |
| TRANSITIONS edges | 76 (71 direct + 5 transactional) |

## Known limitations

1. **Status type detection is heuristic.** Name pattern `/status|state|phase|stage|step|workflow|lifecycle/i` OR 2+ status-like values. Produces false positives for UI step types (~35% noise).
2. **Transition detection is regex-based.** Complex patterns (dynamic field names, computed values, spread operators) are missed.
3. **Entity-to-type matching relies on naming convention.** Non-standard naming falls back to value-based matching, which can misattribute.
4. **Generic assignment may over-match.** Any `.status = 'value'` is detected — including UI state and test mocks.
5. **Python/Java support is basic.** Type detection works, but transition detection only covers generic patterns (assignment, setter). No Django ORM, JPA, or ActiveRecord patterns yet.
6. **Pipeline only scans TS/TSX for transitions.** Python/Java transition detection is available but not wired into the pipeline yet.
7. **Transition metadata encoded in reason string.** `fromStatus`, `toStatus`, `entityType` stored as `direct-update:grant:DRAFT->ACTIVE`, not separate LadybugDB columns.
8. **No transition validation.** Doesn't check if the target value is valid for the StatusType.

## Test plan

- [x] 14 unit tests (union types, enums, Python Enum, Java enum, Prisma, generic assignment, setter)
- [x] Schema count assertions updated
- [x] Full test suite passes
- [x] Real-repo validation: all 7 core types, 76 transitions

title: feat: source-sink security scanning + Parameter data flow
body:
## Summary

Two capabilities aligned with the architecture assessment's security analysis roadmap:

1. **Source-Sink Structural Scanning (Phase A)** — New `source_sink` MCP tool. BFS over existing CALLS graph from source-adjacent to sink-adjacent functions. No new node types needed.
2. **Parameter-Level Data Flow (Phase B)** — New `Parameter` node type with `PASSES_TO` edges mapping call-site arguments to callee parameters.

## Source-Sink Scanning

### Coverage (13 frameworks)

| Framework | Source patterns | Sink patterns |
|-----------|---------------|--------------|
| Express/Next.js | req.body, request.json, req.query, req.params | eval, exec, innerHTML |
| Django/Flask | request.GET/POST, request.data/form/args | subprocess.run, os.system |
| PHP | \$_GET, \$_POST, \$_REQUEST | shell_exec |
| Go | r.Body, r.FormValue, r.URL.Query() | os.exec, sql.Query, template.HTML |
| Rust/Actix | web::Json, web::Query, web::Path | Command::new, sqlx::query |
| Spring | @RequestBody, @RequestParam, @PathVariable | jdbcTemplate.query, Runtime.exec |
| Rails | params[], request.body | system(), AR::Base.connection.execute |
| Ktor | call.receive, call.parameters | — |

### User-extensible via `.gitnexus/security.json`

```json
{
  "sources": [{ "pattern": "myInput", "category": "user_input", "description": "Custom source" }],
  "sinks": [{ "pattern": "dangerousOp", "owasp": "A03-injection", "severity": "high", "description": "Custom sink" }]
}
```

## Parameter Data Flow

- **Parameter node type** — each function parameter as a graph node (name, index, type, isRest)
- **PASSES_TO edges** — maps call-site arg positions to callee parameter positions
- Tree-sitter extraction for **all 13 supported languages**
- Handles: simple, typed, destructured, rest, default parameters

## Schema changes

- New `Parameter` node table: `id, name, filePath, paramIndex INT32, declaredType, isRest BOOL`
- `PASSES_TO` and `DATA_FLOWS_TO` added to REL_TYPES
- FROM/TO pairs for Function/Method/Constructor -> Parameter, Parameter -> Parameter/Community/Process
- New `source_sink` MCP tool (tools.ts, local-backend.ts, server.ts)

## Real-world validation (Next.js + Prisma, 30K nodes)

| Metric | Count |
|--------|-------|
| Source-adjacent route files | 341 / 431 (79%) |
| Sink-adjacent route files | 392 / 431 (91%) |
| Parameter nodes | 8,604 |
| PASSES_TO edges | 416 |

## Known limitations

### Source-Sink
1. **Structural reachability, not taint tracking.** BFS finds paths but doesn't verify data actually flows through them. Sanitizers not detected.
2. **High sink rate by design.** In ORM-heavy apps, most routes are sink-adjacent. Results need manual review.
3. **Catalog coverage uneven.** Strong for Express/Next.js/Django/Go/Rust. Weaker for Spring/Rails/FastAPI.
4. **No sanitizer awareness.** Future work: sanitizer catalogs.

### Parameter Data Flow
5. **Types are text strings, not resolved.** `param: User` stores "User" as text, not linked to the User class node.
6. **Positional matching only.** Named/keyword arguments (Python `foo(key=value)`) matched by position.
7. **No inter-procedural chaining.** PASSES_TO shows one hop, not multi-hop chains. Full taint tracking requires function summaries.
8. **Destructured params stored as text.** `({ a, b }: Props)` creates one node, not individual nodes.
9. **DATA_FLOWS_TO reserved but not emitted.** Schema placeholder for future intra-function assignment tracking.

## Test plan

- [x] 32 source-sink tests (catalog matching, BFS, integration)
- [x] 23 parameter tests (schema, extraction, processor, integration)
- [x] Schema count assertions updated
- [x] Full build passes (tsc clean)
- [x] Real-repo validation: 341 sources, 392 sinks, 8604 parameters, 416 PASSES_TO

body:
## Summary

- Configure Prettier as the code formatter for the monorepo with lint-staged + Husky pre-commit hook integration
- Format entire codebase (344 files, style-only — no logic changes)
- Pre-commit hook: lint-staged (prettier) → tsc (typecheck). Tests stay in CI only.

## What's included

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `package.json` (root) | New — prettier, lint-staged, husky, prettier-plugin-tailwindcss |
| `.prettierrc` | New — `singleQuote`, `trailingComma: "all"`, `printWidth: 100`, `endOfLine: "lf"`, TW v4 `tailwindStylesheet` |
| `.prettierignore` | New — excludes fixtures, vendor, `*.d.ts`, `*.snap`, `*.md` |
| `.gitattributes` | New — `* text=auto eol=lf` for Windows line-ending consistency |
| `.husky/pre-commit` | Updated — lint-staged + tsc only (vitest removed, stays in CI) |
| `gitnexus/package.json` | Removed `husky` devDep (moved to root) |
| `.git-blame-ignore-revs` | New — hides bulk format commit from `git blame` |

## Key decisions

- **lint-staged v15** (not v16) — v16 has Windows regressions with tinyexec
- **`endOfLine: "lf"`** + `.gitattributes` — prevents line-ending churn on Windows
- **`tailwindStylesheet`** (not `tailwindConfig`) — required for Tailwind CSS v4's CSS-based config
- **No vitest in pre-commit** — tests belong in CI, pre-commit should be fast (lint-staged + tsc)
- **`*.md` excluded** — markdown files have intentional formatting
- **`node_modules/.bin/`** paths instead of `npx` — saves 2-7s on Windows per commit

## Post-merge setup

Contributors run `npm install` at repo root to get prettier + activate Husky hooks. After merge, run:
```bash
git config blame.ignoreRevsFile .git-blame-ignore-revs
```

title: RFC: Program Dependence Graph (PDG) Subsystem Design
body:
## RFC: Program Dependence Graph (PDG) Subsystem for GitNexus

### Context

After shipping PRs for workflow/state detection (#560), source-sink scanning (#578), and guard clause detection (#559), we identified that #559 takes a heuristic approach to control dependence that would be better served by a formal PDG subsystem. This RFC proposes the design.

This builds on:
- The architecture assessment's identification of CFG as "the hard boundary"
- Ferrante et al. 1987 PDG paper (shared for reference)
- Analysis of 9 open-source implementations (Joern, CodeQL, Semgrep, tree-climber, IBM codeviews, Fraunhofer CPG, etc.)
- Review by @magyargergo (all 6 requested changes incorporated)

---

### 1. Problem Statement

GitNexus currently has:
- **Call graph** (CALLS edges with type-resolved receivers) — inter-procedural, cross-file
- **Execution flows** (Process nodes via BFS over CALLS) — traces entry → terminal
- **No intra-function analysis** — cannot answer "under what condition does line X execute?" or "where does variable Y flow within this function?"

PR #559 attempted guard clause detection as a heuristic workaround for control dependence. The PDG provides the formal foundation.

---

### 2. Proposed Design: Two-Phase PDG Construction

> **Opt-in only.** PDG construction is off by default. Enable via `--pdg` CLI flag or `.gitnexus/config.json`:
> ```json
> { "pdg": { "enabled": true, "edgeBudget": 500000, "maxFunctionLines": 500 } }
> ```

#### Phase 4.6: CFG (Control Flow Graph)

> **Why Phase 4.6?** CFG needs completed CALLS edges + MRO resolution (Phase 4.5). Slots after MRO, before Communities (Phase 5). Phase numbering follows @magyargergo's review.

**What:** Per-function graph connecting basic blocks via control flow edges.

**New node type:** `BasicBlock` — lightweight intra-function node:
```
BasicBlock (id STRING, filePath STRING, startLine INT64, endLine INT64, text STRING, PRIMARY KEY (id))
```

**How:** Walk tree-sitter AST control structures using a visitor pattern (per-language visitors via LanguageProvider dispatch table). Handle: `if_statement`, `while_statement`, `for_statement`, `switch_statement`, `try_statement`, `return_statement`, `break_statement`, `continue_statement`, `throw_statement`.

**New edge type:** `CFG` — "control flow from basic block A to basic block B"

**Node granularity:** Start with **basic-block** (coarser, fewer edges, better for large functions). Statement-level as future opt-in.

**Reference:** tree-climber (MIT) uses Joern's CfgCreator algorithm adapted for tree-sitter.

**Scope:** Start with TypeScript/JavaScript, expand via LanguageProvider.

#### Phase 4.7: CDG + REACHING_DEF

**CDG (Control Dependence Graph):**
1. Compute post-dominator tree from CFG (Lengauer-Tarjan algorithm, O(N α(N)))
2. For each CFG edge (A,B) where B does not post-dominate A, walk up post-dominator tree marking control dependence (Ferrante et al. Section 3.1.1)

**New edge types:**
- `CDG` — "destination is control-dependent on source" (with `label: 'T' | 'F'` property)
- `POST_DOMINATE` — optional, for debugging/querying dominator relationships

**This replaces:** PR #559's guard clause heuristics. Guard clauses become a query pattern over CDG edges:
```cypher
MATCH (pred)-[:CDG {label:'F'}]->(ret)
WHERE ret.type = 'ReturnStatement' AND ret.statusCode IS NOT NULL
RETURN pred.condition, ret.statusCode
```

**REACHING_DEF (Data Dependence):**
Iterative fixpoint dataflow analysis on CFG. For each basic block, compute GEN (definitions created) and KILL (definitions overwritten), then propagate until stable.

**New edge type:** `REACHING_DEF` — with `variable: STRING` property indicating which variable is propagated.

#### Future: Interprocedural Summaries

Per-function summaries: "parameter 0 flows to return value" / "parameter 1 flows to argument 0 of callee X." Context-insensitive initially.

---

### 3. Edge Budget & Circuit Breaker

**The main risk is graph size.** Rough estimate for a 30K-node TypeScript repo: ~5K functions × 15 basic blocks avg = **75K CFG nodes + ~150K CFG edges + ~50K CDG edges + ~100K REACHING_DEF edges ≈ 300K new edges** (4-5× current).

**Mitigations:**
- **Opt-in only** — PDG never runs unless explicitly requested
- **Per-repo edge budget** — default 500K PDG edges, configurable. Early termination + warning when budget exceeded
- **Skip large functions** — functions > 500 lines are excluded (configurable `maxFunctionLines`)
- **Per-function construction** — parallelizable in worker pool
- **Basic-block granularity** — fewer nodes/edges than statement-level

---

### 4. Schema Changes

New edge types added to `REL_TYPES`:

| Edge | Description | Properties |
|------|-------------|-----------|
| `CFG` | Control flow between basic blocks | (none) |
| `CDG` | Control dependence | `label: 'T' \| 'F'` |
| `REACHING_DEF` | Data dependence (variable flow) | `variable: STRING` |
| `POST_DOMINATE` | Post-dominator relation (optional) | (none) |

New node type:

| Node | Description | Properties |
|------|-------------|-----------|
| `BasicBlock` | Intra-function basic block | `id, filePath, startLine, endLine, text` |

---

### 5. Pipeline Integration

```
Current:                              With PDG (opt-in):
Phase 1+2: Scan + Structure           (unchanged)
Phase 3+4: Parse + Resolve            (unchanged)
Phase 3.5: Routes                     (unchanged)
Phase 3.6: Tools                      (unchanged)
Phase 3.7: ORM Dataflow               (unchanged)
Phase 3.8: Workflow Detection          (unchanged)
Phase 14: Cross-file propagation       (unchanged)
Phase 4.5: MRO                        (unchanged)
                                       Phase 4.6: CFG Construction (NEW, opt-in)
                                       Phase 4.7: CDG + REACHING_DEF (NEW, opt-in)
Phase 5: Communities                   (unchanged)
Phase 6: Processes                     (unchanged)
```

---

### 6. LadybugDB Indexing Investigation

REACHING_DEF queries (Section 7) filter by `variable` property on edges. This requires efficient property filtering in LadybugDB.

**Investigation needed before committing:**
- Can LadybugDB create property indexes on relationship tables?
- If not, benchmark variable-length path queries with property filters on synthetic 100K-edge datasets
- Fallback: encode variable name in edge ID or separate lookup table

---

### 7. Concrete Query Examples

**Security: "Find routes where auth check doesn't control-dominate data access"**
```cypher
MATCH (route:Route)-[:HANDLES_ROUTE]->(handler:Function)
MATCH (handler)-[:CFG*]->(dataAccess)
WHERE dataAccess.text CONTAINS 'prisma.'
AND NOT EXISTS {
  MATCH (authCheck)-[:CDG]->(dataAccess)
  WHERE authCheck.text CONTAINS 'requireAuth'
}
RETURN route.name, handler.name, dataAccess.text
```

**Data flow: "Trace user input to database write"**
```cypher
MATCH path = (source)-[:REACHING_DEF*1..5]->(sink)
WHERE source.text CONTAINS 'request.json'
AND sink.text CONTAINS 'prisma.create'
RETURN [n IN nodes(path) | n.name] AS flow,
       [r IN relationships(path) | r.variable] AS variables
```

---

### 8. Incremental Re-indexing

When a file changes:
1. Delete all `BasicBlock` nodes for functions in the changed file (keyed by `filePath`)
2. Delete all `CFG`, `CDG`, `REACHING_DEF` edges involving those blocks
3. Re-run Phase 4.6 + 4.7 for affected functions only

This is efficient because PDG is per-function — file-level invalidation is sufficient.

---

### 9. MCP Tool Integration

- **`impact` tool:** Extend with optional PDG traversal — show control/data dependencies alongside CALLS graph
- **`context` tool:** Include CDG edges in the 360-degree view when PDG is indexed
- **New `pdg_query` tool (future):** Specialized queries like "what controls this statement?" and "where does this variable flow?"

---

### 10. Test Strategy

- **Snapshot tests:** 10-function TypeScript fixture with if/for/while/try — verify CFG/CDG/REACHING_DEF edges match expected snapshots
- **Property tests:** Verify basic invariants (every BasicBlock reachable from function entry, CDG edges only exist where post-dominance fails)
- **Benchmark tests:** Track edge counts and construction time on real repos to detect regressions

---

### 11. What Happens to Existing PRs

| PR | Status | After PDG |
|----|--------|-----------|
| #559 (Guard Clauses) | Open — decision pending | **Subsumed by CDG.** Ship as stopgap if immediate demand, otherwise hold. |
| #560 (Workflow/State) | Ready to merge | **Independent of PDG.** Domain-level detection. |
| #578 (Source-Sink) | Ready to merge | **Independent of PDG.** Works on existing CALLS graph. |

---

### 12. Reference Implementations (All MIT/Apache-2.0)

| Project | License | What to use |
|---------|---------|-------------|
| [tree-climber](https://github.com/bstee615/tree-climber) | MIT | CFG builder algorithm (visitor for tree-sitter, based on Joern) |
| [Joern CPG spec](https://cpg.joern.io/) | Apache-2.0 | Edge type definitions (CFG, CDG, REACHING_DEF) |
| [Fraunhofer CPG](https://github.com/Fraunhofer-AISEC/cpg) | Apache-2.0 | Multi-language frontend pattern (TranslationConfiguration) |
| [IBM tree-sitter-codeviews](https://github.com/IBM/tree-sitter-codeviews) | Apache-2.0 | Multi-view architecture pattern |

---

### 13. Suggested Timeline

| Phase | Scope | Estimate |
|-------|-------|----------|
| Phase 4.6 (CFG) | TypeScript/JavaScript | 2-3 weeks |
| Phase 4.6+ | Expand to Python, Java, Go | +1 week per language |
| Phase 4.7 (CDG + REACHING_DEF) | All CFG-supported languages | 3-4 weeks |
| Interprocedural summaries | Function boundary analysis | 4-6 weeks |

---

/cc @abhigyanpatwari @magyargergo

title: RFC: MethodExtractor abstraction — per-language method metadata extraction
body:
## Enhancement Summary

**Deepened on:** 2026-03-28
**Research agents used:** Architect (ECC), Explorer, TypeScript Pro (Voltagent), Architecture Strategist, Pattern Recognition, Simplicity Reviewer
**Sources:** claude-mem #21460 (design decision), #20233 (pipeline DAG), #19975 (FieldInfo contracts), #18453 (LanguageProvider)

### Key Simplifications (from validation)
1. **5 PRs → 2 PRs** — defer METHOD_IMPLEMENTS, methodReturnTypeMap, and 9 language configs
2. **Drop BaseMethodExtractor class** — config + factory is sufficient (11/12 field extractors use this)
3. **Drop AbstractnessKind enum** — collapsed to `isAbstract: boolean` before storage
4. **Drop methodReturnTypeMap** — SymbolTable.returnType + ownerId already handles chain resolution; add `lookupMethodByOwner` if needed
5. **Reuse FieldVisibility** — type alias, not a new type

### Edge Cases Identified
- Diamond inheritance: MRO already handles; METHOD_IMPLEMENTS emitted per-class not transitively
- Default interface methods (Java 8+): METHOD_IMPLEMENTS should emit for ALL interface methods, not just abstract
- Go structural typing: out of scope (no explicit IMPLEMENTS edges)
- Extension methods (C#/Kotlin): excluded by label (Function, not Method)
- Overloaded interface methods: must match by name + parameterTypes, not name alone



# MethodExtractor Abstraction — Per-Language Method Metadata Extraction

Formalize method metadata extraction as a first-class abstraction mirroring the existing FieldExtractor pattern. Enables structured overload resolution and interface dispatch with `isAbstract`/`isFinal` flags.

## Problem Statement

PR #540 (Java method refs + overloads + interface dispatch) exposed that method metadata extraction is ad-hoc:
- `extractMethodSignature()` gives only `parameterCount`, `parameterTypes[]`, `returnType`
- No `isAbstract` flag → can't distinguish interface methods from implementations for dispatch
- No structured `ParameterInfo` → overload disambiguation lacks `isOptional`/`isVariadic`
- Interface dispatch uses runtime `ImplementorMap` but no persisted graph edges

## Proposed Solution (Simplified)

### Architecture

```
┌────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  method-types.ts                               │
│  MethodInfo, ParameterInfo, ExtractedMethods,  │
│  MethodExtractionConfig, MethodExtractor iface │
└────────────────────┬───────────────────────────┘
                     │
┌────────────────────▼───────────────────────────┐
│  method-extractors/generic.ts                  │
│  createMethodExtractor() factory               │
│  (no class hierarchy — config + factory only)  │
└────────────────────┬───────────────────────────┘
                     │
              ┌──────┴──────┐
              ▼              ▼
    configs/jvm.ts    (others on demand)
```

### Key Types

```typescript
// method-types.ts

import type { FieldVisibility } from './field-types.js';

// Reuse FieldVisibility — same set of language visibility levels
export type MethodVisibility = FieldVisibility;

export interface ParameterInfo {
  name: string;
  type: string | null;
  isOptional: boolean;
  isVariadic: boolean;
}

export interface MethodInfo {
  name: string;
  returnType: string | null;
  parameters: ParameterInfo[];
  visibility: MethodVisibility;
  isStatic: boolean;
  isAbstract: boolean;     // critical for dispatch
  isFinal: boolean;        // cannot be overridden
  annotations: string[];
  sourceFile: string;
  line: number;
}

export type MethodTypeMap = Map<string, MethodInfo[]>;

export interface MethodExtractorContext {
  filePath: string;
  language: SupportedLanguages;
}

export interface ExtractedMethods {
  ownerFqn: string;
  methods: MethodInfo[];
  nestedTypes: string[];   // mirror ExtractedFields
}

export interface MethodExtractor {
  language: SupportedLanguages;
  extract(node: SyntaxNode, context: MethodExtractorContext): ExtractedMethods | null;
  isTypeDeclaration(node: SyntaxNode): boolean;
}

export interface MethodExtractionConfig {
  language: SupportedLanguages;
  typeDeclarationNodes: string[];
  methodNodeTypes: string[];
  bodyNodeTypes: string[];
  defaultVisibility: MethodVisibility;
  extractName: (node: SyntaxNode) => string | undefined;
  extractReturnType: (node: SyntaxNode) => string | undefined;
  extractParameters: (node: SyntaxNode) => ParameterInfo[];
  extractVisibility: (node: SyntaxNode) => MethodVisibility;
  isStatic: (node: SyntaxNode) => boolean;
  isAbstract: (node: SyntaxNode) => boolean;
  isFinal: (node: SyntaxNode) => boolean;
  extractAnnotations?: (node: SyntaxNode) => string[];
}
```

### Pipeline Integration (no new phase)

Method extraction runs **inline in Phase 3+4** (parse worker), same as fields:

```
Phase 3+4: Parse + Resolve (workers)
  └─ nodeLabel === 'Method' → extractMethodSignature() (existing, unchanged)
  └─ if provider.methodExtractor → MethodExtractor.extract() (NEW)
       └─ enriches node properties: isAbstract, isFinal, annotations

Phase 4.5: MRO (existing, unchanged for now)
  └─ METHOD_IMPLEMENTS edges deferred to follow-up PR
```

### New Files (4 total)

| File | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `method-types.ts` | All interfaces + MethodExtractor + MethodExtractionConfig |
| `method-extractors/generic.ts` | `createMethodExtractor()` factory (no class hierarchy) |
| `method-extractors/configs/helpers.ts` | Re-export from `field-extractors/configs/helpers.ts` |
| `method-extractors/configs/jvm.ts` | Java + Kotlin configs |

### Modified Files (4 total)

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `gitnexus-shared/src/graph/types.ts` | Add `isAbstract?`, `isFinal?` to NodeProperties |
| `language-provider.ts` | Add `methodExtractor?: MethodExtractor` |
| `workers/parse-worker.ts` | Call MethodExtractor, cache + serialize results |
| `languages/index.ts` | Wire Java/Kotlin with methodExtractor |

## Incremental Rollout (2 PRs)

### PR 1: Types + Factory + JVM Config + Worker Integration

Everything needed to get Java/Kotlin method extraction working end-to-end.

- [x] Create `method-types.ts` with all interfaces (MethodInfo, ParameterInfo, MethodExtractionConfig, MethodExtractor, ExtractedMethods)
- [x] Create `method-extractors/generic.ts` with `createMethodExtractor()` factory
- [x] Create `method-extractors/configs/helpers.ts` (re-export from field helpers)
- [x] Create `method-extractors/configs/jvm.ts` (Java + Kotlin)
- [x] Add `isAbstract?`, `isFinal?` to NodeProperties in gitnexus-shared
- [x] Add `methodExtractor?: MethodExtractor` to LanguageProviderConfig
- [x] Wire into `parse-worker.ts` with `methodInfoCache` (mirror `fieldInfoCache` pattern)
- [x] Add `methodInfoCache.clear()` to `clearCaches()`
- [x] Wire Java/Kotlin language providers
- [x] Tests: verify MethodInfo extracted for Java classes, interfaces, abstract classes, enums

### PR 2: Additional Language Configs (on demand)

Add configs as concrete needs arise. Priority order based on `isAbstract` semantics:

- [x] TypeScript/JavaScript (abstract keyword + interface body)
- [x] Python (@abstractmethod decorator detection)
- [x] C/C++ (pure virtual = 0 detection)
- [x] C# (abstract modifier + interface body)
- [x] Others (Swift, Go, Rust, PHP, Ruby, Dart) as needed

## Deferred Work (follow-up PRs, not part of this plan)

### METHOD_IMPLEMENTS Edge (when a query consumer needs it)
- Add `METHOD_IMPLEMENTS` to RelationshipType + schema
- Emit in `mro-processor.ts`
- Must match by name + parameterTypes (not name alone) for overloaded interface methods
- Emit for ALL interface/trait methods, not just abstract (default methods establish contracts too)

### lookupMethodByOwner on SymbolTable (if chain resolution needs it)
- Add `lookupMethodByOwner(ownerNodeId, methodName)` to SymbolTable
- Follows existing `lookupFieldByOwner` pattern
- Avoids introducing a separate methodReturnTypeMap

## Abstractness Detection Per Language

| Language | Pattern | Detection in config |
|----------|---------|-------------------|
| Java/Kotlin | `abstract` modifier | `hasModifier(node, 'modifiers', 'abstract')` |
| Java/C#/Kotlin | Interface body | Check `ownerNode.type === 'interface_declaration'` |
| TypeScript | `abstract` keyword | `hasKeyword(node, 'abstract')` |
| Python | `@abstractmethod` | Walk sibling decorators |
| C++ | `= 0` pure virtual | Find `pure_specifier` child |
| Swift | Protocol body | `ownerNode.type === 'protocol_declaration'` |

## Design Decisions

1. **Config + factory only (no class hierarchy)** — 11 of 12 field extractors use the factory. BaseMethodExtractor would add a file and indirection for zero value. `normalizeType`/`resolveType` extracted as standalone functions if needed.

2. **`isAbstract: boolean` (not AbstractnessKind enum)** — the enum is never stored or queried. Language-specific detection logic lives in config functions, not type tags.

3. **Reuse FieldVisibility** — `MethodVisibility = FieldVisibility`. Same visibility levels across methods and fields. `findVisibility` helper reused directly.

4. **Defer METHOD_IMPLEMENTS** — ImplementorMap already handles interface dispatch at runtime. Graph edge added only when a query consumer needs it.

5. **No methodReturnTypeMap** — SymbolTable.returnType + ownerId already resolves chains. If a cross-file gap exists, add `lookupMethodByOwner` to SymbolTable (follows `lookupFieldByOwner` pattern).

6. **Start with Java/Kotlin only** — PR #540 drove this need. Other languages added on demand. No speculative configs.

7. **Parameters as node properties, not graph nodes** — avoid graph explosion. Promote to Parameter label only if a query pattern requires it.

## Sources

- PR #540 comments: method extractors needed, interface dispatch gap
- claude-mem #21460: MethodExtractor design mirrors FieldExtractor
- claude-mem #20233: Pipeline DAG (14 phases, no new phase needed)
- claude-mem #19975: FieldInfo/ExtractedFields contracts to mirror
- claude-mem #19945: Generic factory with extractNames pattern
- claude-mem #18453: LanguageProviderConfig interface structure
- Architecture review: lookupMethodByOwner > methodReturnTypeMap, signature matching for overloads
- Pattern review: 10 deviations found and addressed (visibility reuse, cache shape, clearCaches)
- Simplicity review: 5 PRs → 2 PRs, 15 files → 8 files, ~60-70% LOC reduction

title: feat: lookupMethodByOwner on SymbolTable for chain resolution
body:
## Parent RFC: #568
## Depends on: #569

## Summary

Add `lookupMethodByOwner(ownerNodeId, methodName)` to SymbolTable, following the existing `lookupFieldByOwner` pattern. Enables cross-class chained call resolution (`user.getAddress().save()`) without a separate methodReturnTypeMap.

## Modified Files

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `gitnexus/src/core/ingestion/symbol-table.ts` | Add `lookupMethodByOwner` method + index |
| `gitnexus/src/core/ingestion/call-processor.ts` | Use in `walkMixedChain` for method return type resolution |

## Implementation

## Summary

Closes #569 (PR 1 of RFC #568)

- Add structured method metadata extraction mirroring the FieldExtractor pattern

- Java and Kotlin configs with `isAbstract`/`isFinal` detection, structured `ParameterInfo`, annotations, visibility
- Worker integration with overload-safe `methodInfoCache` (keyed by `name:line`, not name alone)
- `isAbstract`, `isFinal`, `annotations` added to `NodeProperties` in gitnexus-shared

### New Files (3)
| File | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `method-types.ts` | `MethodInfo`, `ParameterInfo`, `MethodExtractionConfig`, `MethodExtractor`, `ExtractedMethods` |
| `method-extractors/generic.ts` | `createMethodExtractor()` factory |

### Modified Files (5)
| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `gitnexus-shared/src/graph/types.ts` | `isAbstract?`, `isFinal?`, `annotations?` on NodeProperties |
| `language-provider.ts` | `methodExtractor?: MethodExtractor` on LanguageProviderConfig |

1. **Config + factory only** — no `BaseMethodExtractor` class (11/12 field extractors use the factory, base class is dead weight)

title: Dart language resolution support — tree-sitter-dart loads but no symbols extracted
body:
## Summary

As of v1.4.10, `tree-sitter-dart` loads successfully (confirmed via `--verbose`), but GitNexus only indexes Dart files at the **File level** — no class, method, function, or import symbols are extracted. This means tools like `context`, `impact`, and `detect_changes` return no useful data for Dart/Flutter codebases.

## Environment

- GitNexus version: v1.4.10
- Node.js: v20+
- OS: macOS
- Project: Large Flutter codebase (~300 screens), migrated from React Native

## Steps to Reproduce

1. `npx gitnexus@latest analyze --force --verbose` in a Flutter project
2. No Dart-related skip/error messages in verbose output (parser loads fine)
3. Run `query({query: "SomeClassName"})` via MCP — returns file-level matches only
4. Run `context({name: "SomeClassName"})` — no symbol found

## Expected Behavior

Dart symbols (classes, methods, functions, mixins, extensions) should be extracted with:
- **Imports** — `import` / `export` / `part` / `part of` resolution
- **Exports** — public symbol detection (Dart has no `export` keyword, everything without `_` prefix is public)
- **Heritage** — `extends`, `implements`, `with` (mixins)
- **Type Annotations** — explicit types for receiver resolution
- **Constructor Inference** — `self`/`this` resolution
- **Frameworks** — Flutter widget detection (`StatelessWidget`, `StatefulWidget`, `State<T>`)

## Actual Behavior

tree-sitter-dart parses the AST successfully, but no language-specific resolution logic exists to extract symbols from the AST. Only file nodes are created in the knowledge graph.

## Context

v1.4.10 fixed tree-sitter peer dependency conflicts (#537, #538) and pinned tree-sitter-dart to an ABI-14-compatible commit. This ensures the parser **loads** without crashing, but loading the parser ≠ having resolution support.

Dart/Flutter is one of the fastest-growing mobile frameworks. Adding full Dart resolution would make GitNexus usable for a large developer community.

## Summary

Closes #570. Adds TypeScript and JavaScript method extraction configs to the MethodExtractor framework, following the established JVM (PR #576) and C# (PR #582) patterns.

- **New file:** `method-extractors/configs/typescript-javascript.ts` — shared config base with two one-liner exports (mirrors field extractor pattern)
- **Modified:** `languages/typescript.ts` — wired `methodExtractor` into both `typescriptProvider` and `javascriptProvider`
- **Tests:** 16 new tests (11 TS + 5 JS) covering all acceptance criteria

### Key Detection Logic
| Feature | Detection |
|---------|-----------|
| isAbstract | `hasKeyword(node, 'abstract')` OR `ownerNode.type === 'interface_declaration'` |
| Visibility | Two-pass: `accessibility_modifier` child first, then `findVisibility` fallback |
| Parameters | Handles `required_parameter`, `optional_parameter`, `rest_parameter` (TS) + `identifier`, `assignment_pattern`, `rest_pattern` (JS) + destructured `object_pattern`/`array_pattern` |
| Return type | `return_type` field → unwrap `type_annotation` |
| Decorators | Walk preceding siblings in class body (decorators are body-level, not method children) |
| isAsync/isOverride | `hasKeyword` one-liners |

### Design Decisions
- **Single shared base** — TS-only node types (`abstract_class_declaration`, `interface_declaration`, `abstract_method_signature`, `method_signature`, `interface_body`) are harmless no-ops for JS grammar. Matches field extractor precedent.
- **Rest params via `required_parameter`** — tree-sitter-typescript wraps `...args` as `required_parameter` with a `rest_pattern` child, not as `rest_parameter`. Detected and handled.
- **Default params** — `required_parameter` with `value` field → `isOptional: true`

## Summary

Adds opt-in support for using system-provided ONNX Runtime bindings and fixes embeddings in sandboxed environments by ensuring a writable Transformers.js cache directory.

## Motivation / context

Packaging in sandboxed environments needs a way to use a prebuilt `onnxruntime_binding.node` without disabling features. Embeddings were also failing because Transformers.js tried to write its cache under a read-only install path. Related to issue #376.

- Add loader that redirects `onnxruntime_binding.node` to a user-specified path.
- Wire the override into both core embedder entrypoints.
- Configure Transformers.js cache dir to a writable location for sandboxed installs.
- Document the environment variable and usage.

**Explicitly out of scope / not done here**

- The override hooks Node’s module resolution so that requests for `onnxruntime_binding.node` resolve to the path in `GITNEXUS_ORT_BINDING_PATH`.
- Transformers.js cache is set to `$HOME/.cache/gitnexus/transformers` when possible, avoiding writes to read-only install paths.
