title: feat: add --incremental flag to analyze command
body:
## Summary

Adds an `--incremental` flag to the `analyze` command that skips re-parsing unchanged files on subsequent runs. This dramatically reduces re-index time for large repos when only a few files changed.

## How it works

1. During indexing, computes SHA-256 hashes for every parsed file
2. Stores hashes in `meta.json` alongside the existing repo metadata
3. On subsequent runs with `--incremental`, compares current hashes against stored ones
4. Only files with changed hashes are re-parsed — structure scanning and graph phases still run fully to ensure correct community/process detection
5. Stale nodes (from deleted/renamed files) are removed from LadybugDB instead of wiping and recreating

## Performance

For a 60K+ symbol TypeScript repo, re-index time drops from ~30s to ~2-5s when only a few files changed between runs.

## Usage

```bash
gitnexus analyze /path/to/repo                # full index (default)
gitnexus analyze -i /path/to/repo             # incremental (skip unchanged)
gitnexus analyze --incremental /path/to/repo  # same
```

Docker:
```bash
docker run -e GITNEXUS_INCREMENTAL=1 ...      # enables --incremental on container restart
```

## Files changed

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `src/storage/file-hasher.ts` | **NEW** — `computeFileHashes()` and `diffFileHashes()` |
| `src/cli/index.ts` | Register `-i/--incremental` CLI flag |
| `src/cli/analyze.ts` | Forward `incremental` option to `runFullAnalysis` |
| `src/core/run-analyze.ts` | Load previous hashes, pass to pipeline, save new hashes, incremental LadybugDB merge |
| `src/core/ingestion/pipeline.ts` | Accept `previousFileHashes`, filter parse phase to changed files only, return `fileHashes` in result |
| `src/types/pipeline.ts` | Add `fileHashes` to `PipelineResult` |
| `src/storage/repo-manager.ts` | Add `fileHashes` to `RepoMeta` |
| `Dockerfile` | Production two-stage build with incremental support |
| `entrypoint.sh` | Container entrypoint — indexes repos, starts eval-server |

## Test plan

- [ ] `gitnexus analyze /path/to/repo` produces same graph as before (no regression)
- [ ] `gitnexus analyze -i /path/to/repo` on second run skips unchanged files (check console output: "Incremental: N changed, M removed, K unchanged")
- [ ] Deleting a source file and re-running with `-i` removes stale nodes from the graph
- [ ] Adding a new file and re-running with `-i` indexes only the new file
- [ ] `meta.json` contains `fileHashes` after first run

title: fix(cli): flatten repo-local Claude skill generation
body:
## Summary

This changes the repo-local `gitnexus analyze` skill output to use a flat
Claude skill layout under `.claude/skills/` instead of nested directories like
`.claude/skills/gitnexus/<skill>/SKILL.md` and
`.claude/skills/generated/<area>/SKILL.md`.

The current nested layout makes the generated skills hard to discover in Claude
Code. This update makes the repo-local output match the flat layout already
used by the global setup flow.

## What changed

- Install bundled repo-local GitNexus skills directly under
  `.claude/skills/<skill>/SKILL.md`.
- Generate community skills as flat directories named
  `.claude/skills/gitnexus-generated-<area>/SKILL.md`.
- Update generated `AGENTS.md` and `CLAUDE.md` references to the new flat
  paths.
- Remove legacy nested generated directories during regeneration so reruns do
  not leave stale skill trees behind.
- Tighten managed block replacement for `AGENTS.md` and `CLAUDE.md` so marker
  text mentioned in prose does not corrupt the injected GitNexus block.
- Fix the `skills-e2e` helper so repos that end up with only bundled skills and
  no generated community skills still follow the intended skip behavior for the
  flaky C# parser path in CI.
- Update tests and documentation to reflect the new layout.

## Why

Claude Code appears to discover local skills only one directory deep under
`.claude/skills/`. With the current output, bundled and generated GitNexus
skills land one level too deep, so they are not reliably discoverable.

Flattening the repo-local skill layout fixes that without changing the skill
content itself. It also makes the per-repo `analyze` flow consistent with the
existing global `gitnexus setup` skill installation behavior.

## Testing

- Ran focused unit tests:
  - `./node_modules/.bin/vitest run test/unit/ai-context.test.ts test/unit/skill-gen.test.ts`
- Ran the relevant integration regression locally:
  - `npx vitest run test/integration/skills-e2e.test.ts -t CSharp`
- Built shared package needed by the CLI/test workspace:
  - `./node_modules/.bin/tsc -p ../gitnexus-shared/tsconfig.json`
- Built the CLI package:
  - `./node_modules/.bin/tsc -p tsconfig.json`
- Ran end-to-end fixture validation:
  - `node dist/cli/index.js analyze <fixture-repo> --skills`
  - Confirmed bundled skills were written as flat entries like
    `.claude/skills/gitnexus-exploring/SKILL.md`
  - Confirmed generated community skills were written as flat entries like
    `.claude/skills/gitnexus-generated-data/SKILL.md`

    paths
- Ran end-to-end validation against this repo:
  - `node dist/cli/index.js analyze /path/to/GitNexus --skills`
  - Confirmed community skills were generated under flat
    `gitnexus-generated-*` directories

## Notes for review

- This is intentionally scoped to repo-local skill generation and AI context
  output.
- Global editor setup paths stay flat and continue to work as before.
- Generated community skills keep a distinct `gitnexus-generated-` prefix to
  avoid collisions with bundled skills.

title: Web UI enters reconnect loop after successful local bridge connection in serve mode
body:
### Area

gitnexus-web (browser UI / WASM / workers)

### Summary

After connecting the hosted web UI to a local gitnexus serve instance, the graph loads successfully but the app later re-enters the “Server Connected / Preparing your code knowledge graph...” flow and loops between connected and reconnecting.

### Context

I was using GitNexus bridge mode with the hosted web UI and a locally indexed repo.

Commands used:

npx gitnexus@latest analyze
npx gitnexus@latest serve
Then I opened:

https://gitnexus.vercel.app
The local repo was already indexed and the UI successfully loaded the graph for it.

I also recorded the behavior:

a 23s screen recording shows the graph fully loaded
then the app unexpectedly shows the full-screen reconnect overlay again
then the graph returns without me reloading the page
Possible implementation clue:

serve defaults to 127.0.0.1
the web UI defaults to http://localhost:4747
the web app also has separate onboarding probe and heartbeat reconnect paths
Relevant files:

gitnexus/src/cli/serve.ts
gitnexus/src/server/api.ts
gitnexus-web/src/config/ui-constants.ts
gitnexus-web/src/hooks/useBackend.ts
gitnexus-web/src/services/backend-client.ts
gitnexus-web/src/App.tsx

### Expected behavior

Once the hosted UI connects to the local serve bridge and the graph is loaded, the app should remain in the graph/explorer view without bouncing back into the connection/loading overlay unless the local server actually goes down.

### Actual behavior

The hosted UI connects, loads the graph, and shows the repo normally. After a short delay, it re-enters the full-screen “Server Connected / Preparing your code knowledge graph...” overlay, as if it is reconnecting. After several seconds, the graph view comes back again. This repeats/feels like a connect-disconnect loop.

Importantly:

the graph was already loaded
the local server appeared to still be listening
the same repo and same graph came back after the reconnect overlay

### Steps to reproduce

1. Open a terminal inside an existing indexed repo, or index one first:
   npx gitnexus@latest analyze

2. Start the local bridge server:
   npx gitnexus@latest serve

3. Open the hosted UI in Chrome:
   https://gitnexus.vercel.app

4. Let the app auto-detect/connect to the local server and load the repo graph.

5. Wait on the loaded graph screen for several seconds without reloading.

6. Observe that the app unexpectedly re-enters the full-screen
   "Server Connected / Preparing your code knowledge graph..." overlay.

7. After several seconds, the graph view comes back again on its own.

8. This can repeat, creating a connect/disconnect-style loop even though the graph was already loaded.


### Environment

OS: Windows
Node: v20.20.0
Browser: Chrome desktop
GitNexus version: 1.4.10
Web UI: https://gitnexus.vercel.app

### Logs / screenshots

Local verification from investigation:

- `npx gitnexus@latest analyze` completed successfully
- `npx gitnexus@latest serve` started successfully
- local server was listening on 127.0.0.1:4747
- requesting http://127.0.0.1:4747 returned 404 Not Found
  (server alive, but root path is not a normal page)
- web UI still loaded the graph successfully and showed:
  - 88 nodes
  - 203 edges

Recorded behavior from screen capture:
- ~0s to ~10s: graph is loaded and stable
- ~11s: app suddenly shows full-screen "Server Connected" overlay again
- ~11s to ~20s: overlay remains visible
- ~21s: graph returns without manual reload

Relevant implementation clues:
- serve default host: 127.0.0.1
- web UI default backend URL: http://localhost:4747
- web app uses both:
  - onboarding probe polling
  - heartbeat/EventSource reconnect handling

Likely result:
- a false disconnect/reconnect transition in the web UI connection lifecycle,
  even while the local bridge is still up

title: v1.4.10: .gitnexusignore negation patterns silently produce 0 nodes
body:
## Environment
- macOS 15 (arm64, Apple M1 Max)
- Node 22
- gitnexus v1.4.10 (via `npx -y gitnexus@latest`)

## Bug

When a `.gitnexusignore` file uses the gitignore-style "exclude all then whitelist" pattern, v1.4.10 produces **0 nodes / 0 edges**. The same file works correctly in v1.3.11 (55k nodes).

### `.gitnexusignore` contents:
```
# Exclude everything by default
*

# Include iOS source code
!iOS/
!iOS/**

# Include only backend/living_plan
!backend/
!backend/living_plan/
!backend/living_plan/**

# Exclude tests everywhere
**/Tests/
**/tests/
```

### Steps to reproduce
1. Create the `.gitnexusignore` above in a repo with Python + Swift code
2. Run `npx -y gitnexus@1.4.10 analyze`
3. Observe: `0 nodes | 0 edges | 0 clusters | 0 flows` (completes in ~1.9s, clearly not parsing)
4. Remove `.gitnexusignore` and re-run → `38,872 nodes` (Python only, Swift skipped separately)
5. Run with `npx -y gitnexus@1.3.11 analyze` with the same ignore file → `55,429 nodes` ✅

### Root cause
The `!` negation patterns (whitelist after `*` blacklist) appear to be silently broken in v1.4.10. The analyzer doesn't error; it just finds 0 files to parse.

## Secondary issue: tree-sitter-swift missing from v1.4.10

Both v1.3.11 and v1.4.10 fresh `npx` installs ship without `tree-sitter-swift`, producing:
```
Skipping 976 swift file(s) — swift parser not available (native binding may not have built)
```

Manually installing it into the npx cache fixes this:
```
npm install --prefix <npx-cache-dir> tree-sitter-swift
```

Swift is listed as a supported language in the README, so it should either be bundled or installed automatically.

## Workaround
Pin to v1.3.11:
```
claude mcp add gitnexus -- npx -y gitnexus@1.3.11 mcp
npx -y gitnexus@1.3.11 analyze
```

title: Fix/wiki script escape and llm token param
body:
These are the same changes as #371. I have created a new merge request.

## Summary

Fix XSS vulnerability in wiki HTML viewer by escaping HTML-significant characters in embedded JSON, and add automatic `max_tokens` → `max_completion_tokens` parameter fallback in the LLM client for models that reject the legacy parameter name.

## Motivation / context

1. **Script injection in wiki HTML:** The wiki viewer embeds page content as JSON inside a `<script>` tag using raw `JSON.stringify`. If any wiki page content contains `</script>`, the HTML parser closes the script block early, enabling XSS. This is especially dangerous because wiki content is LLM-generated and its exact output is unpredictable.
2. **LLM token parameter compatibility:** Newer OpenAI models (e.g. `o3-mini`, `gpt-4.1`) reject the `max_tokens` parameter with a 400 error, requiring `max_completion_tokens` instead. Users hitting this error had no recourse other than manually configuring the correct parameter. The auto-switch makes the wiki generator work out of the box with both old and new model families.

## Areas touched

- [x] `gitnexus/` (CLI / core / MCP server)
- [ ] `gitnexus-web/` (Vite / React UI)
- [ ] `.github/` (workflows, actions)
- [ ] `eval/` or other tooling
- [ ] Docs / agent config only (`AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `.cursor/`, `llms.txt`, etc.)

## Scope & constraints

**In scope**

- `safeJSON()` helper that Unicode-escapes `<`, `>`, `&` in serialized JSON so it is safe to embed in `<script>` tags
- Content-Security-Policy meta tag added to generated wiki HTML (`default-src 'none'`; allows inline scripts, the marked CDN, and data/https images)
- Auto-retry in `callLLM` that switches `max_tokens` to `max_completion_tokens` on a 400 mentioning `'max_tokens'`, without consuming a retry attempt
- Unit tests for both changes

**Explicitly out of scope / not done here**

- Migrating the wiki viewer away from inline scripts entirely (would require a bundler or separate JS asset)
- Server-side HTML sanitization of LLM-generated markdown (the CSP and JSON escaping are defense-in-depth at the embedding layer)
- Proactively detecting the model family to choose the correct token parameter up front (the reactive fallback is simpler and model-list-agnostic)

## Implementation notes

- **`safeJSON` replacement order matters:** `<` and `>` are replaced before `&` because their replacements (`\u003c`, `\u003e`) contain no `&`, so the final `&` pass cannot double-escape them. The function round-trips cleanly through `JSON.parse`.
- **Token-param switch is one-shot:** A `switchedTokenParam` boolean prevents infinite retry loops. The `attempt--` ensures the switch itself doesn't consume one of the 3 retry budget slots.
- **CSP policy is intentionally permissive for inline scripts** (`'unsafe-inline' 'unsafe-eval'`) because the wiki viewer relies on inline `<script>` blocks and `marked.js` uses `new Function`. This still blocks all other sources (`default-src 'none'`), which is a meaningful improvement over no CSP.

## Testing & verification

- [x] `cd gitnexus && npm test`
- [ ] `cd gitnexus && npm run test:integration` *(if core/indexing/MCP paths changed)*
- [x] `cd gitnexus && npx tsc --noEmit`
- [ ] `cd gitnexus-web && npm test` *(web not changed)*
- [ ] `cd gitnexus-web && npx tsc -b --noEmit` *(web not changed)*
- [ ] Manual / Playwright E2E

**New test coverage:**

- `wiki-html-viewer.test.ts` — 7 tests: `safeJSON` escaping of `<`, `>`, `&`, `</script>` XSS vector, round-trip fidelity, no double-escaping, undefined/non-serializable handling, and CSP meta tag presence in generated HTML
- `wiki-llm-client.test.ts` — 4 new tests: successful auto-switch, no trigger on unrelated 400s, no trigger when already using `max_completion_tokens` (reasoning models), and verification that the switch doesn't consume a retry attempt

## Risk & rollout

- **Low risk.** Both changes are additive/defensive and do not alter the happy path.
- `safeJSON` is a strict superset of `JSON.stringify` — output is always valid JSON that `JSON.parse` can round-trip.
- The token-param auto-switch only activates on a specific 400 error shape that would otherwise be a hard failure, so it cannot make a working request worse.
- No index refresh needed (`npx gitnexus analyze` not required).
- No breaking changes or migrations.

## Checklist

- [x] PR body meets repo minimum length (workflow may label short descriptions)
- [x] If `AGENTS.md` / overlays changed: headers, scope block, and changelog updated per project conventions
- [x] No secrets, tokens, or machine-specific paths committed

title: feat(vue): add Vue SFC (.vue) support for indexing
body:
Vue Single File Components are now fully supported in the indexing pipeline.
The implementation extracts <script> / <script setup> blocks from .vue files
and parses them using the existing TypeScript tree-sitter grammar — no new
npm dependencies required.

Key changes:
- SFC script extractor: regex-based extraction of <script setup lang="ts">
  blocks with correct line offset mapping back to the .vue file
- Vue language provider: reuses TypeScript queries, type config, field
  extractors, and named binding extraction
- Import resolution: .vue added to EXTENSIONS so `import Foo from './Foo'`
  resolves to Foo.vue; Vue import resolver delegates to TS resolver for
  tsconfig path alias support
- Export detection: <script setup> top-level bindings are implicitly exported
- Template component detection: PascalCase tags in <template> emit CALLS edges
- Line offsets applied to all emitted positions (startLine, endLine, route
  lineNumbers, decorator positions) in both worker and sequential paths

Validated on a 3,553-file Vue project:
  Before: 24,693 nodes | 73,614 edges | 0 symbols from .vue
  After:  30,495 nodes | 112,324 edges | 5,213 symbols from .vue
          18,682 imports from .vue | 5,826 vue-to-vue imports

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

title: feat(vue): Vue SFC support + destructured call result tracking
body:
## Summary                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  
  
  Adds full Vue SFC (`.vue`) indexing by extracting `<script setup>` / `<script>` blocks and parsing them with the existing TypeScript tree-sitter grammar. Also extends the TypeEnv to track destructured call results (`const { x } = fn()`), improving type
   resolution for Vue composables, React hooks, and Pinia stores.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              
  ## Motivation / context                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     
  
  GitNexus completely skipped `.vue` files during indexing — in a 5,200-file Vue project, 3,553 `.vue` files (68% of the codebase, 512K lines) produced zero symbols and zero relationships. Additionally, the dominant Vue pattern of destructuring          
  composable return values (`const { isMaker } = useUserRole()`) was untracked in the TypeEnv because `extractPendingAssignment` only handled identifier RHS, not `call_expression` RHS.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              
  **Validated on a production Vue project:**                                                                                                                                                                                              
  
  | Metric | Before | After |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 
  |--------|--------|-------|                               
  | Nodes | 24,693 | 30,495 (+23%) |                                                                                                                                                                                                                          
  | Edges | 73,614 | 112,324 (+53%) |                                                                                                                                                                                                                         
  | Symbols from .vue | 0 | 5,213 |                                                                                                                                                                                                                           
  | Imports from .vue | 136 | 18,682 |                                                                                                                                                                                                                        
  | Vue-to-Vue imports | 0 | 5,826 |                                                                                                                                                                                                                          
  | Clusters | 1,732 | 2,458 (+42%) |                                                                                                                                                                                                                         
  | Flows | 235 | 300 (+28%) |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              
  ## Areas touched                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              
  - [x] `gitnexus/` (CLI / core / MCP server)                                                                                                                                                                                                                 
  - [ ] `gitnexus-web/` (Vite / React UI)
  - [ ] `.github/` (workflows, actions)                                                                                                                                                                                                                       
  - [ ] `eval/` or other tooling                                                                                                                                                                                                                              
  - [ ] Docs / agent config only (`AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `.cursor/`, `llms.txt`, etc.)                                                                                                                                                                     
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              
  ## Scope & constraints                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              
  **In scope**                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                
                                                            
  - Vue SFC script extraction: regex-based `<script setup>` / `<script>` block extraction with correct line offset mapping                                                                                                                                    
  - Vue language provider: reuses TypeScript queries, type config, field extractors, import resolution
  - Import resolution: `.vue` added to EXTENSIONS; Vue import resolver delegates to TS resolver for tsconfig path alias support                                                                                                                               
  - Export detection: `<script setup>` top-level bindings are implicitly exported                                                                                                                                                                             
  - Template component detection: PascalCase tags in `<template>` emit CALLS edges                                                                                                                                                                            
  - Line offsets: applied to all emitted positions in both worker and sequential paths                                                                                                                                                                        
  - Destructured call results: `const { x } = fn()`, `const { x } = await fn()`, `const { x } = obj.method()` → synthetic `callResult` + N `fieldAccess` items                                                                                                
  - Renamed destructuring: `const { address: addr } = fn()`                                                                                                                                                                                                   
  - Extract `collectDestructuredFields` helper to deduplicate property iteration                                                                                                                                                                              
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              
  **Explicitly out of scope / not done here**                                                                                                                                                                                                                 
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              
  - Return-type inference from function bodies (composables without explicit `returnType` annotations won't resolve property types — requires analyzing `return { ... }` statements, a separate effort)                                                       
  - `<template>` expression analysis beyond PascalCase component detection
  - Nuxt/Vue Router file-based route extraction                                                                                                                                                                                                               
  - `gitnexus-web` WASM pipeline changes (browser-side Vue support)                                                                                                                                                                                           
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              
  ## Implementation notes                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              
  **Vue SFC support** — The approach pre-extracts `<script>` content from `.vue` files via regex, then feeds it to the existing TypeScript tree-sitter parser. No new npm dependencies. The `extractVueScript()` utility handles `<script setup lang="ts">`,  
  `<script lang="ts">`, both blocks coexisting (prefers setup), and computes line offsets by counting newlines before the script content. The Vue language provider reuses `TYPESCRIPT_QUERIES`, `typescriptConfig`, `tsExportChecker`,
  `extractTsNamedBindings`, and `typescriptFieldExtractor`.                                                                                                                                                                                                   
                                                            
  **Destructured call results** — For `const { isMaker, isChecker } = useUserRole()`, we emit:                                                                                                                                                                
  1. `{ kind: 'callResult', lhs: '__destr_useUserRole_42', callee: 'useUserRole' }`
  2. `{ kind: 'fieldAccess', lhs: 'isMaker', receiver: '__destr_useUserRole_42', field: 'isMaker' }`                                                                                                                                                          
  3. `{ kind: 'fieldAccess', lhs: 'isChecker', receiver: '__destr_useUserRole_42', field: 'isChecker' }`                                                                                                                                                      
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              
  The existing fixpoint resolver processes this in 2 iterations. No changes to `type-env.ts`, `PendingAssignment` types, or `call-processor.ts`.                                                                                                              
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              
  **Tradeoff:** Full property-type resolution requires the callee to have a declared `returnType` in the SymbolTable. Most Vue composables use arrow functions without annotations, so property types remain unresolved — graceful degradation. The           
  infrastructure is ready for when return-type inference is added.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              
  ## Testing & verification                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   
  
  - [x] `cd gitnexus && npm test` — 4,581 tests pass, 0 regressions                                                                                                                                                                                           
  - [x] `cd gitnexus && npx tsc --noEmit` — compiles clean  
  - [x] Re-indexed production Vue project (3,553 `.vue` files), verified via MCP cypher/query/context tools                                                                                                                                                   
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              
  **Vue SFC tests:**                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          
  - 12 unit tests for SFC extractor (script extraction, line offsets, template components, multiline attrs, edge cases)                                                                                                                                       
  - 8 integration tests with `vue-basic` fixture (symbol extraction, line offsets, imports .vue↔.ts, exports, cross-file CALLS)                                                                                                                               
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              
  **Destructured call result tests:**                                                                                                                                                                                                                         
  - 7 new unit tests in `type-env.test.ts` (destructured calls, await, method calls, renamed, graceful degradation, synthetic variable resolution)                                                                                                            
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              
  ## Risk & rollout                                         
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              
  - **No breaking changes** — new language support and new TypeEnv items; no existing behavior altered                                                                                                                                                        
  - **Index refresh recommended** — run `npx gitnexus analyze --force` on Vue projects to pick up `.vue` file indexing
  - **Performance:** Vue SFC extraction adds negligible overhead (regex-based, no new parser). Destructured call items add 1 + N items to the fixpoint resolver per destructured call — negligible for typical composables.                                   
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              
  ## Checklist                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              
  - [x] PR body meets repo minimum length                                                                                                                                                                                                                     
  - [ ] If `AGENTS.md` / overlays changed: headers, scope block, and changelog updated per project conventions
  - [x] No secrets, tokens, or machine-specific paths committed

title: feat: gitnexus:keep marker preserves custom context sections
body:
## Summary

When `<!-- gitnexus:keep -->` is placed inside the GitNexus-generated block in CLAUDE.md or AGENTS.md, `analyze` only updates the stats line (node/edge/flow counts) instead of replacing the entire section with the verbose default template.

This lets users trim the auto-generated context to a lean custom format without it being overwritten on every reindex.

## Problem

Every `analyze` run regenerates the full GitNexus section in CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md with the verbose template (tool descriptions, usage instructions, risk levels, etc.). Teams that maintain a lean custom format have to re-edit the file after every reindex.

## Solution

- If keep marker is present but no stats line is found, the section is preserved as-is

title: fix(embeddings): dispose ONNX Runtime session before process exit
body:
## Summary

Fixes #151

- Fixes `libc++abi: terminating due to uncaught exception of type std::__1::system_error: mutex lock failed: Invalid argument` crash when running `gitnexus analyze --embeddings --skills`
- The ONNX Runtime inference session was never disposed after the embedding pipeline completed
- When `process.exit(0)` fires, both ONNX Runtime's and LadybugDB's C++ `atexit` destructors race with each other, crashing on a mutex that's already been invalidated

## Fix

Call `disposeEmbedder()` in `run-analyze.ts` in two places:

1. **Happy path** — immediately after `runEmbeddingPipeline()` completes, inside the `if (!embeddingSkipped)` block
2. **Error path** — in the outer `catch` block, before `closeLbug()`, so a failed embedding run also cleans up the ONNX session

This ensures the ONNX Runtime session is released before LadybugDB closes and before `process.exit(0)`, eliminating the C++ destructor race on both success and failure paths.

## Verification

- Tested against a repo that consistently reproduced the crash (`v0-quorum-report-redesign-concep`)
- Full `--force --embeddings --skills` re-index completed cleanly (exit code 0, no crash)
- Full test suite passes (4,555 tests passed)

## Test plan

- [x] `gitnexus analyze --embeddings --skills --force` completes without mutex crash
- [x] `gitnexus analyze` (no embeddings) still exits cleanly
- [x] Full test suite passes (4,555 tests, 0 failures)

title: ci: use CHANGELOG.md for GitHub Release notes
body:
## Summary

Replaces `generate_release_notes: true` in the publish workflow with a step that extracts the current version's section from `gitnexus/CHANGELOG.md` and uses it as the GitHub Release body.

## Problem

The auto-generated release notes just list PR titles grouped by label — not useful for announcements and requires manual editing after every release.

## Solution

Since we already write a thorough, reviewed CHANGELOG entry as part of every release PR, the publish workflow now:

1. Extracts the section between `## [X.Y.Z]` and the next `## [` from `CHANGELOG.md`
2. Uses that as the GitHub Release body via `body_path`
3. Falls back to auto-generated notes if no CHANGELOG entry is found (safety net)

**Before:** Tag push → publish → auto-generated PR list → maintainer manually edits release notes
**After:** Tag push → publish → CHANGELOG section used automatically → done

## How it works

```bash
# awk extracts lines between ## [1.5.0] and the next ## [
awk '/^## \[1.5.0\]/{found=1; next} /^## \[/{if(found) exit} found' gitnexus/CHANGELOG.md
```

The CHANGELOG.md becomes the single source of truth — written and reviewed during the release PR, automatically used by the publish workflow.

body:
### Area

gitnexus (CLI / core / indexing / MCP server)

### Summary

# Description
`gitnexus@1.5.0` published to npm contains a `file:` protocol dependency that only works in the monorepo:

```json
"gitnexus-shared": "file:../gitnexus-shared"
```

This makes v1.5.0 **uninstallable** from npm:

```
ERR_PNPM_LINKED_PKG_DIR_NOT_FOUND  Could not install from "…/gitnexus-shared" as it does not exist.
```

The same failure occurs with `npm install -g gitnexus@latest`.

**Root cause:** The `gitnexus-shared` workspace package is not published to npm, and the `file:` reference was not replaced during the publish step. Previous versions (1.4.9 and earlier) did not have this dependency.

**Suggested fix:** Either:
1. Publish `gitnexus-shared` as a separate npm package and reference it by version (e.g., `"gitnexus-shared": "^1.5.0"`)
2. Bundle the shared code into the `gitnexus` package before publishing (e.g., via a `prepack` script that copies or builds it in)
3. Use a monorepo publish tool (e.g., `changesets`, `lerna`, `nx release`) that rewrites `file:` references to registry versions automatically

**Workaround:** Pin to `gitnexus@1.4.9`.

title: v1.5.0: Cannot find package 'gitnexus-shared' when installed from npm
body:
## Bug

`npx gitnexus analyze` fails with:

```
Error [ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND]: Cannot find package 'gitnexus-shared' imported from
.../node_modules/gitnexus/dist/core/ingestion/pipeline.js
```

## Cause

`package.json` in v1.5.0 declares:

```json
"gitnexus-shared": "file:../gitnexus-shared"
```

This is a workspace-local reference that only resolves inside the monorepo. When `gitnexus` is installed from npm (via `npx` or `npm i -g`), `gitnexus-shared` is not included in the published tarball and `file:../gitnexus-shared` points to nothing.

## Affected

- `npx gitnexus analyze` (any repo)
- `npm i -g gitnexus@1.5.0` then `gitnexus analyze`
- Any command that imports `pipeline.js` (analyze, presumably)

## Not affected

- `gitnexus list`, `gitnexus --version`, `gitnexus --help` (don't import pipeline.js)
- v1.4.10 and earlier (no gitnexus-shared dependency)

## Workaround

```bash
npm i -g gitnexus@1.4.10
```

## Suggested fix

Either:
1. Bundle `gitnexus-shared` into the `gitnexus` npm package before publishing
2. Or publish `gitnexus-shared` as a separate npm package and reference it by version instead of `file:`

## Environment

- Node.js v23.7.0
- npm 10.x
- macOS 14 (ARM64)

title: feat(cpp): C/C++ MethodExtractor config with pure virtual detection
body:
## Summary

Closes #572 (parent RFC: #568, depends on #569)

- New `c-cpp.ts` method extractor config for C++ and C
- Pure virtual (`= 0`) detected via token scanning → `isAbstract: true`
- `virtual`, `final`, `override` via `hasKeyword` and `virtual_specifier` children
- Access specifier visibility via backward sibling walk (`public:`/`private:`/`protected:`)
- Pointer/reference parameter types extracted correctly
- Constructor and destructor support via `declaration` node type
- Static detection via `storage_class_specifier`
- Wired into both `cppProvider` and `cProvider` in `languages/c-cpp.ts`

## Key Design Decisions

- `methodNodeTypes` includes `field_declaration`, `function_definition`, and `declaration` — C++ has no dedicated method node type. Non-method nodes (data members, typedefs) are filtered by `extractName` returning `undefined` when no `function_declarator` is found.
- `final`/`override` are `virtual_specifier` children of the `function_declarator` (not the method node), so a dedicated `hasVirtualSpecifier` helper drills into the declarator.
- C config is minimal — C has no OOP methods, but exists for completeness.

## Known Gaps (documented in code)

- Out-of-class method definitions (`void Foo::bar() {}`) not linked as `HAS_METHOD`
- Friend declarations not extracted
- Template method explicit specializations

## Test Plan

- [x] 16 new C++ tests covering all acceptance criteria
- [x] Pure virtual → `isAbstract: true`, `isVirtual: true`
- [x] Virtual non-pure → `isAbstract: false`, `isVirtual: true`
- [x] `final`, `override`, `static` detection
- [x] Pointer/reference parameter types

1. Refactor buildTypeEnv declaration type-node lookup so grammar-specific declaration-type discovery lives in language configs.
2. Add end-to-end Java method_reference (::) support by capturing method_reference in JAVA_QUERIES and resolving those call sites in both worker and sequential call-processing paths.

## Motivation / context

Java method references already had parser support and fixture coverage in the repo, but they were not being turned into CALLS edges end-to-end. The missing pieces were query capture and support in the sequential/re-processing path.

While working in nearby type-resolution code, I also cleaned up declaration type-node lookup in buildTypeEnv by moving language-specific AST-shape knowledge into per-language configs, which makes the hot path easier to follow and reduces grammar-specific branching in type-env.ts.

title: [group] Intra-repo service communication tracking
body:
## Summary

Adds a group system for repository analysis with intra-repo service communication tracking for microservice monorepos. This is the foundation for cross-repo impact analysis (follow-up PR).

**What changed:**
- Group infrastructure: types, config parser, contract registry, exact matching engine
- Service boundary detection for monorepos (package.json, go.mod, Dockerfile, pom.xml, Cargo.toml markers)
- HTTP route extractor (Spring, Express, Laravel, FastAPI + fetch/axios consumers)
- gRPC extractor (proto parsing + Go/Java/Python/TS server/client detection)
- Topic extractor (Kafka, RabbitMQ, NATS producers/consumers across 4 languages)
- Intra-repo matching between services within the same monorepo
- CLI commands: `group create/add/remove/list/sync/contracts/query/status`
- MCP tools: `group_list`, `group_sync`, `group_contracts`, `group_query`, `group_status`
- Documentation for new CLI commands and MCP tools in both READMEs

**Why:**
The GitNexus author requested intra-repo service tracking as a prerequisite for cross-repo analysis (#606). Proving that microservice monorepos index well is the foundation — once intra-repo works, the same extractors feed directly into the virtual graph for multi-repo support.

### Backward compatibility & roadmap

Groups are fully **opt-in** — `gitnexus analyze` continues to work exactly as before. For small/medium monorepos (2-20 services), a single `analyze` on the whole repo already captures everything in one graph, and `impact`/`query` tools see inter-service relationships through existing CALLS/IMPORTS edges.

Groups become valuable for:
- **Large monorepos** (20+ services) where per-service indexing is faster and less noisy
- **Multi-repo setups** where services live in separate git repositories

The gRPC, Kafka/RabbitMQ/NATS, and HTTP extractors currently run only inside `group sync`. A natural next step is integrating them into the standard `analyze` pipeline so that inter-service communication edges (gRPC calls, topic pub/sub) are captured automatically for **all** repos — no group setup required. This would make service communication tracking zero-config for monorepos of any size, while groups remain available for cross-repo and advanced use cases.

**How to verify:**
```bash
cd gitnexus
npx tsc --noEmit                    # typecheck
npm run test:unit                   # 2658 unit tests
npm run test:integration            # 1973 integration tests
# Monorepo fixture test:
npx vitest run test/integration/group/monorepo-sync.test.ts
```

**Risk / rollback:**
- All new code is in `src/core/group/` — isolated from existing functionality
- No existing APIs changed; `service` field is optional and backward-compatible
- `gitnexus analyze` behavior is completely unchanged
- Rollback: revert the PR (no migrations, no schema changes)

**Not in this PR (follow-up):**
- Cross-repo impact analysis (`group_impact` tool) — #606
- Manifest-declared cross-links (`links` in group.yaml)
- BM25/embedding matching cascade
- Integration of extractors into the `analyze` pipeline (zero-config mode)

## Test plan

- [x] 15 unit tests — ServiceBoundaryDetector
- [x] 16 unit tests — matching (incl. 4 intra-repo cases)
- [x] 13 unit tests — GrpcExtractor
- [x] 19 unit tests — TopicExtractor
- [x] 14 unit tests — GroupService
- [x] 9 unit tests — sync pipeline + stableRepoPoolId
- [x] Config parser, storage, types, HTTP extractor tests
- [x] 3 integration tests — monorepo sync (fixture with auth/orders/gateway)
- [x] Full regression: all existing tests pass

### Area

gitnexus (CLI / core / indexing / MCP server)

### Summary

GitNexus does not create nodes for Kafka or RabbitMQ listeners when analyzing a Spring Boot project

### Context

I ran GitNexus analyze on a Spring Boot project that contains methods annotated with @KafkaListener and @RabbitListener to process messages. After analysis, there are no nodes representing these listeners in the GitNexus graph. Since these listener methods act as the first node (entry endpoint) of an event processing flow, their absence prevents tracking or querying event flows in the graph.

When analyzing a Spring Boot project, GitNexus should detect message listeners (methods annotated with @KafkaListener and @RabbitListener) and create corresponding nodes in the graph. These listeners should be treated as endpoints / entry nodes for event flows so the event processing paths can be discovered and tracked.

All listener methods annotated with @KafkaListener or @RabbitListener are not recognized and do not appear in the graph, so event processing flows can't be represented or queried in GitNexus.

title: Bug: False "404 Not Found" Connection Timeout During Heavy Initial Repository Analysis
body: ### Area gitnexus-web (browser UI / WASM / workers) ### Summary False "404 Not Found" connection timeout during heavy initial repository analysis. ### Context When analyzing a Repo, completely unindexed remote repository for the very first time via the web UI, the frontend network client aggressively drops the connection and throws an error before the backend worker ever has a chance to finish the git clone process. Bug Preview Demonstration: https://youtu.be/8qrA4GZ1Wx0 ### Expected behavior The frontend should intelligently maintain the connection and wait for the backend worker to finish cloning/analyzing the initial heavy payload. The REST client should utilize an elevated, long-polling timeout limit for /api/repo resolution requests, rather than adhering to a strict global 10-second ceiling. ### Actual behavior The frontend unilaterally terminates its connection about 10,000ms, raising a false 404 Red Error Banner that traps the user on the DropZone. Meanwhile, the backend terminal prints several resolveRepo 404 logs but silently allows the background worker to continue cloning unaffected. Once the background worker naturally finishes minutes later, a manual page refresh and then the same repo get indexed to the list above on the frontend side and when click, it instantly resolves the repository without issue. ### Steps to reproduce Start the GitNexus application. Paste the URL of a large, completely unindexed repository into the "Analyze New" UI. Click "Analyze". Wait for about 10 seconds. The UI will abruptly drop the stream, showing a red error banner reading Request to ... timed out after 10000ms. Check the backend terminal logs: it will show resolveRepo 404 errors immediately, but if you wait several minutes, you will eventually see Worker exited [code: 0, success: true] proving the background process never actually stopped. ### Environment OS: Windows 11 Node: v24.14.0 Browser: Chrome / Edge ### Logs / screenshots

title: fix: resolve false 404 errors and stale repo context during multi-repo switching on Windows
body:
## Fixes

Closes #632

---

## Summary

This PR resolves a cluster of race conditions and context-management bugs that caused false 404 errors, incorrect AI responses, missing file content, and stale URL state during multi-repo switching — all traced back to the same root architectural gap: the frontend did not properly coordinate with the backend's async analysis lifecycle, and the active repository context was never reliably propagated through the app.

---

## Changes

### Backend — gitnexus/src/server/api.ts

**esolveRepo — Smart Hold Queue + Path Normalization**
- Accepts both short repo names (	odo.txt-cli) and full Windows paths (C:\Users\...\todo.txt-cli) by normalizing to path.basename() before registry lookup — prevents an infinite 404 retry loop on Windows
- When a repo is not yet in the registry, polls JobManager for an active clone/analysis job and holds the HTTP connection open (up to 5 minutes) until the job completes — eliminates the false 404 during first-time analysis
- Adds a deep  ackend.init() re-sync fallback to handle Windows file-system race conditions after a clone completes

### Frontend — gitnexus-web/src/services/backend-client.ts

** etchRepoInfo — Extended Timeout**
- Raises the per-request timeout from the global 10,000ms default to 300,000ms for the repo resolution endpoint, matching the backend's 5-minute hold window

### Frontend — gitnexus-web/src/App.tsx

**handleServerConnect — Windows Path Fix + State Persistence**
- Prefers esult.repoInfo.name (already the short name) as the project name, and falls back to normalizing Windows \ paths before splitting — prevents the full path from becoming the project name on Windows
- Stores the active project in ?project= URL param on successful connection for bookmarkability and refresh-resilience

**useAppState retry loop**
- 3-attempt retry loop in switchRepo re-enqueues the backend hold queue if a 404 is encountered, allowing seamless recovery from page refreshes during active analysis

### Frontend — gitnexus-web/src/hooks/useAppState.tsx

**initializeAgent — Repo Context Sync**
- Syncs epoRef.current from overrideProjectName before building the agent context — previously handleServerConnect called initializeAgent(projectName) but never set epoRef, causing every agent query to target epos[0] regardless of which repo was open

**switchRepo — Full Context Reset**
- Nulls ^GgentRef.current, clears chat history, and re-initializes the agent on every repo switch — prevents the AI from retaining context from a previously opened repo
- Uses pNameStr (the clicked repo name) instead of connectedRepo.name for the ?project= URL param — fixes URL always showing the first repo
- Normalizes Windows backslash paths when extracting the short project name from epoPath
- Adds BackendError to imports for typed 404 detection in retry logic

### Frontend — gitnexus-web/src/components/CodeReferencesPanel.tsx

**eadFile — Active Repo Targeting**
- Passes projectName as the epo param in eadFile calls — previously omitted, causing the file viewer to always load content from the first indexed repo regardless of which repo was selected

---

## Testing

- Analyzed a large fresh repository (claude-code) and confirmed the frontend waits over 3 minutes without disconnecting
- Switched between 6 different repos; verified file tree, code inspector, and AI assistant all update correctly to each repo's context
- Simulated F5 refresh during active analysis; confirmed the UI re-joins the hold queue and auto-connects on completion
- Verified on Windows 11, Node v24.14.0, Chrome/Edge

title: Bug: AI assistant always describes the first indexed repo regardless of which repo is open
body:
## Area

gitnexus-web (hooks / agent / context-builder)

## Summary

When connecting to a GitNexus server, the AI assistant always describes the **first registered repository** regardless of which repo the user opened. Switching repos updates the file tree correctly but the AI retains the original repo's context.

## Root Cause

`initializeAgent` reads `repoRef.current` to scope all graph queries. However, `handleServerConnect` in `App.tsx` calls `initializeAgent(projectName)` without ever setting `repoRef.current`. On first connection it is `undefined`, so every `backendRunQuery(cypher, repo)` call omits the repo param and the backend defaults to `repos[0]`.

## Expected Behavior

The AI answers questions about the repository the user is currently viewing. Switching repos produces a fresh agent context scoped to the new repo.

## Actual Behavior

- `repoRef.current` is `undefined` after first connection
- All graph queries (`buildCodebaseContext`, hotspots, folder tree) run against `repos[0]`
- AI system prompt contains wrong repo's data
- Chat answers describe the wrong repo regardless of switching

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Start GitNexus with 2+ indexed repositories
2. Connect to any repo **other than** the first one in the list
3. Ask the AI "What does this project do?"
4. Observe: the AI describes the first indexed repo, not the one you opened

title: Bug: URL ?project= param stays on first repo after switching — breaks F5 refresh and bookmarking
body:
## Area

gitnexus-web (hooks / App.tsx / URL state)

## Summary

After switching to a different repository via the sidebar dropdown, the browser URL `?project=` parameter always shows the **first connected repo's name** rather than the currently active repo. This breaks bookmarkability and causes wrong repo to auto-connect on F5 refresh.

## Root Cause

In `switchRepo` inside `useAppState.tsx`, the URL was updated using `connectedRepo.name` — a value returned from `result.repoInfo` by the backend. On Windows, this value can be a full path like `C:\Users\...\todo.txt-cli` instead of the short name `todo.txt-cli`. Additionally, `connectedRepo.name` could reflect the previously connected repo due to React state batching timing.

The fix is to use `pNameStr` — the name explicitly derived from what the user clicked — for the URL parameter.

## Expected Behavior

After switching repos, the URL updates to `?project=<new-repo-name>` immediately. Pressing F5 reconnects to the correct repo.

## Actual Behavior

- User switches from `oh-my-codex` to `flash-pkg`
- URL remains `?project=oh-my-codex` (or shows a full Windows path)
- Pressing F5 reconnects to `oh-my-codex` instead of `flash-pkg`

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Open GitNexus with 2+ indexed repositories
2. Connect to the first repo — URL shows `?project=repo-a`
3. Switch to a second repo via the sidebar
4. Observe: URL still shows `?project=repo-a`

fix(pipeline): avoid spread push for large deferred call batches
body:
## Summary

This PR replaces spread-based append for deferred worker calls with iterative append in the ingestion pipeline.  
The change preserves behavior/order while avoiding argument-list overflow when a chunk produces a very large call array.

## Motivation / context

`Array.prototype.push(...largeArray)` can fail with a `RangeError` in high-volume scenarios due to argument-list limits.  
This fix hardens chunked parsing/call-resolution flow against large repositories and high call density inputs.

## Areas touched

- [x] `gitnexus/` (CLI / core / MCP server)
- [ ] `gitnexus-web/` (Vite / React UI)
- [ ] `.github/` (workflows, actions)
- [ ] `eval/` or other tooling
- [ ] Docs / agent config only (`AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `.cursor/`, `llms.txt`, etc.)

## Scope & constraints

**In scope**

- Replace `deferredWorkerCalls.push(...chunkWorkerData.calls)` with iterative append in `runChunkedParseAndResolve`.
- Keep aggregation semantics unchanged (same element order, same downstream behavior).

**Explicitly out of scope / not done here**

- No broad refactor of other spread-based `push(...arr)` usages in the file/codebase.
- No changes to ingestion algorithm, chunking strategy, or resolver logic.
- No UI/docs/workflow updates.

## Implementation notes

- Previous:
  - `deferredWorkerCalls.push(...chunkWorkerData.calls)`
- New:
  - Iterate and `push` one item at a time.
- Rationale: iterative append avoids large variadic argument expansion while maintaining identical output ordering.

## Testing & verification

- [x] `cd gitnexus && npm test`
- [x] `cd gitnexus && npm run test:integration`
- [x] `cd gitnexus && npx tsc --noEmit`
- [x] `cd gitnexus-web && npm test` 
- [x] `cd gitnexus-web && npx tsc -b --noEmit`
- [x] Manual / Playwright E2E

Additional focused verification:

- [x] `cd gitnexus && npx vitest run test/integration/pipeline.test.ts`  
  Result: `1 file passed, 7 tests passed`.

## Risk & rollout

- Risk level: low.
- Change is local to deferred call aggregation and does not alter functional flow.
- No migration needed.
- No breaking API changes.
- Standard rollout; monitor ingestion on large repos for absence of overflow regressions.

## Checklist

- [x] PR body meets repo minimum length (workflow may label short descriptions)
- [x] If `AGENTS.md` / overlays changed: headers, scope block, and changelog updated per project conventions *(not applicable; no such files changed)*
- [x] No secrets, tokens, or machine-specific paths committed

## Summary

Large Unreal C++ projects were hitting a 30-second worker pool timeout during `gitnexus analyze`, causing the entire parallel parse phase to abort and fall back to slow sequential parsing (observed: 24% after 666s on a project with 264-file batches).

The root cause is that Unreal C++ headers with dense `UCLASS`/`UFUNCTION`/`UPROPERTY` macros are legitimately slow to parse with tree-sitter (~150–400ms each), far exceeding the hard-coded 30s limit designed for pathological JS minification.

## Changes

Three tuning knobs, all optional, under a new `analyze` block in `.gitnexus-unreal.json` (or the local `.gitnexus/unreal/config.json` override):

```json
{
  "analyze": {
    "worker_sub_batch_size": 300,
    "worker_timeout_ms": 120000,
    "max_file_size_kb": 256
  }
}
```

| Field | Default | Recommended (large UE) | Effect |
|---|---|---|---|
| `worker_sub_batch_size` | 1500 | 300 | Files per `postMessage` — smaller batches reduce peak memory |
| `worker_timeout_ms` | 30000 | 120000 | Per-sub-batch timeout before sequential fallback |
| `max_file_size_kb` | 512 | 256 | File size ceiling — drops more generated headers before parse |

Values flow from `UnrealConfig.analyze` → `PipelineOptions` → `createWorkerPool` + `walkRepositoryPaths`. Non-Unreal repos are unaffected (the config load is try/catch and silently skipped).

title: feat: METHOD_IMPLEMENTS edges, overload disambiguation, MethodExtractor unification (#574)
body:
## Summary

This PR started as METHOD_IMPLEMENTS edge support and grew into a comprehensive MethodExtractor unification — making `provider.methodExtractor` the single source of truth for all method metadata extraction across GitNexus's 12 supported languages.

**79 files changed, +3450/−1576 across 15 commits.**

## What's New

### 1. METHOD_IMPLEMENTS edges
- New `METHOD_IMPLEMENTS` relationship: `ConcreteMethod → InterfaceMethod`
- BFS ancestor walking with diamond deduplication
- `parameterTypesMatch` confidence tiering (1.0 exact, 0.7 lenient)
- Dart `implements Class` label gate (prevents class-body method inheritance)
- `findInheritedMethod` for EXTENDS + IMPLEMENTS chain walking (Java 8+ default methods)
- IMPLEMENTS BFS ambiguity detection (returns null when multiple interfaces provide same default method)

### 2. OVERRIDES → METHOD_OVERRIDES rename
- Backward-compatible dual-read via `flatMap` expansion in both `impact()` and `impactByUid()`
- Legacy `OVERRIDES` alias kept in `REL_TYPES` until future major version
- `MIGRATION.md` documents the rename

### 3. Overload disambiguation via `#<paramCount>` arity suffix
- Method/Constructor node IDs now include `#<paramCount>`: `Method:file:Class.method#2`
- Overloaded methods with different parameter counts produce distinct graph nodes
- `findEnclosingFunctionId` in both worker and sequential paths generates matching IDs
- `extractFuncNameFromSourceId` strips `#<arity>` for receiver-type index lookups
- Same-arity overloads (different types, same count) remain collapsed — documented as known limitation

### 4. MethodExtractor unification (major refactor)
Eliminated 3 legacy AST heuristics from `ast-helpers.ts`, making the MethodExtractor the sole source of method metadata:

| Removed | Lines | Replacement |
|---------|-------|-------------|
| `extractMethodSignature` | 270 | `provider.methodExtractor` (parameterCount, parameterTypes, returnType) |
| `extractFunctionName` | 250 | `provider.methodExtractor.extractFunctionName` (per-language hook) |
| `countMethodParameters` | 90 | `getMethodInfo` / `extractFromNode` based arity |
| `TypeConfig.extractReturnType` post-hoc fallback | 130 | Doc-comment parsing moved INTO MethodExtractor configs (PHPDoc, YARD, JSDoc) |

**ast-helpers.ts: 897 → ~380 lines (−58%)**. Now contains only shared constants and generic traversal helpers — zero language-specific extraction logic.

### 5. Post-extraction cleanup
- Deduplicated `genericFuncName` (was triplicated in 3 files) → single export in ast-helpers.ts
- Deduplicated `inferFunctionLabel` + backing Sets (was in 2 files) → single export
- Extracted `buildMethodProps` to shared `method-props.ts` (was divergent between sequential/worker paths)
- Removed dead `TypeConfig.extractReturnType` interface field + 3 dead implementations
- Moved `isCppInsideClassOrStruct` and `isKotlinClassMethod` to their language provider files
- Fixed `resolveMethodReturnType` to handle class names as receivers (latent bug surfaced by ID change)
- Added `FUNCTION_NODE_TYPES` drift-prevention documentation

## Per-language MethodExtractor enhancements

| Language | What was added |
|----------|---------------|
| PHP | PHPDoc `@return` extraction, `function_definition` in methodNodeTypes |
| Ruby | YARD `@return [Type]` extraction |
| TypeScript/JS | JSDoc `@returns {Type}` extraction, `function_declaration`/`function_signature` in methodNodeTypes |
| C# | `local_function_statement` in methodNodeTypes |
| C/C++ | `extractFunctionName` hook (declarator unwrapping) |
| Swift | `extractFunctionName` hook (init/deinit) |
| Rust | `extractFunctionName` hook (impl_item) |

## Test coverage

- **23 new overload dispatch integration tests** across Java, C#, Kotlin, TypeScript, Swift
- **51+ MRO unit tests** including METHOD_IMPLEMENTS confidence tiering, diamond deduplication, IMPLEMENTS BFS ambiguity
- **Invariant tests**: variadic method sourceId validity, impactByUid legacy OVERRIDES dual-read
- Integration tests for METHOD_IMPLEMENTS across 8 languages (Java, C#, Kotlin, TS, Dart, Rust, Swift, PHP)

## Known limitations

- **Same-arity overloads** (same param count, different types) still share a node ID — tracked in #651
- **Ruby singleton_class** handling differs between sequential and worker paths — tracked in #652

## Files changed summary

| Category | Count |
|----------|-------|
| Production code | 35 files |
| Test files | 24 files |
| Test fixtures | 15 files (5 new fixture directories) |
| Documentation | 5 files |

## How to test

```bash
cd gitnexus
npx tsc --noEmit           # Type check
npx vitest run test/unit/  # 2862 unit tests
npx vitest run test/integration/  # 2182+ integration tests
```

title: fix(mcp): unify stdout silencing to prevent embedder/pool-adapter conflicts
body:
## Summary
- Export `silenceStdout()`/`restoreStdout()` from pool-adapter so all modules use the same ref-counted mechanism
- Embedder now uses centralized silencing instead of independent stdout patching
- Export `realStderrWrite` for safe stderr restore in embedder
- Added 6 unit tests including a concurrent-usage simulation

## Root Cause
The embedder and pool-adapter independently patched `process.stdout.write`. When both ran concurrently (e.g. a DB query during model load), the embedder could capture a stale no-op reference while pool-adapter had stdout silenced. On restore, it put back the no-op instead of the real write function, permanently breaking stdout and corrupting the MCP JSON-RPC stream.

**Note:** This fixes the Node-level race condition between pool-adapter and embedder. If KuzuDB's native C++ addon writes directly to fd 1 (bypassing Node's `process.stdout.write`), that would require fd-level redirection or a different transport — a separate issue.

## Changed Files
- `gitnexus/src/core/lbug/pool-adapter.ts` — export `silenceStdout`, `restoreStdout`, `realStderrWrite`
- `gitnexus/src/mcp/core/embedder.ts` — use centralized silencing instead of independent patching

title: fix(server): return clean CORS rejection instead of 500 error
body:
## Summary
- Changed CORS rejection from `callback(new Error(...))` to `callback(null, false)` — no more 500 errors for disallowed origins
- **Changed serve default host from `127.0.0.1` to `::` (dual-stack)** — fixes the actual CORS errors users see when `localhost` resolves to `::1` (IPv6)

## Root Cause
Two separate issues combined to create the CORS problem:

1. **500 on rejected origins:** The CORS middleware threw `new Error('Not allowed by CORS')`, which crashed into Express's default error handler returning 500 instead of a clean CORS block.

2. **IPv6 binding (the real issue for most users):** `gitnexus serve` bound to `127.0.0.1` only. On systems where `localhost` resolves to `::1` (common on Linux with IPv6), the server was unreachable via `localhost`. The browser's request never reached the server, so no CORS headers came back — the browser reported a CORS error even though the allowlist was correct.

## Changed Files
- `gitnexus/src/server/api.ts` — CORS callback fix + display `localhost` instead of `::` in console
- `gitnexus/src/cli/serve.ts` — default host changed from `127.0.0.1` to `::` (dual-stack)

title: feat: Multi-repository unified knowledge graph
body:
## Summary

Adds multi-repository support to GitNexus — view combined knowledge graphs across repos and see how they connect at the code level.

### Backend: Code-Level Dependency Detection

- New `CodeDepExtractor` that detects when repo B imports symbols from repo A's npm package
- Builds on the existing group contract pipeline using the `lib` contract type and `shared_libs` detection flag
- Three new extractors: `manifest-reader.ts` (reads package.json for name + deps), `import-scanner.ts` (scans ES/CJS imports matching sibling packages), `code-dep-extractor.ts` (orchestrates provider/consumer contract extraction)
- Auto-discovers package mappings when `config.packages` is empty by reading each repo's package.json
- Matched contracts produce `CrossLink` records with `type: 'lib'` via the existing `runExactMatch` pipeline

### CLI Commands

- `gitnexus group auto-discover [directory]` — scans a parent directory for all indexed repos and creates a group with code-level dependency detection
- `gitnexus group repos <paths...>` — creates a group from explicitly specified repo paths
- `gitnexus group graph <name> <symbol>` — traverses the cross-repo knowledge graph for a symbol, returns local context plus all cross-repo connections via CrossLinks
- Supports `--name`, `--force`, `--skip-sync`, `--depth`, `--direction`, `--json` options

### MCP Tools

- `group_discover` — auto-discover repos and create a group programmatically
- `group_graph` — cross-repo symbol traversal with configurable depth and direction

### Server API

- `GET /api/groups` — list configured groups
- `GET /api/group-graph?group=NAME` — merged graph with namespaced node IDs (`repoName::nodeId`) and synthetic `CROSS_REPO_IMPORT` edges from contracts.json
- `GET /api/group-status?group=NAME` — staleness info per repo in the group

### Web UI

- **Landing page**: Repos/Groups tab bar. Groups tab shows group cards with repo count and last sync time. Repos tab unchanged.
- **Graph visualization**: File/Folder nodes colored by repo. Hover tooltip shows repo name. `CROSS_REPO_IMPORT` edges rendered in amber.
- **Repo legend** (top-left): Clickable toggle dots per repo — amber = highlighted (default), grey = dimmed. Deselected repos' nodes and edges dim to ~12% opacity and render behind highlighted ones.
- **File tree sidebar**: In group mode, files grouped under collapsible repo headers with amber dots and bold labels.
- **Single-repo mode**: All existing behavior completely unchanged.

### How to use

\`\`\`bash
# Index repos individually
cd repo1 && gitnexus analyze
cd ../repo2 && gitnexus analyze

# Create a group (pick one)
gitnexus group auto-discover          # scans current dir
gitnexus group repos /path/repo1 /path/repo2 --name my-workspace

# View in web UI
gitnexus serve
# Open browser → Groups tab → select group → combined graph loads
# Click repo dots in legend to highlight/dim each repo's point cloud

# CLI exploration
gitnexus group contracts my-workspace --type lib
gitnexus group graph my-workspace "functionName" --repo repo1
\`\`\`

### Test plan

- [ ] 5177 backend tests pass (`cd gitnexus && npm test`)
- [ ] 218 web tests pass (`cd gitnexus-web && npm test`)
- [ ] TypeScript clean in both packages
- [ ] Manual: index 2 repos → create group → serve → web UI Groups tab → combined graph → repo legend toggles → file tree grouping

title: fix(c): detect function calls inside cast expressions
body:
## Summary

- **Add tree-sitter query patterns for `call_expression` nested inside `cast_expression`** — Ghidra-decompiled C code frequently produces `(float)func(args)`, `(longlong)func(args)`, `(char)func(args)` patterns where the type cast wraps the function call
- **Without this fix, ~30% of C function calls are missed** — the existing C queries only match top-level `call_expression` nodes, not those wrapped in `cast_expression`

Two new patterns added to `C_QUERIES` in `tree-sitter-queries.ts`:
```
(cast_expression value: (call_expression function: (identifier) @call.name)) @call
(cast_expression value: (call_expression function: (field_expression field: (field_identifier) @call.name))) @call
```

**Note:** `CPP_QUERIES` has the same gap for C-style casts in C++ code — out of scope for this PR, can be addressed in a follow-up.

- [x] Query compilation smoke test (`query-compilation.test.ts`) — 12/12 pass, confirms new patterns compile against tree-sitter C grammar
