title: CLI surface drift: detect_changes exists in backend/MCP but not as a direct command
body:
## Summary

`gitnexus 1.6.1` still implements `detect_changes` in the local backend / MCP layers, but the direct CLI does not expose a `detect-changes` command.

## Evidence

Installed package contents show:

- `dist/mcp/local/local-backend.js` implements `detectChanges(...)`
- `dist/mcp/tools.js` still declares `detect_changes`
- `dist/cli/ai-context.js` and packaged skills still instruct agents to run `gitnexus_detect_changes()`
- `gitnexus --help` does **not** list `detect-changes`

So the documented contract and the user-facing CLI surface drifted apart.

## Expected

One of these needs to happen:

1. expose a direct CLI command, e.g.
   - `gitnexus detect-changes`
   - alias `gitnexus detect_changes`
2. or stop generating docs/skills/instructions that require the command

## Why this matters

Agent workflows that correctly follow the generated GitNexus instructions fail repeatedly on fresh installs because the command surface is missing even though the implementation exists.

## Temporary local fix

I verified that adding a direct CLI bridge to the existing backend implementation restores the command and works correctly on a live repo.

title: ai-context: CLAUDE.md generated block duplicates content already in skill files
body:
## Summary

The block that `npx gitnexus analyze` injects into a project's `CLAUDE.md` (between `<!-- gitnexus:start -->` and `<!-- gitnexus:end -->`) contains three sections that are already documented inside the installed skill files at `.claude/skills/gitnexus/*/SKILL.md`:

- **Tools Quick Reference** table — same content as `gitnexus-guide/SKILL.md`'s tools table
- **Impact Risk Levels** table — same content as `gitnexus-impact-analysis/SKILL.md`
- **Self-Check Before Finishing** — same checklist as `gitnexus-refactoring/SKILL.md` and the "Never Do" list

Because both the CLAUDE.md block and the skill files are always loaded into context in Claude Code, this is duplicated tokens on every turn of every conversation in the repo.

## Where

`gitnexus/src/cli/ai-context.ts` — `generateGitNexusContent()` (lines ~89–190). The generated block is ~100 lines; ~40 of those lines restate content the skill files already contain.

## Context

While auditing a downstream project's `.claude/` configuration I noticed the GitNexus section is the single largest chunk of CLAUDE.md, and most of it is reference material that the agent will already see once it reads the relevant skill file. The skill files are the right home for the detailed tables — CLAUDE.md only needs to tell the model *which skill to read when*.

## Suggested shape

Keep in the generated CLAUDE.md block:
- The one-line index freshness warning
- The "Always Do" imperative rules (MUST run impact, MUST run detect_changes)
- The "Never Do" list
- The **skills routing table** at the bottom (the most load-bearing part — it's what tells the model which skill file to read)
- Resources list (the URI patterns are unique to the project name)

Move out of the block (already in skill files, no need to duplicate):
- Tools Quick Reference table → covered by `gitnexus-guide/SKILL.md`
- Impact Risk Levels table → covered by `gitnexus-impact-analysis/SKILL.md`
- Self-Check Before Finishing → covered by `gitnexus-refactoring/SKILL.md`
- "When Debugging" / "When Refactoring" step lists → covered by `gitnexus-debugging/SKILL.md` and `gitnexus-refactoring/SKILL.md`
- Keeping the Index Fresh detail paragraph → the single-line warning at the top plus `gitnexus-cli/SKILL.md` is enough

Rough estimate: the generated block could drop from ~100 lines to ~35 without losing any information, since everything trimmed is still reachable by reading the skill the routing table points to.

## Why it matters

- Lower token cost per turn on every Claude Code session in the repo
- Skill files become the single source of truth for the details — fewer places to keep in sync when the API evolves
- CLAUDE.md is easier to read for humans

Happy to open a PR if you agree with the direction.

---

Reported via an audit of a consuming project's `.claude/` config. CLAUDE.md had 369 lines total; ~100 of those were the gitnexus block and a significant fraction was reference material already in the skill files.

title: Tree-sitter 0.25 upgrade readiness
body:
# Tree-sitter 0.25 upgrade readiness


`tree-sitter@0.21.x` (ABI 13–14) → target `tree-sitter@0.25.0` (ABI 13–15).

## TL;DR

**Blocked** — 10 grammars are not yet 0.25-compatible. Upstream movement: yes — 2 grammars have unreleased fixes on main.

- 5/15 npm-installed grammars already accept tree-sitter@0.25.0
- 2 intentionally pinned (see below)
- 2 waiting on an upstream npm release
- 5 blocked on upstream (no fix even on main)
- 1 could not be checked (npm registry unreachable)
- **2 bump candidate(s) you can take TODAY** (npm-latest is newer than the pin AND its peer dep accepts our current runtime)

## What you can do today

These pins lag npm latest and the latest version's peer dep already accepts our current `tree-sitter@0.21.x` runtime. Bumping is independent of the 0.25 upgrade and should be a quick PR.

- `tree-sitter-dart`: `—` → `1.0.0` (peer `none`)
- `tree-sitter-kotlin`: `—` → `0.3.8` (peer `^0.21.0`)

## Disposition

### Ready for 0.25 (5)

These grammars' npm-latest peer dep already accepts the target runtime. No action needed for the upgrade.

- `tree-sitter-c-sharp` — pinned `0.23.1`, npm latest `0.23.5`
- `tree-sitter-dart` — pinned `—`, npm latest `1.0.0`  _(also a bump candidate — see above)_
- `tree-sitter-go` — pinned `^0.23.0`, npm latest `0.25.0`
- `tree-sitter-javascript` — pinned `^0.23.0`, npm latest `0.25.0`
- `tree-sitter-python` — pinned `0.23.4`, npm latest `0.25.0`

### Intentionally pinned (2)

Deliberately held below npm latest. These are **not** drift — each entry lists the issue motivating the pin and the condition for unpinning.

body:
Bumps [@huggingface/transformers](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers.js) from 3.8.1 to 4.1.0.
Release notes

Sourced from @​huggingface/transformers's releases.

4.0.0

🚀 Transformers.js v4

We're excited to announce that Transformers.js v4 is now available on NPM! After a year of development (we started in March 2025 🤯), we're finally ready for you to use it.

npm i @huggingface/transformers

Links: YouTube Video, Blog Post, Demo Collection

New WebGPU backend

The biggest change is undoubtedly the adoption of a new WebGPU Runtime, completely rewritten in C++. We've worked closely with the ONNX Runtime team to thoroughly test this runtime across our ~200 supported model architectures, as well as many new v4-exclusive architectures.

In addition to better operator support (for performance, accuracy, and coverage), this new WebGPU runtime allows the same transformers.js code to be used across a wide variety of JavaScript environments, including browsers, server-side runtimes, and desktop applications. That's right, you can now run WebGPU-accelerated models directly in Node, Bun, and Deno!

We've proven that it's possible to run state-of-the-art AI models 100% locally in the browser, and now we're focused on performance: making these models run as fast as possible, even in resource-constrained environments. This required completely rethinking our export strategy, especially for large language models. We achieve this by re-implementing new models operation by operation, leveraging specialized ONNX Runtime Contrib Operators like com.microsoft.GroupQueryAttention, com.microsoft.MatMulNBits, or com.microsoft.QMoE to maximize performance.

For example, adopting the com.microsoft.MultiHeadAttention operator, we were able to achieve a ~4x speedup for BERT-based embedding models.

  • ONNX Runtime improvements by @​xenova in huggingface/transformers.js#1306
  • Transformers.js V4: Native WebGPU EP, repo restructuring, and more! by @​xenova in huggingface/transformers.js#1382

New models

Thanks to our new export strategy and ONNX Runtime's expanding support for custom operators, we've been able to add many new models and architectures to Transformers.js v4. These include popular models like GPT-OSS, Chatterbox, GraniteMoeHybrid, LFM2-MoE, HunYuanDenseV1, Apertus, Olmo3, FalconH1, and Youtu-LLM. Many of these required us to implement support for advanced architectural patterns, including Mamba (state-space models), Multi-head Latent Attention (MLA), and Mixture of Experts (MoE). Perhaps most importantly, these models are all compatible with WebGPU, allowing users to run them directly in the browser or server-side JavaScript environments with hardware acceleration. We've released several Transformers.js v4 demos so far... and we'll continue to release more!

Additionally, we've added support for larger models exceeding 8B parameters. In our tests, we've been able to run GPT-OSS 20B (q4f16) at ~60 tokens per second on an M4 Pro Max.

title: feat(ingestion): language-agnostic call extractor with config+factory pattern
body:
## Summary

The ingestion pipeline's call extraction is currently inline in `parse-worker.ts` (~225 lines) with ad-hoc language switches via `call-sites/extract-language-call-site.ts` (only Java covered). This should follow the same config+factory architecture as method and field extractors.

## Architecture Direction

The method and field extractors established a proven language-agnostic pattern in the ingestion pipeline:

1. **Types file** defines domain interfaces (`CallExtractionConfig`, `CallExtractor`, `ExtractedCallSite`)
2. **Generic factory** (`createCallExtractor(config)`) converts a declarative config into a runtime extractor
3. **Per-language configs** in `call-extractors/configs/<lang>.ts` specify AST node types and extraction hooks
4. **Language provider wiring** adds `callExtractor` to `LanguageProvider` interface
5. **Parse worker consumption** replaces inline logic with `provider.callExtractor.extract()`

The call extractor should follow this exact pattern, absorbing:
- The inline call extraction logic in `parse-worker.ts` (lines ~1657-1883)
- The `call-sites/extract-language-call-site.ts` switch statement
- The `call-sites/java.ts` method reference parsing (becomes part of JVM call config)

## Key Technical Decisions

- **Call extractor replaces inline parse-worker logic**: The ~225 lines of call extraction in parse-worker.ts move into `CallExtractionConfig` hooks. The parse worker calls `provider.callExtractor.extract()` instead of inline `inferCallForm`/`extractReceiverName`. Shared utilities in `call-analysis.ts` remain -- configs call them.
- **`CallExtractionConfig` absorbs `call-sites/` directory**: The `extractParsedCallSite` switch statement and `java.ts` become the Java call config. The `call-sites/` directory is removed after migration.
- **Shared call utilities stay in `utils/call-analysis.ts`**: `inferCallForm`, `extractReceiverName`, `countCallArguments`, `extractMixedChain`, `extractCallArgTypes` are AST utilities used by configs, not owned by any single language.
- **`CallExtractionConfig` mirrors method/field pattern**: `language`, node type sets, extraction hooks (`extractCallName`, `extractCallForm`, `extractReceiverName`, `isBuiltIn`, `extractLanguageCallSite`)

title: feat(ingestion): language-agnostic variable extractor with config+factory pattern
body:
## Summary

`Const`, `Static`, and `Variable` NodeLabels exist in the graph schema but carry no structured metadata. Labels are inferred from tree-sitter capture tags (`@definition.const`, `@definition.static`) in `ast-helpers.ts`, but no type, visibility, mutability, or scope information is extracted. A variable extractor following the method/field config+factory pattern would fill this gap.

## Architecture Direction

Following the same language-agnostic pattern as method and field extractors:

1. **Types file** defines domain interfaces (`VariableExtractionConfig`, `VariableExtractor`, `VariableInfo`)
2. **Generic factory** (`createVariableExtractor(config)`) converts a declarative config into a runtime extractor
3. **Per-language configs** in `variable-extractors/configs/<lang>.ts` specify AST node types and extraction hooks
4. **Language provider wiring** adds `variableExtractor` to `LanguageProvider` interface
5. **Parse worker consumption** enriches `Const`/`Static`/`Variable` nodes with structured metadata

## Key Technical Decisions

- **Variable extractor is new**: No existing extractor to refactor. Adds `VariableExtractionConfig` for extracting metadata from `@definition.const`, `@definition.static`, and variable declaration nodes.
- **Reuses `FieldVisibility`** from `field-types.ts` for visibility levels (no new type needed).
- **Scope boundary with field extractors**: Variable extractors handle module/file-scoped declarations. Field extractors (already implemented) handle class-scoped properties. No overlap.
- **Existing label inference preserved**: Label detection in `ast-helpers.ts` remains for backward compatibility. Variable extractor adds metadata, doesn't replace label detection.

## Implementation Units

### Unit 1: Variable extraction types and factory

**Goal:** Define `VariableExtractionConfig` interface and `createVariableExtractor()` factory

**Files:**
- Create: `gitnexus/src/core/ingestion/variable-types.ts`
- Create: `gitnexus/src/core/ingestion/variable-extractors/generic.ts`
- Modify: `gitnexus/src/core/ingestion/language-provider.ts`
- Test: `gitnexus/test/unit/variable-extraction.test.ts`

**Approach:**
- `VariableInfo`: `name`, `type` (string | null), `visibility` (reuse `FieldVisibility`), `isConst` (boolean), `isStatic` (boolean), `isMutable` (boolean), `scope` ('module' | 'file' | 'block'), `sourceFile`, `line`
- `VariableExtractionConfig`: `language`, `constNodeTypes[]`, `staticNodeTypes[]`, `variableNodeTypes[]`, `extractName(node)`, `extractType(node)`, `extractVisibility(node)`, `isConst(node)`, `isStatic(node)`, `isMutable(node)`
- `VariableExtractor` interface: `extract(node, context): VariableInfo | null`, `isVariableDeclaration(node): boolean`
- Factory converts node type arrays to Sets at construction time

**Patterns to follow:**
- `gitnexus/src/core/ingestion/field-types.ts` for types structure
- `gitnexus/src/core/ingestion/field-extractors/generic.ts` for factory pattern

### Unit 2: Per-language variable configs

**Goal:** Create variable extraction configs for all 16 tree-sitter languages

**Files:**
- Create: `gitnexus/src/core/ingestion/variable-extractors/configs/typescript-javascript.ts`
- Create: `gitnexus/src/core/ingestion/variable-extractors/configs/jvm.ts`
- Create: `gitnexus/src/core/ingestion/variable-extractors/configs/csharp.ts`
- Create: `gitnexus/src/core/ingestion/variable-extractors/configs/python.ts`
- Create: `gitnexus/src/core/ingestion/variable-extractors/configs/ruby.ts`
- Create: `gitnexus/src/core/ingestion/variable-extractors/configs/go.ts`
- Create: `gitnexus/src/core/ingestion/variable-extractors/configs/rust.ts`
- Create: `gitnexus/src/core/ingestion/variable-extractors/configs/c-cpp.ts`
- Create: `gitnexus/src/core/ingestion/variable-extractors/configs/php.ts`
- Create: `gitnexus/src/core/ingestion/variable-extractors/configs/dart.ts`
- Create: `gitnexus/src/core/ingestion/variable-extractors/configs/swift.ts`

**Approach:**
- TypeScript/JavaScript: `const`/`let`/`var` declarations at module scope; `export const` -> public visibility
- Java/Kotlin: top-level Kotlin `val`/`var` and Java `static` imports (class-scoped `static final` already covered by field extractor)
- Python: module-level assignments, `UPPER_CASE` convention for constants
- Go: `var`/`const` declarations at package scope
- Rust: `const`/`static`/`let` at module scope
- C/C++: global/namespace-scoped variable declarations, `const`/`constexpr`
- Each config uses `field-extractors/configs/helpers.ts` for visibility/modifier detection

### Unit 3: Wire variable extractor into parse worker

**Goal:** Consume `provider.variableExtractor` in parse-worker.ts to enrich variable/const/static nodes with metadata

**Files:**
- Modify: `gitnexus/src/core/ingestion/workers/parse-worker.ts`
- Modify: all 16 language provider files in `gitnexus/src/core/ingestion/languages/`

**Approach:**
- When the definition capture resolves to `Const`, `Static`, or `Variable` label, check `provider.variableExtractor`
- If available, call `.extract(node, context)` and enrich `ParsedNode.properties` with type, visibility, mutability metadata
- Existing label inference in `ast-helpers.ts` remains for backward compatibility
- Each language provider wires `variableExtractor: createVariableExtractor(<lang>VariableConfig)`

## Scope Boundary: Variables vs Fields

Variable extractors handle **module/file-scoped** declarations:
- TypeScript/JavaScript: `const`, `let`, `var` at module scope
- Python: module-level assignments, `UPPER_CASE` constants
- Go: `var`/`const` at package scope
- Rust: `const`/`static`/`let` at module scope
- C/C++: global/namespace-scoped declarations

Field extractors (already implemented) handle **class-scoped** properties. There is no overlap.

## What Does NOT Change

- Label inference in `ast-helpers.ts` (existing `Const`/`Static`/`Variable` labels preserved)
- Type environment (`type-env.ts`) assignment tracking
- Graph schema (`NodeLabel` already has `Variable`, `Const`, `Static`)
- Field extractors (class-scoped properties)

### Deferred to Separate Tasks

- Variable type inference from initializer expressions: future iteration
- Cross-file variable resolution: future iteration

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `VariableExtractionConfig` + `createVariableExtractor()` factory exists
- [ ] Per-language configs exist for all 16 tree-sitter languages
- [ ] `variableExtractor` field on `LanguageProvider` interface
- [ ] Parse worker enriches variable/const/static nodes with structured metadata
- [ ] All existing tests pass (no regression)
- [ ] New unit tests for variable extraction configs

## References

- Pattern to follow: `field-extractors/generic.ts`, `field-extractors/configs/`
- Reuse: `field-extractors/configs/helpers.ts` for shared AST helpers
- Prior art: `docs/plans/2026-03-28-feat-method-extractor-abstraction-plan.md`

The call extractor (#874), variable extractor (#875), and class config migration (#876) complete this convergence. ## What Changes

title: refactor(SM-20): wire SemanticModel as first-class resolution input
body:
## Summary

PR #786 extracted TypeRegistry, MethodRegistry, and FieldRegistry into a standalone `model/` module behind a SemanticModel interface. However, no consumer queries the model directly -- all 37 internal call sites still route through SymbolTable.lookup* delegate wrappers. This issue completes Phase 6 of the fuzzy-lookup elimination roadmap by wiring SemanticModel as the direct resolution input.

## Context: The Fuzzy-Lookup Elimination Roadmap

This is the final phase of a 6-phase architectural transformation:

| Phase | Status | What |
|-------|--------|------|
| Phase 1 | Done | TypeRegistry + lookupClassByName |
| Phase 2 | Done (PR #739) | HeritageMap built after all chunks complete |
| Phase 3 | Done (SM-19) | Decompose resolveCallTarget into thin dispatcher |
| Phase 4 | Done (SM-14) | BindingAccumulator for cross-file type propagation |
| Phase 5 | Done (SM-18, PR #769) | Delete lookupFuzzy, globalIndex, callableIndex |
| **Phase 6** | **This issue** | **Wire SemanticModel as first-class resolution input** |

The target architecture: language providers feed a SemanticModel during ingestion; all resolution flows through the model via O(1) owner-scoped lookups instead of name -> filter -> filter -> filter.

## What Changes

### Expose SemanticModel on SymbolTable
- Add `readonly model: SemanticModel` property to `SymbolTableReader` interface
- Internal `MutableSemanticModel` widened to `SemanticModel` at the interface boundary to prevent external mutation

### Migrate All 37 Internal Call Sites
Replace `symbols.lookupClass/Method/Field/Impl` calls with `table.model.types/methods/fields.*` equivalents across:
- `call-processor.ts` (21 call sites)
- `resolution-context.ts` (5 call sites)
- `type-env.ts` (7 call sites)
- `heritage-map.ts` (4 call sites)

### Fix PR #786 Review Findings
- Duplicate JSDoc in model files
- Missing `model/index.ts` barrel exports
- O(n^2) BFS `array.shift()` in `buildParentMapFromHeritage` -- replace with queue

### Update lookupMethodByOwnerWithMRO Signature
- Change from `symbols: SymbolTable` to `model: SemanticModel`, removing last SymbolTable dependency from `model/resolve.ts`

### Feeding Audit
- Verify every `symbol-table.add()` call site correctly populates SemanticModel registries
- Constructor symbols (`type === 'Constructor'`) must be indexed in methodByOwner

## What Does NOT Change

- SymbolTable.lookup* delegate wrappers stay alive (deprecated with @deprecated JSDoc) for backward compatibility -- deletion is a follow-up
- `callableByName` and `fileIndex` stay in SymbolTable -- not part of SemanticModel (owner-scoped registries only)
- Language providers, tree-sitter queries, graph schema, MCP tools unchanged

## Key Constraints

- `model/resolve.ts` must NOT import `resolution-context.ts` (circular dependency prevention)
- All `model/` -> `symbol-table.ts` imports must use `import type` (erased at runtime)
- TypeEnv remains ephemeral per-file -- BindingAccumulator collects outputs separately
- SM-19 lesson: silent dispatcher bypass in call-processor.ts is the dominant failure mode -- run resolver suite after every batch of migrations

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `table.model.*` used for all owner-scoped lookups in call-processor, resolution-context, type-env, heritage-map
- [ ] SymbolTable.lookup* wrappers marked @deprecated
- [ ] `model/index.ts` barrel exports: SemanticModel, MutableSemanticModel, registries, factories, lookupMethodByOwnerWithMRO
- [ ] Self-index regression check: `npx gitnexus analyze` symbol/relationship counts match baseline +/-0
- [ ] All resolver integration tests pass across 12 languages
- [ ] `npx tsc --noEmit` passes

## References

- Plan: `docs/plans/2026-04-11-003-refactor-sm20-wire-up-semantic-model-plan.md`
- Roadmap: `docs/plans/2026-04-06-002-refactor-eliminate-fuzzy-lookups-roadmap-plan.md`
- Structural extraction: PR #786
- Prior phases: PR #739 (Phase 2), SM-19 (Phase 3), SM-14 (Phase 4), PR #769 (Phase 5)

title: refactor(ingestion): split ImportSemantics into per-strategy hooks (Strategies 1-4)
body:
## Summary

The import resolution system uses a monolithic \`ImportSemantics\` interface where each language provider implements all strategies in one block. This should be split into per-strategy hooks following the same config-driven pattern established by method, field, and call extractors -- making import resolution language-agnostic and composable.

## Context

Import resolution currently uses 4 strategies that are tightly coupled inside each language provider's \`ImportSemantics\` implementation:

1. **Strategy 1**: Direct path resolution (e.g., \`import './foo'\` -> \`foo.ts\`)
2. **Strategy 2**: Package/module resolution (e.g., \`import 'lodash'\` -> \`node_modules/lodash\`)
3. **Strategy 3**: Language-specific resolution (e.g., Go workspace, Rust crate, Python package)
4. **Strategy 4**: Fallback/heuristic resolution

Each language implements all strategies monolithically. Adding a new resolution strategy or modifying one for a specific language means touching the entire import resolution block for that language.

## Architecture Direction

Split into per-strategy hooks on the language provider, following the extractor config+factory pattern:
- Each strategy becomes an independent, composable hook
- Languages opt into the strategies they need
- Shared strategies (path resolution, node_modules) are reusable across languages
- Language-specific strategies (Go workspace, Rust crate) are isolated in their config

This is the import resolver equivalent of what the extractor work did for method/field/call/variable extraction.

## What Does NOT Change

- Import capture tags (\`@import\`, \`@import.source\`)
- Named binding extraction
- Cross-file resolution in call-processor.ts
- Graph schema

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Import resolution strategies are independent, composable hooks on LanguageProvider
- [ ] Each language opts into only the strategies it needs
- [ ] Shared strategies are reusable across languages without duplication
- [ ] All existing import resolution tests pass (no regression)
- [ ] \`npx tsc --noEmit\` passes

## References

- Plan: \`docs/plans/2026-04-14-001-refactor-import-resolution-strategies-plan.md\`
- Pattern to follow: method-extractors config+factory, field-extractors config+factory

title: feat(ingestion): language-agnostic heritage extractor with config+factory pattern
body:
## Summary

Heritage extraction (extends/implements/mixins) is currently handled inline in the parse worker via \`@heritage.*\` tree-sitter captures with ad-hoc language switches (e.g., Go struct embedding detection, Ruby mixin routing via CallRouter). This should follow the same config+factory pattern as method, field, call, and variable extractors.

## Architecture Direction

Following the same language-agnostic pattern established across all other extractors:

1. **Types file** defines domain interfaces (\`HeritageExtractionConfig\`, \`HeritageExtractor\`, \`HeritageInfo\`)
2. **Generic factory** (\`createHeritageExtractor(config)\`) converts a declarative config into a runtime extractor
3. **Per-language configs** in \`heritage-extractors/configs/<lang>.ts\` specify AST node types and extraction hooks
4. **Language provider wiring** adds \`heritageExtractor\` to \`LanguageProvider\` interface
5. **Parse worker consumption** replaces inline heritage logic with \`provider.heritageExtractor.extract()\`

## Current State

Heritage extraction lives in several places:
- Parse worker inline logic for \`@heritage.class\`, \`@heritage.extends\`, \`@heritage.implements\` captures
- Go-specific struct embedding detection (named field skip logic)
- Ruby \`CallRouter\` handling heritage-like calls (\`include\`, \`extend\`, \`prepend\`)
- \`heritage-processor.ts\` for cross-file heritage resolution (stays unchanged)
- \`heritage-map.ts\` in \`model/\` for MRO-aware lookup (stays unchanged)

## What Changes

- New types file: \`heritage-types.ts\` (or extend existing \`ExtractedHeritage\` in parse-worker)
- New factory: \`heritage-extractors/generic.ts\`
- 11 config files in \`heritage-extractors/configs/\`
- Parse worker heritage capture handling replaced by \`provider.heritageExtractor?.extract()\`
- Ruby CallRouter heritage routing absorbed into Ruby heritage config

## What Does NOT Change

- \`heritage-processor.ts\` (cross-file resolution, runs in pipeline)
- \`model/heritage-map.ts\` (MRO-aware lookup, SemanticModel layer)
- \`ExtractedHeritage\` interface (consumed by heritage-processor)
- MRO strategies in \`mro-processor.ts\`
- Tree-sitter query capture tags

## Dependencies

- Should land after: #874 (call extractor), #875 (variable extractor), #876 (class config migration)
- Completes the full set of language-agnostic extractors

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] \`HeritageExtractionConfig\` + \`createHeritageExtractor()\` factory exists
- [ ] Per-language configs for all 16 tree-sitter languages
- [ ] \`heritageExtractor\` field on \`LanguageProvider\` interface
- [ ] Parse worker uses \`provider.heritageExtractor\` instead of inline logic
- [ ] Ruby heritage-like call routing absorbed into config
- [ ] All existing tests pass (no regression)
- [ ] New unit tests for heritage extraction configs

## References

- Pattern to follow: \`method-extractors/generic.ts\`, \`call-extractors/configs/\`
- Related: \`model/heritage-map.ts\`, \`heritage-processor.ts\`

title: feat(ingestion): unify CLI and web ingestion pipeline via gitnexus-shared
body:
## Summary

Both the CLI and web surfaces must share a single DAG-based ingestion pipeline. Currently the web has an independent ingestion implementation that drifts behind the CLI. The extractors, SemanticModel, and pipeline phases should be centralized in \`gitnexus-shared\` so both surfaces consume the same logic.

## Context

Architectural decisions from March 2026 established that:
- Web and CLI must route through a single, shared ingestion pipeline (no separate implementations)
- The pipeline must follow a DAG execution model (implemented in CLI via topological phase runner with 12 declared phases)
- Pure-logic files (~14) were extracted to \`@gitnexus/shared\` as a first step (PR #536 moved web to backend-only)
- Platform-specific files (pipeline runner, workers, import resolution) stayed in their packages

The CLI ingestion pipeline is now significantly more advanced than the web's:
- Config+factory extractors for method, field, class, call, variable
- SemanticModel with TypeRegistry, MethodRegistry, FieldRegistry
- DAG phase runner with typed phase outputs
- BindingAccumulator for cross-file type propagation

## Architecture Direction

### What Moves to gitnexus-shared
- Extractor types and configs (pure data + pure functions, no Node.js deps)
- SemanticModel interfaces and registries
- Pipeline phase contracts and types
- Resolution context interfaces

### What Stays Platform-Specific
- Pipeline runner (Node.js worker threads vs web worker)
- Tree-sitter grammar loading (native bindings vs WASM)
- File system access patterns
- Worker pool management

### Key Constraint
- \`gitnexus-shared\` must have zero \`node:\` imports (CI gate already exists)
- Uses \`"NodeNext"\` module resolution (not \`"Bundler"\`)
- SymbolTable shared as interface, not concrete class

## Dependencies

- Depends on: all extractor issues (#874, #875, #876, heritage extractor)
- Depends on: SM-20 SemanticModel wiring (stabilize the model layer first)
- Depends on: import resolution strategies refactor (clean composable hooks)

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Single source of truth for ingestion pipeline logic in gitnexus-shared
- [ ] Both CLI and web consume shared pipeline types and extractors
- [ ] Zero \`node:\` imports in gitnexus-shared (CI enforced)
- [ ] Web ingestion produces identical graph output as CLI for the same input
- [ ] All CLI tests pass
- [ ] All web tests pass

## References

- Architectural decision: PR #536 (browser-to-server migration)
- Plan: \`docs/plans/2026-03-21-unify-ingestion-engine-plan.md\`
- Related: \`gitnexus-shared/src/graph/types.ts\` (shared graph types already exist)

title: feat(extractors): detect jQuery $.ajax/$.get/$.post and axios object-form as HTTP consumers
body:
Closes #828.

## Summary

Extend the JS/TS HTTP consumer extractor (`gitnexus/src/core/group/extractors/http-patterns/node.ts`) so that three widely-used call shapes emit `consumer` contracts the same way `fetch()` and `axios.<verb>()` already do:

- **jQuery shorthand:** `$.get('/api/x')`, `$.post('/api/x', data)`
- **jQuery ajax form:** `$.ajax({ url: '/api/x', method: 'GET' })` / `$.ajax({ url: '/api/x', type: 'GET' })`
- **axios object form:** `axios({ method: 'POST', url: '/api/x' })`

## Why

`group sync` over any Laravel / legacy frontend repo currently produces zero consumer contracts for files that use `$.ajax`/`$.get`/`$.post` — the cross-link between the frontend caller and the backend route is silently invisible, so downstream impact analysis misses real dependencies. Same story for codebases that call `axios({ method, url })` instead of the dotted shorthand.

## Implementation

`node.ts`:
- 3 new `PatternSpec`s alongside the existing `FETCH_*_SPEC` / `AXIOS_SPEC`: `JQUERY_SHORTHAND_SPEC`, `JQUERY_AJAX_SPEC`, `AXIOS_OBJECT_SPEC`.
- `NodePatternBundle` gains `jqueryShorthand` / `jqueryAjax` / `axiosObject` slots, compiled once per JS / TS / TSX grammar via the existing `compileBundle()` path.
- New `readStringProp()` helper walks `pair` children of an `(object)` literal and resolves `url` / `method` / `type` keys independent of declaration order.
- 3 new scan loops in `scanBundle()` emit `HttpDetection { role: 'consumer', framework: 'jquery' | 'axios', ... }` with confidence `0.7` (matching the existing source-scan consumers) and default method `GET` when absent (matches both jQuery `$.ajax` and axios runtime defaults).

### Deviation from the issue's proposed patterns

The issue sketches one tree-sitter query per pattern that encodes `url` and `method` as adjacent `pair` children. S-expression matching is positional — that forces a specific key order, which isn't guaranteed for JS object literals. This PR instead captures the options object and resolves keys in TypeScript post-processing, so `{ url, method }` and `{ method, url }` are both matched. The same path also accepts jQuery's `type:` synonym for `method:` (jQuery supports both; the issue example only showed `type`).

## Tests

`gitnexus/test/unit/group/http-route-extractor.test.ts` — 4 new `it()` cases under the existing consumer-extraction block:

1. `extracts jQuery $.get and $.post shorthand` — asserts `http::GET::/api/users` and `http::POST::/api/users` with `framework: 'jquery'`.
2. `extracts jQuery $.ajax with method: and type: keys and default GET` — covers `method: 'PUT'`, `type: 'DELETE'`, and a method-less call defaulting to `GET`.
3. `extracts axios({ method, url }) object form regardless of key order` — proves post-processing is order-independent and that a url-only call defaults to `GET`.
4. `does not emit consumers for unrelated object-literal calls (negative control)` — `$.fn.extend(...)`, `$.each(...)`, a non-axios helper call, and a bare `const cfg = { url, method }` all produce zero consumer contracts, so the new patterns can't overmatch.

## Test plan

- [x] `npx vitest run test/unit/group/http-route-extractor.test.ts` → `22 passed` (18 existing + 4 new)
- [x] `npm run test:unit` → only the 4 pre-existing unrelated failures (`test/unit/skip-git-cli.test.ts` and `test/unit/git-utils.test.ts` — both fail identically on `main` before this change; neither touches the extractor surface)
- [x] `npx tsc --noEmit` → clean
- [x] Pre-commit hook (lint-staged + eslint + prettier + tsc) → pass

## Safety / backwards-compat

- Purely additive: new `PatternSpec`s, new bundle slots, new loops. No existing code path modified.
- No changes to `HttpDetection` / `ExtractedContract` shape — the orchestrator normalises these detections identically to the existing fetch/axios consumers.
- `framework: 'jquery'` is a new label; `framework: 'axios'` is reused so downstream grouping stays consistent.
- Patterns are structurally disjoint (`axios(...)` identifier-form vs `axios.x(...)` member-form; `$.get` / `$.post` shorthand vs `$.ajax` object), so no dedup state is needed.

title: feat(mcp): rank context/impact disambiguation candidates and expose kind/file_path hints
body:
Closes #470.

## Problem

`context` already returned `{ status: 'ambiguous', candidates }` when a name hit multiple symbols, but the candidates were in **arbitrary DB order** and the only hint accepted was `file_path`. `impact` was worse — when its name resolver found multiple viable matches it **silently picked the first** row from a priority UNION, giving no signal back that a different symbol might have been intended. A second user confirmed the impact failure mode in the issue comments: "the returned match is uncertain, which often leads to incorrect parsing results and meaningless tool calls."

## What changed

New shared resolver `resolveSymbolCandidates(repo, query, hints)` on `LocalBackend`. Both `context` and `impact` now go through it, so resolution behaviour can't drift between the two tools.

Behaviour, in order:

1. **Direct uid** → zero-ambiguity short-circuit (both tools).
2. **Name / qualified-id query** with optional `WHERE n.filePath CONTAINS $filePath` filter. `LIMIT 20` (was 10) so the ranker has headroom.
3. **#480 Class/Constructor collapse preserved** — when the only ambiguity is a Class and its own Constructor sharing name+filePath, the Class wins silently. Covered by existing `java-class-impact.test.ts` (still green).
4. **Ranking** (pure TS, no extra DB round-trip):
   - base `0.50`
   - `+0.40` when `file_path` hint matches (substring, case-insensitive)
   - `+0.20` when `kind` hint exactly matches the candidate's kind
   - When no `kind` hint: small priority bonus `Class > Interface > Function > Method > Constructor` (`+0.10, +0.08, +0.06, +0.04, +0.02`)
   - Capped at `1.0`
   - Stable tiebreak: shorter `filePath` first, then lex `uid`
5. **Confident single-result promotion**: if top score `≥ 0.95` *and* beats runner-up by `≥ 0.10`, resolve as `{ kind: 'ok' }` instead of emitting ambiguous. A strong `file_path` + `kind` hint can cut through without a disambiguation round-trip.
6. Otherwise `{ kind: 'ambiguous', candidates: [{..., score}] }`.

## API surface

**`context`** input schema gains `kind`. Response shape is a **strict superset** of today's — every candidate now carries a `score` field; all existing keys (`uid, name, kind, filePath, line`) preserved.

**`impact`** input schema gains `target_uid`, `file_path`, `kind`. New response variant when the target is ambiguous:

```json
{
  \"status\": \"ambiguous\",
  \"message\": \"Found N symbols matching 'X'. Use target_uid, file_path, or kind to disambiguate.\",
  \"target\": { \"name\": \"X\" },
  \"direction\": \"upstream\",
  \"impactedCount\": 0,
  \"risk\": \"UNKNOWN\",
  \"candidates\": [
    { \"uid\": \"...\", \"name\": \"X\", \"kind\": \"Function\", \"filePath\": \"src/...\", \"line\": 42, \"score\": 0.76 }
  ]
}
```

## Backward compatibility

- `context` ambiguous shape — strict superset. `eval-formatters.test.ts` (which parses the old shape) is unchanged and still passes. `rename` tool delegates to context and forwards `status === 'ambiguous'` unchanged.
- `impact` going from silent-first-pick to structured ambiguous is the point of the issue. Callers that were relying on silent-first-pick now get an actionable response and can retry with `target_uid` / `file_path` / `kind`.
- `#480` Class/Constructor preference preserved inside the shared resolver; covered by `java-class-impact.test.ts` (green).

## Scope declined for v1

**`module` / `community` hint.** The issue lists it as one of several hints, but `kind` + `file_path` cover the vast majority of disambiguation needs in practice, and a community-label filter requires an extra graph query per candidate. Natural v2 follow-up — the ranker and the tool schemas are designed so that bolting on community signal later only touches `scoreCandidate` + one schema field.

## Tests

Added / extended in `gitnexus/test/unit/calltool-dispatch.test.ts` (6 changes, all use the existing `executeParameterized` mock pattern):

1. **extend** `context tool returns disambiguation for multiple matches` — asserts every candidate now carries a numeric `score ∈ [0,1]` and the list is sorted descending.
2. `context tool ranks file_path match higher than non-match` — confident single-result promotion kicks in when `file_path: 'App.tsx'` narrows two Functions to one.
3. `context tool returns ranked candidates when file_path only partially narrows` — asserts the exact computed score (0.56) for tied base-case candidates.
4. `context tool boosts the candidate whose kind matches the hint` — Function + Method sharing a name; `kind: 'Function'` bubbles the Function to top.
5. `impact tool returns ambiguous shape with ranked candidates when target has multiple matches` — the core new behaviour.
6. `impact tool resolves via target_uid without running the name-based resolver` — inspects `executeParameterized.mock.calls` to assert no `WHERE n.name = \$symName` query fires.

## Test plan

- [x] `npx vitest run test/unit/calltool-dispatch.test.ts` — **64 passed**
- [x] `npx vitest run test/integration/java-class-impact.test.ts` — **pass** (#480 regression guard green)
- [x] `npx vitest run test/unit/eval-formatters.test.ts` — **pass** (backward-compat shape)
- [x] `npm run test:unit` — **3642 passed**, 4 pre-existing env failures unchanged (`skip-git-cli.test.ts` needs built `dist/`; `git-utils.test.ts` Windows-tmpdir issue — both fail identically on `main`)
- [x] `npx tsc --noEmit` — clean
- [x] Pre-commit hook (lint-staged + eslint + prettier + tsc) — passed

title: feat(embeddings): AST-aware chunking with offset-based splitting
body:
## Summary

- Replace global line-number based AST matching (`findNodeByRange`) with offset-based `findFunctionNode`/`findDeclarationNode` that work on snippet content, fixing the fundamental issue where tree-sitter parses relative rows (0-based) but old code matched against absolute line numbers (1-based)
- Add declaration-aware chunking for `Class`/`Interface` labels that splits by member boundaries, grouping consecutive field-like members together instead of using raw character windows
- Fix positional array column mapping bug in `queryEmbeddableNodes` where `description` was read from wrong index depending on whether the label has an `isExported` column
- Add legacy schema migration in `fetchExistingEmbeddingHashes`: rows missing `chunkIndex`/`startLine`/`endLine` are detected as stale, forcing rebuild from single-embedding-per-node to chunk-aware schema

### Key changes

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `ast-utils.ts` | New `findFunctionNode`/`findDeclarationNode` with multi-language type sets; parser cache per language key |
| `chunker.ts` | New `declarationChunk` path for Class/Interface; unified `chunkByUnits` with oversized-unit fallback |
| `line-index.ts` | Extracted `buildLineIndex`/`resolveChunkLines`/`lineFromOffset` (was duplicated in character-chunk + chunker) |
| `embedding-pipeline.ts` | Fix column index mapping; extract `collectBestChunks`; deterministic `contentHashForNode` |
| `lbug-adapter.ts` | Detect legacy non-chunk rows as stale (null `chunkIndex`/`startLine`/`endLine`) |
| `text-generator.ts` | Add Interface support via shared `generateStructuralTypeText`; include chunk body in embedding text |
| `parser-loader.ts` | New `createParserForLanguage`/`resolveLanguageKey`/`getLanguageGrammar` for per-key parser instances |
| `local-backend.ts` | Deduplicate vector search via `collectBestChunks`; use table/index name constants |

## Test plan

- [x] 67 unit tests pass (chunker, ast-utils, embedding-pipeline, text-generator, semantic-chunk-search, lbug-embedding-hashes)
- [x] P2 fix verified: `maps positional query rows with description/isExported columns correctly`
- [x] P1 fix verified: `treats rows without chunk-aware metadata as stale even when contentHash exists`

- [ ] Manual: verify Class/Interface chunking produces member-aware chunks (not character windows)

title: feat(ingestion): language-agnostic heritage extractor with config+factory pattern
body:
Heritage extraction (extends/implements/mixins) was handled inline in the parse worker, call-processor, and heritage-processor via ad-hoc `@heritage.*` capture map checks with language-specific switches (Go named field skip, Ruby mixin routing). This migrates it to the same config+factory pattern used by method, field, call, and variable extractors, and **removes all legacy inline heritage paths**.

### Types & factory

- `heritage-types.ts` — `HeritageExtractionConfig`, `HeritageExtractor`, `HeritageInfo` interfaces
- `heritage-extractors/generic.ts` — `createHeritageExtractor(config)` factory converts declarative config to runtime extractor. Accepts either a full `HeritageExtractionConfig` (for languages with custom hooks) or a bare `SupportedLanguages` enum value for default capture-based extraction — no per-language config file needed for the default case.

### Per-language configs (2 files in `heritage-extractors/configs/`)

Only languages with actual custom extraction logic have dedicated config files:
- **Go** (`go.ts`) — `shouldSkipExtends` filters named struct fields from embedding captures
- **Ruby** (`ruby.ts`) — `callBasedHeritage` absorbs `include`/`extend`/`prepend` mixin routing previously in `routeRubyCall`

All other languages use the default extraction path by passing the `SupportedLanguages` enum directly to the factory.

### Provider wiring

`heritageExtractor` added to `LanguageProviderConfig`. All 16 providers wired:

```typescript
// Languages with custom hooks pass a full config:
heritageExtractor: createHeritageExtractor(goHeritageConfig),

// Languages with default capture-based extraction pass the enum:
heritageExtractor: createHeritageExtractor(SupportedLanguages.Java),
```

### Parse worker, call-processor & heritage-processor

All inline heritage capture logic replaced with `provider.heritageExtractor?.extract()`:

- **parse-worker.ts** — Pre-pass heritage extraction for `buildTypeEnv` now uses `heritageExtractor.extract()`. Call-based heritage checked via `extractFromCall` before the call router. Heritage case removed from callRouter dispatch.
- **call-processor.ts** — Pre-pass heritage extraction migrated identically. `extractFromCall` check added before callRouter (was previously missing). Heritage case removed from callRouter switch.
- **heritage-processor.ts** — `processHeritage` inline captureMap checks (extends/implements/trait-impl with Go named field skip) replaced with `heritageExtractor.extract()` + new `resolveAndAddHeritageEdge` helper that bridges `HeritageInfo` to graph edge resolution. `extractExtractedHeritageFromFiles` updated identically.

### Legacy path removal

- **`routeRubyCall`** — Heritage routing removed (include/extend/prepend → `{kind:'heritage'}`). `RubyHeritageItem` interface and heritage variant removed from `RubyCallRouting` union. Router now returns `skip` for these calls since `heritageExtractor.extractFromCall` intercepts them first.
- **`processHeritage`** — ~100 lines of inline captureMap checks replaced with extractor delegation.
- **Pre-pass heritage** in parse-worker and call-processor — Hardcoded Go `field_declaration` skip removed, now handled by `goHeritageConfig.shouldSkipExtends`.

### What did NOT change

- `heritage-processor.ts` cross-file resolution logic (resolveHeritageId, resolveExtendsType)
- `model/heritage-map.ts` / MRO strategies
- `ExtractedHeritage` interface
- Tree-sitter query capture tags
- Graph schema (node labels, edge types, ID generation)

### Tests

27+ unit tests covering factory construction (both enum and full config paths), Go named field filtering, Ruby call-based heritage extraction (include/extend/prepend with constants, scope resolution, modules, multiple args, missing enclosing class). Default language extractors verified to have no custom hooks. Provider wiring test ensures all 15 tree-sitter providers have `heritageExtractor` defined. Integration tests exercise Ruby `callBasedHeritage` and TypeScript heritage against real tree-sitter ASTs. Call-routing tests updated for new skip behavior.

title: Regenerate the Wiki so previous work is considered
body:
### Area

Other

### Problem or opportunity

When running the wiki function there are errors. The wiki is created without some parts, the ones that failed.



### Proposed solution

It would be nice to have a way to take advantage of what is already generated and only regenerate the ones missing. 


### Alternatives considered

title: 常量和枚举类的调用关系缺失，需要增加
Python dotted imports can resolve Django framework modules to local files
body:
## Summary
Python dotted imports that should remain external can be misresolved to unrelated local files.

## Reproduction
Use a Django-style repo with multiple local modules named like common framework submodules:

- `accounts/apps.py` and `billing/apps.py` both contain `from django.apps import AppConfig`
- `config/urls.py` contains `from django.urls import path`
- `config/asgi.py` contains `from django.core.asgi import get_asgi_application`
- `config/wsgi.py` contains `from django.core.wsgi import get_wsgi_application`

When GitNexus indexes the repo, it can emit incorrect `IMPORTS` edges between local files instead of treating those `django.*` imports as unresolved external dependencies.

## Actual behavior
Examples observed locally:

- `accounts/apps.py -> accounts/apps.py`
- `billing/apps.py -> accounts/apps.py` or `billing/apps.py`
- `config/urls.py -> config/urls.py`
- `config/asgi.py -> config/asgi.py`
- `config/wsgi.py -> config/wsgi.py`

## Expected behavior
- External imports like `django.apps`, `django.urls`, `django.core.asgi`, and `django.core.wsgi` should not resolve to local repo files.
- Real local imports should still resolve normally, e.g. `from accounts.models import Customer` from `billing/models.py`.

## Suspected cause
Python import resolution appears to let unresolved dotted imports fall through to generic suffix matching, so a basename like `apps.py` or `urls.py` can win even when the leading package (`django`) does not exist in the repo.

## Impact
This creates incorrect `IMPORTS` edges and can mislead downstream graph queries, impact analysis, and any resolution logic that depends on import edges.

title: fix(python): avoid local matches for external dotted imports
body:
## Summary
Prevent external dotted Python imports like `django.apps` from falling through to generic suffix matching when the leading package does not exist in-repo, and add Django-based regression coverage for that case.

## Motivation / context
Closes #898.

The bug shows up in Django-style projects where multiple local files share framework-like basenames such as `apps.py`, `urls.py`, `asgi.py`, or `wsgi.py`. GitNexus could emit local `IMPORTS` edges for `django.*` imports instead of leaving them unresolved as external dependencies.

## Areas touched

- [x] `gitnexus/` (CLI / core / MCP server)
- [ ] `gitnexus-web/` (Vite / React UI)
- [ ] `.github/` (workflows, actions)
- [ ] `eval/` or other tooling
- [ ] Docs / agent config only (`AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `.cursor/`, `llms.txt`, etc.)

## Scope & constraints
**In scope**

- Guard the Python import strategy so unresolved dotted imports with no in-repo leading package do not suffix-match unrelated local files
- Add a Django fixture with two apps and a real local cross-app import to reproduce the bug
- Add unit and integration regressions for `django.apps`, `django.urls`, `django.core.asgi`, and `django.core.wsgi`

**Explicitly out of scope / not done here**

- Broader redesign of Python import resolution or package-indexing semantics
- Any changes to web UI, MCP contracts, or non-Python resolvers
- Golden snapshot updates unrelated to this fix

## Implementation notes
The change is intentionally narrow in `gitnexus/src/core/ingestion/import-resolvers/configs/python.ts`.

For dotted imports, the Python resolver now checks whether the leading segment appears anywhere in the repo before allowing generic fallback. That keeps internal imports like `accounts.models` working while absorbing external imports like `django.apps` so they do not resolve to local files such as `accounts/apps.py` or `config/urls.py`.

## Testing & verification
- [x] `cd gitnexus && npx vitest run test/unit/import-resolver-factory.test.ts test/integration/resolvers/python.test.ts`
- [x] `cd gitnexus && npx tsc --noEmit`
- [ ] `cd gitnexus && npm test` — the full-suite run hit an unrelated failure in `test/integration/pipeline-graph-golden.test.ts` (`fatal: not a git repository`) plus vitest worker-exit noise; rerunning `npx vitest run test/integration/pipeline-graph-golden.test.ts` alone passed

## Risk & rollout
Low risk: the behavioral change is limited to Python dotted-import fallback before generic suffix resolution.

No migrations or config changes are required. If the behavior needs to be rolled back, reverting this PR cleanly removes both the resolver guard and the Django regression fixture/tests.

title: MCP stdio handshake fails in Codex; startup logs on stdout and SIGINT shutdown throws ERR_INVALID_ARG_TYPE
body:
## Summary

I'm seeing GitNexus MCP fail to handshake in Codex Desktop on Windows.

Two symptoms seem related:

1. Codex reports:
   `MCP startup failed: timed out handshaking with MCP server after 30s`

2. Running the MCP server manually shows:
   `GitNexus: MCP server starting with 1 repo(s): rpa`

   Then on Ctrl+C:
   `GitNexus MCP: unhandled rejection — The "code" argument must be of type number. Received type string ('SIGINT')`

This makes me suspect there are two issues:
- MCP startup is writing human-readable logs to `stdout`, which may corrupt stdio MCP handshake
- SIGINT shutdown passes the signal string into `process.exit()`

## Environment

- OS: Windows
- GitNexus version: `1.5.3`
- MCP client: Codex Desktop
- Repo is indexed successfully
- `.gitnexus/meta.json` exists and looks healthy

## Codex MCP config

```toml
[mcp_servers.gitnexus]
command = "cmd"
args = ["/c", "npx", "-y", "gitnexus@latest", "mcp"]
```

## What works

- `npx gitnexus --version` works
- Repo indexing works
- `.gitnexus/meta.json` is present
- Running `npx gitnexus mcp` starts the process

## What fails

In Codex Desktop, MCP startup fails with:

```txt
failed to get client: MCP startup failed: timed out handshaking with MCP server after 30s
```

## Manual run output

```txt
PS D:\github\rpa> npx gitnexus mcp
GitNexus: MCP server starting with 1 repo(s): rpa
GitNexus MCP: unhandled rejection — The "code" argument must be of type number. Received type string ('SIGINT')
GitNexus MCP unhandledRejection: TypeError [ERR_INVALID_ARG_TYPE]: The "code" argument must be of type number. Received type string ('SIGINT')
    at process.set [as exitCode] (node:internal/bootstrap/node:119:9)
    at process.exit (node:internal/process/per_thread:231:24)
    at process.shutdown (file:///C:/Users/Administrator/AppData/Roaming/npm/node_modules/gitnexus/dist/mcp/server.js:276:17)
```

## Suspected code path

In my installed package, `dist/mcp/server.js` appears to have logic like:

- `process.on('SIGINT', shutdown);`
- `shutdown(exitCode = 0) { ... process.exit(exitCode) }`

So when SIGINT fires, the string `'SIGINT'` seems to be passed into `process.exit(...)`.

Also, startup appears to print a normal log line before/stdout during stdio mode:
`GitNexus: MCP server starting with 1 repo(s): rpa`

For MCP stdio servers, that output likely needs to go to `stderr` instead of `stdout`.

## Expected behavior

- MCP server should complete stdio handshake cleanly in Codex
- No non-protocol logs should be written to `stdout`
- SIGINT/SIGTERM shutdown should exit cleanly without throwing

## Suggested fix ideas

- Send all human-readable startup logs to `stderr`
- Wrap signal handlers like:
  `process.on('SIGINT', () => shutdown(0))`
  `process.on('SIGTERM', () => shutdown(0))`
- Keep `stdout` reserved strictly for MCP protocol messages

## Notes

I did not find a public issue matching this exact behavior yet, so opening this in case it's a real MCP compatibility bug on Windows/Codex.

title: refactor(ingestion): position-indexed enclosing-function lookup — resolution via the semantic model, extraction from the AST
body:
Post-extraction cleanup in `gitnexus/src/core/ingestion/`. Most items in the issue (`genericFuncName` / `inferFunctionLabel` single-source, `TypeConfig.extractReturnType` removal, `extractMethodSignature` removal, `isCppInsideClassOrStruct` / `isKotlinClassMethod` moved to language providers) had already landed via #874/#875/#876. Remaining work was a duplicated parent-walk and a poorly-signposted divergence between two similarly-named helpers that — once the names exposed the phase split — turned out to share enough logic to collapse into a single shared extractor, with resolution lifted out of the AST entirely and onto the semantic model.

### Deduplicate enclosing-owner walk
- New `findEnclosingOwnerNode(node, resolveEnclosingOwner?)` in `utils/ast-helpers.ts`.
- Removes `findEnclosingClassNode` from `workers/parse-worker.ts` (5 call sites) and `seqFindEnclosingOwnerNode` from `parsing-processor.ts` (2 call sites). Both were the same loop; the shared helper preserves no-hook (raw container, e.g. Ruby `singleton_class` for static-method detection) and hooked (provider remap) semantics.
- Drops the now-unused `CLASS_CONTAINER_TYPES` import in both consumers; corrects a stale doc reference in `ast-helpers.ts`.

### Enforce extraction vs resolution phase split structurally
The two enclosing-function helpers were doing nearly the same work in different phases. Rather than just renaming them and documenting the divergence, the work has been refactored so the phase boundary is enforced by code structure: extraction is the only phase that touches the AST, and resolution is the only phase that consumes the semantic model — and crucially, resolution no longer walks the AST at all, it asks the model.

#### Shared extraction-phase helper
- New `gitnexus/src/core/ingestion/utils/enclosing-function.ts` is the single owner of the AST → enclosing-function-ID logic. It exports `extractEnclosingFunctionId` plus its supporting infrastructure (`getMethodInfo`, `cachedFindEnclosingClassInfo`, `findClassNodeByQualifiedName`, per-module caches, `clearEnclosingFunctionCaches`). All inputs are AST + `LanguageProvider` hooks — no `ResolutionContext`, no SymbolTable, no graph lookups.
- `workers/parse-worker.ts` no longer defines its own `extractEnclosingFunctionId`, `cachedFindEnclosingClassInfo`, `findClassNodeByQualifiedName`, `getMethodInfo`, `methodInfoCache`, `classIdCache`, or `functionIdCache`; it imports them from the shared module and delegates `clearCaches()` to `clearEnclosingFunctionCaches()`. Dead imports (`findEnclosingClassInfo`, `EnclosingClassInfo`, `MethodExtractorContext`) removed.
- The shared helper gains an `extractFromNode` fallback for top-level methods (Ruby `def`, Go top-level methods) so the AST-derived ID matches the definition phase exactly. This was the case the old SymbolTable fast-path in the resolver was silently covering — making it explicit in the extractor lets the fast-path go away without losing behavior.

#### Resolution via the semantic model (O(log N) lookup, zero AST traversal)
- New `gitnexus/src/core/ingestion/model/enclosing-function-index.ts` is a position-indexed registry on the semantic model: `(filePath, line) → enclosing function nodeId`. Per-file sorted-array binary search on `startLine ASC, endLine DESC` so the innermost containing range wins (handles nested closures, lambdas, local functions). Lookups are O(log N) average; inserts are O(1) amortised.
- Wired into `MutableSemanticModel` as `enclosingFunctions`, exported from `model/index.ts`, and cleared by `cascadeClear`.
- Extraction populates the index. `parse-worker.ts` extends `ParsedSymbol` with `startLine?/endLine?` (populated only for Function/Method/Constructor) and the parsing-processor's worker-merge loop and sequential path both register the lexical range against the model alongside the SymbolTable add. A new `getDefinitionEndRow` helper in `ast-helpers.ts` folds in Dart's sibling `function_signature` + `function_body` shape so the registered range covers the body.
- `call-processor.ts` deletes `resolveEnclosingFunctionId` (~240 LOC) and `enclosingFnExtractCache` entirely. All five call sites switched from an AST parent-walk to `ctx.model.enclosingFunctions.lookup(file.path, node.startPosition.row + 1)` — pure semantic-model query, no AST traversal, no SymbolTable name lookup, no ID construction in the resolver. The per-file `clearEnclosingFunctionCaches()` call from the resolution loop is gone (the resolver no longer touches the AST extractor). Dead imports (`findEnclosingClassInfo`, `inferFunctionLabel`, `typeTagForId`, `constTagForId`, `buildCollisionGroups`, `MethodInfo`) removed.
- After the refactor, `extractEnclosingFunctionId` is imported only by `parse-worker.ts` (the extraction phase). The `enclosing-function.ts` module docstring was updated to make this boundary explicit and to direct resolution-phase callers to `model.enclosingFunctions`.

No changes to `LanguageProvider`, extractor config+factory, capture loop, graph schema, MCP contracts, or generated IDs.

title: Analyze crashes in parse phase on any C# file: "Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'length')"
body:
### Area

gitnexus (CLI / core / indexing / MCP server)

### Summary

Analysis failed: Phase 'parse' failed: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'length')

### Context

_No response_

### Expected behavior

The parse phase completes without error. Hello.cs is indexed with symbol-level detail comparable to what other built-in languages            
  (TypeScript, Python, Java, Go, etc.) produce. Specifically, after analyze the knowledge graph should contain:                                   
  - Nodes                                                                                                                                      
    - File for Hello.cs
    - Class Greeter (with filePath, startLine, endLine)
    - Method Greet (visibility public, parameterCount 1, returnType string)
    - Method Main (visibility public, isStatic true, parameterCount 1)
    - Interface IFoo
    - Method Bar on IFoo (abstract, parameterCount 0, returnType void)
  - Edges
    - DEFINES: Hello.cs → Greeter, Hello.cs → IFoo
    - HAS_METHOD: Greeter → Greet, Greeter → Main; IFoo → Bar
    - CALLS: Main → Greet, Main → Console.WriteLine (or filtered as a built-in per BUILT_INS in languages/csharp.js)
  - CLI output
    - analyze exits 0, reports a non-zero symbol count, and no Analysis failed line.

  For the real repo (mixed TS + C#), the same guarantees should apply to every .cs file, so graph queries like MATCH (m:Method) WHERE
  m.filePath ENDS WITH '.cs' RETURN count(m) return a non-zero value.

### Actual behavior

A repo with ~454 .cs files + a TypeScript frontend. analyze reports success:

  Repository indexed successfully (4.0s)
  1,231 nodes | 1,836 edges | 38 clusters | 38 flows

  But querying the graph shows zero C# symbols:

  MATCH (n) RETURN DISTINCT label(n) AS label, count(n) AS cnt ORDER BY cnt DESC
  -- File: 596, Function: 189, Folder: 170, Section: 132,
  -- Process: 38, Interface: 37, Method: 26, Community: 23,
  -- Route: 4, Property: 2, Class: 1
  -- (every Class/Method/Interface/Function above is from frontend/*.ts; zero from backend/*.cs)

  So the worker-level failure on .cs files is being caught somewhere upstream in the multi-file case and logged as zero symbols rather than    
  surfacing — worth checking alongside the root cause.

### Steps to reproduce

  mkdir gnx-csharp-repro && cd gnx-csharp-repro
  git init -q
  cat > Hello.cs <<'EOF'
  namespace Demo;

  public class Greeter
  {
      public string Greet(string name) => $"Hello, {name}!";

      public static void Main(string[] args)
      {
          var g = new Greeter();
          System.Console.WriteLine(g.Greet("world"));
      }
  }

  public interface IFoo
  {
      void Bar();
  }
  EOF
  git add -A && git -c user.email=t@t -c user.name=t commit -q -m init
  NODE_ENV=development npx gitnexus analyze --force --verbose

  Expected: Hello.cs is parsed; Greeter, Greet, Main, IFoo, Bar appear as nodes.

  Actual:

  ▶ Phase: scan
  ✓ Phase: scan (5ms)
  ▶ Phase: structure
  ✓ Phase: structure (0ms)
  ▶ Phase: markdown
  ✓ Phase: markdown (0ms)
  ▶ Phase: cobol
  ✓ Phase: cobol (0ms)
  ▶ Phase: parse
  📂 Scan: 1 paths, 1 parseable (0MB), 1 chunks @ 20MB budget

    Analysis failed: Phase 'parse' failed: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'length')

  Exit code 1. No stack trace surfaced — the CLI's console.error swallows err.stack and err.cause (see dist/cli/analyze.js:233-234).

### Environment

  - gitnexus 1.6.1 (global install via npm i -g gitnexus)
  - Node.js v24.11.1
  - Windows 11 Pro 10.0.26200, PowerShell / Git Bash
  - No Swift / Dart / Kotlin optional deps installe

Both the CLAUDE.md block **and** every skill file are loaded into every Claude Code session, so this duplication costs tokens on every turn of every conversation in every indexed repo.

## What changed

Rewrote the template literal inside \`generateGitNexusContent()\` at [gitnexus/src/cli/ai-context.ts](gitnexus/src/cli/ai-context.ts). Kept only content that is genuinely unique-per-repo or load-bearing for the agent before it picks a skill:

**Retained:**
- Header + \`projectName\` + stats line

- \`## Always Do\` (imperatives the agent must know up-front)
- \`## Never Do\` (safety constraints the agent must know up-front)

**Removed:**
- \`## Tools Quick Reference\`, \`## Impact Risk Levels\`, \`## Self-Check Before Finishing\`, \`## When Debugging\`, \`## When Refactoring\`, \`## Keeping the Index Fresh\`

**Net reduction: 58 lines / ~2900 characters (~52% smaller).** Post-trim block is ~40 lines / ~2580 characters.

## Backward compatibility

- \`<!-- gitnexus:start -->\` / \`<!-- gitnexus:end -->\` markers unchanged → the idempotent block-replacement logic continues to work on re-runs.
- \`generateAIContextFiles()\` signature, export surface, and caller contracts unchanged — called from [analyze.ts](gitnexus/src/cli/analyze.ts) and [run-analyze.ts](gitnexus/src/core/run-analyze.ts) with the same arguments.
- All six skill files continue to be installed unchanged; they are now the single source of truth for the trimmed content.
- \`skipAgentsMd\` and \`noStats\` flags are unaffected (they operate outside the template body).
- No graph/index/storage schema change. Revert is a pure text rollback with no side effects.

## Tests

Three new assertions added to [gitnexus/test/unit/ai-context.test.ts](gitnexus/test/unit/ai-context.test.ts):

1. **KEEP invariant** — block still contains the freshness warning, \`## Always Do\`, \`## Never Do\`, \`## Resources\`, the \`projectName\`-interpolated URI (\`gitnexus://repo/TestProject/context\`), and the four skills-routing targets (impact-analysis, refactoring, debugging, cli).
2. **TRIM invariant** — block does NOT contain any of the six removed headers.
3. **BUDGET invariant** — block length < 2700 chars (catches any regression that pads the block back toward the original 5465 size; current post-trim is 2582).

All 6 existing tests still pass — including \`updates existing CLAUDE.md without duplicating\` (single \`gitnexus:start\` marker on re-run).

## Test plan

- [x] \`npx vitest run test/unit/ai-context.test.ts\` → **9 pass** (6 existing + 3 new)
- [x] \`npm run test:unit\` → **3770 pass** (same 4 pre-existing env failures unchanged — \`skip-git-cli.test.ts\` needs built \`dist/\`, \`git-utils.test.ts\` Windows worktree tmpdir)

Meta: Pure Scope-Based Resolution in the Semantic Model
body:
**RFC:** [🧭 RFC: Pure Scope-Based Resolution in the Semantic Model](https://www.notion.so/346dc50b6ed281cfaacbe480bf231d50)
**Predecessor:** [🏗️ RFC: From fuzzy lookups to a semantic model](https://www.notion.so/33adc50b6ed2819eaff5f522f278196d)
**Complements:** [🗺️ Ingestion Roadmap — Phase 3 + Phase 4](https://www.notion.so/344dc50b6ed281619ab5f9527ee789b3)
**Triggering feedback:** #902 (closed; work absorbed into #912)

---

## What this is

Replace today's call-resolution DAG and `TieredCandidates` API with a pure scope-based resolution layer on the SemanticModel. Resolver consults **three scope-aware per-kind entry points** — `ClassRegistry.lookup(name, scope)`, `MethodRegistry.lookup(name, scope)`, `FieldRegistry.lookup(name, scope)` — backed by a scope tree with declarations, imports, and type bindings. Confidence and provenance become first-class per resolution. No AST reads at resolution time. Details in the Notion RFC.

## Rollout — 5 rings, shadow-first

```
Ring 1 (types) → Ring 2 (plumbing: shared + package-local)
             → Ring 3 (per-language migrations, parallel)
             → Ring 4 (DAG retirement, gated on all production langs flipped)
             → Ring 5 (perf + docs)
```

Per-language flip threshold: **≥ 99% fixture parity, ≥ 98% corpus parity** vs legacy DAG under shadow mode. See RFC §6 for the full delivery plan.

## Child issues

### Ring 1 — Types & contracts
- [x] #910 — Scope-resolution types + constants in `gitnexus-shared`
- [x] #911 — LanguageProvider hook interface extensions

### Ring 2 — SHARED (pure logic, to `gitnexus-shared`)
- [x] #912 — `Scope` / `ScopeTree` / `PositionIndex` (generalizes closed #902)
- [x] #913 — `DefIndex` / `ModuleScopeIndex` / `QualifiedNameIndex`
- [x] #914 — `MethodDispatchIndex` build function over `HeritageMap`
- [x] #915 — SCC-aware finalize algorithm (bounded fixpoint)
- [x] #916 — `resolveTypeRef` (strict helper)
- [x] #917 — `ClassRegistry` / `MethodRegistry` / `FieldRegistry` + evidence composition
- [x] #918 — Shadow-mode diff/comparison logic

### Ring 2 — PACKAGE-LOCAL (integration + I/O, to `gitnexus/`)
- [x] #919 — `ScopeExtractor` driver (tree-sitter + provider hooks → shared ScopeTree)
- [x] #920 — `parse-worker.ts` integration — emit `ParsedFile` artifacts
- [x] #921 — Finalize orchestrator
- [x] #922 — Per-language import-target resolution adapters
- [x] #923 — Shadow harness + parity dashboard
- [x] #924 — `REGISTRY_PRIMARY_<LANG>` flag routing
- [x] #925 — `ReferenceIndex` emission to LadybugDB

### Ring 3 — Per-language migrations (parallel; one ticket per `SupportedLanguages` member)
- [x] #926 — LANG-python *(first rollout; biggest calibration signal)*
- [x] #934 — LANG-csharp
- [x] #927 — LANG-typescript
- [x] #928 — LANG-javascript
- [x] #929 — LANG-java
- [x] #930 — LANG-go
- [x] #931 — LANG-ruby
- [x] #932 — LANG-rust
- [x] #933 — LANG-kotlin
- [x] #935 — LANG-cpp
- [x] #936 — LANG-c
- [x] #937 — LANG-swift
- [x] #938 — LANG-php
- [x] #939 — LANG-dart
- [x] #940 — LANG-vue
- [x] #941 — LANG-cobol *(regex provider; validates parse-source-agnostic contract)*

### Ring 4 — DAG retirement (gated)
- [x] #942 — Delete call-resolution DAG stages 1–4
- [x] #943 — Delete `ResolutionContext.resolve`, `TieredCandidates`, legacy plumbing
- [x] #944 — Delete shadow harness

### Ring 5 — Performance + docs
- [ ] #945 — Calibrate `EvidenceWeights` against corpus parity
- [ ] #946 — Benchmark finalize phase
- [x] #947 — Update ARCHITECTURE.md + skill docs
- [ ] #948 — Close #429 (centralized confidence constants)

## How to contribute

**Ring 3 language tickets are the natural _good first issue_** for external contributors who know a given language. Each is self-contained: one `scopes.scm` (or regex tagger for COBOL), a few `LanguageProvider` hooks, a fixture set, and shadow-mode parity verification. See RFC §5 for the extraction contract.

**Ring 2 plumbing (#912–#925), Ring 4 deletions (#942–#944), Ring 5 calibration (#945–#948)** are core-team work.

## Critical path

`Ring 1 (#910, #911) → Ring 2 (#912–#925) → all production Ring 3 (#926–#941) → Ring 4 (#942–#944)`

Ring 3 languages can draft `scopes.scm` and fixture sets in parallel with Ring 2 — the contract in RFC §5.1 is stable. Ring 5 floats.

## Status

| Ring | State |
|------|-------|
| Ring 1 | Ready to start |
| Ring 2 SHARED | Blocked on Ring 1 (#910 #911) |
| Ring 2 PKG | Blocked on Ring 2 SHARED |
| Ring 3 | Blocked on Ring 2 (can draft `scopes.scm` + fixtures in parallel) |
| Ring 4 | Blocked on all production Ring 3 languages flipped + stable for one release cycle |
| Ring 5 | Can run alongside any ring |

title: RING2-SHARED-4: SCC-aware finalize algorithm with bounded fixpoint
body:
**Ring 2 SHARED** · Parent: #909 · Depends on: #910 #911 · [RFC §3.2 Phase 2](https://www.notion.so/346dc50b6ed281cfaacbe480bf231d50)

## Scope
Implement the cross-file finalize algorithm as pure logic: SCC-aware topological processing with bounded fixpoint link pass for cyclic imports.

## Deliverables
- [ ] `gitnexus-shared/src/finalize-algorithm.ts`:
  - Tarjan SCC over the raw import graph (O(V+E))
  - Topological processing of the SCC condensation DAG
  - Bounded fixpoint link pass within each SCC, capped at `N = |edges in SCC|`
  - Edges still unlinked after cap marked `linkStatus: 'unresolved'`
  - Wildcard expansion: `import * from M` → one `BindingRef` per exported name
  - Re-export flattening with `transitiveVia` populated
  - Module-scope bindings materialization, delegating precedence to `provider.mergeBindings`
  - Dynamic imports rule: string-literal targets linked normally; runtime-computed → `kind: 'dynamic-unresolved'`, no `BindingRef`
- [ ] Pure function interface
- [ ] Unit tests: acyclic, single-SCC cycle, multi-SCC, wildcard chains, re-export chains, dynamic-unresolved edges

## Acceptance
- Cyclic imports (A↔B) finalize without hanging.
- Hard cap prevents infinite loops on malformed sources.
- Unresolved edges retain the `linkStatus: 'unresolved'` marker for the capped-signal rule in §4v2.
- Disjoint SCCs can be processed in parallel (algorithm exposes SCC-DAG boundaries).

## Depends on
- #910 #911 #912 #913

title: RING2-SHARED-5: resolveTypeRef strict helper
body:
**Ring 2 SHARED** · Parent: #909 · Depends on: #910 #911 #912 · [RFC §4.6](https://www.notion.so/346dc50b6ed281cfaacbe480bf231d50)

## Scope
Strict single-return type resolver used by `Registry.lookup` Step 2 and by callers resolving `TypeRef`s. Narrower contract than `Registry.lookup`: no name-only global fallback, only strict origins, fails fast on non-type shadowing.

## Deliverables
- [ ] `gitnexus-shared/src/resolve-type-ref.ts`:
  - `resolveTypeRef(ref: TypeRef, model, providers): SymbolDefinition | null`
  - Strict origins: `['local', 'import', 'namespace', 'reexport']`
  - Starts scope walk from `ref.declaredAtScope` (not call site)
  - Non-type shadowing binding → returns `null` (fails fast, no global fallback)
  - Dotted fallback via `QualifiedNameIndex.byQualifiedName` (no name-only global)
- [ ] Unit tests: param annotation, return annotation, aliased import, re-exported type, shadowed by local variable, qualified type name, missing type

## Acceptance
- Behavior matches RFC §4.6 pseudocode verbatim.
- Returns `null` rather than a low-confidence guess when ambiguous.
- `resolveTypeRef({ rawName: 'User', declaredAtScope: parameterScope, source: 'parameter-annotation' })` on `def save_user(user: Account)` where `Account` is an aliased import of `User` resolves to the `User` class def.

title: RING2-PKG-1: ScopeExtractor driver (tree-sitter + provider hooks → shared ScopeTree)
body:
**Ring 2 PKG** · Parent: #909 · Depends on: #910 #911 #912 · [RFC §5.3](https://www.notion.so/346dc50b6ed281cfaacbe480bf231d50)

## Scope
The central extractor driver in `gitnexus/`. Consumes `readonly Capture[]` from providers and builds the shared `ScopeTree` + attaches declarations, imports (raw), type bindings, and reference sites.

## Deliverables
- [ ] `gitnexus/src/core/ingestion/scope-extractor.ts`:
  - `extract(captures, filePath, provider): ParsedFile`
  - Pass 1: build `ScopeTree` (uses `provider.resolveScopeKind`, `provider.shouldCreateScope`)
  - Pass 2: attach `ownedDefs` + local `bindings` (uses `provider.bindingScopeFor`)
  - Pass 3: collect raw `ImportEdge[]` (with `targetModuleScope`/`targetDefId` null — linked in finalize)
  - Pass 4: collect `typeBindings` (uses `provider.interpretTypeBinding`)
  - Pass 5: collect reference sites (uses `provider.classifyCallForm`)
- [ ] Enforces invariants centrally (non-module has parent; parent range contains child; sibling ranges don't overlap)
- [ ] Unit tests with a mock provider emitting synthetic captures

## Acceptance
- Source-agnostic: equally consumes captures from tree-sitter or COBOL's regex tagger.
- One AST walk per language (inside `provider.emitScopeCaptures`); five capture-passes but zero further AST traversal.
- No `Tree` type leaks into the central driver.
