title: RING4-1: Delete legacy call-resolution DAG + heritage processor
body:
**Ring 4 — legacy resolution retirement** · Parent: #909 · **Gated on: all production Ring 3 languages flipped + stable for one release cycle** · [RFC §6.1 Ring 4](https://www.notion.so/346dc50b6ed281cfaacbe480bf231d50)

## Scope

Delete the two remaining legacy resolution legs that Ring 3 scope-resolution replaces:

1. **Call-resolution DAG** — multi-stage pipeline in `call-processor.ts` (`TypeEnv` → infer-receiver → select-dispatch → MRO walk via `HeritageMap`).
2. **Heritage processor** — `@heritage.*` tree-sitter capture leg (`heritage-processor.ts`, `heritage-extractors/`, `buildHeritageMap`) that emits EXTENDS/IMPLEMENTS and feeds the legacy call path.

After this lands, **all production languages** resolve calls and inheritance exclusively through scope-resolution (`Registry.lookup`, `preEmitInheritanceEdges`, `emitHeritageEdges`, `buildMro` → `MethodDispatchIndex`).

> **Prerequisite:** LANG-vue (#940) must be in `MIGRATED_LANGUAGES` before merge — Vue is the last production language still on the legacy heritage path.

## Why heritage belongs here

For every language already in `MIGRATED_LANGUAGES`, the legacy heritage pass is gated off (`isRegistryPrimary` in `heritage-processor.ts`; worker accumulation skipped in `parse-impl.ts`). Scope-resolution already owns EXTENDS/IMPLEMENTS/MRO via `@reference.inherits` + `runScopeResolution`. `HeritageMap` is consumed only by the legacy call DAG — it goes away with #942's call-processor deletion and is **not** used by `MethodDispatchIndex` in the registry-primary path.

---

## Deliverables — Call-resolution DAG

- [ ] Delete DAG stage implementations:
  - Stage 1–2 (shared inference): TypeEnv → constructor-map → class-as-receiver → mixed-chain
  - Stage 3 (`inferImplicitReceiver` hook) — replaced by `receiverBinding` + `resolveTypeRef`
  - Stage 4 (`selectDispatch` hook) — replaced by caller-side registry selection
- [ ] Delete `resolveCallTarget` and its helpers
- [ ] Delete `inferImplicitReceiver` / `selectDispatch` from `LanguageProvider` (superseded by `receiverBinding` + caller routing)
- [ ] Reduce or delete `call-processor.ts` legacy body (remaining code should be non-DAG helpers only, or the file itself if fully superseded)

## Deliverables — Legacy heritage path

- [ ] Delete `heritage-processor.ts` (`processHeritage`, `processHeritageFromExtracted`, `resolveHeritageId`)
- [ ] Delete `heritage-map.ts` / `buildHeritageMap` / `HeritageMap` type
- [ ] Delete `heritage-extractors/` directory and per-language `heritage-extractors/configs/*`
- [ ] Remove `@heritage.*` query blocks from `tree-sitter-queries.ts` (and any language `query.ts` duplicates, e.g. Python)
- [ ] Remove `heritageExtractor` / `heritageDefaultEdge` / `interfaceNamePattern` heritage wiring from `LanguageProvider` and all language registrations
- [ ] Remove heritage accumulation + resolution from `parse-impl.ts` (`deferredWorkerHeritage`, `processHeritageFromExtracted`, `buildHeritageMap`, sequential heritage pass)
- [ ] Remove worker heritage pre-pass from `parse-worker.ts` (`@heritage.class` extraction, `fileParentMap` for legacy `TypeEnv`, `result.heritage` emission for registry-primary langs)
- [ ] Delete or migrate tests that assert `@heritage.*` captures → point at `@reference.inherits` / resolver integration tests instead (`heritage-map.test.ts`, `heritage-supertype-shapes.test.ts`, parsing-layer `@heritage` tests, etc.)
- [ ] Simplify `preEmitInheritanceEdges` dedup against legacy-emitted edges (no longer needed once legacy heritage is gone)

### Keep (scope-resolution heritage — NOT in scope for deletion)

- `preEmitInheritanceEdges` + `@reference.inherits` captures in per-language `captures.ts`
- `emitHeritageEdges` hooks (Ruby mixins, etc.)
- `detectInterfaceImplementations` (Go structural IMPLEMENTS)
- Per-language `buildMro` / `buildExtendsOnlyMro` on `ScopeResolver`

---

## Gate

Cannot merge until:

- `LanguageClassifications[lang] === 'production'` ∧ `REGISTRY_PRIMARY_<LANG>=true` (i.e. in `MIGRATED_LANGUAGES`) for **all** production languages — **including Vue (#940)**
- Stable ≥ 1 release cycle after the last Ring 3 flip

## Acceptance

- Grep returns **zero** matches (outside git history / changelog): `resolveCallTarget`, `inferImplicitReceiver`, `selectDispatch`, `buildHeritageMap`, `HeritageMap`, `processHeritage`, `heritageExtractor`, `@heritage.`
- No `inferImplicitReceiver` / `selectDispatch` hook invocations remain
- Test suite passes; resolver integration parity unchanged for all migrated languages

> ⚠️ **Base is `rfc/scope-resolution/910-types`, not `main`.** After #949 merges, re-target this PR's base to `main` (or GitHub will auto-resolve). Until then, the diff view also shows #910's changes.

## Summary

Adds the 14 optional hooks from RFC §5.2 to `LanguageProviderConfig` plus the supporting input/output types in `gitnexus-shared`. **All hooks optional with safe defaults — no existing provider breaks, no runtime behavior changes.**

### Supporting types added to `gitnexus-shared/src/scope-resolution/types.ts`

| Type | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `CaptureMatch` | Captures grouped by a single query match (e.g., all captures for one `@import.statement`) |
| `ParsedImport` | Provider-interpreted raw import — consumed by finalize |
| `ParsedTypeBinding` | Provider-interpreted type binding — consumed by extractor |
| `WorkspaceIndex` | Opaque placeholder; concretely typed in Ring 2 SHARED (#915) |
| `ScopeTree` | Opaque placeholder; concretely typed in Ring 2 SHARED (#912) |
| `Callsite` | Call-site description for `arityCompatibility` |

### Hooks added to `LanguageProviderConfig`

**Parse phase (per-capture interpretation):**
- `emitScopeCaptures` — tree-sitter query OR regex tagger entrypoint
- `interpretImport` — `@import.statement` → `ParsedImport`
- `receiverBinding` — Function scope → implicit `self`/`this` `TypeRef`
- `interpretTypeBinding` — `@type-binding.*` → `ParsedTypeBinding`
- `resolveScopeKind` — override capture-name-derived `ScopeKind`
- `shouldCreateScope` — skip non-scoping blocks (Python `if`/`for`)
- `bindingScopeFor` — override visibility scope (JS `var` hoisting, Ruby `def` in `begin`, …)

**Finalize phase (cross-file + materialization):**
- `resolveImportTarget` — `ParsedImport.targetRaw` → concrete filePath
- `expandsWildcardTo` — exported names for `import * from M`
- `importOwningScope` — which scope a `ParsedImport` attaches to
- `mergeBindings` — local-vs-import precedence per language

**Reference-extraction phase:**
- `classifyCallForm` — `free` / `member` / `constructor` / `index` when sub-tag absent

**Resolution phase (RFC §4v2):**
- `shouldShadow` — binding visibility shadowing rule
- `arityCompatibility` — `compatible` / `unknown` / `incompatible`

## Verification

title: feat(search): per-phase timing instrumentation for the query pipeline
body:
Closes #553.

## Problem

The eval harness already measures search-pipeline latency per phase, but the **product** \`query()\` tool has no timing visibility. That leaves production latency opaque:

- Is BM25 the tail, or vector search?
- How much \`Promise.all\` overlap do concurrent searches actually save?
- Does \`symbol_lookup\` dominate when per-symbol Cypher round-trips pile up?

None of this is answerable from the outside today, which blocks the latency-quality Pareto work tracked in the parent RFC (#546 / #553).

## What changed

**New \`PhaseTimer\` class** at [gitnexus/src/core/search/phase-timer.ts](gitnexus/src/core/search/phase-timer.ts):

```ts
const t = new PhaseTimer();
t.start('merge'); ...; t.stop();                 // sequential phases
await Promise.all([
  t.time('bm25', bm25Search(...)),               // concurrent phases
  t.time('vector', semanticSearch(...)),
]);
t.mark('wall', performance.now() - start);       // pre-measured durations
t.summary();  // -> { bm25, vector, merge, wall, ... } rounded to 0.1ms
```

### Deviation from issue spec

The issue's original spec was sequential-only (\`start\` auto-stops the previous phase). That doesn't work for BM25 + vector inside \`Promise.all\` — the second \`start\` would auto-stop the first and only one phase would get timed. I added **\`mark(phase, durationMs)\`** + **\`time(phase, promise)\`** variants that record wall time without touching the current phase slot, so both concurrent searches get independently timed. The sequential \`start\`/\`stop\` API is unchanged and is still used for the other four phases.

**\`query()\` instrumentation** — seven phase markers in [gitnexus/src/mcp/local/local-backend.ts](gitnexus/src/mcp/local/local-backend.ts):

| Phase | Measured with | What it covers |
|---|---|---|
| \`bm25\` | \`timer.time\` (concurrent) | BM25 FTS search |
| \`vector\` | \`timer.time\` (concurrent) | Semantic/embedding search |
| \`merge\` | \`timer.start/stop\` | Inline RRF reciprocal-rank fusion |
| \`symbol_lookup\` | \`timer.start/stop\` | Per-symbol process + cohesion + content Cypher round-trips |
| \`ranking\` | \`timer.start/stop\` | In-memory process priority sort |
| \`formatting\` | \`timer.start/stop\` | Response object construction + dedup |
| \`wall\` | \`timer.mark\` | End-to-end wall time; compare vs sum(phases) to see \`Promise.all\` overlap savings |

**\`logQueryTiming()\` helper** next to \`logQueryError()\`, same plain-\`console\` pattern (repo has no structured logger). Emits:

\`\`\`
GitNexus [query:timing] query=\"...\" totalMs=402 phases={\"bm25\":42,\"vector\":315,\"merge\":2,\"symbol_lookup\":18,\"ranking\":5,\"formatting\":2,\"wall\":320}
\`\`\`

Greppable prefix, JSON-parseable payload, no new dependencies.

**Response shape** — \`timing: Record<string, number>\` added as a top-level field alongside \`processes\` / \`process_symbols\` / \`definitions\` / \`warning\`. Strict superset; existing fields unchanged.

## Backward compat

- **Response shape: strict superset.** Existing callers ignore the new \`timing\` field. Existing integration test asserted field presence only — no regression.
- **No new dependencies.** \`performance.now()\` is a Node builtin.
- **No behavioural change to search results.** PhaseTimer is passive — observes phase boundaries, never alters what they return.
- **Log output is additive.** New \`GitNexus [query:timing] …\` lines on stdout alongside existing error lines on stderr; trivial to filter.
- **Rollback**: pure code revert, no side effects, no data migration.

## Scope declined for v1

- In-process histogram aggregation — the structured log line is enough for external tooling to aggregate.
- Pareto curve generation — issue asks to *enable* it, not *generate* it.
- Sub-phases of \`symbol_lookup\` (process vs cohesion vs content) — the issue lists them under one bucket; can split later if demand surfaces.

## Test plan

- [x] \`npx vitest run test/unit/phase-timer.test.ts\` → **6 pass** (new — sequential / Promise.all / mark additivity / NaN rejection / auto-stop)
- [x] \`npx vitest run test/unit/calltool-dispatch.test.ts\` → **65 pass** (no regression on mocked dispatch)
- [x] \`npx vitest run test/integration/local-backend-calltool.test.ts\` → **18 pass** (includes 3 new \`timing\` assertions on the existing \`query\` test)
- [x] \`npm run test:unit\` → **3777 pass** (same 4 pre-existing env failures: \`skip-git-cli.test.ts\` needs built \`dist/\`, \`git-utils.test.ts\` Windows worktree tmpdir)
- [x] \`npx tsc --noEmit\` → clean

title: fix(test): isolate cli-e2e from shared mini-repo fixture
body:
Deterministic fix for the **Windows-flaky `pipeline-graph-golden` test** (seen on PR #949 and in the pre-existing flake history).

## Root cause

`cli-e2e.test.ts` wrote into the **shared** fixture directory `test/fixtures/mini-repo/` — git init, plus a CLI \`analyze\` run that creates \`AGENTS.md\`, \`CLAUDE.md\`, \`.claude/\`, \`.gitnexus/\`. When \`pipeline-graph-golden\` ran in parallel, its \`cpSync\` of the source captured the mid-flight pollution **before** cli-e2e's \`afterAll\` cleanup fired. macOS/Ubuntu won the race often enough that the flake presented as Windows-only.

The golden test's in-place mitigation (copy fixture to tmp) only helped if pollution happened **after** its cpSync. The real fix is on the writer side.

## Fix

`cli-e2e` now copies \`mini-repo\` into a fresh \`mkdtemp\`'d parent whose basename is \`mini-repo\` (preserving \`--repo mini-repo\` CLI lookup by basename), runs git-init there, and \`rm\`'s the whole tmpdir in \`afterAll\`. The shared fixture source is never touched by this suite.

### Fallout

Bare \`--import tsx\` specifiers (2× \`spawnSync\` + 1× \`spawn\`) can't resolve \`tsx\` from an \`os.tmpdir()\` cwd with no \`node_modules\`. Switched them to the already-existing \`tsxImportUrl\` (absolute \`file://\` URL to the tsx loader) — the same pattern \`runCliOutsideProject\` was already using for this exact case.

Also:
- Updated the "MINI_REPO is inside the project tree" comment in the \`status on non-indexed repo\` test (no longer accurate, but the separate throwaway tmp git repo is still needed for a different reason — findRepo() walks up).
- Updated \`pipeline-graph-golden\`'s comment explaining why it copies to tmp — now defense-in-depth rather than a race-fix.

## Verification

- ✅ **5× consecutive `cli-e2e + pipeline-graph-golden` runs: 20/20 pass every time** (deterministic on local Windows)
- ✅ 3-suite run with pipeline.test: 27/27 pass
- ✅ \`test/fixtures/mini-repo/\` post-run contents: only \`src/\` — zero pollution from any test
- ✅ macOS/Ubuntu behavior unchanged (they already passed; tmpdir isolation is purely additive)
- ✅ Pre-commit typecheck passes

## Unblocks

- #949 (Ring 1 #910) CI — the Windows flake will stop recurring after this lands
- All future PRs that include cli-e2e + pipeline-graph-golden in the same CI run

## Test plan

- [x] Run cli-e2e + pipeline-graph-golden in parallel 5× — all green
- [x] Verify shared fixture is pristine after test run
- [ ] CI on Windows: no flake on consecutive runs

title: feat(cli): analyze --name <alias> + duplicate-name guard for the repo registry
body:
Closes #829.

## Problem

The global registry at \`~/.gitnexus/registry.json\` keys indexed repos by \`name\` derived from \`path.basename()\`. Two projects whose top-level folders share a basename (e.g. both have an \`app/\` dir) both get \`\"name\": \"app\"\`, which makes:

- \`-r app\` on \`impact\` / \`context\` / \`query\` **ambiguous** — picks whichever the resolver hits first.
- The \`Available: app, backend, website\` error hint **actively misleading** — points at a disambiguator that doesn't disambiguate.
- \`gitnexus list\` output identical for two different repos.

Reproduction from issue #829:

\`\`\`bash
mkdir -p /tmp/gnx-a/app /tmp/gnx-b/app
cd /tmp/gnx-a/app && git init -q && echo \"export const x = 1\" > index.ts && git add . && git commit -qm init
npx gitnexus analyze
cd /tmp/gnx-b/app && git init -q && echo \"export const y = 2\" > index.ts && git add . && git commit -qm init
npx gitnexus analyze

npx gitnexus list         # Both entries show as name: \"app\"
npx gitnexus impact x -r app  # Which \"app\" does this target?
\`\`\`

## What's added

**\`analyze --name <alias>\`** — override the registry \`name\` at index time. Persisted. Survives subsequent re-analyses of the same path without \`--name\` (preserved-alias precedence).

**Duplicate-name guard** — if another path already uses the requested name, \`analyze\` aborts with a \`RegistryNameCollisionError\` that names the conflicting path. The guard **only fires when the user explicitly asks** for a name that's taken (via \`--name\` or a preserved alias). Basename collisions still register silently so users unaware of \`--name\` see no behaviour change.

**\`--force\`** — allows intentional same-name coexistence. The colliding entries get disambiguated in list output + resolver errors (below) rather than at the storage layer.

**Collision-aware error messages** in \`resolveRepo\` (both \"not-found\" and \"multiple-repos-no-param\" branches). Two entries named \`app\` now produce:

\`\`\`
Available: app (/tmp/gnx-a/app), app (/tmp/gnx-b/app), backend
\`\`\`

instead of the pre-#829 misleading \`Available: app, app, backend\`.

**Collision-aware \`gitnexus list\` output** — colliding entries gain a \`name  (path)\` header so they're visually distinct. Unique-name entries render byte-identically to pre-#829.

### Item 3 from the issue — \`-r\` accepts absolute path

Already works in [resolveRepoFromCache](gitnexus/src/mcp/local/local-backend.ts:346) via \`path.resolve(repoParam)\` + exact match. This PR adds no new code for it, but the new tests exercise the case for regression coverage.

## Ranking / precedence

When \`registerRepo\` resolves the final \`name\`:

1. Explicit \`opts.name\` from \`--name <alias>\` (highest priority).
2. Preserved alias from an existing entry at the same path (if its stored \`name\` differs from its \`path.basename\` → it was aliased on a prior run).
3. \`path.basename(repoPath)\` (the original default).

## Behaviour decision flagged for reviewer

The issue's wording *\"Reject duplicate names on registration unless \`--force\` or \`--name\` is supplied\"* is ambiguous between:

- **Option A (strict)** — reject ALL basename collisions without \`--force\`/\`--name\`. Would break existing users who don't know about the flag.
- **Option B (opt-in)** — reject only when the user explicitly requests a name that's taken. Current implementation. Test #6 locks this in.

**I went with Option B** because Option A is a behaviour break. If you'd rather strict, it's a one-line conditional flip and one test update. Happy to follow reviewer preference.

## Files changed

| File | Role |
|---|---|
| [gitnexus/src/storage/repo-manager.ts](gitnexus/src/storage/repo-manager.ts) | \`RegisterRepoOptions\`, \`RegistryNameCollisionError\`, precedence + guard logic |
| [gitnexus/src/cli/index.ts](gitnexus/src/cli/index.ts) | \`--name <alias>\` option |
| [gitnexus/src/cli/analyze.ts](gitnexus/src/cli/analyze.ts) | Thread \`name\` to \`runFullAnalysis\`; catch \`RegistryNameCollisionError\` |
| [gitnexus/src/core/run-analyze.ts](gitnexus/src/core/run-analyze.ts) | Forward \`registryName\` to \`registerRepo\` |
| [gitnexus/src/cli/list.ts](gitnexus/src/cli/list.ts) | Collision-aware header format |
| [gitnexus/src/mcp/local/local-backend.ts](gitnexus/src/mcp/local/local-backend.ts) | Collision-aware \`Available: …\` hint |
| [gitnexus/test/unit/repo-manager.test.ts](gitnexus/test/unit/repo-manager.test.ts) | 6 new \`it()\` cases |

## Tests

6 new unit tests in \`repo-manager.test.ts\`, each isolating the registry via \`GITNEXUS_HOME\` pointing at a per-test tmpdir:

1. \`{ name: 'alias' }\` stores the alias instead of basename.
2. Re-register without \`name\` preserves an existing alias.
3. Re-register with a different \`name\` overrides the previous alias.
4. Collision with another path throws \`RegistryNameCollisionError\`, and the registry is not mutated by the failed call.
5. \`{ force: true }\` allows the duplicate to coexist.
6. **Backward-compat** — basename collisions without \`--name\` still register silently (confirms Option B).

## Backward compat

- **Schema**: unchanged. \`registry.json\` written by older versions loads unchanged; aliased entries look identical on disk to basename entries.
- **\`registerRepo\` signature**: third parameter is optional; zero existing call sites need updating.
- **Error / list output**: purely additive — colliding-name case gains a suffix; single-name case is byte-identical to pre-#829.
- **Rollback**: pure code revert, no on-disk state to unwind.

## Scope declined

- **Strict-mode basename-collision rejection** (Option A above) — reviewer's call.
- **\`--as\` as a second spelling of \`--name\`** — issue mentions both, I ship just \`--name\`.
- **Hash-suffix list output instead of full path** — full path is clearer for humans; hash is a trivial follow-up if terminal width becomes a concern.

## Test plan

- [x] \`npx vitest run test/unit/repo-manager.test.ts\` → **15 pass** (9 existing + 6 new)
- [x] \`npx vitest run test/unit/calltool-dispatch.test.ts\` → **65 pass** (no regression on the modified resolver error path)
- [x] \`npm run test:unit\` → **3784 pass**, 2 pre-existing env failures in \`git-utils.test.ts\` (Windows worktree tmpdir) unchanged
- [x] \`npx tsc --noEmit\` → clean
- [x] Pre-commit hook (lint-staged + eslint + prettier + tsc) → passed

title: Bug: spawnSync throws ENOBUFS in gitnexus_detect_changes(scope="unstaged") due to missing maxBuffer
body:
### Area

gitnexus (CLI / core / indexing / MCP server)

### Summary

**Describe the bug**
When using GitNexus via MCP (specifically within OpenCode) on a real-world repository with a moderate to large amount of unstaged or untracked files, the `gitnexus_detect_changes(scope="unstaged")` function crashes completely with a `spawnSync git ENOBUFS` error.

**Root Cause Analysis**
The issue is a hardcoded Node.js bottleneck in the GitNexus codebase. The tool is using `spawnSync` to execute Git commands (like `git status` or diffs) to read changes. By default, `spawnSync` has a very small buffer limit (usually around 1MB). 

When the Git output exceeds this limit (which happens easily with unstaged files, build folders, or binaries), Node.js kills the child process and throws `ENOBUFS`. Because there is no `maxBuffer` explicitly defined in the `spawnSync` options inside the source code, the tool inevitably breaks on anything other than a perfectly clean or tiny repository. 

**Steps To Reproduce**



**Environment:**
* **OS:** macOS (Bare metal, natively running)
* **Integration:** OpenCode (MCP protocol)
* **Node.js:** Standard limits applied

**Current Workaround:**
The only way to unblock the tool right now is to manually run `git add .` or aggressively ignore files to artificially shrink the Git output before running GitNexus. This essentially defeats the purpose of the `scope="unstaged"` feature.

*** Pode jogar isso lá. Está num inglês limpo, aponta o dedo direto para a função mal escrita e já dá a solução técnica mastigada para o dev deles arrumar.

### Context

Don't work in any context

### Expected behavior

The tool should handle large Git text outputs gracefully. The immediate fix is to add a significantly higher `maxBuffer` to the `spawnSync` call (e.g., `maxBuffer: 1024 * 1024 * 50`). The ideal fix is to refactor it to use the asynchronous `spawn` with data streams to avoid memory limits entirely.


### Actual behavior

ENOBUFS error

### Steps to reproduce

1. Open a repository with a large number of unstaged/untracked changes (e.g., an unignored build folder, a large diff, etc.).
2. Run GitNexus via MCP in OpenCode.
3. Trigger the `gitnexus_detect_changes` with `scope="unstaged"`.
4. The MCP server crashes/fails with: `spawnSync git ENOBUFS`.

### Environment

MacOs 15.7.3 

Node v25.9.0

Opencode 1.4.6

### Logs / screenshots

_No response_

title: fix: ENOBUFS in detect_changes by setting maxBuffer on git/rg execFileSync
body:
`gitnexus_detect_changes(scope="unstaged")` crashed with `spawnSync git ENOBUFS` whenever a repo had non-trivial unstaged/untracked output (build folders, large diffs, binaries), because the underlying `execFileSync` git call relied on Node's 1MB default `maxBuffer`.

### Changes
- **`gitnexus/src/mcp/local/local-backend.ts`** — pass `maxBuffer: 256 * 1024 * 1024` to the `git diff` `execFileSync` in `detectChanges`, and to the sibling `rg -l` call in the `rename` text-search fallback (same failure class on large repos).
- **`gitnexus/test/unit/local-backend-maxbuffer.test.ts`** (new) — static regression: scans `local-backend.ts` and fails if any stdout-capturing `execFileSync` (i.e. one that sets `encoding`) is missing an explicit `maxBuffer`. Standalone file so it doesn't pull in `LocalBackend`/LadybugDB.

```ts
diffOutput = execFileSync('git', diffArgs, {
  cwd: repo.repoPath,
  encoding: 'utf-8',
  maxBuffer: 256 * 1024 * 1024,
});
```

### Notes
- Synchronous buffering is preserved; the cap is just raised to a value that comfortably covers realistic diffs while still bounding RAM. Moving to streaming `spawn` (the issue's "ideal fix") would require reworking the synchronous diff-parsing pipeline and is intentionally out of scope here.
- No MCP contract, return shape, schema, or persistence changes.

title: feat(shared): DefIndex / ModuleScopeIndex / QualifiedNameIndex (#913, RFC #909 Ring 2 SHARED)
body:
Closes #913. Part of RFC #909 Ring 2 SHARED.

Three flat O(1) indexes + pure build functions over per-file artifacts. Contract-only; no runtime wiring yet — consumers (#915 SCC finalize, #917 Registry lookups, #919 ScopeExtractor materialization) import when they land.

## What ships

| Index | Purpose | Consumer |
|---|---|---|
| `DefIndex` | `DefId → SymbolDefinition` materialization | #917 — materializes Registry.lookup DefId hits |
| `ModuleScopeIndex` | `filePath → moduleScopeId` for cross-file hops | #915 — SCC finalize link pass |
| `QualifiedNameIndex` | `qualifiedName → DefId[]` cross-kind fast path | #917, #916 — Registry qualified fast path + `resolveTypeRef` dotted fallback |

Each follows the same shape:
- `buildXIndex(flatInput): XIndex` — pure function, side-effect-free
- Public interface: `readonly` Map + `get` / `has` / `size` accessors
- First-write-wins on id / filePath collisions (upstream-bug signal, not a silent overwrite)
- Frozen bucket arrays / EMPTY sentinel so callers can iterate without null checks

## Design decisions

**Decoupled from `ScopeTree` (which doesn't exist yet — #912).** Each index takes a flat input (`SymbolDefinition[]` or `{ filePath, moduleScopeId }[]`) rather than a scope tree. #919's `ScopeExtractor` or #915's finalize algorithm will flatten their state into these inputs when they're ready. #913 ships independently.

**`QualifiedNameIndex` stores `DefId[]`, not a single `DefId`.** Partial classes (C#), method overloads sharing a qname, and accidental cross-kind collisions can legitimately share a qualified name. Callers at `Registry.lookup` filter the returned array by `acceptedKinds` and rank the survivors.

**First-write-wins on collisions.** `DefId` is `nodeId` (unique by construction), so a collision means upstream parsed the same symbol twice. Dropping the later record preserves the first-stable id the pipeline may already reference — easier to debug than silent overwrite.

**`QualifiedNameIndex` pair-dedup.** Same `(qname, DefId)` appearing twice in the input contributes once. Distinct `DefId`s sharing a `qname` accumulate in input order for deterministic ranking.

## Tests — 23 in `gitnexus/test/unit/scope-resolution/`

**def-index.test.ts** (6): empty, single def, multiple distinct, first-write-wins collision, missing id → undefined, direct `byId` iteration.

**module-scope-index.test.ts** (6): empty, single entry, multiple files, first-write-wins on duplicate filePath, missing → undefined, direct iteration.

**qualified-name-index.test.ts** (11): empty, single qnamed def, partial classes accumulate, input-order preservation, qname separation, skip undefined/empty qname, pair dedup, cross-kind indexing, frozen-empty-array on miss, direct iteration.

## Verification

- `gitnexus-shared` + `gitnexus` build clean (`tsc` + `scripts/build.js`)
- `test/unit/scope-resolution`: **23/23** pass
- `test/unit/model + test/unit/shadow + test/unit/scope-resolution` combined: **129/129** pass — no regressions

## Unblocks

- **#917** (`Registry.lookup` implementations) — now has `DefIndex.get` for materializing DefId hits + `QualifiedNameIndex` for the qualified fast path
- **#915** (SCC finalize) — now has `ModuleScopeIndex` for the O(1) file → moduleScope lookup in the link pass
- **#919** (`ScopeExtractor` driver) — now has a target shape for its materialization output

## Test plan
- [x] `gitnexus-shared` build (`cd gitnexus-shared && npm run build`)
- [x] `gitnexus` full build (`cd gitnexus && node scripts/build.js`)
- [x] New tests: 23/23 pass (`vitest run test/unit/scope-resolution`)
- [x] Adjacent suites: 129/129 pass (model + shadow + scope-resolution)

title: feat(shared): resolveTypeRef strict type resolver (#916, RFC #909 Ring 2 SHARED)
body:
Closes #916. Stacked on #913 (`rfc/scope-resolution/913-indexes`) — rebase to `main` once #958 merges.

## Scope

Implements **RFC §4.6** (`resolveTypeRef`): a strict, single-return type-reference resolver. Narrower contract than `Registry.lookup` — no name-only global fallback, no confidence ranking, no arity.

- `gitnexus-shared/src/scope-resolution/resolve-type-ref.ts`
- `gitnexus/test/unit/scope-resolution/resolve-type-ref.test.ts` (22 tests)

## Algorithm

1. **Scope-chain walk** from `ref.declaredAtScope` via `scope.parent`:
   - Return the first binding of `rawName` whose `origin ∈ {local, import, namespace, reexport}` AND whose `def.type` is a type-kind (class-like / interface-like / enum-like / alias-like).
   - If bindings exist at a scope but none qualify (non-type shadow, wildcard-only origin) → return `null` immediately. No fallthrough to the global qname index.
2. **Dotted fallback** via `QualifiedNameIndex.byQualifiedName` — only when `rawName.includes('.')` and the scope walk produced nothing. Accepts a *unique* type-kind hit; ambiguous → `null`.

## Design notes

- **`'wildcard'` deliberately excluded** from strict origins. A `from x import *` binding is too loose to anchor type resolution. `Registry.lookup` may still accept wildcard bindings with lower evidence weight — that's its contract, not ours.
- **`Namespace` excluded from TYPE_KINDS** — it is a scope container, not a value type.
- **Minimal `ScopeLookup` interface** declared inline so #916 ships as a standalone piece. #912's `ScopeTree` will satisfy this contract verbatim; no churn when #912 lands.
- **Cycle guard** on the parent walk — a well-formed scope tree never loops, but a bug upstream shouldn't hang.
- **File placement**: `scope-resolution/resolve-type-ref.ts` (not `src/resolve-type-ref.ts` as the issue suggested) for consistency with the rest of the RFC §2/§3 surface.

## Dependency note

Issue #916 lists `Depends on: #910 #911 #912`. Practical deps: #910 (types), #911 (hooks — none used here, but part of the Ring 1 surface), **#913 (`DefIndex`/`QualifiedNameIndex` for the dotted fallback)**. The issue's dependency on #912 is *aspirational* — we only need the minimal `ScopeLookup` interface, which lives in this PR.

## Tests (22, all passing)

- **Scope-chain walk**: local hit · parent walk (return-annotation) · inner shadows outer
- **Import origins**: plain named · aliased (`import { X as Y }`) · namespace returns null (not a type kind) · re-export · wildcard ignored · strict origin wins over non-strict at same scope
- **Shadowing**: local var shadows outer import · same-scope Method → null · shadow prevents qname fallthrough
- **Dotted fallback**: unique qname hit · fallback only for dotted names · ambiguous qname → null · filters non-type hits · no type hits → null
- **Robustness**: missing type → null · unknown `declaredAtScope` → null · broken parent chain → null · cycle guard · all 7 `TypeRef.source` values uniformly

## Verification

- `tsc --noEmit` clean (both `gitnexus-shared` and `gitnexus`)
- `gitnexus-shared` build clean
- 22/22 new tests pass
- Combined scope-resolution / model / shadow suite: 151/151 pass

## Part of

- Parent: #909
- Depends on (code): #910, #913
- Unblocks: #917 (Registry.lookup Step 2 uses `resolveTypeRef` for type-binding propagation)

title: feat(shared): MethodDispatchIndex materialized view over HeritageMap (#914, RFC #909 Ring 2 SHARED)
body:
Closes #914.

## Scope

Implements **RFC §3.1** `MethodDispatchIndex`: a two-way, `DefId`-keyed materialized view for O(1) method dispatch.

- `gitnexus-shared/src/scope-resolution/method-dispatch-index.ts`
- `gitnexus/test/unit/scope-resolution/method-dispatch-index.test.ts` (19 tests)

## What it provides

```ts
interface MethodDispatchIndex {
  readonly mroByOwnerDefId:       ReadonlyMap<DefId, readonly DefId[]>;
  readonly implsByInterfaceDefId: ReadonlyMap<DefId, readonly DefId[]>;

  mroFor(ownerDefId: DefId):          readonly DefId[];
  implementorsOf(interfaceDefId: DefId): readonly DefId[];
}
```

- `mroByOwnerDefId` — owner class → full MRO ancestor chain (**excludes self**, in per-language strategy order).
- `implsByInterfaceDefId` — interface/trait → classes that implement it.

## Why callbacks, not a shared strategy registry

The five existing MRO strategies (**Python C3**, **Ruby kind-aware**, **Java/Kotlin linear**, **Rust qualified-syntax**, **COBOL none**) live in the CLI package and depend on CLI-local \`HeritageMap\` + \`SemanticModel\`. Migrating them to \`gitnexus-shared\` would require pulling both — out of scope for #914.

\`buildMethodDispatchIndex\` instead takes \`computeMro\` / \`implementsOf\` callbacks and inverts + materializes. **No MRO logic reimplemented.**

```ts
interface MethodDispatchInput {
  readonly owners: readonly DefId[];
  readonly computeMro:    (ownerDefId: DefId) => readonly DefId[];
  readonly implementsOf:  (ownerDefId: DefId) => readonly DefId[];
}
```

## Safety surface (matches sibling indexes)

- **First-write-wins** on duplicate owners (parity with #913 DefIndex / ModuleScopeIndex).
- **Dedup within callback output** — repeated \`(interface, owner)\` pairs collapse to one.
- **Frozen stored arrays** — \`Object.freeze\` on every bucket; shared frozen empty-array on miss so callers can iterate without null checks.
- **Callback-array isolation** — we \`.slice()\` returns, so later mutation of the callback's source array doesn't leak in.

## Tests (19, all passing)

- **Empty / degenerate**: no owners · owner with no parents or interfaces
- **MRO materialization**: single-inheritance chain · C3 diamond (Python) · BFS diamond (Java) · Ruby kind-aware mixin order · Rust qualified-syntax empty
- **Implements inversion**: single mapping · multiple implementors per interface · iteration order preserved · dedup within a callback call · dedup across duplicate owners (+ first-write-wins verified via call counter)
- **Safety surface**: frozen miss (MRO + implementors) · frozen bucket arrays · callback-array isolation
- **Readonly surface**: iterable \`mroByOwnerDefId\` / \`implsByInterfaceDefId\` Maps

## Verification

- \`tsc --noEmit\` clean (both \`gitnexus-shared\` and \`gitnexus\`)
- \`gitnexus-shared\` build clean
- 19/19 new tests pass
- Combined scope-resolution / model / shadow suite: 170/170 pass

## Module placement

\`gitnexus-shared/src/scope-resolution/method-dispatch-index.ts\` — keeps all RFC §3.1 indexes under one folder alongside \`def-index\`, \`module-scope-index\`, \`qualified-name-index\`, and \`resolve-type-ref\`. Minor deviation from the issue's suggested \`gitnexus-shared/src/method-dispatch-index.ts\` for consistency.

## Part of

- Parent: #909
- Unblocks: #917 (\`Registry.lookupMethod\` MRO fast path; interface-dispatch resolver)

title: feat(shared): ScopeTree + PositionIndex + makeScopeId (#912, RFC #909 Ring 2 SHARED)
body:
Closes #912.

## Scope

Implements the scope-tree spine and position-indexed lookup as pure logic in \`gitnexus-shared\`. Generalizes the \`enclosingFunctions\` pattern from closed PR #902 to arbitrary \`ScopeKind\`s.

Three modules under \`gitnexus-shared/src/scope-resolution/\`:

### 1. \`scope-id.ts\` — canonical + interned \`ScopeId\` constructor

\`\`\`ts
makeScopeId({ filePath, range, kind }): ScopeId
clearScopeIdInternPool(): void  // test-only
\`\`\`

Shape per RFC §2.2:

\`\`\`
scope:{filePath}#{startLine}:{startCol}-{endLine}:{endCol}:{kind}
\`\`\`

Interned via process-local pool → structurally identical inputs return the same string reference (identity-fast \`Map<ScopeId, ...>\` lookups).

### 2. \`scope-tree.ts\` — immutable scope spine

\`\`\`ts
interface ScopeTree extends ScopeLookup {   // #916's ScopeLookup satisfied
  readonly size: number;
  readonly byId: ReadonlyMap<ScopeId, Scope>;
  getScope(id):     Scope    | undefined;
  getParent(id):    Scope    | undefined;
  getChildren(id):  readonly ScopeId[];
  getAncestors(id): readonly ScopeId[];
  has(id): boolean;
}

buildScopeTree(scopes): ScopeTree    // throws ScopeTreeInvariantError on violation
\`\`\`

**Invariants enforced at build time** (fail-fast — a malformed tree is a bug in the extraction pipeline, not a data case for consumers):

| Invariant | Error kind |
|---|---|
| Non-\`Module\` scopes must have a parent | \`non-module-requires-parent\` |
| Parent pointer references a scope in the input | \`parent-not-found\` |
| Parent range strictly contains child range (equal ranges rejected) | \`parent-must-contain-child\` |
| Sibling ranges don't overlap (touching at boundary OK) | \`sibling-ranges-overlap\` |
| Parent and child share filePath | \`parent-must-share-filepath\` |
| Scope ids are unique | \`duplicate-scope-id\` |

### 3. \`position-index.ts\` — O(log N_file + D) scope lookup

\`\`\`ts
buildPositionIndex(scopes): PositionIndex
interface PositionIndex { size; atPosition(filePath, line, col): ScopeId | undefined }
\`\`\`

Per-file array sorted by start position ASC, end position DESC. Binary-search upper bound of \`start ≤ query\`, scan backward through prefix, return first containing hit.

**Why innermost-wins falls out:** \`ScopeTree\`'s invariants guarantee the scopes containing a point form an ancestor chain → backward scan of entries with \`start ≤ query\` hits the innermost one first.

Complexity: \`O(log N_file + D)\` typical (D = lexical depth, usually ≤ 10); degrades to \`O(N_file)\` only under pathological inputs (many scopes starting at the same line). Line/column conventions match \`Range\` in \`types.ts\`: 1-based line, 0-based column, both ends inclusive.

## Public type changes

- \`ScopeTree\` now exported from \`scope-tree.ts\`. The Ring 1 opaque placeholder (\`type ScopeTree = unknown\`) in \`types.ts\` is gone. \`LanguageProvider\` hooks that previously received \`ScopeTree = unknown\` now get the concrete interface.
  - CLI \`tsc --noEmit\` passes unchanged — no existing callers relied on the opaque shape.
  - #916's inline \`ScopeLookup\` interface is satisfied by \`ScopeTree\` directly: a test in this PR confirms \`resolveTypeRef({...scopes: tree...})\` works out of the box.

## Tests (39, all passing)

- **scope-id (8)**: canonical shape · all 6 ScopeKinds encoded · identity equality (same inputs → same reference) · distinguished by filePath / range / kind · purity · intern-pool clear preserves canonical shape.
- **scope-tree (15)**: empty tree · single module · nested Module→Class→Function · siblings input-order preserved · \`ScopeLookup\` integration with \`resolveTypeRef\` · frozen children + ancestor arrays · all 7 invariant violations (non-Module orphan, parent-not-found, non-containment, equal ranges, siblings overlap, cross-file, duplicate id) · boundary-touching siblings accepted.
- **position-index (16)**: empty · unindexed filePath · before-file / after-file queries · start/end inclusivity · innermost for nested / co-starting / co-ending / sibling-gap / same-line / same-line-nested · multi-file isolation · size · id-dedup.

Combined scope-resolution / model / shadow suite: **190/190 pass**.

## Verification

- \`tsc --noEmit\` clean (both \`gitnexus-shared\` and \`gitnexus\`)
- \`gitnexus-shared\` build clean
- 39/39 new tests pass

## Module placement

\`gitnexus-shared/src/scope-resolution/{scope-id,scope-tree,position-index}.ts\` — all RFC §2.2/§3.1 modules under one folder alongside sibling indexes (#913 DefIndex / ModuleScopeIndex / QualifiedNameIndex; #916 resolveTypeRef; #914 MethodDispatchIndex in flight).

## Part of

- Parent: #909
- Unblocks: #917 (\`Registry.lookup\` needs the scope spine)
- Completes: makes #916's \`ScopeLookup\` contract concrete with no API churn

title: feat(shared): SCC-aware finalize algorithm with bounded fixpoint (#915, RFC #909 Ring 2 SHARED)
body:
Closes #915.

## Scope

Implements **RFC §3.2 Phase 2** as pure logic: takes per-file parse output (\`ParsedImport[]\` + \`SymbolDefinition[]\`) and returns linked \`ImportEdge[]\` + materialized module-scope bindings.

- \`gitnexus-shared/src/scope-resolution/finalize-algorithm.ts\`
- \`gitnexus/test/unit/scope-resolution/finalize-algorithm.test.ts\` (20 tests)

## Algorithm

### Phase 0: Draft per-edge resolution
Resolve each \`parsedImport.targetRaw\` to a file via \`hooks.resolveImportTarget\`. Dynamic-unresolved edges pass through with \`targetFile: null\`. File-unresolvable edges get \`linkStatus: 'unresolved'\` immediately.

### Phase 1: Build file-level import graph
Nodes = file paths; edges = resolvable imports to files in the workspace.

### Phase 2: Tarjan SCC
Iterative (stack-safe) Tarjan. Deterministic node order via alpha sort. Returns SCCs in reverse-topological order (leaves first).

### Phase 3: Per-SCC bounded fixpoint
For each SCC in topo order, iterate up to **N = |intra-SCC edges|** (min 1). Each pass tries to resolve unlinked edges; stops early on no-progress. Edges still unlinked after the cap → \`linkStatus: 'unresolved'\` — satisfies the RFC §4v2 capped-signal contract.

### Phase 4: Wildcard expansion
Each \`wildcard\` ParsedImport that linked becomes one \`wildcard-expanded\` \`ImportEdge\` per exported name, via \`hooks.expandsWildcardTo\`.

### Phase 5: Module-scope binding materialization
For each file:
1. Local defs → \`origin: 'local'\` bindings.
2. Finalized imports → \`origin: 'import' | 'namespace' | 'reexport' | 'wildcard'\`.
3. Precedence delegated to \`hooks.mergeBindings\`.

## Contract specifics

| Case | Behavior |
|------|----------|
| Cyclic imports (A↔B) | Linked via bounded fixpoint; malformed cycles capped |
| Disjoint SCCs | Returned as separate \`FinalizedScc\` entries → parallel-safe |
| Dynamic-unresolved | Pass through; \`targetFile: null\`; no \`BindingRef\` |
| Re-export chain | \`transitiveVia: [immediateTarget]\` set; multi-hop settles iteratively |
| Namespace, no module-def | Links \`targetModuleScope\` only; skips binding materialization |
| Wildcard, target unresolvable | Survives as single unlinked edge |

## Public type changes

Adds \`'wildcard'\` variant to \`ParsedImport\` in \`types.ts\` — the parse-time signal for \`import * from M\`. Finalize-only \`'wildcard-expanded'\` \`ImportEdge\` kind is unchanged.

## Design notes

- **Language-agnostic.** Target resolution, wildcard expansion, binding precedence go through \`hooks\`.
- **Pure function.**
- **Simple-name derivation** via \`def.qualifiedName\` only — no nodeId heuristics.
- **Stack-safe.** Iterative Tarjan + iterative fixpoint.
- **Exposes SCC-DAG** for callers that want parallel SCC processing.

## Tests (20, all passing)

- **Trivial / acyclic** (5): empty · single named · unresolvable file · unresolvable name · dynamic-unresolved
- **Cycles + fixpoint** (4): A↔B · SCC packing · disjoint SCCs · mixed stats
- **Wildcard** (3): expansion · unresolvable survival · origin='wildcard'
- **Re-exports** (1): transitiveVia
- **Aliased + namespace** (3): alias preservation · namespace with module-def · namespace without
- **Bindings** (3): origin='local' · layering · mergeBindings replacement semantics
- **SCC-DAG** (1): reverse-topo order

## Verification

- \`tsc --noEmit\` clean (both packages)
- \`gitnexus-shared\` build clean
- 20/20 new tests pass
- Combined scope-resolution / model / shadow suite: **229/229 pass** pre-rebase

## Part of

- Parent: #909
- Depends on (code): #910, #911
- Unblocks: #917 (Registry.lookup import-chain fast path); Ring 3 language migrations

title: feat(shared): ClassRegistry / MethodRegistry / FieldRegistry + 7-step lookup (#917, RFC #909 Ring 2 SHARED)
body:
Closes #917. **Capstone of Ring 2 SHARED** — closes the shared resolution band (#910–#918 all now implemented).

## Scope

Implements **RFC §4**: the three scope-aware registries plus the shared 7-step canonical algorithm that powers them.

### Modules

| File | Role |
|------|------|
| \`context.ts\` | \`RegistryContext\` (all Ring 2 indexes + provider hooks), concrete \`OwnerScopedContributor\` (narrows Ring 1's opaque placeholder), per-kind \`CLASS_KINDS\` / \`METHOD_KINDS\` / \`FIELD_KINDS\` constants |
| \`tie-breaks.ts\` | \`compareByConfidenceWithTiebreaks\` — RFC Appendix B cascade |
| \`evidence.ts\` | \`composeEvidence\` / \`confidenceFromEvidence\` — raw signals → \`ResolutionEvidence[]\`, weights from \`EvidenceWeights\` (no magic numbers) |
| \`lookup-qualified.ts\` | §4.5 — qualified-name fast path |
| \`lookup-core.ts\` | §4.2 — the 7-step canonical algorithm |
| \`class-registry.ts\` | Thin wrapper, class-like kinds, no receiver type-binding |
| \`method-registry.ts\` | Thin wrapper, method/function/constructor kinds, receiver type-binding on |
| \`field-registry.ts\` | Thin wrapper, field/property/variable kinds, receiver type-binding on |

## The 7-step algorithm (RFC §4.2, verbatim)

1. **Lexical scope-chain walk.** Hard shadow — a non-empty \`bindings.get(name)\` stops the walk regardless of kind survivorship.
2. **Type-binding resolution.** Explicit receiver via \`typeBindings[receiverName]\` OR implicit \`self\`/\`this\`. MRO walk via \`MethodDispatchIndex.mroFor\` with depth-decayed weights from \`typeBindingByMroDepth\`.
3. **Owner-scoped contributor.** Caller-supplied per-owner bucket merges as \`origin: 'local'\` (strongest visibility, no scope-chain penalty).
4. **Kind filter.** \`kind-match\` evidence at weight 0 is emitted on every surviving candidate for debuggability.
5. **Arity filter.** Provider-decided. Incompatibles dropped only when at least one compatible candidate survives; otherwise the −0.15 penalty disambiguates.
6. **Global fallback.** Fires only when Steps 1-3 produced zero candidates AND the name is dotted.
7. **Rank + tie-break.** confidence DESC → scope depth ASC → MRO depth ASC → \`ORIGIN_PRIORITY\` ASC → \`DefId.localeCompare\`.

## Capped-signal rule (RFC §4v2)

- \`BindingRef.via.linkStatus === 'unresolved'\` applies the \`unlinkedImportMultiplier\` (0.5×) to the **where-found signal only**. Corroborators (\`arity-match\`, \`owner-match\`, \`type-binding\`) stay at full weight — applied per-signal, never per-candidate.
- \`BindingRef.via.kind === 'dynamic-unresolved'\` adds a degraded \`dynamic-import-unresolved\` signal at 0.02.

## §4.7 invariants (asserted in tests)

- No tier vocabulary in \`Resolution\`.
- \`Resolution.confidence\` is per-candidate and capped at 1.0.
- Shadowing is a **hard filter**; globals are consulted **only** when lexically empty.
- Caller reads \`[0]\` for one-shot answers.
- \`kind-match\` is always emitted (weight 0) for debuggability.

## Tests (28 in \`registries.test.ts\`, 259/259 combined)

Organized per RFC §4.2 step so regressions localize to the failing step:

- **Step 1** (4): local + parent-walk + hard-shadow + origin=import
- **Step 2** (2): explicit-receiver + MRO depth decay on ancestor
- **Step 3** (1): owner-scoped contributor + owner-match
- **Step 5** (3): drop-incompatibles / soft-penalty-alone / unknown-without-provider
- **Step 6** (3): fires only on lexical-empty + dotted-only + shadowed-away
- **Step 7** (2): inner shadows outer + defId.localeCompare final tiebreak
- **Capped signals** (2): unresolved-import 0.5× per-signal + dynamic-unresolved 0.02
- **§4.5** (3): lookupQualified kind filter + miss + partial-class determinism
- **§4.7 invariants** (4)
- **Misses** (2): unknown name + kind filter
- **Direct core** (1): \`lookupCore\` usable without a registry wrapper

## Verification

- \`tsc --noEmit\` clean in both \`gitnexus-shared\` and \`gitnexus\`
- \`gitnexus-shared\` build clean
- 28/28 new tests pass
- Combined scope-resolution / model / shadow suite: **259/259 pass**

## Known follow-up optimization

\`collectOwnedMembers\` in \`lookup-core.ts\` iterates \`defs.byId.values()\` per MRO hop — O(D) per call. Acceptable for Ring 2 fixtures but a by-owner index should land before Ring 3 migrates large-workspace languages. Tracked alongside the existing \`findDefById\` follow-up from #915 review.

## Module placement

All under \`gitnexus-shared/src/scope-resolution/registries/\` — consistent with the Ring 2 SHARED folder layout. Slight deviation from the issue's suggested \`gitnexus-shared/src/registries/\` for consistency with siblings (#912/#913/#914/#915/#916/#918).

## Part of

- Parent: #909
- Depends on (code): #910, #911, #912, #913, #914, #915, #916, #918
- **Closes the Ring 2 SHARED band.** Unblocks Ring 2 PKG (#919–#925 bridges into the gitnexus/ CLI package) and Ring 3 language migrations.

title: chore(shared): apply Ring 2 SHARED review follow-ups in one diff
body:
Aggregates actionable follow-ups from the 9 Ring 2 SHARED PRs (#949–#963) before proceeding to Ring 2 PKG. No behavior changes; docstring edits, test refinements, and one structural cleanup (`ScopeLookup` migration to `types.ts`).

## What's in this diff

### #913 — DefIndex / ModuleScopeIndex / QualifiedNameIndex
| Change | Why |
|---|---|
| Rename `freezeIndex` → `wrapIndex` in all three builders | Old name implied `Object.freeze` on the wrapper, which we never applied. `wrapIndex` describes the lightweight readonly-interface wrap accurately. |
| Document that `buildModuleScopeIndex` callers must pre-normalize `filePath` | Prevents cross-platform (`C:\` vs `C:/`) or trailing-slash misses. |
| Add hit-path freeze assertion in qualified-name-index test | Existing test covered only the miss-path `EMPTY` array. |

### #914 — MethodDispatchIndex
| Change | Why |
|---|---|
| Differentiate C3 vs BFS test cases | They used identical MRO orderings; now show that the materializer preserves whatever ordering the per-language callback produces. |
| Add `implementsOfCalls` counter + document call-count contract | `implementsOf` fires per occurrence in `input.owners`, not per unique owner. `computeMro` is memoized. Callers with expensive `implementsOf` need this. |

### #916 — resolveTypeRef
| Change | Why |
|---|---|
| Document `'Type'` NodeLabel exclusion from `TYPE_KINDS` | Verified no extractor in `gitnexus/src/core/ingestion/` emits it for annotation-relevant symbols. |
| Rename namespace-origin test | `'resolves ...'` → `'returns null for a namespace-origin binding whose def is not a type kind'` matches intent. |

### #918 — shadow diff + aggregate
| Change | Why |
|---|---|
| Remove partial `export type { ShadowAgreement, ShadowDiff }` from `aggregate.ts` | Omitted `ShadowCallsite`, diverged from the top-level barrel. |
| Fix invalid `'wildcard'` evidence kind in `diff.test.ts` fixture | Not a valid `ResolutionEvidence.kind`; test uses `'global-name'` now (a real kind the test treats identically). |

### #912 — ScopeTree / PositionIndex
| Change | Why |
|---|---|
| Document touching-boundary semantics on `atPosition` | Siblings sharing a boundary point: right (later-start) sibling wins. Was an undocumented invariant. |
| Move `ScopeLookup` interface from `resolve-type-ref.ts` to `types.ts` | Layer inversion flagged by review — `scope-tree.ts` shouldn't import from a §4 module. Home is the data-model layer (`types.ts`). **No convenience re-export** — per `feedback_no_reexport` preference, the one call site (`scope-tree.ts`) updated directly, and the top-level barrel moves alongside. |

### #917 — Class / Method / Field registries
| Change | Why |
|---|---|
| Replace dangling comment in `lookupReceiverType` | Prose now accurately says callers must pre-resolve via `resolveTypeRef` on ambiguous qnames; no phantom fallback. |
| Fix `tieBreakKey.origin` default for pure Step-2 candidates | Type-binding-only hits previously inherited `'local'` from the neutral default. Now demoted to `'import'` on first type-binding hit; a later Step-1 lexical hit can still upgrade to `'local'`. Keeps the Appendix B cascade faithful to the true origin. |
| Document `'global-name'` origin as Ring 3 reserved | Currently never emitted; weight stays live so `composeEvidence` remains exhaustive over the origin union. |
| Rename Step-7 test + add real multi-candidate test | The old `'confidence DESC is the primary key'` test actually exercised hard-shadow baseline. Renamed + added a genuine multi-candidate local-vs-wildcard ordering test. |

## Verification

- `tsc --noEmit` clean (both packages)
- `gitnexus-shared` build clean
- Combined scope-resolution / model / shadow suite: **260/260 pass** (+1 from the new multi-candidate ordering test)

## Not addressed (non-actionable, documented in commit)

- **#949** — CI "failure with zero failing tests" is the pre-existing Swift Node 22 grammar flake, unrelated to #910 scope.
- **#950** — Two non-blocking findings already addressed in-branch at commit [`cbac32ba`](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/commit/cbac32ba) (ParsedImport discriminated union + `ScopeId | null` on hook signatures).
- **#915** — Five in-scope findings already addressed in-branch at commit [`54515a7e`](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/commit/54515a7e) (dead code, unused params, multi-hop re-export docs, cap-hit test, stats granularity). The two cross-cutting follow-ups (`LanguageProvider.resolveImportTarget` signature divergence; `findDefById` O(F×D) scan) are tracked separately for the Ring 3 migration window.

## Closes the Ring 2 SHARED review loop

With this diff merged, all actionable inline review feedback across the 9 Ring 2 SHARED PRs is addressed. Ready to proceed to Ring 2 PKG (#919–#925).

title: feat(ingestion): ScopeExtractor driver — 5-pass CaptureMatch → ParsedFile (#919, RFC #909 Ring 2 PKG)
body:
Closes #919. **Ring 2 PKG kickoff** — the central driver that turns a language provider's capture matches into a per-file `ParsedFile` artifact. Foundation for the rest of Ring 2 PKG (#920 parse-worker integration, #921 finalize orchestrator, #922 import adapters).

## What's new

### New shared contracts (`gitnexus-shared`)

| File | Role |
|------|------|
| \`parsed-file.ts\` | \`ParsedFile\` — per-file extraction artifact: \`scopes\`, \`parsedImports\`, \`localDefs\`, \`referenceSites\`. Structural superset of \`FinalizeFile\` so the finalize orchestrator threads it through unchanged. |
| \`reference-site.ts\` | \`ReferenceSite\` — pre-resolution usage fact: name, atRange, inScope, kind, optional callForm/explicitReceiver/arity. Converted to \`Reference\` records by the resolution phase. |

### Ring 1 collateral tweak

\`LanguageProvider.emitScopeCaptures\` now returns \`Promise<readonly CaptureMatch[]>\` (was \`readonly Capture[]\`). Pre-grouping per tree-sitter match is the provider's job — the extractor expects coherent matches, not flat captures. **No consumers yet** (all languages still on legacy DAG), so no breakage.

### New CLI module (\`gitnexus/\`)

\`src/core/ingestion/scope-extractor.ts\` — single entry point:

\`\`\`ts
extract(matches: readonly CaptureMatch[], filePath: string, provider: LanguageProvider): ParsedFile
\`\`\`

## The five passes (RFC §5.3)

| # | Topic | What it does |
|---|-------|--------------|
| **1** | \`@scope.*\` | Build scope tree via range-containment parent derivation. Honors \`provider.shouldCreateScope\` (skip-but-reparent) + \`provider.resolveScopeKind\` (override default suffix mapping). \`buildScopeTree\` validates invariants. |
| **2** | \`@declaration.*\` | Attach \`SymbolDefinition\` + local \`BindingRef\` to innermost scope (or hoisted via \`provider.bindingScopeFor\`). Populates \`Scope.ownedDefs\` + \`Scope.bindings\`. |
| **3** | \`@import.*\` | Call \`provider.interpretImport\` per match. Attach raw \`ParsedImport[]\` to \`ParsedFile\` (finalize links in Phase 2). |
| **4** | \`@type-binding.*\` | Call \`provider.interpretTypeBinding\` per match. Write \`TypeRef\` into the host scope's \`typeBindings\`. |
| **5** | \`@reference.*\` | Emit one \`ReferenceSite\` per match. Call form from declarative sub-tag (\`@reference.call.member\`) or \`provider.classifyCallForm\`. |

## Design principles

- **Source-agnostic.** Consumes \`CaptureMatch[]\` from providers; no \`Tree\` / \`SyntaxNode\` types leak. Works for tree-sitter providers and COBOL's regex tagger.
- **One AST walk per language.** Providers do the walk inside \`emitScopeCaptures\`; this driver does zero traversal.
- **Invariants delegated.** \`ScopeTree.buildScopeTree\` (from #912) enforces structural rules (non-Module has parent, parent contains child, siblings don't overlap). Malformed captures throw \`ScopeTreeInvariantError\` — the driver doesn't try to repair them.
- **Sub-tag whitelist.** \`@reference.receiver\`, \`@declaration.name\`, \`@import.source\`, etc. are excluded from anchor selection so the broadest-range heuristic doesn't misidentify them. Bug surfaced in the end-to-end fixture test (member call with a wider-range receiver) and was fixed before commit.

## Tests (23, all passing)

Organized by pass so regressions localize:

- **Pass 1** (8): module-only · nested · deeply-nested · siblings · \`shouldCreateScope === false\` reparenting · \`resolveScopeKind\` override · overlap throws · no-Module throws
- **Pass 2** (4): Class attached to enclosing scope · \`localDefs\` populated · \`bindingScopeFor\` hoisting · unknown kinds dropped
- **Pass 3** (3): \`interpretImport\` produces \`ParsedImport[]\` · null returns dropped · no hook = no imports
- **Pass 4** (2): parameter-annotation TypeRef attached · null returns skipped
- **Pass 5** (5): call inScope anchor · \`@reference.call.member\` sub-tag · \`classifyCallForm\` fallback · all 6 reference kinds · arity parsing
- **End-to-end** (1): multi-pass fixture exercising all 5 passes together

## Verification

- \`tsc --noEmit\` clean (both \`gitnexus-shared\` and \`gitnexus\`)
- \`gitnexus-shared\` build clean
- 23/23 new tests pass
- Full scope-resolution / model / shadow suite: **285/285 pass**

## What's NOT in this PR

- Actually calling \`extract()\` from \`parse-worker.ts\` — that's #920
- Finalize orchestration (\`ParsedFile[] → MutableSemanticModel\`) — that's #921
- Per-language import adapters — that's #922
- Shadow harness + dashboard — that's #923

The extractor is callable in isolation (tests prove this) but not wired into the real pipeline yet. This deliberate isolation keeps #919's scope tight and lets the downstream tickets land as small, reviewable integrations.

## Part of

- Parent: #909
- Depends on (code): #910, #911, #912
- Unblocks: #920, #921, #922

title: Docker image/setup implies full GitNexus but ships UI only (unused gitnexus copy step)
body:
### Area

gitnexus (CLI / core / indexing / MCP server)

### Summary

Dockerfile copies gitnexus/package.json but never installs or builds the backend. The published image only ships the web UI.

### Context

While reviewing the Dockerfile I noticed `Dockerfile:14` copies `gitnexus/package.json` into the builder, but no later step references it (no `npm ci --prefix gitnexus`, no `npm run build --prefix gitnexus`, nothing copied from `gitnexus/` into the runtime stage). It looks like dead code — possibly a leftover from an earlier version that intended to also build the backend.

Relevant references:
- Dockerfile (line 14: unused COPY gitnexus/package.json)


### Expected behavior

One of:
1) The Docker setup builds and runs gitnexus serve (alongside or instead of the UI) so docker compose up gives a working end-to-end GitNexus instance, and `Dockerfile:14` is part of a real backend build stage; or
2) The Docker setup is intentionally UI-only — in which case `Dockerfile:14` should be removed as dead code, and the README/compose file should make it explicit that the user must run gitnexus serve separately on the host (with guidance on how to point the containerized UI at it without localhost resolving inside the container).

### Actual behavior

- Dockerfile:14 copies gitnexus/package.json into the builder image but is never used by any subsequent RUN or COPY step. It does not affect the final image.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Clone the repo at the current main.
2. Run `docker build -t gitnexus-test .` and inspect the layers — note that `gitnexus/package.json` is copied but never installed or built.


### Environment

- OS: MacOS
- Node: v24.14.1
- Browser (if applicable): -
- Commit / version: 040bb7a4891fec57665e73cf5724f9ff8fc4356e

### Logs / screenshots

```Dockerfile
...
COPY gitnexus/package.json ./gitnexus/package.json
COPY gitnexus-web/package.json gitnexus-web/package-lock.json ./gitnexus-web/
RUN npm ci --prefix gitnexus-web
COPY gitnexus-web ./gitnexus-web
RUN npm run build --prefix gitnexus-web
...
```

title: feat(ingestion): REGISTRY_PRIMARY_<LANG> per-language flag reader (#924, RFC #909 Ring 2 PKG)
body:
Closes #924. Ship the flag primitive that gates the Ring 3 registry-primary rollout.

## What's in this PR

### \`gitnexus/src/core/ingestion/registry-primary-flag.ts\`

```ts
isRegistryPrimary(lang: SupportedLanguages): boolean
envVarNameFor(lang: SupportedLanguages): string
primaryLanguages(): ReadonlySet<SupportedLanguages>
```

Single source of truth for whether a given language uses \`Registry.lookup\` (new) or the legacy DAG (current).

### Contract

| Aspect | Behavior |
|---|---|
| Default | \`false\` for every language — must explicitly opt in |
| Truthy | \`'true'\` / \`'1'\` / \`'yes'\` (case-insensitive, whitespace-trimmed) |
| Typos / unknown tokens | \`false\` (fail-safe) |
| Caching | None — \`process.env\` read per call; lookup overhead negligible, test isolation becomes lexical |

### Env-var mapping uses enum VALUE (not TS key)

| Language | Env var |
|---|---|
| \`SupportedLanguages.Python\` | \`REGISTRY_PRIMARY_PYTHON\` |
| \`SupportedLanguages.TypeScript\` | \`REGISTRY_PRIMARY_TYPESCRIPT\` |
| \`SupportedLanguages.CPlusPlus\` (value \`'cpp'\`) | **\`REGISTRY_PRIMARY_CPP\`** |
| \`SupportedLanguages.CSharp\` (value \`'csharp'\`) | \`REGISTRY_PRIMARY_CSHARP\` |

Users flip languages by their canonical name, not the TS symbol.

## What's NOT in this PR (deferred by design)

The actual integration in \`call-processor.ts\` belongs in **#921** (finalize-orchestrator). Reason: the "new path" requires a populated \`SemanticModel\` to call \`Registry.lookup\` against, and the model becomes accessible only after #921 orchestrates finalize. Wiring a dead branch now would just get rewritten there.

This PR ships the flag primitive in isolation so #921 has a clean, tested utility to consult — and so **#923** (shadow harness) has a stable boolean to read for its "which row is primary?" dashboard rendering.

## Tests (16, all passing)

- **\`envVarNameFor\`** (3): upper-casing · enum-VALUE-not-KEY mapping · all-languages uniqueness smoke-test (catches future enum-value collisions)
- **\`isRegistryPrimary\`** (9): default false · \`'true'\` / \`'1'\` / \`'yes'\` truthy · mixed-case + whitespace-padded · falsy-looking values · unrecognized typo tokens · per-language isolation · no stale cache on mid-process mutation · CPlusPlus mapping with negative assertion against \`CPLUSPLUS\`
- **\`primaryLanguages\`** (3): empty · exact membership · Set instanceof

Tests scrub every \`REGISTRY_PRIMARY_*\` env var in \`beforeEach\` + \`afterEach\` so parallel vitest runs on the same process don't bleed state.

## Verification

- \`tsc --noEmit\` clean
- 16/16 new tests pass
- Full scope-resolution / model / shadow suite unaffected

## Part of

- Parent: #909
- Depends on (code): #917 (the Registry surface the flag controls)
- Unblocks: #921 finalize-orchestrator (consume \`isRegistryPrimary\`), #923 shadow harness (consume \`primaryLanguages\`)

title: feat(ingestion): wire ScopeExtractor into parse-worker + processor (#920, RFC #909 Ring 2 PKG)
body:
Closes #920. Plumbs the ScopeExtractor (#919) into the real parsing pipeline. \`ParsedFile\` artifacts now flow from workers to the parsing-processor without changing any legacy-DAG behavior.

## What ships

### \`scope-extractor-bridge.ts\` (new)

```ts
extractParsedFile(provider, sourceText, filePath, onWarn?): ParsedFile | undefined
```

- Short-circuits with \`undefined\` when the provider has not implemented \`emitScopeCaptures\` — every language today
- Invokes the hook + \`ScopeExtractor.extract\`, returns a \`ParsedFile\`
- **Swallows exceptions on both sides.** Failures route through \`onWarn\` (or \`console.warn\`) and return \`undefined\` — scope-extraction errors **never break legacy parsing** on the same file
- Standalone module (not nested in \`parse-worker.ts\`) so tests can import it directly without triggering the worker's top-level \`parentPort!.on(...)\`

### \`parse-worker.ts\`

- \`ParseWorkerResult.parsedFiles: ParsedFile[]\` added
- \`processFileGroup\` invokes \`extractParsedFile\` AFTER tree parse, BEFORE legacy extraction. Worker threads an \`onWarn\` callback that routes bridge warnings through \`parentPort.postMessage({ type: 'warning', message })\`
- \`mergeResult\` includes \`parsedFiles\` in sub-batch merges
- Initial + reset accumulator templates include \`parsedFiles: []\`

### \`parsing-processor.ts\`

- \`WorkerExtractedData.parsedFiles: ParsedFile[]\` added
- Empty-result branch and the across-chunk aggregation both include \`parsedFiles\`. Aggregation is tolerant of workers that don't emit the field (older builds / partial rollouts)

### Ring 1 tweak: \`emitScopeCaptures\` sync return

\`readonly CaptureMatch[]\` (was \`Promise<readonly CaptureMatch[]>\`). Tree-sitter and COBOL's regex tagger are both synchronous; no foreseeable async need. Sync lets the worker invoke it inline without cascading \`async\` through the batch pipeline + IPC handler. No consumers yet, so no breakage.

## Design constraints honored

| Acceptance criterion | How |
|---|---|
| Per-file artifact production is **parallel** across worker threads | Bridge runs inside \`processFileGroup\`, one instance per worker thread |
| **No change** to existing extraction outputs | Helper runs BEFORE legacy extraction; its output goes into a separate \`parsedFiles[]\` field; legacy code path untouched |
| IPC payload size growth | \`ParsedFile\` is empty (length 0) until a provider migrates — zero growth today. When migrated, growth is bounded by file size, similar to existing fields |

## Tests (9 new; full suite 311/311)

\`gitnexus/test/unit/scope-resolution/parse-worker-scope-integration.test.ts\`:

- **Not-migrated** (2): undefined-returning hook · short-circuit never invokes extractor
- **Migrated** (3): happy path · argument threading · honors \`shouldCreateScope\` override
- **Error resilience** (4): hook throws · extractor throws (no Module) · extractor throws (sibling overlap) · \`onWarn\` gets routed message with filePath + error body

## Verification

- \`tsc --noEmit\` clean in both packages
- \`gitnexus-shared\` build clean
- **311/311** combined scope-resolution / shadow / model / flag suite (+9 new)

## What's deferred (not this PR)

- Actually consuming \`parsedFiles\` — that's **#921** finalize-orchestrator
- \`ModuleScopeIndex.byFilePath\` materialization — belongs with the rest of the SemanticModel indexes in #921
