title: docs(ai-context): emit AUTO-GENERATED notice in marker block
body:
## Summary

Adds a single HTML comment immediately after `< gitnexus:start -->` in the block emitted by `npx gitnexus analyze`:

```html
< AUTO-GENERATED by `npx gitnexus analyze` (src/cli/ai-context.ts). Do NOT hand-edit between the gitnexus:start/gitnexus:end markers; rerun the CLI instead. Add prose in sections OUTSIDE this block. -->
```

## Motivation

A downstream consumer's `AGENTS.md` accumulated **two** `<!-- gitnexus:start -->` blocks (with only one `<!-- gitnexus:end -->`) because contributors hand-edited content between the markers — likely thinking that was where they were supposed to add MCP rules. The next `analyze` run would silently wipe those edits, which is a bad surprise.

Surfacing the contract in the file itself, on the very first line a human sees, prevents the class of bug without changing behavior.

## Changes

- `gitnexus/src/cli/ai-context.ts` — one new line in the template string.

## Risk

- **Cosmetic.** No runtime behavior change. Existing AGENTS.md / CLAUDE.md files get the notice on next `npx gitnexus analyze` run.
- The marker-replace logic in `replaceGitNexusBlock` already operates on `startIdx` / `endIdx` of the markers themselves, so the new line is included in/excluded from replacement just like every other line in the block.
- No tests touched (this template is plain text with no behavioral assertions in the test suite).

## Tested

- `npm test` (CLI suite) — unchanged behavior.
- Pre-commit (lint-staged + tsc) green.

title: fix(cli): translate Commander --no-stats into noStats option (#704)
body:
## Problem

Commander's negatable-boolean convention sets `options.stats = false` when `--no-stats` is passed — **not** `options.noStats = true`. The three call sites that forward CLI options into `runFullAnalysis` / `generateAIContextFiles` all read `options.noStats`, so the flag was silently ignored and volatile symbol/file counts always got written into `AGENTS.md` / `CLAUDE.md`.

Confirmed broken on 1.6.1 and 1.6.2.

## Fix

Add `?? (options?.stats === false)` fallback at all three call sites:

- `gitnexus/src/cli/analyze.ts:231` — `runFullAnalysis` options
- `gitnexus/src/cli/analyze.ts:301` — `generateAIContextFiles` in skills path
- `gitnexus/src/core/run-analyze.ts:382` — `generateAIContextFiles` in core path

No new API surface, no behaviour change when `--no-stats` is not passed (`options.stats` is `undefined` in that case, so `undefined === false` is `false` and the fallback doesn't fire).

Closes #704

title: wiki: module grouping collapses real source packages into ~4 pages while generating 10+ pages for IntelliJ .iml files
body:
### Area

gitnexus (CLI / core / indexing / MCP server)

### Summary

`gitnexus wiki` on a medium-sized Java module generates more pages for IntelliJ `.iml` files and Gradle config than for actual source code, while hundreds of Java classes are collapsed into a single "src-main" page.

### Context

Tried using `gitnexus wiki` on a subdirectory of the DataHub monorepo (`metadata-io/`), after discovering that running it on the full monorepo exceeded Anthropic's 1M-token context limit (separate issue — happy to file if useful). The wiki generation itself succeeded (exit 0, 471s) but the grouping/page structure produced is not a useful architectural map of the module.

### Expected behavior

Wiki pages should correspond to meaningful functional subsystems of the code — e.g. one page per Java package or per call-graph community. IDE/build metadata files (`.iml`, `gradle.lockfile`, `.idea/`) should not generate top-level module pages.

### Actual behavior

21 pages produced for `metadata-io/`:

| Category | Pages | Example files |
|---|---|---|
| IntelliJ `.iml` project files | **10** | `root-metadata-io-iml.md`, `root-oss-datahub-metadata-io-main-1-iml.md`, `root-oss-datahub-metadata-io-testgenerateddatatemplate-iml.md`, … |
| Gradle config | 2 | `root-build-gradle.md`, `root-gradle-lockfile.md` |
| README | 1 | `root-readme-md.md` |
| metadata-io-api | 3 | `metadata-io-api.md`, `metadata-io-api-src.md`, `metadata-io-api-metadata-io-api.md` (near-duplicate) |
| **Source tree** | **4** | `src.md`, `src-main.md` (~11 KB covering ~400 main Java files), `src-test.md`, `src-testfixtures.md` |
| Overview | 1 | `overview.md` |

3 modules failed — all non-code artifacts (`gma-create-all.sql`, `gma-drop-all.sql`, `Root`).

Specifically:

1. **`.iml` files get first-class module pages** — 10 of them, more than the source pages (4). These are IDE-generated project descriptors, not code modules.
2. **Hundreds of production Java classes share a single page.** `src-main.md` is one 11 KB markdown file that in my run focused almost entirely on the consistency framework. Substantial subsystems — `entity/ebean/`, `graph/elastic/`, `graph/neo4j/`, `aspect/validation/`, `search/`, `timeline/`, `systemmetadata/` — get no dedicated page, no mermaid diagram, and barely any text.
3. **The overview contradicts the page structure.** `overview.md` opens with an architecture diagram naming `AspectDao`, `ESBulkProcessor`, `TimelineServiceImpl`, `QueryFilterRewriteChain`, `PropertiesCollector`, etc., but its "Module Structure" section only lists `metadata-io-api` and `src`. The grouping step clearly has richer symbol data than it uses for page creation.

**Suggested fixes**

- **Exclude IDE / build metadata from module detection by default**: `*.iml`, `gradle.lockfile`, `.idea/`, and possibly de-prioritize `build.gradle` so it isn't treated as a top-level module. A `.gitnexusignore`-style convention seems to exist per `--help`; bundling sensible defaults would cover this.
- **Descend into language-aware package structure for Java/Kotlin.** JVM projects almost always have a flat `src/main/java/` root, so "one page per src root" effectively means "one page for the whole module." Walking `src/main/java/<package-path>/` and creating pages per package (or per sub-package cluster of size N) would produce useful output.
- **Use cluster count as the grouping signal** rather than filesystem layout. The analyzer already produced 779 clusters for `metadata-io/`; grouping by cluster + call-graph communities would yield meaningful per-subsystem pages even without language-specific heuristics.
- **Deduplicate pages**: `metadata-io-api.md` and `metadata-io-api-metadata-io-api.md` appear to be near-duplicates of the same module.

### Steps to reproduce

```bash
# Target repo: https://github.com/datahub-project/datahub (Java / Gradle / Spring monorepo)
# Target subdir: metadata-io/

git clone https://github.com/datahub-project/datahub
cd datahub

gitnexus analyze metadata-io --skip-git --skip-agents-md
# Output: 20,097 nodes | 52,381 edges | 779 clusters | 300 flows | 611 Java source files

gitnexus wiki metadata-io --model claude-sonnet-4-6
# Output: 21 pages generated in ~471s

ls metadata-io/.gitnexus/wiki/*.md
# See the table above — 10 of 21 pages are IntelliJ .iml metadata
```

### Environment

- OS: macOS (Darwin 25.1.0)
- Node: v22.22.0 (via mise)
- GitNexus: `1.6.2` (installed via `mise use npm:gitnexus@1.6.2`)
- LLM provider: Anthropic, `claude-sonnet-4-6`
- Target codebase: DataHub monorepo at commit `fdc3bd2`, `metadata-io/` subdirectory

### Logs / screenshots

**`gitnexus analyze` output:**

```
Repository indexed successfully (16.0s)
20,097 nodes | 52,381 edges | 779 clusters | 300 flows
/Users/pedro/dev/oss/datahub/metadata-io
```

**`gitnexus wiki` output:**

```
Wiki generated successfully (471.1s)
Mode: full
Pages: 21
Output: /Users/pedro/dev/oss/datahub/metadata-io/.gitnexus/wiki
Failed modules (3):
  - Root — gma-create-all.sql
  - Root — gma-drop-all.sql
  - Root
```

**Generated page listing** (`ls metadata-io/.gitnexus/wiki/*.md`):

```
metadata-io-api-metadata-io-api.md
metadata-io-api-src.md
metadata-io-api.md
overview.md
root-build-gradle.md
root-datahub-metadata-io-main-iml.md
root-gradle-lockfile.md
root-metadata-io-iml.md
root-oss-datahub-metadata-io-iml.md
root-oss-datahub-metadata-io-main-1-iml.md
root-oss-datahub-metadata-io-main-iml.md
root-oss-datahub-metadata-io-maingenerateddatatemplate-iml.md
root-oss-datahub-metadata-io-test-iml.md
root-oss-datahub-metadata-io-testfixtures-iml.md
root-oss-datahub-metadata-io-testfixturesgenerateddatatempla.md
root-oss-datahub-metadata-io-testgenerateddatatemplate-iml.md
root-readme-md.md
src-main.md
src-test.md
src-testfixtures.md
src.md
```

Happy to share the full `overview.md`, `src-main.md`, or `meta.json` if useful.

title: chore(web): bump vite 5.4.21 -> 6.4.2 (iter 1 of 3)
body:
## Summary

Step **1 of 3** of the iterative vite 5 → 8 upgrade for `gitnexus-web`. Single-line bump: `vite ^5.2.0` → `^6.4.2`. **Zero config or engine changes.**

## Why iterative

Dependabot #1040 attempted vite 5 → 8 in one shot and failed CI on `@tailwindcss/vite@4.1.18`'s peer range (`^5.2.0 || ^6 || ^7`, no `^8`). Splitting the upgrade into three small, independently revertable PRs lets each major bake on `main` and isolates regressions.

| PR | Bump | Other changes |
|----|------|---------------|
| **this PR** | vite 5 → 6.4.2 | none |
| next | vite 6 → 7.3.2 | `engines.node` → `^20.19.0 \|\| >=22.12.0`, `setup-node` pin to `20.19.0` |
| final | vite 7 → 8.0.10 | `@vitejs/plugin-react@^5.2.0`, `@tailwindcss/vite@^4.2.4`, `tailwindcss@^4.2.4`, `vitest@^4.x`, `@vitest/coverage-v8@^4.x` |

## Why this hop is safe

- `@tailwindcss/vite@4.1.18` already lists vite `^6` as a peer
- `@vitejs/plugin-react@5.1.x` already supports vite `^6`
- `vitest@3.2.4` peer is `vite ^5 || ^6 || ^7`
- Vite 6 still supports Node 18/20/22 — `engines.node` stays put
- None of vite 6's breaking changes (sass legacy API, postcss-load-config v6, `json.stringify` default, Environment API, fs.allow auto-detect) touch this app's `vite.config.ts` / `vitest.config.ts` surface

## Test plan

Local validation:
- [x] `npm install` clean (+4 / −8 packages, no peer warnings)
- [x] `npx tsc -b --noEmit` clean
- [x] `npm test` — 220 / 220 unit tests pass
- [x] `npm run build` — succeeds in 8.17s, dist tree shape matches main
- [x] Pre-existing warnings only (chunk size > 500 kB, `ProcessFlowModal` mixed import)

CI to confirm:
- [ ] Quality (typecheck-web)
- [ ] Tests (web unit + coverage)
- [ ] E2E (chromium against `gitnexus serve` + Vite dev server)
- [ ] Vercel preview renders mermaid + langchain deep import + sigma graph

## References

- Vite 6 migration guide: https://vite.dev/guide/migration
- Supersedes #1040

title: fix(ci): skip docker.yml tag-input validation on direct tag pushes
body:
## Summary

The Docker Build & Push workflow failed on the v1.6.3 tag push:
https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/actions/runs/24897853631/job/72907431113

\`\`\`
##[error]No tag provided to docker.yml — refusing to build/push.
\`\`\`

**Root cause:** The \"Validate tag input\" step runs on both \`workflow_call\` and \`push\` events, but on a tag push \`inputs.tag\` is always empty — the tag comes from \`github.ref\`. The guard was added in #983 with the intent of protecting the RC reusable-workflow path, but the \`|| push\` branch causes every real release to fail at that gate.

The downstream \"Verify tag matches gitnexus/package.json version\" step already handles both cases by falling back to \`GITHUB_REF\` when \`INPUT_TAG\` is empty, so the early guard only needs to cover \`workflow_call\`.

## Fix

Restrict the validate step to \`workflow_call\` only and add a comment explaining why \`push\` must not be included.

## Test plan

title: On Windows, --embeddings writes HuggingFace cache into ./undefined/ when HOME env is unset
body:
## Description

On Windows, running `gitnexus analyze --embeddings` creates an `undefined/` directory inside the repository root and writes the HuggingFace model cache (`Snowflake/snowflake-arctic-embed-xs/...`, ~86 MB ONNX model + tokenizer/config) under `./undefined/.cache/huggingface/...` instead of `~/.cache/huggingface/...`.

The literal folder name `undefined` strongly suggests the embedding pipeline is doing something equivalent to:

```js
path.join(process.env.HOME, '.cache', 'huggingface', ...)
```

without falling back to `process.env.USERPROFILE` (or `os.homedir()`) on Windows. On a default Windows installation `HOME` is not set, so `process.env.HOME` is `undefined`, which then gets stringified into the path.

This pollutes the working tree, shows up as untracked files in `git status`, gets committed by accident if the user does a wide `git add`, and bloats every repo that gets indexed because the model is re-downloaded into the next repo's `./undefined/` instead of being cached centrally.

## Environment

- OS: Windows 11 (pwsh 7)
- Node: installed locally, `gitnexus.cmd` shim invoked via npm global
- gitnexus: **1.6.3** (npm global)
- Persistent `HOME` env: not set at User or Machine scope (default Windows)
- `USERPROFILE`: `C:\Users\<user>`

## Steps to reproduce

1. On a fresh Windows shell where `HOME` is not set:
   ```pwsh
   [Environment]::GetEnvironmentVariable('HOME','User')   # empty
   [Environment]::GetEnvironmentVariable('HOME','Machine')# empty
   $env:HOME                                              # empty
   ```
2. In any indexed git repository:
   ```pwsh
   gitnexus analyze --embeddings -f
   ```
3. After indexing finishes, `git status` shows:
   ```
   Untracked files:
           undefined/
   ```
4. Inspect the directory:
   ```
   undefined/.cache/huggingface/Snowflake/snowflake-arctic-embed-xs/
       config.json                (737 B)
       tokenizer.json             (711 KB)
       tokenizer_config.json      (1.4 KB)
       onnx/model.onnx            (86.2 MB)
   ```

## Expected behavior

Embedding model cache should be written to a stable, user-scoped location, e.g. `os.homedir()` or `path.join(os.homedir(), '.cache', 'huggingface', ...)`, never to a path containing the string `undefined`, and never inside the repo working tree.

## Suggested fix

In whichever module resolves the cache root (likely a transformers.js / `@xenova/transformers` consumer or a custom resolver), replace any direct `process.env.HOME` reads with one of:

```js
const os = require('node:os');
const home = os.homedir(); // works on Windows, macOS, Linux
```

or, if you must read env vars directly:

```js
const home = process.env.HOME || process.env.USERPROFILE;
if (!home) throw new Error('Could not resolve user home directory');
```

A quick way to confirm the suspicion: search the gitnexus dist/source for `process.env.HOME` and for `huggingface` cache initialisation.

## Workaround for current users

Either set `HOME` once:

```pwsh
setx HOME "$env:USERPROFILE"
# new shells only; restart terminal afterwards
```

or set it per-shell before running `gitnexus`:

```pwsh
$env:HOME = $env:USERPROFILE
gitnexus analyze --embeddings -f
```

After the bug fires once, the model can be salvaged by moving `./undefined/.cache/huggingface/` into `~/.cache/huggingface/` and deleting the `undefined/` directory, so future runs reuse the model instead of re-downloading 86 MB.

## Impact

- Pollutes git working tree of every indexed repo (`undefined/` is untracked).
- Risk of accidentally committing 86 MB binary model into the repo.
- Cache is not actually shared between repos: each repo grows its own `./undefined/.cache/...` instead of reusing one global cache.

docs: clarify PostToolUse hook is notification-only, not auto-reindex
body:
## Summary

The README, AGENTS.md, and `gitnexus-cli` skill all claim the PostToolUse hook runs `analyze` **automatically** after `git commit` and `git merge`. The hook source itself ([`gitnexus/hooks/claude/gitnexus-hook.cjs`](gitnexus/hooks/claude/gitnexus-hook.cjs)) explicitly chose notification-only:

> Instead of spawning a full `gitnexus analyze` synchronously (which blocks the agent for up to 120s and risks KuzuDB corruption on timeout), we do a lightweight staleness check: compare `git rev-parse HEAD` against the lastCommit stored in `.gitnexus/meta.json`. If they differ, notify the agent so it can decide when to reindex.

So users (and any AI agent reading the docs) form an incorrect mental model: they expect zero-touch reindex but actually get repeated stale-index notifications until they run `npx gitnexus analyze` themselves.

## What this PR changes

Four user-facing doc lines updated to match real behavior. No code changes — the hook already behaves correctly; only the docs were lying.

| File | Change |
| ---- | ------ |
| `README.md` (Editor Support callout) | "auto-reindex after commits" → "detect a stale index after commits and prompt the agent to reindex" |
| `AGENTS.md` (Keeping the Index Fresh) | "PostToolUse hook handles this" → "detects a stale index … and prompts the agent to run `analyze`. The hook does not invoke `analyze` itself." |
| `gitnexus/skills/gitnexus-cli.md` (analyze → When to run) | "runs `analyze` automatically" → "detects staleness … notifies the agent to run `analyze`" + adds the "why not auto-run" reasoning the hook author already wrote |
| `.claude/skills/gitnexus/gitnexus-cli/SKILL.md` (analyze → When to run) | Same wording as above |

The Enterprise "Auto-reindexing" line at `README.md:71` is left intact — that describes a real Enterprise feature, distinct from the OSS hook.

## How I noticed this

I ran several `git commit` / `git merge` operations on a project that had GitNexus indexed, and each one fired the `[GitNexus] index is stale` notification. The CLAUDE.md generated by `gitnexus analyze` told me a hook would auto-reindex, so I assumed the hook was broken. After reading the hook source I realised the docs were the bug — the design choice is sound, just under-described.

## Test plan

- [x] No code changes — only Markdown text
- [x] Verified `gitnexus/hooks/claude/gitnexus-hook.cjs` does not call `gitnexus analyze` in any code path on PostToolUse (only `sendHookResponse` with the staleness message)
- [x] Skill markdown is included in published npm package output → end-user CLAUDE.md will reflect the corrected wording on next `gitnexus analyze`

title: hybrid RAG cannot fully execute on current query entrypoints (MCP loses semantic, Web search path loses BM25)
body:
### Area

gitnexus (CLI / core / indexing / MCP server)

### Summary

GitNexus documents hybrid retrieval as BM25 + semantic + RRF, but in the current implementation no single query entrypoint reliably executes both BM25 and semantic together.

### Context

I am trying to inspect the RAG pipeline itself, including intermediate retrieval stages and final retrieval results, while excluding LLM effects as much as possible.

My goal is to debug and benchmark the RAG layer directly:
- what BM25 retrieved
- what semantic retrieved
- how hybrid/RRF merged them
- what the final retrieval output looks like

While doing that, I found functional gaps across the current entrypoints.

Relevant context:
- I am using a real indexed repo 
- I already ran:
  - `gitnexus analyze --embeddings`
  - `gitnexus serve`
- I also added RAG tracing/logging locally to inspect the retrieval stages

### Expected behavior

Any query path described or exposed as "hybrid" should be able to execute:
- BM25 retrieval
- semantic retrieval
- RRF merge

This should work consistently on the supported query entrypoints, especially:
- MCP / `gitnexus query`
- Web AI search path
- direct HTTP `/api/search`

Also, the Web AI flow should not depend on hidden initialization differences that make retrieval behavior diverge from direct `/api/search` calls.

### Actual behavior

### MCP / `gitnexus query`
- BM25 works because the MCP pool initializes `fts`
- semantic does not reliably work because the query path does not initialize `VECTOR`
- current behavior often falls back with vector extension unavailable

### Web AI search path
- The Web app initializes the agent and auto-triggers `/api/embed`
- But when the AI uses the `search` tool, that path still goes through `backendSearch()` -> `/api/search`
- I do not see any FTS initialization on the HTTP search path
- So on the Web AI `search` retrieval path, BM25 is not reliably available

Important clarification:
- I am **not** claiming the whole Web AI experience is broken
- The AI can still answer via other tools like `cypher`, `grep`, `read`, `explore`, etc.
- The issue is specifically that the **Web AI search retrieval path** does not appear to initialize FTS, so BM25 in that path is unreliable / effectively unavailable

### Direct HTTP `/api/search`
- default mode is `hybrid`
- but the HTTP search path does not explicitly initialize FTS
- and the semantic path does not explicitly initialize VECTOR
- so direct `/api/search` cannot reliably execute full BM25 + semantic hybrid retrieval either

### `/api/embed` failure
I also observed that `/api/embed` can fail with:

`Prepare failed: Binder exception: Trying to insert into an index on table CodeEmbedding but its extension is not loaded.`

This appears related to the embedding pipeline inserting into `CodeEmbedding` before the VECTOR extension is loaded in the current process/session.




### Steps to reproduce

1. Index a real repo with embeddings
```bash
cd /path/to/repo
npx gitnexus analyze --embeddings
```

2. Start the server:
```bash
gitnexus serve
```
3. Test the MCP / LocalBackend path:
```bash
npx gitnexus query --repo myRepo "Home page logic"
```
Observe:

BM25 path executes
semantic often falls back / is unavailable
4. Test the HTTP search path directly:
```bash
curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:4747/api/search \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "repo":"myRepo",
    "query":"Home page logic",
    "limit":10,
    "mode":"hybrid",
    "enrich":true,
  }'
```
Observe:

no clear FTS initialization on this query path
hybrid cannot reliably run BM25 + semantic together
5. Test the Web embedding path:
```bash
curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:4747/api/embed \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"repo":"myRepo"}'
```
Then poll:
```
curl http://127.0.0.1:4747/api/embed/<jobId>
```
Observe:

job may fail with:
Trying to insert into an index on table CodeEmbedding but its extension is not loaded.

### Environment

title: Scope extraction fails on files over ~32 KB on Windows (Invalid argument, 2^15 boundary)
body:
Here is the final version with both values filled in. Everything below the line is ready to paste directly into the bug report.

---

### Area
gitnexus (CLI / core / indexing / MCP server)

### Summary
Scope extraction fails with `Invalid argument` on every Python source file at or above approximately 32 KB (32,768 bytes / 2^15). Files below this threshold parse cleanly. The boundary is sharp, reproducible, and unchanged between v1.4.8 and v1.6.3. The 2^15 byte threshold suggests a signed 16-bit integer overflow in the scope extraction code path or its native dependencies.

### Context

Verified on two GitNexus versions with identical results:

- v1.4.8 (initial install via `npm install -g gitnexus`)
- v1.6.3 (verified per maintainer request via `npm install -g gitnexus@latest`, confirmed with `gitnexus --version`)

Both runs produce the same 26 file failures, same error text, same approximate 32 KB boundary, and graph metrics within 1 node of each other (18,937 vs 18,938 nodes; 25,467 edges in both runs). The affected code path appears unchanged between the two releases.

### Expected behavior

Scope extraction should complete successfully on all Python source files that pass the parsing phase, regardless of file size, up to the documented 512 KB skip threshold. Files between approximately 32 KB and 512 KB should be processed by the scope extractor without error and contribute complete within-file scope data (variable scopes, `self`/`this` receiver resolution, intra-file call edges) to the knowledge graph.

The CLI output should report a clean run with no per-file warnings when all files are within the supported size range.

### Actual behavior

Scope extraction fails with `Invalid argument` on every Python file at or above approximately 32 KB. The boundary is sharp:

- Largest file that parsed successfully: 31.7 KB
- Smallest file that failed: 32.5 KB
- Total files affected: 26 of 26 files at or above 32.5 KB
- Total files below threshold: 0 failures
- File size range of failures: 32.5 KB to 293.1 KB
- Files above the documented 512 KB skip threshold are correctly skipped (not affected by this bug)

Each failure produces a single line of the form:

```
scope extraction failed for <path>: Invalid argument
```

The overall index still completes (`Repository indexed successfully`) and reports node, edge, cluster, and process counts. Affected files appear in the resulting cluster summaries with their top-level symbols counted, suggesting the parsing and clustering phases handled them but scope extraction did not.

Behavior is deterministic across `--force` re-indexes: the same 26 files fail on every run with identical error text. The `--verbose` flag does not surface additional detail about the failures; it only adds the list of files skipped at the 512 KB threshold.

The 32 KB / 2^15 boundary suggests a signed 16-bit integer overflow somewhere in the scope extraction path (tree-sitter native binding, LadybugDB, or the scope extraction logic itself), but the root cause is not visible from CLI output alone.

### Steps to reproduce

1. On Windows 11 with Node.js installed, install GitNexus globally: `npm install -g gitnexus@latest`
2. Confirm the version: `gitnexus --version` (currently 1.6.3)
3. In a Python repository that contains source files larger than 32 KB, run from the repo root: `gitnexus clean --force` followed by `gitnexus analyze --skills --verbose --force`
4. Observe the CLI output. Files at or above approximately 32.5 KB produce `scope extraction failed for <path>: Invalid argument` warnings. Files below approximately 31.7 KB parse without warning.
5. Confirm the run completes with `Repository indexed successfully` despite the warnings, and that affected files still appear in cluster summaries with non-zero symbol counts.
6. Re-run `gitnexus analyze --skills --verbose --force` to confirm the failure set is deterministic; the same files produce the same error on every run.

### Environment

- OS: Windows 11
- Shell: PowerShell
- GitNexus version: 1.6.3 (also reproduced on 1.4.8)
- Node.js version: v22.22.2
- npm version: 10.9.7
- Target language: Python
- Target codebase size: approximately 150 source files, mixed sizes from under 1 KB to 293 KB

### Logs / screenshots

Truncated CLI output from `gitnexus analyze --skills --verbose --force` on v1.6.3 (file paths shown to file basenames; full set of 26 failures included):

```
  GitNexus Analyzer
  Skipped 9 large files (>512KB, likely generated/vendored)
  [9 files listed, all data/binary/markdown, correctly skipped]
scope extraction failed for *****: Invalid argument

  Generating repo-specific skills...
    [17 cluster skill files generated successfully]
  Repository indexed successfully (6.5s)
  18,938 nodes | 25,467 edges | 295 clusters | 203 flows
```

File size distribution of the 26 failures (KB, descending):
293.1, 157.1, 145.9, 109.0, 106.7, 96.8, 83.4, 67.4, 66.6, 62.3, 52.7, 51.0, 48.4, 46.7, 44.7, 44.2, 44.2, 39.4, 38.9, 38.4, 38.3, 38.1, 37.4, 34.7, 32.9, 32.5

Largest successfully parsed file: 31.7 KB. Gap between largest success and smallest failure: 0.8 KB.

title: query subcommand always returns empty + logs "read-only database" FTS errors
body:
### Area

gitnexus (CLI / core / indexing / MCP server)

### Summary

Every `gitnexus query` invocation fails to initialize FTS indexes and returns empty results, regardless of repo size, content, or filesystem. Other subcommands (`cypher`, `context`, `impact`) work correctly against the same index, so the graph itself is healthy — only the FTS-backed `query` path is broken.

Reproduces on `gitnexus@1.6.3` and `gitnexus@1.6.4-rc.1`.

### Context

_No response_

### Expected behavior

After `gitnexus analyze` completes successfully on a repo containing the
function `resolve_shooting` (and helper functions `roll_to_hit`,
`roll_to_wound`), running:

    gitnexus query "shooting"

should:

1. Initialize the FTS indexes (file_fts, function_fts, class_fts,
   method_fts, interface_fts) if they have not yet been built — either
   silently on first call, or eagerly during `analyze`.
2. Return non-empty BM25 / vector results referencing the matching
   symbols, e.g. `resolve_shooting`, `roll_to_hit`, `roll_to_wound`.
3. Emit no errors to stderr.

The same query should succeed when invoked via the MCP `query` tool over
the `gitnexus mcp` stdio server, with the same result shape inside the
`tools/call` response.

### Actual behavior

`gitnexus query "shooting"` returns empty results and emits five FTS-init
errors to stderr — one per FTS table — on every invocation:

    [gitnexus] FTS index ensure failed for repo "gn-repro" table "File"
      (index "file_fts"): Connection exception: Cannot execute write
      operations in a read-only database!. Will retry on next query.
    [gitnexus] FTS index ensure failed for repo "gn-repro" table
      "Function" (index "function_fts"): Connection exception: Cannot
      execute write operations in a read-only database!. Will retry on
      next query.
    [gitnexus] FTS index ensure failed for repo "gn-repro" table "Class"
      (index "class_fts"): Connection exception: Cannot execute write
      operations in a read-only database!. Will retry on next query.
    [gitnexus] FTS index ensure failed for repo "gn-repro" table "Method"
      (index "method_fts"): Connection exception: Cannot execute write
      operations in a read-only database!. Will retry on next query.
    [gitnexus] FTS index ensure failed for repo "gn-repro" table
      "Interface" (index "interface_fts"): Connection exception: Cannot
      execute write operations in a read-only database!. Will retry on
      next query.

The JSON response body is empty:

    {
      "processes": [],
      "process_symbols": [],
      "definitions": [],
      "timing": { "vector": 8.3, "bm25": 42.4, "merge": 0,
                  "symbol_lookup": 0, "ranking": 0, "formatting": 0,
                  "wall": 42.7 }
    }

The "Will retry on next query" message is misleading: subsequent
invocations of `gitnexus query` repeat the same five errors and return
the same empty result. The retry never succeeds because each invocation
opens a fresh read-only DB handle and the FTS-ensure code runs the same
write attempt against it. There is no condition under which a future
query could succeed without code changes.

Re-running `analyze --force` does not change behavior. The same failure
also reproduces over the MCP `query` tool when invoked via `gitnexus mcp`
stdio, so this is not CLI-specific.

By contrast, `cypher`, `context`, and `impact` against the same index
return correct results — the graph itself is healthy; only the FTS-backed
`query` path is broken.

### Steps to reproduce

## Minimal reproduction

```bash
mkdir /tmp/gn-repro && cd /tmp/gn-repro
git init -q
cat > shooting.py << 'PY'
def resolve_shooting(unit, target):
    return roll_to_hit(unit) and roll_to_wound(target)
def roll_to_hit(unit): return True
def roll_to_wound(target): return True
PY
git add -A && git -c user.email=t@t -c user.name=t commit -qm init
npx --yes gitnexus@1.6.3 analyze
npx --yes gitnexus@1.6.3 query "shooting"
```

## Actual output

```
[gitnexus] FTS index ensure failed for repo "gn-repro" table "File" (index "file_fts"): Connection exception: Cannot execute write operations in a read-only database!. Will retry on next query.
[gitnexus] FTS index ensure failed for repo "gn-repro" table "Function" (index "function_fts"): Connection exception: Cannot execute write operations in a read-only database!. Will retry on next query.
[gitnexus] FTS index ensure failed for repo "gn-repro" table "Class" (index "class_fts"): Connection exception: Cannot execute write operations in a read-only database!. Will retry on next query.
[gitnexus] FTS index ensure failed for repo "gn-repro" table "Method" (index "method_fts"): Connection exception: Cannot execute write operations in a read-only database!. Will retry on next query.
[gitnexus] FTS index ensure failed for repo "gn-repro" table "Interface" (index "interface_fts"): Connection exception: Cannot execute write operations in a read-only database!. Will retry on next query.
{
  "processes": [],

  "timing": { "vector": 8.3, "bm25": 42.4, "merge": 0, "symbol_lookup": 0, "ranking": 0, "formatting": 0, "wall": 42.7 }
}
```

The "Will retry on next query" message is misleading — every subsequent `query` invocation reproduces the same five errors and returns empty results.

title: Bash files indexed as File nodes but produce zero symbols, leading to misleading partial graph coverage
body:
## Summary

Files with extensions GitNexus has no parser for (e.g. `.sh`) are still added to the graph as `File` nodes, but no symbols, calls, or relationships are extracted from them. Queries against the graph return Python/JS/etc. matches via semantic ranking, and users have no signal that the bash half of their project is invisible.

## Reproduction

In a bash-heavy repo:

```bash
$ npx gitnexus analyze
$ # ... (analysis runs cleanly, no warnings)
```

Verify via cypher:

```
MATCH (f:File) WHERE f.filePath ENDS WITH '.sh' RETURN count(*)  →  102
MATCH (f:File) WHERE f.filePath ENDS WITH '.py' RETURN count(*)  →  40
MATCH (fn:Function) WHERE fn.filePath ENDS WITH '.sh' RETURN count(*)  →  0
MATCH (fn:Function) WHERE fn.filePath ENDS WITH '.py' RETURN count(*)  →  328
```

102 bash files indexed, 0 functions extracted from them. The 40 Python files produced 328 functions.

## Why this is worse than "no support"

If `.sh` files were excluded from indexing entirely, `query()` would return only the Python results — clearly partial, the operator knows to grep for the rest. Instead, current behavior:

1. `File` nodes for bash exist → graph appears complete
2. Semantic search ranks Python symbols against bash-related queries → plausible-looking noise (e.g. searching for "ollama chat completion payload" returns `validate_url`, `log_action`, `_load_state`)
3. `impact()` and `context()` on bash function names return empty / disambiguation candidates, but only if you know the bash function's name to begin with
4. The `stats` summary in `gitnexus://repo/{name}/context` reports the file count, not the parser-coverage ratio

Net effect: agents and humans using GitNexus on bash-heavy repos get **plausible incomplete answers** with no signal that anything is missing.

## Two asks (in priority order)

**1. Short-term (bug fix, no new dependencies):** surface unparsed files in `context` output and/or skip them from File-node creation. Concrete options:

- Add `parser_status` field to `File` nodes (`indexed` / `extension_unsupported` / `parse_error`)
- Emit per-language coverage in `gitnexus://repo/{name}/context`:

  ```yaml
  parser_coverage:
    python:    {files: 40, functions: 328}
    bash:      {files: 102, functions: 0, status: "no parser"}
  ```

- Or: log a warning at analyze time when N% of files are unsupported

**2. Long-term (feature):** add `tree-sitter-bash` to the bundled grammars. Bash orchestration is common in indie / DevOps / data-pipeline projects. The grammar exists in the tree-sitter ecosystem and is reasonably mature.

## Environment

- GitNexus 1.6.2
- macOS Darwin 25.3.0
- Repo: 1066 files, 5107 symbols, 6148 relationships, 112 processes
- Bundled grammars in `node_modules`: c, c-sharp, cpp, go, java, javascript, php, python, ruby, rust, typescript

## Why I'm filing this

Hit it during an automated bug-hunt workflow that uses your MCP `query` tool as Phase 2 reconnaissance — the agent reads the graph to map an attack surface, then forms hypotheses against confirmed callers. In a bash-heavy repo the graph silently returned plausible Python noise instead of the real bash callers; the agent pursued the wrong leads for ~10 minutes before falling back to grep. Fix shipped after the grep pass found 8 actual callers.

The agent use case is the strongest argument for the short-term ask: an LLM with no parser-coverage signal will treat noise as evidence and waste tokens chasing it. Even just the `parser_coverage` field would fix that.



---

## Related issues

Found these in the same family while triaging:

- **#176** (closed) — Crash on unsupported language (Swift) instead of graceful skip. Resolved by silent skipping — this issue argues the silent skip needs a coverage signal so the skip isn't invisible to downstream consumers.
- **#584** (open) — Dart loads tree-sitter parser but no symbols extracted. Same observable symptom as bash (file indexed, 0 symbols), different cause (extraction broken vs no parser at all). A `parser_coverage` signal would surface both cases uniformly.
- **#1057** (open) — Unable to parse Dart; install request for tree-sitter-dart.
- **#531** (open) — feat: Add Solidity language support.
- **#748** (open) — feat: Add GDScript (Godot) language support.
- **#157** (open) — Feature: Markdown as a first-class language for knowledge graph indexing.

The short-term ask (parser_coverage signal) generalizes across all of these — every language without symbol extraction would surface the same way to MCP consumers, regardless of cause.

title: fix: use os.homedir() instead of process.env.HOME for HuggingFace cache dir
body:
## Summary

On Windows, `HOME` environment variable is not set by default. When running `gitnexus analyze --embeddings`, the cache directory resolves to `undefined/.cache/huggingface/` because `process.env.HOME` returns `undefined`, which gets stringified into the path.

This pollutes the working tree with an `undefined/` directory containing ~86 MB of model files, risks accidental commits, and prevents cache sharing between repos.

## Changes

- Replace `process.env.HOME` with `os.homedir()` which correctly resolves the user home directory on Windows, macOS, and Linux
- Use `path.join()` for cross-platform path construction instead of template literals
- Applied to both `gitnexus/src/core/embeddings/embedder.ts` and `gitnexus/src/mcp/core/embedder.ts`

## Test

- Verified on Linux that `os.homedir()` returns the correct home directory
- `HF_HOME` environment variable priority is preserved

Fixes #1068

title: Add Lua language support (tree-sitter-lua)
body:
## Request

Adding Lua to the supported language list would significantly broaden GitNexus's usefulness for game-server, embedded-scripting, and config-as-Lua codebases.

## Why this matters in practice

Tested against a LandSandBoat-derived FFXI server fork (~19k indexed files, ~17k of them `.lua`) on `gitnexus@1.6.3`:

| Query | Result |
|-------|--------|
| `MATCH (f:File) WHERE f.filePath ENDS WITH '.lua' RETURN count(f)` | **17,140** Lua files indexed |
| `MATCH (fn:Function) WHERE fn.id CONTAINS '.lua' RETURN count(fn)` | **0** Lua functions extracted |
| (cross-check, C++) | 1,208 functions |
| (cross-check, Python) | 404 functions |
| Total Function nodes | 9,232 |

So Lua files appear as file nodes (good for path-based queries) but no symbol extraction happens — `gitnexus_impact`, `gitnexus_query`, `gitnexus_rename` are effectively blind to anything in `scripts/`, `modules/`, `quests/`, etc. For a codebase that's ~90% Lua this is a meaningful gap.

## Why it's a reasonable ask

`tree-sitter-lua` is well-established and battle-tested (used by Neovim, GitHub's linguist, etc.). The current parser list bundled with GitNexus already covers 14 languages including Dart, Kotlin, Swift, Ruby — Lua is a smaller jump than several of those.

## Scope of work (best guess from reading the codebase)

- Add `tree-sitter-lua` to dependencies
- Author the scope-extraction queries Lua needs (the `Provider must emit at least one @scope.module capture` contract — same pattern as the other languages)
- Wire it into the language registry / file-extension mapping

Happy to test against my repo once a beta is published. Thanks for the great tool!

— Filed from `gitnexus@1.6.3` analyze run on Windows 11

title: fix(ingestion): two-channel binding lifecycle (closes #1066) + scope-resolution I8 hardening
body:
## Summary

Fixes [issue #1066](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/issues/1066) and refactors the C# cross-file binding fanout so we no longer mutate finalized scope bindings — the original `cloneBindingBucket` workaround violated `ScopeResolver` Invariant I8 in spirit and was the wrong layer to patch.

This PR consolidates everything into one coherent change:

1. **Direct fix for #1066** (commit `a18f6e1`):
   - Adaptive tree-sitter buffer (`getTreeSitterBufferSize`) on cache-miss `parse()` calls in C#, Python, and TypeScript captures — eliminates the `Invalid argument` crash on large files (>32KB).
   - Workaround `cloneBindingBucket` helper to copy frozen `BindingRef[]` arrays before pushing — fixes the `Cannot add property N, object is not extensible` crash.
   - Comprehensive regression tests (unit + integration + 77KB padded fixture).

2. **Architectural refactor** (commits `0a9679b1` → `c23a4620`): the workaround in step 1 contradicted I8. The clean fix is a two-channel binding lifecycle:
   - `indexes.bindings` — finalize-output channel, deep-frozen post-finalize, never mutated by hooks.
   - `indexes.bindingAugmentations` — new append-only post-finalize channel for hooks like `populateNamespaceSiblings`.
   - All read sites consult both channels via a new `lookupBindingsAt` helper.
   - C# `populateNamespaceSiblings` now writes to `bindingAugmentations`, not `bindings`. `cloneBindingBucket` is deleted.
   - Dev-mode validator `validateBindingsImmutability` (gated on `NODE_ENV !== 'production' && VALIDATE_SEMANTIC_MODEL !== '0'`) catches drift if a future hook regresses.
   - Invariant I8 in `contract/scope-resolver.ts` rewritten to capture the new contract; lifecycle comment in `gitnexus-shared/types.ts` extended.

## Commit-by-commit

| # | Commit | Purpose |
|---|--------|---------|
| 1 | `a18f6e1` fix(csharp): adaptive tree-sitter buffer + frozen-bucket clone for cross-namespace siblings (#1066) | Direct #1066 fix (workaround) + regression suite. |
| 2 | `0a9679b1` refactor(scope-resolution): add bindingAugmentations channel to indexes | Step 1 — interface + finalize-orchestrator return empty Map. |
| 3 | `b88570fd` feat(scope-resolution): add lookupBindingsAt dual-source helper | Step 2 — helper + `namesAtScope` companion + 8 unit tests. |
| 4 | `40e2864c` refactor(scope-resolution): route binding lookups through lookupBindingsAt | Step 3 — `findClassBindingInScope` / `findCallableBindingInScope` / `findExportedDefByName` / `propagateImportedReturnTypes` go through the merger. |
| 5 | `516e03f1` refactor(csharp): write namespace siblings to bindingAugmentations channel | Step 4 — switch C# write target; delete `cloneBindingBucket`. |
| 6 | `c23a4620` feat(scope-resolution): tighten I8 + add validateBindingsImmutability dev guard | Step 5 — contract docs + dev-mode validator + 6 validator tests. |

## Validation

- `npx tsc --noEmit` clean.
- `npx prettier --check` clean (only `.cursor/hooks.json` warns — untracked workspace file).
- 7235 / 7327 vitest tests pass. 6 failures are pre-existing and unrelated:
  - 4 Swift `METHOD_IMPLEMENTS` regressions (verified on baseline pre-PR).
  - 1 Swift method-extraction unit test (Swift parser-side issue).
  - 1 Swift constructor-inference unit test (Swift type-env issue).
  - 1 LadybugDB vector-extension test failed to acquire its file lock on Windows temp dir (documented gotcha in `AGENTS.md`).
- All 4 issue #1066 regression integration tests green (`csharp-large-cache-miss-resolution`).
- All 8 `walkers-augmentations.test.ts` cases green (precedence, dedup-by-`def.nodeId`, empty-arrays-merge, fast-path miss).
- All 6 `validate-bindings-immutability.test.ts` cases green.

### Bidirectional regression verification (Step 7 of plan)

To prove each architectural piece carries weight, the architecture was reverted in two surgical ways and the regressions were observed before re-applying.

- **Reverted Step 4 alone** (write target back to `indexes.bindings`):
  ```
  TypeError: Cannot add property 1, object is not extensible
    at populateCsharpNamespaceSiblings (.../namespace-siblings.ts:346:19)
  ```
  ✅ Same crash as #1066. Re-applied — green.

- **Reverted Step 3 alone** (read sites bypass `lookupBindingsAt`):
  ```
  AssertionError: expected undefined to be defined  // CreateUser -> User constructor
  AssertionError: expected [ 'import-resolved', 'global' ] to include 'scope-resolution: call'  // CreateUser -> Save
  ```
  ✅ Augmentations invisible to readers; cross-file C# resolution regresses. Re-applied — green.

## Test plan

- [x] `npx tsc --noEmit`
- [x] `npx prettier --check` (touched dirs)
- [x] Full vitest run (`npm test`)
- [x] Targeted regression: `test/integration/resolvers/csharp.test.ts -t "issue #1066"`
- [x] Step-7 bidirectional reversal sanity (documented above)
- [x] Step-by-step commit verification (each commit is independently green; pre-commit hook ran `tsc` on every commit)

## Notes for reviewers

- This is intentionally a single PR with the immediate fix (commit 1) followed by 5 architectural commits. The first commit alone resolves #1066 in production behavior; commits 2–6 replace the workaround with a clean architecture without changing behavior. Any commit can be cherry-picked / inspected in isolation.
- `validateBindingsImmutability` is a dev-mode-only guard. In production it is a no-op (`return 0` on the first line).
- `lookupBindingsAt` returns the existing array by reference when only one channel populates it (zero allocation for the common case where augmentations are empty).

Closes #1066.

title: fix(csharp): copy-on-read frozen binding arrays in namespace-siblings
body:
## Summary

`scope-extractor.ts` freezes per-name binding arrays via `frozenBindings.set(name, Object.freeze(refs.slice()))` (line 180). When `populateCsharpNamespaceSiblings` later reads back an existing entry via `scopeBindings.get(name) ?? []` and tries to `existing.push(...)` on it, the frozen reference throws

```
TypeError: Cannot add property N, object is not extensible
    at Array.push (<anonymous>)
    at Object.populateCsharpNamespaceSiblings [as populateNamespaceSiblings]
      (.../csharp/namespace-siblings.js:321:26)
    at runScopeResolution (.../scope-resolution/pipeline/run.js:113:18)
    ...
  Phase 'scopeResolution' failed
```

…which abandons scope resolution for the **entire repo** (the index is never produced). The populator's leading comment says "indexes.bindings is typed ReadonlyMap<...> but is a plain Map at runtime; mutating here is the established pattern" — that's true for the outer `Map`, but the inner per-name arrays are nonetheless frozen by the extractor, so the established pattern is silently broken at three sites.

## Reproduction

Triggered when a file locally declares a class with the same simple name as a class in a sibling namespace imported via `using`. Hit live on the [PersistentWindows](https://github.com/kangyu-california/PersistentWindows) real-world WinForms repo (large mix of `.Designer.cs` + namespaced classes); also hit on smaller mixed-namespace C# codebases.

Minimal fixture added under `test/fixtures/cross-file-binding/csharp-frozen-binding-collision/`:
- `Models/User.cs` declares `Collision.Models.User`
- `App/Program.cs` imports `using Collision.Models;` AND locally declares `class User` in `Collision.App` — the local declaration causes scope-extractor to populate (and freeze) `User` in the Module scope's bindings; the populator's namespace-import path then attempts to push `Collision.Models.User` into the same frozen array.

## Fix

Spread to a fresh mutable copy on read at all three sites in `populateCsharpNamespaceSiblings`:

```diff
- const existing = scopeBindings.get(name) ?? [];
+ const existing: BindingRef[] = [...(scopeBindings.get(name) ?? [])];
```

When the populator hits a name pre-populated by the extractor, it now appends to a fresh array and writes that back, replacing the frozen entry in the per-scope Map. Origin precedence (`local` shadows `namespace`) is preserved by the existing `csharpMergeBindings` ordering (see `csharp-hooks.test.ts`).

Three sites fixed:
- `populateCsharpNamespaceSiblings` using-static loop (`origin: 'import'`)
- `populateCsharpNamespaceSiblings` namespace-import loop (`origin: 'namespace'`)
- `populateCsharpNamespaceSiblings` cross-namespace bucket loop (third namespace-injection site)

## Verification

- **`npx tsc --noEmit`** clean
- **`npx vitest run test/integration/resolvers/csharp.test.ts test/unit/scope-resolution/csharp/ test/unit/named-bindings/csharp.test.ts`** → 5 test files / 282 tests / 0 fail (3 of those are the new regression test + 279 existing).
- **Pre-fix** `beforeAll` of the new test rejects with `Phase 'scopeResolution' failed: Cannot add property N, object is not extensible`. **Post-fix** all three test cases pass: scope resolution completes, both `User` declarations are detected, and `new User()` inside `Program.Run()` resolves to the local `Collision.App.User` (origin:local shadows origin:namespace).

## Risk / rollback

Minimal — purely a copy-on-read tweak in a populator that already documented its intent to mutate the per-name arrays. Behavior is unchanged for callers that don't pre-populate the same name. The `Object.freeze` upstream in `scope-extractor.ts` is left in place; if a future change wants to enforce true immutability throughout, this is the right starting point because it makes the freeze contract honest at the populator boundary instead of silently broken.

Rollback: revert the commit; the upstream behavior degrades back to crashing on collision.

## Test plan

- [x] `npx tsc --noEmit` in `gitnexus/`
- [x] Full C# test suite green (integration + unit + named-bindings)
- [x] New regression test fails before fix, passes after
- [ ] Optional: maintainer to run on a wider corpus

title: test(csharp): companion fixture for #1066 frozen-bucket regression
body:
## Summary

Adds a small-file companion fixture for the freeze-contract regression fixed in #1082. The merged `csharp-large-cache-miss-resolution` fixture reproduces the failure via the >32 KB tree-sitter cache-miss reparse path; this fixture trips the same `Object.freeze` contract in `populateCsharpNamespaceSiblings` through a different trigger that doesn't depend on file size:

> An importer locally declares a class with the same simple name as a sibling reachable through `using`, so scope-extractor pre-populates (and freezes) `User` in the importer's Module bindings before the populator's namespace-import loop tries to append the cross-file `Collision.Models.User`.

Pre-#1082 the populator pushed onto the frozen array → `TypeError: Cannot add property N, object is not extensible` → the whole `scopeResolution` phase aborted for the repo. Post-#1082 the augmentation channel keeps both bindings visible to readers; the local `Collision.App.User` shadows the namespace-imported one per origin precedence.

This is the trigger we originally hit on the [PersistentWindows](https://github.com/kangyu-california/PersistentWindows) real-world WinForms repo and used to reproduce the bug in the (now-closed) #1083 — adding it here as resolver coverage so the freeze contract is locked-in on both reproduction paths.

## Fixture

`test/fixtures/lang-resolution/csharp-frozen-binding-collision/`:
- `Models/User.cs` — `namespace Collision.Models { public class User { ... } }`
- `App/Program.cs` — `using Collision.Models;` + `namespace Collision.App { public class User { ... } public class Program { ... } }`

Tiny by design — the bug is shape-driven, not size-driven, so the fixture stays small and fast (567 ms for the new describe vs ~25 s for the cache-miss fixture in the same suite).

## Tests

New describe block in `test/integration/resolvers/csharp.test.ts`, sibling to the merged `'C# large-file + frozen-bucket regression (issue #1066)'` block:

- `completes scopeResolution without throwing on the colliding bucket` — the freeze regression itself.
- `detects both User declarations across the two namespaces` — pins augmentation visibility.
- `resolves Program.Run -> local Collision.App.User constructor (origin:local shadows namespace)` — pins the precedence contract that makes the augmentation channel architecturally correct (not just non-throwing).

Crossreference: `test/integration/resolvers/csharp.test.ts:2454` (cache-miss-reparse trigger) ↔ new block (collision-via-using-import trigger). Both anchor on the same `bindingAugmentations` machinery added in #1082; either one reverting reproduces #1066.

## Validation

- `npx vitest run test/integration/resolvers/csharp.test.ts` → **207 passed / 0 failed** (was 204; +3 new).
- `npx tsc --noEmit` → clean.
- Pre-commit hook (typecheck) green.
- Verified end-to-end on PersistentWindows after rebuilding from `upstream/main` (#1082 merged): 0 freeze errors, **1113 nodes / 2987 edges / 39 clusters / 97 flows** vs **1025 / 1715 / 28 / 25** with the closed #1083 workaround. The augmentation channel reaches ~74 % more cross-file edges than copy-on-read could.

## Test plan

- [x] `npx vitest run test/integration/resolvers/csharp.test.ts` (full file)
- [x] `npx tsc --noEmit` in `gitnexus/`
- [x] New describe runs in <1 s isolated; doesn't slow the resolver suite materially
- [x] Each new test fails on a hypothetical revert of #1082's Step 4 (write target back to `indexes.bindings`) — same shape as the merged #1066 fixture's bidirectional revert verification

title: scope-extractor: 'Namespace has kind Namespace but no parent' on C# files where compilation_unit and a single top-level namespace_declaration share an identical range
fix(scope-resolution): allow same-range Module-as-parent for top-level scopes (closes #1086)
body:
## Summary

Closes #1086 — `scopeResolution` aborts (silently, via `extractParsedFile`'s try/catch) for any C# file whose `compilation_unit` and single top-level `namespace_declaration` have **identical** tree-sitter ranges. The triggering shape is shape-driven, not size-driven: any file with no leading content outside the namespace block AND no trailing newline after the closing `}` produces coincident ranges. Hit on three real-world `*.Designer.cs` files in PersistentWindows; the four-case empirical repro (2 fail, 2 ok) is in #1086.

The fix is a single carve-out in the parent-validity contract: a `Module` may parent a same-range non-`Module` child. The relationship stays acyclic because the carve-out is direction-asymmetric — only Module-as-outer parents a same-range non-Module, never the reverse.

This is **option (b)** from the issue (named `canParentScope` helper at the contract layer). Option (a) (in-place tightening of `pass1BuildScopes`'s while-loop with a sort tie-breaker) was also feasible and slightly smaller, but option (b) keeps the carve-out as a single named, documented helper that lives in **both** `scope-extractor.ts` and `scope-tree.ts` — the two places that previously duplicated the same `rangeStrictlyContains` and that need to agree on what a well-formed parent edge looks like. Putting the carve-out behind a named helper makes the contract greppable and the asymmetry guard impossible to miss.

## Changes

- **`gitnexus/src/core/ingestion/scope-extractor.ts`** — new `canParentScope(outer, inner, outerKind, innerKind)` helper next to `rangeStrictlyContains`. `pass1BuildScopes` consults it for parent-finding. Sort tie-breaker added so a same-range Module sorts before a non-Module candidate, ensuring the Module lands on the parent-stack first regardless of tree-sitter capture iteration order.
- **`gitnexus-shared/src/scope-resolution/scope-tree.ts`** — mirrors the helper. `buildScopeTree`'s `parent-must-contain-child` check now uses `canParentScope` so the validator agrees with the extractor. Error message updated to spell out the new contract: \"… does not contain child '...' (allowed: strict containment, or equal-range Module-as-parent)\".

`rangeStrictlyContains` keeps its strict semantics in both files — position-index lookups, hook-side range comparisons, and other call sites are unchanged.

## Tests

- **New regression fixture** `test/fixtures/lang-resolution/csharp-namespace-as-root-no-trailing-newline/` — both `Models/User.cs` and `App/Program.cs` end exactly on the closing `}` of their namespace with no trailing newline. ~250 bytes total. Each commit's pre-commit hook verifies the trigger byte (`tail -c 1` is `0x7D`).
- **New `csharp.test.ts` describe** — scope extraction completes for both files (the bug surface), and the cross-file `IMPORTS` edge resolves through the scope-resolution path with `reason: 'csharp-scope: using'`. The `csharp-scope:` reason prefix is the signal that scope-resolution drove the resolution rather than the legacy DAG fallback.
- **`scope-tree.test.ts`** — replaced the prior \"rejects child ranges identical to the parent\" case with three new ones:
  - non-Module parent still rejected at equal range (Namespace-as-parent of same-range Class).
  - Module-as-parent of a same-range non-Module **accepted** (the #1086 carve-out itself, with `getParent`/`getChildren` round-trip).
  - Module-as-parent of another Module **still rejected** (the asymmetry guard — two same-range Modules would imply two roots / cyclic structure).

## Validation

- `npx vitest run test/unit/scope-resolution test/integration/resolvers` → **2514 passed / 77 skipped / 0 failed** (52 test files, 85 s).
- `npx tsc --noEmit` clean in both `gitnexus/` and `gitnexus-shared/`.
- Pre-commit hook (typecheck) green.
- End-to-end on PersistentWindows after rebuilding from this branch (verification on local Docker image): **3 prior `scope extraction failed for *.Designer.cs` warnings → 0**. Existing post-#1082 baseline is 1113 nodes / 2987 edges / 39 clusters / 97 flows; the 3 newly-recovered files contribute additional cross-file resolution beyond that baseline.

## Cross-language note

`canParentScope` is language-agnostic. Other languages whose query emits `(compilation_unit) @scope.module` plus a single same-range top-level scope (e.g. Python's `module` matching a single top-level `class_definition` on a file with no leading/trailing trivia) can naturally hit the same byte shape on minimal files; this fix applies to all of them uniformly.

## Test plan

- [x] `npx vitest run test/unit/scope-resolution test/integration/resolvers` (52 files / 2514 tests)
- [x] `npx tsc --noEmit` in both packages
- [x] New regression test fails on the original codebase (verified via empirical 4-case probe in #1086)
- [x] Asymmetry guard exercised by the third new `scope-tree.test.ts` case
- [ ] Maintainer to re-run on a wider corpus if desired

title: fix(server): sanitize repo name to prevent argument injection
body:
## Summary

Sanitizes the extracted repository name to prevent argument injection during `git clone` operations and ensures compatibility with various file systems.

## Motivation / context

When a user provides a repository URL that ends in a segment starting with a dash (e.g., `https://github.com/user/--upload-pack=payload.git`), the current implementation extracts `--upload-pack=payload` as the repository name. This name is then used as the target directory in the `git clone` command. Git interprets leading dashes in the target path as command-line flags, potentially leading to unintended behavior or security risks.

## Areas touched

- [x] `gitnexus/` (CLI / core / MCP server)

## Scope & constraints

**In scope**

- Stripping leading dashes from the extracted repository name.
- Sanitizing unsafe directory characters (`<>:"/\\|?*`) to ensure cross-platform compatibility.
- Added unit tests to verify the sanitization logic.

**Explicitly out of scope / not done here**

- Changes to the core indexing pipeline or UI.
- Broad architectural changes to the job management system.

## Implementation notes

The fix is applied within `extractRepoName` in `git-clone.ts`. I chose to strip all leading dashes rather than just the first one to ensure the resulting name never starts with a dash, regardless of how many were provided in the URL. I also added a generic sanitization step for common unsafe characters to make the clone directory more robust.

## Testing & verification

- [x] `cd gitnexus && npm test test/unit/git-clone.test.ts` (Verified the logic via new test cases for argument injection and unsafe characters).

## Risk & rollout

Low risk. This only affects the naming of the local clone directory. Existing indexes are not affected unless they are re-analyzed from a URL that previously triggered the issue.

## Checklist

- [x] PR body meets repo minimum length
- [x] No secrets, tokens, or machine-specific paths committed

title: Improvement: Restrict analysis scope to a configurable root directory in server mode
query command: BM25 FTS index always fails with "Cannot execute write operations in a read-only database"
body:
## Description

The `query` command's BM25 full-text search (FTS) index fails to build because the LadybugDB file is opened read-only at query time. Every `gitnexus query` call prints the following errors and returns empty `processes` / `process_symbols` results:

```
[gitnexus] FTS index ensure failed for repo "X" table "File" (index "file_fts"): Connection exception: Cannot execute write operations in a read-only database!. Will retry on next query.
[gitnexus] FTS index ensure failed for repo "X" table "Function" (index "function_fts"): Connection exception: Cannot execute write operations in a read-only database!. Will retry on next query.
[gitnexus] FTS index ensure failed for repo "X" table "Class" (index "class_fts"): Connection exception: Cannot execute write operations in a read-only database!. Will retry on next query.
[gitnexus] FTS index ensure failed for repo "X" table "Method" (index "method_fts"): Connection exception: Cannot execute write operations in a read-only database!. Will retry on next query.
[gitnexus] FTS index ensure failed for repo "X" table "Interface" (index "interface_fts"): Connection exception: Cannot execute write operations in a read-only database!. Will retry on next query.
```

## Repro Steps

1. `npm install -g gitnexus`
2. `cd <any repo> && gitnexus analyze --embeddings`
3. `gitnexus query "any search term"` — errors appear on every call

## Observed Behavior

- `query` returns `{"processes": [], "process_symbols": [], "definitions": [...]}` — `definitions` is populated via vector search, but `processes` and `process_symbols` are always empty.
- The "Will retry on next query" message is misleading: the error repeats on every subsequent `query` call without recovery.
- Vector search (embedding-based) works, so the DB connection itself is valid for reads — the issue is that FTS index creation requires write access, which is denied.
- `context`, `cypher`, and `impact` commands work correctly.

## Expected Behavior

`query` should return populated `processes` and `process_symbols` results using BM25 full-text search. The DB should be opened with write access (or FTS indexes should be built during `analyze`) so that index creation succeeds at query time.

## Environment

- macOS 15.3 (Darwin 25.3.0)
- Node.js v24.11.1
- gitnexus latest (npm)
- Reproduced on two separate repos (Python, ~80 files and ~200 files)

## Workaround

None known — the FTS index path is internal to gitnexus.

title: Python methods classified as kind="Function" despite has_method edge from owning class
body:
## Summary

`context()` and `impact()` return `kind: "Function"` for Python methods (both regular and dunder), even though gitnexus correctly records the `Class → method` `has_method` edge.  Queries that filter on `kind="Method"` therefore silently exclude all Python methods.

## Version

gitnexus 1.6.3

## Minimal reproducer

```python
# example.py
class Foo:
    def bar(self):
        """Regular instance method."""
        return 1

    def __getitem__(self, key):
        """Dunder method."""
        return None
```

```sh
mkdir /tmp/mwe && cd /tmp/mwe
# write example.py as above
git init -q && git add . && git -c user.email=a@b -c user.name=a commit -qm init
npx gitnexus analyze
```

Then via the MCP/CLI query layer:

```
context(name="bar")
  → "kind": "Function",
    "incoming": { "has_method": [ { "name": "Foo" } ] }

context(name="__getitem__")
  → "kind": "Function",
    "incoming": { "has_method": [ { "name": "Foo" } ] }
```

## Expected

Either:

1. `"kind": "Method"` when an inbound `has_method` edge exists, or
2. `kind="Method"` filters on `context()` / `impact()` should match symbols whose stored kind is `"Function"` but which have a `has_method` edge.

Today, `context(name="bar", kind="Method")` returns nothing useful, even though the same query without the `kind` filter does.

## Impact

Affects every Python codebase with classes.  The data is in the graph (the `has_method` edge is correct); only the `kind` label on the method symbol itself is misleading.  Practical consequence: developers who reach for `kind="Method"` to disambiguate common method names get empty/ambiguous results and have to fall back to the broader unfiltered search, which has more candidates to sort through.

May be related to #926 (LANG-python: Migrate Python to scope-based resolution).

title: tool_map returns identical flows array for every tool, instead of per-tool projection
body:
## Summary

`tool_map` reports the same `flows` array for every tool in a repo, regardless of what each tool actually calls.  The list appears to be a *repo-wide* enumeration tagged onto every tool entry, not a per-tool projection of the call graph rooted at that tool's handler.  The result is unusable per-tool detail and significant output bloat from N× duplication.

## Version

gitnexus 1.6.3

## Minimal reproducer

```python
# server.py
from mcp.server.fastmcp import FastMCP

mcp = FastMCP("demo")

def _helper_a():
    return "a"

def _helper_b():
    return _deep_b()

def _deep_b():
    return "b"

@mcp.tool()
def alpha():
    """Calls chain A."""
    return _helper_a()

@mcp.tool()
def beta():
    """Calls chain B (one level deeper)."""
    return _helper_b()
```

```sh
mkdir /tmp/mwe && cd /tmp/mwe
# write server.py as above; add a minimal pyproject.toml (or requirements.txt)
# referencing mcp so the import resolves
git init -q && git add . && git -c user.email=a@b -c user.name=a commit -qm init
npx gitnexus analyze
```

Then `tool_map` returns:

- `alpha.flows` and `beta.flows` are byte-identical despite distinct call graphs.
- Implausible cross-attributions: trivial tools come back with flows that pass through helpers they do not call.

## Expected

`flows` for tool `T` should be the set of execution flows reachable from `T`'s handler function via the call graph — i.e., a per-tool projection.  Two tools whose handlers call non-overlapping helpers should have non-overlapping `flows` arrays.

## Real-world severity

The symptom scales linearly with tool count.  On a server with ~20 `@mcp.tool()`-decorated functions in one file, every tool entry came back with the same ~70-element flows list, byte-identical across all 20.  Output ballooned to ~74 KB where the unique data was a few hundred bytes (tool names + handler paths); the rest was 19× duplication.  This makes `tool_map` impractical for the use case its description suggests (\"Understanding tool APIs, finding tool implementations, impact analysis for tool changes\") on any non-trivial multi-tool repo.

## Sub-issue (smaller)

`description` is empty for every tool, even when each handler has a non-trivial docstring (which is what FastMCP exposes as the MCP `description`).  Worth checking whether `tool_map` is intended to extract Python docstrings as descriptions; the MCP spec uses the docstring as the agent-facing description, so empty descriptions limit `tool_map`'s usefulness for understanding tool intent at a glance.

title: fix(group): add configurable cross-link path exclusions to reduce false positives
body:
## Problem

When running `group sync` on a large group (60 repos), the exact-match cross-linking pass produces a high volume of false-positive cross-links. In our case, 108 out of 108 cross-links were false positives — zero were real service dependencies.

Two categories of noise:

1. **Health-check endpoints** (`/ping`, `/health`, `/healthcheck`, etc.) — nearly every service exposes one. Since they all normalize to the same contract ID (e.g. `http::GET::/ping`), every consumer that hits `/ping` gets cross-linked to every provider that serves `/ping`. With 60 repos this produces N×M false links.

2. **Param-only catch-all routes** (`/{param}`, `/{param}/{param}`) — after path normalization, routes like `GET /:id`, `GET /{userId}`, and `GET /[slug]` all collapse to `http::GET::/{param}`. Any consumer fetching a parameterized path matches any provider with a single-param route, regardless of whether they're actually related.

These false links drown out the real cross-repo dependencies and make the contract registry unreliable for impact analysis.

## Solution

Add two new optional fields to `matching` in `group.yaml`:

```yaml
matching:
  exclude_links_paths:
    - /ping
    - /health
    - /healthcheck
    - /
  exclude_links_param_only_paths: true
```

- `exclude_links_paths` — explicit list of HTTP paths to exclude from cross-link matching. Contracts are still extracted and visible in the registry; they just don't participate in the matching pass.
- `exclude_links_param_only_paths` — boolean that filters out routes where every path segment is `{param}` (e.g. `/{param}`, `/{param}/{param}`).

**Defaults are `[]` and `false`** — no behavior change unless the operator explicitly configures exclusions. Fully backward compatible.

## Changes

- `types.ts` — added optional `exclude_links_paths` and `exclude_links_param_only_paths` to `MatchingConfig`
- `config-parser.ts` — added defaults for the new fields
- `matching.ts` — added `buildNoisyContractFilter()` that reads from config; wired into `buildProviderIndex()` and `runExactMatch()`
- `sync.ts` — passes `config.matching` through to `runExactMatch()`

## Verification

- All existing unit tests pass (47/47 in matching, config-parser, sync)
- Typecheck clean
- Tested on a 60-repo group:
  - Without config: 108 cross-links (original behavior preserved)
  - With exclusions configured: 2 cross-links (both verified as real service dependencies)
