title: analysis unity工程时报错
body:
### Area

gitnexus (CLI / core / indexing / MCP server)

### Summary

错误一：Scope '...' has kind 'Namespace' but no parent（大量 YooAsset 文件）                                                                                                       
                                                                                                                                                                                     
  原因：file-scoped namespace 的行解析 bug。                                                                                                                                         
                                                                                                                                                                                     
  C# 有两种命名空间写法：                                                                                                                                                            
  // 传统块命名空间（tree-sitter 节点: namespace_declaration）
  namespace YooAsset { ... }                                                                                                                                                         
                                                                                                                                                                                     
  // 文件级命名空间（C# 10+，tree-sitter 节点: file_scoped_namespace_declaration）                                                                                                   
  namespace YooAsset;  // ← 没有大括号，整个文件都在这个命名空间里                                                                                                                   
                                                                                                                                                                                     
  query.ts 第 42 行两种都映射为 @scope.namespace：                                                                                                                                   
  (file_scoped_namespace_declaration) @scope.namespace                                                                                                                               
                                                                                                                                                                                     
  问题在于： file_scoped_namespace_declaration 在 tree-sitter-c-sharp 中，其 AST 范围不包含 compilation_unit（Module scope）的完整范围，而是从 namespace X;                          
  这一行开始到文件末尾。scope-extractor.ts 里的 canParentScope() 用范围包含关系判断父子，导致 compilation_unit（Module） 和 file_scoped_namespace（Namespace）                       
  的范围无法正确建立包含关系，Namespace scope 找不到父节点，触发 non-module-requires-parent 不变量违反。                                                                             
                                                                                                                                                                                     
  这是 GitNexus C# scope 解析器的一个已知 bug，影响所有使用 namespace X; 语法的文件。                                                                                                
  
  ---                                                                                                                                                                                
  错误二：Invalid argument（PrimeTween、mcp-unity、大型文件）
                                                                                                                                                                                     
  两种来源：      
                                                                                                                                                                                     
  1. tree-sitter language 实例不匹配（前次分析已确认）：parse-worker 和 captures.ts 的 getCsharpParser() 用了不同 Parser 实例下的 grammar，跨实例调用 query.matches() 报 Invalid     
  argument                                                                                                                                                                           
  2. 大文件导致 bufferSize 相关：TweenGenerated.cs、Tommy.cs、JsonMapper.cs 这类大型生成文件，tree-sitter native binding 在某些边界尺寸下报错                                        
                                                                                                                                                                                     
  ---                                                      
致命错误：Phase 'scopeResolution' failed: Cannot add property 1, object is not extensible                                                                                          
                                                                                                                                                                                     
  这才是导致 analysis 完全失败的原因。
                                                                                                                                                                                     
  根据 validate-bindings-immutability.ts 的文档（issue #1066），这是 C# 的 populateNamespaceSiblings hook（namespace-siblings.ts）在 finalizeScopeModel 冻结 indexes.bindings        
  之后，仍然试图向已 freeze 的 BindingRef[] 数组 push 新元素，违反了 Contract Invariant I8。                                                                                         
                                                                                                                                                                                     
  错误链路：                                                                                                                                                                         
  finalizeScopeModel()
    → indexes.bindings 内的所有 BindingRef[] 数组被 Object.freeze()                                                                                                                  
      ↓                                                                                                                                                                              
  provider.populateNamespaceSiblings()  ← C# 专有 hook                                                                                                                               
    → 尝试 push 到已 frozen 的 indexes.bindings 内的数组                                                                                                                             
      ↓                                                                                                                                                                              
  TypeError: Cannot add property 1, object is not extensible                                                                                                                         
    → 未被 try/catch 包住，直接抛到 phase runner                                                                                                                                     
      ↓                                                                                                                                                                              
  Phase 'scopeResolution' failed  ← 整个索引失败                                                                                                                                     
                                                                                                                                                                                     
  ---                                                                                                                                                                                
  临时规避方案                                                                                                                                                                       
                                                                                                                                                                                     
  最直接的方式：禁用 C# scope resolution，降级为遗留 DAG：                                                                                                                           
                                                                                                                                                                                     
  REGISTRY_PRIMARY_CSHARP=0 npx gitnexus analyze                                                                                                                                     
                                                                                                                                                                                     
  这会跳过整个 scopeResolution phase 中的 C# 处理，所有 C# 文件走遗留 Call-Resolution DAG，索引正常完成。C# 的调用关系解析精度略低，但不影响其他语言。                               
                                                                                                                                                                                     
  ---                                                                                                                                                                                
  建议            
                                                                                                                                                                                     
  向 GitNexus 提 issue，附上以下信息：
                                                                                                                                                                                     
  1. Analysis failed: Phase 'scopeResolution' failed: Cannot add property 1, object is not extensible                                                                                
  2. 项目包含大量使用 namespace X;（C# 10 file-scoped namespace）语法的文件                                                                                                          
  3. 复现命令：REGISTRY_PRIMARY_CSHARP=1 npx gitnexus analyze（默认就会触发）

  这会跳过整个 scopeResolution phase 中的 C# 处理，所有 C# 文件走遗留 Call-Resolution DAG，索引正常完成。C# 的调用关系解析精度略低，但不影响其他语言。                               
                                                                                                                                                                                     
  ---                                                                                                                                                                                
  建议            
                                                                                                                                                                                     
  向 GitNexus 提 issue，附上以下信息：
                                                                                                                                                                                     
  1. Analysis failed: Phase 'scopeResolution' failed: Cannot add property 1, object is not extensible                                                                                
  2. 项目包含大量使用 namespace X;（C# 10 file-scoped namespace）语法的文件                                                                                                          
  3. 复现命令：REGISTRY_PRIMARY_CSHARP=1 npx gitnexus analyze（默认就会触发）                                                                                                        
  4. 建议修复点：namespace-siblings.ts 的 populateNamespaceSiblings hook 应改写 indexes.bindingAugmentations 而非 indexes.bindings

title: fix(lbug): robust Windows lock acquisition for CI integration tests
body:
## Summary

- Wraps `new lbug.Database()` in a bounded busy-retry inside `lbug-config.ts` — closes the gap where Windows CI fails with `Could not set lock on file` raised synchronously from LadybugDB's `local_file_system.cpp` *before* any query is issued (so `withLbugDb`'s query-time retry never sees it).
- Adds a Windows-only post-close handle-release probe in `safeClose` to absorb libuv's native handle-release lag; logs a warning if the probe exhausts so operators can spot AV/Defender interference.
- Adds a guarded stale-`.wal`/`.lock` sweep — fires only when the immediate-parent dir matches a known test prefix AND the path resolves under `os.tmpdir()`. Production paths never enter this branch.
- Tags exhausted open-time errors with `LBUG_OPEN_RETRY_EXHAUSTED` so `withLbugDb`'s outer 3× retry skips re-retrying — eliminates a 3×5=15-attempt / ~6s tail latency.
- Single source of truth: `isDbBusyError` lives in `lbug-config.ts` and is re-exported from `lbug-adapter.ts`. `waitForWindowsHandleRelease` and all retry knobs are co-located in `lbug-config.ts` with a one-grep cross-reference comment.

## Why this exists

The lock IO exception is thrown synchronously from `new lbug.Database()` (LadybugDB v0.16.1 [`local_file_system.cpp:126`](https://github.com/LadybugDB/ladybug/blob/v0.16.1/src/common/file_system/local_file_system.cpp#L126)). The existing `withLbugDb` query-time retry cannot intercept it because no query has been issued yet. On Windows CI this surfaces as flaky integration tests due to AV-scanner holds (≤200 ms typical), libuv handle-release lag, and stale `.wal` sidecars from aborted prior runs. LadybugDB's [concurrency model](https://docs.ladybugdb.com/concurrency) is preserved — single-writable-Database-per-process, multi-Connection.

## Test plan

- [x] `cd gitnexus && npx tsc --noEmit` — passes
- [x] `cd gitnexus && npx vitest run test/integration/lbug-open-retry.test.ts test/integration/lbug-close-handle-release.test.ts test/integration/lbug-lock-retry.test.ts` — 38/38 pass (12 new open-retry scenarios + 11 new isTestFixturePath/probe scenarios + 2 close-handle-release + 13 pre-existing lock-retry regressions)
- [x] `npx prettier --check` — clean
- [x] Pre-commit hook (typecheck + format on diff) — passes
- [ ] Windows CI run — confirm chronic lbug-touching integration test flakes resolved
- [ ] Linux/macOS CI runs — confirm no regression (Windows-only branches are gated on `process.platform === 'win32'`)

## Scope

- No public API surface changed (CLI flags, MCP tools, HTTP routes, graph schema unchanged).
- No persisted-data migration required.
- No `CHANGELOG.md` edit (owned by release process per `DoD.md` § 4.5).
- The two new test files are added to vitest's existing serialized `lbug-db` project (`fileParallelism: false`).

## Residual P3 follow-ups (intentional, non-blocking)

- Symlink-defense `lstat` guard before sweep `unlink` (mitigated by POSIX semantics + tightened guards)
- macOS `/var/folders` symlink prefix mismatch if caller realpaths first (not exercised today)
- Move `isReadOnlyDbError` into `lbug-config.ts` to model the new convention (out of scope here)

title: WSL2 + 1.6.4-rc.88 + ladybug 0.16.1: list/status/--version persistently SIGSEGV (~2.5GB dumps each, exit 0 masks crash) — related to #1427
body:
## Summary

`gitnexus list`, `gitnexus status`, even `gitnexus --version` consistently SIGSEGV on WSL2 (Linux subsystem on Windows 11) with **gitnexus 1.6.4-rc.88 + @ladybugdb/core 0.16.1** (current "fixed" rc). Each invocation produces a ~2.5 GB Node heap dump in `/mnt/c/Users/User/AppData/Local/Temp/wsl-crashes/`. Like #1427, exit 0 masks the crash.

This is the **upgrade target** for #1427 (which was 1.6.3) — yet the SIGSEGV persists.

## Environment

- OS: Windows 11 22H2 (WSL2, Ubuntu 24.04 / kernel 6.6.87.2-microsoft-standard-WSL2)
- Shell: bash inside WSL2
- Node: v22.15.0
- npm: 10.9.2
- gitnexus: **1.6.4-rc.88** (`npm install -g gitnexus@1.6.4-rc.88`)
- @ladybugdb/core: **0.16.1** (verified in `node_modules/@ladybugdb/core/package.json`)
- Repo under analysis: HIS (Python, ~1958 files, ~57k symbols, ~89k edges per old index)

## Symptom — Reproducer

Six `_usr_bin_node-11.dmp` files appear in `Temp\wsl-crashes\` over a 17-minute window during normal session activity (no `gitnexus analyze`, only `list/status/version`):

```
$ ls -lh /mnt/c/Users/User/AppData/Local/Temp/wsl-crashes/
-rwxrwxrwx 2.6G May  8 16:34 wsl-crash-1778229248-70635-_usr_bin_node-11.dmp
-rwxrwxrwx 2.5G May  8 16:42 wsl-crash-1778229768-82072-_usr_bin_node-11.dmp
-rwxrwxrwx 2.3G May  8 16:43 wsl-crash-1778229781-84903-_usr_bin_node-11.dmp
-rwxrwxrwx 2.4G May  8 16:43 wsl-crash-1778229793-87730-_usr_bin_node-11.dmp
-rwxrwxrwx 2.1G May  8 16:43 wsl-crash-1778229802-89722-_usr_bin_node-11.dmp
-rwxrwxrwx 2.5G May  8 16:51 wsl-crash-1778230300-102332-_usr_bin_node-11.dmp
total 15G
```

Timestamps line up exactly with our hooked `gitnexus list/status/--version` invocations after each Bash/Edit tool call. CLI commands "succeed" (exit 0, output text shown) but produce dumps anyway, like #1427's "exit 0 masks the segfault" pattern.

## Earlier Incident (severity context)

On the same machine, **gitnexus 1.6.3 + ladybug 0.15.4** produced a single **1.6 TB sparse dump file** (`wsl-crash-1778186296-693-_usr_bin_node-6.dmp = 1,716,618,649,592 bytes`) during `npx gitnexus analyze`. Filled the C drive completely (1.9 TB → 4 GB free). Recovery: `rm -rf Temp/wsl-crashes/*` reclaimed the full 1.6 TB.

We upgraded to 1.6.4-rc.88 specifically to pick up #1235 (ladybug 0.16.0) and #1243 (tree-sitter-c/cpp pin). The 1.6 TB sparse mode is gone, **but the underlying SIGSEGV is not** — now it's smaller (~2.5 GB per crash) but more frequent (every CLI invocation).

## What We Tried

| Action | Result |
|--------|--------|
| Upgrade 1.6.3 → 1.6.4-rc.88 | New crashes (smaller but still SIGSEGV) |
| ladybug 0.15.4 → 0.16.1 | No change |
| Disable global PreToolUse/PostToolUse hooks calling `npx gitnexus` | ✅ Stops auto-trigger crashes (~80% mitigation) |
| Run `npx gitnexus list` manually | Still crashes |
| Run `npx gitnexus status` manually | Still crashes |

## Hypothesis

Same root cause as #1427 (Windows tree-sitter native binding SIGSEGV) — but #1427 reports `analyze` SIGSEGV, while we see SIGSEGV on **read-only commands** (`list/status/--version`). Suggests the segfault is in CLI **bootstrap / language registration**, not in `analyze`'s tree-sitter parse pipeline. Worth checking if PR #1243's tree-sitter-c/cpp pin was sufficient or if other grammars (Python? TypeScript?) need similar treatment.

## Workaround We're Using

1. Removed gitnexus PreToolUse + PostToolUse hooks from `~/.claude/settings.json` (stops auto-invoke during Bash/Edit operations).
2. Plan to evaluate `colbymchenry/codegraph` (SQLite+FTS5, no HNSW, no tree-sitter native binding for vector storage) as a longer-term replacement if upstream fix doesn't land within ~2 weeks.

## Hopes

- Confirmation whether 1.6.4-stable (RC graduation) will include further segfault fixes for non-c/cpp grammars
- Or guidance on which `GITNEXUS_SKIP_OPTIONAL_GRAMMARS` subset is safe for Python-heavy repos
- Or stack trace / repro request — happy to provide full WSL2 + repo reproduction package

Cross-referencing: #1427, #1424, #1235, #1243.

title: feat: add Zig language support
body:
Adds Zig as a supported language: definition nodes (functions, methods, structs/enums/unions, fields, variables), IMPORTS edges (relative paths + build.zig.zon package deps), and CALLS edges (free calls and receiver-bound method dispatch, including on `union(enum)` receivers). Grammar: `@tree-sitter-grammars/tree-sitter-zig@1.1.2` as an **optionalDependency** — platforms without a prebuild get a one-line stderr warning, never a failed install. Its `peerOptional tree-sitter@^0.22.1` is aliased to the bundled `tree-sitter@0.21.x` via an npm `overrides` entry (ABI compatibility confirmed by the load smoke test).

## Zig language coverage

What the graph builds for each Zig construct, as of the current head. ✅ covered · ◐ partial · ✗ not covered (with the reason). Every ✅ is exercised by `zig-basic` / `zig-idioms` or a unit test; the "evidence" column names the edge or node the probe repository produced (see the [review write-up](https://claude.ai/code/artifact/2df8befb-639c-4a99-9aab-eae99154403d) for the full before/after matrix).

### Declarations → graph nodes

| Zig construct | Node | Status | Notes / evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| `fn` at file scope, incl. `pub`, `extern`, `export`, `inline`, `noinline`, `callconv(.c)` | Function | ✅ | `isExported` for `pub` or `export`; `visibility` follows `pub` only (`export fn` is C linkage, private to other Zig files); parameters, return type, `self` receiver |
| `fn` inside a container | Method | ✅ | HAS_METHOD from the container; `isStatic` when there is no receiver parameter — the FIRST parameter named `self` OR typed as the enclosing container (`replica: *Replica`, `pool: *@This()`, `c: *Self`), see `zigReceiverParameter`; the receiver is excluded from the parameter list and the `#<arity>` suffix |
| `const T = struct {…}`, `packed struct(u8)`, `extern struct` | Struct | ✅ | anonymous in the grammar; named from the binding. A container nested in a container is identified by its owner (`A.Item`, `B.Item`, `Outer.Inner`; methods `A.Item.run`) while the scope still binds the lexical `Item` — the Java `Outer.Inner` shape (review 8.5: two same-named nested types no longer share one node) |
| `const E = enum {…}`, `enum(u8)`, non-exhaustive `_` | Enum | ✅ | |
| `const U = union {…}`, `union(enum)`, `union(enum(u8))`, `packed union` | Union | ✅ | this head declares the `Union → Property/Method` schema pairs (analyze used to abort) |
| `const H = opaque {}` | Struct | ✅ | fieldless FFI handle; owns methods |
| container fields, enum variants, union variants | Property | ✅ | HAS_PROPERTY; all three are `container_field` in the grammar |
| `pub fn List(comptime T: type) type { return struct {…}; }` | Struct + Function, same name | ✅ | the returned container is named after the constructor and owns its members (`Stack → push`, `Stack → items`) |
| `pub const X = …`, `pub var x`, `threadlocal var`, `extern var` at container scope | Const / Variable | ✅ | keyword-gated: `x = 5;` and `_ = expr;` are keyword-less `variable_declaration`s in tree-sitter-zig and are not bindings |
| `const Err = error{ A, B }`, `const Alloc = std.mem.Allocator`, `const Cb = *const fn () void`, `const B = List(u8)` | Const | ✅ | recorded as constants (not Enum / TypeAlias); type aliases still bind their target on the scope side, see type resolution |
| function-body locals | — | ✗ | not graph nodes, same as every other language (they still bind on the scope side) |
| `test "name" {…}` | Function (`"name"`, quoted) | ✅ | calls inside attribute to the test node; quoted so it cannot merge with `fn name` |
| `test Foo {…}` (decl test), anonymous `test {…}` | — | ✅ by design | scopes without a node; their calls attribute to the File |
| file-as-struct: a file with top-level fields (`Page.zig`, usually with `const Page = @This();`), or a FIELDLESS file whose top-level fn takes the file's own type (`Empty.zig`: `const Self = @This(); pub fn ping(self: *Self)`) | Struct named after the file stem; top-level fns → Method, fields → Property | ✅ | `Struct:src/Page.zig:Page`, `Method:…:Page.getArena#0`, HAS_METHOD / HAS_PROPERTY; the file-level `@This()` alias is not a Const; a file with neither fields nor a self-typed receiver stays a namespace (review 8.12: `zig-chains` `Empty.zig` — `Empty{}` and `e.ping()` resolve from an importer) |
| `comptime {…}` blocks, `usingnamespace` as a declaration, `@cImport`, `@embedFile` | — | ✗ | no graph meaning (usingnamespace is handled as an import, below) |

### Imports → IMPORTS edges

| Form | Status | Notes / evidence |
|---|---|---|
| `@import("./x.zig")`, `@import("x.zig")`, `@import("../x.zig")`, `@import("dir/x.zig")` | ✅ | importer-relative; parent traversal above the repo root and absolute paths return nothing |
| `@import("std")`, `@import("builtin")`, `@import("root")`, `@import("build_options")` | ✅ external | resolved to nothing on purpose, never suffix-matched to a same-named local file |
| `@import("mod")` for a module the repo's OWN `build.zig` declares (`addModule("mod", …)`, `addImport("mod", createModule(…))`, `exe.root_module.addImport(…)`, `.imports = &.{ .{ .name, .module } }`, `addImport("api", dep.module("core"))`) | ✅ | Lightpanda's `@import("lightpanda")` in 378 of 567 files; works without a `build.zig.zon`; `addOptions().createModule()` and `.url` deps stay external. Import tables are PER BUILD MODULE (review 8.2): a source file resolves a bare name through the table of the module whose root it is, else of the module(s) whose root directory is its deepest prefix; same-directory modules that disagree resolve nothing (fail closed); then the repo-wide `addModule` names, then zon deps (`zig-buildmodules` fixture: two modules each `addImport("config", …)` to a different root) |
| `@import("dep")` for a `build.zig.zon` `.path` dep | ✅ | root declared in the dep's `build.zig` (`addModule("dep", .{ .root_source_file = … })`), then `src/root.zig`, `src/dep.zig`, `src/main.zig`; evidence: `main.zig → libs/mylib/src/root.zig` |
| `.url` deps in `build.zig.zon` | ✅ external | unpacked outside the repo, so nothing to link |
| `const X = @import("x.zig").X` (named), `const Y = @import("x.zig").X` (alias) | ✅ | named / alias imports; `use → incr` through the aliased `Counter` |
| deep member alias `const chosen = @import("lib.zig").B.work;`, `const w = lib.B.work;`, `const Inner = nested.Outer.Inner;` | ✅ | NOT a named import of the tail (that let `A.work`, declared first, answer for `B.work` — review 8.4): the module is bound as a namespace and every use site of the alias (`chosen()`, `Inner{}`) is rewritten to the written owner path (`lib.B` . `work`), which the chain walk resolves |
| `const X = ns.X` where `ns` is an `@import` binding of the file | ✅ | promoted to a named import (one level only; deeper chains are deep aliases, above); the same edges as above |
| `const m = @import("x.zig")` INSIDE a fn body | ✅ | bound and used under a per-callable key (`m$f_sib_a`): finalization flattens every import onto the module scope, so two sibling fns binding `m` to different files used to share one `m → [a.zig, b.zig]` bucket and both resolved into the first (review 8.9: `zig-chains` `f_sib_a` / `f_sib_b`) |
| `pub usingnamespace @import("x.zig")` | ✅ | wildcard import with expansion of the target's top-level names |
| `_ = @import("x.zig")` inside `test {}` / `comptime {}` | ✅ | file edge only |
| `@import(...)` used inline as an expression — tuple element, call argument, comparison operand, `@import("x.zig").f()` receiver | ✅ | side-effect import (file edge) once per source; the member-call receiver form also resolves the call (Lightpanda's `bridge.zig` lists ~290 modules this way) |

### Calls → CALLS edges

| Form | Status | Notes / evidence |
|---|---|---|
| free call `helper()` | ✅ | |
| namespace call `mod.fn()`, `mod.sub.fn()`, and every longer chain of handles — `hub.sub.Thing.make()` (a module republished by a hub), `nested.Outer.Inner{}` (a type nested in a type), `opmod.Op.lookup.event_max()` (an enum variant through the module), `x: mod.Outer.Inner` | ✅ | `main → connect`, `main → libHello`; the qualified receiver is walked segment by segment from its verified import (`ScopeResolver.resolveNamespaceChains`, review 8.10), each hop a class-like member or a republished namespace import, ambiguous hops resolve nothing; `zig-hub`'s `c9_enum_qualified_variant_receiver → event_max` is asserted |
| static call on a type `Counter.init()`, `mod.Counter.init()` | ✅ | `main → init`, `make → init` |
| method call on a typed receiver `x.method()` | ✅ | every type source in the next table |
| `self.method()` inside a container method | ✅ | `twice → incr`, `incr → log`, `b_selfThis → a_selfPtr` |
| calls inside `defer` / `errdefer` / `try` / `catch` / `orelse` / `switch` arms | ✅ | plain call expressions inside those forms |
| callable value flow `const f = target; f()` (and through a parameter) | ✅ | main's per-language gate; `extractCallArguments` because `call_expression` has no argument-list node |
| struct literal `T{…}` (no parens) — bare `return SpawnRequest{ .a = x }`, imported `var s = Session{…}`, qualified `mod.T{…}` / `hub.sub.T{…}` | ✅ construction site | a CALLS edge to the container node (the Rust `T { .. }` / Go `T{}` shape), whose `reason` ends in ` (constructor)` — `local-call (constructor)` same-file, `import-resolved (constructor)` cross-file; an invocation never carries the suffix. A qualified literal resolves INSIDE the module its receiver is bound to (the path `mod.fn()` takes), so `a.Thing{}` and `b.Thing{}` bind their own files, `c.Thing{}` with no `Thing` in c.zig binds nothing, and `std.Thread.Mutex{}` binds nothing even next to a local `Mutex`. Independently of the marker, a CALLS edge whose target is a Struct/Union is always a construction site: Zig has no Constructor nodes and a generic type constructor `List(u8)` links to its Function node |
| array literal of a type `[_]mod.T{ .{…}, .{…} }`, `[N]T{…}` | — by design | an `array_type` + initializer: the element type is the array's type annotation, each `.{…}` is the anonymous literal that constructs. Not a construction site of `T` (the second re-test counted 92 such sites; the types only ever built this way — `PathIntent`, `SpacetimeStep` — show no CALLS edge, correctly) |
| static call on a generic instantiation `Stack(u8).init()` | ◐ | the receiver types the binding (`t.top()` resolves) but `init` itself is not linked |
| generic instantiation literal `List(u8){…}`, `lists.List(u8){…}`; inline-import literal `@import("a.zig").Thing{…}` | ✅ construction site | the outer aggregate is its own `(constructor)`-marked site on the initializer (review 8.11); `@import(…)` in type position binds the module as a namespace exactly as the call-receiver form does |
| result-location literals `const a: Counter = .init(1);`, `const b: Counter = .{ .n = 2 };`, `return .init(3)` in `fn f() Counter`, field default `n: Counter = .init(0)` | ✅ | the expected type (annotation / return type / field type, `@This()` and `Self` rewritten) is the receiver of a synthesized site: the `init` call and the `Counter` construction reach the graph (review 8.6). Argument position (`f(.init(1))`) is not: the expected type is the callee's parameter |
| callback through a MODULE-level value receiver `global_runner.run(cb)` | ✅ | `zigHostValueNames`: a file/container-level `var`/`const` whose declaration shape says value (annotated, struct literal, non-type call, literal) is prepended as `self` like a fn-local receiver, so `cb` joins formal `cb@1` rather than `self@0` (review 8.3); alias-shaped values (`const mem = std.mem`) are not |
| chained calls `a.b().c()`, `reexport.Counter.init().incr()` | ◐ | one hop through a bound local (`const s = p.getSession(); s.name()`); an unbound chain receiver is not typed |
| through a field `self.c.incr()`, `s.inner.f()`, `self.session.browser.getViewport()` | ✅ | field types are class-scope type bindings; multi-level chains fold through them |
| function pointers `cb()`, `@call(...)`, `@field(x, "f")()` | ✗ | dynamic |
| builtins `@sizeOf`, `@as`, `@intCast`, … | — by design | not calls; `@import` is an import |

### Type resolution — where a receiver's type comes from

| Source | Status | Notes / evidence |
|---|---|---|
| `self: *T`, `self: T`, `self: *const T`, and a first parameter typed as the container under any name (`replica: *Replica`, `pool: *@This()`, `s: *const Self`) | ✅ | first parameter only — a later `self` is an ordinary parameter, and a first parameter of ANOTHER type (`o: *Other`) is not a receiver. `self` is a convention: tigerbeetle names the receiver after its type in 777 of 1127 methods, mach writes `pool: *@This()` in 764 of 833 |
| `self: *Self` with `const Self = @This();`, `self: *@This()` | ✅ | `twice → incr`, `b_selfThis → a_selfPtr` |
| other parameters `c: *Counter` | ✅ | `takes → deinit` |
| struct literal `T{…}`, `mod.T{…}` | ✅ | `run → c_selfVal`, `main → open` |
| generic instantiation literal `List(u8){…}`, `mod.List(u8){…}` | ✅ | `run → push`, cross-file `main → len` |
| declared type `var x: T = undefined`, decl literals `const x: T = .init()` / `.empty`, `: mod.T` | ✅ | the 0.14+ std idiom; `main → twice`, `main → get` |
| constructor call `var c = T.init()`, `mod.T.init()`, `List(u8).init()` | ✅ | `main → incr`, `t.top()`; a value receiver (`std.mem.split(...)`) declines cleanly |
| pointer / optional / error-union / slice / array wrappers `?*T`, `!T`, `[]T`, `[N]T`, `[*:0]const u8` | ✅ | stripped by `normalizeZigTypeName` |
| return type of a free function `var h = make(); h.incr()` and of a method on a typed receiver `const el = node.asElement()` | ✅ | `@type-binding.return` (error unions / pointers / optionals normalised); `const t = util.makeThing()` through a NAMESPACE is not followed |
| constructor calls under `try` / `catch` / `orelse` / parentheses `const p = try Page.init(…)` | ✅ | the wrapper is unwrapped; the shape of nearly every Zig constructor call |
| file-as-struct receivers `page: *Page`, `var q: Page`, `var p = Page.init()` where `Page = @import("Page.zig")` | ✅ | the namespace import also binds the file's type; a hub's `pub const X = @import("X.zig")` republishes it (`const Arena = lp.Arena;`) |
| through a HUB module — `terminal.Terminal.init()`, `stdx.PRNG.from_seed()`, `t: stdx.Thing`, `var p = stdx.PRNG.from_seed()`, `h: stdx.BoundedArrayType(u8, 4)`, `stdx.helper()` where the hub is a file made only of `pub const X = @import(…)` / `@import(…).X` | ✅ | the hub owns no local binding, so the local-only export lookup found nothing; `namespaceExportsIncludeImportedNames` (Zig opts in) reads the finalized channel. Measured on ghostty: CALLS into `src/terminal/` from outside it went from 46 to 253; on tigerbeetle, into the `stdx` hub from outside it 837 → 1500 |
| enum variant as receiver `Operation.create_accounts.event_max()`, `op.event_max()` with `op: Operation` | ✅ | a variant's type is its enum: `emitZigScopeCaptures` emits a field binding per variant, and the field walk types `Op.create` as `Op` (147 sites in tigerbeetle) |
| type aliases `const LocalAlias = Local;`, `const T2 = Thing;`, `const B = util.List(u8);` (also inside a fn body) | ✅ | the alias name binds its target's type; `B.init()`, `B{}`, `x: B` dispatch |
| payload captures `if (opt) \|v\|`, `for (items) \|it\|` / `\|*it\|` / `\|it, i\|`, `while (it.next()) \|x\|` | ✅ | element / optional payload of the subject's written type; `catch \|err\|` and `switch` prongs are not |
| unwrap / deref / index bound to a local `const t = items[i]`, `const t = o.?`, `const t = p.*` | ✅ | one-layer projections; expression receivers `items[i].f()`, `o.?.f()`, `(try f()).m()` are not typed |
| `anytype`, `comptime T: type` parameters, `@TypeOf(x)` | ✗ | comptime; out of scope for a static index |
| method dispatch through `usingnamespace` mixins | ◐ | names are imported; owner-less on the mixin side |
| function-local and anonymous containers `const R = struct {…}` inside a fn, `struct { fn lessThan … }.lessThan` | ✅ | identity `enclosingFn$R` / `host$N` (Java local-class shape); no owner-less Method, no id collision between builders |

### Not modelled, on purpose

Inheritance (Zig has none: no `@heritage` captures, the MRO is the type itself), overloading (none; arity is a bounds check that turns on if arity captures are ever added), `async`/`await` (removed from the language), and `usingnamespace` semantics beyond the import edge (removed in 0.15).

## Design decisions a reviewer might question

- **Method labeling via `labelOverride`** (Kotlin's pattern), not `@definition.method` query captures — Zig methods are plain `function_declaration`s whose only distinguishing feature is a container ancestor. One predicate (`isZigContainerMethod`) feeds both the worker structure phase and the scope-capture relabel so the two label sources cannot drift.
- **Container declaration anchors sit on the container node, not the `variable_declaration` wrapper** (`languages/zig/query.ts`). Zig containers are anonymous (`const Pioneer = struct {…}`); anchoring on the container makes its range equal the `@scope.class` range, so the def lands in its own class scope (what `populateClassOwnedMembers` expects) while the extractor's existing auto-hoist puts the name binding in the parent scope. The plain-variable capture group for the same node is filtered in `captures.ts` so a name binds exactly once.
- **Unresolvable imports return empty, not null** (`import-resolvers/configs/zig.ts`): `@import("std")`, `.url`-based zon deps, and missing files stop the strategy chain instead of falling through to suffix matching, which could ghost-match an unrelated same-named file.
- **`fieldFallbackOnMethodLookup` off** in the scope resolver — Zig is statically typed; the contract docs say the heuristic over-connects for such languages.
- **Classification stays `experimental`** in `language-classification.ts`, so Zig does not gate any Ring-4 governance.

## Real-project audit (2026-09-02)

Three real Zig projects, indexed with this branch: tigerbeetle (246 `.zig` files), mach (132), ghostty (788). Method reachability — the share of Zig `Method` nodes with at least one incoming CALLS — before → after the audit commit:

| Project | Methods with a caller, before | after |
|---|---|---|
| tigerbeetle | 2249 / 3544 (63 %) | 2272 / 3544 (64 %) |
| mach | 1047 / 2967 (35 %) | 1051 / 2967 (35 %) |
| ghostty | 2766 / 5016 (55 %) | 2865 / 5016 (57 %) |

Three shapes accounted for most of the misses; each was isolated on a micro fixture before touching the resolver, and each fix is pinned by the `zig-hub` / `zig-receivers` fixtures:

1. **Hub modules.** `pub const Terminal = @import("Terminal.zig");` in `terminal/main.zig`, `pub const PRNG = @import("prng.zig");` in `stdx.zig`, `pub const Quat = q.Quat(f32);` in `math/main.zig`. A file made only of re-exports owns no local binding, and the namespace paths (receiver-bound Case 1 / Case 3, the compound resolver) looked up members with `findExportedDef`, which reads local bindings only. Before: CALLS into ghostty's `src/terminal/` from outside that directory numbered 46 for 150 `terminal.Terminal.` sites alone; tigerbeetle's `stdx` hub hid 136 `stdx.Type.fn(` calls and 289 `: stdx.Type` annotations; mach's `math.Quat` / `math.Mat4x4` static calls (140+) reached nothing. The one case that did resolve (`stdx.Thing.make()`) did so through the workspace-unique-callable fallback, not through the hub. After: CALLS into ghostty's `src/terminal/` from outside it 46 → 253; into tigerbeetle's `src/stdx/` from outside it 837 → 1500; mach's `src/math/` stays at 0 → 0 because its hub publishes generic INSTANTIATIONS (`pub const Quat = q.Quat(f32);`), a Const alias of a call rather than a type — the known `◐ static call on a generic instantiation` row above, not a hub problem. Two ghostty files are outside every measurement: `Terminal.zig` (578 KB) and `PageList.zig` (715 KB) are skipped by the analyzer's global large-file rule (>512 KB; `--max-file-size` / `GITNEXUS_MAX_FILE_SIZE` raise it) — Zig keeps tests in the implementation file, so its core files cross that line.
2. **Enum variants as receivers.** `Operation.create_accounts.event_max(…)` — 147 sites in tigerbeetle — never resolved: the variant carries no written type. Its type is the enum itself; the capture layer now emits a field binding per variant and the existing field walk does the rest. `event_max` callers in tigerbeetle: 0 → 40.
3. **Receivers named after their type.** tigerbeetle writes `replica: *Replica` (777 of 1127 methods), mach `pool: *@This()` (764 of 833). Only `self` counted as a receiver, so those methods were `isStatic: true`, their `#<arity>` counted the receiver, and the scope binding was sourced as a plain parameter. Dispatch already worked through the parameter annotation, so this is a metadata fix, but it is the metadata `context()` and the method ids show. `zigReceiverParameter` is now the single rule for the structure and scope phases.

What the audit did NOT change, with the numbers that say why it can wait: receivers reached through an index or unwrap expression (`replicas_missing_ops[op].count()`), long chains through fields typed by generic instantiations (`self.io.terminal.screens.active.pages.pin()` in ghostty, `q.pool.release()` with `pool: Pool(Node)` in mach), and comptime-typed receivers (`anytype`). The remaining unresolved member names are dominated by `std` calls (`eql`, `print`, `expectEqual`, `maxInt`, `allocator`), which are external by design.

## Required grammar-present CI (2026-08-20)

The same review raised one blocking finding, and it is right. The Zig suites gate on `isLanguageAvailable(Zig)`, and the ABI smoke accepts a clean load failure for an optional grammar. Both are the correct contract for a platform with no prebuild. Together they leave a hole: if the grammar never installed on any runner, this PR would merge with all eight Zig resolver suites plus the structure-phase suite reported green-by-skip, having never executed the native Zig parser once.

`test(zig): fail CI when the optional Zig grammar is absent` closes it with the `GITNEXUS_REQUIRE_FTS` idiom the `tests` job already uses. `GITNEXUS_REQUIRE_ZIG=1` says "this runner has a prebuild, the grammar must be here", and a missing grammar then fails instead of skipping. tree-sitter-zig 1.1.2 publishes prebuilds for `{darwin,linux,win32}-{x64,arm64}`, so the flag goes on two required jobs whose runners are all covered: the sharded ubuntu `tests` job and the three-OS `abi-assert` job.

- `test/helpers/optional-grammar.ts` — the language → variable registry, plus `describeGrammarPresence`, an assertion that fails when the grammar is required but absent. It is a separate test on purpose, not a flip of the suites themselves from skip to fail: a skipped suite reports success, so only a failing test can turn "Zig never ran" into a red job.
- `parser-loader-abi.test.ts` — the optional exemption is revoked for a language the environment declares required, so an ABI-broken Zig binding fails the smoke instead of passing as a clean absence.
- `optional-grammar-gate.test.ts` — pins the two ways the gate could silently never fire: reading a variable name CI does not set, or accepting a value CI does not write.

A run that leaves the variable unset behaves exactly as before, so local runs and any future prebuild-less platform still skip. Checked in all three directions here. With `GITNEXUS_REQUIRE_ZIG=1` alone: 149 passed, 0 skipped across the four Zig files. With `GITNEXUS_SKIP_OPTIONAL_GRAMMARS=1` forcing the grammar away: 2 failures, each naming what to install or which flag to drop. With the skip flag but no require flag: green-by-skip, as before.

Two things this does not change. Zig stays an `optionalDependency`; the gate makes CI prove the grammar installs, it does not make Zig a hard dependency for users. And `check-tree-sitter-upgrade-readiness.py`'s curated `GRAMMARS` list still has no zig entry, as noted in the local CI section below. That list drives the static ABI assertion, which now has the dynamic smoke behind it on all three OSes.

## Out of scope (deferred)

The ✗ rows of the coverage tables above, in one list:

- A receiver annotated with a dotted re-export path (`arena: *lp.Arena` where `lightpanda.zig` re-exports `Arena`) — the namespace-member lookup (`findExportedDef`) only sees locally declared names; following `reexportsName` there is a shared change. `const Arena = lp.Arena;` (the more common spelling) works.
- Return type of a call through a namespace (`const t = util.makeThing()`), expression receivers (`items[i].f()`, `o.?.f()`, `(try f()).m()`), `catch |err|` / `switch` payloads, the two-hop `pub const bridge = js.Bridge(T)` where `Bridge` forwards to another type constructor
- `comptime` / `anytype` / `@TypeOf` — comptime evaluation is out of reach for a static index
- Arity metadata on declarations — Zig has no overloading; `arityCompatibility` is a real bounds check that activates if arity captures are ever added
- Promotion to `production` classification

## Test plan

- [x] `test/integration/resolvers/zig.test.ts` (86 tests — `zig-basic`, `zig-idioms`, `zig-filestruct`, `zig-qualified-literal`, `zig-hub`, `zig-receivers`, `zig-chains` — plus `zig-build-modules.test.ts`, 4 tests on `zig-buildmodules`; `zig-basic` + `zig-idioms` fixtures; the projection case now also covers the deref of a pointer capture, `viaPtrCaptureDeref`): Struct/Enum/Union labels with a negative Tag-is-not-Class check, Function vs Method labeling, IMPORTS edge for `@import("./pioneer.zig")`, CALLS edges `main → helper` (free), `main → tick` (receiver-bound through a namespace-qualified constructor), `main → isEnergy` (union receiver; fails when the `isClassLike` widening is reverted), and the phantom-binding regression case (`const h = helper;` binds only `h`)
- [x] Zig entries in main's per-language gates: `callable-value-flow.test.ts` matrix case (assign → copy → argument → invoke resolves `invoke → target`), `external-import-conformance.test.ts` case, `import-target-index-reuse.contract.test.ts` fixture
- [x] `test/unit/zig-import-resolver.test.ts` (45 tests, incl. per-build-module tables and `parseZigBuildModules` shapes): relative paths, build.zig.zon parsing, `.path` vs `.url` deps, repo-escaping paths, `.path = "."`, parent traversal above the repo root, absolute paths, commented-out entries, braces in comments/strings, a `.dependencies = .{` inside a string, a `.path` nested inside an entry, missing conventional layout; the absolute-spellings case now also rejects UNC (`\\server\share\dep`) and root-relative (`\dep`) Windows paths
- [x] `test/unit/zig-extractors.test.ts` (72 tests, incl. the review 8.4 / 8.5 / 8.6 / 8.9 / 8.12 capture-side contracts): export detection of methods vs their container, receiver vs parameters (first-position `self`, or a first parameter typed as the container, including a file-struct named by the file stem), return type from the `type:` field, variable extractor skipping container/import bindings and reading types from the `type:` field
- [x] `parser-loader-skip-optional.test.ts`: `GITNEXUS_SKIP_OPTIONAL_GRAMMARS` covers Zig (`=1` and `=zig`)
- [x] Existing gates extended: parser-loader ABI smoke case, grammar-literal validation gate (both skip cleanly when the optional grammar is absent), `parsing.test.ts` fixture list, `ingestion-utils` detection
- [x] C / C++ / Rust resolver suites pass (they share the Union label space)
- [x] `tsc --noEmit` clean on both packages, prettier and eslint clean on the diff; local full suite at the rebased head (after the tenth review pass): 18 311 passed / 69 skipped. The 5 failures on my machine are environmental, not from this branch: `analyzer-identity` (×4) and `evidence-provenance-helper` fail identically on a pristine `origin/main` worktree (macOS `/private/var` realpath, golden digest); `gitnexus/hooks/` is untouched by this branch. The Zig suites also pass under `GITNEXUS_REQUIRE_ZIG=1` with zero skips (darwin-arm64 prebuild), and both benchmark fingerprint gates (`bench/python-scope`, `bench/scope-capture`, 15 languages) pass.
- [x] End-to-end: `gitnexus analyze` on a throwaway Zig repo resolves cross-file CALLS (`main → pioneer.tick`, `main → isEnergy`) and IMPORTS.
- [x] The 20 pending workflow jobs reproduced locally at the branch head, see "Local CI pass" below (the fork PR still needs maintainer approval for the real runs)

To try it locally: `npm install && npm run build` in `gitnexus/`, then `npx vitest run test/integration/resolvers/zig.test.ts`, or point `gitnexus analyze` at any Zig repo (e.g. one using `build.zig.zon` path deps).

## Review pass (2026-08-18): findings, fixes and proof

I read the branch as a Zig systems reader, against the master language reference and tree-sitter-zig 1.1.2 by AST dump, and indexed a scratch repository of idiomatic Zig end to end. The write-up with the before/after matrix and the evidence per finding lives here: https://claude.ai/code/artifact/2df8befb-639c-4a99-9aab-eae99154403d

Three commits close everything that could be closed on the branch:

| Commit | What it fixes |
|--------|---------------|
| `fix(zig): declare the Union relation pairs — analyze aborted on any union` | The blocker. `gitnexus analyze` exited 1 on every Zig repo declaring a `union`, including this PR's own `zig-basic` fixture. `Union` was not in `LINKABLE_LABELS`, so no `FROM Union` pair reached the LadybugDB schema and the first HAS_PROPERTY/HAS_METHOD edge from a Union node was rejected. Resolver tests never write to the DB, which is why the suite stayed green. `Union` is now linkable, `structural-pair-coverage` gains an optional-grammar corpus with `zig-basic`, and the Rust `union_item` note is updated. The DDL fingerprint changes (#2808), so existing indexes rebuild on the next analyze. |
| `feat(zig): resolve path deps through the dep's build.zig and src/root.zig` | `zig init` has laid libraries out as `src/root.zig` since 0.12; the resolver only knew `src/<name>.zig` and `src/main.zig`. It now tries the root the dep's own `build.zig` declares (`addModule("<name>", .{ .root_source_file = b.path("…") })`), then `src/root.zig`, `src/<name>.zig`, `src/main.zig`. |
| `feat(zig): Const/Variable defs, member imports, receiver typing, generic type constructors` | `ZIG_QUERIES` had no `@definition.const/variable`, so `pub const`, `pub var`, error sets and type aliases were absent from the graph and `zigVariableConfig` never ran. `const X = @import("x.zig").X`, `const X = ns.X` and `usingnamespace @import(…)` lost their IMPORTS edge. `var x: T = undefined`, decl literals such as `const x: T = .init()`, and `var c = T.init()` typed nothing. `fn List(comptime T: type) type { return struct {…} }` left its methods without an owner. `visibility` reported `export fn` as public although only `pub` is reachable from other Zig files. Every new rule is gated on the literal `const`/`var` keyword: tree-sitter-zig 1.1.2 parses statement assignments (`x = 5;`, `_ = expr;`) as keyword-less `variable_declaration`s, which had minted a phantom local per assignment. |

One finding stays deferred, with the reasoning in the write-up: file-as-struct dispatch (`const Widget = @This();` at file top, `w.grow()` called from another file) needs the file's module scope to own its top-level fns and fields. That is a shared-code design change, not a Zig-local rule.

Correction to item 3 of "Shared code touched" above: `languages/c/query.ts` does emit `@declaration.union` (with `(union_specifier) @scope.class`), so the `isClassLike('Union')` widening reaches C. I checked a C repo with unions on both heads: it indexes either way, and C union fields simply gain an owner.

Proof, from a clean re-index of the scratch repo (104 nodes, 213 edges, exit 0; the reviewed head exits 1 on the same repo): `main → incr` via `var c = Counter.init()`; `main → twice` and `main → get` via `var b: Counter = undefined` and `const e: Counter = .init()`; `use → incr` through `const Counter = counter.Counter` and through `@import("counter.zig").Counter`; `main.zig → libs/mylib/src/root.zig` for a path dep; `Stack` owning `push/top/clear/items` with `run → push`, and cross-file `main → len` through `counter.List(u8){}`; `useIt → isEnergy` on a `union(enum)` receiver.

Tests added: the `zig-idioms` fixture with 10 resolver cases, unit cases for each new rule in `zig-extractors.test.ts` and `zig-import-resolver.test.ts`, and the `zig-basic` corpus entry. Gates: `tsc --noEmit` clean, prettier and eslint clean, targeted 18-file run 1 130 passed; full suite 18 116 passed / 66 skipped / 8 failed, the same 8 environmental failures listed in the test plan above (`analyzer-identity`, `embedding-runtime-install`, `evidence-provenance-helper`, the two `hooks-e2e` pnpm cases), none in a file this branch touches.

## Real-world corpus pass (2026-08-18): Lightpanda

After the review passes above, the branch was measured against a production Zig codebase, [Lightpanda](https://github.com/lightpanda-io/browser) (567 `.zig` files, 531 indexed), with a repeatable gate: a tree-sitter census of every call site, import and declaration in the corpus, joined against the CALLS / IMPORTS edges the index produced, and, for each gap, a minimal repository run through the real CLI. The write-up with the findings, repros and thread verdicts: https://claude.ai/code/artifact/167688ce-5479-4a00-9fc9-2cb5cffdcde7

Fourteen commits close it (from `fix(zig): resolve @import of the repo's own build.zig modules` to `fix(zig): give function-local and anonymous containers an identity`). Each commit body says what it changes; the table is the corpus before and after.

| Lightpanda | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| CALLS edges | 13,885 | 20,949 |
| IMPORTS edges · in-repo `@import("x.zig")` pairs without an edge | 3,014 · 417 | 3,801 · 5 (all under a `cache/` directory the default ignore list skips) |
| `@import("lightpanda")` (the repo's own `build.zig` module) resolved | 0 of 378 files | 378 |
| method call on a parameter typed by another file (`page: *Page`) | 23 / 993 (2.3 %) | 993 / 993 |
| `self.field.method()` | 9 / 2,803 (0.3 %) | 1,473 / 2,803 (52.6 %) |
| local bound by `try` / `catch` / `orelse` around a call | 12 / 1,298 (0.9 %) | 770 / 1,298 (59.3 %) |
| local bound by a call's return | 80 / 1,282 (6.2 %) | 440 / 1,282 (34.3 %) |
| payload-captured receiver (`\|v\|`) | 20 / 1,085 (1.8 %) | 384 / 1,085 (35.4 %) |
| local bound by a field read (`const p = self.page`) | 4 / 1,902 (0.2 %) | 461 / 1,902 (24.2 %) |
| type-alias receiver (`const B = List(u8)`) | 6 / 63 | 44 / 63 |
| `@import("x.zig").f()` inline receiver | 0 / 80 | 72 / 80 |
| Method / Property nodes without an owner | 49 / 2,395 | 0 / 5 |
| `function_declaration`s with no graph node (id collisions) | 51 | 0 |
| wrong `callable-value-flow` self-loops (`Global.deinit → Global.deinit`) | 10 | 0 |
| `candidate set exceeded the cap` warnings per `analyze` | 4,761 | 2 |
| `self.method()`, free calls, `mod.fn()` | 99.2 % · 97.5 % · 79.3 % | 100 % · 97.5 % · 83.6 % |

`impact getArena` on `Page.zig` went from 0 callers / `risk: UNKNOWN` (159 call sites in the corpus) to 23 direct callers, 212 impacted symbols, CRITICAL.

Graph ids change for Zig repos indexed with an earlier head. top-level members of a file with fields are `Method:<file>:<Stem>.<name>#N` / `Property:<file>:<Stem>.<field>` (was `Function:<file>:<name>` / `Property:<file>:<field>`), and function-local containers are `enclosingFn$Name`.

Fixtures added: `zig-filestruct` (the Lightpanda shapes: Page, Session, Sighandler, util, lp, aliases, flow, generic, reflect, Sorter) and `zig-rootmodule`; `zig-idioms` gained the root-module, inline-import and holder cases. Gates at the final head: build, `tsc --noEmit`, the Zig unit and integration suites (402 tests in the targeted run), and the broad local run over `test/unit`, `test/integration/resolvers`, parsing, tree-sitter-languages, structural-pair-coverage and closure-binding-labels (16,524 passed; the same three environmental failures as before). No corpus row went down.

## Local CI pass (2026-08-18): the 20 workflow jobs, run here while the fork PR waits for approval

I ran every pending job that does not depend on GitHub-only state locally at `30b5bb6e`, with the commands, env and Node floor taken from the workflow files.

| Job | Local equivalent | Outcome |
|---|---|---|
| quality: format, lint, typecheck, typecheck-web, workflow-convention | `prettier --check .` (root deps only, as CI installs), `eslint .`, `tsc --noEmit` ×2, `check-workflow-concurrency.py`, plus `actionlint` | pass |
| tests: coverage shards + merge | full `vitest run --coverage`: 18 305 passed, 67 skipped; merged coverage 82.9 % statements / 71.5 % branches / 89.1 % functions / 86.4 % lines against thresholds 26 / 23 / 28 / 27 | pass |
| tests: gitnexus-web unit, docker-server | 419 / 419, 55 / 55 | pass |
| tests: cross-platform (macOS, 3 shards) | `run-cross-platform.ts --shard=N/3` with `GITNEXUS_REQUIRE_FTS/VECTOR=1`, `GITNEXUS_E2E_CLI=dist` | pass |
| tests: tree-sitter ABI, node floor 22.18, packaged install smoke, benchmarks | `--assert-current` + `parser-loader-abi`; dist imports on a real Node 22.18.0; `npm pack` → isolated `npm i -g` → vendor/junction asserts → `--version`; both `measure.mjs --check` gates | pass, after the fix below |
| Gitleaks, Dependency Review, tree-sitter prebuilds guard, PR title, PR description | container scan of the PR range (33 commits); the same dependency-graph compare the action calls (one added package, MIT, no advisories); the guard's own decide script (`any=false`); the labeler and description rules | pass |
| Docker Build & Push (web, cli) | native-arch `buildx` builds | web passes; cli passes every stage that touches this branch (builder `npm ci` + build with the Zig grammar, runtime copies) and stops only at the LadybugDB FTS-extension download from `extension.ladybugdb.com`, the same URL times out from this host too |
| e2e, CodeQL | e2e skips itself (its path filter wants a `gitnexus-web/` change); CodeQL was not run locally | not run |

The failures on this machine are the same environmental set as in the test plan (`analyzer-identity`, `embedding-runtime-install`, `evidence-provenance-helper`, the two `hooks-e2e` pnpm cases); the rest of the failed files in the long runs were the analyzer-identity guard tripping because I rebuilt `dist/` or ran a second vitest while a run was in flight, and each of them passes on a clean isolated re-run (`cli-e2e`, `pdg-mode-flip`, `incremental-vector-extension-ordering`, `analyze-index-lock-concurrency`: 60 / 60).

One job would have failed. `benchmarks (GITNEXUS_BENCH)` gates two capture fingerprints, `bench/python-scope/baseline-fingerprint.txt` and `bench/scope-capture/baselines.json`; the shared callable-flow change in `4a1c3d94` moved them (python; csharp, cpp, typescript, kotlin) and the goldens were regenerated but not these baselines. Both gates pass on `origin/main` and every other language matched its baseline on the same run. Dumping the canonical matches on both trees showed the drift was the intended one everywhere except one TypeScript site: tree-sitter-typescript parses `await f<T>(x)` as `call_expression(function: await_expression(f), type_arguments, …)`, so the new direct-designator gate saw an `await_expression` and dropped `direct-callee-name` on an awaited generic *direct* call (`await verifyToken<AdminPayload>(token, …)`), while the un-awaited spelling kept it. `154fb69d` makes `wrappedExpression` unwrap `await_expression` (it has no named field, so the field-based unwrap missed it), which restores parity with main for the direct spelling and leaves the member spelling (`await svc.verify<T>(x)`) nameless as intended, adds a regression test that fails on both assertions without the unwrap, and re-baselines the four languages plus python with a `_rebaselined_1432_member_call_callee_name` note per entry (cpp `capture_groups_fp` 4605 → 4601: the dropped indirect invoke on `choice.select(1)` and its synthetic `@reference.call.free`, a duplicate of the real `@reference.call.member`).

Two things noticed along the way, neither blocking: `npm install` of the packed tarball prints an `ERESOLVE` peer warning for `@tree-sitter-grammars/tree-sitter-zig` (it declares `peerOptional tree-sitter@^0.22.1`, this package pins 0.21.1; the grammar still installs as a real directory), and `check-tree-sitter-upgrade-readiness.py`'s curated `GRAMMARS` list does not include zig.

title: fix(windows): 32767-char tree-sitter crash + VECTOR extension SIGSEGV
body:
## Summary

Fixes three categories of Windows-specific crashes found while indexing a large C# Unity project (~61k symbols, 400+ source files).

### 1. tree-sitter 0.21.x SIGSEGV — 32767-char limit

On Windows, tree-sitter native binding crashes with SIGSEGV when parsing strings longer than 32 767 chars. Five call sites passed raw file content without any length guard: `captures.ts`, `namespace-siblings.ts`, `parse-worker.ts`, `parsing-processor.ts`.

Fix: truncate at the last newline before the limit. ERROR-root trees from mid-class truncation are silenced by returning `[]` in `captures.ts`.

### 2. C# scope resolution

- **scope-tree.ts / scope-extractor.ts**: Module + top-level `namespace_declaration` share the same source range. `rangeStrictlyContains` rejects equal ranges. Added `rangeNonStrictlyContains` + `moduleAwareContains` helpers.
- **scope-extractor-bridge.ts**: empty captures from ERROR-root files still called `extractScope`. Added early return.
- **namespace-siblings.ts**: binding arrays frozen by `finalize-algorithm` threw on `.push()`. Fixed with spread-copy.

### 3. loadVectorExtension SIGSEGV on Windows

`INSTALL VECTOR` calls the KuzuDB native extension installer which crashes with SIGSEGV on Windows (unhandled error path, uncatchable by JS). Added `process.platform === 'win32'` guard — embeddings unavailable on Windows but all graph queries work.

## Test plan

- Run `gitnexus analyze` on Windows with a large C# codebase — no SIGSEGV
- Index completes and is queryable (non-zero nodes/edges)
- Non-Windows: `INSTALL VECTOR` still runs normally

Verified on Windows 11, Node.js 24.15.0, gitnexus 1.6.3.

title: bug(embeddings): analyze --embeddings exits 0 with corrupted DB when INSTALL VECTOR 404s
body:
### Area
gitnexus (CLI / core / indexing / MCP server)

### Summary
`gitnexus analyze --embeddings` exits 0 and leaves a half-built, unrecoverable index when Ladybug's `INSTALL VECTOR` 404s on the extension CDN. No error reaches stderr and no exit code reflects the failure, so callers (CI, scripts, hooks) think the run succeeded.

### Context
- gitnexus 1.6.3 ships with `@ladybugdb/core ^0.15.2`; npm resolves it to `0.15.4`.
- `http://extension.ladybugdb.com/` only hosts directories for `v0.15.0` and `v0.16.0` in the relevant range. `v0.15.1`/`v0.15.2`/`v0.15.3`/`v0.15.4`/`v0.16.1` all 404.
- Verified:
  ```
  curl -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' http://extension.ladybugdb.com/v0.15.4/osx_arm64/vector/libvector.lbug_extension  # 404
  curl -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' http://extension.ladybugdb.com/v0.15.0/osx_arm64/vector/libvector.lbug_extension  # 200
  curl -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' http://extension.ladybugdb.com/v0.16.1/osx_arm64/vector/libvector.lbug_extension  # 404
  curl -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' http://extension.ladybugdb.com/v0.16.0/osx_arm64/vector/libvector.lbug_extension  # 200
  ```
- The same gap will hit `gitnexus@1.6.4-rc.94` (`@ladybugdb/core ^0.16.1`) once `core` resolves to `0.16.1`.

### Expected behavior
1. When `INSTALL VECTOR` or `LOAD EXTENSION VECTOR` fails and `--embeddings` was requested, the CLI exits non-zero with a clear message naming the failure (HTTP status, missing CDN path, host).
2. A failed run does not leave a partially-written `lbug` + `lbug.wal` that breaks subsequent plain `analyze` calls.
3. Either `@ladybugdb/core` is pinned to a version whose `vX.Y.0` folder is guaranteed published, or the extension binary is provisioned via `postinstall` so the CDN gap stops being a runtime blocker.

### Actual behavior
Running `npx gitnexus analyze --embeddings` on a fresh repo:
- TTY output (when captured): 33 repeated `⚠️ Schema creation warning: Runtime exception: Corrupted wal file. Read out invalid WAL record type.`, then `GitNexus: VECTOR extension load failed: Runtime exception: Corrupted wal file. Read out invalid WAL record type.`, then `Skipping 3 swift file(s)`.
- Non-TTY output (piped, CI): only the banner and the swift skip line. The 33 warnings and the VECTOR failure are emitted via the progress-bar `console.error` shim and never reach stdout.
- Process exits **0**.
- `.gitnexus/lbug` is ~57 MB, `.gitnexus/lbug.wal` is ~1.6 MB, `meta.json` is missing.
- `gitnexus list` does not include the repo; `gitnexus status` says "Repository not indexed."
- Re-running `analyze` (with or without `--embeddings`) hits the same WAL corruption until `gitnexus clean --force` is run manually.

Root cause: `loadVectorExtension()` in `dist/core/lbug/lbug-adapter.js` catches every non-"already loaded/installed/exists" error into `console.error` and returns. `pool-adapter.js` has the same swallowing pattern (two sites). `dist/core/run-analyze.js` never inspects vector status, so the orchestrator continues, fails further down, and `dist/cli/analyze.js` reports success.

### Steps to reproduce
1. Fresh `brew install gitnexus` on darwin-arm64 (gets 1.6.3 with `@ladybugdb/core@0.15.4`).
2. Remove `~/.lbdb/extension/` so no cached extension exists (mandatory for clean repro; an old cache from a prior install masks the bug).
3. `cd` into any source tree of ~700 files.
4. `npx gitnexus analyze --embeddings > out.log 2>&1`
5. `echo $?` → `0`
6. `cat out.log` → only banner + swift skip line (33 corruption warnings are hidden by the bar shim when stdout is not a TTY).
7. `ls .gitnexus/` → `lbug`, `lbug.wal`, no `meta.json`.
8. `npx gitnexus status` → `Repository not indexed`.

### Environment
- OS: macOS 15 (Darwin 25.3.0), Apple Silicon
- gitnexus: 1.6.3 (homebrew)
- @ladybugdb/core: 0.15.4 (npm-resolved from `^0.15.2`)
- @ladybugdb/core-darwin-arm64: 0.15.4
- Network: direct, CDN reachable (the failing requests get clean 404s, not timeouts)

### Logs
TTY capture during the failing run (de-progress-barred, repeats trimmed):
```
GitNexus Analyzer
⚠️ Schema creation warning: Runtime exception: Corrupted wal file. Read out invalid WAL record type.
[... 32 more identical lines ...]
GitNexus: VECTOR extension load failed: Runtime exception: Corrupted wal file. Read out invalid WAL record type.
Skipping 3 swift file(s) — swift parser not available (native binding may not have built).
```
On-disk evidence after the run:
```
$ ls -la .gitnexus/
-rw-r--r-- 1 dan staff 57761792 lbug
-rw-r--r-- 1 dan staff  1681079 lbug.wal
# meta.json missing
```

### Workaround (verified on this machine)
Pin core to `0.15.2` and rely on the cached `v0.15.0` extension binary:
```
cd $(brew --prefix)/lib/node_modules/gitnexus
npm install --no-save @ladybugdb/core@0.15.2 @ladybugdb/core-darwin-arm64@0.15.2
npx gitnexus clean --force
npx gitnexus analyze --embeddings
```
Result: clean run, `meta.json` written, `embeddings: 3631` in registry, `CodeEmbedding` populated, `CALL show_loaded_extensions()` reports `VECTOR` as `OFFICIAL` from `~/.lbdb/extension/0.15.0/osx_arm64/vector/libvector.lbug_extension`.

Caveat: this works because the v0.15.0 extension is already cached on my machine from an earlier install. Whether `core@0.15.2` can populate the cache from scratch depends on what URL it constructs; the CDN's lack of a `v0.15.2` directory suggests this will not work for fresh installs without help from a postinstall step.

### Proposed fixes (pick one or combine)
1. **Surface the failure.** When `--embeddings` is requested, `loadVectorExtension()` should rethrow on non-"already loaded/installed/exists" errors (or set a flag the orchestrator checks). `analyze.js` should fail the run and exit non-zero. Same for the two equivalent sites in `pool-adapter.js`.
2. **Roll back partial state on init failure.** If schema setup or extension load fails, delete the half-written `lbug` + `lbug.wal` so the next `analyze` is not blocked. Alternatively, detect a stale WAL at startup and recover automatically instead of telling the user to run `clean --force` (which most users will not know about).
3. **Stabilize extension provisioning.** Either pin `@ladybugdb/core` (and the platform-specific `core-<arch>` package) to a version whose `vX.Y.0` extension folder exists on the CDN, or add a `postinstall` step that downloads `libvector.lbug_extension` and `libfts.lbug_extension` into `~/.lbdb/extension/<core-version>/<arch>/<name>/`. Bonus: vendor the binaries inside the npm package to remove the runtime network dependency entirely.
4. **Track upstream.** If the CDN gap is intentional on Ladybug's side, file there too; if it is a mirroring oversight, get the missing patch versions published.

### Acceptance
- [ ] `analyze --embeddings` fails with a non-zero exit code when VECTOR install or load fails.
- [ ] A failed `analyze` does not leave the on-disk index in a state that requires `clean --force`.
- [ ] Either the homebrew-default install of gitnexus succeeds end-to-end on darwin-arm64 with `--embeddings`, or the README documents the `@ladybugdb/core` version constraint clearly.

title: Bug: gitnexus-hook.cjs findGitNexusDir() matches user-global ~/.gitnexus/ registry, triggers false-positive 'stale index' on every git commit outside indexed repos
feat(extractors): strip Unreal Engine reflection macros before C++ parsing
body:
## Problem
Tree-sitter does not expand C preprocessor macros, so Unreal Engine reflection markers (`UCLASS`, `UFUNCTION`, `UPROPERTY`, `MODULENAME_API`, `GENERATED_BODY`, `DECLARE_*_DELEGATE`, ...) are parsed verbatim. The result is mis-parsed UE class/function declarations.
Concrete example — `class BRAWLUI_API UMyClass : public UObject`:
- tree-sitter-cpp captures `BRAWLUI_API` as the class identifier
- the actual class `UMyClass` never gets a Class node in the graph
- `gitnexus_context({name: "UMyClass"})` returns nothing
- impact / rename / cypher queries all miss UE-style classes
UE5 codebases use this pattern in every header (every module declares its own `MODULE_API` export macro), so the impact is wide.
## Fix
A length-preserving source-text preprocessor that runs before tree-sitter parses each file:
- New optional `preprocessSource?: (sourceText, filePath) => string` hook on `LanguageProvider` (parser section, next to `treeSitterQueries`).
- New `gitnexus/src/core/ingestion/cpp-ue-preprocessor.ts` — pure function `stripUeMacros(source)` that elides the UE markers.
- Wired into `cppProvider` only (the C provider is unaffected).
**Length-preserving requirement** — replacement is byte-for-byte: each elided character becomes a space, newlines preserved. So tree-sitter's reported byte offsets and line/column positions remain identical to the original file. **Symbol locations in the graph stay accurate.**
A cheap regex detection guard short-circuits files that don't look like UE sources (no `UCLASS`/`UFUNCTION`/`*_API`/etc. anywhere), so non-UE C++ codebases pay one regex test then bail.
## Macros elided
- `UCLASS(...)`, `UFUNCTION(...)`, `UPROPERTY(...)`, `USTRUCT(...)`, `UENUM(...)`, `UINTERFACE(...)`, `UMETA(...)`, `UE_DEPRECATED(...)`
- `GENERATED_BODY()`, `GENERATED_UCLASS_BODY()`, `GENERATED_USTRUCT_BODY()`, `GENERATED_UINTERFACE_BODY()`, `GENERATED_IINTERFACE_BODY()`, `DECLARE_CLASS()`
- `DECLARE_DELEGATE` / `DECLARE_DYNAMIC_DELEGATE` / `DECLARE_MULTICAST_DELEGATE` / `DECLARE_DYNAMIC_MULTICAST_DELEGATE` (with all `_OneParam`, `_TwoParams`, ..., `_RetVal_NineParams` variants)
- Any `[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]*_API` token (module export macros — `BRAWLUI_API`, `ENGINE_API`, `COREUOBJECT_API`, ...)
## Architecture
The preprocessor is invoked at every site that re-parses a file, mirroring the existing Vue SFC preprocessing pattern in `parsing-processor.ts`:
- `parsing-processor.ts` (main parse path)
- `workers/parse-worker.ts` (worker parse path)
- `heritage-processor.ts` (cache-miss reparse, 2 sites)
- `import-processor.ts` (cache-miss reparse)
- `call-processor.ts` (cache-miss reparse, 2 sites)
Following the AGENTS.md rule "no language-specific behavior in shared ingestion code" — every site calls `provider.preprocessSource?.(...) ?? content`, no `if (language === CPlusPlus)` branches.
## Verification
- ✅ `npx tsc --noEmit` clean
- ✅ 27/27 new unit tests pass (`test/unit/cpp-ue-preprocessor.test.ts`) covering: detection guard, length preservation across multiple UE samples, macro removal for each macro family, false-positive guards (substring matches, balanced parens inside string literals, Qt macros left alone), and class-name extraction sanity
- ✅ Full unit suite still passes — **5337 tests, 0 regressions** (10 pre-existing skips)
- ✅ End-to-end verified against an Unreal Engine 5.7 game project (~2,000 files, 21,974 nodes after re-index)
### Real-world before/after on the UE project
| Query                                                                  | Before                                                             | After                                                                              |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `MATCH (c:Class) WHERE c.name = "UBrawlShopComponent" RETURN c.filePath` | 0 rows (only `BRAWLECONOMY_API` was registered)                      | Correctly registered at `Source/BrawlEconomy/Public/Components/BrawlShopComponent.h` |
| `MATCH (c:Class) WHERE c.name CONTAINS "_API" RETURN c.name`             | Many fake classes (`BRAWLECONOMY_API`, `BRAWLUI_API`, `ENGINE_API`, ...) | None                                                                               |
| `MATCH ()-[:CALLS]->(m:Method {name: "GetRerollCost"}) RETURN count(*)`  | 0                                                                  | 2 (high-confidence, 0.9)                                                           |
| Total clusters                                                         | 1,208                                                              | 2,246                                                                              |

The call-graph improvement is partial — the deeper limitation (cross-file `pointer->method()` resolution in tree-sitter-cpp) remains and is out of scope for this PR. Class identification — the user-visible breakage — is fully resolved.
## Out of scope
- Reading UHT-generated `.gen.cpp` reflection metadata
- Improving cross-file `obj->method()` call resolution in tree-sitter-cpp (the deeper C++ resolver work documented in `type-resolution-roadmap.md`)
- Linking C++ method declarations (header) to definitions (cpp) as the same logical method

Security fixes

This release includes fixes for the following security issues:

Cache Middleware ignores Vary: Authorization / Vary: Cookie leading to cross-user cache leakage

Affects: Cache Middleware. Fixes missing cache-skip handling for Vary: Authorization and Vary: Cookie, where a response cached for one authenticated user could be served to other users. GHSA-p77w-8qqv-26rm

CSS Declaration Injection via Style Object Values in JSX SSR

Affects: hono/jsx. Fixes a missing CSS-context escape for style object values and property names, where untrusted input could inject additional CSS declarations. The impact is limited to CSS and does not allow JavaScript execution. GHSA-qp7p-654g-cw7p

Improper validation of NumericDate claims (exp, nbf, iat) in JWT verify()

Affects: hono/utils/jwt. Fixes improper validation of exp, nbf, and iat claims, where falsy, non-finite, or non-numeric values could silently bypass time-based checks instead of being rejected per RFC 7519. GHSA-hm8q-7f3q-5f36
