title: ci: add fork-safe PR autofix pipeline
body:
## Summary

Adds a two-workflow autofix pipeline that posts `prettier` + `eslint --fix` output as inline review-comment suggestions on PRs — including fork PRs — without ever running fork-controlled ESLint plugins under a privileged token.

| Workflow | Trigger | Token | Role |
|---|---|---|---|
| `pr-autofix.yml` | `pull_request` (incl. forks) | `permissions: {}` | Untrusted: runs `lint:fix` + `format`, uploads diff as artifact. No write capability. |
| `pr-autofix-publish.yml` | `workflow_run` | `pull-requests: write`, `actions: read` | Trusted: never touches fork code. Posts inline suggestions via `reviewdog` and one sticky summary comment when there's actually something to fix. |

## Why split into two halves

ESLint loads plugins from fork-controlled `node_modules`, so running it in a job with `pull-requests: write` would let a malicious fork PR ship a poisoned ESLint plugin and execute arbitrary code under that token. The untrusted half runs fork code with `permissions: {}` (no token to abuse) and the trusted half consumes only the diff artifact (data, not code) — same pattern as autofix.ci.

## Hardening applied (from multi-agent review)

- **Concurrency** keyed on PR number with fork fallback to head-repo+branch — `workflow_run.id` (per-run unique) is the anti-pattern called out by name in `CONTRIBUTING.md`.
- **Metadata allowlist**: every `metadata.json` field is regex-validated before being exported to `$GITHUB_OUTPUT`, closing the `head_ref` newline-injection vector that would otherwise let a fork redirect bot comments to a victim PR.
- **Sticky-comment author filter**: lookup matches `.user.login == "github-actions[bot]"` so a regular user posting a comment with the marker can't permanently DoS the upsert.
- **Reviewdog binary pinned** to `v0.21.0` (not `latest`) — bad release otherwise breaks every PR.
- **`gh` API retry** on transient 5xx for the idempotent calls (GET, PATCH).
- **Sticky only when actionable**: when `prettier`/`eslint` are clean, `npm run lint:fix && npm run format` produces an empty diff and no comment is posted. The sticky carries a fenced `gitnexus-autofix` JSON block under a stable HTML marker so agents can parse state without regex.
- **`paths-ignore`** on `package-lock.json` / snapshots / `dist/` / `node_modules/` to avoid reviewdog's 406-on-3k-lines failure mode.

## Required out-of-band repo settings

To replace the previously-considered `chinthakagodawita/autoupdate` (unmaintained since 2023):

- [ ] Enable **merge queue** on `main`.
- [ ] Branch protection: **Require branches to be up to date before merging**.
- [ ] Optionally: add a CI-automation note to `CONTRIBUTING.md` describing the sticky-comment marker and `gitnexus-autofix` JSON schema (follow-up).

## Test plan

`workflow_run` cannot run from a feature branch — first execution is post-merge. Manual validation:

- [ ] Open a small same-repo PR with a deliberate prettier/eslint violation; confirm reviewdog suggestions appear on the PR head and one sticky comment with the JSON block.
- [ ] Open a fork PR with the same violation; confirm same behaviour.
- [ ] Open a clean PR; confirm no sticky comment and no inline suggestions.
- [ ] Open a PR touching only `package-lock.json`; confirm the workflow doesn't fire.
- [ ] Verify `python3 .github/scripts/check-workflow-concurrency.py .github/workflows` passes (it does locally).

## Follow-ups (intentionally out of scope)

- `actionlint` workflow to catch YAML/expression typos in future PRs.
- Emit a `Check Run` so the `success`/`neutral` status itself reflects autofix outcome (currently agents must read the sticky's JSON block).
- Document the `<!-- gitnexus:pr-autofix-summary -->` marker + `gitnexus-autofix` schema in `CONTRIBUTING.md`.

title: `gitnexus analyze` crashes with 0xC0000005 (Windows access violation, exit -1073741819) on a Python project — crash is post-read, in or before the LMDB write phase
body:
**gitnexus version:** `1.6.3` (also reproduced on `1.6.2`).
**Platform:** Windows 11, Node `v24.15.0`, npm global install.
**Severity:** blocking — `analyze` cannot complete on the affected repository. We have not been able to isolate the trigger from outside the gitnexus codebase.

---

## Symptom

```
PS> & npx gitnexus analyze
  GitNexus Analyzer
  Skipped 4 large files (>512KB, likely generated/vendored)
scope extraction failed for src/<project>/ai/__init__.py: ScopeExtractor: no Module .
scope extraction failed for src/<project>/ui/__init__.py: ScopeExtractor: no Module .
PS> "exit $LASTEXITCODE"
exit -1073741819     # 0xC0000005 — Win32 access violation
```

No stderr output beyond the two soft `scope extraction failed` warnings. No JS stack trace. No partial index written. Crash takes ~3 seconds from invocation.

---

## What we know

- **Worked previously.** A week before this report, the same repo indexed cleanly: 4095 symbols, 5526 relationships, 32 execution flows. The codebase has not changed materially since (most recent file write in the affected tree is 6 days old).
- **Native crash.** `0xC0000005` is a Win32 access violation, with no JS-side stack trace — strongly suggests the crash is inside a native module (Tree-sitter parser, LMDB binding, or similar), not in JavaScript code.
- **Reinstall did not fix.** A fresh `npm uninstall -g gitnexus && npm install -g gitnexus` (which forced a recompile of all native dependencies against the current Node v24.15.0) produced the identical crash signature. So this is not a stale-binary or Node-ABI issue.
- **Crash is post-read, not in the file walker.** We instrumented Node's `fs` module via a `--require` preload to log every file read to unbuffered stderr. Of the **~11,300 file reads** logged before the crash, all completed cleanly — including every source file in the project. The crash happens *after* the read phase, in either: (a) the cross-file scope-extraction / graph-build, or (b) the persistence phase that writes to `.gitnexus/lbug` / `.gitnexus/lbug.wal`.
- **`.gitnexus/lbug` stays at 4096 bytes on every crash; `lbug.wal` at ~25 KB.** Both regenerate on each run. This suggests the crash happens at or just before significant write activity to the LMDB store — i.e. very early in persistence, possibly during the first batch write.
- **The two `scope extraction failed` warnings on empty `__init__.py` files are soft** — gitnexus logs them and continues. The hard crash is downstream of those.

---

## Hypotheses we falsified (so you can skip these dead ends)

| Hypothesis | How we tested | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Node v24 ABI mismatch with stale native modules | Forced full reinstall of gitnexus globally; native deps recompiled against current Node | **Crash unchanged** — fresh build, same signature |
| A specific directory name (`config/`) is the trigger | Removed the only `package.json` at the repo root (an accidentally-empty `{}` file from a prior `npx` invocation) and re-ran | **Crash unchanged** — not a `config/` or `package.json` issue |
| A specific file's content is the trigger, isolatable from outside | Iterative `.gitnexusignore` exclusion bisection across `src/` subdirs; `.gitnexusignore` does not appear to filter directory enumeration on this version, only file walking | **Bisection produced false positives** — apparent "fix" results from removing files were not reproducible across runs, suggesting the crash trigger depends on cross-file state, not single-file content |

---

## Methodology — `trace_fs.js`

If useful: the file-read trace was produced by a 60-line Node `--require` preload that hooks `fs.openSync`, `fs.readFileSync`, `fs.promises.readFile`, `fs.statSync`, `fs.lstatSync`, `fs.readdirSync`, and writes each path to **unbuffered stderr** via `fs.writeSync(2, ...)` (Node's stdout is buffered and the buffer is lost on a native crash). This is what let us confirm all file reads complete cleanly before the crash. Happy to share the script.

---

## What we cannot do from outside

- See *which* file is being processed at the moment of the crash (the read-phase trace shows reads, not parse/scope-extract/persist work).
- Distinguish a parser crash from an LMDB write crash without source-level instrumentation.
- Determine whether the trigger is single-file or cross-file (combinatorial) without source.

What would help us: a `--verbose` / `--debug` mode that logs "starting scope extraction on X" / "writing to lbug: N entries" per step. The CLI's `--help` output we have does not expose any such flag.

---

## Environment details

- **OS:** Windows 11
- **Node:** `v24.15.0` (`C:\Program Files\nodejs\node.exe`)
- **gitnexus:** `1.6.3` (also reproduced on `1.6.2`)
- **Install:** `npm install -g gitnexus`
- **Invocation:** `npx gitnexus analyze`
- **Exit code:** `-1073741819` (`0xC0000005`)
- **Time to crash:** ~3 seconds
- **`.gitnexus/`** state on crash: `lbug` (4096 bytes) + `lbug.wal` (~25 KB), both binary, regenerated on each attempt.
- **Project under analysis:** ~80 Python source files. Happy to share the codebase privately if it helps reproduce.

---

## Workaround in use

We have disabled gitnexus on this codebase. Our code-intelligence layer that depends on it is degraded. Will revisit when an upstream fix lands.

Happy to instrument further, run patches you provide, or share the affected codebase under NDA if that would speed things up.

title: feat: shared resilient-fetch (retries + circuit breaker)
body:
## Summary

Adds a small, runtime-agnostic resilience layer in `gitnexus-shared` and migrates every backend HTTP outbound call (CLI, **MCP**, wiki LLM, web → backend) through it. Bounded exponential-backoff-with-jitter retries on transient failures; honors `Retry-After` (capped at 30s); per-process circuit breaker fails fast when an endpoint flaps.

## Helpers — `gitnexus-shared/src/integrations/`

| File | Role |
|---|---|
| `retry.ts` | `withRetry(fn, opts)` — bounded loop with caller-supplied retryability classification and full-jitter exponential backoff. |
| `circuit-breaker.ts` | Closed/Open/Half-Open state machine with injectable clock + a keyed registry so callers targeting the same endpoint share state. |
| `resilient-fetch.ts` | Composed wrapper. Retries 5xx + 429 + retryable network throws; treats `AbortSignal.timeout()` and 4xx (other than 429) as terminal; `CircuitOpenError` when the breaker opens. |

Defaults: 3 attempts, base 500ms, cap 5000ms, breaker opens after 3 consecutive failures, 30s cooldown.

## Migrations (no behavioural regression — all existing tests pass)

- `gitnexus/src/core/embeddings/http-client.ts` — covers `analyze` *and* the **MCP** query path (`httpEmbedQuery`). Replaces inline linear-backoff retry.
- `gitnexus/src/core/wiki/llm-client.ts` — preserves the Azure content-filter branch; `resilientFetch` handles 5xx/429 backoff.
- `gitnexus-web/src/services/backend-client.ts` (`fetchWithTimeout` helper) — small retry budget (2 attempts, 250–1500ms) so a dead local backend still fails fast for the user.
- `gitnexus-web/src/core/llm/settings-service.ts` — OpenRouter model list.

## Deliberately not migrated

- `gitnexus-web/src/services/backend-client.ts` `streamJob()` — Server-Sent Events stream; the existing reconnect-with-`Last-Event-ID` logic is not unary-fetch shaped.
- `gitnexus-web/src/components/SettingsPanel.tsx` `checkOllamaStatus()` — one-shot health probe; retrying delays the "Ollama not running" error rather than improving UX.

## Tests

41 new helper tests in `gitnexus/test/unit/integrations/` cover:
- Backoff math (full-jitter range bounds, `afterMs` capping).
- Breaker state transitions (Closed → Open → Half-Open → Closed/Open) with an injected clock.
- `Retry-After` parsing — delta-seconds *and* HTTP-date forms.
- 401/403/404/422 returned as Response without retry, breaker not incremented.
- `TimeoutError` rethrown immediately, no retry, breaker not incremented.
- Three exhausted retry batches → breaker opens → 4th call fails fast without invoking fetch.

Existing `rate-limit.test.ts` (which exercises `httpEmbedBatch`) still passes — the migration is behavior-compatible.

## Test plan

- [x] `npx vitest run test/unit/integrations/` — 41/41 pass.
- [x] `npx vitest run test/unit/rate-limit.test.ts` — 20/20 pass (existing http-client tests).
- [x] `npx tsc --noEmit` clean in both `gitnexus/` and `gitnexus-web/`.
- [x] `gitnexus-shared` builds clean.

## Follow-ups

- Add `analyze` and `wiki` end-to-end tests that simulate a 5xx → 5xx → 204 sequence to verify the migration on real CLI paths.
- Consider exposing `--retry`/`--no-retry` CLI flags for users who want a single-shot dispatch (e.g., scripted callers).

Plan doc (local working artifact, not committed): `docs/plans/2026-05-09-001-feat-uq-publish-retry-circuit-breaker-plan.md` — its scope was expanded mid-execution to cover all fetch sites.

title: GitNexus MCP Server: Lazy FTS Index Creation Fails on Read-Only Database
body:
### Area

gitnexus (CLI / core / indexing / MCP server)

### Summary

GitNexus 1.6.3 opens LadyBugDB databases in **read-only mode** in `pool-adapter.js` (used by the MCP endpoint path). Meanwhile, `bm25-index.js` no longer creates FTS indexes during `gitnexus analyze` (done in 1.6.3 to save ~2s per repo in CI pipelines) and instead creates them **lazily on first query** via `CALL CREATE_FTS_INDEX(...)`. This call is a write operation that fails against the read-only database, causing BM25 full-text search to return zero results for every query until the indexes are eventually created by some other code path.

The error is logged once per query per table (File, Function, Class, Method, Interface) and retried on every subsequent query — flooding stdout of the MCP server.

### Context

GitNexus has two distinct database connection paths:

| Path | Entry Point | DB Adapter | Database Open | Used By |
|------|------------|------------|---------------|---------|
| **CLI / HTTP server** | `dist/cli/index.js serve` → `server/api.js` | `lbug-adapter.js` | `new lbug.Database(dbPath)` — read-write (default `readOnly=false`) | `gitnexus serve`, `gitnexus query` CLI |
| **MCP endpoint** | `/api/mcp` → `local-backend.js` | `pool-adapter.js` | `new lbug.Database(dbPath, 0, false, true)` — **read-only** | MCP clients (Claude Code, chat app, Cursor, etc.) |

### The Inconsistency

**`pool-adapter.js:247-249`** (MCP endpoint path):
```javascript
const db = new lbug.Database(dbPath, 0,          // bufferManagerSize
                             false,               // enableCompression
                             true);               // readOnly = TRUE
```

The comment above explains the intent:
> *"Open in read-only mode — MCP server never writes to the database. This allows multiple MCP server instances to read concurrently, and avoids lock conflicts when `gitnexus analyze` is writing."*

This was a valid assumption in gitnexus <= 1.6.2, where `analyze` created FTS indexes during ingestion.

**`bm25-index.js`** (changed in 1.6.3):
```javascript
// FTS indexes are created lazily on first query (via `ensureFTSIndex`) — see
// `lbug-adapter.ts` for the rationale. This keeps `analyze` fast (the
// ~440 ms × 5 LadybugDB CREATE_FTS_INDEX cost dominates pipeline time on
// small repos / CI runners) at the cost of paying that overhead on the
// first `query`/`context` call in a session.
```

**`bm25-index.js:ensureFTSIndexViaExecutor()`** (MCP path, lazy creation):
```javascript
await executor(`CALL CREATE_FTS_INDEX('${table}', '${indexName}', [${propList}], stemmer := 'porter')`);
//   ^^^^^^ FAILS — write operation on read-only database
```

### The Contradiction

| Component | Assumption | Date |
|-----------|-----------|------|
| `analyze` (v1.6.3) | FTS indexes created lazily at query time | Changed in 1.6.3 |
| `pool-adapter.js` | No writes needed at query time (analyze handled it) | Legacy from <= 1.6.2 |

When these meet: lazy FTS creation tries to write → read-only DB rejects it → BM25 broken.

### The Silent Fallback Makes It Worse

Notably, the CLI path (`lbug-adapter.js` → `bm25-index.js` else-branch) **silently swallows** the error:
```javascript
await ensureFTSIndex(table, indexName, [...properties]).catch(() => { });
//                                                        ^^^^^^^^^^ silent
```

So the HTTP server path (`gitnexus serve`) also loses BM25 but gives **no warning**. Only the MCP endpoint path (pool-adapter) logs the error, making the bug discoverable in one path but silently degrading the other.

### Expected behavior

When an MCP client queries a freshly analyzed repository via `gitnexus_query`, the first query should lazily create FTS indexes on the 5 node tables (`CREATE_FTS_INDEX` on File, Function, Class, Method, Interface). Once created, the indexes persist on disk and all subsequent queries use hybrid search (BM25 keyword + vector semantic via Reciprocal Rank Fusion). BM25 results should contain scored file matches for the search terms.

The lazy-creation phase should be transparent to the caller — the first query takes ~2.2s longer (5 × ~440ms) but returns correct results. Subsequent queries are fast.

### Actual behavior

On the first query, `CALL CREATE_FTS_INDEX(...)` fails with `Cannot execute write operations in a read-only database` because the MCP endpoint path opens the database read-only. The FTS index is never created. BM25 returns zero results for **every** query on that repo. Only vector search works, severely degrading query quality for keyword-heavy searches.

The error is retried on every subsequent query (5 warnings per query), but the indexes can never be created because the database access mode never changes. The only escape is to restart the database in read-write mode (Fix A) or re-run `gitnexus analyze` (which opens read-write).

### Steps to reproduce

1. Start gitnexus on a freshly analyzed repo (no existing FTS indexes):

2. Wait for the MCP server to be healthy (registry auto-scanned)

3. Send an MCP query that triggers FTS:
   ```bash
   # Example: trigger gitnexus_query tool via MCP client
   ```

4. Observe container logs:
   ```
   [gitnexus] FTS index ensure failed for repo "repo-name" table "File"
     (index "file_fts"): Connection exception: Cannot execute write
     operations in a read-only database!. Will retry on next query.
   [gitnexus] FTS index ensure failed for repo "repo-name" table "Function"
     (index "function_fts"): Connection exception: Cannot execute write
     operations in a read-only database!. Will retry on next query.
   [gitnexus] FTS index ensure failed for repo "repo-name" table "Class"
     (index "class_fts"): Connection exception: Cannot execute write
     operations in a read-only database!. Will retry on next query.
   [gitnexus] FTS index ensure failed for repo "repo-name" table "Method"
     (index "method_fts"): Connection exception: Cannot execute write
     operations in a read-only database!. Will retry on next query.
   [gitnexus] FTS index ensure failed for repo "repo-name" table "Interface"
     (index "interface_fts"): Connection exception: Cannot execute write
     operations in a read-only database!. Will retry on next query.
   ```

5. Check query timing — BM25 phase returns zero results:
   ```
   GitNexus [query:timing] query="main entry point" totalMs=652.8
     phases={"vector":597.5,"bm25":652.4,"merge":0.1,...}
   ```
   Note: BM25 returning 0 results despite valid search terms.

### Environment

| Property | Value |
|----------|-------|
| **OS** | CachyOS (Arch-derivative), Linux 6.19.9-1-cachyos, x86_64 |
| **GitNexus** | 1.6.3 (Docker image `ghcr.io/abhigyanpatwari/gitnexus:1.6.3`) |
| **LadyBugDB Core** | 0.15.3 (bundled in the Docker image) |
| **Deployment** | Docker Compose  |
| **Container user** | `node` (uid 1000) |
| **Host permissions** | `-rw-r--r--` on lbug database files |

### Logs / screenshots

_No response_

title: fix(security): Harden CI permissions
body:
This PR addresses the Scorecard U9 remediation scope for `TokenPermissions`: enforce least-privilege workflow token defaults across all GitNexus CI workflows.

> **Note on the Docker piece.** PR #1454 originally also pinned Docker base image digests for the Scorecard `PinnedDependencies` check. That work was completed independently in **PR #1455** (`node:22-bookworm-slim` digest + `ARG NPM_VERSION` centralization across `Dockerfile.cli`, `Dockerfile.web`, `gitnexus/Dockerfile.test`). The merge from `main` into this branch resolved Dockerfile conflicts by taking main's version, so this PR's net contribution is the workflow-level `permissions:` hardening only.

## What this PR changes

**Two release-publishing workflows keep `permissions: {}` (the strictest valid form):**
- `.github/workflows/publish.yml`
- `.github/workflows/release-candidate.yml`

These workflows had `permissions: {}` before this PR was first opened. The original commit replaced it with `permissions: read-all`; this PR restores `{}` and the explanatory comment (`# No workflow-level permissions — scoped per job below.`). Every job in both files already declares its own `permissions:` block, so the workflow-level default only matters for jobs added later without one — and `{}` fails closed where `read-all` would silently grant read access.

**Thirteen other workflows declare `permissions: contents: read` at the top level** (down from the original `read-all`):

```
.github/workflows/ci.yml
.github/workflows/ci-e2e.yml
.github/workflows/ci-quality.yml
.github/workflows/ci-scope-parity.yml
.github/workflows/ci-tests.yml
.github/workflows/claude.yml
.github/workflows/codeql.yml
.github/workflows/dependency-review.yml
.github/workflows/docker.yml
.github/workflows/gitleaks.yml
.github/workflows/pr-labeler.yml
.github/workflows/trivy.yml
.github/workflows/workflow-lint.yml
```

Per-job snapshot used to validate the narrowing:

| Workflow | Jobs | Job-level blocks | Narrowing safe? |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ci.yml` | quality, tests, scope-parity, save-pr-meta, ci-status | quality/tests/scope-parity have `contents: read`; save-pr-meta + ci-status have none | yes — save-pr-meta only uses `upload-artifact` (no token scopes); ci-status is pure shell |
| `ci-e2e.yml` | check-changes, e2e | none | yes — checkout + npm + playwright + upload-artifact only |
| `ci-quality.yml` | format, lint, typecheck, typecheck-web, workflow-convention | none | yes — read-only checks |
| `ci-scope-parity.yml` | discover, parity | none | yes — checkout + scan |
| `ci-tests.yml` | tests, cross-platform | none | yes — checkout + npm + vitest + upload-artifact |
| `claude.yml` | claude | `pull-requests: write`, `issues: write`, `id-token: write`, `actions: read` | yes |
| `codeql.yml` | analyze | `security-events: write`, `actions: read` | yes |
| `dependency-review.yml` | review | `pull-requests: write` | yes |
| `docker.yml` | build-push | `packages: write`, `id-token: write`, `attestations: write` | yes |
| `gitleaks.yml` | gitleaks | `pull-requests: write` | yes |
| `pr-labeler.yml` | autolabel, validate-title | `pull-requests: write`, `pull-requests: read` | yes |
| `trivy.yml` | scan | `security-events: write` | yes |
| `workflow-lint.yml` | zizmor, actionlint | `security-events: write`, `contents: read` | yes |

Where a job's `permissions:` block was already explicit, it is unchanged. Where a job had no block, `contents: read` from the new workflow-level default is the operational scope and was verified sufficient.

## Why `{}` for two workflows but `contents: read` for the rest

`publish.yml` and `release-candidate.yml` are the only two workflows that publish releases (npm + Docker images + GitHub Releases). Their blast radius for a misconfigured future job is high enough to justify the strictest top-level default. Every other workflow runs read-only checks or PR feedback at the workflow level; `contents: read` is sufficient and still tighter than `read-all`.

## Verification

- `zizmor --min-severity high` is clean on the resulting tree. The 21 medium and 4 informational findings reported by zizmor are pre-existing issues in unrelated workflows (`secrets-inherit` in `release-candidate.yml` -> `docker.yml` reusable call, `artipacked` in `tree-sitter-upgrade-readiness.yml` and `triage-sweep.yml`, `superfluous-actions` notes) — none touched by this PR.
- Scorecard `TokenPermissions` remains compliant. Both `permissions: {}` and `permissions: contents: read` are accepted forms.
- All in-PR CI workflows (CodeQL, gitleaks, dependency-review, workflow-lint) trigger on this PR and will run with the new top-level scopes; failures should surface in this PR's checks, not post-merge.

## Out of scope

- `.github/workflows/scorecard.yml` also uses `permissions: read-all` but pre-existed PR #1454 and is deferred to a follow-up PR per scope boundary.
- Codifying a "Workflow permissions convention" section in `CONTRIBUTING.md` analogous to the existing concurrency convention — separate doc-only PR if desired.

## Branch hygiene

The branch carries an `Initial plan` empty commit (Copilot planning artifact) and 5 successive `Merge branch 'main'` commits from earlier in the PR's lifecycle. Use **Squash and merge** at merge time to collapse the entire history into a single commit on `main` — no force-push rebase needed.

title: fix(security): Pin Docker Node base images, remove runtime package-manager CVE surface, verify Trivy on PRs, and harden Dependabot policy
body:
Trivy was still flagging medium-severity findings after the base-image work because the published images inherited vulnerable packages from the bundled npm CLI layer. This change aligns the Dockerfiles on a pinned Node 22 bookworm-slim base, removes package-manager tooling from shipped runtime images, updates the Trivy workflow so Docker-related PRs are scanned before merge, and hardens Dependabot policy so workflow lint/zizmor passes cleanly.

- **Pinned and aligned Docker bases**
  - Standardize `Dockerfile.cli`, `Dockerfile.web`, and `gitnexus/Dockerfile.test` on the same `node:22-bookworm-slim@sha256:...` digest
  - Replace the web image's Alpine base with the same pinned Debian base to keep image behavior and vulnerability posture consistent

- **Remediated bundled package-manager findings**
  - Bootstrap `npm 11.14.1` in build/test contexts so image builds do not rely on the vulnerable npm bundled with the upstream Node image
  - Remove `npm`, `npx`, and `corepack` from the final CLI/web runtime layers, since published GitNexus images only need `node` at runtime

- **Reduced shipped attack/vuln surface**
  - Published runtime images no longer include the bundled package-manager dependency tree that carried the Trivy findings (`picomatch`, `brace-expansion`, `ip-address`)
  - Keeps the remediation in Dockerfiles rather than documenting a dismissal in `SECURITY.md`

- **Closed the Trivy verification gap for this class of change**
  - Update `.github/workflows/trivy.yml` to run on `pull_request` when Dockerfiles or the Trivy workflow itself change
  - Expand Trivy severity scanning from `HIGH,CRITICAL` to `MEDIUM,HIGH,CRITICAL` so the workflow matches the U10 issue scope

- **Added Docker digest maintenance coverage**
  - Update `.github/dependabot.yml` so pinned Docker base-image digests in the root Dockerfiles and `gitnexus/Dockerfile.test` receive automated update PRs
  - Reduces the frozen-digest maintenance gap introduced by pinning the Node base images

- **Hardened Dependabot update policy**
  - Add explicit `cooldown` policies to all Dependabot update blocks in `.github/dependabot.yml`
  - Fix the zizmor `dependabot-cooldown` findings properly across the whole file, not just the new Docker entries
  - Keeps version-update PR creation rate controlled for GitHub Actions, Docker, and npm ecosystems while leaving security updates unaffected

```dockerfile
# node:22-bookworm-slim
FROM node:22-bookworm-slim@sha256:9f6d5975c7dca860947d3915877f85607946403fc55349f39b4bc3688448bb6e AS runtime

RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends curl git && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/* \
    && rm -rf /usr/local/lib/node_modules/npm \
    && rm -rf /usr/local/lib/node_modules/corepack \
    && rm -f /usr/local/bin/npm /usr/local/bin/npx /usr/local/bin/corepack
```

---

## Image size trade-off (web)

Switching `Dockerfile.web` from `node:22-alpine` to `node:22-bookworm-slim` increases the final image by roughly ~150 MB (musl/Alpine ~150 MB → glibc/Debian ~300 MB). The trade-off is intentional: the web runtime now shares the same pinned bookworm-slim digest as the CLI and test images, so all three runtimes inherit the same CVE posture and Dependabot updates land everywhere at once. `docker-server.mjs` is pure JavaScript with no native module dependencies, so the libc switch is transparent at runtime.

## Node 22 alignment + centralized npm bootstrap

Follow-up commit on this branch addresses the LOW findings from the Final Re-Review:

- **Node 22 across CI** — `engines.node` is now `>=22.0.0`. All four CI workflows (`ci-quality`, `pr-autofix`, `publish`, `release-candidate`) and both composite setup actions are pinned to Node 22, matching the test Docker image. Node 20 reached EOL on 2026-04-30.
- **Centralized npm bootstrap** — Each Dockerfile now declares `ARG NPM_VERSION=11.14.1` once. A future security bump only requires updating one default per file, with cross-reference comments calling out the other two Dockerfiles to keep them in lockstep.
- **Linearized history** — The Copilot `Initial plan` empty commit and the two `Merge branch 'main'` commits have been rebased away; the branch now has 6 clean substantive commits.

title: fix(security): log-injection, http-to-file-access, client-side-request-forgery
body:
Remediates 8 medium CodeQL alerts across 4 files: `js/log-injection` (3), `js/http-to-file-access` (3), and `js/client-side-request-forgery` (2).

## Changes

### `wiki/llm-client.ts` — http-to-file-access (3 alerts)
New `validateLLMBaseUrl()` called at the top of `callLLM()` before any `fetch()`, breaking the taint flow from user-controlled config URL → HTTP response → disk write:
- Rejects non-`http`/`https` schemes
- Restricts `http://` to loopback hosts only (`localhost`, `127.0.0.1`, `[::1]`) — remote LLM servers must use `https://`
- Error messages use `parsed.protocol` / `parsed.origin` instead of the raw input URL to avoid leaking embedded credentials

```ts
// Throws before fetch() is ever called:
validateLLMBaseUrl('file:///etc/passwd');    // → "must use http:// or https://"
validateLLMBaseUrl('http://192.168.1.1/v1'); // → "Insecure http:// … (got http://192.168.1.1)"
validateLLMBaseUrl('http://localhost:11434/v1'); // ✓ Ollama / local LiteLLM
```

### `bridge-db.ts` — log-injection (1 alert)
CRLF-strips both `groupDir` and `lastErr.message` before `bridgeLogger.debug()`. Defence-in-depth on top of pino's existing JSON escaping.

### `api.ts` — log-injection (2 alerts)
Two `console.log` calls in `resolveRepo` that embedded user-controlled `normalizedName`/`job.id` in format strings replaced with `logger.debug` + explicit CRLF sanitization on each value.

### `backend-client.ts` — client-side-request-forgery (2 alerts)
New `validateBackendUrl()` called inside `setBackendUrl()` before the URL is stored as the fetch target base. Rejects non-`http`/`https` schemes (`javascript:`, `file://`, `data:`, etc.) while allowing any well-formed http/https origin. Error messages use `parsed.protocol` only — no raw input echoed.

## Tests
- `wiki-llm-client.test.ts`: 11 new cases covering `validateLLMBaseUrl` happy paths (including uppercase `LOCALHOST`), all rejection branches (RFC 1918 / IMDS IPs, hostname-spoofing, non-loopback IPv6, `ftp://`), IPv6 loopback (`[::1]`), and credential hygiene (raw URL not present in error messages)
- `server-connection.test.ts`: 9 new cases covering `validateBackendUrl` and `setBackendUrl` rejection paths, credential hygiene, and a state-preservation test proving `_backendUrl` is unchanged when validation fails

title: fix(autofix): verify reviewdog actually posted before claiming "click Apply"
body:
## Summary

The sticky **PR Autofix** comment was telling users to "Click **Apply suggestion** on each" even when reviewdog had landed **zero** inline review comments — leaving the user staring at a sticky that promised buttons that didn't exist (see below for an example from #1305).

The script unconditionally set `posted=true` after running reviewdog regardless of whether any comments were actually created. Reviewdog with `-filter-mode=added` correctly filters out fixes that target lines outside the PR's added range — but the publish workflow had no way of knowing that happened, so the sticky lied.

## What changed

The "Post inline suggestions" step now snapshots the count of `github-actions[bot]` review comments **before** and **after** reviewdog runs. The delta is the authoritative "did anything actually post?" signal:

| Δ | `posted` output | Sticky state | Behaviour |
|---|---|---|---|
| `> 0` | `true` | `suggestions-posted` | "Click Apply suggestion on each" — accurate. |
| `0` (and patch was non-empty) | `no-overlap` | `diff-no-overlap` | "Formatter found fixable issues, but they're on lines outside this PR's added range — there's nothing to click here. Run locally." |

Plus a matching `gitnexus/autofix` **Check Run** conclusion (still `neutral`, distinct title) so agents reading `gh pr checks` see the same signal without parsing the sticky.

## Three machine-distinguishable states in the JSON block

The sticky's fenced `gitnexus-autofix` block now reports one of three values for `state`:

- `suggestions-posted` — at least one inline suggestion exists; click Apply.
- `diff-no-overlap` — fixes exist but fall outside the PR's added range.
- `skipped-too-large` — diff exceeds GitHub's ~3000-line review-comment cap.

## Test plan

- [ ] Push to a PR where `npm run lint:fix && npm run format` produces a diff that overlaps the PR's added lines → sticky says **suggestions-posted**, Apply buttons appear inline.
- [ ] Push to a PR where the formatter only touches non-added lines → sticky says **diff-no-overlap**, no inline comments, message tells the user to run locally.
- [ ] Push a clean PR → sticky doesn't appear (existing behaviour, untouched).
- [ ] Verify `gh pr checks <pr> --json` shows the new `gitnexus/autofix` check title for each branch.

## Screenshot of the original confusing case (PR #1305)

> ✨ PR Autofix
> Posted formatting / unused-import suggestions inline. Click **Apply suggestion** on each, or run locally: `npm run lint:fix && npm run format`.

… with no Apply Suggestion buttons anywhere on the diff. After this fix, that same PR would show the **diff-no-overlap** message instead.

title: feat(autofix): replace inline reviewdog with /autofix ChatOps button
body:
## Summary

Pivot the PR autofix UX from per-line reviewdog inline suggestions to a single ChatOps button. Contributors comment `/autofix` on a PR; a new trusted workflow downloads the existing autofix patch artifact, applies it to the PR head, and pushes a commit back.

## Why

The current pipeline has three failure modes that all reduce to "the sticky tells the user to do something but the actionable thing isn't usable":

- **3K+ diffs** hit GitHub's review-comment API 406 limit → sticky says "run locally" with no concrete patch.
- **No-overlap diffs** (formatter touched lines outside PR's added range) get filtered by `-filter-mode=added` → reviewdog posts nothing. PR #1457 fixed the lying sticky, but the UX dead-end remained.
- **Per-line click-Apply** is high-friction for big diffs and easy to apply unevenly.

A single `git apply` + push works at any size and lands the fixes atomically. This is the standard ChatOps pattern (Dependabot's `@dependabot rebase`, Mergify's `@mergify rebase`).

## What changed

- `.github/workflows/pr-autofix-publish.yml`: removed `Install reviewdog` and `Post inline suggestions` steps. Collapsed three sticky states (`suggestions-posted`, `diff-no-overlap`, `skipped-too-large`) into one (`fixes-available`). Schema bumped v1 → v2 with new `apply_command` field; all v1 fields preserved.
- `.github/workflows/pr-autofix-apply.yml` (new): listens for `issue_comment` with body matching `^/autofix\s*$`, validates commenter has `write`/`admin`/`maintain` OR is PR author, locates latest successful `pr-autofix.yml` run for PR head SHA, downloads artifact, applies patch, pushes commit. Reacts 👀/✅/👎 on the triggering comment per outcome. Idempotent (`git apply --check --reverse` detects already-applied state).
- `CONTRIBUTING.md`: documented v2 schema and the `/autofix` flow, including the **Allow edits by maintainers** requirement for fork PRs.

## Trust posture

- Apply workflow runs from default-branch code only, under `issue_comment` trigger.
- Comment body + author login flow through env vars and pattern-matched, never interpolated into shell.
- Permission gate (write/admin/maintain OR PR author) before any artifact fetch.
- Fork PRs require "Allow edits by maintainers" (GitHub-native; we don't bypass).
- No fork-controlled string flows into a URL or shell-injection sink. CodeQL js/server-side-request-forgery and template-injection posture preserved.

## Test plan

Post-merge manual matrix on test PRs against `main`:

- [ ] Small PR (≤50 lines) with prettier violations overlapping added range → sticky shows `fixes-available` + `/autofix` instruction. Comment `/autofix` → bot reacts 👀, then ✅, push lands as `chore(autofix): ...` commit.
- [ ] Small PR with formatter touching only non-added lines → same flow.
- [ ] Synthetic 3K+ diff (drop `paths-ignore` for one snapshot temporarily) → no `skipped-too-large` state; `/autofix` works.
- [ ] Idempotent re-invoke after success → bot reacts ✅ no push.
- [ ] Comment `/autofix --foo` (extra args) → silently ignored (no reaction).
- [ ] Comment `please don't /autofix this` → silently ignored.
- [ ] User without write access (and not PR author) comments `/autofix` → 👎 + refusal reply.
- [ ] No successful pr-autofix run for current head SHA (e.g., right after force-push) → 👎 + regenerate instruction.
- [ ] Fork PR without **Allow edits by maintainers** → 👎 + enable-instruction reply.
- [ ] `gh pr checks <pr> --json name,conclusion,output | jq '.[] | select(.name == "gitnexus/autofix")'` returns the new neutral title.
- [ ] Sticky JSON: `jq '.schema'` reads `gitnexus.pr-autofix/v2`, `.apply_command == "/autofix"`.

## Notes

- Replaces (does not stack with) the inline-suggestions UX. The reviewdog binary pin and 60+ lines of YAML are removed.
- After merge, the `no-overlap` state introduced in #1457 becomes dead code (the new state machine has no `no-overlap`). Consider closing #1457 or rebasing it on top of this.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

## Supersedes

Closes #1457 — this PR includes that commit (`e1f0fe7e`) as a base and pivots beyond it. The `no-overlap` state #1457 introduced becomes dead code with the inline reviewdog removal, but the commit history is preserved.

## Codex adversarial review (post-pivot follow-up)

Codex flagged two trust gaps in the pivot. Both addressed in commit `a4e1b220`:

- **U1 (high)**: `pr-autofix-publish.yml` now cross-verifies artifact identity (`pr_number`, `head_sha`, `head_repo`) against `github.event.workflow_run` authority before any sticky/check-run side effect. Fork-PR fallback uses `gh api commits/{sha}/pulls`.
- **U2 (medium)**: `pr-autofix-apply.yml` now pushes with `--force-with-lease=refs/heads/${HEAD_REF}:${HEAD_SHA}` against the resolved SHA. Distinct `lease-failed` result code + retry-message reply (separate from `push-failed` for fork-maintainer-edit so contributors can diagnose the actual cause).

## Residual review findings - all resolved in commit a7dcd4f4

All five P2 items from ce-code-review (#6 gh_retry on locate, #7 artifact-expired fallback, #8 re-entrancy loop guard, #10 producer-still-running UX, #12 gh_retry wrapper port) landed in this PR. Every code path in pr-autofix-apply.yml now sets a meaningful `result=` that maps to a specific user-facing reaction + reply.

title: feat(cursor): upgrade Cursor hook integration to 2.4 preToolUse/postToolUse for Read/Grep coverage
body:
## Problem

`gitnexus-cursor-integration/hooks/hooks.json` only registers `beforeShellExecution`, so graph augmentation in Cursor only fires when the agent runs `rg`/`grep` via shell. The agent's native `Read`, `codebase_search`, and `Grep` tools — which it uses far more often than shell — get no graph context.

Compared to Claude Code (which intercepts `Grep|Glob|Bash` via `PreToolUse` + `PostToolUse` and gets full graph augmentation per `gitnexus/hooks/claude/gitnexus-hook.cjs` and `gitnexus-claude-plugin/hooks/hooks.json`), Cursor users get a significantly weaker experience. The README integration table at `README.md:122` reflects this gap today.

## Cursor 2.4 added what we need

Cursor 2.4 (released 2026-01-22) added generic `preToolUse` and `postToolUse` hooks with matchers `Shell | Read | Write | Grep | Delete | Task | MCP:<tool_name>`. The `postToolUse` hook can return `{\"additional_context\": \"...\"}` which the agent sees alongside the tool result — functionally equivalent to Claude Code's PreToolUse-stdout-prepended-to-result pattern.

- Docs: https://cursor.com/docs/agent/hooks
- Changelog: https://cursor.com/changelog/2-4

> *\"Improved capabilities & coverage for hooks: `stop` hook; modify prompts `beforeSubmitPrompt`; `PreToolUse` and `PostToolUse` hooks.\"* — Cursor 2.4 changelog

The current `gitnexus-cursor-integration/` was last touched 2026-02-13 — about 3 weeks after Cursor 2.4 shipped, which is presumably why nobody picked it up.

## Proposal

1. Replace `gitnexus-cursor-integration/hooks/hooks.json` with a `postToolUse` config matching `Shell|Read|Grep` (and optionally `preToolUse` if we want to gate as well as augment):
   ```json
   {
     \"version\": 1,
     \"hooks\": {
       \"postToolUse\": [
         {
           \"matcher\": \"Shell|Read|Grep\",
           \"command\": \"./hooks/augment.sh\",
           \"timeout\": 5000
         }
       ]
     }
   }
   ```
2. Update `gitnexus-cursor-integration/hooks/augment-shell.sh` (or replace with a Node script for cross-platform support — the current bash + `jq` pipeline doesn't run on Windows) to:
   - Read the `postToolUse` JSON event shape (`tool_name`, `tool_input`, `tool_output`)
   - Extract a search pattern (for `Read` it's the file path; for `Grep` the query; for `Shell` the existing rg/grep parsing)
   - Call `gitnexus augment <pattern>` as today
   - Wrap stdout in `{\"additional_context\": \"...\"}` instead of `{\"agent_message\": \"...\"}`
3. Update doc references:
   - `gitnexus/src/core/augmentation/engine.ts:5` (\"Cursor beforeShellExecution\")
   - `gitnexus/src/cli/augment.ts:5` (same)
   - `README.md:122` integration table (Cursor row should match Claude Code's coverage)
   - `gitnexus/README.md:35`

## Open question — `codebase_search`

Cursor's semantic search tool isn't in the documented matcher list at https://cursor.com/docs/agent/hooks. It might fire under `Grep`, or it might not be hookable at all by name. Worth empirically logging the `tool_name` value from the hook input to find out. Worst case, semantic search misses augment but `Read`/`Grep`/`Shell` still work — already a huge upgrade from \"Bash only.\"

## Why this matters

Without this, Cursor users see graph context maybe 10% as often as Claude Code users — only when the agent happens to drop to shell. With it, Cursor's `Read` and `Grep` get the same graph augmentation that makes the Claude Code experience strong.

## Risk

Low. Change is isolated to `gitnexus-cursor-integration/` plus a few doc string updates. No backend changes — `gitnexus augment` and the `core/augmentation/engine.ts` API don't care which harness called them.

title: feat(cursor): upgrade hooks to Cursor 2.4 postToolUse for Read/Grep/Shell coverage
body:
## Summary

Closes #1466.

Cursor 2.4 (released 2026-01-22) shipped generic `preToolUse`/`postToolUse` hooks with matchers `Shell|Read|Write|Grep|Delete|Task|MCP:<tool>`. The current `gitnexus-cursor-integration/hooks/hooks.json` still uses the 2.3-era `beforeShellExecution`, so graph augmentation only fires when the agent runs `rg`/`grep` via shell — `Read` and `Grep` (the agent's far more common tools) get no graph context.

This PR brings Cursor parity (and slight superset) with the Claude Code hook coverage:

- **`gitnexus-cursor-integration/hooks/hooks.json`** — single `postToolUse` entry matching `Shell|Read|Grep`, invoking the new Node script.
- **`gitnexus-cursor-integration/hooks/gitnexus-hook.cjs`** (new) — cross-platform Node hook ported from the bash + `jq` script. Mirrors safety patterns from `gitnexus/hooks/claude/gitnexus-hook.cjs`:
  - `path.isAbsolute(cwd)` validation
  - `.gitnexus/` discovery with linked-worktree fallback (`git rev-parse --git-common-dir`)
  - Global-registry exclusion (`isGlobalRegistryDir` heuristic)
  - `npx.cmd` on Windows, `--` end-of-options marker (#200), `.slice(0, 200)` debug truncation
  - Graceful failure (`status === 0`, no broken pipe to Cursor)
  - Per-tool pattern extraction:
    - `Grep` → `toolInput.query` (also `pattern` / `regex` aliases)
    - `Read` → file basename stripped to identifier chars (≥ 3 chars)
    - `Shell` → existing rg/grep arg parser
  - Emits `{ "additional_context": "..." }` (Cursor 2.4 shape), not Claude's nested `hookSpecificOutput`.
- **`gitnexus-cursor-integration/hooks/augment-shell.sh`** (deleted) — bash + `jq` pipeline doesn't run on Windows and only covered Shell.
- **`gitnexus/test/unit/cursor-hook.test.ts`** (new) — 33 regression tests. Coverage:
  - File presence + legacy `augment-shell.sh` removal
  - `hooks.json` wiring (matcher, command, version, no leftover `beforeShellExecution`)
  - Source-level invariants: no `shell: true`, `npx.cmd`, `path.isAbsolute(cwd)`, `.slice(0, 200)`, `additional_context` (not `hookSpecificOutput`), pattern length ≥ 3, end-of-options marker, `.gitnexus` gating, linked-worktree resolution
  - `extractPattern` coverage per tool (Grep / Read / Shell)
  - Behavioral early-exit tests: empty stdin, invalid JSON, relative cwd, unindexed cwd, unknown tool name, non-search Shell commands, 2-char query, basename with no identifier chars, missing file path, case-insensitive tool name matching
  - Output parser sanity (well-formed JSON, empty stdout, malformed JSON)
- **`README.md` / `gitnexus/README.md`** — editor-support table now reads `**Cursor** | Yes | Yes | Yes (postToolUse) | **Full**` instead of `— | MCP + Skills`.
- **`gitnexus/src/cli/augment.ts`** + **`gitnexus/src/core/augmentation/engine.ts`** — doc-string `Cursor beforeShellExecution` → `Cursor postToolUse`; engine doc tool list expanded to `grep/glob/read/search`.

### Design notes

- **`postToolUse` only**, not also `preToolUse`. Augmentation is observational (the agent sees enriched context after the tool ran), not gating, so the second matcher is dead weight.
- **Read pattern = file basename** (stripped to identifier chars), not the raw file path. Engine uses BM25 over symbol names, so the basename is a higher-signal token than `src/auth/handler.ts`.
- **`codebase_search` left unhandled.** Cursor's docs (https://cursor.com/docs/agent/hooks) don't list it as a matchable tool name. Per the issue's open question, semantic-search miss is acceptable — `Read`/`Grep`/`Shell` already cover the dominant paths.

### Risk

Low. Change is isolated to `gitnexus-cursor-integration/` plus four doc-string / README cells. The augment CLI and `core/augmentation/engine.ts` API are unchanged — neither cares which harness called them. Cursor users on 2.3 will silently lose hook augmentation; users on 2.4+ gain `Read`/`Grep` coverage on top of the existing `Shell` path.

title: gitnexus@1.6.3 analyze crashes on Windows with exit code -1073741819
body:
﻿## Summary

`gitnexus@1.6.3 analyze` crashes on Windows with exit code `-1073741819` during indexing. No JavaScript stack trace is printed.

The same repository can be indexed successfully with `gitnexus@1.2.9`, so this appears to be related to the newer native storage/indexing path rather than the repository being completely unsupported.

## Environment

- OS: Windows
- Shell: PowerShell
- Node versions tested:
  - v18.20.8
  - v20.20.2
  - v22.22.0
- npm: 10.9.4
- GitNexus: 1.6.3
- Repository type: Java / NeoForge Minecraft mod
- Repo size after old GitNexus indexing:
  - 2231 files
  - 8009 symbols
  - 18886 edges
  - 491 clusters
  - 300 flows

## Commands Tested

```powershell
npm exec --yes --package gitnexus@1.6.3 -- gitnexus analyze --force
```

Also tested a smaller path:

```powershell
npm exec --yes --package gitnexus@1.6.3 -- gitnexus analyze src/main --force --skip-git --name Koniavacraft-src-main
```

Also tested by directly invoking the CLI script with Node 20:

```powershell
node path\to\node_modules\gitnexus\dist\cli\index.js analyze src/main --force --skip-git --name Koniavacraft-src-main-node20
```

## Result

All `gitnexus@1.6.3 analyze` attempts exit with:

```text
EXIT=-1073741819
```

The only visible output is:

```text
GitNexus Analyzer
Warning: no .git directory found — commit-tracking and incremental updates disabled.
```

No stack trace or JS error is printed.

## What Works

`gitnexus@1.2.9` works on the same repo:

```powershell
node path\to\gitnexus@1.2.9\node_modules\gitnexus\dist\cli\index.js analyze --force
```

Output:

```text
Repository indexed successfully
8009 nodes | 18886 edges | 491 clusters | 300 flows
```

## Expected Behavior

GitNexus 1.6.3 should either index the repository successfully on Windows, or fail with a diagnostic error instead of a native access violation.

## Notes

This does not appear to be a single Node version issue because Node 18, 20, and 22 were tested and all produced the same exit code.

title: fix(markdown): handle CRLF line endings in section heading parser
body:
## Summary

The markdown processor's section heading parser silently produces zero `Section` nodes for files with CRLF line endings (Windows-authored markdown). One-line fix: split on `/\r\n|\r|\n/` instead of `'\n'`.

## Root cause

`gitnexus/src/core/ingestion/markdown-processor.ts` line 39 (pre-fix):

```typescript
const lines = file.content.split('\n');
```

`split('\n')` on CRLF content produces lines that retain a trailing `\r`. The heading regex on line 14:

```typescript
const HEADING_RE = /^(#{1,6})\s+(.+)$/;
```

uses `^` and `$` anchors without multiline mode. `$` matches before end-of-string, not before `\r`. Result: `"## Heading\r"` fails to match; the line is treated as non-heading content; no `Section` node is created. The file is silently ingested with zero structural metadata — the markdown-processor's `(no headings found)` early-return path (or the equivalent fallback in caller) treats it as a one-blob file.

## Empirical evidence

Surfaced during a controlled retrieval-comparison pilot. Test corpus: 10 markdown files in a flat directory.

| File | Line endings | Section nodes after `gitnexus analyze` |
|---|---|---:|
| `properties/buy-box-criteria.md` | **CRLF** (669 CR, 0 LF) | **0** |
| All 9 other files | LF only | 12-59 each |

After CRLF → LF conversion on `buy-box-criteria.md` (no other change), `gitnexus analyze` registered **47 Section nodes** for that file (registry total 366 → 414 nodes). All structural; no source change beyond line endings.

The same bug existed downstream in our Qdrant chunker (different codebase, same pattern). Patched both — this PR is the GitNexus-side fix.

## The patch

```diff
-    const lines = file.content.split('\n');
+    // Normalize CRLF/CR to LF before splitting so that line-end agnostic
+    // markdown files (Windows-authored, mixed) yield correct headings.
+    // Without this, `## Heading\r\n` produces `## Heading\r` after split,
+    // and the HEADING_RE regex (anchored with `$`) fails to match because
+    // `$` matches before end-of-string, not before `\r`.
+    const lines = file.content.split(/\r\n|\r|\n/);
```

The codebase already handles CRLF elsewhere — `gitnexus/src/core/lbug/lbug-adapter.ts:75` uses `crlfDelay: Infinity` — so this fix is consistent with existing CRLF-awareness elsewhere in GitNexus.

## Tests

Added `gitnexus/test/integration/markdown-processor-crlf.test.ts` with 5 cases:

- LF baseline (3 sections expected)
- CRLF (the regression — pre-fix returns 0; post-fix returns 3)
- CR-only (old Mac OS Classic; bonus tolerance)
- Mixed CRLF + LF
- `startLine`/`endLine` correctness on CRLF content (regression guard against an off-by-one when normalizing)

The CRLF case is the regression test: before this patch it would return 0; after, 3.

## Backward compatibility

Pure additive — files with LF-only line endings produce identical output before and after this patch. `split(/\r\n|\r|\n/)` behaves identically to `split('\n')` on LF-only content. CR-only line endings (old Mac OS Classic) become tolerated, which is a minor side benefit at zero risk.

## Out of scope (not bundled)

- YAML frontmatter offset awareness — the parser walks raw lines (doesn't strip frontmatter), so `startLine`/`endLine` already match the original file. No fix needed.
- IMPORTS edge source-line metadata.
- File-type include/exclude flags at the CLI walker.

Happy to follow up on any of these in separate PRs if there's interest.

Error: dlopen(/Users/chendacai/.nvm/versions/node/v24.15.0/lib/node_modules/gitnexus/node_modules/@ladybugdb/core/lbugjs.node, 0x0001): tried: '/Users/chendacai/.nvm/versions/node/v24.15.0/lib/node_modules/gitnexus/node_modules/@ladybugdb/core/lbugjs.node' (no such file)

title: ci(release): skip rc build on release PRs
body:
## Summary

Suppresses the auto-fired **Release Candidate** workflow when a release lands on \`main\`, so the rc cycle no longer races \`publish.yml\` on the v-tag.

## Why

When PR #1473 (v1.6.4) was squash-merged, \`release-candidate.yml\` auto-fired on the merge commit and started bumping rc.15 — at the same time the \`v1.6.4\` tag push fired \`publish.yml\`. We had to manually \`gh run cancel\` the rc run. This automates that.

## How (belt-and-suspenders)

The \`guard\` job now short-circuits to \`should_run=false\` if **either**:

1. **Commit-subject heuristic** — HEAD commit subject matches \`chore: release vX.Y.Z\` (the canonical release-PR title in this repo).
2. **Label-based opt-out** — the squash-merged PR carries the \`release\` label (looked up via \`gh pr view\` on the \`(#NNNN)\` suffix in the merge commit subject).

Either match suppresses rc. A failed \`gh\` API call falls through to the existing dedup logic rather than silently suppressing rc builds (so a transient API hiccup can never accidentally pause the rc cycle).

The \`release\` label has been created on the repo with green color and a description.

## Diff scope

- \`.github/workflows/release-candidate.yml\` — \`guard\` job: adds \`pull-requests: read\` permission, two new short-circuit branches before the existing dedup check.
- No changes to \`publish.yml\`, \`docker.yml\`, or any rc-cycle counter logic.

## Test plan

- [ ] CI passes
- [ ] After merge, next normal commit to \`main\` still triggers rc as before
- [ ] Next release PR (v1.6.5) labelled \`release\` will skip rc automatically

title: test(u8): de-flake regex linearity assertions
body:
## Summary

Replaces the brittle single-trial 2× input + 3× ratio bound in `test/unit/u8-redos-resource-exhaustion.test.ts` with a robust median-of-N methodology. Eliminates a real CI flake without losing regression-detection power.

## Problem

A real macOS CI run failed with:

```
parseCargoPackageName: ratio 3.01× exceeds bound 3× (small=7.41ms, large=22.31ms)
```

Both timings were above the 5ms noise floor, but close enough that single-shot scheduler jitter pushed the ratio just over 3×. The test was correctly running against linear code — it just couldn't tell linear-with-jitter from a regression.

## Fix — four stacked techniques

1. **Warmup runs** (3) before timing — let the JIT tier up
2. **Median of 5 trials** per measurement — eliminates GC pauses, scheduler jitter, OS interrupts
3. **4× input ratio** (was 2×) — linear gives ~4×, O(n²) gives ~16× → much bigger gap between "linear" and "regressed"
4. **8× ratio bound** with a 20ms noise floor on the LARGE measurement

### Headroom math

| Behaviour | Time on 4× input | Bound | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| Linear (expected) | ~4× | 8× | ✅ pass with 2× safety |
| O(n²) regression | ~16× | 8× | ❌ fail loudly |
| Catastrophic backtracking | ≫16× or >500ms cap | 8× / 500ms | ❌ fail loudly |

Catastrophic backtracking is also still caught by the absolute `<500ms` cap on each measurement, so even if the ratio assertion is skipped (when the large run is below the noise floor), exponential blowup still fires.

## Verification

10 consecutive local runs of `test/unit/u8-redos-resource-exhaustion.test.ts` all passed (13/13 each).

## Test plan

- [ ] CI passes
- [ ] No new flakes in the next ~10 CI runs across macOS / ubuntu / windows matrices

title: fix(augment): add CONTAINS fallback when FTS indexes unavailable
body:
## Problem

When the GitNexus MCP server is running alongside the `gitnexus augment` CLI (e.g. in Claude Code hooks), the MCP server holds the KuzuDB write lock. The augment CLI opens the DB via `pool-adapter` in read-only mode. FTS indexes cannot be created in read-only mode, so `searchFTSFromLbug` returns `ftsAvailable: false` with an empty results array.

The existing code path hits `if (bm25Results.length === 0) return ''` immediately after, producing **no enrichment at all** — silently, with no indication that the graph was reachable but FTS was unavailable.

This also affects first-run scenarios where `gitnexus analyze` has completed but FTS indexes have not been built yet for a session.

## Fix

Add a Cypher `n.name CONTAINS` fallback in `augment()` that fires **only** when:
1. `ftsAvailable === false` (indexes genuinely unavailable, not just no matches), AND
2. `symbolMatches` is empty after the BM25 mapping loop

The fallback does a direct graph name search — slower than FTS but always available when the graph is indexed. It is wrapped in `.catch(() => [])` and cannot throw.

```ts
if (symbolMatches.length === 0 && !ftsAvailable) {
  const firstWord = pattern.replace(/'/g, "''").split(/\s+/)[0];
  const fallbackRows = await executeQuery(repoId, `
    MATCH (n)
    WHERE n.name CONTAINS '${firstWord}'
    RETURN n.id AS id, n.name AS name, labels(n)[0] AS type, n.filePath AS filePath
    LIMIT 5
  `).catch(() => []);
  // push to symbolMatches...
}
```

## Safety

- **No behaviour change** when FTS indexes exist — the fallback branch is never reached
- **No new dependencies**
- **Graceful**: `.catch(() => [])` means any graph error still results in `return ''`
- Does not depend on any specific tooling setup (Claude Code, context-mode, etc.)

## Changed file

- `gitnexus/src/core/augmentation/engine.ts` — 25 insertions, 3 deletions

title: `--no-stats` flag has no effect (commander.js negation collides with `options.noStats` reads)
body:
## Summary

The `--no-stats` flag on `gitnexus analyze` is documented as *"Omit volatile file/symbol counts from AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md"* (see [#704](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/issues/704), implemented in [#1059](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/pull/1059)) but does nothing — the volatile `(N symbols, N relationships, N execution flows)` phrase still appears in the rewritten markdown after the flag is passed.

Root cause is a [commander.js](https://github.com/tj/commander.js) naming-convention mismatch: `.option('--no-stats', ...)` registers the option as `options.stats` (boolean, default `true`, set to `false` when the flag is passed). The source reads `options?.noStats`, which is always `undefined`, so the omit branch in the AGENTS.md / CLAUDE.md template never fires.

## Environment

- gitnexus `1.6.4` (latest stable on npm at time of filing)
- Node 22.x, Windows 11 (also reproducible on macOS — pure JS bug)
- Repro repo: any indexed repo with a populated AGENTS.md / CLAUDE.md `<!-- gitnexus:start -->` block

## Reproduction

```bash
# in any indexed repo
grep -E '\([0-9]+ symbols' CLAUDE.md   # expected: present (counts)
npx gitnexus analyze --no-stats
grep -E '\([0-9]+ symbols' CLAUDE.md   # expected: absent
                                       # actual:   STILL PRESENT (with possibly-different counts)
```

## Code pointers

Three call sites read `options?.noStats`; the two action-handler-level reads are wrong, the third (in `ai-context.js`) is correct because it reads from a downstream object that's been re-packed.

`dist/cli/analyze.js:298`
```js
            noStats: options?.noStats,    // ← always undefined; should be options?.stats === false
```

`dist/cli/analyze.js:367`
```js
}, skillResult.skills, { skipAgentsMd: options?.skipAgentsMd, noStats: options?.noStats });
//                                                            ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ same bug
```

`dist/cli/ai-context.js:249` is OK (the `options` here is the downstream object built by analyze.js, so `noStats` is correct given the caller passes it explicitly):
```js
const content = generateGitNexusContent(projectName, stats, generatedSkills, groupNames, options?.noStats);
```

## Suggested fix

Replace `options?.noStats` with `options?.stats === false` at the two action-handler reads in `analyze.js`. The strict `=== false` check (rather than `!options?.stats`) avoids treating an absent options object or absent `.stats` field as `noStats=true`.

```diff
-            noStats: options?.noStats,
+            noStats: options?.stats === false,
```

```diff
-}, skillResult.skills, { skipAgentsMd: options?.skipAgentsMd, noStats: options?.noStats });
+}, skillResult.skills, { skipAgentsMd: options?.skipAgentsMd, noStats: options?.stats === false });
```

The `ai-context.js:249` read can stay as-is.

A regression test would be: `npx gitnexus analyze --no-stats` followed by an assertion that the rewritten markdown does NOT match `/\([0-9]+ symbols/`.

## Workaround

`--skip-agents-md` works correctly (different code path: it skips the markdown rewrite entirely). Heavier hammer — also blocks auto-updates of skill links and group registrations in the gitnexus block — but reliably stops the volatile-count drift the original feature request was about.

## Why this matters

The whole point of #704 was to stop chore-commit churn on every reindex. With the flag silently ineffective, repos that adopted it as documented are still getting count drift on every `analyze` and producing a chore commit per reindex anyway. (Discovered while debugging the same churn pattern in a downstream project.)

Happy to send a PR if useful.

title: fix(cli): make --no-stats actually omit volatile counts (#1477)
body:
## Summary

The `--no-stats` flag added in #1059 (closes feature request #704) was a no-op: the count phrase still appeared on every reindex. This PR makes the flag effective by fixing a commander.js negation-flag misread, plus adds two regression tests so it cannot silently regress again.

## Motivation / context

Filed as bug [#1477](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/issues/1477). Original feature request: [#704](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/issues/704). Closing PR for the feature: [#1059](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/pull/1059).

Discovered while debugging chore-commit churn in a downstream marking-OS project: every `npx gitnexus analyze` run produced a tiny diff in `CLAUDE.md` / `AGENTS.md` because the cluster boundary count drifts mildly between runs. Adding `--no-stats` as documented didn't help — turns out the flag was silently broken.

## Areas touched

- [x] `gitnexus/` (CLI / core / MCP server)
- [ ] `gitnexus-web/`
- [ ] `.github/`
- [ ] `eval/` or other tooling
- [ ] Docs / agent config only

## Root cause

`.option('--no-stats', ...)` in `src/cli/index.ts:38` follows commander.js's [negation-flag convention](https://github.com/tj/commander.js/blob/master/Readme.md#other-option-types-negatable-boolean-and-booleanvalue): the option is registered under the accessor `stats` (boolean, default `true`; `false` when the user passes `--no-stats`), **not** `noStats`. Two action-handler reads in `src/cli/analyze.ts` were reading `options?.noStats`, which is always `undefined`, so the `noStats` payload reached `runFullAnalysis` (at line 414 pre-fix) and `generateAIContextFiles` (at line 500 pre-fix) as `undefined`/falsy, and the count branch in the template always rendered.

The `AnalyzeOptions` interface in `analyze.ts` also declared `noStats?: boolean`, which was a static-type misrepresentation of what commander actually provides at runtime — a contributing factor that hid the bug from a TypeScript-aware reader.

The internal `AnalyzeOptions` in `core/run-analyze.ts` and `AIContextOptions` in `cli/ai-context.ts` correctly use `noStats?: boolean` because they're not commander-shaped — they receive the *re-packed* options object built at the bridge in `analyze.ts`. Those reads are unchanged.

## Scope & constraints

**In scope**

- Fix both action-handler reads (`analyze.ts:414` and `analyze.ts:500`) to use `options?.stats === false`. The strict `=== false` check (rather than `!options?.stats`) preserves the documented default-on behaviour when the flag is omitted entirely.
- Update the CLI-level `AnalyzeOptions` interface to declare `stats?: boolean` (matching commander's runtime shape) with a JSDoc explaining the negation.
- Two regression tests in `test/unit/ai-context.test.ts` covering both branches of the contract.

**Explicitly out of scope / not done here**

- No changes to internal/core types (`run-analyze.ts`, `ai-context.ts`) — those continue to use `noStats?: boolean` because they're not commander-shaped.
- No documentation updates — the `--no-stats` help text already describes the intended behaviour correctly; only the implementation was wrong.

## Implementation notes

The diff is intentionally minimal and surgical:

```diff
-        noStats: options?.noStats,
+        // commander.js `.option('--no-stats', …)` registers the flag as
+        // `options.stats` (boolean, default true; `false` when the user
+        // passed --no-stats). Reading `options?.noStats` here returns
+        // undefined every time, so the flag was a no-op on the markdown
+        // rewrite path before this fix. See #1477.
+        noStats: options?.stats === false,
```

Comment at the bridge explains the gotcha so the next maintainer who touches this won't re-introduce the same bug under a different surface (e.g. someone adding a similar negation flag).

## Testing & verification

- [x] `cd gitnexus && node_modules/.bin/vitest.cmd run test/unit/ai-context.test.ts` → **13/13 pass** (11 prior + 2 new).
- [ ] `cd gitnexus && npm run test:integration` — not run; my Windows machine couldn't complete the build script (`scripts/build.js` failed because `npx tsc` resolved to a non-TypeScript binary on PATH; unrelated to this PR). Vitest's transform handles the TypeScript directly so unit tests still ran cleanly.
- [x] `cd gitnexus && npx tsc --noEmit` — pre-existing `gitnexus-shared` resolution errors only (require the build step that I couldn't run locally). My changes do not introduce new TypeScript errors.
- [x] **Manual verification on a real repo:**
  - On `main`: ran `npx gitnexus analyze --no-stats` against an indexed repo. Count phrase still present in CLAUDE.md → bug confirmed.
  - On this branch: same command. Count phrase absent → fix confirmed.

## Risk / rollback

- **Risk:** very low. Two-line behavioural change at a flag-handling bridge, isolated unit tests prove the contract.
- **Rollback:** plain `git revert` is safe — no data migrations, no schema changes, no on-disk format implications.

## Why this matters

The whole point of #704 was to stop chore-commit churn on every reindex. With the flag silently ineffective for the entire duration #1059 has been merged, repos that adopted `--no-stats` as documented are still getting count drift on every `analyze` and producing a chore commit per reindex. This PR delivers what was advertised.

title: feat(analyze): incremental indexing (parse cache + DB writeback + scope-res short-circuit)
body:
## Summary

Incremental analyze is now the default. On a 1000-file TypeScript repo (this codebase, 24K nodes / 32K edges):

| Run | Time | vs. `--force` |
|---|---|---|
| Cold full reindex | **86s** | (was 143s; **40% faster**) |
| Warm cache, no source changes | **3s** | early-return |
| Warm cache + 1-file edit | **38s** | (was 134s; **72% faster**) |

All paths produce **byte-identical** `{nodes, edges, clusters, flows}`. Verified by running `analyze` and `analyze --force` from the same edited state and comparing graph stats — they match exactly. `--force` remains the escape hatch when you want to wipe and start over.

## How

Three independent layers compose to deliver the speedup. Each preserves correctness on its own; together they give the headline numbers.

1. **Incremental DB writeback.** Hash all source files at end of analyze, store in `meta.json.fileHashes`. Next run diffs current vs. stored: only rows for `changed ∪ added ∪ deleted` files are deleted+rewritten in LadybugDB. Unchanged-file rows are never touched. `Community`/`Process` (graph-wide) are always regenerated by their phases on the merged graph, preserving the "Leiden runs on the FULL graph" invariant. Crash recovery via the `incrementalInProgress` dirty flag in `meta.json` — set before destructive ops, cleared on success, forces a full rebuild on the next run if found set.

2. **Chunk-level parse cache.** Cache file at `.gitnexus/parse-cache.json`. Key is `sha256(sorted("filePath:fileContentHash" for each file in chunk))`; value is the raw `ParseWorkerResult[]` returned by the worker pool. Cache hit → skip worker dispatch entirely, replay via the extracted `mergeChunkResults` helper. Content-addressed, so it survives `--force`. Two stability fixes: a JSON replacer/reviver that round-trips `Map`/`Set` instances cleanly (without it, `ParsedFile.scopes[*].typeBindings` collapses to `{}` and crashes on iteration); alphabetical sort on `parseableScanned` before chunking, so filesystem ordering noise doesn't shift files between chunks.

3. **Scope-resolution short-circuit.** This is the bulk of the cold-rebuild saving. The workers already produce `ParsedFile` artifacts via `extractParsedFile` and stash them in `ParseWorkerResult.parsedFiles` — the previous code threw them away, then `runScopeResolution` re-parsed every file from scratch on the main thread because workers can't pass tree-sitter `Tree` objects across `MessageChannel`. Now those `ParsedFile`s are aggregated through `ParseOutput.parsedFiles` into `runScopeResolution`'s new `preExtractedParsedFiles` map; the extract loop uses them directly when present. Same `extractParsedFile` function on the same input → byte-equivalent output. **scopeResolution phase: 58s → 5s.**

Plus a foundational change required by the equivalence test:

4. **Seeded Leiden RNG.** The vendored `graphology-communities-leiden` defaults to `Math.random` for tie-breaking, which makes community assignments non-deterministic. Added a `mulberry32` seeded PRNG (`LEIDEN_SEED = 0xC0DE`) so the same graph always produces the same partition. Required for incremental ≡ full-rebuild equivalence.

## Correctness contract

**Incremental output ≡ full-rebuild output.** A run of `analyze` (default, incremental) on a repo that previously had `analyze --force` against state S₁ and is now at state S₂ produces a LadybugDB whose contents (nodes, edges, MEMBER_OF, STEP_IN_PROCESS, etc.) are identical to running `analyze --force` against S₂ from a fresh state. This is the gating invariant; every architectural decision was in service of preserving it.

The pipeline still parses every file every run. The "speedup" comes from skipping tree-sitter on cached chunks (Layer 2) and skipping scope-resolution's redundant re-parse (Layer 3), not from skipping files outright. Cross-file resolution always sees full data.

## Prior art / credits

This PR draws on three open community PRs that each tackled part of the problem. None of them shipped as-is; the current design is a different architectural path informed by debugging what broke in v1 attempts.

- **#592** (@zenprocess) — `feat: add --incremental flag to analyze command`. Introduced the SHA-256 file-hash + meta.json approach for change detection. The earliest implementation of "incremental" in this repo.
- **#1146** (@azeemshaik025) — `Review fixes for incremental indexing PR #592`. Companion PR with review-fix commits stacked on #592's branch.
- **#533** (@davidbeesley) — `perf: content-addressed parse and embedding caches for faster reindexing`. Source of the **content-addressed parse cache** idea this PR implements (chunk-level here rather than per-file, but the principle is the same — keys derived from file content, not paths).

The spec doc walks through the v1 attempt that failed equivalence and explains why the final architecture sidesteps the issue.

## Spec

`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-05-10-incremental-indexing-design.md` has the full architectural writeup including the v1 attempt that didn't work, the post-mortem, and the code map for reviewers.

## Test plan

- [x] `npx tsc --noEmit` clean across `gitnexus` + `gitnexus-shared`
- [x] Equivalence: edit a file, run `analyze` (incremental), run `analyze --force` from the same state, compare graph stats — byte-identical
- [x] Crash recovery: kill mid-incremental, re-run, verify forced full rebuild and clean meta.json afterwards
- [x] Dirty-tree gate: edit-don't-commit, run `analyze`, verify it doesn't take the `lastCommit==HEAD` early-return shortcut
- [x] Cache survives `--force` (content-addressed)
- [ ] Cross-platform verification (this measurement is on Windows; expect bigger absolute speedups on macOS/Linux)

## Risk / rollback

- The `--force` escape hatch is preserved. If anything looks off, that's the immediate workaround.
- `meta.json.schemaVersion` is checked at run start; bumping this constant in code force-rebuilds everything if a future change makes the cache incompatible.
- `parse-cache.json` is content-addressed and safe to delete at any time.
- Worst case for crash recovery: the dirty flag forces a full rebuild on the next run.

## What's NOT in this PR (follow-ups)

1. **GitNexus's auto-writes during analyze (`AGENTS.md`, `.claude/skills/...`) mutate cache-relevant files**, so the next run sees their content changed and invalidates the chunks containing them. Mitigations are straightforward (workspace-ignore, deterministic auto-gen) but out of scope here.
2. **Per-file parse-cache granularity.** Current granularity is per-chunk; a single edit invalidates one chunk (~150-200 files at 2MB budget). Per-file would invalidate even less but requires changing the worker contract.
3. **Cache-file size optimization.** ~265MB on this repo. Compact JSON. Could be gzipped or moved to a binary format.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **High Risk**
> High risk because it changes the `analyze` orchestration, LadybugDB mutation strategy, and parsing/scope-resolution data flow; subtle edge cases could leave stale graph rows or drop embeddings if invariants are violated.
> 
> **Overview**
> `analyze` now runs **incrementally by default**: it computes per-file SHA-256 hashes, diffs against `meta.json`, and performs **selective LadybugDB delete+rewrite** for changed/added/deleted files (plus importer-closure expansion), instead of wiping and reloading the entire DB.
> 
> Adds a **content-addressed chunk parse cache** (`.gitnexus/parse-cache.json`) that replays cached `ParseWorkerResult[]` on chunk hash hits, and threads worker-produced `ParsedFile` artifacts into scope-resolution to **skip redundant main-thread re-parsing** on warm runs.
> 
> Strengthens correctness/determinism for incremental ≡ full rebuild: introduces subgraph extraction (`extractChangedSubgraph` + `computeEffectiveWriteSet`), added-file shadow seeding (`shadowCandidatesFor`), deterministic Leiden community detection via seeded RNG, crash recovery via `meta.json.incrementalInProgress`, atomic `meta.json` writes, and new tests pinning these behaviors and equivalence.
