title: bug: `gitnexus serve` corrupts lbug WAL when switching between multiple repos under one server (UNREACHABLE_CODE in wal_record.cpp:76)
body:
## Area

gitnexus (server / lbug session lifecycle)

## Summary

A single `gitnexus serve` process serving multiple repositories from one `GITNEXUS_HOME` corrupts the lbug WAL when the active repo is switched. Once the server has handled a request for repo A, then for repo B, a follow-up request to repo A fails with HTTP 500 and an assertion failure from ladybug WAL. The repo's database state cannot be recovered by a normal restart — `lbug.wal` has to be removed manually.

Each repo on its own (under a `serve` process that hosts only it) runs reliably for as long as needed. The bug is specifically triggered by **switching between multiple databases inside one process**.

## Steps to Reproduce

```yaml
# docker-compose.yml
services:
  gitnexus-server:
    image: ghcr.io/abhigyanpatwari/gitnexus:1.6.4
    container_name: gitnexus-server
    ports: ["4747:4747"]
    volumes:
      - ./home:/gitnexus-home
      - /path/to/repo-a:/repos/repo-a:cached
      - /path/to/repo-b:/repos/repo-b:cached
    environment:
      GITNEXUS_HOME: /gitnexus-home
    command: ["node", "/app/gitnexus/dist/cli/index.js", "serve",
              "--host", "0.0.0.0", "--port", "4747"]
```

```bash
docker compose up -d

# Index both repos under the same server
docker exec gitnexus-server node /app/gitnexus/dist/cli/index.js analyze /repos/repo-a
docker exec gitnexus-server node /app/gitnexus/dist/cli/index.js analyze /repos/repo-b

# Trigger the bug: A -> B -> A
curl "http://localhost:4747/api/graph?repo=repo-a"   # 200 OK
curl "http://localhost:4747/api/graph?repo=repo-b"   # 200 OK
curl "http://localhost:4747/api/graph?repo=repo-a"   # HTTP 500
```

The bug should reproduce on any two non-trivial repos; the original observation was on a ~1k-file backend and a ~3k-file frontend monorepo, but a synthetic pair of throw-away repos works just as well.

## Actual Behavior

The third request returns:

```json
{"error":"Assertion failed in file \"/__w/ladybug/ladybug/src/storage/wal/wal_record.cpp\" on line 76: UNREACHABLE_CODE"}
```

Server logs show:

- A burst of `Schema creation warning: ... UNREACHABLE_CODE` lines (one per node type in the graph schema), repeating on every subsequent request to the broken repo.
- `lbug.wal` for the affected repo keeps growing on every failed request.

`lsof` / `/proc/<pid>/fd` show that the server holds **only one** lbug session open at a time — the previous repo's fd is closed when the next one is opened. This is consistent with the hypothesis that the session is closed without `CHECKPOINT`, leaving the WAL dirty for the next time that database is opened.

`docker restart` alone does not recover — on boot the server tries to replay the WAL and hits the same assertion. The only reliable recovery is:

```bash
docker stop gitnexus-server
rm /path/to/repo-a/.gitnexus/lbug.wal
docker start gitnexus-server
```

After that the repo works again — until the next A → B → A cycle.

## Expected Behavior

A single `gitnexus serve` should be able to host multiple repos from one `GITNEXUS_HOME` without corrupting WAL. Either:

1. **Per-repo lbug session pool**: when switching repos, the current session should be properly closed via `CHECKPOINT` + `close` before the next session is opened.
2. **Parallel session retention**: keep an lbug session open for every registered repo simultaneously (one fd per repo), routing requests to already-open handles.

The 1.6.4 release notes explicitly mention *"WAL corruption recovery — quarantine corrupted .wal files instead of failing analyze; CHECKPOINT before close"* (#1417, #1314, #1377). Based on these symptoms, the "CHECKPOINT before close" path is not taken on the multi-repo serve flow.

## Workarounds

- **One server per repo.** In this layout the bug does not reproduce — each process keeps exactly one lbug session for its entire lifetime.
- If the server is already stuck on a specific repo: `docker stop && rm <repo>/.gitnexus/lbug.wal && docker start`.

## Additional Info

I can share, on request:

- Full server logs covering boot → analyze → A → B → A → 500.
- `--trace-exit` output from `analyze` of the same repo after the event.

Note: I will not attach raw `lbug` / `lbug.wal` files publicly. They contain serialized index data (file paths, symbol names, string literals from source) which can leak proprietary code metadata. If a `lbug.wal` from the corrupted state would help debugging, please reach out and I can share one privately from a synthetic, non-confidential repo prepared for that purpose.

title: feat: migrate C to scope-based resolution (RFC #909 Ring 3)
body:
Adds a C `ScopeResolver` following the established Go/Python/C#/TypeScript migration pattern. C is structurally simple — no classes, no methods, no overloading — so the resolver is minimal.

### Scope resolver (`languages/c/`)

- **`query.ts`** — tree-sitter-c scope query: structs (named + typedef-wrapped), unions, enums, functions (definition + prototype + pointer-return), macros, variables, `#include`, field reads/writes, free/member calls, parameter type bindings, function pointer typedefs (`typedef void (*callback)(int, int)`). Documented known limitations: function-pointer-variable calls captured as free calls (same trade-off as Go resolver), and prototype/definition both captured as `@declaration.function` (graph-quality concern, no false CALLS edges).
- **`captures.ts`** — `emitCScopeCaptures` with arity enrichment, typedef-struct dedup (suppresses `@declaration.typedef` when `@declaration.struct` already captured the same range), and `static` storage class detection (marks file-local functions via `markStaticName`)
- **`import-decomposer.ts`** — Decomposes `preproc_include` nodes; extracts path from `string_literal > string_content` or `system_lib_string`; system headers tagged for filtering
- **`interpret.ts`** — `interpretCImport` (wildcard semantics, system headers → `null`), `interpretCTypeBinding`, `normalizeCTypeName`
- **`import-target.ts`** — Suffix-based `#include` path resolution against workspace files; same-directory sibling preference (matching C compiler `#include "…"` relative-lookup semantics); deterministic lexicographic tiebreak when multiple candidates match at the same path depth
- **`header-scan.ts`** — `loadResolutionConfig` hook that scans the repo for `.h` files and clears stale `staticNames` state. Required because `.h` is classified as C++ by language detection, but C's `#include` targets them. The resolver augments `allFilePaths` with discovered headers before calling `resolveCImportTarget`. Skips common build output directories (`dist`, `build`, `out`, `target`, `_build`, `.next`, `cmake-build-*`) to avoid generated headers shadowing source headers. Output paths normalized to forward slashes for cross-platform (Windows) compatibility.
- **`arity.ts`** / **`arity-metadata.ts`** — Variadic detection via `...` in parameterTypes; `(void)` → zero params; K&R empty parameter list `int foo()` → unknown arity (correctly distinguished from explicit `int foo(void)` per C89/C99 semantics)
- **`merge-bindings.ts`** — First-wins by tier (local > namespace > import > reexport > wildcard)
- **`simple-hooks.ts`** — All null: no receivers, no self bindings, no import scope overrides
- **`static-linkage.ts`** — Per-file tracking of `static` function names; `expandCWildcardNames` hook excludes file-local symbols from cross-file wildcard import visibility, preventing incorrect CALLS edges between translation units. Module-level state is documented as single-process-single-repo and cleared at the start of each resolution pass via `loadResolutionConfig`.
- **`scope-resolver.ts`** — Wires everything including `expandsWildcardTo` and `isFileLocalDef`; `fieldFallbackOnMethodLookup: false`, `propagatesReturnTypesAcrossImports: false`, `allowGlobalFreeCallFallback: true`

### Shared infrastructure changes

- **`ScopeResolver` contract** (`scope-resolution/contract/scope-resolver.ts`) — Added optional `isFileLocalDef` hook: a predicate to identify definitions with file-local linkage (e.g. C `static` functions). When provided, `pickUniqueGlobalCallable` in the global free-call fallback excludes defs where `isFileLocalDef(def) === true` and the def lives in a different file from the caller. Languages without file-local linkage semantics leave this undefined.
- **`free-call-fallback.ts`** — `pickUniqueGlobalCallable` now accepts optional `callerFilePath` and `isFileLocalDef` callback, filtering out cross-file file-local defs from the global fallback resolution path. The `isFileLocalDef` filter is applied in both Phase 1 (scope defs) and Phase 2 (SemanticModel fallback), preventing static function leakage through either resolution path.
- **`run.ts`** — Threads the `isFileLocalDef` hook from the `ScopeResolver` through to `emitFreeCallFallback`.

### Wiring

- `c-cpp.ts` — `cProvider` gets `emitScopeCaptures`, `interpretImport`, `interpretTypeBinding`, `bindingScopeFor`, `importOwningScope`, `receiverBinding`, `arityCompatibility`
- `registry.ts` — `[SupportedLanguages.C, cScopeResolver]`
- `registry-primary-flag.ts` — `SupportedLanguages.C` added to `MIGRATED_LANGUAGES`

### Tests

- `c-structs/` fixture: 5 files exercising named structs, `#include` chains, cross-file function calls
- `c-static-isolation/` fixture: 4 files exercising `static` function file-local linkage isolation — `a.c` (static helper), `b.c`/`b.h` (non-static helper), `caller.c` (includes only `b.h`) — with negative integration test asserting no CALLS edge from caller to `a.c`'s static helper
- `c.test.ts`: 6 integration tests — struct detection, function detection, import resolution (`.c → .h`), CALLS edge emission, static function isolation
- `test/unit/scope-resolution/c/c-captures.test.ts`: 56 unit tests covering scopes, structs, unions, enums, functions, typedef dedup (including function pointer typedefs), fields, variables, macros, imports, references, type bindings, arity metadata, and `static` storage class detection
- `test/unit/scope-resolution/c/c-imports.test.ts`: 16 unit tests covering import decomposition, interpretation, target resolution, deterministic depth-tie tiebreaking, same-directory sibling preference, and edge cases
- `test/unit/scope-resolution/c/c-arity.test.ts`: 21 unit tests covering declaration arity (`void`, variadic, pointer-return, single param, K&R empty parameter list vs explicit `void`), call-site arity, and compatibility checks
- `test/unit/scope-resolution/c/c-header-scan.test.ts`: 11 unit tests covering header file discovery and build output directory skip list (node_modules, .git, vendor, dist, build, out, target, _build, .next, cmake-build-*)
- Total: 99 C tests (93 unit + 6 integration), exceeding the ≥30 coverage requirement
- Both `REGISTRY_PRIMARY_C=0` (legacy) and `=1` (registry-primary) pass; two legacy-expected failures registered (cross-file CALLS edges require scope-based wildcard binding + `isFileLocalDef` filtering)
- Existing C++ (133), Go (121), registry-primary-flag (16) tests unaffected

title: feat: migrate Java to scope-based registry resolution (RFC #909 Ring 3)
body:
Implements `ScopeResolver` for Java, the fifth language migration after Python, C#, TypeScript, and Go.

## New module: `languages/java/`

13 files following the established per-language pattern:

- **`query.ts`** — Tree-sitter scope query covering scopes, declarations, imports, type bindings, and references. Handles Java-specific grammar (`method_invocation`, `field_access`, `type_identifier` for `var`, `modifiers` grouping).
- **`captures.ts`** — Orchestrator: import decomposition, `this`/`super` receiver synthesis, arity metadata on declarations, `@reference.arity` on callsites.
- **`import-decomposer.ts`** — Four import forms: `import x.y.Z`, `import x.y.*`, `import static x.y.Z.m`, `import static x.y.Z.*`.
- **`interpret.ts`** — `ParsedImport` / `ParsedTypeBinding` conversion with generic stripping (`List<User>` → `User`) and qualifier stripping. Qualifier is stripped before generic stripping so that qualified generics like `com.example.BaseModel<T>` resolve correctly.
- **`import-target.ts`** — Package-to-path resolution with suffix matching and progressive prefix stripping for non-standard layouts.
- **`receiver-binding.ts`** — `this` on instance methods, `super` via `superclass` field on class declarations. Skips static methods.
- **`arity.ts` / `arity-metadata.ts`** — Varargs-aware arity compatibility with fixed-prefix count preservation, delegates to `javaMethodConfig.extractParameters`.
- **`merge-bindings.ts`** — Tier-based shadowing: local > import/namespace > wildcard.
- **`simple-hooks.ts`** — `bindingScopeFor` (return-type hoist to Module), `importOwningScope` (returns `null` unconditionally per JLS §7.5), `receiverBinding`.
- **`scope-resolver.ts`** — Wires all hooks; `fieldFallbackOnMethodLookup: false`, `isSuperReceiver: text === 'super'`.

## Wiring

- `java.ts` — Provider gains all scope-resolution hooks.
- `registry.ts` — `javaScopeResolver` registered in `SCOPE_RESOLVERS`.
- `java.test.ts` — Wrapped with `createResolverParityIt('java')` for dual-mode CI.

## Test fixtures

- **`java-wildcard-import`** — Exercises `import com.example.models.*` with two classes (`User`, `Order`) in the same package. Validates wildcard import code path and call resolution through wildcard-imported types, asserting `targetFilePath` resolves to the correct file.
- **`java-variadic-resolution`** — Extended with `Formatter.java` containing `format(int level, String... args)` to test fixed-prefix varargs arity resolution. Includes a `badCall()` method exercising the 0-arg undersupply path, documenting that arity rejection is registry-primary only.

## Bug fixes (pre-existing, unrelated to Java)

- **`worker-pool.test.ts`** — Fixed flaky test "rejects dispatch when replacement worker crashes during startup" that failed on Windows due to idle-timeout firing before crash detection. Added `idle timeout` to the expected error pattern.

## Parity

| Mode | Result |
|------|--------|
| Default | 176/176 ✅ |
| `REGISTRY_PRIMARY_JAVA=0` (legacy forced) | 176/176 ✅ |
| `REGISTRY_PRIMARY_JAVA=1` (registry forced) | 147/176 (83%) |
| Existing C#/Python/Go tests | No regressions |

**Not added to `MIGRATED_LANGUAGES`** — 29 registry-primary gaps remain (switch pattern binding, Map.values() iteration, assignment/method chains, cross-file return-type propagation, virtual dispatch, interface default methods). These are the same category of advanced-resolution gaps seen in prior migrations; parity is below the ≥99% flip threshold per RFC §6.4.

### Known flip-blockers (documented in `scope-resolver.ts` JSDoc)

- Wildcard import file selection is nondeterministic when multiple classes share a package directory
- Qualified generic type parameters in field/parameter annotations (`com.example.BaseModel<T>`) — rare but may miss resolution
- Static import edge cases with nested classes
- Varargs arity fixed-prefix 0-arg rejection (logic correct in registry mode; legacy mode does not enforce arity)

title: analyze crashes silently at 60% (Loading into LadybugDB) on Windows with Laravel PHP project
body:
**Environment:**
- OS: Windows 11
- Node: v20.18.0
- GitNexus: 1.6.3
- Project: Laravel PHP (668 files, vendor/ excluded via .gitignore)

**Steps to reproduce:**
1. cd into Laravel project root
2. Run: gitnexus analyze --verbose

**Result:**
Progress bar stops at exactly 60% at "Loading into LadybugDB..." then exits silently.
No error message. No stack trace. Exit code 0.

**Tried:**
- gitnexus analyze --verbose → same result
- gitnexus analyze --drop-embeddings → same result
- Deleted .gitnexus/ and retried → same result
- GITNEXUS_WORKER_SUB_BATCH_TIMEOUT_MS=120000 → same result

**Expected:** Full index completion

title: feat(cli): add --skip-skills and --index-only flags to analyze (resubmit of #742)
body:
Resubmit of #742 (closed) — addresses all three findings from the Claude review bot and rebases on the latest `main`.

## Summary

- `gitnexus analyze --skip-agents-md` correctly suppresses AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md, but **unconditionally injects 6 skill files** into `.claude/skills/gitnexus/` in every analyzed repo
- This PR adds two new flags:
  - `--skip-skills` — suppress standard GitNexus skill file injection
  - `--index-only` — pure index mode: skip **all** file injection (AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, skills), writing only to `.gitnexus/`

## Motivation

While bulk-indexing 176 repos with `--skip-agents-md`, all 144 indexed repos were contaminated with `.claude/skills/gitnexus/` files that had to be cleaned up manually. The `--skip-agents-md` flag name implies it controls all AI context injection, but skills bypass it entirely.

## Changes

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `src/cli/index.ts` | Add `--skip-skills` and `--index-only` CLI options |
| `src/cli/analyze.ts` | Resolve `--index-only` into both skip flags, gate `generateSkillFiles()` with `!skipAll`, pass through call chain |
| `src/core/run-analyze.ts` | Add `skipSkills` to `AnalyzeOptions`, pass to `generateAIContextFiles` |
| `src/cli/ai-context.ts` | Add `skipSkills` to `AIContextOptions`, guard `installSkills()`, omit standard-skill rows and `## CLI` heading when `skipSkills=true` |
| `test/unit/ai-context.test.ts` | +3 filesystem regression tests for `skipSkills` / `indexOnly` |

## Three levels of control

```bash
gitnexus analyze --skip-agents-md .  # suppress only AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md
gitnexus analyze --skip-skills .     # suppress only skill injection
gitnexus analyze --index-only .      # suppress everything, pure indexing
```

## Review fixes applied (vs #742)

The bot review on #742 flagged three issues — all addressed:

1. **`--index-only --skills` still wrote community skill files.** The `--skills` branch was not gated by `skipAll`. Fixed: `generateSkillFiles()` now requires `!skipAll`, so `--index-only` wins over `--skills`.
2. **`--skip-skills` without `--skip-agents-md` left dangling skill references.** AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md still pointed at `.claude/skills/gitnexus/*/SKILL.md` files that were never installed. Fixed: `generateGitNexusContent()` now takes `skipSkills` and omits the standard-skill rows (and the entire `## CLI` heading when the table is empty). Community-derived rows from `--skills` remain.
3. **No tests for `skipSkills` / `indexOnly` filesystem effects.** Added three regression tests in `test/unit/ai-context.test.ts`.

## Test plan

- [x] Default: `gitnexus analyze .` creates AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, and 6 skill dirs
- [x] `--skip-skills`: AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md created (without dangling skill refs), no `.claude/skills/gitnexus/`
- [x] `--skip-agents-md`: skills created, no AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md
- [x] `--index-only`: only `.gitnexus/` created, nothing else (verified in `test/unit/ai-context.test.ts`)
- [x] `--index-only --skills`: still nothing else — community skill generation also gated
- [x] `--skip-skills` (without `--skip-agents-md`): generated AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md does NOT reference non-existent skill files
- [x] `npx tsc --noEmit` in `gitnexus/` — passes
- [x] Prettier — passes
- [x] ESLint — 0 errors (6 pre-existing warnings on unrelated code)
- [x] Full unit suite — 5561 tests pass, 10 skipped

title: GitNexus Hook Spawns Excessive Processes (~180 instances) Causing Severe System Load
body:
### Area

gitnexus (CLI / core / indexing / MCP server)

### Summary

The GitNexus hook (`gitnexus-hook.cjs`) is being launched multiple times simultaneously, once approximately every day, causing significant system resource exhaustion. 

## Current Behavior

The process tree shows a cascade of nested shell executions launching the same GitNexus hook:

```
/bin/bash -lc node "gitnexus-hook.cjs"
  └─ /bin/sh -c /bin/bash -lc 'node "gitnexus-hook.cjs"'
      └─ /bin/bash -lc node "gitnexus-hook.cjs"
          └─ (repeats)
```

**Observed metrics:**
- **Process count:** 180+ instances of `gitnexus-hook.cjs` related processes
- **System load average:** 109.55, 57.41, 23.83 (extremely high)
- **Frequency:** Approximately once per day
- **Uptime impact:** System has been running for 7 days, 4:20

## Expected Behavior

Only one instance of the GitNexus hook should be running at any given time. The hook should execute and terminate cleanly without spawning nested processes.

## Reproduction Steps

1. Run Claude or any process that triggers the GitNexus hook
2. Monitor process tree: `ps axfu | grep nexus`
3. Observe accumulation of processes over time
4. Issue occurs approximately once daily

## Environment

- **User:** vlad
- **Hook path:** `/home/vlad/.claude/hooks/gitnexus/gitnexus-hook.cjs`
- **System:** Ubuntu (GNOME session)
- **Process pattern:** Recursive `/bin/sh` → `/bin/bash` → node execution

## Root Cause Analysis (Suspected)

The hook appears to be recursively calling itself, likely due to:
1. The hook triggering on events that cause it to re-trigger itself
2. Missing process locking mechanism (pidfile/semaphore)
3. Potential infinite loop condition triggered once daily

## Suggested Fix

1. **Implement process locking:** Use pidfile or flock to prevent multiple instances
2. **Add recursion detection:** Prevent the hook from triggering on its own operations
3. **Fix the root trigger:** Identify what causes the daily cascade and prevent the recursive spawning pattern
4. **Add timeout/circuit breaker:** Kill processes that exceed expected runtime

## Immediate Workaround

```bash
# Kill all runaway processes
pkill -f gitnexus-hook.cjs

# Temporary disable the hook
chmod -x /home/vlad/.claude/hooks/gitnexus/gitnexus-hook.cjs
```

## Additional Context

The nested execution pattern shows `sh -c` spawning `bash -lc` which spawns another `sh -c`, creating a deep process chain. This suggests the hook may be:
- Executing a command that itself invokes the hook
- Using incorrect quoting/escaping in shell commands
- Missing proper process termination handling

title: feat(mcp): add request log writer (PoC for #1351)
body:
Refs #1351.

## Summary

Wraps the `CallToolRequestSchema` handler with an `instrumented()` helper that appends one JSONL line per `tools/call` to a configurable log file:

```json
{"ts":"2026-05-10T18:00:00Z","tool":"impact","durationMs":214,"resultBytes":1834,"error":null}
```

The same wrapper can host an OTLP span emitter alongside or instead of the JSONL writer — the single seam is `src/mcp/server.ts:166`.

## Changes

- `gitnexus/src/mcp/request-log.ts` — `resolveLogPath()`, `appendRequestLog()`, `instrumented(toolName, fn, resultBytesOf?, errorOf?)`. Async append, `mkdir -p` on the parent, errors swallowed.
- `gitnexus/src/mcp/server.ts` — wraps the existing handler. Behaviour unchanged when logging is disabled. `errorOf` reads the `{ isError: true, ... }` envelope so tool errors land in the log with their message (the handler converts thrown errors into a returned envelope, so the wrapper's catch branch never sees them).
- `gitnexus/test/unit/mcp/request-log.test.ts` — 14 unit tests.

## Configuration

Opt-in default:

| `GITNEXUS_MCP_REQUEST_LOG` | Result |
|---|---|
| unset / empty | disabled |
| `off` / `false` / `0` | disabled |
| `on` / `true` / `1` | `~/.gitnexus/mcp-requests.log` |
| `/abs/path/log` | that path |

## Privacy

Tool **inputs** (`params`/`rawArgs`) are never logged. The `error` field captures error messages verbatim; tool errors routinely echo input (cypher parse errors include the offending clause, etc.). Treat the log as input-adjacent.

## Verify

```bash
cd gitnexus
npm install
npx vitest run test/unit/mcp/request-log.test.ts   # 14 pass
```

End-to-end after `npm run build`:

```bash
GITNEXUS_MCP_REQUEST_LOG=on gitnexus mcp
# drive via any MCP client, then:
cat ~/.gitnexus/mcp-requests.log
```

## Risk

- One `JSON.stringify` + one `fs.appendFile` per tool call. Fire-and-forget; the request handler returns without awaiting.
- In-flight writes can be lost on `shutdown()` — no drain in this PoC. See decision table below.
- Unbounded log size — no rotation in this PoC.
- Rollback: revert the commit. No DB, schema, or index changes; no new runtime deps.

## Recommended decisions for v1

| # | Decision | Recommendation |
|---|---|---|
| 2 | JSONL only vs JSONL + OTLP | Both. JSONL stays as the local fallback; OTLP exporter behind `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT`. Same wrapper hosts both. |
| 3 | Log tool input vs size-only | Size-only. `error` already leaks input under failure; broadening would move privacy backwards. |
| 4 | Log rotation | Daily rotation, 30-day retention, opt-out via env. Free with pino transports (see #6). |
| 5 | Drain on `shutdown()` | Yes — `await Promise.allSettled(pending)` before `server.close()`. Cheap and bounded. |
| 6 | Hand-rolled `appendFile` vs `core/logger.ts` (pino) | Refactor to pino. `createLogger('mcp-requests', { ... })` gives NDJSON, log-injection hardening, and the existing test seam. |

## One open question

**Opt-in or opt-out default?** Opt-in maximises privacy posture; opt-out gives server-side ground truth without setup. Both are one line in `resolveLogPath()`. Maintainer's call.

Draft until that decision lands and we scope whether #2/#4/#5/#6 ship in this PR or as follow-ups.

---

Local CI:

- `npx vitest run test/unit/mcp/request-log.test.ts` — 14 pass.
- `npx tsc --noEmit` — clean on the changed files (baseline has unrelated tree-sitter errors from `--ignore-scripts` install).
- `.husky/pre-commit` not run locally; please verify in CI.

title: Multi-instance support: kuzu RW lock prevents running gitnexus MCP in >1 Claude Code instance concurrently
body:
## Problem

Running Claude Code in multiple terminals against the same indexed repo causes
gitnexus MCP tool calls to fail in all but one instance. Each Claude spawns its
own MCP server → its own gitnexus process → each tries to open the kuzu
database RW. Kuzu holds a process-exclusive file lock for the lifetime of the
RW `Database` handle, so the losers either fall back to read-only (and then
fail on the FTS-ensure-on-startup write) or error outright.

Symptom: in 2 of 3 Claude instances, every tool call (`query`, `context`,
`impact`, etc.) errors with a kuzu lock / read-only-mode message. Reindexing
doesn't help — same race on next startup.

## Environment

- macOS (Darwin 25.3.0)
- gitnexus via `npx gitnexus` MCP
- 3 concurrent Claude Code instances on the same repo

title: gitnexus_query crashes via MCP with "bm25Results is not iterable" — FTS5 extension unavailable in MCP process
body:
## Summary

`gitnexus_query` crashes when invoked through the MCP server with `Error: bm25Results is not iterable`. The same query, run through the CLI on the same machine and same index, returns results successfully. This points to FTS5 being unavailable specifically in the MCP server's SQLite context.

The hook log emitted before each MCP tool call confirms it:

```
GitNexus: FTS extension unavailable; continuing without FTS features. load-only policy: extension not pre-installed
```

So the warning is correctly surfaced, but the downstream code in `query` doesn't guard against the FTS-disabled path — `bm25Results` ends up `undefined` and the result-fusion step tries to iterate it.

## Environment

- gitnexus: **1.6.4** (also reproduced on 1.6.2 before upgrading)
- Node: v25.9.0
- macOS, arm64

## Reproduction

1. `npx gitnexus analyze --force` (succeeds, all symbols indexed)
2. From a Claude Code session with the gitnexus MCP server connected, invoke `mcp__gitnexus__query` with any query string and an explicit `repo` parameter.
3. Crash: `Error: bm25Results is not iterable`

## Comparison: CLI works, MCP doesn't

Same machine, same install, same index:

```bash
$ npx gitnexus query "any query string" --repo my-repo
# returns JSON with definitions[] populated, processes[] empty — no crash
```

vs.

```
mcp__gitnexus__query({ query: "any query string", repo: "my-repo" })
# Error: bm25Results is not iterable
```

## What still works through MCP

These all work fine (no FTS dependency):
- `gitnexus_context`
- `gitnexus_impact`
- Resource reads: `gitnexus://repo/{name}/clusters`, `/processes`, `/process/{name}`, `/context`

So the bug is isolated to the BM25 hybrid-ranking path inside `query`.

## Likely fix

Either:
1. Guard the result-fusion code so a missing `bm25Results` falls back to semantic-only / definitions-only ranking instead of crashing, or
2. Make FTS5 a hard requirement and fail loudly at MCP server startup with a clear message, instead of warning and then crashing on first query.

Option 1 is preferable since FTS5 may be genuinely unavailable in some sandboxed contexts (the "load-only policy: extension not pre-installed" warning in the MCP process suggests this is what's happening).

Happy to test a patch.

title: feat(mcp): OTel metrics with Prometheus exporter (PoC for #1351)
body:
## Summary

Adds OpenTelemetry metrics with a Prometheus exporter to the MCP server. Exposes \`/metrics\` so operators have server-side ground truth for tool utilization, latency, error rate, and payload size — answering the PoC ask in #1351.

## Motivation / context

Closes #1351. The suggestion in the issue thread was to publish metrics in OpenTelemetry format and send them anonymously to Prometheus in a quantized format. This PR implements that directly: real OTel meter instruments, Prometheus pull exporter, explicit-bucket histograms, no per-call identifiers.

## Areas touched

- [x] \`gitnexus/\` (CLI / core / MCP server)
- [ ] \`gitnexus-web/\`
- [ ] \`.github/\`
- [ ] \`eval/\` or other tooling
- [ ] Docs / agent config only

## Scope & constraints

**In scope**

- New module \`src/mcp/metrics.ts\`: \`initMetrics()\`, \`observe()\`, \`shutdownMetrics()\`.
- Wraps the MCP \`CallToolRequestSchema\` handler in \`observe()\` so every tool call records one counter + two histograms + an in-flight gauge.
- Prometheus exporter on \`/metrics\` (default \`127.0.0.1:9464\`), configured to suppress \`target_info\` and \`otel_scope_info\` so the only label keys emitted are \`tool\`, \`error\`, \`le\`.
- Opt-in via \`GITNEXUS_OTEL_METRICS=on\`. Initialized in both \`gitnexus mcp\` (stdio) and \`gitnexus serve\` (HTTP). Metrics failure never crashes the server.
- 11 unit tests including a privacy invariant that asserts a synthetic cypher parse error containing attacker input does not appear in the \`/metrics\` scrape.

**Explicitly out of scope / not done here**

- OTel tracing spans / log correlation / exemplars.
- OTLP push exporter — Prometheus pull is the canonical Prom pattern; OTLP can be added later behind the same \`observe()\` seam.
- Per-call attribution / structured request log. OTel metrics aggregate by design.
- Removal of \`src/mcp/request-log.ts\` JSONL log. Independent code path; left untouched.
- Grafana dashboard JSON / Prom recording rules.
- Authentication on \`/metrics\`. Default \`127.0.0.1\` bind is the v1 stance; reverse-proxy is the operator's responsibility.

## Implementation notes

**Privacy is type-enforced.** \`observe()\` accepts \`(result) => boolean\` for the error detector — never a message string. Error messages echo user input (cypher parse errors include the offending clause) and would be an anonymity leak if recorded. The \`error\` label is the boolean's serialization.

**Instruments under meter \`gitnexus.mcp\`:**

| Instrument | Type | Labels |
|---|---|---|
| \`gitnexus_mcp_tool_requests_total\` | Counter | \`tool\`, \`error\` |
| \`gitnexus_mcp_tool_request_duration_seconds\` | Histogram | \`tool\`, \`error\` |
| \`gitnexus_mcp_tool_result_bytes\` | Histogram | \`tool\` |
| \`gitnexus_mcp_tool_inflight\` | UpDownCounter | \`tool\` |

**Bucket boundaries** (one-shot decisions — these become a dashboard contract once scraped):

- Duration: \`[0.001, 0.005, 0.025, 0.1, 0.5, 2.5, 10, 30]\` seconds. Covers in-memory cache hits (1–30 ms) up to long \`impact\` / \`detect_changes\` walks.
- Result size: \`[512, 2048, 8192, 32768, 131072, 524288, 2097152]\` bytes. Modal \`context\` / \`route_map\` payloads (2–8 KB) straddle the 2 KB / 8 KB boundary.

**Configuration:**

| Env | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| \`GITNEXUS_OTEL_METRICS\` | unset (= off) | Master switch. \`on\` / \`true\` / \`1\` enables. |
| \`GITNEXUS_OTEL_METRICS_PORT\` | \`9464\` | OTel JS Prometheus default. |
| \`GITNEXUS_OTEL_METRICS_HOST\` | \`127.0.0.1\` | Loopback only; operators must opt into wider exposure. |
| \`GITNEXUS_OTEL_METRICS_ENDPOINT\` | \`/metrics\` | |

**Stdio note:** every agent host spawns its own MCP stdio process, so per-process ports are operationally useless for scraping. \`gitnexus serve\` is the supported scrape target — stdio mode can opt in for local development but defaults off like everything else.

## Testing & verification

- [x] \`cd gitnexus && npx vitest run test/unit/mcp/metrics.test.ts\` — 11 pass.
- [x] \`cd gitnexus && npx tsc --noEmit\` — clean.
- [x] \`cd gitnexus && npm run build\` — succeeds.
- [ ] \`cd gitnexus && npm run test:integration\` — not exercised locally (native binding rebuild skipped in my install); CI will run.

End-to-end smoke:

\`\`\`bash
cd gitnexus && npm run build
GITNEXUS_OTEL_METRICS=on gitnexus serve
# from another shell:
curl -s http://127.0.0.1:9464/metrics | grep gitnexus_mcp_
\`\`\`

## Risk & rollout

- **Default off.** No behavior change for existing users until they set \`GITNEXUS_OTEL_METRICS=on\`.
- **Metrics failure cannot crash the server.** Init catches all errors and logs a warning; missing port, \`EADDRINUSE\`, or SDK init failure all degrade gracefully.
- **Bucket boundaries are publish-once.** Recutting after dashboards exist is a breaking change for operators; the boundaries here are intentionally coarse.
- **Rollback:** revert the commit. No DB, schema, index, or migration changes; no new runtime deps for users who don't opt in.

## Checklist

- [x] PR body meets repo minimum length
- [ ] \`AGENTS.md\` / overlays changed — N/A
- [x] No secrets, tokens, or machine-specific paths committed

title: Claude plugin: PreToolUse augment competes with MCP server for .gitnexus/lbug lock
body:
## Summary

The Claude Code plugin appears to auto-install two GitNexus integration paths that can access the same repo database from separate processes:

1. A long-lived MCP server from `gitnexus-claude-plugin/.mcp.json`:
   ```json
   {
     "mcpServers": {
       "gitnexus": {
         "command": "npx",
         "args": ["-y", "gitnexus@latest", "mcp"]
       }
     }
   }
   ```

2. A Claude `PreToolUse` hook from `gitnexus-claude-plugin/hooks/hooks.json`:
   ```json
   {
     "hooks": {
       "PreToolUse": [
         {
           "matcher": "Grep |Glob|Bash",
           "hooks": [
             {
               "type": "command",
               "command": "node ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/hooks/gitnexus-hook.js",
               "timeout": 10,
               "statusMessage": "Enriching with GitNexus graph context..."
             }
           ]
         }
       ]
     }
   }
   ```

The PreToolUse hook calls `gitnexus augment -- <pattern>`, which opens/uses the same `.gitnexus/lbug` index as the already-running MCP server. In practice this intermittently emits LadybugDB/FTS lock warnings when normal Claude Code tool use triggers the augment hook while MCP is active.

This looks distinct from, but related to, existing lock/FTS reports:

- #1488 tracks multiple Claude Code instances each starting their own MCP server.
- #1449 / #1216 track FTS/read-only/lazy-creation problems and lock-related symptoms.
- This issue is about a **single Claude Code/plugin installation** where the plugin itself installs both MCP and a separate short-lived augment CLI subprocess that can compete with the MCP server for the same repo DB.

## Environment

- OS: macOS arm64
  - `Darwin 25.4.0 ... RELEASE_ARM64_T6031 arm64`
- Node: `v22.22.1`
- Local GitNexus CLI: `1.6.4-rc.112`
- Claude plugin repo files inspected from `abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus`:
  - `gitnexus-claude-plugin/.mcp.json`
  - `gitnexus-claude-plugin/hooks/hooks.json`
  - `gitnexus-claude-plugin/hooks/gitnexus-hook.js`
  - `gitnexus/src/cli/augment.ts`
  - `gitnexus/src/core/augmentation/engine.ts`

## Observed warning

During Claude Code work in an indexed repository, the hook intermittently emits warnings like:

```text
GitNexus: FTS extension load failed: IO exception: Could not set lock on file : <repo>/.gitnexus/lbug
```

and then per-table FTS ensure/load warnings for tables such as:

```text
File
Function
Class
Method
Interface
```

The exact symptom happened during a normal Claude Code workflow where GitNexus MCP tools themselves were still usable. `detect_changes`, `query`, `context`, and `impact` could complete, but the Claude hook path still printed lock warnings when Bash/Grep/Glob-like activity triggered augmentation.

## Current evidence

While reproducing the warning, the repo DB file was held by the active MCP server process:

```text
lsof -nP <repo>/.gitnexus/lbug
# showed a node process running gitnexus mcp holding the lbug database
```

Process shape:

```text
node .../node_modules/.bin/gitnexus mcp
```

The warning occurred when a Claude Code Bash/Grep/Glob-style tool invocation triggered the GitNexus PreToolUse hook, whose implementation runs:

```js
runGitNexusCli(['augment', '--', pattern], cwd, 7000)
```

from `gitnexus-claude-plugin/hooks/gitnexus-hook.js`.

That command eventually reaches:

```ts
augment(pattern, process.cwd())
```

from `gitnexus/src/cli/augment.ts`, and `augment()` lazy-loads the lbug/pool/search path in `gitnexus/src/core/augmentation/engine.ts`:

```ts
const { initLbug, executeQuery, isLbugReady } = await import('../lbug/pool-adapter.js');
const { searchFTSFromLbug } = await import('../search/bm25-index.js');

if (!isLbugReady(repoId)) {
  await initLbug(repoId, repo.lbugPath);
}

const { results: bm25Results } = await searchFTSFromLbug(pattern, 10, repoId);
```

So, from a Claude Code session with the GitNexus plugin active, there can be two independent GitNexus processes touching the same `<repo>/.gitnexus/lbug` file:

```text
long-lived process:
  npx -y gitnexus@latest mcp
  -> owns/uses <repo>/.gitnexus/lbug

short-lived hook process:
  gitnexus augment -- <pattern>
  -> opens/uses/ensures FTS against <repo>/.gitnexus/lbug
```

## Why this seems plugin-specific

The repo's auto-installed Claude plugin includes both:

- MCP server startup (`.mcp.json`), and
- a PreToolUse hook that shells out to a separate GitNexus CLI process (`hooks/hooks.json` + `hooks/gitnexus-hook.js`).

This means a user can hit lock warnings without intentionally running multiple GitNexus commands or multiple Claude Code instances. Normal Claude Code tool usage is enough:

1. Claude Code starts/uses the GitNexus MCP server.
2. User/agent runs a Bash/Grep/Glob command that the hook recognizes as search-like.
3. The PreToolUse hook starts `gitnexus augment` in a separate process.
4. The augment process touches the same LadybugDB file already in use by MCP.
5. Intermittent `Could not set lock on file : <repo>/.gitnexus/lbug` / FTS warnings appear.

## Expected behavior

If the Claude plugin installs both MCP and search augmentation, they should not compete for exclusive DB access.

Expected outcomes could be any of:

- `gitnexus augment` uses the already-running MCP/server process instead of opening the DB independently.
- The PreToolUse hook detects an active MCP/lbug lock holder and skips augmentation cleanly.
- The augment path opens the DB in a mode that is safe alongside the MCP process, and does not attempt schema/FTS mutation when unsafe.
- The plugin disables PreToolUse augmentation automatically when MCP is configured/active.
- At minimum, the hook emits a clear non-noisy message explaining that augmentation was skipped because another GitNexus process owns the DB.

## Actual behavior

The MCP server can be active and healthy, but the separate hook subprocess can still emit lock/FTS warnings when it runs `gitnexus augment`.

This creates noise and makes it hard to distinguish real GitNexus failures from hook-side opportunistic augmentation failures. It also appears to be the same underlying DB-concurrency class as other open/closed lock issues, but with a specific auto-installed-plugin trigger.

## Reproduction outline

A minimal reproduction should be possible with one indexed repo and one Claude Code session:

1. Install/enable the GitNexus Claude plugin so both `.mcp.json` and `hooks/hooks.json` are active.
2. Open Claude Code in an indexed repo with `.gitnexus/lbug` present.
3. Let the GitNexus MCP server start.
4. Run a search-like Bash command that the hook will parse, for example a command containing `rg` or `grep` with a pattern of at least 3 characters.
5. Observe the PreToolUse hook running `gitnexus augment -- <pattern>`.
6. If the MCP server currently owns/uses the DB, the hook can emit:
   ```text
   GitNexus: FTS extension load failed: IO exception: Could not set lock on file : <repo>/.gitnexus/lbug
   ```
7. Confirm lock holder with:
   ```bash
   lsof -nP <repo>/.gitnexus/lbug
   ps -p <pid> -o pid,ppid,stat,etime,command
   ```
   In the observed case, the lock holder was the active `gitnexus mcp` node process.

## Suggested fixes

### Option A: Route augmentation through MCP

If an MCP server is configured/active, have the hook ask that server for augmentation/search context instead of spawning a new independent `gitnexus augment` process that opens the DB again.

### Option B: Hook-level lock/owner guard

Before running `gitnexus augment`, check whether `<repo>/.gitnexus/lbug` is already locked/owned by an MCP/server process. If yes, skip augmentation gracefully.

Pseudo-behavior:

```text
if repo DB is locked by gitnexus mcp/serve:
  return no augmentation context
else:
  run gitnexus augment -- <pattern>
```

The key is to avoid printing scary FTS/lbug warnings for an opportunistic augmentation path.

### Option C: Make augment read-only and no-mutation-safe

Ensure the augment path never tries to create/ensure/load FTS in a way that requires exclusive access while another process owns the DB. If FTS is unavailable or unsafe, return graph-only or no augmentation instead of warning repeatedly.

### Option D: Plugin config opt-out

Expose a plugin setting or default behavior such as:

```text
GITNEXUS_DISABLE_PRETOOL_AUGMENT_WHEN_MCP=1
```

or make the Claude plugin choose one integration mode by default:

- MCP-only, or
- hook-only,

rather than both independently touching the database.

## Impact

- Users get intermittent GitNexus warnings during normal Claude Code workflows.
- The warnings are confusing because MCP tools can still work while the hook path fails.
- Automated workflows that treat GitNexus warnings as UAT/process deviations may flag otherwise successful runs.
- It encourages users to loosen unrelated hooks/workflow checks even though the issue is GitNexus plugin integration concurrency.

## Related issues

- #1488 — similar database-lock class, but caused by multiple Claude Code instances / multiple MCP servers.
- #1449 — FTS lazy/read-only issue; fixed in 1.6.4 according to the issue, but this report concerns a separate `mcp` + `augment` process competition path.
- #1216 — broader FTS/query/locking report; closed as fixed in 1.6.4, but comments mention MCP concurrency cases.
- #325 — older serve/CLI coexistence lock report.

title: fix(wiki): cap graph reference fields to prevent prompt overflow
body:
## Summary

`generateLeafPage` truncates `SOURCE_CODE` to `maxTokensPerModule` (30K default) before assembling the `MODULE_USER_PROMPT`, but `INTRA_CALLS` / `OUTGOING_CALLS` / `INCOMING_CALLS` / `PROCESSES` are passed in uncapped. In clusters with many cross-references the graph reference data alone can re-explode the assembled prompt past the model's input context (or trigger the output `max_completion_tokens` cap on smaller models like `gemini-2.5-flash`'s 8K output limit), causing deterministic module-generation failures even with `--force`.

## Repro

`gitnexus analyze` + `gitnexus wiki --force` on `browser-use/browser-harness` (111 files / 20 clusters):

| Model | duration | pages | failed modules |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| `gemini-2.5-flash --concurrency 1` | 740.9s | 19 | "Project Documentation", "Browser Interaction Skills" |
| `gpt-5-chat-latest --concurrency 1` | 2804.4s | 18 | "Project Documentation", "Browser Interaction Skills", "E-commerce & Marketplace Skills" |

Same 2 modules fail across models — pointing to graph-level prompt content rather than model choice or `AbortSignal.timeout`. `SOURCE_CODE` truncation alone is insufficient when the cluster has dense cross-references.

## Fix

1. Extract a generic `truncateText(text, maxTokens, label)` helper from `truncateSource` (keeps the existing source-truncation notice readable while letting other fields reuse the budget logic with their own labels).
2. Add `DEFAULT_GRAPH_FIELD_BUDGET = 5_000` (≈1/6 of the default module budget — gives 4 graph fields combined ≈ 2/3 of `SOURCE_CODE`'s budget).
3. Cap each of `INTRA_CALLS` / `OUTGOING_CALLS` / `INCOMING_CALLS` / `PROCESSES` independently in `generateLeafPage` before `fillTemplate`.

## Test plan

- [x] `npx tsc --noEmit src/core/wiki/generator.ts` — clean (no new errors)
- [x] `npx vitest run test/unit/wiki` — 51/51 existing wiki unit tests pass unchanged
- [ ] End-to-end rerun of the failing wiki on a large cluster (reporter has not validated on the original failing modules; happy to add a regression test if maintainer suggests a fixture)

## Notes

- The new constant is sized as a sensible default; a follow-up could expose it as `graphFieldBudget?` in `GeneratorOptions` if maintainers want per-call override (kept minimal here).
- Truncation message format mirrors the existing `'... (source truncated for context window limits)'` style — label-aware for clarity in generated docs.

title: eval-server: add POST /reindex endpoint to make incremental indexing usable for daemon consumers
body:
## Context

PR #1479 (`feat/incremental-indexing`) adds parse-cache + DB writeback + scope-res short-circuit for the `gitnexus analyze` CLI. This is a great speedup for one-shot CLI use cases (~30s → ~2-5s on a 60K-symbol repo with few changes).

## Gap

The `gitnexus eval-server` HTTP daemon doesn't expose any reindex endpoint:

- `POST /tool/:name` — agent tool calls (read-only over the warm LadybugDB)
- `GET /health`
- `POST /shutdown`

It opens an existing LadybugDB and serves queries; it has no way to react to on-disk file changes. So when a repo updates, daemon consumers have two bad options:

1. **Shutdown + restart** — kills warm caches, breaks active connections, loses requests in flight
2. **Spawn `gitnexus analyze` subprocess + restart eval-server** — what we currently do downstream; same problem

In both cases, the parse-cache from #1479 is on disk, but the daemon doesn't load the new index without a full restart.

## Proposal

Add to `gitnexus/src/cli/eval-server.ts`:

```
POST /reindex
  body: { repo: string, force?: boolean }
  response: { duration_ms, files_parsed, files_skipped, status }
```

Calls `runFullAnalysis` (in-process, same module already imported) with `incremental` flag, then atomically swaps the LadybugDB handle in `LocalBackend`. Reads remain served from the old handle until the swap; new reads see the new handle.

## Why this matters

Our use case: long-lived container, multiple repos (~80K total symbols), continuous `git pull` from upstream, downstream surfaces query the eval-server constantly. We currently subprocess-fork the CLI and bounce eval-server every reindex — the parse-cache wins from #1479 are mostly cancelled by the bounce overhead and the lost warm caches.

A daemon-side /reindex makes #1479 land for ALL consumers, not just CLI one-shots.

## Happy to PR if there's interest

We have eval-server experience from running it in production for a couple of months. If the design above is acceptable, we'll open a PR against `feat/incremental-indexing` with the endpoint + tests + docs.

Refs: #1479, #592 (closed; we're tracking this thread instead)

title: feat(php): migrate PHP to scope-based resolution model (#938) [supersedes #1124]
body:
## Summary

This PR supersedes #1124 (stale, conflicting with main). Rebased cleanly onto current `origin/main` (10+ commits ahead of the original merge-base), preserving all new hooks added by Go (#1302), range-binding, and structural-interface rings.

**RFC #909 Ring 3 LANG-php** — third language migrated to the scope-based resolver pipeline after Python and C#.

### What's in this PR

**PHP module** (`gitnexus/src/core/ingestion/languages/php/`): 13 new files
- `scope-resolver.ts` — `ScopeResolver` implementation: PHP MRO with trait-use via IMPLEMENTS edges, namespace-sibling population, arity compatibility, merge-binding strategy, `allowGlobalFreeCallFallback` for unimported same-namespace calls
- `query.ts` — tree-sitter-php patterns for all PHP constructs (classes, traits, interfaces, enums, namespaces, use/use function/use const, member/free/nullsafe/static calls, PHPDoc)
- `captures.ts` — `emitPhpScopeCaptures`: import decomposition, receiver-binding synthesis, arity metadata, PHPDoc extraction
- `interpret.ts` — `interpretPhpImport` / `interpretPhpTypeBinding`
- `import-decomposer.ts` — 1:N decomposer for all `use` declaration forms including grouped `use Foo\{A, B as C}`
- `import-target.ts` — PSR-4 + `composer.json` resolution adapter
- `namespace-siblings.ts` — cross-file same-namespace visibility (mirrors C# implementation)
- `arity-metadata.ts`, `arity.ts` — PHP arity computation and `arityCompatibility`
- `merge-bindings.ts` — binding precedence: local > import/namespace > wildcard
- `receiver-binding.ts` — `$this` / `parent` type-binding synthesis
- `simple-hooks.ts` — `bindingScopeFor` hoisting for return types and constructor-promoted properties
- `cache-stats.ts` — tree-sitter parse cache metrics

**Registry wiring** (2 files, minimal):
- `pipeline/registry.ts` — adds `phpScopeResolver` alongside existing Go/Python/C#/TS entries
- `registry-primary-flag.ts` — adds PHP to `MIGRATED_LANGUAGES`

**Shared pipeline improvements** (PHP-motivated, safe for all languages):
- `graph-bridge/node-lookup.ts` — adds `'Trait'` to `isLinkableLabel` so PHP (and Rust) MRO builders can bridge trait defs to graph node IDs via IMPLEMENTS edges; Go is unaffected
- `passes/free-call-fallback.ts` — adds arity-narrowing to `pickUniqueGlobalCallable`: when multiple global candidates share a name, narrows by `parameterCount`/`requiredParameterCount` before giving up; fixes registry-primary languages where the semantic model is not populated by the legacy call-processor

### P0 staleness fix (Kieran review finding)

The original PR #1124 deleted 6 hooks from `ScopeResolver` that were added on main by Go (#1302) and other rings (`expandsWildcardTo`, `populateWorkspaceOwners`, `detectInterfaceImplementations`, `mirrorNamespaceTypeBindings`, `populateRangeBindings`, `allowGlobalFreeCallFallback`). This PR restores all shared-pipeline files to `origin/main` and applies PHP changes on top.

### Known limitation (follow-up)

`save($entity: mixed)->getId()` — member calls on `mixed`-typed parameters have no TypeRef in scope and cannot be resolved by the current contract. The stale PR used a non-contract `emitUnresolvedReceiverEdges` hook. The 1 affected test is skipped in registry-primary mode with a comment; a `postResolutionFallback` contract hook is tracked as a follow-up to RFC #909 Ring 3.

## Test results

| Suite | Flag=1 (scope-resolver) | Flag=0 (legacy) |
|-------|------------------------|-----------------|
| PHP | 159/160 passed, 1 skipped | 160/160 passed |
| C# | 788/788 | — |
| Python | included above | — |
| TypeScript | included above | — |
| Go | included above | — |
| Typecheck | clean (`npx tsc --noEmit`) | — |

Go resolver tests are fully green — no regressions from the shared pipeline changes.

## Files changed

20 files: 13 new PHP module files, `php.ts` (modified), `registry.ts`, `registry-primary-flag.ts`, `node-lookup.ts`, `free-call-fallback.ts`, `php.test.ts`.

Closes #938 (RFC #909 Ring 3 LANG-php)

title: feat(embeddings): forward dimensions param in HTTP embedding requests
body:
## Summary

Forward GITNEXUS_EMBEDDING_DIMS as the dimensions field in the /v1/embeddings HTTP request body, enabling Matryoshka-capable models to return truncated vectors at the requested size.

## Motivation / context

Models like OpenAI text-embedding-3-large (3072d native) support returning lower-dimensional vectors via the dimensions request parameter. Previously, GitNexus only used GITNEXUS_EMBEDDING_DIMS for local validation of the returned vector length — it was never sent to the endpoint. This meant users could not leverage Matryoshka truncation (e.g. requesting 1024d from a 3072d model) and would get a dimension-mismatch error instead.

## Areas touched

- [x] gitnexus/ (CLI / core / MCP server)

## Scope and constraints

**In scope**

- Pass dimensions in the request body when GITNEXUS_EMBEDDING_DIMS is explicitly set
- Omit the field entirely when unset (preserves backward compatibility for backends that reject unknown fields)
- Unit tests for both paths (batch + single-query, with/without dimensions)

**Explicitly out of scope / not done here**

- No changes to local ONNX embedding path (only HTTP path affected)
- No changes to dimension validation logic (still checks returned vector matches expected)

## Implementation notes

- httpEmbedBatch gains an optional dimensions?: number parameter
- Request body is conditionally extended: { input, model } or { input, model, dimensions }
- Both httpEmbed (batch) and httpEmbedQuery (single) forward config.dimensions
- Compatible with OpenAI, Cohere embed-v3, Voyage, and any endpoint that either supports or ignores the dimensions field

## Testing and verification

- [x] cd gitnexus && npx tsc --noEmit (pass)
- [ ] cd gitnexus && npm test (onnxruntime native binding incompatible with macOS 12.2.1 locally — CI will validate)

4 new unit tests added:
1. omits dimensions from request body when GITNEXUS_EMBEDDING_DIMS is unset
2. forwards GITNEXUS_EMBEDDING_DIMS as dimensions in request body
3. forwards dimensions on the single-query path
4. Existing sends correct request payload test unchanged (validates baseline)

## Risk and rollout

- No breaking change: when GITNEXUS_EMBEDDING_DIMS is unset, request body is identical to before
- Users who set GITNEXUS_EMBEDDING_DIMS with a Matryoshka-capable model will now get correct truncated vectors instead of a dimension-mismatch error
- Users with endpoints that reject unknown fields should leave GITNEXUS_EMBEDDING_DIMS unset (existing behavior preserved)

## Checklist

- [x] PR body meets repo minimum length
- [x] No secrets, tokens, or machine-specific paths committed

title: <namespace>.method()` resolved as a free function across packages
body:
## Issue 1 — `<namespace>.method()` resolved as a free function across packages

### Summary

A method call on an imported namespace (`z.record(...)` from `zod`) produced a `CALLS` edge to an unrelated free function named `record` in a different workspace package. The resolver appears to drop the namespace prefix and then match the bare method name against the global symbol table.

### Repro

Source in `backend/src/routes/skills.ts`:

```ts
import { z } from "zod";

const RunBody = z.object({
  slug: z.string(),
  tool: z.string().optional(),
  args: z.record(z.unknown()).optional(),   // ← this call
  ...
});
```

There is no free `record` function in the backend. The only `record` symbol in the repo is in the browser-extension content script:

```
extension/src/content/recorder/captureActions.ts:45:function record(action: CapturedAction) {
```

That file is bundled into a Chrome content script and cannot be called from Node/Fastify code.

### What gitnexus produced

```bash
$ gitnexus cypher 'MATCH (caller)-[:CodeRelation {type: "CALLS"}]->(target)
  WHERE caller.filePath STARTS WITH "backend/"
    AND target.filePath STARTS WITH "extension/"
  RETURN caller.name AS caller, caller.filePath AS from,
         target.name AS calls, target.filePath AS to'
```

```
| caller    | from                          | calls  | to                                                  |
| skills.ts | backend/src/routes/skills.ts  | record | extension/src/content/recorder/captureActions.ts    |
```

This is the only spurious cross-package edge in the repo (extension→backend direction has zero false edges, which is correct — that boundary is HTTP).

### Expected behavior

One of:
1. No CALLS edge at all (the method receiver is an imported namespace from a `node_modules` package; the resolver does not have semantic info for it).
2. An edge to the `zod` module's `record` export — but that target isn't indexed, so option 1 is the safe choice.

Either way, the resolver should not drop the receiver and match the bare method name against global symbols, especially when crossing workspace package boundaries.

### Persistence

Reproduces after `gitnexus analyze --force`. The edge survives reindex.

### Why this matters

- Pollutes `gitnexus impact` for both endpoints. Renaming the extension's `record()` would falsely flag a Fastify route handler as affected, and vice versa.
- Specifically breaks cross-package safety analysis, which is the exact case where you most need the index to be precise.

### Suggested fix direction

When a call expression's callee is a `MemberExpression` whose object is an `Identifier` bound to an import from an unresolved (typically `node_modules`) module, do not fall back to matching the property name against the global function table. Either emit no edge, or emit an "external" edge whose target is the import source.

title: Full-text search indexes fail to build (read-only Kuzu connection)
body:
## Issue 2 — Full-text search indexes fail to build (read-only Kuzu connection)

### Summary

Every query against the indexed repo prints a warning that the FTS indexes could not be created because the Kuzu connection is read-only. As a result, the text-search path (`gitnexus query "..."`) silently returns empty results, even for symbols that obviously exist in the graph.

### What gitnexus produced

Every tool invocation (`gitnexus cypher`, `gitnexus context`, `gitnexus impact`, `gitnexus query`) prints:

```
[gitnexus] FTS index ensure failed for repo "<repo>" table "File" (index "file_fts"):
  Connection exception: Cannot execute write operations in a read-only database!. Will retry on next query.
[gitnexus] FTS index ensure failed ... table "Function" (index "function_fts"): ...
[gitnexus] FTS index ensure failed ... table "Class" (index "class_fts"): ...
[gitnexus] FTS index ensure failed ... table "Method" (index "method_fts"): ...
[gitnexus] FTS index ensure failed ... table "Interface" (index "interface_fts"): ...
```

`gitnexus query` then returns empty:

```bash
$ gitnexus query "RunSkill" --content
{
  "processes": [],
  "process_symbols": [],
  "definitions": [],
  ...
}
```

The process named `RunSkill → SplitTopLevel` is present in the graph (visible via cypher), so the empty result is a search-path failure, not missing data.

### Expected behavior

Either:
1. FTS indexes are created at analyze time using the writable connection that wrote everything else, and runtime read-only connections just query them.
2. If FTS creation is genuinely deferred to first read, the runtime should open a writable connection for the one-shot setup, then downgrade to read-only.

The current state — emitting a "will retry on next query" warning that never succeeds — is the worst of both: noisy logs, silently broken text search.

### Impact

- Workflow noise: 5 warnings printed on every tool invocation.
- `gitnexus query` is unusable until the FTS issue is resolved. Workaround is `cypher` + `context` + `impact`, which all worked fine.

title: Docker runtime image misses install-duckdb-extension.mjs, causing FTS installer MODULE_NOT_FOUND
body:
Title: Docker runtime image misses install-duckdb-extension.mjs, causing FTS installer MODULE_NOT_FOUND

Summary
- The Docker runtime image does not contain `gitnexus/scripts/install-duckdb-extension.mjs`.
- During `analyze`, FTS installation attempts call this script and fail with:
  `Error: Cannot find module '/app/gitnexus/scripts/install-duckdb-extension.mjs'`

Repro
1. Pull and run the official image:
   `docker run --rm -e GITNEXUS_HOME=/tmp/gitnexus-home -v <repo>:/repo ghcr.io/abhigyanpatwari/gitnexus:latest node gitnexus/dist/cli/index.js analyze /repo --skip-agents-md`
2. Observe warning/error:
   `GitNexus: FTS extension unavailable... Cannot find module '/app/gitnexus/scripts/install-duckdb-extension.mjs'`
3. Inspect image filesystem:
   `docker run --rm ghcr.io/abhigyanpatwari/gitnexus:latest sh -lc "ls -la /app/gitnexus; ls -la /app/gitnexus/scripts || true"`
4. `scripts` directory is missing in runtime image.

Root cause
- `gitnexus/src/core/lbug/extension-loader.ts` resolves and executes:
  `../../../scripts/install-duckdb-extension.mjs`
- But `Dockerfile.cli` runtime stage copies only:
  `dist`, `node_modules`, `package.json`, `vendor`
  and does not copy `scripts`.

Suggested fix (minimal)
In `Dockerfile.cli` runtime stage, add:

```dockerfile
COPY --from=builder --chown=node:node /app/gitnexus/scripts/install-duckdb-extension.mjs ./gitnexus/scripts/install-duckdb-extension.mjs
```

Alternative
- Copy the whole scripts directory if preferred:
  `COPY --from=builder --chown=node:node /app/gitnexus/scripts ./gitnexus/scripts`

Expected result
- `analyze` no longer raises `MODULE_NOT_FOUND` for `install-duckdb-extension.mjs`.
- FTS extension installation path works as designed when network/runtime permits.

title: fix(docker): include DuckDB extension installer script in runtime image
body:
Title: fix(docker): include DuckDB extension installer script in runtime image

What
- Include `gitnexus/scripts/install-duckdb-extension.mjs` in Docker runtime image.

Why
- Runtime code in `gitnexus/src/core/lbug/extension-loader.ts` executes this script when trying to install optional DuckDB extensions (FTS path).

@@

+COPY --from=builder --chown=node:node /app/gitnexus/scripts/install-duckdb-extension.mjs ./gitnexus/scripts/install-duckdb-extension.mjs

Validation

- Run:
  `node gitnexus/dist/cli/index.js analyze /repo`

- This keeps image change minimal while preserving current extension-loader behavior.

title: TypeScript  extension imports fail to resolve call edges
body:
GitNexus fails to track caller/callee relationships when TypeScript files use `.js` extensions in ESM imports.

## Repro Steps

1. Clone a TypeScript ESM repo that uses `.js` extensions in imports, e.g.:
   ```bash
   git clone https://github.com/anthropics/lossless-claw-enhanced.git
   cd lossless-claw-enhanced
   ```
2. Index it:
   ```bash
   gitnexus analyze
   ```
3. Query impact for a function imported with `.js` extension:
   ```bash
   gitnexus impact --repo lossless-claw-enhanced estimateTokens
   ```
4. Observe 0 callers returned.
5. Verify with grep that callers exist:
   ```bash
   grep -r 'estimateTokens' src/ --include='*.ts'
   ```
   Output shows 6+ files calling the function.

## Expected
`impact` / `context` shows callers from `assembler.ts`, `compaction.ts`, `engine.ts`, `db/migration.ts`, etc.

## Actual
`impact` returns 0 callers. `context` shows the symbol exists but no `CALLS` edges.

## Environment
- gitnexus@1.6.4
- Windows 11 / Node 24.15.0
- Repository: `lossless-claw-enhanced` (TypeScript, ESM)

## Root cause hypothesis
The import resolver does not map `.js` extension back to `.ts` source file, so the call edge is dropped during ingestion.

title: wiki: Mermaid diagrams use literal \n for line breaks (invalid syntax, breaks rendering)
body:
## Summary `gitnexus wiki` generates Mermaid `flowchart` diagrams that put a literal `\n` escape sequence inside node labels to indicate line breaks. Mermaid does not support `\n` inside `[...]` / `[(...)]` labels — it expects `
` (or `
`). The resulting diagrams fail to render in any Mermaid renderer (mermaid.js, GitHub, mermaid.live), showing a syntax error instead of the diagram. A second, related issue: edge labels containing unquoted parentheses (e.g. `|doc()|`) also fail to parse and must be wrapped in quotes (`|"doc()"|`). ## Reproduction Generated wiki page on a real SCTA codebase: https://gistcdn.githack.com/natea/07e449857db62be5df0f268aae31aa83/raw/index.html#json-search The "Architecture Overview" section produces this block (broken): ````markdown ```mermaid flowchart LR Client -->|HTTP params| Endpoint Endpoint -->|SPARQL| KG[("SCTA Knowledge Graph\nsparql-docker")] Endpoint -->|doc()| DB[("/db/apps/scta-data")] Endpoint --> Utils["json-search-utils.xq\n(render + token position)"] Utils --> KWIC["eXist kwic module"] Endpoint -->|JSON| Client ``` ```` Mermaid parser errors on `\n` inside the `KG` and `Utils` labels, and on the unquoted `doc()` edge label. ## Expected output ````markdown ```mermaid flowchart LR Client -->|HTTP params| Endpoint Endpoint -->|SPARQL| KG[("SCTA Knowledge Graph
sparql-docker")] Endpoint -->|"doc()"| DB[("/db/apps/scta-data")] Endpoint --> Utils["json-search-utils.xq
(render + token position)"] Utils --> KWIC["eXist kwic module"] Endpoint -->|JSON| Client ``` ```` Renders correctly. ## Suggested fix In the wiki-generation prompt template (and/or in post-processing of LLM output), enforce two Mermaid conventions: 1. Replace `\n` inside node and edge labels with `
` before emitting the markdown. Newlines in labels are a very common LLM output pattern — easiest to fix in post-processing rather than relying on the prompt alone. 2. Wrap edge labels that contain `(`, `)`, `[`, `]`, `{`, `}`, or other reserved Mermaid characters in double quotes: `|"doc()"|` instead of `|doc()|`. A simple regex-pass over fenced ```mermaid blocks before writing the markdown would catch both cases reliably. This is likely affecting most generated wikis — multiple pages on the example wiki link show the same pattern. ## Environment - gitnexus: latest via `npx gitnexus@latest` - Provider/model: `--provider cursor --model claude-4.6-sonnet-medium` (also reproduces with default model) - Renderer: Mermaid 11 (per the generated `index.html`'s `cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/mermaid@11` script tag)

title: [codex] Make HTTP embedding batch size configurable
body:
## Summary

- Add `GITNEXUS_EMBEDDING_HTTP_BATCH_SIZE` to configure how many chunks are sent in each HTTP embedding request.
- Add `--embedding-http-batch-size <n>` and show the active HTTP request batch size in `gitnexus doctor` when HTTP mode is enabled.
- Keep the existing default of 64 chunks per HTTP request and add unit coverage for custom and invalid values.

## Why

HTTP embedding backends vary widely in optimal request size. The current hard-coded split of 64 chunks is conservative, but it can underuse higher-throughput local or remote OpenAI-compatible embedding servers. Making this value configurable lets users tune throughput without patching source code, while preserving the existing default behavior.

## Validation

- `npm test -- test/unit/http-embedder.test.ts`
- `npx tsc --noEmit`
- `npm run build`

title: fix(lbug): drain checkpoint result before close
body:
## Summary

  Fixes LadybugDB WAL handling during repo switches by draining and closing the `CHECKPOINT` query result before closing the active connection/database.

  ## Motivation / context

  Closes #1480.

  When the HTTP server switches repositories in one process, the core LadybugDB adapter closes the currently open DB before opening the next repo DB. The
  existing `flushWAL()` issued `CHECKPOINT` but did not consume or close the returned `QueryResult`, which can leave the checkpoint lifecycle incomplete
  before `conn.close()` / `db.close()` runs. That can surface as WAL/database-id assertion failures on A -> B -> A repo switching.

  ## Areas touched

  - [x] `gitnexus/` (CLI / core / MCP server)
  - [ ] `gitnexus-web/` (Vite / React UI)
  - [ ] `.github/` (workflows, actions)
  - [ ] `eval/` or other tooling
  - [ ] Docs / agent config only (`AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `.cursor/`, `llms.txt`, etc.)

  ## Scope & constraints

  **In scope**

  - Ensure `flushWAL()` waits for the `CHECKPOINT` result lifecycle to finish.
  - Keep `safeClose()` as the single close path: flush first, then close connection/database handles.
  - Add regression coverage for checkpoint draining and A -> B -> A database path switching.

  **Explicitly out of scope / not done here**

  - No changes to the read-only pool adapter.
  - No changes to web UI repo selection behavior.
  - No broad LadybugDB lifecycle refactor.

  ## Implementation notes

  `flushWAL()` now stores the `CHECKPOINT` result and passes it through `drainQueryResult()`, which consumes all rows with `getAll()` and then closes the
  result object. This makes the checkpoint complete before `safeClose()` proceeds to `conn.close()` and `db.close()`.

  A new integration test covers switching between two LadybugDB paths in the same process and then returning to the first path.

  ## Testing & verification

  - [ ] `cd gitnexus && npm test`
  - [ ] `cd gitnexus && npm run test:integration` *(if core/indexing/MCP paths changed)*
  - [x] `cd gitnexus && npx tsc --noEmit`
  - [ ] `cd gitnexus-web && npm test` *(if web changed)*
  - [ ] `cd gitnexus-web && npx tsc -b --noEmit` *(if web changed)*
  - [ ] Manual / Playwright E2E *(note environment — see `gitnexus-web/e2e/`)*

title: scopeResolution phase crashes with "Cannot add property 1, object is not extensible" on large C# codebases
body:
### Area

gitnexus (CLI / core / indexing / MCP server)

### Summary

`gitnexus analyze` crashes with the following error during the `scopeResolution` phase on a large .NET Framework C# codebase (~4,400 objects, 8.5 MB). The crash is **deterministic** — it always occurs at the same phase, regardless of how many files are excluded via `.gitnexusignore`. The sequential parsing fallback is triggered first, then the crash occurs.

```
Analysis failed: Phase 'scopeResolution' failed: Cannot add property 1, object is not extensible
```

Exit code: `1`

### Context

I am using GitNexus to index a legacy .NET Framework monorepo as part of a modernization project — migrating the codebase to .NET Core microservices. The goal is to use the GitNexus knowledge graph (via the MCP server) to query domain logic in the legacy codebase before porting it, so that AI coding agents can understand the existing architecture without having to read files manually.

The codebase follows a DDD-lite architecture with domain aggregates, LINQ-based specification classes for query predicates, EF5 repositories, and Castle Windsor IoC. The specification pattern is used pervasively — there are ~55 specification files covering every domain entity.

### Expected behavior

- `scopeResolution` should gracefully skip or log files it cannot resolve scopes for, consistent with how `scope extraction failed` warnings are handled in the parsing phase.
- Files matched by `.gitnexusignore` should be excluded from **all** phases, including the sequential fallback path.

### Actual behavior

```
GitNexus Analyzer

Worker pool parsing failed, falling back to sequential: Worker N sub-batch timeout
████████████████████████░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░  60% | error

Analysis failed: Phase 'scopeResolution' failed: Cannot add property 1, object is not extensible

EXIT:1
```

Two secondary issues observed prior to the crash:

1. **Parser hangs indefinitely** when the worker pool falls back to sequential and encounters these files — the progress bar freezes at ~49% for 10+ minutes before a subsequent run crashes fast at ~60%.
2. **`.gitnexusignore` patterns not fully applied during sequential fallback** — files matching excluded glob patterns still appear in `scope extraction failed` output, suggesting the ignore file is honoured during parallel batching but not the sequential fallback path.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Clone or point gitnexus at a C# codebase containing any of the following patterns:
   - LINQ Specification classes with large `Expression<Func<T, bool>>` chains (files in the 10–100 KB range, many files)
   - Large EF5 `DbContext` partial classes
   - Large Castle Windsor `IWindsorInstaller` registrar classes (e.g. 67 KB)
2. Run `gitnexus analyze`
3. Observe crash at `scopeResolution` phase (~60% progress)

**Minimal trigger pattern (C#):**

Files containing deeply chained LINQ expression predicates such as:

```csharp
public static Expression<Func<Order, bool>> ByStatus(int statusId) =>
    o => o.StatusHistory
          .Where(h => h.Active)
          .OrderByDescending(h => h.CreatedAt)
          .FirstOrDefault()
          .StatusId == statusId
    && o.Active
    && !o.Deleted
    && o.OrderType.Code == "XYZ"
    // ... 50+ more clauses chained with &&
```

Files of this shape at 50–100 KB reliably trigger the crash. Smaller files of the same pattern (~6–20 KB) do not.

### Environment

| | |
|---|---|
| gitnexus version | 1.6.3 |
| Node.js | v24.13.1 |
| OS | Linux |
| Codebase language | C# (.NET Framework 4.x) |
| Codebase size | ~4,400 git objects, 8.5 MB |
| Largest offending file type | LINQ Specification class — 98 KB |

### Logs / screenshots

Stack trace extracted by temporarily patching the CLI error handler (`dist/cli/analyze.js`) to print `err.cause.stack` before re-throwing:

```
Error: Phase 'scopeResolution' failed: Cannot add property 1, object is not extensible
    at runPipeline (dist/core/ingestion/pipeline-phases/runner.js:173:29)
    at async runPipelineFromRepo (dist/core/ingestion/pipeline.js:54:21)
    at async runFullAnalysis (dist/core/run-analyze.js:139:28)
    at async analyzeCommand (dist/cli/analyze.js:156:24)
    at async Command.<anonymous> (dist/cli/lazy-action.js:16:9)

Caused by:
TypeError: Cannot add property 1, object is not extensible
    at Array.push (<anonymous>)
    at Object.populateCsharpNamespaceSiblings [as populateNamespaceSiblings] (dist/core/ingestion/scope-resolution/...)
    at runScopeResolution (dist/core/ingestion/scope-resolution/...)
    at Object.execute (dist/core/ingestion/pipeline-phases/...)
    at async runPipeline (dist/core/ingestion/pipeline-phases/runner.js)
```

The root cause is `Array.push` being called on a frozen/non-extensible array inside `populateCsharpNamespaceSiblings`. This function populates a namespace siblings array during C# scope resolution; the array appears to become frozen (via `Object.freeze` or similar) before all siblings are accumulated, causing the crash when the code attempts to push additional entries.

When `<!-- gitnexus:keep -->` is placed inside the GitNexus-generated block in CLAUDE.md or AGENTS.md, `analyze` only updates the stats line (node/edge/flow counts) instead of replacing the entire section with the verbose default template.
