title: fix(ingestion): optional per-parse timeout to prevent worker deadlocks
body:
## Summary

Adds an opt-in `GITNEXUS_PARSE_TIMEOUT_MICROS` env var that applies `Parser.setTimeoutMicros` around every call routed through `parseSourceSafe`. When the limit is hit, the wrapper converts tree-sitter's `null` return into a catchable `ParseTimeoutError` — which existing callers in `call-processor.ts` already handle by skipping the file.

When unset (default), behaviour is identical to previous versions.

## Why

On large repositories the worker-pool idle timeout (default 30s) can fire while a worker is blocked inside a sync `parser.parse()` on a pathological file. The replacement path then calls `worker.terminate()` while the native parser is still running; on macOS this races the tree-sitter binding and the process aborts with:

```
libc++abi: terminating due to uncaught exception of type Napi::Error
```

The crash is unrecoverable from JavaScript because the throw originates in C++ during teardown and bypasses `try/catch`. Setting a per-parse timeout slightly below the worker idle timeout lets tree-sitter abort cooperatively before the pool tries to terminate the worker, so the race window never opens.

## Repro

Reproduced on a ~8k-file polyglot Nx monorepo (TS + .NET + Python + others), gitnexus 1.6.4, Node 25.9, macOS 25.4.

```
npx gitnexus analyze
# → Worker N parse job idle timeout. Splitting into X/Y item jobs.
# → libc++abi: terminating due to uncaught exception of type Napi::Error
# (no .gitnexus index produced)
```

Workaround that confirmed the trigger by avoiding the split/terminate path entirely:

```
npx gitnexus analyze --worker-timeout 300
# succeeds in ~617s (vs ~90s pre-1.6.0); index complete (94,901 nodes / 220,850 edges)
```

With this change, exporting `GITNEXUS_PARSE_TIMEOUT_MICROS=$((25 * 1000 * 1000))` (i.e. 25s, below the 30s default worker timeout) avoids the race without forcing users to disable the idle timeout entirely.

## Scope

This removes the dominant trigger but does **not** fix the underlying race in `worker-pool.replaceWorker` (cancelling a worker mid-`parser.parse` is inherently fragile with the current node-tree-sitter binding). Two natural follow-ups, both out of scope here to keep the diff minimal and bisectable:

- (a) Make the post-`terminate()` path tolerant of in-flight native work (or drain it cooperatively).
- (b) Auto-derive `GITNEXUS_PARSE_TIMEOUT_MICROS` from `--worker-timeout` so users get the protection by default. Happy to send a follow-up PR if you'd prefer that wiring instead of an env-only opt-in.

## Test plan

- [x] `npx vitest run test/unit/safe-parse.test.ts` → 10/10 pass (7 pre-existing + 3 new)
- [x] `npx tsc --noEmit` → no errors
- [x] `npx eslint gitnexus/src/core/tree-sitter/safe-parse.ts gitnexus/test/unit/safe-parse.test.ts` → clean
- [x] Manual: re-ran `gitnexus analyze` on the same monorepo with `GITNEXUS_PARSE_TIMEOUT_MICROS=25000000` and the default 30s worker timeout (no `--worker-timeout` override) — index completed, no Napi::Error.

New test cases cover:

- no-op behaviour when the env var is unset (backward compatibility),
- `ParseTimeoutError` thrown when the limit is exceeded,
- timeout reset after each call so a reused parser is unaffected.

## Risk / rollback

- Default code path is untouched when the env var is absent (a single `process.env` read is added).
- `ParseTimeoutError` is thrown from `parseSourceSafe`; all current call sites already wrap the call in `try { … } catch { continue; }`.
- To roll back: revert this commit; no schema/data migration involved.

title: fix(hooks): cap concurrent augment subprocesses (#1486)
body:
## Summary

Fixes #1486. The `gitnexus-hook.cjs` PreToolUse hook had no cap on concurrent `gitnexus augment` subprocesses. When Claude Code fired parallel Grep/Glob/Bash tool calls, each spawned its own Node + LadybugDB cold start, holding resources for several seconds. Under heavy parallel-search bursts these accumulated faster than they finished — the reporter saw 180+ piled-up processes and a load average over 100.

### Diagnosis (not what the report claims)

The report blames "recursive self-invocation" in the hook. **The hook does not invoke itself.** Every `spawnSync` call in `gitnexus-hook.cjs` is shell-free and direct — `git`, `node <cliPath>`, `npx` — none invoke `bash`. The nested `bash -lc → bash -lc → bash -lc` chain in the reporter's process tree is produced by Claude Code's `sh -c '<command>'` wrapper combined with the user's login-shell init scripts (likely nvm / shell-integration) re-exec'ing. That isn't something the hook can or should fix.

The real bug — and what causes the same observable symptoms — is **the absence of a concurrency guard**. N parallel tool calls = N concurrent `gitnexus augment` cold-starts, with nothing capping the fan-out.

### Fix

Add a lockfile-based concurrency guard under `<.gitnexus>/.hook-locks/`:

- Each running hook writes `<pid>.lock` before spawning augment.
- Before claiming a slot, the guard counts existing lockfiles, pruning entries whose PID is no longer alive (`process.kill(pid, 0)`) or whose mtime is older than 30s (safety net against PID reuse / hung hooks).
- If `MAX_INFLIGHT` (3) live slots are already in use, the hook bails silently. Augment is best-effort enrichment — missing a few fires during a burst is far better than melting the box.
- Cleanup runs in `finally {}` and via `process.on('exit')` for hard kills.

Applied to all three hook variants that spawn augment:
- `gitnexus/hooks/claude/gitnexus-hook.cjs` (npm-installed Claude hook copied by `gitnexus setup`)
- `gitnexus-claude-plugin/hooks/gitnexus-hook.js` (Claude plugin hook)
- `gitnexus-cursor-integration/hooks/gitnexus-hook.cjs` (Cursor hook — same shape, same exposure)

### Out of scope

- The 7s `spawnSync` timeout is unchanged. Tightening it without telemetry on real cold-start tails risks breaking legitimate slow-but-completing augments.
- The `npx -y gitnexus` fallback cold start remains heavy. A longer-term fix would route augment through the already-running MCP server (overlaps with #1492's lock-contention angle).
- The user's nested `bash -lc` shell wrapping is environment-specific and upstream of GitNexus.

## Test plan

- [x] `npx vitest run test/unit/hooks.test.ts` — all 95 tests pass (4 new)
- [x] `npx vitest run test/unit/cursor-hook.test.ts` — 41 tests pass
- [x] `npx tsc --noEmit` — clean
- [x] New regression tests cover:
  - source-level: `acquireHookSlot` is defined and called from `handlePreToolUse` in both CJS + Plugin variants
  - integration: hook bails silently with 3 sentinel lockfiles for genuinely live PIDs (spawned `node -e "setTimeout(...)"` children)
  - integration: hook prunes lockfiles for dead PIDs

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Adds a new cross-process lockfile-based concurrency cap around `gitnexus augment`, which can change when/if augmentation runs under heavy parallel tool usage and may surface edge cases on unusual filesystems or permissions.
> 
> **Overview**
> PreToolUse/postToolUse hooks now wrap `gitnexus augment` with a **hard concurrency guard** that limits in-flight subprocesses to 3 via atomic fixed-name lock slots under `.gitnexus/.hook-locks/`, including stale lock takeover based on PID liveness and age.
> 
> When the lock directory can’t be created or all slots are occupied, the hook **skips augmentation silently** instead of spawning additional processes, and the new unit/integration tests assert the guard wiring, fail-closed behavior, slot reclamation, and the hard-cap under burst contention.
>

title: fix(incremental): address review findings F1, F4 + unit coverage
body:
While you iterate on #1479, here's a small drive-by patch addressing two of the still-open changes-requested findings, rebased onto the current `feat/incremental-indexing` head. Cherry-pick whatever's useful, rework it, or ignore — no pressure. We're consuming the incremental analyzer in a downstream integration and wanted to contribute the fixes back.

### What's in it

**F1 (Blocker) — cross-file edges between unchanged files.** Adds `computeEffectiveWriteSet(graph, toWriteSet)` to `subgraph-extract.ts`: one pass over the new graph's edges, pulling the unchanged-side file of every writable-boundary-crossing edge into the write set. `run-analyze` composes it **on top of** the existing importer-BFS expansion and feeds the combined set to **both** `deleteNodesForFile` and `extractChangedSubgraph`, so the delete cascade and the writeback subgraph cover identical files (asymmetry would leave stale rows or PK-conflict at COPY time). The two layers are complementary: the BFS reads `IMPORTS` from the pre-pipeline DB (catches a file that *stopped* importing a changed file); the edge walk reads the new graph (catches refined `CALLS` edges the pre-run DB couldn't predict — e.g. a barrel re-export shifting a symbol from B to D). `extractChangedSubgraph` stays a pure filter — all expansion is the orchestrator's job.

**F4 (Medium) — restore alphabetical chunk sort.** `parseableScanned` is sorted before chunking. Filesystem-scan order isn't stable enough across runs/platforms (notably macOS APFS) to keep chunk hashes consistent, so the parse cache thrashes without it. The pre-existing Ruby cross-file-resolution order-dependency the old comment cited is independent — the sort surfaces it but doesn't cause it; worth tracking separately rather than leaving the cache cold.

**Tests** — `incremental-subgraph-extract.test.ts` rewritten to lock the F1 invariants: `extractChangedSubgraph` as a pure filter (only the set it's given, plus graph-wide nodes; edge fires on one writable endpoint), and `computeEffectiveWriteSet` over the barrel-re-export scenario, the symmetric edge-into-changed-file case, the no-boundary-crossed no-op, graph-wide-node edges, and input immutability. This **supersedes** the existing `extractChangedSubgraph`-only test file on the branch — flagging that explicitly in case you'd rather keep both.

### What was dropped (already handled on the branch)

The original internal patch also touched F3 / F5 / F6, but those are already done on `feat/incremental-indexing`:
- **F3** — parser-grammar fingerprint in the cache key: covered by `PARSE_CACHE_VERSION = ${SCHEMA_BUMP}+${GITNEXUS_PKG_VERSION}`.
- **F5** — atomic `saveMeta`: already does tmp-file + rename.
- **F6** — `AGENTS.md` phrasing: already accurate.

So this PR only carries the genuine delta. If you'd rather we hold until #1479 merges and re-submit against `main`, say the word and we'll close this.

### Notes
- Rebased onto `feat/incremental-indexing` (the conflicts were the F1 area in `run-analyze.ts`, the `saveMeta` doc comment, the `AGENTS.md` paragraph, and the add/add on the test file — resolved as above, keeping your F3/F5/F6 work intact).
- No build run on my side (no `node_modules` in my checkout); the changes are type-consistent with the surrounding code but please run CI.

body:
Bumps the uv group with 1 update in the /eval directory: [urllib3](https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3). Updates `urllib3` from 2.6.3 to 2.7.0
Release notes

Sourced from urllib3's releases.

2.7.0

🚀 urllib3 is fundraising for HTTP/2 support

urllib3 is raising ~$40,000 USD to release HTTP/2 support and ensure long-term sustainable maintenance of the project after a sharp decline in financial support. If your company or organization uses Python and would benefit from HTTP/2 support in Requests, pip, cloud SDKs, and thousands of other projects please consider contributing financially to ensure HTTP/2 support is developed sustainably and maintained for the long-haul.

Thank you for your support.

Security

Addressed high-severity security issues. Impact was limited to specific use cases detailed in the accompanying advisories; overall user exposure was estimated to be marginal.

  • Decompression-bomb safeguards of the streaming API were bypassed:

    1. When HTTPResponse.drain_conn() was called after the response had been read and decompressed partially. (Reported by @​Cycloctane)
    2. During the second HTTPResponse.read(amt=N) or HTTPResponse.stream(amt=N) call when the response was decompressed using the official Brotli library. (Reported by @​kimkou2024)

    See GHSA-mf9v-mfxr-j63j for details.

  • HTTP pools created using ProxyManager.connection_from_url did not strip sensitive headers specified in Retry.remove_headers_on_redirect when redirecting to a different host. (GHSA-qccp-gfcp-xxvc reported by @​christos-spearbit)

Deprecations and Removals

  • Used FutureWarning instead of DeprecationWarning for better visibility of existing deprecation notices. Rescheduled the removal of deprecated features to version 3.0. (urllib3/urllib3#3763)
  • Removed support for end-of-life Python 3.9. (urllib3/urllib3#3720)
  • Removed support for end-of-life PyPy3.10. (urllib3/urllib3#4979)
  • Bumped the minimum supported pyOpenSSL version to 19.0.0. (urllib3/urllib3#3777)

Bugfixes

  • Fixed a bug where HTTPResponse.read(amt=None) was ignoring decompressed data buffered from previous partial reads. (urllib3/urllib3#3636)
  • Fixed a bug where HTTPResponse.read() could cache only part of the response after a partial read when cache_content=True. (urllib3/urllib3#4967)
  • Fixed HTTPResponse.stream() and HTTPResponse.read_chunked() to handle amt=0. (urllib3/urllib3#3793)
  • Updated _TYPE_BODY type alias to include missing Iterable[str], matching the documented and runtime behavior of chunked request bodies. (urllib3/urllib3#3798)
  • Fixed LocationParseError when paths resembling schemeless URIs were passed to HTTPConnectionPool.urlopen(). (urllib3/urllib3#3352)
  • Fixed BaseHTTPResponse.readinto() type annotation to accept memoryview in addition to bytearray, matching the io.RawIOBase.readinto contract and enabling use with io.BufferedReader without type errors. (urllib3/urllib3#3764)

title: feat(cli): add export command with multi-format graph output
body:
## Summary

Adds a new `gitnexus export` CLI command that reads the LadybugDB knowledge graph for the current repository and writes node/edge tables to `.gitnexus/export/` (or a user-specified directory) in JSON (default), CSV, or Parquet format.

## Motivation / context

Closes #1335. Users need a first-class way to extract raw graph data for downstream analysis, dashboards, and tooling integrations. The current workaround of querying KuzuDB directly is undocumented and fragile.

## Areas touched

- [x] gitnexus (CLI / core / MCP server)
- [ ] gitnexus-web (Vite / React UI)
- [ ] .github (workflows, actions)
- [ ] eval or other tooling
- [ ] Docs / agent config only

## Scope & constraints

**In scope**

- New `gitnexus export [path]` command with `-o/--output <dir>`, `--format <fmt>`, `-f/--force`, and `--embeddings` flags
- JSON extension loading via `ExtensionManager` in `lbug-adapter.ts`
- `BACKTICK_NODE_TABLES` set in `schema.ts` for correct KuzuDB `COPY TO` quoting
- Unit, integration smoke, and schema constant tests

**Explicitly out of scope / not done here**

- `gitnexus import` / round-trip ingestion
- Streaming / incremental export for very large graphs
- Web UI export surface

## Implementation notes

- **Default format is JSON** — requires the KuzuDB JSON extension. If the extension cannot be loaded, the command exits with code 1 and a clear error message directing the user to `--format parquet`.
- **Embeddings are opt-in** via `--embeddings` because the table can be very large.
- Empty node tables are skipped automatically.
- Windows-safe path handling via `normalizeCopyPath` (backslash → forward slash) for KuzuDB `COPY TO` statements.
- `BACKTICK_NODE_TABLES` must be kept in sync with any future node-table DDL additions that use backtick-quoted identifiers.
- `loadJsonExtension` in `lbug-adapter.ts` mirrors the existing `loadVectorExtension` pattern, tracks `jsonExtensionLoaded` module-level state, and resets it in `withLbugDb`, `doInitLbug`, and `closeLbug` teardown paths.

## Testing & verification

```bash
cd gitnexus && npm test
cd gitnexus && npm run test:integration
cd gitnexus && npx tsc --noEmit
```

- [x] `cd gitnexus && npm test`
- [x] `cd gitnexus && npm run test:integration`
- [x] `cd gitnexus && npx tsc --noEmit`
- [ ] `cd gitnexus-web && npm test` *(not applicable — no web changes)*
- [x] Manual testing: exported JSON, CSV, and Parquet against a real indexed repo; verified output structure.

**Edge cases verified:** empty tables skipped, `--force` overwrites existing files, missing JSON extension surfaces correct error, `--embeddings` opt-in and skip logic.

## Risk & rollout

- No breaking changes to existing CLI commands or public MCP API.
- No index migration required; export reads the existing LadybugDB database.
- `gitnexus_impact` run on modified shared symbols (`loadJsonExtension` entry points in `lbug-adapter.ts`, `BACKTICK_NODE_TABLES` in `schema.ts`) — no upstream callers affected.
- `gitnexus_detect_changes` confirmed diff scope is limited to `export.ts`, `index.ts` (new command registration), `lbug-adapter.ts`, `schema.ts`, and their test files.
- README / CLI help updated to document the new command and flags.

## Checklist

- [x] PR body meets repo minimum length
- [ ] If AGENTS.md / overlays changed: headers, scope block, and changelog updated *(not applicable)*
- [x] No secrets, tokens, or machine-specific paths committed

title: GitNexus fails on macOS Intel (x86_64) with 'Cannot find module ../bin/napi-v6/darwin/x64/onnxruntime_binding.node'
body:
## Bug Description

GitNexus fails to run on macOS Intel (x86_64) architecture with a module not found error for onnxruntime-node's native binding.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. On a macOS Intel (x86_64) machine
2. Run `gitnexus analyze --embeddings` or `ONNX_WEB_BACKEND=wasm npx gitnexus analyze --embeddings`
3. See the error

## Expected Behavior
GitNexus should run successfully on macOS Intel (x86_64) or provide a clear error message indicating unsupported platforms.

## Actual Behavior
Error:
```
GitNexus Analyzer

  Analysis failed: Cannot find module '../bin/napi-v6/darwin/x64/onnxruntime_binding.node'
Require stack:
- .../@huggingface/transformers/node_modules/onnxruntime-node/dist/binding.js
- .../@huggingface/transformers/node_modules/onnxruntime-node/dist/backend.js
- .../@huggingface/transformers/node_modules/onnxruntime-node/dist/index.js
```

## Environment
- OS: macOS (Darwin)
- Architecture: x86_64 (Intel)
- GitNexus version: latest

## Root Cause Analysis
The issue is that @ladybugdb/core (GitNexus's core dependency) only includes precompiled onnxruntime-node binaries for:
- ✅ darwin-arm64 (Apple Silicon)
- ✅ linux-x64
- ✅ win32-x64
- ✅ linux-arm64
- ❌ **darwin-x64 (macOS Intel) - missing**

## Impacted Platforms
| Platform | Status |
|----------|--------|
| macOS Intel (x86_64) | ❌ Not supported |
| macOS Apple Silicon (arm64) | ✅ Supported |
| Linux x86_64 | ✅ Supported |
| Windows x86_64 | ✅ Supported |
| Linux arm64 | ✅ Supported |

## Possible Solutions
1. Add darwin-x64 precompiled binaries to the @ladybugdb/core package
2. Provide a fallback mechanism for unsupported architectures
3. Document platform support clearly in the README

title: GitNexus Fails with ONNX_WEB_BACKEND=wasm on macOS Intel (x86_64)
body:
# GitNexus Fails with `ONNX_WEB_BACKEND=wasm` on macOS Intel (x86_64)

## Problem

GitNexus fails immediately when running with `--embeddings` on macOS Intel (x86_64), even when attempting to use the WASM backend.

### Commands Tried

```bash
ONNX_WEB_BACKEND=wasm npx gitnexus analyze --embeddings
npx gitnexus analyze --embeddings --embedding-device wasm
```

### Error Message

```
Analysis failed: Cannot find module '../bin/napi-v6/darwin/x64/onnxruntime_binding.node'
Require stack:
- /Users/.../node_modules/gitnexus/node_modules/@huggingface/transformers/node_modules/onnxruntime-node/dist/binding.js
- /Users/.../node_modules/gitnexus/node_modules/@huggingface/transformers/node_modules/onnxruntime-node/dist/backend.js
- /Users/.../node_modules/gitnexus/node_modules/@huggingface/transformers/node_modules/onnxruntime-node/dist/index.js
```

---

## Root Cause Analysis

### 1. The Failure Happens at Module Import Time (Before Code Execution!)

**Key observation:** The error occurs during `require()`, **before any GitNexus business logic runs!**

The stack trace shows the failure happens when `onnxruntime-node` tries to load its native binding, which is triggered by the top-level import.

### 2. Why the Import Fails

**`@huggingface/transformers` imports `onnxruntime-node` at its own top level!**

Execution flow:
1. `gitnexus` imports `@huggingface/transformers` (line 15 in `embedder.js`)
2. `@huggingface/transformers` immediately imports `onnxruntime-node` at its top level
3. `onnxruntime-node` tries to load the platform-specific native module `../bin/napi-v6/darwin/x64/onnxruntime_binding.node`
4. **But the `onnxruntime-node` packaged in `@ladybugdb/core` only includes:**
   - ✅ `darwin-arm64` (Apple Silicon)
   - ✅ `linux-x64` / `linux-arm64`
   - ✅ `win32-x64` / `win32-arm64`
   - ❌ **`darwin-x64` (macOS Intel) — MISSING!**

### 3. Why `--embedding-device wasm` Doesn't Help

**Because WASM backend selection happens at runtime, but the import failure happens before that!**

Timeline:

```
1. Module Import Phase (must succeed 100%)
   ├─ gitnexus imports → @huggingface/transformers
   └─ @huggingface/transformers → imports onnxruntime-node → loads native binding → ❌ FAILS!

2. Code Execution Phase (never reached)
   └─ parse --embedding-device wasm → set env → select backend
```

### 4. What is `ONNX_WEB_BACKEND` Anyway?

This environment variable isn't used by GitNexus at all! It might be for other projects (like `onnxruntime-web`), but:
1. GitNexus code never reads this variable
2. Even if it did, it couldn't affect module import phase behavior

---

## Technical Details

### 1. onnxruntime-node is Missing darwin-x64 Binaries

Verified directory structure:
```
onnxruntime-node/bin/napi-v6/
├── linux/
│   ├── x64/     ✅
│   └── arm64/   ✅
├── darwin/
│   └── arm64/   ✅ (Apple Silicon only)
│   └── x64/     ❌ (MISSING!)
└── win32/
    ├── x64/     ✅
    └── arm64/   ✅
```

### 2. --embedding-device wasm IS Actually Supported in Code

GitNexus `config.js` does support the `wasm` device:
```javascript
parseDevice = (value) => {
    if (value === 'auto' || value === 'dml' || value === 'cuda' || 
        value === 'cpu' || value === 'wasm') {  // ← wasm is listed
        return value;
    }
}
```

`embedder.js` also has WASM backend logging:
```javascript
else if (isDev && device === 'wasm') {
    logger.info('🔧 Using WASM backend (slower)...');
}
```

**BUT THE CODE NEVER GETS THIS FAR!**

---

## This is a Unique Problem

This isn't just a normal "doesn't support macOS Intel" issue. This is a **"module import contract" problem**:

| Scenario | Outcome |
|----------|---------|
| If code checks platform BEFORE importing | ✅ Can show graceful "not supported" message |
| If module imports unconditionally at top-level | ❌ Crashes immediately, before even reaching checks |

---

## Possible Solutions (Ordered by Recommendation)

### Solution 1: Use Docker (Simplest & Most Reliable)

```bash
# Run GitNexus in a Linux container
docker run -it -v $(pwd):/repo node:20 bash
cd /repo
npm install -g gitnexus
gitnexus analyze --embeddings
```

### Solution 2: Use an Apple Silicon Mac

If you have an M1/M2/M3 Mac, GitNexus works perfectly there.

### Solution 3: Don't Use the Embeddings Feature

```bash
npx gitnexus analyze  # without --embeddings
```

This way GitNexus won't import the embeddings code and won't load `onnxruntime-node`.

### Solution 4: Fix GitNexus with a PR

Fix approach:
1. Change `@huggingface/transformers` import to **dynamic import** (`import()`)
2. Check platform compatibility BEFORE dynamic import
3. Show friendly error message BEFORE attempting import if platform not supported

Pseudo-code:
```javascript
// DON'T import at top-level!
// import { pipeline, env } from '@huggingface/transformers';

async function initEmbedder() {
    // 1. Check platform first
    if (!isPlatformSupported()) {
        throw new Error('Platform not supported. Please use Docker or Apple Silicon.');
    }
    // 2. Then dynamic import
    const { pipeline, env } = await import('@huggingface/transformers');
    // ...
}
```

---

## Summary

| Question | Answer |
|----------|--------|
| Why doesn't `ONNX_WEB_BACKEND=wasm` work? | It doesn't affect module import phase, and GitNexus doesn't read it anyway |
| Why doesn't `--embedding-device wasm` work? | Code never gets there - crashes during module import |
| What's the root cause? | `@ladybugdb/core` packages an `onnxruntime-node` missing `darwin-x64` binaries, AND modules import unconditionally at top-level |
| Whose problem is this? | GitNexus dependency packaging issue + import timing issue |
| Quickest fix? | Use Docker, or don't use `--embeddings` |

---

## System Information

- OS: macOS (Darwin)
- Architecture: x86_64 (Intel)
- GitNexus version: 1.6.5-rc.4

title: feat(cpp): migrate C++ to scope-based resolution model (#938)
body:
Closes #935

## Summary

This PR completes the remaining C++ scope-resolution parity work and removes the last legacy parity expected failure.

Key fixes:
- Improves C++ overload / receiver type propagation cases for scope-resolution.
- Fixes cross-file and method-chain resolution regressions.
- Fixes write-access edge deduplication for compound assignments.
- Removes the remaining C++ legacy parity expected failure after both resolver paths reach full parity.

The final write-access issue was caused by the legacy DAG `processCalls` path using a separate `pendingWrites` flow whose `ACCESSES` edge id did not include the assignment line. As a result, multiple writes to the same field in the same function, e.g. `user.name = ...` and `user.name += ...`, were deduplicated into one edge. This PR adds assignment line information to preserve each write site.

title: fix(ci): make /review reliably post PR comments
body:
## Summary
- `.github/workflows/claude.yml` was passing an invalid PR ref (`owner/repo/pull/N`) to `/code-review:code-review`. `gh` interprets that string as a branch name, so the plugin's early `gh pr view` calls failed with `no pull requests found for branch "..."` and only later recovered via `gh pr diff <N> --repo ...`.
- More impactfully, the prompt omitted `--comment`. Per the [code-review plugin docs](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/blob/main/plugins/code-review/commands/code-review.md), without `--comment` the review only displays in terminal output — `gh pr comment` is never invoked, which matches the observed symptom (green CI, long transcript, no comment on the PR).
- Switching to a full PR URL + `--comment` makes the plugin post during the session via its own `gh` tool calls. That also routes around upstream bugs [anthropics/claude-code-action#1061](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code-action/issues/1061) (P1: `issue_comment` triggers silently drop the action's post-step comments) and [#1087](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code-action/issues/1087) (plugin's final turn is `TodoWrite` → `result: ""` → nothing captured), where the documented workaround is precisely to have Claude call `gh pr comment` itself.

## Change
One line in `.github/workflows/claude.yml`:

```diff
- prompt: '/code-review:code-review ${{ github.repository }}/pull/${{ steps.pr.outputs.number }}'
+ prompt: '/code-review:code-review https://github.com/${{ github.repository }}/pull/${{ steps.pr.outputs.number }} --comment'
```

## Test plan
- [ ] Comment `/review` on an open PR after this merges and confirm a review comment appears on the PR thread.
- [ ] Check the action logs no longer show `no pull requests found for branch "..."` from `gh pr view`.
- [ ] Confirm no regression to the non-review `@claude` path (separate step, unchanged).

title: ci(claude): fix /review PR comments blocked by Bash approval in Actions
body:
## Problem

The \/review\ path runs the code-review plugin in GitHub Actions. Bash commands such as \gh pr comment\ and \gh api\ were returning **\This command requires approval\\**, which cannot be satisfied in CI, so the workflow finished green but **posted no PR comment**.

Example: workflow run 25720169951 (logs show repeated approval errors; MCP inline-comment tool is not available in this environment, so the plugin falls back to shell).

## Change

Add \claude_args: '--dangerously-skip-permissions'\ **only** to the **Run Claude Code Review** step so headless CI can execute the shell commands the plugin uses to publish feedback.

This is scoped to the review job only; the default interactive approval behavior remains for the non-review \@claude\ step unless we decide to align later.

## Security note

This relaxes Claude Code permission prompts for that step. It is appropriate for trusted automation where the runner already holds \GITHUB_TOKEN\ with \pull-requests: write\ and the checkout is pinned to the PR head SHA for forks.

title: plugin system
body:
## Summary

Introduce a plugin system (Parser/Analyzer/Processor/Integration plugins), external plugin packages for framework-specific analysis, Spring Boot YAML config extraction with @Value link, and translate all Chinese plugin documentation to English.

## Motivation / context

GitNexus lacked an extensible plugin architecture for framework-specific analysis (Spring Boot, JPA, MyBatis, Kafka, Markdown). Users had no way to parse non-code config files like YAML/yml or link @Value annotations to config entries. Documentation was exclusively in Chinese, creating a barrier for non-Chinese-speaking contributors and users.

## Areas touched

- [x] `gitnexus/` (CLI / core / MCP server)
- [ ] `gitnexus-web/` (Vite / React UI)
- [ ] `.github/` (workflows, actions)
- [ ] `eval/` or other tooling
- [x] Docs / agent config only (`docs/`)

## Scope & constraints

**In scope**

- Plugin system infrastructure: PluginManager, PluginLoader, PluginHooks, CLI commands (`plugin list/install/uninstall/create`)
- Four plugin types: ParserPlugin, AnalyzerPlugin, ProcessorPlugin, IntegrationPlugin
- External plugin packages under `gitnexus-plugins/`: yaml-parser, jpa-plugin, kafka-plugin, markdown-plugin, mybatis-plugin, spring-boot-plugin
- YAML/yml config file parsing as a ParserPlugin using js-yaml, creating CodeElement nodes (YamlConfig/YamlSection/YamlProperty/YamlArrayItem) with CONTAINS edges
- Spring Boot `@Value` annotation resolution linked to YAML config entries, integrated as a `config` pipeline phase
- English translation of all `docs/plugins/*` files (README, quickstart, API reference, dev guide, LLM guide, changelog, troubleshooting, examples)
- Original Chinese docs preserved under `docs/zh/`

**Explicitly out of scope / not done here**

- Plugin marketplace or remote registry — plugins load from local filesystem only
- No built-in `@Value` → YAML value content resolution (only node linking; the consumer resolves at runtime)
- No `gitnexus-web/` changes

## Implementation notes

- Plugin lifecycle: `beforePipeline` / `afterPipeline` hooks registered in `pipeline.ts`
- PluginLoader scans `.gitnexus/plugins.json` and `gitnexus-plugins/` directory at startup
- ParserPlugin interface: `parse(content, filePath) → { nodes, edges, metadata }`
- YAML parsing uses `js-yaml` (already a dependency) — no additional native deps
- `buildPhaseList()` in `pipeline.ts` now includes an optional `pluginPhase` that runs between `parse` and `mro`
- Docs translation preserves code blocks and type definitions verbatim; only prose is translated

## Testing & verification

- [x] `cd gitnexus && npx tsc --noEmit` (passes; pre-existing `pino` module error unrelated)

Manual verification pending for plugin loading and YAML extraction — no automated tests added in this PR.

## Risk & rollout

- **Non-breaking** — existing languages and pipeline phases unaffected
- Plugin system is opt-in: no external plugins ship as defaults (wired but not auto-loaded)
- YAML parser plugin is registered as a default plugin in `plugins/index.ts`
- Index refresh not required (new nodes are additive to existing graph)
- `npx gitnexus plugin list` to verify loaded plugins post-merge

## Checklist

- [x] PR body meets repo minimum length

title: fix: resolve TypeScript ESM .js extension imports to .ts source files
body:
## Summary

Fixes #1503 — TypeScript ESM imports with `.js` extensions now correctly resolve to `.ts` source files.

## Problem

TypeScript ESM (`moduleResolution: node16/bundler`) requires imports to use `.js` extensions:
```typescript
import { estimateTokens } from './utils.js'; // source file is utils.ts
```

The import resolver tried `utils.js` directly and appended more extensions (`utils.js.ts`, etc.), but never stripped `.js` to try `.ts`. Result: 0 call edges for any ESM project.

## Fix

In `resolveImportPath` (TS/JS relative path branch only):
1. If direct resolution fails and the path ends with a JS-family extension (`.js`/`.jsx`/`.mjs`/`.cjs`), strip it and re-resolve — matching TypeScript compiler behavior.
2. Added `.mts`/`.cts` to the EXTENSIONS list.

The fallback is scoped to TypeScript/JavaScript only — no impact on other languages.

## Testing

- 15 new unit tests covering all extension mappings, priority (real .js wins), non-TS languages, and edge cases.
- Manual verification: indexed a minimal ESM repo with `./utils.js` import → `context estimateTokens` correctly shows the caller.

## Verification

```
$ gitnexus context --repo esm-test estimateTokens
{
  "status": "found",
  "symbol": { "name": "estimateTokens", "filePath": "src/utils.ts" },
  "incoming": { "calls": [{ "name": "index.ts", "filePath": "src/index.ts" }] }
}
```

title: Path alias imports with .js extensions do not trigger ESM fallback resolution
body:
## Problem

When using tsconfig path aliases with `.js` extensions (e.g. `import { foo } from '@/utils.js'`), the ESM extension fallback does not apply. The resolver strips `.js` → `.ts` only for **relative imports** (`./utils.js`), but the alias branch in `resolveImportPath` calls `tryResolveWithExtensions(rewritten, allFiles)` without the `stripJsExtension` retry logic.

## Expected Behavior

`@/utils.js` should resolve to `src/utils.ts` (after alias rewriting to `src/utils.js`, then stripping `.js` and retrying with `.ts`).

## Current Behavior

`@/utils.js` fails to resolve because `src/utils.js` does not exist, and no fallback strips the extension.

## Proposed Fix

Apply the same `stripJsExtension` + `tryResolveWithExtensions` fallback in the tsconfig alias branch (lines 56-81 of `standard.ts`) after the initial `tryResolveWithExtensions` call fails.

## Context

Identified during review of #1525. The relative-import fix is scoped correctly; this is a separate code path that needs the same treatment.

Related: #1503

title: feat(analyze): allow updating CLAUDE.md without creating or updating AGENTS.md
body:
## Summary

Please add a way for `gitnexus analyze` to update `CLAUDE.md` while skipping creation/update of `AGENTS.md`.

## Current behavior

`gitnexus analyze` updates both generated context files:

- `CLAUDE.md`
- `AGENTS.md`

The current CLI help exposes `--skip-agents-md`, but its behavior/description is broader than the name suggests:

> Skip updating the gitnexus section in AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md

That means there is no apparent way to keep the useful `CLAUDE.md` GitNexus block fresh while preventing GitNexus from creating or changing `AGENTS.md`.

## Why this matters

Some repositories use `CLAUDE.md` as the canonical agent instruction file and do not use `AGENTS.md`. In those repos, every analyze run creates Git status noise or modifies an unwanted file, even though the generated `CLAUDE.md` block is still useful.

The existing all-or-nothing skip options/workarounds do not fit this case because they also stop `CLAUDE.md` from being updated.

## Proposed solution

Add a per-context-file generation control. Any of these would work:

1. A CLI flag such as:
   - `gitnexus analyze --skip-agents-md --update-claude-md`
   - `gitnexus analyze --no-agents-md`
   - `gitnexus analyze --context-files claude`
2. A config option such as:
   ```json
   {
     "contextFiles": ["CLAUDE.md"]
   }
   ```
3. Separate booleans, for example:
   ```json
   {
     "writeClaudeMd": true,
     "writeAgentsMd": false
   }
   ```

## Desired behavior

When configured for Claude-only context files:

- `gitnexus analyze` updates the `<!-- gitnexus:start --> ... <!-- gitnexus:end -->` section in `CLAUDE.md` as it does today.
- `gitnexus analyze` does not create `AGENTS.md` if it does not exist.
- `gitnexus analyze` does not modify `AGENTS.md` if it already exists.
- Index generation, MCP registration, staleness checks, and other analyze behavior continue unchanged.
- Default behavior can remain unchanged for backward compatibility.

## Related issues

This is related to, but narrower than:

title: fix: apply ESM .js extension fallback to tsconfig path alias resolution
body:
## Summary

Fixes #1528 — Path alias imports with `.js` extensions now correctly resolve to `.ts` source files.

## Problem

`import { foo } from '@/utils.js'` (via tsconfig path aliases) failed to resolve because the alias branch in `resolveImportPath` called `tryResolveWithExtensions` without the `stripJsExtension` retry logic that was already applied to relative imports in #1525.

## Fix

Apply the same `stripJsExtension` + `tryResolveWithExtensions` fallback in the tsconfig alias branch after the initial direct resolution fails. Also removed the now-outdated NOTE comment about this being a known limitation.

## Testing

- 5 new unit tests covering: alias + `.js` → `.ts`, alias + `.jsx` → `.tsx`, real `.js` wins over fallback, alias with baseUrl prefix, and null for missing files.
- All existing tests continue to pass (25 unit + 2 integration).
- `tsc --noEmit` passes.

title: fix(build): use platform-aware tsc command for win32
body:
## Summary

On Windows, `npx tsc` in the build script can fail due to path resolution issues with `.cmd` wrappers, causing build timeouts or ENOENT errors. This PR replaces `npx tsc` with a platform-aware direct path to `node_modules/.bin/tsc.cmd` (win32) / `node_modules/.bin/tsc` (unix).

## Motivation / context

`execSync('npx tsc', ...)` spawns a nested shell process that on Windows must resolve through `tsc.cmd` → `node tsc.js`. This indirection is fragile—it can time out, fail to find the correct `tsc` binary in monorepo setups, or produce misleading error messages. Using the direct binary path eliminates the indirection and aligns with how `package.json` scripts already invoke TypeScript.

## Areas touched

- [x] `gitnexus/` (CLI / core / MCP server)

## Testing & verification

- [x] `cd gitnexus && npm run build` — passes on Windows 11 (win32)
- [x] No change on unix — `process.platform !== 'win32'` still uses `node_modules/.bin/tsc`

## Risk & rollout

Minimal — the change is gated behind `process.platform === 'win32'`. Non-Windows paths are unchanged. No index refresh required.

title: Feature request: a stable call-graph contract (tool / endpoint) rather than raw Cypher against the LadybugDB schema
body:
**Context / use case.** I consume GitNexus from a host service: after `gitnexus analyze`, the host fetches the resolved call graph and feeds it into downstream analysis (architectural metrics, dead-code, impact). Today the only way to get that graph programmatically is `POST /tool/cypher` (eval-server) or `gitnexus tool cypher` with a hand-written query like:

```cypher
MATCH (a)-[r:CodeRelation]->(b)
WHERE r.type IN ['CALLS','IMPORTS','ACCESSES','EXTENDS','METHOD_OVERRIDES','CONTAINS']
RETURN a.id, a.name, labels(a)[0], b.id, b.name, labels(b)[0], r.type
```

That couples the consumer to GitNexus's internal graph schema — node labels, the `CodeRelation` relation, property names. A schema-touching change (e.g. the recent scope-based-resolution refactor, or a relation rename) silently breaks the consumer's query with no contract to notice it against.

**Request — for your consideration, not a demand:** would you be open to a first-class, stable call-graph surface? E.g. a `gitnexus tool call-graph --repo <name>` tool (and/or `GET /api/graph/call-graph?repo=<name>` exposed on the *eval-server*, not just on `gitnexus serve`) returning a documented shape such as:

```json
{ "repo": "...", "commit": "...",
  "nodes": [{ "id": "...", "name": "...", "kind": "function|class|module|file", "file": "...", "range": [..] }],
  "edges": [{ "from": "...", "to": "...", "kind": "calls|imports|accesses|extends|overrides|contains" }] }
```

That'd let consumers depend on a versioned contract instead of the storage schema. Happy to discuss the shape — or to put up a PR if you'd take one. Curious what your view is on whether this belongs in GitNexus or stays the consumer's problem.

title: Feature request: `gitnexus list --json` (machine-readable repo registry, incl. the on-disk path)
body:
**Context.** A host service that drives `gitnexus analyze` and then queries the result needs to map *its* notion of a repo (a clone directory it created) to GitNexus's registry name (which appears to be the last path segment of the URL/path). `gitnexus list` already prints exactly what's needed — ``` helix-db Path: /app/data/repos/HelixDB__helix-db Commit: b776c7b ... ``` — the `Path:` line *is* the mapping. But it's only available as human-formatted text, so a programmatic consumer is reduced to scraping that output or guessing the name from the directory basename (which doesn't always match — `HelixDB__helix-db` ≠ `helix-db`). **Request — for your consideration:** a `--json` flag on `gitnexus list` emitting something like `[{ "name": "...", "path": "...", "commit": "...", "indexed_at": "...", "stats": {...} }, ...]`. Then a consumer can resolve `path → name` reliably. (A `gitnexus resolve --path

` would also do it, but `list --json` seems the more generally-useful primitive.) Small change; happy to PR it if you'd take one. What's your preference?

title: gitnexus wiki command throws timeout error
body:
### Area

gitnexus (CLI / core / indexing / MCP server)

### Summary

When the code base is large, the "gitnexus wiki" command throws timeout error after 60 seconds. Then it fails to generate the Wiki. This is introduced by version 1.6.4.

### Context

When the code base is large, the "gitnexus wiki" command throws timeout error after 60 seconds. Then it fails to generate the Wiki. This is introduced by version 1.6.4. It was working fine before 1.6.4.

### Expected behavior

It takes 20 minutes or longer to generate wiki if the code base is large. The "gitnexus wiki" command should not fail after 60 seconds and throw timeout error.

### Actual behavior

Run "gitnexus wiki" command and it throws `Error: The operation was aborted due to timeout` after 60 seconds.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Setup the gitnexus config.json with local LLM provider.
2. Go to a large code base project.
3. Run "gitnexus analyze" command.
4. Run "gitnexus wiki" command. It throws `Error: The operation was aborted due to timeout` after 60 seconds.

### Environment

- OS: Macbook Pro
- Node: v22.15.0

### Logs / screenshots

This issue does not exist before 1.6.4.

title: fix(wiki): sanitize generated mermaid diagrams

title: analyze: generated CLAUDE.md examples omit repo parameter in multi-repo environments
body:
### Area

gitnexus (CLI / core / indexing)

### Problem

When `npx gitnexus analyze` generates the GitNexus section in CLAUDE.md, the tool call examples use unqualified calls like:

```
gitnexus_impact({target: "symbolName", direction: "upstream"})
gitnexus_detect_changes()
gitnexus_context({name: "symbolName"})
```

In environments with multiple indexed repositories (e.g. 12 in my case), the `repo` parameter is required for correct resolution. The generated examples should include it, since the project name is already known at generation time.

### Expected behaviour

Generated examples should be repo-qualified:

```
gitnexus_impact({repo: "my-project", target: "symbolName", direction: "upstream"})
gitnexus_detect_changes({repo: "my-project"})
gitnexus_context({repo: "my-project", name: "symbolName"})
```

The repo name is already used in the resource URIs (`gitnexus://repo/my-project/context`), so it's available during generation.

### Impact

Agents following the generated CLAUDE.md instructions in multi-repo environments may query the wrong index, producing incorrect impact analysis and blast-radius checks. Manual edits to add `repo` are overwritten on every subsequent `npx gitnexus analyze` run.

### Version

1.6.4

title: MCP server leaks orphaned gitnexus mcp processes after Cursor/Claude sessions
body:
## Area

gitnexus (CLI / core / indexing / MCP server)

## Summary

GitNexus MCP processes can become orphaned (`PPID 1`) after Cursor/Claude MCP sessions and continue consuming high CPU for hours instead of shutting down.

## Context

I use GitNexus through Cursor MCP in a project with this config:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "gitnexus": {
      "command": "pnpm",
      "args": ["exec", "gitnexus", "mcp"]
    }
  }
}
```

Today the laptop became hot and sluggish. Investigation showed dozens of stale `node ./node_modules/.bin/../gitnexus/dist/cli/index.js mcp` processes. They were all parented by PID 1, which suggests the original editor/agent parent process exited but the MCP child processes remained alive.

## Expected behavior

When the MCP client/editor session ends, the GitNexus MCP server should shut down promptly. At most one active `gitnexus mcp` process should remain per live MCP client/session.

## Actual behavior

Many orphaned GitNexus MCP processes remained alive for 4-9 hours and each consumed significant CPU. System CPU reached 0% idle and load average exceeded 100.

## Steps to reproduce

I do not yet have a minimal deterministic repro, but the observed setup was:

1. Configure Cursor MCP to launch GitNexus via `pnpm exec gitnexus mcp`.
2. Use Cursor/Claude agents across multiple sessions in the same repo.
3. Let sessions finish, crash, or be interrupted/restarted over the day.
4. Inspect processes:

```bash
ps -arcwwwxo pid,ppid,%cpu,%mem,etime,args | grep 'gitnexus/dist/cli/index.js mcp'
```

Observed: many old `gitnexus mcp` processes with `PPID 1` and high CPU.

## Environment

- OS: macOS Darwin 25.4.0
- Node: v24.15.0
- pnpm: 10.33.2
- GitNexus: 1.6.4
- Editor/client: Cursor MCP launching `pnpm exec gitnexus mcp`

## Debug logs / findings

Initial system state:

```text
Load Avg: 79.33, 98.98, 110.21
CPU usage: 83.69% user, 16.30% sys, 0.0% idle
PhysMem: 23G used, 191M unused
```

Hot process sample:

```text
PID    PPID  %CPU  %MEM  ELAPSED   COMMAND
3214      1  47.2   0.7  06:09:31  node ./node_modules/.bin/../gitnexus/dist/cli/index.js mcp
222       1  36.3   0.7  06:10:58  node ./node_modules/.bin/../gitnexus/dist/cli/index.js mcp
33378     1  34.9   0.7  08:44:14  node ./node_modules/.bin/../gitnexus/dist/cli/index.js mcp
35399     1  34.8   0.7  07:58:56  node ./node_modules/.bin/../gitnexus/dist/cli/index.js mcp
55936     1  34.4   0.7  06:30:37  node ./node_modules/.bin/../gitnexus/dist/cli/index.js mcp
76576     1  34.3   0.7  07:01:57  node ./node_modules/.bin/../gitnexus/dist/cli/index.js mcp
21512     1  34.2   0.7  06:01:49  node ./node_modules/.bin/../gitnexus/dist/cli/index.js mcp
63892     1  33.9   0.7  04:00:36  node ./node_modules/.bin/../gitnexus/dist/cli/index.js mcp
```

There were 36 matching GitNexus MCP processes before cleanup.

After killing only the GitNexus MCP processes:

```text
Load Avg: 70.79, 90.75, 105.59   # decaying slowly
CPU usage: 27.6% user, 23.0% sys, 49.92% idle
PhysMem: 18G used, 5338M unused
gitnexus mcp left: 0
```

A later clean check showed no real `gitnexus/dist/cli/index.js mcp` processes and the remaining Node processes were normal Cursor language servers near 0% CPU.

## RCA / suspected failure mode

I checked current upstream source and GitNexus does have normal cleanup hooks in `gitnexus/src/mcp/server.ts`:

- `SIGINT` / `SIGTERM` handlers
- `process.stdin.on('end', shutdown)`
- `stdin` / `stdout` error handlers
- fatal `uncaughtException` shutdown
- shutdown calls `backend.disconnect()`, `server.close()`, then exits

`LocalBackend.disconnect()` also closes LadybugDB connections.

However, the observed leaked processes had `PPID 1`, meaning the original parent exited and macOS `launchd` adopted them. That suggests one of these paths is failing:

1. The MCP child is not receiving `SIGTERM` when Cursor/Claude/pnpm exits.
2. `stdin end` is not firing or stdin remains open after the parent chain dies.
3. `pnpm exec` may introduce a parent/child lifecycle where the actual Node process survives client disconnect.
4. There is no parent-PID watchdog / orphan self-reaper, so once adopted by PID 1 the MCP server can continue forever.

## Suggested fix direction

Consider adding an MCP orphan guard in addition to stdio/signal cleanup, for example:

- Capture parent PID at startup.
- Periodically check whether `process.ppid === 1` or the original parent no longer exists.
- If the MCP server is a stdio server and becomes orphaned, call the same shutdown path.
- Optionally log a warning before exit.

This would make shutdown robust even when the editor, agent runtime, or package-manager wrapper fails to propagate signals/stdio closure.

title: Documented Docker workflow (`gitnexus index /workspace/<repo>` on `:ro` mount) is broken in two places
body:
## Summary

The README's documented "Make repos on your host machine indexable" Docker workflow is broken in two distinct ways. Both bugs together mean that the literal command shown in the README cannot be executed end-to-end against the published image.

## Reproduction (deterministic, 100% from clean state)

```bash
# Clean slate
rm -rf .gitnexus ~/.gitnexus
docker compose down -v

# Step 1 of the documented workflow (host-side analyze)
npx -y gitnexus@1.6.5-rc.19 analyze
# → succeeds, creates ./.gitnexus/ + ~/.gitnexus/registry.json

# Step 2 of the documented workflow (bring up stack with read-only workspace)
WORKSPACE_DIR="$PWD" \
  SERVER_IMAGE=ghcr.io/abhigyanpatwari/gitnexus:1.6.5-rc.19 \
  docker compose up -d
docker inspect gitnexus-server --format \
  '{{range .Mounts}}{{if eq .Destination "/workspace"}}{{.Destination}}: mode={{.Mode}} RW={{.RW}}{{end}}{{end}}'
# → /workspace: mode=ro RW=false   (matches .env.example "Optional read-only mount")

# Step 3 — the README's literal command:
docker compose exec gitnexus-server gitnexus index /workspace
# → exec: "gitnexus": executable file not found in $PATH

# Workaround for the PATH bug:
docker compose exec gitnexus-server node /app/gitnexus/dist/cli/index.js index /workspace
# → Error: EROFS: read-only file system,
#   open '/workspace/.gitnexus/.gitignore'
#     at async ensureGitNexusIgnored (file:///app/gitnexus/dist/storage/repo-manager.js:209:5)
#     at async indexCommand (file:///app/gitnexus/dist/cli/index-repo.js:99:5)
```

Same outcome on the latest stable image (`ghcr.io/abhigyanpatwari/gitnexus:latest` = v1.6.4, built 2026-05-10).

## Bug A — `gitnexus` is not on `PATH` inside the published image

The README documents:

```
docker compose exec gitnexus-server gitnexus index /workspace/my-repo
```

But `which gitnexus` inside the container is empty:

```bash
$ docker compose exec gitnexus-server sh -c 'echo $PATH; which gitnexus || echo MISSING'
/usr/local/sbin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/sbin:/usr/bin:/sbin:/bin
MISSING
```

Root cause: `Dockerfile.cli` does `npm prune --omit=dev` (line 37) after the builder stage, which removes `node_modules/.bin/` entries. Nothing in the runtime stage symlinks `gitnexus` onto `PATH` or adds `/app/gitnexus/node_modules/.bin` to `PATH`. The container's `CMD` works because the Dockerfile invokes Node directly:

```dockerfile
CMD ["node", "gitnexus/dist/cli/index.js", "serve", "--host", "0.0.0.0", "--port", "4747"]
```

But users typing the literal README command get `exec: "gitnexus": executable file not found in $PATH`.

## Bug B — `gitnexus index` writes to `/workspace`, breaking the documented `:ro` mount

Even with the PATH bug worked around, `gitnexus index /workspace` fails on the read-only workspace mount that the README and `.env.example` both document:

```
/workspace: mode=ro RW=false
```

Stack:

```
EROFS: read-only file system, open '/workspace/.gitnexus/.gitignore'
  at async ensureGitNexusIgnored (gitnexus/src/storage/repo-manager.ts:287)
  at async indexCommand (gitnexus/src/cli/index-repo.ts:118)
```

Root cause:

1. `getStoragePath(repoPath)` (`gitnexus/src/storage/repo-manager.ts:138`) returns `path.resolve(repoPath) + '/.gitnexus'`. The path is hardcoded — `GITNEXUS_HOME` is the **global registry** dir, not the per-repo storage dir, so there's no env-var escape hatch.

2. `ensureGitNexusIgnored` (`gitnexus/src/storage/repo-manager.ts:287`) unconditionally `fs.writeFile`s `<repoPath>/.gitnexus/.gitignore` and (via `ensureGitInfoExclude`) `<repoPath>/.git/info/exclude`. There's no skip-if-already-correct fast path and no tolerance for `EROFS`/`EACCES`.

3. `indexCommand` (`gitnexus/src/cli/index-repo.ts:118`) calls `ensureGitNexusIgnored(repoPath)` AFTER `registerRepo`, so the global-registry write succeeds (entry is visible in `/api/repos`) but the gitignore-write fails the whole command with a non-zero exit.

This is a regression from PR #1248 ("fix(cli): keep GitNexus ignores inside .gitnexus", merged 2026-05-01). That PR intentionally moved the gitignore write from the user's root `.gitignore` to `<repo>/.gitnexus/.gitignore` — sensible — but didn't cover the documented Docker workflow where `<repo>` lives on a `:ro` bind mount. The PR's test plan covered analyze + index unit/integration tests, not container exec against a read-only workspace.

## Proposed fix

Two small, self-contained PRs:

1. **Tolerate read-only filesystems in `ensureGitNexusIgnored`.**
   Skip the write when the file already exists with the correct content; if it doesn't and the FS is read-only, downgrade to a warning instead of throwing. Preserves the safety intent on writable mounts while fixing the documented Docker path. Will send as a PR.

2. **Expose `gitnexus` on `PATH` in the published image.**
   Add a symlink (`/usr/local/bin/gitnexus -> /app/gitnexus/dist/cli/index.js` with shebang) or extend `PATH` in `Dockerfile.cli` so the README's literal command works. Will send as a separate PR.

Happy to take feedback on the shape of either before opening the PRs if you'd prefer a different approach (e.g. surfacing a `--no-gitignore` flag instead of catching EROFS).

## Versions

- Image: `ghcr.io/abhigyanpatwari/gitnexus:1.6.5-rc.19` (also reproduced on `:latest` = v1.6.4)
- Host CLI: `npx gitnexus@1.6.5-rc.19` (Node v20.20.2 host, EBADENGINE warning is benign)
- docker compose v2.40.x; Docker engine 28.x; Ubuntu 24.04 LTS host
- `docker-compose.yaml` at repo HEAD `8083c39f`

title: fix(cli): tolerate read-only workspace in `ensureGitNexusIgnored` (#1549)
body:
## Summary

Fixes the documented Docker workflow described in issue #1549: `gitnexus index /workspace/<repo>` against a `:ro` bind mount (per `.env.example` "Optional read-only mount" + the README example) currently fails with `EROFS: read-only file system, open '/workspace/.gitnexus/.gitignore'`.

Root cause is a regression introduced by PR #1248 ("fix(cli): keep GitNexus ignores inside .gitnexus"). That PR — intentionally and correctly — moved the gitignore write out of the user's root `.gitignore` and into `<repo>/.gitnexus/.gitignore`. The new code unconditionally writes that path inside the workspace, which fails on a read-only bind mount even when the host has already created an identical file during a prior `analyze`.

## What this PR does

Two complementary changes inside `ensureGitNexusIgnored` and `ensureGitInfoExclude`:

1. **Idempotent fast path** — read the existing `.gitnexus/.gitignore` content first; if it already matches the desired value (`*\n`), skip the write entirely. This covers the common Docker workflow case (host did `analyze`, container does `index`).

2. **`EROFS`/`EACCES` tolerance** — when a write is genuinely needed but the filesystem refuses it, log a structured `logger.warn(...)` via the existing `pino` logger and continue. `registerRepo` runs before `ensureGitNexusIgnored` in `indexCommand`, so the global-registry write is already committed when we get here; letting the gitignore failure propagate leaves the user with a registered-but-error-exited command (visible in `/api/repos`, but `gitnexus index` exits non-zero — confusing).

Both code paths still write on a normal writable filesystem and still produce the same content as before. Behaviour only changes for the read-only / permission-denied case.

## Test plan

- `cd gitnexus && npx tsc --noEmit` — clean.
- `cd gitnexus && npx vitest run test/unit/repo-manager.test.ts` — `PASS (61) FAIL (0)`. Three new tests cover idempotent fast-path and `:ro` parent dir (simulated via `chmod 0o555`).
- `cd gitnexus && npx vitest run test/unit/index-repo-command.test.ts` — `PASS (11) FAIL (0)`.
- `cd gitnexus && npx vitest run test/unit/run-analyze.test.ts` — `PASS (18) FAIL (0)`.
- `npx prettier --check gitnexus/src/storage/repo-manager.ts gitnexus/test/unit/repo-manager.test.ts` — clean.

Reproducer for the Docker workflow itself (verified before/after the fix):

```bash
# Before this PR — fails with EROFS:
rm -rf .gitnexus ~/.gitnexus
docker compose down -v
npx -y gitnexus@1.6.5-rc.19 analyze
WORKSPACE_DIR="$PWD" SERVER_IMAGE=ghcr.io/abhigyanpatwari/gitnexus:1.6.5-rc.19 \
  docker compose up -d
docker compose exec gitnexus-server node /app/gitnexus/dist/cli/index.js index /workspace
# → Error: EROFS: read-only file system,
#   open '/workspace/.gitnexus/.gitignore'

# After this PR (built locally from the branch), the same command exits 0
# and the repo is registered cleanly in the global registry inside the
# named volume.
```

## Notes

- The companion `gitnexus` PATH issue from #1549 is the subject of a separate, smaller PR — I kept the two changes apart so each can be reviewed/reverted on its own.
- No public CLI/MCP contract changes. The behaviour for writable workspaces (the host-side `analyze` workflow) is byte-identical to before.

Closes #1549 (in conjunction with the Dockerfile.cli `PATH` PR).

title: fix(docker): symlink `gitnexus` binary onto $PATH in runtime image (#1549)
body:
## Summary

Fixes one of the two bugs reported in #1549: the documented Docker workflow command

```
docker compose exec gitnexus-server gitnexus index /workspace/my-repo
```

currently fails with `exec: "gitnexus": executable file not found in $PATH`. This PR adds a single symlink in the runtime stage of `Dockerfile.cli` so the command works as written.

## Mechanism

`gitnexus/package.json` declares `"bin": { "gitnexus": "dist/cli/index.js" }`. In a normal `npm install` that exposes `node_modules/.bin/gitnexus` and (if installed globally) `/usr/local/bin/gitnexus`. But the builder stage runs `npm prune --omit=dev --prefix gitnexus` (Dockerfile.cli line 37), which strips `node_modules/.bin/` entries, and nothing in the runtime stage re-adds the `gitnexus` name to `$PATH`. The container's own `CMD` works because the Dockerfile invokes Node directly:

```dockerfile
CMD ["node", "gitnexus/dist/cli/index.js", "serve", ...]
```

…but anyone following the README has no way to know that without reading the Dockerfile.

`dist/cli/index.js` already carries `#!/usr/bin/env node` and 755 perms, so a single symlink into `/usr/local/bin` is the minimal fix.

## Test plan

```bash
docker build -f Dockerfile.cli -t gitnexus:local-pr-test .

# Symlink + version (was: "executable file not found in $PATH")
docker run --rm gitnexus:local-pr-test which gitnexus
# → /usr/local/bin/gitnexus
docker run --rm gitnexus:local-pr-test gitnexus --version
# → 1.6.4
docker run --rm gitnexus:local-pr-test gitnexus --help | head -2
# → Usage: gitnexus [options] [command]

# CMD path unchanged
docker run --rm -d --name t gitnexus:local-pr-test
sleep 4
docker exec t curl -s localhost:4747/api/health
# → {"status":"ok"}
```

Both verified locally.

title: parse-cache save can fail with "Invalid string length" on large incremental runs
body:
## Bug Description
On a large repository, `gitnexus analyze --index-only` can complete successfully but fail to persist `parse-cache.json` with:

```text
Warning: could not save parse cache (Invalid string length); continuing.
```

This leaves incremental metadata available in `meta.json`, but no persisted parse cache for subsequent runs.

## Reproduction Steps
1. Run incremental indexing on a sufficiently large repository:
   ```bash
   gitnexus analyze --index-only
   ```
2. Observe a successful index completion with a warning during parse-cache persistence.
3. Check the `.gitnexus` directory and note that `meta.json` exists, while `parse-cache.json` may be absent.

## Expected Behavior
- Parse cache should be persisted successfully after a completed run.
- Large repositories should not lose parse-cache persistence due to serialization size.
- If the cache is too large for the current storage format, the tool should either shard it, stream it, or fail in a more actionable way.

## Actual Behavior
```text
$ gitnexus analyze --index-only

  GitNexus Analyzer

  GITNEXUS_MAX_FILE_SIZE: effective threshold 5120KB (default 512KB)

Incremental: changed=63, added=0, deleted=9 (skipping wipe + 4029 unchanged file rows preserved)
Incremental: +420 importer(s) added to writable set (BFS depth ≤ 4)
Warning: could not save parse cache (Invalid string length); continuing.
  ████████████████████████████████████████ 100% | Done

  Repository indexed successfully (2880.5s)

  43,682 nodes | 123,197 edges | 1119 clusters | 231 flows
```

## Investigation / Suspected Cause
From reading the current implementation:

- `runFullAnalysis` treats parse-cache persistence as best-effort and continues on failure.
- `saveParseCache` serializes the entire cache in one shot using `JSON.stringify(...)`.
- Cache entries store raw `ParseWorkerResult[]`, which can contain large payloads including `parsedFiles`, scopes, bindings, nodes, relationships, imports, calls, and related structures.
- This looks consistent with a monolithic serialization / string allocation limit rather than missing incremental support.

In other words, the failure seems to be caused by the current cache format/layout:
- one large `parse-cache.json`
- one full-cache materialization in memory
- one full `JSON.stringify(...)`

## Suggested Direction
Possible fixes, in increasing scope:
1. Shard the parse cache by `chunkHash` rather than storing everything in a single file.
2. Avoid whole-cache `JSON.stringify(...)` in one allocation.
3. Consider a more compact per-entry format (for example MessagePack/CBOR, optionally with compression).
4. Add metrics/logging around cache entry count and serialized size before save, so failures are easier to diagnose.

## Additional Notes
This does **not** appear to be a language-specific “incremental indexing is unsupported” issue. The more likely problem is parse-cache persistence blowing up on large payloads.

title: gitnexus analyze crashes with malloc corruption during default FTS extension path
body:
## Summary

`gitnexus analyze .` can crash during analysis with a native allocator error when using the default extension behavior. Re-running the same analysis with LadybugDB extension installation disabled succeeds, which suggests the failure is tied to the optional FTS/vector extension install/load path rather than repository parsing itself.

## Environment

- GitNexus: `1.6.4`
- Node.js: `v24.15.0`
- OS: `linux/x64`
- ONNX: `1.26.0`

`gitnexus doctor` reported:

```text
Graph store:      available
Full-text search: available
VECTOR index:     available
Semantic mode:    vector-index
```

## Failing Command

```bash
gitnexus analyze .
```

## Error

The analyzer starts, then prints:

```text
GitNexus Analyzer

malloc(): largebin double linked list corrupted (nextsize)
```

The process then hangs for a while and exits unsuccessfully.

## Workaround

This succeeds:

```bash
GITNEXUS_LBUG_EXTENSION_INSTALL=never gitnexus analyze . --skip-agents-md --name sanitized-repo
```

It prints:

```text
GitNexus: FTS extension unavailable; continuing without FTS features. extension install policy is "never"
Repository indexed successfully
```

## Expected Behavior

If FTS/vector extension install or load fails, `analyze` should degrade gracefully, as documented, rather than crashing with native memory corruption.

## Notes

This looks related in spirit to previous native crash/FTS initialization issues, but I did not find an exact open issue for this allocator error on `1.6.4` with LadybugDB.

title: fix: parse cache persistence fails on large repos with Invalid string length
body:
### Summary

`gitnexus analyze` can fail to persist the parse cache on large repositories with:

```text
Warning: could not save parse cache (Invalid string length); continuing.
```

When this happens, incremental analyze falls back to a much heavier path on every run because the parse cache never reaches disk.

### Environment

- GitNexus: `1.6.5-rc.19`
- OS: Windows 11 x64
- Node: `v24.14.0`
- Repo shape: large mixed-language monorepo

### Reproduction

On a large repo, run `gitnexus analyze .` or `gitnexus analyze --force .`.

Observed output:

```text
Warning: could not save parse cache (Invalid string length); continuing.
```

After the run completes successfully, there is no parse cache file on disk, so the next incremental analyze still reparses far more than expected.

### Root Cause

`saveParseCache()` currently serializes the entire cache as one huge JSON string:

- `entries: Object.fromEntries(cache.entries)`
- `JSON.stringify(out, mapReplacer)`

On large repositories, each cache value stores a full `ParseWorkerResult[]`, including heavy `parsedFiles` / scopes / type binding structures. The final single JSON string can exceed V8 string or contiguous allocation limits and throws `Invalid string length`.

### Proposed Fix

Store the parse cache in a sharded format instead of one giant JSON file.

Example layout:

```text
.gitnexus/parse-cache/
  index.json
  <chunk-hash>.json
  <chunk-hash>.json
  ...
```

- `index.json` stores `version` and the chunk key list
- each chunk file stores one `ParseWorkerResult[]`
- `loadParseCache()` remains backward compatible by falling back to the legacy single-file `parse-cache.json` if the sharded directory is absent

### Validation

I patched my local install with a sharded save/load implementation and validated:

1. round-trip of `Map` / `Set` payloads still works
2. legacy single-file cache can still be loaded
3. real repository now persists parse cache successfully
4. the warning disappears

On my repo, incremental analyze time changed from:

- before fix: `908.9s`
- after sharded cache was generated and reused: `419.4s`

So this does not solve every incremental-cost problem, but it does fix the broken parse-cache persistence path and gives a large improvement on repeated runs.

### Notes

I can open a PR with the source-level change if this direction looks acceptable.

Tracking issue for the C++ scope-resolution gaps that PR #1520 (`cpp-scope-resolution-parity`) intentionally left out of scope. Parent: #935 (LANG-cpp migration). Related: #909 (RFC scope resolution). > **Status (verified 2026-05-16 against `main` @ f28185d6):** 12 of 14 checklist bullets are **done on `main`**. The two remaining bullets are in flight as [#1578](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/issues/1578) / PR [#1606](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/pull/1606) and [#1579](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/issues/1579) / PR [#1623](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/pull/1623). Local verification: `REGISTRY_PRIMARY_CPP=1 npx vitest run test/integration/resolvers/cpp.test.ts` — **215/215** on `main`, **218/218** on PR #1606, **220/220** on PR #1623. ## Context PR #1520 plus its follow-up work shipped the C++ scope-resolution path as a **scope-aware approximation** of ISO C++ name lookup. Integration tests pass under `REGISTRY_PRIMARY_CPP=1`, but several documented divergences from full ISO semantics remain (see open bullets below). Each item below is independently scoped. Completed items are checked off with links to the sub-issue or merge PR. --- ## ISO C++ conformance posture GitNexus's C++ resolver is **not an ISO-conforming C++ front-end**. It is a **graph-safe under-approximation** of ISO C++ name lookup with a clear failure-mode preference: > When in doubt, **suppress** (emit zero edges) rather than **guess** (emit a possibly-wrong edge). This matters for downstream consumers (impact analysis, refactor safety, wiki) that rely on the graph not lying — false negatives are recoverable by re-reading the source; false positives silently mislead. ### Target language version The resolver targets **shared C++17 lookup/overload semantics** plus a partial **C++20 constraint posture** delivered by #1579 / PR #1623. The implementation is intentionally syntactic — no template instantiation, no constexpr evaluator. Where ISO demands richer semantics, the resolver either documents the approximation or suppresses. ### Where the resolver matches ISO (implemented on `main` @ `f28185d6`) | Rule | ISO clause | Implementation | |------|-----------|----------------| | Ordinary unqualified lookup ∪ ADL union before overload | `[basic.lookup.unqual]`, `[basic.lookup.argdep]` | `free-call-fallback.ts:107-197` (#1599 / #1576) | | ADL blocked when ordinary lookup finds a non-function or block-scope function | `[basic.lookup.argdep]` p4 | `findCallableBindingsAndAdlBlocker` (#1599) | | Class, pointer, reference, template-spec associated entities | `[basic.lookup.argdep]` p3 bullets 2/4 | #1571 / #1592, #1572 / #1595, #1573 / #1596 | | Base-class associated namespaces via MRO | `[basic.lookup.argdep]` p3 bullet 3 | `adl.ts:344` (`mroFor`) (#1574 / #1597) | | Enum-arg and hidden-friend ADL | `[basic.lookup.argdep]` p3 bullet 6, `[class.friend]` p11 | #1599 | | Inline namespace expansion in qualified + ADL lookup | `[namespace.def]` p6 | `inline-namespaces.ts` | | Inline namespace same-name ambiguity → suppress (zero edges) | `[namespace.def]` p6 + `[basic.lookup.qual]` | `'ambiguous'` sentinel (#1577 / #1600) | | Template-base `EXTENDS` capture, cross-file dependent-base resolution | `[temp.dep.type]`, `[temp.dep.candidate]` | #1567, #1568 (`populateCppDependentBases` workspace-wide) | | Template-specialization graph identity | `[temp.class.spec]` | `templateArguments` in `graph-bridge/ids.ts:103-106` (#1569) | | Two-phase lookup: | `isOverloadAmbiguousAfterNormalization` | ### Where the resolver intentionally diverges (open, tracked per-issue) Each divergence is tracked in a sub-issue with a concrete code anchor (`file:line`) and the relevant ISO clause: | Divergence | ISO clause | Tracked | |-----------|-----------|---------| | Standard-conversion-sequence ranking (`f(int)` vs `f(double)` for `f(2.5)`) | `[over.ics.rank]`, `[over.match.best]` | #1578 / PR #1606 | | Pointer / `nullptr` / ellipsis conversion ranks | `[conv.ptr]`, `[conv.fctptr]`, `[over.ics.ellipsis]` | #1637 (extends #1578) | | User-defined conversion sequence ranking | `[over.ics.user]`, `[class.conv.ctor]` | #1631 | | SFINAE / `requires` candidate filtering | `[temp.deduct.general]` p8, `[temp.constr.constr]` | #1579 / PR #1623 | | Tier-A `` predicate registry expansion | `[meta.unary.cat]`, `[meta.unary.prop]` | #1629 | | Template partial ordering | `[temp.func.order]`, `[temp.over]` | #1635 | | Operator overload resolution (`a + b`, `os << x`) | `[over.match.oper]`, `[over.binary]` | #1636 | | Strict function-type associated entities (parameter/return types, not enclosing namespace) | `[basic.lookup.argdep]` p3 bullet 5 | #1633 (replaces #1598 approximation) | | Inline-ns qualified lookup with call-site arity/types | `[basic.lookup.qual]`, `[over.match]` | #1632 | | Dependent-base resolution across namespaces / inline namespaces | `[temp.dep.type]`, `[basic.scope.namespace]` | #1634 | ### Cross-cutting limitations - **cv/ref/pointer marker loss** — `normalizeCppParamType` strips `[&*]+` and Tracked as #1630; blocks #1629 and #1637. - **Structured suppression diagnostics** — suppressed calls return bare `undefined` / `'ambiguous'` without `{ kind, reason, candidateIds }`. Downstream cannot distinguish ADL-blocked, normalization-collision, constraint-unmodeled, etc. Tracked as #1638. --- ## Documentation / labeling ### [x] Rename "C++ parity" → "scope-aware C++ resolver with known gaps" Done in #1566. --- ## Template support ### [x] Add `base_class_clause` heritage emitter for template_type bases Done in #1567. ### [x] Cross-file dependent-base name resolution Done in #1568 (`populateCppDependentBases` now uses a workspace-wide class index). ### [x] Template-specialization disambiguation Done in #1569 (`templateArguments` fingerprints in graph IDs / lookup). ### [x] Positive resolution inside template bodies Done in #1570 and follow-up #1590 (`this->` + `using ns::name` in template bodies). --- ## ADL (V2 closure rules) ### [x] Pointer-type unwrapping — #1571 / #1592 ### [x] Reference-type unwrapping — #1572 / #1595 ### [x] Class-template-specialization associated namespaces — #1573 / #1596 ### [x] Base-class associated namespaces — #1574 / #1597 ### [x] Function-pointer argument associated entities — #1575 / #1598 (GitNexus approximation: free-function reference contributes enclosing namespace) ### [x] Merge ADL with non-empty ordinary lookup — #1576 / #1599 --- ## Inline namespace ### [x] Same-name ambiguity across multiple inline children Done in #1577 / #1600 (`'ambiguous'` sentinel in `inline-namespaces.ts`). --- ## Overload resolution ### [x] Full standard-conversion-sequence ranking **Open:** #1578 — PR [#1606](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/pull/1606) (`cppConversionRank`, primitive exact/promotion/conversion ranks). Follow-ups tracked separately (see below). --- ## Follow-up (ISO review gaps — not blocking #1578 / #1579) ### In flight (open PRs) - [x] #1578 — PR [#1606](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/pull/1606) (**rebase required:** branch is behind `main` and would revert #1600 inline-namespace ambiguity handling) - [x] #1579 — PR [#1623](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/pull/1623) ### Post-merge / incremental (from external ISO C++ review audit, 2026-05-16) - [x] Expand SFINAE `type_traits` predicate registry — #1629 - [x] Type-class sidecar for `normalizeCppParamType` (cv/ref/pointer) — #1630 - [x] User-defined conversion sequence ranking — #1631 - [x] Inline-namespace qualified lookup: thread call-site types + conversion rank (`outer::foo(42)` false negative on `main`) — #1632 - [x] Strict ISO function-type ADL (replace #1598 enclosing-namespace approximation) — #1633 - [x] Dependent-base resolution V2 (cross-namespace / inline-namespace) — #1634 - [x] Template partial ordering — #1635 - [x] Overloaded operator call resolution — #1636 - [x] Pointer / `nullptr` / ellipsis conversion ranks (extends #1578) — #1637 - [x] Structured suppression diagnostics (`ResolutionOutcome`) — #1638 ### Sub-issue dependency graph GitHub `blocked_by` dependencies were set 2026-05-16. Backporting is intentionally out of scope. The scope-resolver path is correctness-authoritative; legacy is maintained only for the `REGISTRY_PRIMARY_CPP=0` parity gate. - `does NOT resolve unqualified save() to User::save via #include` - `does NOT resolve unqualified foo() to ns::foo via #include` - `emits zero CALLS edges when process(int)/process(long) collide after normalization` - `emits zero CALLS edges for ambiguous foo() bound via two using-namespace declarations` - `Derived::g() -> f() does NOT bind to Base::f (dependent base)` - `record(p) where p is audit::Event* emits zero CALLS — V1 ADL excludes pointer args` - `process(t, 42) emits zero CALLS edges when ADL surfaces process(Token,int)/process(Token,long) (collide after C++ int normalization)` - `outer::foo() resolves to outer::v1::foo (inline child), NOT outer::v0::foo` - `Base::method() does NOT mis-route to a class method outside the MRO` - `unqualified f() inside Derived::g() does NOT bind to outer::v1::Base::f (dependent base across inline namespace)` --- ## How to ship a unit 1. Pick a bullet, comment to claim it. 2. The cpp resolver state lives in five module files: - `cpp/scope-resolver.ts` — the contract implementation - `cpp/captures.ts` — capture-time tree-sitter walks - `cpp/file-local-linkage.ts` — file-local + non-globally-visible state - `cpp/two-phase-lookup.ts` — dependent-base detection - `cpp/adl.ts` — Koenig lookup - `cpp/inline-namespaces.ts` — inline-namespace state 3. All per-pipeline state is cleared in `loadResolutionConfig` — add a `clearX()` call there if you introduce new module-level state. 4. Each fix ships with at least one positive and one negative fixture under `gitnexus/test/fixtures/lang-resolution/`. The Definition of Done forbids bounds-only assertions — use exact `.toBe(N)` / `.toEqual(...)`. 5. Run both modes before opening a PR: - `npx vitest run test/integration/resolvers/cpp.test.ts` (registry-primary) - `REGISTRY_PRIMARY_CPP=0 npx vitest run test/integration/resolvers/cpp.test.ts` (legacy parity) 6. Add new negative-only assertions to `LEGACY_RESOLVER_PARITY_EXPECTED_FAILURES.cpp` if legacy cannot satisfy them. ## Reference - PR #1520 (migration baseline) - Scope-resolution contract: `gitnexus/src/core/ingestion/scope-resolution/contract/scope-resolver.ts` - ISO C++ working draft / cppreference: clause anchors cited per-section above; sub-issue bodies (#1629–#1638) carry the concrete code anchors and ISO references
