title: Speed up scope-resolution reference resolving by replacing Step 2 owner-member scans with owner-keyed lookup
body:
### Area

gitnexus (CLI / core / indexing / MCP server)

### Problem or opportunity

I spent some time profiling indexing on a fairly large C# repository locally, and the biggest remaining bottleneck is the scope-resolution `resolve` stage.

On a warm run, almost all of the time was going into receiver/MRO-based member lookup in Step 2. The hot path was:

- `runScopeResolution(...)`
- `resolveReferenceSites(...)`
- `lookupForSite(...)`
- `lookupCore(...)`
- `walkReceiverTypeBinding(...)`
- `collectOwnedMembers(...)`

The main problem is that `collectOwnedMembers(...)` scans `ctx.defs.byId.values()` for every `(ownerDefId, memberName)` lookup. On a large repo, that becomes very expensive very quickly.

The local profiler numbers on the large repo looked like this before the change:
- `extract=262ms`
- `finalize=141990ms`
- `propagate=1050ms`
- `resolve=1444496ms`
- `emit=45859ms`
- `total=1633658ms`

The most important part there is the `resolve` bucket: about `24 minutes` spent almost entirely in Step 2 owner/member lookup.

The detailed profiler output pointed to the same thing:

- `ownedScan=1430237ms`
- `defsAvg=64511`
- `sites=848578`
- `registryCalls=1144544`
 
That strongly suggests the dominant cost is not ranking or arity filtering, but repeated full-definition scans inside the Step 2 lookup path.

### Proposed solution

Replace the Step 2 owner-member full scan with an owner-keyed lookup backed by the existing semantic-model registries.

Concretely, the narrow fix is:

- add an optional owner-keyed member lookup hook to `RegistryContext`
- thread that hook through `resolveReferenceSites(...)`
- supply it from `runScopeResolution(...)` using the already-existing:
  - `methods.lookupAllByOwner(...)`
  - `fields.lookupFieldByOwner(...)`
- update `collectOwnedMembers(...)` to use that hook first
- keep the current full-scan behavior as a compatibility fallback when the hook is not present

The reason I like this approach is that it stays very local to the real hotspot. It does not require a shared-core redesign, and it does not change the public lookup flow more than necessary.

On the same large repo, this dropped the scope-resolution timings to roughly:

- `extract=205ms`
- `finalize=101891ms`
- `propagate=692ms`
- `resolve=1480ms`
- `emit=24912ms`
- `total=129180ms`

So in practical terms, it turned scope-resolution from roughly `~27 minutes down to ~2 minutes`, and the resolve hotspot itself from roughly `~24 minutes to ~1.5 seconds`.

That is the main reason I think this is worth landing as a focused optimization.

I already have the patch implemented and validated locally, and I can open a PR for review.

For context: while validating parity on a large C# repo, I also uncovered a separate C# using import-resolution issue in the registry-primary path. I do **not** think that should be part of this PR. I’d prefer to keep this issue/PR strictly about the Step 2 performance optimization so it stays reviewable and low-risk.

Local patch scope is limited to:

- `gitnexus-shared/src/scope-resolution/registries/context.ts`
- `gitnexus-shared/src/scope-resolution/registries/lookup-core.ts`
- `gitnexus/src/core/ingestion/resolve-references.ts`
- `gitnexus/src/core/ingestion/scope-resolution/pipeline/run.ts`
- `gitnexus/test/unit/scope-resolution/registries.test.ts`

title: perf(scope-resolution): use owner-keyed lookup for Step 2 member resolution
body:
## Summary
- replace Step 2 owner/member full-definition scans with owner-keyed lookups on the scope-resolution resolve path
- keep the compatibility fallback when the owner-keyed lookup is not supplied
- add focused coverage for Step 2 registry behavior and `resolveReferenceSites` threading

Closes #1656.

## Motivation / context
On a large real-world repository, scope-resolution reference resolving was dominated by Step 2 receiver/MRO member lookup. Profiling showed `collectOwnedMembers(...)` repeatedly scanning the full definition set inside the hottest path. This change reuses the existing owner-keyed semantic-model registries instead of rescanning all defs for every `(owner, memberName)` lookup.

The intent of this PR is narrow: land the performance improvement only. It does **not** include the later C# import-parity experiment that changed `IMPORTS|csharp-scope: using` behavior.

## Areas touched
- `gitnexus-shared/src/index.ts`
- `gitnexus-shared/src/scope-resolution/registries/context.ts`
- `gitnexus-shared/src/scope-resolution/registries/lookup-core.ts`
- `gitnexus/src/core/ingestion/resolve-references.ts`
- `gitnexus/src/core/ingestion/scope-resolution/pipeline/run.ts`
- `gitnexus/test/unit/scope-resolution/registries.test.ts`
- `gitnexus/test/unit/scope-resolution/resolve-references.test.ts`

## Scope & constraints
### In scope
- add an optional owner-keyed lookup hook to `RegistryContext`
- thread that hook through `resolveReferenceSites(...)`
- supply the hook from `runScopeResolution(...)` using the authoritative method/field registries already present on the semantic model
- preserve the old full-scan fallback for compatibility

### Out of scope
- C# import-target parity changes
- compare-lbug tooling
- broader shared scope-resolution redesign
- follow-up finalize-stage optimization work

## Implementation notes
- `collectOwnedMembers(...)` now prefers an injected `ownedMembersByOwner(ownerDefId, memberName)` lookup and falls back to scanning `ctx.defs.byId.values()` only when that hook is absent.
- `resolveReferenceSites(...)` accepts and passes through the optional owner-keyed hook in `RegistryContext`.
- `runScopeResolution(...)` supplies the hook from `readonlyModel.methods.lookupAllByOwner(...)` and `readonlyModel.fields.lookupFieldByOwner(...)`.
- Tests cover three important behaviors:
  - hook-provided method resolution for Step 2
  - overload arrays still flowing through existing arity filtering
  - field/property resolution through accepted-kind filtering
- Added focused `resolveReferenceSites` tests to pin both hook-threaded behavior and the compatibility fallback.

## Testing & verification
Validated locally with:
- `npm run build` in `gitnexus-shared`
- `npm test -- test/unit/scope-resolution/resolve-references.test.ts`
- `npm test -- test/unit/scope-resolution/registries.test.ts`
- `npm test -- test/unit/scope-resolution/reconcile-ownership.test.ts`
- `npm test -- test/unit/scope-resolution/workspace-index.test.ts`
- `npm test -- test/unit/scope-resolution/emit-references.test.ts`
- `npx tsc --noEmit`

Observed impact on a large repository before the later C# parity experiment:
- scope-resolution total dropped from roughly ~27 minutes to ~2 minutes
- the `resolve` bucket dropped from ~24 minutes to ~1.5 seconds

## Risk & rollout
Main risk is semantic parity on the Step 2 lookup path. The change is intentionally constrained to reuse the same authoritative registries already used elsewhere in scope-resolution, and it retains the old scan fallback when no owner-keyed lookup is supplied.

The current worktree comparison on a TypeScript project matched exactly. The separate C# import-edge drift investigation is intentionally excluded from this PR.

## Checklist
- [x] Narrow, issue-scoped change
- [x] Focused tests added/updated
- [x] Typecheck passes
- [x] Compatibility fallback preserved
- [x] No C# parity experiment included in this PR

title: MCP repo resolution silently picks first duplicate-name worktree sibling
body:
## Summary

When multiple indexed repositories share the same registry `name` (common with a main checkout plus Claude Code/git worktrees), MCP tool calls with `repo: \"<name>\"` can silently resolve to the first matching repo instead of failing as ambiguous or preferring the current working directory's matching worktree.

This caused `detect_changes` to report `No changes detected` for an active worktree PR even though the worktree was indexed and had a diff against `master`. Passing the absolute worktree path as `repo` worked correctly.

## Repro shape

1. Index the canonical checkout and a linked worktree for the same remote.
2. `list_repos` shows two entries with the same `name` and different `path` values:
   - `/path/to/repo`
   - `/path/to/repo/.claude/worktrees/feature-branch`
3. From inside the worktree, call:
   ```json
   detect_changes({"scope":"compare","base_ref":"master...HEAD","repo":"repo-name"})
   ```
4. The call resolves to the main checkout entry and can return `No changes detected` or analyze the wrong index.
5. Calling with the absolute worktree path works:
   ```json
   detect_changes({"scope":"compare","base_ref":"master...HEAD","repo":"/path/to/repo/.claude/worktrees/feature-branch"})
   ```

## What I found in code/docs

- `list_repos` already exposes sibling entries for matching `remoteUrl`, so GitNexus can see both the main checkout and worktree.
- `repo-manager.ts` has `RegistryAmbiguousTargetError` with an actionable absolute-path hint for duplicate registry names.
- But MCP `LocalBackend.resolveRepoFromCache()` currently loops over `this.repos.values()` and returns the first case-insensitive `handle.name` match. That means duplicate-name entries are not treated as ambiguous in MCP tool calls.
- The guide/impact-analysis docs say `repo` can be a repository name or path, but do not warn that duplicate-name worktree siblings require an absolute path.

## Expected behavior

Any of these would prevent silent wrong-repo analysis:

1. If `repo` matches multiple handles by `name`, return an ambiguity error listing paths and instructing the caller to use an absolute path.
2. Prefer the registered repo whose path contains / equals the MCP server cwd's git toplevel when there are duplicate-name sibling worktrees.
3. Expose stable repo IDs in `list_repos` and document using those for MCP calls.
4. Update generated GitNexus guide / skills to warn: in worktree workflows, pass the absolute worktree path as `repo` when duplicate names appear in `list_repos`.

## Why it matters

This failure mode is easy for agents to miss: all tools return valid-looking output, but from the wrong checkout. For pre-commit / PR impact analysis, a false `No changes detected` is worse than an explicit ambiguity error.

## Workaround

Use the absolute worktree path as the `repo` parameter for MCP calls:

```json
{"repo":"/absolute/path/to/worktree"}
```

title: Python: cross-module CALLS edges drop for non-aliased `from X import Y` patterns (regression-shaped against #337/#417)
body:
## Summary

In a 680-file Python codebase, GitNexus indexes call/import edges for same-file callers correctly but **misses the vast majority of cross-module CALLS edges** for the most common Python import pattern: bare `from X import Y` followed by a direct call to `Y()` in another module.

This shows up as `impact --direction upstream` and `context` returning `direct: 1` for functions that grep shows have 5–6+ callers across modules. Risk verdicts are LOW for functions that are actually load-bearing across cron, routers, and services.

Loosely related to #337 (Python repos produce 0 CALLS edges — fixed) and #417 (Python aliased imports missing — fixed). This case is the **non-aliased** variant of #417: no `as` rename, just `from services.X import Y` and `await Y(...)` in a different module.

## Environment

- GitNexus: **1.6.4-rc.32** (npm `latest` is 1.6.5 at time of report; I have not validated against 1.6.5 yet — pasting the rc.32 result because that's what teams have installed today)
- Node: v22 on Windows 11
- Repository: 680 Python files (~140K LOC backend), 2892 total File nodes, indexed at commit `135680c`
- Index stats after `npx gitnexus analyze`: 66,710 nodes / 100,071 edges / 1,077 clusters / 300 flows

## Reproduction

### Setup

```python
# backend/services/amazon_sync.py:2580
async def _sync_amazon_sales_impl(org_id: str, user_id: str, days_back: int, store_id: str, store: dict):
    ...

# backend/services/amazon_sync.py:4489
async def sync_amazon_sales_internal(org_id: str, user_id: str, store_id: str = None):
    ...
    result = await _sync_amazon_sales_impl(...)  # same-file call

# backend/routers/cron.py:31
from services.amazon_sync import (
    _sync_amazon_sales_impl,
    sync_amazon_inventory_internal,
    sync_amazon_sales_internal,
    ...
)

# backend/routers/cron.py:945, 1947, 1970
await _sync_amazon_sales_impl(org_id, owner_id, days_back=..., store_id=store_id, store=store)

# backend/routers/sync.py:28
from services.amazon_sync import ..., _sync_amazon_sales_impl

# backend/routers/sync.py:1407
return await _sync_amazon_sales_impl(org_id, user_id, days_back, resolved_store_id, store)
```

### Query

```bash
npx gitnexus impact "_sync_amazon_sales_impl" --direction upstream
```

### Expected

5 direct callers (3 in `cron.py`, 1 in `routers/sync.py`, 1 in same-file `sync_amazon_sales_internal`).

### Actual

```json
{
  "direction": "upstream",
  "impactedCount": 1,
  "risk": "LOW",
  "summary": { "direct": 1, "modules_affected": 1 },
  "byDepth": {
    "1": [{
      "id": "Function:backend/services/amazon_sync.py:sync_amazon_sales_internal",
      "name": "sync_amazon_sales_internal",
      "relationType": "CALLS",
      "confidence": 0.85
    }]
  }
}
```

Only the same-file caller is reported. All four cross-module callers are missing.

### Direct graph verification

```bash
npx gitnexus cypher 'MATCH (c)-[r:CodeRelation {type: "CALLS"}]->(t) WHERE t.name = "_sync_amazon_sales_impl" RETURN c.filePath, c.name'
# Returns 1 row: backend/services/amazon_sync.py | sync_amazon_sales_internal

npx gitnexus cypher 'MATCH (f1:File)-[r:CodeRelation {type: "IMPORTS"}]->(f2:File) WHERE f1.filePath = "backend/routers/cron.py" RETURN f2.filePath'
# Returns 0 rows
```

`backend/routers/cron.py` has 58 import statements (19 of which are `from services.*`) yet the graph shows **zero IMPORTS edges** out of that file. Without IMPORTS edges, the call resolver has no way to find the cross-module target.

## Severity / scope across the repo

```bash
# 680 Python files; only 350 (51%) have any IMPORTS edges
MATCH (f:File) WHERE f.filePath ENDS WITH ".py" RETURN count(*)                                # 680
MATCH (f1:File)-[:CodeRelation {type: "IMPORTS"}]->() WHERE f1.filePath ENDS WITH ".py"
  RETURN count(DISTINCT f1)                                                                    # 350

# Of 7858 total Python CALLS edges, only 1123 (14%) cross a file boundary
MATCH (c)-[:CodeRelation {type: "CALLS"}]->(t) WHERE c.filePath ENDS WITH ".py" AND t.filePath ENDS WITH ".py"
  RETURN count(*)                                                                              # 7858
MATCH (c)-[:CodeRelation {type: "CALLS"}]->(t) WHERE c.filePath ENDS WITH ".py" AND t.filePath ENDS WITH ".py"
  AND c.filePath <> t.filePath RETURN count(*)                                                 # 1123
```

For comparison, TypeScript in the same repo shows **4805 IMPORTS edges** (vs Python's 622) and the top-10 importer files are all TypeScript. The Python side is roughly 8× sparser per file.

## Impact on a real workflow

When using GitNexus to assess change-risk before editing `_sync_amazon_sales_impl` (a function called from cron entry points + a public sync endpoint + an internal wrapper that's called from preview install + sku_matching post-match), the tool returned `risk: LOW`. A grep cross-check showed 5+ direct callers, including three scheduled cron paths. **An agent that trusts the tool's verdict would edit without surfacing the actual blast radius.**

We worked around this by adding an "indexer limitation" warning to the project's V1-0 implementation spec telling agents to trust grep over `gitnexus impact` for caller counts. That's tooling friction, not a fix.

## Suspected root cause

Same shape as #337 root-cause hypothesis: `resolveCallTarget()` cannot follow `from services.X import Y` to the defining file because the IMPORTS edge isn't there. #417 fixed this for the aliased case (`from X import Y as Z`); the non-aliased case appears to still miss something — either the IMPORTS edge for the plain pattern is dropped during the worker→pipeline merge, or `resolveCallTarget()` doesn't consult the symbol table for non-aliased imports.

The plain `from services.X import Y` pattern was a deliverable on #926 (Python scope-resolution migration, closed) — so this may be a regression introduced after that landed, OR the deliverable shipped covering only `import X` and missed `from X import Y` for the non-aliased case.

## Suggested next step

Repro fixture (would be happy to PR one against `gitnexus/test/fixtures/python/`):

```
# pkg_a.py
def hello(): return "hi"

# pkg_b.py
from pkg_a import hello

def use_it():
    return hello()
```

Expected: `gitnexus impact hello --direction upstream` returns `use_it` with `depth: 1`. Actual on 1.6.4-rc.32: returns 0 callers.

Happy to validate against 1.6.5 GA + 1.6.6-rc.7 if you'd like; we held off pending input from the maintainer on the right version to test.

title: PostToolUse hook hint hardcodes `npx gitnexus`, bypassing PATH-installed wrappers
body:
## Summary

The PostToolUse Claude Code hook installed by `gitnexus setup` (`~/.claude/hooks/gitnexus/gitnexus-hook.cjs`, around line 271) hardcodes its remediation hint to `npx gitnexus analyze` instead of using a PATH-resolved `gitnexus`. When the hook fires, the surrounding agent often follows the literal hint, which bypasses any shell-function or shim wrapper the user has placed around `gitnexus`.

```js
const analyzeCmd = `npx gitnexus analyze${hadEmbeddings ? ' --embeddings' : ''}`;
sendHookResponse(
  'PostToolUse',
  `GitNexus index is stale (last indexed: ${...}). Run \`${analyzeCmd}\` to update the knowledge graph.`,
);
```

## Why this matters

Wrappers around `gitnexus` are a legitimate pattern, and `npx gitnexus …` deliberately routes around them. My concrete case:

- I keep a zsh function at `~/.config/zsh/functions/gitnexus` that injects `--skip-agents-md` on `analyze`, because the default `gitnexus analyze` run overwrites a hand-maintained `<!-- gitnexus:start -->` block in `AGENTS.md` / `CLAUDE.md` with upstream-generated content.
- The hook fires on every git operation that advances HEAD past the indexed commit (i.e. constantly, in active development).
- Any agent that follows the hint verbatim runs `npx gitnexus analyze`, bypassing the wrapper, and silently regresses both files. Recovery is `git checkout HEAD -- AGENTS.md CLAUDE.md` — annoying, not fatal, but it happens on every stale-index event for users who haven't yet learned to ignore the hint.

The blast radius isn't limited to my wrapper. Anyone who wraps `gitnexus` (telemetry, project-scoped flags, alternate config paths, rate-limiting) gets the same footgun, since `npx` invocation deliberately bypasses PATH resolution.

## Repro

1. Place an executable wrapper named `gitnexus` earlier on `PATH` than the npm-installed binary (or define a shell function with that name) that prints its argv and forwards to the real binary.
2. Make a commit so the indexed commit lags HEAD.
3. Run any tool that triggers a `Bash(git *)` in Claude Code.
4. The hook prints `Run \`npx gitnexus analyze\` to update the knowledge graph.`
5. Following the hint does not invoke the wrapper. Following bare `gitnexus analyze` does.

## Proposed fix

Prefer a PATH-resolved `gitnexus` and fall back to `npx` only when the binary isn't installed:

```js
const onPath = spawnSync('which', ['gitnexus'], { stdio: 'pipe' }).status === 0;
const analyzeBin = onPath ? 'gitnexus' : 'npx gitnexus';
const analyzeCmd = `${analyzeBin} analyze${hadEmbeddings ? ' --embeddings' : ''}`;
```

This preserves the defensive behavior when `gitnexus` somehow isn't on PATH while letting wrappers do their job in the common case.

Happy to send a PR if you'd prefer that route.

title: fix(ingestion): surface skipped large-file paths by default (#1659)
body:
## Summary

Closes #1659. The 512 KB skip threshold in `filesystem-walker.ts` is necessary, but the existing warning was only `Skipped N large files (>512KB, likely generated/vendored)` with no path list unless `GITNEXUS_VERBOSE=1` was set. In a repo with one or two oversized first-party files (a 17K-line cron handler in this case), every `IMPORTS` and `CALLS` edge from that file silently disappeared and the surface looked exactly like a Python resolver bug.

#1659 was filed for that reason. The resolver is fine on current main, the file was being dropped before parse.

## Changes

- Always print up to 5 skipped paths after the count line.
- If more than 5 are skipped, append `...and N more (set GITNEXUS_VERBOSE=1 to list them all)`.
- When running at the default threshold, emit `Set GITNEXUS_MAX_FILE_SIZE=<KB> to include files above the default cap.` so operators know how to widen it. Suppressed when an override is already active.
- Three new tests in the existing `large file skip threshold (#991)` describe block (default-path-listed, hint-emitted-on-default, hint-omitted-on-override) plus a new describe block for the >5 preview-cap path.

## Before / after on the reporting repo (680 Python files)

Before:
```
Skipped 3 large files (>512KB, likely generated/vendored)
```
`gitnexus impact _sync_amazon_sales_impl --direction upstream` returned 1 caller out of 5 real ones. `cron.py` was the dropped file but the user could not tell.

After:
```
Skipped 3 large files (>512KB, likely generated/vendored)
  - backend/schema_contracts/gitnexus-export.json
  - backend/schema_contracts/manifest.json
  - backend/routers/cron.py
  Set GITNEXUS_MAX_FILE_SIZE=<KB> to include files above the default cap.
```
Re-running with `GITNEXUS_MAX_FILE_SIZE=1024` then returns `impactedCount: 9` for the same query, including every cron.py caller.

## Why not raise the default cap

512 KB is intentional and covers the common generated/vendored case. The bug here is a diagnostics gap, not a threshold choice, so this PR fixes diagnostics only and leaves the default unchanged.

## Test plan

- [x] `npx vitest run test/integration/filesystem-walker.test.ts` — 23 tests pass (existing 19 plus 4 new)
- [x] `npx vitest run test/unit/max-file-size.test.ts` — pass
- [x] `npx tsc --noEmit` clean
- [x] `npx prettier --check` clean
- [x] `npx eslint` clean for changed files
- [x] End-to-end on the originating 680-file repo: cron.py now listed by name, impactedCount goes from 1 to 9 after bumping the cap

## Notes for triage

- Issue reporter was on `1.6.4-rc.32` (published 2026-04-30 21:39 UTC). The two related Python fixes #1241 and #1253 landed 2026-05-01 and 2026-05-02 respectively, so the resolver-side concern in the issue body is genuinely already fixed on main, but the user-visible symptom would have recurred on any large file. After this lands the issue can be closed.

title: MCP detect_changes differs from CLI for indexed git worktree repo path
body:
## Summary

`detect_changes` behaves differently through the MCP tool vs the GitNexus CLI when targeting an indexed git worktree by absolute path.

In this setup, both the main checkout and a linked git worktree are indexed. The CLI correctly detects uncommitted and compare-scope changes when passed the absolute worktree path, but the MCP `detect_changes` tool returns `No changes detected` for the same absolute worktree path and scope.

This is related to, but distinct from, #1658. That issue covers duplicate repo-name resolution selecting the wrong sibling. This issue is about absolute worktree-path targeting: the CLI works, while the MCP tool returns no changes.

All paths, repo names, branch names, and commit IDs below are sanitized.

## Environment

- GitNexus CLI: `1.6.4`
- OS: macOS / Darwin
- Git layout: main checkout plus linked git worktrees under the repository directory
- Both the main checkout and the active worktree are indexed by GitNexus

## Sanitized repository layout

`git worktree list --porcelain` shape:

```text
worktree /Users/<user>/repos/example-repo
HEAD <main-checkout-commit>
branch refs/heads/main

worktree /Users/<user>/repos/example-repo/.claude/worktrees/agent-detached-worktree
HEAD <detached-worktree-commit>
detached
locked

worktree /Users/<user>/repos/example-repo/.claude/worktrees/feature-worktree
HEAD <feature-worktree-commit>
branch refs/heads/feature-worktree
```

`npx gitnexus list` shape:

```text
Indexed Repositories (...)
  example-repo  (/Users/<user>/repos/example-repo)
    Path:    /Users/<user>/repos/example-repo
    Commit:  <main-indexed-commit>
    Stats:   ...

  example-repo  (/Users/<user>/repos/example-repo/.claude/worktrees/feature-worktree)
    Path:    /Users/<user>/repos/example-repo/.claude/worktrees/feature-worktree
    Commit:  <feature-indexed-commit>
    Stats:   ...
```

Inside the active worktree:

```text
$ git rev-parse --show-toplevel
/Users/<user>/repos/example-repo/.claude/worktrees/feature-worktree

$ git rev-parse --git-common-dir
/Users/<user>/repos/example-repo/.git

$ git status --short --branch
## feature-worktree...origin/feature-worktree
 M AGENTS.md
 M CLAUDE.md

$ npx gitnexus status
Repository: /Users/<user>/repos/example-repo/.claude/worktrees/feature-worktree
Indexed commit: <feature-indexed-commit>
Current commit: <feature-indexed-commit>
Status: ✅ up-to-date
```

## Reproduction

From inside `/Users/<user>/repos/example-repo/.claude/worktrees/feature-worktree`, with two uncommitted markdown file changes:

### CLI works with absolute worktree path

```bash
npx gitnexus detect-changes \
  --scope all \
  --repo "/Users/<user>/repos/example-repo/.claude/worktrees/feature-worktree"
```

Actual CLI output:

```text
Changes: 2 files, 2 symbols
Affected processes: 0
Risk level: low
Changed symbols:
  undefined GitNexus — Code Intelligence → AGENTS.md
  undefined GitNexus — Code Intelligence → CLAUDE.md
```

```bash
npx gitnexus detect-changes \
  --scope unstaged \
  --repo "/Users/<user>/repos/example-repo/.claude/worktrees/feature-worktree"
```

Actual CLI output:

```text
Changes: 2 files, 2 symbols
Affected processes: 0
Risk level: low
Changed symbols:
  undefined GitNexus — Code Intelligence → AGENTS.md
  undefined GitNexus — Code Intelligence → CLAUDE.md
```

```bash
npx gitnexus detect-changes \
  --scope compare \
  --base-ref main \
  --repo "/Users/<user>/repos/example-repo/.claude/worktrees/feature-worktree"
```

Actual CLI output shape:

```text
Changes: 13 files, 148 symbols
Affected processes: 42
Risk level: critical
Changed symbols:
  undefined GitNexus — Code Intelligence → AGENTS.md
  undefined GitNexus — Code Intelligence → CLAUDE.md
  undefined <symbol> → path/to/file.swift
  ... and 133 more
Affected execution flows:
  • <flow> — changed: <symbols>
  ...
```

### MCP returns no changes for the same absolute worktree path

MCP call:

```json
{
  "scope": "all",
  "repo": "/Users/<user>/repos/example-repo/.claude/worktrees/feature-worktree"
}
```

Actual MCP output:

```json
{
  "summary": {
    "changed_count": 0,
    "affected_count": 0,
    "risk_level": "none",
    "message": "No changes detected."
  },
  "changed_symbols": [],
  "affected_processes": []
}
```

MCP call:

```json
{
  "scope": "compare",
  "base_ref": "main",
  "repo": "/Users/<user>/repos/example-repo/.claude/worktrees/feature-worktree"
}
```

Actual MCP output:

```json
{
  "summary": {
    "changed_count": 0,
    "affected_count": 0,
    "risk_level": "none",
    "message": "No changes detected."
  },
  "changed_symbols": [],
  "affected_processes": []
}
```

For comparison, MCP with the duplicate repository name returned compare changes, but that is ambiguous in this setup and appears to target a different sibling/index selection path:

```json
{
  "scope": "compare",
  "base_ref": "main",
  "repo": "example-repo"
}
```

Actual MCP output shape:

```json
{
  "summary": {
    "changed_count": 148,
    "affected_count": 42,
    "changed_files": 13,
    "risk_level": "critical"
  },
  "changed_symbols": [ ... ],
  "affected_processes": [ ... ]
}
```

## Expected behavior

When `repo` is an absolute path to an indexed worktree, the MCP `detect_changes` tool should match CLI behavior for that same path:

- `scope: all` should detect the two uncommitted file changes.
- `scope: unstaged` should detect the two uncommitted file changes.
- `scope: compare`, `base_ref: main` should detect the branch-vs-main changes.

If MCP cannot operate on that absolute path, it should return an explicit error explaining why, rather than `No changes detected`.

## Actual behavior

The GitNexus CLI detects changes correctly for the absolute worktree path.

The MCP tool returns `No changes detected` for the same absolute worktree path and scopes.

## Why this matters

Claude Code agents use MCP `detect_changes` for pre-commit and PR impact checks. A false `No changes detected` is easy to miss and is worse than an explicit failure, because it can make a verification step look clean even when there are real code changes.

This is especially likely in Claude Code workflows because worktrees under `.claude/worktrees/...` are common, and the main checkout plus worktree often share the same GitNexus repository name.

## Possible causes to investigate

- MCP backend and CLI may resolve absolute worktree paths differently.
- MCP may be normalizing the worktree path to the common `.git` directory or main checkout.
- MCP may be selecting an index handle correctly but running git diff from a different cwd.
- Duplicate-name sibling handling from #1658 may still influence absolute-path requests in MCP.

## Workaround

For now, run the CLI directly in the worktree:

```bash
npx gitnexus detect-changes --scope all --repo "$(pwd)"
npx gitnexus detect-changes --scope compare --base-ref main --repo "$(pwd)"
```

Do not rely only on MCP `detect_changes` in indexed worktrees until this is fixed or explicitly disambiguated.

title: group sync returns 0 cross-links and unmatched contracts for Java/Dubbo repositories
body:
### Area

title: Avoid `analyze` worker-thread native crashes (`Napi::Error`) on C/C++ repos with per-chunk sequential routing
body:
`gitnexus analyze` could terminate with an unhandled native binding error (`Napi::Error`) on repositories with heavy C/C++ parsing workloads (e.g., TensorFlow Lite Micro / ExecuTorch). This change makes the failure mode non-fatal while keeping full parallel worker throughput for all non-C/C++ language chunks.

- **Worker scheduling guard for native-risk language sets**
  - Added a dedicated language guard helper to detect worker-unsafe languages:
    - `src/core/ingestion/workers/worker-language-guard.ts`
  - Detects presence of `C` / `C++` files (`.c`, `.cc`, `.cpp`, `.cxx`, `.h`, `.hpp`, `.hxx`, `.hh`) and signals per-chunk worker bypass.

- **Parse pipeline behavior change — per-chunk, not global**
  - Worker pool creation is **unconditional** (respects normal file/byte thresholds).
  - Inside the parse loop each chunk is inspected individually: if it contains C/C++ files, `processParsing` receives `undefined` as the worker pool argument, falling through to `processParsingSequential` in the main thread (safe from native crashes). Chunks with no C/C++ files continue dispatching to worker threads exactly as before.
  - C/C++ source files are **fully indexed** — symbol extraction, imports, calls, and heritage all run; only the execution context (main thread vs. worker thread) differs.
  - A one-time `WARN` log explains the per-chunk behaviour.

- **Operator override + discoverability**
  - Introduced env override for advanced users:
    - `GITNEXUS_ALLOW_CPP_WORKERS=1`
  - Surfaced in CLI help text so the behavior is explicit and configurable.

- **Focused unit coverage**
  - Added unit tests for guard behavior covering all relevant C/C++ extensions:
    - non-C/C++ inputs → workers allowed
    - `.c`, `.cpp`, `.h`, `.hpp`, `.hxx`, `.hh` → worker-unsafe detected
    - empty input → workers allowed

```ts
const chunkHasWorkerUnsafeFiles =
  workerPool &&
  process.env.GITNEXUS_ALLOW_CPP_WORKERS !== '1' &&
  hasWorkerUnsafeLanguages(chunkFiles);

chunkWorkerData = await processParsing(
  ...,
  chunkHasWorkerUnsafeFiles ? undefined : workerPool,
  ...
);
```

title: Go HTTP extractor only matches `http.HandleFunc`; misses idiomatic `mux.HandleFunc` and method-reference handlers
body:
## Summary

`gitnexus/src/core/group/extractors/http-patterns/go.ts` only matches the literal `http.HandleFunc("/p", handler)` form. Two common variants are silently dropped:

1. **Local-receiver routers.** Any code that wires routes onto a local `*http.ServeMux` or `gorilla/mux.Router` looks like `mux.HandleFunc(...)` or `router.HandleFunc(...)`. These are the idiomatic stdlib + gorilla/mux patterns.
2. **Method-reference handlers.** A method passed as the handler (`mux.HandleFunc("/p", apiHandler.HandleFoo)`) is a `selector_expression`, not a bare `identifier`, so the existing pattern rejects it.

Result: a Go project that uses either form ends up with **zero provider contracts** for its HTTP surface, breaking cross-repo HTTP contract matching for that repo.

## Repro

\`\`\`go
// cmd/server.go
package main

func healthHandler(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {}

func main() {
    mux := http.NewServeMux()
    mux.HandleFunc("/api/health", healthHandler)             // missed: operand is "mux", not "http"
    mux.HandleFunc("/api/users", apiHandler.ListUsers)       // missed: handler is selector_expression
}
\`\`\`

Running \`gitnexus group sync <group>\` against a repo containing the file above yields no provider contracts for \`/api/health\` or \`/api/users\`.

## Root cause

The current tree-sitter query hard-codes the operand:

\`\`\`
operand: (identifier) @pkg (#eq? @pkg "http")
\`\`\`

and the handler arg:

\`\`\`
(identifier) @handler
\`\`\`

Neither constraint is necessary — \`HandleFunc\` as a field name with a (string, callable) argument shape is a strong-enough signal on its own.

## Proposed fix

Drop the operand constraint and emit a second pattern that accepts `selector_expression` handlers. PR opening shortly.

title: fix(extractors): match `mux.HandleFunc` and method-reference handlers
body:
Closes #1668.

## What

The Go HTTP provider extractor at `gitnexus/src/core/group/extractors/http-patterns/go.ts` hard-coded the operand identifier as `http` and the handler argument as a bare `identifier`. Two idiomatic Go patterns are silently dropped as a result:

1. **Local-receiver routers** -- `mux.HandleFunc(...)` / `router.HandleFunc(...)`. This is the canonical pattern for code that wires routes onto a local `*http.ServeMux` or `gorilla/mux.Router` rather than the package-level `http.DefaultServeMux`.
2. **Method-reference handlers** -- `mux.HandleFunc(\"/p\", h.Foo)`, where the handler arg is a `selector_expression` rather than an `identifier`.

## How

- Drop the operand constraint -- `HandleFunc` as a field name plus the (string, callable) argument shape is sufficient signal.
- Emit a second pattern variant that accepts `selector_expression` handlers.

## Verify

\`\`\`bash
cd gitnexus
npx tsc --noEmit
npx vitest run test/unit/group/http-route-extractor.test.ts -t HandleFunc
\`\`\`

Three tests pass: the existing \`http.HandleFunc\` test plus two new ones covering \`mux.HandleFunc\` (local ServeMux) and method-reference handlers.

## Risk

Low. The new patterns are strictly broader than the old one; the existing stdlib-`http.HandleFunc` form continues to match. No call sites changed.

title: Go `http.HandleFunc` providers emitted as GET only; non-GET consumers never cross-link
fix(extractors): emit HandleFunc providers for all common verbs
body:
Closes #1670.

## What

`net/http.HandleFunc` registers a handler for **all** HTTP methods; the method dispatch happens inside the handler body, not at registration. The extractor was hard-coding `method: 'GET'`, so any consumer doing POST/PUT/DELETE/PATCH against a HandleFunc-registered provider failed the exact-match cascade and never cross-linked.

## How

Emit one provider detection per common verb (`GET`, `POST`, `PUT`, `DELETE`, `PATCH`) for each HandleFunc call. Confidence drops from 0.8 to 0.6 to reflect that we don't actually know which methods the handler accepts (it's a registration-time inference, not a declaration).

## Verify

\`\`\`bash
cd gitnexus
npx tsc --noEmit
npx vitest run test/unit/group/http-route-extractor.test.ts -t HandleFunc
\`\`\`

The existing test grew an assertion loop covering all five verbs.

## Risk

- Provider rows grow 5x for each HandleFunc call (a few hundred per typical Go service). Memory + sync time impact is small; the matcher dedups by contractId before output.
- Confidence drop from 0.8 to 0.6 puts these slightly below framework routes (gin/echo/chi at 0.8) for tiebreaking. Intentional -- we genuinely have less information.

## Alternative considered

Emit a single provider with a sentinel `ANY` method and teach the matcher to treat it as a wildcard. More invasive (matcher changes + a meta field), so the per-verb emission is the smaller surface.

title: HTTP source-scan skipped whenever the graph returns any routes; polyglot repos silently drop providers
body:
## Summary

`gitnexus/src/core/group/extractors/http-route-extractor.ts` falls back to the source-scan extractors ONLY when graph-assisted Strategy A returns zero entries:

\`\`\`ts
const providers =
  graphProviders.length > 0
    ? graphProviders
    : this.extractProvidersSourceScan(await getScannedFiles(), getDetections);
\`\`\`

In a homogeneous-language repo this is fine. In a **polyglot repo** it silently drops providers: as soon as one language's ingester populates a single `HANDLES_ROUTE` edge, the source-scan fallback is skipped for the **whole repo** — even though other languages in the same repo may have no route ingester at all (e.g. Python `@app.get`, Go `http.HandleFunc`, Java Spring `@GetMapping` etc. -- whichever ingesters are wired or not at a given moment).

## Repro

\`\`\`
repo/
├── src/controller/UserController.java     # has HANDLES_ROUTE edge from Java ingester
└── cmd/server.go                          # http.HandleFunc(...) — no Go ingester
\`\`\`

After `gitnexus group sync <group>`:
- `http::GET::/api/v2/users` -> present (Java, graph-derived)
- `http::GET::/api/health` -> **missing**, even though `http-patterns/go.ts` would extract it correctly

The Go provider is silently dropped because the Java graph entry made `graphProviders.length > 0` true, which short-circuits the Go source-scan.

## Proposed fix

Union the two strategies and dedupe on `contractId`. Graph entries take precedence (they carry richer `symbolUid` metadata); source-scan entries supplement them. No language-specific changes required — this is a one-method orchestrator fix.

PR opening shortly.

title: fix(extractors): union graph + source-scan strategies in HTTP route extractor
body:
Closes #1672.

## What

`HttpRouteExtractor` orchestrator fell back to source-scan only when graph-assisted Strategy A returned zero entries. In a polyglot repo this drops providers as soon as one language's ingester populates a single `HANDLES_ROUTE` edge.

## How

Replace the ternary with a union:

\`\`\`ts
private async unionGraphAndSourceScan<T extends { contractId: string }>(
  graph: T[],
  sourceScan: () => Promise<T[]>,
): Promise<T[]> {
  const seen = new Set(graph.map((c) => c.contractId));
  const supplemental = (await sourceScan()).filter((c) => !seen.has(c.contractId));
  return [...graph, ...supplemental];
}
\`\`\`

Graph entries are emitted first and their `contractId`s are taken as authoritative (richer `symbolUid`, real handler names). Source-scan entries that introduce **new** `contractId`s are appended. Source-scan rows that overlap graph rows are dropped, so we don't double-count.

Same logic applies symmetrically to consumers.

## Verify

\`\`\`bash
cd gitnexus
npx tsc --noEmit
npx vitest run test/unit/group/http-route-extractor.test.ts
\`\`\`

30/30 pass. The new polyglot test mixes a graph-resident Java provider with a source-scan-only Go provider and confirms both survive the union.

## Risk

- **Slightly more work in homogeneous-language repos**: source-scan now always runs even when graph returned full coverage. The glob is cheap (single pass, ignore-aware) and detections are cached per file via `getDetections`, so the realistic cost is one extra dedup pass.
- **No matcher changes**: dedup is on `contractId`, which is already the matcher's identity.
- **No behaviour change for repos that previously returned zero graph entries** -- they continue to get pure source-scan results.

title: Windows + Node v24.14.0: gitnexus@1.6.3 analyze crashes at LadybugDB persist (60%)
body:
## Environment
- **OS:** Windows 10/11, PowerShell 5.1
- **Node:** v24.14.0
- **GitNexus:** 1.6.3 (npm global install)
- **Repo:** Go project (~300 files)

## Bug
npx gitnexus analyze --force prints "GitNexus Analyzer" banner then exits with -1073741819 (0xC0000005). No JS stack trace.

## Detailed Diagnosis
Bypassing the CLI entry point and calling runFullAnalysis() directly via ESM file:/// import with progress callbacks shows the full pipeline works, then crashes:

PROGRESS: extracting 0-9% Scanning files
PROGRESS: structure 9-12% Building structure
PROGRESS: parsing 12-49% Parsing code
PROGRESS: enriching 50% enriching
PROGRESS: communities 50-56% Detecting communities
PROGRESS: processes 56-59% Detecting processes
PROGRESS: complete 60% Pipeline complete
PROGRESS: lbug 60 Loading into LadybugDB...   [CRASH HERE]

The crash is in LadybugDB WAL flush (closeLbug() persist). Resulting .gitnexus/ has lbug (4KB) + lbug.wal (~25KB) but no meta.json. The .wal size is consistently ~25KB regardless of repo size.

## Evidence Ruling Out Other Causes
1. @ladybugdb/lbug-win32-x64 loads fine via require() -- crash is runtime WAL persist, not module load
2. ensureHeap() child re-exec is irrelevant -- crash reproduces with and without child spawn

4. No V8 flag combination helps -- tested --max-old-space-size and --stack-size, all same crash
5. Pure JS pipeline works fine -- tree-sitter parsing, communities, processes all complete
6. Native SEH exception (0xC0000005) -- pure JS cannot catch, no stack trace possible

## Related Issues

- #1483 -- Same "60% Loading into LadybugDB" crash on Windows (closed)
- #1431 -- WSL2 + LadybugDB persistently SIGSEGV (open -- LadybugDB native issues on Windows)
- #1649 -- windsurf cannot start mcp on windows (open -- potentially related)

title: Python f-strings (and r/b/u prefixes) poison HTTP consumer contract IDs with literal `f"`
body:
## Summary

`unquoteLiteral` in `gitnexus/src/core/group/extractors/tree-sitter-scanner.ts` strips the surrounding quote characters from a string literal but leaves Python string **prefixes** (`f`, `r`, `b`, `u`, plus their two-letter combinations) intact. As a result, every Python f-string used as an HTTP URL ends up with a literal `f\"` baked into the consumer contract ID, and the matcher can never cross-link it.

## Repro

\`\`\`python
import requests

BASE = \"https://svc.local\"

def call():
    return requests.get(f\"{BASE}/api/items\")
\`\`\`

After `gitnexus group sync <group>`, the consumer contract for the `requests.get(...)` call appears with a `contractId` of roughly `http::GET::/f\"{param}/api/items` -- the leading `f\"` and the trailing `\"` survive into the normalized path. Same for `r\"...\"` raw strings, `b\"...\"` bytes literals, and `u\"...\"` unicode literals.

Result: every consumer URL that came from an f-string is silently locked out of the matcher's exact-match cascade.

## Root cause

`unquoteLiteral` inspects only the first and last characters of the raw literal text. For `f\"{BASE}/api/items\"`:
- first char = `f` (not `\"`, `'`, or `\``)
- the function falls through to `return raw` with the prefix + quotes intact

## Proposed fix

Strip Python string prefixes when they are followed by a quote, before the quote-pair detection runs:

\`\`\`ts
raw = raw.replace(/^[fFrRbBuU]{1,2}(?=[\"'\`])/, '');
\`\`\`

The lookahead constraint (`(?=[\"'`])`) keeps this Python-specific in practice -- 1-2 letters from `[fFrRbBuU]` followed by a quote character don't occur in Java/Go/JS/TS string literals.

PR opening shortly.

## Out of scope

This issue does NOT attempt to also un-prefix the base-URL placeholder that survives normalization (e.g. `{BASE}/api/items` becoming `/api/items`). That's a separate design question -- the leading `{...}` segment could legitimately be a route param (e.g. `/{lang}/api/items`). Worth its own ticket if the matcher needs to grow tolerance for base-URL placeholders.

title: fix(extractors): strip Python string prefixes (f/r/b/u) in `unquoteLiteral`
body:
Closes #1675.

## What

`unquoteLiteral` inspected only the first and last characters of the raw token, so Python f-strings / r-strings / b-strings survived with their **prefix** intact. Every Python f-string URL ended up with a literal `f\"` baked into the consumer `contractId`, locking the matcher out.

## How

One-liner before the quote-pair check:

\`\`\`ts
raw = raw.replace(/^[fFrRbBuU]{1,2}(?=[\"'\`])/, '');
\`\`\`

Lookahead keeps it Python-specific in practice — 1-2 letters from that set followed by a quote don't appear in Java/Go/JS/TS string literals.

## Verify

\`\`\`bash
cd gitnexus
npx tsc --noEmit
npx vitest run test/unit/group/http-route-extractor.test.ts
\`\`\`

30/30 pass. The new test covers all three prefix flavours (`f\"...\"`, `r\"...\"`, `b\"...\"`).

## Risk

Low. The replace only triggers when the leading 1-2 chars are letters from `[fFrRbBuU]` AND the next char is a quote. The only way that matches in non-Python source is also a string literal whose body would have been preserved verbatim afterwards — stripping the prefix is harmless because the quote-pair check still unwraps the rest.

## Out of scope

Not addressing the base-URL-placeholder issue (`{BASE}/api/items` -> `/api/items`); that's a separate design call.

title: Swift HTTP extractor missing; iOS / macOS / Swift-on-server consumers never cross-link
body:
## Summary

`gitnexus/src/core/group/extractors/http-patterns/` ships plugins for Java, Go, Python, PHP, JavaScript, TypeScript, and TSX -- but **not Swift**, despite `tree-sitter-swift` being a declared dependency in `gitnexus/package.json`. As a result, the source-scan fallback (Strategy B) emits zero contracts for any `.swift` file: `HTTP_SCAN_GLOB` doesn't include `.swift`, and even if it did `getPluginForFile()` would return undefined for that extension.

For groups that include an iOS / macOS / Swift-on-server consumer of a backend in the same group, the consumer side is completely invisible to the matcher. The Swift app might call a dozen of the backend's endpoints from `Client.get(path: \"/api/foo\")` calls -- none of them produce a `consumer` contract, so none of the backend `provider` contracts can ever cross-link.

## Repro

Add an iOS-style wrapper to any group repo:

\`\`\`swift
// Sources/RelayClient.swift
enum RelayClient {
    static func get(path: String) async throws -> Data { Data() }
    static func post(path: String, body: Data) async throws -> Data { Data() }
}

func caller() async throws {
    _ = try await RelayClient.get(path: \"/api/customers\")
    _ = try await RelayClient.post(path: \"/api/devices/register\", body: Data())
}
\`\`\`

After `gitnexus group sync <group>`: zero contracts emitted from the Swift file, regardless of how many consumer paths it contains.

## Proposed plugin

Cover the dominant Swift HTTP pattern: a verb-method on some receiver (`Client.get(...)`, `AF.delete(...)`, etc.) where the path is either a labeled `path:` argument or the positional first string argument. Two tree-sitter query variants:

1. \`<receiver>.<verb>(path: \"<literal>\", ...)\` — labeled `path:` wrapper style.
2. \`<receiver>.<verb>(\"<literal>\", ...)\` — positional first-argument style (Alamofire, lightweight wrappers).

Both extract the HTTP method from the verb's `simple_identifier` and the path from the `line_str_text` capture. Confidence 0.7 (matches other source-scan plugins).

Out of scope for the first cut:
- Correlating `request.httpMethod = \"POST\"` with a separate `URLRequest(url: ...)` statement -- requires intra-procedural analysis the source-scan path doesn't have.
- The bare `URL(string: \"...\")` / `URLSession.shared.dataTask(...)` form -- too noisy as a default GET when most code wraps it.

PR opening shortly.

title: feat(extractors): add Swift HTTP consumer plugin (verb-method patterns)
body:
Closes #1677.

## What

Adds `gitnexus/src/core/group/extractors/http-patterns/swift.ts` and wires it into the registry + `HTTP_SCAN_GLOB`. `tree-sitter-swift` was already a declared dependency, so this is purely a new plugin file + 2 lines of registry plumbing.

## Why

iOS / macOS / Swift-on-server consumers of a backend in the same group were completely invisible to the contract matcher -- the source-scan extractor returned zero detections for `.swift` files.

## Coverage

Two query variants, both extracting the HTTP method from the navigation-suffix identifier (`get` / `post` / `put` / `delete` / `patch`):

| Pattern | Shape | Example |
|---------|-------|---------|
| A | `<receiver>.<verb>(path: \"<literal>\", ...)` | `Client.get(path: \"/api/foo\")` |
| B | `<receiver>.<verb>(\"<literal>\", ...)` | `AF.delete(\"/api/items/42\")` |

Pattern B post-filters to skip arguments that carry a label (pattern A already covers those) and dedupes by node position.

## Verify

\`\`\`bash
cd gitnexus
npx tsc --noEmit
npx vitest run test/unit/group/http-route-extractor.test.ts
\`\`\`

31/31 pass. The two new tests cover labeled-`path:` and positional Alamofire-style.

## Out of scope

- Correlating `request.httpMethod = \"POST\"` with a separate `URLRequest(url: ...)` statement — needs intra-procedural analysis the source-scan path doesn't have.
- Bare `URL(string: \"...\")` / `URLSession.shared.dataTask(...)` — too noisy as a default GET; most production Swift code wraps these and pattern A/B catches the wrappers.

## Risk

Zero behavior change for existing languages (new file + new map entry + glob expanded). Swift files that previously matched no plugin now match the Swift plugin; the rest of the pipeline (path normalization, contract id, matcher) is unchanged.

title: feat(eval-server): add --host flag for cross-network bind
body:
## Summary

Adds `--host <addr>` to `gitnexus eval-server` (default `127.0.0.1`, fully backward compatible). Without this flag the server is loopback-only, which blocks split-container and multi-host deployments where the eval-server runs in one container and clients reach it across a Docker network or VM boundary.

This is a clean, CI-green rebuild of the existing PR lineage on this feature:

- **#1602** by @vvladescu-tb introduced the original `--host` patch.
- **#1667** by @sanguine59 built on #1602 with input validation, comprehensive error handling, and additional tests, but has been stuck on quality CI checks.

Both authors are credited as `Co-authored-by:` trailers on the commit, and the test files retain the in-line comment "Original test by Val Vladescu (PR #1602)". The intent here is collaborative — to unblock the work, not to disparage either prior attempt.

## What's included

- `validateHost(raw)` helper: accepts IPv4, IPv6, or `localhost` (normalised to `127.0.0.1`); returns `null` for invalid input. Invalid `--host` value exits with a clear, example-rich error and `exit(1)`.
- `server.on('error')` taxonomy with code-specific messages:
  - `EADDRINUSE` — port already in use, with stop-or-change-port guidance
  - `EADDRNOTAVAIL` — address not assigned to a local interface, with an extra IPv6-disabled hint for Docker/CI environments
  - `EACCES` — privileged port without privileges
  - generic fallback for everything else
- READY signal extended from `GITNEXUS_EVAL_SERVER_READY:<port>` to `GITNEXUS_EVAL_SERVER_READY:<host>:<port>` (existing consumers that only need the port can still parse it).
- IPv6 host bracketing in the banner (e.g. `http://[::1]:4848`).
- 8 new unit tests for `validateHost` (localhost / valid IPv4 / valid IPv6 / non-IP hostnames / out-of-range octets / incomplete IPs / empty / whitespace).
- 1 new e2e test that spawns the real CLI with `--host 127.0.0.1` and asserts the option is registered and the READY signal emits.

## Local CI status

All upstream CI gates pass locally on Node 22.22.1:

| Gate | Result |
|---|---|
| `npx prettier --check .` (root) | exit 0 — "All files formatted correctly" |
| `npx eslint .` (root) | exit 0 — no new warnings introduced (`eval-server.ts` has the same 15 pre-existing `no-explicit-any` warnings before and after this patch) |
| `npx tsc --noEmit` (`gitnexus/`) | exit 0, zero output |
| `npx vitest run test/unit/eval-formatters.test.ts` | 37/37 pass |
| `npx vitest run test/integration/cli-e2e.test.ts` | 27/27 pass |

## Why this matters downstream

A per-project code-intelligence sidecar (argus) consumes the eval-server across containers and currently carries a `socat` loopback shim to work around the 127.0.0.1-only bind. Landing this lets that workaround be retired.

## Notes for reviewers

- This is filed from `zenprocess/GitNexus:feat/eval-server-host`. The branch is based on current `main` (commit `7d500390b` / PR #1655), so it's not behind.
- I've intentionally not closed #1602 or #1667 — the maintainers are best placed to decide whether to close those in favour of this clean version, redirect commentary here, or take another path.

Refs: #1602, #1667

title: [Bug] Incorrect edge relationships when duplicate package, class, and method names exist across different modules
body:
### Area

gitnexus (CLI / core / indexing / MCP server)

### Summary

Description:
In multi-module projects, gitnexus generates incorrect edge relationships if there are classes with the exact same package name, class name, and method name across different modules. The dependency resolution seems to confuse them, leading to inaccurate dependency graphs.



Suggested Solution:
I suggest introducing a "same-module priority" matching strategy. When resolving method calls or dependencies, the engine should prioritize matching the target class/method within the caller's own module before searching across other modules.

### Context

_No response_

### Expected behavior

The tool should accurately distinguish between classes with identical Fully Qualified Names (FQNs) that reside in different modules and draw the edges to the correct target.

### Actual behavior

The generated dependency graph shows an incorrect edge pointing to the identically named method/class in module2 instead of the correct target in module1.

### Steps to reproduce

Example/Steps to Reproduce:
Consider a project with the following structure:

module1/src/main/java/com/example/UserService.java

module2/src/main/java/com/example/UserService.java

If a method in module1 calls a method inside its own com.example.UserService, the generated edge might incorrectly point to the UserService in module2 (or vice versa).

title: MCP error with Claude: Failed to reconnect to gitnexus: -32000
body:
### Area

gitnexus (CLI / core / indexing / MCP server)

### Summary

### Problem

After global install:

npm install -g gitnexus

PowerShell resolves `gitnexus` to:

C:\Users\<user>\AppData\Roaming\npm\gitnexus.ps1

If MCP is configured with that path:

claude mcp add gitnexus -- "...gitnexus.ps1" mcp

Claude fails with:

Failed to reconnect to gitnexus: -32000

---

### Cause

Claude runs MCP servers as stdio processes.  
`.ps1` requires a PowerShell host, so the process exits immediately.

---

### Fix

Use the `.cmd` launcher instead:

claude mcp add gitnexus -- "C:\Users\<user>\AppData\Roaming\npm\gitnexus.cmd" mcp

---

### Suggestion

Add a Windows note in the docs:

> When configuring MCP on Windows, always use `gitnexus.cmd`, not `gitnexus.ps1`.

Failed to reconnect to gitnexus: -32000

title: analyze hangs or stalls on microsoft/TypeScript repo root (raised file-size limits)
body:
## Summary

`gitnexus analyze` on [microsoft/TypeScript](https://github.com/microsoft/TypeScript) **from the repo root** either appears to hang (raised `--max-file-size`) or takes many hours without an obvious completion signal (default 512KB skip). Analyzing only `src/` with the same raised limits completes successfully in ~2 minutes and indexes `compiler/checker.ts`.

This is not a fundamental restriction on indexing from root — it is a combination of **repo scale**, **pathological test fixtures**, and **worker-pool failure handling**.

## Environment

- GitNexus: `main` (local investigation, May 2026)
- Target: shallow clone of `microsoft/TypeScript`
- Command (raised limits — reproduces hang):

```bash
GITNEXUS_MAX_FILE_SIZE=32768
GITNEXUS_WORKER_SUB_BATCH_TIMEOUT_MS=600000
gitnexus analyze /path/to/TypeScript \
  --force --index-only --skip-agents-md --skip-skills \
  --max-file-size 32768 --worker-timeout 600 \
  --name bench-ts
```

## Observed behavior

### Raised limits (`--max-file-size 32768`)

- Parse progresses across many files, then worker pool logs idle timeouts and retries.
- Eventually fails a **single-item** job after 600s + 1200s:

```
Worker 0 parse job idle timeout after 1200s
(single item: tests/cases/fourslash/reallyLargeFile.ts, 3502391 bytes, last progress: 1)
Analyze will retry through sequential fallback.
```

- Run then falls into **sequential fallback** on the affected chunk and appears to stall indefinitely (no `meta.json` after 80+ minutes in our test).
- **Not** blocked by `src/compiler/checker.ts` (~3.0 MB) — that file completes in ~64s in the full parse-worker path.

### Default limits (512KB skip)

- Log reports: `Skipped 103 large files (>512KB, likely generated/vendored)` including `checker.ts`, `parser.ts`, and `reallyLargeFile.ts`.
- Still **~39k** parseable `.ts`/`.tsx` files remain (mostly under `tests/`).
- No index after ~68 minutes in our test — likely still in progress, not a silent success (extrapolated ~2+ hours at `src/` throughput).

### Control: `src/` only (works)

```bash
gitnexus analyze /path/to/TypeScript/src \
  --force --index-only --skip-git --skip-agents-md --skip-skills \
  --max-file-size 32768 --worker-timeout 600
```

- **~139s**, exit 0
- **622 files**, 40,241 nodes, 117,562 edges
- `compiler/checker.ts` present in the graph

## Scale

| Scope | `.ts`/`.tsx` files |
|-------|-------------------|
| Repo root | ~39,300 |
| `tests/` | ~20,400 |
| `src/` | ~709 |

Root is ~55× more files than `src/`.

## Root causes (investigated)

### 1. Pathological fixture with raised limits: `reallyLargeFile.ts`

`tests/cases/fourslash/reallyLargeFile.ts` (~3.5 MB) exceeds default 512KB skip but is included when limits are raised.

Full **parse-worker** path timing (legacy `TYPESCRIPT_QUERIES` + `buildTypeEnv` + `emitTsScopeCaptures` + call extraction):

| File | Size | Time |
|------|------|------|
| `src/compiler/checker.ts` | 3.0 MB | ~64s |
| `tests/.../reallyLargeFile.ts` | 3.5 MB | **>15 min** (did not finish) |

Tree-sitter `parse()` and scope-query `.matches()` alone are fast on `checker.ts` (~300ms each). Cost is in **post-parse extraction** inside `parse-worker.ts`.

### 2. `emitTsScopeCaptures` was O(matches × AST) on large files (partial fix identified)

`getTsScopeQuery().matches()` returns ~68k matches on `checker.ts`. The loop in `languages/typescript/captures.ts` previously called `findNodeAtRange(tree.rootNode, …)` per match — full-tree DFS each time — causing multi-minute hangs.

**Fix direction:** walk from capture nodes via parent links (`findAncestorOfType`) instead of re-scanning from root. On `checker.ts` this reduces `emitTsScopeCaptures` from **>7 min → ~2.5s**.

This does **not** fix the legacy worker extraction cost (~64s on `checker.ts`, unbounded on `reallyLargeFile.ts`).

### 3. Worker pool failure amplifies a single bad file

When a singleton sub-batch times out after retries, `worker-pool.ts` rejects the dispatch. `parsing-processor.ts` then runs **sequential fallback for the entire chunk** with **no per-file timeout**, re-processing the same pathological file.

Relevant locations:

- `gitnexus/src/core/ingestion/workers/worker-pool.ts` (idle timeout / split / retry)
- `gitnexus/src/core/ingestion/parsing-processor.ts` (chunk-level sequential fallback)
- `gitnexus/src/core/ingestion/workers/parse-worker.ts` (`processFileGroup` legacy extraction loop)

### 4. Default root run is slow, not necessarily broken

With 512KB skip, ~39k files remain. At `src/` throughput (~0.22s/file end-to-end), root needs **hours**, not minutes. Lack of `.gitnexus/` after ~1h is consistent with still running.

title: fix(api): open lbug read-only for /api/graph, /api/search, /api/grep
body:
## Summary

- `/api/graph` (stream + non-stream), `/api/search`, and `/api/grep` now open the LadybugDB with `{ readOnly: true }` — they only query, they never write.
- Adds `test/unit/api-readonly-wiring.test.ts` as a static-analysis guard so future read-only endpoints can't silently re-introduce the bug.

## The bug

When the WebUI clicks a repo card → `connectToServer` → `fetchGraph` → `GET /api/graph`, the server opened the lbug DB in **write mode**. Write-mode opens engage LadybugDB's checkpoint machinery (`.shadow` sidecar). On Windows the sidecar handling races with file-handle release and the engine throws:

```
IO exception: Cannot open file. path: <storage>/.gitnexus/lbug.shadow
Error 2: The system cannot find the file specified.
```

The error renders on the landing screen via `DropZone.tsx`'s error banner, the test never reaches `[data-testid="status-ready"]`, and four E2E specs time out (`onboarding.spec.ts` Flow 4, `server-connect.spec.ts` lightbulb / turn-off-highlights). All four require entering the exploring view.

The same trigger (W-mode open of read-only endpoints) surfaces differently on other platforms — e.g. macOS hits the WAL-replay path instead and reports `Corrupted wal file. Read out invalid WAL record type`.

## Evidence

1. Engine strings in `lbugjs.node` confirm `.shadow` is a checkpoint sidecar (\`Found a shadow file for database...\`, \`Couldn't replay shadow pages under read-only mode...\`).
2. `pool-adapter.ts:274` already opens with \`readOnly: true\` — the MCP path was hardened separately and never hit the bug.
3. PR #1655 set the precedent: \`/api/query\` already passes \`{ readOnly: true }\`. This PR brings the remaining read-only endpoints in line.
4. Empirical probe: read-only opens against a freshly-indexed DB never create \`.shadow\`; write-mode opens do.

## Endpoints touched

| Line | Endpoint | Before | After |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1026 | `GET /api/graph` (stream) | RW | RO |
| 1040 | `GET /api/graph` (non-stream) | RW | RO |
| 1097 | `POST /api/search` | RW | RO |
| 1301 | `GET /api/grep` | RW | RO |
| 650 | `POST /api/query` | already RO (#1655) | — |
| 1701 | `POST /api/embed` | RW (correct — writes) | — |

## Test plan

- [x] `npx vitest run test/unit/api-readonly-wiring.test.ts test/unit/api-query-readonly-wiring.test.ts` — 8/8 passing.
- [x] `tsc --noEmit` clean.
- [ ] Re-run E2E suite on Windows: 4 previously-failing graph-load specs should pass.
- [ ] macOS user from #1611 verifies the \`Corrupted wal file\` symptom is gone.

## Related

Related: #1611 — same root trigger, different OS-specific symptom on macOS. Marking as "related" rather than "fixes" so a macOS reviewer can confirm before closing.
