title: Windows: FTS skip-guard too aggressive when extension is locally installed (BM25 returns 0 results despite present binary)
fix(detect-changes): guard resolveWorktreeCwd against overriding a separately-indexed worktree
body:
## Problem

Fixes #1659. `detect_changes` returns no results when `repo` is set to
the absolute path of a **separately-indexed linked worktree** (i.e. both
the main checkout and the worktree are registered in GitNexus).

Root cause: `resolveWorktreeCwd` was designed to auto-detect when the
MCP server launches from a worktree. But when `repo.repoPath` already
points to a separately-indexed worktree, the function saw that it and
`process.cwd()` (the main checkout) share the same `getCanonicalRepoRoot`
and silently replaced the correct worktree path with the main checkout.
Result: `git diff` ran from the main checkout — where the changes don't
exist — and returned empty.

## Fix

Added an early-exit guard in `resolveWorktreeCwd`: if
`tryRealpath(repoPath) !== tryRealpath(getCanonicalRepoRoot(repoPath))`,
then `repoPath` is itself a linked worktree and is returned unchanged.
Auto-detection only fires when `repoPath` is the main checkout (the two
values are equal).

This does not affect the original auto-detection behaviour from #1654:
when `repoPath` is the main checkout and the server is launched from a
worktree, the guard does not trigger and auto-detection still works.

## Changes

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `src/mcp/local/local-backend.ts` | Early-exit guard in `resolveWorktreeCwd`; also normalises `launchCanonical` comparison to use `tryRealpath` |
| `test/unit/detect-changes-worktree.test.ts` | Regression test for the exact failure path |

title: fix(lbug): probe-then-load FTS extension on Windows (#1690)
body:
Closes #1690.

## Problem

The Windows skip-on-`process.platform === 'win32'` guard in `gitnexus/src/core/lbug/pool-adapter.ts` (both `doInitLbug` and `initLbugWithDb`) hard-skips `loadFTSExtension()` on every Windows host — even when the FTS extension binary is already present locally at `~/.lbdb/extension/<version>/win_amd64/fts/libfts.lbug_extension`.

That made sense as a workaround for the install-time SIGSEGV documented in #1199 / #1217. But once the binary is on disk it becomes too aggressive: `LOAD EXTENSION fts` would succeed, yet `loadFTSExtension` is never called. BM25 silently returns 0 hits on hosts with a working FTS extension; `gitnexus doctor` still reports FTS as available. Repro and root-cause analysis in #1690.

## Fix

Add `hasLocalWinFtsExtension()` and gate the Windows skip on it:

```ts
if (process.platform === 'win32') {
  shared.ftsLoaded = (await hasLocalWinFtsExtension())
    ? await loadFTSExtension(available[0], { policy: 'load-only' })
    : true;
} else {
  shared.ftsLoaded = await loadFTSExtension(available[0], { policy: 'load-only' });
}
```

`hasLocalWinFtsExtension()` probes `~/.lbdb/extension/*/win_amd64/fts/libfts.lbug_extension`. If at least one version dir has the binary on disk, we call `loadFTSExtension(..., { policy: 'load-only' })`. The crashing install path is never exercised — `load-only` short-circuits `extensionManager.ensure` before reaching `installDuckDbExtensionOutOfProcess`. Applied at both guard sites.

## Why the original SIGSEGV doesn't reappear

`#1199` / `#1217` documented the crash inside the install path. Two empirical reasons it stays mitigated here:

1. **`load-only` skips install entirely** — `extensionManager.ensure` returns false without invoking the installer when LOAD fails under `load-only`. `bm25-index.js`'s downstream noop continues to handle the unavailable case gracefully.

2. **LadybugDB resolves `LOAD EXTENSION fts` to a single version-specific path internally** — it does not glob across `~/.lbdb/extension/*/`. Stale or zero-byte sibling version dirs are inert: LadybugDB never `dlopen`s them. Errors at the resolution path (missing binary, zero-byte stub) propagate as JS exceptions and are caught by `tryLoad`'s `try/catch` in `gitnexus/src/core/lbug/extension-loader.ts`, then funneled through `markUnavailable`. No silent greenlight, no `dlopen` of a stale binary.

## Verification (Windows 10 Pro Education 10.0.19045 + Node 22.19.0 + gitnexus 1.6.5 + @ladybugdb/core 0.16.1 + FTS extension cached at 0.16.0)

| Scenario                                                                                                                | Exit | FTS-unavailable log? | BM25 ms | Outcome              |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---- | -------------------- | ------- | -------------------- |
| Real 0.16.0 binary only                                                                                                 | 0    | no                   | ~1100   | Real hits            |
| Real 0.16.0 binary + stubs at 0.15.0, 0.16.1, 0.17.0 (adversarial mixed)                                                 | 0    | no                   | ~8000   | Real hits            |
| Stub-only at non-resolution path 0.16.1                                                                                 | 0    | yes (`extension not pre-installed`)             | ~120    | FTS unavailable      |
| Stub-only at exact resolution path 0.16.0                                                                                | 0    | yes (`extension not pre-installed`)             | ~115    | FTS unavailable      |
| No `~/.lbdb/extension/` dir                                                                                              | 0    | no                   | 0       | Upstream skip path (preserved) |

No crashes, no silent greenlights, BM25 timings prove FTS actually ran when the binary was present, `gitnexus context` / `impact` / `cypher` unaffected on every variant.

## Notes / follow-ups not addressed here

- `gitnexus doctor` still reports `Full-text search: available` regardless of actual load state — covered by #1217's last bullet, deliberately scoped out of this PR. Happy to send a follow-up that has `doctor` consult `extensionManager.getCapabilities()` instead.
- An optimization is possible: version-scope the probe to `~/.lbdb/extension/<core-expected-version>/win_amd64/fts/...` to skip a guaranteed-to-fail load attempt when only stale version dirs are on disk (saves ~120ms in that edge case). Not done here because identifying "the version LadybugDB expects" from JS isn't trivially derived — on this build, `@ladybugdb/core` package version is 0.16.1 but the resolved FTS binary version is 0.16.0. The broad probe is correct; the perf nit is genuinely a perf nit.
- Happy to gate behind `GITNEXUS_LBUG_EXTENSION_LOAD_ON_WIN32=allow-if-present` env var if a more conservative rollout shape is preferred.

title: fix(workers): resilient + zero-copy ingestion worker pool — prevent analyze hangs on TS-root-scale loads
body:
## Summary Hardens the ingestion worker path so a single pathological file (e.g. microsoft/TypeScript's `tests/cases/fourslash/reallyLargeFile.ts`) can't hang `analyze` and worker death can't permanently degrade the pool. Lands in three phases: 1. **Resilience layers** — auto-respawn budget, per-slot circuit breaker, session-scoped quarantine, authoritative in-flight tracking, cumulative timeout budget, ready-handshake startup gate, slot-generation late-event guard. 2. **Zero-copy IPC via native `postMessage`** — workers and pool exchange POJO directly via `worker.postMessage(value, transferList)`. Node's structured-clone algorithm preserves Map / Set / Date / RegExp / BigInt / TypedArray / undefined / circular refs out of the box. File contents move zero-copy via `transferList` (`TextEncoder.encode` per file → dedicated `ArrayBuffer` → ownership transfer, never pool-backed). No custom protocol framing layer — one structured-clone walk per message, period. 3. **Cache integrity** — chunk-cache writes suppressed when any chunk file is quarantined, so a partial worker result can't be locked in under the full-coverage chunk hash and silently replayed on a later analyze. Workers are the **sole** failure-recovery contract for ingestion: there is no main-thread sequential rescue when a worker dies. Falling back to sequential would re-run the same tree-sitter parser that just killed the worker — for native-binding SIGSEGV (the most common quarantine cause), this turns silent missing-symbols into a loud analyze-wide crash. The pool's layered resilience is the contract; quarantined files surface in the warn log + stats; the next analyze with a fresh pool retries cleanly via cache-skip. --- ## Architecture ```mermaid flowchart TB classDef main fill:#1e3a5f,stroke:#4a90d9,color:#fff classDef pool fill:#2d4a3e,stroke:#7ab87d,color:#fff classDef layer fill:#3d3a2d,stroke:#d9b04a,color:#fff classDef worker fill:#4a3d4f,stroke:#b87dc4,color:#fff CLI[analyze CLI / MCP]:::main PI[parse-impl.ts chunk loop]:::main PP[parsing-processor.ts processParsing]:::main Cache[parseCache cross-run]:::main subgraph Pool["worker-pool.ts — createWorkerPool"] direction TB Disp[dispatch]:::pool Stats[getStats / getQuarantinedPaths]:::pool subgraph Layers["Resilience layers"] direction LR L1[Layer 1 Respawn budget]:::layer L2[Layer 2 Circuit breaker]:::layer L3[Layer 3 Quarantine]:::layer L4[Layer 4 Starting-file attribution]:::layer L5[Layer 5 Cumulative timeout]:::layer end subgraph Slots["Slot pool"] direction LR S0[Slot 0]:::pool S1[Slot 1]:::pool SN[... Slot N-1]:::pool end end W0[Worker 0 parse-worker.ts]:::worker W1[Worker 1 parse-worker.ts]:::worker WN[Worker N-1 parse-worker.ts]:::worker CLI --> PI PI -->|chunkFiles| PP PP -->|dispatch| Disp Disp --> Layers Layers --> Slots S0 <-->|postMessage + transferList| W0 S1 <-->|postMessage + transferList| W1 SN <-->|postMessage + transferList| WN PP -->|quarantine snapshot| PI PI -->|write only if no quarantine| Cache Stats -.->|verbose log| PI ``` --- ## Dispatch sequence (happy path) ```mermaid sequenceDiagram autonumber participant PI as parse-impl chunk loop participant PP as processParsing participant Pool as WorkerPool participant Slot as Slot N participant W as Worker N participant Cache as parseCache PI->>PI: computeChunkHash(files) PI->>Cache: usedKeys.add(chunkHash) PI->>Cache: entries.get(chunkHash) Cache-->>PI: undefined — cache miss PI->>PP: processParsing(chunk, workerPool) PP->>Pool: dispatch(items) Note over Pool: filter quarantined paths
buildDispatchMessage encodes each
file content via TextEncoder Pool->>Slot: postMessage(payload, transferList) Slot->>W: structured-clone payload
zero-copy transfer file ArrayBuffers Note over W: TextDecoder.decode
content Uint8Array → string
at tree-sitter call site loop per file W->>Slot: starting-file path Slot-->>Pool: record in-flight path W->>W: tree-sitter parse + extract W->>Slot: progress end W->>Slot: sub-batch-done W->>Slot: result Slot-->>Pool: collect results Pool-->>PP: results PP-->>PI: mergedData PI->>Cache: entries.set(chunkHash, rawResults) Note over Cache: cache write proceeds —
no quarantine intersection ``` --- ## Worker death + quarantine + cache-skip ```mermaid sequenceDiagram autonumber participant PI as parse-impl chunk loop participant PP as processParsing participant Pool as WorkerPool participant Slot as Slot N participant W as Worker N (alive) participant W2 as Worker N (replacement) participant Cache as parseCache PI->>PP: processParsing(a.ts, poison.ts, c.ts) PP->>Pool: dispatch Pool->>Slot: postMessage(payload, transferList) Slot->>W: deliver W->>Slot: starting-file a.ts Slot-->>Pool: inFlightPath = a.ts W->>Slot: progress + sub-batch-done for a.ts W->>Slot: starting-file poison.ts Slot-->>Pool: inFlightPath = poison.ts Note over W: tree-sitter SIGSEGV
or uncaught throw W--xSlot: exit code 134 Slot->>Pool: handleWorkerDeath inFlight=poison.ts Note over Pool: Layer 3 quarantine.add(poison.ts)
respawnCount slot N ++ (within budget) Pool->>W2: spawn replacement W2->>Slot: ready handshake Pool->>Slot: re-dispatch c.ts only Note over Slot: poison.ts filtered out
by Layer 3 pre-dispatch Slot->>W2: postMessage W2->>Slot: result for c.ts Slot-->>Pool: collect results Pool-->>PP: merged data — a.ts and c.ts only Note over PP: poison.ts symbols absent
from this run's graph PP->>Pool: getQuarantinedPaths() Pool-->>PP: [poison.ts] PP->>PP: warn log — 1 file quarantined PP-->>PI: mergedData (no rescue) PI->>Pool: getQuarantinedPaths() Pool-->>PI: [poison.ts] Note over PI: chunkFiles intersects quarantine PI--xCache: SKIP entries.set(chunkHash) Note over Cache: chunk stays uncached
next analyze gets a fresh pool
cache miss triggers retry ``` --- ## Circuit breaker trip ```mermaid sequenceDiagram autonumber participant PP as processParsing participant Pool as WorkerPool participant L1 as Layer 1 Respawn participant L2 as Layer 2 Breaker participant Slot as Slot N participant W as Worker N loop until threshold PP->>Pool: dispatch Pool->>Slot: deliver Slot->>W: postMessage W--xSlot: exit Slot->>L1: bump respawn + consecutiveFailures alt budget OK L1->>Slot: replaceWorker else respawnCount exceeded L1->>Pool: drop slot end Note over L2: check threshold
crashes AND pure-timeouts both count end L2--xPool: tripBreaker Note over Pool: WorkerPoolDispatchError
carries quarantinedPaths snapshot Pool-->>PP: reject — no sequential rescue PP-->>PP: error propagates to analyze entry Note over PP: operator sees hard failure
with quarantine snapshot
instead of silently-degraded graph ``` --- ## Resilience layers (the contract) | # | Layer | Triggered when | Bound | |---|---|---|---| | 1 | **Respawn budget** | Worker exits / errors / messageerrors | `maxRespawnsPerSlot` (default 3, env `GITNEXUS_WORKER_MAX_RESPAWNS_PER_SLOT`) — slot dropped from rotation when exceeded | | 2 | **Circuit breaker** | Per-slot consecutive failure count crosses threshold (crashes AND idle-timeout retries both count) | `consecutiveFailureThreshold` (default `max(3, poolSize)`, env `GITNEXUS_WORKER_CONSECUTIVE_FAILURE_THRESHOLD`) — pool rejects further dispatches | | 3 | **Session-scoped quarantine** | In-flight file identified at moment of worker death | `Set` on the pool — filtered out of subsequent dispatches; surfaced via `getQuarantinedPaths()` | | 4 | **Starting-file attribution** | Worker emits `{type:'starting-file', path}` before each parse | Pool's `inFlightPath[slot]` is the authoritative culprit on death; falls back to `items[lastProgress]` heuristic when no starting-file observed | | 5 | **Cumulative timeout budget** | Total wall-time across a job's retries/splits exceeds budget | `maxCumulativeTimeoutMs` (default 5× sub-batch timeout, env `GITNEXUS_WORKER_MAX_CUMULATIVE_TIMEOUT_MS`) — prevents exponential backoff from inflating into multi-hour stalls | | — | **Ready handshake** | Initial spawn + every replacement spawn | `WORKER_READY_TIMEOUT_MS` (5s) — worker emits `{type:'ready'}` after top-of-script init; pool drops the slot if not seen within budget | | — | **Slot-generation guard** | Late events arriving after a slot has been respawned | Per-slot generation counter; handlers short-circuit on stale generation, no double-recovery | --- ## IPC: native `postMessage` + zero-copy `transferList` No custom wire format. Workers and pool exchange POJO via `worker.postMessage(value, transferList)`. Node's `postMessage` runs V8's structured-clone algorithm internally — the same algorithm that preserves Map / Set / Date / RegExp / BigInt / TypedArray / undefined / circular refs natively. There is no JSON layer to lose them. **Dispatch payload shape** (built by `buildDispatchMessage`): ```ts { type: 'sub-batch', files: Array<{ path: string; content: Uint8Array }> } ``` The file `content` is a `Uint8Array` (not a string) so its underlying `ArrayBuffer` can be transferred zero-copy via the `transferList` argument. The worker calls `TextDecoder.decode` lazily at the tree-sitter call site — one decode pass on the worker thread, in parallel with continued main-thread work. **Transfer-safety contract.** Content `Uint8Array` instances are allocated via `TextEncoder.encode`, which produces a dedicated `ArrayBuffer` per call. `Buffer.from(str, 'utf8')` and `Buffer.alloc` may carve from Node's shared `Buffer.poolSize` slab, and transferring one pool-backed `ArrayBuffer` detaches every other Buffer sharing the slab — silent data corruption. TextEncoder bypasses the pool; transferring its outputs is safe. Pinned by `test/unit/worker-pool-transferlist.test.ts` (8 ArrayBuffer identities for 8 small files). **Why no wrapper protocol.** An earlier iteration of this PR introduced a binary frame (`protocol.ts` — 1-byte tag + 4-byte LE length + V8-serialized body). Removed in commit `6c6fc774`: that layer was a redundant `V8.serialize → Buffer → postMessage(struct-clone-Buffer)` double-walk, because `postMessage` runs the same structured-clone algorithm `v8.serialize` would call. Dropping the wrapper cut one full clone pass per message and ~430 LOC of framing code + tests. --- ## Cross-run cache integrity ```mermaid flowchart LR classDef path fill:#2d4a3e,stroke:#7ab87d,color:#fff classDef skip fill:#4a2d2d,stroke:#c97a7a,color:#fff A[Chunk N dispatched]:::path B{Any chunk file in pool.getQuarantinedPaths?} C[cache.entries.set chunkHash, rawResults]:::path D[SKIP cache.entries.set]:::skip E[cache.usedKeys.add chunkHash both branches] F[Next analyze fresh pool cache hit/miss] A --> B B -->|No| C B -->|Yes| D C --> E D --> E E --> F ``` Before the fix, a chunk containing a quarantined file would persist the *partial* worker output under the *full-coverage* chunk hash. The next analyze with unchanged content would hit the cache and silently replay incomplete results — symbols for the quarantined file permanently missing until the file's content changed. After the fix, the chunk stays uncached so the next analyze gets a fresh pool (quarantine is session-scoped) and a clean retry. --- ## Configuration knobs | Env var | CLI flag | Default | Purpose | |---|---|---|---| | `GITNEXUS_WORKER_POOL_SIZE` | `--workers ` | `min(16, cores-1)` | Parse worker pool size. `0` = sequential. | | `GITNEXUS_PARSE_CHUNK_CONCURRENCY` | — | 2 | Pre-fetch concurrency for chunk file reads (dispatch itself stays serial — pool is non-reentrant). | | `GITNEXUS_CHUNK_BYTE_BUDGET` | — | `2 MB` | Per-chunk byte budget. Smaller = finer cache-invalidation granularity. | | `GITNEXUS_WORKER_SUB_BATCH_TIMEOUT_MS` | `--worker-timeout ` × 1000 | 30000 | Per-sub-batch idle timeout. | | `GITNEXUS_WORKER_SUB_BATCH_MAX_BYTES` | — | `8 MB` | Per-job byte budget the pool sends in one `postMessage`. | | `GITNEXUS_WORKER_MAX_RESPAWNS_PER_SLOT` | — | 3 | Layer 1 — per-slot respawn budget before drop. | | `GITNEXUS_WORKER_MAX_CUMULATIVE_TIMEOUT_MS` | — | 5× sub-batch timeout | Layer 5 — total wall-time budget per job. | | `GITNEXUS_WORKER_CONSECUTIVE_FAILURE_THRESHOLD` | — | `max(3, poolSize)` | Layer 2 — consecutive deaths to trip breaker. | | `GITNEXUS_VERBOSE` | `-v / --verbose` | unset | Verbose ingestion logging (skipped-file warnings, per-chunk throughput, parse-cache stats). | --- ## Implementation highlights - **Layered pool resilience** (`worker-pool.ts`): all five layers + ready-handshake + slot-generation, all bounded - **TS captures parent-walk** (`captures.ts`): `findSelfOrAncestorOfType[s]` replaces per-match root-DFS in `findNodeAtRange`; drops `emitTsScopeCaptures` on `checker.ts` from ~7 min to ~3 s - **Quarantine module extraction** (`workers/quarantine.ts`): session-scoped `Set`-keyed snapshot API - **Native IPC + zero-copy** (`buildDispatchMessage` in `worker-pool.ts`): no custom wire format; `TextEncoder.encode` per content; `transferList` for ownership transfer - **Chunk-cache integrity** (`parse-impl.ts`): cache-write guard skips when any chunk file is quarantined - **Sequential-fallback removal** (`parsing-processor.ts`): workers are the sole resilience contract; pool failures propagate as hard errors instead of silent degradation - **CLI threading** (`analyze.ts`, `cli/index.ts`): `--workers`, env snapshot/restore, `--workers 0` - **Chunk concurrency** (`parse-impl.ts`): pre-fetch K chunks ahead via `parseChunkConcurrency`; dispatch stays serial - **Deferred extraction** (`parse-impl.ts`): per-chunk extraction passes batched to end-of-loop so workers stay busy --- ## Testing - **Worker pool resilience** — `test/unit/worker-pool-resilience.test.ts` (26 tests), `worker-pool-slot-generation.test.ts`, `worker-pool-windows-quarantine.test.ts`, `worker-pool-cumulative-timeout.test.ts`, `worker-pool-options.test.ts` - **Dispatch payload shape** — `test/unit/worker-pool-transferlist.test.ts` (6 tests pinning: Uint8Array per content, transferList in input order, pool-slab independence, non-parse / empty / mixed-shape fallback) - **Quarantine module** — `test/unit/workers/quarantine.test.ts` - **Cache integrity** — `test/integration/parse-impl-quarantine-cache-skip.test.ts` — real `worker_threads`, custom worker script crashes on poison.ts, asserts (a) surviving files in graph, (b) poison.ts NOT in graph (no rescue), (c) chunk hash absent from `parseCache.entries`, (d) second pass cache-misses + re-dispatches + still doesn't cache - **TS captures** — `test/unit/scope-resolution/typescript/typescript-captures-anchor.test.ts` — exact-count assertions on every anchor type the rewrite touches - **Wall-clock + multi-chunk** — `test/integration/parse-impl-large-fixture.test.ts` — synthetic large fixture, 30 s `Promise.race` budget - **Worker-pool integration** — `test/integration/worker-pool.test.ts` (28 tests) — real `Worker` threads, full lifecycle (death, respawn, breaker, ready handshake) - **Scope-parity cache-miss regressions** (#1066) — `test/integration/resolvers/{python,go,typescript,csharp}.test.ts` — exercise large UTF-8/ASCII files through real workers; native postMessage preserves Map fidelity so scope-resolution doesn't choke on the worker round-trip DoD §2.7 exact-count assertions throughout. **270/270 unit files + 7/7 worker-pool/parse-impl integration files green. 6133 unit tests + 822 integration tests passing.** --- ## Production-readiness review checkpoints External multi-lane review surfaced four addressable items, all closed: - **F1** — Unused `findMatch` helper removed (CodeQL was right; the sibling `countMatchesTsx` flag was a false positive — it IS called). - **F2** — `bench/parse-throughput.md` retitled as scaffold; self-contradictory "fill in before merging" instruction dropped. - **F3** — `WorkerPoolDispatchError.fallbackExcludePaths` renamed to `quarantinedPaths` (the "fallback" terminology was load-bearing under the pre-sequential-removal design; after the rescue path was removed, the rename reflects what the field actually carries). - **F4** — Timeout-retry IIFE in `worker-pool.ts` now checks `consecutiveFailureThreshold` and trips the circuit breaker. Closes a gap where chronic pure-timeout deaths accumulated counts that never tripped the breaker. Plus the CI-discovered issue that drove the architecture pivot: an early iteration of the IPC layer used a JSON-based protocol body, which silently destroyed every `Map` / `Set` / `Date` / `BigInt` / `TypedArray` / `undefined` value in the worker output. Production scope-resolution keys data structures on Maps throughout, so JSON serialization manifested as `'typeBindings is not iterable'` on large fixtures. The fix went through two iterations: first a swap to `v8.serialize` (binary structured-clone in a Buffer), then realizing the whole wrapper was redundant and dropping `protocol.ts` entirely for native `postMessage`. Final state — no explicit serializer — is both correct (full structured-clone fidelity inherent in `postMessage`) and faster (one clone walk instead of two). Deferred follow-ups (non-blocking, P2): - `groupedNodes` parallel map in `captures.ts:188` — replace with `Record` to eliminate implicit sync. - Exit-code-0 quarantine exemption in `worker-pool.ts` `exitHandler` — bounded by quarantine + respawn budget today; tightening adds a dedicated code-0 branch. - `WorkerPool.dispatch` non-reentrancy is documented in comments but not enforced by an assertion. No production caller violates it. --- ## Original task - [x] Inspect ingestion worker / fallback codepaths and existing tests - [x] Reproduce current behavior with baseline failures / perf hotspots - [x] Implement minimal robust worker subprocess handling so pathological single files cannot stall full-chunk parsing - [x] Add focused tests for timeout / retry / fallback behavior + performance guardrails - [x] Run targeted tests + required validation; summarize results

title: fix(mcp): setup fallback on Windows when global `gitnexus` resolves to a non-spawnable shim
body:
On Windows, `gitnexus setup` could persist a global `gitnexus` path that was discoverable via `where` but not actually spawnable by Claude/OpenCode MCP hosts. That left users with a broken MCP command and reconnect failures such as `Failed to reconnect to gitnexus: -32000`.

- **Windows MCP command resolution**
  - Tightened `resolveGitnexusBin()` so the Windows fast path only accepts a real `.cmd` / `.bat` launcher.
  - If `where gitnexus` returns only a shim/non-wrapper path, setup now falls back to the existing `npx` entry instead of writing an invalid command into editor config.

- **Affected setup outputs**
  - Claude Code MCP config now avoids persisting non-wrapper Windows paths in `~/.claude.json`.
  - OpenCode MCP config gets the same fallback behavior for its local command array format.

- **Regression coverage**
  - Updated the Windows setup regression tests to assert `npx` fallback when no spawnable wrapper is present.
  - Added coverage for the OpenCode JSONC path so both config writers stay aligned.
  - Added explicit `.ps1`-only Windows fallback tests so the original PowerShell repro path is covered directly.
  - Added direct Windows fallback assertions for Cursor and Codex so all MCP host config writers are covered, not just Claude Code and OpenCode.

```ts
if (isWin) {
  const cmdLine = lines.find((l) => /\.(cmd|bat)$/i.test(l));
  return cmdLine || null;
}
```

title: query returns empty results on Windows with "FTS indexes missing" warning
body:
### Area

gitnexus (CLI / core / indexing / MCP server)

### Summary

On Windows, `gitnexus query` / the MCP `query` tool appears to be unusable or degraded. A query against an indexed repository returns no results even though the repository has indexed symbols/processes, and the response warns that FTS indexes are missing.

### Environment

- OS: Windows 11 Pro 10.0.26100
- Shell used by Claude Code: bash on Windows
- GitNexus npm package latest version checked from registry: 1.6.5
- GitNexus MCP repo path observed:
  - `C:\workspace\source\open\claude-proxy`
- Indexed repo stats:
  - files: 61
  - nodes: 1818
  - edges: 4532
  - communities: 133
  - processes: 160
  - embeddings: 0

### Reproduction

Run a GitNexus query through MCP on Windows:

```json
{
  "query": "authentication",
  "goal": "minimal repro of GitNexus query on Windows",
  "task_context": "checking query failure for GitHub issue",
  "repo": "claude-proxy",
  "service": "src",
  "limit": 1,
  "max_symbols": 5,
  "include_content": false
}
```

### Expected behavior

The query should return relevant processes/symbols from the indexed repository, or `gitnexus analyze --force` should reliably build the required FTS/search indexes on Windows.

### Actual behavior

```json
{
  "processes": [],
  "process_symbols": [],
  "definitions": [],
  "timing": {
    "bm25": 30.9,
    "vector": 31,
    "merge": 0,
    "symbol_lookup": 0,
    "ranking": 0,
    "formatting": 0,
    "wall": 33.9
  },
  "warning": "FTS indexes missing — keyword search degraded. Run: gitnexus analyze --force to rebuild indexes."
}
```

### Additional notes

From reading the current search code, the warning appears to mean that all FTS query attempts failed, not merely that an FTS query returned zero matches. Empty FTS result arrays should still count as successful FTS availability.

GitNexus also appears to use LadybugDB FTS calls such as `CREATE_FTS_INDEX` / `QUERY_FTS_INDEX`, rather than SQLite FTS5 virtual tables. So this may be closer to a Windows LadybugDB FTS extension/index availability issue in the MCP/query path than an empty SQLite FTS table issue.

The `embeddings: 0` stat may be a separate but compounding problem: semantic/vector search has no data, so hybrid query falls back to BM25/FTS, and BM25/FTS is unavailable.

### Suggested diagnostics

- Surface/log the actual per-index error from each failed `QUERY_FTS_INDEX` call instead of only returning the generic `FTS indexes missing` warning.
- Confirm whether the Windows MCP repo/query connection pool successfully loads the LadybugDB FTS extension for the connections used by query execution.
- Confirm whether `gitnexus analyze --force` successfully creates the configured FTS indexes on Windows, and whether failures are being swallowed or downgraded.
- Distinguish these cases in status/query output:
  - FTS extension failed to load
  - FTS index does not exist
  - FTS index exists but query returned zero matches
  - FTS query threw an execution error

title: chore(security): remediate advisory noise from dev deps and auxiliary Python manifests
body:
## Summary

Workspace and Dependabot scanners report multiple GHSA/PYSEC advisories across the monorepo. Investigation shows **no known vulnerabilities in the shipped CLI (`gitnexus/`) production tree** (`npm audit` → 0). Findings come from **dev-only npm deps**, a **CI triage script**, and a **lang-resolution test fixture**.

This issue tracks cleanup so repo-wide scans (Dependabot, `npm audit`, OSV/IDE warnings) stop flagging false-positive production risk.

## Findings

### `gitnexus/` (CLI) — clean

- `npm audit` reports **0 vulnerabilities** in the production dependency tree.

### `gitnexus-web/` — devDependencies only

Source: `@vercel/node` in `gitnexus-web/package.json` (devDependency).

| Advisory | Package | Notes |
|----------|---------|-------|
| GHSA-2g4f-4pwh-qvx6 | `ajv` | via `@vercel/static-config` |
| GHSA-9wv6-86v2-598j | `path-to-regexp` | via `@vercel/node` |
| GHSA-2mjp-6q6p-2qxm, GHSA-4992-7rv2-5pvq, GHSA-c76h-2ccp-4975, GHSA-cxrh-j4jr-qwg3, GHSA-g9mf-h72j-4rw9, GHSA-v9p9-hfj2-hcw8, GHSA-vrm6-8vpv-qv8q | `undici@5.28.4` | via `@vercel/node` |
| GHSA-f886-m6hf-6m8v, GHSA-jxxr-4gwj-5jf2 | `brace-expansion` | via `@vercel/node` → `glob` / `ts-morph` (`1.1.12`, `5.0.5`) |
| GHSA-73rr-hh4g-fpgx | `diff` (jsdiff) | via `@vercel/node` → `ts-node` |

**Risk:** Does not ship in the production Vite bundle; affects dev/CI installs only.

### Python — CI triage script

Source: `.github/scripts/triage/requirements.txt` (used by `.github/workflows/triage-sweep.yml`).

| Advisory | Package | Fix |
|----------|---------|-----|
| PYSEC-2024-110 / GHSA-jw8x-6495-233v | `scikit-learn` | Constraint `>=1.4.0` allows vulnerable 1.4.x; bump to **`>=1.5.0`** |

### Python — test fixture

Source: `gitnexus/test/fixtures/lang-resolution/python-django-app-imports/requirements.txt`.

| Advisory | Package | Fix |
|----------|---------|-----|
| GHSA-5hrc-gvxj-w55p, GHSA-7h2m-m8vj-598h, GHSA-w26r-rmm8-9c29 | `Django==6.0.4` | Bump to **`>=6.0.5`** |

**Risk:** Fixture for indexing tests only; not a runtime service dependency.

### Not in scope of these warnings

- `eval/` (`pyproject.toml` / `uv.lock`) — no `scikit-learn` or `Django` in lockfile.
- `gitnexus-shared/` — no issues identified in this pass.

## Proposed remediation

- [ ] **`gitnexus-web`:** Update or replace `@vercel/node`; run `npm audit fix` for non-breaking transitive bumps (`brace-expansion`, `diff`).
- [ ] **Triage script:** Change `scikit-learn>=1.4.0` → `scikit-learn>=1.5.0` in `.github/scripts/triage/requirements.txt`.
- [ ] **Django fixture:** Bump `Django==6.0.4` → `Django==6.0.5` (or latest 6.0.x) in the lang-resolution fixture `requirements.txt`.
- [ ] Re-run `npm audit` in `gitnexus-web/` and confirm Dependabot/OSV alerts clear for the listed advisories.
- [ ] (Optional) Document in CONTRIBUTING or security docs that auxiliary manifests are scanned repo-wide and must stay patched.

## Verification

```bash
cd gitnexus && npm audit          # expect 0
cd gitnexus-web && npm audit      # expect 0 (or document accepted dev-only residual)
uv tool run pip-audit -r .github/scripts/triage/requirements.txt
```

## References

- Security scan plan: `docs/plans/2026-05-03-001-feat-automated-security-scans-plan.md`
- Dependency Review workflow: `.github/workflows/dependency-review.yml`
- Dependabot config: `.github/dependabot.yml` (npm: `gitnexus`, `gitnexus-web`, `gitnexus-shared` — no Python ecosystems configured today)

title: `--no-stats` does not strip index-summary symbol counts from AGENTS.md / CLAUDE.md
body:
### Summary

`gitnexus analyze --no-stats` is documented as *"Omit volatile file/symbol counts from AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md"*, but it does not strip the index-summary sentence inside the `<!-- gitnexus:start -->` block. That line still carries volatile counts, and because it's regenerated on every `analyze`, it causes merge conflicts when `AGENTS.md` / `CLAUDE.md` are committed and multiple developers run `analyze`.

### Environment

- gitnexus: 1.6.4
- node: v24.11.1
- OS: macOS (darwin)

### Steps to reproduce

1. In a repo with a committed `AGENTS.md` containing a gitnexus block, run:
   ```
   gitnexus analyze --no-stats
   ```
2. Inspect the regenerated block in `AGENTS.md` / `CLAUDE.md`.

### Expected

With `--no-stats`, the index-summary line is emitted without volatile counts, e.g.:

> This project is indexed by GitNexus as **<name>**. Use the GitNexus MCP tools to understand code, assess impact, and navigate safely.

### Actual

The counts are still present and change on every run:

> This project is indexed by GitNexus as **<name>** (9309 symbols, 15221 relationships, 292 execution flows). Use the GitNexus MCP tools to ...

Only the prettier-vs-gitnexus table formatting differs; the counts line is untouched by `--no-stats`.

### Why it matters

When `AGENTS.md` / `CLAUDE.md` are committed (the default, since `analyze` generates them), every developer's `analyze` rewrites this exact line with different numbers. Two branches that both ran `analyze` then conflict on it — a recurring, no-value merge conflict. `--skip-agents-md` avoids it by skipping the file entirely, but that also drops legitimate guidance updates.

### Suggested fix

Make `--no-stats` also omit the parenthetical counts from the index-summary sentence (symbols / relationships / execution flows) — or document that the flag does not cover that line and point to `--skip-agents-md` instead.

title: autoCheckpoint: true with 16MB threshold causes WAL rename crash during large indexing runs
body:
### Summary

  On large repositories (~60K+ node graphs), gitnexus analyze crashes mid-run with:

  Error renaming lbug.wal to lbug.wal.checkpoint: No such file or directory

  The process exits uncleanly and the index is left in a partial state.

  ### Environment

  - gitnexus: 1.6.5
  - @ladybugdb/core: 0.16.1
  - OS: Linux x86_64 (container, Debian bookworm)
  - Workload: ~60K node / ~63K edge Java codebase, full embedding run with Azure OpenAI text-embedding-3-large

  ### Root Cause

  In src/core/lbug/lbug-config.ts, createLbugDatabase hardcodes:

  true, // autoCheckpoint
  -1,   // checkpointThreshold

  checkpointThreshold: -1 is the sentinel that maps to LadybugDB's C++ default of 16 MB. During a large embedding run with thousands of node upserts, the
  WAL crosses 16 MB repeatedly. The race is:

  1. A checkpoint fires and deletes lbug.wal after flushing
  2. The next transaction's auto-checkpoint fires before the new lbug.wal is created
  3. LadybugDB tries to rename lbug.wal → lbug.wal.checkpoint — file doesn't exist yet → crash

  ### Workaround

  Patching the compiled output to set checkpointThreshold to Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER stops the crash — effectively disabling auto-checkpointing and relying
  on the explicit checkpoint in closeLbugConnection.

  ### Suggested Fix

  Change createLbugDatabase in src/core/lbug/lbug-config.ts to pass autoCheckpoint: false:

  false, // autoCheckpoint — disable mid-run checkpoints; rely on explicit checkpoint in closeLbugConnection
  -1,    // checkpointThreshold (unused when autoCheckpoint is false)

  autoCheckpoint: false is already a first-class supported option in the LadybugDB Node.js bindings (ladybug-nodejs main branch, src_js/database.js). The
  explicit db.close() in closeLbugConnection already triggers a final checkpoint cleanly.

  Alternatively, expose autoCheckpoint as a config option so callers can opt in/out.

title: gitnexus analyze crashes on Windows x64 — LadybugDB LOAD VECTOR segfault (0xC0000005)
body:
## Summary

`gitnexus analyze` crashes with `STATUS_ACCESS_VIOLATION (0xC0000005)` on every run on Windows x64. The root cause is in `@ladybugdb/core`'s VECTOR extension: `LOAD VECTOR` triggers a native segfault.

**Upstream bug:** [LadybugDB/ladybug#499](https://github.com/LadybugDB/ladybug/issues/499)

## Reproduction

```powershell
# Any git repo on Windows, any size — even a single-file repo
mkdir test && cd test
git init
echo "console.log('hi');" > test.js
git add . && git commit -m "init"
gitnexus analyze .
# Output:
#   GitNexus Analyzer
# <process exits with code -1073741819>
```

## Root Cause

The crash chain:

```
gitnexus analyze
  → analyzeCommand() (cli/analyze.js)
    → runFullAnalysis() (core/run-analyze.js)
      → initLbug() (core/lbug/lbug-adapter.js)
        → doInitLbug()
          → new lbug.Database(dbPath)         ✅
          → new lbug.Connection(db)            ✅
          → SCHEMA_QUERIES (33 queries)        ✅
          → loadVectorExtension()
            → conn.query('INSTALL VECTOR')     ✅
            → conn.query('LOAD VECTOR')        💥 0xC0000005
```

## Environment

| Item | Value |
|------|-------|
| OS | Windows 11 x64 |
| Node.js | v22.15.0 |
| gitnexus | 1.6.3 |
| @ladybugdb/core | 0.15.4 |

## Suggested Workaround

Until LadybugDB fixes the VECTOR extension on Windows, `loadVectorExtension()` in `lbug-adapter.js` could:

1. **Wrap `LOAD VECTOR` in a try/catch** and set `vectorExtensionLoaded = false` on failure (currently it already catches but the segfault kills the process before catch).
2. **Skip vector extension loading on Windows** as a temporary platform-specific guard.
3. **Add a `--no-vector` CLI flag** to `gitnexus analyze` to opt out of vector search.

Option 2 or 3 would restore basic `gitnexus analyze` functionality on Windows (minus semantic/embedding search) while the upstream fix is pending.

## Impact

**All `gitnexus analyze` usage on Windows is completely broken.** No repository can be indexed regardless of size or content.

title: fix(ingestion): Prioritize same-module Java type resolution for duplicate FQNs across modules
body:
In multi-module Java repos, duplicate package/class names (same FQN shape across modules) could be resolved against the wrong class candidate, producing missing or misdirected call relationships. This change introduces same-module-first candidate ordering so callers prefer targets in their own module before cross-module fallbacks.

- **Java resolver: same-module candidate ordering**
  - Added a Java-specific `orderSameNameTypeCandidates` hook in `language-provider` wiring.
  - For ambiguous same-name class candidates, Java now applies a **generic path-affinity ranking** based on shared directory-prefix depth between the caller file and candidate definition paths.
  - This avoids hardcoded repository-structure assumptions (e.g., `src/main`, `src/test`) while still preferring structurally local candidates when a clear signal exists.
  - If no structural signal is available (all candidates tie), ordering falls back conservatively.

- **Legacy call path scope adjustment**
  - Reverted the legacy DAG-specific Java ambiguity-ordering changes in `call-processor.ts` to keep legacy resolution unchanged while that path is being phased out.
  - The duplicate-FQN preference remains implemented through the Java provider ordering hook.

- **Scope-resolution safety**
  - Removed Java-specific same-module fallback heuristics from shared generic `walkers.ts` so non-Java resolver paths are not affected by Java layout rules.

- **Regression coverage: multi-module duplicate-FQN fixture**
  - Added `java-duplicate-fqn-modules` fixture with:
    - `module1/src/main/java/com/example/UserService.java`
    - `module2/src/main/java/com/example/UserService.java`
  - Added integration assertions ensuring each module’s `run()` resolves to its own module’s `UserService`.
  - Added negative assertions ensuring wrong cross-module `CALLS` edges are **not** emitted.

- **Parity-run handling for phased-out legacy DAG**
  - Updated resolver test parity helpers to mark the two new duplicate-FQN Java assertions as expected skips in legacy parity mode (`REGISTRY_PRIMARY_JAVA=0`).
  - This keeps parity sweeps green while preserving strict assertions in default/scope-resolution mode.

```ts
// java.ts
orderSameNameTypeCandidates: orderJavaSameNameTypeCandidates
```

title: [Feature Request] Support edge creation for unresolved external method calls with filtering mechanism
body:
### Area

gitnexus (CLI / core / indexing / MCP server)

### Problem or opportunity

**Background & Problem Description:**
When analyzing code graphs using GitNexus, I noticed that if the implementation of a called method is not within the current project scope, GitNexus does not establish an edge for this call. This results in the loss of critical business call-chain information (e.g., cross-system/microservice RPC calls, crucial infrastructure API invocations).

As shown in the attached image, the business code initiates a core asynchronous interface call via `B_InvokeInterface.B_asyncInvoke`. However, because the implementation of this interface is missing from the currently analyzed project, this call edge is not created, leading to a gap in key trace information.

**Expected Benefits:**
Enhances GitNexus's capability to visualize and analyze cross-system and dependency library call relationships, preventing broken business traces. Additionally, a flexible filtering mechanism ensures graph clarity and a high signal-to-noise ratio.

<!-- Failed to upload "image.png" -->

### Proposed solution

1. **Retain External Call Edges:** During code analysis, even if the implementation of a called method is not found in the current project, generate an "External/Unresolved Node" and establish the call edge to ensure the complete representation of the business logic flow.
2. **Provide Blacklist Filtering Configuration:** To prevent excessive noise in the graph caused by creating edges for all external calls (such as standard output, logging, etc.), introduce configurable filtering rules via a configuration file or UI. Allow the use of wildcards or regular expressions to ignore specific packages or method names.
* Configuration example: `ignore_unresolved_calls: ["*log*", "println*", "java.util.*"]`

title: [Bug] FTS indexes consistently fail on large repositories — query returns empty results even after repeated analyze --force``
body:
### Area gitnexus (CLI / core / indexing / MCP server) ### Summary ### Summary When indexing **large repositories** (5000+ files), the FTS (Full-Text Search) indexes consistently fail to build. `gitnexus query` always returns empty results with the warning: ``` "warning": "FTS indexes missing — keyword search degraded. Run: gitnexus analyze --force to rebuild indexes." ``` **Critically, running `gitnexus analyze --force` does NOT fix the issue.** Even after: - Repeated `analyze --force` multiple times → **same warning, same empty results** - Deleting the entire `.gitnexus` directory and re-analyzing from scratch → **same result** - The `analyze` command reports "Repository indexed successfully" every time → **but FTS indexes are still missing** The warning itself suggests `analyze --force` as the fix, but **the fix does not work**. This creates a dead-loop: ``` query fails → "run analyze --force" → analyze --force succeeds → query fails → "run analyze --force" → ... ``` Smaller repositories (< 100 files) index and query without any issues. ### Observed Behavior **Small repo (PythonCodeHub, ~86-132 files):** ```bash gitnexus analyze --force # ✅ indexing succeeds, FTS works, query returns results ``` **Large repo (bk-monitor, 5000+ Python files):** ```bash # First attempt gitnexus analyze --force # → "Repository indexed successfully" gitnexus query -r bk-monitor "models.py" { "processes": [], "process_symbols": [], "definitions": [], "timing": { "vector": 16.3, "bm25": 17.3, "merge": 0, "symbol_lookup": 0, "ranking": 0, "formatting": 0, "wall": 17.9 }, "warning": "FTS indexes missing — keyword search degraded. Run: gitnexus analyze --force to rebuild indexes." } # Second attempt — run analyze --force AGAIN gitnexus analyze --force # → "Repository indexed successfully" (again) gitnexus query -r bk-monitor "models.py" # → Same empty result, same FTS warning ❌ # Third attempt — delete everything and start over rm -rf .gitnexus gitnexus analyze --force # → "Repository indexed successfully" (again) gitnexus query -r bk-monitor "models.py" # → Same empty result, same FTS warning ❌ ``` Key observations: - **`analyze --force` completes "successfully" every time** but FTS indexes are NEVER created for large repos - **Deleting `.gitnexus` entirely and re-analyzing does NOT help** - **Repeated `analyze --force` does NOT help** — the warning is self-referential and the suggested fix is ineffective - **Other tools work fine**: `context`, `impact`, `cypher` all return normal results — the graph itself is built correctly - **Only `query` is broken** — because it depends on FTS/BM25 which never gets created - **Small repos never hit this issue** — FTS indexes are created successfully ### Dead-Loop Diagram ```mermaid flowchart TD A["gitnexus query
→ empty results + FTS warning"] --> B["Warning says:
Run analyze --force"] B --> C["gitnexus analyze --force
→ 'Repository indexed successfully'"] C --> D["gitnexus query
→ empty results + FTS warning"] D --> B E["rm -rf .gitnexus
gitnexus analyze --force"] --> C style A fill:#f44336,color:#fff style D fill:#f44336,color:#fff style C fill:#FF9800,color:#fff ``` > ⚠️ The suggested fix (`analyze --force`) is part of the problem — it gives a **false sense of success** while FTS indexes remain missing. ### Root Cause Analysis This appears to be related to the FTS index creation lifecycle for large repositories. Based on the code and prior issues (#1074, #1107): ```mermaid flowchart TD A["gitnexus analyze --force"] --> B["Parse files & build graph
✅ Works for large repos"] B --> C{"Create FTS indexes?"} C -->|"Small repo"| D["✅ FTS created
query works"] C -->|"Large repo"| E["❌ FTS creation fails
silently or crashes"] E --> F["Possible causes:
1. OOM / memory pressure
2. LadybugDB FTS segfault
3. Timeout swallowed
4. Batch size too large"] F --> G["analyze reports success
but FTS never exists"] G --> H["query: no FTS → no BM25
→ empty results forever"] style E fill:#f44336,color:#fff style G fill:#f44336,color:#fff style H fill:#f44336,color:#fff ``` Possible causes for large-repo failure: 1. **Memory pressure**: Large repos generate more FTS data, potentially causing OOM or native crashes during `CREATE_FTS_INDEX` (similar to the segfault observed in #1107) 2. **LadybugDB FTS extension instability**: The FTS extension may crash silently under load, and the analyze pipeline doesn't detect the failure — it exits with "Repository indexed successfully" 3. **Timeout or connection issues**: FTS creation may time out for large data sets but the error is swallowed 4. **Silent failure in index creation**: The `analyze` command may not verify that FTS indexes actually exist after creation, so a failed creation goes unreported ### Expected Behavior 1. `gitnexus analyze --force` should **reliably** create FTS indexes for repositories of any size 2. If FTS creation fails, `analyze` should **report it as an ERROR** — not claim "Repository indexed successfully" 3. `gitnexus query` should return results for large repos just as it does for small ones 4. At minimum, provide a **standalone command** to create/repair FTS indexes without re-analyzing the entire repo (e.g. `gitnexus fts-rebuild`) ### Steps to Reproduce 1. Clone a large Python/Django repository (5000+ files, e.g. bk-monitor with 5000+ Python files) 2. `gitnexus analyze --force` → reports "Repository indexed successfully" 3. `gitnexus query -r "models"` → returns empty results with FTS warning 4. `gitnexus analyze --force` again → reports "Repository indexed successfully" again 5. `gitnexus query -r "models"` → **still empty, same warning** 6. `rm -rf .gitnexus && gitnexus analyze --force` → same result 7. Try on a smaller repo (e.g. < 100 files) → **FTS works fine**, query returns results ✅ ### Environment | Item | Value | |------|-------| | OS | Windows (PowerShell) | | Node.js | v22.x | | **gitnexus** | **v1.6.5** | | Repo size | 5000+ Python files | | Symptom | `query` always empty, `analyze --force` claims success but FTS never created | ### Suggested Improvements - [ ] **Fix the core bug**: FTS index creation should work for large repositories, not just small ones - [ ] Add **FTS verification step** at the end of `analyze` — verify indexes actually exist before reporting success - [ ] Change `analyze` exit code to **non-zero** if FTS creation failed, instead of exit 0 with "success" message - [ ] Add **`gitnexus fts-rebuild`** standalone command to rebuild FTS indexes without full re-analysis - [ ] Improve **error handling** — if `CREATE_FTS_INDEX` fails, surface a clear error instead of silent degradation - [ ] Add **`--verbose`** flag to `analyze` to show FTS creation progress/results - [ ] Consider **batched FTS creation** for large repos (create indexes in smaller chunks to avoid memory/crash issues) - [ ] Update the **warning message** — currently it suggests `analyze --force` as the fix, but since that doesn't work, the message is misleading and creates a dead-loop ### Context _No response_ ### Expected behavior 1. `gitnexus analyze --force` should **reliably** create FTS indexes for repositories of any size, regardless of scale 2. If FTS index creation fails, `analyze` should **explicitly report an error** (non-zero exit code + error message) — not claim "Repository indexed successfully" 3. `gitnexus query` should return search results normally on large repositories, just as it does on small ones 4. `gitnexus analyze --force` should **actually fix** the missing FTS indexes — not create a dead-loop of "suggest fix → run fix → still fails → suggest fix" 5. If FTS indexes truly cannot be created via `analyze`, a **standalone command** (e.g. `gitnexus fts-rebuild`) should be provided to rebuild FTS indexes independently without re-analyzing the entire repository ### Actual behavior On large repositories (5000+ files): 1. `gitnexus query` **always returns empty results** for any search term with the warning: `"FTS indexes missing — keyword search degraded. Run: gitnexus analyze --force to rebuild indexes."` 2. `gitnexus analyze --force` **always reports "Repository indexed successfully"** but FTS indexes are **never actually created** 3. The warning suggests `analyze --force` as the fix, but **running it repeatedly never resolves the issue** — creating a dead-loop where the suggested fix is ineffective 4. Deleting `.gitnexus` directory entirely and re-analyzing from scratch **does not help** — same result every time 5. Other tools (`context`, `impact`, `cypher`) **work normally** — the graph is built correctly, only FTS-dependent `query` is broken 6. Smaller repositories (< 100 files) **work fine** with the same commands — FTS indexes are created successfully and queries return results ### Steps to reproduce 1. Clone a large Python/Django repository (~500+ files), e.g. `bk-monitor`: ```bash cd D:\projects git clone ``` 2. Navigate to the project and run `analyze --force`: ```bash cd bk-monitor gitnexus analyze --force ``` → Observe: "Repository indexed successfully" (no error) 3. Run any `query` command: ```bash gitnexus query -r bk-monitor "models.py" ``` → Observe: Empty results with FTS warning 4. Run `analyze --force` again (as suggested by the warning): ```bash gitnexus analyze --force gitnexus query -r bk-monitor "models.py" ``` → Observe: Still empty, same warning 5. Delete `.gitnexus` and try fresh: ```bash rm -rf .gitnexus gitnexus analyze --force gitnexus query -r bk-monitor "models.py" ``` → Observe: Still empty, same warning 6. **Control test** — try on a small repo: ```bash gitnexus analyze --force -r gitnexus query -r "common term" ``` → Observe: Works correctly, returns results ✅ ### Environment _No response_ ### Logs / screenshots _No response_

title: feat: Add `analyze --repair-fts`, enforce FTS verification, and harden repair safeguards
body:
Large repositories could end up in a false-success loop: `analyze --force` reported success while query remained degraded with missing FTS indexes. This change makes FTS failures explicit and adds a fast repair path that rebuilds only search indexes.

- **Problem surface tightened (P0)**
  - `analyze` now verifies all configured FTS indexes are queryable after index creation.
  - If verification fails, analyze exits with a clear error instead of reporting successful indexing.
  - FTS index creation no longer silently no-ops when FTS extension load fails; it now raises actionable errors.

- **Dedicated FTS repair path (P1-preferred)**
  - Added `gitnexus analyze --repair-fts`.
  - Rebuilds FTS indexes on top of an existing analyzed repo without full parse/graph rebuild.
  - Fails with explicit guidance when no base index exists yet.

- **Dead-loop warning updated**
  - Query degradation warning now points to `analyze --repair-fts` first, with `--force` as full-rebuild fallback.

- **Core implementation updates**
  - Extended `createSearchFTSIndexes` with per-index hooks.
  - Added `verifySearchFTSIndexes(...)` probe utility used by both full analyze and repair mode.
  - Normalized analyze option plumbing (`repairFts`) across CLI/core.
  - Hardened identifier handling in FTS verification probes.

- **Follow-up hardening from review**
  - `--repair-fts` now validates that the base graph store exists as a valid file before opening LadybugDB (not just path presence), preventing false “repair succeeded” outcomes on missing/invalid stores.
  - Invalid graph-store shape errors are now explicit (for example, reporting directory/symlink/socket vs expected file) with actionable rebuild guidance.
  - CLI rejects ambiguous usage of `--repair-fts` together with `--force` in early argument validation (before progress-bar startup) with a clear actionable error and exit code 1.
  - Added/updated focused failure-path tests covering:
    - repair without prior base analysis/meta,
    - repair with missing graph store,
    - repair with non-file graph-store path,
    - repair verify still reporting missing indexes after rebuild,
    - extension-unavailable error propagation,
    - full analyze failing when post-create FTS verification reports missing indexes,
    - early CLI rejection path for `--repair-fts` + `--force` including user-facing error assertion.
  - README command docs explicitly highlight `--repair-fts` (fast FTS-only path) vs `--force` (full rebuild).

```ts
// New fast repair path
gitnexus analyze --repair-fts

// Query warning now recommends repair-first:
"FTS indexes missing — keyword search degraded. Run: gitnexus analyze --repair-fts (or gitnexus analyze --force) to rebuild indexes."

// Ambiguous flag combination now fails fast:
"Cannot combine `--repair-fts` with `--force`..."
```

title: `validateHost()` normalize `localhost` into `127.0.0.1` pre-resolving and forcing device to use IPv4, cause problem if device only know IPv6
body:
### Area

gitnexus (CLI / core / indexing / MCP server)

### Problem or opportunity

`validateHost()` in @eval-server.ts normalize `localhost` into `127.0.0.1` which is an IPv4, this automatically force the device to use IPv4. The main purpose of `validateHost()` was to prevent user to pass arbitrary hostname into `--host` since passing a hostname might cause unpredictable DNS lookup. Therefore, this might cause problem for devices that only know how to resolve IPv6

### Proposed solution

This could be solved by not normalizing `localhost` since it is universally defined in /etc/hosts, decision between translating `localhost` will be done by the OS (OS will decide which IP to be bind).

### Alternatives considered

_No response_

### Acceptance criteria

- When the `validateHost()` doesn't normalize `localhost`

title: bug: ERR_DLOPEN_FAILED on Windows with Node.js v22 due to invalid prebuilt @ladybugdb/core binary
body:
### Area

gitnexus (CLI / core / indexing / MCP server)

### Summary

GitNexus crashes immediately on startup on Windows + Node v22 because the prebuilt binary for @ladybugdb/core fails to load via process.dlopen.

### Context

I was trying to set up GitNexus globally (and run it via MCP in VS Code) to configure AI models on a feature branch. However, the CLI commands fail immediately because the native database bindings crash on Node v22.x environments under Windows.

### Expected behavior

The tool should install and execute commands like 'gitnexus analyze', 'gitnexus serve', or 'gitnexus mcp' without native binary compilation or linking failures.

### Actual behavior

The app crashes instantly with 'Error: The specified module could not be found' pointing to lbugjs.node (ERR_DLOPEN_FAILED). This indicates that the prebuilt binary hosted on npm has broken DLL dependencies or was compiled against an incompatible toolchain/SDK version for standard Windows Node v22 runtimes.

### Steps to reproduce

Steps to reproduce

1. Use a Windows 10/11 x64 machine.
2. Activate Node.js v22.x (e.g., v22.22.3 via NVM).
3. Run npm install -g gitnexus (or invoke via npx gitnexus mcp).
4. Execute gitnexus analyze.

A manual workaround that fixes this for me is running node install.js directly inside the %AppData%\Roaming\nvm\v22.22.3\node_modules\gitnexus\node_modules\@ladybugdb\core directory

### Environment

body:
## Summary

Closes #933.

Adds a Kotlin scope-resolution adapter for the RFC #909 Ring 3 pipeline, following the Java migration pattern from #1482:

- add Kotlin scope captures for scopes, declarations, imports, type bindings, receivers, arity, local assignment aliases, and for-loop element bindings
- add Kotlin import interpretation / target resolution, binding merge, receiver binding, arity compatibility, and companion-owner population
- register `kotlinScopeResolver` in `SCOPE_RESOLVERS`
- wrap Kotlin resolver integration tests with `createResolverParityIt('kotlin')`

Kotlin is intentionally **not** added to `MIGRATED_LANGUAGES` yet. Forced registry mode currently passes 154/175 Kotlin resolver fixtures, below the RFC #909 flip threshold, so default behavior remains legacy while the adapter is available for forced/shadow validation.

title: fix(install): materialize vendored grammars to fix Windows EPERM (#1728)
body:
## Summary

Fixes #1728 — Windows `npx gitnexus` / MCP install failing with `EPERM` when npm tries to symlink vendored `tree-sitter-dart` (and proto/swift) from `file:./vendor/*` optionalDependencies.

- Remove `file:` optionalDependencies for vendored grammars (symlink/junction step during npm reify).
- Add `materialize-vendor-grammars.cjs` postinstall step: `fs.cpSync` from `vendor/` → `node_modules/` (real directories).
- Add `build-tree-sitter-swift.cjs` and strip Swift vendor `install` script (same #836 hygiene as dart/proto).
- Update packaging tests and README skip-grammars note.

## Root cause

Published `@ladybugdb`-style issue but for tree-sitter: npm ships `vendor/` in the tarball **and** declares `file:./vendor/...`, so install still tries to link vendor into `node_modules`. Windows without Developer Mode / symlink rights → `EPERM`.

## Test plan

- [x] `cd gitnexus && npx tsc --noEmit`
- [x] `npx vitest run test/unit/cli-commands.test.ts test/unit/materialize-vendor-grammars.test.ts`
- [x] `npm pack` + clean `npm install ./gitnexus-*.tgz` — no EPERM; `gitnexus --version` works; `tree-sitter-dart` is a regular directory with built `.node`
- [ ] CI full `npm test` on Windows runner (recommended follow-up)
- [ ] Manual `npx gitnexus@<next> mcp` on Windows host without Developer Mode

Closes #1728

title: feat(setup): implement antigravity integration setup and hook adapter…
body:
## Summary

  Adds Antigravity (Google) to the list of editors `gitnexus setup` configures automatically. Closes the gap
  raised in #79.

  When `~/.gemini/antigravity` exists, setup now writes:

  - **MCP server** → `~/.gemini/antigravity/mcp_config.json` (stdio entry, same shape as the Cursor/Claude Code
  configs).
  - **JSON Hooks** → `~/.gemini/config/hooks.json` under a top-level `gitnexus` group, with `PreToolUse`
  (`grep_search|run_command`) and `PostToolUse` (`run_command`) entries per the [Antigravity JSON Hooks 
  docs](https://antigravity.google/docs/features).
  - **Hook adapter + lock helpers** → `~/.gemini/config/hooks/gitnexus/gitnexus-antigravity-hook.cjs` (plus
  `hook-lock.cjs` and `hook-db-lock-probe.cjs` reused from the Claude adapter).
  - **Skills** → `~/.gemini/antigravity/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` per the [Antigravity skills 
  codelab](https://codelabs.developers.google.com/getting-started-with-antigravity-skills).

  The adapter mirrors the Claude Code hook but respects Antigravity's contract differences:

  - Tool names are snake_case (`grep_search`, `run_command`) instead of Pascal-case (`Grep`, `Glob`, `Bash`).
  - `PostToolUse` stdout **must** be `{}` — stale-index hints go to stderr rather than via 
  `hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext`.
  - `PreToolUse` surfaces graph context to the agent via `{ decision: "allow", reason: "..." }` so the tool 
  still runs.

  Setup is idempotent: re-running detects existing `gitnexus` hook entries and skips duplicates. Corrupt config 
  files are left untouched (same safety policy as the other editor adapters).

  ## Files changed

  - `gitnexus/hooks/antigravity/gitnexus-antigravity-hook.cjs` — new adapter.
  - `gitnexus/src/cli/setup.ts` — `setupAntigravity()`, `installAntigravityHooks()`, 
  `installAntigravitySkills()`, `mergeAntigravityHooksJsonc()`, wired into `setupCommand`.
  - `gitnexus/src/cli/index.ts` — updated `setup` command description.
  - `gitnexus/test/unit/setup-antigravity.test.ts` — 14 new tests.
  - `README.md`, `gitnexus/README.md` — Antigravity row in editor support table + manual MCP snippet.

  ## Test plan

  - [ ] `cd gitnexus && npx vitest run test/unit/setup-antigravity.test.ts` — 14 passing locally.
  - [ ] `cd gitnexus && npx vitest run test/unit/setup.test.ts test/unit/setup-codex.test.ts 
  test/unit/setup-jsonc.test.ts test/unit/hooks.test.ts test/unit/cursor-hook.test.ts 
  test/unit/setup-antigravity.test.ts` — 238 passing locally (no regressions).
  - [ ] `cd gitnexus && npx tsc --noEmit` — clean.
  - [ ] Manual: with Antigravity installed, run `gitnexus setup` and verify `mcp_config.json`, `hooks.json`,
  hook adapter files, and `skills/` directory are all written.
  - [ ] Manual: re-run `gitnexus setup` and confirm hook entries are not duplicated.
  - [ ] Manual: in an indexed repo, run a `grep_search` from Antigravity and confirm graph context surfaces; run
   `git commit` and confirm a stale-index hint appears on stderr after the index drifts.

  Refs #79

body:
Bumps [github/codeql-action](https://github.com/github/codeql-action) from 4.35.3 to 4.35.4.
Release notes

Sourced from github/codeql-action's releases.

v4.35.4

  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.25.4. #3881
Changelog

Sourced from github/codeql-action's changelog.

CodeQL Action Changelog

See the releases page for the relevant changes to the CodeQL CLI and language packs.

[UNRELEASED]

  • Breaking change: Bump the minimum required CodeQL bundle version to 2.19.4. #3894
  • Add support for SHA-256 Git object IDs. #3893

4.35.5 - 15 May 2026

  • We have improved how the JavaScript bundles for the CodeQL Action are generated to avoid duplication across bundles and reduce the size of the repository by around 70%. This should have no effect on the runtime behaviour of the CodeQL Action. #3899
  • For performance and accuracy reasons, improved incremental analysis will now only be enabled on a pull request when diff-informed analysis is also enabled for that run. If diff-informed analysis is unavailable (for example, because the PR diff ranges could not be computed), the action will fall back to a full analysis. #3791
  • If multiple inputs are provided for the GitHub-internal analysis-kinds input, only code-scanning will be enabled. The analysis-kinds input is experimental, for GitHub-internal use only, and may change without notice at any time. #3892
  • Added an experimental change which, when running a Code Scanning analysis for a PR with improved incremental analysis enabled, prefers CodeQL CLI versions that have a cached overlay-base database for the configured languages. This speeds up analysis for a repository when there is not yet a cached overlay-base database for the latest CLI version. We expect to roll this change out to everyone in May. #3880

4.35.4 - 07 May 2026

  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.25.4. #3881

4.35.3 - 01 May 2026

  • Upcoming breaking change: Add a deprecation warning for customers using CodeQL version 2.19.3 and earlier. These versions of CodeQL were discontinued on 9 April 2026 alongside GitHub Enterprise Server 3.15, and will be unsupported by the next minor release of the CodeQL Action. #3837
  • Configurations for private registries that use Cloudsmith or GCP OIDC are now accepted. #3850
  • Best-effort connection tests for private registries now use GET requests instead of HEAD for better compatibility with various registry implementations. For NuGet feeds, the test is now always performed against the service index. #3853
  • Fixed a bug where two diagnostics produced within the same millisecond could overwrite each other on disk, causing one of them to be lost. #3852
  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.25.3. #3865

4.35.2 - 15 Apr 2026

  • The undocumented TRAP cache cleanup feature that could be enabled using the CODEQL_ACTION_CLEANUP_TRAP_CACHES environment variable is deprecated and will be removed in May 2026. If you are affected by this, we recommend disabling TRAP caching by passing the trap-caching: false input to the init Action. #3795
  • The Git version 2.36.0 requirement for improved incremental analysis now only applies to repositories that contain submodules. #3789
  • Python analysis on GHES no longer extracts the standard library, relying instead on models of the standard library. This should result in significantly faster extraction and analysis times, while the effect on alerts should be minimal. #3794
  • Fixed a bug in the validation of OIDC configurations for private registries that was added in CodeQL Action 4.33.0 / 3.33.0. #3807
  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.25.2. #3823

4.35.1 - 27 Mar 2026

  • Fix incorrect minimum required Git version for improved incremental analysis: it should have been 2.36.0, not 2.11.0. #3781

4.35.0 - 27 Mar 2026

  • Reduced the minimum Git version required for improved incremental analysis from 2.38.0 to 2.11.0. #3767
  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.25.1. #3773

4.34.1 - 20 Mar 2026

  • Downgrade default CodeQL bundle version to 2.24.3 due to issues with a small percentage of Actions and JavaScript analyses. #3762

4.34.0 - 20 Mar 2026

title: feat(group): add rule-based HTTP mappings
body:
## Summary

Fixes #701.

This refreshes the closed #703 work on top of current `upstream/main` and adds rule-based HTTP mappings for repository groups. The feature lets `group sync` connect frontend gateway-prefixed HTTP consumers to backend provider routes when their literal paths differ.

## Background

@ivkond's PRs covered part of the broader group direction: manifest-declared links and the cross-linking / cross-repo infrastructure. They do not cover the core #701 / #703 case: deterministic rule-based gateway path rewrite, where a frontend URL like `/api/titans/<service>/<version>/...` needs to match a backend route like `/...` inside a specific repo/service boundary.

This PR keeps that behavior explicit and auditable through `group.yaml` rather than trying to infer gateway rewrite rules from source code.

## What changed

- Add `http_mappings` to `group.yaml` parsing and group creation templates.
- Preserve the public snake_case YAML shape when `group add` / `group remove` rewrite the config.
- Apply mapping rules before exact matching during `group sync`.
- Emit mapped links as `matchType: "manifest"` with `fromContractId` / `toContractId` bookkeeping.

title: Enhancement: group sync support for Consul and dynamic service discovery (.NET microservices)
body:
### Area

gitnexus (CLI / core / indexing / MCP server) — `group sync`, `group contracts`, cross-repo contract linking

### Problem

When using `gitnexus group sync` to map dependencies between microservices, GitNexus does not detect call relationships when services use **Consul (or similar) dynamic service discovery** instead of hard-coded URLs.

**Typical setup**

- Architecture: .NET Core microservices (.NET 3.1 / 6 / 8) communicating via Consul
- Service A calls Service B without a static URL such as `http://user-service/api/user`
- At runtime, Service A queries Consul for `"user-service"`, then builds the full request URL from the returned address/port and calls it with `HttpClient`

**Why static analysis misses the edge**

GitNexus builds cross-repo links from **static** extraction (literal strings, static imports, declared HTTP routes, etc.). When the final URL is assembled from Consul’s network response, the analyzer only sees a generic async call (e.g. `consulClient.Health.ServiceAsync("user-service")` followed by `HttpClient.GetAsync(dynamicUrl)`). It cannot prove that Service A depends on Service B.

**Expected vs actual**

| Expected | Actual |
|----------|--------|
| `group sync` recognizes that Service A depends on Service B (via Consul query patterns, discovery middleware, or declared mappings) | `group sync` reports no cross-repo dependencies, or omits critical edges, producing incomplete architecture graphs |

**Root cause**

Static parsers cannot predict return values from Consul (or other discovery) calls. A call like `consulClient.Health.ServiceAsync("user-service")` is treated as an opaque external call, not as a dependency on the `user-service` microservice.

**Impact**

Teams using service mesh / service discovery (especially .NET + Consul) get incomplete group-level dependency graphs, which weakens impact analysis and cross-service navigation.

### Proposed solution

Extend parsing / resolution / clustering (or group contract extraction) to support **dynamic discovery patterns**, in roughly this priority order:

1. **Configurable service map**  
   Allow a mapping file (e.g. `.gitnexus/service-map.yml`) to declare logical dependencies:  
   `order-service` → `payment-service` via Consul.

2. **Consul API pattern detection**  
   Recognize common call sites and treat the service name argument as a dependency edge, e.g.:
   - `consulClient.Health.Service("user-service")`
   - `consulClient.Catalog.Service("user-service")`
   - `consulClient.KV.Get("services/user-service")`

3. **Constant / config propagation**  
   When the service name flows from a constant or configuration key, connect it to discovery calls:
   - `private const string UserServiceName = "user-service"`
   - `IConfiguration["ServiceUrls:UserService"]`
   - `consulClient.Health.Service(UserServiceName)`

4. **.NET discovery library patterns**  
   Detect Steeltoe Discovery (`AddDiscoveryClient`, `AddServiceDiscovery`), `Consul.Extensions.Configuration`, and custom `DelegatingHandler` / `IServiceDiscovery` abstractions.

5. **HttpClient factory names**  
   Treat named clients configured with service discovery (e.g. `CreateClient("user-service")`) as consumers of that logical service.

### Alternatives considered

| Approach | Trade-off |
|----------|-----------|
| Manual documentation only | Error-prone; defeats automation |
| Runtime tracing only (Jaeger, Application Insights) | Accurate but outside GitNexus’s static model; could be a future hybrid import |
| Static config / pattern rules (above) | Best MVP within static analysis |

### Acceptance criteria

GitNexus should infer **order-service → user-service** (or equivalent) when code matches patterns like:

**Example 1 — direct `IConsulClient`**

```csharp
var services = await _consulClient.Health.Service("user-service", string.Empty, true);
var entry = services.Response.FirstOrDefault();
var serviceUrl = $"http://{entry.Service.Address}:{entry.Service.Port}";
var response = await _httpClient.GetAsync($"{serviceUrl}/api/users/{userId}");
```

**Example 2 — `IServiceDiscovery` abstraction**

```csharp
var userServiceUrl = await _serviceDiscovery.GetServiceUrlAsync("user-service");
var response = await _httpClient.GetAsync($"{userServiceUrl}/api/users/{orderId}");
```

**Example 3 — Steeltoe Discovery**

```csharp
services.AddDiscoveryClient(Configuration);
services.AddHttpClient("user-service").AddServiceDiscovery();
// ...
var client = _httpClientFactory.CreateClient("user-service");
var response = await client.GetAsync($"/api/users/{userId}");
```

Minimum bar for an MVP:

- [ ] Documented config override (service map YAML)
- [ ] Detection of `IConsulClient.Health.Service` / `Catalog.Service` with string literal service names
- [ ] `group sync` emits cross-repo consumer/provider edges for at least Example 1

### .NET / Consul integration landscape (priority)

| Library / approach | Typical pattern | Detection difficulty |
|------------------|-----------------|----------------------|
| Official Consul client | `consulClient.Health.Service("svc")` | Medium |
| Steeltoe Discovery | `AddDiscoveryClient()` + `AddServiceDiscovery()` | Higher (config + factory) |
| Winton.Extensions.Configuration.Consul | Consul KV configuration | Medium |
| Custom `ServiceDiscoveryHandler` | `DelegatingHandler` subclass | Higher |

Suggested implementation order: official Consul client calls first, then Steeltoe configuration + named `HttpClient` factories.

### Constraints

- Must remain compatible with GitNexus’s static analysis model (no requirement to run Consul at index time).
- False positives should be controllable via config overrides.
- C# / .NET analyzers should follow existing `LanguageProvider` / group extractor patterns.

### Contribution

- [x] Reporter is willing to open a PR (may need design discussion first).

---

_Original report was in Chinese; description translated and restructured for clarity per maintainer request._

title: fix(analyze): prevent cache-hit native workers from aborting
body:
## Summary

Fixes an intermittent `gitnexus analyze` abort seen on warm parse-cache runs, where the analyzer could still start parse workers even when every chunk was a cache hit.

This PR keeps the fix intentionally narrow:

- delays parse worker pool creation until the first cache miss actually needs workers
- falls back to sequential parsing when the initial worker ready handshake drops every slot
- captures/tees respawned analyzer stdout/stderr so native aborts are classified separately from heap OOM
- preserves single-line progress rendering when respawn output is piped for diagnostics
- routes large-file skip warnings through the progress logger while analyze progress is active
- adds targeted tests for cache-hit no-worker behavior, initial worker readiness fallback, respawn crash classification, progress terminal bridging, and warning routing

## Root cause

Warm-cache analysis was replaying cached chunk results, but `runChunkedParseAndResolve` had already created a worker pool before the chunk cache check. That meant a cache-hit-only run could still execute the parse-worker top-level module and load tree-sitter / N-API native bindings. On newer runtimes (observed with Node 25), that native path can abort the process before any cache miss requires parsing.

A second issue made diagnosis misleading: the heap-respawn path inherited child stdio, so the parent could not inspect child stderr/stdout after abnormal exits. Native `SIGABRT` / status 134 failures could be reported as heap OOM even when stderr contained a native binding crash signature.

## Validation

- GitNexus impact analysis before editing:
  - `ensureHeap` → LOW
  - `runChunkedParseAndResolve` → LOW
  - `createWorkerPool` → MEDIUM
  - `WorkerPool` → MEDIUM
  - `walkRepositoryPaths` → LOW
- GitNexus `detect_changes` on staged linked worktree → risk `medium`, 9 changed files, affected analyze execution flows only
- `./node_modules/.bin/vitest run test/unit/analyze-heap-respawn.test.ts test/unit/analyze-respawn-progress-terminal.test.ts test/unit/parse-impl-worker-lazy-cache.test.ts test/integration/filesystem-walker.test.ts test/integration/worker-pool.test.ts`
- `npx tsc --noEmit`
- `npm run build`
- `NODE_OPTIONS='--max-old-space-size=8192' npm test` → 355 files / 9140 tests passed, 1 skipped
