title: fix(php): avoid Blade templates triggering PHP scope extraction warnings
body:
## Summary `gitnexus analyze` emits repeated non-fatal scope extraction warnings for Laravel Blade templates (`*.blade.php`). Indexing completes successfully, but the warnings are noisy and confusing because Blade files are currently classified as PHP and passed through the PHP scope-resolution path. Example warning shape: ```text scope extraction failed for resources/views/.../*.blade.php: ScopeExtractor: no Module scope found for 'resources/views/.../*.blade.php'. Provider must emit at least one @scope.module capture per file. ``` ## Privacy note This report is based on a private Laravel application. The paths and examples below are intentionally minimized and sanitized; they do not include real project names, domains, credentials, business identifiers, or private source snippets. ## Why this happens GitNexus appears to classify files by the final extension. A Blade file such as: ```text resources/views/example.blade.php ``` is treated as PHP because it ends in `.php`. The PHP analyzer uses the `tree-sitter-php` `php_only` grammar and the PHP scope query expects a module capture like: ```scheme (program) @scope.module ``` However, Blade templates are not pure PHP. A minimal Blade file can contain Blade directives plus HTML: ```blade @php $label = __('example.label'); @endphp
{{ $label }}
``` When parsed as pure PHP, this can produce an error-root tree instead of a normal `program` root. As a result, no `@scope.module` capture is emitted, and `ScopeExtractor` reports: ```text ScopeExtractor: no Module scope found ... Provider must emit at least one @scope.module capture per file. ``` ## Expected behavior GitNexus should avoid noisy PHP scope-extraction warnings for Laravel Blade templates. Possible expected behavior: - Detect `.blade.php` before generic `.php` handling. - Do not run PHP scope extraction on Blade templates unless there is a Blade-aware parser/preprocessor. - Keep lightweight template scanning for useful route/form/AJAX URL discovery if desired. ## Actual behavior - `gitnexus analyze` completes successfully. - The same Blade files can emit repeated warnings during parse and/or scope-resolution phases. - The warnings are non-fatal, but they look like real analysis errors to users. ## Suggested fix One possible fix direction: 1. Add a Blade-specific classification before generic PHP extension detection. 2. Exclude `.blade.php` from PHP registry-primary scope extraction. 3. Preserve the existing template URL/form scanning behavior for `.blade.php` files. 4. Consider adding Laravel generated view cache directories to default ignores or documentation: ```text storage/framework/views/ storage/framework/cache/ ``` ## Relevant implementation areas Likely relevant files: - `gitnexus-shared/src/language-detection.ts` - `gitnexus/src/core/ingestion/languages/php/query.ts` - `gitnexus/src/core/ingestion/languages/php/captures.ts` - `gitnexus/src/core/ingestion/scope-extractor-bridge.ts` - `gitnexus/src/core/ingestion/scope-resolution/pipeline/phase.ts` - `gitnexus/src/core/ingestion/pipeline-phases/routes.ts` ## Environment Observed with GitNexus `1.6.5` on a Linux environment while indexing a Laravel application with Blade templates. ## Notes This is not a fatal indexing failure. The repository is still indexed successfully. The issue is that Blade templates are currently handled as PHP source files for scope extraction, which creates noisy warnings and may confuse users.

title: ci(web): use npm ci for deterministic Vercel installs
body:
## Summary

Switch the `gitnexus-web` Vercel install from `npm install` to `npm ci --include=dev` so the deployment install is deterministic and immune to build-cache drift.

## Motivation / context

Vercel restores a cached `node_modules` snapshot and runs the custom `installCommand` incrementally. With `npm install`, a lockfile change makes the incremental reconcile leave `gitnexus-web` without a usable `tsc` binary, so `npm run build` (`tsc -b && vite build`) fails with `sh: line 1: tsc: command not found` (exit 127). This is exactly what blocks #1705, whose dependency-graph change invalidated the cached snapshot.

`npm ci` is the npm-sanctioned install for CI/deploy: it ignores whatever is in the restored tree and installs exactly what `package-lock.json` specifies, so the build tooling (typescript, vite) is always present. `--include=dev` keeps devDependencies installed even if the build env sets `NODE_ENV=production`.

Related: #1705

## Areas touched

- [x] `gitnexus-web/` (Vite / React UI) — deployment config only (`vercel.json`)

## Scope & constraints

**In scope**

- `gitnexus-web/vercel.json` installCommand: `npm install` -> `npm ci --include=dev` for the web install step.

**Explicitly out of scope / not done here**

- The `gitnexus-shared` install step is left as-is (it builds cleanly today).
- No dependency version changes; no application/runtime source changes.

## Testing & verification

- Config-only change (no TS/source touched), so package typecheck/tests are unaffected.
- Real verification is the Vercel preview deploy on this PR — it should build green using `npm ci`.

## Risk & rollout

- Low. `npm ci` adds ~30s per deploy (relink only; Vercel still caches the npm download store, so nothing is re-downloaded). It does **not** disable Vercel's cache.
- Requires `package-lock.json` in sync with `package.json` (true on `main`). If it ever drifts, `npm ci` fails fast and visibly instead of silently shipping a broken install.
- Rollback: revert this one-line change.

## Checklist

- [x] PR body meets repo minimum length
- [x] No secrets, tokens, or machine-specific paths committed

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Low Risk**
> Low risk config-only change affecting deployment installs; main impact is deploy-time behavior (fails fast if `package-lock.json` is out of sync).
> 
> **Overview**
> Switches `gitnexus-web`’s Vercel `installCommand` from `npm install` to `npm ci --include=dev` to ensure deterministic installs and reliably include build tooling during deploys.

title: fix(cli): apply --no-stats to keep-marker stats line (#1706)
body:
## What

Closes #1706.

`gitnexus analyze --no-stats` is documented as *"Omit volatile file/symbol counts from AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md"*, but it did not strip the counts from the index-summary line when the block carries a `<!-- gitnexus:keep -->` marker.

The regular (no keep marker) path already respects `--no-stats` via `generateGitNexusContent` (#1477). The keep-marker branch of `upsertGitNexusSection`, however, rebuilt the stats line itself and always re-injected `(N symbols, N relationships, N execution flows)` — `noStats` was never passed to that function. For teams that commit a trimmed `AGENTS.md` / `CLAUDE.md` with a keep marker, every `analyze` rewrote that line with different numbers, producing recurring no-value merge conflicts between branches.

## How

- Thread `noStats` into `upsertGitNexusSection`.
- In the keep-marker branch, under `--no-stats` the stats line becomes `Indexed as **<name>**` — no parenthetical counts.
- The project name still refreshes, so a repo rename still propagates.
- `statsPattern`'s parenthetical is now optional, so a count-free line left by a prior `--no-stats` run still matches — the name keeps refreshing, and counts return if `--no-stats` is later dropped.
- `generateAIContextFiles` passes `options?.noStats` into both `upsertGitNexusSection` calls.

## Tests

- Updated the `#1508` review-F3 test: under `noStats` + keep marker it now asserts the volatile counts are **stripped** (previously it expected them rewritten), while keeping its Always-Do-tuple corruption guards.
- Added a test confirming the project name still refreshes under `--no-stats` + keep when the existing line has no parenthetical to match.

Full `test/unit` suite is green; `prettier --check` and `eslint` clean on the touched files.

## Risk / rollback

Low. `upsertGitNexusSection` is a private function with only the two in-file callers updated here. No public CLI/MCP contract changes — the `--no-stats` help text already promised this behavior. Revert is a single-commit revert.

title: ci(kotlin): add non-blocking forced-mode preview check with parity counts
body:
This PR adds CI visibility for Kotlin scope-resolution under forced registry-primary mode (`REGISTRY_PRIMARY_KOTLIN=1`) while keeping the required migrated-language parity gate unchanged and Kotlin production default on legacy mode.

- **What changed**
  - Added a new workflow: `.github/workflows/ci-kotlin-forced-preview.yml`.
  - The workflow runs on PRs that touch Kotlin resolver integration surfaces (Kotlin resolver source, resolver registry wiring, or Kotlin resolver integration tests).

- **Forced-mode preview execution**
  - Runs the Kotlin resolver suite in forced mode:
    ```yaml
    REGISTRY_PRIMARY_KOTLIN=1 npx vitest run test/integration/resolvers/kotlin.test.ts \
      --reporter=default \
      --reporter=json \
      --outputFile=kotlin-forced-preview-results.json
    ```
  - Marked as non-blocking via `continue-on-error: true` to preserve current baseline behavior while still surfacing regressions/progress.

- **PR-visible parity metrics**
  - Parses Vitest JSON output and publishes `total/passed/failed/skipped` counts to `GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY`.
  - Emits the same counts as a workflow notice for quick check-level scanning.

- **Scope intentionally unchanged**
  - No change to `MIGRATED_LANGUAGES`.
  - No change to required `ci-scope-parity` enforcement for already-migrated languages.

title: fix(lbug): add WAL checkpoint-threshold control
body:
Fixes the WAL rename/remove race that crashed large `gitnexus analyze` runs mid-index when LadybugDB auto-checkpoint hit the default ~16 MiB threshold. Keeps native auto-checkpoint always on (per maintainer requirement) and adds a JS-side manual checkpoint driver that pre-empts the native rotation, so the race window moves into a path where bounded retries can absorb transient FS failures (AV scanners, NTFS shadow copy, file locks).

## Behavior

- **Manual checkpoint driver** (`gitnexus/src/core/lbug/wal-checkpoint-driver.ts`): periodic `CHECKPOINT` issued from JS during analyze, wrapped in 3 attempts with 50 / 200 / 500 ms jittered back-off. Retries only on `isLbugCheckpointIoError`; every other error surfaces immediately. Opt-out via `GITNEXUS_WAL_MANUAL_CHECKPOINT=0`. Driver is analyze-only; MCP and other long-lived flows keep relying on the close-time `safeClose` flush.
- **Default checkpoint threshold raised** from `-1` (Ladybug stock ~16 MiB) to `67108864` (64 MiB). Default users no longer hit the original race; the recovery hint and the new default match.
- **Recovery hint** on persistent checkpoint failure recommends the same 64 MiB value plus a 32 MiB fallback for small-disk / CI runners. Hint detection moved into `lbug-config.ts` next to `isWalCorruptionError`; matcher uses strict + permissive regex tiers so a future Ladybug message-shape change degrades to the permissive fallback instead of silently breaking. Ladybug version is pinned in a comment beside the regexes.

## Public surface

- **CLI flag:** `--wal-checkpoint-threshold <bytes>` (integer ≥ -1; default 67108864; `-1` keeps Ladybug stock ~16 MiB).
- **Env var:** `GITNEXUS_WAL_CHECKPOINT_THRESHOLD` (same semantics). Flag overrides env when both are set — documented in `--help`.
- **Invalid env value** now emits a `logger.warn` and falls back to the default, closing the previous CLI-vs-env asymmetry (CLI rejects; env silently fell through).
- **Typed `RecoveryHint` union** in `gitnexus/src/cli/cli-message.ts` enumerating the 8 existing hint tags so this enum can't drift unnoticed. New tag: `'wal-checkpoint-threshold'`.

## Docs

- Root `README.md` and `gitnexus/README.md` updated with the new flag, env var, default (`67108864`), and a tradeoff note: larger threshold reduces checkpoint frequency but increases WAL size at rotation.

## Tests

- New integration test under `gitnexus/test/integration/analyze-wal-checkpoint-failure.test.ts` — drives a real `lbug.Database` + CLI spawn via `tsx` and provokes a real checkpoint failure portably (planting a directory at the rename target). No `vi.mock` of the orchestrator; no test-only injection hook.
- New unit suite for the checkpoint driver covering retry budget, backoff, opt-out, propagation of non-checkpoint errors, and exhaustion.
- Existing unit tests updated for the new default threshold, the `wal-*` rename, the strict + permissive regex tiers, and the warn-on-invalid-env path.

## Verification

- `tsc --noEmit`: clean.
- Affected unit tests: 67 / 67 passing.
- Integration test: 1 / 1 passing.

Example:

```bash
# default (64 MiB threshold + manual driver — safer on large runs)
gitnexus analyze

# disable the manual driver
GITNEXUS_WAL_MANUAL_CHECKPOINT=0 gitnexus analyze

# tune the native threshold explicitly
gitnexus analyze --wal-checkpoint-threshold 33554432
# equivalent:
GITNEXUS_WAL_CHECKPOINT_THRESHOLD=33554432 gitnexus analyze
```

title: fix(lang-kotlin): smart-cast type refinement for when/is and if/is (#1758)
body:
## Summary

Implements Kotlin smart-cast type narrowing for `when (x) { is T -> ... }` arms and `if (x is T) { ... }` blocks under `REGISTRY_PRIMARY_KOTLIN=1`. Closes sub-issue #1758 of the Kotlin scope-resolution migration tracker (#1746).

Today the Kotlin tree-sitter query has no captures for `when`/`if`-with-type-test, so narrowed receivers fall through to their declared type (`Any`) and `obj.member()` calls inside arms emit no `CALLS` edges. This PR adds:

- `@scope.block` captures for `when_entry` bodies (when condition is a single `is`-test) and `if_expression` then-branches (when condition is a `check_expression`).
- `synthesizeKotlinSmartCastBindings` in `captures.ts` — walks `when_expression` and `if_expression` nodes, emits a `@type-binding.annotation` capture binding the subject identifier to the tested type, anchored on the body so it lands in the matching Block scope.
- A `@type-binding.narrowed` marker + `kotlinBindingScopeFor` override so the scope-extractor's auto-hoist does not promote the narrowed binding to the enclosing function scope (which it otherwise would for unbraced arm bodies whose anchor coincides with the Block scope's range).

title: fix(lang-kotlin): cross-file iterable return propagation (#1759)
body:
## Summary

Closes sub-issue #1759 of the Kotlin scope-resolution migration tracker (#1746). Fixes two related cross-file return-type propagation gaps under `REGISTRY_PRIMARY_KOTLIN=1`:

1. **Package-scoped imports silently committed to the wrong file.** `import models.getRepo` resolved to `models/User.kt` (the first `.kt` file inside `models/` by iteration order) because `findKotlinFile` returned a single directory child as a fallback. The importer's module-scope mirror therefore only picked up `getUser → User` — `getRepo → Repo` was never mirrored, and `repo.save()` inside `processRepo()` fell through to no edge. This is why the test 487 \"identical fixture\" mystery existed: `processUser` worked by coincidence (first file alphabetically held `getUser`), `processRepo` failed because `getRepo` lived in a *different* file.

2. **For-loops over cross-file callables produced no element-type binding.** `for (x in getUsers())` did not produce a `x → User` binding when `getUsers()` was imported from another file, because `inferKotlinIterableElementType`'s call-expression arm consulted only the local file's `returnTypes` map.

## Implementation

- **`import-target.ts`** — split the legacy `findKotlinFile` into `findKotlinExactOrSuffix` (no directory-child fallback) and `findKotlinDirectoryChild` (legacy single-child preserved for compatibility). Added `findKotlinPackageFiles` returning `readonly string[]` — every `.kt`/`.kts` file inside a package directory. The resolver now fans out the stripped path through `findKotlinExactOrSuffix → findKotlinPackageFiles`, and the finalize pass picks whichever candidate's `localDefs` actually exports the imported name. This uses the existing `FinalizeHooks.resolveImportTarget: string | readonly string[] | null` contract — no shared-types changes.
- **`captures.ts`** — `inferKotlinIterableElementType` for `call_expression` now falls back to the callee identifier text when local return-types miss. `propagateImportedReturnTypes` chain-follows `loopvar → callee → ElementType` once the imported `callee → ElementType` mirror lands at module scope (which now works thanks to fix #1).

title: fix(lang-kotlin): method-chain fixpoint receiver types (#1760)
body:
## Summary

Closes sub-issue #1760 of the Kotlin scope-resolution migration tracker (#1746). Multi-step intra-file chains lose their type binding two hops before the call site:

```kotlin
val user = getUser()        // user → User ✓ (existing)
val addr = user.address     // addr → ?    ← navigation_expression value, not handled
val city = addr.getCity()   // city → ?    ← call_expression with navigation_expression callee, not handled
city.save()                 // no edge — city is unbound
```

The Kotlin extractor's `inferKotlinPropertyType` only handled `simple_identifier` and bare `call_expression` (simple-identifier callee) value shapes. Navigation expressions returned null, breaking the chain.

## Implementation

- **`collectKotlinClassMembers(rootNode)`** — per-file index of class fields (primary-constructor `val`/`var` params + body property declarations) and method return types. Per-file scope matches the existing extractor's design boundary.
- **`inferKotlinPropertyType`** gains two new cases:
  1. `navigation_expression` value — receiver type via `localTypes`, field type via `classMembers.fields`.
  2. `call_expression` with `navigation_expression` callee — receiver type via `localTypes`, method return type via `classMembers.methods`.
  Both return null when any link is unknown (safe over-conservative).

title: fix(lang-kotlin): overload target-id selection by parameter types (#1761)
body:
## Summary

Closes sub-issue #1761 of the Kotlin scope-resolution migration tracker (#1746). Same-arity Kotlin class-method overloads collapsed onto whichever graph node was registered first — `lookup("alice")` resolved to `lookup(Int)` even though the picker correctly narrowed it to `lookup(String)`.

## Root cause

`populateKotlinOwners` (which calls `populateClassOwnedMembers`) assigns `ownerId` and qualified names to class-owned function defs but leaves `def.type === 'Function'`. The graph parsing-processor, in contrast, emits a `Method` node label for class members. `resolveDefGraphId`'s parameter-typed key lookup (`graph-bridge/ids.ts:108-116`) is gated on `def.type === 'Method'`, so it was skipped for every Kotlin class method. With the type-keyed lookup skipped, the resolver fell through to `simpleKey`, which is first-wins by registration order — and the `Int` overload always registered first in these fixtures.

Traced through to confirm: `pickImplicitThisOverload` / `narrowOverloadCandidates` already pick the correct def by type (`lookup("alice")` → `[String]` candidate). Only the graph-id lookup was broken.

## Fix

`populateKotlinOwners` upgrades `def.type` from `Function` to `Method` after `populateClassOwnedMembers` assigns `ownerId`. This aligns the scope-resolution model with the graph's node labels so parameter-typed key registration and lookup operate in the same keyspace.

23 lines, single file.

title: fix(lang-kotlin): virtual dispatch via constructor type override (#1762)
body:
## Summary

Closes sub-issue #1762 of the Kotlin scope-resolution migration tracker (#1746). Kotlin virtual dispatch via constructor-type override didn't work under `REGISTRY_PRIMARY_KOTLIN=1`:

```kotlin
val animal: Animal = Dog()
animal.speak()  // should dispatch to Dog.speak (override), not Animal.speak
```

## Root cause

The Kotlin scope query emits both an annotation type-binding (`animal -> Animal`) AND a constructor-inferred type-binding (`animal -> Dog`). The generic scope-extractor's `typeBindingStrength` (scope-extractor.ts:874) ranks annotation sources (`2`) higher than constructor-inferred sources (`1`), so the annotation always won and `animal.speak()` dispatched against the static type — finding `Animal.speak` (not the override) or no edge at all.

Kotlin's runtime dispatch semantics expect the dynamic type: when the RHS is a constructor call, that's the class that actually runs, so its overrides should be the targets.

## Fix

In `emitKotlinScopeCaptures`, suppress the `@type-binding.annotation` capture when the underlying `property_declaration` has a `call_expression` value sibling. The constructor-inferred capture remains, becomes the sole binding for the variable, and receiver-bound resolution dispatches against the constructed class (and walks its MRO).

Intentionally Kotlin-specific. Flipping the generic precedence would change behavior for other languages whose static annotations are still the correct binding (e.g. C# with explicit interface types where the call should dispatch via the interface). Kotlin is the language where the constructor RHS is the dispatch target by design.

## Verification

title: fix(lang-kotlin): interface default method dispatch via implements-split MRO (#1763)
body:
## Summary

Closes sub-issue #1763 of the Kotlin scope-resolution migration tracker (#1746). Final sub-issue in the set — `user.validate()` on a class implementing an interface with a default-bodied method resolved to no edge under `REGISTRY_PRIMARY_KOTLIN=1`:

```kotlin
class User(val name: String) : Validator
interface Validator { fun validate(): Boolean = true }

fun run() {
  val user = User("alice")
  user.validate()  // should resolve to Validator.validate (default method)
}
```

## Root cause

The generic `buildMro` (`scope-resolution/passes/mro.ts:49`) walks `EXTENDS` edges only. Kotlin classes link to their interfaces via `IMPLEMENTS` edges (per the parsing-processor), so the implementor's MRO never picks up the interface's default methods — `findOwnedMember(User, validate)` returns undefined and there's no fallback to walk to Validator.

## Fix

Replace `defaultLinearize` with a Kotlin-specific MRO builder modeled after PHP's `buildPhpMro` (trait composition pattern):
1. Run the generic `buildMro` (EXTENDS-only) as the base layer.
2. Collect direct `IMPLEMENTS` edges as `class → interface[]` map.
3. For each class, walk its EXTENDS-MRO ancestors AND its own IMPLEMENTS edges to seed interface candidates, then BFS-close to pick up transitive interface inheritance (`interface A : B`).
4. Append the interface closure after the EXTENDS chain. Kotlin requires explicit overrides on conflict, so first-seen-in-MRO ordering is a safe approximation for method lookup.
5. Classes with no EXTENDS but with IMPLEMENTS edges (the #1763 fixture shape) get their MRO seeded directly from their interfaces.

## Verification

title: fix(analyze): make FTS index creation non-fatal during analyze
body:
## Problem

When the LadybugDB FTS extension cannot be loaded (e.g. macOS 12 where system `libc++` lacks `std::to_chars(double)`, or container environments without the native extension), `gitnexus analyze --embeddings` fails at 85% and aborts before embedding generation can run.

```
Analysis failed: FTS extension unavailable - cannot create FTS index File.file_fts.
```

This blocks the entire embedding pipeline even though FTS and embeddings are independent features.

## Root Cause

`createSearchFTSIndexes()` in `runFullAnalysis()` throws on failure, which is inconsistent with the MCP server's behavior: `pool-adapter.ts` already treats FTS load failure as a graceful degradation (`ftsLoaded = false`, BM25 search degrades, other features continue).

## Fix

Wrap `createSearchFTSIndexes()` in try/catch so that:
- FTS creation failure logs a warning instead of throwing
- Embedding generation (Phase 4) proceeds normally
- `--repair-fts` remains available for explicit FTS retry
- BM25 keyword search degrades gracefully (same as MCP read path)

## Affected Users

- macOS 12 (Monterey) — `libc++` missing `__ZNSt3__18to_charsEPcS0_d`
- Any platform where the FTS extension binary is incompatible with the system C++ runtime

## Testing

Verified on macOS 12.2.1 (arm64):
- Before: `analyze --embeddings` fails at 85% with FTS error
- After: FTS warning printed, embedding generation proceeds via HTTP API and completes successfully

title: feat(lang-kotlin): flip Kotlin to MIGRATED_LANGUAGES + close #1756 / #1757 (refs #1746)
body:
## Summary

This PR completes the Kotlin scope-resolution migration (RFC #909 Ring 3, parent tracker #1746) by flipping `SupportedLanguages.Kotlin` into `MIGRATED_LANGUAGES`. The flip is supported by closing two named flip blockers (#1756 companion-vs-instance dispatch, #1757 lambda scopes) and obsoleting the third (#1755 forced-mode preview CI is replaced by the post-flip `.github/workflows/ci-scope-parity.yml` matrix that auto-discovers Kotlin).

Closes #1756, closes #1757, refs #1746.

## What's in the PR

**Migration flip (U1):**
- `SupportedLanguages.Kotlin` added to `MIGRATED_LANGUAGES` in `gitnexus/src/core/ingestion/registry-primary-flag.ts`. Default production resolution now flows through the scope-resolution pipeline; the legacy DAG runs only under explicit `REGISTRY_PRIMARY_KOTLIN=0` for the CI parity comparison.
- `AGENTS.md` changelog row records the migration.
- Maintainer waiver of RFC §6.4 corpus criterion captured on #1746 (corpus-mode wiring tracked in #927); fixture criterion (≥99%) met.

**#1756 — companion-vs-instance dispatch (U2–U5):**
- New optional `ScopeResolver.isStaticOnly?(def): boolean` hook on the generic resolver contract.
- Filter wired across Cases 0 (compound receiver), 3b (chain-typebinding), 4 (simple typeBinding), and 5 (value-receiver bridge) of `receiver-bound-calls.ts`. Case 0.5 (`this`-receiver) documented as no-op because Kotlin doesn't enable `resolveThisViaEnclosingClass`.
- Filter runs **before** `narrowOverloadCandidates` (U2) so same-arity static+instance collisions don't collapse to `OVERLOAD_AMBIGUOUS`.
- Filter applied **inside** the MRO chain walk (U2) so a derived class's static-only member doesn't suppress an ancestor's legitimate instance method.
- Named companions (`companion object Helper { ... }`) and companions containing nested classes promote correctly via a new `(companion_object) @scope.companion` query capture + `kotlin/companion-scopes.ts` side-channel (U4).
- `__kotlinCompanionStatic` marker migrated to a module-level `WeakSet<SymbolDefinition>` (U5) — eliminates `as` casts, type-system illusion, and any serialization-survival risk.
- Cross-file companion factory: `Foo.create()` resolves via Case 2 cross-file (U6); chain-typebinding cross-file (`val x = Foo.create(); x.method()`) deferred as a follow-up issue (substantial fix needed in `imported-return-types.ts`).

**#1757 — lambda scopes (U9):**
- Lambda bodies create a new lexical scope (`(lambda_literal) @scope.block` query rule).
- Lambda parameter bindings (`forEach { user -> user.save() }`) and implicit `it` (`users.forEach { it.save() }`) bind only inside the lambda body via `synthesizeKotlinLambdaBindings` + `@type-binding.lambda-scoped` gate.
- Receiver-type inference for stdlib idioms: `forEach`/`map`/`filter` → element type, `let`/`apply`/`also`/`run`/`takeIf`/`use` → receiver type. `with(...)` and non-stdlib higher-order functions deferred as follow-up.
- Nested lambda shadowing is deterministic; the outer-`it`-shadow case is handled correctly.

**Tests + fixtures:**
- 6 new fixtures: `kotlin-companion-vs-instance/`, `kotlin-companion-mro-shadow/`, `kotlin-companion-named/`, `kotlin-companion-other-cases/`, `kotlin-companion-cross-file/`, `kotlin-lambda-scopes/`.
- New unit test `test/unit/kotlin-static-marker.test.ts` exercises the WeakSet round-trip.
- 33+ new integration tests in `test/integration/resolvers/kotlin.test.ts`: MRO same-name shadowing, named companions, compound/chain/value-receiver crossovers, lambda dispatch, edge-type completeness (USES/ACCESSES absence on crossover).
- Scope-resolver-only correctness wins registered in `LEGACY_RESOLVER_PARITY_EXPECTED_FAILURES.kotlin` with prose rationale (8 entries: 1 original + 3 MRO + 1 lambda + 1 named-companion crossover + 2 other-cases crossovers).

## Verification

| Run | Result |
|---|---|
| `REGISTRY_PRIMARY_KOTLIN=true npx vitest run test/integration/resolvers/kotlin.test.ts` (forced) | **208 / 208** |
| `npx vitest run test/integration/resolvers/kotlin.test.ts` (default, post-flip = registry-primary) | **208 / 208** |
| `REGISTRY_PRIMARY_KOTLIN=0 npx vitest run test/integration/resolvers/kotlin.test.ts` (legacy parity) | 200 passed + 8 documented expected skips |
| `npx vitest run test/integration/resolvers/java.test.ts` (regression net — Java not silently skipped) | 178 / 178 |
| `npx vitest run test/integration/resolvers/` (full suite) | **2254 / 2254** across 27 test files |
| `npx tsc --noEmit` | clean |

## Migration policy

Per parent tracker #1746, the flip requires either RFC §6.4 corpus parity (≥99% fixtures / ≥98% corpus) or explicit maintainer waiver of the corpus criterion. The **fixture criterion is met** (208/208 forced-mode passing, 200+8-skip legacy-parity). The **corpus criterion is waived** because corpus-mode shadow-harness wiring is tracked separately in #927 and never gated Kotlin specifically — same waiver precedent set for TypeScript in the `MIGRATED_LANGUAGES` JSDoc. The waiver is recorded in the #1746 tracker thread alongside this PR.

## Deferred follow-ups (filed as separate issues)

- Cross-file chain-typebinding (`val l = Foo.create(); l.method()` where `Foo` is imported from another file). Probe-found in U6; substantial fix needed in `imported-return-types.ts`.
- Companion overload graph-node registration (`fun build(Int)` + `companion object { fun build(String) }` produces only one Method node). Discovered in U7; uncommon idiom but worth tracking.
- `@JvmStatic` annotation handling for companion methods.
- `Foo.Companion.create()` explicit-qualifier dispatch.
- Local-variable-shadowing-class-name disambiguation.
- Receiver-type inference for `with(...)` and non-stdlib higher-order functions (U9 minimum scope deferred this).
- General `isStaticOnly` adoption for other languages (Python `@staticmethod` diagnostic, JS `static`).

title: fix(lbug): acquireInitLock fails with EROFS on read-only Docker workspace mount
body:
## Bug

When running `gitnexus index` + `serve` against a `:ro` Docker bind mount (the documented workflow in `.env.example`), the LadybugDB adapter crashes with:

```
EROFS: read-only file system, open '/workspace/dir/.gitnexus/lbug.init.lock'
```

### Root cause

`doInitLbug()` in `gitnexus/src/core/lbug/lbug-adapter.ts` (line ~729) calls `acquireInitLock(dbPath)` **unconditionally** — even when `readOnly=true`. The init lock creates a file at `${dbPath}.init.lock` inside the workspace, which fails on a read-only filesystem.

The lock's purpose is preventing a TOCTOU race during **DB creation** (orphan sidecar cleanup). Read-only opens don't create databases and don't need the lock or sidecar cleanup.

### Related

- PR #1550 fixed `ensureGitNexusIgnored` to tolerate `:ro` mounts, but this is a separate code path (LadybugDB adapter, not repo-manager)
- Reported by @sengirab in #1549 (comment) — confirmed on latest version

### Proposed fix

In `doInitLbug`, skip `acquireInitLock` and orphan sidecar cleanup when `readOnly=true`. The read-only path should go straight to `openLbugConnection(lbug, dbPath, { readOnly: true })`.

### Reproduction

1. `docker compose up` with workspace as `:ro` bind mount (per `.env.example`)
2. Run `gitnexus index /workspace/<repo>` (succeeds after #1550)
3. Any query/serve operation that opens LadybugDB → EROFS on `lbug.init.lock`

title: fix(lbug): skip init lock and filesystem mutations for read-only opens (#1783)
body:
## Summary

- Splits `doInitLbug` into a read-only fast path and a writable path
- Read-only opens skip: path cleanup (symlink/directory removal), `acquireInitLock`, orphan sidecar removal, and `fs.mkdir` — all of which write to the workspace filesystem
- Read-only opens go straight to `preflightLbugSidecars` (with `allowQuarantine: false`) → `openLbugConnection` → `ensureReadOnlyConnectionUsable`
- Writable opens retain the existing behavior unchanged (lock, cleanup, open)

Fixes the `EROFS: read-only file system, open '/workspace/dir/.gitnexus/lbug.init.lock'` error reported in #1783 and by @sengirab in #1549.

This is the companion fix to #1550, which addressed the same `:ro` mount issue in `ensureGitNexusIgnored`. The LadybugDB adapter was the remaining code path that unconditionally mutated the workspace filesystem.

## Test plan

- [ ] `npx tsc --noEmit` — clean
- [ ] `npx vitest run test/unit/repo-manager.test.ts` — existing tests pass
- [ ] `npx vitest run test/integration/lbug-lock-retry.test.ts` — lock retry tests pass
- [ ] Manual: Docker compose with `:ro` workspace mount → `gitnexus index` + query via MCP → no EROFS

title: fix: avoid forced exit after embedding analyze
body:
## Summary
- let successful embedding-enabled analyze runs unwind naturally instead of forcing process.exit(0)
- keep the existing forced-exit behavior for successful non-embedding analyzes
- add unit coverage for embedding analyze shutdown classification

## Why
On macOS arm64 / Node 20, local embedding runs initialize transformers.js / ONNX Runtime successfully, write metadata and embeddings, then abort during process.exit(0) with:

```
libc++abi: terminating due to uncaught exception of type std::__1::system_error: mutex lock failed: Invalid argument
```

A minimal probe showed natural Node exit after local embedding is clean, while process.exit(0) after embedder initialization reproduces the abort. This matches the post-success crash reported in #151.

## Validation
- npm test -- analyze-embeddings-limit.test.ts
- npx tsc --noEmit
- patched source CLI on disposable repo with --embeddings --skip-agents-md: EXIT_CODE=0, EMBEDDINGS=1
- patched source CLI on disposable repo without --embeddings: EXIT_CODE=0

title: fix(php): avoid Blade templates entering PHP analysis
body:
## Summary
- classify Laravel Blade templates as template/markup files instead of routing them through the PHP provider
- preserve PHP and PHTML analysis, including namespace-less PHP config and Mage-OS/Magento-style PHTML templates
- extract Laravel route parsing into a pure route extractor, ignore compiled Blade view cache, and link static Blade template URLs to prefixed Laravel routes
- exclude Laravel `asset()` helper URLs from Blade route signals so static assets cannot create false `FETCHES` edges when their paths collide with application routes

Fixes #1752

## Validation
- `cd gitnexus-shared && npm run build`
- `cd gitnexus && npx vitest run test/unit/ingestion-utils.test.ts test/unit/php-template-scope.test.ts test/unit/blade-template-routes.test.ts test/unit/laravel-route-extraction.test.ts test/unit/ignore-service.test.ts test/unit/worker-pool-slot-generation.test.ts test/unit/parsing-worker-fallback.test.ts test/unit/parse-impl-fallback.test.ts`
- `cd gitnexus && npx tsc --noEmit`
- `npx prettier --check gitnexus/src/core/ingestion/pipeline-phases/routes.ts gitnexus/src/config/ignore-service.ts gitnexus/src/core/ingestion/route-extractors/laravel.ts gitnexus/test/unit/ingestion-utils.test.ts gitnexus/test/unit/blade-template-routes.test.ts`
- `git ls-files -z | xargs -0 npx prettier --check --ignore-unknown`
- `git diff --check`

- Existing Laravel repos with prefixed route groups will show corrected route URLs after re-indexing, for example `/orders` inside `prefix('admin')` becomes `/admin/orders`.

title: fix(windows): pass windowsHide:true to every child_process spawn-family call
body:
### Summary

On Windows, every spawn-family call in this codebase
(`spawn` / `spawnSync` / `execFile` / `execFileSync` /
`execFileAsync` / `execSync`) asks `CreateProcess` to create a child
without `windowsHide: true`. Node then uses `STARTF_USESHOWWINDOW`
with `SW_SHOWDEFAULT` and a black console window flashes onto the
user's desktop for the duration of each call.

The flashes are unavoidable in two contexts:

- **Hook layer** (`gitnexus/hooks/`, `gitnexus-claude-plugin/hooks/`,
  `gitnexus-cursor-integration/hooks/`) — every `PostToolUse` / `Stop`
  event from Claude Code spawns `node` / `npx.cmd` / `git` / `lsof`.
  Under active editor use this is a near-continuous stream of
  pop-ups; the flashes stack on the taskbar and steal focus.
- **Daemon-spawned children** in `src/mcp/local/local-backend.ts`
  (`git diff` / `rg` for `detect_changes` and search) and
  `src/server/git-clone.ts` (`git config` / `git clone` from
  `gitnexus serve`) and `src/core/git-staleness.ts` (`git rev-list`
  on every MCP staleness check) — these run from processes that have
  no parent console, so Windows allocates one for the child and the
  flag matters even more.

CLI sites are less visible (the user has a console; `stdio:'inherit'`
shares it) but the flag is harmless and the test invariant should
hold uniformly.

### Fix

One option per spawn site, applied to every call:

```js
spawnSync(cmd, args, {
    /* ...existing options... */
    stdio: ['pipe', 'pipe', 'pipe'],
    windowsHide: true,            // ← new
});
```

`windowsHide` is **a no-op on macOS/Linux** ([Node docs][1]: "Hide
the subprocess console window that would normally be created on
Windows systems"). The patch is platform-neutral and zero-risk on
POSIX — the option is silently dropped by the POSIX spawn path.

[1]: https://nodejs.org/api/child_process.html#optionswindowshide

### Behavioural notes (preserved verbatim)

- **`stdio: 'inherit'`** callers (e.g. `cli/wiki.ts:522` opens the
  editor in the user's terminal) keep their interactive UX. The child
  inherits the parent's stdio handles; no new console is allocated;
  `windowsHide` has nothing to hide.
- **Piped callers** (`stdio: ['pipe',…]`) continue to deliver every
  byte of stdout/stderr back to the parent. No output is swallowed —
  the parent reads via the pipe and re-prints / processes the data as
  before.
- **`execSync` / `execFileSync`** callers that previously had no
  `stdio` option keep their default pipe semantics (`.toString()`
  still works) — `windowsHide` is added alongside the existing `cwd`
  / `timeout` / `maxBuffer` options.

### Files touched

**Hook layer (19 spawn sites):**

| File | Sites |
|---|---|
| `gitnexus/hooks/claude/gitnexus-hook.cjs` | 4 |
| `gitnexus/hooks/claude/hook-db-lock-probe.cjs` | 3 |
| `gitnexus-claude-plugin/hooks/gitnexus-hook.js` | 6 |
| `gitnexus-claude-plugin/hooks/hook-db-lock-probe.cjs` | 3 |
| `gitnexus-cursor-integration/hooks/gitnexus-hook.cjs` | 3 |

**Source tree (21 spawn sites):**

| File | Sites |
|---|---|
| `src/cli/analyze.ts` | 1 |
| `src/cli/setup.ts` | 2 |
| `src/cli/wiki.ts` | 3 |
| `src/core/embeddings/embedder.ts` | 1 |
| `src/core/git-staleness.ts` | 3 |
| `src/core/run-analyze.ts` | 1 |
| `src/core/wiki/cursor-client.ts` | 2 |
| `src/core/wiki/generator.ts` | 3 |
| `src/mcp/local/local-backend.ts` | 2 |
| `src/server/git-clone.ts` | 2 |
| `src/core/lbug/extension-loader.ts:96` | (already had it; convention source) |

Total: **40 spawn sites** now guarded. The pre-existing fix at
`src/core/lbug/extension-loader.ts:96` established the convention;
this PR generalizes it.

### Regression test

`gitnexus/test/unit/hooks.test.ts` gains a `windowsHide regression`
block (next to the existing "no `shell: true`" and ".cmd extension"
regression tests, same shape and spirit). It walks 16 files
(5 hooks + 11 source), counts spawn-family invocations in code
(stripping comment lines), counts `windowsHide: true` occurrences,
and asserts `hideCount >= spawnCount` per file with a `spawnCount > 0`
sanity gate.

The check is source-level rather than behavioural because:

- the flag's effect is observable only on Windows;
- GitHub Actions runs vitest on Linux for these tests;
- regressing this is easy (every new spawn site has to remember the
  flag), and a runtime check on a Windows-only CI leg would still
  let a PR land on `main` first.

Adding a new file is one tuple entry in `HOOK_FILES` or `SRC_FILES`;
the test itself never needs editing.

### Verification

- **Pre-fix (Windows 10 22H2, Node 22.21, gitnexus 1.6.5):** 2–3
  visible black-console flashes per Claude Code Edit/Write tool call,
  and additional flashes per MCP `detect_changes` and `gitnexus serve`
  git operation.
- **Post-fix (same host, locally-built tarball from this branch):**
  zero console flashes across an extended Claude Code session against
  a large mixed-language repo, plus MCP `detect_changes` and
  `gitnexus analyze` interactive runs (output appears in the terminal
  unchanged).
- **Linux/macOS:** byte-identical output; `windowsHide` is silently
  dropped by the POSIX spawn path. Existing CI smoke unchanged.

title: Feat/godot language support
gitnexus-web: Redesign the graph explorer for better readability on larger repos
body: ### Area gitnexus-web (browser UI / WASM / workers) ### Problem or opportunity The current graph explorer becomes visually hard to understand once the graph gets moderately large. In the current force-directed presentation, many nodes and edges overlap into a dense cluster, which makes it difficult to identify structure, communities, and meaningful relationships at a glance. In practice, this reduces the usefulness of the graph for exploration because the user sees “activity” but not much hierarchy or separation. A more structured presentation, like the second screenshot, is much easier to scan and reason about. There may also be a naming issue: if this mode is currently referred to as “Force View”, that label is not very clear to end users. It describes the implementation style more than the user benefit. ### Proposed solution Redesign the graph explorer so large graphs are easier to read by default. Possible direction: - Use a clearer structured layout for larger graphs, or offer it as the default/recommended layout. - Keep the force-directed layout as an optional mode if needed, but not the primary experience for dense graphs. - Improve visual separation of clusters / communities so the graph communicates structure earlier. - Reduce central overlap and edge clutter. - If the UI currently says “Force View”, rename it to something clearer such as “Graph View” or “Force-Directed View”. The goal is not just a different layout algorithm, but a graph experience that helps users quickly understand the repo structure instead of presenting a visually dense network. There is a sample layout: ### Alternatives considered One alternative is to keep the current force-directed layout and only add minor styling tweaks like smaller nodes, thinner edges, or different colors. That may help a bit, but it likely will not solve the main clarity problem for larger graphs. Another alternative is to keep the current layout as-is and only add zoom/filter controls. Those are useful, but the default first impression would still be hard to parse. A better approach would be to improve the default layout/readability first, then keep advanced controls as secondary tools. ### Acceptance criteria - Large graphs are meaningfully easier to read than in the current dense force-directed view. - Major communities / clusters are visually distinguishable without requiring heavy manual interaction. - The default graph presentation avoids collapsing most nodes into one central mass. - Users can more quickly identify overall structure from the initial render. - If the current label is “Force View”, it is renamed to a clearer user-facing term. ### Constraints - Should still perform reasonably well in the browser for larger repositories. - Should not remove access to the current force-directed behavior if it is still useful for some workflows. - Changes should preserve the exploratory feel of the graph, not turn it into something overly rigid or hard to navigate. ### Contribution - [x] I am willing to open a PR for this (may need design discussion first).

title: chore(ci): consolidate parity shards and narrow cross-platform matrix
body:
## Summary

- **Consolidate scope-resolution parity** from 9 separate GH Actions jobs into 1 job running `scripts/run-parity.ts`. Each old shard did full checkout + npm ci + build (~5 min) for a single test file (~15 sec). Saves ~45 runner-minutes per PR.
- **Narrow cross-platform** (Windows/macOS) from full 373-file suite to 45 platform-sensitive files. Full suite + coverage still runs on Ubuntu. Saves ~300 redundant test runs per PR on each of Win/Mac.
- **Fix 2 lbug tests** (`lbug-orphan-sidecar-recovery`, `lbug-readonly-init`) that were missing from the sequential `lbug-db` vitest project despite using native LadybugDB.
- **Rewrite TESTING.md** to document all test lanes, parity strategy, cross-platform rationale, and orphan check instructions.

### CI lane structure (after)

| Lane | What runs | OS |
|------|-----------|-----|
| Full suite + coverage | All 373 test files + coverage thresholds | Ubuntu |
| Cross-platform | 45 platform-sensitive files only | Win/Mac |
| Scope parity | 9 migrated langs × 2 modes (legacy + registry-primary) in 1 job | Ubuntu |
| Web tests | gitnexus-web vitest | Ubuntu |
| E2E | Playwright (conditional on web changes) | Ubuntu |

### Estimated savings

~50-60 runner-minutes per PR (from ~120 to ~60-70).

### Safety invariants preserved

- No orphaned tests — `default` vitest project catches all files
- Parity auto-discovers MIGRATED_LANGUAGES from TypeScript source (no workflow edit needed for new languages)
- Coverage thresholds unchanged
- lbug-db sequential isolation preserved (and improved)
- Cross-platform list maintained in `scripts/cross-platform-tests.ts` with categorized sections and file-existence check

title: fix(php): reduce memory during deferred-call accumulation and scope-resolution
body:
## Summary

Reduces memory pressure during deferred-call accumulation and scope-resolution when indexing large PHP vendor trees such as Mage-OS/Magento 2 (14K-16K PHP files, 300+ Composer packages). This is a partial fix for #1741 — a later OOM in `populatePhpNamespaceSiblings` Step 3b (#1803) remains and must be addressed separately.

Three targeted changes:

- **Filter registry-primary calls from deferred accumulation** — calls for PHP/Python/Go/etc. were accumulated in `deferredWorkerCalls` but never consumed by `processCallsFromExtracted` (which skips them). For 14K PHP files: 269,558 → 48,752 objects (**82% reduction**, ~500MB saved)
- **Release file contents after each language's scope-resolution** — `files`, `contents`, and `preExtractedByPath` entries freed after each language completes, allowing GC to reclaim before the next language starts
- **Heredoc-aware PHP namespace extraction** — when no cached tree-sitter tree is available, `extractPhpFileStructure` uses a line scanner (skipping heredoc/nowdoc bodies and comments) instead of re-parsing. Eliminates ~16K tree-sitter re-parses during `populatePhpNamespaceSiblings`

**Note:** This PR does not fully resolve #1741. After these patches, the pipeline progresses further but crashes at `populatePhpNamespaceSiblings` Step 3b with O(PHP files × classDefs) FQN augmentation entries (#1803). That fix is tracked separately.

## Context

Mage-OS (community fork of Magento 2) installs 300+ modules via Composer into `vendor/`. Indexing these is essential for dependency analysis — plugins, preferences, and event observers wire together at runtime via XML config. Without vendor in the graph, impact analysis has massive blind spots.

The `vendor` directory is in `DEFAULT_IGNORE_LIST` (sensible default), but Magento projects override via `.gitnexusignore` negation (`!vendor/mage-os/`). This produces 14K-16K PHP files for scope-resolution.

### Before this PR

| Stage | Heap | Result |
|-------|------|--------|
| Parsing (27 chunks) | ~1.1GB | ✅ |
| processCallsFromExtracted | 16GB+ | ❌ OOM (deferredWorkerCalls: 269K objects) |

### After this PR

| Stage | Heap | Result |
|-------|------|--------|
| Parsing (27 chunks) | ~1.1GB | ✅ |
| processCallsFromExtracted | ~1.1GB | ✅ (deferredWorkerCalls: 49K objects) |

title: fix(php): synthesize module scope for namespace-less PHP files (.phtml)
body:
## Summary

PHP template files (`.phtml`) and namespace-less scripts are silently dropped from the GitNexus index when tree-sitter produces an ERROR root node. This PR fixes two cascading failures in scope extraction that cause these files to be skipped.

**Note:** PR #1790 fixed `.blade.php` (Laravel) by skipping them entirely via `isBladeTemplateFilename()`. That approach cannot work for `.phtml` — Magento/Adobe Commerce/Mage-OS **requires** `.phtml` files to be indexed for dependency analysis. This PR addresses the underlying scope extraction issue generically.

## Problem

Complex `.phtml` templates (Hyvä theme's Alpine.js components, Magento admin widgets) contain mixed PHP/HTML/JavaScript. tree-sitter-php produces an `ERROR` root node instead of `program` on these files:

1. `(program) @scope.module` query doesn't match → no Module scope emitted
2. `ensureModuleScope()` throws because captures exist but no `@scope.module` → file dropped
3. `buildScopeTree()` throws on orphan Function scopes (PHP closures with no parent)

### Real errors from Mage-OS 2.3.0 + Hyvä theme:

```
scope extraction failed for vendor/hyva-themes/.../hyva.phtml:
  Scope '...' has kind 'Function' but no parent. Only 'Module' scopes may be root-level.

scope extraction failed for vendor/mage-os/module-backend/.../grid/column_set.phtml:
  ScopeExtractor: no Module scope found
```

Hundreds of these across the vendor tree.

## Fix

Two changes, both generic (not `.phtml`-specific):

### 1. `scope-extractor.ts` — synthesize module scope instead of throwing

```typescript
// Before: only synthesized for empty files (matchCount === 0)
if (scopeDrafts.length === 0 && matchCount === 0) { ... }
throw new Error('no Module scope found');

// After: always synthesize, log warning for diagnostics
if (scopeDrafts.length !== 0 || matchCount !== 0) {
  logger.warn(`No @scope.module capture for '${filePath}' — synthesizing path-based module scope`);
}
// synthesize...
```

### 2. `scope-tree.ts` — re-parent orphan scopes instead of throwing

```typescript
// Before: throw on non-Module root scope
throw new ScopeTreeInvariantError('non-module-requires-parent', ...);

// After: find synthetic Module scope for same file, re-parent under it
const moduleScope = scopes.find(s => s.kind === 'Module' && s.filePath === scope.filePath);
if (moduleScope) { scope.parent = moduleScope.id; }
else { continue; } // graceful skip
```

## Why `.phtml` cannot be skipped

`.phtml` is **the** template format for Magento 2 / Adobe Commerce / Mage-OS — not an edge case:

- Every storefront page, admin panel, and email uses `.phtml`
- Templates contain direct PHP method calls: `$block->getChildHtml()`, `$escaper->escapeHtml()`, `$viewModel->getData()`
- Block→template wiring is essential for impact analysis
- The Hyvä theme (modern Magento frontend) has templates with 500+ lines of mixed PHP/JS/HTML
- Skipping `.phtml` creates massive blind spots in the dependency graph

This also affects Zend Framework and Laminas projects which use `.phtml` for view templates.

## What this does NOT change

- Blade templates (`.blade.php`) — already handled by #1790
- PHP files with valid `namespace` declarations — unaffected (they emit `@scope.module` correctly)
- Graph output format — synthetic Module scope uses the same `makeScopeId` as empty-file synthesis

## Test plan

- [ ] Existing `php-template-scope.test.ts` tests continue to pass (simple phtml)
- [ ] Add test for complex phtml with inline closures (ERROR root node)
- [ ] Verify no scope extraction warnings on Mage-OS vendor tree (14K+ PHP/phtml files)
- [ ] Verify namespace-less PHP scripts (e.g., `config/database.php`) still work

Refs #1752

`analyze --embeddings` silently corrupts WAL at final sub-batch (1.6.3, local embedder)
body:
# `gitnexus analyze --embeddings` 在最后一批 sub-batch / 向量索引创建阶段静默崩溃

## Environment

- gitnexus: **1.6.3** (`/opt/homebrew/bin/gitnexus`, npm global on macOS)
- OS: macOS 25.4.0 (Darwin), arm64
- Node: (whatever ships with global npm)
- Repo: TypeScript / pnpm monorepo, 538 files, 8649 nodes, 13436 edges
- Embeddings backend: **local model** (transformers.js, no `GITNEXUS_EMBEDDING_*` env vars set)

## Repro

```bash
cd <large-ts-monorepo>          # 538 files, ~8k symbols
gitnexus clean --force
gitnexus analyze --embeddings   # NO other flags
```

Reproduces 100% on the affected codebase. Plain `gitnexus analyze` (no `--embeddings`) succeeds in ~10s.

Previously hypothesized that `--skills --verbose` combined with `--embeddings` was the trigger — testing with `--embeddings` alone proves the flag itself is sufficient.

## Symptom

Progress bar reaches `Embedding 6576/6582` (the last sub-batch, given `EMBED_SUB_BATCH = 8`) and the process exits. Exit code observed as 0 in some shells, but:

- `meta.json` is **never updated** (stays at the timestamp of any prior baseline analyze)
- `lbug.wal` grows to ~2.8 MB and is **never checkpointed**
- `~/.gitnexus/registry.json` was observed empty (`[]`) on a clean repro (no prior baseline)
- Subsequent `gitnexus mcp` calls fail with:
  ```
  Runtime exception: Corrupted wal file. Read out invalid WAL record type.
  ```

`gitnexus status` after the failed run reports either "Repository not indexed" or stale baseline metadata.

No error message is printed to stdout/stderr — the progress bar simply stops at 6576/6582.

## Likely location

`dist/core/embeddings/embedding-pipeline.js`, around lines 326–372:

```js
const EMBED_SUB_BATCH = 8;
for (let si = 0; si < allTexts.length; si += EMBED_SUB_BATCH) {
  ...
  try {
    embeddings = await embedBatch(subTexts);
  } catch (embedErr) {
    console.error(`❌ embedBatch failed ...`);   // logged
    throw embedErr;
  }
  ...
  await batchInsertEmbeddings(executeWithReusedStatement, dbUpdates);   // NO try/catch logging
}
// Phase 4
await createVectorIndex(executeQuery);   // NO try/catch logging
```

Two candidates for the silent throw:

1. `batchInsertEmbeddings()` on the final sub-batch (6577–6582) — Kuzu FLOAT[N] insert.
2. `createVectorIndex(executeQuery)` right after the loop — vector index build.

Either way, the throw bubbles up to the top-level catch at line 377, but `if (isDev)` gates the `console.error` so production runs see nothing. The error is then re-thrown but apparently swallowed somewhere in the CLI layer because `gitnexus analyze` returns exit code 0.

## Captured log (last bytes, ANSI stripped, CR collapsed)

```
... 97% | Embedding 6544/6582
... 97% | Embedding 6560/6582
... 97% | Embedding 6576/6582
<EOF>
```

No "Done", no "embedding model loaded", no error trace.

## Suggested fix

1. Move the `console.error('❌ Embedding pipeline error:', error)` (line 380) out of the `if (isDev)` block — production users should see this.
2. Wrap `batchInsertEmbeddings()` and `createVectorIndex()` with their own labeled try/catch so the failing phase is identifiable.
3. Ensure analyze CLI returns non-zero exit code when the embedding pipeline throws (currently appears to return 0).
4. Either checkpoint the WAL on partial failure or roll back the WAL so a subsequent `gitnexus analyze` recovers without manual `clean`.

## Workaround

Stick with BM25-only indexing: `gitnexus analyze` without `--embeddings`. Hybrid search degrades to keyword-only but `query`, `context`, `impact`, and `detect_changes` all remain functional.

title: feat(java): add Java to MIGRATED_LANGUAGES with 100% scope-resolution parity
body:
## Summary

Adds Java to `MIGRATED_LANGUAGES`, routing Java files through the scope-resolution pipeline instead of the legacy single-threaded `processCallsFromExtracted` path. This directly addresses **issue #1741** where `gitnexus analyze` hangs indefinitely on large Java codebases (25K+ files) because the legacy call processor runs sequentially on the main thread.

Achieving 100% parity (178/178 integration tests) required fixing 29 scope-resolver gaps across tree-sitter captures, import resolution, MRO, constructor resolution, and cross-file type propagation.

## What changed

**Tree-sitter query additions** (`query.ts`, +75 lines):
- `var x = method()` call-result inference, `var alias = var`, `var x = obj.field` alias chains
- `for (var x : iterable)` enhanced-for with `var` type inference
- `instanceof` pattern bindings (Java 16+), `switch` case pattern bindings (Java 21+)
- Method references: `User::getName`, `this::save`, `super::method`, `User::new`

**Import resolution fix** (`interpret.ts`):
- `importedName` was set to the full qualified path (`com.example.models.User`) but `findExportByName` matches against the simple name (`User`). Fixed to use the simple class/member name. This single fix unblocked 5 tests.

**Scope resolver enhancements** (`scope-resolver.ts`, +205/-55 lines):
- Custom `buildJavaMro` with IMPLEMENTS edge transitive closure for interface default method resolution
- `populateJavaPackageSiblings` hook for same-package implicit class visibility (Java equivalent of C#'s namespace-siblings)
- Cross-file return-type mirroring from imported class files via `populateRangeBindings`
- `collapseMemberCallsByCallerTarget: true` for legacy dedup parity

**Captures post-processing** (`captures.ts`, +103 lines):
- `resolveVarTypeBindings` resolves `var` type bindings from same-file method return types and explicit variable types
- Variable-aware argument type inference for overload disambiguation

**Pipeline fix** (`free-call-fallback.ts`):
- `pickConstructorOrClass` now walks child scopes to find Constructor defs (scope-resolution places them in Function scopes, not directly in Class scope ownedDefs)

## Test plan

- [x] `REGISTRY_PRIMARY_JAVA=1 npx vitest run java.test.ts` — 178/178 passed
- [x] `REGISTRY_PRIMARY_JAVA=0 npx vitest run java.test.ts` — 176 passed, 2 skipped (expected legacy failures)

title: License clarification: pre-built index distribution + Dockerfile for Mage-OS community
body:
Hi @abhigyanpatwari,

We've been working on making GitNexus accessible to the Mage-OS (Magento 2 community fork) ecosystem and wanted to clarify licensing before publishing.

## What we've built

[ProxiBlue/mage-os-gitnexus](https://github.com/ProxiBlue/mage-os-gitnexus) — a free, open-source project that provides:

1. **A pre-built GitNexus index** (the `.gitnexus/lbug` database) for the Mage-OS 2.3.0 vendor tree (189K nodes, 489K edges). Distributed as a GitHub Release artifact (121MB compressed).

2. **A Dockerfile** that installs gitnexus via `npm install -g gitnexus` at build time, downloads the pre-built index, and runs `gitnexus mcp` as the entrypoint. Users build the image locally — we are **not** distributing a pre-built Docker image.

3. **Patches** (PRs #1800, #1801, #1808) applied via sed/node scripts during the Docker build to fix OOM and phtml scope extraction issues for large PHP vendor trees.

The goal is to let Mage-OS developers use GitNexus for code intelligence (impact analysis, dependency graphs, etc.) without needing to run the 90-minute indexing process themselves.

## License questions

GitNexus is licensed under PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0. We want to make sure we're compliant:

1. **Pre-built index data** (`.gitnexus/lbug`, `meta.json`) — this is generated output from running `gitnexus analyze`. We believe this is not the software itself and is not subject to the source license. Is that correct?

2. **Dockerfile that installs gitnexus** — our Dockerfile runs `npm install -g gitnexus` during `docker build`. The user builds locally; we don't distribute a pre-built image with gitnexus inside it. This is functionally the same as telling users to install gitnexus themselves. Is this acceptable?

3. **Patches applied at build time** — our Dockerfile applies patches (sed commands + a JS script) to fix issues we've submitted as PRs (#1800, #1801, #1808). These modify the installed gitnexus files inside the user's local Docker image. Is modifying the installed copy for bugfix purposes within the license terms?

4. **Required notice** — we've included the required copyright notice in our README. Is there anything else needed?

## Our intent

- This is a **free, open-source, noncommercial** community project
- We want to **promote GitNexus** to the Mage-OS/Magento community — happy to add prominent attribution, links, and references throughout our documentation
- We are **not** forking or competing — we're building tooling on top of GitNexus to make it work better with large PHP codebases
- We've contributed back: PRs #1800, #1801, #1808 fixing real issues we found

We'd love your blessing on this approach. Happy to adjust anything to align with your licensing preferences.

Thanks for building GitNexus — it's a powerful tool and we want to help more PHP developers benefit from it.

— Lucas van Staden / ProxiBlue

title: cpp two-phase: thread base-specifier qualifier through dependent-base lookup for ISO-correct sibling disambiguation
body:
## Symptom

`populateCppDependentBases` currently disambiguates sibling-namespace candidates (`detail::Inner` vs `public_api::Inner`) by suppressing when multiple candidates share a namespace prefix. ISO C++ would use the **base specifier's syntactic qualifier** to navigate from the current scope and resolve unambiguously.

## Background

This is Option A from PR #1634 / PR #1814. The prefix-contains filter (Option B, shipped in #1814) correctly suppresses collisions, but the qualifier is available in the AST at `captures.ts:611` (`qualified_identifier` scope). Plumbing it would let `detail::Inner` vs `public_api::Inner` resolve to the correct one rather than suppressing.

## Anchor

- `captures.ts:601` — `extractBaseLookupName`: currently returns only the simple name; should also extract the namespace qualifier
- `two-phase-lookup.ts:63` — `markCppDependentBase`: signature would need to accept and store the qualifier
- `two-phase-lookup.ts:45` — `dependentBasesByFile`: storage would need a qualifier field
- `two-phase-lookup.ts:96` — `populateCppDependentBases`: resolver would use qualifier for exact namespace targeting instead of prefix-contains

title: fix(build): skip build.js when running outside the monorepo (#1795)
body:
## Summary

- Fixes #1795 — `spawnSync /bin/sh ENOENT` when running `npm install` from a global install directory on Debian 13 (and any non-monorepo context)

`scripts/build.js` (the `prepare` lifecycle script) assumes the monorepo sibling `gitnexus-shared/` exists at `../gitnexus-shared`. When a user runs `npm install --ignore-scripts=false` from within a globally-installed package directory, `prepare` fires and `execSync(tsc, { cwd: nonExistentPath })` crashes with the misleading `spawnSync /bin/sh ENOENT` (Node reports a bad CWD as the shell not being found).

Adds an early guard in `build.js`:
- If `gitnexus-shared/` is absent **and** `dist/` already exists → skip cleanly (published package context, already pre-built)
- If `gitnexus-shared/` is absent **and** `dist/` is missing → exit with a helpful error pointing to the monorepo checkout

## Test plan

- [ ] `node --check gitnexus/scripts/build.js` — syntax valid
- [ ] From the monorepo root: `cd gitnexus && node scripts/build.js` — builds normally (guard does not fire)
- [ ] Simulate published-package context: `mkdir /tmp/gn-test && cp -r gitnexus/scripts gitnexus/dist /tmp/gn-test/ && cd /tmp/gn-test && node scripts/build.js` — prints "skipping" and exits 0
- [ ] Simulate broken install (no dist, no shared): `mkdir /tmp/gn-test2 && cp -r gitnexus/scripts /tmp/gn-test2/ && cd /tmp/gn-test2 && node scripts/build.js` — prints helpful error and exits 1

title: fix(lbug): resolve non-ASCII paths for KuzuDB on Windows (#1811)
body:
## Summary

- Fixes #1811 — `COPY failed for File: IO exception: Cannot open file` when the repo path contains Chinese (or other non-ASCII) characters on Windows

KuzuDB's native C++ layer uses `CreateFileA` (ANSI), not `CreateFileW`. UTF-8 bytes from Node.js are misinterpreted via the system's Active Code Page (e.g. GBK on Chinese Windows), producing a garbled path — "Error 3: The system cannot find the path specified."

### Approach

Layered workaround in `toNativeSafePath()`:

1. **8.3 short path** (fast, stateless) — resolves the path to its Windows short-name form via `cmd.exe` `for` expansion. Path passed via environment variable (`%GITNEXUS_SP%`) to avoid command injection (CodeQL clean).
2. **NTFS junction fallback** — when 8.3 is disabled, creates a junction from an ASCII temp path (`os.tmpdir()/gitnexus-junction-<hash>`) to `path.dirname(p)`, returns `junction/basename(p)`.
3. **Diagnostic warning** — when both fail, logs remediation advice and returns the original path.

Applied at all paths into KuzuDB's native layer:
- **DB open:** `openLbugConnection()` converts before `createLbugDatabase()`
- **COPY CSV:** `normalizeCopyPath()` converts before embedding in SQL; `loadGraphToLbug()` stages CSVs in `os.tmpdir()` when `storagePath` is non-ASCII on Windows
- **Pool adapter:** all 4 `createLbugDatabase()` call sites wrapped

### Safety

- No-op on ASCII paths and on Linux/macOS (zero cost for existing users)
- Junction cleanup on `process.exit` / `SIGTERM` / `SIGINT` (correct exit codes: 143/130 on Windows)
- Orphan scan on startup removes stale junctions from prior crashes (uses `lstatSync` to avoid UNC blocking)
- Worker threads skip junction creation (`isMainThread` guard) — use 8.3 only
- Sidecar sweep operates on `safePath` (the path KuzuDB opened), not the original

### Files changed

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `gitnexus/src/core/lbug/lbug-config.ts` | `toNativeSafePath()`, junction lifecycle, signal handlers, orphan scan |
| `gitnexus/src/core/lbug/lbug-adapter.ts` | `normalizeCopyPath()` integration, tmpdir CSV staging |
| `gitnexus/src/core/lbug/pool-adapter.ts` | `toNativeSafePath()` at all 4 `createLbugDatabase` sites |
| `gitnexus/test/unit/lbug-native-safe-path.test.ts` | Unit tests: ASCII passthrough, short-path conversion, junction, nonexistent path |
| `gitnexus/test/integration/lbug-non-ascii-path.test.ts` | E2E: initLbug + loadGraphToLbug + query with CJK directory name |
| `gitnexus/test/unit/pool-wal-recovery.test.ts` | Mock updated for new `toNativeSafePath` export |
| `gitnexus/test/unit/lbug-pool-win-fts-probe.test.ts` | Mock updated for new `toNativeSafePath` export |
| `gitnexus/scripts/cross-platform-tests.ts` | Integration test registered in cross-platform matrix |
| `gitnexus/vitest.config.ts` | Integration test registered in lbug-db project |

## Test plan

- [x] `npx vitest run test/unit/lbug-native-safe-path.test.ts` — 5 passing
- [x] `npx vitest run test/integration/lbug-non-ascii-path.test.ts` — 3 passing (all platforms)
- [x] `npx vitest run test/unit/pool-wal-recovery.test.ts test/unit/lbug-pool-win-fts-probe.test.ts` — 20 passing (no regression)
- [ ] On Windows with a repo under a CJK-named directory: `npx gitnexus analyze` completes without COPY ENOENT
- [ ] On Windows with an all-ASCII path: behavior unchanged
- [ ] On Linux/macOS: behavior unchanged (function is a no-op)

title: feat(mcp): add limit/offset/summaryOnly pagination to impact tool
body:
## Summary

Fixes #414 — `gitnexus_impact()` produces unbounded output (140KB+) for hub symbols (base error classes, shared utilities), exceeding MCP client limits and getting truncated. `maxDepth` alone does not help when most dependents are at depth 1.

### New parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|-----------|------|---------|-------------|
| `summaryOnly` | boolean | `false` | Returns only counts, risk, affected\_processes, and affected\_modules — omits the full `byDepth` symbol list |
| `limit` | integer | `100` | Caps symbols returned per depth level. Prevents unbounded `byDepth` arrays |
| `offset` | integer | `0` | Skips symbols per depth level for pagination |

### Response shape changes

- **`byDepthCounts`** (new, always present) — total symbol count per depth level, even when `byDepth` is paginated or omitted via `summaryOnly`
- **`pagination`** (new, conditional) — `{ limit, offset, truncated: true }` present when `byDepth` is a subset (head or tail truncation)
- **`byDepth`** — now paginated by `limit`/`offset`; use `byDepthCounts` for true totals

### Internal safety: cross-repo impact not silently truncated

- `_runImpactBFS` treats missing `limit` as uncapped (Infinity). Only `_impactImpl` (MCP entry point) applies the default of 100.
- `impactByUid` (Phase-2 cross-repo fan-out) calls `_runImpactBFS` without limit → uncapped results.
- Group impact path passes `GROUP_LOCAL_PHASE_LIMIT` (10000) so `collectImpactSymbolUids` sees all symbols for bridge queries.
- `callToolAtGroupRepo` forwards `limit`/`offset`/`summaryOnly` so group-mode MCP callers can use pagination.
- `Number.isFinite` guard on `limit`/`offset` prevents NaN from producing silent empty results.

### Files changed

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `gitnexus/src/mcp/tools.ts` | Added `limit`, `offset`, `summaryOnly` to input schema; updated description with per-depth pagination tip |
| `gitnexus/src/mcp/local/local-backend.ts` | Extracted `ImpactParams` interface; pagination + summary logic in `_runImpactBFS`; `NaN` guard; group-mode param forwarding |
| `gitnexus/src/core/group/service.ts` | Added `limit`, `offset`, `summaryOnly` to `GroupToolPort.impact` interface |
| `gitnexus/src/core/group/cross-impact.ts` | Extracted `GROUP_LOCAL_PHASE_LIMIT` constant; passes it for local UID collection |
| `gitnexus/src/cli/tool.ts` | Added `--limit`, `--offset`, `--summary-only` to `impactCommand` |
| `gitnexus/src/cli/index.ts` | Registered new CLI flags |
| `gitnexus/src/cli/help-i18n.ts` | i18n keys for new flags |
| `gitnexus/src/cli/i18n/en.ts` | English help strings |
| `gitnexus/src/cli/i18n/zh-CN.ts` | Chinese help strings |
| `gitnexus/src/cli/eval-server.ts` | `formatImpactResult` uses `byDepthCounts` for accurate "N more" display |
| `gitnexus/test/unit/impact-pagination.test.ts` | 15 tests: pagination, summaryOnly, offset, multi-depth, NaN guard, internal uncapped path, `collectImpactSymbolUids` |

title: feat(cpp): thread base-specifier qualifier through dependent-base lookup (#1815)
body:
## Summary

Infrastructure for #1815. Provide the syntactic namespace qualifier (e.g. `detail` in `detail::Inner<T>`) from AST capture through storage to resolution. Part of #1564.

## Changes

**captures.ts:**
- `extractBaseLookupQualifier` — reads the `scope` field from `qualified_identifier` AST nodes (e.g. `detail` from `detail::Inner<T>`)
- `isBaseDependent` fix — now recognizes `qualified_identifier` bases (previously rejected unconditionally); they descend into children to check for template parameter references

**two-phase-lookup.ts:**
- `dependentBasesByFile` storage changed from `Set<baseName>` to `Map<baseName, qualifier>`
- `markCppDependentBase` accepts optional `qualifier` parameter
- `classesBySimpleName` index deduplicated by nodeId (last-wins Map); removes duplicate entries caused by scope-extractor and class-extractor overlap
- V3 qualifier-based exact targeting in multi-candidate path (dormant — see note below)
- V2 prefix-heuristic fallback unchanged

## What's proven

| Component | Status |
|-----------|--------|
| Qualifier extraction | ✓ Extracts `"detail"` from `detail::Inner<T>` |
| isBaseDependent fix | ✓ `qualified_identifier` bases now processed |
| Qualifier storage | ✓ Capture → storage → resolver |
| Index dedup | ✓ Duplicate nodeId entries eliminated |

## What's dormant

The V3 qualifier targeting and V2 prefix-heuristic both rely on `nsPrefix` derived from `def.qualifiedName` on `parsed.localDefs` entries. The class extractor's `buildQualifiedName` correctly produces `mylib.detail.Inner` but this qualifiedName doesn't reach `localDefs` — the scope-extractor creates separate defs with simple-name qualifiedNames like `"Inner"` and `"Inner.Inner"`. Fixing this requires changes in `parsing-processor.ts` to thread the class extractor's qualifiedName into `@declaration.qualified_name` captures (tracked separately).

title: feat(trace): shortest call path MCP tool -- how does A reach B in one call
body:
## The gap

The single most common debugging question in any codebase is *"how does A reach B?"* — yet right now answering it means chaining 3-8 context/impact calls by hand, one hop at a time. Each hop is a round-trip; on a typical 5–7 hop call chain that's **15–30 seconds of manual graph walking** for a question that should be answered in one call.

You never know if you're on the shortest path, and when the chain breaks you're left guessing where the gap is.

## What 	race would do

A new MCP tool + gitnexus trace <from> <to> CLI command that returns the **shortest directed call chain** between two symbols:

`
gitnexus trace validateUser executeQuery
`

Response shape — ordered hops with file:line, edge confidence, and inline source:

`json
{
  "status": "ok",
  "from": "validateUser",
  "to": "executeQuery",
  "hopCount": 3,
  "hops": [
    { "name": "validateUser",     "filePath": "app/services/auth.ts",  "startLine": 42 },
    { "name": "checkPermissions", "filePath": "app/services/auth.ts",  "startLine": 89 },
    { "name": "executeQuery",     "filePath": "app/lib/db.ts",         "startLine": 23 }
  ],
  "edges": [
    { "relType": "CALLS", "confidence": 1.0 },
    { "relType": "CALLS", "confidence": 0.95 },
    { "relType": "CALLS", "confidence": 1.0 }
  ]
}
`

When no path exists, it reports the furthest reachable node so you know exactly where the chain breaks — dynamic dispatch, reflection, or external API boundary.

## Why it fits now

The data is already there — CALLS edges are fully ingested by the parse pipeline. Cypher has shortestPath(). The BFS traversal is proven in _impactImpl. Symbol resolution lives in esolveSymbolCandidates. This is the last piece to connect "find a symbol" → "trace the full runtime flow."

## Implementation sketch

| Step | Approach |
|------|----------|
| Core pathfinding | Cypher shortestPath() first; fallback to directed BFS over CALLS + HAS_METHOD |
| Symbol resolution | Reuse esolveSymbolCandidates (name→UID disambiguation included) |
| Gap reporting | BFS to deepest reachable node when target isn't found |
| MCP surface | Tool definition in 	ools.ts + handler in local-backend.ts |
| CLI surface | gitnexus trace <from> <to> with --from-uid, --to-uid, --max-hops, --no-content |
| Tests | Unit test for BFS fallback + integration test against a real indexed call chain |

## Follow-ups (PR candidates)

There are a few things we'd clean up in the same PR:

- Fix tuple-index fallback in _traceBFS (LadybugDB may return tuple-shaped rows; the positional indices for elType and confidence need verification)
- Batch content fetch (currently N+1 Cypher queries per hop; should be one batched lookup)
- Remove a dead RELATION_TYPES variable
- Add 	race to the MCP tools table in ARCHITECTURE.md
- Correct the internal comment from "bidirectional BFS" to "directed BFS"

None of these are blockers — just things worth fixing while we're in the area.

## What's the ask

Thoughts on the approach? Happy to open a PR with the implementation if this direction sounds right.
