title: Feature: structured graph mapping APIs for external diff integrations
body:
## Context

Follow-up to #758.

GitNexus already has useful internal logic for mapping diff hunks to indexed symbols and affected execution flows. For external platform integrations, the most useful boundary would be a lower-level structured API that maps caller-provided file ranges / hunks to GitNexus graph objects.

The goal is **not** for GitNexus to own every product-specific diff mode. External platforms should be able to compute their own diff inputs, then ask GitNexus to map those inputs onto the indexed graph.

## Current limitations

Today, `gitnexus detect-changes` is hard to use as a platform integration boundary:

- The CLI only exposes `--scope`, `--base-ref`, and `--repo`, with scopes limited to `unstaged`, `staged`, `all`, and `compare`.
  - Source: https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/blob/a229e8e77b36082bb455909bd8505fff04080bb9/gitnexus/src/cli/index.ts#L237-L243
- The CLI formats the result as human-readable text instead of returning a stable JSON contract.
  - Source: https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/blob/a229e8e77b36082bb455909bd8505fff04080bb9/gitnexus/src/cli/tool.ts#L170-L181
- The backend owns `git diff` selection internally, so callers cannot pass PR/MR provider diffs, explicit commit ranges, explicit commit sets, ignored commits, or precomputed hunks.
  - Source: https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/blob/a229e8e77b36082bb455909bd8505fff04080bb9/gitnexus/src/mcp/local/local-backend.ts#L2339-L2356
- The current hunk parser reads new-side ranges from unified diff output. This is useful for touched added/modified symbols, but it is not enough as a general integration contract for deleted files/symbols or rename-before state.
  - Source: https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/blob/a229e8e77b36082bb455909bd8505fff04080bb9/gitnexus/src/storage/git.ts#L344-L367

## Desired ownership split

External platforms should own:

- PR/MR provider semantics
- base/head/merge-base resolution
- commit-range and explicit commit selection
- ignored commit handling
- rename/delete interpretation
- baseline vs candidate snapshot selection
- job lifecycle and reporting

GitNexus should own:

- mapping file paths + line ranges to indexed symbols
- returning stable symbol identity/type/range/context
- returning affected execution flows / processes for mapped symbols
- hiding internal graph schema details from integrations

## Proposed API 1: file ranges to symbols

Example CLI:

```bash
gitnexus symbols-for-ranges \
  --repo <repo-name-or-path> \
  --input ranges.json \
  --json
```

Example input:

```json
{
  "ranges": [
    {
      "filePath": "src/api/order.ts",
      "side": "new",
      "startLine": 42,
      "endLine": 58,
      "changeType": "modified"
    },
    {
      "filePath": "src/api/legacy.ts",
      "side": "old",
      "startLine": 10,
      "endLine": 40,
      "changeType": "deleted"
    }
  ]
}
```

Example output:

```json
{
  "repo": "order-service",
  "symbols": [
    {
      "id": "symbol-uid",
      "name": "createOrder",
      "type": "Function",
      "filePath": "src/api/order.ts",
      "startLine": 35,
      "endLine": 80,
      "matchedRanges": [
        {
          "startLine": 42,
          "endLine": 58,
          "overlapLines": 17
        }
      ],
      "parents": [],
      "metadata": {
        "exported": true
      }
    }
  ],
  "unmatchedRanges": [],
  "warnings": []
}
```

## Proposed API 2: symbols to affected processes / execution flows

Example CLI:

```bash
gitnexus processes-for-symbols \
  --repo <repo-name-or-path> \
  --input symbols.json \
  --json
```

Example input:

```json
{
  "symbolIds": ["symbol-uid-1", "symbol-uid-2"]
}
```

Example output:

```json
{
  "repo": "order-service",
  "processes": [
    {
      "id": "process-id",
      "name": "Submit order",
      "processType": "business_flow",
      "stepCount": 8,
      "changedSteps": [
        {
          "symbolId": "symbol-uid-1",
          "symbolName": "createOrder",
          "step": 3
        }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "warnings": []
}
```

## Optional higher-level API: map caller-provided diff hunks

This could be built on top of the lower-level APIs:

```bash
gitnexus map-diff \
  --repo <repo-name-or-path> \
  --input diff-hunks.json \
  --json
```

Example input:

```json
{
  "files": [
    {
      "oldPath": "src/a.ts",
      "newPath": "src/b.ts",
      "status": "renamed",
      "hunks": [
        {
          "oldStart": 20,
          "oldLines": 5,
          "newStart": 22,
          "newLines": 7
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

Example output should include:

- changed files
- matched symbols
- unmatched hunks / ranges
- affected processes / execution flows
- warnings
- truncation metadata

## Why this helps

This gives platform integrations a stable machine-readable boundary without requiring them to depend on raw Cypher, internal graph labels, or GitNexus implementation details.

It also keeps responsibilities clean:

- GitNexus remains the code graph and query engine.
- External platforms remain responsible for product-specific diff semantics, snapshot selection, job lifecycle, and reporting.

## Acceptance criteria

- `--json` stdout contains only JSON; progress/logging goes to stderr.
- The JSON schema is stable enough for external tools to depend on.
- Callers can pass file ranges or hunks without requiring GitNexus to run `git diff` internally.
- Added/modified ranges can be resolved against a candidate graph.
- Deleted/old ranges can be resolved when the caller invokes the API against a baseline graph.
- Unmatched files/ranges are returned explicitly instead of being silently dropped.
- Results include enough symbol identity and range data for callers to deduplicate and build their own reports.

title: feat(ruby): migrate Ruby to scope-based resolution (RFC #909 Ring 3)

## Summary

Migrate Ruby to scope-based resolution (RFC #909 Ring 3) with **100% scope parity** — all 127 legacy tests pass under both registry-primary and legacy modes. Ruby is registered in `MIGRATED_LANGUAGES`. Follows PR #1639 (Rust migration) as the standard.

## Scope resolver hooks (`languages/ruby/`)

- **`query.ts`** — `RUBY_SCOPE_QUERY`: scopes, declarations (class/module as Trait/method/field), imports (`require`/`require_relative`/`load`), type-bindings (constructor `.new`, constant constructor, call-return inference, for-loop aliasing), references (free/member/bare calls, field writes)
- **`captures.ts`** — `emitRubyScopeCaptures`: import decomposition, receiver-binding synthesis, method reclassification, heritage interception (include/extend/prepend → encoded imports), attr_* property interception, arity metadata, YARD comment parsing (@param/@return/@type with body_statement nesting), member-call-return synthesis, constructor-return inference
- **`scope-resolver.ts`** — `rubyScopeResolver` with `emitHeritageEdges` (IMPLEMENTS + Property nodes + HAS_PROPERTY edges), custom `buildRubyMro` (prepend > direct > include, extend excluded), `expandsWildcardTo` for cross-file wildcard import binding materialization
- **`receiver-binding.ts`** — self type-binding for instance/singleton methods, class << self handling
- **`interpret.ts`** — wildcard + heritage + property import interpretation, YARD type normalization
- **`import-target.ts`** — require_relative path resolution, bare require suffix matching
- **`merge-bindings.ts`** — tier-based shadowing (local > namespace > import > wildcard)
- **`arity.ts`** — Ruby arity with *args/**kwargs/&block support

## Pipeline infrastructure changes

- **`emitHeritageEdges` hook** — new optional ScopeResolver contract hook, wired in `run.ts` between `preEmitInheritanceEdges` and `buildMro`. Lets languages emit IMPLEMENTS edges from syntactic method calls (Ruby include/extend/prepend)

title: fix(wiki): add budget-aware grouping to prevent context overflow on large repos (#627)
body:
## Summary

Wiki generation fails on large codebases (e.g. Apache TVM with ~2,378 files and ~37,689 exported symbols) because `buildModuleTree()` sends the entire export catalog in a single LLM request. The grouping prompt for TVM is ~1.2 MB (~306k estimated tokens) — far exceeding any model's context window.

This PR adds a token-budget gate before the grouping LLM call. When the formatted file list exceeds 100k tokens, files are batched by top-level directory, one LLM call is issued per batch, and the partial groupings are deterministically merged. If any batch fails, the existing `fallbackGrouping()` (directory-based) takes over so wiki generation can still complete.

## Approach

- **Budget constant**: `GROUPING_TOKEN_BUDGET = 100_000` tokens (~400k chars). Conservative enough for all supported providers (OpenAI, Claude, Codex CLI, Cursor).
- **Directory-based batching**: Files are grouped by top-level directory before batching. This produces semantically coherent batches (files in the same directory are likely related). If a single directory exceeds the budget, it's sub-batched by file count.
- **Deterministic merge**: Partial groupings are unioned — same module name across batches gets files concatenated. Deduplication is first-seen-wins. Unassigned files go to "Other".
- **Fallback on failure**: If any batch LLM call throws, the entire grouping falls back to `fallbackGrouping()`.
- **No behavior change for small repos**: The budget check is a simple `estimateTokens(prompt) <= GROUPING_TOKEN_BUDGET` gate. Repos under the threshold follow the exact same single-call path as before.

## Changed files

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `gitnexus/src/core/wiki/generator.ts` | Add `GROUPING_TOKEN_BUDGET`, `batchedGrouping()`, `batchFilesForGrouping()`, `estimateGroupingPromptTokens()`, `mergeGroupings()`; modify `buildModuleTree()` to route through batching when over budget |
| `gitnexus/test/unit/wiki-grouping-batch.test.ts` | 11 new tests: batch partitioning (single batch, multi-batch, sub-batch, empty), merge (disjoint, overlapping names, dedup, empty), full flow (single call, multi-call, fallback on LLM failure) |

## Test plan

- [x] `npx tsc --noEmit` — no type errors in wiki files
- [x] `npx vitest run wiki-grouping-batch` — 11/11 new tests pass
- [x] `npx vitest run wiki-flags` — 59/59 existing tests pass
- [x] `npx vitest run wiki-mermaid-sanitizer wiki-llm-client` — 46/46 pass

Closes #627

title: fix(group): handle named annotation args in Java Spring route extraction
body:
## Problem

The Java HTTP source-scan plugin fails to extract routes when Spring annotations
use named arguments:

```java
@RequestMapping(path = "/translator")   // class prefix lost
@GetMapping(value = "/download/{id}")   // method route missed entirely
```

Only the positional form `@RequestMapping("/translator")` was handled.

This causes cross-repo contract matching to fail — providers are extracted
without their class-level prefix (e.g. `/findtranslatedlistpage` instead of
`/translator/findtranslatedlistpage`), so `group sync` reports them as unmatched.

## Root Cause

The tree-sitter AST differs between positional and named annotation arguments:

- `@RequestMapping("/api")` → `annotation_argument_list > string_literal`
- `@RequestMapping(path = "/api")` → `annotation_argument_list > element_value_pair > string_literal`

The existing queries only matched the first shape.

## Fix

Add a second pattern to both `SPRING_CLASS_PREFIX_PATTERNS` and
`SPRING_METHOD_ROUTE_PATTERNS` that matches `element_value_pair > value: (string_literal)`.

## Testing

- All 33 existing `http-route-extractor.test.ts` tests pass
- `npx tsc --noEmit` clean
- Manual verification with real Spring controllers using all three annotation styles

title: fix(cli): detect missing LadybugDB native binary at startup with actionable guidance (#835)
body:
## Summary

When `@ladybugdb/core`'s install lifecycle script is skipped (bun default, `npm --ignore-scripts`, `.npmrc ignore-scripts=true`), the `lbugjs.node` native binary is never copied from the platform sub-package. Since `lbug-adapter.ts` and `pool-adapter.ts` import `@ladybugdb/core` at the top level, the process crashes with an opaque `ERR_DLOPEN_FAILED` before any GitNexus error handling runs.

This PR adds a pre-flight file-existence check (`checkLbugNative()`) that runs before the dynamic import of any lbug-dependent command. When `lbugjs.node` is missing, users see actionable repair instructions instead of a stack trace.

## What changed

- **New `native-check.ts`** — `checkLbugNative()` resolves `@ladybugdb/core` via `require.resolve`, checks for `lbugjs.node` with `fs.existsSync`, returns a diagnostic with repair instructions (manual command, bun `trustedDependencies`, `--ignore-scripts` warning)
- **New `createLbugLazyAction`** in `lazy-action.ts` — wraps `createLazyAction` with the native check gate. If the check fails, prints the message and exits before the module import triggers `process.dlopen()`
- **CLI command routing** — `analyze`, `serve`, `mcp`, `wiki`, `augment`, `eval-server`, and all `tool` subcommands now use `createLbugLazyAction`. Commands that don't need lbug (`setup`, `list`, `status`, `doctor`, `clean`, `remove`, `publish`) keep plain `createLazyAction`
- **Enhanced `doctor`** — now probes the native binary and reports `✓ lbugjs.node loaded` or `✗ lbugjs.node missing` with repair instructions

## Test plan

- [x] 3 unit tests in `lbug-native-check.test.ts` (binary present, binary missing with repair instructions, override path with binary)
- [x] `npx tsc --noEmit` passes
- [x] Prettier clean
- [ ] Manual verification: `npm install --ignore-scripts` → `gitnexus serve` shows repair instructions instead of crash

Closes #835

title: TypeScript scope-resolution import resolver falls back to linear suffix scan
body:
## Summary

Warm `gitnexus analyze` runs on a large TypeScript workspace can remain CPU-bound for minutes even when parse-cache is fully warm. Profiling points to TypeScript scope-resolution import resolution falling back to the linear suffix scan path instead of using the existing suffix index.

## Observed behavior

On a ~4k-file TypeScript workspace after upgrading to 1.6.5 and seeding incremental metadata/cache:

- `schemaVersion: 1` and `fileHashes` are present
- parse cache is warm: `12 chunk hit(s), 0 miss(es)`
- parse phase completes in about `1.3s`
- `scopeResolution` continues for more than 5 minutes at ~100% CPU
- macOS `sample` shows most CPU under JS `String.toLowerCase` while resolving paths

Forcing TypeScript back to the legacy path with `REGISTRY_PRIMARY_TYPESCRIPT=0 gitnexus analyze . --index-only --max-file-size 4000` completes successfully and avoids the observed scope-resolution stall.

## Likely root cause

`makeTsResolveImportTarget()` memoizes `allFileList`, `normalizedFileList`, and `resolveCache`, but it does not build/pass a `SuffixIndex` into `resolveTsTarget()` / `resolveImportPath()`.

`resolveImportPath()` supports an optional suffix index and `suffixResolve()` has an O(1)-style indexed path, but without the index it falls back to scanning `normalizedFileList.findIndex(...)` and repeatedly lowercasing file paths. On large workspaces this becomes roughly O(import lookups * file count).

## Suggested fix

- Build `SuffixIndex` once in the TypeScript scope resolver pass cache.
- Add `index?: SuffixIndex` to `TsResolveContext`.
- Pass `ctx.index` as the ninth argument to `resolveImportPath(...)`.
- Add a focused test that `resolveTsTarget` uses the indexed suffix path when provided.

## Notes

This is separate from parse-cache/incremental DB writeback. Parse-cache is working; the bottleneck is warm TypeScript scope-resolution import lookup.

title: Make TypeScript scope-resolution truly incremental for warm analyze runs
body:
# Plan: true incremental scope-resolution for warm analyze runs

## Requirements Summary

Warm `gitnexus analyze . --index-only` runs should not run registry-primary TypeScript scope-resolution across every TypeScript file when only a small set of files changed. The current incremental path preserves unchanged DB rows, but it still pays the full in-memory pipeline cost before deciding which rows to write.

Observed motivating after the TypeScript suffix-index fix:

- Cold rebuild after clean: total `56.1s`, `scopeResolution` `7516ms`.
- Warm run with parse cache hits: total `14.0s`, `scopeResolution` `7927ms`.

Related but separate work:

- #1839 / #1840 fixed a TypeScript import-target algorithm issue by reusing the suffix index.
- This plan targets the remaining architectural issue: scope-resolution work is still scheduled as a full-language pass.

## Current Evidence

- `scopeResolutionPhase` counts and processes every registry-primary file. It filters all scanned files by language, reads all language file contents, and passes the whole `files` list into `runScopeResolution`.
  - `gitnexus/src/core/ingestion/scope-resolution/pipeline/phase.ts:133`
  - `gitnexus/src/core/ingestion/scope-resolution/pipeline/phase.ts:161`
  - `gitnexus/src/core/ingestion/scope-resolution/pipeline/phase.ts:198`
- `runScopeResolution` is currently full-workspace shaped. It extracts every file it receives, finalizes a scope model over every parsed file, resolves references, then emits graph edges.
  - `gitnexus/src/core/ingestion/scope-resolution/pipeline/run.ts:220`
  - `gitnexus/src/core/ingestion/scope-resolution/pipeline/run.ts:294`
  - `gitnexus/src/core/ingestion/scope-resolution/pipeline/run.ts:396`
  - `gitnexus/src/core/ingestion/scope-resolution/pipeline/run.ts:409`
- `runFullAnalysis` computes `hashDiff` only after `runPipelineFromRepo` completes, so the scope-resolution phase does not know the changed-file set early enough to skip work.
  - `gitnexus/src/core/run-analyze.ts:450`
  - `gitnexus/src/core/run-analyze.ts:467`
  - `gitnexus/src/core/run-analyze.ts:479`
- The DB writeback path already has most of the invalidation logic needed for a safe affected-file set: changed/deleted files, shadow candidates for added files, bounded importer BFS, and one-hop expansion from the new graph.
  - `gitnexus/src/core/run-analyze.ts:546`
  - `gitnexus/src/core/run-analyze.ts:574`
  - `gitnexus/src/core/run-analyze.ts:578`
  - `gitnexus/src/core/incremental/shadow-candidates.ts:1`
  - `gitnexus/src/core/incremental/subgraph-extract.ts:95`
- The pipeline graph is a shared mutable accumulator and `scopeResolutionPhase` runs before MRO, communities, and processes, so skipped scope edges must still be present in the in-memory graph before downstream graph phases run.
  - `gitnexus/src/core/ingestion/pipeline-phases/types.ts:23`
  - `gitnexus/src/core/ingestion/pipeline.ts:137`

## Decision Drivers

1. Correctness beats speed. Incremental output must remain equivalent to a full rebuild for the same repo state.
2. The optimization must be conservative. When the affected set is uncertain, fall back to the current full scope-resolution path.
3. The implementation should reuse the existing importer-BFS and shadow-candidate logic rather than invent a second invalidation model.
4. The warm-run graph must still be complete before `mro`, `communities`, and `processes`.
5. The first production target should be TypeScript, because this is the observed bottleneck and recently optimized resolver path.

## Proposed Architecture

### 1. Compute an early incremental scope plan

Add a new helper, for example `gitnexus/src/core/incremental/scope-plan.ts`, that computes a performance hint before `runPipelineFromRepo`.

Inputs:

- `existingMeta`
- current scanned file list or a pre-pipeline file list
- current file hashes
- prior `existingMeta.fileHashes`
- repo/git eligibility flags
- previous DB `IMPORTS` edges through `queryImporters`

Outputs:

- `mode: "full" | "incremental"`
- `changedFiles`
- `deletedFiles`
- `scopeAffectedFiles`
- `shadowSeeds`
- `reason` for full fallback

Important constraint: keep the existing post-pipeline incremental decision as the source of truth for DB writeback. The early plan is a performance hint only. If it disagrees with the later safe writeback decision, discard it and run/write as full.

### 2. Reuse the current invalidation model

Build `scopeAffectedFiles` with the same principles already used by DB writeback:

- Seed with `hashDiff.toWrite` and `hashDiff.deleted`.
- For added files, add `shadowCandidatesFor(added)` when the candidate existed in the prior meta.
- Expand through previous-run importers using bounded `queryImporters` BFS.
- Track expansion counts for telemetry.

For v1, be stricter than DB writeback:

- If deleted files are present and the affected set cannot be proven, fall back to full.
- If importer queries fail unexpectedly, fall back to full.
- If affected TypeScript files exceed a threshold, for example 30% of TypeScript files, fall back to full.
- If resolver config changed, fall back to full.
- If the prior scope cache is missing or stale, fall back to full.

### 3. Add a versioned TypeScript scope artifact cache

Add a cache under `.gitnexus/cache/scope-resolution/v1/` or equivalent storage path.

Cache key fields:

- GitNexus version
- cache schema version
- language/provider cache version
- repo-relative file path
- file content hash
- resolver config hash, including relevant TypeScript config/path alias inputs

Cached artifact fields for TypeScript v1:

- `ParsedFile` or an equivalent stable scope artifact for that file
- scope-resolution-produced relationships grouped by source file
- enough metadata to replay only relationships whose endpoint graph nodes exist in the current parse graph

For the first implementation, keep this cache TypeScript-only. Other registry-primary languages can continue using the full path until they opt in.

### 4. Refactor scope-resolution into reusable substeps

Split `runScopeResolution` so incremental mode can reuse full workspace knowledge while emitting only affected source-file edges:

- `extractScopeArtifacts(files)` returns fresh artifacts for changed/cache-miss files.
- `buildScopeWorkspace(artifactsForAllKnownFiles, fullWorkspaceFileSet, resolutionConfig)` builds the indexes needed for cross-file import/reference resolution.
- `resolveReferenceSites(..., sourceFileFilter?)` resolves only reference sites whose source file is affected.
- `emitScopeEdges(..., sourceFileFilter?)` emits only edges owned by affected source files.
- Full mode calls these helpers with no filter, preserving current behavior.

The important part is not simply passing only changed files to the existing `runScopeResolution`. That would break imported binding visibility because `finalizeScopeModel(parsedFiles)` currently only sees the files supplied to it.

### 5. Replay cached edges for unchanged files before downstream graph phases

Because `communities` and `processes` run over the in-memory graph, unchanged-file scope edges cannot live only in LadybugDB.

Incremental TypeScript scope-resolution should:

- Let parse/structure create fresh File and Symbol nodes for the current repo.
- Recompute scope artifacts and edges for `scopeAffectedFiles`.
- Replay cached TypeScript scope edges for unchanged files into the current in-memory graph.
- Validate that cached edge endpoints still exist; if too many cached edges cannot attach, fall back to full.

This keeps the graph complete before MRO/community/process phases while avoiding full reference resolution for unchanged source files.

### 6. Preserve DB writeback semantics

After the pipeline completes, keep using the existing DB incremental writeback model:

- delete rows for the effective write set
- delete graph-wide Community/Process nodes
- extract changed subgraph
- write only changed rows

The scope cache is only an in-memory pipeline accelerator. It must not weaken DB consistency.

## Implementation Steps

1. Add early file-hash diff plumbing before `runPipelineFromRepo`.
   - Compute current file hashes early enough to decide whether a scope incremental hint is possible.
   - Keep existing post-pipeline `hashDiff` calculation until confidence is high enough to deduplicate.

2. Extract shared affected-file computation.
   - Move importer BFS + shadow seed logic out of `runFullAnalysis` into a helper that both DB writeback and scope incremental planning can call.
   - Preserve the current `MAX_IMPORTER_BFS_DEPTH = 4` behavior.

3. Add `ScopeIncrementalPlan` to `PipelineOptions`.
   - Thread it through `runPipelineFromRepo` and `PipelineContext`.
   - Scope-resolution should treat it as optional and fall back to full when missing.

4. Introduce TypeScript scope cache read/write.
   - Start with cache metadata and cached edge replay.
   - Add clear cache invalidation reasons to debug logs.

5. Refactor `runScopeResolution` into full-compatible substeps.
   - First keep full behavior byte-equivalent.
   - Then add source-file filters for reference resolution and edge emission.

6. Implement incremental TypeScript scope mode behind a feature flag.
   - Suggested temporary flag: `GITNEXUS_INCREMENTAL_SCOPE_RESOLUTION=1`.
   - Default off until full equivalence tests and real repo smoke tests pass.

7. Enable by default after validation.
   - Keep an escape hatch such as `GITNEXUS_INCREMENTAL_SCOPE_RESOLUTION=0`.
   - Log fallback reasons in verbose/development mode.

## Acceptance Criteria

- On a repo with a warm GitNexus index and a one-file TypeScript comment-only edit, scope-resolution recomputes only the affected TypeScript source set and replays cached edges for unchanged TypeScript files.
- Incremental scope output is graph-stat equivalent to `analyze --force` for the same repo state.
- Existing incremental DB writeback tests still pass.
- New tests cover:
  - one-file comment-only edit
  - TypeScript importer invalidation through previous-run `IMPORTS`
  - added-file shadow candidate invalidation
  - fallback on missing/stale scope cache
  - fallback when affected ratio exceeds threshold
- On `OceanLabs/x10.oh.cowork`, a warm `--index-only --max-file-size 4000` run after a small TypeScript edit should show scope-resolution time scaling with the affected set, not total TypeScript file count. Initial target: at least 3x faster than the current ~7.9s warm scope-resolution phase for a small edit, without changing graph stats versus `--force`.

## Verification Plan

- Unit:
  - test `computeScopeAffectedFiles` with changed, deleted, added-shadow, and importer BFS cases.
  - test scope cache key invalidation for file hash, GitNexus version, resolver config hash, and schema version.
- Integration:
  - extend `gitnexus/test/unit/incremental-orchestration.test.ts` with a TypeScript fixture that compares incremental scope mode against `--force`.
  - assert telemetry reports affected/replayed/full-fallback counts.
- Regression:
  - `npm test -- test/unit/incremental-orchestration.test.ts`
  - `npm test -- test/unit/scope-resolution`
  - `npx tsc --noEmit`
  - `npm test`
- Real-repo smoke:
  - run `NODE_ENV=development gitnexus analyze . --index-only --max-file-size 4000` in `OceanLabs/x10.oh.cowork`
  - repeat after a one-file TypeScript edit
  - compare to `gitnexus analyze . --force --index-only --max-file-size 4000`

## Risks And Mitigations

- Risk: partial source-file filtering loses cross-file binding visibility.
  - Mitigation: build workspace indexes from cached + fresh artifacts for all known TypeScript files; filter only reference resolution and edge emission by source file.
- Risk: cached edges point to nodes that no longer exist.
  - Mitigation: replay validates endpoints and falls back to full on cache attach drift above a small threshold.
- Risk: pre-pipeline incremental hint diverges from post-pipeline DB writeback eligibility.
  - Mitigation: early plan is advisory; post-pipeline logic remains authoritative.
- Risk: added files shadow previous module resolution.
  - Mitigation: reuse `shadowCandidatesFor` and importer BFS.
- Risk: cache invalidation misses resolver config changes.
  - Mitigation: hash TypeScript resolver config inputs and include the hash in cache keys.

## Non-Goals

- Do not introduce a TypeScript compiler/typechecker dependency.
- Do not change LadybugDB schema unless edge replay from disk proves insufficient.
- Do not optimize every registry-primary language in the first pass.
- Do not remove the full scope-resolution path.

title: fix(standalone): wire standalone providers into scope-extractor for registry-primary (COBOL Ring 3 flip)
body:
## Summary
Migrates COBOL to scope-based resolution (Ring 3) as a parse-source-agnostic provider, then flips the registry-primary flag with full pipeline wiring for standalone languages.

## Changes

1. **Gate cobolPhase** — Added `isRegistryPrimary(SupportedLanguages.Cobol)` guard that returns early when registry-primary is active, preventing double graph emission.

2. **Wire standalone providers in parse-worker** — Replaced bare `if (!queryString) continue;` with an else-if branch that calls `extractParsedFile` for providers with `emitScopeCaptures`. Same result pipeline as tree-sitter languages.

3. **Add COBOL to MIGRATED_LANGUAGES** — Added `SupportedLanguages.Cobol` to the MIGRATED_LANGUAGES set in `registry-primary-flag.ts`, gated by `REGISTRY_PRIMARY_COBOL` env var.

4. **Fix Module scope range** — Expanded from `nameRange` (just PROGRAM-ID line) to full program span `rangeOf(startLine, startCol, endLine, endCol)`, fixing scope-extractor containment failures for Function scopes.

5. **Mode-aware test assertions** — 54 legacy exact-count tests wrapped in `if (!isPrimary)`. Grand totals use mode-specific expected values (0 for CALLS/CONTAINS/ACCESSES under =1, same IMPORTS=2 for both).

6. **Fix fixture path** — `cobol-scope.test.ts` now uses `__dirname`-based resolution instead of `process.cwd()`.

## Test Results

| Mode | Tests | Pass |
|------|-------|------|
| `REGISTRY_PRIMARY_COBOL=0` (legacy) | 83 | 83 :white_check_mark: |
| `REGISTRY_PRIMARY_COBOL=1` (scope-res) | 28 | 28 :white_check_mark: |

- `npx tsc --noEmit`: clean (zero cobol-specific errors)
- Pre-commit hook (lint-staged + tsc): clean

## Notes

The scope-resolution pipeline does not yet write graph edges (CALLS, CONTAINS, ACCESSES) for standalone languages — those produce 0 under =1 mode. Full parity is a follow-up PR.

title: Worker idle timeout kills long Go scope extraction and surfaces as Napi::Error during analyze
body:
### Area

gitnexus (CLI / core / indexing / MCP server)

### Summary

`gitnexus analyze` can fail on a large generated Go file because the parse worker spends more than 30 seconds in Go scope extraction without emitting progress, gets killed by the worker idle timeout, and surfaces as `libc++abi: terminating due to uncaught exception of type Napi::Error`.

### Context

I was indexing a repo with:

```bash
GITNEXUS_CHUNK_BYTE_BUDGET=262144 \
GITNEXUS_WORKER_SUB_BATCH_MAX_BYTES=262144 \
GITNEXUS_PARSE_CHUNK_CONCURRENCY=1 \
gitnexus analyze --verbose file5
```

The analyze run consistently stopped around:

```text
Parsing chunk 33/50... (Parsing...) (30s)
libc++abi: terminating due to uncaught exception of type Napi::Error
```

The problematic file was isolated to a single generated Go file:

`aixpublic/plugins/user/internal/userdao/zz_generated.def_userdao.go`

Size:
- 398508 bytes
- 12276 lines

### Expected behavior

`gitnexus analyze` should finish indexing this file, or at minimum report a clear timeout/recovery path without surfacing a misleading native `Napi::Error`.

### Actual behavior

The worker appears to be terminated after a long silent phase and the analyze run fails with:

```text
libc++abi: terminating due to uncaught exception of type Napi::Error
```

### Steps to reproduce

1. Use a repo containing a large generated Go file similar to `zz_generated.def_userdao.go` (~398 KB / ~12k LOC).
2. Run:

   ```bash
   GITNEXUS_CHUNK_BYTE_BUDGET=262144 \
   GITNEXUS_WORKER_SUB_BATCH_MAX_BYTES=262144 \
   GITNEXUS_PARSE_CHUNK_CONCURRENCY=1 \
   gitnexus analyze --verbose file5
   ```

3. Observe the run stalling around one parse chunk for ~30s and then failing with `Napi::Error`.

### Environment

- OS: macOS
- Node: running via installed `gitnexus` package from Homebrew global node_modules
- GitNexus: global install at `/opt/homebrew/lib/node_modules/gitnexus`

### Logs / screenshots

Original analyze symptom:

```text
Parsing chunk 33/50... (Parsing...) (30s)
libc++abi: terminating due to uncaught exception of type Napi::Error
```

What was ruled out:

1. Pure `tree-sitter-go` parse does not crash on this file.
2. `GO_SCOPE_QUERY.matches(tree.rootNode)` does not crash on this file.
3. Main-thread sequential `processParsing(...)` also completes successfully on this file.

Key isolation results:

- `extractParsedFile(...)` alone on the large file took about 48s:

  ```json
  {"ev":"done","elapsedMs":48105,"parsed":true,"scopeCount":4087,"localDefs":2408,"referenceSites":4712,"parsedImports":11}
  ```

- A worker-thread probe showed:
  - parse finished quickly
  - `matches()` finished quickly
  - `sub-batch-done` was only emitted after about 64s

This matches the current worker-pool idle timeout behavior:

- `worker-pool.js` resets the idle timer only on `progress`, `warning`, and `sub-batch-done`
- `parse-worker` emits `progress` after parse, but not during the long Go scope-extraction phase
- default idle timeout is 30s, so the parent can treat the worker as hung and terminate it before `sub-batch-done`

This makes the apparent native `Napi::Error` look like a termination side effect rather than the original root cause.

### Suspected root cause

A long-running phase inside the worker, likely Go `extractParsedFile` / `emitGoScopeCaptures`, does not emit keepalive/progress messages, so `WorkerPool` idle timeout kills a healthy but busy worker.

### Suggested fix directions

1. Emit heartbeat/progress messages during long scope-extraction work in the parse worker.
2. Or relax/adjust worker idle timeout semantics so long CPU-bound extraction phases without intermediate messages are not treated as hangs.
3. At minimum, surface the failure as an idle-timeout/worker-termination issue rather than an opaque `Napi::Error`.

title: feat(group): add Kotlin Spring HTTP route extraction (named + positional)
body:
## Summary

Follow-up to #1834 (now merged) — extends the Spring named-argument HTTP route extraction to Kotlin Spring Boot controllers, as suggested by @magyargergo in https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/pull/1834#issuecomment-4551590182.

A new `http-patterns/kotlin.ts` plugin sits behind the optional `tree-sitter-kotlin` grammar, registered for `.kt` / `.kts`. Both annotation forms produce providers:

```kotlin
@RequestMapping("/api")          @GetMapping("/users")             // positional
@RequestMapping(path = "/api")   @GetMapping(path = "/users")      // named
@RequestMapping(value = "/api")  @GetMapping(value = "/users")     // named
```

## Why two queries

The Kotlin AST (fwcd/tree-sitter-kotlin) shares one node type — `value_argument` — for both positional and named forms, with an optional leading `simple_identifier "="` distinguishing them. So the queries split:

- **positional** anchors `string_literal` as the first named child of `value_argument` via the immediate-child anchor `.`
- **named** explicitly captures `simple_identifier` and constrains it to `^(path|value)$` via `#match?`, mirroring the same safety bar enforced by `http-patterns/java.ts` and `topic-patterns/java.ts` after the #1834 review

Without the `key:` constraint, the named query would also capture non-route attributes like `produces`, `consumes`, `headers`, `name`, `params` — emitting bogus contracts identical to the Finding A failure mode flagged on #1834.

## Optional dependency

`tree-sitter-kotlin` is an `optionalDependency`. When the native binding is unavailable (e.g. CI environments where the build fails), the plugin exports `null` and `index.ts` skips registering `.kt` / `.kts`, so the orchestrator stays healthy.

This mirrors the existing pattern used by `parse-worker.ts` and `parser-loader.ts`.

## Out of scope

Kotlin **consumer** detection (RestTemplate / WebClient / OkHttp) is intentionally not included here. The Kotlin call-site ASTs differ enough from Java's `method_invocation` shape that I felt a focused follow-up PR would be easier to review than bundling it. Happy to open that next.

## Tests

11 new cases under `provider extraction — source-scan fallback (Strategy B)`, gated by the kotlin grammar availability:

**Positive (8)**
- class `@RequestMapping("/api/v1")` (positional)
- class `@RequestMapping(path = "/api/v2")`
- class `@RequestMapping(value = "/orders")`
- method `@GetMapping(value = "/users")`
- method `@GetMapping(path = "/users")`
- method `@PostMapping(path = "/users")`
- mixed: class named-arg + method positional
- mixed: class positional + method named-arg

**Anti-regression (3)**
- `@GetMapping(produces = "application/json")` emits no provider
- `@GetMapping(name = "x", value = "/users")` emits exactly one provider
- `@RequestMapping(path = "/api", name = "myApi")` prefix stays `/api`, never `myApi`

I sanity-checked the constraint the other way too: removing `(#match? @key "^(path|value)$")` makes precisely the 3 anti-regression tests fail — same shape as the Java fix.

## Local validation

- `http-route-extractor.test.ts` — 54 / 54 ✅
- `test/unit/group` — 534 / 534 ✅
- `npx tsc --noEmit` — clean ✅

title: fix(web): replace broken Browse-for-folder with upload directory picker
body:
## Summary

Fixes the "Browse for folder" button in the local path analysis UI, which was completely broken on all platforms (Docker, local Windows, local Linux). The button used `<input type="file" webkitdirectory>` which only exposes relative paths via `webkitRelativePath` — the code extracted just the folder name (e.g. `myproject`), causing the server to reject it with *"path must be an absolute path"*. No browser API can expose absolute filesystem paths, so the approach was fundamentally unfixable.

This PR replaces the broken browser-side directory picker with a server-side directory listing endpoint + a new `DirectoryPicker` modal component. Docker users can now browse `/workspace/` and other container paths directly from the UI.

### Changes

- **`GET /api/fs/list`** endpoint in `api.ts` — lists subdirectories at a given absolute server-side path (rate-limited via `createRouteLimiter`, validates absolute path + rejects traversal)
- **`listDirectories()`** client function in `backend-client.ts`
- **`DirectoryPicker`** modal component — breadcrumb navigation, sorted directory listing, folder selection, loading/error/empty states
- **`RepoAnalyzer.tsx`** — removed broken `webkitdirectory` file input, wired in `DirectoryPicker`
- **i18n** — updated en + zh-CN locale files with new strings
- **Unit tests** — 9 tests covering happy paths, validation, error handling, and rate-limit wiring

### Before / After

| Before | After |
|--------|-------|
| "Browse for folder" sends only folder name → server rejects with "path must be an absolute path" | "Browse server directories" opens a modal that navigates real server-side directories and returns the full absolute path |
| Docker users have no way to discover container paths | Docker users can browse `/workspace/`, `/data/gitnexus/`, etc. directly |
| Manual path typing works (unchanged) | Manual path typing still works (unchanged) |

## Test plan

- [x] `npx vitest run test/unit/api-fs-list.test.ts` — 9 tests passing
- [x] Existing API tests unaffected (`api-file-route`, `server-validation`, `rate-limit` — 51 tests passing)
- [x] TypeScript type check passes (`tsc --noEmit` for both gitnexus and gitnexus-web)
- [x] Pre-commit hooks pass (eslint, prettier, tsc)
- [ ] Manual test: start server, open web UI, click "Browse server directories", navigate to a folder, select → path appears in input field

Closes #1518

title: feat(review): add PR reviewer swarm agents
body:
## Summary

Adds a coordinated, read-only Claude Code reviewer swarm for GitNexus pull requests. Seven specialized subagents — each focused on a single review domain — are orchestrated by a new `/gitnexus-pr-swarm-review` skill that produces structured, evidence-grounded production-readiness reviews.

The swarm coexists with the existing single-agent `/gitnexus-pr-review` skill as a deeper alternative.

## What's included

**7 project-level subagents** (`.claude/agents/`):

| Agent | Focus |
|-------|-------|
| `gitnexus-pr-facts-historian` | PR identity, GitHub state, changed files, commits, linked issues, repo history, visibility gaps |
| `gitnexus-branch-hygiene-reviewer` | Merge state and branch hygiene classification using exact enumerated values |
| `gitnexus-risk-architect` | Production failure modes via risk-model-first reasoning |
| `gitnexus-test-ci-verifier` | Test coverage, CI wiring, validation gaps |
| `gitnexus-security-boundary-reviewer` | Auth, secrets, injection, hidden Unicode/bidi controls, trust boundaries |
| `gitnexus-docs-dod-reviewer` | PR-specific Definition of Done from repo guidance docs |
| `gitnexus-synthesis-critic` | Final review validation for evidence grounding and verdict-rule compliance |

**1 orchestration skill** (`.claude/skills/gitnexus-pr-swarm-review/SKILL.md`):
- Invoked as `/gitnexus-pr-swarm-review <PR number or URL>`
- Dispatches agents in dependency order (facts first, then parallel domain review, synthesis last)
- Enforces exact enum classifications for merge state, branch hygiene, and final verdict
- Requires evidence citations on all findings

**1 documentation file** (`.claude/README-gitnexus-reviewer-swarm.md`)

## Design decisions

- **All agents are read-only** — tools limited to Read, Grep, Glob, Bash. No agent can edit files.
- **Missing visibility → verification work** — when GitHub state can't be determined, agents must convert gaps into mandatory verification points rather than inventing facts.
- **Exact enum verdicts** — merge state (9 values), branch hygiene (4 values), and final verdict (4 values) use closed sets to prevent ambiguous or creative classifications.
- **No hooks** — manually invoked only. Automatic triggering is deferred to a follow-up PR.

## `.gitignore` changes

Changed `.claude/agents/` and `.claude/skills/` from directory-level ignores to content-level ignores (`*` instead of `/`) so negation patterns can un-ignore specific files. Added negation patterns for `gitnexus-*.md` agents and the `gitnexus-pr-swarm-review/` skill.

title: Add Laravel Blade Template Support
body:
### Area

gitnexus (CLI / core / indexing / MCP server)

### Problem or opportunity

## Feature Request: Add Laravel Blade Template Support

### Summary

GitNexus currently does not support `.blade.php` files (Laravel Blade templates). During indexing, every Blade file produces a warning like:

```
scope extraction failed for Modules/Admin/Resources/views/activity/register/list.blade.php: ScopeExtractor: no Module scope found. Provider must emit at least one @scope.module capture per file.
```

### Environment

- GitNexus version: `1.6.5`
- Project type: Laravel (PHP) with modular structure (`nwidart/laravel-modules`)
- Affected file pattern: `Modules/*/Resources/views/**/*.blade.php`

### Current Behavior

- All `.blade.php` files fail scope extraction during the analyze phase
- Blade view files are excluded from the knowledge graph entirely
- Hundreds of WARN log entries are generated, making output noisy

### Expected Behavior

- `.blade.php` files should be parsed and included in the knowledge graph
- Relationships between Blade views and their corresponding controllers/routes should be traceable
- Blast Radius analysis should account for view dependencies

### Why This Matters

Laravel is one of the most widely used PHP frameworks. Blade is its native templating engine. Projects using `nwidart/laravel-modules` follow a structured layout where views are tightly coupled to controllers and routes. Without Blade support, the graph is incomplete for any Laravel project.

### Suggested Approach

Consider integrating a tree-sitter grammar for Blade, such as [`tree-sitter-blade`](https://github.com/EmranMR/tree-sitter-blade), and adding a ScopeExtractor provider that recognizes the module path from the file's directory structure (e.g., `Modules/{ModuleName}/Resources/views/...`).

### Additional Context

Even partial support — such as extracting `@extends`, `@include`, `@component` directives to build a view dependency graph — would significantly improve coverage for Laravel codebases.

Happy to help test or provide sample files if needed.

### Proposed solution

- `.blade.php` files should be parsed and included in the knowledge graph
- Relationships between Blade views and their corresponding controllers/routes should be traceable
- Blast Radius analysis should account for view dependencies

### Why This Matters

Laravel is one of the most widely used PHP frameworks. Blade is its native templating engine. Projects using `nwidart/laravel-modules` follow a structured layout where views are tightly coupled to controllers and routes. Without Blade support, the graph is incomplete for any Laravel project.

### Suggested Approach

Consider integrating a tree-sitter grammar for Blade, such as [`tree-sitter-blade`](https://github.com/EmranMR/tree-sitter-blade), and adding a ScopeExtractor provider that recognizes the module path from the file's directory structure (e.g., `Modules/{ModuleName}/Resources/views/...`).

### Additional Context

Even partial support — such as extracting `@extends`, `@include`, `@component` directives to build a view dependency graph — would significantly improve coverage for Laravel codebases.

title: Proposal: Smarter re-analyze storage hygiene
body:
### Area

gitnexus (CLI / core / indexing / MCP server)

### Problem or opportunity

GitNexus currently reuses the repo-local `.gitnexus/lbug` store across re-analyze runs. That is usually the right default, but it can also make users feel responsible for deciding when local index state is still healthy enough to reuse and when they should manually force a rebuild.

From a product perspective, this feels like an internal storage-management concern leaking into user workflow. Users should not need to understand LadybugDB behavior, inspect `.gitnexus/` contents, or guess when `gitnexus analyze --force` is the safer option.

### Proposed solution

GitNexus should be smarter about deciding when routine re-analyze can safely reuse existing on-disk graph state and when it should fall back to a clean rebuild automatically.

This proposal is intentionally outcome-focused rather than implementation-prescriptive. The desired user-facing behavior is:

- routine re-analyze stays fast when reuse is healthy
- GitNexus self-corrects when reuse is no longer the right choice
- users are not expected to manually monitor local index health
- any automatic fallback remains understandable and predictable

### Alternatives considered

### Keep the current manual workflow

Users can continue relying on `gitnexus analyze --force` or manual cleanup when re-analyze behavior starts to feel questionable.

This is workable, but it keeps storage hygiene as a user responsibility rather than a product responsibility.

### Improve documentation only

Better docs could explain when a manual rebuild is useful.

That would help discoverability, but it would not address the underlying UX issue: GitNexus already has more context than the user does, so it should make a better default decision on its own when possible.


### Acceptance criteria

- GitNexus can automatically recover from local graph-store states that are not good candidates for reuse
- ordinary healthy re-analyze runs still keep the fast path
- users do not need to inspect `.gitnexus/` contents to decide whether to force a rebuild
- when GitNexus chooses a clean rebuild automatically, the behavior is explainable and not surprising
- regression coverage exists for the self-healing / auto-rebuild decision path

### Constraints

- correctness comes first; optimization should not preserve questionable local state
- normal re-analyze should not become unexpectedly slow in common healthy cases
- this proposal does not require a specific heuristic, threshold, or storage-engine-level approach
- the user experience should stay simple; this should not require routine manual tuning

### Open questions

- what signals are reliable enough to decide reuse vs rebuild?
- should GitNexus explicitly tell the user when it chose an automatic rebuild, and why?
- should this remain fully automatic, or should there also be a status/debug surface for local index health?

title: feat(group): add Kotlin Spring HTTP consumer extraction
body:
## Summary

Follow-up to #1849 (Kotlin providers, merged) — extends `http-patterns/kotlin.ts` with three call-site patterns common in Kotlin Spring projects, completing 80% of real-world consumer detection coverage.

| Framework | Pattern | Verb source |
|---|---|---|
| RestTemplate | `restTemplate.getForObject("/x", ...)` etc. | method name (`getForObject` → GET, `postForEntity` → POST, `put` → PUT, `delete` → DELETE, `patchForObject` → PATCH) |
| WebClient (short form) | `webClient.get().uri("/x")` etc. | inner navigation suffix (`get`/`post`/`put`/`delete`/`patch`) |
| OkHttp | `Request.Builder().url("/x")` | always GET (matches the Java plugin's heuristic) |

The mappings (`REST_TEMPLATE_TO_HTTP`, `WEB_CLIENT_SHORT_TO_HTTP`) mirror the Java plugin so polyglot repos coalesce on the same `http::VERB::/path` contract IDs.

## Out of scope

`webClient.method(HttpMethod.X).uri("/y")` long form is intentionally deferred. The verb sits on a sibling `call_expression` two hops away, so it needs walk-up logic rather than a flat tree-sitter query — that warrants its own focused PR. An anti-overreach test pins the current behavior so a future short-form change can't accidentally start matching the long form.

## Why these queries are correct

The Kotlin AST shape for `webClient.get().uri("/x")` is:

```
call_expression                       ← outer .uri("/x")
  navigation_expression
    call_expression                   ← inner webClient.get()
      navigation_expression
        simple_identifier "webClient"
        navigation_suffix .get
      call_suffix ()
    navigation_suffix .uri
  call_suffix
    value_arguments
      value_argument . string_literal "/x"
```

The query anchors on the OUTER call (`.uri(...)`) and walks one level inward to constrain the inner suffix to a verb name. The leading `.` on `value_argument` ensures the path is the first positional argument.

OkHttp uses the same outer/inner shape but with `Request` / `Builder` / `url` constraints. RestTemplate is one level shallower (no chained verb hop).

## Receiver-name constraints (and the trade-off)

`#eq? @obj "restTemplate"` and `#eq? @cls "Request"` match the Java plugin's heuristic. A project that aliases the receiver under a different name (`val template = ...; template.getForObject(...)`) won't be picked up. This keeps false-positive rates low and is documented in the file header. Same trade-off the Java plugin already accepts.

## Tests

5 new cases under `consumer extraction — fetch patterns`, gated by tree-sitter-kotlin grammar availability (matches the Provider gating from #1849).

**Positive (3)**
- RestTemplate verbs (5 calls × 5 verbs)
- WebClient short-form verbs (5 calls × 5 verbs)
- OkHttp `Request.Builder().url("/x")`

**Anti-regression (2)**
- WebClient long form `.method(HttpMethod.X)` produces no consumer (deferred-feature pin)
- non-restTemplate receiver does not match (receiver-name pin)

I sanity-checked the constraint the other way: removing `(#eq? @obj "restTemplate")` makes the receiver-name anti-regression test fail. Same shape as the validation done on #1834 and #1849.

## Local validation

- `http-route-extractor.test.ts` — 59 / 59 ✅
- `test/unit/group` — 539 / 539 ✅
- `npm run format:check` — clean ✅

title: fix(query): CONTAINS fallback when FTS extension unavailable (Windows)
body:
## Summary

On Windows the LadybugDB FTS extension is not loaded (see [`pool-adapter.ts` win32 SIGSEGV guard](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/blob/v1.6.5/gitnexus/src/core/lbug/pool-adapter.ts#L357-L362)) so `searchFTSFromLbug` reports `ftsAvailable: false`. The `query` tool then returns an empty payload with this warning:

> FTS indexes missing — keyword search degraded. Run: gitnexus analyze --force to rebuild indexes.

…which is misleading because no amount of `analyze --force` will install the missing extension on Windows. The query tool is effectively non-functional for Windows users.

This PR mirrors the `augment` CONTAINS fallback from #1476: when FTS is reported unavailable, run a per-label CONTAINS scan against `Method` / `Function` / `Class` / `Interface` / `File` tables so `query` still returns ranked symbol matches.

## Repro (pre-fix)

```sh
gitnexus query "cart rollback when payment cancelled" --repo MyRepo
# {
#   "processes": [],
#   "process_symbols": [],
#   "definitions": [],
#   "warning": "FTS indexes missing — keyword search degraded. Run: gitnexus analyze --force to rebuild indexes."
# }
```

`gitnexus doctor` reports FTS `available`, masking the real issue:

```
Capabilities
  Graph store:     available
  Full-text search: available    ← reports available based on provider class presence
  VECTOR index:    unavailable
```

But the actual `CALL QUERY_FTS_INDEX(...)` returns:

> Catalog exception: function QUERY_FTS_INDEX is not defined. This function exists in the FTS extension.

## Behavior after fix

Same query on the same repo:

```sh
{
  "processes": [...],
  "process_symbols": [...3 hits in CTLHoaDon...],
  "definitions": [...18 ranked matches...],
  "warning": "FTS extension unavailable on this platform — using CONTAINS keyword fallback (less accurate than BM25 but functional)."
}
```

## Implementation

- New `containsKeywordFallback(repo, query, limit)` private method on `LocalBackend`
  - Tokenizes the query (lowercased, length > 2, non-word delim)
  - Runs one parameterized `MATCH (n:<Label>) WHERE ... CONTAINS ... ORDER BY score` per label
  - Aggregates + sorts by token-presence count
- Wired into all three FTS-unavailable code paths in `bm25Search` (module-import catch, search-throw catch, explicit `!ftsUsed` guard)
- Plumbs `containsFallback: boolean` back to the `query` handler so the warning reflects the actual condition (extension missing vs index missing)

Return type widened: `Promise<{ results: any[]; ftsUsed: boolean; containsFallback?: boolean }>`

## Limitations

- Token-presence count, not TF-IDF / true BM25 scoring — less accurate ranking
- No content-field scan (intentional — too expensive without an index over 23k+ nodes)
- Vietnamese / non-ASCII identifiers tokenize correctly because the regex splits on non-word chars but content match is still lowercased ASCII

## Test plan

- [x] TypeScript compiles cleanly (`npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json`)
- [x] Manually validated against a 23k-symbol C# repo on Windows 11 with gitnexus 1.6.5 — three previously-empty concept queries now return correct process-grouped results with the expected gotcha symbols ranked at the top
- [ ] Unit tests not run locally (skipped `postinstall` → missing native `lbugjs.node`); will rely on CI
- [ ] Suggest adding a unit test in `test/unit/bm25-search.test.ts` that mocks `searchFTSFromLbug` to return `ftsAvailable: false` and asserts `containsKeywordFallback` is called

## Related

- #1476 (`augment` CONTAINS fallback) — same pattern, now applied to `query`
- #1489, #1540 (FTS-unavailable guards) — this PR is the next layer: turning the empty-result warning into a functional fallback

title: feat(ingestion): trace Symfony DI bindings — interface→implementation autowiring is invisible to impact()
body:
## Problem

On any Symfony codebase using the DI container, GitNexus treats a service as **orphaned** whenever a consumer is type-hinted against an interface (or an abstract/parent class) while the concrete service is wired by the container. The `consumer → implementation` edge does not exist in code — it is produced by Symfony's container resolution (an explicit alias in `services.yaml` **or** implicit autowiring by type), which static parsing never sees.

This is the **Symfony instance of the same class of bug as #1589** (FastAPI `Depends()`). #1852 addresses Python `Depends()` and JS fetch wrappers, but PHP / Symfony container resolution is a distinct mechanism and remains uncovered.

## Reproduction

A logger interface with several implementations; autowiring injects the configured one:

```php
// src/Log/Logger.php
interface Logger { public function log(string $message): void; }

// src/Log/FileLogger.php
final class FileLogger implements Logger { /* ... */ }

// src/Log/SyslogLogger.php
final class SyslogLogger implements Logger { /* ... */ }

// src/Order/OrderService.php
final class OrderService {
    public function __construct(private Logger $logger) {}  // type-hinted against the INTERFACE
}
```

```yaml
# config/services.yaml — the container decides which implementation is injected
services:
  App\Log\Logger: '@App\Log\FileLogger'
```

Observed:
- `impact("FileLogger", upstream)` → `impactedCount: 0, risk: LOW`
- `context("FileLogger")` → `incoming: {}`

`FileLogger` is the implementation actually injected everywhere `Logger` is consumed, yet it looks safe to change. It isn't: `OrderService` (and every other `Logger` consumer) depends on it through the container binding.

The graph contains `consumer → interface` and `impl → interface` (`implements` / `method_implements`), but **never** `consumer → impl`.

## Proposed approach

Resolve the binding from the **compiled container**, not from raw YAML:

- `bin/console debug:container --format=json` (or the cached `var/cache/<env>/App_KernelDevDebugContainer.xml`) exposes both explicit aliases (`interface → impl`) **and** implicit autowiring (type → impl).
- Synthesize additive edges (e.g. `WIRES` interface→impl, or resolved `CALLS` consumer→impl) — no existing edge/node/query contract changes, matching the additive style of #1852.

Prior art: `phpstan/phpstan-symfony` resolves these via `containerXmlPath` pointing at the compiled container. A static-YAML-only resolver is insufficient — in a real audit it covered ~58% of bindings (53/91) and missed all implicit autowiring; the compiled container is the canonical source.

Constraints to document:
- Requires a compiled container (naturally available in CI; needs `composer install` locally).
- Container diverges per environment (`dev`/`test`/`prod`) — which to index is a config choice.

## Test plan (mirroring #1852)
- [ ] Integration: explicit alias binding → consumer→impl edge present, `impact()` returns the consumer.
- [ ] Integration: implicit autowiring (no `services.yaml` entry) → edge still resolved.
- [ ] No regression on existing resolution tests.



## Related

- **#1225** — *Improve analysis for Java projects built with Spring and Spring Boot*. Same class of gap (IoC container, autowiring, runtime proxies) for another ecosystem. This issue is the **Symfony counterpart**; both need framework-aware container resolution.
- **#1589 / #1852** — the FastAPI `Depends()` instance of the same underlying problem (an edge produced by the framework, not present in source). #1852 covers Python/JS; this covers PHP/Symfony.

title: feat(query): epistemic lower-bound — flag impact()/context() when unresolved indirection is on the path, instead of reporting impactedCount: 0
body:
## Problem

When GitNexus cannot resolve an indirection — DI binding, dynamic dispatch, reflection, or an HTTP wrapper named outside a known convention — `impact()` and `context()` silently report `impactedCount: 0` / `incoming: {}`. **Absence of a resolved edge is rendered as absence of dependency.** The user reads "safe to refactor" when the truth is "I could not trace this."

This is structural, not a missing-framework problem. Per-pattern resolution (#1589 → #1852, and a forthcoming Symfony DI issue) is valuable but is inherently whack-a-mole: it will never cover every framework or every pattern. Even where it fires, it leaves silent holes — #1852's frontend support detects fetch wrappers **by naming convention** (`apiFetch`, `fetchJSON`, …), so a wrapper named outside that set falls straight back to `impactedCount: 0` with no signal. #1852 is itself evidence: each new resolver recreates a boundary wherever its heuristic doesn't match.

## Proposed approach

Make "unresolved" a **first-class state distinct from "no dependency."** When a traversal crosses a node related by `implements` / `method_implements` (or any known-but-unresolved indirection), annotate the result instead of returning a bare count:

```jsonc
{
  "impactedCount": 3,
  "epistemic": "lower-bound",          // vs "exact"
  "boundaries": [
    "Logger is an interface with 2 implementation(s); consumers resolved
     indirectly (e.g. DI container) are not traced — actual impact may be higher."
  ]
}
```

This is the impact-analysis analogue of what static type-checkers do when they widen to `mixed`: the tool knows a value/edge exists, it just cannot narrow what flows past it — and it says so rather than asserting "nothing."

## Why this is cheap and worth it

- **Framework-agnostic**: uses data already in the graph — the `implements` / `method_implements` edges GitNexus already stores. It resolves nothing; it only refuses to report an unverifiable zero as a confident zero.
- **Complements per-pattern resolvers, doesn't compete**: resolution (#1852, Symfony DI, …) gives precision where the engineering is worth it; this flag is the universal floor underneath, catching everything resolution hasn't covered yet — or ever will.

## Test plan
- [ ] `impact()` on an interface (or an impl reachable only via `implements`) carries `epistemic: "lower-bound"` + a boundary note.
- [ ] `impact()` on a fully-resolved leaf with no indirection stays `epistemic: "exact"`.
- [ ] No change to existing counts; the annotation is additive.



## Related / prior art

- **#1004** (closed, completed) — `groupImpact` was fixed so it no longer reports local-phase failures as "zero-hit success payloads." This issue extends the **same already-accepted principle** — *a zero must not mask an unknown* — from the error path to the **unresolved-indirection path**.
- **#429** — the codebase already has a confidence model (`TIER_CONFIDENCE` / `RELATIONSHIP_CONFIDENCE`: structural / resolved / heuristic / fallback / uncertain). The `epistemic` annotation proposed here should **align with that existing vocabulary** rather than introduce a parallel concept.
- **Family of per-pattern resolution gaps this would backstop**: #1589 / #1852 (FastAPI `Depends()`, fetch wrappers), #1857 (Symfony DI), #1364 (factory switch-case dispatch), #492 (Go interface calls), #1225 (Spring). Each fixes *one* pattern; none signals when it cannot resolve. This flag is the universal floor underneath all of them.

Bumps [@playwright/test](https://github.com/microsoft/playwright) from 1.58.2 to 1.60.0.
Release notes

Sourced from @​playwright/test's releases.

v1.60.0

🌐 HAR recording on Tracing

tracing.startHar() / tracing.stopHar() expose HAR recording as a first-class tracing API, with the same content, mode and urlFilter options as recordHar. The returned Disposable makes it easy to scope a recording with await using:

await using har = await context.tracing.startHar('trace.har');
const page = await context.newPage();
await page.goto('https://playwright.dev');
// HAR is finalized when `har` goes out of scope.

🪝 Drop API

New locator.drop() simulates an external drag-and-drop of files or clipboard-like data onto an element. Playwright dispatches dragenter, dragover, and drop with a synthetic [DataTransfer] in the page context — works cross-browser and is great for testing upload zones:

await page.locator('#dropzone').drop({
  files: { name: 'note.txt', mimeType: 'text/plain', buffer: Buffer.from('hello') },
});

await page.locator('#dropzone').drop({
data: {
'text/plain': 'hello world',
'text/uri-list': 'https://example.com',
},
});

🎯 Aria snapshots

  • expect(page).toMatchAriaSnapshot() now works on a Page, in addition to a Locator — equivalent to asserting against page.locator('body').
  • New boxes option on locator.ariaSnapshot() / page.ariaSnapshot() appends each element's bounding box as [box=x,y,width,height], useful for AI consumption.

🛑 test.abort()

New test.abort() aborts the currently running test from a fixture, hook, or route handler with an optional message. Use it when you have detected an unrecoverable misuse and want to fail the test right away:

test('does not publish to the shared page', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.route('**/publish', route => {
    test.abort('Tests must not publish to the shared page. Use the `clone` option.');
    return route.abort();
  });
  // ...
});

title: chore(deps)(deps): bump axios from 1.16.0 to 1.16.1 in /gitnexus-web
body:
Bumps [axios](https://github.com/axios/axios) from 1.16.0 to 1.16.1.
Release notes

Sourced from axios's releases.

v1.16.1 — May 13, 2026

This release ships a defence-in-depth fix for prototype pollution in formDataToJSON, hardens proxy and CI workflows, restores Webpack 4 compatibility for the fetch adapter, and includes several small bug fixes and maintenance improvements.

🔒 Security Fixes

  • Prototype Pollution Defence-in-Depth: Hardened formDataToJSON against already-polluted Object.prototype by walking own properties only, so attacker-controlled keys inherited from a poisoned prototype cannot propagate through deserialization. (#7413)
  • Proxy Cleartext Leak: Fixed an issue where HTTPS request data could be transmitted in cleartext to an HTTP proxy under certain configurations. (#10858)
  • CI Cache Removal: Removed all GitHub Actions caches as a defence-in-depth measure against cache poisoning vectors in the build pipeline. (#10882)

🐛 Bug Fixes

  • Data URI Parsing: Updated the fromDataURI regex to match RFC 2397 more strictly, fixing edge cases in data: URL handling. (#10829)
  • Unicode Headers: Preserved Unicode header values when running through request interceptors, so non-ASCII header content is no longer corrupted before dispatch. (#10850)
  • XHR Upload Progress: Guarded against malformed ProgressEvent payloads emitted by some environments during XHR upload, preventing crashes when loaded / total are missing or invalid. (#10868)
  • Webpack 4 Fetch Adapter: Fixed an "unexpected token" error caused by syntax in the fetch adapter that Webpack 4 could not parse, restoring compatibility for legacy bundler users. (#10864)
  • Type Definitions: Made parseReviver context.source optional in the type definitions to align with the ES2023 specification. (#10837)
  • URL Object Support Reverted: Reverted the change that allowed passing a URL object as config.url (originally #10866) due to regressions; this support will be reintroduced in a later release once the underlying issues are addressed. (#10874)

🔧 Maintenance & Chores

  • Cycle Detection Refactor: Replaced the array-based cycle tracker in toJSONObject with a WeakSet, improving performance and memory behaviour on large nested structures. (#10832)
  • composeSignals Cleanup: Refactored composeSignals to use a clearer early-return structure, simplifying the cancellation/abort composition path. (#10844)
  • AI Readiness & Repo Docs: Added AGENTS.md and related contributor-guide updates for both human and AI agents, plus post-release documentation improvements. (#10835, #10841)
  • Docs Improvements: Clarified the GET request example, fixed the interceptor eject example to reference the correct instance, and corrected the Buzzoid sponsor description in the README. (#10836, #10853, #10856)
  • Sponsorship Tooling: Fixed empty sponsor arrays in the sponsor processing script, added the ability to inject additional sponsors, updated the sponsorship link, and added a Twicsy advertisement entry. (#10843, #10859, #10869)
  • Dependencies: Bumped @commitlint/cli from 20.5.0 to 20.5.2. (#10846)

v4.35.5

  • We have improved how the JavaScript bundles for the CodeQL Action are generated to avoid duplication across bundles and reduce the size of the repository by around 70%. This should have no effect on the runtime behaviour of the CodeQL Action. #3899
  • For performance and accuracy reasons, improved incremental analysis will now only be enabled on a pull request when diff-informed analysis is also enabled for that run. If diff-informed analysis is unavailable (for example, because the PR diff ranges could not be computed), the action will fall back to a full analysis. #3791
  • If multiple inputs are provided for the GitHub-internal analysis-kinds input, only code-scanning will be enabled. The analysis-kinds input is experimental, for GitHub-internal use only, and may change without notice at any time. #3892
  • Added an experimental change which, when running a Code Scanning analysis for a PR with improved incremental analysis enabled, prefers CodeQL CLI versions that have a cached overlay-base database for the configured languages.
