title: Swift parser unavailable in published 1.6.7 when vendored tree-sitter-swift is not materialized
body:
## Summary

`gitnexus@1.6.7` can still skip all Swift files even though the published package includes `vendor/tree-sitter-swift` and the Swift prebuilds from the merged #1130 fix.

The immediate failure appears to be that the runtime loader uses a bare `require('tree-sitter-swift')`, but the vendored package was present only under `node_modules/gitnexus/vendor/tree-sitter-swift` and had not been materialized into a resolvable `node_modules/.../tree-sitter-swift` package.

This is especially confusing because the warning points at #1130, which appears to have been merged to solve this exact Swift parser availability problem.

## Environment

Sanitized local environment details:

- GitNexus: `1.6.7`
- Install path style: `npx gitnexus` cache install
- OS/arch: macOS arm64
- Node: `v22.22.3`
- npm: `11.16.0`
- Project type: Swift-heavy repository

No project-specific paths are included here; local paths below are shown as placeholders.

## What happened

Running `npx gitnexus analyze --force --skip-agents-md --skip-skills` produced warnings like:

```text
GitNexus [analyze]: optional grammar "tree-sitter-swift" is unavailable — .swift files will not be parsed. Reinstall without GITNEXUS_SKIP_OPTIONAL_GRAMMARS=1 (and ensure python3, make, g++) to enable.
[gitnexus] Swift parsing disabled: vendored `tree-sitter-swift` (under `gitnexus/vendor/tree-sitter-swift`) failed to load. Likely cause: no prebuilt `.node` for this platform/architecture. See https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/issues/1130. (Cannot find module 'tree-sitter-swift')
Skipping 545 swift file(s) — swift parser not available (native binding may not have built). Try: npm rebuild tree-sitter-swift
```

The degraded index was tiny compared with a working Swift parse:

```text
1,505 nodes | 2,046 edges | 22 clusters | 79 flows
```

After working around the missing module, the same repository indexed as:

```text
16,967 nodes | 337,720 edges | 569 clusters | 300 flows
```

## Observed package state

Inside the published package cache:

- `node_modules/gitnexus/vendor/tree-sitter-swift/package.json` existed.
- `node_modules/gitnexus/vendor/tree-sitter-swift/prebuilds/darwin-arm64/tree-sitter-swift.node` existed.
- `node_modules/gitnexus/node_modules/tree-sitter-swift` was missing.
- `node_modules/tree-sitter-swift` was also missing before the manual workaround.
- `dist/core/tree-sitter/parser-loader.js` contains:

```js
[SupportedLanguages.Swift]: {
  load: () => _require('tree-sitter-swift'),
  optional: true,
  userSkippable: true,
  unavailableNote: 'Swift parsing disabled: vendored `tree-sitter-swift` ...'
}
```

That means the vendored package can be present but still not loadable if the postinstall materialization step did not run or did not create `node_modules/gitnexus/node_modules/tree-sitter-swift`.

## Dependency/version confusion

There also seems to be a version compatibility trap:

```text
gitnexus@1.6.7 depends on tree-sitter@0.21.1
tree-sitter-swift@0.7.1 peers tree-sitter@^0.22.1
tree-sitter-swift@0.6.0 peers tree-sitter@^0.21.1
```

So installing latest `tree-sitter-swift@0.7.1` manually into the same package cache fails dependency resolution unless forced, while `tree-sitter-swift@0.6.0` installs/builds against the pinned runtime.

I understand from #1130 that GitNexus intentionally kept `tree-sitter@0.21.1` to keep the broader upgrade separate from #858, and that the vendored Swift package adjusts peer support / ships prebuilds. The problem is that the published install path still ended up with the vendored Swift package present but not resolvable by the bare `require('tree-sitter-swift')` call.

## Manual workaround that restored Swift coverage

This workaround repaired the local `npx` cache, but it should not be required for normal users:

```bash
npm install --prefix <npx-cache> tree-sitter-cli@0.21.0
npm install --prefix <npx-cache> tree-sitter-swift@0.6.0
npx gitnexus analyze --force --skip-agents-md --skip-skills
```

After this, `detect_changes` returned Swift symbols and affected flows again.

## Questions / requested fix

1. Is the `tree-sitter@0.21.1` pin still intentional for `1.6.7`, pending #858?
2. Should GitNexus support a newer installed `tree-sitter-swift` when present, or is the intended path exclusively the vendored #1130 runtime?
3. Can the loader fall back to the vendored runtime path directly if bare `require('tree-sitter-swift')` fails?
4. Can `analyze` detect the specific state "vendor package exists but materialized node_modules package is missing" and either materialize lazily or print a more accurate recovery command?
5. If npm/npx script approval or skipped postinstall scripts can cause this, can GitNexus handle that case more explicitly?

Expected behavior: a normal `npx gitnexus analyze` install of `gitnexus@1.6.7` should either load the vendored Swift parser from #1130 or provide an accurate, one-command recovery path that does not require guessing the compatible `tree-sitter-swift` version.

title: bug(hooks): Claude db-lock probe leaks orphaned lsof processes on busy Linux hosts — snowballs to sustained 100% CPU
body:
## Area

Claude Code hooks (`gitnexus/hooks/claude/hook-db-lock-probe.cjs`)

## Summary

On Linux hosts with a high process count, the PreToolUse db-lock probe leaks **orphaned `lsof` processes** (PPID 1, stuck in R state). Each leaked `lsof` adds CPU load, which makes the next probe slower and more likely to leak again — a self-reinforcing snowball. On a 16-core server this accumulated **114 orphaned `lsof` processes and a load average of 122**, pinning all cores at 100% for ~40 minutes until manually cleaned up.

The probe was introduced in #1493 (to fix #1492), so every install since v1.6.x is exposed. This is distinct from #1546 (orphaned `gitnexus mcp` processes), though both were present on the affected host.

## Environment

- gitnexus **1.6.7** (hooks installed by `gitnexus analyze` / `setup`, registered with a 10s timeout on `PreToolUse: Grep|Glob|Bash` and `PostToolUse: Bash`)
- Node v24.15.0, Ubuntu (Proxmox VM), 16 cores, 64 GB RAM
- ~700 processes / ~580 tasks at steady state (busy dev server: MySQL, Redis, nginx, Docker, several editor/agent sessions)
- 2 concurrent Claude Code sessions (with subagents → frequent Grep/Glob/Bash tool calls) open in a repo indexed by GitNexus

## What I observed

```
top - load average: 122.63, 124.17, 127.1   (16 cores)
Tasks: 707 total, 120 running
%Cpu(s): 57.8 us, 41.3 sy, 0.0 id

  PID    USER  ... %CPU  TIME+   COMMAND
2872721  root  ... 100.0 10:07   lsof
2873936  root  ... 100.0  9:09   lsof
...  (114 total, all:)
/usr/bin/lsof -nP -t -- /path/to/repo/.gitnexus/lbug
```

- All 114 `lsof` had **PPID 1** (orphaned) and were in **R state**, each having burned 4–10 minutes of CPU time.
- A **new `lsof` appeared roughly every ~30s** (matching the tool-call cadence of the active agent sessions), replacing any that finished — a stable pile-up.
- Killing the agent sessions' `gitnexus mcp` processes and `pkill -9 -x lsof` immediately recovered the host (load 122 → 19 within a minute, CPU 98.9% idle).

## Root-cause chain

1. The hook fires on **every** Grep/Glob/Bash tool call in an indexed repo, and each invocation runs the db-lock probe before acquiring the hook slot ([`gitnexus-hook.cjs` — probe at L262, `acquireHookSlot` only at L272](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/blob/bde340a5/gitnexus/hooks/claude/gitnexus-hook.cjs#L262)), so probes from concurrent sessions/agents run **unserialized**.
2. `linuxProcScanFindGitNexusServer` walks `/proc/<pid>/fd/*` with `stat(2)` for every process — O(processes × fds). With 700+ processes the default **1200ms budget** (`GITNEXUS_HOOK_LINUX_PROC_BUDGET_MS`) expires before the scan finds the MCP server, returning `false`.
3. The code then falls back to `lsof`: [`spawnSync(lsofPath, ['-nP','-t','--', dbPathAbs], { timeout: 1000 })`](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/blob/bde340a5/gitnexus/hooks/claude/hook-db-lock-probe.cjs#L192). Measured on this host **while idle**, that `lsof` takes **~1.85s** — it can *never* finish within the 1000ms timeout on a busy box, so every fallback ends in ETIMEDOUT.
4. The orphaning itself: `spawnSync`'s timeout normally SIGTERMs the child (verified manually — `lsof` does die promptly on SIGTERM when delivered). But when the **hook process itself is killed first** — e.g. Claude Code's hook timeout (10s) hard-killing a hook that is starved under load, with node startup + the 1.2s proc scan + the blocking `spawnSync` ahead of it — the `lsof` child is never signalled and reparents to PID 1, running to completion (minutes of CPU under load).
5. Each orphan raises the load → the proc scan and `lsof` get slower → more hooks blow their budget and get hard-killed → more orphans. The system converges on "all cores busy running lsof".

## Suggested fix directions (can be combined)

1. **Invert the Linux proc scan** so `lsof` isn't needed at all: first scan `/proc/*/cmdline` (one small read per process, milliseconds for ~700 processes) to find candidate `gitnexus mcp|serve` processes, then stat only *their* fd entries. Complexity drops from O(processes × fds) to ~O(processes), comfortably inside the budget, and the `lsof` fallback can be deleted on Linux.
2. **Make any remaining `lsof` fallback self-destructing**: wrap it with coreutils `timeout` (`spawnSync('timeout', ['-k','1','2', lsofPath, ...])`) so even if the parent hook is SIGKILLed mid-`spawnSync`, the child is reaped after 2s. This removes the snowball precondition entirely.
3. **Cache the probe result** (e.g. a tmp file with a 30–60s TTL keyed by db path). Lock ownership changes rarely; probing on every single tool call is the multiplier that turns a slow probe into a storm.
4. **Acquire the hook slot *before* probing** (swap L262/L272) so at most one probe runs machine-wide at a time — pile-ups become impossible even if a probe is slow.

Happy to submit a PR for (1)+(2)+(4) if maintainers agree with the direction.

## Related

- #1492 / #1493 — where the probe was introduced (this issue is a regression introduced by that fix)
- #2134 — later tweak to the same skip-path
- #1546 — orphaned `gitnexus mcp` processes (separate leak, same "orphans eat the host" family)
- #168 — the hooks being installed globally amplifies exposure: every Grep/Glob/Bash in every project spawns the hook process

title: fix(hooks): bound db-lock probe subprocesses and gate probe behind hook slot (#2163)
body:
## Summary

Stops the orphaned-`lsof` CPU storm from the Claude db-lock probe by (1) wrapping the unix `lsof`/`ps` fallback in a self-destructing coreutils `timeout` guard and (2) acquiring the per-repo hook slot *before* probing, bounding concurrent probes to 3 per `.gitnexus`. Zero contract changes — fail-open/fail-closed semantics, env names, function names, and the Windows path are untouched.

Fixes #2163

## Motivation / context

See #2163 for the full incident analysis. Short version: the probe (introduced in #1493) runs unserialized on every Grep/Glob/Bash tool call. On a busy Linux host the `/proc` scan blows its 1200 ms budget, falls back to `lsof` (which can't finish within its 1 s `spawnSync` timeout there), and when Claude Code's 10 s hook timeout hard-kills the hook mid-`spawnSync`, the `lsof` child is never signalled — it reparents to PID 1 and burns CPU for minutes. Each orphan raises load, making the next probe slower and more likely to be hard-killed: a self-reinforcing snowball that pinned a 16-core host at load 122 with 114 orphaned `lsof` processes.

The fix breaks both factors of that feedback loop: orphan lifetime is now bounded at ~3 s (growth term → zero) and concurrent probes are bounded at 3 per repo (instantaneous term → bounded).

## Areas touched

- [x] `gitnexus/` (CLI / core / MCP server) — hooks + tests only
- [ ] `gitnexus-web/` (Vite / React UI)
- [ ] `.github/` (workflows, actions)
- [ ] `eval/` or other tooling
- [ ] Docs / agent config only

Also touches `gitnexus-claude-plugin/hooks/` (the byte-identical probe copy and the plugin adapter, kept in sync per the #2134 convention).

## Scope & constraints

**In scope**

- `hook-db-lock-probe.cjs` (both copies, byte-identical): new `resolveUnixGuardTimeout()` — resolves coreutils `timeout`/`gtimeout`, validated by a lazy one-shot self-test (`timeout -k 1 1 /bin/sh -c :` must exit 0) so broken wrappers (busybox < 1.34, toybox, dead symlinks) are rejected and the host falls back to current behavior rather than degrading fail-closed to fail-open. `GITNEXUS_HOOK_TIMEOUT_PATH` overrides the binary; the sentinel value `disabled` turns the guard off; an invalid path falls through to the built-in candidates (same semantics as the sibling `GITNEXUS_HOOK_LSOF_PATH`/`PS_PATH` envs).
- Guarded spawns: `lsof` runs under `timeout -k 1 2`, `ps` under `timeout -k 1 1`. The inner `spawnSync` timeouts (1000 ms / 500 ms) are unchanged and always shorter than the wrapper budgets, so on a live hook the existing ETIMEDOUT fail-closed path still triggers first — the wrapper only matters once the hook itself has been SIGKILLed. Defensive mapping of wrapper exit codes 124/137 → fail-closed (coreutils-only belt-and-suspenders, commented as such).
- All three adapters (`gitnexus/hooks/claude/gitnexus-hook.cjs`, `gitnexus-claude-plugin/hooks/gitnexus-hook.js`, `gitnexus/hooks/antigravity/gitnexus-antigravity-hook.cjs`): reordered to cheap guards → `acquireHookSlot` → probe + augment inside `try`/`finally { release() }`. The slot is a non-blocking try-lock, so hook latency only goes down. Worst-case slot hold (~18 s, Windows probe + npx-fallback augment) stays under the 30 s stale threshold with 1.6× margin — `hook-lock.cjs` is untouched.
- Tests (+379 lines in `hooks.test.ts`, +21 in `hook-test-helpers.ts`): source-order contract for all three adapters; slot-gate behavior (probe must not run when slots are full); **orphan reaping** — a SIGTERM-immune fake `lsof` whose hook parent is SIGKILLed must die within 5 s (red on base, green here; this is the incident's minimal reproduction); probe-copy byte parity; no-guard equivalence; broken-guard rejection stays fail-closed.
- CHANGELOG entry under `[Unreleased]`.

**Explicitly out of scope / not done here** (follow-ups proposed in #2163)

- Direction (1): cmdline-first `/proc` scan that removes the Linux `lsof` fallback entirely (performance rework, changes the budget-timeout fail semantics — separate PR).
- Direction (3): TTL cache for probe results (separate PR).
- Windows `win-rm-list-json.ps1` watchdog, Cursor-integration probe gap, `doctor` hook-staleness check, dev-checkout `isGitNexusServerCommand` regex gap — each deserves its own issue.
- No version bump: plugin manifests stay lockstep with the release flow; plugin users pick this up with the next release, npm/antigravity users via `gitnexus setup` (no settings.json changes, no migration).

## Implementation notes

- The two `hook-db-lock-probe.cjs` copies are byte-identical (`diff -q` clean) and the spawn-count/`windowsHide` parity convention is preserved (every spawn-family call site carries `windowsHide: true`, including the new self-test).
- On hosts without a usable guard binary the generated argv is identical to today's, byte for byte — no behavior change.
- macOS ≥ 13 ships a BSD `/usr/bin/timeout` that is syntax-compatible with the flags used; older macOS falls through to `gtimeout` (Homebrew coreutils) or no guard.

## Testing & verification

- [x] `cd gitnexus && npx vitest run test/unit/hooks.test.ts test/unit/resolve-invocation.test.ts test/unit/setup.test.ts test/unit/cli-commands.test.ts` — 172 tests in `hooks.test.ts` (see known limitations for 2 host-specific reds)
- [x] `cd gitnexus && npx vitest run test/integration/antigravity-hook-e2e.test.ts`
- [x] `npx prettier --check` / `npx eslint` on all changed files (0 errors)
- [x] `cd gitnexus && npx tsc --noEmit` — 62 pre-existing errors on main (`src/core/**`, `src/server/upload-ingest.ts`), none in files touched here; base == head verified
- [ ] `cd gitnexus && npm run test:integration` — not run (no core/indexing/MCP paths changed)

**Red/green evidence**: with the five production hook files reverted to base and the new tests kept, the mandatory regression set goes red — source-order ×3, slot-gate ×2, orphan-reaping ×1 (plus 2 strengthened probe-contract assertions). All green with the fix applied.

**Incident-class host verification** (16-core Linux dev server, ~600–700 processes — the same host class as the #2163 incident):

- 50 concurrent hook invocations → 0 `lsof` left, 0 orphans.
- 20 concurrent invocations with every hook process SIGKILLed mid-probe (simulating the Claude Code hook-timeout kill) → 0 orphaned `lsof`, 0 leftover `timeout` wrappers within 5 s.
- Live contrast observed while iterating: running the full test suite against **base** leaked 2 orphaned `lsof` (PPID 1) from real hard-kill timing alone; the same suite against this branch leaks none.

**Known limitations**

- Two pre-existing `#1493` "ENOENT lsof → fail-open" tests are red **on the pathological host itself** (real `/usr/bin/lsof` takes ~2 s there, exceeding the probe's frozen 1 s budget → fail-closed — i.e. the #2163 pathology, present on base, unchanged by this PR). Fast CI runners are unaffected.
- The orphan-reaping test requires a working coreutils `timeout` on the Linux lane (GitHub ubuntu runners ship GNU coreutils; a minimal/container runner without it would skip-fail that one test by design — it *is* the wrapper regression test).

title: fix(hooks): wrap the augment CLI child in the orphan guard (#2163)
body:
## Summary

Wraps the augment CLI child — the longest-lived previously-unwrapped subprocess (7 s local / 12 s npx) — in the same self-tested orphan guard that #2165 introduced for `lsof`/`ps`, closing the remaining SIGKILL-orphan window called out in the tri-review (finding 4). Also adds the cursor-integration slot-skip diagnostic and the guard-availability precheck polish from the same review thread.

Follow-up to #2165 (maintainer-invited: https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/pull/2165#issuecomment-4680727750 → invitation in the merge comment). Part of the #2163 follow-up list.

## Motivation / context

From the #2165 tri-review digest:

> *(pre-existing, out of declared scope)* The augment child (7s local / 12s npx) is now the longest-lived **unwrapped** subprocess; the same SIGKILL-orphan mechanism this PR fixes for lsof/ps applies to it.

When Claude Code's hook timeout SIGKILLs a hook that is blocked in the augment `spawnSync`, the CLI child (a full Node process, far heavier than `lsof`) reparents to PID 1 and runs to completion. The mechanism, the fix, and the test pattern are identical to #2165 — this PR just extends them.

## Areas touched

- [x] `gitnexus/` (CLI / core / MCP server) — hooks + tests only
- [ ] `gitnexus-web/`
- [ ] `.github/`
- [ ] `eval/` or other tooling
- [ ] Docs / agent config only

Also touches `gitnexus-claude-plugin/hooks/` (byte-identical probe copy + plugin adapter) and `gitnexus-cursor-integration/hooks/` (debug line only).

## Scope & constraints

**In scope**

- `hook-db-lock-probe.cjs` (both copies, byte-identical): export `resolveUnixGuardTimeout`. Adapters require the same module instance they already use for the lock probe, so the memo is shared and the lazy self-test still runs at most once per hook process — whoever needs the guard first (probe fallback or augment) pays the one-shot ~5 ms.
- `runGitNexusCli` in the three probe-equipped adapters (claude CJS, plugin JS, antigravity CJS): every CLI-executing branch is wrapped with `timeout -k 1 <ceil(inner_ms/1000)+1>` on Unix when a guard is available. The budget is strictly above each branch's inner `spawnSync` timeout (7000 ms → 8 s, `timeout+5000` → 13 s), so on a live hook Node's own timer always fires first and the existing error/status contract is untouched — the wrapper only matters once the hook has been SIGKILLed. Windows and no-guard hosts produce byte-identical argv to main. The plugin adapter's PATH-direct `gitnexus` branch (its most common production path) is wrapped as well; the cheap `which`/`where` detection spawn (3 s, not a CLI execution) deliberately is not.
- Cursor integration: debug-gated `augment skipped: hook slots saturated` on the slot-starved early return (same observability gap #2165's F2 fixed in the other three adapters), following that file's own `GITNEXUS_DEBUG` truthiness convention.
- Reaping tests (the two from #2165 plus the new one) get a guard-availability precheck that fails with an explicit, actionable message on hosts without a usable coreutils `timeout`. We chose an assertion over `skipIf` on purpose: a skip would let a coreutils-less Linux host go silently green on the exact regression lane this work exists for; GitHub ubuntu runners always ship coreutils, so CI behavior is unchanged.

**Explicitly out of scope / not done here**

- Wrapping the **cursor** integration's augment child: that integration does not install `hook-db-lock-probe.cjs` (see its README manual-install list), so there is no resolver sibling to require. Doing it properly means adding the probe to its install manifest — the "cursor probe" item on the #2163 follow-up list, which we'd rather do as its own PR.
- #2163 directions (1) and (3) — the cmdline-first `/proc` scan and the probe-result TTL cache — remain the next planned follow-ups.
- No version bump; CHANGELOG entry under `[Unreleased]`.

## Implementation notes

- Single-`spawnSync`-literal-per-branch pattern preserved (argv assembled conditionally), so the spawn-count/`windowsHide` parity convention holds in every touched file (verified by the in-suite regression check: CJS 4=4, Plugin 6=6, Antigravity 4=4, probe 4=4, cursor 3=3).
- `resolveUnixGuardTimeout()` is never called on `win32` (guarded at the call sites; the self-test spawns `/bin/sh`). Documented in the export JSDoc and pinned by the source tests.
- The source-pinning test counts the direct-budget formula **exactly** per adapter (Plugin: 2, others: 1), so a partial revert of any single wrapped branch cannot pass unnoticed.

## Testing & verification

- [x] `cd gitnexus && npx vitest run test/unit/hooks.test.ts` — 186/188 (the 2 reds are the pre-existing #1493 ENOENT fail-open pair, environmental to the pathological host documented in #2165's Known limitations; verified red on clean base)
- [x] `cd gitnexus && npx vitest run test/unit/resolve-invocation.test.ts test/unit/setup.test.ts test/unit/cli-commands.test.ts test/integration/antigravity-hook-e2e.test.ts` — all green (135/135 with the setup suites)
- [x] `npx prettier --check` / `npx eslint` on changed files — 0 errors
- [x] `npx tsc --noEmit` — no errors in touched files (remaining errors pre-existing on main)
- [x] Probe copies `diff -q` byte-identical

**Red/green evidence**: with only the three adapter wraps reverted (probe export and tests kept), both orphaned-augment reaping tests go red — the SIGTERM-immune fake CLI survives the hook's SIGKILL for the full poll window. With the wrap applied, the child is reaped in ~9.1 s (8 s budget + 1 s `-k` escalation), green on both the CJS and Plugin paths.

title: requireLocalhostOrigin middleware blocks LAN IPs (e.g. 172.16.x.x) despite CORS already allowing them
fix(ip): Scope write-route origin guard to server's own bound host
body:
`POST /api/analyze` and `POST /api/analyze/upload` were rejected with 403 when the Web UI was accessed via private LAN IPs, because `requireLocalhostOrigin` only permitted loopback hosts. This diverged from existing CORS behavior, which already allowed RFC1918 ranges.

- **Same-host origin guard (replaces blanket RFC1918 trust)**
  - Converted `requireLocalhostOrigin` into a factory `createLocalhostOriginGuard(boundHost)` in `gitnexus/src/server/middleware.ts`.
  - The guard now allows only:
    - Loopback origins (`localhost`, `127.0.0.1`, `[::1]`)
    - The server's own bound host (passed from `createServer`'s `host` parameter)
  - Other LAN devices on the same RFC1918 subnet are **not** trusted — prevents CSRF from arbitrary private-network hosts when `gitnexus serve --host <LAN-IP>` is used.
  - Added explicit protocol parsing so `ftp://` and other non-HTTP origins are rejected.

- **IPv6 loopback fix**
  - Fixed pre-existing dead branch: `new URL('http://[::1]:port').hostname` returns `'[::1]'` (with brackets), so the check now compares against `'[::1]'` instead of `'::1'`.

- **Write-route hardening**
  - Added `requireLocalhostOrigin` guard to previously unguarded write routes:
    - `DELETE /api/repo`
    - `POST /api/embed`
    - `DELETE /api/embed/:jobId`
    - `DELETE /api/analyze/:jobId`

- **Shared private-IP helper**
  - RFC1918/private IPv4 logic extracted into `gitnexus/src/server/private-ip.ts` (used by `isAllowedOrigin` for CORS).

- **Comprehensive test coverage**
  - `gitnexus/test/unit/api-analyze-upload.test.ts`:
    - Default guard: loopback pass, RFC1918 reject (no bound host), `ftp://` reject, `'null'` origin reject, `[::1]` pass
    - Factory guard: bound-host match pass, other RFC1918 reject, loopback still passes
  - `gitnexus/test/unit/private-ip.test.ts`: direct unit tests for `isValidIpv4Address` and `isRfc1918PrivateIpv4`

title: feat(mcp): add trace tool for shortest call path between symbols
body:
## What

Implement the `trace` MCP tool and `gitnexus trace` CLI command that finds the shortest directed call path between two symbols. Closes #1821.

## Why

The most common debugging question in any codebase is "how does A reach B?" — yet answering it means chaining 3-8 context/impact calls by hand, one hop at a time. Each hop is a round-trip; on a typical 5-7 hop call chain that's 15-30 seconds of manual graph walking for a question that should be answered in one call.

## Implementation

- **MCP tool** (`tools.ts`): `trace` tool definition with `READ_ONLY_TOOL_ANNOTATIONS`, added to `BRANCH_SCOPED_TOOLS`
- **Core BFS** (`local-backend.ts`): Directed BFS over CALLS + HAS_METHOD edges with parent-map path reconstruction. Reuses `resolveSymbolCandidates` for symbol resolution (name/UID/file-hint disambiguation). Reports furthest reachable node when no path exists.
- **CLI** (`cli/index.ts` + `cli/tool.ts`): `gitnexus trace <from> <to> [--from-uid] [--to-uid] [--depth]`
- **i18n** (`en.ts`, `zh-CN.ts`, `help-i18n.ts`): English and Chinese translations for command description and all option descriptions
- **Documentation** (`ARCHITECTURE.md`): Added trace to MCP tools table

## Response shape

```json
{
  "status": "ok",
  "from": { "name": "A", "filePath": "src/a.ts", "startLine": 1 },
  "to": { "name": "B", "filePath": "src/b.ts", "startLine": 1 },
  "hopCount": 2,
  "hops": [
    { "name": "A", "filePath": "src/a.ts", "startLine": 1 },
    { "name": "C", "filePath": "src/c.ts", "startLine": 5 },
    { "name": "B", "filePath": "src/b.ts", "startLine": 1 }
  ],
  "edges": [
    { "relType": "CALLS", "confidence": 1.0 },
    { "relType": "CALLS", "confidence": 0.95 }
  ]
}
```

## How to verify

```bash
cd gitnexus && npx tsc --noEmit          # typecheck
cd gitnexus && npx vitest run test/unit/trace-bfs.test.ts test/unit/trace-cli.test.ts  # 16/16 pass
```

## Files changed

- `gitnexus/src/mcp/tools.ts` — trace tool definition + BRANCH_SCOPED_TOOLS entry
- `gitnexus/src/mcp/local/local-backend.ts` — TraceParams, case 'trace' dispatch, trace(), _traceImpl() with directed BFS
- `gitnexus/src/cli/tool.ts` — traceCommand() export
- `gitnexus/src/cli/index.ts` — CLI registration with all options
- `gitnexus/src/cli/i18n/en.ts` — English i18n keys
- `gitnexus/src/cli/i18n/zh-CN.ts` — Chinese i18n keys
- `gitnexus/src/cli/help-i18n.ts` — Command + option description keys
- `ARCHITECTURE.md` — trace entry in tools table
- `gitnexus/test/unit/trace-bfs.test.ts` — 11 unit tests (dispatch, BFS core, ambiguous resolution)
- `gitnexus/test/unit/trace-cli.test.ts` — 5 unit tests (CLI wiring, parameter forwarding)

title: MCP `query` tool: `query` parameter not transmitted by Claude Code —rename parameter as workaround
body:
## Summary

  The `query` MCP tool's required parameter named `query` is consistently not transmitted when called from Claude Code
  (the most widely used MCP client). The server receives an empty `query` value and returns:

  "query parameter is required and cannot be empty."

  The same issue affects the `cypher` tool, which also has a required parameter named `query`.

  ## Verified: Server-side is correct

  Direct MCP protocol calls confirm the server handles `query` correctly —the parameter IS transmitted when bypassing
  Claude Code:

  | Call Method | `query` Param Received | Result |
  |-------------|----------------------|--------|
  | curl →remote HTTP MCP (`/api/mcp`) | ✅ Yes | ✅ Returns search results |
  | Node.js stdio →local MCP (`gitnexus mcp`) | ✅ Yes | ✅ Returns results |
  | Claude Code →MCP (stdio or HTTP via `mcp-remote`) | ❌ No | ❌ "query parameter is required and cannot be empty." |

  All tools with non-`query` parameter names work correctly from Claude Code:

  | Tool | Required Param | Works from Claude Code? |
  |------|---------------|------------------------|
  | `query` | `query` | ❌ |
  | `cypher` | `query` | ❌ |
  | `context` | `name` | ✅ |
  | `impact` | `target` | ✅ |
  | `rename` | `new_name` | ✅ |
  | `list_repos` | (none required) | ✅ |

  ## Root Cause

  The parameter name `query` conflicts with Claude Code's internal parameter handling. When Claude Code constructs MCP
  tool call arguments, the `query` key is dropped. This is reproducible across:

  - Local stdio MCP (tested with `gitnexus setup`)
  - Remote HTTP MCP via `mcp-remote` bridge
  - Multiple Claude Code versions (including latest)

  Since Claude Code is not open source, this cannot be reported upstream. The practical fix is on GitNexus's side.

  ## Suggested Fix

  Rename the affected parameters to avoid the conflict:

  - `query` tool: `query` →`search_query`
  - `cypher` tool: `query` →`statement`

  Files to update:
  - `gitnexus/src/mcp/tools.ts` —inputSchema definitions (lines 123, 217)
  - `gitnexus/src/mcp/local/local-backend.ts` —backend parameter references (lines 1282-1293, etc.)

  ## Impact

  The `query` tool is the primary semantic/hybrid search interface that relies on embeddings (`--embeddings` during
  `analyze`). Without it working from Claude Code, the entire embeddings investment (vector search + BM25 hybrid
  ranking) is inaccessible from the most popular MCP client, significantly reducing GitNexus's practical value.

  ## Environment

  - **GitNexus**: v1.6.7-rc.8
  - **Claude Code**: v2.1.175
  - **OS**: Windows 10
  - **MCP transport**: tested on both local stdio and remote HTTP

title: WebUI fails to load large projects (200K+ nodes) — fetchGraph() downloads entire graph with no pagination or skip   option
body:
## Problem

  When opening the WebUI for a project with a large number of nodes (e.g. 200K+), the browser hangs or crashes because
  `fetchGraph()` downloads **all** nodes and relationships via `/api/graph?stream=true` NDJSON in a single unpaginated
  request. There is no option to skip or partially load the graph.

  ### Steps to Reproduce

  1. Index a large repository (e.g. ~208K nodes, ~350K edges) with `gitnexus analyze`
  2. Open the WebUI and connect to the project
  3. The browser tab hangs —memory usage spikes as the full graph is deserialized into an in-memory `KnowledgeGraph`
  object

  ### Root Cause

  In `gitnexus-web/src/services/backend-client.ts`, `connectToServer()` calls `fetchGraph()` which streams the entire
  graph via NDJSON:

  GET /api/graph?stream=true →all nodes + all relationships

  The frontend then populates a `KnowledgeGraph` instance with every node and relationship —no pagination, no size
  limit, no skip option.

  ### Impact on AI Chat Users

  The WebUI's AI chat feature (7 tools: search, cypher, grep, read, overview, explore, impact) calls the **backend HTTP
  API** directly (`/api/query`, `/api/search`, `/api/grep`, `/api/file`) —it does **not** depend on the frontend
  in-memory `KnowledgeGraph`.

  This means users who primarily use AI chat are forced to wait for a full graph download they don't need, and for large
  projects the download never completes.

  ## Proposed Solution

  ### Option A: `skipGraph` parameter (minimal change)

  Add a `skipGraph` option to `connectToServer()` so the WebUI can connect to a project without downloading the graph:

  - `fetchGraph()` is skipped when `skipGraph: true`
  - `connectToServer()` returns `{ nodes: [], relationships: [], repoInfo }`
  - Graph-dependent visual features (canvas, citation highlighting) are gracefully disabled
  - AI chat and all backend-API-driven features continue to work normally

  This could be surfaced as:
  - A URL parameter: `?skipGraph=1`
  - A UI toggle: "Chat only (skip graph)" button on the repo selection screen
  - Auto-triggered when the backend reports the project exceeds a configurable node threshold (e.g. 50K)

  ### Option B: Graph pagination (more comprehensive)

  Add pagination to `/api/graph`:

  - `GET /api/graph?stream=true&offset=0&limit=50000` —stream only the first N nodes
  - Frontend loads incrementally or lazily as the user navigates
  - Requires both backend API changes and frontend refactoring

  ### Option C: Hybrid (recommended)

  Combine both approaches:

  - For users who want **chat only**: `skipGraph` for instant connection
  - For users who want **visualization**: paginated/lazy graph loading with a progress indicator
  - Auto-detect project size and suggest the appropriate mode

  ## Environment

  - GitNexus version: 1.6.8-rc.17
  - Project size: ~208K nodes, ~350K edges
  - Browser: Chrome (tab becomes unresponsive)
  - Deployment: Docker

  ## Related Files

  - `gitnexus-web/src/services/backend-client.ts` —`fetchGraph()`, `connectToServer()`
  - `gitnexus-web/src/App.tsx` —auto-connect flow
  - `gitnexus-web/src/components/DropZone.tsx` —repo selection and connection
  - `gitnexus-web/src/hooks/useAppState.tsx` —`switchRepo()`, state management

  ## Additional Context

  This issue also intersects with LMDB's default 16 GiB size limit (`GITNEXUS_LBUG_MAX_DB_SIZE`), which causes indexing
  failures for large projects at ~93% progress. That limit is configurable via env var, but the WebUI loading problem
  has no workaround today.

title: feat(taint): interprocedural taint via function summaries over resolved CALLS (#2084)
body:
## M4 — Interprocedural taint via function summaries over resolved CALLS (#2084) Completes **Epic A** (reliable taint analysis). M3 found source→sink flows only within one function; M4 makes taint reliable **across function and file boundaries** using the **functional/summary method** (Sharir-Pnueli; the production approach in Meta's Pysa/Mariana Trench and FB Infer — not full IFDS tabulation), composing per-function summaries over GitNexus's already-resolved `CALLS` graph. All opt-in behind `--pdg`; a default `analyze` run is **byte-identical** (golden parity gate holds). ## Architecture & data flow **Pipeline placement — the central seam.** Per-function summaries are harvested *in-phase* (while the worker-built CFG side channel is still live, alongside the M1–M3 emit), then the cross-function fixpoint runs in its *own* opt-in phase *after* scope-resolution — the first point where the complete, resolved `CALLS` graph exists in `ctx.graph`. ```mermaid flowchart TB subgraph W["Parse worker · --pdg only"] HV["TsHarvester
CFG + def/use + call-site facts"] end HV -. "ParsedFile.cfgSideChannel
(plain, structured-clone-safe)" .-> SR subgraph SR["scopeResolution phase · disk store LIVE (in-phase window)"] direction TB E1["L1 · emit BasicBlock + CFG"] E2["L2 · emit REACHING_DEF"] E3["L3 · emit TAINTED / SANITIZES (intra-procedural)"] U1["M4 · harvest per-function summaries
param→sink/return/callee-arg · source→… · callResults"] end SR -- "functionSummaries" --> OUT["ScopeResolutionOutput"] CALLS[("ctx.graph
resolved CALLS edges")] subgraph TS["taintSummaries phase · post-resolution · enabledWhen pdg===true"] direction TB FX["interproc fixpoint
interproc-solver.ts"] EM["emit TAINT_PATH
interproc-emit.ts · shared path-codec"] end OUT --> FX CALLS --> FX FX --> EM EM --> DB[("LadybugDB
TAINT_PATH edges")] DB --> EXP["MCP explain
interprocedural: true"] ``` **The fixpoint.** The unit of taint is `(function, parameter, source)` — a finite, monotone lattice, so the worklist converges without Tarjan SCC machinery (a recursive call just re-proposes a visited entry). The source discriminator prevents the multi-source collapse; `neutralized` carries sanitizer kills across boundaries (union along the path, intersect-and-re-fire on revisit so a less-sanitized second path is never lost). ```mermaid flowchart TD IN["summaries (by fnId) + CALLS adjacency
indexed callerId → calleeName → edges"] IN --> GR["genReturns fixpoint
seed: sourceToReturn · transitive: callResult dest:return"] IN --> S1["seed: source→callee-arg"] GR --> CR["compose callResults of generative callees"] CR -->|dest:sink| FIND CR -->|dest:callArg| S2["seed taint into toCallee.param"] S1 --> WL S2 --> WL WL["worklist · key = (fn, param, SOURCE)
neutralized: UNION along hops · INTERSECT + re-fire on revisit"] WL --> PROP["param→callee-arg ⇒ taint callee.param"] PROP --> WL WL --> SINK{"param→sink hit
AND kind ∉ neutralized?"} SINK -->|yes| FIND["record finding (deduped)"] SINK -->|no| WL FIND --> CAP["per-run cap maxFindings/maxEdges
⇒ TAINT_PATH edges"] ``` **Two worked cross-function flows** (the P1-1 generative composition and the P1-2 cross-boundary sanitizer): ```mermaid flowchart LR subgraph ex1["Generative source returned across a call (P1-1)"] direction LR gi["getInput()
return req.body
⇒ sourceToReturn"] --> hg["handleGen()
const t = getInput(); exec(t)
⇒ callResult dest:sink"] hg -.->|TAINT_PATH| res1["finding
getInput → handleGen
command-injection"] end subgraph ex2["Sanitizer on the cross-function path (P1-2)"] direction LR a2["A()
relay(req.body)"] --> r2["relay(x)
const y = escape(x); helper(y)
⇒ paramToCallArg neutralized:[cmd-inj]"] r2 --> h2["helper(z)
exec(z) ⇒ paramToSink cmd-inj"] h2 -.->|kind neutralized| res2["SUPPRESSED
(no false positive)"] end ``` ### What landed (one commit per unit) - **U2** — `FunctionSummary` model + deterministic version codec (`summary-model.ts`). - **U1** — in-phase per-function summary harvest (`summary-harvest.ts` + driver): param→return, param→callee-arg, param→sink, source→return, source→callee-arg, `callResults`, derived from the M2 reaching-def facts + M3 matched sites, keyed by resolved `Function`/`Method` node id, threaded out via `ScopeResolutionOutput`. - **U3/U4/U5** — the cycle-safe monotone fixpoint (`interproc-solver.ts`, Tarjan-free worklist over the finite `fn × param × source` lattice, **source-discriminated** state), `TAINT_PATH` materialization via the shared `path-codec` (`interproc-emit.ts`), and the first real opt-in registry phase (`enabledWhen: pdg`). - **U6** — incremental refresh: `TAINT_PATH` validity is a whole-program property (an A→C flow can be invalidated by an intermediate function on a third file), so it's delete-all-then-rebuild on incremental writeback, mirroring the proven Community/Process pattern. - **U7** — MCP `explain` renders cross-function findings (`interprocedural: true`, function-level hops); `TAINT_PATH` pinned out of `VALID_RELATION_TYPES`. - **U8** — `gitnexus-taint-analysis` expert skill (canonical + 2 byte-identical mirrors). - **U9** — cross-file end-to-end integration (one-hop + multi-hop), flag-off golden parity, bench `--check` unaffected. ### Tri-review hardening (all findings fixed — see [resolution comment](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/pull/2179#issuecomment-4689894915)) A multi-engine tri-review (Codex + Claude personas, critic-gated) surfaced 3 P1-class gaps the green suite missed plus 6 P2/P3 items; all are fixed, one commit each: - **P1** — armed the previously-unbounded production fixpoint cap (OOM risk on fan-in); threaded sanitizer exclusions across call-arg boundaries (cross-function false positive); composed generative `sourceToReturn` (a real missed-flow class) and corrected the misleading return docs. - **P2/P3** — `explain` count/truncation accuracy; abort-on-non-benign incremental delete (no duplicate edges); build the function-node index once; respect `maxHops` in seed paths; index call edges by callee name once; surface the same-named-callee caveat in the tool description. ### Validation `tsc` clean · 435 targeted unit + 26 integration tests green (incl. multi-hop + generative cross-file e2e, real-DB `explain`, flag-off byte-identical) · bench `--check` PASS (no fingerprint drift) · root prettier + eslint clean. ## Residual / deferred (documented, not silently dropped) Consistent with the plan's KTD trade-offs; all are sound over-/under-approximations surfaced via the `explain` note + the expert skill: - **Destructured/rest params** before a tainted simple param get a summary port index by binding ordinal, not formal-arg position → cross-function FN for that function. Documented + test-pinned; the precise fix needs a formal-param index threaded from the worker `BindingEntry` (a cache-namespace-affecting change). - **`paramToReturn` precision pass** is reserved — the M3 statement-level floor already covers its recall (the floor treats every call as propagate-through), so consuming it would only refine precision, deferred. - **Direct `exec(getInput())`** (a generative result passed straight into a modelled sink with no binding) is a documented limitation — the sink is occurrence-gated, so it reads as a plain call; the via-binding form (`const t = getInput(); exec(t)`) is the supported path. - **Same-named-callee over-attribution** — the context-insensitive name-join may attribute a flow to a same-named callee the taint didn't reach (sound over-report, never a missed flow); disclosed in the solver doc, the `explain` note, and the tool description. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: perf(hooks): replace the O(procs×fds) Linux db-lock scan with a cmdline-first sweep and drop the lsof fallback (proposal)
body:
## Area

Claude Code hooks (`gitnexus/hooks/claude/hook-db-lock-probe.cjs`) — Linux db-lock probe

## Context

#2163 → #2165 → #2169 contained the orphan storm: probe and augment subprocesses are now guarded, concurrency is slot-bounded, and a busy host can no longer snowball to 100% CPU. What those PRs deliberately did **not** change is the probe's detection algorithm — and on busy hosts it still cannot answer the question it exists for:

- `linuxProcScanFindGitNexusServer` walks `/proc/<pid>/fd/*` with `stat(2)` for **every process** — O(processes × fds). Measured on the incident-class host (~660 processes / ~18,300 fds): **~280 ms** for a full scan on an idle box, and a guaranteed `GITNEXUS_HOOK_LINUX_PROC_BUDGET_MS` (1200 ms) blowout under load.
- The `lsof` fallback then burns its full 1 s `spawnSync` budget (real `lsof` takes ~2 s there) and lands ETIMEDOUT → fail-closed.

Net effect on busy hosts: every Grep/Glob/Bash hook invocation spends ~2.2 s of CPU to conclude "couldn't tell" and skip the augment. The guards from #2165/#2169 make this safe; this proposal makes it *fast and correct*.

## Proposal: invert the scan — identify candidates by name first, stat only their fds

Rewrite `linuxProcScanFindGitNexusServer` (name kept) as a tri-state (`'owned' | 'not-owned' | 'timeout'`) three-phase scan:

1. **Phase 0 — `/proc/<pid>/comm`**: one tiny read per process (kernel serves it from `task->comm`, never touches the target's memory maps; microseconds each). Keep only processes whose comm could plausibly be a Node/gitnexus runner (`node`, `gitnexus`, `bun`, `npm`, …).
2. **Phase 1 — `/proc/<pid>/cmdline`** for survivors only, read via `openSync`+`readSync` capped at 4 KB (guards against D-state processes wedged on `mmap_lock` and against giant cmdlines). Prefilter with the existing `isGitNexusServerCommand`.
3. **Phase 2 — fd stat** for the 0–2 remaining candidates only: compare `dev`+`ino` against the lbug file, exactly as today.

Measured prototype on the same host: **34 ms (phase 0+1 full sweep) + 2 ms (candidate fd stat)** vs 280 ms today — comfortably inside the budget even under heavy load, with answers identical to `lsof`'s.

**Delete the Linux `lsof` fallback entirely.** `lsof` is itself just a procfs reader — it has no incremental detection power over the scan above, and after #2165 it only ever times out on the hosts where it would matter. (macOS keeps its `lsof`+`ps` path; Windows keeps Restart Manager. Linux-only change.)

## The one contract change (why this needs eyes before code)

Budget expiry currently returns `false` from the proc scan and falls through to `lsof`; post-change, `'timeout'` maps to **fail-closed** (treat as owned → skip augment), and the header fail-matrix gets rewritten accordingly. Two notes:

- On busy hosts the *end-to-end* semantics today are already fail-closed (via the lsof ETIMEDOUT arm) — the change removes the 1–2 s of wasted work, not the outcome. The hosts that genuinely change behavior are mid-load Linux boxes where the old fd-walk expired but `lsof` would have answered within 1 s: those now self-throttle (skip augment) instead. Overload self-throttling is precisely what the #2163 incident needed.
- While in there: fix the budget parsing bug — `Number(raw && String(raw).trim())` makes an explicit `"0"` fall back to 1200; proposed semantics `<= 0` → immediate `'timeout'`, which doubles as a deterministic test vector.

## Test plan / merge conditions

- New env `GITNEXUS_HOOK_PROC_ROOT` as a fake-procfs injection point; the test harness defaults to a fixture root so Linux unit tests stop sweeping the real `/proc`. Existing owner tests keep their assertions, only the injection changes; new `hook-db-lock-probe.test.ts` covers the edge cases and registers in the cross-platform suite.
- **Live e2e as a merge condition**: spawn a real `gitnexus mcp` (or a minimal real-lbug opener), wait for it to hold the lbug, assert the proc scan reports `owned`. Rationale: "the lbug handle is fd-visible" is an implementation property of `@ladybugdb/core` with zero CI protection today — a future switch to mmap-only I/O would silently blind the probe and regress #1492 with no red test. Cheap belt: also match candidates' `/proc/<pid>/maps` against the db path.
- Edge rulings (each pinned by a test): candidate's `/proc/<pid>/fd` unreadable (EACCES, cross-user server) → fail-closed `'owned'`, documented tradeoff; pathological hosts (tens of thousands of processes, ~1.5 s linear extrapolation) → `'timeout'` → fail-closed, documented boundary.

## Out of scope / related follow-ups (separate items)

- TTL cache for probe results (the other half of the perf story; tri-state-aware — `timeout` results must be cacheable since that's the load-shedding path).
- Cursor integration probe (it installs no probe sibling today; #2169 left its augment unwrapped for the same reason).
- Guard self-test does not verify group-kill capability (busybox `timeout` passes the exit-propagation test but cannot reap an npx grandchild — noted in #2169's review).
- `isGitNexusServerCommand` dev-checkout blind spot (`node …/gitnexus/dist/cli/index.js mcp` doesn't match; pre-existing, affects old and new scan equally).

Happy to implement this (same flow as #2165/#2169) once the direction — particularly the fail-closed-on-timeout mapping and the lsof-fallback removal — has maintainer sign-off.

title: chore(deps)(deps-dev): bump esbuild from 0.28.0 to 0.28.1 in /gitnexus
body:
Bumps [esbuild](https://github.com/evanw/esbuild) from 0.28.0 to 0.28.1.
Release notes

Sourced from esbuild's releases.

v0.28.1

  • Disallow \ in local development server HTTP requests (GHSA-g7r4-m6w7-qqqr)

    This release fixes a security issue where HTTP requests to esbuild's local development server could traverse outside of the serve directory on Windows using a \ backslash character. It happened due to the use of Go's path.Clean() function, which only handles Unix-style / characters. HTTP requests with paths containing \ are no longer allowed.

    Thanks to @​dellalibera for reporting this issue.

  • Add integrity checks to the Deno API (GHSA-gv7w-rqvm-qjhr)

    The previous release of esbuild added integrity checks to esbuild's npm install script. This release also adds integrity checks to esbuild's Deno install script. Now esbuild's Deno API will also fail with an error if the downloaded esbuild binary contains something other than the expected content.

    Note that esbuild's Deno API installs from registry.npmjs.org by default, but allows the NPM_CONFIG_REGISTRY environment variable to override this with a custom package registry. This change means that the esbuild executable served by NPM_CONFIG_REGISTRY must now match the expected content.

    Thanks to @​sondt99 for reporting this issue.

  • Avoid inlining using and await using declarations (#4482)

    Previously esbuild's minifier sometimes incorrectly inlined using and await using declarations into subsequent uses of that declaration, which then fails to dispose of the resource correctly. This bug happened because inlining was done for let and const declarations by avoiding doing it for var declarations, which no longer worked when more declaration types were added. Here's an example:

    // Original code
{
  using x = new Resource()
  x.activate()
}

    // Old output (with --minify)
    
new Resource().activate();
    

    // New output (with --minify)
    
{using e=new Resource;e.activate()}

  • Fix module evaluation when an error is thrown (#4461, #4467)

    If an error is thrown during module evaluation, esbuild previously didn't preserve the state of the module for subsequent module references. This was observable if import() or require() is used to import a module multiple times. The thrown error is supposed to be thrown by every call to import() or require(), not just the first. With this release, esbuild will now throw the same error every time you call import() or require() on a module that throws during its evaluation.

  • Fix some edge cases around the new operator (#4477)

    Previously esbuild incorrectly printed certain edge cases involving complex expressions inside the target of a new expression (specifically an optional chain and/or a tagged template literal). The generated code for the new target was not correctly wrapped with parentheses, and either contained a syntax error or had different semantics. These edge cases have been fixed so that they now correctly wrap the new target in parentheses. Here is an example of some affected code:

    // Original code
new (foo()`bar`)()
new (foo()?.bar)()

    // Old output
    
new foo()bar();
    
new (foo())?.bar();

title: perf(hooks): cmdline-first Linux db-lock scan, drop the lsof fallback (#2180)
body:
## Summary

Replaces the O(processes × fds) Linux db-lock scan with a comm→cmdline→fd three-phase sweep and removes the Linux `lsof` fallback, as proposed in #2180. On a busy host the old scan blew its budget and fell through to `lsof` (~2 s → ETIMEDOUT → fail-closed); every Grep/Glob/Bash hook spent ~2 s of CPU to conclude "couldn't tell." macOS (`lsof`+`ps`) and Windows (Restart Manager) paths are untouched.

Closes #2180. Final piece of the #2163 follow-up list (cmdline-first scan); the probe-result TTL cache and cursor-probe items remain separate future work.

Measured on a 583-process host with 6 background `gitnexus mcp` servers: **owner detection 6–12 ms, was ~1216 ms + lsof timeout (~100×)**.

## Areas touched

- [x] `gitnexus/` (CLI / core / MCP server) — hooks + tests only
- [ ] others

Also `gitnexus-claude-plugin/hooks/` (byte-identical probe copy).

## What changed

- `linuxProcScanFindGitNexusServer` (name kept — source-pinned; return type now tri-state `'owned' | 'not-owned' | 'timeout'`):
  - **Phase 0** — `/proc/<pid>/comm` prefilter. Kernel `task->comm`, never touches the target's memory maps, so it can't wedge on a D-state process's `mmap_lock`. Truncation-safe whitelist match (comm is capped at 15 visible chars).
  - **Phase 1** — bounded `/proc/<pid>/cmdline` read (`openSync`+`readSync`, default 16 KiB, floor 4 KiB, bounded escalation to a hard ceiling) for survivors only, prefiltered by `isGitNexusServerCommand`.
  - **Phase 2** — `dev`+`ino` fd match for the 0–2 remaining candidates only.
- Dispatch: `'owned'` and `'timeout'` → `true`; `'not-owned'` → `false`. **The Linux `lsof` fallback is removed.**
- Budget parse fix: the old `Number(raw && trim()) ? … : 1200` treated `"0"` as falsy and fell back to 1200; now parse-then-validate, with `<= 0` an explicit immediate timeout (also a deterministic test vector).
- `GITNEXUS_HOOK_PROC_ROOT` (default `/proc`, unset ⇒ zero behavior change) so the Linux scan is unit-testable against a fixture procfs instead of the host's real `/proc`.

## Two tradeoffs worth your eyes

**1. `timeout` → fail-closed (the one contract change).** Budget expiry now maps to "treat as owned, skip augment" instead of falling through to `lsof`. End-to-end on busy hosts this is unchanged — the old `lsof` arm also fail-closed there (ETIMEDOUT), just 2 s slower and spawning the orphan this whole #2163 line was about. The hosts that *change* are mid-load Linux boxes where the old fd-walk expired but `lsof` would have answered within 1 s: those now self-throttle (skip that augment) rather than spend the time. With the 1200 ms default and 6–12 ms typical scans there's ~100× headroom, so only genuinely overloaded (incident-class) hosts reach it — which is exactly where self-throttling is wanted.

**2. Phase 0 comm whitelist is calibrated to `@ladybugdb/core`.** Empirically, a real `gitnexus mcp` server reports `comm = MainThread` (its `worker_threads` setup renames the main thread), **not** `node` — so `MainThread` is whitelisted alongside the launcher basenames; omitting it would blind the probe to every server (#1492-class owner miss). The match is bidirectional-prefix (truncation-safe) and Phase 0 is deliberately over-collecting (a stray candidate only costs one bounded cmdline read; Phase 2's `dev`+`ino` is the authority). The residual: if a future `@ladybugdb`/Node build renames that thread to something whose 15-char prefix matches no whitelist entry, Phase 0 would filter real servers out cheaply and the live e2e (which runs the current build) wouldn't catch it. Documented at the whitelist with a maintenance note; flagging here because it couples this probe to a dependency's thread naming. If you'd prefer a comm-independent prefilter (e.g. read cmdline for all procs — the measured full sweep is still ~34 ms — at the cost of touching unrelated procs' mm), that's a design call I'm happy to take either way.

## Testing & verification

- [x] `cd gitnexus && npx vitest run test/unit/hook-db-lock-probe.test.ts test/unit/hooks.test.ts` — 165 passed, 0 failed (the relaned lsof suites skip on Linux)
- [x] new `hook-db-lock-probe.test.ts` drives all three phases against a fake procfs: comm-truncation safety, Phase 0 trap (cmdline looks like a server but comm doesn't → filtered), 4 KiB-boundary owner-miss guard, `budget=0` immediate timeout, EACCES → fail-closed
- [x] **live-`/proc` e2e** pins the "lbug handle is fd-visible" property of `@ladybugdb` against a real subprocess holder, asserting only on the holder we spawned (background servers on the host can't false-positive a fresh temp lbug)
- [x] `resolve-invocation` / `setup` / `cli-commands` / `antigravity-hook-e2e` — green
- [x] probe copies `diff -q` byte-identical; `windowsHide` parity holds (no new spawns)
- [x] budget-parse red/green: base treats `"0"` as 1200; fixed → immediate timeout

**D5 — relaned lsof tests (the delicate bit).** On this incident-class host the two pre-existing `#1493` "ENOENT lsof → fail-open" tests were already red on base (real `lsof` exceeds its 1 s budget → ETIMEDOUT → fail-closed). Since Linux no longer takes the `lsof` path, the `lsof`/`ps` owner-detection suites are relaned to macOS (assertions unchanged, still guarding the path where it's live), and the `lsof` orphan-reaping suite is removed with a rationale note (no `lsof` is spawned on Linux now; wrapper-reaping stays covered by the augment-reaping suites and the macOS lsof lane). All Linux owner-detection correctness moved to the fake-procfs tests above.

title: fix(web): chat-only mode for large projects to prevent WebUI hang (#2178)
body:
## What & why

The WebUI hangs or crashes when opening a large project (~200K+ nodes). `connectToServer()` unconditionally streams the **entire** knowledge graph (`/api/graph?stream=true`, all nodes + relationships) into an in-memory `KnowledgeGraph` before the UI becomes usable. Users who only need the AI chat — which talks to the backend HTTP API directly (`/api/query`, `/api/search`, `/api/grep`, `/api/file`) and never reads the in-memory graph — are forced through a download that never completes at this scale.

This adds a **chat-only / skip-graph connection mode** with **size-based auto-detection**, so large projects connect instantly without materializing the graph, while small/medium projects keep the full visualization unchanged.

Fixes #2178.

## Approach

Frontend-only — **no backend or API contract change**. The size data needed for the decision is already returned by `/api/repo` (`stats.nodes`, `stats.edges`) and fetched *before* the graph download, so auto-detection costs zero extra round-trips.

- **Auto-detect by size**: the graph download is skipped when a repo's node count exceeds `LARGE_GRAPH_NODE_THRESHOLD` (default **25,000**) **or** its edge count exceeds `LARGE_GRAPH_EDGE_THRESHOLD` (default **50,000**). Edges matter because the browser force-layout cliff is edge-driven and GitNexus graphs carry more edges than nodes — an edge-heavy/node-light repo can still hang. Both are overridable via `window.__GITNEXUS_CONFIG__`.
- **Explicit control**: `?skipGraph=1` forces chat-only, `?skipGraph=0` forces a full download. It is a **bookmark hint honored by the initial auto-connect** for the bookmarked project; in-session repo changes (switch, analyze, landing-screen select) make a fresh per-repo auto-detect decision so a stale override can't leak onto a different repo.
- **Graceful degradation**: chat-only uses an empty-but-non-null `KnowledgeGraph` so every existing `graph?.` consumer keeps working; a `graphMode` flag drives a clear empty-state notice instead of a blank canvas, and suppresses the misleading "0 nodes / 0 edges" stats.
- **Escape hatch**: a "Load graph anyway" button loads the full graph on demand (session-scoped, in-flight-guarded), gated by a fail-safe size-warning confirmation that fires whenever the size is large *or* unknown.

## Key changes

- `decideSkipGraph` / `parseSkipGraphParam` / `shouldConfirmGraphLoad` pure helpers + `LARGE_GRAPH_NODE_THRESHOLD` / `LARGE_GRAPH_EDGE_THRESHOLD` constants
- `connectToServer` skips `fetchGraph` and reports `graphSkipped` (the `fetchGraph` primitive is untouched)
- `graphMode` + `chatOnlyNodeCount` app state; shared `buildGraphFromConnectResult` helper used by all connect entry points
- GraphCanvas chat-only empty state + "Load graph anyway" escape hatch + en/zh-CN i18n; Header/StatusBar hide stats in chat-only mode

## Why graph-skip is safe for chat

The AI chat agent's tools call the backend HTTP API directly and never touch the in-memory graph (verified in `core/llm/tools.ts` and `core/llm/context-builder.ts`, which run over `/api/query`). The one documented degradation in chat-only mode: inline AI *node/file citations* won't auto-pin to the Code panel (the agent can still reference files in chat text) — surfaced to the user in the empty-state notice.

## Scope / deferred

- **Deferred**: full graph pagination / lazy incremental rendering (issue Option B). Rendering 200K+ nodes in a browser sigma canvas isn't viable regardless of how it's downloaded, so chat-only is the correct resolution for very large repos.
- **Out of scope**: the LMDB 16 GiB limit (`GITNEXUS_LBUG_MAX_DB_SIZE`) noted in the issue — an indexing concern, already env-configurable.

## Testing

- Unit + component tests for `decideSkipGraph` (node + edge + boundary + fail-open), `parseSkipGraphParam`, `shouldConfirmGraphLoad`, `connectToServer` skip cases (node-, edge-, explicit-, and stats-absent), `graphMode` state, `switchRepo` auto-detect, `loadGraphAnyway` (success, error, in-flight guard), threshold config overrides, i18n key parity.
- Full `gitnexus-web` suite: **339 tests passing**; `tsc -b --noEmit` clean; eslint 0 errors; prettier clean.

## Review history

This branch went through two review passes:

1. **Single-lane `ce-code-review` (autofix)** — applied the fail-safe load-anyway confirm + authoritative node count, the `loadGraphAnyway` in-flight guard, and the DRY `buildGraphFromConnectResult` helper.
2. **Multi-engine tri-review** (GitNexus risk/test lanes + CE correctness/adversarial/performance/maintainability/react-races personas; Codex lane was unavailable, so this was a two-method, both-Claude review). It caught that pass-1's `?skipGraph` design had introduced a regression. All findings below were fixed in this PR.

### Tri-review findings (all addressed)

- **P1 — cross-repo / F5 chat-only leak (re-introduced the #2178 hang).** Pass-1 persisted `?skipGraph=0` in the URL and threaded `?skipGraph` into every entry point; only `switchRepo` cleared it, so connecting to a *different* large repo (or pressing F5) inherited `skipGraph=false`, bypassed auto-detect, and re-downloaded the full graph. **Fixed:** `?skipGraph` is now a bookmark hint for the initial auto-connect only; `loadGraphAnyway` no longer persists it; in-session entry points auto-detect.
- **P2 (performance) — node-only threshold missed the edge cliff.** **Fixed:** auto-detect now also skips on `stats.edges` (default 50K).
- **P2 — failed `switchRepo` left a stale chat-only overlay.** **Fixed:** `graphMode`/`chatOnlyNodeCount` reset at the top of `switchRepo`.
- **P2 — `serverBaseUrl` set after `handleServerConnect` made "Load graph anyway" briefly a no-op.** **Fixed:** reordered.
- **P2 — misleading "0 nodes / 0 edges" shown for large repos in chat-only mode.** **Fixed:** Header/StatusBar suppress stats in chat-only.
- **P2 — GraphCanvas layout effect ran on the empty chat-only graph.** **Fixed:** added a `graphMode` guard.

### Residual findings — now resolved (one commit per fix)

Planned via `ce-plan` (deepened) and executed via `ce-work`:

- **P2 — agent unaware of chat-only mode** → **Fixed** (`fix(web): make the AI agent and chat surface aware of chat-only mode`). A `chatOnly` flag threads through `initializeAgent → createGraphRAGAgent → buildDynamicSystemPrompt` (resolved as `opts.chatOnly ?? graphModeRef`, so every init site — including lazy/settings re-inits — is correct); the system prompt drops the graph-citation claim and a RightPanel banner shows the degradation where AI output renders. The agent re-inits after "Load graph anyway".
- **P3 — `loadGraphAnyway` not cancellable / unmount-unsafe** → **Fixed** (`fix(web): make Load-graph-anyway cancellable, unmount-safe, fail-safe confirm`). AbortController + mounted-ref guards (keyed on the ref, since an abort surfaces as a `BackendError`), a stale-result guard against a concurrent `switchRepo`, and a confirm that fails **safe** when `window.confirm` is unavailable/throws.
- **P3 — auto-detect fails open with no size stats** → **Fixed** (`fix(web): streaming circuit breaker for graphs with missing size stats`). A mid-stream breaker (`GraphTooLargeError`) enforces the existing node/edge thresholds while parsing NDJSON and falls into chat-only — backstopping the absent-`stats` case without a new magic constant. Disabled for explicit "load anyway".

(The deferred items remain the pre-existing cross-cutting `AbortSignal` gap on `switchRepo`/auto-connect and full graph pagination — see Scope / deferred.)

title: fix(mcp): rename query/cypher params so Claude Code can call them
body:
## Summary

From Claude Code — the most widely used MCP client — `query(...)` and `cypher(...)` were unusable: every call came back with `"query parameter is required and cannot be empty."`, even with a query supplied. Claude Code silently drops a tool-call argument whose key is exactly `query`, so the server received an empty value. Every other GitNexus tool worked, because their required params are named `name` / `target` / `new_name`. The net effect: the entire embeddings + hybrid-search investment was inaccessible from Claude Code.

This renames the advertised parameters to names the client actually transmits — **`search_query`** for the `query` tool and **`statement`** for the `cypher` tool — while the handlers still accept the legacy **`query`** key. Claude Code works now; nothing else breaks.

We can't patch Claude Code (closed source), and the reporter already proved non-`query` names transmit fine, so renaming away from `query` is the fix regardless of the upstream cause.

## What changed

- **Schema** (`gitnexus/src/mcp/tools.ts`): `query` tool advertises `search_query` (required); `cypher` tool advertises `statement` (required). The legacy `query` key is intentionally **not** re-advertised as a property — doing so would re-trigger the exact Claude Code arg-drop. It lives in the field `description` instead.
- **Handlers** (`gitnexus/src/mcp/local/local-backend.ts`): the search text / statement is resolved as `search_query ?? query` and `statement ?? query` at every consumer site — the local handler, the legacy `search` alias, and the cross-repo `@group` forward — so precedence is uniform (**new name wins**) with no hidden param mutation. Both MCP transports (stdio and HTTP `/api/mcp`) share this one backend, so the behavior change is a single chokepoint. `cypher()` now also returns the same friendly required-param error as `query()` instead of a raw DB error.
- **CLI** (`gitnexus/src/cli/tool.ts`): passes the canonical names (user-facing positional args unchanged).
- **Agent-facing docs**: the three example generators (`ai-context.ts`, `skill-gen.ts`, `resources.ts`) and all committed skill mirrors (canonical `gitnexus/skills/*`, `.claude/skills`, the Claude plugin + Cursor distributions, `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, READMEs) now show `query({search_query: ...})` so an agent following them emits the working key.

## Backward compatibility

Strict superset of today's behavior. The advertised `required` array is advisory — the server runs no JSON-schema validation, the handler does its own check — so existing callers that send `query` (curl/HTTP, other MCP clients, the CLI, the cross-repo group path, and the internal `executeCypher`) keep working unchanged. When both keys are supplied, the new name wins.

## Testing

- Unit `calltool-dispatch` (137): new name works, legacy `query` still works, precedence is new-wins, the `@group` forward resolves the alias, the `search` alias accepts `search_query`, empty/whitespace errors, and `cypher` empty-statement returns the friendly error.
- Integration `local-backend-calltool` (31): `search_query` and `statement` exercised end-to-end against a real index.
- Generator suites assert the new example form is present and the old `query({query:` form is gone.
- `tsc`, prettier, and eslint clean.

## Notes for reviewers

- The web REST endpoints `/api/search` and `/api/query` keep their own parameter names and are independent of this MCP rename — no change there.
- `gitnexus/CHANGELOG.md` is intentionally untouched (release-owned).

## Post-deploy monitoring

No additional operational monitoring required — this is an MCP request-shape change with no runtime/infra impact. Confirmation is simply that `query`/`cypher` calls from Claude Code now succeed with the new param names; backward compatibility is guarded by the unchanged legacy-key tests staying green.

Fixes #2175

title: fix(ci): align tree-sitter readiness + grammar-update workflows on a shared manifest (#858)
body:
## What & why

Fixes the **question marks** in the tree-sitter 0.25 upgrade-readiness report (issue #858) and **aligns the two tree-sitter workflows** so they can't drift apart again.

`tree-sitter-upgrade-readiness.yml` (daily report → issue #858) and `grammar-update-monitor.yml` (weekly vendored-grammar auto-PR bot) each hardcoded their own, divergent notion of *which grammars are vendored*. Because of that, the readiness report misclassified all 5 genuinely-vendored grammars (`tree-sitter-c/swift/kotlin/dart/proto`) as npm-installed — they aren't in `package.json` at all — routed them through the npm peer-dep path, and rendered:

- bare `?` for **ABI** (read from an empty `node_modules`),
- `? (fetch failed)` for github-only `tree-sitter-proto` (it has no npm package),
- an unintrospectable `?` upstream-ABI for `tree-sitter-swift`.

Every one of those 5 grammars is in fact checked into `gitnexus/vendor/<name>/src/parser.c` at **ABI 14** — the data the report needed was already in the repo; the script was looking in the wrong place.

## The fix

A single shared manifest — **`.github/vendored-grammars.json`** — is now the source of truth for the vendored **set** + per-grammar policy **holds**. Both scripts read it:

- `update-vendored-grammars.mjs` builds its `GRAMMARS` from the manifest (behavior-preserving — identical exported shape).
- `check-tree-sitter-upgrade-readiness.py` classifies a grammar as vendored by **manifest membership** (not the old `is_vendored_pin` package.json heuristic), reads its ABI from `gitnexus/vendor/<name>/src/parser.c`, skips the npm peer-dep fetch for github-only vendored grammars, surfaces the `tree-sitter-c` hold (held, not "Ready"), and renders **labeled tokens instead of any bare `?`**.

A consistency-guard test asserts the manifest set equals the physical `gitnexus/vendor/tree-sitter-*` directories, so vendoring a 6th grammar without updating the manifest fails CI.

### Readiness matrix — before → after

| Grammar | before (ABI / status) | after |
|---|---|---|
| `tree-sitter-c` | `?` / Intentionally pinned | `14` / **Vendored — held** |
| `tree-sitter-dart` | `?` / Ready | `14` / Vendored (ABI in target range) |
| `tree-sitter-kotlin` | `?` / Blocking | `14` / Vendored (ABI in target range) |
| `tree-sitter-proto` | `?` / **Unknown (fetch failed)** | `14` / Vendored (ABI in target range) |
| `tree-sitter-swift` | `?` / Blocking | `14` (upstream `n/a`) / Vendored (ABI in target range) |

The report now contains **zero bare `?`**, the "Could not check" bucket is gone, and `--assert-current` (the offline #1922 ABI gate) now covers the 5 vendored grammars instead of silently skipping them.

## Changes

- `.github/vendored-grammars.json` *(new)* — shared manifest.
- `.github/scripts/check-tree-sitter-upgrade-readiness.py` — manifest-based vendored classification; no bare `?`; hold surfacing; `--assert-current` coverage.
- `.github/scripts/update-vendored-grammars.mjs` — builds `GRAMMARS` from the manifest.
- `.github/scripts/test_check_tree_sitter_upgrade_readiness.py` *(new)* — stdlib `unittest` suite incl. the consistency guard (11 tests).
- `gitnexus/test/unit/grammar-update-monitor.test.ts` — manifest-agreement tests.
- `.github/workflows/{tree-sitter-upgrade-readiness,grammar-update-monitor}.yml` — header docs; readiness workflow gains a manifest PR-path trigger and runs the unit tests on validation events.
- `CONTRIBUTING.md` — documents the manifest contract.

## Test plan

- `python3 -m unittest test_check_tree_sitter_upgrade_readiness` → 11 pass (incl. consistency guard, verified load-bearing).
- `python3 check-tree-sitter-upgrade-readiness.py` → matrix has **zero** bare `?`.
- `python3 check-tree-sitter-upgrade-readiness.py --assert-current` → all 15 grammars in range.
- `vitest grammar-update-monitor.test.ts` → 8 pass.
- Both workflow YAMLs pass `check-workflow-concurrency.py`.

> Note: `gitnexus/CHANGELOG.md` is intentionally untouched (release-owned).

## Reliable testing (offline / dry-run)

Both scripts hit live npm/GitHub, which made the daily report flaky and the monitor's `detect`/`apply` logic untestable. Added hermetic seams so the network-dependent paths run deterministically in CI:

- **Readiness `--offline`** (or `GITNEXUS_TS_READINESS_OFFLINE=1`) no-ops the npm + upstream fetches; the report renders from local data only (vendored ABIs from the repo, npm columns labeled `offline`, still zero bare `?`). 3 tests assert an offline run touches **zero** network (`urlopen` patched to raise).
- **Monitor `detect()`/`apply()`** accept injected deps (`vendoredVersion`/`resolveUpstream`/`fetchSource`/`readAbi`) so the load-bearing newer/ABI/hold gating runs offline against fixtures; `apply` gains `--dry-run` (resolves + ABI-validates but writes nothing). 6 tests cover newer / same-version / held-`c` / ABI-15-refused / applicable + a no-mutation dry-run.

Test count: **14 Python** (`unittest`, stdlib-only) + **14 vitest** monitor tests, all hermetic.

## Review Findings — all resolved

A multi-persona tri-review (GitNexus risk/test-CI/security-boundary + Compound-Engineering correctness/adversarial/maintainability/testing; Codex unavailable) plus posted CodeQL + autofix-bot comments found **no P0/P1 security or correctness defects**. Every finding — the high-severity ones (the `--assert-current` network regression, sentinel inconsistency, stale docstrings) and all the deferred ones — has now been fixed, **one commit per finding**:

| Commit | Finding |
|---|---|
