title: feat(pdg): control dependence — post-dominators + CDG (Ferrante) [M5 #2085]
body:
## What

Implements **M5 of the PDG subsystem — control dependence** (Epic B). Adds the last PDG layer on top of the existing CFG (M1) + REACHING_DEF (M2) substrate: post-dominators and a Ferrante control-dependence graph, emitting `CDG {label:'T'|'F'}` edges between `BasicBlock` nodes. This makes *"under what condition does block X execute?"* answerable via Cypher — the foundation for guard-clause subsumption and `pdg_query` (deferred to #2086).

Closes #2085. Part of Epic B #2088.

## How

Two pure, deterministic modules over the existing per-function `FunctionCfg`, mirroring the M1/M2 idioms in the same `cfg/` module:

- **`cfg/post-dominators.ts`** — `computePostDominators` builds the immediate-post-dominator tree via **Cooper–Harvey–Kennedy iterative dominators** on the EXIT-rooted reverse CFG. Blocks that cannot reach EXIT (exit-less loops) get `ipdom = NO_IPDOM` and are handled as a sound over-approximation (KTD5). `postDominates(tree, p, b)` climbs the tree.
- **`cfg/control-dependence.ts`** — `computeControlDependence` applies Ferrante §3.1.1: for each CFG edge `(A,B)` where `B` does **not** post-dominate `A`, every block on the post-dom path from `B` up to (excl.) `ipdom(A)` is control-dependent on `A`. The branch sense (`'T'`/`'F'`) rides the relation `reason` column (mirroring how CFG stores its edge kind).
- **`cfg/emit.ts`** — `emitFileCdg` persists the deduped, budgeted CDG projection (+ optional `POST_DOMINATE` debug edges behind `GITNEXUS_PDG_EMIT_POST_DOMINATE`), mirroring `emitFileReachingDefs`.
- **Wiring** — emitted **in-phase** in `scope-resolution/pipeline/run.ts` right after REACHING_DEF, behind the existing `--pdg` opt-in. Off by default ⇒ byte-identical graph. (The issue's "`pipeline-phases/cdg.ts`" subtask predates this in-phase architecture, which M1/M2 established because the worker-built `cfgSideChannel` is only live in this window.)
- **Schema** — adds `CDG` + `POST_DOMINATE` to the shared `RelationshipType` union and `REL_TYPES`; the `CodeRelation` DDL already has `FROM BasicBlock TO BasicBlock` (no new pair). Both stay **out** of `VALID_RELATION_TYPES` (same posture as the taint substrate edges).
- **Incremental safety** — `pdgMaxCdgEdgesPerFunction` is folded into the `RepoMeta.pdg` stamp, so the key-union `pdgModeMismatch` forces a full writeback for any repo already `--pdg`-indexed before CDG existed (the #2099 F1 mechanism). No worker / parse-cache `SCHEMA_BUMP` — CDG is a pure emit-time projection.

## Testing

- **Unit:** `post-dominators.test.ts` (linear/diamond/loop/multi-return/exit-less/single-block/determinism), `control-dependence.test.ts` (diamond, guard-clause, loop self-edge, switch, exit-less-loop, + an **AC2 property test** cross-checking the tree-walk against an independent brute-force reference across 6 topologies), `emit-guard`/`cfg-emit` CDG cases (cap, dedup, `POST_DOMINATE` env gate), `schema.test.ts` + `security.test.ts` edge-type pins.
- **Integration:** `cdg-snapshot.test.ts` (AC1 committed snapshot on the shared `ten-functions.ts` fixture), `pipeline-pdg.test.ts` (AC3 — real `--pdg` analyze emits CDG, default emits none, "what controls block X" is answerable), `basicblock-roundtrip.test.ts` (CDG/POST_DOMINATE bulk-COPY round-trip), `pdg-mode-flip.test.ts` (CDG-cap stamp upgrade forces full writeback).
- Full CFG/PDG/schema/taint surface green (290 tests); `tsc` clean both packages. `gitnexus/CHANGELOG.md` untouched (release-owned).

## Scope boundaries

Deferred to #2086 (guard-clause subsumption + `pdg_query`): the `pdg_query` MCP tool, `impact`/`context` CDG traversal, per-case `switch` arm value labels (M5 ships binary `T`/`F`), and the schema-resource/ARCHITECTURE docs refresh. CDG for languages beyond TS/JS is a per-`cfgVisitor` follow-up (the algorithm is language-agnostic and reused as-is).

## Review

Reviewed via multi-agent code review (correctness, adversarial, testing, maintainability, project-standards, api-contract, performance, agent-native, learnings). **No P0/P1 findings.** Adversarial fuzzed 500k+ pathological CFGs (no divergence/hang/out-of-bounds); performance found no super-linear traps; project-standards clean (no language-naming violation, schema parity correct). Four `safe_auto` fixes were applied in the `fix(review)` commit (explicit `VALID_RELATION_TYPES` exclusion pins, POST_DOMINATE forward-compat doc note, a KTD5 exit-less-loop CDG test, and the `'true'` env-string branch).

## Residual Review Findings

Non-blocking follow-ups surfaced during review (all P2/P3; recorded here for visibility):

- **P2** `gitnexus/test/unit/cfg/post-dominators.test.ts` — the `mkCfg` test helper is duplicated across the two new CFG unit test files (a third variant exists in `reaching-defs.test.ts`); extract a shared `cfg` test-builder. _(maintainability, conf 100)_
- **P2** `gitnexus-shared/src/lbug/schema-constants.ts` — `POST_DOMINATE` is debug-only yet a permanent `REL_TYPES`/`RelationshipType` member; decide keep-as-schema vs out-of-band, and filter `POST_DOMINATE` rows at the MCP/web query surfaces when the debug env is set. (Partly mitigated by a doc note this PR adds.) _(maintainability + api-contract + adversarial, conf 75)_
- **P3** `gitnexus/src/mcp/resources.ts` — `getSchemaResource()` omits CDG/`BasicBlock` (and the whole PDG substrate) from the schema agents read before authoring Cypher; explicitly deferred to #2086 per plan scope. _(agent-native)_
- **P3** `gitnexus/src/core/ingestion/scope-resolution/pipeline/run.ts` — the in-phase PDG block (~200 lines) sits in a >1000-line `run.ts`; extract a `runPdgEmitForFile` helper (pre-existing, grows each milestone). _(maintainability)_
- **P3** `bench/cfg` — add a deeply-nested CDG benchmark fixture for wall-time regression safety. _(performance + learnings)_

Advisory (no action): CDG over-approximates on exit-unreachable regions (sound — never drops a real edge; does not arise for the TS visitor since EXIT stays reverse-reachable); `branchSense` returns `'T'` for an unknown edge kind that passes `isEmitSafeCfg` (defense-in-depth — kinds come from the trusted CFG builder).

title: GitNexus Group Sync: LRU Pool Eviction Causes "LadybugDB Not Initialized" During Manifest Extraction
body:
### Area

gitnexus (CLI / core / indexing / MCP server)

### Summary

GitNexus group sync (`gitnexus group sync`) iterates over all repos in a group, calling `initLbug(poolId, lbugPath)` for each. The pool adapter (`pool-adapter.js`) has a hard-coded `MAX_POOL_SIZE = 5` with LRU eviction — when the 6th repo is initialized, the least-recently-used repo is evicted from the pool via `closeOne()`, which calls `pool.delete(repoId)`.

The executor closures stored in `dbExecutors` survive the eviction — they capture `poolId` in a closure and have no knowledge that the underlying pool entry is gone. When manifest extraction runs after the init loop, it calls these stale executors. `executeParameterized(poolId, ...)` does `pool.get(repoId)` → returns `undefined` → throws `"LadybugDB not initialized for repo X. Call initLbug first."`

The manifest extractor catches the error per-link (logging a warning at level 40) and falls back to a synthetic UID (`manifest::<repo>::<contractId>`). Cross-links are still generated but cannot anchor to real graph symbols, rendering cross-repo impact analysis through manifest-declared contracts non-functional.

### Context

_No response_

### Expected behavior

When `gitnexus group sync marketplace` runs with > 10 repos and > 24 manifest links:
```
{"level":40,"msg":"[manifest-extractor] resolveSymbol failed for http:GET::/api/endpoint in <repo>: LadybugDB not initialized for repo \"<repo>\". Call initLbug first."}
{"level":40,"msg":"[manifest-extractor] resolveSymbol failed for http:GET::/api/endpoint in <repo>: LadybugDB not initialized for repo \"<repo>\". Call initLbug first."}
... (14 total warnings)
```

1. All repos initialize their LadybugDB pools during the per-repo extraction loop.
2. Manifest extraction resolves each link's provider/consumer symbols against the real graph (via Cypher queries to find `HANDLES_ROUTE` relationships, etc.).
3. Cross-links carry real `symbolUid` values from the graph — enabling downstream cross-repo impact analysis to trace through manifest-declared contracts.
4. No "LadybugDB not initialized" warnings appear in the log.

### Actual behavior

Repos 1–5 are LRU-evicted as repos 6–10 are initialized. Their executors become stale. Manifest extraction produces 14 warnings:

All 24 cross-links are generated but with synthetic UIDs instead of real graph symbol references:

```
manifest: 24 cross-links from 24 links (24 declared + 0 discovered)
```

### Steps to reproduce

1. Create a group with more than 5 repos and at least one manifest link referencing one of the first 5 repos:

   ```yaml
   # group.yaml
   version: 1
   name: marketplace
   repos:
     repo-a: repo-a      # will be evicted
     repo-b: repo-b      # will be evicted
     repo-c: repo-c      # will be evicted
     repo-d: repo-d      # will be evicted
     repo-e: repo-e      # will be evicted
     repo-f: repo-f
     repo-g: repo-g
     repo-h: repo-h
   detect:
     http: true
   links:
     - from: repo-h
       to: repo-a         # repo-a's pool is gone
       type: http
       role: consumer
       contract: "GET::/api/data"
   ```

2. Run group sync:

   ```bash
   gitnexus group sync <group_name> --verbose
   ```

3. Observe warnings for repos that were evicted (repos `a`–`e`):

   ```
   {"level":40,"msg":"[manifest-extractor] resolveSymbol failed for http:GET::/api/data in repo-a: LadybugDB not initialized for repo \"repo-a\". Call initLbug first."}
   ```

4. Check the resulting `contracts.json` — cross-links for evicted repos carry `manifest::repo-a::http::GET::/api/data` as `symbolUid` instead of a real graph node ID.

### Environment

| Property | Value |
|----------|-------|
| **OS** | CachyOS (Arch-derivative), Linux 6.19.9-1-cachyos, x86_64 |
| **GitNexus** | 1.6.7 (Docker image `ghcr.io/abhigyanpatwari/gitnexus:1.6.7`) |
| **LadyBugDB Core** | 0.15.3 (bundled in the Docker image) |

### Logs / screenshots

_No response_

title: gitnexus analyze fails with project folder named with a trailing space.
body: ### Area gitnexus (CLI / core / indexing / MCP server) ### Summary ### `gitnexus analyze` reports "Not a git repository" when the repo path contains a trailing space ### Context `gitnexus analyze` fails with **"Not a git repository."** on a directory that is a valid git repository, when the directory name ends with a trailing space. `git` resolves the repo correctly from the same directory, so the repo is valid — GitNexus appears to strip/normalize the trailing space from the path before locating the `.git` directory, then looks in a non-existent path and incorrectly concludes the folder is not a git repo. ### Expected behavior ## Expected behavior GitNexus indexes the repository, the same way `git` resolves it from that directory. ### Actual behavior ``` GitNexus Analyzer Not a git repository. Tip: pass --skip-git to index any folder without a .git directory. ``` Note: `gitnexus status` returns `Repository not indexed. Run: gitnexus analyze` (it only checks the index), so the failure is specific to the git-detection step in `analyze`. ### Steps to reproduce 1. Create or have a git repo whose directory name ends with a space, e.g. `/Users/me/Desktop/test-dir ` (trailing space). 2. `cd` into it. Confirm git works: ``` git rev-parse --is-inside-work-tree # -> true git rev-parse --show-toplevel # -> .../test (with trailing space) ``` 3. Run `gitnexus analyze`. ### Environment - GitNexus version: 1.6.3 (installed globally via npm) - Node: v20.20.0 - Git: 2.40.0 - OS: macOS 26.0 (build 25A354) ### Logs / screenshots ## Root cause (suspected) The repo path is `/Users/me/Desktop/test-dir ` (trailing space, verified with `od -c`: the path bytes end in `... d \n`). GitNexus seems to `.trim()` / normalize the resolved path, yielding `/Users/me/Desktop/test-dir` (no space). That path has no `.git`, so the git check fails — even though the actual working directory is the space-suffixed path where `.git` does exist. ## Suggested fix - Do not trim/strip whitespace from filesystem paths. Preserve the exact path (trailing spaces are valid on macOS/Linux). - Resolve the repo root the way git does (e.g. shell out to `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` or use a git library) instead of manually constructing/normalizing the path before the `.git` existence check. ## Workaround Either rename the directory to remove the trailing space, or run `gitnexus analyze --skip-git` (loses git-aware features).

title: fix(group): pin repos during sync so large groups resolve cross-links
body:
## Summary

`gitnexus group sync` on a group with **more than 5 repos** silently produced cross-links anchored to *synthetic* UIDs (`manifest::<repo>::<contract>`) instead of real graph symbols, so cross-repo impact analysis through manifest-declared contracts could not actually trace into the affected repos. The log showed a burst of `level:40` `LadybugDB not initialized for repo "X". Call initLbug first.` warnings during manifest extraction.

After this change, every group member stays resident through resolution: cross-links anchor to **real** graph symbol UIDs, and the "not initialized" warnings are gone.

Fixes #2189.

## Why it happened

The LadybugDB connection pool caps residency at `MAX_POOL_SIZE = 5` with LRU eviction. `syncGroup` opens one pool per repo in an init loop, then runs **deferred** workspace + manifest cross-repo resolution *after* the loop using executor closures captured in `dbExecutors`. With more than 5 repos, the earliest repos are LRU-evicted as later repos initialize (nothing is checked out between loop iterations, so every prior repo is eligible). By resolution time their pools are gone; the stale executor closures call `executeParameterized` on an evicted `poolId` → throw → the manifest extractor catches it and falls back to a synthetic UID.

A prior fix (#1802) moved deferred resolution *inside* the `try` so the `finally`'s `closeLbug` no longer tore pools down early. That closed one eviction window; this closes the remaining one — eviction *during* the init loop.

```
BEFORE (group of 6, cap 5)          AFTER (pinned)
init r1..r5  → pool {r1..r5}        init r1..r5; pinRepo each
init r6      → evictLRU drops r1     init r6 → evictLRU skips pinned → pool {r1..r6}
resolve r1   → throw "not init"      resolve r1 → real rows → real symbolUid
             → synthetic UID         finally: unpin + close each repo
```

## The fix

Add repo **pinning** to the pool adapter and wire it into `syncGroup`:

- `pinRepo(repoId)` / `unpinRepo(repoId)` on the pool adapter; `evictLRU` and the idle-timeout sweep skip pinned repos; `closeOne` clears the pin on teardown.
- `syncGroup` pins each repo immediately after `initLbug` and, in its `finally`, unpins then closes every opened pool.

Design decisions:

- **Pinning over batching or raising the cap.** Pinning expresses the real invariant ("repos opened for *this sync* must stay resident until resolution completes") with zero re-init churn. Raising `MAX_POOL_SIZE` only moves the failure threshold and re-introduces the mmap-budget risk the cap exists to prevent.
- **Inert when nothing is pinned.** `evictLRU`, the idle sweep, and `closeOne` behave identically for any caller that never pins — MCP query serving, search, and wiki are unaffected.
- **Pins block only *automatic* eviction.** Explicit `closeOne` / `closeLbug` always close and clear the pin, so the sync can always release its own pools. Release is belt-and-suspenders: `unpinRepo` in the `finally` **and** `closeOne` clearing the pin, so a pin never leaks across syncs in the long-lived MCP server, even on error.

## Tests

- `gitnexus/test/unit/lbug-pool-pinning.test.ts` (new) drives the **real** `initLbug` path (mocking only the native LadybugDB layer, so `evictLRU` actually runs): a characterization test proves the un-pinned 6th repo evicts the first; the fix test proves all 6 pinned repos stay resident; plus explicit-close-clears-pin, idle-timeout-skips-pinned (fake timers), unpin-re-enables-eviction, and idempotency.
- `gitnexus/test/unit/group/sync.test.ts` (new block) proves the lifecycle wiring: every initialized repo is pinned, all pins are released on success **and** on a mid-flight throw, and a repo that fails to resolve is never pinned.
- Full affected-area sweep green: 605 tests across `test/unit/group` + pool-adapter unit tests. `tsc --noEmit`, `prettier --check`, and `eslint` all clean on the changed files.

## Review Findings — Addressed in follow-up commits

The tri-review (review 4491805745; 5 Claude lanes + Codex) surfaced three follow-ups. All are now **fixed in this PR**, each as a separate planned + deepened commit:

- **[P2] Concurrent group syncs sharing a repoId** → **fixed** (`refactor(lbug): reference-count pool pins`). `pinnedRepos` is now a `Map<repoId, count>`; pins are reference-counted, so overlapping holders — two windows of one sync, or two concurrent syncs sharing a repo — coexist safely. The repo is freed only when the last lease releases, so one sync's teardown can no longer pull a pool out from under another.
- **[P3] Leak-prone exported pin primitive** → **fixed** (`refactor(lbug): pinRepo returns a leak-proof release disposer`). `pinRepo` returns an idempotent `release()` disposer, so the pin/release pair can't be left dangling.
- **[P2] Large-group unbounded memory residency** → **fixed structurally** (`refactor(group): windowed manifest resolution`). Whole-sync pinning is replaced by windowed deferred resolution: manifest links are partitioned into windows of ≤ `getMaxResidentRepos()` referenced repos; each window re-inits + leases only its own repos, resolves, then **releases** (not closes — released repos stay evictable for the LRU, avoiding teardown of an entry a concurrent reader shares). Peak per-sync residency is bounded regardless of group size, reusing `MAX_POOL_SIZE` via an intent-named accessor (no new threshold constant). The init loop no longer pins — contract extraction runs while each repo is freshly live.

Plan: `docs/plans/2026-06-13-002-refactor-windowed-resolution-refcount-pins-plan.md` (deepened by architecture / repo-pattern / performance lanes). Coverage: refcount + disposer unit tests; a pure `partitionManifestWindows` test (every link in exactly one window — the contract-dedup invariant); and a real-pool test asserting concurrently-open Databases never exceed the resident cap for a group larger than it.

### Remaining follow-up (deferred, documented in the plan)
- **Concurrent-sync aggregate residency.** Reference-counted leases make concurrent syncs *correctness-safe*, but two simultaneous syncs can each hold a window, so process-wide residency can still reach `2 × getMaxResidentRepos()`. A process-global resident-lease semaphore is the structural answer; deferred since in-process concurrent `group_sync` is uncommon.
- Optimal window bin-packing, and the per-endpoint resolution shape (init-once, residency-1), are recorded in the plan as future architecture.

## Post-Deploy Monitoring & Validation

- **Validation:** run `gitnexus group sync <group> --verbose` on a group with **>5 repos** and at least one manifest link targeting an early-initialized repo. Healthy signal: **no** `level:40` `LadybugDB not initialized` warnings during manifest extraction, and `contracts.json` cross-links carry real graph node IDs (not `manifest::…` synthetic UIDs).
- **Log watch:** `[manifest-extractor] resolveSymbol failed … LadybugDB not initialized` should disappear for in-group repos.
- **Failure signal & trigger:** large-group mmap exhaustion is now **mitigated** — windowed resolution bounds a single sync's residency to `getMaxResidentRepos()`. The remaining watch is process RSS during *concurrent* large-group syncs in the MCP server (the deferred aggregate-residency follow-up); a LadybugDB `Mmap for size … failed` there is the trigger to serialize syncs pending the resident-lease semaphore. No rollback concern for the common case (the change is inert outside `group sync`).
- **Owner/window:** maintainer, first few `group sync` runs on multi-repo groups post-merge.

title: Tree-sitter compatibility workarounds
body:
# Tree-sitter compatibility workarounds


Bundled runtime `tree-sitter@0.25.1` (ABI 13–15).

## TL;DR

**Workarounds** — 8 grammars still need one. Upstream movement: yes — 2 grammars have unreleased fixes on main.

- 4/11 npm-installed grammars already accept tree-sitter@0.25.1
- 6/7 vendored grammars at an ABI within the runtime range
- 1 intentionally pinned (see below)
- 2 waiting on an upstream npm release
- 4 need a peer patch with no upstream fix (not even on main)
- **1 bump candidate(s) you can take TODAY** (npm-latest is newer than the pin AND its peer dep accepts our current runtime)

## What you can do today

These pins lag npm latest and the latest version's peer dep already accepts our current `tree-sitter@0.25.x` runtime. When bumping, remove the old version's `AUDITED_PEERS` entry in `gitnexus/scripts/prepare-tree-sitter-bundle.cjs` (prepack fails until you do).

- `tree-sitter-c-sharp`: `0.23.5` → `0.24.0` (peer `^0.25.0`)

## Disposition

### Peer accepts runtime (4)

These grammars' npm-latest peer dep already accepts tree-sitter@0.25.1. No workaround needed at npm latest.

- `tree-sitter-c-sharp` — pinned `0.23.5`, npm latest `0.24.0`  _(also a bump candidate — see above)_
- `tree-sitter-go` — pinned `0.25.0`, npm latest `0.25.0`
- `tree-sitter-javascript` — pinned `0.25.0`, npm latest `0.25.0`
- `tree-sitter-python` — pinned `0.25.0`, npm latest `0.25.0`

### Intentionally pinned (1)

Deliberately held below npm latest. These are **not** drift — each entry lists the issue motivating the pin and the condition for unpinning.

- `tree-sitter-cpp` pinned at `0.23.4` (npm latest `0.23.4`)
  #1242 — last 0.23.x release before tree-sitter-cpp added a runtime dep on the broken-ABI tree-sitter-c@^0.23.1; pinning here removes the need for a transitive override

### Waiting on upstream npm release (2)

Fixes are merged on the upstream main branch but not yet published to npm. The peer patch can be dropped as soon as upstream cuts a release.

- `tree-sitter-php@0.24.2` — peer `^0.22.4`. _peer relaxed to `^0.25.0` on `tree-sitter/tree-sitter-php@master` not yet published_
- `tree-sitter-rust@0.24.0` — peer `^0.22.1`. _peer relaxed to `^0.25.0` on `tree-sitter/tree-sitter-rust@master` not yet published_

### Peer patch required (4)

Peer dep rejects the runtime on both the latest npm release and upstream main. The pack-time peer patch stays until upstream relaxes it.

- `@eagleoutice/tree-sitter-r@1.1.2` — peer `^0.21.0`
- `tree-sitter-java@0.23.5` — peer `^0.21.1`
- `tree-sitter-ruby@0.23.1` — peer `^0.21.1`
- `tree-sitter-typescript@0.23.2` — peer `^0.21.0`

## Pack-time peer patches (9)

`gitnexus/scripts/prepare-tree-sitter-bundle.cjs` adds `0.25.1` to these bundled manifests' tree-sitter peer range. Removing an entry requires bumping (or dropping) the package that brings it in.

- `@eagleoutice/tree-sitter-r@1.1.2` (peer `^0.21.0`) — required: no upstream fix yet
- `tree-sitter-c@0.23.6` (peer `^0.22.1`) — transitive: dropped when the grammar that depends on it is bumped
- `tree-sitter-cpp@0.23.4` (peer `^0.21.1`) — required while intentionally pinned
- `tree-sitter-java@0.23.5` (peer `^0.21.1`) — required: no upstream fix yet
- `tree-sitter-javascript@0.23.1` (peer `^0.21.1`) — transitive: dropped when the grammar that depends on it is bumped
- `tree-sitter-php@0.24.2` (peer `^0.22.4`) — drop once upstream publishes its relaxed peer
- `tree-sitter-ruby@0.23.1` (peer `^0.21.1`) — required: no upstream fix yet
- `tree-sitter-rust@0.24.0` (peer `^0.22.1`) — drop once upstream publishes its relaxed peer
- `tree-sitter-typescript@0.23.2` (peer `^0.21.0`) — required: no upstream fix yet

## Vendored parsers (7)

These grammars ship from `gitnexus/vendor/` rather than the npm registry. Their compatibility is governed by the **vendored ABI** (must lie in the target runtime's range), not by a peer-dep negotiation. The rationale for each vendored copy lives in its own `package.json` `_vendoredBy` field.

title: feat: C-family PDG/CFG visitors (C, C++, C#, Java, Go)
body:
# feat: C-family PDG/CFG visitors (C, C++, C#, Java, Go) ## Summary Add full PDG support — a per-language control-flow visitor plus def/use harvest — for the C-family languages (C, C++, C#, Java, Go) in one PR, so CFG, REACHING_DEF, and CDG light up for each via the existing optional `cfgVisitor` provider hook. The shared PDG core is untouched; the work is additive, `--pdg`-gated, and modeled on the TypeScript visitor. This is the language-coverage prerequisite for any future PDG-backed `impact` analysis. --- ## Problem Frame GitNexus builds program-dependence-graph layers — CFG → REACHING_DEF → CDG → taint — but only **TypeScript** produces them. The parse worker gates CFG construction on `if (PDG_ENABLED && provider.cfgVisitor)`, and only the TypeScript provider supplies a `cfgVisitor`. Every other provider omits it, so PDG is silently skipped for ~13 languages. Any feature that consumes PDG (e.g. taint-aware or data-dependence-narrowed `impact`) would therefore degrade silently on non-TS code, and mixed-language repos — the common case — would behave inconsistently. The architecture already anticipated this: CFG is an optional `LanguageProvider` hook, and everything downstream (`cfg/collect.ts`, `cfg/cfg-builder.ts`, `cfg/emit.ts`, the reaching-defs / post-dominator / CDG solvers, the parse-worker integration) consumes only the serialized `FunctionCfg` shape and is language-agnostic. The work is bounded to writing a `CfgVisitor` (+ harvest) per grammar and wiring it in. This plan does the first and largest batch — the C-family — in one PR, and generalizes the verification infrastructure (which is currently TS-bound) so the remaining languages can follow mechanically. This plan is the **building** prerequisite. The downstream **consumption** work (migrating `impact` to read PDG) is out of scope here — but the build is not inert until then: the `pdg_query` MCP tool (CDG / data-dependence queries) and the `explain` taint consumer already ship on `main` and light up for all five languages the moment this PR merges, so cross-language CDG/REACHING_DEF queries are day-one capability and serve as the interim acceptance bar. --- ## Requirements - R1. Each of C, C++, C#, Java, Go builds a per-function CFG (BasicBlock nodes + typed CFG edges) under `--pdg`, via a provider-supplied `cfgVisitor` — with **no** language-named branching added to shared ingestion code (`cfg/`, the parse worker, `scope-resolution/pipeline/run.ts`). - R2. Each language emits a def/use harvest (binding table + per-statement `defs`/`uses` + `mayDefs`) so the REACHING_DEF and CDG layers populate for that language, not just bare CFG. - R3. A non-`--pdg` run stays byte-identical to today (golden-parity gate) for all five languages; `--pdg` is opt-in and off by default. - R4. New visitors degrade gracefully: a CFG-build throw on an AST shape a visitor doesn't model skips only that one file's CFG (never drops the language file-group), and any dropped/abridged edge logs unconditionally (no silent truncation). - R5. Every tree-sitter node-type/field literal a visitor uses is grammar-validated, and the emitted `CfgEdgeKind` set matches the contract the downstream RD/CDG solvers depend on. The grammar-literal CI gate does **not** scan `cfg/visitors/` today (its collector covers `*-extractors/`, `languages//`, and config files only), so U1 extends the collector's scan surface to include `cfg/visitors/*.ts` — otherwise the gate stays green on dead literals in the new visitors. - R6. Verification scales across languages: a language-parameterized unit + fingerprint harness; worker-mode pipeline assertions (BasicBlock + CFG > 0 with `--pdg`, == 0 without) per language; and the byte-identical-off golden gate as the parity proof. (Registry-primary is now the only resolution path — the legacy dual-leg `REGISTRY_PRIMARY_=0/1` parity harness was removed in RING4, so there are no dual parity legs to run.) - R7. Taint substrate (removable tail): each visitor emits the call-site `sites[]` harvest so TAINTED/TAINT_PATH *can* populate once a per-language source/sink model exists. No C-family taint model ships today (`registerBuiltinTaintModels` registers TS/JS only), and authoring those models is deferred (see Scope Boundaries) — so this requirement covers the config-independent substrate only; positive taint findings are a follow-up. Structured to drop from the PR without affecting R1–R6. --- ## High-Level Technical Design The seam is narrow: each new language adds a visitor file and one provider line. Everything to the right of `cfgSideChannel` already exists and is shared. ```mermaid flowchart TB subgraph NEW["New per-language work (this PR)"] V["cfg/visitors/<lang>.ts
create<Lang>CfgVisitor()
(CFG walk + def/use harvest)"] P["languages/<lang>.ts
cfgVisitor: create<Lang>CfgVisitor()"] end subgraph SHARED["Shared core (untouched)"] C["cfg/collect.ts
collectFunctionCfgs()"] W["workers/parse-worker.ts
if (PDG_ENABLED && provider.cfgVisitor)"] SC["ParsedFile.cfgSideChannel
(plain JSON FunctionCfg[])"] E["cfg/emit.ts (scope-res Phase 4)
emitFileCfgs()"] L["solvers: reaching-defs /
post-dominators / control-dependence"] G["graph: BasicBlock + CFG +
REACHING_DEF + CDG (+ TAINTED)"] end P --> W V --> C W --> C --> SC --> E --> L --> G ``` ### The `CfgVisitor` contract a new language implements `gitnexus/src/core/ingestion/cfg/types.ts` (interface ~`:243`): - `isFunction(node)` — cheap node-type test (gates function enumeration + the per-function line budget). - `buildFunctionCfg(fnNode, filePath)` → `FunctionCfg | undefined` (undefined for non-functions / bodyless). It must produce **pure plain JSON** (no AST refs, no class instances, and — hard rule — **no field named `nodeId`**), populating `functionStartColumn` (load-bearing for BasicBlock id uniqueness). ### Edge-kind contract (must match the TS visitor; consumed by RD/CDG) | Construct | Edge kinds emitted | |---|---| | if / else | `cond-true`, `cond-false` | | while / do-while / for / for-each | `cond-true`, `loop-back`, `cond-false` | | switch / case | `switch-case`, `fallthrough` | | try / catch / finally | `throw` (every protected block → handler), `finally-return` / `finally-break` / `finally-continue` | | return / throw / break / continue | `return` / `throw` / `break` / `continue` (terminator → target) | | straight-line | `seq` | The single-exit invariant (one EXIT block, abnormal exits wired directly and excluded from a block's normal `exits`) is required by the post-dominator / CDG passes — **and EXIT must stay reverse-reachable from every block**, so every potentially-non-terminating loop/`select` needs a structural exit-escape edge (the TS visitor emits `header → loopExit` `cond-false` even for `while(true)`; without it, `emit.ts` skips CDG for that function — CFG/RD survive, CDG silently goes to zero). A visitor that violates these compiles fine but corrupts or empties downstream solvers — they are the real correctness watch-items. --- ## Key Technical Decisions - KTD1. **One shared C/C++ visitor module, two factories.** `cfg/visitors/c-cpp.ts` exports `createCCfgVisitor()` and `createCppCfgVisitor()` over a shared core; C++ extends the C core with exceptions (`try`/`catch`/`throw`) and `for_range_loop`. The grammars overlap heavily and `languages/c-cpp.ts` already houses both providers in one file, so this mirrors the existing organization. Each provider object still gets its own `cfgVisitor:` line. - KTD2. **Depth = CFG + def/use harvest for all five (R1–R2) as the core; taint `sites[]` substrate is a dedicated, removable tail (R7).** "Deepen" means real data/control dependence (RD + CDG), not bare blocks. The taint substrate is genuinely separable (the harvest's `sites[]` is documented-optional) and additionally depends on per-language source/sink config; it ships as the final phase so the PR can land R1–R6 even if the taint tail is split out under review. - KTD3. **Wire only through the optional `cfgVisitor` hook — zero shared-core edits.** No `if (language === …)` anywhere in `cfg/`, the parse worker, or `run.ts` (AGENTS.md no-language-naming rule). A language "lights up" purely by providing the hook; the worker and in-phase emit already gate on `provider.cfgVisitor`. - KTD4. **Generalize the verification infra first.** The `bench/cfg/measure.mjs` harness is hard-bound to TypeScript (grammar, visitor factory, and source generators). Parameterize it by `{grammar, visitorFactory, source-generators}` and generalize the unit-test harness helper before the per-language work, so each language is fingerprint-checkable and the remaining (non-C-family) languages inherit the tooling. - KTD5. **Real-parser regression tests, not snapshot-only.** Snapshots pin whatever the code emits — including bugs (the M5 CDG label bug that all review lanes missed because a unit test used a fictional edge). Each visitor gets real-parse regression tests for branch sense, loop bottom-test, break/continue, and try/catch/finally completion edges. Ground every node-type literal in a real parse via the grammar-introspection probe. - KTD6. **Visitor output obeys the serialized-shape invariants.** Plain JSON onto `cfgSideChannel`; populate `functionStartColumn`; honor the single-exit invariant; accumulate block text via `textParts: string[]` joined once (never `+=`, which is O(n²)); respect the per-function line/edge caps; never re-parse on the main thread. --- ## Scope Boundaries **In scope** - Per-language CFG visitor + def/use harvest for C, C++, C#, Java, Go, wired via `cfgVisitor`. - Language-parameterized unit + bench/fingerprint verification harness. - Worker-mode end-to-end PDG assertions + byte-identical-off golden parity per language. - Taint `sites[]` substrate per visitor (removable tail). ### Deferred to Follow-Up Work - The remaining non-C-family languages (Python, PHP, Ruby, Rust, Swift, Kotlin, Dart, Vue, COBOL) — same recipe, separate PRs, using the harness this PR generalizes. - Authoring per-language taint **source/sink/sanitizer models** (a new `taint/c-family-model.ts` + a `registerBuiltinTaintModels` extension; only TS/JS is registered today via `registerSourceSinkConfig`) — taint *findings* (as opposed to the `sites[]` substrate) depend on these, which is its own work. - Capturing the rollout as an institutional learning (`/ce-compound`) once it lands. ### Out of scope (different work entirely) - Migrating `impact` (or any consumer) to **read** PDG — this plan only makes PDG **buildable** for these languages. The consumption/migration is the downstream goal this unblocks. - Any change to the shared PDG core, schema, solvers, or `--pdg` default. --- ## Implementation Units Grouped into phases. Each per-language unit (U2–U5) depends on U1 but is independent of the others, so they land as separate commits; the maintainer has previously asked for focused, splittable commits. **Minimum landable subset:** each visitor is an independent ~500–1000-line re-derivation over its own grammar (not a config delta over the TS template), so if one language — Go is the likeliest — can't reach the correctness bar within this PR, it splits to a follow-up while C/C++, C#, and Java land. The one-PR batch is the target, not a hard coupling. ### Phase A — Shared verification scaffolding ### U1. Language-parameterized CFG test + bench harness - **Goal:** Make the CFG verification infrastructure language-agnostic so every subsequent language can be unit-tested and fingerprint-checked without bespoke wiring. - **Requirements:** R6 (and enables R5 fingerprinting for all later units). - **Dependencies:** none. - **Files:** - `gitnexus/bench/cfg/measure.mjs` (parameterize: accept a `{lang, grammar, visitorFactory}` and per-language source generators; keep TS scenarios working unchanged. The `taint-dense` scenario hardcodes `TS_JS_TAINT_MODEL` — thread a per-scenario taint-model ref too, or scope the taint scenario to TS only, so it doesn't run the TS model against C-family CFGs) - `gitnexus/bench/cfg/baselines.json` (add per-language scenario baseline slots as languages land) - `gitnexus/test/helpers/literal-collectors.ts` (extend the grammar-literal gate's scan surface to include `cfg/visitors/*.ts`, mapping each visitor file to its grammar(s): `c-cpp.ts` → C + C++, `csharp.ts` → C#, `java.ts` → Java, `go.ts` → Go — without this the CI gate stays green on dead literals in the new visitors, the exact failure KTD5 warns about) - `gitnexus/test/helpers/cfg-harness.ts` (generalize the existing `ts-cfg-harness.ts` `cfgOf`/`cfgsOf` into a grammar+visitor-parameterized helper; keep a thin TS-bound re-export for existing tests) - `gitnexus/test/unit/cfg/harness.test.ts` (test file — proves the generalized harness drives a non-TS grammar end to end) - **Approach:** Introduce a `visitorFactory` + `grammar` parameter on the harness/bench entry points; default to TypeScript so existing scenarios and `--check` baselines stay byte-identical. The bench currently hardcodes `parser.setLanguage(TypeScript.typescript)`, `createTypeScriptCfgVisitor()`, and TS-only `SCENARIOS` — thread these through a per-scenario `lang` field. Remember `bufferSize: getTreeSitterBufferSize(src)` on large synthetic sources, and measure with `maxFunctionLines=0` (the algorithm, not the prod cap). `--check` must still fail loudly without `--expose-gc`. - **Patterns to follow:** `test/integration/cfg/cfg-snapshot.test.ts:23-27` is the canonical seam — it resolves a visitor generically via `getProvider(lang).cfgVisitor`; generalize that dynamic resolution. `bench/scope-capture/measure.mjs` is prior art for per-scenario `lang` fields only — do **not** copy its static 13-language import table, which is the language-naming anti-pattern this work avoids. - **Test scenarios:** - Happy path: the generalized `cfgOf` helper, given the TS grammar+visitor, reproduces the exact CFG (blocks/edges/fingerprint) the old TS-bound harness produced for a known fixture. - Edge: the harness drives a second grammar (use any already-available C-family grammar once U2 lands, or a minimal smoke grammar) and returns a non-empty `FunctionCfg` — proves no residual TS coupling. - Error: running `--check` without `--expose-gc` fails loudly (not a silent green no-op). - Verification: existing TS bench `--check` (all 6 scenarios) passes unchanged against the parameterized harness. - **Verification:** `node --expose-gc --import tsx bench/cfg/measure.mjs --check` passes with no baseline drift; the generalized helper compiles and the TS visitor unit tests still pass. ### Phase B — C and C++ ### U2. C & C++ CFG visitor + harvest - **Goal:** Build CFG + def/use facts for C and C++ functions. - **Requirements:** R1, R2, R4, R5; partially R3. - **Dependencies:** U1. - **Files:** - `gitnexus/src/core/ingestion/cfg/visitors/c-cpp.ts` (create — `createCCfgVisitor()`, `createCppCfgVisitor()`, shared core; harvest inline or in a sibling `c-cpp-harvest.ts`) - `gitnexus/src/core/ingestion/languages/c-cpp.ts` (add `cfgVisitor: createCCfgVisitor()` to `cProvider` after `:403`; `cfgVisitor: createCppCfgVisitor()` to `cppProvider` after `:486`) - `gitnexus/test/unit/cfg/c-cpp-visitor.test.ts` (test file) - `gitnexus/test/integration/cfg/fixtures/c-hazards.c`, `gitnexus/test/integration/cfg/fixtures/cpp-hazards.cpp` (fixtures) - **Approach:** Mirror `cfg/visitors/typescript.ts` structure — a per-function walk instance holding a `ControlFlowContext` + handler stack, driving `CfgBuilder`. Function nodes: `function_definition` (walk the `declarator` chain, reusing the `cCppExtractFunctionName` unwrap pattern), C++ adds `lambda_expression`. Control flow: `if_statement`, `for_statement`, `while_statement`, `do_statement`, `switch_statement`/`case_statement` (C-style fallthrough), `return`/`break`/`continue`, and `goto_statement` + `labeled_statement` (arbitrary jumps — resolve labels within the function; unresolved `goto` routes to EXIT and logs). C++ extends the C core with `try_statement`/`catch_clause`/`throw_statement` (conservative throw edge from every protected block to the handler, per the TS `visitTry` model) and `for_range_loop`. Harvest: bindings (params, `declaration`s) + per-statement defs/uses + may-defs for short-circuit/ternary; member/pointer writes are not scalar defs (exclude, like TS). Note RAII destructor-at-scope-exit is not modeled by tree-sitter — document the gap, don't fake it. - **Patterns to follow:** `cfg/visitors/typescript.ts` (visit dispatch, `visitIf`/`visitWhile`/`visitSwitch`/`visitTry`); `cfg/visitors/typescript-harvest.ts` (two-phase order-independent harvest); `languages/c-cpp.ts` existing `cCppExtractFunctionName`/`cppLabelOverride` for node shapes. - **Execution note:** Before committing to the shared-core factoring, run the grammar-introspection probe against **both** `tree-sitter-c` and `tree-sitter-cpp` for the full control-flow node set and confirm the shared literals match; if they diverge, fall back to two thin visitors over a shared `CfgBuilder` rather than internal C-vs-C++ conditionals (which would brush against the no-language-naming rule). Ground every node-type literal this way before committing; write real-parser regression tests, not snapshots. - **Test scenarios:** - Happy path (C): straight-line function → ENTRY→block→EXIT (`seq`); `if/else` → `cond-true`/`cond-false`; `for`/`while`/`do-while` → header + `loop-back` + dedicated loop-exit. - Edge (C): `switch` fallthrough between cases (`switch-case` + `fallthrough`); `goto` forward and backward to a `labeled_statement`; `goto` to an undefined label routes to EXIT and logs a warning. - Edge (C++): `try/catch` — throw edge from each protected block to the catch handler; `throw` with no enclosing try routes to the function handler/EXIT; `for_range_loop` header + body + loop-back. - Data flow: `int x = a + b; use(x);` produces a def of `x` and a use in the consuming statement; `if (a && (x = f()))` records `x` as a **may-def**, not a must-kill. - Error: a malformed/partial function body returns a partial-or-`undefined` CFG without throwing out of `buildFunctionCfg`. - `functionStartColumn` populated: two same-line C functions get distinct BasicBlock ids. - **Verification:** `c-cpp-visitor.test.ts` green via tsx/vitest (no dist needed); grammar-literal CI gate passes; non-`--pdg` graph for C/C++ fixtures stays golden-identical. ### Phase C — C# ### U3. C# CFG visitor + harvest - **Goal:** Build CFG + def/use facts for C# methods/lambdas. - **Requirements:** R1, R2, R4, R5; partially R3. - **Dependencies:** U1. - **Files:** - `gitnexus/src/core/ingestion/cfg/visitors/csharp.ts` (create) - `gitnexus/src/core/ingestion/languages/csharp.ts` (add `cfgVisitor: createCsharpCfgVisitor()` after `:202`) - `gitnexus/test/unit/cfg/csharp-visitor.test.ts` (test file) - `gitnexus/test/integration/cfg/fixtures/csharp-hazards.cs` (fixture) - **Approach:** Function nodes: `method_declaration`, `local_function_statement`, `constructor_declaration`, `lambda_expression`, expression-bodied members (`=> expr`), `anonymous_method_expression`. Control flow: `if_statement`, `for_statement`, `foreach_statement`, `while_statement`, `do_statement`, `switch_statement`/`switch_section` (+ `switch_expression`/`switch_expression_arm`), `try_statement`/`catch_clause`/`catch_filter_clause`/`finally_clause`, `using_statement` and `lock_statement` (treat `using` like try/finally — deterministic dispose), `return`/`break`/`continue`/`throw`(+`throw_expression`), `goto_statement`, `labeled_statement`, `yield_statement` (model as an exit-ish edge; document iterator-state-machine limitation). Harvest mirrors TS. Pre-empt the known surprise: records are `record_declaration` (not `record_struct_declaration`). - **Patterns to follow:** `cfg/visitors/typescript.ts` (`visitTry`/`visitSwitch`); the TS `using`-like deterministic-dispose handling parallels try/finally. - **Execution note:** Validate literals via the introspection probe against `tree-sitter-c-sharp` (note the `bindings/node` subpath); real-parser regression tests. - **Test scenarios:** - Happy path: `if/else`, `for`, `foreach`, `while`, `do-while` produce the expected edge kinds. - Edge: `using (...) { }` runs the body then the dispose/continuation on both normal and exception exit (finally semantics); `switch_expression` arms; labeled `goto`. - Edge: `try/catch/finally` completion edges (`finally-return`/`finally-break`/`finally-continue`) when `return`/`break` crosses a `finally`. - Data flow: local declaration def + use; `c ?? (c = load())` records `c` as may-def. - Error: unmodeled member shape → graceful partial CFG, no throw. - **Verification:** `csharp-visitor.test.ts` green; grammar-literal gate passes; golden-identical when `--pdg` off. ### Phase D — Java ### U4. Java CFG visitor + harvest - **Goal:** Build CFG + def/use facts for Java methods/constructors/lambdas. - **Requirements:** R1, R2, R4, R5; partially R3. - **Dependencies:** U1. - **Files:** - `gitnexus/src/core/ingestion/cfg/visitors/java.ts` (create) - `gitnexus/src/core/ingestion/languages/java.ts` (add `cfgVisitor: createJavaCfgVisitor()` after `:120`) - `gitnexus/test/unit/cfg/java-visitor.test.ts` (test file) - `gitnexus/test/integration/cfg/fixtures/java-hazards.java` (fixture) - **Approach:** Function nodes: `method_declaration`, `constructor_declaration` (+`constructor_body`), `compact_constructor_declaration`, `lambda_expression`. Control flow: `if_statement`, `for_statement`, `enhanced_for_statement`, `while_statement`, `do_statement`, `switch_expression`/`switch_block`/`switch_block_statement_group`/`switch_rule` (both classic colon form and arrow form) + `switch_label`, `try_statement`/`try_with_resources_statement`/`catch_clause`/`finally_clause` (try-with-resources = auto-close → finally semantics), `synchronized_statement`, `return`/`break`/`continue`(labeled)/`throw`, `labeled_statement`, `yield_statement`. Harvest mirrors TS. Pre-empt surprises: generics are `generic_type` (not `parameterized_type`); enhanced switch uses `switch_rule`/`switch_label`. - **Patterns to follow:** `cfg/visitors/typescript.ts` (`visitTry` finally route-through; labeled break/continue via `ControlFlowContext` label lists). - **Execution note:** Validate literals against `tree-sitter-java`; real-parser regression tests for labeled break/continue and try-with-resources. - **Test scenarios:** - Happy path: `if/else`, classic `for`, `enhanced_for_statement`, `while`, `do-while`. - Edge: `try_with_resources_statement` closes resources on both normal and exceptional exit (finally semantics); labeled `break outer;` from a nested loop targets the correct labeled frame (unlabeled break never matches a labeled-block frame). - Edge: arrow-form `switch_rule` vs classic `switch_block_statement_group`; `yield` in a switch expression. - Data flow: local var def/use; switch case-test recorded as may-def on the dispatch block. - Error: unmodeled shape → graceful partial CFG. - **Verification:** `java-visitor.test.ts` green; grammar-literal gate passes; golden-identical when off. ### Phase E — Go ### U5. Go CFG visitor + harvest - **Goal:** Build CFG + def/use facts for Go functions/methods/closures — the highest-divergence target. - **Requirements:** R1, R2, R4, R5; partially R3. - **Dependencies:** U1. - **Files:** - `gitnexus/src/core/ingestion/cfg/visitors/go.ts` (create) - `gitnexus/src/core/ingestion/languages/go.ts` (add `cfgVisitor: createGoCfgVisitor()` after `:143`) - `gitnexus/test/unit/cfg/go-visitor.test.ts` (test file) - `gitnexus/test/integration/cfg/fixtures/go-hazards.go` (fixture) - **Approach:** Function nodes: `function_declaration`, `method_declaration`, `func_literal`. Control flow: `if_statement` (with `initializer`; `else if` via `alternative`), `for_statement` with `for_clause` (Go's single loop keyword covers C-for, while, and range), `expression_switch_statement`/`expression_case`/`default_case`, `type_switch_statement`/`type_case`, `select_statement`/`communication_case`, `return`/`break`/`continue`(labeled)/`goto_statement`, `fallthrough_statement` (explicit — Go cases do **not** fall through by default), `labeled_statement`, `defer_statement`, `go_statement`. Decisions for Go-specific constructs: model `defer` as LIFO completion legs wired into the function-exit path (closest analogue to stacked finalizers — document the approximation); `select` as non-deterministic dispatch across `communication_case`s (like a switch with no fallthrough); `go` spawns a separate flow — treat the spawned body as its own function-scope CFG or document it as not-followed (pick the simpler correct option and log the limitation). Harvest: `short_var_declaration`/`var_declaration`/`assignment_statement`/`inc_statement`/`dec_statement`; multiple-return assignments define each LHS name. **EXIT-reachability (load-bearing for CDG):** `for {}` (no condition), `select {}` with no default, and goroutine/server loops are common and non-terminating; the post-dominator/CDG pass is sound only when EXIT is reverse-reachable from every block, so — exactly as the TS visitor emits a structural `header → loopExit` `cond-false` edge even for `while(true)` — the Go visitor must emit a structural exit-escape edge for every potentially-non-terminating loop/`select`, or those functions silently emit zero CDG. - **Patterns to follow:** `cfg/visitors/typescript.ts` (switch-without-fallthrough is the closer analogue for Go cases than the C fallthrough model); `languages/go.ts` existing capture code for node shapes; the M2 finally route-through for `defer` threading. - **Execution note:** Go diverges most — validate every literal against `tree-sitter-go`; write explicit regression tests for `defer` ordering and `fallthrough`. Where a construct (`go`, exotic `select`) is approximated, document the gap in the visitor doc-comment and ensure any dropped edge logs. - **Test scenarios:** - Happy path: `if` with initializer; `for_clause` C-style, `for`-as-while (condition only), `for range`; `expression_switch_statement` cases do not fall through by default. - Edge: explicit `fallthrough_statement` adds a `fallthrough` edge to the next case; `defer` body runs on every function-exit path (normal return and, if modeled, panic path) in LIFO order; labeled `break`/`continue`/`goto`. - Edge: `select` dispatches across communication cases (no implicit fallthrough); `type_switch_statement` cases. - Edge (EXIT-reachability): `for {}` (no condition) and `select {}` with no default keep EXIT reverse-reachable (`isExitReachableFromAllBlocks` holds → CDG is **not** skipped for the function). - Data flow: `a, b := f()` defines both `a` and `b`; `x := …; use(x)` def→use. - Error: `go func(){…}()` does not throw; spawned-body handling matches the documented decision. - **Verification:** `go-visitor.test.ts` green (including the `for {}` / `select {}` EXIT-reachability regression); grammar-literal gate passes; golden-identical when off. ### Phase F — Taint substrate (removable tail) ### U6. Call-site `sites[]` harvest across the five visitors - **Goal:** Emit the config-independent taint **substrate** (the call-site `sites[]` harvest) so TAINTED/TAINT_PATH can populate later, once per-language source/sink models exist. - **Requirements:** R7. - **Dependencies:** U2, U3, U4, U5. - **Files:** - `gitnexus/src/core/ingestion/cfg/visitors/c-cpp.ts`, `csharp.ts`, `java.ts`, `go.ts` (extend harvest with `sites[]`) - `gitnexus/test/integration/cfg/taint-snapshot.test.ts` (assert the substrate emits; no positive-taint assertion — see below) - `gitnexus/test/integration/cfg/fixtures/` (small call-site fixtures per language as needed) - **Approach:** Add the `SiteRecord`/`SiteArgOccurrence` call-site harvest (mirroring the TS `visitCall`/`walkChain` model) to each visitor's fact accumulator, emitting `sites` on `StatementFacts` only when non-empty. **No C-family taint model exists today:** `registerBuiltinTaintModels()` (in `taint/typescript-model.ts`) registers only TS/JS via `registerSourceSinkConfig`, and `getSourceSinkConfig()` returns `undefined` for every C-family language — so a `sites[]` harvest with no registered model produces zero TAINTED edges *by design*. Authoring the models (a new `c-family-model.ts` + a `registerBuiltinTaintModels` extension) is **deferred** (see Scope Boundaries); this unit ships only the substrate so the deferred config work has something to match against. Deliberately last and self-contained so it can split into a follow-up PR without touching R1–R6. - **Patterns to follow:** `cfg/visitors/typescript-harvest.ts` `sites` emission; `taint/typescript-model.ts` for the (deferred) model + `registerSourceSinkConfig` registration shape. - **Test scenarios:** - Happy path: a fixture with call sites yields a non-empty `sites[]` on the relevant `StatementFacts` for each language (substrate emitted and serialized). - Negative: with no registered C-family taint model, the worker run produces CFG/REACHING_DEF and **zero** TAINTED edges (substrate is inert without config, as intended); a CFG-only fixture (no `sites`) is unaffected. - (The positive source→sink→TAINTED assertion is deferred to the per-language-model follow-up — it cannot pass until a model is registered, so it is intentionally not part of U6.) - **Verification:** `sites[]` present where call sites exist; CFG/RD/CDG for all five unaffected if this unit is dropped; no TAINTED edges expected until the deferred model lands. ### Phase G — End-to-end verification ### U7. Worker-mode PDG integration, parity, and baselines - **Goal:** Prove all five languages build PDG through the real worker pipeline, stay byte-identical when `--pdg` is off (the golden-parity gate), and emit real CDG on non-trivial control flow. - **Requirements:** R3, R6 (closes verification for R1–R2). - **Dependencies:** U2, U3, U4, U5 (U6 if the taint tail stays in). - **Files:** - `gitnexus/test/integration/cfg/pipeline-pdg.test.ts` (extend: per-language BasicBlock + CFG > 0 with `--pdg`, == 0 without) - `gitnexus/test/integration/cfg/__snapshots__/` (cross-language CFG snapshots via `cfg-snapshot.test.ts`) - `gitnexus/bench/cfg/baselines.json` (add C-family scenario baselines produced via the parameterized harness) - **Approach:** Add per-language fixtures to the worker-pipeline assertion (`runPipelineFromRepo(path, () => {}, { workerThresholdsForTest: { minFiles: 1, minBytes: 1 }, workerPoolSize: 2 })` with `expect(result.usedWorkerPool).toBe(true)`). Assert BasicBlock + CFG counts > 0 per language under `--pdg` and == 0 (golden-identical) without it. Add bench scenarios + baselines for the new languages. Use the byte-identical-off golden gate (`pipeline-graph-golden.test.ts` with `--pdg` off) as the parity proof — registry-primary is the only resolution path, so there are no dual `REGISTRY_PRIMARY_=0/1` legs to run. - **Patterns to follow:** `test/integration/cfg/pipeline-pdg.test.ts` (the both-sinks proof); `cfg-snapshot.test.ts` `serialize()`; `pipeline-graph-golden.test.ts` (byte-identical-off gate). - **Execution note:** Run `node scripts/build.js` before any `pdg: true` pipeline assertion — a stale `dist/parse-worker.js` silently zeros CFG output with no warning. - **Test scenarios:** - Integration: for each of C, C++, C#, Java, Go, a `--pdg` worker run produces BasicBlock + CFG > 0; the same run without `--pdg` produces 0 and a graph byte-identical to the pre-PDG golden. - Integration: REACHING_DEF and CDG counts > 0 per language on a fixture with **real branching and a non-terminating loop/`select`** (not a straight-line fixture — a trivial fixture can pass while real non-terminating functions silently lose CDG via EXIT-unreachability). - Edge: an over-**edge**-cap function logs a dropped-edge warning rather than silently truncating; confirm whether an over-**line**-budget function (whose whole CFG is skipped in `collect.ts`) also surfaces a warning downstream, and if not, log it or note the silent-skip as accepted with a one-line rationale (R4). - Bench: `measure.mjs --check` passes including the new C-family scenarios with no fingerprint drift. - **Verification:** integration suite green after `node scripts/build.js`; the byte-identical-off golden gate passes; bench `--check` green; CDG non-zero on the non-terminating-loop fixture per language. --- ## Risk Analysis & Mitigation | Risk | Mitigation | |---|---| | `bench/cfg/measure.mjs` is TS-bound — adding languages is new infra, not config (flagged by research) | U1 parameterizes it first, defaulting to TS so existing baselines stay byte-identical. | | Wrong `CfgEdgeKind` corrupts RD/CDG silently (M5 label-bug class) | KTD5: real-parser regression tests per construct; mirror the TS edge-kind contract exactly; the edge-kind table is the reference. | | Guessed node-type literals fail silently; C-family grammars have surprises (Java `generic_type`/`switch_rule`, C# `record_declaration`) | Ground every literal via the grammar-introspection probe; the empty-allowlist grammar-literal CI gate enforces it. | | Per-function O(n²) traversal (recurring GitNexus regression family) | Stack-based walk, thread captured nodes, `textParts` join (never `+=`), reuse the per-function line/edge caps. | | Stale `dist/parse-worker.js` zeros worker tests with no warning | U7 execution note: `node scripts/build.js` before every `pdg: true` assertion; worktree node_modules + gitnexus-shared shadow caveats in Prerequisites. | | A visitor throw drops the whole language file-group | Confirm the worker's per-file try/catch still wraps `buildFunctionCfg`; each visitor returns partial/`undefined` rather than throwing on unmodeled shapes (R4). | | Large PR / review load | Phase per language (U2–U5 independent commits); U6 taint tail is split-ready; one commit per review finding. | | Go divergence (`defer`/`select`/`go`/`fallthrough`) under-modeled | Explicitly document approximations in the visitor doc-comment; log dropped edges; regression-test `defer` ordering and `fallthrough`. | | Go non-terminating loops/`select` silently lose CDG (EXIT-unreachable) | U5 emits a structural exit-escape edge per loop/`select`; U7 asserts CDG on a non-terminating fixture, not a straight-line one. | | Grammar-literal CI gate doesn't scan `cfg/visitors/` today → green on dead literals | U1 extends `test/helpers/literal-collectors.ts` to scan `cfg/visitors/*.ts` mapped to each grammar. | | Five visitors aren't a cheap port (TS visitor+harvest ≈ 1,900 lines / ~137 node literals; each grammar re-derived) | Minimum-landable-subset fallback: Go may split to a follow-up while C/C++, C#, Java land. Per-language commits keep review granular. | | Shared-type changes leak into `gitnexus-shared` | Expected none — `FunctionCfg`/`BindingEntry`/`StatementFacts` already exist in `cfg/types.ts`. If a shared edit becomes necessary, shadow `gitnexus-shared` per the worktree caveat and rebuild its dist. | --- ## Alternatives Considered - **One-language-per-PR fan-out.** Smaller, more reviewable diffs and the originally-recommended sequence. Overridden by the explicit "all C-family in one PR" directive; mitigated by per-language commits and the removable taint tail. - **CFG-only now, harvest later.** Valid intermediate (`finish()` with no bindings produces blocks/edges only). Rejected: "deepen" means real data dependence — RD/CDG are the point, and they need the harvest. - **A single generic table-driven "C-family" visitor** parameterized by a per-language node-type config. Attractive for dedup, but the control-flow divergence (Go `defer`/`select`/`fallthrough`-by-default, C# `using`/`yield`, Java try-with-resources/labeled break) makes a pure config table leaky and hard to test. Per-language visitor files matching the `typescript.ts` convention are clearer and align with the no-language-naming-in-shared-code rule. Shared helpers are still factored where genuinely common (the C/C++ pair in KTD1). --- ## Dependencies / Prerequisites - **Work from `main`.** The CFG/PDG code only exists on `main` (#2188); cwd `/workspace` is a stale pre-#2188 checkout. Use a `main` worktree (e.g. `/tmp/gn-main/gitnexus`) for all reading and building. - **Worktree node_modules + shared shadow.** Worktrees have no `node_modules`; symlink per-package deps (with `.bin`) to the main checkout for `node scripts/build.js`. If `gitnexus-shared` is edited, shadow it and rebuild its dist (else phantom `cfgSideChannel` tsc errors); prefer doing shared edits in the main checkout. - **Build before worker tests.** `node scripts/build.js` (~10s) before any worker/pipeline (`pdg: true`) assertion. - **Grammar introspection probe** available for literal validation against each grammar's `node-types.json` + a live `Parser.Query`. - **Landing mechanics.** Branch off `main`; push to the contributor's own fork; open the PR against `abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus:main`. Do **not** edit `gitnexus/CHANGELOG.md`. Conventional commits (`feat(cfg): …`). Treat a Vercel "authorization required" red as non-actionable, but CodeQL reds as real and merge-blocking. --- ## System-Wide Impact - **Developers / downstream PDG consumers:** five more languages gain CFG/REACHING_DEF/CDG (and, with the tail, the taint substrate) under `--pdg`. Two consumers already ship on `main` — the `pdg_query` MCP tool and `explain` — and light up for these languages on merge (day-one interim value), independent of the deferred `impact` migration. This is also the prerequisite that lets a future `impact` migration apply PDG refinement consistently across mixed-language repos instead of silently degrading on non-TS code. - **Index size / cost:** PDG remains opt-in (`--pdg` off by default); no change for default runs. Under `--pdg`, C-family files now carry a `cfgSideChannel` payload and emit BasicBlock/CFG/RD/CDG nodes/edges — bounded by the existing per-function line/edge caps. - **No behavior change when `--pdg` is off** (R3, golden-parity gate) — the dominant path for existing users is untouched.

title: feat(cfg): PDG/CFG visitors for all supported languages (#2195)
body:
## PDG/CFG construction for all supported languages

Today only TypeScript/JS builds the program-dependence-graph layers — the parse worker gates CFG construction on `provider.cfgVisitor`, and only the TS provider supplied one, so CFG / REACHING_DEF / CDG (and the taint substrate) were silently skipped for every other language. Any future PDG consumer (`pdg_query`, `explain`, a PDG-backed `impact`) therefore degrades silently on non-TS code, and mixed-language repos behave inconsistently.

This PR closes that gap: **every supported language except COBOL now builds CFG/REACHING_DEF/CDG under `--pdg`.**

### Coverage

| | CFG / REACHING_DEF / CDG under `--pdg` |
|---|---|
| Before | TypeScript / JavaScript only |
| After | + **C, C++, C#, Java, Go, Python, PHP, Ruby, Rust, Swift, Kotlin, Dart**, and **Vue** (reuses the TS visitor on the extracted `<script>`) |
| Deferred | **COBOL** — deliberate non-goal (no installed grammar; exotic PERFORM/GO-TO/paragraph control flow). Documented in `cobol.ts` + the `worker-roundtrip` gate. |

### Approach

Each language adds a per-grammar `CfgVisitor` + def/use harvest under `cfg/visitors/<lang>.ts`, wired into its provider via the existing optional `cfgVisitor` hook — **no language naming added to the shared ingestion core** (AGENTS.md rule). The shared CfgBuilder / solvers / emit / parse-worker integration are untouched; the work is additive and `--pdg`-gated (a non-`--pdg` run stays byte-identical).

Shared scaffolding:
- `test/helpers/cfg-harness.ts` — language-agnostic CFG unit-test harness (function discovery delegates to `visitor.isFunction`).
- Extended the grammar-literal CI gate to scan `cfg/visitors/` (validates every node-type literal per grammar).
- `cfg/visitors/call-site-harvest.ts` — shared call-site `sites[]` taint substrate (C-family). Inert today: no per-language taint model exists yet, so it produces zero TAINTED edges by design — the per-language source/sink models are a deliberate follow-up.
- Parameterized `bench/cfg/measure.mjs` by grammar+visitor (TS baselines byte-identical; added a `go:branchy` scaling scenario).

### Correctness

- **Real-parser regression tests** per language (not snapshot-pinning, which pins bugs as "expected"); every node-type/field literal grounded in a real parse and enforced by the CI gate.
- **EXIT-reachability** (the soundness precondition for the post-dominator / CDG passes) verified against the **production** `computeControlDependence` solver for every non-terminating shape — `while(true)`, `loop{}`, `for{}`, Go `select{}` — so CDG is never silently skipped.
- **Worker-mode pipeline** proves all 14 surfaces end-to-end through the real worker pool (BasicBlock + CFG + REACHING_DEF + CDG all > 0), e.g. Go 151 BB / 56 CDG, Ruby 122 / 45.

Surfaced + fixed two latent issues: 3 dead node-type literals in the TS visitor (`for_of_statement`, `async_function_declaration`, `async_arrow_function` — absent from every grammar it serves), and a stale `worker-roundtrip` assertion.

### Verification

868 tests across 40 files green (unit visitors + taint + integration); bench `--check` PASS (7 scenarios, TS fingerprints byte-identical); `tsc` clean; dist builds.

### Notes

- Per-unit commits (U1–U15) for granular review.
- `CHANGELOG.md` intentionally untouched (release-owned).
- Documented per-language limitations live in each visitor's doc-comment (e.g. async/await straight-line, generator/yield state machines, value-position switch/if inlined, RAII destructors).

Implements #2195 (the C-family scope) and extends it to the remaining languages.

title: perf(cfg): SSA-sparse reaching-defs to replace the dense-set worklist (deferred from #2195 U3)
body:
## Summary

Replace the dense GEN/KILL worklist reaching-defs solver with an **SSA-sparse** formulation that propagates facts along def-use chains instead of dense per-block lattice sets.

## Background

The reaching-defs solver (`gitnexus/src/core/ingestion/cfg/reaching-defs.ts`) is a classic monotone GEN/KILL worklist fixpoint. It is superlinear (≈ O(blocks²·³)) on pathologically deep loop nests because each pass re-propagates and re-merges dense binding sets.

During #2195 we evaluated **WTO / loop-aware iteration ordering** (Bourdoncle 1993) as the fix and **rejected it empirically** — 104/104 byte-identical but **0% faster**: the cost is inherent dense-set propagation + lattice merges, not visitation order, and the loop-body-skip shortcut is unsound on irreducible (goto) CFGs. See the no-go comment at the RPO-order site in `reaching-defs.ts` and `DEFAULT_PDG_MAX_REACHING_DEF_BLOCK_REVISITS` in `emit.ts` (PR #2197).

The shipped `blocks × 64` block-revisit ceiling is the **sound backstop** (a deep nest truncates to a sound-empty REACHING_DEF for that one function, never wrong facts) — but it is a coverage cap, not a perf fix.

## Proposed work

- Implement SSA-sparse reaching-defs (propagate along def-use chains; sparse evaluation graph) so deep-loop-nest functions solve in (near-)linear time and the ceiling becomes a safety net that effectively never fires on real code.

## Acceptance

- Byte-identical REACHING_DEF projection on the existing `reaching-defs-snapshot` + `bench --check` oracles.
- Measurable speedup on the `dense-bindings` bench scenario (currently the superlinear one).
- The `blocks × 64` ceiling stops firing on the dense-loop benchmark.

Deferred follow-up from #2195 (U3). Refs #2195.

title: perf(cfg): streaming/chunked PDG graph emit for full-kernel-scale repos
body:
## Summary

Stream/chunk the PDG graph emit (BasicBlock + REACHING_DEF / CDG / TAINTED) to the durable store incrementally, so peak RSS is bounded by chunk size rather than total graph size — unblocking full-kernel-scale repos.

## Background

PDG scale validation (PR #2197) ran clean up to the Linux kernel `fs/` subsystem:

| target | LOC | BasicBlock | CDG | peak RSS | PDG solve |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| postgres | ~1.4M | 350,971 | 257,407 | 5.4 GB | 4.46 s |
| linux `fs/` | 1.63M | 511,396 | 406,244 | 7.2 GB | 7.16 s |

The PDG **solve** is cheap (≤ 7 s). The constraint is **memory**: the whole graph is materialized in process during emit, so peak RSS tracks total graph size (~7 GB at 511K BasicBlocks). Extrapolating, the **full** kernel (~30M LOC) needs ~100 GB RAM and OOM-kills before finishing.

## Proposed work

- Stream the per-file CFG/PDG emit (see `gitnexus/src/core/ingestion/scope-resolution/pipeline/run.ts`) to the durable store in bounded chunks, flushing + releasing in-memory nodes/edges between chunks, so peak RSS is O(chunk) not O(graph).

## Acceptance

- A graph that currently OOMs (full kernel, or a synthetic 5M+ BasicBlock fixture) completes with bounded, configurable peak RSS.
- Byte-identical persisted graph vs the non-streamed path on the existing scale repos.

Surfaced by #2195 scale validation. Refs #2195.

title: perf(ingestion): large-repo analyze wall time dominated by graph-DB emit, not PDG
body:
## Summary

Large-repo `analyze` wall time is dominated by the parse + graph-DB-write pipeline, not the PDG layer. Investigate emit/persistence throughput.

## Background

PDG scale validation (PR #2197) timing breakdown:

| target | files | total wall | scope-resolution | emit | **pdg solve** |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| postgres | 2,398 | ~39 min | 20.6 s | 12.4 s | 4.46 s |
| linux `fs/` | 2,176 | ~65 min | 179 s | 171 s | **7.16 s** |

The analyze wall is ~1–1.6 s/file at scale. The PDG algorithms are a tiny fraction (kernel `fs/`: 7.2 s out of a 65-min wall). The time goes to parsing and **graph-DB persistence** of ~1M-edge graphs (LadybugDB writes), plus scope-resolution.

This is a pre-existing pipeline-throughput property — **not** a regression from the PDG work — but it dominates the at-scale experience.

## Proposed work

- Profile the emit/persistence path on the postgres / kernel-`fs/` benchmarks; investigate batched/bulk inserts, fewer write round-trips, or parallelized emit.

## Acceptance

- Measurable files/sec improvement on the postgres and kernel-`fs/` benchmarks with byte-identical graph content.

Surfaced by #2195 scale validation. Refs #2195.

title: fix(cfg): Kotlin if/when/try in expression position emit no control dependence (CDG under-populated)
body:
## Summary

Kotlin `if` / `when` / `try` used in **expression position** (the idiomatic Kotlin case) emit **no control-flow branches**, so the CDG (and RD precision) is severely under-populated.

## Evidence

Cross-language PDG validation (PR #2197) — CDG / BasicBlock ratio:

| lang | repo | CDG/BB |
|---|---|---|
| **kotlin** | **cashapp/turbine** | **3%** |
| **kotlin** | **JetBrains/Exposed** | **6%** |
| dart | dart-lang/args | 18% |
| swift | swift-argument-parser | 24% |
| rust | serde-rs/json | 30% |
| python | requests | 34% |
| go | gorilla/mux | 41% |
| java | JSON-java | 44% |
| c/c++ | zlib | 76% |

Two independent Kotlin repos sit at **3–6%**, far below every other language (18–76%) — including the other expression-conditional languages (Rust 30%, Swift 24%). `Exposed` is a branch-heavy SQL DSL (dialect/column-type dispatch) that should be control-dependence-dense, so this is a visitor gap, not linear code.

## Root cause

In `gitnexus/src/core/ingestion/cfg/visitors/kotlin.ts`, `visitStmt` routes the expression constructs through `isStatementPosition`:

```ts
case 'if_expression':
  return this.isStatementPosition(stmt) ? this.visitIf(stmt)   : this.visitSimple(stmt);
case 'when_expression':
  return this.isStatementPosition(stmt) ? this.visitWhen(stmt) : this.visitSimple(stmt);
case 'try_expression':
  return this.isStatementPosition(stmt) ? this.visitTry(stmt)  : this.visitSimple(stmt);
```

`isStatementPosition` is true only when the parent is `statements` / `control_structure_body`. So any `if`/`when`/`try` nested under a declaration, `return`, assignment, or argument — i.e. `val x = when (k) { ... }`, `return if (c) a else b`, `val v = try { ... } catch { ... }` — is collapsed into a single straight-line `visitSimple` block. Idiomatic Kotlin uses these as expressions pervasively, so most branching is lost.

## Proposed work

- Model value-position `when` (≥2 arms) / `if`-`else` / `try` as control flow, wiring the arm edges so the assigned binding / returned value is control-dependent on the condition. The per-arm value flowing into the binding is the data-dependence (RD) payoff.

## Acceptance

- A fixture `val x = when (k) { A -> 1; B -> 2 else -> 3 }` emits CDG edges for each arm; `val r = if (c) a else b` emits true/false arms.
- Kotlin CDG/BB on Exposed/turbine rises into the cross-language range.
- `kotlin-visitor` + cdg-snapshot/bench oracles updated.

Surfaced by #2195 cross-language validation. Refs #2195.

title: fix(cfg): harvest/finalizer soundness gaps in match-arm / guard-case / switch-expr bindings (Rust, Swift, Dart, C#)
body:
## Summary

The per-language CFG verification swarm (after #2195) found several **def/use harvest + finalizer** soundness gaps — distinct from CFG *topology* (which was verified sound, with three fixes landed in 25b5f036 / 3a6b9cf2 / 15579cce). These cause taint/reaching-defs **false negatives or false kills** even though the CFG shape is correct. Severity is below the topology bugs (they don't break EXIT-reachability), but each is a real soundness hole with a concrete repro.

## Findings

### 1. Rust — `match`-arm pattern bindings never harvested as defs (taint false-negative)
`visitMatch` (`rust.ts`) harvests guard *uses* and visits arm *bodies*, but never harvests `arm.childForFieldName('pattern')` for the binding defs. `RustHarvester` has `defPattern` + pre-declares match patterns in `prescan`, but there is no `armPatternFacts` call.
```rust
fn f(x: E) { match x { Some(n) => use_n(n), _ => z() } }   // `n` has a use but NO def/may-def anywhere
```
Impact: `match user_input { Some(n) => sink(n) }` can't propagate taint to `n`. Fix: add an `armPatternFacts` (likely **may-def**, like `while let`) attached to each arm body entry. Test gap: `rust-visitor.test.ts:205-219` asserts `hasUse(n)` but never `hasDef`.

### 2. Swift — `guard case` / `if case` enum-pattern bindings resolve to a synthetic global (taint false-negative)
`SwiftHarvester.declareOptionalBindings` (swift-harvest.ts:~222) scans only *direct* `bound_identifier` field children; `guard case .some(let v) = e` nests the binder inside a `pattern` node, so `v` is never declared → falls through to a synthetic `@module` global with a use but no def.
```swift
func f(e: E) { guard case .some(let v) = e else { return }; use(v) }   // `v` = synthetic global, no def
```
(`guard let`, `if let`, `switch case let .x(n)`, `for x in xs` all bind correctly — `switch` works because `prescan` has a `switch_pattern` case.)

### 3. Dart — `switch`-expression arm side-effects are HARD defs, not may-defs (false kill)
`DartHarvester.walkValue` has no `switch_expression` case, so an assignment in an arm becomes an unconditional def that **kills** the prior definition, even though only one arm runs. The dart-harvest module docstring *claims* this is a may-def, but the code doesn't implement it.
```dart
void f(int x){ int z = 0; var y = switch(x){ 1 => z = 10, _ => z = 20 }; }  // z = HARD def, kills z=0
```
Contrast (correct): ternary `x>0 ? (z=10) : (z=20)` → `z` is a may-def. Fix: walk `switch_expression_case` values under `this.conditional(...)`, mirroring the `conditional_expression` case.

### 4. C# — `using var f = …;` declaration form loses its dispose finalizer (missing finalizer edge)
The C# 8 `using var f = Open();` declaration form parses as `local_declaration_statement` (not `using_statement`), so `visitUsing`/`buildProtectedSynthetic` never run — no `dispose` block, no `finally-return` for a return in its scope. The block form `using (var f = …){ … }` is correct. Lower severity (a *missing* finalizer, never a wrong one), but the declaration form is now idiomatic.

## Acceptance
- Rust/Swift arm/case bindings appear as defs (or may-defs) reachable from the matched subject; Dart switch-expr arm writes are may-defs; C# `using var` emits the dispose finalizer. Each with a `hasDef`/`hasMayDef` regression test (the current suites only assert `hasUse`).

Found by the #2195 per-language CFG verification swarm. Refs #2195.

title: feat(cfg): model value-position switch/if expressions as control dependence (Java, C#, PHP, Dart, Swift)
body:
## Summary

Extend value-position branch CDG modeling (the Kotlin #2205 / Ruby fix) to the remaining expression-conditional languages. These are **not bugs** — value-position branches collapse inline today, which is a *sound over-approximation* (no missed control dependence, just lost arm-level precision) — but they leave CDG/taint blind to which arm runs.

## Background

`if`/`switch`/`match` used as a **value** (binding RHS, return, expression body) collapse into one block, emitting no `switch-case`/`cond-*` edges and 0 CDG for the arms. This was fixed for Kotlin (`val x = when(…)`, #2205, commit b672c49a) and Ruby (`x = if/case`, e9787a26) by modeling the branch and rejoining arms at a binding continuation. The verification swarm confirmed the same gap, all documented/intended, in:

| lang | value-position construct | confirmed |
|---|---|---|
| **Java** | `var y = switch(x){ case 1 -> a; default -> b; };` | ✅ 0 `switch-case`, 0 CDG (the gap ruby.ts explicitly cited) |
| **C#** | `var y = x switch { 1 => a, _ => b };` | ✅ inline, 0 CDG (mirrors Java) |
| **PHP** | `$y = match($x){ 1 => a, default => b };` | ✅ inline, 0 CDG; also a `throw` inside an arm emits no throw edge |
| **Dart** | `var y = switch(x){ 1 => a, _ => b };` (Dart 3) | ✅ inline (CFG); see also the harvest may-def gap in the sibling issue |
| **Swift** | `let x = if c { a } else { b }` / `let y = switch k {…}` (Swift 5.9) | ✅ inline, 0 CDG (latent, undocumented) |

## Proposed work

Model value-position `switch`/`if`/`match` arms as control flow in the binding/return carriers, mirroring `kotlin.ts` `visitBindBranch` / `ruby.ts` `assignmentBranch`. Reuse each visitor's existing `visitSwitch`/`visitIf`/`visitMatch`; route the value-branch carrier out of the coalescing path and rejoin arms at a continuation carrying the LHS def.

## Caveat (measured)

Impact varies **hugely** by language idiom — Kotlin `when` lifted Exposed CDG +55%, but Ruby `if/case` only ~+3% on rack/sinatra (value-position assignment is rare in idiomatic Ruby; much of the low CDG is micro-branch idiom). So scope per-language by how common the construct actually is, and measure before/after on a real repo. Java/C# `switch` expressions and Swift 5.9 `if`/`switch` are the higher-value targets (newer, increasingly idiomatic); PHP `match` and Dart `switch`-expr are moderate.

## Acceptance
- Per language: a value-position branch emits `switch-case`/`cond-*` edges + non-zero CDG for its arms; cfg snapshot/bench + a new visitor test updated; before/after CDG ratio measured on a representative repo.

Found by the #2195 per-language CFG verification swarm. Refs #2195, #2205.
