title: feat(cfg): model value-position branches as control dependence (#2205, #2207)
body:
## Value-position branch control-dependence modeling

Closes #2205. Closes #2207.

Until now the PDG/CFG layer only modeled a branch (`if` / `when` / `switch` / `match` / `try`) as control flow when it appeared in **statement** position. The same construct used as an **expression value** — the increasingly idiomatic form across modern languages — was collapsed into one straight-line block, so its arms produced **zero control-dependence (CDG) edges** and the binding's data flow was flattened. This PR teaches every affected language's CFG visitor to model the value-position form as a real dispatch, mirroring the established Rust `visitLet` / Kotlin `visitBindBranch` pattern.

The mechanism is uniform per language: **detect the carrier → route it out of `visitSeq` coalescing → visit the branch with the existing `visitIf`/`visitSwitch`/`visitWhen`/`visitMatch`/`visitTry` → rejoin the arms at a facts-only continuation that carries the binding's def** (the subject + arm-value uses stay on the branch's own blocks). The arms become control-dependent on the dispatch; the bound name is defined at the join.

### #2207 — value-position `switch`/`if`/`match` (Java, C#, PHP, Dart, Swift)

| lang | construct | carriers modeled |
|---|---|---|
| **Java** | `switch` expression (≥2 arms) | `var x = switch(…){…}`, `return switch(…){…}` |
| **C#** | `switch` expression (≥2 arms) | `var x = k switch {…}`, `return k switch {…}`, `=> k switch {…}` expression body |
| **PHP** | `match` (≥2 arms) | `$x = match(…){…}`, `return match(…){…}` |
| **Dart** | `switch` expression (Dart 3, ≥2 arms) | `var x = switch(…){…}`, `return switch(…){…}` |
| **Swift** | value-position `if`/`switch` (5.9+) | `let x = if … else …` / `let x = switch v {…}`, `return if/switch …` |

### #2205 — Kotlin's remaining deferred carriers

The initial #2205 work (shipped in #2197) modeled the `val/var x = <branch>`, `return`, and `fun f() = <branch>` carriers for `when`/`if`. This PR completes the deferred ones:

- **assignment RHS** — `x = when(k){…}` / `x = if(c)a else b` / `x = try{…}` (a plain `=` only; a compound `+=` and a plain-call RHS stay inline).
- **value-position `try`** — `val x = try{…}catch{…}` is now a modelable value branch (reusing `visitTry`), so the binding/assignment carriers route it through control flow.

### Deliberately left inline (documented gaps)

An **argument-position** branch (`f(when …)` / `var x = f(switch …)`), a **multi-declarator/multi-binding** decl, and (for Java/C#) an **assignment RHS** stay inline — the value flows to a single coalesced block. Micro-branches (`?:` ternary, Kotlin elvis `?:`/`?.`, `??`) are excluded by design, consistent with the existing visitors. Each visitor's header docstring records exactly which carriers are modeled vs inline.

### Soundness & verification

- **Per-construct unit tests** — 24 new regression tests across the six `*-visitor.test.ts` suites assert `switch-case`/`cond-true`/`cond-false`/`throw` edges, `computeControlDependence(cfg).edges.length > 0`, the binding def reaching its downstream use, and `isExitReachableFromAllBlocks(cfg)` (the CDG soundness gate). Inline-boundary tests pin the documented gaps so they can't silently change. The full CFG unit + integration suite is green (**676 tests**).
- **CDG snapshot oracle** — `test/integration/cfg/cdg-snapshot.test.ts` (the ten-functions TypeScript fixture) stays **byte-identical**.
- **Bench `--check`** — `bench/cfg/measure.mjs --check` is **byte-identical** across all 7 scenarios: the modeling is purely additive on the opt-in `--pdg` path; non-PDG analyze and untouched languages are unaffected.
- One Dart `#2206` may-def regression test was re-pointed to an argument-position fixture (which still coalesces) — under the new declaration model, a per-arm write is a real per-path def (more precise than the inline may-def), so the may-def harvest path is verified through the inline carrier instead.

### Impact varies by idiom

As the #2197 empirical pass established, the CDG yield of this class of fix depends heavily on how much a codebase uses the value form (Kotlin `when` was +55% on Exposed; Ruby `if`/`case` only +3%). The modeling is sound and regression-free everywhere; the aggregate gain shows up in codebases that actually use these expression forms. An empirical before/after on representative OSS repos follows in a comment.

Each language is its own commit. No `CHANGELOG` edits (release-owned).

title: perf(cfg): SSA-sparse reaching-defs to replace the dense-set worklist (#2201)
body:
## Summary

Replaces the dense GEN/KILL worklist reaching-definitions solver (`gitnexus/src/core/ingestion/cfg/reaching-defs.ts`) with an **SSA-sparse** formulation, resolving the WTO no-go deferral recorded in #2195/#2197. Closes #2201.

The dense worklist is superlinear (≈O(blocks²) work) on loop-heavy / many-binding functions because it re-materializes a dense per-block lattice and re-merges every binding on every fixpoint pass. The new solver builds pruned SSA — **Cooper-Harvey-Kennedy dominators → Cytron dominance frontiers + φ-placement → stack renaming over a synthetic entry → SCC-condensed φ-walkback** — and answers block-entry reaching-set queries from the def-use graph, skipping pass-through blocks and capturing loop merges statically (depth-independent).

## Approach (and an honest pivot)

External research first pointed at a **per-variable sparse worklist** as the lowest byte-identity risk. It was implemented and proven byte-identical — but measurement showed it was **2–4× slower** on the `dense-bindings` target (it still walks pass-through blocks per binding). The genuinely faster, asymptotically-better fix is true SSA, which is what shipped.

Production **auto-dispatches** (`computeInSetsAuto`): SSA for looping functions ≥16 blocks (where construction amortizes), the dense worklist everywhere else (small / loop-free) and for the throw-edge / unreachable-block shapes the SSA path does not model. The dense solver is retained as the differential **equivalence oracle**. Because both are held byte-identical, dispatch is a pure performance heuristic.

## Results (measured, `bench/cfg/measure.mjs --check`)

- **`dense-bindings` rd_scaling 5.2 → 0.86** (linear; **5×–23× faster** absolute, asymptotic in N). Budget tightened 10 → 2.
- **`deep-nest` (new scenario): the `blocks×64` ceiling stops firing** — under the production budget the SSA solver computes full facts (164 ≥ floor) where the dense worklist would truncate to empty.
- **Tiny / loop-free functions: ~1.0× (no regression)** — they take the dense path.

## Acceptance (#2201)

- ✅ **Byte-identical** REACHING_DEF projection: the committed snapshot oracle, taint (M3/M4) snapshots, summary-harvest, and the 13-language `--pdg` worker pipeline are all unchanged. Validated by a differential fuzz comparing SSA vs the dense oracle across **300k random CFGs (~1.2M comparisons)** + a 100k run that exercises the production auto-dispatcher's SSA branch at ≥16 blocks.
- ✅ **Measurable speedup** on `dense-bindings`.
- ✅ **Ceiling stops firing** on the deep-loop benchmark.

CFG fingerprints are unchanged — CFG construction is untouched; only the in-memory solve changed.

## Tests / validation

- `test/unit/cfg/reaching-defs-equivalence.test.ts` — permanent differential fuzz (dense oracle vs SSA + auto-dispatcher), shape-coverage guard incl. `hadLargeLoop` (the production SSA-dispatch path), canonical hard CFGs (irreducible, self-loop, throw, diamond, unreachable, back-edge-into-entry).
- `test/unit/cfg/reaching-defs.test.ts` — unit hazards + R5 contrast (dense ceiling fires, SSA converges).
- `reaching-defs-snapshot`, `taint`, `summary-harvest`, `pipeline-pdg` (13 langs, post-build), `bench --check` (8 scenarios) — all green. `tsc` clean.

## Notes

- `gitnexus/CHANGELOG.md` intentionally untouched (release-owned).
- The plan lives at `docs/plans/2026-06-15-001-perf-ssa-sparse-reaching-defs-plan.md` (the repo gitignores `docs/`, so it is a local decision artifact).

## Residual Review Findings

From the multi-agent code review (run `20260615-145253-4d86bad5`). None are merge-blockers; all are tracked follow-ups (the byte-identity contract is fuzz-proven and all oracles pass).

- **[P2] #7 (correctness/robustness)** `reaching-defs.ts` (~`computeInSetsSparse`): the SSA path is *less tolerant* than the dense solver of a corrupted/stale durable store — an out-of-range binding index in `defs`/`uses` throws (crashing the file's taint + summary-harvest layers) where dense tolerated it as a Map key. `taint/emit.ts` and `taint/summary-harvest-driver.ts` lack the `hasEmitSafeFacts` gate that `emitFileReachingDefs` has (pre-existing gap that SSA newly exposes). Fix: range-check binding indices in `solveReachingDefs` (fall back to dense/no-facts), or gate the taint/harvest call sites.
- **[P2] #8 (perf)** `computeInSetsAuto` dispatch: wide many-merge-point looping functions (≥16 blocks + loop + many bindings) can run ~2.7× slower / ~2× heavier under SSA while producing the identical truncated result (`maxFacts` does not bound SSA value-graph construction). Fix: gate SSA on an estimated-work signal beyond block-count+loop, or add a value-graph size cap that falls back to dense; add a bench scenario for the shape.
- **[P2] #9 (perf)** `reachByScc` unions copy full reaching-sets across SCC boundaries — potential O(defs²) at high-fan-out φ merge points (not covered by the one-binding `deep-nest` bench). Fix: flat sorted-array / lazy SCC reach sets; add a many-bindings-many-merges bench gate.
- **[P2] #10 (api-contract)** Deep-loop functions that previously truncated (empty REACHING_DEF) now compute full facts (the intended R5 win) — repos indexed on the prior version carry stale partial coverage until reindex. Verify the pdg/RepoMeta stamp forces a full writeback on solver-version change.
- **[P2] #11 (maintainability)** `reaching-defs.ts` grew ~496 → ~1050 lines; `computeInSetsSparse` bundles dominators + DF + φ-placement + renaming + SCC. Extract the sub-stages into helpers or split into `cfg/reaching-defs-sparse.ts`. (project-standards review found no hard line-count violation.)
- **[P3] #12 (perf)** Hot-path micro-allocations in the shared sweep / SSA setup (`keys.sort` per use, `sameStmtDefs` spread+Set per stmt, per-block Set in `dPredsX` dedup) — deliberately not auto-applied (hot-path, byte-identity-sensitive; marginal). Reuse scratch buffers; verify via the fuzz.

title: perf(lbug): cut graph-DB emit/persistence wall time (#2203)
body:
## Summary

Large-repo `analyze` wall time is dominated by the parse + graph-DB-write pipeline, not the PDG layer (Refs #2203: kernel `fs/` was 65 min wall, of which PDG solve was 7.2 s). This targets the **graph-DB emit/persistence path** with three byte-identical-safe changes, plus the profiling and measurement that were missing to attribute the wall in the first place.

The biggest win: relationships used to be written to a monolithic `relations.csv`, then **re-read line-by-line (a regex per edge) and re-split** into per-label-pair files before `COPY` — the entire ~1M-edge set written and read twice. They're now routed to their per-pair file directly during the single emit pass, so the monolithic write, the re-read, and the per-edge regex are gone.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  subgraph BEFORE
    G1[graph ~1M edges] -->|emit| RC[relations.csv]
    RC -->|re-read + regex/edge| SP[split]
    SP --> PP1[rel_A_B.csv ...] --> DB1[(LadybugDB)]
  end
  subgraph AFTER
    G2[graph ~1M edges] -->|emit: route by label| PP2[rel_A_B.csv ...] --> DB2[(LadybugDB)]
  end
  style RC fill:#fdd,stroke:#c00
  style SP fill:#fdd,stroke:#c00
```

## What changed

- **`PROF_LBUG_LOAD` profiling** — `loadGraphToLbug` was un-timed; the analyze "emit" number is the *scope-resolution* emit bucket, not the DB-write path. Setting `PROF_LBUG_LOAD=1` now logs one `[lbug-load prof] csv-emit=… copy-nodes=… copy-rels=… fallback=… total=… (N nodes, M rels)` line per load. Zero-cost when off (mirrors `PROF_SCOPE_RESOLUTION`).
- **Direct per-pair relationship emit** — a shared `RelPairRouter` routes each edge to its `rel_{from}_{to}.csv` during emit, applying the same `getNodeLabel` + valid-table filter the old split did. `splitRelCsvByLabelPair` is **retained as a differential oracle** (a byte-identity test diffs the new output against it).
- **Per-row microtask elimination** — `BufferedCSVWriter.addRow` awaited an already-resolved promise on every buffered row (millions of microtask ticks at scale); it now returns a promise only on an actual flush, and the node loop awaits once per iteration.
- **Build-free emit bench + CI gate** — `bench/emit-persistence/measure.mjs` times `streamAllCSVsToDisk` at two scales and gates an order-independent CSV-line fingerprint (the byte-identity guard) plus a linear scaling budget. Wired into `ci-tests.yml` alongside the cfg/scope-capture benches.

## Byte-identical graph content

Non-negotiable per the issue. Guaranteed three ways: the new differential test asserts the direct-emit per-pair files are byte-for-byte identical to the retained oracle (including `skipped`/`total` accounting, the `comm_`/`proc_` label prefixes, and invalid-label skips); the bench fingerprint (`04096714…`) is unchanged and CI-gated; and the existing `basicblock-roundtrip` / `lbug-core-adapter` COPY round-trips pass unchanged.

## Emit-path measurements (synthetic bench)

| scale | nodes | edges | emit median |
|---|---|---|---|
| small | 2,400 | 2,400 | ~48 ms |
| large | 9,600 | 9,600 | ~190 ms |

Scaling ratio ~1.0 (linear); fingerprint stable. The bench measures CSV generation only — the LadybugDB `COPY` half needs a live DB, so its timing lives in the `PROF_LBUG_LOAD` breakdown.

## Scope / deferred

- **`COPY` parallelism is deferred.** `PARALLEL=false` and the single writable connection are load-bearing (LadybugDB is single-writer); concurrent COPY needs empirical capability validation that the new `PROF_LBUG_LOAD` breakdown is the prerequisite for. This PR makes that follow-up *measurable*, not blind.
- **At-scale numbers** (postgres / kernel-`fs/`) are a maintainer-run validation — the in-repo evidence is the synthetic emit bench delta + the `PROF_LBUG_LOAD` breakdown, not a reproduction of the 65-min run.

## Test plan

- `test/unit/rel-pair-routing.test.ts` (new): router error / backpressure / teardown via an injected mock stream; `getNodeLabel` prefixes.
- `test/integration/csv-pipeline.test.ts`: differential byte-identity vs the oracle + the migrated determinism block.
- `test/integration/lbug-load-prof.test.ts` (new): `PROF_LBUG_LOAD` gate on/off.
- `bench/emit-persistence/measure.mjs --check`: fingerprint + scaling gate.
- `basicblock-roundtrip` + `lbug-core-adapter`: full COPY round-trips, unchanged.

Refs #2203.

title: perf(cfg): streaming/chunked PDG graph emit for full-kernel-scale repos (#2202)
body:
## Summary

Streams the per-file PDG/CFG graph emit (BasicBlock nodes + CFG / REACHING_DEF / CDG / POST_DOMINATE / TAINTED / SANITIZES edges) to CSV-on-disk **during** the `--pdg` scope-resolution emit loop instead of materializing it in the in-memory `KnowledgeGraph`. Peak RSS for the PDG layer becomes **O(chunk buffer)** rather than **O(graph)** — unblocking full-kernel-scale repos (the layer is ~7 GB at 511K BasicBlocks today; the full kernel would need ~100 GB and OOMs).

Closes #2202.

> ### ⚠️ Stacked on #2203 — do not merge as-is
> #2202 depends on the #2203 emit-persistence path (`streamAllCSVsToDisk`, per-pair CSV routing, `BufferedCSVWriter`), which is **not yet on `main`**. This branch was built on a snapshot of #2203 and carries 4 `#2203 U1–U4` commits (`8681c6a6..e305561d`) as ancestors. The canonical #2203 branch (`perf/2203-emit-persistence`, currently `760f3ce8`) has since **diverged** — notably a ~677-line `csv-generator.ts` rewrite — so those ancestor commits here are **stale**.
>
> **Merge process:** land #2203 first, then rebase this branch onto the updated `main` (the rebase drops the redundant #2203 ancestors and leaves only the `#2202` commits). Opened as **draft** until then. **Review focus: the `#2202 U1–U6` + `fix(review)` commits.**

## Approach

A `PdgEmitSink` (`gitnexus/src/core/lbug/pdg-emit-sink.ts`) is a **write-routing façade** over the `KnowledgeGraph`: the PDG emit functions are write-only and compute every edge endpoint by deterministic id, so the sink routes BasicBlock node rows + PDG edge rows straight to bounded **synchronous** CSV writers (the emit loop is synchronous — an async stream writer couldn't apply backpressure mid-loop and would buffer unbounded) and never stores them. Everything else (structural nodes/edges, the whole-program M4 `TAINT_PATH` edges) is delegated to the real graph unchanged. At persist time `loadGraphToLbug` COPYs the streamed CSVs (a manifest) alongside the structural CSVs.

- **Opt-in, off by default** (`GITNEXUS_STREAM_PDG_EMIT` / `streamPdgEmit` option) ⇒ byte-identical default behavior.
- **Full-rebuild only** (`force === true`): the incremental writeback reads BasicBlocks back from the in-memory graph, so streaming is gated to full rebuilds (which is the OOM target anyway).
- **Byte-identical** persisted graph: the sink reuses the shared `buildBasicBlockRow` / `buildRelRow` row builders and mirrors the graph's first-writer-wins dedup, so the streamed CSV row **set** equals the whole-graph emit's.
- **Memory-only knobs** (`GITNEXUS_PDG_EMIT_CHUNK_SIZE`) are not stamped into `RepoMeta.pdg`, so toggling never trips `pdgModeMismatch`.

Plan: `docs/plans/2026-06-15-003-perf-streaming-pdg-emit-plan.md` (local).

## Implementation units

- **U1** `refactor(lbug)` — extract shared `buildBasicBlockRow` + `BASICBLOCK_CSV_HEADER` in `csv-generator.ts`.
- **U2** `perf(lbug)` — `PdgEmitSink` façade + bounded synchronous CSV writers.
- **U3** `perf(lbug)` — `GITNEXUS_STREAM_PDG_EMIT` / `GITNEXUS_PDG_EMIT_CHUNK_SIZE`, full-rebuild gate (`resolveStreamPdgEmit`), excluded from `pdgModeMismatch`.
- **U4** `perf(lbug)` — route the `--pdg` emit through the sink (`run.ts`), own its lifecycle + manifest passthrough (`phase.ts` → `PipelineResult`).
- **U5** `perf(lbug)` — `loadGraphToLbug` COPYs the streamed manifest alongside the structural CSVs.
- **U6** `test(lbug)` — byte-identity + bounded-RSS bench (`measure-streaming.mjs --check`) + full-pipeline streamed-vs-non-streamed integration test.
- **`fix(review)`** — applied cross-engine review feedback (see below).

## Code review (multi-persona, pre-PR)

8 reviewers (correctness, adversarial, performance, reliability, api-contract, maintainability, testing, project-standards) ran against the `#2202` diff. They surfaced — and this PR **fixes** — a cross-corroborated **P1 byte-identity bug**: a `.ts` module imported by a `.vue` SFC is PDG-emitted in *both* the TypeScript and Vue context passes; the in-memory graph dedups by id, but the original dedup-free sink wrote the rows twice (byte-identity drift + a BasicBlock PRIMARY KEY conflict masked by `IGNORE_ERRORS`). The fix originally restored per-id dedup parity with the graph’s Map; the later tri-review (below) showed that retained every id for the whole run (O(total ids) ≈ 4 GB at full-kernel, defeating the O(chunk) claim), so review #1 **replaced it with per-file dedup**. Plus reliability fixes (writer-fd cleanup via try/finally + fd-safe close, `fs.writeSync` partial-write loop, manifest preserved on the `!anyRan` path) and cleanups (dead-field removal, chunk-size guard, CI-gated the streaming bench).

### Residual review findings (advisory — no blocking actionable work remains)
- **P2 (maintainability)** — `phase.ts` introduces an `ingestion → lbug` import. *Accepted:* the project-standards reviewer found no rule violated; it's the natural orchestration→persistence direction. A "move the manifest type to `src/types/` and inject the sink via options" refactor was judged not worth the churn.
- **P3 (api-contract)** — the full-pipeline test passes `streamPdgEmit` without `force`. *Intentional:* `runPipelineFromRepo` is the lower-level API; the force gate is unit-tested separately in `stream-pdg-emit-config.test.ts`.
- **P3 (testing)** — no test for the no-storage-path fallback branch or the fd-leak-on-throw path. *Low priority:* both branches are simple and fd cleanup is now structurally guaranteed by try/finally + idempotent `close()`.

## Tri-review findings addressed (post-PR)

A `/pr-tri-review` (Codex + GitNexus swarm + CE personas) posted a `COMMENT` review on this PR. All 8 findings are now fixed, **one commit each** (review #6 folded into #1 + #4, since the per-id seen-sets it concerned were removed):

| # | Sev | Finding | Fix | Commit |
|---|-----|---------|-----|--------|
| 1 | P2 (headline) | "O(chunk) peak RSS" overstated — per-id `seenNodeIds`/`seenRelIds` retained every id for the whole run (O(total ids), ~4 GB extrapolated) | Replace per-id dedup with **per-file** dedup (`Set<filePath>` in `run.ts`, O(files) ≈ O(chunk)); the sink is now a pure pass-through | `434bca3e` |
| 2 | P2 | Streamed `pdg-csv` dir not relocated on Windows non-ASCII paths (structural `csv` dir is) → bulk COPY can fail | Shared `resolveNativeSafeStorageDir` mirrors the ASCII-safe `os.tmpdir()` relocation for the streamed dir | `7c0d2dbb` |
| 3 | P2 (latent) | `loadGraphToLbug` manifest merge silently overwrote on key collision | Disjoint-key assertions throw loudly before the COPY (a BasicBlock-leak-into-graph would otherwise drop a structural CSV) | `f23cc08d` |
| 4 / 6 | P3 | Sink IO errors (disk-full `writeSync`, EMFILE `openSync`) swallowed by the emit loop's per-file CFG try/catch → partial manifest COPYed silently | Poison the writer / record open-failures; `finalize` surfaces any IO fault loudly so a truncated CSV is never COPYed | `97dcddda` |
| 5 | P3 | Docstring claimed "byte-identical regardless of order"; the sink doesn't re-sort under `GITNEXUS_SORT_GRAPH_OUTPUT` | Narrow the claim to **set-identical / DB-identical** (CSVs are deleted post-COPY; their byte order is never observed) | `071c074c` |
| 7 | test | Bounded-retention test was vacuous (`TOTAL=50, chunk=2` → everything flushed before the mid-stream read) | `TOTAL=51` (non-multiple of the chunk) so the final row is genuinely buffered; assert exactly `TOTAL-1` flushed mid-stream | `74abd37f` |
| 8 | test | No real Vue+TS cross-pass fixture (dedup only covered synthetically); no no-storage-path fallback test | Real `.vue`-imports-`.ts` fixture (verified out-of-band: disabling dedup doubles 33→61 rows) + no-storage fallback test | `023e0bd7` |

The earlier pre-PR "Residual review findings (advisory)" P3 testing gap (no-storage-path fallback) is **now closed** by review #8.

## Test plan

- `pdg-emit-sink.test.ts` — sink routing, byte-identity vs `streamAllCSVsToDisk`, bounded retention, **duplicate-emission dedup parity** (regression for the P1), invalid-label skip. ✅
- `stream-pdg-emit-config.test.ts` — gating (pdg + force + signal), chunk-size resolution, no `pdgModeMismatch` on streaming knobs. ✅
- `pdg-emit-streaming-roundtrip.test.ts` — streamed manifest → real LadybugDB COPY round-trip (BasicBlocks + all PDG edge types, no double-COPY). ✅
- `pipeline-pdg-streaming.test.ts` — full pipeline streamed vs non-streamed: 0 resident BasicBlocks under streaming, manifest counts equal the baseline. ✅
- `measure-streaming.mjs --check` — byte-identity fingerprint + `resident_basic_blocks === 0` at 7.2K BasicBlocks / 36K edges; **now CI-gated**. ✅
- Regression: `pipeline-pdg.test.ts` (default `--pdg` path unchanged), `csv-pipeline.test.ts`, `basicblock-roundtrip.test.ts` — all green.

title: feat(analyze): private GitHub repos via PAT + Azure DevOps Server support (#2076, #2210)
body:
## Summary

Combines two community contributions onto current `main` as one mergeable branch, with conflicts resolved and original authors credited as co-authors:

- **#2076** — optional Personal Access Token for cloning **private GitHub repos** (by @apecia-kenghzou)
- **#2210** — **Azure DevOps Server** (on-premise) + cloud repository support (by @cagriman)

Both PRs touched the same files (`git-clone.ts`, `api.ts`, `RepoAnalyzer.tsx`, the locale JSON, and `git-clone.test.ts`); #2076 also conflicted with `main` after its `/api/analyze` refactor. This branch resolves all of that in one place.

## What each feature does

**Private GitHub repos (#2076).** An optional PAT field on the GitHub mode of the analyze form. The token travels form → `POST /api/analyze` → `cloneOrPull` and is injected into git via the `GIT_CONFIG_*` env protocol (`http.extraHeader = "Authorization: Basic …"`), so it never appears in argv, the URL, or the process listing. Transient (form state only), never persisted, cleared on mode change, cancel, and completion. Backend validates token shape (1–256 chars, restricted charset) to block CRLF header smuggling.

**Azure DevOps (#2210).** `resolveRemoteUrl` detects the `_git` path pattern for self-hosted (`AZURE_DEVOPS_URL`) and cloud (`dev.azure.com` / `*.visualstudio.com`) instances, injecting a PAT from `AZURE_DEVOPS_PAT` via `-c http.extraHeader` (scoped to the single git invocation, never written to `.git/config`). New Azure DevOps onboarding tab in `RepoAnalyzer`, the `AzureDevops` icon, i18n strings (en, zh-CN), and `.env.example` docs.

## Conflict resolution notes

- **`git-clone.ts`** — `runGit` now takes a single options bag `{ token?, url? }` carrying both mechanisms: `token` → `buildGitEnv` (env-based GitHub PAT), `url` → `buildAuthArgs` (arg-based Azure PAT). The two auth paths are independent; a request may use either, both, or neither.
- **`api.ts`** — re-threaded #2076's token destructuring + validation onto `main`'s refactored `/api/analyze` route (kept `requireLocalhostOrigin` and the simplified path validation), and threaded the token into the actual `cloneOrPull` call.
- **`RepoAnalyzer.tsx`** — kept `main`'s extracted `trackJob` helper and re-homed the GitHub-token reset into it; the GitHub-token UI and the Azure tab/input coexist.

## Testing

- `npx tsc --noEmit` clean (gitnexus) and `npx tsc -b --noEmit` clean (gitnexus-web)
- `git-clone.test.ts` 78/78 (covers `buildGitEnv` token injection + `isAzureDevOpsUrl` / Azure URL handling)
- `rate-limit.test.ts` 23/23
- pre-commit gate (prettier + eslint + tsc, both packages) passed

## Relationship to existing PRs

Supersedes #2076 and #2210 — once this merges, both can be closed. Credit is preserved via `Co-authored-by` trailers on each commit.

title: perf(lbug): overlap node COPY with relationship emit (#2203)
body:
## Summary

Finishes the deferred **"parallelized emit"** leg of #2203. PR #2215 cut the relationship write round-trips (the `RelPairRouter` direct per-pair emit) and added the `PROF_LBUG_LOAD` profiling it explicitly framed as the prerequisite for parallelizing the load — but left the parallelism itself deferred behind an open question: is it even safe given LadybugDB's single-writer model?

This change answers that question and lands the one form of parallelism that is safe: **node `COPY` now runs concurrently with the relationship CSV emit pass**, so the time spent loading nodes into the DB overlaps the time spent serializing ~1M edges to disk instead of running strictly after it.

External research (Kuzu, which LadybugDB mirrors) ruled out the two obvious alternatives, so the scope is deliberate rather than conservative:

- **Intra-`COPY` parallelism (`PARALLEL=true`) is unsafe for our data and stays off.** Kuzu's parallel CSV reader splits the file into byte ranges parsed concurrently and cannot find line boundaries when a quoted field contains an embedded newline ([kuzudb/kuzu#5778](https://github.com/kuzudb/kuzu/issues/5778); error: *"Quoted newlines are not supported in parallel CSV reader. Please specify PARALLEL=FALSE"*). Our `content`/`text` columns hold source code, so quoted multiline fields are guaranteed. `PARALLEL=false` is therefore **mandatory for correctness** — this PR locks it in as a tested invariant.
- **Concurrent `COPY` statements are impossible** — there is at most one active write transaction, so parallel COPYs would just serialize at the DB.

The remaining safe lever is pipeline-overlap: node `COPY` uses the single DB connection and never touches the rel files; the relationship emit pass writes `rel_*.csv` files and never touches the connection — disjoint resources. The relationship `COPY` still waits for node `COPY` (foreign-key precondition), so the DB load order and content are unchanged.

```mermaid
flowchart TB
  subgraph BEFORE["Serial — before"]
    direction LR
    NE1[node CSV emit] --> RE1[rel CSV emit] --> CN1[COPY nodes] --> CR1[COPY rels]
  end
  subgraph AFTER["Overlap — this PR"]
    direction LR
    NE2[node CSV emit] --> RDY{{node CSVs flushed}}
    RDY --> CN2[COPY nodes]
    RDY --> RE2[rel CSV emit]
    CN2 --> J{{join}}
    RE2 --> J
    J --> CR2[COPY rels]
  end
```

## What changed

- **`streamAllCSVsToDisk` exposes the node/rel phase boundary** via an optional, additive `onNodePhaseComplete` hook fired right after every node CSV is flushed and before the relationship pass writes any `rel_*.csv`. The node-file manifest construction is hoisted above the rel pass and reused in the return, so output is **byte-for-byte identical** when no callback is supplied (the only existing caller is unchanged).
- **`loadGraphToLbug` overlaps node `COPY` with rel emit.** Node `COPY` (extracted into `copyNodeCSVs`) starts in the hook and runs while the rel pass continues; the relationship `COPY` waits on it at a foreign-key barrier. The in-flight node-`COPY` promise is captured so a mid-emit failure can't leak as an unhandled rejection, and node-`COPY` errors are rethrown at the barrier.
- **`PARALLEL=false` is now a tested correctness invariant**, not a quiet default: a live-DB test round-trips a multiline-quoted field byte-for-byte (it fails loudly if anyone flips the flag), plus a static guard on the generated `COPY` queries, plus a source comment citing kuzudb/kuzu#5778.
- **`GITNEXUS_SERIAL_LBUG_LOAD=1` escape hatch** forces the legacy strictly-sequential path — both an operator rollback and the differential-test oracle.
- **`PROF_LBUG_LOAD` gains `mode=overlap|serial`**; under overlap, `copy-nodes` becomes the *residual* node-`COPY` time after emit returns (it trends to 0 as the overlap hides node `COPY` behind rel emit).

## Byte-identical graph content (issue acceptance)

Non-negotiable per the issue. Guaranteed three ways: the new `lbug-load-overlap.test.ts` loads the same fixture via the overlap path and the serial escape hatch into two fresh DBs and asserts they are content-equivalent (per-table node counts, per-type edge counts, byte-for-byte multiline `content`/`text`, and identical `insertedRels`/`skippedRels`/`warnings`); the `bench/emit-persistence/measure.mjs` fingerprint is unchanged (this change does not alter emitted bytes); and `basicblock-roundtrip` / `csv-pipeline` differential-oracle tests pass unchanged.

## Measurement

The saved wall time is `min(copy-nodes, rel-emit)` — workload-dependent. Per the #2215 precedent, **at-scale numbers (postgres / kernel-`fs/`) are a maintainer-run validation** via `PROF_LBUG_LOAD`; the in-repo evidence is correctness (the differential gate) plus the now-attributable `mode=overlap` breakdown. The synthetic emit bench is DB-free and cannot observe the COPY overlap, so its fingerprint staying constant is the byte-identity guard, not the throughput measurement.

## Test plan

- `test/integration/copy-parallel-invariant.test.ts` (new): multiline-quoted content round-trips with `PARALLEL=false`; static guard that every `COPY` query keeps `PARALLEL=false`.
- `test/integration/lbug-load-overlap.test.ts` (new): overlap-vs-serial differential content equivalence.
- `test/integration/csv-pipeline.test.ts`: `onNodePhaseComplete` fires once, after node CSVs exist and before any `rel_*.csv`; callback-absent output is byte-identical.
- `test/integration/lbug-load-prof.test.ts`: asserts `mode=overlap` on the default path; zero-cost when off.
- `basicblock-roundtrip` + `bench/emit-persistence/measure.mjs --check`: full COPY round-trip + fingerprint, unchanged.

Refs #2203. Builds on #2215.

## Residual Review Findings (all resolved)

The tri-review residuals are now fixed — each as its own commit:

- **P1 — rel-emit failure with node COPY in flight** → test added (`eaf56c67`): the emit error surfaces with no unhandled rejection (plus the both-fail diagnostic).
- **P1 — node-COPY hard-failure rethrow at the FK barrier** → test added (`b767f0f8`).
- **P2 — overlap-win attenuation** → periodic `setImmediate` yield in the relationship-emit loop (`a3149c18`); byte-identical (emit fingerprint unchanged). At-scale `PROF_LBUG_LOAD` validation remains maintainer-run.
- **P2 — manifest rel-pair collision test** → added for both the overlap and serial paths (`8de257e9`).
- **P2 — duplicated `IGNORE_ERRORS` retry** → extracted `copyCsvWithRetry` (`c3d4136c`), behavior-preserving.
- **Advisory — non-transactionality** → documented on `loadGraphToLbug` (`63ec345a`).

The CodeQL `js/insecure-temporary-file` alert was fixed earlier (`917ae46a`; 0 open alerts).

title: group impact returns cross=0 — Kuzu rejects multi-label MATCH in manifest-extractor.js
body:
## Summary

`group impact` always returns `cross: 0` even when cross-repo dependencies exist.

## Root cause (traced)

`detect.workspace_deps` works and contracts are created correctly. However, `resolveSymbol` in `manifest-extractor.js` generates a Kuzu query with a multi-label MATCH pattern:

```cypher
MATCH (n:Function|Method|Class|...|CodeElement)
```

Kuzu rejects this syntax — multi-label alternation in MATCH is not supported.

## Impact

Cross-repo impact analysis is silently broken. `intra` counts are correct; `cross` is always 0.

## Environment

- GitNexus version: 1.6.7
- OS: linux/x64
- Group: 2 repos (pi-workflow-sdk, pi-airflow-script)
- `detect.workspace_deps: true`

title: Feature Request: Julia and Zig Language Support
body:
### Area

gitnexus (CLI / core / indexing / MCP server)

### Problem or opportunity

## Summary

Add support for **Julia** (`.jl`) and **Zig** (`.zig`) languages to GitNexus — parsing, symbol extraction, import resolution, and scope-resolution where feasible.

## Motivation

Both languages are actively used in data science, scientific computing (Julia) and systems programming (Zig). Adding them would make GitNexus useful for those ecosystems.



### Proposed solution

## Tree-sitter Grammars

Both have mature, maintained tree-sitter grammars with native Node bindings:

| Language | Grammar | Notes |
|----------|---------|-------|
| Julia | [`tree-sitter-grammars/tree-sitter-julia`](https://github.com/tree-sitter-grammars/tree-sitter-julia) | Published as [`tree-sitter-julia`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/tree-sitter-julia) on npm |
| Zig | [`tree-sitter-grammars/tree-sitter-zig`](https://github.com/tree-sitter-grammars/tree-sitter-zig) | Published as [`tree-sitter-zig`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/tree-sitter-zig) on npm |

Both grammars build cleanly with `tree-sitter build` (native DLL) on Windows x64 without requiring `node-gyp` or Python.

## Required Changes

### 1. `gitnexus-shared/src/languages.ts` — Add enum members

```typescript
export enum SupportedLanguages {
  // ... existing ...
  Julia = 'julia',
  Zig = 'zig',
}
2. gitnexus/src/core/ingestion/languages/ — Add providers
- languages/julia.ts — LanguageProvider with:
- Extensions: ['.jl']
- Tree-sitter queries for: @definition.function (function/macro), @definition.class (struct/abstract type), @import.statement + @import.source (import X / using X), @call.name
- Import semantics: namespace (Julia's module system resembles Python's)
- MRO: first-wins (Julia has multiple dispatch, not classical inheritance)
- languages/zig.ts — LanguageProvider with:
- Extensions: ['.zig']
- Tree-sitter queries for: @definition.function (fn), @definition.class (struct/enum/union), @import.statement + @import.source (@import("...")), @call.name
- Import semantics: named
- MRO: none
3. gitnexus/src/core/tree-sitter/parser-loader.ts — Register grammars
[SupportedLanguages.Julia]: {
  load: () => require('tree-sitter-julia'),
  unavailableNote: 'Julia parsing requires `tree-sitter-julia`. ...',
},
[SupportedLanguages.Zig]: {
  load: () => require('tree-sitter-zig'),
  unavailableNote: 'Zig parsing requires `tree-sitter-zig`. ...',
},
4. gitnexus/package.json — Add dependencies
{
  "dependencies": {
    "tree-sitter-julia": "^0.23.0",
    "tree-sitter-zig": "^0.5.0"
  }
}
5. (Optional) SCOPE_RESOLVERS — Scope-resolution hooks
For deeper analysis (import resolution, binding resolution, type extraction), each language needs a ScopeResolver implementation. Julia's module/import system is closer to Python's; Zig's @import is more like Go's package-level import. A basic ScopeResolver can follow in a follow-up PR.
Testing
Both grammars have been verified to parse correctly with the standalone tree-sitter CLI:
- Julia: Parses function definitions, type annotations (::), struct declarations, string interpolation, and module/import statements.
- Zig: Parses function declarations, struct/enum/union types, @import expressions, variable declarations, and control flow.
Example AST outputs are available if needed.
Scope
This request covers basic parsing and graph construction. Full scope-resolution (binding resolution, type propagation, MRO) for both languages can be added incrementally in later PRs.

### Alternatives considered

_No response_

### Acceptance criteria

_No response_

### Constraints

_No response_

### Contribution

- [ ] I am willing to open a PR for this (may need design discussion first).

title: feat(spring): detect scheduled event and messaging handlers
body:
Parent tracking issue: #1225

Status: remaining work

Goal
Treat non HTTP Spring handlers as application entry points.

Scope
Detect Scheduled methods, EventListener methods, common message listener annotations, and listener style methods that Spring invokes without an HTTP route.

Acceptance criteria
1. Scheduled methods are marked as entry points.
2. Event listener methods are marked as event driven handlers.
3. Common messaging listener annotations are represented where the dependency is present in source.
4. Process or context output can start from these handlers the same way it can start from HTTP routes.
5. Tests cover scheduled, event listener, and one messaging listener fixture.

title: feat(spring): import optional actuator runtime data
body:
Parent tracking issue: #1225

Status: remaining work

Goal
Optionally enrich static Spring analysis with runtime data from Spring Boot actuator endpoints.

Scope
Support an opt in path for actuator mappings, beans, conditions, configprops, and env payloads. Runtime data should confirm or add metadata without replacing static analysis by default.

Acceptance criteria
1. Runtime import is explicit and disabled by default.
2. Imported mappings and beans are marked as runtime confirmed.
3. Conditions and configprops can enrich existing static nodes when they match.
4. Mock actuator payloads are covered by tests.
5. Sensitive env values are not stored or printed in analysis output.

title: [Regression] --force --embeddings fails with duplicate CodeEmbedding primary keys after an interrupted run
body:
### Area

gitnexus (CLI / core / indexing / MCP server)

### Summary

### Area

gitnexus (embedding pipeline / analyze crash recovery)

### Summary

On GitNexus 1.6.9, retrying `analyze --force --embeddings` after a
previous interrupted or partially completed embedding run can fail with
a duplicate `CodeEmbedding` primary key.

`--force` rebuilds the graph but preserves existing embeddings by
default. Partial embedding rows can therefore survive and collide with
the retry because `batchInsertEmbeddings()` currently uses `CREATE`.

This appears to be a regression of the idempotency behavior addressed
by #822 / PR #823.


### Context

### Error

```text
Batch execution failed for rows 1-4: Runtime exception:
Found duplicated primary key value
Variable:src/inkmagic/models/plot.py:type:0,
which violates the uniqueness constraint of the primary key column.

CREATE (e:CodeEmbedding {
  id: $id,
  nodeId: $nodeId,
  chunkIndex: $chunkIndex,
  ...
})
```

The final `:0` is the embedding chunk index, so the collision is on an
existing `(nodeId, chunkIndex)` embedding row rather than two source
symbols sharing the same name.


### Expected behavior

An embedding retry should be crash-safe and idempotent:

- detect and reuse unchanged existing embeddings, or
- delete/reinsert the affected `(nodeId, chunkIndex)` rows safely.

`--force` should not require users to know that partial embeddings must
be dropped manually.


### Actual behavior

The pipeline retries `CREATE` for an embedding row left by the previous
partial run, causing a primary-key violation and aborting analysis.


### Steps to reproduce

I‘ve write a reproduce script, please view the attachment.
reproduce it via `python reproduce.py`

[reproduce.py](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/29966850/reproduce.py)

### Environment

- OS: Windows 11 x64
- Node.js: 22.20.0
- GitNexus: 1.6.9
- LadybugDB: 0.18.1
- Embedding backend: local
- Device: DirectML
- VECTOR unavailable; exact-scan fallback enabled

feat: add gitnexus auto-sync for scheduled remote clone and analyze
body:
## Summary

Adds `gitnexus auto-sync` for scheduled clone/pull of configured remotes and analysis. This replaces implicit startup via `AUTO_UPDATE_AND_ANALYZE_FLAG` with a config-driven operator daemon.

Local incremental re-index is a different product: `gitnexus analyze --watch` (shipped in #3072). This PR does not implement that. `gitnexus watch` is reserved: it prints the split and exits without starting either job.

## Motivation / context

Auto-sync needed a safer, inspectable operating model than an env flag. Behavior is explicit through `GITNEXUS_HOME/watch_config.yml`, a single process per `GITNEXUS_HOME`, and recorded runtime state.

## Areas touched

- [x] `gitnexus/` (CLI / core / MCP server)
- [ ] `gitnexus-web/` (Vite / React UI)
- [ ] `.github/` (workflows, actions)
- [ ] `eval/` or other tooling
- [x] Docs / agent config (`README.md`, package README, CLI skill)

## Scope & constraints

**In scope**

- Add `gitnexus auto-sync [init|start|restart|stop|status|reset]`.
- Reserve `gitnexus watch` as a disambiguation error (not a daemon, not local `--watch`).
- Load config from `GITNEXUS_HOME/watch_config.yml`.
- Keep runtime files under `GITNEXUS_HOME/watch/` (directory name is not the CLI verb).
- PID, lock, and status files for single-instance execution.
- `branches` with legacy `branch` compatibility; try branches in order and skip the repo when all fail or time out.
- Restrict remotes to SSH SCP URLs on `github.com`, `gitlab.com`, and `gitee.com`.
- Per-repo git timeout via `repo_git_timeout`.
- Analyze consecutive-failure tracking and `analyze_failure_threshold`.
- Human-readable `project_commit_info.txt`.
- CLI help, i18n, README, and unit tests.

**Explicitly out of scope / not done here**

- No Web UI changes.
- No change to ordinary `gitnexus analyze` or to `gitnexus analyze --watch`.
- No support for multiple concurrent auto-sync instances under one `GITNEXUS_HOME`.
- No migration tool for older auto-sync config/state files.

## Implementation notes

- Removed implicit env-flag startup from CLI initialization.
- `auto-sync init` creates a default config and does not overwrite an existing file.
- Machine state: `GITNEXUS_HOME/watch/auto-sync-state.json`. `project_commit_info.txt` is inspection-only.
- Web/API clone repo-name compatibility stays on `extractWebRepoName`; auto-sync keeps stricter remote/repo validation.
- Clone/pull gained auto-sync-only SSH support and branch-specific clone/pull.
- After merging `origin/main` (#3072), local watch lives in `cli/analyze-watch.ts`; auto-sync lives in `cli/auto-sync.ts`.

## Testing & verification

- [x] `cd gitnexus && npm test`

Focused unit coverage added/updated for:

- auto-sync config parsing and validation
- branch fallback and unavailable branch handling
- analyze failure threshold skipping
- PID/lock/status lifecycle
- `auto-sync init` / CLI help, and reserved `gitnexus watch`
- auto-sync SSH clone path and timeout behavior
- web clone repo-name compatibility

## Risk & rollout

Operators using `AUTO_UPDATE_AND_ANALYZE_FLAG` must switch to `gitnexus auto-sync start` and create `GITNEXUS_HOME/watch_config.yml`.

Runtime artifacts live under `GITNEXUS_HOME/watch/`; older state files outside that directory are not migrated.

Index refresh is not required for existing local repositories. Auto-sync-managed remotes re-analyze when the configured branch commit changes or a prior analysis failed.

## Related: not the same as #3072 / #3030

- **This PR:** `gitnexus auto-sync` — scheduled clone/pull of configured remotes, then analyze.
- **#3072:** `gitnexus analyze --watch` — chokidar on the local working tree, debounced incremental refresh (implements #3030).

They share no unique commits. Implementations are split (`cli/auto-sync.ts` vs `cli/analyze-watch.ts`). Docs describe both products. `gitnexus watch` is not an alias for either.

title: Ship tool-usage policy via MCP server instructions instead of injecting a block into CLAUDE.md / AGENTS.md
body:
> **Correction (see comment below):** my original filing claimed `gitnexus setup` injects the block and that no opt-out exists. Both were wrong — `analyze` writes it, and `--skip-agents-md` already ships. The body below has been corrected. Apologies for the noise; the remaining ask stands on its own.

### Summary

`gitnexus analyze` writes a ~660-token "GitNexus — Code Intelligence" section into the host's project-instruction files (`CLAUDE.md` / `AGENTS.md`), regenerating everything between its `<!-- gitnexus:start -->` / `<!-- gitnexus:end -->` markers. Most of that section is **tool-usage policy** — which MCP already has a first-class channel for, and which GitNexus's MCP server currently doesn't use.

Shipping the policy as MCP server `instructions` would let it travel with the tool, apply wherever the server is connected, stay correct as GitNexus changes, and stop it competing for space in a file other tools also write to.

### Why the current placement is awkward

**1. MCP already has a channel for this, and GitNexus doesn't use it.**
An MCP server can return `instructions` during initialization; hosts surface them to the model automatically. In a Claude Code session I can see instruction blocks contributed by Context7, GitHub, Linear, Sentry and others. GitNexus's server contributes none — which is why the policy has to be written into `CLAUDE.md` instead. As server instructions it would be present whenever the server is connected, and versioned with the server rather than frozen at whatever `analyze` last wrote.

**2. The written section is a snapshot, and every consuming repo forks your docs.**
It records counts (`2306 symbols, 2439 relationships`) that drift immediately, and it only exists in repos that have been analyzed. When GitNexus's own guidance changes, N repos carry N stale copies.

**3. It's partly redundant with the `augment` hook.**
The `gitnexus augment` PreToolUse hook already injects graph context into searches — `[GitNexus] N related symbols found` appears on grep-shaped commands automatically. A section instructing the agent to consult GitNexus before grepping largely restates what the hook already does at the point of use, which is the better place for it.

**4. The instruction file is contended real estate.**
This is the concrete cost, not a hypothetical. `CLAUDE.md` also carries content mandated by other specs. Because the whole marked region is regenerated, any block that lands *inside* those markers is destroyed on the next `analyze`. In our workflow repo this required an entire migration (plus 11 test fixtures and a review cycle) whose sole purpose was ensuring our spec-mandated block is anchored **above** the GitNexus region so it can't be eaten. That's a lot of engineering spent on block placement.

For scale, measured with `o200k_base`: the region is **661 tokens** — 39% of that repo's `CLAUDE.md`, 11–14% in larger ones. The token cost is minor and prompt-cached; the *structural* cost of two tools writing one file is what hurts.

### Suggested change

**Ship the usage policy as MCP server `instructions`.** The "Always Do" / "Never Do" guidance (~270 tokens of the section) is pure MCP-tool policy and is the natural fit — live, versioned with the server, and requiring no file mutation at all.

If the written section stays for non-MCP contexts, the parts that genuinely aren't MCP-scoped (the CLI table, the resource list) are small. A one-line "use the graph to locate code before falling back to text search", plus MCP instructions, would cover the intent at a fraction of the footprint — and `--skip-agents-md` then becomes a niche escape hatch rather than the only way to keep the file yours.

Observed on gitnexus 1.6.4 and 1.6.9, host: Claude Code.

body:
## Summary

Adds first-class support for [Factory AI (Droid)](https://docs.factory.ai/), revisiting the goal of #195 against current `main`. There are two surfaces, mirroring how Codex is supported: a `gitnexus setup -c droid` target, and a standalone `gitnexus-factory-plugin/` that installs with `droid plugin install`.

## Motivation / context

Factory Droid users can't use GitNexus's MCP tools, skills, or search augmentation today. #195 tried this before and stalled; the table below shows how each concern raised there is handled.

| #195 concern | Resolution |
| --- | --- |
| Skills duplication (7 copied skills) | No copies. Skills install from the canonical `skills/` root via `setup`; the plugin ships none |
| Regex `\brg$` missed full paths | Execute commands are tokenized with the #2938 shell tokenizer (quotes, escapes, `--regexp=`, `-eVALUE`) |
| Hook timeout mismatch | Outer 10s / inner 8s aligned |
| `jq` dependency | Hook is pure Node |
| Stale / needed rebase | Merged with current `main` |

## Areas touched

- [x] `gitnexus/` (CLI / core / MCP server): `setup`, `editor-targets`, sync and cross-platform scripts, tests
- [ ] `gitnexus-web/` (Vite / React UI)
- [ ] `.github/` (workflows, actions)
- [x] `eval/` or other tooling: new `gitnexus-factory-plugin/` and `.factory-plugin/marketplace.json`
- [x] Docs / agent config only: root and npm `README.md`

## Scope & constraints

**In scope**

- **`gitnexus setup -c droid`**: registers `droid` in `editor-targets.ts`, writes the MCP server to `~/.factory/mcp.json`, and installs skills to `~/.factory/skills/`. It only runs when `~/.factory/` exists. `uninstall` reverses it, and the setup/uninstall round-trip test covers this.
- **`gitnexus-factory-plugin/`**: `.factory-plugin/plugin.json`, a root `mcp.json`, and a PostToolUse search-augment hook matching `Grep|Glob|Execute`.
- **`.factory-plugin/marketplace.json`**: without it, Droid falls back to the Claude marketplace and installs a translated Claude plugin instead (a `Bash` matcher that never fires, and an `@latest` MCP).
- **Pinned execution**: the hook's `npx` fallback and the plugin's MCP launch are pinned to `gitnexus@<version>`, never `@latest`. All three Factory surfaces are registered in `sync-plugin-manifests.mjs`, so every release re-pins them.
- **Guarded hook**: the hook reuses the Claude adapter's guards, bundled byte-identical: `acquireHookSlot` fan-out cap (#1486), the LadybugDB owner probe (#2396), and the `registry-query.cjs` repo/storage lookup (#3060), so external and branch-slot indexes resolve. A drift test fails if any bundled copy diverges.
- **Windows**: the hook prefers `GITNEXUS_HOOK_CLI_PATH` via `node <cli>` (Node won't spawn `.cmd` shims without a shell), and `factory-plugin.test.ts` is in the Windows CI lane (`cross-platform-tests.ts`).

**Explicitly out of scope / not done here**

- De-duplicating the hook guard modules into a shared package. They already exist as 3–4 identical copies across the Claude, Cursor, and Antigravity adapters; this PR adds one more, enforced by a drift test. It deserves its own change.
- The two `gitnexus-check` findings on `hook-lock.js` (stale-slot eviction race) and `hook-db-lock-probe.cjs` (unbounded cmdline cap). Both are in the canonical shared code, byte-identical in every adapter, so the fix belongs upstream of this PR. Replied inline.
- The coreutils `timeout` orphan guard the full Claude adapter wraps around augment (#2163). Same scope as the Cursor integration.

## Implementation notes

- The hook reads its pin version from `../.factory-plugin/plugin.json` at load time, so the manifest is the single runtime source of truth.
- The repo is resolved via `resolveHookRepo(cwd)` (registry row first, then local owned `.gitnexus`). The fan-out slot is keyed on `repo.storagePath` and the owner probe on `repo.lbugPath`, matching the Claude and Cursor hooks after #3060.

## Testing & verification

After merging current `main` (`60b1034b`):

- [x] `cd gitnexus && npx tsc --noEmit`: clean
- [x] `cd gitnexus && npx vitest run test/unit/factory-plugin.test.ts test/unit/hooks.test.ts test/unit/cursor-hook.test.ts test/unit/hook-db-lock-probe.test.ts test/unit/setup.test.ts test/unit/setup-selection.test.ts test/unit/uninstall.test.ts test/integration/setup-uninstall-roundtrip.test.ts test/unit/sync-plugin-manifests.test.ts`: 9 files, 474 passed, 27 skipped
- [x] `npx prettier --check` on changed files: clean. ESLint on changed files: 0 errors
- [x] Manual install lifecycle on `droid` v0.202.0 (at `54870b41`): `droid plugin marketplace add` → `install` → load. The installed cache has matcher `Grep|Glob|Execute`, a pinned `gitnexus@<version>` MCP, and no `resolve-analyze-cmd.cjs`, which confirms the Factory plugin installed rather than the translated Claude one.
- [ ] Full `npm test`, and Windows CI on the current head: needs a maintainer to approve the fork workflow runs

## Risk & rollout

Additive: a new `EditorId`, plus new setup functions gated on `~/.factory/` existing. No existing editor path changes. `uninstall` fully reverses setup, and rollback is reverting the commits. No index refresh is needed. Release note: "Adds Factory AI (Droid) support: `gitnexus setup -c droid` and `droid plugin install gitnexus@GitNexus`."

## Checklist

- [x] PR body meets repo minimum length
- [ ] If `AGENTS.md` / overlays changed: N/A, not changed
- [x] No secrets, tokens, or machine-specific paths committed

<!-- gitnexus-pr-summary:v1:start -->

### 📝 Summary by GitNexus

## Summary

*This appears to be a broad editor integration change centered on Factory AI (Droid), with coordinated updates across plugin hooks, CLI setup, manifests, documentation, tests, and publishing. Its critical posture comes from touching shared installation and hook behavior alongside the release workflow.*

**🔴 CRITICAL blast radius. A Factory AI (Droid) integration change spanning the `gitnexus-factory-plugin` package, shared editor hooks, and CLI setup, with impact extending through dependent setup and hook paths.**

The change is concentrated in the human-named `Hooks`, `Cli`, and `Claude` modules. Key review areas are the new Factory plugin files, including `gitnexus-factory-plugin/.factory-plugin/plugin.json`, `gitnexus-factory-plugin/mcp.json`, and its hook implementations, together with shared lock and registry behavior in `gitnexus-claude-plugin/hooks/hook-db-lock-probe.cjs`, `gitnexus-claude-plugin/hooks/hook-lock.js`, and `gitnexus-cursor-integration/hooks/hook-lock.cjs`. Start with the lock acquisition, process detection, and storage resolution functions, since those changes land across multiple editor integrations.

The CLI path also changes through `gitnexus/src/cli/editor-targets.ts`, `gitnexus/src/cli/setup.ts`, and `gitnexus/src/cli/index.ts`, with matching localization, documentation, manifest synchronization, and setup roundtrip coverage. Review that Factory registration, installation, uninstall, and generated manifest behavior remain aligned with the existing Claude and Cursor integrations.

` .github/workflows/publish.yml` is a HIGH risk file and should receive focused review for release and publishing behavior alongside the new `.factory-plugin/marketplace.json` entry.

title: fix(eval): drop tags from the benchmark's per-arm clone
body:
## What

Fourth (and, per the evidence so far, final) layer of the skill-evolution activation chain — after node_modules install (#2575), the Task/Agent permission-mode fix (#2576), and stdout diagnostics (#2577). After #2576/the corrected `GITNEXUS_BENCH_AUTH_TOKEN` secret landed, the proposer session succeeded end-to-end for the first time ([run 29738099937](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/actions/runs/29738099937): real Opus turn, $0.81 cost, valid overlay written) — but every benchmark-arm session then failed identically:

```
error_kind: "infra-error"
error_detail: "RuntimeError: sanitized graph snapshot preparation failed: clone has more than 1024 references; refusing incomplete sanitization"
```

## Why

`make_worktree()` (`eval/workflow_bench/runner_artifacts.py`) creates each benchmark arm's throwaway clone via a plain `git clone`, which inherits every tag and branch from the source repo. This repository's history has grown to **1144 tags** (a `v1.6.9-rc.N` release-candidate series) out of 1650 total refs — verified directly (`git for-each-ref | wc -l`) — exceeding `oracle_assets.MAX_CLONE_REFS = 1024`, a fail-closed safety guard in `sanitize_clone_for_hidden_oracles()` that refuses to proceed unless it can enumerate and delete *every* ref before handing a sanitized snapshot to a benchmark session (so an agent can never discover oracle test answers via a ref the sanitization missed).

## How

`ref` at every call site (`evolve.py:476`, `runner.py:1037`, `sanitized_graph.py:345`) is always a bare SHA or the literal `"HEAD"` — never a branch name — so `--single-branch --branch <ref>` isn't viable (`git clone --branch` requires a name). Tags are never used by the existing `checkout(ref)` → `checkout(origin/{ref})` fallback or by sanitization's own delete-everything behavior, so dropping them via `--no-tags` removes the 1144-ref majority without touching branch-fetch behavior, without weakening `MAX_CLONE_REFS` itself, and without touching any real repository tags or branches.

## Testing

- New regression test `test_make_worktree_clone_has_no_tags_but_keeps_all_branches`: builds a small repo with a tag and a second branch holding a commit unreachable from the default branch, clones it via the fixed `make_worktree()`, and asserts the clone has zero tags while the non-default-branch commit still resolves via the existing fallback. **Mutation-verified** two ways: fails pre-fix (tag present), and separately fails if `--single-branch` were added (proving branch-fetch isn't accidentally restricted).
- **Verified against the real repository**, not just the fixture: cloning `/workspace` itself (1650 refs, 1144 tags) via the fixed `make_worktree()` now produces a clone with 237 total refs and 0 tags.
- `cd eval && uv run --locked pytest tests/test_workflow_bench_sessions.py tests/test_sanitized_graph.py -q` → 72 passed, 1 skipped (unrelated real-binary canary). Ruff clean.

## Post-Deploy Monitoring & Validation

After merge, re-dispatch the skill-evolution workflow (`workflow_dispatch` on `main`) and confirm a benchmark-arm session actually runs (no `SandboxError`/`RuntimeError` at task binding or clone-sanitization) and a `promotion.json` decision is reached based on real, non-excluded runs. This is the first change in this chain with the chance to observe a complete propose → benchmark → gate cycle.

https://claude.ai/code/session_01Va5uu9Ar3e45QZ5xFsG4AZ

title: fix(eval): size the buffered-fallback budget for the real graph index
body:
## Summary

Seventh blocker in the skill-evolution activation chain (after #2575, #2576, #2577, #2579, #2580 — all merged). After #2580 fixed the hooks-mount blocker, the proposer session now succeeds completely (real 13-turn Opus session, genuine proposal produced), but every benchmark-arm session failed identically in CI run 29750271566:

```
"error_kind": "infra-error",
"error_detail": "SandboxError: task asset filesystem cannot reflink the snapshot and the buffered fallback limit would be exceeded"
```

`eval/workflow_bench/sanitized_graph.py` captures a pre-built GitNexus graph index (`.gitnexus/lbug`, measured 290 MiB in this checkout, historically estimated up to ~428 MiB) as a `TaskAssetCache` snapshot, then reflinks it into every benchmark-arm clone. When the underlying filesystem can't do copy-on-write reflink (`FICLONE`), materialization falls back to a buffered copy bounded by `MAX_BUFFERED_FALLBACK_BYTES` — previously 16 MiB, sized only for tiny fixtures.

`FICLONE` reflink is btrfs/XFS-only — never ext4 (GitHub-hosted runners' work disk) or 9p (this dev container's own `/workspace` mount, confirmed via `mount`). So in both real environments this harness runs in, reflink always fails and the real ~290 MiB index must go through the buffered path, instantly blowing the old 16 MiB cap.

- Raises `MAX_BUFFERED_FALLBACK_BYTES` to 512 MiB — clears the real (290 MiB) and historically-estimated (428 MiB) index size with headroom, while staying a full 4x below the existing 2 GiB `MAX_TASK_ASSET_BYTES` total-capture ceiling, so a genuinely oversized or malformed future declaration still fails closed.
- Adds a test that exercises the real (non-monkeypatched) default constant against a 20 MiB payload with `_try_reflink` forced unavailable — proven to fail under the old default and pass under the new one.

## Test plan

- [x] `cd eval && uv run --locked pytest tests/ -q` — 304 passed, 10 skipped
- [x] New test proven to fail pre-fix with the exact production error string, pass post-fix
- [x] Empirically confirmed this container's `/workspace` (9p) genuinely cannot `FICLONE` (raw ioctl → `EXDEV`)
- [x] Ran the real, fully unmocked production code path end-to-end against the actual 290 MiB `.gitnexus/lbug` — captured and materialized successfully under the new budget
- [x] Independent review (fresh agent, re-verified all claims against source, independently re-derived the discrimination proof) — READY, no findings

title: feat(spring): resolve Resource injection semantics
body:
Parent tracking issue: #1225

Builds on: #2414

Related dependency: #2413

Status: remaining work

Goal
Model Spring's JSR-250 Resource injection semantics without treating Resource as ordinary type-only Autowired injection.

Scope
Recognize javax.annotation.Resource and jakarta.annotation.Resource on fields and single-argument setter methods. Resolve explicit resource names, default names derived from the field or bean property, Spring's name-first lookup and type fallback where applicable, and statically declared type overrides. Use names from stereotype beans and Bean factory methods when those providers are available. Dynamic or runtime-only lookup metadata such as lookup and mappedName should remain unresolved instead of producing guessed relationships. Resource collection injection must not fan out to every implementation.

Acceptance criteria
1. Both javax.annotation.Resource and jakarta.annotation.Resource are recognized.
2. Explicit Resource names resolve to matching named bean providers when statically known.
3. An omitted name uses the field or setter property name first, then falls back to type only where Spring permits it.
4. Static type overrides are honored, while dynamic or runtime-only names fail closed.
5. Named providers from stereotype annotations and Bean factory methods can participate in resolution as those inventories become available.
6. Collection-typed Resource injection does not emit Autowired-style collect-all fan-out edges.
7. Missing or ambiguous providers are represented conservatively instead of inventing one exact target.
8. Tests cover javax and jakarta variants, field and setter injection, explicit and default names, type fallback, ambiguity, static type overrides, and collection negative cases.

title: Root analysis ignores nested .gitignore files in submodules
body:
## Description

When GitNexus analyzes a repository containing nested repositories, submodules, or monorepo packages, it applies only the analysis root's `.gitignore` and `.gitnexusignore`.

Nested `.gitignore` files are not loaded. GitNexus therefore indexes files that Git excludes within the nested repository, including generated JavaScript bundles. This pollutes the graph and can substantially increase parsing and memory usage.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Create a parent Git repository containing a nested repository or submodule:

   ```text
   workspace/
   ├── .git/
   └── app/
       ├── .git/
       ├── .gitignore
       ├── src/index.ts
       └── public/generated/bundle.js
   ```

2. Add this rule to `app/.gitignore`:

   ```gitignore
   public/generated/
   ```

3. Confirm Git considers `app/public/generated/bundle.js` ignored within `app`.
4. Run `gitnexus analyze --force` from `workspace/`.
5. Inspect the root `.gitnexus/meta.json`.

## Expected Behavior

GitNexus should not recurse into a nested repository while silently discarding that repository's ignore rules.

Either behavior would be consistent:

1. Stop traversal at nested Git repository/submodule boundaries by default; or
2. If nested repositories are intentionally included in the root graph, apply each nested directory's `.gitignore` using directory-relative Git ignore semantics.

Ignored directories should be pruned before file stat, reading, parsing, and graph generation.

## Actual Behavior

`walkRepositoryPaths()` recursively scans the analysis root with `glob('**/*', ...)`. Its filter comes from `createIgnoreFilter(repoPath)`, while `loadIgnoreRules(repoPath)` reads only the root `.gitignore` and `.gitnexusignore`. It does not discover nested ignore files or account for `.gitmodules` boundaries.

In a Yarn/Turborepo workspace with a checked-out `landing-page` submodule:

- `landing-page/.gitignore` contains `public/play`.
- `landing-page/public/play` is generated build output.
- The root `.gitnexus/meta.json` contains 174 paths below `landing-page/public/play`.
- 154 of those paths are generated JavaScript chunks.
- The indexed generated subset is approximately 1.63 MiB.
- The complete ignored directory contains 602 files totaling approximately 34.91 MiB.

The generated paths represented 2.78% of files in this root index. Parsing bundled JavaScript can create disproportionate AST and graph work relative to its byte size. Analysis caused a severe memory spike and crashed the OpenCode host process, so it was not rerun during investigation.

## Environment

- GitNexus: 1.6.9
- Node.js: 22.16.0
- OS: Linux
- Repository shape: Yarn 1 + Turborepo workspace containing Git submodules
- Analysis command: `gitnexus analyze --force`
- Embeddings: disabled

## Screenshots/Logs

No complete crash log is available because the host process became unstable. The resulting root `.gitnexus/meta.json` provides persistent evidence that nested ignored files were indexed.

## Additional Context

No exact duplicate was found.

- #231 introduced root-level `.gitignore` support, but does not implement nested ignore discovery.
- #241 discusses recursive filesystem-scanning performance.
- #1983 reports a large-repository OOM symptom, but not nested-ignore behavior.
- #2193 concerns multi-repository graph support rather than ignore semantics.

Suggested acceptance criteria:

- [ ] A nested `.gitignore` rule excludes matching descendants during root analysis.
- [ ] Patterns are resolved relative to the directory containing the ignore file.
- [ ] Nested ignored directories are pruned before file reads and parsing.
- [ ] Root `.gitnexusignore` behavior and negation precedence remain intact.
- [ ] Tests cover an ordinary nested package and a Git submodule/nested repository.
- [ ] The submodule policy is documented: stop at the boundary or traverse while honoring nested rules.

title: npm package is 140 MiB unpacked — exceeds the 80 MiB cnpm/npmmirror sync limit
body:
## Problem

The [v1.6.9 release page](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/releases/tag/v1.6.9) instructs users to run:

```
npm install -g gitnexus@1.6.9
```

This fails because v1.6.9 was never published to npm. The npm registry shows:

- `latest` tag: **1.6.6**
- Highest version available: **1.6.7-rc.8**
- v1.6.8 and v1.6.9 are both missing

```
$ npm view gitnexus dist-tags
{ latest: '1.6.6', rc: '1.6.7-rc.7' }

$ npm view gitnexus versions | tail -5
'1.6.7-rc.5',
'1.6.7-rc.6',
'1.6.7-rc.7',
'1.6.7-rc.8'
```

## Impact

Users following the official upgrade instructions get an error. The only workaround is to clone the repo and build from source, which is not practical for most users.

## Expected

Publish v1.6.9 (and v1.6.8 if applicable) to npm so that `npm install -g gitnexus@1.6.9` works as documented on the release page.

title: Support indexing hidden directories and extensionless shebang scripts
body:
## Problem

Two common source layouts can currently be absent from the knowledge graph:

1. Legitimate source code stored beneath a hidden directory is not traversed because repository walking excludes dot-directories. An explicit negation in `.gitnexusignore` cannot opt such a directory back in if traversal never visits it.
2. Extensionless executable scripts are not assigned a language when language detection relies only on filename extensions, even when the file has an unambiguous shebang such as `#!/usr/bin/env python3`.

Together, these behaviors can omit operationally important workflow, automation, and command code from symbol, call-graph, process, and impact analysis. The resulting graph can appear healthy while impact queries for those symbols return unknown or no matches.

## Requested behavior

Please provide an explicit, safe opt-in for both cases:

- Allow selected hidden directories to be traversed, either through an `--include-hidden` option or by honoring explicit `.gitnexusignore` negations during filesystem traversal.
- When a file has no recognized extension, use a supported shebang as a fallback language signal.
- Preserve the current default exclusions unless the user opts in.
- Keep hard safety exclusions, ignore precedence, and diagnostics clear so users can see which files were skipped or how an extensionless file was classified.

## Suggested acceptance criteria

- A hidden source directory explicitly opted in by configuration is traversed and indexed.
- A more-specific ignore rule can still exclude generated or sensitive descendants beneath that directory.
- An extensionless file with a supported Python shebang produces the same relevant file/function/call nodes as an equivalent `.py` file.
- Unsupported or ambiguous shebangs remain safely unclassified.
- Default indexing behavior is unchanged when no opt-in is configured.
- `context`, `impact`, and `detect_changes` can map the original repository paths for opted-in hidden and shebang-classified source files.

## Why this is useful

Hidden configuration directories increasingly contain real executable automation and agent/workflow source, while extensionless commands are a longstanding Unix convention. Indexing these files when explicitly requested would make graph completeness and blast-radius analysis more representative without increasing default noise.

title: feat(spring): index @Bean factories and @Resource injection
body:
## Summary

- index Java and Kotlin Spring `@Bean` factory methods as synthetic Bean declarations, including default names, aliases, return types, factory dependencies, and MCP context/impact metadata
- support `javax.annotation.Resource` and `jakarta.annotation.Resource` with conservative name-first resolution, default-name type fallback, explicit type overrides, runtime lookup fail-closed behavior, and Kotlin use-site targets
- pre-index provider names and provided types in the DI phase to keep named Resource resolution sub-quadratic
- include Bean declaration drift in incremental write-set expansion and bump the Spring Bean inventory feature version
- add Java/Kotlin pipeline, MCP, incremental, argument-parser, conflict, collection, and lowercase Kotlin typealias coverage
- run the end-to-end Bean/Resource scaling test in the dedicated serial `GITNEXUS_BENCH` CI job

## Compatibility and behavior

- Java and Kotlin use the same resolved-FQN semantics; local annotations named `Bean` or `Resource` are ignored
- `@Resource` explicit names do not fall back to type, while default names may use a low-confidence type fallback
- `lookup` and `mappedName` remain unresolved unless they are the empty default
- collection factory parameters preserve fan-out semantics
- Bean factory methods are not also emitted as owner-class injection sites when combined with `@Autowired` or qualifier annotations
- lowercase Kotlin type aliases are preserved during type normalization

## Validation

- `npm run build`
- Spring suite: 22 files passed, 125 tests passed, 6 skipped
- `GITNEXUS_BENCH=1 npx vitest run --no-file-parallelism test/integration/spring-bean-resource-benchmark.test.ts`: 3/3 passed

- full `npm test`: 15,238 passed, 99 skipped, 10 failed; the registry-race FTS failure passed 18/18 when rerun in isolation, while the remaining 9 failures are existing macOS path/Linux descriptor/ambiguous-impact baseline limitations outside the Spring change
