title: MCP/CLI read path never loads VECTOR, and can't recover from serve's shadow
body:
Two defects on the same path. MCP and gitnexus cypher/context/impact go through pool-adapter.js + local-backend.js; serve goes through lbug-adapter.js. The former is missing two things the latter has, and both fail silently.                                                                                
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  
gitnexus 1.6.9, @ladybugdb/core ^0.18.0, macOS Intel x86_64, Node v24.14.0.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  
1. VECTOR is never loaded. CALL QUERY_VECTOR_INDEX(...) through the MCP cypher tool:                                                                                                                                                                                                                            
Catalog exception: function QUERY_VECTOR_INDEX is not defined. This function exists in the VECTOR extension.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           
FTS works on the same connection. loadVectorExtension is only called from embedding-pipeline.js and lbug-adapter.js:2137 — never from pool-adapter.js or local-backend.js. local-backend.js:1837 guards on isVectorExtensionSupportedByPlatform(), but that's platform !== 'win32', not a readiness check.      
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  
The throw is swallowed by a bare catch {} in semanticSearch, then the exact-scan fallback hits if (embeddingCount > exactScanLimit) return [] with DEFAULT_EXACT_SCAN_LIMIT = 10_000. So on a repo with 45,193 embeddings, semantic search returns nothing, with no warning. serve's /api/search on the same  data is correct in 0.4 s.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  
Asks: load VECTOR here — loadVectorExtension already returns false on win32 internally (lbug-adapter.js:2070), so this doesn't regress #1178/#1181; same shape as #2624. And separately, make that return [] warn — "cannot run" currently looks identical to "no matches".                                     
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  
2. serve's shutdown sidecars break MCP. serve writes lbug.shadow + lbug.wal on graceful SIGTERM (not during the run). Afterwards a fresh serve reads the repo fine, logging quarantined WAL + read-only recovery, while pool-adapter fails with Couldn't replay shadow pages under read-only mode. Same files,  outcome tracks the code path. Only analyze --force repairs it; incremental analyze says Already up to date; doctor doesn't detect it.                                                                                                                                                                           
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  
Ask: have pool-adapter use the existing sidecar quarantine primitives instead of its own replayShadowPagesWithWritableOpen branch (pool-adapter.js:388), which never succeeds. Related to #2979 but inverted — there the shadow is missing and the web UI breaks; here it's present, the web UI is fine, MCP  breaks.

title: impact() still returns a normal result when analyze dropped files
body:
### Area

gitnexus (CLI / core / indexing / MCP server)

### Summary

If `analyze` drops a file (`scope extraction failed …` and then continues), `impact` still returns a normal JSON blob with a risk level. Nothing on the result says the graph is incomplete.

### Context

I was checking how often a blast-radius answer is missing real callers because the indexer failed a file and kept going. Public repo, pinned commit.

This is not another report of the >32KB `Invalid argument` parse bug. That's #2466 / #1082, and on 1.6.9 I don't see those warnings on `psf/requests` anymore. What's left is the query side: `impact` fail-opens.

#1095 already asked to put a warning on tool results when a file's relationship layer was empty. Closing that as "parse is fixed" still means the next extraction failure looks like a complete answer to whatever's calling `impact` (an agent, mostly).

### Expected behavior

If analyze logged `scope extraction failed` for a file that contains a caller of the target, `impact` should refuse or mark the result incomplete. `risk: LOW` / `epistemic: exact` shouldn't come out of a partial index.

### Actual behavior

**gitnexus 1.6.3**, `psf/requests` @ `23953c0c875219a715f081cf3de7c149a7629ccf`

`analyze` warned and continued for:

- `src/requests/models.py` (`Invalid argument`)
- `src/requests/sessions.py` (`Invalid argument`)
- `src/requests/utils.py` (`Invalid argument`)
- `tests/test_requests.py` (`Invalid argument`)
- `tests/testserver/__init__.py` (`no Module scope found`, a different failure)

(the `Invalid argument` files are all well under the 512KB cap)

Then `gitnexus impact to_key_val_list` came back `risk=LOW` with `impactedCount: 0` and an empty `byDepth`. Same result with `--include-tests --depth 5`.

Same files on disk:

    src/requests/models.py:167:            for k, vs in to_key_val_list(data):
    src/requests/models.py:200:        fields = to_key_val_list(data or {})
    src/requests/models.py:201:        files = to_key_val_list(files or {})
    src/requests/sessions.py:96:    merged_setting = dict_class(to_key_val_list(session_setting))
    src/requests/sessions.py:97:    merged_setting.update(to_key_val_list(request_setting))

**gitnexus 1.6.9**, same commit: no scope-extraction failures, `1,397 nodes | 2,461 edges`, and the same `impact` query is `risk=CRITICAL`, 3 direct (`sessions.py:merge_setting`, `models.py:_encode_params`, `models.py:_encode_files`). So the parse side looks fixed. The 1.6.3 `impact` output just never said anything was missing.

Same pattern on 1.6.3 with `ranaroussi/yfinance` @ `38c73ce33fb1ee77d37a0998c95c06e60356298e` (`const.py`, `scrapers/history.py`, `scrapers/quote.py`, `utils.py` dropped). I didn't re-run yfinance on 1.6.9.

### Steps to reproduce

On 1.6.3 (where the fail-open is visible):

1. `npm i -g gitnexus@1.6.3`
2. `git clone https://github.com/psf/requests && git checkout 23953c0c875219a715f081cf3de7c149a7629ccf`
3. `gitnexus analyze . --force --skip-agents-md --name requests-repro`
4. `analyze` prints `scope extraction failed for src/requests/models.py` (and sessions/utils)
5. `gitnexus impact to_key_val_list -r requests-repro` → LOW, 0 callers
6. `grep -n 'to_key_val_list(' src/requests/models.py src/requests/sessions.py` → the extra call sites

On 1.6.9 those warnings are gone and this particular query is complete. To see the fail-open on current you'd need a file that still fails extraction, or 1.6.3.

### Environment

- OS: Linux x86_64
- Node: v22.23.1
- GitNexus: 1.6.3 (original) and 1.6.9 (recheck today)
- Target: psf/requests @ 23953c0

### Notes

I used a small grep-vs-graph check to find this: https://github.com/klmtseng/impact-audited
Not asking you to depend on it. The commands above are enough.

title: analyze: incremental re-index of a tiny diff is as slow as a full cold index — graph-wide Leiden/process/FTS phases run unconditionally
body:
## Summary

On a 128k-node / 365k-edge repo, an incremental `analyze` of an 8-file diff took **longer** than a full cold index of the same repo. Re-indexing a single 1-line change was slower still. The incremental fast-path correctly preserves unchanged file rows and scopes the `lbug` write to the changed subgraph, but the dominant costs — full-graph community detection (Leiden), process/flow detection, and the FTS index rebuild — run on every persisting analyze regardless of diff size. Net effect: incremental provides little to no wall-clock speedup, which defeats the "warm re-index" use case (per-worktree / CI / agent-loop reindex where the index is already ~current).

## Related issues

- #1841 (open) — "Make TypeScript scope-resolution truly incremental for warm analyze runs" establishes the same underlying principle: the incremental path preserves unchanged rows but *"still pays the full in-memory pipeline cost before deciding which rows to write."* That issue targets the **scope-resolution** phase specifically. This issue extends the same finding to the **community (Leiden), process/flow, and FTS** phases, and reports a case (128k-node Rust workspace) where incremental is actually **slower** than cold.
- #1496 (open) — reindex endpoint for daemon consumers; same warm-reindex motivation.
- #1809 (open) — user question about incremental scanning; same expectation that a small change should re-index cheaply.

## Environment

- gitnexus **1.6.9** (npm global CLI)
- macOS (Apple Silicon), Node 22
- Backend: ladybugdb (Kuzu), `lbug` ≈ 860 MB for this repo
- Repo under test: Rust multi-crate workspace, ~8.8k files → 128,439 nodes / 365,333 edges / 5,090 clusters / 300 flows

## Measurements (same repo, same machine, solo runs)

| Run | Diff vs indexed commit | Wall time |
|-----|------------------------|-----------|
| Cold `analyze` (fresh, no prior index) | full | **164.6 s** |
| Incremental (index at commit A, tree at commit B) | changed=5, added=3, deleted=12 | **259.5 s** |
| Incremental (index at A, tree at A + 1-line edit) | ~1 file | **321.7 s** |

All incremental runs ≥ cold. The 1-line run rebuilt all **20 FTS tables** and recomputed **5,045 clusters + 300 flows**. `--index-only` was used (no embeddings, no AI-context file writes) — so this is the floor, not the ceiling.

> Note on repro method: the incremental runs above were seeded by copying an existing `.gitnexus/` (only for convenience — the effect is fully reproducible in-place without any copy; recipe below). Seeding a *live* `.gitnexus/` additionally carried a `lbug.wal` that made one run abort with `AnalysisNotFinalizedError` (stale WAL) — orthogonal, but suggests `analyze` could detect+recover a stale-WAL seed instead of erroring.

## Clean repro (no seeding)

```bash
# 1. cold index a large repo in place
gitnexus analyze --index-only        # note the reported seconds (T_cold)

# 2. make a trivial change
echo '// benign' >> some/file.rs

# 3. incremental re-index
gitnexus analyze --index-only        # note the seconds (T_incremental)

# Observed: T_incremental >= T_cold on a 128k-node repo.
```

## Root cause (code, v1.6.9)

The incremental branch preserves changed-file rows but then runs the whole-graph phases unconditionally:

- **`src/core/run-analyze.ts:1267`** — `await deleteAllCommunitiesAndProcesses();` runs on every persisting analyze. The adjacent comment states this is *"Required for the 'Leiden runs on the FULL graph' correctness invariant"* — i.e. communities/processes are intentionally dropped and recomputed whole-graph.
- **`src/core/ingestion/pipeline-phases/communities.ts`** — Leiden phase header: `@reads graph (all nodes and relationships)`.
- **`src/core/ingestion/pipeline-phases/processes.ts`** — process/flow phase header: `@reads graph (all nodes and relationships)`.
- **FTS rebuild** — `createSearchFTSIndexes` (imported into `run-analyze.ts`) rebuilds the search indexes; **all 20 FTS tables were rebuilt** on the 1-line run (observed directly in `--verbose` logs: `FTS: creating … / FTS: ready …` for File, Function, Class, Method, Trait, Impl, Macro, … 20 tables).

For contrast, the `lbug` write is **already incremental-scoped**: `loadGraphToLbug(subgraph, …)` at `run-analyze.ts:1302` receives the changed subgraph, so the COPY is not a whole-graph fixed cost — the clustering + flow + FTS phases are.

Incremental bookkeeping is real and correct (logs from `run-analyze.ts:1092–1094`, `:1226`: `skipping wipe + N unchanged file rows preserved`, `+N importer(s) added to writable set`), but the savings are swallowed by the graph-wide clustering/flow/FTS costs above.

## Why it matters (use case)

Agent/CI workflows re-index a working tree that is already ~current (per git-worktree runs, per CI job, per agent iteration before `impact` / `detect-changes`). These gates need an up-to-date **structural** graph (nodes/edges/callers/callees) for the changed files — they do **not** necessarily need freshly recomputed communities/flows/FTS on every call. Today there is no way to get a fast structural refresh; every refresh pays the full ~165–320s.

## Requested options (any one helps; not prescriptive)

1. **Fast structural-incremental mode** — a flag (e.g. `analyze --structural-only` / `--skip-clustering --skip-flows --skip-fts`) that updates only nodes/edges for changed files and skips Leiden/process/FTS recompute. Sufficient for `detect-changes` / `impact` on existing symbols; document that community/flow results may be stale until a full pass.
2. **Scoped / incremental clustering & flows** — recompute communities/processes only for the changed subgraph + affected neighborhood instead of the whole graph, trading exactness for speed under a flag.
3. **Incremental FTS** — update FTS rows for changed files instead of rebuilding all 20 tables.

Even option (1) alone would make warm re-index viable for agent/CI loops.

## Open questions for maintainers

- Is the Leiden/full-graph invariant strictly required for `detect-changes` and `impact`, or only for `query`/`context` ranking? If the two gate commands don't consume communities/flows, a structural-only mode is low-risk.
- Would you accept a PR adding `--structural-only` (skip clustering/flows/FTS) behind an explicit "results may be stale" warning?

title: fix(ingestion): index NestJS decorator routes so api_impact and route_map stop reporting live endpoints as non-existent
body:
## Summary

Fixes #3009. The indexer never extracted NestJS `@Controller` / `@Get` routes, so a NestJS repo produced essentially no `Route` nodes — and `route_map`, `api_impact` and `shape_check` all read `Route` nodes and answer "no routes matching …" when there are none.

On a production NestJS backend, `Route` nodes go from **3 to 212**, and `route_map({route: "/venues"})` goes from `No routes matching "/venues"` to 26 routes with resolved handlers.

## Motivation / context

TypeScript's `extractDecoratorRoutes` hook was, in full (`languages/typescript.ts:130`):

```ts
const extractJsTsRoutes = (...args: Parameters<typeof extractDispatchGuardRoutes>) => [
  ...extractDispatchGuardRoutes(...args),
  ...extractDataRouteTableRoutes(...args),
];
```

Dispatch guards and static data route tables only. Java wires `extractDecoratorRoutes: extractSpringRoutes`, but nothing in `route-extractors/` handled NestJS — there was no `nest.ts`, and no file in that directory mentioned Nest or `@Controller`.

`ARCHITECTURE.md` said otherwise, which is probably why the gap survived:

> | AST-level route in a normal file | `extractDecoratorRoutes` | Spring, FastAPI, **NestJS**, JS/TS dispatch guards and static data route tables |

NestJS was documented and not implemented. That row is corrected here.

**Why this is worse than a missing feature.** The tools do not degrade politely — they assert absence. On a backend with 33 `@Controller` classes and 209 route decorators, the index held 3 `Route` nodes, and all 3 were URL string literals scraped out of utility code (a Bull Board mount, a parsed YouTube URL, an image-URL normaliser). Meanwhile `api_impact`, documented as the thing to run *"BEFORE modifying any API route handler"*, answered "No routes found matching …" for every live endpoint — and a not-found reads as a safe change. That is a false-safe on a pre-change safety check.

## Areas touched

- [x] `gitnexus/` (CLI / core / MCP server — ingestion, the routes phase, and the group-contract HTTP scan)
- [ ] `gitnexus-web/` (Vite / React UI)
- [ ] `.github/` (workflows, actions)
- [ ] `eval/` or other tooling
- [x] Docs (`ARCHITECTURE.md` route-source table)

## Scope & constraints

**In scope**

- `route-extractors/nest.ts`: class-prefix + method-verb extraction, wired into the existing TS/JS `extractDecoratorRoutes` hook.
- `SCHEMA_BUMP` so warm parse caches re-extract (now **76** — see *Changes during review*).
- Correct the `ARCHITECTURE.md` framework list.

**Explicitly out of scope / not done here**

- **`shape_check` stays blind on NestJS.** It needs `responseKeys` extracted from `.json({...})` calls; NestJS handlers return objects directly and never call `.json()`, so `responseKeys` is empty by construction even now that routes exist. Making it read the handler's return type is a separate change (noted in #3009, and the same likely applies to FastAPI).
- **`tool_map` returning `flows: []`** — observed during the same audit, unrelated to routes, left in #3009.
- **Non-literal decorator arguments are dropped, not resolved.** `@Get(ROUTES.SEARCH)` and `@Controller(BASE)` produce no route. (The *array* form is no longer in this bucket — see *Changes during review*.) Spring solves this with the `constant-resolver.ts` fold and JS/TS now has a binding for it (#3008), so wiring the two together is a natural follow-up — deliberately not bundled here.
- **Non-`@Controller` decorator sources** (`@Resolver` GraphQL, microservice `@MessagePattern`, gateway `@SubscribeMessage`) are not routes and are not extracted.

## Implementation notes

The shape mirrors `spring.ts`, which solves the identical two-decorator problem for `@RequestMapping` + `@GetMapping`: collect class-level prefixes, then attach each method decorator's path to its enclosing class's prefix. As there, the prefix travels on `ExtractedDecoratorRoute.prefix` and the routes phase joins it via `normalizeExtractedRoutePath`, so NestJS routes are keyed identically to every other framework's.

Three things the AST forced, each found by testing against real code rather than by reading the grammar:

1. **Decorator placement differs by export-ness.** `@Controller('a') class A {}` puts the decorator INSIDE `class_declaration`; `@Controller('a') export class A {}` puts it in the `export_statement`, as a SIBLING of the class. Handling only one silently drops half of all controllers.

2. **Comments break a naive decorator walk.** A real controller had four stacked decorators, then a JSDoc block, then the method. Walking backwards from the method and stopping at the first non-decorator made the entire route invisible. Both the backward walk and the leading-children walk now skip comments.

3. **A pathless `@Get()` must emit `'/'`, not `''`.** `claim()` in `call-processor.ts` short-circuits on a falsy `routePath`, so an empty string still creates the `Route` node but silently loses its handler symbol — the controller's index route would exist with nothing attached. Both spellings normalize to the same URL.

**Precision.** A method decorator is only believed when its enclosing class carries a `@Controller`; `Get`/`Post`/`Delete` are ordinary identifiers and any library reusing those names would otherwise mint phantom endpoints. An argument that is present but not a plain literal — a constant, a member expression, an interpolated template — drops the route rather than guessing a URL. `route_map` presents its output as fact, so a wrong path is worse than a missing one.

**Cache version.** A bump is needed for the same reason 68 → 69 was taken when #2969 added data-route-table routes to this channel: a warm cache replays unchanged worker results, which for every already-indexed NestJS repo means replaying the empty route set this change exists to fix. Without it the fix appears to do nothing until something else invalidates the cache. The value has since moved twice — it is **76** now, and the reasoning is in *Changes during review*. Per the convention in `parse-cache.ts`, **re-check against `origin/main` and open PRs immediately before merging**.

## Testing & verification

New: `test/unit/nest-decorator-routes.test.ts` (15 tests) covering prefix joining, all verbs, pathless `@Controller()` and `@Get()`, multiple controllers per file, non-exported controllers, stacked decorators, comments in both decorator positions, handler-name capture — and the precision guards: a non-`@Controller` class is ignored, and unreadable prefixes/paths/templates/arrays all drop rather than guess.

- [x] `cd gitnexus && npm test` — 12786 passed / 7 failed. The 7 are `analyzer-identity`, `assert-publish-grammar-coverage`, `review-agent-workflow`, `wiki-llm-client`; running those four files alone gives `7 failed | 142 passed`, identical to pristine `main`, so every failure is pre-existing (build-artifact, CI-contract and env-credential tests).
- [x] `cd gitnexus && npm run test:integration` — **5357 passed, 0 failed**, 11 skipped
- [x] `cd gitnexus && npx tsc --noEmit` — clean
- [x] `npx eslint` on changed files — no errors, no new warnings
- [ ] `cd gitnexus-web && npm test` *(web untouched)*

**Verified end to end, not just at the unit level.** A synthetic NestJS fixture indexed through the real pipeline produces 4 `Route` nodes with correct verbs, joined URLs, and `HANDLES_ROUTE` edges, each resolving to its handler method (`Method:…VenueController.findAll#0` etc.).

**Verified against real repositories.** Run standalone over two production NestJS codebases, the extractor reaches exact parity with a text scan for `^\s*@(Get|Post|Put|Patch|Delete|Head|Options|All)\s*\(`:

| repo | text-visible decorators | extracted | mismatching files |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| backend A (428 `.ts`) | 209 | 209 | 0 |
| backend B (smaller) | 23 | 23 | 0 |

Fully re-indexed, backend A goes from **3 `Route` nodes to 212** (209 NestJS + the 3 pre-existing URL literals), and the tool that motivated the issue now answers:

```
route_map({repo, route: "/venues"})  ->  26 routes, each with a resolved handler
```

versus `No routes matching "/venues"` before.

## Risk & rollout

- **Requires a re-index to take effect** on existing repositories — that is what the `SCHEMA_BUMP` is for. `npx gitnexus analyze` picks it up; no `--force` needed.
- **New `Route` nodes appear where there were none.** Anything that treated "no routes" as "not an API" will now see an API. That is the point, but it does change `route_map` / `api_impact` / `shape_check` output on NestJS repos, and grows the graph by roughly one node per endpoint.
- **Direction of error is recall, not precision.** Every ambiguity drops the route; nothing is guessed. The `@Controller` requirement bounds false positives to code that genuinely declares a NestJS controller.
- **The realistic false positive** is a non-NestJS class that both carries a decorator named `Controller` and has methods decorated `Get`/`Post`. Narrowing to an import-checked `@nestjs/common` provenance is the lever if that shows up.
- **Rollback:** revert the commit. The `SCHEMA_BUMP` revert would leave already-upgraded caches on 71 and simply cause one extra re-extraction, which is harmless.
- Release notes: `fix` → 🐛 Bug Fixes.

## Checklist

- [x] PR body meets repo minimum length
- [x] `ARCHITECTURE.md` updated (the route-source table it contradicted)
- [x] No secrets, tokens, or machine-specific paths committed
- [x] No new `GITNEXUS_*` environment variables
- [x] `SCHEMA_BUMP` bumped and its pin test updated; re-check against `origin/main` before merge

## Changes during review

Everything above is the original change. This section records what moved after review, so the diff and the body do not disagree.

### Review findings addressed

Thirteen findings from the multi-engine review, each answered in its thread. The one that produced a *wrong* fact rather than a missing one:

- **Escape sequences were deleted, not decoded.** tree-sitter splits a literal around every `escape_sequence`, and the extractor kept only the `string_fragment` children and joined them — so `@Get(':id(\\d+)')` was stored as `:id(d+)` and `@Get('/v\u0069ews')` as `/vews`. Both are URLs the app never serves, i.e. exactly what this module's own header forbids. Fixed by delegating to `plainString`, the judge `data-route-table.ts` already uses.

The rest, briefly: `abstract class` controllers and the object form `@Controller({ path })` were dropping whole controllers; the extractor could never emit a route on the JavaScript provider (that grammar makes a method decorator a *child* of `method_definition`, not a preceding sibling) despite the provider already declaring `framework: 'nestjs'`; `@Sse` was missing from the verb map; and `collectClassRoutes` was O(n²) in methods-per-controller because `namedChildren` is an uncached getter — 800 methods went 360 ms → 7.4 ms.

Two behaviours are documented rather than fixed, deliberately: URLs are **controller-relative** (`setGlobalPrefix` and URI versioning live in the bootstrap file, and the "drop rather than guess" floor is unavailable because honouring it would drop every Nest route in every repo), and a decorator orphaned by a commented-out handler is absorbed onto the next method (indistinguishable from a documented handler at the AST level).

Found while fixing, not in the review: the verb table was an object literal, so `@toString()` on a controller method resolved to `Object.prototype.toString` — truthy, and emitted verbatim as the route's `httpMethod`. Now a `ReadonlyMap`.

### Multi-path (array) decorators

`@Get(['a','b'])` mounts one handler at two URLs and was dropped. The recorded objection — that supporting it forces the literal reader to an array type — was about a *private helper's* signature, not the layer's contract: the contract is `ExtractedDecoratorRoute[]`, and N paths is already N entries, which is exactly how `spring.ts` models `@GetMapping({"/a","/b"})` (#2281).

The class-level array form still suppresses the class, matching `spring.ts`, which detects an array-form class `@RequestMapping` only to suppress it and leaves the prefix × method cross-product to #2280. An array with any unreadable element drops entirely rather than emitting the readable ones — a partial emit presents an incomplete route set as complete.

### The group layer now reads routes through the indexer's extractor

`group/extractors/http-patterns/node.ts` had its own NestJS implementation, and the two had drifted in both directions. The group side read `class_declaration` only, only five verbs, required a string `@Controller` argument, did not decode escapes — and **invented** `/` when a method argument was not a readable string, so `@Get(ROUTES.SEARCH)` published `GET /venues` there while the indexer correctly published nothing.

Rather than share constants and keep nine behaviours in sync by hand, the group scan now calls `extractNestRoutes` over the same tree — the shape that file already uses one function over for `scanDataRouteTables`. Divergence becomes structurally impossible instead of test-enforced. **Net −140 lines**, and a new `test/unit/group/nest-route-parity.test.ts` whose 18 cases include 12 that fail against the previous implementation.

Incidentally much faster: the deleted helpers indexed `parent.namedChild(i)` per decorator, the same uncached-getter quadratic. An 800-method controller went 666 ms → 30.6 ms.

### A route-identity defect found by the review, fixed here (#3049)

A method-agnostic route (`@All`, a Django function view, a verb-less dispatch guard) keys by URL alone. Filesystem routes are pre-seeded into `routeRegistry` and never pass through `claim()`. When both produce the same URL, the wildcard route claimed the key unopposed, then lost first-writer-wins and was dropped — and the surviving **filesystem** node read its handler, presenting another application's controller method as its own.

Reproduced end to end with two controls:

| case | Route nodes | handler |
|---|---|---|
| Next.js `/api/venues` alone | 1 | none ✓ |
| `@Get('venues')` | 2 | none / `handleEverything` ✓ |
| **`@All('venues')`** | 1 | **`handleEverything`** ✗ |

Fixed with one guard in the routes phase: a pre-seeded source can never legitimately appear in `routeHandlerSymbols`, so a key that does is by construction a route that lost. Dropping the losing route is untouched — that is the separate, deliberate consequence of URL-only identity (#2289), and it omits rather than invents.

### Test coverage added

- `test/integration/nest-route-pipeline.test.ts` + `test/fixtures/nest-route-app/` — every sibling extractor at this tier had a pipeline test and a fixture app; this had neither, and the unit suite cannot reach the tier #3009 is actually about.
- `test/unit/group/nest-route-parity.test.ts` — the guard the repo already wrote for Spring after #2265.
- Two cases in `test/integration/multi-verb-route-identity.test.ts` for #3049.
- The unit suite went from 15 tests to 38.

### Cache version, twice

`SCHEMA_BUMP` was 71 here when `origin/main` was 70. Main then cascaded to 74 (#2980 took 71; the Convex change took 74, skipping 73 for open PR #3046), so 71 would have been *below* main — the version would move backwards on merge and the reuse gate would never fire. Re-applied the ledger's own rule at merge time rather than authoring time (next free value above `origin/main` **and** above every in-flight claim) → 75.

Then 75 → **76**, a second bump on this branch: 75 was claimed before the array form landed, and that form changed worker output, so a dev or CI cache written at v75 would replay pre-feature captures under a byte-identical `PARSE_CACHE_VERSION`. The rule is about what a warm cache can replay, not about how the number was reached. Re-checked: main 74, #3046 at 73, #1616 a stale 2.

title: fix(ingestion): ignore emitted Next.js build output, and delete the inert public/build entry
body:
## Summary

Fixes #3007. `DEFAULT_IGNORE_LIST` had `.next` (the build *cache*) but not `_next` (the emitted *output*), so a Capacitor/Cordova-wrapped Next.js app had its shipped bundle indexed as source — and every `Route` node such a repo produced pointed at a minified webpack chunk instead of at code anyone wrote.

Also restores `'public/build'`, which had been sitting in that set matching nothing at all.

## Motivation / context

`.next` and `_next` are different directories. A Capacitor shell copies the built output to `<platform>/app/src/main/assets/public/_next/static/…`, and none of `android`, `app`, `src`, `main`, `assets`, `public`, `_next`, `static` or `chunks` is in the ignore list.

The filename heuristics do not catch them either — `isIgnoredFile` matches `.bundle.`, `.chunk.` and `.generated.`, while Next.js emits hashed names like `6862-9d1cdcb99f169a06.js`.

The visible symptom on a real repo was that every `Route` node came from bundle output:

```
Route:POST /api/notifications/register-device
  filePath: android/app/src/main/assets/public/_next/static/chunks/6862-9d1cdcb99f169a06.js
```

Minified single-line bundles were also the source of `callable-value-flow: candidate set exceeded the cap` warnings during analysis, so this costs time as well as accuracy.

**The second bug.** `'public/build'` was a member of `DEFAULT_IGNORE_LIST`, but that set is tested one path SEGMENT at a time:

```ts
const parts = normalizedPath.split('/');
for (const part of parts) {
  if (DEFAULT_IGNORE_LIST.has(part)) return true;
}
```

and it is also read by `isHardcodedIgnoredDirectory(name)`, which receives a bare directory name. A slash-containing member can never compare equal to either, so the entry had never matched anything since it was added.

## Areas touched

- [x] `gitnexus/` (CLI / core / MCP server)
- [x] `gitnexus-web/` (Vite / React UI)
- [ ] `.github/` (workflows, actions)
- [ ] `eval/` or other tooling
- [ ] Docs / agent config only

## Scope & constraints

**In scope**

- Add `_next` to the segment ignore list, and pin that it matches as a whole path segment.
- Delete the inert `'public/build'` entry outright (see Implementation notes for why deleting beat relocating).
- A guard test pinning the invariant that made the dead entry possible.
- Add `_next` to the web upload filter's `EXCLUDED_DIRS`, which had the same `.next`/`_next` gap on the live browser ingestion path.

**Explicitly out of scope / not done here**

- **No "looks minified" heuristic.** #3007 floats treating a very long single line as generated. It would catch every bundler's naming scheme at once, but it is a content-based judgement that can misfire on legitimate generated-and-wanted source, so it deserves its own change with its own evidence.
- **Other bundlers' output directories** (`.svelte-kit/output`, `.angular/cache`, Vite's `.vite`) are not audited here; only the reported `_next` gap and the already-intended `public/build` are addressed.
- ~~**`env` over-matching.**~~ *Resolved on `main` while this PR was open:* #3043 removed `'env'` and `'generated'` from the name set and gated them behind `ROOT_ARTIFACT_DIRECTORIES` + a `pyvenv.cfg` probe, so a JS project's `src/lib/env/` is no longer skipped. Nothing left to do here.
- **A repo with hand-written source in a directory literally named `_next`** loses that subtree, because `_next` goes into the *unanchored* name set. Measured on fixtures: a `packages/_next/` source tree loses 5 of 11 files including its `package.json`, `tsconfig.json` and `go.mod`. Judged acceptable — `_next` is Next.js's reserved *emitted* path, not a source convention, and unlike `'packages'` (deliberately removed from this set for exactly that reason) there is no observed repo that uses it for source. A working remedy exists if one ever appears: child-anchored fragments (`_next/static`, `_next/server`, `_next/data`, `_next/image`) plus an `existsSync` probe in `isHardcodedIgnoredDirectoryAtPath`, following the pattern #3043 established for `env`/`generated`. Verified to keep all tests green while recovering the source tree and still dropping every chunk. Not adopted here because the trigger is hypothetical.
- **The `.gitnexusignore` escape hatch is spelling-sensitive** and this PR does not change that. `!_next`, `!_next/` and `!**/_next/` recover the files; `!_next/*`, `!_next/**` and `!**/_next/**` *alone* are silent no-ops, because `childrenIgnored` prunes the directory before any file reaches `ignored()`. The repo's own #596 test writes the working `!dir/` + `!dir/**` pair. Pre-existing, unchanged by #3043, worth its own issue.
- **An ancestor negation voids the new rule.** `!android/` in `.gitnexusignore` *or* `.gitignore` short-circuits `hasExplicitUnignore` so `DEFAULT_IGNORE_LIST` is never consulted below it — measured: all 5 Capacitor chunks leak, on `main` and on this branch alike. Pre-existing #771 precedence, but it means a Capacitor user who unignores the native shell must also add an explicit `_next/` line.
- **`FETCHES` edges stay empty** on such a repo. That was reported alongside this in #3007; the graph-assisted consumer path needs `Route` nodes built from source, which this makes possible but does not itself deliver.

## Implementation notes

**`'public/build'` is deleted, not relocated.** The first draft of this PR moved it into a new `DEFAULT_IGNORED_PATH_FRAGMENTS` list with a matching `shouldIgnorePath` branch. Review established that the mechanism, while correct, was *unreachable*: all four of its match forms (`===`, `startsWith(f + '/')`, `includes('/' + f + '/')`, `endsWith('/' + f)`) put a `/` or an end-of-string on both sides of `build`, so a fragment match strictly implies `build` is a whole path segment — which the per-segment `DEFAULT_IGNORE_LIST` loop already catches one branch earlier. Measured over 768,420 generated paths: **65,506 fragment matches, 0 of them decisive, 0 implication violations.** Deleting the branch left every assertion in this PR green.

So the entry was inert *in that set*, but its paths were never unignored — bare `'build'` covered `public/build/**` on both sides. That makes this a redundant string, not a coverage hole, and #3007 offered exactly this branch: *"real two-segment handling, **or removal**."* Removal wins: it is a smaller diff than the mechanism it replaces, and it leaves nothing dead behind.

**`_next` is now pinned as a segment match.** The original five tests could not distinguish a segment rule from a substring rule — replacing the entry with `normalizedPath.includes('_next')` passed all of them, while silently eating `src/_nextgen/index.ts`. Added negative cases close that.

**The web upload filter had the same gap.** `gitnexus-web/src/lib/upload-filter.ts` `EXCLUDED_DIRS` is the live browser path (`RepoAnalyzer.tsx:402` → `filterRepoFiles` → `POST /api/analyze/upload` → the CLI walker) and listed `.next` but not `_next`, so a #3007-shaped repo uploaded its whole minified tree against the server's 20000-file / 250 MB caps for files the analyzer then discards. (Note there is *also* a `gitnexus-web/src/config/ignore-service.ts` carrying the same gap — it is orphaned dead code with zero importers since #536 retired the in-browser pipeline, verified by module-graph reachability from `src/main.tsx`, so it is left alone here.)

The guard test asserts no member of `DEFAULT_IGNORE_LIST` contains `/`, so the next person who adds `foo/bar` there gets a failing test instead of a silently inert entry. I verified the guard actually fails by reintroducing `'public/build'` into the name set — it reports `expected [ 'public/build' ] to deeply equal []` — rather than trusting that a green test proves anything.

## Testing & verification

New: `gitnexus/test/unit/ignore-build-output.test.ts` (6 tests) — `_next` in both bare and Capacitor/Cordova positions; `_next` as a whole segment vs a substring (`src/_nextgen/index.ts`, `packages/my_next/src/index.ts`, `src/prefix_next.ts`); `public/build` at repo root and nested; the slash-free guard; plus negative cases ensuring ordinary source is untouched (`src/next-steps.ts`, `src/nextConfig/index.ts`, `packages/next-auth/src/index.ts`, `public/favicon-loader.ts`, `src/public/api.ts`).

New: a case in `gitnexus-web/src/lib/upload-filter.test.ts` covering `_next` at bare, Android and iOS positions plus the `_nextgen` negative.

**Both new behaviors were ablated, not just observed green.** Removing `'_next'` from `EXCLUDED_DIRS` fails the web case; swapping the segment rule for `normalizedPath.includes('_next')` fails the substring case. A test that cannot go red pins nothing.

- [x] `cd gitnexus && npm test` — 12776 passed / 7 failed. The 7 (`analyzer-identity`, `assert-publish-grammar-coverage`, `review-agent-workflow`, `wiki-llm-client`) fail identically on pristine `main`; all pre-existing.
- [x] `cd gitnexus && npx tsc --noEmit` — clean
- [x] `npx eslint` on changed files — no errors, no new warnings
- [x] `cd gitnexus-web && npm test` — 419 passed / 1 failed (`agent-history.test.ts`, ambient-env credential leak; fails identically with this branch's changes stashed)

**Measured as a diff, not just as a count.** Against a production Capacitor-wrapped Next.js app (1558 JS/TS files on disk), comparing this branch's `shouldIgnorePath` with `main`'s over every file:

| | |
| --- | --- |
| newly ignored | **256** |
| of those, under `src/` | **0** |
| previously ignored, now indexed (regressions) | **0** |

The 256 are all under `_next/`, `android/` or `ios/`.

> **⚠️ This table was measured against `main` at `aac7515d`, before #3043 landed.** Its footnote used to explain three `src/` files as ignored on both sides via the `'env'` entry and the `.d.ts` rule — #3043 has since **deleted both of those rules**, so `src/lib/env/*.js` and `*.d.ts` are now ignored by neither side and the footnote no longer applies. The headline numbers have not been re-measured against the current base because the source repo is not available here; the `_next` behavior itself is covered by the ablated tests above.

## Risk & rollout

- **Requires a re-index to take effect.** `npx gitnexus analyze` re-walks; affected repos will drop the bundle files from their index and lose the bogus `Route` nodes built from them.
- **Node counts will fall** on repos that were indexing build output, and `Route` nodes sourced from bundles disappear. That is the intended correction, but it is a visible change to graph size and to `route_map` output for those repos.
- **This also affects group sync**, which builds its file list through the same `createIgnoreFilter` — a welcome side effect, since bundle output produced no useful contracts.
- **The realistic false positive** is a project that genuinely keeps hand-written source in a directory named `_next` or under `public/build`. Both are conventional build-output locations. On the **CLI/analyze path** a `.gitnexusignore` negation recovers such a tree — use the bare `!_next/` form, which works at any depth; `!_next/**` *alone* is a silent no-op, because `childrenIgnored` prunes the directory before any descendant pattern is tested. On the **browser upload path** there is no escape hatch at all: `EXCLUDED_DIRS` is a client-side pre-filter that reads no repository ignore rules, so a negation cannot recover what it drops.
- **Rollback:** revert the commit; the next `analyze` restores the previous behavior.
- Release notes: `fix` → 🐛 Bug Fixes.

## Checklist

- [x] PR body meets repo minimum length
- [x] No `AGENTS.md` / overlay changes in this PR
- [x] No secrets, tokens, or machine-specific paths committed
- [x] No new `GITNEXUS_*` environment variables

### 📝 Summary by GitNexus

## Summary

*A broad repository ignore and upload-filter change with critical graph reach, centered on build-output handling and accompanied by targeted tests. The file-level risk is low, but the affected configuration sits on paths used across the codebase.*

**🔴 CRITICAL blast radius. This appears to be an ingestion and ignore-filter change spanning `gitnexus/src/config/ignore-service.ts` and the web upload filter, with broad downstream reach.**

The main review focus is `gitnexus/src/config/ignore-service.ts`, where `DEFAULT_IGNORE_LIST`, `createIgnoreFilter`, `loadIgnoreRules`, `shouldIgnorePath`, `isRootArtifactDirectory`, and related ignore helpers changed. This area has the strongest architectural concentration in `Extractors`, with additional impact across `Config`, `Wiki`, `Group`, `Typescript`, `Import-resolvers`, and `Storage`.

The web side changes `FilterResult`, `EXCLUDED_DIRS`, and `MAX_FILE_BYTES` in `gitnexus-web/src/lib/upload-filter.ts`. title: test/ is never typechecked: tsconfig.json includes only src/**/*
body:
## The gap

`gitnexus/tsconfig.json` ends with:

```json
"include": ["src/**/*"]
```

So `npx tsc --noEmit`, the CI quality gate, checks the source tree and nothing else. Vitest does not close the gap either: it transforms TypeScript by stripping types, so a test file with a genuine type error runs green. Between the two, **no gate in this repo ever typechecks `test/`**.

## What it cost, concretely

In #1432 I added a test helper and called it from `test/unit/parser-loader-abi.test.ts`. `tsc --noEmit` was clean, prettier and eslint were clean, and 426 tests passed. The file did not compile:

```
test/unit/parser-loader-abi.test.ts(155,52): error TS2345: Argument of type 'string'
  is not assignable to parameter of type 'SupportedLanguages'.
```

The `gitnexus-check` bot caught it in review ([discussion_r3821789768](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/pull/1432#discussion_r3821789768)). A review bot is the wrong place for a compiler error to surface. Probing the rest of that PR's own files with a scoped `tsc` then turned up two more nobody had seen: `Parser.Language` is not an exported member, and a `ParsedImport` filter that never narrowed the union, so a property was read through `!` on an arm that does not have it. All three are fixed in the PR. The point is that a compiler would have caught all three in a second, and nothing in CI ever asked it to.

## Scale, measured

Same compiler options as `tsconfig.json` (including `strict: false`), `include: ["test/**/*.ts", "src/**/*"]`, `exclude: ["test/fixtures/**"]`, run at `aac7515d`:

| | |
|---|---|
| Errors | **734** |
| Files with at least one error | **135** |
| Test files in scope (`test/**/*.ts`, no fixtures) | 939 |
| Already clean | **86 %** |

`test/fixtures/**` has to stay excluded and is not part of this: it is parser input, much of it deliberately malformed or importing packages that are not installed. Including it adds 216 errors that mean nothing.

## Why this is smaller than 734 suggests

The errors are concentrated, and two mechanical patterns account for most of them.

| Slice | Errors | Share |
|---|---|---|
| `test/unit/type-env.test.ts` alone | 354 | 48 % |
| Top 10 files | 497 | 68 % |
| Top 50 files | 640 | 87 % |

| Pattern | Errors | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| A string literal where the parameter wants `SupportedLanguages` (`'typescript'` → `SupportedLanguages.TypeScript`) | 401 | mechanical |
| `Parser.Language` (not an exported member) → `Parameters<Parser['setLanguage']>[0]` | 20, in 8 files | mechanical, one line each |
| Everything else (mock shapes missing properties, incompatible return types, unnarrowed unions) | 313 | case by case |

421 of 734 errors (**57 %**) are those two patterns. And 106 of the 135 affected files have three errors or fewer, so most of the tail is a one-line fix per file.

## Suggested shape

1. `gitnexus/tsconfig.test.json` — extends `tsconfig.json`, `noEmit`, includes `test/**/*.ts`, excludes `test/fixtures/**`.
2. Clear the two mechanical patterns and `type-env.test.ts` first; that is roughly two thirds of the total in a reviewable diff.
3. Work down the tail. The 106 files with ≤3 errors are decent `good first issue` material.
4. Add `npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.test.json` to the quality job once it is green, so it cannot regress.

Step 4 can also go first as a non-blocking step, if you would rather see the number in CI before anyone is held to it.

## Reproducing

```bash
cd gitnexus
cat > tsconfig.probe.json <<'JSON'
{
  "extends": "./tsconfig.json",
  "compilerOptions": { "noEmit": true, "rootDir": ".", "declaration": false },
  "include": ["test/**/*.ts", "src/**/*"],
  "exclude": ["test/fixtures/**"]
}
JSON
npx tsc -p tsconfig.probe.json
```

All of this is measured under the repo's current `strict: false`. Turning strictness up on the test tree is a separate and much larger conversation, and nothing above assumes it.

I can take steps 1 and 2 if that helps.

title: fix(group)!: stop group sync claiming matching it never did
body:
## Summary

Fixes #3006. Every place `gitnexus group sync` told you something untrue about its matching, in one pass.

It started narrow: `gitnexus group create` wrote `matching.bm25_threshold` and `matching.embedding_threshold` into every generated `group.yaml`, and no matcher ever read either. Investigating turned up a whole surface — config keys, a CLI flag, an MCP parameter, localized help in two languages — describing a BM25/embedding matching cascade that was never built.

Review then found the same defect in the flags left behind. `--exact-only` was inert too, and strictly worse: it promised to suppress a stage that **does** run and **does** write cross-links. Honouring it exposed the next layer — a sync could now deliberately produce a narrower graph, and nothing recorded that, so `group_impact` and cross-repo `trace` reported a knowingly incomplete answer as complete.

So this does three things: **removes** the surface describing work never done, **honours** the flag whose stage actually exists, and **reports** a narrowed result everywhere it is read — the registry, the bridge, three MCP payloads and three CLI renderers — under its own truncation reason, because its remedy (re-run without the flag) differs from re-syncing a repo that failed to read.

> ⚠️ **Breaking.** Two CLI flags (`--skip-embeddings`, `--allow-stale`), one MCP parameter
> (`skipEmbeddings`), and five `group.yaml` keys (`matching.bm25_threshold`,
> `matching.embedding_threshold`, `matching.max_candidates_per_step`,
> `detect.embedding_fallback`, `detect.shared_libs`) are removed. The CLI removals ARE a
> runtime break — commander exits 1 on an unknown option, before the action runs. Existing
> `group.yaml` files keep loading and keep their keys. See Risk & rollout.

## Motivation / context

The inert surface, in full:

| Surface | State |
| --- | --- |
| `matching.bm25_threshold` / `matching.embedding_threshold` | parsed (`config-parser.ts`), persisted (`storage.ts`), read by nothing |
| `detect.embedding_fallback` | defaulted and written to the template, read by nothing |
| `MatchType = 'exact' \| 'manifest' \| 'wildcard' \| 'bm25' \| 'embedding'` | 2 of 5 variants unreachable |
| `SyncOptions.skipEmbeddings` | declared in `sync.ts` and never read — the only occurrence in the file was the declaration |
| `gitnexus group sync --skip-embeddings` | accepted, threaded through `GroupService`, ignored |
| CLI help, `en` + `zh-CN` | *"Exact + BM25 only (no embedding fallback)"* |
| MCP `group_sync` schema | `skipEmbeddings`, described as *"Exact + BM25 only (Demo PR: same as default exact path)"* |

`sync.ts` imports exactly `buildProviderIndex`, `runExactMatch` and `runWildcardMatch`, and the printed cascade has one stage:

```
Matching cascade:
  exact:     1 cross-links (confidence 1.0)
  unmatched: 225 contracts
```

This matters beyond tidiness. An operator whose links do not match reaches for those thresholds first, and turning either knob changes nothing. Config that silently does nothing is how people conclude a feature is broken.

## Why remove rather than implement

Measured on a real backend/frontend pair. Of **165 consumer contracts, 149 link exactly and 16 do not**:

- **9 are third-party** — Google OAuth (`/oauth2/v3/tokeninfo`, `/oauth2/v2/userinfo`), Apple public keys (`/auth/keys`), PostHog, image annotation. These have no in-group provider *by construction*. Similarity matching cannot recover them; it can only invent false links.
- **2 are verb mismatches.** The frontend calls `POST /links` and `GET /links/check-exists`; the backend declares `GET /links` and eleven other `/links/*` routes, but neither of those. A fuzzy path match would link a POST consumer to a GET provider — worse than leaving it unmatched.
- **The rest are path-extraction artifacts** — a leading `{param}` from an unresolved base URL, and a ternary inside a template.

So roughly **none** of the sixteen would be correctly recovered, and several would be actively mis-linked. Cross-link output is presented as fact, so a wrong link costs more than a missing one.

Worth noting for anyone weighing the other direction: the repo's existing BM25 code (`core/search/bm25-index.ts`) is `searchFTSFromLbug`, a per-repo full-text query over graph symbols. It is not a path-vs-path similarity scorer, so wiring the cascade would mean writing a new matcher, not reusing what is there.

## Areas touched

- [x] `gitnexus/` (CLI / core / MCP server)
- [ ] `gitnexus-web/` (Vite / React UI)
- [ ] `.github/` (workflows, actions)
- [ ] `eval/` or other tooling
- [ ] Docs / agent config only

## Scope & constraints

**In scope**

- Remove the two `matching` thresholds and `detect.embedding_fallback` from the schema, defaults, and generated template.
- Remove the unreachable `'bm25' | 'embedding'` `MatchType` variants.
- Remove `skipEmbeddings` from `SyncOptions`, `GroupService`, the CLI flag, both help catalogues, and the MCP `group_sync` schema.

**Explicitly out of scope / not done here**

- **No matcher is added or changed.** `runExactMatch` / `runWildcardMatch` behavior is untouched; this only deletes surface that described a stage that never ran.
- **`exclude_links_paths` and `exclude_links_param_only_paths` stay.** Those are read and work (`matching.ts`).
- **`matching.max_candidates_per_step` and `detect.shared_libs` are now also removed.** Review found both inert in exactly the same three-place way as the keys above: declared, defaulted, written into every generated `group.yaml`, and read by nothing. `shared_libs` gates no extractor at all — `'lib'` contracts come only from the operator-declared manifest extractor.
- **The `POST /links` / `GET /links/check-exists` mismatch is not investigated.** It surfaced while gathering evidence and looks like a genuine frontend/backend divergence in that codebase, not a GitNexus bug.

## Implementation notes

**Existing `group.yaml` files keep loading.** `parseGroupConfig` builds its config as `{ ...DEFAULT_MATCHING, ...(raw.matching as object) }`, so a removed key present in a user's YAML is simply not part of the typed schema any more — it does not throw, and nothing reads it. A regression test pins this, and pins PRESERVE rather than merely "does not throw": a legacy config carrying every removed key still parses AND still carries those keys through, which matters because `group add` / `group remove` round-trip the operator's file through `loadGroupConfig` -> `yaml.dump` -> write. Anything the parser dropped would be deleted from their checked-in `group.yaml` on their next `group add`.

**The tests that changed asserted defaults that no longer exist.** The minimal-config case now asserts `exclude_links_paths` / `exclude_links_param_only_paths`, which are genuinely read; the legacy-config case gained preserve assertions for every removed key.

The YAML fixtures across the group test suite still carry the old keys, deliberately — they are now backward-compatibility evidence rather than schema examples.

## Testing & verification

- [x] `cd gitnexus && npx vitest run test/unit/group/ test/unit/tools.test.ts test/integration/group/` — 1167 passed / 0 failed.
- [x] `cd gitnexus && npx tsc --noEmit` — clean. `tsc -p tsconfig.test.json --noEmit` is 987 against a 989 baseline taken on the branch tip before the config-key removal — a gate that drifted to 994 mid-PR and was caught by review, not CI, since `tsconfig.json` is src-only and no workflow sees test-file type errors (measured against the branch tip, not `origin/main`, so the number reflects this work rather than the whole branch).
- [x] `cd gitnexus && npx tsc --noEmit` — clean
- [x] `npx eslint` — 0 errors (21 pre-existing non-null-assertion warnings, none new)
- [ ] `cd gitnexus-web && npm test` *(web untouched)*

Behavior checked against a real group:

```
$ gitnexus group sync <group> --skip-embeddings
error: unknown option '--skip-embeddings'

$ gitnexus group sync <group>
Matching cascade:
  exact:     1 cross-links (confidence 1.0)
Wrote contracts.json (233 contracts, 1 cross-links)
```

The exact/wildcard cascade is unchanged; only the flag is gone.

## Risk & rollout

- **BREAKING: two CLI flags, one MCP parameter and five config keys are removed.** Both were accepted and ignored, so nothing behaves differently — but a script or agent passing them now fails with `unknown option` rather than being silently misled. That is the intended trade: a loud failure beats a flag that pretends to do something. If maintainers prefer to stage this over a release, the alternative is to keep the flag accepted and mark it a documented no-op; happy to switch.
- **Persisted artifacts gain one optional field.** `contracts.json` and the bridge's `meta.json` now carry `suppressedMatchStages`. Additive and absent-tolerant both ways: a new build reads an old artifact as "not recorded", an older build ignores the key. No re-index or re-sync is required, and no schema version is bumped — see the forward-compatibility item under *Deliberately not done*.
- **Existing configs are unaffected** — verified by the legacy-config regression test.
- **`detect_changes` reports HIGH**, but that is process membership rather than blast radius: `registerGroupCommands` is step 1 of ten `RegisterGroupCommands → …` flows because it is the CLI entry point for every group subcommand. The genuine risk in this PR is the removed flag above, not the process count.
- **Rollback:** revert the commit. Nothing persisted depends on it.
- Release notes: `fix` with `!` → 💥 Breaking Changes.

## Checklist

- [x] PR body meets repo minimum length
- [x] Breaking change flagged with `!` in the title and `BREAKING CHANGE:` in the commit body
- [x] No secrets, tokens, or machine-specific paths committed
- [x] No new `GITNEXUS_*` environment variables

---

## Follow-up round: review findings addressed

This PR was reviewed by a multi-engine pass (five reviewer lenses plus an independent cross-model pass). Ten findings; all are closed here.

**The flags now do what they say.** `--exact-only` was inert in exactly the way `--skip-embeddings` was — declared, threaded through the CLI and MCP, read by nothing — and strictly worse, because the stage it promised to suppress *does* run and *does* write links. It is now honoured. `--allow-stale` had no stage to gate (the staleness check lives in `group status`, a different path), so it is removed under the same rationale as `--skip-embeddings`.

**A narrowed sync now says so.** An `--exact-only` run writes fewer cross-links, and nothing recorded that a stage had been suppressed by request. `contracts.json` and the bridge now carry `suppressedMatchStages`, and `crossRepoCompleteness` folds it in — so `group_impact`, cross-repo `trace`, `group_contracts` and `group status` stop reporting a narrowed graph as complete. It gets its own truncation reason (`'suppressed-stage'`) rather than reusing `'incomplete-sync'`, because the remedy differs: re-run without the flag, not repair a repo that read fine.

**`group_sync` validates its input.** `Boolean(params.exactOnly)` on an untyped MCP payload made the string `"false"` truthy — a routine shape for an LLM caller — so a caller asking to KEEP wildcard matching got it suppressed and persisted. Rejected now, not coerced. The two retired parameters are refused by name, matching what the CLI already does.

**Output and descriptions match behavior.** `group sync` reports every matching stage and names a skipped one as skipped rather than printing `0`; the CLI, both locales, and the MCP schema now agree with each other and with the code.

### Deliberately not done

**Forward-compatibility for group persisted artifacts across mixed CLI/MCP versions.** An
`--exact-only` sync writes a narrowed graph carrying `suppressedMatchStages`; a build that
predates the field ignores it, sees both repo lists empty, and reports the artifact complete.
This is newly *exposed* by this PR — before it, `exactOnly` was inert, so no older reader could
meet a freshly-narrowed graph. What is pre-existing is the underlying gap: group artifacts have
no forward-versioning contract for new completeness semantics. `contracts.json` is still
`version: 1` and its reader does not enforce that version at all.

Not fixed here, and specifically **not** by bumping `BRIDGE_SCHEMA_VERSION`: that constant gates
the LadybugDB schema under a documented discard-and-resync contract, so using it to version
metadata semantics would misuse it — and would fix only half the problem, since old
`contracts.json` readers would still ignore the field. A real fix is a format/generation protocol
with fail-closed semantics, which is its own change. The risk shape to watch in the meantime is
a new CLI alongside a still-running old MCP server against the same group directory.

**Shared registry+bridge generation identity.** The two artifacts are published independently, so
a failed bridge write after a committed registry leaves them describing different syncs. This PR
contains that case by withdrawing the stale bridge's provenance so nothing calls its answer
complete, but atomic generation identity across both artifacts is the architectural fix and is
out of scope.

A repo-wide unknown-parameter layer for every MCP tool. Five parameters are read by backends and declared in no schema, and three tools dispatch with no schema entry at all, so a strict layer would reject working calls until each is reconciled — that reconciliation is the work, and it is larger than this PR.

<!-- gitnexus-pr-summary:v1:start -->

---

### 📝 Summary by GitNexus

## Summary

*A broad group subsystem change removes the advertised matching cascade across core logic, CLI and MCP surfaces, with substantial downstream reach. The overall blast level is critical, despite the individual file risk remaining low.*

**🔴 CRITICAL blast radius. A group subsystem change removing the advertised matching cascade, spanning CLI, MCP, core group code, and tests with reach into 34 dependents.**

title: Exact CLI reads eagerly warn about missing VECTOR with zero embeddings
body:
### Area

gitnexus (CLI / core / indexing / MCP server)

### Summary

Exact `context` and `cypher` reads eagerly probe the optional VECTOR extension and emit a level-40 warning even when the index has zero `CodeEmbedding` rows and the command does not perform semantic retrieval.

### Context

This was discovered while using an exact-symbol `gitnexus context --file ... --content` command as an index-freshness witness. The warning made the failure appear to be caused by a missing VECTOR extension, but the actual command result was that an extensionless Python script was not indexed. That separate source-coverage request is already tracked by #2707.

The current read-pool initialization in `src/core/lbug/pool-adapter.ts` eagerly calls `loadVectorExtension(..., { policy: 'load-only' })` for every pool. This affects exact symbol lookup and raw Cypher, not just semantic/hybrid search.

### Expected behavior

- Exact `context`, UID lookup, and raw `cypher` operations that do not use semantic retrieval should return clean machine-readable output without an irrelevant high-severity VECTOR warning.
- VECTOR should be loaded lazily when a semantic operation requires it, or the unavailable probe should be debug-level/suppressed when the current command can proceed exactly.
- A genuine command error such as `Symbol '<name>' not found` should remain the clear terminal diagnostic.

### Actual behavior

Every exact read initializes the shared pool, attempts `LOAD VECTOR`, and writes this level-40 record before the command JSON:

```json
{"level":40,"name":"gitnexus","msg":"GitNexus: VECTOR extension unavailable; continuing without VECTOR features. load-only policy (no install attempted); LOAD VECTOR failed: Binder exception: Extension: vector is an official extension and has not been installed. You can install it by: install vector."}
```

This occurs even though:

- `MATCH (e:CodeEmbedding) RETURN count(e)` returns `0`;
- `gitnexus doctor` reports the supported `exact-scan` fallback;
- an exact context lookup in an indexed `.py` file succeeds;
- raw node-count Cypher succeeds and has no semantic dependency.

For a missing symbol, the same warning precedes the real JSON error and can cause wrappers that surface the nonzero command's diagnostic stream to report VECTOR as the apparent cause.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Analyze a repository without embeddings so it contains no `CodeEmbedding` rows.
2. Leave VECTOR uninstalled; do not set `GITNEXUS_LBUG_EXTENSION_INSTALL`.
3. Confirm the index has no embeddings:

   ```sh
   gitnexus cypher 'MATCH (e:CodeEmbedding) RETURN count(e) AS embeddingCount' --repo /path/to/repo
   ```

   The command returns `embeddingCount = 0` but first emits the VECTOR warning.

4. Run an exact symbol lookup:

   ```sh
   gitnexus context known_symbol --repo /path/to/repo --file path/to/file.py --content
   ```

   The lookup succeeds but first emits the same warning.

5. Run a missing-symbol lookup:

   ```sh
   gitnexus context missing_symbol --repo /path/to/repo --file path/to/script --content
   ```

   The warning precedes the actual `{ "error": "Symbol 'missing_symbol' not found" }` result.

### Environment

- OS: macOS arm64
- Node: v26.7.0
- GitNexus: 1.6.10-rc.211
- LadybugDB: 0.19.1
- Embedding backend: configured HTTP provider, reported supported by `gitnexus doctor`
- `GITNEXUS_LBUG_EXTENSION_INSTALL`: unset
- VECTOR index: unavailable
- Semantic mode: exact-scan
- CodeEmbedding rows: 0

### Logs / screenshots

Successful exact lookup:

```text
{"level":40,...,"msg":"GitNexus: VECTOR extension unavailable; continuing without VECTOR features..."}
{
  "status": "found",
  "symbol": { "name": "delegate_complete_state_tier", "filePath": "scripts/tests/spec-feature-orchestrator-state-test.py" },
  "epistemic": "exact"
}
exit 0
```

Missing exact lookup:

```text
{"level":40,...,"msg":"GitNexus: VECTOR extension unavailable; continuing without VECTOR features..."}
{
  "error": "Symbol 'validate_review_lease_terminal_ledger' not found"
}
exit 1
```

title: macOS arm64 1.6.6: incremental analyze SIGBUS in FTSIndex::deleteFromTermsTable; poisoned lbug.wal then SIGSEGVs every DB open (WALReplayer::replayNodeDeletionRecord)
body:
## Environment

- gitnexus **1.6.6** (global npm install), Node v25.9.0, **macOS 26.4 (25E246), Apple Silicon (M4)**
- Repo: ~3,800-file Electron + TS + Python monorepo; index ~29.7k nodes; embeddings enabled (`analyze --embeddings`, ~20k embeddings)
- Several idle `gitnexus mcp` processes from other sessions were alive during the crash window

## Crash 1 — incremental analyze SIGBUS in FTSIndex::deleteFromTermsTable

Routine incremental `gitnexus analyze` (a few commits changed) crashed natively near the end of the run, while deleting stale FTS terms:

```
EXC_BAD_ACCESS SIGBUS — KERN_PROTECTION_FAILURE
lbugjs.node             lbug::storage::NodeTable::initScanState(...)
libfts.lbug_extension   lbug::fts_extension::FTSIndex::deleteFromTermsTable(...)
libfts.lbug_extension   lbug::fts_extension::FTSIndex::delete_(...)
lbugjs.node             lbug::storage::NodeTable::delete_(...)
lbugjs.node             lbug::processor::SingleLabelNodeDeleteExecutor::delete_(...)
lbugjs.node             lbug::processor::DeleteNode::getNextTuplesInternal(...)
```

The run was invoked as `analyze | tail`, so the shell surfaced **tail's exit 0** and the crash went unnoticed: `incrementalInProgress` stayed set and a dirty `lbug.wal` was left behind.

## Crash 2 — every subsequent DB open SIGSEGVs replaying the poisoned WAL

Any later write open (including the automatic full-rebuild escalation and `--repair-fts`) dies in WAL recovery:

```
EXC_BAD_ACCESS SIGSEGV — KERN_INVALID_ADDRESS at 0x0
lbugjs.node  lbug::storage::NodeTable::delete_(...)
lbugjs.node  lbug::storage::WALReplayer::replayNodeDeletionRecord(...)
lbugjs.node  lbug::storage::WALReplayer::replayActiveWAL(...)
lbugjs.node  lbug::storage::WALReplayer::replay(...)
lbugjs.node  lbug::storage::StorageManager::recover(...)
lbugjs.node  lbug::main::Database::Database(...)
```

Additionally, **query processes from other sessions crash-looped** (macOS `.ips` crash reports every ~30–45 s) while the poisoned WAL existed — each `gitnexus query` opens the DB and hits the same replay crash.

## Reproduced twice in one evening

The WAL poisoning reproduced a second time: a rebuild that regenerated embeddings for new/changed nodes (delete + insert path) died mid-run and again left a WAL that SIGSEGVs every open. Symptom triad during recovery: `Could not set lock on file` (a repair-sidecar `analyze --force` holding the single-writer lock) → `WAL checkpoint rotation failed` → `LOAD fts failed after successful INSTALL`.

## Workaround that recovered both times

```bash
mv .gitnexus/lbug .gitnexus/lbug.quarantine
mv .gitnexus/lbug.wal .gitnexus/lbug.quarantine.wal
GITNEXUS_LBUG_EXTENSION_INSTALL=auto gitnexus analyze --embeddings --force --wal-checkpoint-threshold 67108864
```

(~8 min full rebuild; embeddings regenerated/preserved; the cross-session crash storm stops immediately once the poisoned file is renamed away.)

## Related

- #1710 (WAL rename crash during large indexing runs — where the `--wal-checkpoint-threshold` guidance comes from)
- #1196 / #1221 (VECTOR extension crashes with `--embeddings`)
- #2233 (native crash with @ladybugdb/core)

The stacks point at LadybugDB internals (FTS delete path + WAL replay of node deletion records), but filing here since gitnexus bundles the native module and orchestrates these code paths. Happy to attach the full `.ips` files if useful.

title: repoId() collision suffix is a prefix of the path, so every colliding repo on a machine hashes to the same id (L1VzZX on macOS)
body:
`gitnexus@1.6.4`, `dist/mcp/local/local-backend.js`. Two same-named repositories at different paths are given the *same* disambiguated id, so the collision handler disambiguates nothing and the registry becomes last-write-wins. The result is a bare-name query silently answering from the wrong index — no error, no warning, and `gitnexus list` reports everything as healthy.

## The code

```js
repoId(name, repoPath) {
    const base = name.toLowerCase();
    for (const [id, handle] of this.repos) {
        if (id === base && handle.repoPath !== path.resolve(repoPath)) {
            const hash = Buffer.from(repoPath).toString('base64url').slice(0, 6);
            return `${base}-${hash}`;
        }
    }
    return base;
}
```

`Buffer.from(path).toString('base64url')` is an **encoding**, not a hash — its output is positional, so `.slice(0, 6)` keeps the first 4.5 bytes of the *path string itself*. Every absolute path on macOS starts `/Users`, and on Linux `/home`, so every colliding entry on a machine produces an identical suffix.

## Reproduction

Two real checkouts of the same repo on this machine:

```
$ node -e '
  const h = p => Buffer.from(p).toString("base64url").slice(0,6);
  console.log(h("/Users/me/code/_depwork/my-repo"));   // L1VzZX
  console.log(h("/Users/me/code/platform/my-repo"));   // L1VzZX
'
L1VzZX
L1VzZX
```

Both map to `my-repo-L1VzZX`. `refreshRepos()` then does `this.repos.set(id, handle)` in registry-file order, so the last one written wins and the earlier index becomes unreachable by *either* name — the bare name and the suffixed name both resolve to the same single entry.

## Why this is not an edge case for worktree users

GitNexus names a repository after its **git remote**, and every git worktree of a repo shares that remote. So `gitnexus analyze` run from a worktree registers a second entry under the same name. Any workflow that uses worktrees routinely — one per task, per agent, per issue — produces name collisions as the *normal* state, not an exceptional one.

In our case a `CLAUDE.md` instruction reading "run impact analysis before editing any symbol" was answering from a six-week-old index for weeks, because the collision resolved to the stale entry. Nothing surfaced it: the tool returned plausible results the whole time.

## Suggested fix

Use an actual hash of the resolved path rather than an encoding of its prefix:

```js
const hash = crypto.createHash('sha256')
                   .update(path.resolve(repoPath))
                   .digest('hex').slice(0, 8);
```

Three things worth pairing with it:

1. **Resolve both sides.** The comparison already uses `path.resolve(repoPath)` for the equality test, but hashes the *unresolved* `repoPath`. Two spellings of one path would then get two different ids.
2. **Make the collision visible.** A collision is currently silent. A one-line warning naming both paths — and having `gitnexus list` mark the colliding entries — would have turned weeks of wrong answers into a five-minute fix.
3. **Decide what a bare name means under collision.** Right now it means "whichever entry appears first in the registry file", which is insertion order and not something any caller can reason about. Erroring with the candidate ids would be more useful than picking one.

## Environment

- `gitnexus@1.6.4`, installed globally via npm
- macOS 24.6 (Darwin), Node via nvm
- Registry at `~/.gitnexus/registry.json`, 6 entries, one name duplicated across two real checkouts
