title: api_impact schema rejected by Grok 4.6: root anyOf needs object type
body:
## Summary

Calling `gitnexus_api_impact` from the main agent chat fails when the model is Grok 4.6. The call never reaches the backend. The error is:

`invalid-argument: gitnexus_api_impact: tool parameter root must be an object type (root schema is an anyOf/oneOf union with a non-object branch)`

The same call from a `@fixer` subagent session works, so this looks like a schema problem that only strict validators trip on.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Install `gitnexus@1.6.9` globally and register `gitnexus mcp` as an MCP server in OpenCode.
2. Set the chat model to Grok 4.6 (xAI, SuperGrok plan).
3. Ask the main agent to run an API impact check, for example on route `/api/grants`.
4. The run fails with the `invalid-argument` error above before any backend code executes.

## Expected

The tool accepts `{ "route": "/api/grants" }` or `{ "file": "src/routes/x.ts" }` under Grok 4.6, same as under other models.

## Actual

Grok 4.6 rejects the tool definition itself, so no call shape works from the main chat.

## Environment

- gitnexus: 1.6.9 (global npm install)
- opencode: 1.18.18
- OS: Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS, kernel 7.0.0-30-generic, ThinkPad Z16 Gen 2
- Model: Grok 4.6 via xAI, SuperGrok subscription
- Working case: same call from a `@fixer` subagent session succeeds

## Root cause (found while debugging locally)

In the published package, `dist/mcp/tools.js` (around lines 690-704) defines the `api_impact` input as an object schema with `route`, `file`, `method`, `repo` properties, but also puts this at the schema root:

`anyOf: [{ required: ["route"] }, { required: ["file"] }]`

Those branches have no `type: "object"`, so a validator that requires the tool root to be an object rejects it. The runtime in `local-backend.js` (`apiImpact`) already requires at least one of `route`/`file`, so the root `anyOf` adds nothing the backend does not check.

## Suggested fix

Drop the root `anyOf` from the `api_impact` input schema and keep one object schema with optional `route` and `file`. Move the "at least one of route or file" rule into the property descriptions or validate it in the backend (it already does). I patched my local install this way and both call shapes validate. Happy to open a PR if that helps.

## Scope

In: `api_impact` tool input schema in the MCP `tools/list` output.
Out: backend logic, other tools, docs.

title: feat(zig): mark CALLS edges inside comptime-false branches as staticGated
body:
## Summary

Adds `staticGated` metadata to CALLS edges: `true` when the call site sits in a branch that is provably unreachable from the indexed source at compile time. First producer is Zig, where `if (CONST_FALSE) { ... }` and the `else` of `if (CONST_TRUE)` are the idiomatic feature-flag pattern (`pub const UPGRADERS_ENABLED: bool = false;`). A consumer that opts in (an impact view, say) can rank or filter those callers; nothing in the core does, and the edge itself is unchanged.

## Graph contract (added after review)

`CALLS` keeps its meaning: "there is a resolved call site from A to B". It has never meant "B is reachable from A", and this PR does not make it mean that. `staticGated` is additional, statically provable path-feasibility metadata on the edge, an opt-in analysis layer: no core pass reads it, process tracing, communities, impact BFS and every count treat the edge exactly as before, and the only surface that shows it today is a boolean on `impact` frontier edges. A future consumer that wants to treat gated callers differently must opt in explicitly and say so in its own contract. The wording used throughout is "provably unreachable from the indexed source at compile time"; the index has no production build configuration and makes no claim about production.

## Motivation / context

Follow-up to #1432 (Zig language support), item 3 of the real-project review there: build-mode / constant-gated branches were the one shape flagged as affecting reachability that the provider did not model. This is the static-gating half of that item, ported from `feat/zig-static-gated-edges-v2` (16 commits, written against the pre-#1432 provider) onto the merged one. The comptime evaluation itself is unchanged from that branch; only the wiring is new, because the merged provider emits Zig CALLS edges through the scope-resolution pipeline rather than the legacy call-processor path.

## Areas touched

- [x] `gitnexus/` (CLI / core / MCP server)
- [ ] `gitnexus-web/`
- [ ] `.github/`
- [ ] `eval/` or other tooling
- [ ] Docs / agent config only

Also `gitnexus-shared/` (two optional fields on `ReferenceSite` / `Reference`, and `GraphRelationship.staticGated`).

## Scope & constraints

**In scope**

- `call-extractors/zig-static-gating.ts`: file-local `const X: bool = true|false` table, re-aliased const chains (up to 5 hops, cycle-safe), `==` / `!=` against known bools, `and` / `or` folding, `var` never counts, else / else-if chain awareness. New `collectZigStaticGatedRanges` + `isPositionStaticGated` so a layer that only keeps `Capture.range` can use it.
- Zig capture emitter stamps `@reference.static-gated` on call captures inside a dead range. Same zero-range marker idiom as Go's `@reference.callee-position`; absent everywhere else, so no other language's captures change.
- `scope-extractor` -> `ReferenceSite.staticGated` -> `Reference.staticGated` -> `GraphRelationship.staticGated`, written by both Zig emit paths (`references-to-edges`, `free-call-fallback`) and the generic `tryEmitEdge*` bridge.
- Persistence: `staticGated BOOLEAN` column on the relationship table, CSV header/row column (`0`/`1`), legacy line-by-line loader tolerant of the 6-column form.
- `impact` MCP output: `staticGated: true` on `byDepth` items reached over such an edge (field absent = live or unmodelled; documented on the tool's byDepth contract). Traversal and risk do not filter or rank on it. Older indexes and other languages read as live.
- Condition shapes that fold: identifiers, bare literals, `and` / `or` / `==` / `!=`, parentheses, and prefix `!` (which tree-sitter-zig parses as `error_union_type`); both `if` statements and `if` expressions (`const x = if (c) a() else b();`).
- `SCHEMA_BUMP` 92 -> 93 (parse-time captures changed).

**Explicitly out of scope / not done here**

- Cross-file constants (tracked in #3162) (`if (cfg.FOO)` with `const cfg = @import("cfg.zig")`). The module resolves them via `lookupBoolsForPath`, but the capture emitter runs per file inside the parse worker with only `{ path, content }`, so it cannot open the sibling source. The two positive cross-file cases in `zig-static-gating.test.ts` are `it.skip` with that reason; the negative ones pass. Wiring it needs the emitter (or a post-pass) to see imported files; happy to do that as the next PR if the shape here is acceptable.
- `builtin.mode == .Debug` / `.ReleaseFast` gates. That needs a build-mode input the index does not have; on a real project (below) those are the majority of gated branches, so this PR is deliberately conservative: it never marks an edge it cannot prove.
- Consumers acting on the flag (`impact --live-only` etc.). This PR only records the fact.

## Implementation notes

- Why a marker capture rather than a resolver hook: sites are built generically in `scope-extractor` from `CaptureMatch` records, which carry ranges and text but no `SyntaxNode`; the only place both the AST and the file are in hand is the language's capture emitter. Computing dead ranges once per file there (`collectZigStaticGatedRanges`) and testing each call anchor's position is O(calls + ifs) and keeps the generic layer language-agnostic.
- Why `reason`-independent: the flag is orthogonal to how the edge resolved (`local-call`, `import-resolved`, the `(constructor)` marker), so it is a property, not a reason suffix.
- Three commits: the first squashes the eight evaluation-logic commits of the source branch (module + fixture + tests, file content unchanged); the second is the new wiring; the third is the original `feat(graph): add staticGated edge property` cherry-picked with its two conflicts resolved onto the current `RelPairRouter` / `queryAndDrain` writers (the CSV column now lives in `REL_CSV_HEADER` / `buildRelRow`, the single source of relationship row bytes).

## Testing & verification

- [x] `cd gitnexus && npx tsc --noEmit` clean; `gitnexus-shared` builds.
- [x] `npx vitest run test/integration/resolvers/zig-static-gating.test.ts test/integration/resolvers/zig.test.ts test/integration/lbug-load-overlap-errors.test.ts test/integration/lbug-core-adapter.test.ts test/integration/csv-pipeline.test.ts` -> 168 passed, 3 skipped (the two cross-file cases above + one pre-existing skip).
- [x] Prettier / eslint clean on the diff (pre-commit hook).
- [x] Real project, 199-file Zig codebase (FuryForged, same one as the #1432 rounds), indexed from scratch:
  - graph identical to the merged head (`932d9370`): 9,711 nodes / 21,005 edges / 5,461 CALLS, edge-by-edge diff +0 / -0, so the marker changes nothing where no constant gate exists;
  - `staticGated` present on every relationship (`MATCH ()-[r]->() RETURN r.staticGated, count(*)` -> `false: 21005`), zero `true`: the project's one file-local bool gate (`if (!ENABLED) return NO_ZONE;`) has no call in its dead branch, and its seven `if (builtin.mode == .Debug)` gates are the out-of-scope shape above. No false positives is the result that matters here.
  - index time 53.8s from scratch, same as before the change.
- [ ] `npm test` full unit suite (not run locally; CI).

## Risk & rollout

- Schema change: one nullable BOOLEAN column on the relationship table; `SCHEMA_BUMP` bumped, so existing indexes re-analyze on next run. Old indexes without the column read as `staticGated` undefined = live.
- Non-Zig languages: no capture, site, or edge changes; the CSV row gains a trailing `0`.
- No behaviour change for any consumer until one opts to filter on the flag.

title: zig: staticGated does not evaluate cross-file (@import) constants
body:
Follow-up to #3161 (Zig `staticGated` CALLS edges), tracking the two cases that PR ships as `it.skip`.

## What is not modelled

`staticGated` v1 evaluates `if` conditions from the **same file only**. A condition that reaches through an `@import` alias is left untagged (fail-open = live):

```zig
const cfg = @import("./cfg.zig");   // cfg.zig: pub const FOO: bool = false;

if (cfg.FOO) {
    gated_cross_file_foo();          // NOT tagged today
}
if (cfg.BAR) { ... } else {
    gated_cross_file_else();         // NOT tagged today (BAR is true)
}
```

Both cases have fixtures and tests in `test/integration/resolvers/zig-static-gating.test.ts` (`it.skip`, citing this issue) and `test/fixtures/lang-resolution/zig-static-gating/src/{main.zig,cfg.zig}`. The negative cross-file cases (unknown member, non-bool member) already pass because unknown folds to live.

## Why v1 skipped it

The stamp runs in the Zig capture emitter (`stampZigStaticGating` in `languages/zig/captures.ts`), which executes inside the parse worker with only `{ path, content }` of the current file. Resolving `cfg.FOO` needs the imported file's bool-constant table (`buildZigBoolConstMap` over `cfg.zig`), which the worker cannot see. The evaluator already accepts a `lookupBoolsForPath` callback (`collectZigStaticGatedRanges` / `evalCond`, `field_expression` case) — the worker just has no source for it.

## Options

1. **Second pass after all files are parsed**: keep per-file `ZigBoolConstMap` from the worker as a side output, then re-run only the `field_expression` conditions on the main thread and stamp the resulting ranges onto already-collected `ReferenceSite`s. Cheapest; needs sites to be addressable by position after the fact.
2. **Give the worker a read-only import pre-pass**: resolve `@import("./x.zig")` relative to `path` and read that file's constants directly. Simple but re-parses imported files per importer and only works when the import target is on disk with the same layout.
3. Model `builtin.mode` / `@import("builtin")` gates (`if (builtin.mode == .Debug)`) at the same time, since they are the other common compile-time gate and need the same hook (a synthetic table rather than a file).

Not blocking anything: unmodelled conditions stay live, which is the conservative direction.

title: fix(build): build the web UI from prepack, not from every npm ci
body:
## Summary

`npm ci` in `gitnexus/` no longer installs and Vite-builds a second package. The web UI is now built by `prepack` — the one lifecycle hook that actually needs it — instead of by `prepare`.

## Motivation / context

`node floor compat` has been failing repeatedly with:

```
Error: spawnSync /bin/sh ETIMEDOUT
  at file:///.../gitnexus/scripts/build.js:117:5
  spawnargs: [ '-c', 'npm ci' ], signal: 'SIGTERM'
```

That is not a hung install. `prepare` → `build.js` ran a nested `npm ci` for `gitnexus-web` (a separate ~650-package tree: React, Vite, LangChain, Mermaid) under an `execSync` timeout of 300s. On CI that install is uncached and has been observed taking ~7 minutes, so `execSync` SIGTERM'd a perfectly healthy install mid-flight and npm reported it as a build failure.

The job it kept killing only import-links the compiled CLI `dist` against the Node engines floor. It has no use for the web UI at all — and neither do typecheck, unit/integration tests, the tree-sitter ABI jobs, or `Dockerfile.cli`. Every one of them was paying for a full second product install because of where the build was wired.

A bigger timeout only moves the fuse. This removes the work.

## Areas touched

- [x] `gitnexus/` (CLI / core / MCP server)
- [ ] `gitnexus-web/` (Vite / React UI)
- [x] `.github/` (workflows, actions)
- [ ] `eval/` or other tooling
- [ ] Docs / agent config only

## Scope & constraints

**In scope**

- `scripts/build.js`: web build is opt-in via `--web` or `GITNEXUS_BUILD_WEB=1`.
- The fallback `npm ci` for `gitnexus-web` is **untimed**. A half-killed install leaves a broken tree and reports a misleading `ETIMEDOUT`; CI job timeouts are the right bound. `tsc`/`vite` keep a bounded timeout, raised 300s → 600s.
- `prepack` passes `--web`, so `npm pack` / `npm publish` still ship `web/` exactly as before. Added `npm run build:web` for local use.
- `packaged-install-smoke` and `publish` install `gitnexus-web` in their own visible step, so a slow install shows up as a slow step instead of dying inside an `execSync`.

**Explicitly out of scope / not done here**

- No dependency changes to `gitnexus-web`. Mermaid and `playwright-core` growth is what made the nested install expensive enough to trip the timeout, but trimming them is separate work.
- No npm caching added for the two jobs that do install the web tree; they pay roughly what the nested install cost before, just visibly and bounded by the job timeout.
- `gitnexus serve` from a monorepo checkout now falls back to `gitnexus-web/dist` or the built-in landing page unless you run `npm run build:web`. That fallback already existed and the landing page already tells you to run `cd gitnexus-web && npm run build`.

## Implementation notes

`Dockerfile.cli` never copies `gitnexus-web` into its build context, so it already skipped this path — its "the image is API-only" comment is now true by construction rather than by accident.

## Testing & verification

- [x] `cd gitnexus && npx tsc --noEmit` — clean
- [x] `npx prettier --check` on all changed files — clean
- [x] `npx vitest run` over the packaging/workflow suites (`build-web-optin`, `dockerfile-runtime-asset-parity`, `assert-publish-grammar-coverage`, `review-agent-workflow`, `skill-evolution-workflow`) — 101 passed

Both build paths were run end to end, not just asserted:

```
$ node scripts/build.js
[build] skipping web UI (pass --web or set GITNEXUS_BUILD_WEB=1 to include it)
[build] done — rewrote 437 files.
real 0m30.678s

$ node scripts/build.js --web
[build] copied web UI → gitnexus/web/
real 0m37.151s          # web/ contains index.html + assets/
```

New `gitnexus/test/unit/build-web-optin.test.ts` pins the contract so this cannot drift back: default build carries no `--web`, `prepack` does, the fallback install carries no timeout, pack/publish install the web tree first, and `node-floor-compat` never installs it.

title: Update-check scheduler spins at 1ms when refresh lock is held
body:
When another process holds the refresh lock, refresh() returns without updating the cache; the scheduler computes the next delay from the stale cache timestamp, which is already past due, producing a 1ms re-schedule loop of disk reads and lock attempts until the holder publishes.

**Suggested fix:** When the cache is still stale after a refresh attempt (lock-busy skip), schedule the next cycle with a bounded delay from now (e.g. 30-60s jittered) instead of deriving it from the stale checkedAt.

**Evidence:** `gitnexus/src/core/update-check.ts:275 — const delay = Number.isFinite(checkedAt) && checkedAt <= now ? Math.max(1, checkedAt + UPDATE_CACHE_TTL_MS - now) : UPDATE_CACHE_TTL_MS;`

title: Future-dated cache timestamp poisons monotonic publication
body:
A machine with a fast clock writes a future lastCheckAt; monotonic publication then suppresses every correctly-timed later write while freshness treats the entry as stale, so refresh runs every cycle yet never repairs the cache.

**Suggested fix:** Reject future-dated lastCheckAt during publication (and treat as stale at read), allowing a later lock holder to replace skew-poisoned entries.

**Evidence:** `gitnexus/src/core/update-check.ts:183 — if (current && Date.parse(current.lastCheckAt) > attemptStartedAt) return;`

title: feat: notify users when a newer gitnexus version is available
body:
## Summary

GitNexus now tells you when a newer version exists, on every human-facing surface: one stderr line on interactive CLI runs, a `gitnexus doctor` line, one structured stderr log per MCP server process, and a dismissible banner in the web UI fed by new optional `/api/info` fields.

## Motivation / context

Users on old versions hit already-fixed bugs and file stale issues; no surface previously reported that an upgrade exists (the web client even shipped an unused `fetchServerInfo`). The check is cache-first against the npm `latest` dist-tag (24h shared cache under `GITNEXUS_HOME`), so it adds no synchronous network latency and costs a firewalled machine at most one background attempt per day.

Residual review tickets addressed on this PR: #3167, #3168, #3169, #3170, #3171, #3172, #3173, #3174 (closed).

## Areas touched

- [x] `gitnexus/` (CLI / core / MCP server)
- [x] `gitnexus-web/` (Vite / React UI)
- [ ] `.github/` (workflows, actions)
- [ ] `eval/` or other tooling
- [ ] Docs / agent config only (`AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `.cursor/`, `llms.txt`, etc.)

## Scope & constraints

**In scope**

- Shared fail-open update checker (`src/core/update-check.ts` + `update-cache.ts` + `install-context.ts`): validated cache, hardened registry fetch, strict `x.y.z` compare, install-eligibility classification
- CLI: one i18n'd stderr line (TTY-gated) + hidden `__update-check` refresh child + `doctor` line
- MCP (stdio and `--http`): at most one structured pino info line per process per version, after connect, catch-isolated
- `serve`: `/api/info` gains optional `latestVersion`/`updateAvailable` from an in-memory snapshot refreshed on a 24h unref'd scheduler
- Web: dismissible, accessible (`role="status"`, keyboard-focusable dismiss) banner in the exploring view; dismissal persists per version
- README documents the behavior and opt-outs; `Dockerfile.cli` sets `GITNEXUS_NO_UPDATE_NOTIFIER=1`

**Explicitly out of scope / not done here**

- No update text in any MCP protocol payload (tool results, resources, prompts, instructions, initialize metadata) — agent silence is contractual and pinned by a protocol-snapshot test; MCP `notifications/message` was rejected (deprecated in the 2026-07-28 spec)
- No self-update / install execution; no npx, dev-checkout, or Docker notifications; no prerelease-channel notices
- `eval-server` excluded by command identity; `mcp --http` `/health` keeps its minimal contract

## Implementation notes

- Cache-first display with stale-while-revalidate: freshness gates the refresh, never the display; the first eligible invocation after a publish is silent, the next one notifies
- Refresh never runs in the CLI command process — a detached, unref'd hidden-command child does it, gated by a live lock-owner probe so N parallel invocations coalesce to one child
- Cross-process coordination reuses the repo's atomic writer + `acquireFileLock` (zero retries; busy = someone else is refreshing); publication is monotonic so a late failure never overwrites a newer success
- Registry URL honors `npm_config_registry`, is treated as untrusted (http(s) only, userinfo stripped, no auth tokens, private/loopback redirects refused via the git-clone hardening, 64 KiB body cap); auth-required registries are unsupported by design (fail open)
- `getGlobalDir` was extracted to `storage/global-dir.ts` (re-exported from `repo-manager.ts`; no caller changes)

## Testing & verification

- [x] `cd gitnexus && npm test` — see note below
- [x] `cd gitnexus && npx tsc --noEmit`
- [x] `cd gitnexus-web && npm test` (444 pass; 1 pre-existing `agent-history` failure reproduces on base)
- [x] `cd gitnexus-web && npx tsc -b --noEmit`
- [x] Manual / Playwright E2E — Playwright suite: 14 pass / 25 environment-skipped / 0 fail; plus a live-browser check (Playwright chromium + real `serve`): exploring view rendered the banner from a seeded newer-version cache, dismiss worked, dismissal persisted across reload

Note on `npm test`: this container cannot start the ingestion worker pool (native tree-sitter/LadybugDB bindings), so analyze/integration families fail en masse on base and branch alike. All feature suites are green: 22 checker unit cases (guard matrix, lock, monotonicity, SSRF hardening, eligibility fixtures), CLI unit + spawn-level integration (stdout purity, exit latency), MCP protocol-snapshot freeze + import-closure, serve controller tests, 12 banner unit tests (states, dismissal, i18n, a11y, ordering, poll cadence), plus repo-manager (115) and group/storage (1233) regression suites.

## Risk & rollout

- No breaking changes; `/api/info` is purely additive (existing fields byte-compatible)
- New outbound call: one GET to the npm registry per 24h per installation, off the command path; opt out via `GITNEXUS_NO_UPDATE_NOTIFIER` / `NO_UPDATE_NOTIFIER`, automatic under `CI`
- No index refresh or migration needed

## Checklist

- [x] PR body meets repo minimum length (workflow may label short descriptions)
- [x] If `AGENTS.md` / overlays changed: headers, scope block, and changelog updated per project conventions (not changed)
- [x] No secrets, tokens, or machine-specific paths committed

Release prep for **v1.6.11**.

## Summary

Single `chore: release v1.6.11` commit that bumps every version-bearing surface to 1.6.11 and records the changelog for the 64 commits on `main` since `v1.6.10`.

## What's in the commit

- `gitnexus/package.json` + `gitnexus/package-lock.json` — `1.6.10` → `1.6.11`
- `gitnexus/CHANGELOG.md` — new `## [1.6.11] - 2026-09-04` section
- 14 plugin manifest surfaces stamped by `scripts/sync-plugin-manifests.mjs` (the `version` lifecycle hook): both marketplaces, both plugin manifests, and the 10 skill `mcp.json` launch args
- `gitnexus/test/integration/cli/update-notice.test.ts` — read the installed version from `package.json` instead of hardcoding `1.6.10` (same release-day drift class as #3064)

`eval/workflow_bench/runtime_mounts.py` already derives `PINNED_GITNEXUS_VERSION` from `package.json`, so it does not need a hand edit.

## Release contents

64 non-merge commits since `v1.6.10` (2026-08-27): ~20 features, ~24 fixes, 2 performance changes, and a dependency-maintenance set. npm `@rc` is already at `1.6.11-rc.48`.

Highlights:

- **Zig language support** — declarations, `@import` / `build.zig` modules / `build.zig.zon` path deps, receiver-bound CALLS; `comptime`-false branches are `staticGated` (#1432, #3161)
- **Update notifications** on CLI, `doctor`, MCP, and the web UI (#3175)
- **`gitnexus auto-sync`** for scheduled remote clone/pull + analyze, and **`analyze --watch`** for local incremental re-index (#2493, #3072)
- **Spring / JVM modeling** — vendor-suffix mappings, messaging destinations, Kotlin decorator routes and config consumers, Actuator import, Lombok/Kotlin accessors, `getBeans` lookups, wildcard/star-import route constants
- **More contract surfaces** — AsyncAPI 3.x destinations, wrapped-client HTTP consumers, GraphQL cross-repo contracts, PHP generated-client consumers
- **Reliability** — incremental analyze reuse, parse-cache stability, `group` degraded-link/UID impact, grep contract, `impact` File risk axes, optional `serve` MCP bearer auth

No breaking changes are called out in this release.

title: feat(indexing): add Objective-C semantic indexing support
body:
## Summary

Adds deterministic parsing and semantic indexing for Objective-C source (`.m`) and Objective-C declarations in Objective-C++ (`.mm`) files, plus content-classified Objective-C headers (`.h`).

The change adds Objective-C parsing to the existing indexing pipeline, including Objective-C declarations in Objective-C++ files. It extracts Objective-C declarations and conservative static relationships while preserving existing language behavior.

## Areas touched

- [x] `gitnexus/` (language provider, scope resolution, parser loading, CLI / MCP)
- [x] `gitnexus-web/` (language display constants)
- [x] `.github/` (vendored grammar and native prebuild workflows)
- [x] Docs (`README.md`, `ARCHITECTURE.md`, `AGENTS.md`, Objective-C provider guide)

## Scope & constraints

**In scope**

- Vendor `tree-sitter-objc` and package its prebuilds through the existing grammar pipeline.
- Detect `.m` / `.mm` files and identify Objective-C `.h` files without claiming plain C/C++ headers.
- Extract classes, protocols, categories, extensions, methods, properties, ivars, C functions, imports, declarations, and implementations.
- Emit imports, inheritance, protocol conformance, category membership, implementation evidence, and statically resolvable Objective-C message-send edges.
- Rebuild indexes containing Objective-C candidate files when Objective-C provider or grammar semantics change.

**Explicitly out of scope / not done here**

- Runtime dispatch, swizzling, reflection, dynamic selector construction, arbitrary category replacement, and general `id` flow inference.
- Macro expansion or framework-specific macro rules. Bare file-scope marker macros are only removed length-preservingly for parser recovery.
- Deep C++ semantic extraction inside Objective-C++ `.mm` bodies; these files use the Objective-C parser path in this MVP.

## Implementation notes

- Objective-C is implemented through the existing `LanguageProvider` and `ScopeResolver` hooks; shared ingestion code remains language-agnostic.
- Header classification is content-based, so generic `.h` files remain available to C/C++ analysis.
- Method identities contain owner, full selector, and `+` / `-` kind to keep class and category methods distinct.
- Dynamic and macro-wrapped receivers produce unresolved evidence instead of guessed `CALLS` edges.
- Missing grammar loading produces an actionable `tree-sitter-objc` diagnostic rather than silently returning a partial index.

## Testing & verification

- [x] `cd gitnexus && npm test -- test/unit/objective-c-provider.test.ts test/unit/objective-c-parser-loader.test.ts test/unit/objective-c-macro-marker-preprocess.test.ts test/integration/objective-c-provider.test.ts` *(4 files, 20 tests passed)*
- [x] `cd gitnexus && npx tsc --noEmit`
- [ ] Full `npm test` suite *(20,216 passed, 244 skipped, 51 environment-related failures: optional Zig parser, local JDK compatibility, and install-permission assumptions; no Objective-C test failures)*
- [ ] Manual / Playwright E2E *(no browser workflow changed)*

Focused coverage verifies:

- Grammar loading and the unavailable-grammar diagnostic.
- `.m` / `.mm` detection and Objective-C header classification without taking plain C/C++ headers.
- Semantic nodes and stable IDs for classes, protocols, categories, methods, properties, ivars, C functions, imports, and implementation evidence.
- Local imports, inheritance, protocol conformance, category membership, and declaration/implementation links.
- Static `self`, `super`, class, local, property, ivar, and protocol receiver resolution.
- Dynamic `id` and macro receivers remaining unresolved rather than becoming certain call edges.
- Safe, idempotent recovery from bare file-scope markers such as `RCT_EXTERN_C_BEGIN` / `RCT_EXTERN_C_END`.
- Persisted `query` / `context` behavior and incremental output matching a force rebuild after Objective-C changes.

## Risk & rollout

The behavior is limited to Objective-C source extensions and headers that positively match Objective-C content. Resolution is deliberately conservative: uncertain runtime behavior remains explicit unresolved evidence.

Indexes containing Objective-C candidate files rebuild when the provider or grammar metadata changes. Repositories without Objective-C candidate files retain their current analysis path. Rollback is a normal code rollback followed by an index rebuild.

## Checklist

- [x] PR body meets repo minimum length
- [ ] If `AGENTS.md` / overlays changed: headers, scope block, and changelog updated per project conventions
- [x] No secrets, tokens, or machine-specific paths committed

> Review split: this PR is now represented by four focused, dependent PRs: #3190 (fallback/export precision), #3191 (Go test siblings), #3192 (workspace discovery), and #3193 (flow/community filtering). Review and merge that stack in order; do not merge this aggregate PR as well. Verified follow-up review fixes and current validation are documented in the split PRs. The original description below is historical, including its test and language-visibility claims.

## Summary

Four precision fixes to scope resolution, measured on large real-world repos while running GitNexus as a PR-review engine. The governing rule for all of them: **an incorrect edge is worse than a missing one** — where the analyzer cannot know, it now refuses or labels instead of guessing.

### 1. Name-fallback guesses are labelled, and impossible ones refused (`fix(resolution)`)
The global unique-name call fallback emitted its edges as `import-resolved` at confidence 0.85 — byte-identical to a genuinely resolved edge. Those edges now carry reason `global-name-fallback` at confidence 0.5. Per-language visibility hooks refuse edges the language makes impossible (Go unexported names across packages, non-`pub` Rust items, Swift `private`/`fileprivate`, Dart `_private` across libraries, Ruby class-owned methods with no namespace evidence). In the shared finalize pass, `export *` fan-out and TS/JS/Vue named imports bind module-level declarations only, and a star-vs-star collision is refused and recorded as `reexport-ambiguous`. Each run logs a census and persists it as `RepoMeta.nameFallbackEdges`.

### 2. Go `_test.go` files join their package's sibling table (`fix(go)`)
Test files were excluded from the sibling table, so every same-package call from a test fell to the global fallback. On grafana: **4,857 guesses → 7**.

### 3. Nested workspace roots and source entry discovery (`fix(workspace)`)
Only the repo-root `package.json` / `pnpm-workspace.yaml` was read; a nested workspace (e.g. keycloak's `js/`) contributed nothing. Nested roots are discovered (gated by the outer scope), entries pointing at build output are found from `source` / `publishConfig` / vite `lib.entry` / `src/main` / `src/index` (refused when ambiguous), a package whose `exports` map has no `"."` no longer receives a fabricated root entry, and the scan is deterministic and memoised per run (invalidated before the index lock).

### 4. Guessed edges never seed processes or communities (`fix(flows)`)
Process tracing and community detection gate on the edge reason as well as confidence: a `global-name-fallback` edge sits exactly on the 0.5 threshold, so a confidence filter alone never excluded it.

## Compatibility
- No language is named in shared pipeline code; everything goes through `LanguageProvider` / `ScopeResolver` hooks.
- Consumers asserting `reason === 'import-resolved'` keep working for genuinely resolved edges; only former guesses change reason and confidence.
- Rebased onto v1.6.11 (resolved against the Zig `staticGated` pending-edge shape in `free-call-fallback.ts`).

## Tests
New unit tests: name-fallback visibility per language, wildcard `topLevelOnly` gate, Go sibling tables incl. external test packages, nested workspace roots / entry discovery / rootless exports, flow gating on reason. Full `gitnexus` and `gitnexus-shared` suites green on the rebased branch.

title: Add full native Svelte 5 / SvelteKit support
body:
### Area

gitnexus (CLI / core / indexing / MCP server)

### Problem or opportunity

GitNexus currently supports TypeScript and JavaScript, but `.svelte` files are not natively parsed or represented in the code graph.

This creates a significant blind spot for Svelte and SvelteKit projects. Much of the application logic may live inside `.svelte` components, including:

* TypeScript inside `<script lang="ts">`
* component imports and usage
* props
* Svelte 5 runes such as `$state`, `$derived`, `$effect`, and `$props`
* bindings and event relationships
* dependencies between components and ordinary `.ts` modules
* SvelteKit route files such as `+page.svelte` and `+layout.svelte`

As a result, GitNexus can index the surrounding TypeScript modules in a SvelteKit project, but it cannot build a complete dependency graph through the component layer.

For example:

```svelte
<script lang="ts">
  import Card from '$lib/components/Card.svelte';
  import { xmpl } from '$lib/stores/xmpl';

  let { test } = $props();
  let selected = $state(false);
</script>

<Card {card} />
```

Ideally GitNexus should understand that this component:

* depends on `Card.svelte`
* depends on the `xmpl` store
* exposes/uses the `test` prop
* contains Svelte-specific state through `$state`
* references `Card` from the template

Without Svelte-aware parsing, impact analysis and codebase navigation can miss an important portion of the frontend architecture.

### Proposed solution

Add native Svelte support so `.svelte` files participate in GitNexus indexing and dependency analysis alongside TypeScript and JavaScript.

At minimum, GitNexus should:

* recognize and index `.svelte` files
* parse `<script>` and `<script lang="ts">` blocks
* extract symbols, imports, exports, and references from component scripts
* connect `.svelte` components to imported `.ts`, `.js`, and `.svelte` modules
* detect component usage inside Svelte templates
* understand Svelte/SvelteKit file relationships where applicable

Ideally, support would also include Svelte 5 semantics such as:

* `$props`
* `$state`
* `$derived`
* `$effect`

and common template relationships such as:

* component references
* bindings
* event handlers
* slots/snippets where useful for dependency analysis

The desired outcome is that a SvelteKit project produces a code graph that spans both the regular TypeScript application code and the Svelte component tree, allowing GitNexus features such as dependency tracing, impact analysis, and agent codebase exploration to work across the entire frontend rather than stopping at `.svelte` boundaries.

### Alternatives considered

_No response_

_No response_

### Constraints

_No response_

title: fix(zig): resolve cross-file static gates
body:
## Summary

- add a generic pre-finalization hook for workspace-level reference enrichment
- resolve Zig `@import("./file.zig")` aliases against sibling boolean constants
- mark cross-file dead branches without reading files from parse workers
- enable the two executable regressions from #3162

## Why this boundary

Static-gating captures are produced per file in parse workers, where sibling source is unavailable. The enrichment therefore runs after all `ParsedFile`s have been collected but before reference finalization. It reuses cached trees when available and keeps unknown members, non-boolean declarations, and external imports fail-open.

Closes #3162.

title: LadybugDB pool: LRU eviction races the fire-and-forget close(), causing "checkpoint is in progress" errors on read
body:
### Area

gitnexus (CLI / core / indexing / MCP server)

### Summary

The LadybugDB connection pool's LRU eviction closes the evicted repo's Database with a fire-and-forget `close()` (no await), so the caller's next connection open can race that still-in-flight checkpoint; a related, deeper issue leaves some repos permanently unable to reopen for reads after one evict+reopen cycle.

### Context

Found while self-hosting `gitnexus serve` for a small team (8-31 indexed repos). A PR with a root-caused fix + regression test for the first issue is up: https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/pull/3187

### Expected behavior

`GET /api/graph?repo=<path>&stream=true` (and other pool-backed reads) succeed regardless of how many distinct repos were recently accessed, as long as each repo's own index is valid.

### Actual behavior

Once more than `MAX_POOL_SIZE` (hardcoded to `5` in `dist/core/lbug/pool-adapter.js`) distinct repos are accessed within a short window, reads intermittently fail with:

```json
{"type":"error","error":"Runtime exception: Cannot open database in read-only mode while checkpoint is in progress. Please retry later."}
```

**Root cause #1 (root-caused, fixed in the linked PR):** `closeOne()` closes the evicted repo's shared `Database` with `shared.db.close().catch(() => {})` — no `await`. Both call sites that evict-then-reopen (`evictLRU()` in `doInitLbug`, and the "idle & changed" path in `initLbug`) proceed to open the *new* connection immediately after, without waiting for the evicted repo's close (and the checkpoint it triggers) to finish. Additionally, `initLbug` has no cross-call synchronization, so two concurrent calls for two different repos can each evict-and-reopen at the same time, racing each other.

Verified with an A/B docker build (`ghcr.io/abhigyanpatwari/gitnexus:1.6.10`/`1.6.11` — `pool-adapter.js` is byte-identical between the two): 7 tiny local repos, analyzed, then queried via `/api/graph` with genuinely concurrent (parallel, not sequential — a naive sequential test does not reproduce this) requests. Without the fix: 7/7 fail. With the fix (await the two call sites + a small mutex around `initLbug`): 7/7 succeed, on a freshly-analyzed pool.

**Root cause #2 (observed, not understood, not fixed):** Running the same concurrent-request test repeatedly (5 rounds back-to-back) shows the first round succeeding but nearly every request failing from the second round onward — identically with and without the fix above. This suggests that once a repo's connection has gone through one evict+reopen cycle (unavoidable once you have more repos than `MAX_POOL_SIZE`), something leaves it unable to reopen for reads again, independent of the race condition. Matches what we saw on two real deployments (8 and 31 indexed repos): a repo that worked right after being re-analyzed (`gitnexus analyze --force <repo> --index-only`) would fail again as soon as a few other repos were accessed (evicting it), and this persisted across a full `gitnexus serve` process restart — ruling out in-memory state, and pointing at on-disk state (WAL/shadow file) or the native engine's own bookkeeping. Could not pin this down further without native engine internals; filing it here so it's visible next to the JS-level fix, since #1 alone does not fully resolve the user-visible symptom.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Index (`gitnexus analyze --skip-git --index-only <path>`) 6 or more distinct small local repos.
2. Start `gitnexus serve`.
3. Fire `GET /api/graph?repo=<path>&stream=true` for more than `MAX_POOL_SIZE` (5) of those repos **concurrently** (e.g. background shell jobs fired together, not one at a time — sequential requests against tiny repos finish too fast for the close to still be in flight and won't reproduce it).
4. Some of the requests fail with the checkpoint error above.
5. Repeat step 3 a few more times against the same repos: from the second round on, nearly every request fails (root cause #2).

### Environment

- OS: macOS (also reproduced on EKS/Linux in the two real deployments referenced above)
- Node: v22 (bundled with the image)
- Commit / version: `1.6.10` and `1.6.11` (latest at filing time) — `pool-adapter.js` confirmed byte-identical between the two, and `MAX_POOL_SIZE = 5` unchanged back through `1.6.3` (earlier tags no longer published on ghcr.io)

### Logs / screenshots

```json
{"type":"error","error":"Runtime exception: Cannot open database in read-only mode while checkpoint is in progress. Please retry later."}
```

title: fix(lbug): await evict-then-reopen so it can't race the checkpoint
body:
## Summary

`closeOne()`/`evictLRU()` close the evicted repo's LadybugDB connection with a fire-and-forget `db.close().catch(() => {})` (no `await`); the caller then opens the next repo's connection immediately, racing the still-in-flight checkpoint. Fixes that, plus serializes `initLbug` across concurrent callers so two different repos can't race each other's evict-then-reopen either, plus fixes a zombie-pool-entry window that review caught in the first version of this fix (see below).

## Motivation / context

Related to #3186 (does not close it — see that issue for why). Self-hosted `gitnexus serve` deployments with more than `MAX_POOL_SIZE` (5) actively-used repos hit `"Runtime exception: Cannot open database in read-only mode while checkpoint is in progress. Please retry later."` on `/api/graph` and other pool-backed reads, routinely.

## Areas touched

- [x] `gitnexus/` (CLI / core / MCP server)
- [ ] `gitnexus-web/` (Vite / React UI)
- [ ] `.github/` (workflows, actions)
- [ ] `eval/` or other tooling
- [ ] Docs / agent config only (`AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `.cursor/`, `llms.txt`, etc.)

## Scope & constraints

**In scope**

- `gitnexus/src/core/lbug/pool-adapter.ts`: make `closeOne`/`evictLRU` async and await the two evict-then-reopen call sites (`doInitLbug`'s `evictLRU()`, and the "idle & changed" reopen in `initLbug`).
- Wrap the exported `initLbug` in a small async mutex (`initLbugInner` does the real work) so concurrent calls for different repos serialize instead of racing each other's pool mutations.
- Also await `closeOne()` at `closeLbug`'s two call sites — required once `closeOne` is async, or `closeLbug` can resolve before `pool.delete()` actually ran (caught by the existing `lbug-pool-pinning.test.ts` "explicit close beats the pin" test).
- `closeOne` now removes the pool entry (`pool.delete`, pin clear, listener notify) **before** the newly-awaited `db.close()`, not after. Review found that the previous order left the closed entry reachable via `pool.get(repoId)` — `isLbugReady(repoId)` still `true` — for the duration of that await, so a same-repo query/init landing in that window would hit a `Connection pool integrity error` in `checkout()` instead of just reopening.

**Explicitly out of scope / not done here**

- `MAX_POOL_SIZE` itself is unchanged (still hardcoded to 5). Raising it or making it configurable would reduce how often eviction happens but doesn't address either bug; left as a separate discussion.
- The second, deeper issue noted in #3186 (a repo that has gone through one evict+reopen cycle sometimes becomes permanently unable to reopen for reads, identically with and without this fix) — did not reproduce with mocks, not root-caused, intentionally not attempted here. Further investigation (version bisection, native-engine-vs-JS isolation) is tracked on that issue, not this PR.

## Implementation notes

The idle-timer sweep's `closeOne(repoId)` call is still fire-and-forget on purpose: it's periodic best-effort cleanup with nothing waiting on its completion, unlike the two paths this PR fixes (which are immediately followed by opening a new connection) and unlike `closeLbug` (whose callers observably depend on the close having completed).

## Testing & verification

- [x] `cd gitnexus && npm test` — full unit suite green; the handful of failures seen on an earlier run (`run-analyze.test.ts`, `run-analyze-fts-repair.test.ts`) are pre-existing analyzer-identity flakiness under full-suite parallel load, reproduced identically against `main` with this change reverted.
- [x] `cd gitnexus && npx tsc --noEmit` — clean.
- [x] `test/unit/lbug-pool-evict-reopen-race.test.ts` (mocks `@ladybugdb/core` the same way as `lbug-pool-pinning.test.ts`), two tests:
  - Asserts the evicted repo's `close()` (gated on a controllable delay) completes before the `initLbug` call that triggered the eviction settles. Confirmed it fails against `main` (repo-6's init resolves before the gated close finishes) and passes with this fix.
  - Asserts `closeLbug(repoId)`'s own promise doesn't resolve before the underlying (delay-gated) `close()` does. Confirmed it fails when the corresponding `await` is dropped.
- [x] Manual A/B against the compiled/published bundle: built `ghcr.io/abhigyanpatwari/gitnexus:1.6.10` into a Docker image, indexed 7 tiny local repos, fired genuinely concurrent (not sequential) `/api/graph?...&stream=true` requests across all 7. Without this fix (stock image): 7/7 fail. With this fix applied to the compiled output: 7/7 succeed, on a freshly-analyzed pool. (Sequential requests against tiny repos don't reproduce it — the fire-and-forget close finishes before the next request arrives regardless of the bug; only genuine concurrency, or a large enough repo that the checkpoint takes measurable time, exposes it.)

## Risk & rollout

No behavior change for the common case (pool under `MAX_POOL_SIZE`, no eviction). For the eviction path, callers now wait a bit longer for `initLbug`/`closeLbug` to resolve (bounded by however long the evicted repo's `close()`/checkpoint takes) instead of racing it — strictly safer, no data-shape or API change. No new `GITNEXUS_*` env var.

## Checklist

- [x] PR body meets repo minimum length
- [ ] N/A — no `AGENTS.md`/overlay changes
- [x] No secrets, tokens, or machine-specific paths committed

<!-- gitnexus-pr-summary:v1:start -->

## Summary
*This appears to be a concentrated data-layer and connection-pool lifecycle change with broad transitive reach. The implementation footprint is small, but the critical blast level warrants close review of asynchronous eviction, reopening, and checkpoint ordering.*

**🔴 CRITICAL blast radius. A change to the Lbug pool adapter in `gitnexus/src/core/lbug/pool-adapter.ts` reaches 133 dependents despite being confined to two files.**

The change is concentrated in 14 symbols in `gitnexus/src/core/lbug/pool-adapter.ts`, including `ensureIdleTimer`, `touchRepo`, `closeOne`, `initLbug`, `doInitLbug`, `isLbugReady`, `closeLbug`, `executeParameterized`, `executeQuery`, and `withTimeout`. Impact is strongest in `Local`, with additional graph reach through `Wiki`, `Lbug`, `Cli`, `Group`, `Integration`, `Search`, `Cfg`, `Graph`, `Embeddings`, `Mcp`, and `Server`. The report traces 41 affected flows, so review should follow callers through those areas rather than treating this as an isolated adapter change.

No HIGH or CRITICAL risk files and no cross-repo consumers were identified.

title: LadybugDB pool: eviction/reopen race + a native engine regression (0.18.3→0.19.0) both cause "checkpoint is in progress" errors
body:
### Area

gitnexus (CLI / core / indexing / MCP server)

### Summary

Self-hosted `gitnexus serve` deployments with more than `MAX_POOL_SIZE` (5) actively-used repos intermittently fail reads with `"Runtime exception: Cannot open database in read-only mode while checkpoint is in progress. Please retry later."` Two independent root causes, both now fully diagnosed and fixed:

1. **A real JS-level race** in the LadybugDB connection pool (`gitnexus/src/core/lbug/pool-adapter.ts`): `closeOne()`/`evictLRU()` close the evicted repo's connection with a fire-and-forget `db.close()` (no `await`), so the caller's next connection open can race the still-in-flight checkpoint. Fixed in the linked PR.
2. **A native `@ladybugdb/core` regression** between `0.18.3` and `0.19.0` that fix #1 alone doesn't touch — bisected to a single dependency-bump commit with zero application-code changes. The linked PR pins the dependency back to `0.18.3` as an immediate mitigation; the actual regression needs fixing upstream (tracked at [LadybugDB/ladybug#919](https://github.com/LadybugDB/ladybug/issues/919)).

Supersedes #3186 / #3187 — closed those because the investigation moved well past their original scope and it was cleaner to restart from the final, verified picture than keep appending corrections to that thread (including one retraction of a testing-methodology mistake I made along the way — noted below for transparency).

### Expected behavior

`GET /api/graph?repo=<path>&stream=true` (and other pool-backed reads) succeed regardless of how many distinct repos were recently accessed, as long as each repo's own index is valid.

### Actual behavior

Once more than `MAX_POOL_SIZE` (hardcoded to `5`) distinct repos are accessed within a short window, reads intermittently — and on `1.6.10`+, essentially permanently after the first round — fail with:

```json
{"error":"Runtime exception: Cannot open database in read-only mode while checkpoint is in progress. Please retry later."}
```

### Root cause #1: fire-and-forget close races the reopen (fixed)

`closeOne()` closes the evicted repo's shared `Database` with `shared.db.close().catch(() => {})` — no `await`. Both call sites that evict-then-reopen (`evictLRU()` in `doInitLbug`, and the "idle & changed" path in `initLbug`) proceed to open the *new* connection immediately after, without waiting for the evicted repo's close (and the checkpoint it triggers) to finish. On the real engine the new open can then collide with that still-in-flight checkpoint.

Verified with an A/B docker build: 7 tiny local repos, analyzed, then queried via `/api/graph` with genuinely concurrent (parallel, not sequential — sequential doesn't reproduce it) requests. Without the fix: 7/7 fail from round 2 onward. With the fix: 7/7 succeed — *on `1.6.9`'s native engine*. On `1.6.10`+'s native engine, this fix alone is not sufficient (see root cause #2).

Three rounds of code review on the original PR (#3187) caught real follow-up issues in the fix itself, all addressed in the current commit:
- A "zombie" pool entry stayed reachable via `pool.get(repoId)` during the newly-awaited `close()`, since `pool.delete()` ran after it — a concurrent same-repo call could hit a misleading `Connection pool integrity error` instead of just reopening. Fixed by deleting the entry (and clearing its pin, and notifying listeners) *before* the awaited close.
- The idle-timeout sweep called `closeOne()` directly, outside the mutex added below — an unsynchronized idle close racing a concurrent `initLbug` for the same repo reopened the exact same race via the idle path. Routed it through the same lock.
- Once idle-close was routed through the lock, it could queue behind an in-progress `initLbug` and become stale by the time its turn came (the repo may no longer be idle). Added a re-check inside the lock, right before closing.
- `closeLbug()`'s no-arg ("close everything") branch looped over a snapshotted `pool.keys()` without the lock — a concurrent `initLbug` could register a fresh entry the snapshot never saw. Wrapped it in the same lock.
- Removed a resulting dead-code path (`initPromises`, a per-repoId init-dedup map that became unreachable once every `initLbug` call serializes through the new global lock).

### Root cause #2: native engine regression, `0.18.3` → `0.19.0` (mitigated by pinning)

Bisected with `git bisect`, building the **actual** `Dockerfile.cli` at each candidate commit (not a from-source approximation — an earlier attempt at that gave false results due to missing the FTS-extension bake-in step, a baked-in `GITNEXUS_LBUG_MAX_DB_SIZE` env var, and running as the wrong user; all had to be ruled out first) and running the 7-repo / 3-round concurrent repro against each, completely unmodified.

**First bad commit: `e91ea0ca` — "chore(deps): bump @ladybugdb/core in /gitnexus", `0.18.3` → `0.19.0`.** Touches only `package.json`/`package-lock.json`. Confirmed by independent manual re-test of that commit and its direct parent, not just the automated bisect run.

Isolated further with two clean tests (real dependency changes + full rebuilds each time, **no post-build engine-swapping** — see the transparency note below for why that distinction matters):

- `v1.6.11`, completely unmodified, with `@ladybugdb/core` downgraded to `0.18.3` (`npm install @ladybugdb/core@0.18.3 --save-exact`, full rebuild): **0 failures across 8 rounds / 56 concurrent requests.**
- `v1.6.11` + this issue's own JS fix, with `@ladybugdb/core` upgraded to the current latest, `0.20.2`: **still fails**, same signature, same round-1-clean-then-fails-every-round-after pattern.

So this is fully isolated to the native engine: none of GitNexus's own JS changes since `1.6.9` are load-bearing, and the regression has not been fixed as of the latest `0.20.2` release. Filed upstream at [LadybugDB/ladybug#919](https://github.com/LadybugDB/ladybug/issues/919); a maintainer there is already engaged and has confirmed a related-but-separate `0.20.2` issue (opening databases created by older versions) will be fixed in an upcoming `0.20.3`. Whether that also fixes *this* is unknown — I could not reduce this to a minimal engine-only repro (see below), so it needs someone with visibility into the engine internals to confirm.

**Transparency note on methodology:** earlier in this investigation I tested engine versions by building once and then `docker cp`-ing a different version's npm package over the installed one. That method has a real flaw — the FTS extension is baked in at build time under a version-specific path, and swapping the engine afterward doesn't update it, so the swapped runtime engine and the on-disk extension version disagree in a way that varies unpredictably by starting version. I posted a claim based on that flawed method (that `0.20.2` fixed the simpler case) and had to retract it once I found the flaw. All the results in this issue use real dependency changes + full rebuilds instead, specifically to avoid that trap.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Index (`gitnexus analyze --skip-git <path>`, or `-f` to force) 6 or more distinct small local repos.
2. Start `gitnexus serve`.
3. Fire `GET /api/graph?repo=<path>` for more than `MAX_POOL_SIZE` (5) of those repos **concurrently** (backgrounded shell jobs fired together, not one at a time).
4. Round 1 typically succeeds; from round 2 on (repeat step 3), nearly every request fails with the checkpoint error above, indefinitely, on `1.6.10`+'s native engine — and does not self-heal, including across a full process restart.
5. Repeat against `v1.6.9`'s native engine (`0.18.3`), or against the fix in the linked PR: does not reproduce.

### Environment

- OS: macOS (arm64) and Linux (arm64, both Docker Desktop VM and native containers) — reproduces on both.
- Node: v22 (bundled with the image)
- Versions tested: `1.6.9` through `1.6.11` (current latest at filing time); native engine `0.18.3` (clean) through `0.20.2` (current latest, still fails)

### Logs / screenshots

```json
{"error":"Runtime exception: Cannot open database in read-only mode while checkpoint is in progress. Please retry later."}
```

### Fix

Both root causes are fixed in the linked PR: the pool-adapter.ts race (with the additional review-caught fixes above) plus pinning `@ladybugdb/core` back to `0.18.3` as an immediate mitigation for root cause #2, pending an upstream fix.

title: fix(lbug): checkpoint race in pool-adapter.ts + pin @ladybugdb/core to 0.18.3
body:
## Summary

Fixes both root causes of #3188 (`"checkpoint is in progress"` errors on pool-backed reads once more than `MAX_POOL_SIZE` repos are active): the JS-level eviction/reopen race in `pool-adapter.ts`, plus a native `@ladybugdb/core` regression that fix alone doesn't touch, mitigated here by pinning the dependency back to the last known-good version. Also adds a fail-fast, actionable diagnostic for a related failure mode a reviewer identified: opening an index that was written by a newer, unpinned `@ladybugdb/core` build than the one now installed.

## Motivation / context

Closes #3188. Self-hosted `gitnexus serve` deployments with more than `MAX_POOL_SIZE` (5) actively-used repos hit the checkpoint error on `/api/graph` and other pool-backed reads, routinely and — on `1.6.10`+, once the native regression below is in play — essentially permanently after the first access round.

## Areas touched

- [x] `gitnexus/` (CLI / core / MCP server)
- [ ] `gitnexus-web/` (Vite / React UI)
- [ ] `.github/` (workflows, actions)
- [ ] `eval/` or other tooling
- [ ] Docs / agent config only (`AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `.cursor/`, `llms.txt`, etc.)

## Scope & constraints

**In scope**

- `gitnexus/src/core/lbug/pool-adapter.ts`: make `closeOne`/`evictLRU` async and await the two evict-then-reopen call sites, wrap the exported `initLbug` in a small async mutex so concurrent calls for different repos can't race each other's pool mutations, and await `closeOne()` at `closeLbug`'s two call sites.
- Five follow-up fixes on the same mutex, all caught by code review across this fix's iterations (see commit messages for detail): a zombie pool-entry window in `closeOne`, the idle-timeout sweep bypassing the new lock, a staleness window that introduced, `closeLbug`'s no-arg branch also bypassing the lock, `closeLbug`'s single-repo branch bypassing the lock, and the idle-timeout sweep's in-lock recheck not accounting for a repo pinned after the sweep was queued.
- Removed a resulting dead-code path (`initPromises`) that became unreachable once every `initLbug` call serializes through the global lock.
- `gitnexus/package.json` / `package-lock.json`: pin `@ladybugdb/core` back to `0.18.3` (from `^0.19.0`) — see commit message for the bisection that isolates the regression to this exact version boundary, with zero application-code involvement.
- `gitnexus/src/core/lbug/lbug-config.ts`: new `isStorageVersionMismatchError()` matcher for the native "database file with a different version" error, plus an actionable `STORAGE_VERSION_MISMATCH_SUGGESTION` message (`gitnexus analyze --force` to rebuild).
- Wired that check into **both** places that actually open a LadybugDB connection — `pool-adapter.ts`'s `doInitLbug` (MCP tools / wiki / group-sync) and the separate `lbug-adapter.ts`'s `doInitLbug` (the single-connection path `/api/graph` and `/api/query` use via `withLbugDb`) — so downgrading this dependency over an index written by a newer engine fails fast with a clear message instead of retrying the same exception `LOCK_RETRY_ATTEMPTS` times and surfacing a generic "unavailable, retry later" (review finding on this PR — see "Risk & rollout" below for what this does and doesn't cover).

**Explicitly out of scope / not done here**

- `MAX_POOL_SIZE` itself is unchanged (still hardcoded to 5).
- The actual native-engine regression is not fixed here — it can't be, from this repo. Tracked upstream at [LadybugDB/ladybug#919](https://github.com/LadybugDB/ladybug/issues/919). The dependency pin in this PR is a pragmatic mitigation, not a resolution; recommend revisiting it once that issue is resolved, since `0.19.0`+ presumably ships fixes of its own that `0.18.3` lacks.
- No automatic migration of existing 0.19.x-written indexes back to the 0.18.3 storage format, and no embedding-preservation guarantee across that boundary — the storage-version diagnostic makes the failure loud and actionable (`gitnexus analyze --force`), it doesn't perform or verify a migration. Flagged explicitly by a reviewer as a real gap; see "Risk & rollout".

## Implementation notes

The idle-timer sweep's `closeOne(repoId)` call is fire-and-forget from the *interval callback's* perspective on purpose (periodic best-effort cleanup, nothing awaits its return value directly) — but it's now routed through the same `withPoolLock` mutex as every other pool-mutating call site, so it's still fully serialized against concurrent `initLbug`s; only the callback itself doesn't block waiting for it.

`pool-adapter.ts` and `lbug-adapter.ts` are two **separate, non-shared** database-access mechanisms in this codebase (a multi-repo LRU pool vs. a single-connection session-locked adapter) — worth calling out explicitly, since it's easy to assume there's one code path here. `/api/graph` and `/api/query` go through `lbug-adapter.ts` only; MCP tools, wiki generation, group sync, and search go through `pool-adapter.ts`'s pool. Both root causes and both PR-review fixes had to be checked/applied against the correct one of the two — see "Testing & verification" for exactly what each test targets.

## Testing & verification

- [x] `cd gitnexus && npx tsc --noEmit` — clean.
- [x] `cd gitnexus && npx vitest run test/unit` (full unit suite, rerun against this branch's final state, rebased onto current `upstream/main`): **709 files / 14981 tests passed, 4 files / 12 tests failed, 43 skipped.** All 4 failing files confirmed pre-existing and unrelated — none reference `lbug`/`ladybugdb`/`pool-adapter`/`storage-version`: `analyzer-identity.test.ts` (macOS realpath symlink resolution) and `review-agent-workflow.test.ts` (subprocess retry-count assertion) were already known; `analyzer-identity-in-process-guards.test.ts` and `hooks.test.ts` (real-`ps`/subprocess-driven, environment-sensitive) were newly checked this round and confirmed to fail identically on a clean `upstream/main` worktree with none of this branch's changes applied.
- [x] A bot review finding caught that the new `isStorageVersionMismatchError` import — called unconditionally in both `doInitLbug` catch blocks — broke 10 test files that wholesale-mock `lbug-config.js` (via `vi.mock` or `vi.doMock`) without that export, since Vitest rejects access to an undeclared mocked export. Fixed by adding a stubbed `isStorageVersionMismatchError: vi.fn(() => false)` to each. Caught the first 6 via the bot + a targeted grep; caught the remaining 4 (which use `vi.doMock` instead of `vi.mock`, so didn't match the same grep) only by actually running the full suite rather than trusting the `-t lbug` name filter used earlier, which doesn't match those files' test names.
- [x] `test/unit/lbug-pool-evict-reopen-race.test.ts` (mocks `@ladybugdb/core`, same pattern as `lbug-pool-pinning.test.ts`): asserts the evicted repo's `close()` completes before the triggering `initLbug` call settles, and that `closeLbug()`'s own promise doesn't resolve before the underlying close does. Both assertions fail against the pre-fix code and pass with it. **This mocked test — not the real-engine A/B below — is the actual evidence for the `pool-adapter.ts` race fix**: a direct real-engine repro (`initLbug`/`executeQuery` called straight from `pool-adapter.js`, bypassing HTTP, 7 repos over `MAX_POOL_SIZE`=5, 8 rounds) came back 8/8 clean on *both* the pre-fix and post-fix code against the real (buggy) `0.19.1` engine — the race's real-world timing window is narrow enough that this harness doesn't reliably trigger it either way. The mocked test's controlled timing is what actually demonstrates the ordering bug and its fix; the real-engine tests below demonstrate root cause #2 (the engine regression) and exercise `lbug-adapter.ts`, not `pool-adapter.ts`.
- [x] Manual A/B against the compiled/published bundle, built via the actual `Dockerfile.cli` (not a from-source approximation) at several points, no native-engine swapping (a technique that turned out to be unreliable — see #3188 for why). **These all go through `/api/graph`, i.e. `lbug-adapter.ts` — they demonstrate root cause #2 (the native engine regression) and the pin's fix for it, not the pool-adapter.ts race fix:**
  - `v1.6.9` (native `0.18.3`, as released) vs `v1.6.10`/`v1.6.11` (native `0.19.1`, as released): 7 tiny repos, 3–5 rounds of genuinely concurrent `/api/graph` requests each. `1.6.9`: 0 failures. `1.6.10`/`1.6.11`: fails every round from round 2 on.
  - `v1.6.11`, completely unmodified, with only `@ladybugdb/core` downgraded to `0.18.3` (real `npm install`, full rebuild, no other change): 0 failures across 8 rounds / 56 requests — isolates the regression to the native engine alone.
  - `v1.6.11` + this PR's own pool-adapter.ts fix, with `@ladybugdb/core` upgraded to the current latest `0.20.2`: still fails — confirms a newer engine alone isn't sufficient without the pin (and, per the point above, isn't evidence about the pool-adapter.ts fix either way, since `/api/graph` never calls into `pool-adapter.ts`).
  - This PR's branch: 0 failures across the same repro.
- [x] Storage-version diagnostic, verified end-to-end against the real native engine on both code paths: registered a repo under the pinned `0.18.3` build (a genuine storage-version-42 index), swapped its `.gitnexus/lbug` file for one written by an unmodified `v1.6.11` (`0.19.1`, storage version 43) image, restarted the server to bypass the in-memory connection cache, then queried `/api/graph`:
  ```json
  {"error":"This index was written by a different @ladybugdb/core build (a different storage version) than the one currently installed. Run `gitnexus analyze --force` on this repo to rebuild it with the current engine. (Runtime exception: Trying to read a database file with a different version. Database file version: 43, Current build storage version: 42)"}
  ```

## Risk & rollout

**Pool-adapter.ts change:** no behavior change for the common case (pool under `MAX_POOL_SIZE`, no eviction). For the eviction path, callers now wait a bit longer for `initLbug`/`closeLbug` to resolve (bounded by however long the evicted repo's `close()`/checkpoint takes) instead of racing it — strictly safer, no data-shape or API change.

**Dependency pin:** a real (if pragmatic) production-dependency downgrade, not just an internal fix — worth a maintainer's judgment call on whether `0.18.3` lacks anything load-bearing that landed since. Full unit suite passing with the pin is reassuring but not exhaustive. No new `GITNEXUS_*` env var either way.

**Storage-version incompatibility (flagged by review):** installing this PR's pin over a deployment whose `serve`/MCP indexes were already written by `0.19.x` will make those indexes fail to open — that's inherent to the pin, not something this PR's diagnostic fixes. What the diagnostic does: turns that failure from a confusing generic "unavailable, retry later" (retried `LOCK_RETRY_ATTEMPTS` times for nothing, since the on-disk version doesn't change between retries) into an immediate, actionable message pointing at `gitnexus analyze --force`. It does **not** provide an automated migration path or a guarantee that re-running `analyze --force` preserves previously-computed embeddings — that would need its own design and wasn't attempted here. Operators upgrading/downgrading across this pin on an existing deployment should plan for a rebuild of affected repos' indexes, not assume a transparent in-place fix.

## Checklist

- [x] PR body meets repo minimum length
- [ ] N/A — no `AGENTS.md`/overlay changes
- [x] No secrets, tokens, or machine-specific paths committed

title: fix(resolution): label fallback guesses and preserve export visibility
body:
Global unique-name guesses currently look like resolved imports, and barrel imports can bind declarations that are private to another scope. This change labels guesses as `global-name-fallback` at confidence 0.5, applies language-owned visibility checks, and preserves module export boundaries without changing tool signatures.

Part 1 of the four-PR replacement for #3182. Review/merge in order: fallback and exports → Go test siblings → workspace discovery → flow filtering. The following PRs target their predecessor so each diff contains only its own concern. #3182 remains available as the original reference.

Includes verified review fixes: Go dot-import/method visibility, Rust imported-name and alias matching, unknown Ruby source handling, CommonJS bracket exports, JavaScript import rejection, distinct file/name census denominators, and accurate wildcard ambiguity reporting. Existing source visibility and CommonJS object-method regression tests travel with this change. Dart remains conservative where library membership is unknown.

Follow-up review fixes: locally shadowed CommonJS receivers cannot disable ESM privacy; synthesized default-export HOCs carry export evidence; Rust relative imports and Swift target-layout checks remain conservative; Go external tests may dot-import exported declarations. The census preserves its existing call-site units and no longer claims to count final deduplicated edges. Regression assertions now check all matching edges, and fixtures clean up on failure.

Validation on the provenance implementation: 5,884 resolver/extraction/cache tests passed, 5 skipped, zero failures; shared/core builds and core typecheck passed. The 15-language capture benchmark passed without relaxing performance thresholds. Regressions failed before their fixes. The broader local run had 20,680 passing tests and 31 failures, including macOS/temp-worktree failures and a PHP analysis interrupted by a concurrent rebuild; the stable-source PHP rerun passed both tests. Several environment-sensitive failures also reproduced on unchanged main. Full CI is rerunning on the pushed commit; these results are not a claim that the whole local suite is green. No changelog edits or dependency changes.

Stack: #3190 → #3191 → #3192 → #3193. Part 4 wires the heuristic reason predicate into flow/community consumers; its absence in this first diff is intentional. Do not merge #3182 as well.

Compatibility: inferred graph edges intentionally change; public CLI/MCP signatures do not. Existing indexes must be refreshed to observe new precision. Revert this commit to restore the previous graph semantics.

Architectural follow-up for https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/pull/3190#discussion_r3942896368: extraction now retains optional `ParsedImport.declaredAtScope` independently of import execution timing. An opt-in resolver hook lets finalization bind imports at that lexical scope, without changing file-level dependency/SCC edges. Rust enables it and receives the call site's scope in the fallback guard, so an import in a sibling inline module cannot authorize either a precise binding or a name guess. Local imports no longer contribute to the file-level re-export closure. Return-type propagation mirrors into the binding-owning scope, preserving method calls on locally imported factory results. Legacy/synthesized imports without provenance and non-opted-in languages retain prior binding behavior. Regression coverage includes named/aliased/wildcard imports, full ingestion, and disk ParsedFile round-trips.

Warm-index compatibility: parse-cache schema 93 → 94 invalidates cached worker/ParsedFile output that lacks import provenance or corrected export evidence; the next indexing run reparses. Check this allocation against main before merging. Public CLI/MCP signatures and graph schema are unchanged. The Go fixture golden and Go/JS/TS scope-capture fingerprints were updated for intentional fixture/export changes; performance budgets are unchanged and the 15-language benchmark passes.

Remaining limitation: the separate integration-test crate-boundary comment (#discussion_r3942896357) needs metadata-backed validation; a path-only rejection is unsafe because explicit `mod foo` can legitimately include a sibling file. This change does not claim to implement complete Cargo crate/module visibility.

The Go fixture review (#discussion_r3942896367) is a false positive: sibling `animal.go` declares `Dog` and `Classify`; full Go integration passes. No review threads were dismissed solely because tests passed.
