title: fix(mcp): reject unknown tool arguments and honor depth
body:
## Summary

MCP `tools/call` now rejects unknown top-level arguments instead of answering from a silent default, and `impact` / `trace` honor `depth` as `maxDepth`.

A client that sent CLI-style `depth` used to get the default-depth walk with no error. A client that sent a key nobody reads used to get a well-formed success. Both are now a named error or the intended walk.

Fixes #3261.

## Motivation / context

Same class as silently discarded selectors: the caller believes they set a parameter, and the success payload cannot reveal that it was dropped. The CLI already teaches `--depth` for the same concept the MCP schema named `maxDepth`.

Related: #3198

Related: #3266

## Areas touched

- [x] `gitnexus/` (CLI / core / MCP server)
- [ ] `gitnexus-web/` (Vite / React UI)
- [ ] `.github/` (workflows, actions)
- [ ] `eval/` or other tooling
- [ ] Docs / agent config only (`AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `.cursor/`, `llms.txt`, etc.)

## Scope & constraints

**In scope**

- Fail-closed unknown top-level keys at `tools/call` (error names every unknown key; backend not invoked)
- `additionalProperties: false` on advertised tool schemas
- Advertised `depth` alias for `maxDepth` on `impact` and `trace`, including group-forward
- Keep unpublished handler aliases (`query` on query/cypher/search; `context` `target` in group mode)
- Keep more-specific read-only rejection messages (policy checks still run first)

**Explicitly out of scope / not done here**

- JSON-plus-markdown tool footer parse contract
- HTTP `POST /tool/:name` eval-server path
- Value-domain enforcement beyond the existing `0` omitted-sentinel (non-integer `depth` is follow-up)
- `gitnexus-web/` Graph-RAG surfaces

## Implementation notes

Session-settled decisions carried from planning: scope is this issue only, no footer change (user-directed, over bundling the footer observation); unknown keys fail closed (user-approved, over an `ignoredArguments` success payload); CLI `depth` is a working alias for `maxDepth` on `impact` and `trace` (user-approved, over rejecting `depth` without honoring it).

Validation runs after `assertMcpReadOnlyToolCall` against the advertised (policy-scrubbed) schema. Numeric `depth` → `maxDepth` fold lives in `normalizeToolParams` so local and group-forward paths share it. Literal `0` remains the omitted sentinel. Suggestions come from advertised keys only.

## Testing & verification

Targeted unit coverage plus typecheck. Full vitest suite and integration not run (plan: skip unless an unclear failure).

- [ ] `cd gitnexus && npm test`
- [x] Targeted: `mcp-tool-arguments`, `server`, `tools`, `calltool-dispatch`, `mcp/group-repo-routing`, `mcp-read-only`
- [ ] `cd gitnexus && npm run test:integration` *(if core/indexing/MCP paths changed)*
- [x] `cd gitnexus && npx tsc --noEmit`
- [ ] `cd gitnexus-web && npm test` *(if web changed)*
- [ ] `cd gitnexus-web && npx tsc -b --noEmit` *(if web changed)*
- [ ] Manual / Playwright E2E *(note environment — see `gitnexus-web/e2e/`)* — N/A, MCP-only

## Risk & rollout

**Breaking for MCP clients** that sent unknown top-level keys and previously received a success. That is the intended fail-closed contract. Clients already sending only advertised keys, plus unpublished `query` / group `context` `target`, keep working. Clients sending `depth` on `impact`/`trace` now get a bounded walk instead of the default.

No index refresh. No migration.

## Checklist

- [x] PR body meets repo minimum length (workflow may label short descriptions)
- [x] If `AGENTS.md` / overlays changed: headers, scope block, and changelog updated per project conventions
- [x] No secrets, tokens, or machine-specific paths committed

title: detect-changes omits removed symbols for whole-file deletions after header parsing fix
body:
### Area

gitnexus (CLI / core / indexing / MCP server)

### Summary

A tracked whole-file deletion maps only to the new-side line-1 anchor, so `detect-changes` omits the removed indexed symbols and their affected execution flows even after the file-header recognition fix in #3251.

### Context

Discovered while investigating https://github.com/dpearson2699/ios-options-wheel-tracker/issues/1051. GitNexus 1.6.11 rejects a deletion-only diff because its parser recognizes only `+++ b/` and skips `+++ /dev/null`. The installed parser and local-backend files match the official npm 1.6.11 tarball byte for byte.

#3251 improves header recognition. I tested the published 1.6.12-rc.36 package, which includes that fix, in a disposable two-file repository. With an index built by that same release candidate immediately before deletion, it recognizes the changed file but reports no overlapping indexed symbols. No OptionsWheelTracker harness or configuration is involved.

Related prior discussion exists in closed, unmerged #141 and open #1901. This report is scoped to the existing `detect-changes` command's missing removed-symbol mapping, rather than new external mapping APIs or Added/Modified/Deleted classification.

### Expected behavior

With a fresh index of the committed base, deleting a tracked source file should report its removed indexed functions and the already-indexed execution flows that contain them. In this reproduction, `removedHelper` and `removedCaller` are removed, and the indexed `retainedCaller -> removedCaller -> removedHelper` flow is affected.

### Actual behavior

On 1.6.11, both staged and unstaged deletion-only runs exit 1:

```text
PARTIAL RESULT: a graph query failed, so changed symbols may be missing. Do not read this as a clean pre-commit check.
Could not parse the git diff output — no file headers recognised.
```

On 1.6.12-rc.36, both runs exit 0 with:

```text
Diff touched 1 file(s) but no indexed symbols overlap those hunks — not a clean tree.
```

The message correctly acknowledges the changed file, but the removed symbols and affected flow are still absent. Before deletion, `gitnexus context removedHelper` reports the symbol at lines 3–5, its caller `removedCaller`, and the three-step flow `RetainedCaller → RemovedHelper`.

The current-main parser at `68c42009df8ce4dd0f59042cbbfede9aa3784096` and published rc parser both reduce a whole-file `@@ -1,9 +0,0 @@` deletion to:

```json
{
  "files": [{
    "filePath": "removed.ts",
    "hunks": [{"startLine": 1, "endLine": 1}]
  }],
  "unparsedGitHeaders": 0
}
```

That becomes graph range `[0,0]`. Both removed functions start after that line, so the overlap query cannot select them. The full deleted old-side range is discarded. This is a separate remaining behavior from the header parsing improved by #3251.

### Steps to reproduce

Use GitNexus 1.6.12-rc.36 for the current post-#3251 behavior, or 1.6.11 for the original header error. Keep the same version for indexing and detection.

```sh
repro_dir=$(mktemp -d)
cd "$repro_dir"
git init -q
cat > removed.ts <<'TS'
// A tracked source file to delete.

export function removedHelper(): number {
  return 42;
}

export function removedCaller(): number {
  return removedHelper();
}
TS
cat > kept.ts <<'TS'
import { removedCaller } from "./removed";

export function retainedCaller(): number {
  return removedCaller();
}
TS
git add removed.ts kept.ts
git -c user.name=Reproduction -c user.email=repro@example.invalid \
  -c core.hooksPath=/dev/null commit -qm 'test: seed deletion reproduction'
gitnexus analyze --index-only .
gitnexus status
gitnexus context removedHelper --repo "$PWD"
rm removed.ts
gitnexus detect-changes --scope all --repo "$PWD"
git add removed.ts
gitnexus detect-changes --scope all --repo "$PWD"
```

Both analyzed versions reported an up-to-date index covering both files before deletion. The test intentionally leaves the referencing file in place so the base graph has an observable affected flow; it is testing diff-to-symbol mapping, not application compilation.

### Environment

- macOS 26.6.2, arm64.
- Node.js v26.8.2.
- Stable 1.6.11, npm `gitHead` `c0c3fa18a9b27d210099f908095fec373dd3d2d5`.
- Release candidate 1.6.12-rc.36, npm `gitHead` `357d397107df2b38870c63281aee7887ea55d73f`.
- Current-main parser separately executed at `68c42009df8ce4dd0f59042cbbfede9aa3784096` and produced the same single-line range.
- The release candidate was unpacked separately and used existing dependencies with the same declared dependency contract; the globally installed CLI was left unchanged.

### Logs / screenshots

The ordinary Git patch begins:

```diff
diff --git a/removed.ts b/removed.ts
deleted file mode 100644
--- a/removed.ts
+++ /dev/null
@@ -1,9 +0,0 @@
```

Relevant current code: [parseDiffHunksResult](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/blob/68c42009df8ce4dd0f59042cbbfede9aa3784096/gitnexus/src/storage/git.ts#L960) handles zero new-side lines as a single anchor; [detectChanges](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/blob/68c42009df8ce4dd0f59042cbbfede9aa3784096/gitnexus/src/mcp/local/local-backend.ts#L5688) builds symbol-query bounds from those ranges.

title: Compatibility: SIGSEGV after relationship loading with GitNexus 1.6.11 / Ladybug 0.19.1 in a constrained F1 runner (WSL2 x64)
body:
### Area

gitnexus (CLI / core / indexing)

### Summary

A fresh initial index of CustomerMasterDevelopment exits with native signal 11
after reaching relationship loading under a customized, resource-bounded F1 runner.
An ordinary supported serial-loading run also failed. We are asking for supported
configuration/compatibility guidance; **this has not been reproduced with an
unmodified stock CLI, and an upstream root cause is not established**.

### Expected behavior

Complete the initial structural index, or return a handled resource/configuration
error that explains an unsupported or insufficient setting. We need one verified
code query after indexing; no embeddings or PDG are required for this route.

### Environment and effective configuration

| Item | Observed value |
|---|---|
| Host environment | WSL2, Ubuntu 26.04 LTS, Linux x86_64, kernel 6.18.33.2-microsoft-standard-WSL2 |
| OS page size / glibc metadata | 4,096 bytes / 2.43 |
| Node / GitNexus / native dependency | 22.22.3 / 1.6.11 / @ladybugdb/core 0.19.1 |
| Node heap / autopilot | Explicit 512 MiB; GITNEXUS_MEMORY=off |
| Native buffer pool | Explicit 268435456 bytes (256 MiB); overrides adaptive graph sizing |
| Native maxDBSize | Explicit 268435456 bytes (256 MiB), versus GitNexus's 16-GiB default |
| Parser workers / query threads | One parser worker; F1 substitutes new Connection(db, 1) |
| Latest loading mode | GITNEXUS_SERIAL_LBUG_LOAD=1; existing COPY statements still use PARALLEL=false |
| Extension policy | load-only; FTS unavailable; embeddings disabled |
| Other observed defaults | Compression false; automatic checkpoint enabled; no contrary WAL threshold override found (upstream default 64 MiB) |
| Source revision at latest attempt | 6645ce8a5804ca020d251b7761eb87aa1c4de0b4; clean before and after |

The OS metadata was inspected after the run on the same host. Recorded launch
receipts bind the Node/runtime settings. Buffer memory, maximum database/address
space and actual disk growth are distinct quantities. We do not assume that a
256-MiB value accepted by the JavaScript API is sufficient for this workload.

### F1 modifications that may matter

This is a modified runner, not stock-default GitNexus:

- Storage, registry, HOME, cache and temporary paths are routed outside the source
  checkout. Source Git-exclude edits are suppressed.
- The F1 loader substitutes exact-bound repo metadata, repository manager and
  database configuration JavaScript files. It forces
  --force --index-only --skip-agents-md --skip-skills --workers 1.
- A sealed observer records lifecycle and worker events and bypasses parser-cache
  reuse. The provisioned runtime also contains an anonymous-node-class compatibility
  repair for tree-sitter 0.21.1.
- A supervisor observes elapsed time and disk charges and preserves failed
  candidates without publishing them. Its observed native exit was -11; it did
  not initiate that exit by sending a cancellation signal to the analyzer.

No custom additional tracing preload was used in the latest real run. We have
not ruled out an interaction introduced by these adaptations.

### Observed execution and scope

This is the recorded local route, **not a portable or minimal stock reproduction**:

1. Start with no accepted index for the repository. Use the explicit isolated
   structural profile and the pinned customized runtime above.
2. F1 invokes runObservedAnalyze for CustomerMasterDevelopment with --name
   CustomerMasterDevelopment, through its initial-index acceptance driver.
3. The latest run parses its selected input and reaches graph persistence. Its
   ordinary progress output reports the following sequence.

```text
60% | Loading into LadybugDB...
64% | Loading nodes 1/11: File (431 rows)
66% | Loading nodes 2/11: Folder (67 rows)
68% | Loading nodes 4/11: Class (85 rows)
71% | Loading nodes 7/11: Process (284 rows)
72% | Loading nodes 9/11: Const (33 rows)
74% | Loading edges: 8,553 across 30 CSV files
74% | Loading edges: 5/30 files (File -> File)
75% | Loading edges: 10/30 files (File -> Class)
75% | Loading edges: 18/30 files (Function -> Function)
```

Progress is sampled: 18/30 is the last reported position, **not proof of the exact
operation that failed**. The later graph-load completion marker is absent.
Publication and the code query did not run. The candidate is retained unpublished.

| Existing check | Result and limit |
|---|---|
| Earlier full F1 initial index, normal loading order | Native signal 11; earlier source revision 28e9bd46a115a7df14087fe3ce96f2a91be4b2e5 |
| First retained-node replay | Verifier failed before COPY because its inline trace assertion was too small; not a native reproduction |
| Corrected retained-node replay | All 11 nonempty node tables, checkpoint and close passed at unchanged 256-MiB settings; relationships were not replayed |
| Full F1 initial index with supported serial loading | Native signal 11 again on source 6645ce8a; ordinary progress as above |
| Unmodified stock CLI/default-size comparison | NOT RUN |
| Version substitution | NOT RUN |

The source revisions differ between the two real attempts, so this is not a
controlled same-input A/B test of serial loading. The successful node-only replay
does not prove complete graph persistence or exclude a resource problem.

Earlier-attempt evidence: a saved kernel event at 23:27:14 UTC was historically
matched to the installed Ladybug bytes and identified a null-address read in
`lbug::storage::BufferManager::claimAFrame`. Time, module and phase support the
attribution, but the journal thread PID was not directly mapped to the supervised
analyzer PID. There is no complete stack or proven initiating operation. This is
retained evidence from the earlier attempt, **not proof that the latest serial
crash has the same site**; no new binary inspection was performed for this report.

The serial attempt started at 2026-09-08T23:58:34Z. Its controller took 15.007
seconds; supervision covered 9.295 seconds and confirmed all recorded writers
stopped. The observed peak charge was 193867784 bytes against a 268435456-byte
limit, below its 300-second deadline. The charge combines observed writes and
positive allocation growth; it is not resident memory or retained database size.
Full lifetime I/O measurement is incomplete. Source/configuration checks remained
unchanged, and no failed candidate was published.

### Guidance requested

1. Is this combination of a 256-MiB buffer, 256-MiB maxDBSize and one query thread
   supported for initial CSV loading, and are there documented minimums or
   relationships between these settings that our runner has missed?
2. Does this initial-load phase and failure signature match a known issue or a
   specific supported correction? If not, which ordinary configuration comparison
   would most clearly distinguish an F1 integration issue from an engine issue?
3. Is there an existing small upstream fixture covering node plus relationship
   COPY and finalization that can establish that distinction without repeatedly
   indexing the full repository?

### Related reports checked

- [GitNexus #2631](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/issues/2631) concerns
  a handled buffer-pool allocation error during node COPY. Ours is signal 11
  after reaching relationships on a 4-KiB-page x64 host; equivalence is unproved.
- [GitNexus #3188](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/issues/3188) reports
  checkpoint/reopen failures in a multi-repository read pool. Its reported version
  mitigation has not been shown to fix this single fresh initial-index failure.

No confirmed matching correction emerged from those reports. We can provide the
saved ordinary progress, effective configuration, version/hash bindings and
supervision receipts for a specific follow-up; a self-contained upstream
reproducer is not yet available.

title: fix(parse-cache): retire a chunk whose durable generation could not be reset
body:
Closes #3204.

## The defect

PR #3200 made a parse chunk uncacheable when `prepareDurableParsedFileChunk` fails, but it only skipped the parse-cache **write**. The chunk hash was already in `parseCache.usedKeys` from the lookup, so at shutdown `saveParseCache` copied the **pre-existing** `.v8` shard forward from the live cache directory, and the durable store — pruned to exactly the keys `saveParseCache` returns — kept the mixed directory and re-indexed it.

The state is reachable because a chunk can be a live `.v8` entry **and** a re-dispatched miss in the same run: the coherence gate re-dispatches when a cached chunk's durable shards are missing or unreadable. The next run then serves a warm hit out of a directory the previous run had already decided it could not account for.

## The fix

- `ParseCache.staleKeys` (transient, never serialized). `markParseCacheChunkStale` marks the hash and drops it from `entries`/`onDiskKeys`, which is what `loadParseCacheChunk` reads.
- `saveParseCache` filters stale keys out of its key list. That one filter reaches **both** stores, because the durable prune keeps exactly the keys this function returns. It sits at save time deliberately: `run-analyze` re-adds keys to `usedKeys` after the parse phase (the #2106 sibling fold and the unreadable-meta retention fallback), so an invalidation applied earlier would be undone.
- Retirement is conditional on evidence. `prepareDurableParsedFileChunk` is rm-then-mkdir; only an **rm** failure leaves a generation nobody cleared. An rm that succeeded before a failing mkdir leaves no directory at all, and retiring there would discard a good cache entry for nothing — and under a correlated failure would discard a great many at once.
- Worker-quarantined chunks get the same retirement: they reach the save with no in-memory entry, which is the same copy-forward path.
- The durable prune's per-entry `fs.rm` and the staged→live overlay's `replaceDurableChunkDir` are both guarded. The causes that break a reset break those deletes too, and either one aborting its loop skipped the durable index rewrite for every remaining chunk.

## Verification

Written test-first; each new test was observed failing for its intended reason before the fix. The prune test reproduced the original defect directly — `EACCES` propagating out of `pruneAndSaveDurableParsedFileStore` with the index never written.

- `npx vitest run test/unit/parse-impl-warm-cache-parsedfile-coverage.test.ts test/unit/parsedfile-store.test.ts test/unit/incremental-parse-cache.test.ts test/integration/parse-impl-quarantine-cache-skip.test.ts` — 108 passing.
- `npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json` — clean.
- Full unit suite: failures are identical with and without this change (13 files / 56 tests, verified by running the same set against a stashed tree). They are pre-existing in this environment — native-DB project tests, env-dependent config tests, and worker-startup timeouts.

No `PARSE_CACHE_VERSION` bump: `staleKeys` is transient, both index shapes are unchanged, and the change only ever removes keys, so version skew is safe in both directions.

**🔴 CRITICAL blast radius. This change updates parse-cache and durable parsed-file handling across the analysis pipeline, with impact extending through callers and transitive dependents.**

## Summary
- Vendor Ladybug FTS for linux-x64/arm64, darwin-x64/arm64, and win32-x64 so analyze can path-load a packaged artifact without `~/.lbdb`, a CDN, or host install. Pin core↔extension pairing so Dependabot cannot ship a skew. `win32-arm64` stays an explicit unsupported tuple.
- Make an in-place `CREATE_FTS_INDEX` abort recoverable on macOS, Windows, and Linux: stamp an FTS dirty phase, park a poisoned live WAL without wiping the graph, skip CREATE until `--repair-fts`, and refuse MCP/serve readers with a structured repair message. Staging never parks the live WAL.
- Windows still needs system OpenSSL 3 and the VC++ redistributable. This PR replaces Git Bash / `PATH` prepend advice with that vendor-neutral prerequisite; shipping OpenSSL DLLs is blocked until a Windows loader probe (OQ1) and a named CVE owner (KTD13).

## What's changed
A unit test (`gitnexus/test/unit/publish-rc-guard.test.ts`) that pins the rc-guard release-PR skip regex shipped in `.github/workflows/publish.yml`:

  • #11369 d6ad973 Thanks @​hntrl! - fix(langchain): use unified endpoint for gateway

  • #11342 3b0e4c4 Thanks @​thushanth-bengre-langchain! - feat(core): mark errors as retryable or not, and stop retrying the ones that aren't

    Retry middleware retried every failure up to maxRetries, including deterministic ones like a bad API key or an unknown model. Retries also nest, so a single such failure could cost dozens of API calls.

    @langchain/core/errors adds stampRetryable(error, retryable) and getRetryable(error). Marking an error leaves its class and shape untouched, so a provider SDK error can be classified without breaking instanceof. getRetryable returns undefined for errors nobody classified, and both are exported so tool authors can mark their own failures.

    modelRetryMiddleware and toolRetryMiddleware now respect the mark by default, and retries stop as soon as one is found rather than each layer spending its own budget. Aborted calls, context overflow, and oversized payloads are marked non-retryable out of the box. Models accept a per-call maxRetries so a surrounding retry loop can take over.

    Behavior change: errors marked non-retryable now fail on the first attempt. Unclassified errors — including any from third-party integrations or custom tools — retry exactly as before. Pass retryOn: () => true to restore the old default. A custom onFailedAttempt replaces the built-in handler and opts out of marking.

title: WebUI white-screens on large graphs: unguarded noverlap.assign throws RangeError: Set maximum size exceeded
body:
## Summary

The WebUI's large-graph protection (added for #2178 via `gitnexus-web/src/lib/graph-load-decision.ts`) only gates the **graph download**. It does **not** gate the **layout** step.

`noverlap.assign(graph, NOVERLAP_SETTINGS)` in `gitnexus-web/src/hooks/useSigma.ts` is called with **no node-count guard and no `try/catch`**. Once a large graph is actually laid out, V8 throws `RangeError: Set maximum size exceeded`, React unmounts the tree, and the page goes **completely blank**.

This is reachable from plain upstream code — no fork needed — via `?skipGraph=0` or the "Load graph anyway" escape hatch, and (see "the unprotected gap" below) potentially even on graphs *below* the 25k auto-skip threshold.

## Environment

- GitNexus: `1.6.9` (npm `gitnexus`), served via `gitnexus serve --host 0.0.0.0 --port 4747`
- Browser: Chromium (Playwright-driven), Windows 11
- Repo indexed: 76,538 nodes / 116,504 edges (`/api/repos` reports 116,504; UI shows 110,828 edges after filtering)
- Graph payload: ~78 MB downloaded before layout

## Steps to reproduce

1. Index a large repo (ours: 76,538 nodes).
2. Open the WebUI forcing a full graph load:
   `http://<host>:4747/?skipGraph=0`
   (Equivalently: open a >25k-node repo, get the chat-only panel, and click **"Load graph anyway"**.)
3. Wait for the graph to download and render.

## Expected

Either the layout completes, or a large graph degrades gracefully (skip noverlap / keep chat-only). **Never** a blank page.

## Actual

The graph downloads and renders successfully, then the layout cleanup runs and the page goes blank.

Console:

```
RangeError: Set maximum size exceeded
    at Set.add (<anonymous>)
    at t.exports (assets/index-ShtVvrCM.js:325:115482)   # graphology-layout-noverlap
    at s (assets/index-ShtVvrCM.js:325:117780)
    ...
```

→ React unmounts the whole tree → blank white page (root element emptied).

## Root cause

`graphology-layout-noverlap` keeps **one `Set` shared across all grid cells** for pair de-duplication. Every intra-cell pair key is added to that single `Set`, so it accumulates `Σ C(pᵢ, 2)` entries. Once the total crosses V8's hard `Set` limit of **2²⁴ = 16,777,216**, `Set.add` throws.

Measured empirically (Node v22):

```
V8 Set limit reached at size = 16777216
error = RangeError: Set maximum size exceeded
2^24 = 16777216
C(p,2) >= 2^24  =>  p ~ 5794   # nodes in a single grid cell that trips the limit
```

Upstream call site (current `main`, `gitnexus-web/src/hooks/useSigma.ts`, inside `stopAllLayouts`):

```ts
if (graph && options.layoutMode !== 'tree' && options.layoutMode !== 'circles') {
  noverlap.assign(graph, NOVERLAP_SETTINGS);   // no node-count guard, no try/catch
}
```

with

```ts
const NOVERLAP_SETTINGS = {
  maxIterations: 20,
  ratio: 1.1,
  margin: 10,
  expansion: 1.05,   // no gridSize → graphology default 20
};
```

With `gridSize = 20` and a clustered graph, a single cell exceeding ~5,794 nodes is enough to trip the limit.

## Why the existing large-graph protection doesn't save you

From `gitnexus-web/src/config/ui-constants.ts`:

```ts
const DEFAULT_LARGE_GRAPH_NODE_THRESHOLD = 25_000;
const DEFAULT_LARGE_GRAPH_EDGE_THRESHOLD = 50_000;
```

`decideSkipGraph()` only answers *"should we download the graph?"* — it says nothing about *"can we lay it out?"*. Two paths remain unprotected:

1. **Above threshold** → chat-only panel is shown, but the documented **"Load graph anyway"** escape hatch downloads and lays out the graph → **crash**.
2. **Below threshold** (e.g. 10k–25k nodes) → no skip and no confirmation at all, it's a *normal* load → layout → **can still crash**, because noverlap's real ceiling is ~5.8k nodes *per grid cell*, not 25k nodes globally.

So `LARGE_GRAPH_NODE_THRESHOLD` and noverlap's actual carrying capacity are unrelated numbers, and the gap between them is unprotected. The 25k threshold protects download/transfer; nothing protects layout.

## Suggested fix

Guard the call by node count and make failure non-fatal, so a layout problem degrades instead of blanking the app:

```ts
// Suggested: reuse/extend a constant in config/ui-constants.ts
const NOVERLAP_MAX_NODES = 20_000;

if (graph && options.layoutMode !== 'tree' && options.layoutMode !== 'circles') {
  try {
    if ((graph.order || 0) <= NOVERLAP_MAX_NODES) {
      noverlap.assign(graph, NOVERLAP_SETTINGS);
    }
  } catch (err) {
    // Layout is cosmetic: never let it take down the WebUI.
    console.warn('[useSigma] noverlap cleanup skipped after failure', err);
  }
}
```

Notes:

- For large graphs this skips anti-overlap cleanup, so nodes may overlap slightly. That is a far better outcome than a blank page.
- Ideally the threshold would be derived from cluster density rather than raw node count (grid-cell occupancy is what actually overflows the `Set`), but a node-count guard plus `try/catch` removes the failure mode entirely and is a small, safe change.
- `shouldConfirmGraphLoad()` already exists for the "Load graph anyway" path; wiring the layout guard to the same threshold constants would keep behaviour consistent.

**We verified this works.** We applied the guard at bundle level on our deployment and re-ran the exact same failing deep link: the 76,538-node graph renders normally (7 canvas layers, 396 svg elements, file tree intact) with **zero page errors**, where before it crashed every time.

## Additional context — how we hit it (fork-local bypass, upstream-native bug)

We maintain an internal fork that adds a `?focus=<node-id>` deep link, because upstream `App.tsx` does not read a `focus` URL parameter (it only reads `?skipGraph`). For a focus target to be highlightable the graph must be loaded, so our fork coerces the parameter:

```ts
skipGraph ?? (focus ? '0' : null)
```

That bypasses the large-graph protection entirely and put us directly on the crash path. To be explicit:

- The **`focus` bypass is fork-local** — upstream `App.tsx` is unaffected.
- The **unguarded `noverlap` call is not** — it is upstream code, reachable via `?skipGraph=0` and "Load graph anyway".

We are reporting this because the underlying bug is upstream and will bite any user who loads a large graph, not because of our fork.

Possible follow-up (separate feature request): native `?focus=` deep-link support would let downstreams deep-link into a node **without** forcing a full graph download — which is what made us reach for `skipGraph=0` in the first place. Happy to file that separately if useful.

title: fix(embeddings): keep ONNX off the install and analyze critical path
body:
## Summary
- Isolate local ONNX inference in a `child_process` sidecar so analyze, serve, MCP, and embeddings-sync never load `onnxruntime-node` in the parent. Ladybug writes stay in-process; the child is reaped before every `process.exit`.
- Take `@huggingface/transformers` and `onnxruntime-node` off default `npm install`. Pins live in `package.json` `gitnexusEmbeddingStack`; `gitnexus embeddings install` (and analyze/sync auto-heal) writes a user-level prefix. `onnxruntime-common` stays a hard dep.
- Refuse Intel Mac and an unloadable runtime prefix **before** any registry download. HTTP embeddings remain the escape hatch; wasm is not treated as a rescue.
- Drop vendored grammar source from the published tarball now that every grammar has 6/6 prebuilds. First ship stays above the 80 MiB cnpm limit (`#2704`).
- Review and simplify follow-ups: native-abort deaths do not respawn the sidecar; `AbortSignal` is honored after embed return; MCP `query()` surfaces vector-lane degradation; analyze/sync share one runtime assessment; shutdown paths share a safe reap helper.

## Test plan
- [ ] `cd gitnexus && npx tsc --noEmit`
- [ ] `npx vitest run test/unit/embedding-sidecar-client.test.ts test/unit/embedding-runtime-support.test.ts test/unit/embedding-runtime-install.test.ts test/unit/embeddings-install-command.test.ts test/unit/embeddings-sync-command.test.ts test/unit/analyze-local-embedding-error.test.ts test/unit/analyze-worker-reap.test.ts test/unit/local-backend-disconnect-reap.test.ts test/unit/local-backend-semantic-warn.test.ts test/unit/semantic-search-ready.test.ts test/unit/assert-publish-grammar-coverage.test.ts test/unit/http-embedder.test.ts test/unit/embedder.test.ts`
- [ ] `node scripts/assert-publish-grammar-coverage.cjs` reports prebuilds-only coverage
- [ ] Fresh `npm install` in a clean tree does **not** fetch `@huggingface/transformers` / `onnxruntime-node`
- [ ] `gitnexus embeddings install` then `gitnexus analyze --embeddings` embeds via the sidecar (parent process has no ONNX mapping)
- [ ] Intel Mac / Node without `module.registerHooks` fails fast with the platform/prefix message and does not start an npm heal
- [ ] HTTP mode (`GITNEXUS_EMBEDDING_URL` + model) still embeds without a local stack
- [ ] Serve/MCP semantic search on an empty embedding table does not spawn the sidecar
- [ ] Cancel-before-start analyze worker reaps before `process.exit`
- [ ] `npm pack` omits `vendor/**/src/parser.c` and still includes grammar prebuilds, bindings, Leiden, and FTS artifacts

Relates to #2370, #1515, #2704, #3255.

**🔴 CRITICAL blast radius. An embeddings and ONNX installation-path change centered on `gitnexus/src/core/embeddings/`, reaching 31 direct dependents.**

The core impact is concentrated in the `Embeddings` module, including `gitnexus/src/core/embeddings/types.ts`, the hottest changed file, plus the local initialization, sidecar, runtime-install, runtime-support, and embedding pipeline code. title: feat(auto-sync): preserve PDG indexes across updates
body:
## Motivation

Auto-sync did not preserve or request PDG mode. Re-running `analyze --pdg` after every sync is not durable: the next auto-sync can rebuild without PDG and replace that index. It also races the watcher, can turn lock contention into recorded failures, duplicates expensive analysis, and leaves stale windows.

## Changes

- add per-project `pdg`, preserving omitted legacy mode under the writer lock
- recover ambiguous metadata when mode is explicit
- request atomic incremental publication where supported
- extend analysis timeouts and coalesce missed ticks

## Validation

- 136 focused tests passed
- TypeScript check and production build passed
- full suite reached the 30-minute shared-host cap without a reported failure

title: Tool staleness payload carries no indexed ref, so a feature-branch index is indistinguishable from a current main index (residual of #2655)
body:
### Area

gitnexus (CLI / core / indexing / MCP server)

### Problem or opportunity

#2655 wired `staleness` into the `query` / `context` / `impact` / `cypher` tool responses, and #3256 gave "could not tell" its own name (`status: unknown | current | behind | diverged`) instead of collapsing it into "fresh". Both shipped in 1.6.12 and both are real improvements — this issue is about what those two leave uncovered, and one way in which #2655 makes it sharper.

**The staleness payload answers "how old?" but never "old *relative to what*?"**

`stalenessPayload` (`core/staleness-status.ts`) emits `{ status, commitsBehind, hint }`. There is no `branch`, no `lastCommit`, no `indexedAt`. So a tool response says the index is *N* commits behind, but not **which ref it is an index of**.

That matters because `commitsBehind` is measured against the registered clone's own working tree:

```
git rev-list --count <lastCommit>..HEAD     # core/git-staleness.ts
```

`HEAD` is whatever that clone happens to have checked out. Since #3199, a branch-pinned analyze gets its own clone directory and its own registry entry, so "whatever is checked out" is routinely **not** the default branch.

**Compose those two facts with `stalenessPayload`'s suppression rule and a gap opens:**

```ts
if (status === 'current') return undefined;   // core/staleness-status.ts
```

and `attachToolStaleness` adds nothing when the payload is `undefined`. So:

> A clone pinned to a feature branch, freshly analyzed at that branch's head, measures **0 commits behind** → `status: 'current'` → **no `staleness` field at all** on the `impact` response.

An `impact` answer computed from a feature branch is therefore **byte-identical, in its freshness signalling, to one computed from `main`**. The caller has no field to read, and the tool is behaving exactly as designed.

**Why #2655 sharpens this rather than fixing it.** Before #2655, silence on an `impact` response meant nothing — no tool carried staleness, so there was nothing to infer. After #2655, a caller learns that these tools *do* warn when the index is behind. Silence now reads as a positive "this index is current". For the feature-branch case that inference is wrong, and it is wrong in the reassuring direction: `impact` is the tool whose entire value is being complete and current about the mainline, and a stale-or-sideways answer is invisible at the point of use.

This is the residual of the same concern #3226 fixed on the HTTP side. #3226's argument applies verbatim here — the data already exists and is simply not wired to this surface:

- `RegistryEntry.branch` / `.branches[]` (`storage/repo-manager.ts`)
- `listRepos()` already emits `branch: h.branch` (`mcp/local/local-backend.ts`)
- the resolved repo handle passed to `stalenessForTool(repo)` already carries `branch`, `lastCommit` and `indexedAt`

The only happy-path carrier of `branch` + `indexedAt` in a tool response today is the FTS-degraded warning context added by #2767 — which fires only when FTS is degraded.

### Proposed change

Two parts; the first is the one that closes the gap.

**1. Carry the indexed ref on the tool staleness signal, and emit it even when `current`.**

Add `branch`, `lastCommit` and `indexedAt` to `StalenessPayload` from the already-resolved repo handle. The suppression rule is what has to change for the feature-branch case: today `current` means "no field", which is indistinguishable from "current index of `main`". Either emit a minimal payload when the indexed ref is not the repository's default branch, or always carry the ref and keep `commitsBehind` optional.

This keeps #3256's design intact — `status` still distinguishes `unknown` from `current` — and adds the axis `status` cannot express, because `current` is a statement about a *ref*, not about the repository.

**2. Measure `commitsBehind` against the default branch, or say which ref it is against.**

`<lastCommit>..HEAD` is a defensible quantity, but the question a blast-radius caller is asking is "is this index current with the mainline?". At minimum the response should name the ref the count is against, so `commitsBehind: 0` cannot be read as "current with `main`" when it means "current with `feature/x`".

If measuring against the default branch is unattractive (it needs a fetch, or an `origin/HEAD` that may not resolve), naming the ref alone resolves the ambiguity and costs nothing — the handle already has it.

### Expected behavior

An agent calling `impact` can tell, from the response alone, **which ref** the answer describes — and can distinguish "current index of the default branch" from "current index of some feature branch".

### Actual behavior

Both cases produce a response with **no `staleness` field whatsoever**. The ref is not recoverable from any tool response on the happy path; the caller must separately call `list_repos` or read the `gitnexus://repo/<name>/context` resource, which is the round-trip #2655 set out to remove.

### Environment

Read against the published `gitnexus@1.6.12` tarball (`npm pack`), `dist/` — `core/staleness-status.js`, `core/git-staleness.js`, `mcp/local/local-backend.js`, `storage/storage-resolver.js`.

**Bound, stated plainly:** this is read from source, not reproduced live. I have not stood up a branch-pinned clone and observed the empty `staleness` field on an `impact` call, so the composition above is an argument from the code paths rather than a measurement. If it does reproduce differently, the reading of `stalenessPayload`'s `current` short-circuit is the step most likely to be where I am wrong.

Separately, and for the record since it points the other way: I went looking for `listRepos` emitting a graph-presence flag and found that 1.6.12 already handles it — `LIST_STORAGE_REQUIREMENTS.requireCodeIndexDB` plus the `hasCodeIndexDB` check in `listRegisteredRepos({ validate: true })` means a metadata-only registry entry is excluded from the listing rather than reported as indexed. That was going to be a second issue and it is already solved.

title: fix(cursor-hook): keep npx fallback under the postToolUse host budget
body:
## Summary

The Cursor integration's `hooks.json` grants `postToolUse` a **10 second** budget (seconds, per Cursor's manifest contract). Inside the hook, the local-CLI branch runs `augment` with a 7s `spawnSync` timeout, but the npx fallback branch adds a flat `+5000` ms on top — an effective **12s** budget, past the host deadline.

On machines without a local `gitnexus` install — exactly the cold-start scenario the fallback exists for — npx has to resolve and download the package, so the child routinely needs the full budget. Cursor kills the hook process at 10s before the child finishes, the partial result is discarded, and the user silently loses augmentation every time.

Cap the fallback timeout at `10000 - 2000 = 8000` ms (host budget minus headroom for node startup and the final stdout write) via `Math.min`, so the fallback can never exceed the host deadline again:

```js
const npxTimeout = Math.min(
  timeout + 5000,
  CURSOR_HOST_BUDGET_MS - CURSOR_NPX_HEADROOM_MS,
);
```

## Testing

- `npx vitest run test/unit/cursor-hook.test.ts`: 83 tests pass, including a new source-level regression test asserting the cap wiring (`CURSOR_HOST_BUDGET_MS`, `CURSOR_NPX_HEADROOM_MS`, `Math.min`, and no bare `timeout + 5000` assignment), following the same style as the existing #1486 concurrency-guard source regression.

title: fix(mcp): name the indexed ref on hot read tool staleness (#3291)
body:
Closes #3291.

## Problem

`#2655` wired a `staleness` signal into the `query` / `context` / `impact` / `cypher` responses, and `#3256` gave "could not tell" its own name. The issue observed what those leave uncovered, and it reproduces exactly as filed:

1. `checkStalenessAsync` measures `<lastCommit>..HEAD` against **the clone's own checkout** (`core/git-staleness.ts:118`). A clone pinned to `feature/x` and freshly analyzed at that branch's head counts **0** — even when `feature/x` is two commits short of the mainline.
2. `stalenessPayload` suppressed the payload entirely for `current` (`core/staleness-status.ts:85`).
3. `attachToolStaleness` adds nothing when the payload is `undefined`.

Net: an `impact` answer computed from a behind-mainline feature-branch index was **`JSON.stringify`-identical** to one from a current index of the default branch, and the ref was not recoverable from the response at all. After `#2655`, silence reads as a positive "this index is current" — so the wrong inference was the reassuring one.

The issue was filed from source reading ("I have not stood up a branch-pinned clone"). It was reproduced live first: a test drives real `callTool('impact')` against two real clones with real `git`, with a measured precondition (the feature branch is genuinely 2 commits behind `main`) and a negative control, so it cannot pass vacuously.

## Fix

`stalenessPayload` gains an opt-in `ref` (`{ branch?, lastCommit, indexedAt }`) and `status` widens to include `current`. When a ref is supplied the payload is emitted for **every** status and names the index it describes:

```jsonc
"staleness": {
  "status": "current",
  "branch": "feature/checkout-v2",
  "lastCommit": "4f2a1c9e…",
  "indexedAt": "2026-09-15T07:12:00.000Z",
  "measuredAgainst": "HEAD"
}
```

`measuredAgainst` names what `commitsBehind` is counted against — the clone's own checkout, never the remote — which is the issue's part 2.

**Where the ref lives, and why it differs by surface.** The issue proposed adding the ref fields to `StalenessPayload`. Source says that is half right: `list_repos` and both `serve` repo routes already report the ref as **top-level siblings** of `staleness` (#3226). Duplicating it inside the payload there would be redundant, so **those surfaces pass no ref and are byte-identical** — `repo-projection.test.ts` and `server-repo-freshness.test.ts` both assert the exact payload with `toEqual` and pass **unmodified**, which is the proof.

The hot read tools are the documented exception: a tool result is an arbitrary object and `attachToolStaleness` may add exactly one key, so the ref has to ride inside it there.

That split also protects a consumer TypeScript cannot see: `gitnexus-web/src/services/backend-client.ts:43-47` keeps a *structural copy* of the payload typed `'behind' | 'diverged' | 'unknown'`. It is a copy, not an import — a blanket widening would have silently falsified it.

`branch` is best-effort: a plain analyze stamps the checked-out branch (`run-analyze.ts:1089`, `:4275`), but a detached HEAD, a non-git folder, or a legacy index leaves it absent. `lastCommit` is always present and identifies the index in that case.

No new I/O: the ref comes off the already-resolved `RepoHandle`. No git spawn, no metadata read, and the `stalenessForTool` TTL cache is untouched.

## ⚠️ Compatibility — behaviour change

**The `staleness` field is now present on every `query` / `context` / `impact` / `cypher` response, including when the index is current.** Previously its absence was the "fresh" signal. Any consumer asserting an exact response shape will see an extra key.

This is not theoretical — three in-repo parameter-normalization tests asserted `toEqual({status:'normalized'})` on tool results and needed relaxing to `toMatchObject`. External consumers cannot be updated here, so it is called out rather than buried.

Related: `status: "unknown"` now also rides on these four tools when a ref is present, which relaxes `#3256`'s deliberate suppression. The reasoning: with the ref attached the field is no longer only a warning — it is an identity statement, and which index answered is knowable even when its freshness is not. Reviewers who prefer keeping `unknown` suppressed should say so.

Both guide copies are updated and `shipped-skills-sync` pins the new shape string plus `measuredAgainst`, so the ref half of the contract cannot be silently dropped the way `#2899` dropped the section itself.

## Testing

- `tool-staleness.test.ts` — ref-absent parity for all four statuses (bit-identical to before), ref-present emission for `current`, `diverged` still carrying no invented count, and `branch` omitted for a detached HEAD.
- `repro-3291-staleness-indexed-ref.test.ts` — real `git`, two real clones, no `vi.mock` of `core/git-staleness.js`; the two responses are now distinguishable and each names its ref. Measured precondition and negative control retained.
- Unchanged and passing: `repo-projection`, `staleness`, `staleness-fallback`, `server-repo-freshness` (the byte-stability proof).
- `483 tests / 13 files` green on the final tree; `274` in `calltool-dispatch`; `npx tsc --noEmit` clean.

Blast radius: `context` reports `epistemic: "exact"`, so the caller set is *proven* complete — repo-wide there are exactly three `stalenessPayload(` call sites, two of which pass no ref. `detect_changes scope=compare`: 69 symbols, 9 files, **0 affected processes**.

## Known limitation

The full unit suite is **not** certified green here. It is environment-flaky on the v9fs (WSL2 9p) host used for this work, established by controlled experiment rather than assumed:

| condition | result |
| --- | --- |
| overlayfs worktree, pre-change code | 90/90 pass |
| v9fs worktree, this change | 9 fail |
| v9fs worktree, **this change reverted** | **13 fail** |

Reverting the change made it *worse* and shifted the failing set, so the controlling variable is the mount, not the diff. The affected suites (`run-analyze`, `skip-git-cli`) spawn CLIs under hard-coded timeouts, and a plain analyze takes ~33 s on this box. CI should be treated as the authority for the full-suite result.

title: fix(rust): respect Cargo target boundaries in name fallback
body:
Fixes #3253.

Rust's bare-call fallback conflated Cargo targets by directory prefix. A library caller could receive a `global-name-fallback` CALLS edge to a helper defined only in a binary, integration test, bench, or example. Cargo entry-file identity and module membership now constrain those guesses through the existing Rust provider hook.

## Implementation

- Load bounded Cargo metadata statically; production code never invokes Cargo/rustc or repository build scripts. Preserve explicit targets, auto-discovery, workspace editions/dependencies, library names and shared `#[path]` sources.
- Require matching library-root evidence for cross-target named/glob imports. Match the imported root's role even when its source is also a module in another target.
- Recognize unshadowed built-in derives and standard expression macros. Inspect macro arguments for module declarations/nested expansion. Custom derives, unknown macros, ambiguous macro imports and unsupported expansion remain unknown.
- Enumerate manifests/target slots, then discover referenced modules and explicit source paths on demand. This retains real sources beneath `target/` without recursively indexing every artifact or every `.rs` file. Excluded control/dependency paths stay excluded; reads remain bounded and descriptor-validated.
- Use the same AST snapshot to distinguish actual public re-exports from private/restricted uses, including globs. Retain visible aliases and inline-module/re-export evidence.
- Normalize trailing slashes on explicit workspace directories. Preserve `crate`/`self`/`super` glob qualifiers. Parse-cache version 101 invalidates old keyword-glob and restricted-reexport captures.
- Require visible import evidence for cross-file bare root guesses even within one Cargo target: compilation membership is not lexical visibility. Keep the maintainer's benchmark CI gate and regression tests. Register the Cargo filesystem unit suite for Windows/macOS as well as Ubuntu.

## Review verification

Confirmed and covered: ordinary built-in derive/macros losing the snapshot, source directories/explicit roots beneath `target`, private and `pub(crate)` glob exports, shared-root role confusion, trailing-slash workspace pointers, weak alias/source assertions, and the oversized-payload-only race test. README Config matrices are updated.

Two proposed changes were not applied:

- `package.workspace` is a **directory**, not a manifest filename. Cargo 1.96 accepts `../..` and rejects `../../Cargo.toml` by attempting `Cargo.toml/Cargo.toml`. Tests pin this distinction and the valid trailing-slash form.
- Cargo 1.96 requires names for explicit `[[bin]]`/`[[test]]` targets; path-only probes fail with `bin.name` / `test.name is required`.

Unknown expansion cannot safely be localized to a sibling target solely from the completed walks. A controlled macro that includes `tests/helper.rs` and loads `src/lib.rs` makes their call valid in a third target; both rustc and a Cargo binary unit-test build accept it. The implementation retains uncertainty for that case rather than manufacturing a disjointness proof. The extern-crate alias test now explicitly asserts unknown metadata and a labeled 0.5 guess, rather than claiming alias resolution.

## Validation

- 309 focused tests pass after integrating the maintainer's `ae9a59b4` changes and the subsequent same-target lexical-visibility review: Cargo regressions, Rust scope/import tests, capture goldens, cache invalidation, and platform-shard checks. The import-free same-target reproduction failed before the fix; named and glob `crate`/`super` positive controls pass.
- Typecheck/build/formatting pass; lint has warnings but no errors.
- The new Cargo benchmark passes with its existing fingerprint and all membership floors; observed normalized 4n/n load ratio 0.975 against the unchanged 1.6 budget.

New React DOM Features

  • browser(): a new react-dom API that returns a usable which errors during server rendering and resolves in the browser. use(browser()) inside a <Suspense> boundary marks a subtree as browser-only without reporting a recoverable error (@​gnoff: #37143, #37241)
    • Added an onBrowserBailout option to the react-dom/server APIs to observe when a subtree defers to the browser (@​gnoff #37193)

    OpenAI recently changed the disposition of encrypted_content to contain the canonical payload on the final done event. Encrypted content also does not need to be a parameter in the include call options in order to propagate.

@​langchain/openai@​1.5.10

  • #11399 5c9fdf2 Thanks @​gethin-langchain! - Map OpenAI's cache_write_tokens to cache_creation in usage_metadata.input_token_details, mirroring the existing cached_tokens -> cache_read mapping across the Chat Completions and Responses APIs. Previously, prompt cache-write token counts were silently dropped.

@​langchain/openai@​1.5.8

Patch Changes

  • #11342 3b0e4c4 Thanks @​thushanth-bengre-langchain! - feat(openai): mark OpenAI provider errors as retryable or not

    Builds on stampRetryable in @langchain/core so the retry middleware can tell a transient failure from a deterministic one. Timeouts and rate limits are marked retryable; aborts, context overflow, invalid tool results, bad credentials, and unknown models non-retryable. Anything else stays unmarked and retries as before.

title: analyze --embeddings 0` on a large already-indexed repo OOMs the V8 heap during `Caching embeddings...` even when the incremental diff is tiny
body:
## Summary

`gitnexus analyze --embeddings 0 --worker-timeout 300 --pdg` on a **large repo that has already been successfully indexed** (so a normal increment indexes only a handful of changed nodes) crashes with a **JavaScript heap OOM** (not a system-RAM OOM) while it is at **`Caching embeddings...`** — before any embedding work for the actual new/changed nodes has happened.

The crash is a `FATAL ERROR: NewSpace::EnsureCurrentCapacity Allocation failed - JavaScript heap out of memory` inside `loadCachedEmbeddings`, which pulls **the entire existing embedding table into one JS array** (`embedding.map(Number)`) on every run, regardless of how small the diff is.

## Environment

- GitNexus 1.6.12 (Docker, official `gitnexus-server` container)
- `@ladybugdb/core` 0.18.3 (pinned)
- Host: 64 GB RAM; the JS heap cap auto-sized to ~48 GB (≈ 0.75×RAM), so **physical memory is not the constraint**
- A high-dimensional embedding model (e.g. 500-dim) served via a self-hosted / internal embedding endpoint

## Reproduction

Large monorepo (~1.93M node graph; 500-dim embedding model). Index was **successfully built once** with `--embeddings 0` (469,294 nodes already have embeddings). Then run the same incremental command after a tiny code change:

```bash
gitnexus analyze --embeddings 0 --worker-timeout 300 --pdg
```

Expected: an incremental run that only regenerates embeddings for the small set of changed nodes.

Actual:

```
Previous analyze ended at an embedding checkpoint (469294/469384 nodes); resuming from persisted hashes and regenerating 90 pending node(s).
  ░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░   0% | Caching embeddings... {"msg":"GitNexus: reclaimed quarantined WAL ..."}
  ░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░   0% | Caching embeddings... (3m 1s)

<--- Last few GCs --->
[28743:0x819c000]   202382 ms: Scavenge 15788.4 (16207.4) -> 15816.5 (16236.4) MB, ... allocation failure;
[28743:0x819c000]   202477 ms: Scavenge 15816.5 (16236.4) -> 15790.7 (16322.2) MB, ... allocation failure;

<--- JS stacktrace --->
FATAL ERROR: NewSpace::EnsureCurrentCapacity Allocation failed - JavaScript heap out of memory
...
  Analysis likely ran out of memory (heap cap auto-sized to 48185MB ≈ 0.75x RAM).
```

Note: a **previous run of the same command already died against a different ceiling** (`Buffer manager exception: Maximum database size of 137438953472 bytes has been reached`) after it had consumed ~128 GiB of max_db_size space on the embedding write-back — see the follow-on correlation below.

## Root cause

`loadCachedEmbeddings` (`gitnexus/src/core/lbug/lbug-adapter.ts`, around line 2077) loads the **entire** existing embedding table into V8 heap on every run:

- It issues one `MATCH (e:CodeEmbedding) RETURN e.nodeId, e.chunkIndex, e.startLine, e.endLine, e.embedding, e.contentHash` (line 2114) and drains **all rows** into a JS array.
- For each row it does `embedding: Array.isArray(embedding) ? embedding.map(Number) : Array.from(embedding).map(Number)` (lines 2140-2142), producing a **pure-JS `Number[]` copy** for every stored vector.

For a repo with ~470k already-embedded nodes this creates ~470k **JS Float64 arrays** resident in the V8 old/… space *before* any incremental embedding work begins. That single data structure exceeds the ~48 GB JS-heap cap and OOMs, even though:

- the actual incremental change is only 90 nodes (per the checkpoint log above), and
- the machine has tens of GB of free system RAM (the limit hit is V8's heap cap, not RSS).

`run-analyze.ts` calls this **unconditionally** whenever caching is requested (lines 2223-2229): `cachedEmbeddings = cached.embeddings` is kept in memory and later used for re-insert / orphan detection, so the full table is resident regardless of how few nodes are actually new.

## Why this is important

- **Regression-ish UX**: on an already-indexed large repo, a routine tiny increment should not require re-loading the full embedding history into memory; here it makes the whole run unusable.
- **`--embeddings 0` is documented as “disable the cap”, not “load everything”** — operators reasonably expect it to mean “embed all nodes unconditionally”, and on an incremental pass that should only concern nodes without embeddings. Instead every node is re-materialized as a JS vector.
- The failure mode masks a simple small-diff run behind a scary OOM, and two different resource ceilings (`max_db_size` then V8 heap) can be hit on consecutive runs of the same command.

## Possible fixes / suggestions

A few directions the maintainers may want to consider (open to adjustment):

1. **Don't materialize full vectors in JS for dedup/identity.** The incremental path only needs `nodeId → contentHash` to decide what to regenerate; the actual `embedding` array is only needed for the nodes being re-inserted. `loadCachedEmbeddings` could stream/iterate the table (or query only `nodeId, contentHash`) and keep full vectors only for the pending set, instead of `map(Number)`-ing every row.
2. **Batch / bound the cache read.** If a full embed array must be held for write-back, page over it (load in slices of N rows) rather than one unbounded `MATCH` draining every row.
3. **Reconsider the meaning of `--embeddings 0` with an existing index**: when `0` (disable cap) is passed and a large embedding set already exists, either (a) only embed the missing/changed subset (what the logs already try to do) without loading the whole history, or (b) warn loudly that the cache-load itself will require significant heap.
4. **Cap the heap waste**: `Array.from(...).map(Number)` copies unnecessarily when the row already yields JS numbers — avoid the double allocation.

If useful I can provide a smaller synthetic repro (generated `.gitnexus` fixture with N embeddings) that triggers the heap spike proportional to N, and/or the exact heap-retention trace from the crash.

## Related

The immediately-preceding failure of the **same command** was:

```
Buffer manager exception: Maximum database size of 137438953472 bytes has been reached.
manual WAL checkpoint failed after retries
```

i.e. `--embeddings 0` on this repo can also blow past an explicitly-raised `GITNEXUS_LBUG_MAX_DB_SIZE` (128 GiB) during the embedding write-back. Both symptoms stem from treating the full embedding set as an unbounded in-memory/in-db pass.

- Relevant code: `gitnexus/src/core/lbug/lbug-adapter.ts` — `loadCachedEmbeddings`
- Caller: `gitnexus/src/core/run-analyze.ts` — embedding cache load (~line 2223) and re-insert (~line 3935)
- Environment rigor: Docker `gitnexus-server` image, official build, no engine swap.

title: auto-sync: support self-hosted Git hosts (custom remote_urls domain)
body:
### Problem
`gitnexus auto-sync` rejects self-hosted Git remotes. Any `remote_urls` entry whose host is not exactly `github.com`, `gitlab.com`, or `gitee.com` fails config validation and the whole sync is skipped:

```text
[auto-sync] Invalid watch_config.yml: projects[0].remote_urls[0] host must be one of github.com, gitlab.com, or gitee.com; ... Auto sync is skipped.
```

### Use case
Company self-hosted GitLab over SSH (SCP form), e.g.:

```yaml
projects:
  - local_path: /data/gitnexus/repos
    branches: [main]
    remote_urls:
      - git@gitlab.mycompany.com:group/repo.git
```

Same `git@host:group/repo.git` SCP shape as the allowed hosts, just a custom domain. HTTPS is not required.

### Why this should be safe
- Clone target is already namespaced by full identity (`runner.ts:getConfiguredRepoPath` + `getAutoSyncRepoIdentity`): `{local_path}/{host}/{namespace...}/{repo}`, so a custom host cannot collide with `github.com/...` entries.
- `validateAutoSyncRemoteUrl` already enforces no query/fragment, no traversal, strict repo-name charset — only the host set needs relaxing.
- `cloneOrPull` with `allowAutoSyncSsh` delegates to the same validator, so no second host gate to change.

### Suggestion
Allow custom SSH hosts for `auto-sync`, e.g. one of:

1. Accept any syntactically valid `git@<host>:<path>` SCP host by default (keep path/name/branch validation as-is), or
2. Add an opt-in per-config allowlist, e.g. `allowed_hosts: [gitlab.mycompany.com]`, merged with the built-in three.

Option 2 keeps the current secure default while unblocking self-hosted users. Happy to test a snapshot build against our internal GitLab.

### Repro
1. `gitnexus auto-sync init`
2. Put a self-hosted SSH URL in `remote_urls` (see above).
3. `gitnexus auto-sync start` -> validation error, sync skipped.

### Environment
- `gitnexus@latest`, macOS/Linux
- Remote: self-hosted GitLab, SSH SCP form

title: fix(swift): resolve inherited protocol extension calls
body:
## Problem

Bare calls inside a Swift conforming type only checked methods owned directly by that type. Protocol-extension defaults were skipped, so resolution fell through to global same-name candidates and became file-order dependent. Extension methods also retained no owner when the extended protocol or type was declared in another file. The downstream member call could then lose the helper's exact return type during parse-cache replay.

## Fix

- reconcile ownerless extension members against a unique workspace type owner
- let implicit-receiver lookup walk the owner MRO nearest-first so overrides keep precedence
- persist and replay exact call-result assignments, including `try` / `await` wrappers, without conflating same-named methods
- add counterfactual fixtures for unrelated private decoys, target isolation, shadowing, override precedence, and cached return-type propagation

## Test

- hosted CI gate passed at `bc0b870c` (format, lint, typecheck, CodeQL, benchmarks, Ubuntu coverage shards, Windows/macOS platform shards, and packaged install smoke)
- full Swift resolver suite: 104 passed
- focused implicit-this / index / extractor / store / C++ matrix: 442 passed
- `npx tsc --noEmit`
- `git diff --check`

## Risk

The shared return-type replay path is broader than the original Swift-only fix. It is constrained to exact callee identities and explicit callable returns; ambiguous duplicate metadata fails closed. Swift inherited lookup is gated to Swift and only runs after the enclosing type has no compatible direct method.

Fixes #3273

title: fix(embeddings): stop Caching embeddings OOM on large incremental analyze
body:
## Summary

- Stream `CodeEmbedding` rows under the connection lock and spill vectors to a temp Float32 file once the in-memory row limit is exceeded (default 2048), so incremental `analyze` no longer builds a full-table JS `number[]` heap at `Caching embeddings...`.
- Restore wipe and surgical paths from that snapshot in 200-row batches, keeping the original cached `contentHash` so unchanged live embeddings do not call the model.
- Fail cache load loudly (warn-and-continue) instead of adopting an empty snapshot; rescue stays extension-forced only.

## Motivation / context

Fixes #3306. On a ~469k-row / 500-dim already-embedded index, the old `getAll()` plus `map(Number)` path allocated on the order of 3 GB of JS vectors before any new embed ran. This change keeps vectors on disk after the in-memory limit and leaves identity metadata (`nodeId` + stable `contentHash`) in RAM.

## Areas touched

- [x] `gitnexus/` (CLI / core / MCP server)
- [ ] `gitnexus-web/` (Vite / React UI)
- [ ] `.github/` (workflows, actions)
- [ ] `eval/` or other tooling
- [ ] Docs / agent config only (`AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `.cursor/`, `llms.txt`, etc.)

## Scope & constraints

**In scope**

- Stream-and-spill cache load, snapshot lifecycle, Phase 3.5 materialize, spill dispose, and the tests that prove them.

**Explicitly out of scope / not done here**

- Changing what `--embeddings 0` means (`deriveEmbeddingCap` / the 50k node cap).
- Raising or writing back Ladybug `max_db_size` / `GITNEXUS_LBUG_MAX_DB_SIZE`.
- Replacing restore with a full re-embed of the live graph.
- Streaming `fetchExistingEmbeddingHashes`.
- Claiming O(1) heap (leftover identity catalog is about 150–250 MB at the #3306 shape, plus an ~897 MiB spill file).

## Implementation notes

- Spill format: `GNXE` / version 1 / little-endian dims / native-endian Float32 body, `wx` + `0o600` under `os.tmpdir()`.
- `GITNEXUS_EMBEDDING_CACHE_IN_MEMORY_LIMIT` overrides the RAM row cap; `0` always spills.
- Small tables still expose `snapshot.embeddings` so skip-fts and existing mocks keep working.
- `loadCachedEmbeddings` stays a leaf under `withConnLock` and does not call unlocked `streamQuery` (#2264).
- Phase 3.5 still swallows a last-resort `batchInsert` failure; Phase 4 still builds its skip-set from all cached hashes (KTD7 durable hole, pinned in test, not redesigned).

## Testing & verification

- [ ] `cd gitnexus && npm test`
- [ ] `cd gitnexus && npm run test:integration` *(if core/indexing/MCP paths changed)*
- [x] `cd gitnexus && npx tsc --noEmit`
- [ ] `cd gitnexus-web && npm test` *(if web changed)*
- [ ] `cd gitnexus-web && npx tsc -b --noEmit` *(if web changed)*
- [ ] Manual / Playwright E2E *(note environment — see `gitnexus-web/e2e/`)*

Local commands that passed:

- `cd gitnexus && npx vitest run test/unit/embedding-restore-spill.test.ts`
- `cd gitnexus && npx vitest run test/integration/load-cached-embeddings-spill.test.ts test/integration/lbug-conn-serialization.test.ts`
- `cd gitnexus && npx vitest run test/unit/run-analyze-fts-repair.test.ts test/unit/run-analyze-fts-crash-marker.test.ts`
- Combined spill + lock re-run: 21 passed

Host flakes (parse-worker ready timeout / vitest fork exit; not embedding-assertion failures): `incremental-dirty-recovery`, `incremental-orchestration`, `incremental-index-extension-dml-gate`, `skip-fts`. Re-run those in CI or with `GITNEXUS_WORKER_READY_TIMEOUT_MS=60000`.

## Risk & rollout

No index-format or CLI-flag change. Operators on large already-embedded repos should see `Caching embeddings...` complete instead of a V8 OOM. Spill files live under the process temp dir for the restore window (~897 MiB at 470k × 500) and are unlinked after restore or on abort; a SIGKILL can leave `gitnexus-embed-restore-*.bin` until OS tmp clean.

## Known residuals

- Ladybug `QueryResult` may still retain decoded VECTOR cells for the scan (soak-only).
- Swallowed Phase 3.5 insert + spill unlink can leave a durable hole while Phase 4 still skips those hashes.
- Leftover spill files after SIGKILL / worker retry are not reaped.

## Post-Deploy Monitoring & Validation

- Logs: `Caching embeddings...`, `Warning: could not load cached embeddings`, `Preserving N embedding row(s) across the forced rebuild`, `Restoring N cached embeddings...`.
- Healthy: incremental analyze of a large already-embedded repo finishes cache load; `stats.embeddings` for unchanged live nodes does not drop to 0; no model call for those rows.
- Failure: V8 heap OOM at cache load, silent empty cache (no warning), or wipe restore that rembeds the whole live set.
- Rollback: revert this PR; prior `getAll()` path returns.
- Window: first incremental analyze on a large embedded index after deploy; owner is the merge author.
