title: Process-detection budget (`maxProcesses`/`maxBranching`/`maxTraceDepth`) is hard-coded — no config or env to opt into fuller flow coverage on large repos
body:
## Summary

Execution-flow (process) detection silently down-samples on large repositories, and its budget is **compiled-in with no way to raise it**. On a large monorepo the analyzer warns that only a small fraction of candidate entry points are ranked into flows (`[processes] N flows reported, but whole flows are MISSING: … entry point(s) never ranked in`), yet there is **no CLI flag, env var, or config key** to increase the process budget or disable the capping.

This makes the (correct and useful) `entryPointCandidatesDropped` warning un-actionable: the user can see flows are being sampled away, but cannot opt into more complete coverage.

## Background

Flow detection caps are defined in `gitnexus/src/core/ingestion/process-processor.ts`:

- `maxTraceDepth` = 10 (max steps per trace)
- `maxBranching` = 4 (max branches followed per node)
- `maxProcesses` = 75 (interface default), but the pipeline sets it dynamically:

```ts
computeDynamicMaxProcesses(symbolCount) // max(20, round(symbolCount / 10))
```

`gitnexus/src/core/ingestion/pipeline-phases/processes.ts:38-40`

So the per-repo flow cap scales with symbol count (`symbols/10`), but all three deep-traversal caps (`maxBranching`, `maxTraceDepth`, per-entry trace budget) are fixed constants with no override surface. Adding up, a repo whose entry-point candidate list exceeds ~200 already drops candidates (`processes.ts:584`, `ENTRY_POINT_CANDIDATE_LIMIT`), independent of the other budgets.

The phase already surfaces this honestly — `ProcessTruncationStats` distinguishes "whole flows dropped at maxProcesses" from "traces cut at maxTraceDepth", and `pipeline-phases/processes.ts` routes only the whole-flow-missing counters to `warn`. The gap is that **the operator cannot mitigate it**.

## Why it matters

`process` data is not decorative — it powers several read paths:

- `query()` returns ranked execution flows for a concept (not just symbol matches).
- `detect_changes()` maps a diff onto symbols and reports **affected processes**.
- `impact()` reports `affected_processes` (flows that would break, and at which step).
- `context(symbol)` shows which flows a symbol participates in.

When the budget drops whole flows, an edit's blast radius over *flows* is under-reported. `impact()` correctly marks this as budget-exhausted (`risk: UNKNOWN`, and its resource `riskScale` names the exhausted budget) rather than claiming no effect — that part is right. But today the only remedy is to throw more RAM at the machine, because the budget itself cannot be raised.

## Request

Expose the flow-detection budget via configuration so large repositories can opt into fuller coverage, e.g.:

- env vars such as `GITNEXUS_MAX_PROCESSES`, `GITNEXUS_MAX_PROCESS_BRANCHING`, `GITNEXUS_MAX_PROCESS_TRACE_DEPTH`, or
- entries in the `.gitnexusrc` config added by `analyze --process-budget <...>`, or
- an "also include a fuller flow set" flag.

Because the caps exist to bound memory/time on very large graphs (the dynamic `symbols/10` cap and the per-entry trace budget are the anti-OOM guardrail), defaults should stay as-is and the config should be a **raise/down only from an explicit operator choice** — with the existing truncation warnings reflecting the chosen budget.

I am not certain which surface (`env` vs `.gitnexusrc` vs a flag) best fits GitNexus's existing config conventions — happy for the maintainers to pick. The core ask is simply **an override path for the process budget today.**

## Suggested implementation pointers

- Defaults: `gitnexus/src/core/ingestion/process-processor.ts` — `DEFAULT_CONFIG` (`maxBranching`, `maxTraceDepth`, `minSteps`).
- Dynamic cap: `gitnexus/src/core/ingestion/pipeline-phases/processes.ts` — `computeDynamicMaxProcesses` (`symbols/10`), and where it is applied (`processProcesses(…, { maxProcesses: dynamicMaxProcesses, minSteps: 3 })`).
- Entry-point candidate limit: `process-processor.ts` — `ENTRY_POINT_CANDIDATE_LIMIT` (~200) and the `entryPointCandidatesDropped` accounting.
- Most other `ProcessDetectionConfig` fields are already threaded through; only `maxProcesses` is overridden at the call site today, so wiring a user-supplied override there mirrors existing structure.

Alternatively, if full coverage is considered undesirable for any graph (not just resource-constrained ones), a docs note explaining "the flow list is a sample by design" at the user-facing surface would at least make the limitation discoverable without introspection.

title: TypeSafe Jev for first-tool / skill routing (~300ms, fail-open) — not indexing
body:
### Area
- gitnexus-web (browser UI / WASM / workers) — primary
- gitnexus (CLI / core / indexing / MCP server) — optional follow-up, opt-in only

### Problem or opportunity

GitNexus is already fast at the things it owns: tree-sitter parse, LadybugDB, BM25/hybrid `query`, Cypher. TypeSafe **Jev cannot speed any of that** (and must not be asked to). It is a judgment model (`POST /v1/systemone`, Choice + Noul, ~300ms, max output tokens 0) — it names *which option*, it does not generate Cypher, embeddings, or answers.

Two hops still go through a **chat model** today, and those are the only places Jev helps:

1. **Web Graph RAG agent (`gitnexus-web/src/core/llm/agent.ts`)** — `createReactAgent` with 7 tools (`search`, `cypher`, `grep`, `read`, `overview`, `explore`, `impact`). Every user question starts with a full LLM tool-call just to pick the first tool. `BASE_SYSTEM_PROMPT` is ~1.3k tokens of tool policy before that hop. Recursion limit is 50. Related: #435 (prompt dilution), #438 (iteration budget).

2. **Host-agent GitNexus skills** — `gitnexus analyze` installs a small overlapping catalog (`gitnexus-exploring` / `impact-analysis` / `debugging` / `refactoring` / `guide` / `cli`, plus plan/review/work/pdg/taint). `ai-context.ts` already documents the failure mode: *“skills are skipped 56% of the time (Vercel eval data)”*, which is why the CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md block inlines workflows. Related: #2510 (move tool-usage policy off AGENTS.md onto MCP `instructions`). A calibrated picker would make those skills actually load instead of stuffing more RFC 2119 into the markdown.

MCP currently exposes ~17 tools (`query`, `cypher`, `context`, `impact`, `explain`, `pdg_query`, `route_map`, `tool_map`, …) with **no** MCP `instructions` field (`gitnexus/src/mcp/server.ts`). Hosts guess among schemas; GitNexus then appends “Next:” hints because *“Agents often stop after one tool call.”*

### Proposed solution

Treat Jev as an optional **router**, never as a provider or indexer.

**Phase 1 — web chat only (small, shippable)**

Before the LangChain ReAct loop, one TypeSafe call:

- `which` = Choice over the 7 Graph RAG tool names (short criteria, not the full system prompt)
- gate nouls: `code_question`, `needs_graph`, `needs_file_read` (same 0.30 mean as the [skill-suggestion cookbook](https://docs.typesafe.ai/cookbooks/skill_suggestion.md))
- On a hit: seed the agent with that tool call (or a one-line “start with `search`”) so the chat model skips the first selection hop
- On miss / no key / timeout: **fail-open** — today’s ReAct path unchanged
- Wall: ~2.5s abort, 1 attempt, **no** tiny/smol/chat fallback (a wrong first tool is worse than none)
- Only when the user already opted into a cloud LLM **and** has `TYPESAFE_API_KEY` (web chat is already a network path)

Live check of this cookbook shape (39-way Choice, `jev-1.13.0`): p50 ~330ms, p95 ~372ms, 0/6 over 2.5s. Seven tools should be cheaper.

**Phase 2 — optional MCP `route` (only with a key)**

A single opt-in tool, e.g. `gitnexus_route({ prompt })` → `{ skill?, tool, hint }`, Choice over the standard skill catalog + MCP tool names. Disabled unless `TYPESAFE_API_KEY` is set. Complements #2510: policy can shrink because a judge picks the tool instead of a 660-token CLAUDE.md block. Default MCP stays local/no-network.


### Privacy / no-network policy (opt-in, minimal payload)

GitNexus’s advertised contract is **CLI+MCP: “Everything local, no network.”** Web UI: **“Everything in-browser, no server.”** A TypeSafe hop is a cloud API call, so this feature is **off by default on every path**. Having an OpenAI/Anthropic/Ollama key is **not** consent for a second vendor.

**Payload (the whole point of Jev being cheap):** one `POST /v1/systemone` whose `state` is the current user question, hard-truncated (e.g. 500 chars). Choice options are the public 7 Graph RAG tool names already in `GRAPH_RAG_TOOL_NAMES`. **Not sent:** source, diffs, graph, Cypher, embeddings, repo path, remotes, `SKILL.md` bodies, prior chat, system prompt, or tool results. That is a strict subset of what web chat already sends to the session LLM.

**User opt-in, not an env-var side effect:**
- Web: Settings toggle default **off**, with copy that this sends the question text (not code) to TypeSafe. Requires a TypeSafe key in the same panel.
- CLI+MCP: both `GITNEXUS_TYPESAFE_ROUTING=1` **and** `TYPESAFE_API_KEY`. A TypeSafe key alone does not enable it. `gitnexus_route` is absent from `ListTools` otherwise. GitNexus never auto-calls TypeSafe; the host must invoke the tool.
- `analyze` / embeddings / default `mcp` / `serve`: **zero** TypeSafe requests (network-intercept tests).

TypeSafe states they [do not train on Input](https://typesafe.ai/privacy) and offer [enterprise ZDR](https://docs.typesafe.ai/legal.md). GitNexus still sends as little as possible, only after the toggle/flag.

See the follow-up comment on this issue for the acceptance-criteria extras.

**Explicitly out of scope**

| Idea | Why not |
| --- | --- |
| Speeding `analyze`, tree-sitter, LadybugDB, embeddings | Different bottleneck. See #1444 / #3295 |
| Generating Cypher or chat answers with Jev | Max output tokens 0 |
| Default-on for CLI+MCP | README: “Everything local, no network.” A TypeSafe hop is a cloud call — opt-in only |
| Replacing hybrid/BM25 `query` or `--embeddings` | Jev is not an embedder |
| Tournament / GodsBoy-style chunking | Catalog is 7 tools / ~6–10 skills, far under Choice’s 255 cap |

### Alternatives considered

- **Bigger system prompt / more RFC 2119** — already the current design, and skills are still skipped 56% of the time.
- **MCP `instructions` only (#2510)** — still the right place for *policy*; it does not pick among 17 tools in 300ms. This issue is the picker; that one is the transport.
- **Cheaper chat model as router** (`gpt-4o-mini` / Ollama) — still a generation model, still seconds, still can emit a wrong tool name with high confidence. Jev’s product is calibrated Choice/Noul, not tokens.
- **Heuristic regex** (“what breaks” → `impact`) — cheap and local; keep as a no-key fallback. It will miss paraphrases, which is the 56% skip problem.

### Acceptance criteria

- Web: with TypeSafe authenticated, the first Graph RAG action is chosen without a chat-model tool-selection hop on obvious queries (`search` vs `impact` vs `grep`).
- Web: without a key, with HTTP error, or past 2.5s, behavior is byte-identical to today (fail-open tests).
- Jev is never registered as an LLM provider in `gitnexus-web/src/core/llm/types.ts`.
- CLI `analyze` / embeddings / MCP default path make **zero** TypeSafe calls.
- If Phase 2 ships: `gitnexus_route` is absent from the tool list unless `TYPESAFE_API_KEY` is set; read-only policy treats it as read-only.
- Docs: one README/env row for `TYPESAFE_API_KEY` (required by CONTRIBUTING for new `GITNEXUS_*` / related env).

### Constraints

- Privacy: must not phone home during index/serve for users who never set a TypeSafe key.
- `pi-fabric` / TypeSafe clients do **not** auto-retry; a late inject is worse than none.
- Do not change `TypeSafeJudge`-style retry budgets used by other products; this path wants 1 attempt.
- Cookbook call 2 (rerank top-3 with SKILL.md excerpts) is unnecessary at 7 tools.

### Prior art

- TypeSafe cookbook: [Skill suggestion](https://docs.typesafe.ai/cookbooks/skill_suggestion.md) (call 1 = Choice + 3 gate nouls, gate 0.30)
- Native `POST /v1/systemone` usage: elizaOS, LangChain `langchain_typesafe`, Vercel typesafe-ai — Jev is not a chat model
- GitNexus already has the catalog and the eval number (56% skill skip) — this is wiring a judge in front of lists that already exist

Dropping a folder onto the Local Folder panel of the analyzer now uploads it through the same path as the "Upload a folder" button. Directories on the shared exclusion list (`.git`, `node_modules`, `dist`, and the rest of `EXCLUDED_DIRS`) are pruned before they are read, so a large checkout never has its dependency tree enumerated in the browser.

## Motivation / context

The `webkitdirectory` picker enumerates every file first (the browser walks `node_modules` and `.git` in full) and `filterRepoFiles` throws most of it away afterwards. With the File and Directory Entries API a dropped folder can be pruned before descending, which is the point of dropping over picking on a big repo. Drag and drop is also the interaction most people try first on a panel that says "folder". No issue exists for this; happy to open one if you want the discussion tracked there.

- [ ] `gitnexus/` (CLI / core / MCP server)

- [ ] `eval/` or other tooling

## Scope & constraints

**In scope**

- New module `gitnexus-web/src/lib/folder-drop.ts`: `collectDropEntries` (synchronous, reads `dataTransfer.items` before the first `await`) and `readDroppedFolder` (the walk). The walk loops `readEntries` until the empty batch, prunes `EXCLUDED_DIRS` before creating a reader, stops at the server's 20000 file cap and 64 path segments, skips unreadable directories and files instead of failing the drop, supports an `AbortSignal`, and reports progress every 50 files. Each `File` gets `webkitRelativePath = <folder>/<rest>` as an own property, so `filterRepoFiles` and the server see exactly the picker's shape. The exclusion list is imported, not copied, so `upload-filter-ignore-drift.test.ts` keeps guarding it.
- `RepoAnalyzer.tsx`: the Local Folder panel is the drop target (a drop that lands on the path input a few pixels above the button is caught too, and the browser never navigates to a stray dropped file). Drag highlight on the button with an enter/leave depth counter, a "Reading folder" indicator with the running count, Analyze and the picker blocked while the walk runs, and the walk under the request controller so a mode switch or unmount aborts it. `handleFolderUpload` is split into `handleFolderUpload` (picker) and `startFolderUpload` (shared tail); the picker path behaves as before.
- Refusals with a message: loose files or several folders at once (the server accepts one top-level folder), more than 20000 files, and browsers without `webkitGetAsEntry` (the picker button keeps working there and the hint is hidden).
- Seven new strings in `en` and `zh-CN` (`selectedDrop`, `dropHint`, `dropActive`, `reading`, `dropSingleFolder`, `dropTooManyFiles`, `dropUnsupported`). The zh-CN wording was drafted by a non-native speaker; corrections welcome.

**Explicitly out of scope / not done here**

- Dropping on the URL tabs with an implicit switch to Local Folder mode (would reset the URL fields through `handleModeChange`).
- A client-side pre-check of the 250 MiB total and the 2 MiB manifest cap. The picker path does not have one either; the server's 413 surfaces through `formatBackendError` as today. Easy follow-up if wanted, in `startFolderUpload` for both paths.
- Server changes. The manifest is byte-for-byte the shape the picker produces.

## Implementation notes

- Paths are joined from entry names, never from `entry.fullPath`, so the result has forward slashes and no leading slash in every engine.
- The depth check runs per directory: a directory whose files would have a 65th segment is skipped as a unit and counted, matching the server's `MAX_PATH_DEPTH`.
- The drop summary uses its own string (`selectedDrop`) because the walk counts pruned directories, not the files inside them, while the picker counts files. The two counts are kept apart instead of summed.
- `webkitGetAsEntry` is feature-detected per item, so jsdom tests can supply plain fixture entries.

## Testing & verification

- [x] `cd gitnexus-web && npm test` (477 tests in 43 files)
- [x] `cd gitnexus-web && npx tsc -b --noEmit`
- [x] `cd gitnexus && npx vitest run test/unit/upload-filter-ignore-drift.test.ts`
- [x] `npx eslint` on the changed files, zero warnings; `npx prettier --check` clean; pre-commit hook passed
- [x] Manual, Chromium against `gitnexus serve` (1.6.12 dev build) and `npm run dev`: a real OS-level folder drop, injected with the DevTools protocol (`Input.dispatchDragEvent` with a directory path), produced one `POST /api/analyze/upload` (202). The staging directory held `README.md`, `src/index.ts` and `src/util/math.ts` only; `node_modules`, `.git` and `dist` never left the browser. The analysis finished and the graph opened (9 nodes, 7 edges). A single file dropped on the path input and two folders dropped at once are refused with the message and the tab stays on the app.

New tests:

- `gitnexus-web/src/lib/folder-drop.test.ts` (18 cases): path shape, `readEntries` batching, pruning before read, loose file / several roots / empty drop, file cap, abort mid-walk and abort during the last file read, unreadable directory and unreadable file, depth cap, progress cadence, root named like build output, round trip through `filterRepoFiles` with an aligned manifest, `collectDropEntries` feature detection.
- `gitnexus-web/test/unit/repo-analyzer-folder-drop.test.tsx` (12 cases): upload through the existing path with an aligned manifest, reading state, the three refusal messages, empty folder, abort on mode switch, Analyze disabled during the walk, a drop on the path input, highlight depth counting, non-file drags ignored, no second upload while one is in flight.

Playwright cannot synthesise a `DataTransfer` whose items yield directory entries, so there is no e2e for the drop itself; the existing `e2e/folder-upload.spec.ts` still covers the picker path, which the drop converges into right after the walk.

## Risk & rollout

No contract or server change, no new dependency, no migration. Picker users see no difference except the hint line under the button. Rollback is reverting the single commit.

## Checklist

- [x] PR body meets repo minimum length (workflow may label short descriptions)
- [ ] If `AGENTS.md` / overlays changed: headers, scope block, and changelog updated per project conventions (not changed)
- [x] No secrets, tokens, or machine-specific paths committed

body:
Bumps [@playwright/test](https://github.com/microsoft/playwright) from 1.62.1 to 1.63.0.
Release notes

Sourced from @​playwright/test's releases.

v1.63.0

🔒 Test locks

Tests that access a shared resource — an external service, a global account setting — can now declare a named lock. Tests that share a lock name never run concurrently, across files, workers and projects, while everything else keeps running in parallel:

test('update user settings', { lock: 'user-settings' }, async ({ page }) => {
  // never runs at the same time as other tests holding 'user-settings'
});

A test can hold multiple locks, and test.describe() accepts a lock for the whole group. Learn more about test locks.

🪟 Locate across frames

page.frameLocator() and frame.frameLocator() called without a selector search in any frame of the subtree, so you no longer need to locate the iframe first:

// Finds the button in any frame on the page.
await page.frameLocator().getByRole('button').click();

The rest of the locator resolves inside a single frame, just like a regular locator, and an error is thrown when it matches elements in several frames.

👁️ Visible-only locators

New locator.visible() returns a locator that matches only visible elements. It is the recommended replacement for the :visible CSS pseudo-class:

await page.locator('button').visible().click();

🧾 Step params and subtitles

Steps now carry structured data for reporters. Playwright API steps report the target locator and call arguments, and test.step() accepts subtitle and params options for your own steps:

await test.step('Login', async () => {
  // ...
}, { subtitle: 'as admin', params: { user: 'admin' } });

Reporters receive them via testStep.subtitle and testStep.params. For Playwright API

title: FTS abort certifies raised flows as defaults
body:
A budget-only process-detection raise now rewrites Community/Process in place before FTS. An in-place FTS native abort parks WAL and `saveMeta`s the start-of-run meta. The next flagless analyze sees a default or missing `processDetection` stamp, takes already-up-to-date, and backfills defaults onto the raised sample.

## Suggested fix
After in-place FTS-park recovery, do not take already-up-to-date until `processDetection` is rewritten to the budget that produced the live Community/Process rows. Force a derived-layer rebuild on native-abort recovery when the crashed write set was empty, or stamp the resolved budget in `persistFtsNativeAbortRecovery`.

## Evidence
- `gitnexus/src/core/run-analyze.ts:1697` -- `await saveMeta(metaDir, existingMeta);`
- `gitnexus/src/core/run-analyze.ts:4591` -- `processDetection` is stamped only on successful end-of-run `saveMeta`.
- `gitnexus/src/core/ingestion/process-detection-budget.ts:188-193` -- missing stamp plus defaults is a match.

title: feat(analyze): expose process-detection budget overrides
body:
## Summary

Operators who see `[processes] … whole flows are MISSING` can now raise the process-detection budget on the next `analyze` and get a fuller Process set in `query` / `impact` / `context` / `detect_changes`. Unset runs keep today's caps.

## Motivation / context

On large repos the warning was correct and un-actionable: `maxProcesses` was always overwritten by `symbols/10`, and branching / depth / the 200 entry-point pool were compiled in. This PR adds an explicit raise/down path only.

Fixes #3313

## Areas touched

- [x] `gitnexus/` (CLI / core / MCP server)
- [ ] `gitnexus-web/` (Vite / React UI)
- [ ] `.github/` (workflows, actions)
- [ ] `eval/` or other tooling
- [ ] Docs / agent config only (`AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `.cursor/`, `llms.txt`, etc.)

## Scope & constraints

**In scope**

- Four analyze-time knobs (process count, branching, trace depth, entry-point pool) via CLI, `.gitnexusrc`, and `GITNEXUS_*` env
- Stamp + skip already-up-to-date / derived-layer reuse when the resolved budget changes (no `--force`)
- Loud-warning remedies for whole-flow drops only; shape caps stay debug

**Explicitly out of scope / not done here**

- Changing shipped defaults when no override is set
- A new MCP setter or query-time fuller-flow flag
- Collapsing the #2899 warn-vs-debug split
- Treating `0` as unlimited
- Leiden-only rematch on budget mismatch (communities still re-run with processes)

## Implementation notes

Precedence is CLI > `.gitnexusrc` > env > default. Explicit `maxProcesses` replaces the dynamic formula, including values below 20. Invalid tokens warn and fall through to the next source; the warning no longer claims the built-in default already won.

`RepoMeta.processDetection` records `maxProcesses: null` for the dynamic formula. A missing stamp plus defaults is a match and backfills; a missing stamp plus any override is a mismatch.

## Testing & verification

- [x] Targeted unit: `process-detection-budget`, `process-processor`, `processes-phase-sink-wiring`, `analyze-config`, `analyze-gitnexusrc`, `analyze-process-budget`, `watch-paths` (151 passed), plus the review-copy retest (28 passed)
- [ ] `cd gitnexus && npm test` (full suite not run in this worktree)
- [ ] `cd gitnexus && npm run test:integration`
- [x] `cd gitnexus && npx tsc --noEmit`
- [ ] `cd gitnexus-web && npm test` *(web unchanged)*
- [ ] `cd gitnexus-web && npx tsc -b --noEmit` *(web unchanged)*
- [ ] Manual / Playwright E2E — no web routes in this diff

## Risk & rollout

No MCP contract change. Existing indexes without a stamp keep the already-up-to-date path until an override is set. After merge, operators raise knobs and re-analyze; no release bump in this PR.

Known follow-ups (not blocking this close): in-place FTS-park after a budget-only rewrite can recertify raised flows as defaults; `runFullAnalysis` mismatch gates are helper-tested, not integration-tested.

## Checklist

- [x] PR body meets repo minimum length (workflow may label short descriptions)
- [x] If `AGENTS.md` / overlays changed: headers, scope block, and changelog updated per project conventions
- [x] No secrets, tokens, or machine-specific paths committed

title: refactor(analyze): move detected-branch sanitization off CLI config
body:
## Summary

- Move never-throw `sanitizeDetectedBranch` next to `validateBranchName` in `core/git-ref` so `run-analyze` no longer loads CLI `.gitnexusrc` parsing just to label an index slot.
- When git reports a checkout name the existing branch rules reject, warn once on `onLog` after the write lock settles and still write the workspace/flat slot (exit 0). Legal `--branch` still wins placement; detached / non-git / empty detect and `resolveDefaultBranch` stay silent.
- Escape hidden/bidi/quote characters in that warning so a git-legal U+202E name cannot reverse the log line, and pin that `run-analyze` does not import `cli/analyze-config`.

## Motivation / context

Cluster 3 layering leak: the indexer imported CLI analyze-config for a 7-line wrapper around core git-ref rules. A git-legal but GitNexus-illegal checkout (documented case: a backtick in the name) was dropped to unlabeled with no operator warning.

Plan: `docs/plans/2026-09-17-2110-refactor-analyze-layer-leak-plan.md`

## Areas touched

- [x] `gitnexus/` (CLI / core / MCP server)
- [ ] `gitnexus-web/` (Vite / React UI)
- [ ] `.github/` (workflows, actions)
- [ ] `eval/` or other tooling
- [ ] Docs / agent config only (`AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `.cursor/`, `llms.txt`, etc.)

## Scope & constraints

**In scope**

- Lift `sanitizeDetectedBranch` into `gitnexus/src/core/git-ref.ts` (catch `InvalidBranchError` only)
- CLI re-export for `resolveDefaultBranch` and existing analyze-config tests
- One `Warning: …; continuing.` per `runFullAnalysis` after lock settle, including `alreadyUpToDate`
- Layering pin in `run-analyze` unit tests

**Explicitly out of scope / not done here**

- Moving `generateAIContextFiles` off `run-analyze`
- Breaking the remaining two-file import cycles
- Forwarding detect-reject warnings on non-verbose `--watch` and auto-sync
- Closing the #2106 / #2354 hole where a forbidden checkout after a stamped primary still overwrites the flat slot while keeping the old stamp
- New branch-name rules, `.gitnexusrc` parsing changes, or fail-closed `--branch` behavior

## Implementation notes

- Warn predicate is raw detect non-null **and** sanitize empty — not `checkedOutBranch === null`.
- `resolveWriteTarget` can run more than once under lock; the warning is emitted once after the relock loop, not inside the helper (so `resolveDefaultBranch` stays silent).
- Hidden/bidi code points in the rejected name are rendered as `\uXXXX` in the warning; backticks such as `feat\`x` stay visible.

## Testing & verification

- [x] `cd gitnexus && npx vitest run test/unit/git-ref.test.ts test/unit/analyze-config.test.ts`
- [x] `cd gitnexus && npx vitest run test/unit/run-analyze.test.ts` (targeted detect-reject / pin / formatter cases; full file had 3 embedding-pipeline flakes on a 5s parse-worker ready timeout that passed on retry with `GITNEXUS_WORKER_READY_TIMEOUT_MS=30000`)
- [ ] `cd gitnexus && npm run test:integration` *(multi-branch integration is environment-flaky here; unlabeled placement + one warning are covered on the already-up-to-date unit path)*
- [x] `cd gitnexus && npx tsc --noEmit`
- [ ] `cd gitnexus-web && npm test` *(if web changed)*
- [ ] `cd gitnexus-web && npx tsc -b --noEmit` *(if web changed)*
- [ ] Manual / Playwright E2E *(note environment — see `gitnexus-web/e2e/`)*

## Risk & rollout

No index schema / storage-layout change. Existing unlabeled-slot behavior is unchanged except the new warning. No migration or release bump.

## Post-Deploy Monitoring & Validation

- Log search: `not a usable index label`
- Healthy: interactive `gitnexus analyze` on a forbidden checkout still exits 0, writes the workspace slot, and prints one warning that names the detected ref
- Failure: analyze throws/exits non-zero on a rejected checkout name, creates a `branches/` slug from that name, or `run-analyze` starts importing `cli/analyze-config` again
- Rollback: revert this PR; prior silent unlabeled fallback returns
- Window: first interactive analyze after deploy on a repo whose HEAD is a git-legal but GitNexus-illegal ref

## Checklist

- [x] PR body meets repo minimum length (workflow may label short descriptions)
- [ ] If `AGENTS.md` / overlays changed: headers, scope block, and changelog updated per project conventions
- [x] No secrets, tokens, or machine-specific paths committed

title: enancement: Nothing reclaims per-branch index slots whose branch no longer exists
body:
### Area

gitnexus (CLI / core / indexing / MCP server)

### Problem or opportunity

## Summary

`analyze --branch <name>` creates a per-branch index slot, but nothing ever reclaims a slot whose branch no longer exists. Deleting the branch, re-analyzing, and running `doctor` all leave the slot and its `branches[]` registry entry in place indefinitely.

`clean --branch <name>` can remove one, but it has to be invoked manually, per slot, with the exact branch name — which the user typically no longer has, because the branch is the thing that got deleted.

## Repro

gitnexus 1.6.12, Node v24.18.0, git 2.47.3, Linux x86_64. Sandboxed `GITNEXUS_HOME`, one-file TypeScript repo.

```
$ git checkout -q feature/x
$ gitnexus analyze --index-only --branch feature/x
  registry: name=myproj branches[]=['feature/x']
  on disk:  .gitnexus/branches/feature_x-217d2bf5

$ git checkout -q main && git branch -D feature/x     # merged, deleted
  live refs: main

$ gitnexus analyze --index-only                       # re-analyze
  registry: name=myproj branches[]=['feature/x']      # still there
  on disk:  .gitnexus/branches/feature_x-217d2bf5     # still there

$ gitnexus doctor
  (no mention of branch slots)

$ gitnexus clean --branch feature/x --force           # manual path works
  registry: name=myproj branches[]=(absent)
  on disk:  branches/ now exists with 0 entries
```


### Proposed solution

## Expected

Some automatic path that reclaims slots whose branch is no longer a live ref.

## Why it matters

A slot is a full index, not a delta. In the repro above — a repository containing **one** `.ts` file — the slot is **4.7 MB**:

```
4.7M    .gitnexus/branches/feature_y-a2bcce4a
```

So ~4.7 MB is the floor per abandoned branch, before repo size is taken into account. On a normal branch-per-ticket workflow that accumulates monotonically and silently: nothing warns, `doctor` doesn't flag it, and the only signal is disk usage. The registry side grows the same way, so `branches[]` steadily fills with refs that no longer resolve.

## Possible shapes

Rough preference order, all reasonable:

1. `gitnexus clean --branch --stale` (or `--prune`) — drop every slot whose slug matches no live ref. Explicit, no behavior change unless asked for.
2. Prune during `analyze` — at analyze time the live ref set is already known, so a slot whose branch is gone could be reclaimed as part of the run. Would probably want to be opt-in, or at least announced in output.
3. `doctor` reporting orphaned slots with their total size, even without deleting anything. Lowest risk, and would have surfaced this.

A detail worth deciding either way: after `clean --branch` removes the last slot, an empty `branches/` directory is left behind.

## Workaround in use

A `post-merge` git hook that lists live refs, maps them to slugs (`refs/heads/<name>` → `<name>` with `/`→`_`), matches `branches/<slug>-<8hex>/` against that set, removes the unmatched, and filters the matching `branches[]` entries out of `registry.json`. That works, but it hand-parses the slot naming convention and hand-edits the registry, which is exactly what it shouldn't have to do — see the companion issue about third-party registry writes.


### Alternatives considered

_No response_

### Acceptance criteria

_No response_

### Constraints

_No response_

### Contribution

- [ ] I am willing to open a PR for this (may need design discussion first).

title: No supported way for external tooling to edit registry.json under the registry lock
body:
### Area

gitnexus (CLI / core / indexing / MCP server)

### Problem or opportunity

## Summary

`~/.gitnexus/registry.json` is a machine-global file that gitnexus now guards properly for its own writes — `withRegistryLock` around read/merge/write, `writeFileAtomic`, a hard `registry is corrupt` error instead of a silent fallback. That part is solid, and this issue isn't about a bug in it.

The gap is that there is no supported way for anything *outside* gitnexus to participate in that lock. External tooling that needs to edit the registry — git hooks, cleanup scripts, CI steps — has only two options, and both are bad:

1. Reimplement the lock protocol by hand (`registry-lock` directory, `O_EXCL` pidfile, holder metadata, stale-holder reclaim). Getting stale reclaim subtly wrong is *worse* than not locking, because it can steal a live holder's lock.
2. Write the registry unlocked and accept a lost-update race against a concurrent `analyze`.

Neither is something a hook author should be choosing between.

## Context

The concrete case is a `post-merge` hook that reclaims dead per-branch index slots (companion issue). It has to remove entries from `branches[]`, so it does a read-modify-write of `registry.json` from Python with an atomic `os.replace` — correct in isolation, invisible to `withRegistryLock`. With several repositories on one machine analyzing concurrently (a hook in each), that write races gitnexus's own registry transaction.

The lock lives in `dist/storage/index-lock.js` and is internal, so the protocol isn't something external code can depend on staying stable across releases.



### Proposed solution

## Asks

Either would resolve it, roughly in preference order:

1. **A CLI verb that performs the mutation under the lock.** For the case above that's something like `gitnexus registry prune-branches --repo .`, but the general shape — any registry edit going through gitnexus rather than through a third-party file write — is the point. This is the version that keeps the protocol private.
2. **Document the lock protocol as a supported contract**: the lock directory's location, the pidfile format, the holder fields, the staleness rule, and the timeout semantics. Enough that a shell or Python hook can take the lock correctly and stay correct across releases.

If the companion branch-slot pruning issue is implemented, this stops being a problem for that particular hook — nothing external would need to write the registry at all. Filing it separately because the general question (how should third-party tooling mutate the registry safely?) outlives that one use case.

## Environment

gitnexus 1.6.12, Node v24.18.0, Linux x86_64.

title: analyze --name silently renames the existing registry entry for the same path
body:
### Area

gitnexus (CLI / core / indexing / MCP server)

### Summary

`analyze --name <alias>` silently renames the existing registry entry when one already exists for that path. There's no warning, no confirmation, and no indication in the output that an alias was replaced rather than assigned.


### Context





### Expected behavior

Something that distinguishes "assign an alias" from "replace the alias this path already has" — a warning line at minimum (`renaming registry entry "myproj" → "other"`), or an explicit `--rename` / `--force` for the replacing case.




### Actual behavior

`registerRepo` already has a `RegistryNameCollisionError` guard for the case where the requested name belongs to a *different* path, which is good. The same-path rename goes through with no equivalent signal, and the alias is the identifier everything else refers to: MCP `repo` arguments, `list` output, group membership files, and any documentation or scripts pinned to the old name. All of those break at once, and the only evidence is that the name changed.

The sharp edge is automation that passes a default alias. A script or git hook that does `--name "$(basename "$PWD")"` looks harmless, but on a repository whose directory name is generic — `app`, `web`, `api`, `server` in a monorepo subdirectory, or a worktree — it will silently overwrite a deliberately-chosen alias with the generic basename on the next run. That's how this was found: a hook that mirrored a `basename` default nearly renamed an intentional alias to its directory name, and nothing in the output would have said so.

The existing name-resolution precedence (explicit `--name` → preserved alias on the existing entry → remote URL name → basename) is sensible, and this isn't a request to change it. Omitting `--name` correctly preserves the existing alias. The request is only that the destructive branch of the explicit case announce itself.

### Steps to reproduce


```
$ gitnexus analyze --index-only --name myproj
  registry: name=myproj

$ gitnexus analyze --index-only --name other      # same path, existing alias
  exit=0
  registry: name=other                            # renamed, silently
```


### Environment

gitnexus 1.6.12, Node v24.18.0, git 2.47.3, Linux x86_64. Sandboxed `GITNEXUS_HOME`, one-file repo.


### Logs / screenshots

_No response_

title: Lexical containment misses branches/ symlink escape
body:
An operator who runs `gitnexus clean --stale --force` in a checkout whose `.gitnexus/branches` is a symlink recursively deletes directories outside the storage slot. The preview prints the lexical path, so `--force` is not informed consent.

## Suggested fix
In `removeBranchSlot`, refuse when `lstat(path.join(storagePath, BRANCHES_DIR))` is a symlink/junction. If the target dir itself is a symlink, unlink it only (do not `fs.rm` through it). Contain `realpath(dir)` against `path.join(await realpath(storagePath), BRANCHES_DIR)` with the existing `path.relative` idiom. Mirror `lbug-adapter.ts:894-907`.

title: feat(cli): reclaim leftover per-branch indexes after branch delete
body:
## Summary

After a local feature branch is deleted, leftover per-branch indexes can be listed and reclaimed without typing the deleted branch name.

## Motivation / context

`analyze --branch` writes a full index under `.gitnexus/branches/<slug>-<8hex>/` plus a `branches[]` registry row. Deleting the git branch does not reclaim either. Named `clean --branch` still works when the operator remembers the exact recorded label.

Fixes #3331.
Fixes #3335.
Fixes #3337.

## Areas touched

- [x] `gitnexus/` (CLI / core / MCP server)
- [ ] `gitnexus-web/` (Vite / React UI)
- [ ] `.github/` (workflows, actions)
- [ ] `eval/` or other tooling
- [ ] Docs / agent config only (`AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `.cursor/`, `llms.txt`, etc.)

## Scope & constraints

**In scope**

- cwd-scoped `gitnexus clean --stale` (preview without `--force`, delete with `--force`)
- cwd-only `doctor` leftover-slot report and size total
- empty `branches/` removal after the last per-branch slot
- disk-only and registry-only drift
- named `clean --branch` still resolves by exact recorded `branches[].branch`
- refuse `branches/` symlink/junction escape and unlink-only slot symlinks (`#3335`)
- doctor retry-git copy when local heads cannot be listed (`#3337`)

**Explicitly out of scope / not done here**

- prune during `analyze`
- treating a remote-only name as live (live means local `refs/heads` only)
- reclaiming the workspace/flat slot when its `meta.branch` is stale
- third-party writes to `registry.json` (#3332)

## Implementation notes

- `--stale` is an exclusive clean mode and wins the if-chain before `--branch`.
- A git-list failure returns `null` heads and does not delete. An empty list means every recorded branch is stale.
- When any leftover slot is `heads-unavailable`, doctor prints `clean.stale.headsUnavailable` and omits the orphaned heading, totals, and reclaim line.
- Directory rm happens before the registry drop. A failed rm keeps the row so a later clean can retry. A proven-absent registry-only row drops the summary with no rm.
- If `stat` fails with anything other than ENOENT/ENOTDIR, the row is skipped rather than treated as registry-only.
- Slot deletes refuse a `branches/` symlink and unlink a slot symlink without walking the target.
- Long-running `mcp` / `serve` may keep a Ladybug handle until the next registry refresh. An open handle can make `fs.rm` fail; the command reports it and keeps the row.

## Testing & verification

- [x] Targeted unit: `stale-branch-slots`, `clean-stale`, `doctor-format`, `git`, `clean-command-ownership`, `repo-manager-rm-failure`, `cli-i18n`
- [x] `cd gitnexus && npx vitest run test/integration/clean-stale-branch-slots.test.ts`
- [x] `cd gitnexus && npx tsc --noEmit` (pre-commit on each commit)
- [ ] `cd gitnexus && npm test`
- [ ] `cd gitnexus && npm run test:integration` *(if core/indexing/MCP paths changed)*
- [ ] `cd gitnexus-web && npm test` *(if web changed)*
- [ ] `cd gitnexus-web && npx tsc -b --noEmit` *(if web changed)*
- [ ] Manual / Playwright E2E *(note environment — see `gitnexus-web/e2e/`)*

The integration spec materializes a leftover slot and deletes the git branch, then runs `clean --stale --force`. It does not run full `analyze`.

## Risk & rollout

No index-format migration. Operators who keep only an origin branch after deleting the local head will see that pin as stale in preview. If a branch query still names a removed slot, refresh or restart `gitnexus mcp` / `serve`.

## Checklist

- [x] PR body meets repo minimum length (workflow may label short descriptions)
- [ ] If `AGENTS.md` / overlays changed: headers, scope block, and changelog updated per project conventions
- [x] No secrets, tokens, or machine-specific paths committed

title: feat(ingestion): add tRPC procedure detection and MCP chain/route surfacing
body:
## What

tRPC-aware ingestion and MCP surfacing, in four pieces:

1. **Ingestion** — new `route-extractors/trpc.ts` line-scans TS/JS router files (path-gated to `/routers/`, `/trpc/`, `/server/`) and emits `/trpc/<router>.<procedure>` routes with inferred methods (`query` → GET, `mutation` → POST). Tree-sitter scope/definition queries gain HOC-wrapped pair patterns (`runWorkflow: publicProcedure.input(...).mutation(async ...)`) — without them the arrow registers as anonymous, so procedures are invisible and their inner calls fall back to file-level attribution — plus curried-call patterns (`f(x)(y)`, awaited form).
2. **Entry-point scoring** — files under router paths get a `trpc` framework boost (3.0×); accessor-style procedure names (`getX`/`setX`/`isX`) skip the utility-pattern penalty inside router files only, so procedures like `setSettings` can become process entry points.
3. **MCP contract** — `context`/`query` accept optional `chain_depth` (BFS call-chain expansion per result, batched id probes); `context` responses now surface `is_entry_point: true` on process entry symbols and the attributed `routes` (via a batched `ENTRY_POINT_OF` lookup); response defaults raised (`limit` 5→10, `max_symbols` 10→25) so multi-procedure routers are not silently truncated. README tools table updated accordingly.
4. Route URLs are keyword-indexed (FTS) so `query "/trpc/..."` finds procedures directly.

## Why

In tRPC-heavy codebases, procedures were effectively invisible: the object-property + `procedure.mutation(...)` shape indexed as anonymous functions, agents could not see endpoints, their call chains, or their HTTP routes. After this change, `appRouter.runWorkflow` indexes as a Function node linked to its router const, participates in process flows, and `context({name: "runWorkflow"})` returns the entry-point flag and its `/trpc/...` route — i.e. an agent can discover "what HTTP surface does this repo expose and what does each endpoint call" end to end.

This has been running on a fork against a tRPC-heavy production codebase; these commits are the upstream-clean subset (the fork's earlier Function/Const dedup is intentionally not included — #2691 superseded it with a better order-independent mechanism).

## How to verify

- `cd gitnexus && npx tsc --noEmit`
- `cd gitnexus && npx vitest run test/unit/scope-resolution/typescript/typescript-captures.test.ts test/unit/calltool-dispatch.test.ts` — 367 passed (existing suites, no test changes needed)
- Smoke: index a fixture containing `src/server/trpc.ts` (`initTRPC`) and `src/server/routers/app.router.ts` with inline procedures over a 3-step call chain, then `gitnexus context runWorkflow`:
  - `uid`: `Function:src/server/routers/app.router.ts:appRouter.runWorkflow` (HAS_METHOD ← `appRouter`, CALLS → `workflow`)
  - `is_entry_point: true`
  - `routes`: `/trpc/app.router.greeting` (GET) and `/trpc/app.router.runWorkflow` (POST)
  - `processes`: `RunWorkflow → StepTwo`, `step_index: 1, step_count: 3`

## Risk / rollback

- Route extraction is path-gated, so non-tRPC repos see no new routes; the tree-sitter pair patterns are generic HOC shapes (same family upstream already covers for `React.forwardRef`-style variables) and only add name-bearing Function captures where previously the arrow was anonymous.
- `chain_depth` is opt-in (default off); batched probes use the existing `LBUG_ID_PROBE_BATCH_SIZE` chunking, no new persistence or schema — routes reuse the existing route storage, chains are computed at query time.
- Rollback: revert the branch; indexes built with it remain valid (additive rows only).

title: fix(lbug): self-heal read-only opens refused by an interrupted checkpoint
body:
## What

Two fixes to the LadybugDB read-only recovery paths, from one homelab incident:

1. **The refusal is now classified.** New `isReadOnlyCheckpointInProgressError` (with the `LADYBUGDB-CONTRACT` marker, live-verified against `@ladybugdb/core` 0.19.1) routed through the existing writable-open recovery in **both** adapters:
   - direct adapter: `ensureReadOnlyConnectionUsable` (probe-time) and `doInitLbug`'s read-only branch (open-time — the refusal can fire before any probe runs),
   - pool adapter: `openReadOnlyDatabase` (with `db.init()` moved inside the try for the same reason).

   Previously only missing-shadow and shadow-replay errors were recovered; this refusal was rethrown raw, so reads failed forever as `LadybugDB unavailable for __wiki__ ... Cannot open database in read-only mode while checkpoint is in progress`.

2. **Recovery is now durable.** Both writable-recovery paths issue an explicit `CHECKPOINT` after the probe. A reproduction matrix on 0.19.1 showed the probe replays the WAL **in memory only** — without `CHECKPOINT` the engine drops those pages at close, and the follow-up read-only open silently serves the pre-checkpoint state (sidecars left behind, data invisible).

## Why

Homelab incident 2026-09-19 (GitNexus image 1.6.10-20260917, `@ladybugdb/core` 0.19.x): a wiki pod killed mid-`CHECKPOINT` left the checkpoint artifacts on disk (`lbug.wal.checkpoint`, `lbug.shadow`, `lbug.checkpoint.intent.lock`, `lbug.checkpoint.apply.lock`), and every later read-only open refused with the message above — permanently, until a writable open (`gitnexus analyze`) happened to run. This was first hit by `gitnexus wiki` via the pooled read path, but the direct adapter had the identical hole.

## How to verify

```bash
cd gitnexus
npx vitest run test/integration/lbug-interrupted-checkpoint-recovery.test.ts   # new end-to-end test
npx vitest run test/unit/sidecar-recovery.test.ts test/unit/lbug-readonly-error.test.ts
npx tsc --noEmit
```

- The new integration test plants the killed-checkpoint signature **deterministically** (checkpointed db + `lbug.wal.checkpoint` + empty `lbug.shadow` + the two zero-byte checkpoint locks — no process killing, no race) and asserts the pooled read-only open self-heals and answers.
- Verified against a real crash too: SIGKILL a writer mid-`CHECKPOINT` on 0.19.1 → fresh-process read-only open throws the exact refusal → pool adapter self-heals → all 80,800 rows intact, sidecars consumed, checkpoint locks cleared.
- Engine-version honesty: the pinned `0.18.3` binary does not emit this message (checked via `strings` on both binaries); `0.19.x` does. The refusal assertion in the test is version-gated (`>= 0.19`), so the suite stays green and meaningful on both. If/when the engine pin moves back to `^0.19`, this recovery is already in place.

## Risk / rollback

- Risk: on this refusal, the read path now opens the DB writable once — the same shape as the existing shadow-replay recovery this extends. On a read-only filesystem the writable open fails with the existing actionable `EROFS`/`EACCES`/`EPERM` message (unchanged).
- Rollback: plain revert; no storage-format changes, no schema changes, no new `GITNEXUS_*` env vars (README env table unaffected).
- `detect-changes` flags HIGH breadth because `doInitLbug` is a hub every DB flow passes through; the behavioral delta is limited to the new error class routing into existing recovery plus the added `CHECKPOINT`.

## Docs

`ARCHITECTURE.md` Storage section: the checkpoint-in-flight artifacts are listed and the self-heal is described (second commit).

body:
Bumps [onnxruntime-common](https://github.com/Microsoft/onnxruntime) from 1.29.0 to 1.30.0.
Release notes

Sourced from onnxruntime-common's releases.

ONNX Runtime v1.30.0

ONNX Runtime 1.30.0 expands generative AI inference, improves CPU and GPU performance, adds Go bindings, and strengthens runtime reliability. These notes cover changes since ONNX Runtime 1.29.1.

Highlights

  • Expanded CUDA inference support with variable-length causal convolution for continuous batching, speculative decoding in paged XQA, and INT4 paged KV caches with per-channel scales (#32168, #32340, #32515).
  • Improved WebGPU PagedAttention, added GPT-OSS support and INT8 KV-cache block quantization, and extended convolution optimizations (#31727, #32277, #32284, #32420).
  • Added fused CPU LinearAttention kernels for AVX-512, Arm64 NEON, and SVE, plus AVX2 LayerNorm/RMSNorm acceleration (#31674, #31973, #32178, #32356).
  • Added Go bindings for the ONNX Runtime C API and DeepSeek Engram contrib operators (#29615, #32268).

Announcements & Compatibility

  • FP4 QMoE kernels are now enabled by default in CUDA builds, with Windows build support added in this release. Source builds can opt out with -Donnxruntime_USE_FP4_QMOE=OFF (#32096, #32163).
  • CUDA fpA-intB builds now default to a compact kernel set for FP16 activations, INT4/INT8 weights, scale-only quantization, and block_size=32. Set -Donnxruntime_USE_FPA_INTB_GEMM_FULL=ON when building from source to retain the full kernel set, including BF16, zero-point, bias, larger-block-size, and native Hopper variants (#32324).
  • CPU FP16 Gemm and MatMul execution is gated on hardware acceleration. CPU-assigned FP16 nodes without a matching kernel now fall back to FP32 (#32301, #32197).
  • WebGPU plugin EP packaging now supports Linux AArch64. Plugin versions were advanced to WebGPU 0.4.0 and CUDA 0.2 (#32287, #31960, #31970).

Security & Reliability

Model Loading, Memory, and Input Validation

  • Limited nested model-graph depth and canonicalized external-data locations to harden model loading (#32344, #32135).
  • Added checked rounding for BFC arena allocations and fixed prepacked-weight reference lifetimes (#32010, #32040).
  • Strengthened shape, rank, and parameter validation for Split, Scan, GatherND, ScatterND, SpaceToDepth/DepthToSpace, Crop, Conv, Normalizer, and pooling (#29461, #31668, #32034, #32039, #32076, #32157, #32160, #32161, #32345, #32349).
  • Hardened generation and attention input handling, including attention-attribute narrowing, BifurcationDetector inputs, generation subgraph shapes, and QEmbed segment inputs. BeamSearch buffer expansion now uses dynamic shape storage (#31648, #31701, #32009, #32078, #32144).
  • Validated TreeEnsemble node references and bounded subtree comparison, rejected non-finite CPU RoiAlign coordinates, and required ImageScaler bias to match the channel count (#32031, #32043, #32011, #32002).
  • Added an allowlist of safe LoRA adapter parameter data types, validated MatMulFpQ4 shape inputs, and checked MLAS blockwise quantization/dequantization index ranges (#31682, #32032, #32007).

GPU Bounds and Resource Lifetimes

  • Hardened CUDA indexing and buffer-size arithmetic in MatMulNBits, RemovePadding, RotaryEmbedding, SparseAttention, Whisper beam search, NMS, QDQ, and GatherElements (#31643, #31994, #31995, #31996, #31998, #32014, #32029, #32030).
  • Fixed overflow in CUDA reduction scans and Softmax offset arithmetic, and handled zero-sized outputs in CUDA random-generator kernels (#32137, #32330, #31997).
  • Fixed CUDA MultiHeadAttention shared-cache scratch lifetimes and kept CudaAsyncBuffer staging storage alive across CUDA graph replay (#31968, #32121).
  • Fixed WebGPU out-of-bounds subgroup-matrix loads for partial tiles, zero-initialized writable device-allocator buffers, and rejected foreign GPU handles in built-in data transfers (#32364, #32063, #32317).

Dependencies and Tooling

  • Upgraded Protobuf to 33.6 and refreshed Python documentation dependencies, including an ONNX security-related update (#29906, #32190, #32424).
  • Updated JavaScript dependencies including js-yaml, joi, fast-uri, and the Next.js end-to-end fixture (#32397, #32486, #32488, #32505, #32508).
  • Pinned GitHub Actions to full-length commit SHAs and strengthened packaging infrastructure with authenticated package feeds and NPM network isolation (#32176, #32005, #32440).

New Features

Core APIs & Runtime

  • Added Go bindings for the ONNX Runtime C API (#29615).
  • Extended memory importing with host-pointer support and added access to preallocated outputs through KernelContext::GetPreallocatedOutput (#29726, #32089).
  • Added packed-attention workspace recipes and estimates, and made workspace input-shape handling aware of optional inputs (#32283, #32321, #32312).
  • Added DeepSeek Engram contrib operators, EngramGate and NGramHashMapping, and expanded kernel coverage for Qwen-3.5 operators (#32268, #32106).

... (truncated)

title: fix: web citation/code panel bugs and serve analyze/route hardening
body:
## Summary

Fixes a set of verified bugs in the web client and the `gitnexus serve` HTTP/analyze path, plus ignores local Vercel link artifacts. Citation chips in chat did nothing, the code panel highlighted the wrong lines, cancelling an analyze leaked the repo lock, and several routes mishandled in-flight analysis, request bodies, and symlink paths.

## Motivation / context

Found by a local audit (typecheck, ESLint, unit tests, and a read of `gitnexus-web/src` plus `gitnexus/src/{server,mcp,cli,storage}`). Each item below was confirmed in source before the change; impact analysis on the edited symbols was LOW.

## Areas touched

- [x] `gitnexus/` (CLI / core / MCP server)
- [x] `gitnexus-web/` (Vite / React UI)
- [ ] `.github/` (workflows, actions)
- [ ] `eval/` or other tooling
- [ ] Docs / agent config only (`AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `.cursor/`, `llms.txt`, etc.)

## Scope & constraints

**In scope**

- Web: citation chips resolve through the graph-backed path resolver; code-panel highlight/scroll uses 1-based node lines; AI citation cards load a snippet via `/api/file`; `sendChatMessage` tracks the active LLM provider; `initializeAgent` reads the live project name; embeddings 409 dedup matches the server's same-repo message; `impact` path targets prefer the File node; ForceAtlas2 layout timeout calls `kill()` so the worker is not leaked.
- Server: `releaseLockOnce` runs when a cancelled/timed-out analyze exits and when `forkWorker` bails on an already-terminal job; `cancelJob` sends `{ type: 'cancel' }` over IPC and signals only after a 15s grace (on Windows `kill('SIGTERM')` is a forceful termination); a failed hold-queue job returns not-found instead of the `__timedOut` sentinel, and every `resolveRepo` consumer answers 503 for that sentinel; `/api/processes`, `/api/process`, `/api/clusters`, `/api/cluster` resolve `?repo=` through the HTTP resolver and are rate-limited; missing/malformed JSON bodies are 4xx; `/api/file` re-checks containment on `realpath`; `unregisterRepo` uses the strict-if-present registry reader; `clean --branch` compares registry paths canonically.
- `.gitignore`: local `.vercel` link files.

**Explicitly out of scope / not done here**

- Pre-existing ESLint warnings (`no-non-null-assertion`, `no-explicit-any`, unused locals).
- The `switchRepo` graph-mode reset on failure, which is the explicit #2178 trade-off.
- LadybugDB FTS/VECTOR extension load failures on this Windows host (environment, not this diff). Three unit files that fail on Windows and are Ubuntu-only in CI (`analyze-launch-branch-settle`, `analyzer-identity`, `repo-manager-reconcile`) fail the same way without this diff.

## Implementation notes

`detect-changes --scope all` reports critical only because the diff spans 36 symbols and 28 flows. Per-symbol upstream impact before each edit was LOW. Cancellation follows the IPC-first path already used by `core/auto-sync/analysis-worker-launch.ts`.

## Testing & verification

- [x] `cd gitnexus && npx tsc --noEmit`
- [ ] `cd gitnexus && npm test` — not the full suite. Ran the unit files covering server, analyze-job/launch, repo-manager, clean/remove, api-file, rate-limit, and MCP repo policy: 962 passed. The 7 failures are the three Ubuntu-only files above (5 of them in `analyze-launch-branch-settle`, confirmed failing with this diff stashed).
- [ ] `cd gitnexus && npm run test:integration` — Windows cross-platform subset (`scripts/run-cross-platform.ts`) was run before these fixes; its failures were the local FTS/VECTOR extension not loading, plus two tests that pass in isolation.
- [x] `cd gitnexus-web && npm test` — 448 passed
- [x] `cd gitnexus-web && npx tsc -b --noEmit`
- [ ] Manual / Playwright E2E

New tests: `cancelJob` sends IPC before any signal, and falls back to a signal when the channel is closed; `/api/file` returns 403 for a symlink that leaves the repo root and 200 for an in-repo symlink (skipped where the host cannot create symlinks).

## Risk & rollout

No index migration. Serve cancellation behavior changes: workers get up to 15s to exit at a JS-visible safe point before a signal. `/api/file` now rejects symlinks whose real path is outside the repo root.

## Checklist

- [x] PR body meets repo minimum length (workflow may label short descriptions)
- [x] If `AGENTS.md` / overlays changed: headers, scope block, and changelog updated per project conventions
- [x] No secrets, tokens, or machine-specific paths committed

<!-- gitnexus-pr-summary:v1:start -->

---

### 📝 Summary by GitNexus

## Summary

*This is a broad, multi-area change spanning web UI behavior, analysis workflow handling, backend connectivity, and deployment configuration. The risk posture is elevated by its reach across core application layers, despite no detected dependent callers or importers.*

**🔴 CRITICAL blast radius. This appears to combine web citation and code panel updates with serve and analyze route hardening across the `gitnexus-web` application and server-facing areas.**

The change spans 60 files and 19 traced execution flows, crossing `Server`, `Components`, `Hooks`, `Services`, `Cli`, `Storage`, `App-state`, and `Llm`. Review the interaction between `AppContent`, `AnalyzeProgress`, `RepoAnalyzer`, `RightPanel`, and `CodeReferencesPanel` first, particularly the analysis lifecycle, grounding handlers, code reference rendering, and path resolution behavior.

`gitnexus-web/src/services/backend-client.ts` is the hottest file, with 27 changed symbols. The most concentrated review area is the connection between that client, `gitnexus-web/src/hooks/useAppState.tsx`, `gitnexus-web/src/lib/path-resolution.ts`, and the related unit and end to end coverage, including `gitnexus-web/e2e/analyze-public-sse.spec.ts` and `gitnexus-web/e2e/repo-path-identity.spec.ts`.

Also inspect deployment and ignore configuration in `.gitignore`, `.vercelignore`, `gitnexus-web/.gitignore`, and `gitnexus-web/vercel.json`, alongside the application changes. The report was truncated because this is a large PR.

_Added by GitNexus for PR #3348. Edit freely — this block is replaced on the next review, everything above it is left untouched._

title: query: process_symbols dedupe by symbol.id drops attaches for multi-process hubs
feat(storage): shared content-addressed index store for sibling checkouts (worktrees)
body:
## Summary

Sibling checkouts of the same logical repository (git worktrees, multi-agent workspaces, `/tmp` session clones) each get a **full, independent `.gitnexus/` index**, even though they share the vast majority of blobs. The parse layer already dedupes by content hash (CPU saved), but the graph/FTS/LadybugDB artifacts are written out in full per checkout (disk + RAM paid N×). Request: a shared, content-addressed index store for sibling checkouts, with per-checkout overlays resolved via the git commit DAG (merge-base aware).

## Measured duplication (this machine, v1.6.12)

| Checkouts (same `origin`) | Index sizes | Duplication |
|---|---|---|
| `box` + 2 research worktrees | 226M + 200M + 148M = 574M | ~2.5× a single index |
| `dr2-reaper-fix` + `dr2-subsystem-docs` (`/tmp`, tmpfs!) | 440M + 440M = 880M | 2×, byte-identical sizes |
| **Total removed as duplicates** | | **~1.2GB** (`gitnexus clean -f` × 4) |

Side effects observed: `/tmp` (16G tmpfs) sat at 60% partly due to 880M of duplicate indexes; `gitnexus-mcp` peaked at 3.1G RAM (systemd) holding multiple loaded graphs for what is largely identical content.

## Use case

Multi-agent coding flows where each agent works in its own linked worktree of the same repo (e.g. parallel subagent dispatch, one worktree per task). Today each worktree pays a full `analyze` worth of disk and a full loaded graph worth of RAM. With N concurrent agents this is the dominant gitnexus footprint, and it lives on tmpfs/swap-constrained boxes.

## Requirements (proposed)

1. **Shared shard store** scoped by repository identity (existing `remoteUrl` sibling key from #2054, or `git rev-parse --git-common-dir` for linked worktrees, which already share the git object DB).
2. **Per-checkout manifest** = base-commit shard set + delta shards, resolved at `analyze` time via merge-base against the shared store. Checkout `.gitnexus/` keeps only the manifest + deltas.
3. **Promote existing content addressing**: `parse-cache` chunk keys (`sha256(filePath:contentHash…)`) and the durable `parsedfile-cache/` are already content-addressed — lift them into the shared store instead of per-checkout copies.
4. **Safe cleanup**: per-checkout `clean` must refcount/GC shared shards (extend the existing `clean` guards in `repo-manager`, which already refuse to touch anything outside the entry's own `storagePath`).
5. **Interplay**: opt-in flag; retention semantics consistent with #3060 (storage tiers); importable form consistent with #3068 (portable index).
6. **Invalidation**: reuse the sibling-drift detection (#2054) so a diverged checkout resolves/ rebuilds deltas instead of reading stale shared shards.

## Suggested touchpoints (v1.6.12 tree)

- `storage/storage-constants.ts` — `GITNEXUS_DIR` plus new shared-store location (per-remote-url cache dir, or git-common-dir for linked worktrees).
- `storage/repo-manager.ts` — sibling detection (~L1526), `storagePath` resolution, `clean`/`clean --all` refcounting.
- `storage/parse-cache.ts`, `storage/parsedfile-store.ts` — promote chunk/durable keys to shared scope.
- `storage/scope-index-store.ts` + LadybugDB init — per-checkout overlay over shared shards.
- `cli/index-repo.ts`, `core/run-analyze.ts` — merge-base-aware resolve on analyze.
- Related: #2054 (detection, done), #3060 (tiers, closed), #3068 (portable index, open), #2974 (worktree identity, open).

## Potential savings

- **Disk**: (N−1) full copies minus deltas. On the measured box: ~700–770MB back (574M→~250–300M for box×3; 880M→~440M+delta for dr2×2).
- **RAM/swap**: one resident shared graph instead of N loaded LadybugDBs; MCP peak (3.1G here) should flatten for worktree-heavy flows.
- **Time**: sibling re-`analyze` already hits parse cache (CPU saved today); sharing would additionally skip most graph/FTS write I/O.
- Generalizes to any N-worktree flow; tmpfs-backed session dirs (like `/tmp/opencode`) benefit most.

## Notes

Verified against installed dist `gitnexus@1.6.12` source (`repo-manager` comments confirm cleanup is entry-path-driven; `parse-cache` header confirms content-addressed chunk keys and that `--force` "only rebuilds graph/FTS" — i.e. the graph is the unshared layer). Happy to test early builds against the box/dr2 worktree setup above.

title: fix(query): keep process_symbols attaches per (id, process_id)

## Summary

`query` now keeps one `process_symbols` row for each `(symbol.id, process_id)` pair and sets `symbol_count` to the number of those rows. A hub that belongs to more than one process no longer disappears from later process cards.

## Motivation / context

A unique-id filter after flatten dropped later attaches of the same symbol. Process cards still reported `symbol_count ≥ 1` with zero joinable rows. Group search and eval formatting inherit the same payload, so they inherit the same join.

Fixes #3351.

Session-settled decisions carried from planning: widen via the shared assembler (user-directed, over query-only); restore per-process attaches (user-approved, over recount-only unique-id).

## Areas touched

- [x] `gitnexus/` (CLI / core / MCP server)
- [ ] `gitnexus-web/` (Vite / React UI)
- [ ] `.github/` (workflows, actions)
- [ ] `eval/` or other tooling
- [ ] Docs / agent config only (`AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `.cursor/`, `llms.txt`, etc.)

## Scope & constraints

**In scope**

- Pair-key attach assembly and `symbol_count` recount
- Tool description for the join key
- Pins on group service-prefix filter and eval process-card join

**Explicitly out of scope / not done here**

- Ranking, graph schema, and reindex
- Adding `process_symbols` to the group merge envelope
- Stripping hub `include_content` from extra attaches

## Implementation notes

Join key is `(id, process_id)` with a NUL pair-key (`id` already contains `:`). Duplicate pairs first-win. Per-process slice still applies `max_symbols` before emit. Reviewer start: `gitnexus/src/mcp/local/query-process-attaches.ts`.

## Testing & verification

- [ ] `cd gitnexus && npm run test:integration` *(if core/indexing/MCP paths changed)*

Response-shaping only. No index refresh. Callers can receive more `process_symbols` rows. Fat-process cards now report `symbol_count` after the `max_symbols` slice (example: 40 hits / max 25 → 25). - Alert: `symbol_count` greater than remaining `process_symbols` rows for that `process_id`.

title: impact returns an identical result for every target; target name is echoed but unused (1.6.12)
body:
## Summary

`impact` returns an identical result body for every target. The `target.name` field is echoed back; the analysis does not use it.

## Environment

- gitnexus 1.6.12
- TypeScript monorepo, pnpm workspaces
- Index freshly built: 58,279 nodes / 99,065 edges / 387 clusters / 512 flows
- Invoked via MCP: `impact({target: "<name>", direction: "upstream"})`

## Reproduction

Three targets, two different packages:

| Target | Defined in |
|---|---|
| `runSweep` | `packages/ticket-worker/src/sweep/index.ts:74` |
| `runPass1` | `packages/ticket-worker/src/sweep/pass1-sweep.ts` |
| `extractLeadingNumber` | `packages/workspace-core/src/eapis/jira.ts:79` |

```
$ diff impact-runSweep.txt impact-extractLeadingNumber.txt
3c3
<     "name": "runSweep",
---
>     "name": "extractLeadingNumber",

$ diff impact-runSweep.txt impact-runPass1.txt
3c3
<     "name": "runSweep",
---
>     "name": "runPass1",
```

Two differing lines in each case. Byte sizes: 102,905 / 102,905 / 102,887.

## Actual

Every target returns:

```
impactedCount   1037
direct          758
risk            CRITICAL
riskSharedAxes  CRITICAL
epistemic       exact
partial         true
summary         { direct: 758, processes_affected: 18, modules_affected: 16 }
byDepthCounts   { "1": 758, "2": 161, "3": 118 }
```

## Expected

`runSweep` has one definition and two call sites, all inside `packages/ticket-worker`:

```
$ rg -n "runSweep" --glob '!node_modules' --glob '!docs' --glob '!prompts'
packages/ticket-worker/src/sweep/index.ts:74:export async function runSweep(env: Env)
packages/ticket-worker/src/index.ts:7:      import { runSweep } from './sweep'
packages/ticket-worker/src/index.ts:41:     const sweep = env.__sweep ?? runSweep
packages/ticket-worker/src/routes/admin.ts:4:  import { runSweep } from '../sweep'
packages/ticket-worker/src/routes/admin.ts:32: const result = await runSweep(c.env)
```

Expected `impactedCount` ≈ 3, `risk` low. Actual is 1037 / CRITICAL.

## Two further defects visible in the same output

**1. The result names none of the target's own package.**

```
$ grep -c "ticket.worker" impact-runSweep.txt
0
```

Zero occurrences across 102,875 characters.

**2. Generated `.d.ts` files are counted as callers.** Most frequent `filePath` values:

```
68  packages/dev-portal-ui/worker-configuration.d.ts
18  packages/dev-portal-old-ui/worker-configuration.d.ts
14  packages/dev-portal-api/worker-configuration.d.ts
 2  packages/sync-app-api/src/workflows/reservation-edit.ts
 2  packages/sync-app-api/src/durable-objects/location-provisioning.ts
```

100 of the reported hits are ambient type declarations, which contain no call sites.

`affected_processes[0]` is `fetch` in `packages/sync-app-api/src/durable-objects/location-provisioning.ts` — unrelated to all three targets.

## Impact

`risk: CRITICAL` on a symbol with two call sites is a false positive that cannot be distinguished from a true one by the caller. Workflows that gate edits on `impact` risk are blocked, and the documented `UNKNOWN` handling does not apply because the result claims `epistemic: "exact"`.

## Analyzer warnings from the same run

```
[processes] 512 flows reported, but whole flows are MISSING:
  1844 of 2044 candidate entry point(s) never ranked in,
  1779 callee(s) skipped at maxBranching,
  30 walk(s) cut by the per-entry trace budget
[scope-resolution] 274 property read/write site(s) name a field defined in this
  workspace but only in another language; per-language inference declined to link them
```

title: Swift multi-package repository: scopeResolution hits Map maximum size in implicit imports
body:
### Area

gitnexus (CLI / core / indexing)

### Summary

`gitnexus analyze` fails on a large Swift monorepo during `scopeResolution`: `emitSwiftImplicitImportEdges` inserts enough relationships to exceed V8's Map capacity. This appears related to the large-repository failure reported in #772, which is closed as completed; the specific Swift grouping path may be a distinct remaining issue or regression.

### Context

The repository has multiple nested Swift packages under `Core/<package>/Package.swift` and `Features/<package>/Package.swift`, plus Xcode application/extension targets. Generated code, build outputs, dependencies, and Xcode generated project files are excluded using a repo-root `.gitnexusignore`. About 5,200 non-generated Swift files remain; they belong to many separate modules, not one target. The repository is private, so I cannot link it.

### Expected behavior

A single complete repository index, with Swift implicit visibility confined to each actual target. A large but modular repository should not require excluding production source to index.

### Actual behavior

The analysis fails and `gitnexus status` reports `Repository not indexed`. The Swift config loader in 1.6.9 checks only root-level `Sources/`, `Package/Sources/`, and `src/`; it does not discover the nested package manifests. With no discovered targets, `groupSwiftFilesBySpmTarget` puts every Swift file in `__default__`. `emitSwiftImplicitImportEdges` then generates a directed IMPORTS relationship for every pair of files in that bucket (about 27 million candidate edges for 5,200 files). This cause is inferred from the source and failing stack; the number of edges was not logged directly.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Use a Swift monorepo with multiple nested packages (for example, `Core/A/Package.swift`, `Features/B/Package.swift`, each containing `Sources/<Target>/`) and enough total Swift files to exceed ~4,100 files after exclusions. Do not add a root-level `Sources/` directory.
2. Run `gitnexus analyze` from the repository root.
3. Run `gitnexus status` after the failure.

### Environment

- GitNexus: 1.6.9 (installed CLI)
- Node: 24.18.1 (V8 13.6.233.17-node.50)
- OS: macOS Darwin 25.5.0, arm64

### Logs

```text
GitNexus Analyzer

Skipped 1 large files (>512KB, likely generated/vendored)
- tools/graphql/schema/schema.graphqls

Analysis failed: Phase 'scopeResolution' failed: Map maximum size exceeded
Caused by: RangeError: Map maximum size exceeded
    at Map.set (<anonymous>)
    at writeRel (gitnexus/dist/core/graph/graph.js:45:25)
    at Object.addRelationship (gitnexus/dist/core/graph/graph.js:85:9)
    at Object.emitSwiftImplicitImportEdges (gitnexus/dist/core/ingestion/languages/swift/implicit-imports.js:46:23)
    at runScopeResolution (gitnexus/dist/core/ingestion/scope-resolution/pipeline/run.js:328:39)
```

`gitnexus status`: `Repository not indexed. Run: gitnexus analyze`.

The one skipped GraphQL schema file is unrelated to the failing Swift import-edge path.

title: fix(query): send hub content once across process_symbols rows
body:
Stacked on #3353. Retarget to `main` after #3353 merges.

## Problem

#3353 keeps one `process_symbols` row per `(id, process_id)`. With `include_content: true`, a hub in several flows carries its full source text on each of those rows, so the payload grows with memberships times body size.

## Change

- `shapeQueryProcessAttaches` keeps `content` on the first row for each symbol id and omits it on later rows. Membership fields, `is_entry_point`, and `symbol_count` are unchanged.
- The `query` tool text states this rule. `tools.test.ts` pins the sentence.
- The KTD5 unit test now expects content on the first hub row only.

No in-repo reader of `process_symbols` uses `content` (eval formatter, group prefix filter), so no reader changes.

## Not in scope

Splitting into a `symbols` list plus thin membership rows. Worth doing only if payloads are large with `include_content` off.

## Validation

- `tsc --noEmit`, eslint: pass

title: fix(ruby): methods in a Struct.new/Data.define/Class.new/Module.new block are owned by the wrong class
body:
### Area

gitnexus (CLI / core / indexing / MCP server)

### Summary

Ruby's grammar has no dedicated AST node for a class-like value created by a block-taking factory call:
```
class SftpAwsSecretResolver
  SftpCredential = Struct.new(:host, :port, keyword_init: true) do
    def auth_method
      private_key.present? ? :publickey : :password
    end
  end
end
```

`Const = Struct.new(...) do ... end / Data.define / Class.new / Module.new` all parse as `(assignment left: (constant) right: (call ... block: (do_block)))`, structurally identical to any other constant assignment. `findEnclosingClassNode/findEnclosingClassInfo` walk `node.parent` looking for a node type in `CLASS_CONTAINER_TYPES`, and `do_block` isn't one, so the walk continues straight past it to whatever real class/module lexically encloses the constant.

Effect: `auth_method` gets a H`AS_METHOD` edge from `SftpAwsSecretResolver`, not from `SftpCredential`. context/impact on the method report the wrong owner, and callers of `SftpCredential#auth_method` resolve (if at all) against the wrong receiver type.

### Context

Analyze a RoR code base

### Expected behavior

SftpCredential materializes as a real Struct node and auth_method's only HAS_METHOD edge comes from it.
```
{
  "status": "found",
  "symbol": {
    "uid": "Method:app.rb:SftpCredential.auth_method#0",
    "name": "auth_method",
    "kind": "Method",
    "filePath": "app.rb",
    "startLine": 3,
    "endLine": 5
  },
  "incoming": {
    "has_method": [
      {
        "uid": "Struct:app.rb:SftpCredential",
        "name": "SftpCredential",
        "filePath": "app.rb"
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

### Actual behavior

auth_method is owned by SftpAwsSecretResolver, the class that lexically encloses the constant, not the Struct the constant is assigned to. SftpCredential never appears as a Struct/Class/anything node in the graph at all.
```
{
  "status": "found",
  "symbol": {
    "uid": "Method:app.rb:SftpAwsSecretResolver.auth_method#0",
    "name": "auth_method",
    "kind": "Method",
    "filePath": "app.rb",
    "startLine": 3,
    "endLine": 5
  },
  "incoming": {
    "has_method": [
      {
        "uid": "Class:app.rb:SftpAwsSecretResolver",
        "name": "SftpAwsSecretResolver",
        "filePath": "app.rb"
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

### Steps to reproduce

```
class SftpAwsSecretResolver
  SftpCredential = Struct.new(:host, :port, keyword_init: true) do
    def auth_method
      1
    end
  end
end
```

1. gitnexus analyze --index-only
2. gitnexus context "auth_method"

title: chore(deps)(deps): bump react-i18next from 17.0.13 to 17.0.14 in /gitnexus-web
body:
Bumps [react-i18next](https://github.com/i18next/react-i18next) from 17.0.13 to 17.0.14.
Changelog

Sourced from react-i18next's changelog.

17.0.14

  • fix: the i18n object returned by useTranslation was only refreshed when i18n.language changed, so a resolvedLanguage (or languages) change of its own kept handing components the previous snapshot. That happens whenever the translations for the current language arrive after the switch — i18next resolves to the fallback until its store has them — and components reading i18n.resolvedLanguage (language switchers, for example) then stayed one switch behind. The cached wrapper is now keyed on all three language fields, which are exactly the ones the surrounding useMemo already depends on; wrapper identity still only changes when the language state does, so the caching from #1885 is unaffected. Reported via next-i18next#2348.
