title: Support Jupyter Notebook (.ipynb) indexing via Python code extraction
body:
### Area

gitnexus (CLI / core / indexing / MCP server)

### Problem or opportunity

Many data science, ML, AI, and Spark repositories contain significant business logic inside Jupyter notebooks. Currently, GitNexus supports Python analysis, but code stored in .ipynb files is not indexed and therefore cannot participate in graph generation, search, navigation, or dependency analysis. 
This creates blind spots when working with notebook-heavy repositories. 
GitNexus already relies on language-specific parsing and indexing pipelines for supported languages.

### Proposed solution

Add support for .ipynb files by extracting code cells and passing the resulting Python source through the existing Python indexing pipeline.

Rather than implementing notebook-specific parsing logic, GitNexus could leverage existing notebook tooling to convert notebook code cells into Python source and then reuse the current Python analysis workflow.

This approach would:

Reuse existing Python language support
Minimize implementation complexity
Avoid maintaining a separate notebook parser
Immediately improve support for data science and Spark repositories
Examples

Use cases that would benefit:

Spark notebooks
Machine learning experiments
Data engineering pipelines
Exploratory data analysis notebooks

Users should be able to discover functions, classes, imports, and dependencies defined inside notebooks just as they can for standard Python files.

### Alternatives considered

_No response_

### Acceptance criteria

Given a repository containing Jupyter notebooks:
 
- GitNexus indexes code contained in `.ipynb` files.
- Functions defined in notebook code cells can be found through GitNexus queries.
- Imports used in notebook code cells are included in dependency analysis.
- Relationships between notebook-defined functions and other Python code are represented in the graph.
- Analysis completes successfully without requiring notebooks to be executed.

### Constraints

_No response_

- [x] I am willing to open a PR for this (may need design discussion first).

title: auto-sync requires SSH remotes, but the published image has no ssh client
body:
*Four related findings from one containerised deployment of 1.6.12, in
descending order of severity. The first is blocking and the rest were found
behind it; happy to split them into separate issues if you would prefer.*

**Version:** 1.6.12 (`ghcr.io/abhigyanpatwari/gitnexus:1.6.12`, amd64)
**Environment:** Kubernetes, `gitnexus serve` and `gitnexus auto-sync start`
as two containers of one pod, both from the image above.

## Summary

`gitnexus auto-sync` validates that every `remote_urls` entry is an SSH URL,
and the published image contains no `ssh` binary. The two requirements are
mutually exclusive, so auto-sync cannot clone **any** repository in the image
it ships in — public repositories included. `serve` is unaffected, which makes
this easy to miss: the server reports healthy while the writer never works.

## Evidence

auto-sync starts, reaches the clone, and git cannot find an ssh client
(`GIT_SSH_COMMAND` was set to `ssh -F /opt/ssh/config` here; unset, git
invokes plain `ssh` and fails identically):

```
  GitNexus Auto Sync (1.6.12)
[auto-sync] Watch loop started at 2026-09-24T14:25:16.503Z.
[auto-sync] Starting sync loop with max_concurrency=1 analyze_failure_threshold=3.
{"level":50,"name":"gitnexus","msg":"git clone stderr: Cloning into '/data/gitnexus/clones/github.com/<owner>/<repo>'...\nssh -F /opt/ssh/config: 1: ssh: not found\nfatal: Could not read from remote repository.\n\nPlease make sure you have the correct access rights\nand the repository exists."}
[auto-sync] Branch main unavailable for git@github.com:<owner>/<repo>.git: git clone failed (exit code 128)
[auto-sync] Watch loop finished: synced=0 analyzed=0 skipped=0 failed=1.
```

No ssh client of any kind is present, though git is:

```console
$ for b in ssh dropbear ssh-keyscan; do command -v $b || echo "$b: absent"; done
ssh: absent
dropbear: absent
ssh-keyscan: absent
$ git --version
git version 2.39.5
```

Substituting an HTTPS remote is rejected by validation rather than falling
back to the transport git does have:

```console
$ GITNEXUS_HOME=/tmp/gnhttps gitnexus auto-sync
  GitNexus Auto Sync (1.6.12)
[auto-sync] Invalid watch_config.yml: projects[0].remote_urls[0] must use an SSH URL on github.com, gitlab.com, or gitee.com. Auto sync is skipped.
```

(`/tmp/gnhttps/watch_config.yml` was a valid config whose only remote was
`https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>.git`.)

## Cause

The runtime stage of `Dockerfile.cli` installs `curl git procps
ca-certificates` and never installs `openssh-client`, while the auto-sync
config validator accepts SSH URLs only.

## Suggested fix

Add `openssh-client` to the runtime stage of `Dockerfile.cli`. It is about
1 MB and pulls in nothing else in practice: every shared library that Debian
bookworm's `ssh` links against (libcrypto, libgssapi_krb5 and the krb5
family, libselinux, libpcre2, libz, libresolv) is already present in
`node:22-bookworm-slim` — I verified this by listing `ldd` output against the
runtime image.

Alternatively, relax the URL validation to accept HTTPS remotes, which the
bundled git can already fetch.

A check in the spirit of `dockerfile-runtime-asset-parity.test.ts` would
prevent a regression: assert that the runtime image provides every external
binary auto-sync can invoke.

## Workaround for anyone else hitting this

Copy `/usr/bin/ssh` out of any Debian **bookworm** image (I used
`registry.k8s.io/git-sync/git-sync:v4.4.0`) into a shared volume and point
`GIT_SSH_COMMAND` at the copy. No libraries need copying. The copied binary
reports `OpenSSH_9.2p1 Debian-2+deb12u3` and authenticates to GitHub normally
under the gitnexus image.

Images built on Debian **trixie** do not work: their `ssh` requires a newer
glibc than `node:22-bookworm-slim` provides.

## Second defect: a timed-out clone permanently blocks retries

`repo_git_timeout` defaults to 10 seconds. That is not enough to clone a
2,464-file repository onto network storage (NFS, in my case: 8m42s, against 4
seconds for the same clone onto local disk), which is a reasonable default to
disagree with — but the failure is not merely a slow retry.

A clone that times out leaves a directory containing only `.git`. On the next
tick auto-sync refuses to pull it:

```
Existing clone at /data/.../owner/repo has no remote.origin — refusing to pull
```

and it will not clone over it either, so **every subsequent tick fails
identically until the directory is deleted by hand**. The refusal is right;
the missing part is recovery. Since `serve` stays healthy, the visible state
is a running service whose index never appears.

Suggested fix: when the existing path is not a valid repository — or has no
`remote.origin` — treat it as a failed clone and re-clone, rather than
refusing forever. A one-line hint in the error naming the directory to remove
would also help.

## Third defect: auto-sync cannot generate embeddings, and `.gitnexusrc` does not reach it

`.gitnexusrc` is documented as project-local configuration for
`gitnexus analyze`, and `embeddings` is one of its keys. It has no effect on
an auto-sync index: `dist/server/analyze-worker.js` and
`analyze-worker-core.js` contain no reference to `gitnexusrc` or to
embeddings, and while `run-analyze.js` can embed, it does so only from
`options.embeddings*` supplied by its caller.

Measured: a repository with a committed `.gitnexusrc` containing
`{"embeddings": true}`, analysed by auto-sync (2,356 files, 37,523 symbols),
produced **0** rows in `CodeEmbedding`. `gitnexus embeddings sync` on the same
index does work.

`watch_config.yml` has no key for analyze flags either, so for an auto-synced
repository there is currently no way to enable embeddings at all. Since
`query` falls back to keyword search without reporting it, the result looks
like working semantic search.

Suggested fix: either honour `.gitnexusrc` in the auto-sync analyze path, or
add an `embeddings` key to `watch_config.yml` (per project, or global). A
warning from `query` when the index it is searching holds no vectors would
turn a silent degradation into a visible one.

## Secondary observation

`analyze_timeout` must be at most half of `sync_interval_minutes`, which is
not documented alongside the `sync_interval_minutes` floor of 5. When it is
violated auto-sync exits immediately:

```
[auto-sync] Invalid watch_config.yml: analyze_timeout must not exceed half of sync_interval_minutes (7.5m). Auto sync is skipped.
```

In a two-container deployment that reads as a crash-looping pod whose server
half is healthy, with this single line as the only clue. Worth a mention in
the `watch_config.yml` reference.

title: fix(impact): fail closed on id-less targets and follow ??/||/?: callable values (#3354)
body:
## Summary

`impact` no longer reports a blast radius for a target that resolved without a node id. Callable-value flow now follows each branch of `??`, `||`, `or`, and `?:`, so `const sweep = env.__sweep ?? runSweep; await sweep(env)` counts as a call to `runSweep`.

## Motivation / context

Refs #3354. The reporter got a byte-identical `impact` result (1037 impacted, CRITICAL, `epistemic: exact`) for three unrelated targets. Only `target.name` differed.

That exact failure did not reproduce. A synthetic copy of their monorepo resolves every target correctly on main. It uses a pnpm workspace, real Wrangler `worker-configuration.d.ts` in five packages, Hono routes, a Durable Object `fetch`, a Workflow, and cross-package imports, and we called `impact` over MCP stdio. Their output still shows one hard fact: the `target` they received had no `id` and no `filePath`, and the traversal path always emits both. This PR makes that state fail closed.

The repro also surfaced a real under-report. The `?? runSweep` injection seam was not seen as a caller, and the answer still claimed `exact`.

## Areas touched

- [x] `gitnexus/` (CLI / core / MCP server)
- [ ] `gitnexus-web/` (Vite / React UI)
- [ ] `.github/` (workflows, actions)
- [ ] `eval/` or other tooling
- [ ] Docs / agent config only

## Scope & constraints

**In scope**

- `_runImpactBFS` throws when the resolved target has no node id. Its three callers already catch, so `impact` returns `impactedCount: null, risk: UNKNOWN` instead of a normal-looking result.
- `synthesizeCallableFlowCaptures` expands a value-selecting source (`a ?? f`, `a || f`, `a or f`, `c ? f : g`, including parenthesized ones) into one flow per branch. The shared rule keys only on operator and field names; grammars with other shapes use the provider hook below.
- `resolveSymbolCandidates` treats a whitespace-only `uid` as omitted. Some strict adapters send `" "` for an omitted optional string. It now falls back to the name instead of returning `not_found`.
- A non-string `uid` / `target_uid` counts as omitted instead of throwing a `TypeError` past `context()`'s catch. The MCP envelope is not type-validated. The `impact` and `trace` not-found messages print a trimmed uid only when it is a non-blank string.
- Grammars that spell value selection without the shared field names get an optional `valueAlternatives` provider hook: Kotlin elvis and `if`, Swift `??` and ternary, Dart `??` and conditional, and Python `a if c else b`. Ruby's hook keeps a multi-statement `if`/`unless`/`elsif` as one opaque source. Without it, the shared ternary rule picked an identifier out of an arbitrary statement and produced a wrong CALLS edge.
- Parse cache `SCHEMA_BUMP` 104 -> 112. Warm caches would otherwise replay the old flow facts. 105 to 111 are claimed by open PR #3326.

**Explicitly out of scope / not done here**

- The root cause of the reporter's id-less target. We cannot reproduce it, and we asked for the raw response and their client or proxy chain on the issue.
- `.d.ts` rows showing up as callers in their output. We will revisit once we know whether that output was anchored to a real symbol at all.

## Testing & verification

- `npx vitest run test/integration/resolvers/typescript-callable-alternatives.test.ts`: 5/5. Before the fix, 3 of 4 original cases failed. The plain alias control passed both before and after.
- `npx vitest run test/unit/calltool-dispatch.test.ts`: 277/277. Both new #3354 tests were mutation checked: reverting each fix makes its test fail.
- `npx vitest run test/unit/incremental-parse-cache.test.ts`: 40/40.
- All 26 test files touching callable-value flow across languages: 830 passed, 2 skipped.
- `npx vitest run test/integration/resolvers`: 3782 passed. 9 failed, all timeouts with no assertion failures, on a host at load average 17 to 29. The three affected files (`cpp`, `rust-cargo-review-regressions`, `rust-import-scope`) all pass when run on their own.
- Review follow-ups: `calltool-dispatch.test.ts` passes 285/285, including non-string `uid` and `target_uid`, and blank `from_uid`/`to_uid` in `trace`. The new `callable-alternatives-providers.test.ts` covers Python, Kotlin, Swift, Dart and Ruby, including a Ruby negative. The TS test adds chained, parenthesized, callable-left and `&&` negative cases. Callable-flow files: 845 passed, 2 skipped. Kotlin, Swift, Dart, Python and Ruby resolver files: 900 passed. Every hook and guard was mutation checked.
- `npx tsc --noEmit` clean. eslint shows no new errors. prettier is clean.
- End to end on the #3354 repro fixture: `impact runSweep` now lists `scheduled` as a direct caller next to `admin.ts`.

## Risk & rollout

- The callable-flow change adds CALLS edges for these shapes in every language that feeds the shared helper. It only adds flows, and only from branches of value-selecting operators.
- Users need `npx gitnexus analyze` to pick up the new edges. The cache bump forces a reparse.

title: feat(storage): share one index store across linked worktrees and sibling clones
body:
## Summary

Linked git worktrees of one repository, and independent clones with the same `origin` URL, now share a single index store instead of each keeping a full `.gitnexus/`. Checkouts at the same commit with no local edits read one shared graph: one copy on disk and one open database in MCP.

## Motivation / context

Multi-agent workflows create one worktree per task. Each worktree paid for a complete index, so disk and MCP memory grew with the worktree count. Reproduced on `main`: a worktree and its main checkout held separate graphs plus byte-identical `parse-cache/` and `parsedfile-cache/` trees. The issue reports 880M for two byte-identical session checkouts and a 3.1G MCP peak.

Related: #3352

## Areas touched

- [x] `gitnexus/` (CLI / core / MCP server)
- [ ] `gitnexus-web/` (Vite / React UI)
- [ ] `.github/` (workflows, actions)
- [ ] `eval/` or other tooling
- [x] Docs / agent config only (`AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `.cursor/`, `llms.txt`, etc.)

The Claude hook `registry-query.cjs` also changed in `gitnexus-claude-plugin/` and `gitnexus-cursor-integration/`; all three copies stay byte-identical (a new test checks this).

## Scope & constraints

**In scope**

- Store at `~/.gitnexus/stores/<repo>/`: shared parse caches, one immutable graph per commit and analysis settings, one slot per checkout.
- A checkout with uncommitted edits gets a private graph, cloned from the nearest shared graph and updated incrementally. On APFS, btrfs and XFS the clone is copy-on-write, so on disk it costs only the pages the edits rewrite; elsewhere it is a full copy. `status` reports which one a checkout got.
- Reference-counted cleanup: `clean` in one worktree keeps graphs others use; analyze deletes graphs no checkout uses right after it publishes; `clean --gc` drops slots whose checkout left the registry.
- Independent clones share automatically: a clone whose normalized `origin` URL matches another registered clone joins that clone's store, or starts one the other joins on its next analyze. A lone clone keeps its own `.gitnexus/`. `--share-with <name-or-path>` names a store explicitly (the `origin` URL must match); `--no-share` leaves and records an opt-out that holds until `--share-with`. `GITNEXUS_SHARED_STORE=off`, `GITNEXUS_STORAGE_PATH` or `GITNEXUS_STORAGE_ROOT` turn sharing off.
- Existing worktree indexes are adopted without deletion. `status` and `doctor` report the leftover; `clean --local-index --force` removes it.
- `<repo>/.gitnexus/store.json` points each checkout at its slot. MCP, the HTTP API, group sync, augmentation and the Claude hook all read the graph the slot points at.

**Explicitly out of scope / not done here**

- Combining a shared base graph and a per-checkout overlay at query time (requirement 2 in the issue). LadybugDB reads one database per query (`ATTACH` switches the active database, it does not union them), and merging results in GitNexus would give wrong answers for callers, impact and flows that cross from edited to unchanged files. The copy-on-write clone above is the storage-level form of the overlay: it gives the disk saving, not a smaller in-memory graph.
- Portable index import (#3068) and storage tiers (#3060).

## Implementation notes

- **Graphs are keyed by commit plus a feature key.** The key hashes every graph shaping metadata field (schema fingerprint, analysis features, PDG, retention, runner identity, embeddings present). Two checkouts share only when all match, so a PDG build never answers for a non PDG checkout.
- **Commit graphs are immutable.** Analyze always writes the slot's own graph; a clean checkout at HEAD then moves it into `commits/` under a store lock. The existing read only MCP open needs no change, and the pool's path keyed database cache gives one open database per commit graph.
- **Only graphs built from a clean tree are shared.** A graph whose build saw dirty files stays private even after the edits are reverted, because the up to date path does not diff a clean tree again.
- **Pointer writes and reclaim share one lock**, so a graph is never deleted between being published and being recorded.
- **Worktrees and sibling clones share by default.** Worktrees share the git object database. Clones are matched by normalized `origin` URL among registered checkouts that still exist, and only a registered sibling triggers sharing. Because graphs are keyed by commit SHA and feature key, two clones only ever share a graph built from the same commit with the same settings, so a mistaken match costs nothing but a store. The opt-out is a `shareOptOut` flag on the registry entry, preserved across re-registration.
- **The server settles the slot the worker wrote.** The analyze worker now reports its `storagePath` over IPC, so a clone's first analyze into a new store is settled in the right place.
- The runner `run.cjs` and the `AGENTS.md` command stay inside the checkout, so committed docs carry no home directory paths.

Session-settled decisions carried from planning: commit keyed graphs in a per repository store (user-directed, over worktree slots in the main checkout's `.gitnexus` and over a dedupe pass). Clone sharing was first opt-in and is now automatic by origin URL with a lasting `--no-share` opt-out (user-directed after review). Query-time overlays stay out because of the engine limit above; copy-on-write clones plus `status` reporting were chosen instead (user-directed).

## Testing & verification

- [x] `cd gitnexus && npx tsc --noEmit`
- [x] Targeted suites pass, including new `shared-store-{analyze,seed,cache,clean,clone-optin,adoption}`, `hooks-shared-store` and the storage unit tests. They run against real temp repos with `git worktree add` and `git clone`, and cover the issue's acceptance cases: shared graph and one MCP database for three worktrees, incremental private graph for an edited worktree, publish after commit, refused foreign clone, clean keeps graphs in use, concurrent publish yields one graph, a clone joining its sibling's store, two standalone clones founding a store, a lone clone kept local, and a sticky `--no-share`.
- [x] The regression test for publishing a graph built from reverted edits fails without its fix.
- [ ] `cd gitnexus && npm test`: run locally, but not clean in this environment. Analyze segfaults while building FTS indexes and parse workers time out at startup under load, so local runs used `GITNEXUS_SKIP_FTS=1` and `GITNEXUS_WORKER_READY_TIMEOUT_MS=90000`. The failing unit files fail on the base commit too (80 failures there, 67 here). The two failures only seen on this branch (`analyze-heap-respawn`) pass when run alone on both sides. CI is the first run with FTS enabled.

Code review: a high effort review pass found 10 issues, all fixed. Among them: publishing a graph built from edits, a reclaim race, unbounded growth of superseded graphs, `clean --gc` dropping opted-in clones, and machine specific paths in `AGENTS.md`.

## Risk & rollout

- On by default for any repository with a linked worktree, and for any clone with a registered sibling clone of the same `origin`. The next `analyze` in such a checkout moves its index into the store; the old `.gitnexus/` contents stay until `clean --local-index --force`.
- Rollback: `GITNEXUS_SHARED_STORE=off`. The next analyze indexes into `<repo>/.gitnexus` again and re-registers there.
- Disk under `~/.gitnexus/stores/` should settle near one graph per distinct commit in use plus one private graph per edited worktree.
- Known residual: after the up to date path, the store registers a checkout whose slot was seeded from a finished commit graph. This skips the rule that an up to date but unregistered index must not register itself (#1169). It is deliberate, since a seeded checkout would otherwise never register.
- On Windows, a commit graph open in MCP cannot be deleted. Reclaim keeps it and a later `clean` or `clean --gc` removes it.

## Checklist

- [x] PR body meets repo minimum length (workflow may label short descriptions)
- [x] If `AGENTS.md` / overlays changed: headers, scope block, and changelog updated per project conventions
- [x] No secrets, tokens, or machine-specific paths committed

## Summary

*This appears to be a broad storage architecture change spanning shared index ownership, CLI workflows, server analysis paths, and integration hooks. The change is critical in scope despite having no graph-resolved dependents, so review should focus on consistency across the storage entry points.*

**🔴 CRITICAL blast radius. A storage and repository-management change centered on shared index stores, reaching CLI, server, local backend, hook, and analysis execution paths.**

The change spans 150 symbols across 47 files, with the densest concentration in `gitnexus/src/storage/repo-manager.ts`. Review `gitnexus/src/storage/repo-manager.ts` first alongside `gitnexus/src/storage/index-lock.ts`, `gitnexus/src/storage/git.ts`, and `gitnexus/src/core/shared-store-analyze.ts`, especially where repository ownership and index storage are selected or coordinated.

The affected areas are `Storage`, `Hooks`, `Server`, `Cli`, `Local`, `Claude`, `Integration`, `Tree-sitter`, `Incremental`, `I18n`, `Group`, `Augmentation`, and `Lbug`. title: feat(mcp): add read_file + grep tools (REST parity for /api/file slice + /api/grep)
body:
## What

Adds two read-only MCP tools closing the REST-MCP parity gap:

- **read_file** — repo-contained source read with optional 0-indexed `startLine`/`endLine` slice (mirrors `GET /api/file`, incl. its slice params and path-traversal containment). Whole-file reads are capped by `maxLines` (default 2000, 0 = no cap) with a `truncated` flag.
- **grep** — regex scan across indexed contents (mirrors `GET /api/grep`: `parseGrepQuery` + lbug File list + worker scan under `GREP_TIME_BUDGET_MS`, `timedOut` surfaced).

Both are registered in `REPO_SCOPED_TOOLS` + `MCP_READ_ONLY_TOOLS`, with next-step hints wired in `server.ts`.

## Why

Agents working purely over MCP previously had no way to read file contents or run a literal fallback search without dropping to bash/REST: `context(include_content)` covers symbol spans only, and graph-first workflows need a bounded textual fallback for empty/ambiguous results. These two tools make a grep-free, REST-free agent loop possible.

## Validation

- `npx tsc --noEmit` clean; `test/unit/tools.test.ts` count 17→19 + names updated.
- Live stdio smoke test against a real index: `read_file` slice returns exact lines + staleness; `grep` returns file:line hits in 0.6s; `../../etc/passwd` refused.

title: fix(auto-sync): HTTPS remotes, OpenSSH image, and rc embeddings
body:
## Summary

The published CLI auto-sync image can clone GitHub over HTTPS or SSH, recover a stuck failed checkout, and apply embeddings from the cloned repo's `.gitnexusrc`. Keyword-only `query` now says when the index has no vectors.

## Motivation / context

Auto-sync previously assumed SSH-only remotes and an image without `openssh-client`. Failed clones stayed in place so later ticks never retried. Embeddings were never read from `.gitnexusrc`, so MCP search stayed BM25-only without saying so.

Fixes #3372

Plan: `docs/plans/2026-09-25-1420-fix-auto-sync-ssh-image-plan.md`

## Areas touched

- [x] `gitnexus/` (CLI / core / MCP server)
- [ ] `gitnexus-web/` (Vite / React UI)
- [ ] `.github/` (workflows, actions)
- [ ] `eval/` or other tooling
- [x] Docs / agent config only (`AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `.cursor/`, `llms.txt`, etc.)

## Scope & constraints

**In scope**

- OpenSSH client in `Dockerfile.cli` runtime
- Allowlisted HTTPS remotes with the same host and path rules as SSH
- Quarantine-and-reclone when auto-sync sees a checkout with no `remote.origin`
- Read embeddings from `.gitnexusrc` in core (no CLI import)
- Surface a no-vector warning on `query`, including a missing `CodeEmbedding` table

**Explicitly out of scope / not done here**

- Expanding the three-host allowlist
- Debian trixie / extra SSH packages
- A `watch_config.yml` embeddings key
- A half-interval `analyze_timeout` cap (not present on this tree)

## Implementation notes

HTTPS URLs reject userinfo and explicit ports. Path rules stay shared with SSH.

`.gitnexusrc` is still a direct file read in auto-sync (not `readRepoControlFile`). Follow-up: bound that read the same way CLI analyze does.

Quarantine still treats any non-timeout `git config` failure as a missing origin. Follow-up: quarantine only on a true missing key.

## Testing & verification

- [x] `cd gitnexus && ./node_modules/.bin/vitest run` on auto-sync, git-clone, dockerfile, embeddings, and semantic-warn units (304 + later 5 tests)

No UI surface in this diff; browser E2E not applicable.

## Risk & rollout

Rebuild/republish the CLI image so OpenSSH is present. Existing auto-sync YAML with HTTPS remotes starts cloning after upgrade. Indexes without embeddings get a `query` warning instead of silent BM25.

title: auto-sync: bound .gitnexusrc read like CLI analyze
body:
Follow-up from review of https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/pull/3378 (issue #3372).

`embeddingsFromGitnexusRc` uses `readFileSync` on a cloned remote's `.gitnexusrc`. CLI analyze uses `readRepoControlFile` (regular file, no symlink, 1MB cap). Auto-sync should share that reader so a malicious clone cannot follow a symlink or a huge blob.

Related: https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/pull/3378

title: auto-sync: quarantine only when remote.origin is actually missing
body:
Follow-up from review of https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/pull/3378 (issue #3372).

`cloneOrPull` quarantines whenever `getRemoteOriginUrl` returns null. That helper maps every non-timeout git error to null, so a locked or corrupt `git config` can relocate a live checkout. Quarantine only on missing `remote.origin` (empty / exit 1), not spawn or lock failures.

Related: https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/pull/3378

title: feat: index Jupyter notebooks as Python
body:
## Summary

GitNexus now indexes `.ipynb` notebooks by extracting Python code cells in-process and parsing them with the existing Python provider. Notebook functions, classes, and imports join the graph without executing a kernel.

## Motivation / context

Fixes #3371.

A GitHub search of open and closed issues/PRs for jupyter / ipynb / notebook found no other on-topic tickets or PRs. #2337 matches on an unrelated string and is not linked.

## Areas touched

- [x] `gitnexus/` (CLI / core / MCP server)
- [ ] `gitnexus-web/` (Vite / React UI)
- [ ] `.github/` (workflows, actions)
- [ ] `eval/` or other tooling
- [x] Docs / agent config only (`AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `.cursor/`, `llms.txt`, etc.)

## Scope & constraints

**In scope**

- Map `.ipynb` to the Python language provider.
- Extract nbformat v4 code cells, remap graph lines to on-disk JSON, and reconstruct Python snippets for FTS.
- Skip non-Python-family kernels; skip `%%` cells; comment `%` / `!` magics in place.
- Bump parse-cache schema so old cached parses cannot mix JSON coordinates with extracted Python.

**Explicitly out of scope / not done here**

- Kernel execution, nbconvert, a new Jupyter language, markdown/raw cells as symbols, R/Julia notebooks.
- Concat-parse of notebooks whose cells are not valid together as one Python buffer.

## Implementation notes

Extraction follows the Vue SFC pattern: the parse worker feeds tree-sitter a Python buffer, then `mapExtractLine` writes 0-based JSON file coordinates. `preprocessSource` stays length-preserving, so cells are not concatenated there.

Session-settled decisions carried from planning: implement in a new git worktree (user-directed); search and link duplicate jupyter/ipynb/notebook tickets on the PR (user-directed).

## Testing & verification

- [x] `cd gitnexus && npx vitest run test/unit/ipynb-extractor.test.ts` (14 passed)
- [x] `cd gitnexus && npx tsc --noEmit`
- [ ] `cd gitnexus && npm test` (full suite not run in this environment)
- [ ] `cd gitnexus && npm run test:integration` — `ipynb-python-pipeline.test.ts` timed out waiting for the parse worker in this environment (worker ready 5s). Treat CI as the source of truth.
- [ ] `cd gitnexus-web && npm test` *(web unchanged)*
- [ ] Manual / Playwright E2E *(indexer-only; no web routes)*

## Risk & rollout

Parse-cache `SCHEMA_BUMP` is 105. Existing indexes need `npx gitnexus analyze` (or equivalent) before notebook coordinates and FTS snippets are correct.

## Checklist

- [x] PR body meets repo minimum length (workflow may label short descriptions)
- [ ] If `AGENTS.md` / overlays changed: headers, scope block, and changelog updated per project conventions
- [x] No secrets, tokens, or machine-specific paths committed

## New concepts

**Notebook code-cell extraction (Vue-style pre-parse)**

Pull Python out of nbformat JSON, parse that buffer, then map each extract line back onto the on-disk JSON. That keeps one Python grammar and keeps graph spans pointing at the file users open.

The obvious alternative is a Jupyter language or running nbconvert. Those add a runtime or a second grammar and still need a line map.

This PR locates each `"cell_type": "code"` `"source"` span in the raw JSON, concatenates decoded cell text for tree-sitter, and stores JSON line ranges on each segment.

Do not use this for files whose on-disk bytes already *are* the language (plain `.py`). Affine per-cell maps also fail if you rewrite magics in a way that changes line counts.

title: feat(analyze): --memory-budget with graceful degradation + collapsed rebuild-gate log + persisted needsFullRebuild (#3137)
body:
## Summary

Implements the three asks from #3137, plus the heap-budget knob that makes the first one actionable:

1. **`--memory-budget <mb>`** — explicit main-thread heap ceiling for the parse phase. Overrides the RAM/cgroup auto-sizer; feeds the existing #2649 heap probes (preflight projection + mid-loop abort at 0.92) and **degrades the worker pool before the run starts** when the projected need exceeds the budget (proportional shrink, floor 1, never overrides an explicit `--workers` upward).
2. **Collapsed multi-gate log** — the nine meta-mismatch rebuild gates (pdg mode, content retention, schema fingerprint, graph-write collapse, analysis features, Spring vendor prefixes, runner identity, FTS CJK mode, embedding dims) used to log individually and set `force: true` nine times over on an upgrade. They now collect into `rebuildReasons[]` and print **one numbered summary block**, setting `force` exactly once. Single-reason runs keep the old inline phrasing.
3. **Persisted `needsFullRebuild` verdict** — when any gate fires, the reasons are written to meta **before** the rebuild starts. If that run is itself interrupted, the next run announces the recorded verdict up front instead of quietly attempting an incremental write on top of an index it has reason to distrust. (This is the ops-facing complement to the `incrementalInProgress` dirty flag — see #3101 for a real-world corruption incident where a persisted verdict would have surfaced immediately.)

## Why these belong together

All three were hit in the same incident: upgrading GitNexus on a 3 GB memory-constrained host tripped schema + runner-identity + CJK gates simultaneously (wall of warnings, rebuilt overnight), the rebuild itself OOM'd under the default pool size, and a later crash left the index half-rebuilt with nothing in meta saying so. `--memory-budget` on a 25k-file Java monorepo with a 12 GB budget pins the heap and lets the pool shrink up front; the collapsed log makes the upgrade story readable at a glance; the persisted verdict makes an interrupted rebuild self-announcing.

## Validation

- `npx tsc --noEmit` — clean
- New tests: `analyze-memory-budget.test.ts` (11), `analyze-needs-full-rebuild.test.ts` (4)
- Full `test/unit` suite re-run on a quiet tree (an earlier red run was traced to concurrent source edits invalidating the analyzer-identity link guard while vitest was mid-flight — a guard working as designed, not a regression)
- Behavior is byte-identical when `--memory-budget` is omitted: the heap limit resolution falls back to `v8.getHeapStatistics().heap_size_limit` and no pool degradation runs

## Checklist

- [x] No new dependencies
- [x] Env-var channels untouched (flag threads through options, not `process.env`)
- [x] Auto-sizer path unchanged when the flag is omitted
- [x] Collapsed log preserves per-gate Tip text verbatim inside the summary entries

Refs #3137

title: fix(analyze): make --memory-budget set the real heap and report rebuild reasons once
body:
## Summary

`gitnexus analyze --memory-budget <mb>` now sets the real main-thread V8 heap, so the existing #2649 memory guards actually enforce it. Every forced full rebuild now reports its reasons once, up front, and an interrupted rebuild names its cause on the next run.

This builds on and completes #3385 (ChunxueLi's `feat-memory-budget`, refs #3137). It keeps that PR's three features and fixes the problems found in review: the budget never reached the mid-loop heap abort, the worker-pool shrink could not lower main-thread heap, the persisted rebuild verdict was written to the wrong slot and erased before the wipe, and CI was red.

## Motivation / context

The #3137 host (3 GB RAM, `--max-old-space-size=8192`) had no single knob that bounds analyze's heap while keeping the guards on. The auto-sizer raises a lower `NODE_OPTIONS` pin, and `GITNEXUS_MEMORY=off` also turns the guards off. Upgrades that tripped several rebuild gates printed a wall of warnings, and a crashed rebuild left nothing behind to explain it.

Related: #3137
Related: #3385

## Areas touched

- [x] `gitnexus/` (CLI / core / MCP server)
- [ ] `gitnexus-web/` (Vite / React UI)
- [ ] `.github/` (workflows, actions)
- [ ] `eval/` or other tooling
- [x] Docs / agent config only (`README.md`, `gitnexus/README.md`)

## Scope & constraints

**In scope**

- `--memory-budget` sets V8's heap limit through the existing `ensureHeap` respawn. The size is exact, young generation included, and it wins over any `--max-old-space-size` pin and over `GITNEXUS_MEMORY=off`. The parse phase has no budget code.
- One `RebuildReasonCollector` covers every path that forces a full rebuild. That is the nine meta gates plus `--force`, `--skills`, `--no-parse-cache`, `--drop-embeddings`, `--repair-fts` retention, Spring Actuator, AsyncAPI, shared-store graph gaps, dirty-flag recovery, and the post-pipeline capability check. One summary prints before the pipeline, and at most one follow-up line prints after it.
- Reasons ride on the existing `incrementalInProgress` crash marker, written to the active slot's `metaDir` by every marker writer. The separate `needsFullRebuild` field is removed.
- One shared integer flag parser (`src/cli/int-option.ts`) replaces the duplicated checks in analyze, watch, and wiki.

**Explicitly out of scope / not done here**

- The budget never changes the worker count, and the PR's pool-shrink block is deleted. A budget-driven worker shrink and recovery from the "replacement worker did not report ready" cascade are left for follow-up issues.
- The MCP / auto-sync worker launch sizes its heap on its own path and does not read `--memory-budget`.

Session-settled decisions carried from planning: budget sets the V8 heap via the respawn (user-approved, over a parse-only guard or dropping the flag); budget is the exact size in both directions (user-directed, over ceiling-only); no worker-count change (user-approved, over a budget-driven shrink); reasons on the existing crash marker (user-approved, over a separate field); one collector checked before and after the pipeline (user-approved, over only the nine gates or a post-pipeline-only summary); one merged recovery entry (user-approved, over a separate preamble); budget applies under `GITNEXUS_MEMORY=off` (user-approved).

## Implementation notes

- **Exact heap size.** V8's `heap_size_limit` is old space plus three semi-spaces, and V8 rounds the semi-space up to a power of two. The respawn picks a semi-space of up to 128 MB and gives old space the rest. Measured on Node 22.18: budget 2000 gives old 1616 plus semi 128, which is exactly 2000. A pin that only equals the budget (2000 on its own gives 2048) still respawns once.
- **No respawn loop.** A child launched by the budget respawn is marked with `GITNEXUS_HEAP_LIMIT_SOURCE=budget` and resolves as already at the budget. The same marker makes the out-of-memory advice point at `--memory-budget` instead of a pin.
- **Stable reason keys.** Reasons are keyed (`schema-fingerprint`, `runner-identity`, and so on), so a reason whose text changed across an upgrade still merges into the interrupted-rebuild entry instead of printing twice.
- **Non-forcing escalation.** The #2409 escalation is recorded as non-forcing. It keeps `escalatedFullWrite` and never sets `options.force`, and its follow-up line reads "Write plan changed", not "Full rebuild also required".
- **Tests.** `runFullAnalysis` returns `rebuildReasons`. This replaces the runner-identity source-regex test with a behavior test and backs a type-checked coverage table that maps every reason key to the test that drives it.
- **Storage requirements.** `--skills` and `--no-parse-cache` no longer fold into `force`, but they still use the forced storage requirements they had before.

## Testing & verification

- [x] `cd gitnexus && npx tsc --noEmit`: clean.
- [x] Targeted unit files: `cli-int-option`, `wiki-flags`, `analyze-heap-respawn`, `analyze-memory-budget`, `parse-impl-heap-guard`, `rebuild-reasons`, `stream-graph-emit-force-ordering`, `run-analyze-fts-crash-marker`, `run-analyze`, `pdg-mode-flip`, `call-summary-schema-version`, `cli-index-help`, `cli-i18n`, `incremental-orchestration`. All pass when each file runs on its own.
- [x] `cd gitnexus && npm run test:unit`: 16637 passed, 8 failed. All 8 are local environment issues, not this change. `analyze-heap-respawn` and `skip-git-cli` are known load flakes, and `analyze-heap-respawn` passes 39/39 on its own. `wiki-llm-client` fails because of a local `~/.gitnexus/config.json` provider setting.
- [x] Real-process check: a child started with the budget's flags reports a live `heap_size_limit` of exactly 256 MB (and 2000 MB with a user pin in front).
- [ ] `npm run test:integration`: not run locally. FTS segfaults on this dev box, which predates this change, so analyze-level tests here ran with `GITNEXUS_SKIP_FTS=1`. CI is the authority.
- [x] Prettier on all changed files and ESLint (0 errors); pre-commit hooks passed on every commit.

## Risk & rollout

- **CLI contract.** `--memory-budget` is new. The shared integer parser now rejects spellings `Number()` used to accept for existing flags (`1e3`, `0x10`, `01`, `5.0`). Messages are unchanged.
- **Meta on disk.** `incrementalInProgress.reasons` is optional and validated on read. Unknown keys from other versions keep their text, and malformed values read as "no reasons recorded". `needsFullRebuild` existed only on the #3385 branch.
- **Logs.** Rebuild output changes from per-gate lines to one summary. Tests now assert collected reason keys instead of log wording.

## Checklist

- [x] PR body meets repo minimum length (workflow may label short descriptions)
- [ ] If `AGENTS.md` / overlays changed: headers, scope block, and changelog updated per project conventions (not changed)
- [x] No secrets, tokens, or machine-specific paths committed

title: fix(swift): model Swift modules like the compiler (nested packages, Xcode targets, linear visibility)
body:
## Summary

`gitnexus analyze` now indexes Swift monorepos made of nested SwiftPM packages. Previously it crashed in `scopeResolution` with `RangeError: Map maximum size exceeded` and left the repo unindexed. Swift modules are now modeled the way the compiler sees them. Each SwiftPM target and each Xcode target is its own module, and same-module visibility costs O(files) instead of O(files²). No module layout can exhaust the graph or the heap.

Fixes #3355

## Motivation / context

The Swift loader read only the root `Package.swift`, so a repo of nested packages collapsed into one `__default__` module. Two same-module passes then did work for every pair of files:
- implicit IMPORTS wrote n·(n−1) File→File edges, about 27M for the reporter's 5,200 files, above V8's 2^24 Map limit;
- the sibling passes copied every file's declarations into every other file, about 3.8 GB of heap at 1,000 files.

## What's touched

- [x] `gitnexus/` (CLI / core / MCP server)
- [ ] `gitnexus-web/` (Vite / React UI)
- [ ] `.github/` (workflows, actions)
- [ ] `eval/` or other tooling
- [ ] Docs / agent config only (`AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `.cursor/`, `llms.txt`, etc.)

## Scope & constraints

**In scope**

- **Module discovery** (`languages/swift/workspace-config.ts`, `xcode-project.ts`):
  - root and nested SwiftPM manifests;
  - SwiftPM's default target folders (`Sources`, `Source`, `src`, `srcs`, `Tests`, `Plugins`);
  - the newest `Package@swift-X.Y.swift` when present;
  - Xcode native targets from `project.pbxproj`, including Xcode 16 synchronized folders. A folder exception removes a file from a target that lists the folder and adds it to one that does not.
- **Module names** follow the compiler's mangling (`my-lib` → `import my_lib`). Xcode targets use a literal `PRODUCT_MODULE_NAME` or `PRODUCT_NAME` when set.
- **SwiftPM rules:** `sources:` and `exclude:` narrow a target. The default target folder is chosen once per package, as SwiftPM does.
- **Files in no module:** each `Package.swift` manifest is a one-file module, as SwiftPM compiles it. Other files outside every target become one-file modules once every manifest and project was read; otherwise they share `__default__`.
- **Membership** (`target-grouping.ts`): SwiftPM targets match by the deepest target directory from the repo root. Xcode targets match by file list and synchronized folders. A file compiled into several Xcode targets belongs to each of them.
- **Same-module visibility, linear:**
  - IMPORTS: one File → `Module` edge per member, reason `module-membership`.
  - Sibling declarations and type bindings: one shared table per module in the namespace channel C# adopted in #1871.
- **Incremental re-analyze:** `queryImportersBatch` treats files sharing a `Module` hub as importers of each other. The rule keys on the `module-membership` reason, so JCL's File→Module include edges are unaffected.
- **`import X`:** resolves to the modules named X, not to any folder named X. A name no module carries is external only when every manifest and project was read completely.
- **Cross-module fallback veto:** uses the same membership, so test targets, custom-path targets and Xcode targets have module identity.

**Explicitly out of scope / not done here**

- Build settings built from other settings (`$(…)`) are not expanded. The module name then falls back to the mangled target name.
- Access levels (`private`, `fileprivate`, `package`) are still not modeled. This predates the PR.

## Implementation notes

- **Behavior change from #2931:** target paths now match from the repo root. #2931 matched a target prefix anywhere in the path, which stood in for the missing nested discovery. A vendored copy of the same layout inside another folder is therefore no longer grouped into the root target. Its own manifest, if it has one, makes it a module.
- **Module node lifecycle:** a `Module` node's `filePath` is its target directory, its `.xcodeproj` path, or `.` for `__default__`. Incremental writeback keys rows by `filePath`, so rewriting any member file pulls in the hub and all of its membership edges.
- **No new schema pairs:** `File→Module` was already declared.
- **Removed:** the caps from the first round of this PR (edge budget, file ceiling, `GITNEXUS_SWIFT_MAX_MODULE_FILES`) are gone.

## Testing & verification

- [x] `cd gitnexus && npx vitest run test/unit/scope-resolution/swift test/unit/scope-resolution/swift-target-grouping.test.ts test/unit/scope-resolution/name-fallback-visibility.test.ts` — all pass. New tests cover:
  - SwiftPM folder rules, version-specific manifests and plugins;
  - the pbxproj parser, including synchronized folders;
  - import-by-name, including a folder named like a module;
  - the veto for test and Xcode targets;
  - one binding per def in a 200-file module;
  - 5,000 files in one module producing 5,000 edges.
- [x] `cd gitnexus && npx vitest run test/integration/resolvers/swift.test.ts` — 111 pass, including new `swift-nested-packages` and `swift-xcode-targets` fixtures. The new import and Xcode assertions were checked red with each mechanism disabled. This host needed `GITNEXUS_WORKER_READY_TIMEOUT_MS=90000`.
- [x] `cd gitnexus && npx vitest run test/integration/lbug-query-importers-batch.test.ts` — the new test asserts module co-members are returned and JCL include edges are not.
- [x] `cd gitnexus && npx tsc --noEmit`
- [x] `node --import tsx bench/scope-capture/measure.mjs --check` — PASS. The Swift fingerprint was rebaselined for corpus growth only.
- [ ] `test/unit/incremental-orchestration.test.ts` did not run locally: its vitest worker crashes on this host before any test starts. CI runs it.
- [ ] `language-availability-skip` (Objective-C header case) fails identically on `main`.

## Risk & rollout

- **`impact` on a Swift file no longer lists every file in its module.** Before, each file imported every other file in the module, so all siblings looked like dependents. Now only files with real references (CALLS, USES and similar) count. That is more precise, but a sibling that relies on a declaration with no recorded reference won't appear.
- No schema change.
- The first `npx gitnexus analyze` after upgrading rebuilds Swift modules as `Module` hubs. Existing indexes keep their old File→File implicit edges until then. The `check --cycles` exclusion for the old reason stays in place.
- Swift CALLS resolution is unchanged on the existing fixture corpus: all 104 prior Swift integration tests pass untouched.

- [x] PR body meets repo minimum length (workflow may label short descriptions)
- [ ] `AGENTS.md` / overlays changed: headers, scope block, changelog updated per project conventions — not applicable

title: analyze skips dirty-to-clean revert at unchanged HEAD, leaving stale content and FTS (1.6.12)
body:
## Summary

GitNexus 1.6.12 can leave reverted, uncommitted content in the index while `analyze` exits 0 and says **Already up to date**.

Sequence: index clean HEAD → edit one tracked file without committing → analyze the dirty tree → restore that file to HEAD → analyze again. HEAD is unchanged throughout. The final working tree is clean, but the index still contains the dirty version.

This was reproduced on a **one-file public fixture** using unmodified GitNexus 1.6.12 and its stock `@ladybugdb/core@0.18.3`, not an experimental dependency override.

## Environment

- Windows x64, Node 24.15.0
- GitNexus 1.6.12, LadybugDB 0.18.3
- Existing Windows FTS extension from the engine-selected 0.18.1 cache directory
- Process-local `GITNEXUS_LBUG_EXTENSION_INSTALL=load-only`; no extension installation during this test
- One parser worker, no embeddings, no debugger or package patches
- Index and registry outside the fixture; no commits during the edit/revert sequence

## Public reproduction

The actual fixture was a sparse clone of LadybugDB/ladybug at tag `v0.20.4` (commit `df58ee387c4e5e9f02bb9d518636b52cd4abe5f7`), containing **only README.md**. This avoids sharing any private repository. Baseline output was 8 nodes / 7 edges.

The following PowerShell recipe uses the same public source. Prerequisites: GitNexus 1.6.12 available as `gitnexus`, Node 24, and its matching FTS extension already available. Run only against the new disposable clone:

```powershell
$demo = Join-Path $env:TEMP ("gitnexus-clean-revert-" + [guid]::NewGuid())
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path $demo | Out-Null
$fixture = Join-Path $demo "repo"
git clone --depth 1 --branch v0.20.4 --no-checkout https://github.com/LadybugDB/ladybug.git $fixture
git -C $fixture sparse-checkout set --no-cone /README.md
git -C $fixture checkout --detach HEAD

$env:GITNEXUS_HOME = Join-Path $demo "registry"
$env:GITNEXUS_STORAGE_PATH = Join-Path $demo "index"
$env:GITNEXUS_LBUG_EXTENSION_INSTALL = "load-only"
$env:GITNEXUS_MEMORY = "off"
$env:GITNEXUS_LBUG_BUFFER_POOL_SIZE = "4294967296"
$env:NODE_OPTIONS = "--max-old-space-size=8192"

gitnexus analyze $fixture --index-only --workers 1 --force --no-parse-cache

Add-Content -LiteralPath (Join-Path $fixture "README.md") -Value "`nTemporary search marker: zqxftsprobe."
gitnexus analyze $fixture --index-only --workers 1 --verbose
gitnexus query zqxftsprobe --repo $fixture
# README.md is returned, as expected.

git -C $fixture restore -- README.md
git -C $fixture status --porcelain
# Empty: the disposable fixture is clean again.
gitnexus analyze $fixture --index-only --workers 1 --verbose
# Actual: Already up to date; exit 0.
gitnexus query zqxftsprobe --repo $fixture
# Actual: README.md is STILL returned.
```

The local test used the already-installed CLI via an absolute Node/CLI path and reused an existing public source checkout for the sparse clone; it did not install dependencies or change global configuration.

## Measured results

| Stage | Marker on disk | Retained File.content contains marker | FTS hit |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Clean baseline | false | false | none |
| Uncommitted edit indexed | true | true | README.md |
| File restored + ordinary analyze | false | **true** | **README.md** |

The dirty analyze explicitly logged:

```text
Incremental: changed=1, added=0, deleted=0 (skipping wipe + 0 unchanged file rows preserved)
Repository indexed successfully
```

After the clean revert, `indexedAt` was unchanged and metadata still contained:

```json
"indexCoverage": { "dirtyPaths": ["README.md"] }
```

A new read-only database connection confirmed both the stale retained text and the stale FTS hit. The CLI query also returned `File:README.md` with BM25 active. This is not an in-memory query cache.

## Likely cause / regression test

In the published `dist/core/run-analyze.js`, the already-up-to-date branch checks matching `lastCommit/currentCommit`, no forced rebuild, and the **current** `isWorkingTreeDirty(repoPath)` result before content-hash comparison. A clean current tree does not imply that the previous index represented clean HEAD. The guard does not use the retained `indexCoverage.dirtyPaths` evidence in this case.

Suggested regression test: clean baseline → index dirty edit at same HEAD → restore clean HEAD → ordinary analyze → assert the restored file is reconsidered, retained text is current, and the removed marker no longer has an FTS hit. Merely asserting exit 0 or matching HEAD would miss the bug.

A full rebuild cleared the stale content in the earlier larger fixture, but that is recovery, not a passing incremental-revert test. This report is about the freshness guard, not a native FTS crash.

title: fix(analyze): revisit dirty snapshots after clean revert

## Summary

title: fix(python): resolve mixin self calls to subtype implementations
body:
## Problem

A Python mixin method can call `self.helper()` while `helper` is defined only by the concrete class that inherits the mixin. The current receiver pass types `self` as the mixin and searches that class and its ancestors, but misses the concrete subtype implementation. The call can also escape unresolved-receiver accounting, leaving incoming-call completeness reported as `exact` despite the missing edge.

Synthetic example:

```python
class HookMixin:
    def first(self):
        return self.helper()

    def second(self):
        return self.helper()

class Worker(HookMixin):
    def helper(self):
        return 1
```

Both callers should be represented when the supported dispatch target can be resolved. When it cannot, receiver incompleteness must remain visible rather than falling through to an unrelated same-name function.

This is a follow-up shape to #2744 / #2747, not the already-fixed compound-receiver case. The typed-self missing-member block was verified unchanged between v1.6.12 and `0261982d9a8c8ac5a187e9c60e414d6e5fa63b09`.

## Scope

Use the existing provider capability and subtype-resolution structures. Keep shared ingestion language-neutral, preserve normal base/MRO resolution, and add synthetic regression coverage. No schema, MCP API, deployment, provider or embedding changes.

## Verification

Current candidate: `1134df83852fd714323e1846e66416fbdf1cd34b`, integrating upstream `86a39202cf5285f79ca1081b7087bee16e9500cb`.

The earlier candidate failed the incompatible-arity assertion: Python call captures did not supply argument counts. The correction produces known call arity, retains unknown splat dispatch as incomplete, and counts bound method parameters independently of receiver spelling. Free/static/nested parameters and typed variadics retain their semantics.

- Golden changes are confined to two mixin fixture digests. Benchmark documentation explains the new known unresolved missing-target call; no performance threshold or shape assertion was relaxed.

title: fix(auto-sync): allow self-hosted remotes via allowed_hosts
body:
## Summary

`gitnexus auto-sync` can clone a self-hosted Git remote when that host is named in top-level `allowed_hosts`. github.com, gitlab.com, and gitee.com stay allowed without being listed. Any other host still fails validation, and the sync is skipped.

## Motivation / context

Fixes #3307

A company GitLab URL such as `git@gitlab.mycompany.com:group/repo.git` failed `watch_config.yml` validation because the host was not one of the three built-in names. The default stays closed. Extra hosts are an explicit list of exact DNS names. A listed parent does not allow subdomains, and wildcards are rejected.

## Areas touched

- [x] `gitnexus/` (CLI / core / MCP server)
- [ ] `gitnexus-web/` (Vite / React UI)
- [ ] `.github/` (workflows, actions)
- [ ] `eval/` or other tooling
- [ ] Docs / agent config only (`AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `.cursor/`, `llms.txt`, etc.)

## Scope & constraints

**In scope**

- Top-level `allowed_hosts`, merged with the three built-in hosts
- SSH SCP (`git@host:owner/repo.git`) and HTTPS
- Clone layout stays `local_path/host/namespace/repo`
- The same list is applied when the clone runs, so a config that loaded is not rejected again

**Explicitly out of scope / not done here**

- Accepting every syntactically valid host by default
- `ssh://` URLs, ports, and userinfo

## Implementation notes

The host becomes a directory under `local_path`, so each extra name must be a DNS hostname. Names are compared case-insensitively and stored lowercase.

## Testing & verification

- [x] `cd gitnexus && npx vitest run test/unit/auto-sync.test.ts test/unit/auto-sync-runner.test.ts`
- [ ] `cd gitnexus && npm test`
- [ ] `cd gitnexus && npm run test:integration` *(if core/indexing/MCP paths changed)*

## Risk & rollout

Existing configs keep the previous behavior. A self-hosted remote syncs only after `allowed_hosts` includes that host and auto-sync is restarted. Reverting this change makes those configs fail validation again.

title: Python subtype fallback treats aliased @classmethod caller as an instance receiver
body:
### Area

gitnexus (CLI / core / indexing / MCP server)

### Summary

An aliased `classmethod` decorator is not recognized when synthesizing a Python receiver binding. The missing-member subtype fallback can then infer an instance-method CALLS edge from a class receiver.

### Minimal case

```python
from builtins import classmethod as cm

class Mixin:
    @cm
    def dispatch(owner):
        return owner.hook()

class Worker(Mixin):
    def hook(self):
        pass
```

Index this source and inspect the target of `owner.hook()` in `Mixin.dispatch`. `Worker.dispatch()` passes the class as `owner`; `Worker.hook` is an ordinary instance method and cannot be called there without an instance.

### Expected

The subtype fallback should withhold the `Mixin.dispatch -> Worker.hook` instance CALLS edge and report uncertain receiver coverage unless the binding is proven to be an instance receiver.

### Current `origin/main` evidence

At `2925cfc02444753f4f3cace342f8c57a6e8d1f42`, `hasDecorator` compares the literal decorator tail with `classmethod`; `@cm` is not recognized ([receiver-binding.ts](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/blob/2925cfc02444753f4f3cace342f8c57a6e8d1f42/gitnexus/src/core/ingestion/languages/python/receiver-binding.ts#L35-L45)). `classifyPythonBoundReceiver` therefore classifies the first parameter as an instance receiver ([same file](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/blob/2925cfc02444753f4f3cace342f8c57a6e8d1f42/gitnexus/src/core/ingestion/languages/python/receiver-binding.ts#L94-L123)); the fallback accepts `typeRef.source === 'self'` ([scope-resolver.ts](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/blob/2925cfc02444753f4f3cace342f8c57a6e8d1f42/gitnexus/src/core/ingestion/languages/python/scope-resolver.ts#L45-L56)). This is a source-path finding; no fresh end-to-end graph reproduction was run for this ticket.

Originally reported in [PR #3390 comment](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/pull/3390#issuecomment-5863980804). A narrow correction was described in an external fork, but it is absent from current `origin/main`.

title: Python subtype dispatch omits unresolved coverage when a sibling subtype has no method
body:
### Area

gitnexus (CLI / core / indexing / MCP server)

### Summary

A mixin call can gain a valid edge to one concrete subtype while another concrete subtype with no matching method is silently omitted. The resulting partial target set can appear complete.

### Minimal case

```python
class Mixin:
    def dispatch(self):
        return self.hook()

class HasHook(Mixin):
    def hook(self):
        pass

class MissingHook(Mixin):
    pass
```

Index this source and inspect `Mixin.dispatch`'s CALLS edges and resolution outcome for `self.hook()`.

### Expected

Keep the valid edge to `HasHook.hook`, and record unresolved receiver coverage for `MissingHook`, whose runtime call would fail.

### Current `origin/main` evidence

At `2925cfc02444753f4f3cace342f8c57a6e8d1f42`, the subtype loop skips a subtype when `picked === undefined` ([receiver-bound-calls.ts](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/blob/2925cfc02444753f4f3cace342f8c57a6e8d1f42/gitnexus/src/core/ingestion/scope-resolution/passes/receiver-bound-calls.ts#L2447-L2453)). A subtype with no matching method is not added to `ambiguousCandidateIds`, `unknownCompatibilityCandidateIds`, or `incompleteInheritanceSubtypeIds`, which are the only missing inputs to coverage ([same file](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/blob/2925cfc02444753f4f3cace342f8c57a6e8d1f42/gitnexus/src/core/ingestion/scope-resolution/passes/receiver-bound-calls.ts#L2469-L2477)). With one valid target, `prepareSubtypeDispatchCoverage` sets `recordUnresolved` to false when that missing set is empty ([same file](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/blob/2925cfc02444753f4f3cace342f8c57a6e8d1f42/gitnexus/src/core/ingestion/scope-resolution/passes/receiver-bound-calls.ts#L346-L369)). This is a source-path finding; no fresh end-to-end graph reproduction was run for this ticket.

Originally reported in [PR #3390 comment](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/pull/3390#issuecomment-5863980804). A correction was described in an external fork, but it is absent from current `origin/main`.

title: Python subtype fallback accepts receiverless method that raises TypeError at runtime
body:
### Area

gitnexus (CLI / core / indexing / MCP server)

### Summary

The missing-member subtype compatibility check can accept a zero-parameter ordinary method as a target of a zero-argument instance call, although Python injects the instance and raises `TypeError` before the method body runs.

### Minimal case

```python
class Mixin:
    def dispatch(self):
        return self.hook()

class Worker(Mixin):
    def hook():
        pass

Worker().dispatch()  # TypeError: Worker.hook() takes 0 positional arguments but 1 was given
```

title: Python subtype fallback can select abstract target decorated through an import alias
body:
### Area

gitnexus (CLI / core / indexing / MCP server)

### Summary

A subtype method decorated with an alias of `abc.abstractmethod` is not marked abstract by the method extractor. The missing-member subtype fallback can therefore treat that declaration as a concrete target.

### Minimal case

```python
from abc import ABC, abstractmethod as am

class Mixin:
    def dispatch(self):
        return self.hook()

class AbstractWorker(Mixin, ABC):
    @am
    def hook(self):
        pass
```

Index this source and inspect the target and resolution outcome for `Mixin.dispatch -> self.hook()`.

### Expected

Do not treat `AbstractWorker.hook` as a proven concrete implementation; report unresolved/unknown coverage until a concrete descendant provides the target. A conservative guard for unproven decorated subtype candidates would also avoid claiming a false target without adding general decorator resolution.

### Current `origin/main` evidence

At `2925cfc02444753f4f3cace342f8c57a6e8d1f42`, `isAbstract` only checks for a decorator literally named `abstractmethod` ([python.ts](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/blob/2925cfc02444753f4f3cace342f8c57a6e8d1f42/gitnexus/src/core/ingestion/method-extractors/configs/python.ts#L307-L309)). The subtype path rejects a declaration only when the graph node's `isAbstract` property is true ([receiver-bound-calls.ts](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/blob/2925cfc02444753f4f3cace342f8c57a6e8d1f42/gitnexus/src/core/ingestion/scope-resolution/passes/receiver-bound-calls.ts#L663-L667), [candidate gate](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/blob/2925cfc02444753f4f3cace342f8c57a6e8d1f42/gitnexus/src/core/ingestion/scope-resolution/passes/receiver-bound-calls.ts#L2407-L2415)). This is a source-path finding; no fresh end-to-end graph reproduction was run for this ticket.

Originally reported in [PR #3390 comment](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/pull/3390#issuecomment-5870512820). The reporter also distinguished this from a method with a genuinely missing required argument, which Python rejects before execution.

title: Go gin/echo routes are never indexed: route_map is empty and impact stops at the handler (false-safe LOW)
body:
### Area

gitnexus (CLI / core / indexing / MCP server)

### Summary

Go HTTP routes (gin / echo) are never turned into `Route` nodes during `analyze`, so `route_map` returns nothing for a Go backend and upstream `impact` from a service method stops at the HTTP handler with `risk: LOW`, even when the handler is registered on a route and called by a frontend.

### Context

`gitnexus/src/core/ingestion/route-extractors/` has extractors for Spring, Kotlin Spring, Laravel, Next.js, Expo, NestJS, Django, FastAPI, tRPC, JS/TS dispatch guards and data route tables. There is no Go extractor, and the Go `LanguageProvider` does not implement `extractDecoratorRoutes`. Go routes are only read in group mode, through the source-scan plugin `core/group/extractors/http-patterns/go.ts`.

That plugin had two gaps of its own: method-value handlers (`admin.POST("/x", h.Method)`) were dropped, and `Group("/p")` prefixes were ignored. Both are fixed in a separate PR (link to follow). This issue covers the index side, which that PR does not touch.

### Expected behavior

For a gin router such as

```go
func RegisterRoutes(r *gin.Engine, svc *service.Service) {
	matchHandler := NewMatchHandler(svc.Match)
	v1 := r.Group("/api/v1")
	{
		admin := v1.Group("/admin")
		admin.POST("/seasons/:seasonId/rounds/:roundId/unfinalize", matchHandler.UnfinalizeRoundHandle)
	}
}
```

- `analyze` creates `Route {name: "/api/v1/admin/seasons/:seasonId/rounds/:roundId/unfinalize", method: "POST"}`, with a `HANDLES_ROUTE` edge from `MatchHandler.UnfinalizeRoundHandle` (defined in `match_handler.go`, not the router file);
- `route_map` lists the route with its handler and any `FETCHES` consumers;
- upstream `impact` from a service method the handler calls reaches the route.

### Actual behavior

Measured on a real gin + React/Vite project with 254 gin routes, all under `r.Group("/api/v1")`, with 245 of them using method-value handlers. Indexed on current `main`:

- `MATCH (r:Route) RETURN count(r)` → `0`
- `impact UnfinalizeRound --direction upstream` → `risk: LOW`, 1–2 direct callers, ending at `UnfinalizeRoundHandle`. The route and the two frontend call sites are invisible, so an agent that trusts `LOW` edits without them.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Create a Go module with the `RegisterRoutes` above, plus `match_handler.go` declaring `type MatchHandler struct{…}` and `func (h *MatchHandler) UnfinalizeRoundHandle(c *gin.Context)`.
2. `gitnexus analyze`
3. `gitnexus cypher "MATCH (r:Route) RETURN count(r)"` → 0; `route_map` is empty.

### Proposed direction

I'd like to work on this, and I'd appreciate a steer on handler resolution before opening the PR.

1. **Extraction.** Add `route-extractors/go-gin.ts` and wire it as the Go provider's `extractDecoratorRoutes`, with `source` set so the `HANDLES_ROUTE` edge does not claim a decorator. It would share the in-function `Group(...)` prefix walk with the group-mode plugin, so both layers produce the same paths.
2. **Handler resolution.** This is the open question. The routes phase resolves `handlerName` by `(filePath, name)` in the route's own file, but gin handlers are almost always methods defined in another file of the same package (`matchHandler.UnfinalizeRoundHandle`). The receiver is a local variable, not a type. Options, most precise first:
   - (a) Infer the receiver's type in the router function from `h := &T{…}` / `T{…}`, or from `h := NewT(…)` via the constructor's declared result type. Then resolve `T.Method` with `model.methods.lookupAllByOwner`, as data route tables already do for `Owner.member`.
   - (b) Fall back to a unique `Method` with that name among the files of the router's package, i.e. the same directory, since a Go package is a directory. This declines on ambiguity (e.g. `AuthHandler.Login` and `AdminAuthHandler.Login`).
   - (c) For `pkg.Func`, resolve the Go import to its package directory and look up a unique function there.

   Anything unresolved is emitted without `handlerSymbolId`, following the existing fail-open contract. My plan is (a) + (b) + (c). Would you prefer something narrower, e.g. only (a), or reusing the Go scope resolver's type bindings instead of a local inference?
3. **Out of scope for the first PR:** groups passed to another function (`registerAdmin(v1)`), chi (`r.Get` / `r.Route`), and echo's trailing route-level middleware.

### Acceptance criteria

- A `test/integration/go-gin-route-pipeline.test.ts` (modelled on `nest-route-pipeline.test.ts`) asserting Route nodes with full group prefixes, method and `handlerSymbolId` for selector, identifier, package-function and inline handlers; ambiguous handlers get no `handlerSymbolId`.
- `route_map` returns those routes; `impact` upstream from a handler dependency reaches the route.
- No change for other languages; shared ingestion code does not name Go (via `LanguageProvider`).

title: fix(python): resolve decorator identity like CPython
body:
## Summary

Make Python decorator identity follow CPython's evaluation rules in one place. This fixes a false `CALLS` edge for `@staticmethod  # comment` and closes the remaining review findings on the #3399 tracker children (#3401, #3403, #3404, #3405).

## Motivation / context

A code review of the merged #3399 children found that two predicates answered the same question differently:

- `hasDecorator` read the raw decorator node text. Tree-sitter keeps a trailing comment inside that node, so `@staticmethod  # type: ignore[misc]` did not match. An explicit first parameter then became a fabricated receiver, and `self.target()` got a `CALLS` edge that CPython rejects with `TypeError`. This predates the range.
- The subtype capacity gate matched the exact first child text. It trusted any `staticmethod` spelling, including a module-level rebinding (`from abc import abstractmethod as staticmethod`) and the `staticmethod(classmethod(f))` stack. CPython cannot call a method built from that stack (`'classmethod' object is not callable`).

## Areas touched

- [x] `gitnexus/` (CLI / core / MCP server)
- [ ] `gitnexus-web/` (Vite / React UI)
- [ ] `.github/` (workflows, actions)
- [ ] `eval/` or other tooling
- [ ] Docs / agent config only (`AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `.cursor/`, `llms.txt`, etc.)

## Scope & constraints

**In scope**

- `decoratorNames` reads the decorator's expression child, never a trailing comment.
- One `isBuiltinDescriptor` check. It accepts a bare builtin descriptor name only when the file does not rebind that name. A decorator name resolves through class, module and builtin scope. The check ignores uses that cannot bind the name: decorator expressions, attribute members, keyword names, `from M import` module paths, and the source side of `import X as Y`.
- `hasPythonProvenCallShape` replaces the inline gate in `recordPythonSubtypeMethodShape`. Only a plain function, or a single builtin `staticmethod` / `classmethod` wrapper, publishes subtype positional capacity.
- Remove the no-op `incompleteInheritanceSubtypeIds` guard; both sets merge into one coverage set. Move the implicit-classmethod comment next to the code it describes.
- Parse-cache schema v120 -> v121.

**Explicitly out of scope / not done here**

- Import resolution for decorator aliases (`@builtins.staticmethod`, `@typing.override`). These stay compatibility-unknown by design; that is a recall trade-off, not a false edge.
- The shadow scan over-approximates: a plain read such as `staticmethod(f)` also counts as a rebinding. That fails closed. The code marks this with a `ponytail:` comment and names the upgrade path.

## Implementation notes

The shadow scan runs once per syntax tree and is cached in a `WeakMap` keyed by the tree. Member-less intermediate subtypes (`class Base(Mixin): pass`) keep partial coverage, because CPython can instantiate `Base`, and `Base().dispatch()` then raises `AttributeError`. A new test pins this.

## Testing & verification

- [x] New unit case for CPython decorator identity: trailing comment, `staticmethod(classmethod(f))`, receiverless `**kw` and `*, k=1`, a module rebinding, and `import staticmethod as sm`. It fails on `main` (the comment case yields `compatible` instead of `incompatible`) and passes here.
- [x] Integration: the negative tests now pin exact `candidateIds` beside a concrete positive-control sibling, plus a new intermediate-subtype case.
- [x] Method extraction: `@staticmethod  # comment` keeps its first parameter.
- [x] `npx vitest run test/unit/method-extraction.test.ts test/unit/scope-resolution/python test/unit/incremental-parse-cache.test.ts`: 524 passed.
- [x] `npx vitest run test/integration/resolvers/python.test.ts`: 269 passed.
- [x] `bench/python-scope/measure.mjs --check` and `import-target-fingerprint.mjs --check` pass, and the capture golden is unchanged.
- [x] `npx tsc --noEmit`, `npm run build`, Prettier.
- [ ] Full `npm test` locally: not run. CI is the full gate.

## Risk & rollout

Impact analysis rated `isPythonStaticLikeMethod` CRITICAL (20 symbols, 6 flows) and `recordPythonSubtypeMethodShape` / `synthesizeConstructorFieldTypeBindings` HIGH. `detect_changes`: 8 files, 21 symbols, 3 flows, MEDIUM, not truncated. The cache bump rebuilds persisted captures.

## Checklist

- [x] PR body meets repo minimum length (workflow may label short descriptions)
- [x] No secrets, tokens, or machine-specific paths committed
