title: feat(r): add R language support with scope-resolution
body:
## Summary

Adds R language support to GitNexus, including full scope-resolution wiring (imports, calls, heritage), closing out issue #1356.

This rebases and completes @taiseii's earlier work in #380, which added R's Function/Class/Method/Property node-extraction path but went stale after the legacy call-resolution DAG it depended on was removed in #942. Credit to @taiseii for the original implementation this builds on.

## What's included

- Rebase of #380 onto current `main`, with two review-bot-flagged fixes applied on top (precompiled `NAMESPACE` `exportPattern()` regexes instead of per-node recompilation; a guard so `attachDeferredROwners`'s full-graph traversal skips non-R nodes immediately) and a few small post-rebase build-breakage fixes (stale `importSemantics` field removed, a required `column` field added to R6/RefClass method-extraction sites per #2936, a scope bug from the rebase itself).
- New scope-resolution wiring for R (`languages/r/{query,captures,interpret,scope-resolver,simple-hooks}.ts` + one `SCOPE_RESOLVERS` registry entry), modeled on the existing Zig and Ruby language implementations:
  - Import resolution for `source()`/`library()`/`require()`, including a guard against the suffix-fallback path minting false `IMPORTS` edges to unrelated same-named files in other languages.
  - Call resolution, including cross-file free-call fallback and R6 method-chain calls (e.g. `obj$method()`).
  - Heritage edges for R6 `inherit=` (both `R6::R6Class(...)` and bare `R6Class(...)` forms) and S4 `contains=`/`contains=c(...)`, including S4's `"VIRTUAL"` base-type sentinel.
  - Registered R in the grammar-literal-validation gate's language maps (`test/helpers/{grammar-introspection,literal-collectors}.ts`) — this was missing since R first landed, which meant that gate had been silently skipping the entire `languages/r/` directory.
- All 39 tests in `test/integration/resolvers/r.test.ts` pass (the 10 scope-resolution scenarios this PR adds, plus the 29 pre-existing node-extraction scenarios, unregressed).
- No changes to any other language's `SCOPE_RESOLVERS` entry or other registered behavior.

## Test plan

- [x] `npx vitest run test/integration/resolvers/r.test.ts` — 39/39 passing
- [x] Full suite run and diffed against a clean `main` baseline — no new failures beyond this PR's own scope
- [x] `npx tsc --noEmit` clean
- [x] `node scripts/build.js` clean

## Follow-ups (deliberately out of scope for this PR)

- NAMESPACE-driven bare-call resolution and native pipe (`|>`) chain resolution — tracked as a separate, sequenced follow-up.
- A pre-existing, unrelated gap this PR's testing surfaced: R is missing from `callable-value-flow.test.ts`'s `CALLABLE_FLOW_PROVIDER_COVERAGE` map (predates this PR, from when R first landed) — filing separately.
- A general policy for S4 heritage to basic/built-in base types (this PR only handles the literal `"VIRTUAL"` sentinel, matching what the existing test fixtures need) — filing separately.

title: wiki: add `anthropic` provider using the native `/v1/messages` endpoint
body:
### Area

gitnexus (CLI / core / indexing / MCP server)

### Problem or opportunity

`gitnexus wiki` only talks to LLM APIs that speak the OpenAI Chat Completions protocol. The `LLMProvider` union in `gitnexus/src/core/wiki/llm-client.ts` lists `openai | openrouter | azure | custom | cursor | claude | codex | opencode | grok | minimax`, and `callLLM()` always builds `POST <baseUrl>/chat/completions` with `Authorization: Bearer …`.

There is no path to call the Anthropic Messages API directly with an `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`. To use a Claude model for wiki generation today you must:

1. Have the Claude Code CLI (`claude`) installed and logged in, then pass `--provider claude`. This spawns `claude -p …` as a child process and reads stdout. It does not work on machines that do not have Claude Code installed (CI, servers, shared hosts).
2. Or go through OpenRouter with `provider = custom`. That works, but the request path, headers, and request body all pass through OpenRouter, which is not what the user asked for when they set an `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`.

So a user with a plain Anthropic key, no Claude Code install, and no OpenRouter account cannot use `gitnexus wiki`. The local-CLI route in #1769 / #2039 covers the "already logged in to Claude Code" case but not the "I have an API key" case.

### Proposed solution

Add a new provider value `anthropic` to `LLMProvider`. When selected, the wiki client should talk to the Anthropic Messages API directly:

- URL: `POST https://api.anthropic.com/v1/messages`
- Headers: `x-api-key: <key>`, `anthropic-version: 2023-06-15`, `Content-Type: application/json`
- Auth source: `--api-key` flag, `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` env var, or `GITNEXUS_API_KEY`
- Model: `--model <id>` (e.g. `claude-sonnet-4-5`, `claude-opus-4-1`)
- Optional base URL override for proxies (`--base-url https://…`) with the same `validateLLMBaseUrl` rules as other HTTP providers

The existing `callLLM()` in `gitnexus/src/core/wiki/llm-client.ts` should branch on `config.provider === 'anthropic'` and translate the OpenAI-style `{role, content}` messages into the Anthropic `{system, messages}` shape, then map the response back to `LLMResponse`. Streaming via SSE is already supported in `readSSEStream`; the Anthropic event names (`message_start` / `content_block_delta` / `message_stop`) need their own small parser or a translation layer.

Interactive `gitnexus wiki` setup in `gitnexus/src/cli/wiki.ts` should get a new menu entry for `anthropic`, mirroring the existing `azure` flow (prompt for API key, optional model, save to `~/.gitnexus/config.json`).

### Alternatives considered

- `provider = custom` with `base-url = https://api.anthropic.com/v1` and `Authorization: Bearer …`. Does not work today because `callLLM()` always appends `/chat/completions` and Anthropic does not serve that path. Would require either a base-URL rewrite or a `provider = anthropic` branch anyway.
- `provider = openrouter` with `model = anthropic/<id>`. Works today at the cost of one more hop, but the user explicitly chose the Anthropic API.
- `provider = claude` (local CLI from #1769). Already supported. Useful when Claude Code is installed and logged in; not a substitute for the bare API key path.
- Add `--anthropic-messages-endpoint` flag to `callLLM` and call the Anthropic API from the existing OpenAI-compatible client. Rejected: mixes two wire formats inside one function and breaks the existing `Azure` / `OpenRouter` branches. A separate provider value is clearer.

### Acceptance criteria

- `gitnexus wiki --provider anthropic --api-key <key> --model claude-sonnet-4-5` produces a wiki end-to-end against `https://api.anthropic.com/v1/messages` and writes the expected output files.
- `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` in the environment is picked up automatically when `--provider anthropic` is set and no `--api-key` is given.
- `gitnexus wiki --provider anthropic --base-url https://proxy.example/v1` works with the same `validateLLMBaseUrl` checks (`https` required, `http` only with allowlist) used for other HTTP providers.
- Streaming output (`onChunk` callback in `callLLM`) still drives progress UI; the Anthropic SSE events are translated to `delta.content` chunks.
- `gitnexus wiki` interactive setup has a new menu entry that saves `provider: "anthropic"` plus the model to `~/.gitnexus/config.json`.
- Unit tests cover: request URL + headers, message translation (system prompt into `system`, user content into `messages`), response translation, and the SSE event parser. `npx tsc --noEmit` and `npm test` pass.

### Constraints

- No new npm dependency. The Anthropic API is plain HTTPS + SSE; reuse the existing `resilientFetch` and `readSSEStream` plumbing.
- The Anthropic API uses different finish reasons and error shapes from OpenAI. Map only what `callLLM` already consumes (`choices[0].message.content`); do not leak Anthropic-specific fields upward.
- Do not change the existing `openai` / `openrouter` / `azure` / `custom` / `claude` / `codex` / `opencode` / `cursor` / `grok` / `minimax` provider behavior. This is a strictly additive change.
- The `claude` local-CLI provider (CLI subprocess path in `local-cli-client.ts`) stays as is. `claude` (local CLI) and `anthropic` (HTTP API) are two distinct providers, similar to how `cursor` and `custom` coexist.

### Contribution

- [ ] I am willing to open a PR for this (may need design discussion first).

title: Python decorator identity: model call-time effects of global/nonlocal rebinds and deferred class bodies
body:
## Summary

`gitnexus/src/core/ingestion/languages/python/builtin-descriptors.ts` (PR #3411) decides whether a method decorator such as `@staticmethod` names the builtin descriptor. It resolves the name the way LOAD_NAME does (Language Reference 4.2.2), with namespace state computed at the point the `def` runs.

Some effects happen only when a function is **called**. Call order is not modelled, so the resolver fails closed in these cases. The method is treated as having an unproven receiver and call shape. This never emits a false `CALLS` edge, but it loses matches that CPython would resolve to the builtin.

## Cases that stay unresolved today

All of these were checked against CPython 3.11.

1. **A `global` delete in a called helper** does not restore the builtin:
   ```python
   staticmethod = lambda f: f
   def reset():
       global staticmethod
       del staticmethod
   reset()
   class A:
       @staticmethod        # CPython: builtin. Resolver: shadowed.
       def t(v): return v
   ```
2. **A `global` rebind** counts as shadowing once its defining statement precedes the decorator, whether or not the function is ever called before the class runs.
3. **A `nonlocal` rebind** in a nested function counts as shadowing anywhere inside the enclosing function, whatever the call order.
4. **A deferred class body** (a class defined inside a function) reads module state at the function's top-level statement. Any module override assigned later in the file is assumed to be visible, because the function may be called after it runs. A `del` after the function definition therefore does not restore the builtin, even when every call happens after it.

## Why it is deferred

Resolving these needs call-order facts across the file: which functions run, when, and in what order relative to the class statement. A per-file name resolver has no such facts, and statically they are undecidable in general. So the current rule prefers unresolved over a false edge.

## Possible approach

- Use the call graph to resolve unconditional top-level calls (`reset()` directly in the module body, before the class) to same-file functions whose bodies unconditionally `global`-delete or rebind the name.
- Treat those calls as executing their effect at the call site.
- Keep everything else fail-closed.

## Acceptance

- The four cases above resolve to match CPython wherever the call order is provable from unconditional top-level statements.
- Unprovable orders stay fail-closed.
- Each case gets a pinned test in `test/unit/scope-resolution/python/python-builtin-descriptors.test.ts`, with its expectation checked against CPython.

Follow-up to PR #3411 and the #3399 tracker.

title: fix(python): model restoring helper calls in decorator identity
body:
## Summary

A method decorated with `@staticmethod`, `@classmethod` or `@property` now keeps builtin receiver typing when a same-file helper, called at module top level, restored the builtin first. This change also closes four paths where the resolver said "builtin" but CPython shadows the name. Those paths could emit false `CALLS` edges.

Fixes #3414

## Motivation / context

PR #3411 made `builtin-descriptors.ts` resolve decorator names like LOAD_NAME. It ignored effects that run only when a function is called. So this program lost receiver typing, even though CPython resolves the decorator to the builtin:

```python
staticmethod = lambda f: f
def reset():
    global staticmethod
    del staticmethod
reset()
class A:
    @staticmethod
    def t(v): return v
```

## Areas touched

- [x] `gitnexus/` (CLI / core / MCP server)
- [ ] `gitnexus-web/` (Vite / React UI)
- [ ] `.github/` (workflows, actions)
- [ ] `eval/` or other tooling
- [ ] Docs / agent config only (`AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `.cursor/`, `llms.txt`, etc.)

## Scope & constraints

**In scope**

- A bare module-level call statement `helper()` restores the builtin at the call site when all of these hold:
  - The helper is a plain module-level `def`. It is not async and not a generator.
  - Every `global` binding of the name in the helper is an unconditional `del` or `from builtins import`.
  - No earlier `return` in the helper's own scope can skip the restore.
  - The helper's `def` is the only binding of its name, and the file has no wildcard import.
  - The call comes after the helper's `def`.
- False builtins that are now shadowed, each checked against CPython 3.11:
  - A `nonlocal` rebind in a nested function now shadows an enclosing function's `from builtins import`. Before, the owned import won even when the rebind ran first.
  - Any name in a `match` case pattern counts as a binding. Before, `case [*staticmethod]`, `case X() as staticmethod`, keyword captures and similar forms were invisible, at module level and inside helpers.
- Parse-cache schema v121 -> v122. Warm caches carry the old verdicts.

**Explicitly out of scope / not done here**

- Cases 2-4 of #3414: an uncalled `global` rebind, an uncalled `nonlocal` rebind, and a module `del` after a deferred class body. Each needs proof that a function is *not* called before the class runs. A per-file resolver cannot prove that, so these stay fail-closed. Each has a pinned test with its CPython result.
- Conditional calls (`if c: reset()`, `flag and reset()`), calls inside class or function bodies, and transitive helper calls stay fail-closed.
- Dynamic rebinding through `globals()`, `exec` or `__code__` is not modelled. This matches the existing model for the descriptor name itself.

## Implementation notes

- The restore is recorded as a synthetic module-scope binding at the callee identifier. The existing `namespaceState` ordering and deferred-class-body logic then treat it like a module-level `del`, so `lookupName` needs no new branch for it.
- Treating every case-pattern name as a capture over-approximates. Class names and value patterns are reads, not bindings. The error is always toward "shadowed", so it only fails closed. The code marks this with a `ponytail:` comment.

## Testing & verification

- [x] `npx vitest run test/unit/scope-resolution/python/`: 232 passed. The descriptor file gained 30 cases. Every expectation was checked by running the program under CPython 3.11.
- [x] `npx vitest run test/unit/incremental-parse-cache.test.ts`: 40 passed.
- [x] `cd gitnexus && npx tsc --noEmit`: clean. ESLint on the changed files: clean.
- [ ] `npx vitest run test/integration/resolvers/python`: 279 passed, 17 failed. The same 17 tests in `python.test.ts` also fail on unmodified `main` (821ffb2fc) in this environment, so this change does not cause them. CI is the authority here.

## Risk & rollout

Only Python receiver typing for decorated methods changes. Every new "builtin" answer is limited to a provable top-level call order, and the other changes only add shadowing. The parse-cache bump forces re-extraction on the next `npx gitnexus analyze`.

## Checklist

- [x] PR body meets repo minimum length (workflow may label short descriptions)
- [ ] If `AGENTS.md` / overlays changed: headers, scope block, and changelog updated per project conventions
- [x] No secrets, tokens, or machine-specific paths committed

title: augment: widely-used symbols return no context because the name fallback only runs when FTS is unavailable
body:
## Summary
`gitnexus augment` (and therefore the Claude Code PreToolUse hook) returns an empty result for the symbols agents search for most: widely-referenced classes/functions. The graph contains them; augment just never looks at the file that defines them.

## Version
gitnexus 1.6.12, LadybugDB 0.18.3, macOS arm64, Node 25. Mixed Python + TypeScript monorepo (~116k nodes).

## Root cause
In `core/augmentation/engine.js`, `augment()`:

1. `searchFTSFromLbug(pattern, 10, repoId)` ranks **files** by BM25. The top hits are the files that *mention* the term most often — callers, tests, migrations, docs.
2. Step 2 only accepts symbols **defined in** those top-5 files whose name `CONTAINS` the pattern.
3. The definition file of a heavily-used symbol almost never makes the top 5, so `symbolMatches` is empty.
4. The name-based fallback is guarded by `if (symbolMatches.length === 0 && !ftsAvailable)`, so with a healthy FTS index it never runs and `augment` returns `''`.

The more widely a symbol is used, the less likely augment finds it.

## Repro
For three central symbols in our repo (a Django manager class, a service function, a service class):

| pattern | top-5 BM25 files | symbol hits in top 5 | exact-name node exists |
|---|---|---|---|
| `SomeManager` | a view, a mixin, a serializer, a migration, … | 0 | yes (`core/managers.py`) |
| `create_order` | 3 test files, a `.ts` types file, a TS test | 0 | yes (`services/orders.py`) |
| `SomeService` | tests, 2 unrelated services | 0 | yes |

`gitnexus augment -- SomeManager` prints only the banner.

## Suggested fix
Run the name fallback whenever step 2 found nothing, and rank exact matches first:

```diff
-        if (symbolMatches.length === 0 && !ftsAvailable) {
+        if (symbolMatches.length === 0) {
             const fallbackRows = await executeQuery(repoId, `
         MATCH (n)
         WHERE n.name CONTAINS '${patternFirstWord}'
-        RETURN n.id AS id, n.name AS name, labels(n)[0] AS type, n.filePath AS filePath
-        ORDER BY id
+        RETURN n.id AS id, n.name AS name, labels(n)[0] AS type, n.filePath AS filePath,
+          CASE WHEN n.name = '${patternFirstWord}' THEN 0 ELSE 1 END AS exactRank
+        ORDER BY exactRank, id
         LIMIT 5
       `).catch(() => []);
```

Measured on the repo above: 13–361 ms per fallback query, well inside the hook's 7 s budget, and the defining symbol comes back first in all three cases (previously nothing). A further improvement would be to query exact-name definitions before (or alongside) BM25, since an identifier-shaped pattern is usually a lookup for its definition.

## Related
Separate from #2396 (lock contention): this reproduces with no MCP server running and a freshly `analyze --force`-built index.

title: feat(go): index gin/echo routes and report them in impact (#3402)
body:
## Summary

Go gin and echo routes are now indexed during `analyze`. Each verb registration with a provable `Group(...)` prefix becomes a `Route` node, and its handler is resolved across the files of the Go package. `impact` now lists the HTTP routes in its blast radius.

Closes #3402.

## Motivation / context

A gin backend with 254 routes indexed zero `Route` nodes. `route_map` was empty, and `impact` on a service method stopped at the HTTP handler with `risk: LOW`. An agent trusting that verdict would edit without seeing the endpoint or its frontend callers.

## Areas touched

- [x] `gitnexus/` (CLI / core / MCP server)
- [ ] `gitnexus-web/` (Vite / React UI)
- [ ] `.github/` (workflows, actions)
- [ ] `eval/` or other tooling
- [ ] Docs / agent config only (`AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `.cursor/`, `llms.txt`, etc.)

## Scope & constraints

**In scope**

- `route-extractors/go-gin-echo.ts`, wired as the Go provider's `extractDecoratorRoutes`. It tracks a proven prefix per local name: engine parameters, `gin.Default()`, `gin.New()`, `echo.New()`, and `x.Group("<literal>")` of a proven router, including chained calls. The handler is the last argument for gin and the second for echo. A file that imports both frameworks, or neither, yields nothing.
- A new optional `LanguageProvider.resolveRouteHandler` hook. `resolveRouteHandlerSymbols` asks it for routes of a language that defines it. Otherwise the existing same-file lookup runs unchanged, so shared ingestion code still names no language.
- `languages/go/route-handler.ts` resolves bare functions, `pkg.Func` through the Go import, and `h.Method` through a receiver hint. The extractor reads that hint from the router function's own syntax: `h := &T{}`, `var h *T`, a typed parameter, or `h := NewT(...)` via the constructor's declared result type. Every step either finds exactly one match or declines.
- `impact` adds `affected_routes` and per-item `routes`, read from `HANDLES_ROUTE`. They are reported only: the traversal and risk scoring are unchanged.
- Parse-cache `SCHEMA_BUMP` 123 to 124, because warm Go worker results carry no routes.

**Explicitly out of scope / not done here**

- Groups passed to another function (`registerAdmin(v1)`), and engines held in a struct field (`s.router`). Both are dropped, not guessed.
- chi, fiber, `net/http HandleFunc`, gin `Any`/`Handle`/`Match`, and echo `Add`/`Any`.
- The group-mode plugin `core/group/extractors/http-patterns/go.ts`. It is fixed separately; the two do not share code yet.
- Counting routes in impact `risk`. That is a policy change for a follow-up.

## Implementation notes

- **Drop rather than guess.** A registration whose prefix cannot be proven is not emitted. This covers a `*gin.RouterGroup` parameter, a computed group path, conflicting assignments, and a closure on an outer group. A wrong URL would be a false fact that `route_map` and FETCHES matching repeat.
- **Cross-file methods.** Route handlers resolve at the end of the parse phase, before scope resolution. At that point a Go method's `ownerId` is keyed on the method's own file, not the struct's. The resolver matches either id, so `MatchHandler` in `types.go` with its methods in `match_handler.go` resolves.
- **Unknown receiver declines.** A receiver whose type is not readable, such as `h := deps.Users` or a package-level var, gets no handler. It does not fall back to a same-named method in the router's directory: in a split-package layout that method belongs to an unrelated type.
- **Route file attribution.** The Route's `filePath` stays on the file that registers it, and the handler is reached through the symbol-level `HANDLES_ROUTE` edge.
- `parse-impl` now loads parsed imports and `go.mod` config for route files of hook-owning languages, not only for data route tables. The multi-file import resolver is the source of truth; the single-file one is derived from it.

## Testing & verification

- [x] `cd gitnexus && npx tsc --noEmit`
- [x] New unit tests:
  - `test/unit/go-gin-echo-routes.test.ts`: prefixes, handler argument, fail-closed cases, and receiver hints.
  - `test/unit/go-route-handler.test.ts`: every resolution step, sibling-file ownership, and each decline path.
  - `test/unit/impact-route-enrichment.test.ts`.
- [x] Updated `test/unit/resolve-route-handler-symbols.test.ts` (hook dispatch and first-writer-wins) and `test/unit/incremental-parse-cache.test.ts` (pin to 124).
- [x] New `test/integration/go-gin-route-pipeline.test.ts` on a fixture with a `go.mod`. It covers the issue router, an import-resolved package function, an inline handler, an ambiguous handler, an echo app, and a dropped RouterGroup route.
- [x] New `test/integration/impact-affected-routes.test.ts` against a real LadybugDB. Upstream `impact` on the service method lists the route.
- [x] Existing route pipelines pass unchanged: nest, spring, kotlin-spring, dispatch-guard.
- [x] Full `test/unit` run: 16988 passed. Every failure is in analyze CLI spawn tests (`skip-git-cli`, `analyze-heap-respawn`, `run-analyze*`), plus `wiki-llm-client`, which reads host credentials. They time out or read host env on this machine and fail the same way on a checkout without this change.

## Risk & rollout

- Go repos need `npx gitnexus analyze` to pick up routes. The schema bump invalidates warm caches automatically.
- `impact` output gains `affected_routes` and optional per-item `routes`. These are additive fields.
- Known follow-ups, all non-blocking:
  - `affected_routes` is capped with the rest of enrichment at `IMPACT_MAX_CHUNKS * 100` symbols without setting `partial`.
  - PDG-mode impact does not report routes.
  - File-level `HANDLES_ROUTE` edges can widen `affected_routes` for File targets.
  - gin routes registered in `_test.go` files are not excluded yet.

## Checklist

- [x] PR body meets repo minimum length (workflow may label short descriptions)
- [ ] If `AGENTS.md` / overlays changed: headers, scope block, and changelog updated per project conventions
- [x] No secrets, tokens, or machine-specific paths committed

The change is concentrated in ingestion code, especially `gitnexus/src/core/ingestion/workers/parse-worker.ts`, the hottest file with 26 changed symbols. title: chore(deps)(deps): bump smol-toml from 1.8.0 to 1.9.0 in /gitnexus
body:
Bumps [smol-toml](https://github.com/squirrelchat/smol-toml) from 1.8.0 to 1.9.0.
Release notes

Sourced from smol-toml's releases.

v1.9.0

Huge update!!! This is most likely the largest update the library received since its release, with lots of new features and improvements.

Performance improvements

Significant parts of the internal parse logic have been rewritten, improving performance by 1.5x-2x. The library was already comfortably ahead of the others, but it is now faster than ever, sitting at 4x faster parse performance than the closest maintained implementation.

Problematic code paths have also been replaced by safer implementations, solving potential DoS vectors. See GHSA-r4xh-jqrq-34v2.

Note: the objects returned by the library now have a null prototype. This is a transparent change for 99.9% of users, and is one of the most significant contributors to the major performance gains in this version.

Full Temporal support

Version 1.8.0 brought support for Temporal in stringify; now the library is also able to emit Temporal objects instead of its own ad-hoc TomlDate object. It is not enabled by default, but it will become the default in v2. Enable by setting useLegacyDate: false in the parser's options.

Better Temporal support in stringify

Temporal support has been improved since it released: Temporal objects that cannot be represented (such as Temporal.PlainMonthDay) now throw an error (instead of silently emitting a bogus object).

A new option has been added to stringify to disallow Temporal objects that cannot be fully represented in TOML. This includes ZonedDateTime objects with a IANA timezone attached instead of a plain offset, and dates with a specific calendar value set. Enable by setting strictTemporal: true in the options.

Handling of unsafe keys

Since its release the library has been protected against prototype pollution attacks, setting properties like __proto__ using safe mechanisms that do not trigger prototype pollution. However, while the returned objects are safe on their own, they may become problematic if used carelessly.

Inspired by secure-json-parse, the library now offers a way to either drop unsafe properties from the returned object, or to throw an error and reject documents altogether. By default, these potentially unsafe keys are preserved and returned.

Miscellaneous updates

  • Unicode BOM is now gracefully accepted and ignored.
  • Table array headers are now properly checked again. Reported in #65.
  • Closed certain gaps where invalid whitespace would be accepted. Reported in #61.
  • Bogus local date and local time values with a UTC offset are no longer accepted.
  • Certain error messages are more accurate and handle errors at line boundaries better.
  • The default export of the lib is now formally deprecated; use a import * instead. Proposed in #50.
  • On Node 20+, strings that contain lone surrogates are now normalised to well-formed strings.
  • On Node 20+, keys that contain lone surrogates are now rejected.

title: Incremental Property FTS fails with Invalid UTF-8 on 1.6.12; --repair-fts cannot recover
body:
### Area

gitnexus (CLI / core / indexing / MCP server)

### Summary

On GitNexus 1.6.12, an incremental analysis of a Swift-heavy repository completed with keyword search degraded after `Property.property_fts` failed with `Failed calling LOWER: Invalid UTF-8`. The recommended `--repair-fts` also failed; a full graph/FTS rebuild restored search.

### Context

Observed on 2026-09-29 during ordinary code review. The repository is private; no project source, database, credentials, or private paths are included here.

This is current-version evidence related to closed #3031 (its closing comment requested a 1.6.10+ report distinguishing hard abort from graceful degradation) and #2889. It may share an underlying cause, but that is not established. Open #3101 specifically involves a local patch enabling streamed incremental graph emission; this observation used the installed release without that patch.

### Expected behavior

Incremental analysis leaves configured FTS indexes available. If an index creation fails, targeted repair restores it or reports the underlying failure sufficiently to diagnose why it remains absent.

### Actual behavior

- Incremental analysis reported three changed files and degraded FTS after a native `LOWER`/UTF-8 failure in the Property index.
- `analyze --index-only --repair-fts .` exited 1, reporting `Property.property_fts` missing after rebuild. Its error did not repeat an underlying per-table cause.
- `analyze --index-only --force .` then succeeded in 82.3 seconds, reusing cached parser output for 781 files.
- Read-only verification after that recovery found all 22 configured FTS indexes in `SHOW_INDEXES`, with the expected indexed columns. A direct `QUERY_FTS_INDEX` call on `Property.property_fts` returned results, and an ordinary CLI query completed with BM25 timing and no degraded-search warning.

Impact: normal incremental maintenance temporarily disabled keyword search and required a full rebuild. Graph indexing completed; this report does **not** establish graph corruption or data loss.

### Steps to reproduce

This is the observed sequence, **not yet a reduced or deterministic reproduction**:

1. Start with an existing healthy index in a linked Git worktree of a Swift-heavy repository (about 2.7k covered files / 52.6k graph nodes).
2. Change two Swift files and one Markdown file, then run `gitnexus analyze --index-only .` from that worktree. The logged plan was `changed=3, added=0, deleted=0`.
3. Observe the Property FTS failure below and the degraded keyword-search warning.
4. Run `gitnexus analyze --index-only --repair-fts .`; observe the missing-index failure below.
5. Run `gitnexus analyze --index-only --force .`; observe successful graph/FTS reconstruction.
6. Verify with `gitnexus doctor`, `CALL SHOW_INDEXES() RETURN *`, and `CALL QUERY_FTS_INDEX('Property', 'property_fts', '<known-property-name>') RETURN node.name, score LIMIT 5` through the CLI, using the exact worktree with `--repo`.

The three changed files at the recovered revision all strictly decode as UTF-8, with no NUL bytes or replacement characters. That rules out malformed bytes in those three final files; it does not prove every stored field or intermediate native string was valid. The failed database was already replaced by the successful recovery, so it is unavailable for row-level comparison. No new failure was induced in the active review worktree.

### Environment

- GitNexus: 1.6.12, installed npm distribution; this is the latest published release observed during diagnosis.
- LadybugDB: 0.18.3 (matches the dependency pinned by GitNexus's v1.6.12 tag).
- Node: v26.8.2.
- macOS: 26.6.2 (25G83), arm64, 16 KiB page size.
- Doctor: native graph store, FTS, and VECTOR extensions available; extension policy load-only/offline.
- Disk: approximately 257 GiB available when checked.
- Successful recovery: 52,651 nodes / 655,073 edges / 1,092 clusters / 724 flows.

### Logs / screenshots

Incremental analysis:

```text
Incremental: changed=3, added=0, deleted=0 (skipping wipe + 2713 unchanged file rows preserved)
FTS index build failed (FTS index build failed for 1 of 22 tables: Property.property_fts (Runtime exception: Failed calling LOWER: Invalid UTF-8.)) — keyword search degraded this run. Graph and embeddings analysis completed successfully. Run `gitnexus analyze --repair-fts` to retry.

Warning: full-text/BM25 search is disabled — the search index build failed this run.
The FTS extension is available; rerun `gitnexus analyze --repair-fts`.
```

Targeted repair:

```text
Analysis failed: FTS repair failed - missing indexes after rebuild: Property.property_fts. Run `gitnexus analyze --force` to perform a full graph+FTS rebuild; if that also fails, verify FTS extension availability via `gitnexus doctor`.
```

Successful recovery:

```text
Rebuilt the graph and FTS while reusing cached parser output for 781 file(s) (parse cache 99+1.6.12).
Repository indexed successfully (82.3s)
52,651 nodes | 655,073 edges | 1092 clusters | 724 flows
```

Diagnosis is bounded to the incremental graph/FTS path and failed targeted recovery. Whether the native tokenizer received bad persisted content, encountered an internal string/scan defect, or left partial FTS state requires upstream investigation. Full rebuild is a verified workaround here, not proof that the underlying defect is fixed.

title: fix(augment): recover symbols missed by FTS file ranking
body:
## What changed

- run the graph-name fallback whenever the top BM25-ranked files contain no matching symbol definition
- rank exact symbol names ahead of partial `CONTAINS` matches
- replace the former FTS-available early-return assertion with recovery coverage and add the widely-referenced-symbol regression

## Why

FTS ranks files by mentions. For widely used symbols, caller/test files can occupy the top results while the definition file is absent, leaving `symbolMatches` empty even though the graph contains an exact-name node. This makes `augment` return an empty result precisely for central symbols.

Closes #3416.

## Verification

- base regression: new exact-name test failed with `expected '' to contain '[GitNexus]'`
- `cd gitnexus && npm test -- --run test/integration/augmentation.test.ts` — 17/17 passed
- `npx prettier --check gitnexus/src/core/augmentation/engine.ts gitnexus/test/integration/augmentation.test.ts`
- `npx eslint gitnexus/src/core/augmentation/engine.ts gitnexus/test/integration/augmentation.test.ts` — no errors (one pre-existing non-null-assertion warning in `engine.ts`)

## Risk / rollback

The fallback adds one bounded graph query only when the BM25 file-to-symbol mapping found no match; the query remains capped at five rows and uses the existing escaped pattern. Reverting this PR restores the previous early-return behavior.

AI-assisted contribution: implementation and tests were prepared with coding-agent assistance and independently exercised against the real LadybugDB integration fixture.

title: Incremental refresh reports current but unchanged symbols become unresolvable
body:
### Area

gitnexus (CLI / core / indexing / MCP server)

### Summary

An incremental refresh can report current content while both CLI and MCP context cannot resolve a previously resolvable unchanged function; a full rebuild restores lookup without source edits.

### Context

Observed during ordinary code analysis. This report describes the retained failure sequence using generic names and paths. The original repository and artifacts are confidential; no application source, original symbol names, private links, commit IDs, or local identity paths are included. A standalone deterministic reproducer has not yet been reduced.

### Expected behavior

An incremental refresh preserves unchanged symbol lookup. If lookup/index state is incomplete, freshness must expose that limitation.

### Actual behavior

Incremental analysis exits 0; freshness matches the current commit and all covered files, but both name-based context and direct-UID context fail. A native forced rebuild restores the same function and its two callers. No FTS/UTF-8 error was logged in this occurrence.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Start with a healthy index in a linked Git worktree of a mixed Swift/Python repository (about 2.7k covered files). Verify a production function and its two callers with `gitnexus context <known-function> --repo <absolute-root>`.
2. Change only a test file; leave that function and its callers unchanged.
3. Run `gitnexus analyze --index-only .` from the exact root. The observed plan was `changed=1, added=0, deleted=0`; 740 importers were added to the writable set.
4. Run `gitnexus status`; it reports current content. Retry CLI and MCP context by name and by the previously returned UID.
5. Run `gitnexus analyze --force --index-only .`, then retry the same lookup.

### Environment

- GitNexus 1.6.12, installed CLI.
- macOS arm64.
- Node.js 26.8.2.
- Exact-root index-only analysis, with freshness checked before querying.

### Logs / screenshots

```text
Incremental analysis: exit 0
Freshness: current commit/content across 2,715 files
CLI and MCP context: Symbol not found
Forced full rebuild: success in 74.7 seconds
Context after rebuild: original function and both callers resolve
```

This is an observed lookup failure, not proof that graph nodes were missing. Related #3032 concerned moved Python symbols on 1.6.9 and is closed; this occurrence is on 1.6.12, involves unchanged Swift source, and has no reported UTF-8 failure. #3421 separately tracks the Property FTS failure.

title: Swift injected closure-property invocation resolves to an unrelated same-name method
body:
### Area

gitnexus (CLI / core / indexing / MCP server)

### Summary

A call to an injected Swift closure property is reported as an exact outgoing edge to an unrelated same-name method.

### Context

Observed during ordinary code analysis. This report describes the retained failure sequence using generic names and paths. The original repository and artifacts are confidential; no application source, original symbol names, private links, commit IDs, or local identity paths are included. A standalone reproduction is included below and was compiled and executed on 2026-09-30.

### Expected behavior

Honor the lexical closure-property binding. If the injected callable target cannot be statically resolved, preserve uncertainty instead of selecting an unrelated method.

### Actual behavior

Two independent context invocations against the fresh index identified the expected enclosing method but returned an unrelated helper type's same-name method as an outgoing callee, with `epistemic: exact`. Source inspection established a stored closure initialized by constructor injection.

### Steps to reproduce

1. In a Swift repository, declare a stored closure property such as `private let clock: @MainActor @Sendable () -> Date`, assign it from an initializer parameter, and invoke `clock()` inside an instance method.
2. Include an unrelated type with a same-name `clock()` method elsewhere in the workspace. These generic names describe the observed binding shape; they have not been verified as a reduced reproducer.
3. Run `gitnexus analyze --index-only .` and verify exact-root freshness.
4. Query the invoking method with `gitnexus context <method> --file Service.swift --repo <absolute-root>`.
5. Inspect its outgoing call target and epistemic metadata.

### Environment

- GitNexus 1.6.11 in the original occurrence; standalone reproduction confirmed on 1.6.12.
- macOS arm64.
- Node.js 26.8.2.
- Exact-root index-only analysis, with freshness checked before querying.

### Logs / screenshots

```text
Selected enclosing method: correct
Outgoing target: unrelated same-name method
epistemic: exact
```

The runtime injection path was established by inspecting the stored property, both initializer assignments, the call site, and the composition-root closure. No runtime failure is attributed to this graph defect.

### Confirmed standalone reproduction on 1.6.12

The following independent example contains no application code. `swiftc -warnings-as-errors` succeeds, and the executable prints `passed`. A fresh index nevertheless attributes `Service.refreshValue`'s `clock()` to `Other.clock`. This reduced context reports `epistemic: lower-bound` for an unresolved incoming chained receiver; that completeness boundary does not make the outgoing decoy a valid callee.

`Caller.swift`:

```swift
import Foundation

enum Example {
    static func runScenario() -> Int {
        makeValue(input: 1)
    }
}

final class Service {
    private let clock: () -> Date

    init(clock: @escaping () -> Date) {
        self.clock = clock
    }

    func refreshValue() -> Date {
        clock()
    }
}
```

`Helpers.swift`:

```swift
import Foundation

extension Example {
    static func makeValue(input: Int) -> Int {
        input + 1
    }
}

enum Other {
    private static func makeValue(other: String) -> Int {
        -1
    }
    static func clock() -> Date {
        Date.distantPast
    }
}
```

`main.swift`:

```swift
import Foundation
precondition(Example.runScenario() == 2)
let fixedDate = Date(timeIntervalSince1970: 100)
precondition(Service(clock: { fixedDate }).refreshValue() == fixedDate)
print("passed")
```

Run in the directory containing those files:

```sh
swiftc -warnings-as-errors Caller.swift Helpers.swift main.swift -o reproducer
./reproducer
gitnexus analyze --index-only .
gitnexus status
gitnexus context refreshValue --file Caller.swift --content --limit 10 --repo "$PWD"
```

Observed outgoing target:

```json
{"uid":"Function:Helpers.swift:Other.clock#0","name":"clock","filePath":"Helpers.swift"}
```

The same small index correctly resolves `Example.runScenario` to `Example.makeValue`; that control distinguishes this closure-property failure from simple concrete extension resolution.

body:
Bumps [i18next](https://github.com/i18next/i18next) from 26.3.6 to 26.4.2.
Release notes

Sourced from i18next's releases.

v26.4.2

  • fix: $&, $`, $' and $$ inside a nested value ($t(key)) now stay literal. nest() handed the resolved value straight to String.replace as the replacement argument, so those sequences were read as replacement patterns: $& re-inserted the $t(...) match, $` / $' inserted the text before / after it, and $$ collapsed to $. Through t() the $& case was worse than a wrong string: the nested lookup resets the shared nesting regexp, so the re-inserted $t(...) was matched again on every pass and t() never returned — also under the default escapeValue: true when the value arrives via a variable forwarded through nesting options ($t(key, { "name": "{{name}}" }) with a name containing $&). The value is now $-escaped at the String.replace call, the same guard interpolate() already has, and a non-string value returned by a formatter in the nesting chain ($t(key, myFormat)) is stringified before that. Nested values are still not HTML-escaped (#854). Thanks @​mahirhir (#2447).

v26.4.1

  • fix(types): the selector-form keyPrefix overload of getFixedT() is now available under enableSelector: 'strict'. Its constraint was gated on true | 'optimize' only, so under 'strict' it collapsed to never, the overload dropped out, and the returned t silently lost its keyPrefix scope (t(($) => $.deep) failed with Property 'deep' does not exist on type '{}'). The same call already typechecked under true and 'optimize'. Thanks @​hovelopin (#2446).

v26.4.0

  • perf: cache toResolveHierarchy results per (code, fallbackCode) pair. The hierarchy resolver runs on every t() call and calls Intl.getCanonicalLocales multiple times, which showed up prominently when profiling render-heavy UIs (e.g. virtualized data grids); with the cache the per-call cost drops from ~886 ns to ~41 ns. The cache is invalidated automatically when options.fallbackLng changes (reassignment or in-place array mutation); if you mutate other resolution-relevant options at runtime (load, lowerCaseLng, cleanCode, nonExplicitSupportedLngs), call i18next.services.languageUtils.clearCache() afterwards. Function-valued fallbackLng and per-call array/object fallbackLng options are never cached, so dynamic fallbacks keep working as before. Thanks @​equaterina (#2444).

title: fix(swift): avoid false calls for injected closure properties
body:
Fixes #3425.

Swift free-call fallback now respects a same-name stored property on the caller's type or a superclass, including calls from extensions in sibling files. The fixture also confirms the exact concrete extension target.

Validation: focused regression tests (7), Swift capture goldens (9), TypeScript typecheck, Prettier, and ESLint passed. The full Windows suite had 22,660 passing and 211 failing tests, including platform/native-dependent failures; the one Swift suite failure also reproduces without this change.

title: fix(config): honor nested .gitignore files during repository walks
body:
## Summary

analyze now applies .gitignore files below the repo root, each one scoped to its own directory, so a package or submodule's ignored output stops getting indexed.

## Motivation / context

Fixes #2675. only the root .gitignore was loaded, so something like `app/.gitignore` with `public/generated/` was ignored and the generated bundles got parsed and indexed. same for a plain monorepo package, not just submodules.

## Areas touched

- [x] `gitnexus/` (CLI / core / MCP server)
- [ ] `gitnexus-web/` (Vite / React UI)
- [ ] `.github/` (workflows, actions)
- [ ] `eval/` or other tooling
- [ ] Docs / agent config only (`AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `.cursor/`, `llms.txt`, etc.)

## Scope & constraints

**In scope**

- nested .gitignore files are read lazily per directory (glob's filter is sync), cached, and matched relative to their own directory, deepest first
- an explicit root .gitnexusignore negation still wins, and GITNEXUS_NO_GITIGNORE / noGitignore skips nested files too
- a nested `!rule` re-includes what the root .gitignore ignored, like git, while .gitnexusignore still wins over it (second commit, after the review bot's note)
- a symlinked .gitignore is not followed (git doesn't follow it either); unreadable files log a warning and count as no rules
- directories that are already pruned are never read, so no extra I/O inside node_modules etc

**Explicitly out of scope / not done here**

- stopping traversal at nested repo / submodule boundaries. the issue lists it as an option, but it changes what gets indexed for everyone, so leaving that call to you
- watch mode's predicate still uses root rules only (it only reloads on root control files, so nested rules there need a reload story)

## Implementation notes

each nested file gets its own `ignore` instance matched against a directory-relative path, instead of rewriting its patterns with a directory prefix. that avoids the newline split and escaped trailing space problems the review found on #3103.

## Testing & verification

- [ ] `cd gitnexus && npm test`
- [ ] `cd gitnexus && npm run test:integration` *(if core/indexing/MCP paths changed)*
- [x] `cd gitnexus && npx tsc --noEmit`
- [ ] `cd gitnexus-web && npm test` *(if web changed)*
- [ ] `cd gitnexus-web && npx tsc -b --noEmit` *(if web changed)*
- [ ] Manual / Playwright E2E *(note environment, see `gitnexus-web/e2e/`)*

what I ran instead of the full suites:

- `npx vitest run test/unit/ignore-service.test.ts`: 175 passed. 11 new tests; the behaviour ones fail on main, including a real walkRepositoryPaths run that still returns `app/public/generated/bundle.js`. the precedence ones from the review (root negation vs deeper ignore, nested negation vs root ignore, hardcoded defaults kept) fail on the earlier commits of this branch
- every unit and integration test file that touches the ignore service or the walker (14 files, incl. ignore-and-skip-e2e, index-content-drift, upload-filter-ignore-drift and the group extractors): 610 passed, also after merging current main. after the review commits: the ignore-service file plus the 4 walker/ignore unit files and the 2 matching integration files, 252 passed

## Risk & rollout

indexes that already contain files a nested .gitignore excludes will drop them on the next analyze (incremental runs see them as deleted). no new env vars, no CLI or MCP contract change.

title: fix(index): guard graph integrity and fail closed on incomplete risk
body:
## Summary

Prevent inconsistent incremental indexes from being published as current, and return `UNKNOWN`/partial change risk when changed source or runtime templates cannot be mapped to symbols. Upgrade LadybugDB to 0.21.1 while preserving graph API and database NULL contracts.

## Motivation / context

The original incident left an index marked current even though function identities and source ranges disagreed, FTS reported invalid UTF-8, and change detection returned zero symbols with LOW risk. A forced rebuild restored the expected symbols and impact results. These safeguards make that inconsistency an analysis failure instead of a trustworthy-looking index.

A reduced native-only fixture demonstrates a scan/primary-key lookup discrepancy with LadybugDB 0.18.3 after incremental COPY. The same fixture is healthy on 0.21.1; it does not establish that the original incident had exactly the same cause.

## Areas touched

- [x] `gitnexus/` (CLI / core / MCP server)
- [ ] `gitnexus-web/` (Vite / React UI)
- [ ] `.github/` (workflows, actions)
- [ ] `eval/` or other tooling
- [ ] Docs / agent config only (`AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `.cursor/`, `llms.txt`, etc.)

## Scope & constraints

**In scope**

- Verify retained and newly written node identities before FTS and again before publication; incomplete COPY writes fail even when warning retention is disabled.
- Publish freshness only after native close, atomic graph swap, and metadata save; preserve graph-dirty recovery when verification or finalization fails.
- Preserve `UNKNOWN`, `partial`, and `unmapped_files` for unmapped supported source and runtime templates, including renames.
- Keep JSON/NDJSON graph responses consistent while preserving stored NULLs, including unresolved destination addresses.
- Ship LadybugDB 0.21.1 with vendored FTS 0.21.0 and validate actual extension loading on supported platforms.
- Add native regression controls, reconciliation scaling checks, checkpoint recovery coverage, and complete CLI child-process failure diagnostics.

**Explicitly out of scope / not done here**

- Proving the precise native row/column corruption mechanism behind the original incident.
- Claiming that the engine upgrade alone fixes every corruption path.
- Weakening FTS assertions or adding retries to hide a failed child process.

## Implementation notes

Identity checks compare IDs, names, paths, and source ranges across complete single-label scans; counts alone cannot detect swapped fields. Relationships, source contents, and the separately maintained Folder/Community/Process/BasicBlock layers are outside this identity oracle.

A failed graph verification cannot be cleared by FTS-only repair. Failure-injection tests cover native close, graph swap, and metadata save for full and selective incremental publication. Metadata-save failure occurs after the graph swap, but must leave registry freshness unchanged.

Checkpoint fixtures release native query results before reopening, preserve the main database and WAL before close, and retain the original failure if cleanup also fails. FTS exit assertions now report `status`, `signal`, `error`, `stdout`, and `stderr` without changing their expectations or time budgets.

## Testing & verification

Evidence is pinned to the tested commits; the earlier scoped run was not repeated in full after the diagnostic-only commit.

| Evidence | Result |
| --- | --- |
| [CI run 36988226174](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/actions/runs/36988226174), head `f59ce033d5161fc38b4c04b01943039992046e92` | **Success**: Linux, macOS, and Windows shards; CI gate; coverage threshold; typecheck, lint, format, benchmarks, Node floor compatibility, and packaged-install checks |
| [macOS FTS job](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/actions/runs/36988226174/job/110778091392) | All 12 FTS E2E tests passed, including fresh-home/load-only; shard passed 886 tests with 6 skipped across 37 files |
| [Scoped safeguard validation](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/pull/3442#issuecomment-5948345813), head `e493968` | 564 tests across 37 files passed, plus build, TypeScript, scoped lint/format checks, and publication failure-injection coverage |
| [Latest local validation](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/pull/3442#issuecomment-5949058917), head `f59ce03` | 102 tests across 5 files passed: 12 FTS E2E tests and 90 API/CSV/native database contract tests; build, TypeScript, scoped lint/format, and diff checks passed |
| Child failure diagnostic probes | SIGTERM, ENOENT, and ETIMEDOUT remained distinguishable, with stdout/stderr retained |
| Latest diagnostic edit impact / `detect_changes` | LOW impact: one test-file caller, zero flows; change scan mapped one file and two symbols, with no partial result |

The [native reduction and scaling instructions](https://github.com/magyargergo/GitNexus/blob/f59ce033d5161fc38b4c04b01943039992046e92/gitnexus/bench/incremental-write-integrity/README.md) document fixture controls and measurement conditions:

| Native fixture phase | LadybugDB 0.18.3 incorrect tuples | LadybugDB 0.21.1 incorrect tuples |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Initial COPY + checkpoint (8,192 rows) | 0 | 0 |
| DELETE (8,128 rows; 64 expected missing) | 0 | 0 |
| Incremental COPY (8,192 rows) | 3,936 | 0 |
| Explicit checkpoint (8,192 rows) | 3,936 | 0 |
| Read-only reopen (8,192 rows) | 3,936 | 0 |

Reconciliation's initial measured normalized scaling was 1.206 against a budget of 2, at 16,384 and 65,536 nodes. This is a scaling guard, not a claim of faster indexing.

Reproduce from `gitnexus/`:

```sh
npm run build
npx tsc --noEmit
npx vitest run test/integration/fts-extension-e2e.test.ts
npx vitest run test/unit/api-graph-streaming.test.ts test/unit/csv-escaping.test.ts test/integration/lbug-core-adapter.test.ts test/integration/spring-destinations-lbug.test.ts
node --import tsx bench/incremental-write-integrity/measure.cjs --check
node bench/incremental-write-integrity/reproduce.cjs
```

## Risk & rollout

This changes graph persistence and publication behavior. Analysis now rejects inconsistent identity scans and requires graph recovery rather than recertifying the index through FTS repair. Existing suspect indexes should be rebuilt with `gitnexus analyze --force`; an already-current legacy index is not retroactively validated by installing the new package.

The original macOS failure returned `status: null` without signal/error diagnostics. It did not recur in the latest CI run, so its termination cause remains unknown; neither a timeout nor a native crash has been established.

All checks in the linked CI run passed. The separate Vercel status remains failed with “Authorization required to deploy”; deployment settings were not changed.

## Checklist

- [x] PR body meets repo minimum length
- [x] No secrets, tokens, or machine-specific paths committed
- `AGENTS.md` / overlays unchanged; header and changelog checklist is not applicable.

<!-- gitnexus-pr-summary:v1:start -->

---

### 📝 Summary by GitNexus

## Summary

*A broad core change around incremental graph publication and persistence, with impact extending well beyond the files being edited. The CRITICAL blast level calls for close review of how graph writes are reconciled and published.*

**🔴 CRITICAL blast radius. This appears to be a graph persistence and analysis change, reaching 75 dependents across direct and second-hop callers/importers.**

The change is concentrated in `gitnexus/src/core/lbug/lbug-adapter.ts` and `gitnexus/src/core/incremental/write-reconciliation.ts`, with related updates in `gitnexus/src/core/run-analyze.ts`. Review the graph write and publication path first, especially `loadGraphToLbug` and `runFullAnalysisInner`, then check the integration coverage in `gitnexus/test/integration/analyze-atomic-swap.test.ts` and `gitnexus/test/integration/lbug-interrupted-checkpoint-recovery.test.ts`.

Impact also reaches the `Lbug`, `Unit`, `Cli`, `Server`, `Storage`, `Local`, `Integration`, `Ingestion`, and `Search` modules. File risk is LOW, with no HIGH or CRITICAL risk files.

Updates `urllib3` from 2.7.0 to 2.8.0


Release notes

Sourced from urllib3's releases.




2.8.0


🚀 urllib3 is fundraising for HTTP/2 support


urllib3 is raising ~$40,000 USD to release HTTP/2 support and ensure long-term sustainable maintenance of the project. If your company or organization uses Python and would benefit from HTTP/2 support in Requests, pip, cloud SDKs, and thousands of other projects please consider contributing financially to ensure HTTP/2 support is developed sustainably and maintained for the long-haul.


Thank you for your support.


Security


Fixed the following security issues:


    

  • The TLS configuration for HTTPS proxies could be ignored or overridden. (High severity, GHSA-8988-9cw3-xx77)
    • 

  • HTTPResponse.stream() and read_chunked() could buffer a chunk-size line of unbounded length in memory. (High severity, GHSA-vxq7-64xx-v4gw)
    • 

  • Chunked Deflate streaming could enter an infinite loop. (Medium severity, GHSA-gh4c-6fx4-qh6g)
    • 





[!IMPORTANT]
urllib3 2.8.0 fixes HTTPS proxy TLS configuration being ignored or overridden by destination settings. Configurations relying on that behavior may require changes.


Configure proxy CA certificates and client certificates in proxy_ssl_context, and proxy identity checks with proxy_assert_hostname or proxy_assert_fingerprint. Destination client certificates and identity overrides no longer apply to HTTPS forwarding proxy connections.






[!NOTE]
CVE IDs had not yet been assigned to these advisories at the time of release due to a backlog at GitHub's CNA.




Deprecations & Removals


    

  • Deprecated using an empty collection as the Retry option allowed_methods to retry any verb. (#5044)
    • 



Features


    

  • Added Url.auth_decoded and Url.auth_decoded_joined convenience properties to the result of parse_url(). (#4945)
    • 

  • Added basic_auth_encoding and proxy_basic_auth_encoding parameters to urllib3.util.make_headers(). (#5092)
    • 



Bugfixes


    

  • 

    Fixed response header handling to replace obsolete folded header lines (obs-fold) with spaces in accordance with RFC 9112, preventing raw CRLF sequences from appearing in header values such as Set-Cookie. (#1362)
    

    • 

  • 

    Fixed usage of proxy_ssl_context with ProxyManager when use_forwarding_for_https=True. Passing ssl_context instead of proxy_ssl_context for HTTPS proxies in this configuration now emits a FutureWarning and will raise an error in v3.0. (#2577)
    

    • 

  • 

    Changed behavior of the default ConnectionPool.pool initialization. LifoQueue is now resolved from the queue module after the ConnectionPool is instantiated instead of using the default cached QueueCls class property. This is done because sometimes the queue.LifoQueue is monkey-patched late in the program, such as by gevent. (#3289)
    

    • 

  • 

    Raised UnrewindableBodyError instead of ValueError when retrying a request whose body had tell() but not seek(). (#3779)
    

    • 

  • 

    Decoded percent-encoded SOCKS proxy credentials before authenticating with the proxy server. (#3785)
    

    • 

  • 

    Fixed HTTPResponse.drain_conn() to discard unread response data in 64 KiB chunks (same as the default amt when doing HTTPResponse.stream(...)). (#5019)
    

    • 

  • 

    Fixed is_ipaddress() to detect non-standard IPv4 forms accepted by socket.connect, such as hex (0x7f000001), octal (0177.0.0.1), and decimal integers (2130706433), ensuring SSL certificate verification uses the correct mode for these addresses. (#5029)
    

    • 

  • 

    Fixed HTTPConnectionPool.urlopen raising a misleading FullPoolError instead of ValueError when called with an invalid timeout argument on a pool created with block=True. (#5059)
    

    • 

  • 

    Fixed port-zero handling to preserve explicit :0 values instead of substituting the default ports 80 or 443 in URL parsing, pool selection, proxy configuration, connection_from_url(), and HTTP/2 request authority. (#5071, #5101)
    

    • 

  • 

    Fixed a bug where PoolManager passed the assert_hostname and assert_fingerprint parameters to HTTP connection pools. (#5077)
    

    • 

  • 

    Fixed HTTPConnectionPool.urlopen() and HTTP proxy forwarding to strip URL fragments from absolute request targets before sending requests. (#5079)
    

    • 

  • 

    Added safeguards to the proxy tunneling code to prevent potential security issues when handling invalid characters in the proxy host and HTTP headers. This change affects users of Python 3.10, Python 3.11, and Python 3.12 when the standard library does not contain the fix; those on newer Python versions should upgrade to 3.13.14+ or 3.14.5+ to get the same security fixes. (#5091)
    

    • 

  • 

    Fixed HTTPSConnection.connect() overriding ProxyConfig.ssl_context's certificate policy and proxy identity checks with the target connection's TLS settings when forwarding through an HTTPS proxy.
    

    HTTPSConnection no longer applies target SNI, assertions, or client credentials to forwarding proxy handshakes and continues to use its ssl_context as a fallback when an HTTPS proxy forwards an HTTP target. (#5093)
    

    • 

  • 

    Fixed URL parsing to more strictly enforce RFC 3986 host syntax, rejecting invalid host input such as raw spaces and control characters, malformed percent-encodings, and percent-encoded control characters in HTTP(S) hosts and IPv6 zone identifiers, including proxy CONNECT tunnel targets. Host normalization now also follows RFC 3986 normalization rules for percent-encoded octets by decoding percent-encoded unreserved characters and uppercasing the hexadecimal digits of retained percent-encoded octets. (#5095)
    

    •

title: fix(staleness): detect rollback with one Git query
body:
## Summary

Related to #3127. A forward commit count of zero can mean that HEAD is older than the indexed commit. The staleness check previously reported that rollback as current.

`checkStaleness` and `checkStalenessAsync` now use one `git rev-list --left-right --count lastCommit...HEAD` query. Two zero counts mean current; indexed-only commits with no HEAD-only commits mean a stale, diverged index. A positive HEAD-only count retains the existing behind count, including divergent and shallow histories. Both counts use the same HEAD snapshot, and successful checks need one Git process.

Failed queries retain the existing HEAD fallback and fail-open values. The async query timeout and both fallback HEAD timeouts remain bounded.

### Credit

The bug was reported by [nikolai-vysotskyi](https://github.com/nikolai-vysotskyi) (maintainer of [trace-mcp](https://github.com/nikolai-vysotskyi/trace-mcp)) in [a comment on #3127](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/issues/3127#issuecomment-5576596012). That comment raised two issues with `checkStaleness`:

1. Every git failure collapsed into `{ isStale: false, commitsBehind: 0 }`, so a `--stale-policy error`-style flag would exit 0 exactly when the check itself was broken.
2. A `commitsBehind` count of `0` was treated as "index matches current tree," but a forward-only count can't tell a true match apart from a checkout of an older/divergent commit.

(1) was already fixed by #3257 (merged), which added the `current`/`behind`/`diverged`/`unknown` status channel this PR builds on. This PR addresses (2), the part that was still open.

The original issue (#3127) also proposes a `--stale-policy` CLI flag. This repo doesn't have a `query`/analogous CLI command matching the issue's example, and threading a new flag through "commands that consume indexed data" is a larger, separate design question the issue itself flags as needing discussion. This PR is scoped to the underlying correctness bug in the staleness check itself, which any such flag would depend on either way.

## Changes

- Classify both commit counts in a shared helper and return `unknown` for malformed output.
- Document the successful rollback case and the distinct fail-open `diverged` result after a Git failure.
- Render stale, diverged group rows as `STALE (index differs from HEAD)`.
- Keep missing disk and cached commit metadata `unknown` in the MCP context resource.
- Cover single-process queries, a concurrent HEAD change, current/rollback/behind count combinations, Git failures, and bounded fallback probes for both helpers. Real-Git rollback and shallow-clone coverage remains in place.

## Test plan

- [x] 137 tests passed across 11 focused staleness, MCP resource, and group suites at the tree published as `9cf8533`.
- [x] TypeScript (`tsc --noEmit`), ESLint, and Prettier passed; the local pre-commit checks also passed.
- [x] The complete published tree matches the locally tested commit.
- [ ] The full local suite was interrupted after several minutes without further progress in native ingestion tests; it is not claimed passing.

Graph change analysis mapped the production edits. Comment-only changes and one test assertion remained unmapped after reindexing and were checked manually.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

### 📝 Summary by GitNexus

## Summary

*This appears to be a core Git staleness logic change, accompanied by CLI, MCP, and test updates. Its reach is broad, so review should focus on the shared staleness computation and the code that presents its status.*

title: `tool_map` returns 0 tools for `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk` `registerTool(name, config, handler)`
body:
**Component:** `gitnexus analyze` → tools phase (`dist/core/ingestion/pipeline-phases/tools.js`)
**Version:** 1.6.12
**Severity:** Silent false negative — the tools phase reports success with an empty tool set

## Summary

The TypeScript/JavaScript fallback in the tools phase only recognises tool
declarations shaped like an object literal with a `name:` property:

```js
{ name: "my_tool", description: "...", inputSchema: { ... } }
```

The `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk` idiom passes the name as a **positional
argument**:

```ts
server.registerTool("my_tool", { title, description, inputSchema }, handler)
```

That shape matches nothing, so a repository that is entirely an MCP server can
index cleanly and still report `tool_map` → `{"tools": [], "total": 0}`.

## Reproduction

### Minimal

Two files in one repo, one per shape, indexed in a single `analyze` run:

`src/tools/positional.ts`
```ts
import { McpServer } from "@modelcontextprotocol/sdk/server/mcp.js";
import { z } from "zod";

export function registerPositional(server: McpServer): void {
  server.registerTool(
    "positional_tool",
    {
      title: "Positional",
      description: "Registered with the positional registerTool(name, config) form.",
      inputSchema: { query: z.string() },
    },
    async ({ query }) => ({ content: [{ type: "text", text: query }] }),
  );
}
```

`src/tools/objectform.ts`
```ts
import { z } from "zod";

export const objectFormTools = [
  {
    name: "object_form_tool",
    description: "Declared with an explicit name/description object.",
    inputSchema: { query: z.string() },
  },
];
```

```sh
gitnexus analyze --skip-fts --skip-agents-md .
# Repository indexed successfully — 8 nodes | 6 edges
```

`tool_map` for that repo:

```json
{
  "tools": [
    {
      "name": "object_form_tool",
      "filePath": "src/tools/objectform.ts",
      "description": "Declared with an explicit name/description object.",
      "flows": []
    }
  ],
  "total": 1
}
```

`positional_tool` is missing. Same repo, same run, same file-path filter — only
the declaration shape differs.

### Real-world

A private MCP server built on the same SDK (25 files / 799 symbols) registers
**11** tools via `server.registerTool(...)`, spread across four files in a
`src/tools/` directory. Every one of those files contains `inputSchema`, and
every path satisfies the `tool` filename filter, so both preconditions of the
heuristic are met.

`tool_map` reports `total: 0`.

The two preconditions of the heuristic *are* met — the files are under a `tools/`
directory and their contents contain `inputSchema` — so the path filter and the
`inputSchema` guard are not the cause here. Only the declaration shape is.

## Root cause

`dist/core/ingestion/pipeline-phases/tools.js`:

```js
// line 35-40
const toolCandidatePaths = allPaths.filter((p) =>
  (p.endsWith('.ts') || p.endsWith('.js')) &&
  p.toLowerCase().includes('tool') && ...);

// line 44
if (!content.includes('inputSchema')) continue;

// line 46
const toolPattern = /name:\s*['"](\w+)['"]\s*,\s*\n?\s*description:\s*[`'"]([\s\S]*?)[`'"]/g;
```

The pattern is anchored on the literal `name:` key, so a positional first
argument is invisible to it.

The other tool source, the parse phase, only emits definitions for **decorator**
tools (`dist/core/ingestion/workers/parse-worker.js:2194`, gated on `dec.isTool`),
which TS/JS `registerTool(...)` never produces. The fallback is therefore the
only path for this shape, and it does not cover it.

Verified directly — running both patterns over the reproduction files:

```
src/tools/positional.ts
  existing  -> []
  candidate -> [ 'positional_tool' ]
src/tools/objectform.ts
  existing  -> [ 'object_form_tool' ]
  candidate -> []
```

## Suggested fix

A second pattern alongside the existing one, for positional registration:

```js
// Positional registration: registerTool("name", { ... description: "..." })
const positionalPattern =
  /(?:registerTool|register_tool|addTool)\(\s*['"]([\w.\/-]+)['"]\s*,\s*\{[\s\S]{0,600}?description:\s*[`'"]([\s\S]*?)[`'"]/g;
```

The `{0,600}` bound keeps the match inside one call rather than running to a
later `description:` in the file. It is additive: the existing pattern still
handles the object form, and the shared `seenToolNames` set already dedupes.

A more complete fix would extract these in the parse phase from the AST
(`call_expression` with callee `registerTool`/`tool` and a string literal first
argument), which would also give a real `handlerNodeId` — the regex path can only
produce name, file, and description, so the resulting `Tool` node carries no
`HANDLES_TOOL` edge to its handler. Worth deciding explicitly which is intended.

Two related gaps, same fallback:

1. The older SDK form `server.tool("name", "description", paramsSchema, cb)` puts
   the description in the **second** positional slot, so it needs its own pattern.
2. The path filter requires `tool` in the filename, so tools registered inline in
   e.g. `src/server.ts` are skipped regardless of shape.

## Workaround

Until fixed, add a declarative array in a file whose path contains `tool`, using
the object shape the heuristic expects:

```ts
// src/tools/manifest.ts — indexed by the current heuristic
export const toolManifest = [
  { name: "search_knowledge", description: "…", inputSchema: { … } },
];
```

Note this only makes `tool_map` list the names; it does not create the
`HANDLES_TOOL` edge to the real handler, so `impact`/`trace` from the tool node
stay unavailable.

## Environment

| | |
|---|---|
| gitnexus | 1.6.12 (distribution build, `sha256:262cf80d…`) |
| Node | v22.22.3 |
| Platform | darwin arm64 |
| Repro repo | 3 files, 8 nodes, 6 edges, `--skip-fts` |
| Real repo | private, 25 files, 799 symbols, 2075 edges |

title: fix(communities): omit memberships for filtered singleton communities
body:
## Summary

Only return memberships whose community node is retained, preventing orphaned `MEMBER_OF` relationships. Preserve all Leiden assignments separately for CLI skill generation, including same-folder singleton fallback skills and their execution flows. Community detection, IDs, labels, ordering and statistics remain unchanged.

## Motivation and attribution

Singleton communities are omitted from the returned community nodes, but their memberships were previously still emitted. Filter graph memberships against the IDs of the community nodes actually returned, while keeping raw assignments available to skill generation.

Adapted from https://github.com/articultur/GitNexus/commit/68be7f65771c3dbdbde2828532f39f139f580b58. Original author and co-author credits are retained in the commit. The repository’s existing license applies.

## Scope

- `gitnexus/src/core/ingestion/community-processor.ts`: separate graph-safe `memberships` from all Leiden assignments in `rawMemberships`. The new field is optional for legacy producers.
- `gitnexus/src/cli/skill-gen.ts`: prefer raw assignments, falling back to `memberships` for legacy results. Preserve folder aggregation when all communities are filtered as singletons. Match execution flows by community ID or member IDs in process traces.
- `gitnexus/test/unit/community-processor.test.ts` and `gitnexus/test/unit/skill-gen.test.ts`: verify the membership contract, CLI fallback and generated skill content.

No dependency, database schema, workflow, web UI or language-support changes.

## Testing and verification

title: fix(setup): honour CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR for Claude Code config paths
body:
## Summary

`gitnexus setup` / `uninstall` now respect `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`. When it's set, the Claude Code MCP entry, skills, hooks and `settings.json` go under that dir, which is where Claude Code actually reads them from.

## Motivation / context

I keep my Claude config in `~/.config/claude` (`CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=~/.config/claude`). In that setup Claude Code reads user MCP servers from `$CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR/.claude.json`, not `~/.claude.json`, and settings/skills/hooks from `$CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` instead of `~/.claude/`. `setup` hardcoded the HOME paths, so on my machine it either wrote everything to files Claude never opens, or (no `~/.claude` at all) just said "Claude Code (not installed)". The devcontainer README in this repo already describes the same lookup rule ("With it set, Claude reads `$CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR/.claude.json`").

## Areas touched

- [x] `gitnexus/` (CLI / core / MCP server)
- [ ] `gitnexus-web/` (Vite / React UI)
- [ ] `.github/` (workflows, actions)
- [ ] `eval/` or other tooling
- [ ] Docs / agent config only (`AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `.cursor/`, `llms.txt`, etc.)

## Scope & constraints

**In scope**

- New `claudeConfigPaths(home, env)` in `cli/editor-targets.ts`. `getEditorTargets` and the `mcpTarget` / `skillTarget` / `hookTarget` lookups take an optional `env` (defaults to `process.env`) and build all four Claude paths from it.
- `setupClaudeCode` and `installClaudeCodeSkills` check for the same root instead of `~/.claude`. The hook installer already gated on `dirname(settingsFile)` so it follows on its own. `uninstall` only uses the factory, so no change there.
- Empty `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` = unset. A relative value is resolved against the cwd.
- README note under Editor Setup + CHANGELOG entry.

**Explicitly out of scope / not done here**

- `CODEX_HOME` has the same problem for `~/.codex/config.toml` and `hooks.json`. I'd rather do that as a separate PR once this one's shape is OK with you.
- The other harnesses (Cursor, OpenCode, …) — haven't checked which of them have a config-dir env var.

## Implementation notes

`vitest.config.ts` now sets `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR: ''` next to `GITNEXUS_LANG`. Without it, anyone running the suite from a shell with the variable set would have the HOME-sandboxed setup tests writing into their real Claude config. Caught that one just before it bit me. The tests that exercise the relocation set it themselves and put it back to `''` afterwards.

## Testing & verification

- [x] `cd gitnexus && npx vitest run test/unit/editor-targets.test.ts test/unit/setup.test.ts test/unit/uninstall.test.ts test/integration/setup-uninstall-roundtrip.test.ts test/integration/setup-skills.test.ts` → 108 passed. 9 of the 10 new tests were red before the change (the 10th is a guard that other editors stay on HOME).
- [x] `cd gitnexus && npx tsc --noEmit`
- [ ] `cd gitnexus && npm test`: still running locally. The only failures so far are 5 cases in `test/unit/incremental-orchestration.test.ts` (that file alone took ~44 min here). It doesn't import setup or editor-targets. I haven't checked them against `main` yet, CI will tell.

New tests: `test/unit/editor-targets.test.ts` (set / unset / empty / relative, plus "other editors untouched"), 3 cases in `setup.test.ts` (MCP file, skills + hooks, skip when the relocated dir is missing even if `~/.claude` exists), 1 in `uninstall.test.ts`.

## Risk & rollout

Nothing changes when `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` isn't set. When it is set, users who already ran `setup` have a stale entry in `~/.claude.json` / `~/.claude/` that Claude never read anyway. `uninstall` now looks in the relocated dir, so it won't clean up those old HOME copies. Happy to add a sweep of the old location if you think it's worth it.

## Checklist

- [x] PR body meets repo minimum length (workflow may label short descriptions)
- [ ] If `AGENTS.md` / overlays changed: headers, scope block, and changelog updated per project conventions
- [x] No secrets, tokens, or machine-specific paths committed

Merged `main` into the branch (da38059c) to clear the conflicts. Two things differ from the description above:

- `gitnexus/vitest.config.ts` keeps the `GITNEXUS_ATOMIC_INCREMENTAL` and `GITNEXUS_RC` pins from `main` next to `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR: ''`.

One test added: `getEditorTargets` reads `CODEX_HOME` from the injected env (the #3460 conflict resolution moved that lookup off `process.env` and nothing asserted it).

With the built CLI and Claude Code 2.1.325, `setup -c claude` under a relocated `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` wrote `.claude.json`, `settings.json`, `hooks/gitnexus` and `skills/` there, `claude mcp get gitnexus` found the entry in user config, and `uninstall --force` removed all of it.
