## Scope & constraints

**In scope**

- Reject missing, non-string, blank, NUL-containing, and exact-UID-mismatched lookup identities before enrichment or traversal.
- Preserve valid opaque IDs, existing not-found responses, and group impact's failure contract.

**Explicitly out of scope / not done here**

- Diagnosing the unavailable private macOS database or repairing incorrect relationships whose IDs are valid.
- Changing index persistence or group aggregation semantics.

## Implementation notes

The entire candidate set is rejected when any identity is invalid; silently dropping a corrupt row could make an unrelated candidate appear unambiguous. Returned IDs remain byte-for-byte unchanged.

## Testing & verification

- Regression tests demonstrated 57 failures before the fix; all 106 cases now pass.
- The final focused run passed 436 tests, including five native database cases proving Python/Swift caller isolation by file and UID.
- `cd gitnexus && npm test -- --maxWorkers=2` — 23,494 passed, 99 skipped, 7 failed across 1,149 files. Two failures were the dispatch fixtures corrected in this PR; the subsequent focused run passed all 436 tests. The other five failures occur in unchanged tests and were reproduced separately as described below.
- The existing AsyncAPI unreadable-directory test fails under the unrestricted root runner, which can read the mode-000 directory. An isolated rerun reproduced that failure under root; all 83 tests in the unchanged file passed in the restricted sandbox.
- Two existing worker-pool tests also fail in isolation: their expected size uses `os.cpus()` (9 CPUs here), while the unchanged implementation uses `os.availableParallelism()` (8 available CPUs), yielding 8 expected versus 7 actual workers. Neither the tests nor worker-pool implementation changed in this PR.
- Two unchanged tests in `git.test.ts` and `sibling-clone-drift.test.ts` also fail in isolation because their temporary-directory fixtures are detected inside an enclosing Git root, contrary to the tests' non-repository assumption.
- [x] `cd gitnexus && npx tsc --noEmit`
- [x] `cd gitnexus && npm run build`
- [x] `cd gitnexus-web && npm test -- --run` — 510 tests passed.
- [x] `cd gitnexus-web && npx tsc -b --noEmit`
- [x] `npx eslint .` — no errors; existing warnings remain.
- `detect-changes --scope all` mapped the production changes as expected. After rebuilding and retrying, it still reported unknown risk because the two edited callbacks in `calltool-dispatch.test.ts` have no mapped symbols. Direct diff review and the passing dispatch suite cover those test-only edits; this is not a clean graph check.
- Browser E2E: not applicable; no UI flows changed.

## Risk & rollout

The shared resolver serves context, impact, trace, rename, and PDG queries. Healthy identities keep their existing behavior; invalid index reads now fail explicitly. Affected users can run `gitnexus analyze --force` from their repository root. No schema migration is required.

- [x] No secrets, tokens, or machine-specific paths committed.

title: setup: replaces an existing HTTP (url) gitnexus MCP entry with stdio, dropping its auth headers
body:
## Summary

`gitnexus setup` unconditionally rewrites `mcpServers.gitnexus` (Claude Code, Cursor) and `[mcp_servers.gitnexus]` (Codex) with the stdio entry `{ command: <gitnexus>, args: ["mcp"] }`. If the user already pointed that entry at an HTTP server (`gitnexus mcp --http`, or a shared team server), the url is replaced, along with any auth headers or token settings. Setup reports `+ Claude Code` / `+ Codex` / `+ Cursor` and gives no warning.

Since `gitnexus mcp --http` (with `--auth-token`) is a supported way to run the server, I'd have expected setup to leave an existing HTTP entry alone, or at least warn, while still installing the skills and hooks. It isn't documented either way, so this may be intended. If so, I'd like to know the recommended way to get skills and hooks without losing an HTTP MCP entry.

## Reproduction (gitnexus 1.6.12 from npm, macOS, Node 26.10, sandboxed HOME)

```bash
H=$(mktemp -d); mkdir -p $H/.claude $H/.codex $H/.cursor
echo '{"mcpServers":{"gitnexus":{"type":"http","url":"http://127.0.0.1:4748/mcp"}}}' > $H/.claude.json
printf '[mcp_servers.gitnexus]\nurl = "http://127.0.0.1:4748/mcp"\n' > $H/.codex/config.toml
echo '{"mcpServers":{"gitnexus":{"url":"http://127.0.0.1:4748/mcp"}}}' > $H/.cursor/mcp.json
HOME=$H gitnexus setup -c claude,codex,cursor
jq -c .mcpServers.gitnexus $H/.claude.json $H/.cursor/mcp.json; cat $H/.codex/config.toml
```

**Expected:** the three HTTP entries stay as they were (skills and hooks still installed).
**Actual:** all three become `{"command":"/usr/local/bin/gitnexus","args":["mcp"]}` (TOML equivalent for Codex). Exit code 0, no warning.

I hit this on a real install first: a user-scope Claude Code `type: http` entry for a launchd-managed `gitnexus mcp --http` was turned back into stdio, so each Claude session started spawning its own server again.

## Variants tried

| Variant | Before | After `setup` |
|---|---|---|
| V1: HTTP entry, url only (Claude, Codex, Cursor) | `url` | stdio `command`/`args`; url gone |
| V2: HTTP entry with auth (`headers.Authorization` for Claude/Cursor, `bearer_token_env_var` for Codex) | `url` + auth | stdio; url **and auth settings** gone |
| V3: no entry (control) | — | stdio entry written (expected) |
| V4: HTTP entry under another name (`gitnexus-remote`) | `gitnexus-remote` | left alone, but a second `gitnexus` stdio server is added, so the tools are registered twice |

The write goes through `mergeJsoncFile(mcpPath, keyPath, getMcpEntry())` in `src/cli/setup.ts` (Claude Code path around `setupClaudeCode`). It merges at the key, so anything already under `gitnexus` is replaced.

## Possible directions (no strong opinion)

- Skip the MCP write when the existing `gitnexus` entry has a `url` (or `type: http`/`sse`), and say so in the summary (e.g. `= Claude Code (existing HTTP entry kept)`).
- Or a flag such as `--skip-mcp` / `--keep-mcp` to install only skills and hooks.

Happy to send a PR for whichever you prefer.

title: docs(mcp): document --http for multi-client setups (one server, many clients)
body:
## Problem

`gitnexus mcp` supports two transports:
- **stdio** (default) - `gitnexus mcp`
- **Streamable HTTP + SSE** - `gitnexus mcp --http [--host] [--port] [--auth-token]`

The HTTP mode works and is production-ready (we run it). But the docs steer
overwhelmingly toward stdio:
- `README.md:407` - `gitnexus mcp  # Start MCP server (stdio) - serves all indexed repos`
- `README.md:1130` - the Agent Interface table lists `MCP (stdio)` as *the* agent interface
- `--http` appeared only in a `GITNEXUS_MCP_AUTH_TOKEN` env-var row, in the context of
  remote/proxied deployments - not as the local multi-client option.

The consequence is a footgun. MCP-over-stdio is **one server process per client** by
protocol design: each client spawns its own `gitnexus mcp` child with its own copy of the
index. A user wiring gitnexus into an agent framework with N concurrent workers silently
runs N full index servers. We made exactly this mistake ourselves before measuring it.

## Measured impact

Measured on a real install (WSL2, 5 cores, 3 indexed repos: 9router 24k symbols,
alexa-testsuite, hermes-meter), 5 concurrent clients issuing the same `query()`:

| | 1 shared `--http` server | 5 per-client stdio |
|---|---|---|
| wall time (5 clients) | **7.66 s** | 30.01 s (**3.9x slower**) |
| per-query latency | **5.5-5.8 s** | 24.7-25.5 s (**4.4x slower**) |
| server RSS | **517 MB, flat** | +514 MB for 5 (**~103 MB/client**) |
| tools per client | 17 | 17 |

Both modes returned identical payloads. The shared server is ~4x faster and the 5th
concurrent client costs **0 MB** instead of ~103 MB.

## This PR (docs only, no code)

1. **`README.md` everyday-commands**: flags both forms, marking stdio as per-client.
2. **New "Multi-client setups" subsection**: why stdio duplicates, how to run `--http`,
   how to point clients at it, the loopback + `--auth-token` requirement for non-loopback
   binds, and the measured numbers.
3. **Agent Interface table**: `MCP (stdio, or HTTP for multi-client)`.

## Suggested follow-up (not in this PR)

A one-line hint in `gitnexus mcp --help` - e.g. *"stdio starts one server per client; use
`--http` to share a single server across clients"* - would prevent this at the point of
use, which is where we missed it. Happy to open that as a separate PR if you prefer.

## Notes

- We run the `--http` mode in production on our side (Hermes Agent, one systemd-managed
  shared server for all profiles and workers) and can supply the benchmark harness or raw
  logs if useful.
- Happy to split or reshape this if you'd rather take it as an issue first.

## Environment

- gitnexus 1.6.12
- Client: Hermes Agent (supports Streamable HTTP / SSE)
- Host: 5 cores, 16 GB, WSL2

<!-- gitnexus-pr-summary:v1:start -->

---

### 📝 Summary by GitNexus

title: Interrupted staged embedding run: the retry re-embeds every chunk (even on resume), and meta.json keeps the staging DB's count
body:
**Version:** 1.6.12. The code involved is unchanged on `main` at 668fac7: `saveEmbeddingCheckpoint` and the staged-build catch path in `gitnexus/src/core/run-analyze.ts`, and `sweepStagingArtifacts` in `storage/index-lock.ts`.
**Embedder:** HTTP, Voyage `voyage-code-4` (1024 dimensions, billed per token).

### Summary
On macOS and Linux, a full rebuild writes into `lbug.staging.<uuid>` and publishes it with the end-of-run swap. (Windows builds in place unless `GITNEXUS_ATOMIC_WINDOWS_SWAP=1`.) If the run dies during Phase 4, two things go wrong.

1. **The vectors it already paid for are thrown away, even when the retry says it is resuming.**
   - On a handled failure, the run's catch block wipes the staging DB (the best-effort #2841 reclaim). After a hard crash, the next run's lock acquisition sweeps it.
   - Either way, the retry's reuse cache comes only from the published DB's `CodeEmbedding` rows.
   - When the published index has no embeddings yet (a first embedding pass), the retry embeds every chunk again. That holds with `--force` and also on a plain resume. The resume logs `resuming from persisted hashes and regenerating 3122 pending node(s)` and then sends every chunk (repro below).
   - If the failure is deterministic, such as a resource limit, each retry pays for the same vectors again before failing at the same point.
2. **meta.json reports the staging DB's embedding count.**
   - The post-window `onCheckpoint` measures `stats.embeddings` in the unpublished staging DB and writes it to meta.json, next to the interrupted `embeddingCheckpoint`. After a crash, meta.json claims embeddings the published index does not have.
   - The comment above `saveEmbeddingCheckpoint` states the rule "Freshness fields may only advance once the index is published". #2790 applied it to `lastCommit` and `fileHashes`, but `stats.embeddings` still moves early.
   - `_deriveEmbeddingMode` reads that field on the next run, as does any tool that reads meta.json. Our own wrapper refused the retry because of it.

### Minimal repro (no provider calls)
Setup:
- a scratch `GITNEXUS_HOME`;
- a local fake OpenAI-compatible `/embeddings` endpoint that counts the input texts it receives;
- a repo with 8,130 embeddable nodes (8,626 chunks).

Every step runs `analyze <repo> --index-only` plus the flags shown. In step 1 the analyze worker is sent SIGKILL as soon as meta.json shows the first post-window checkpoint, to stand in for an OOM kill or a crash.

| Step | Texts sent | meta.json afterwards | Published DB `CodeEmbedding` rows |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0. `analyze <repo> --index-only` | 0 | `stats.embeddings: 0` | 0 |
| 1. `... --force --embeddings 0`, worker killed | 5,512 | `stats.embeddings: 5504`, `embeddingCheckpoint: {kind: "interrupted", nodesProcessed: 5008, totalNodes: 8130}` | 0 (1 staging file left) |
| 2a. Retry with the same command (`--force` discards the checkpoint) | **8,626** | `stats.embeddings: 8626` | 8,626 |
| 2b. Retry without `--force` (a fresh run of steps 0–1, then a resume) | **8,626** | `stats.embeddings: 8626` | 8,626 |

Both retries logged `Cleared 1 orphaned index-staging file(s) from a prior interrupted analyze`. Retry 2b also logged:
- `Previous analyze ended at an embedding checkpoint (5008/8130 nodes); resuming from persisted hashes and regenerating 3122 pending node(s).`
- `Previous analyze run did not complete cleanly (incrementalInProgress flag set) ... forcing full rebuild`.

Both retries re-sent all 8,626 chunks, including the 5,504 that step 1 had already embedded.

### What happened to us
- Our first `analyze --force --index-only --embeddings 0` ran on a repo of about 306k nodes that already had a graph-only index.
- About 100k vectors in, a WAL checkpoint threw `Maximum database size of 17179869184 bytes has been reached`, the default 16 GiB `LBUG_MAX_DB_SIZE`. The staging file was only about 1.9 GB at that point, and it reached 2.8 GB once fully embedded. So something other than the file size used up the cap. We did not investigate further.
- The published index correctly stayed graph-only, while meta.json said `stats.embeddings: 96653`.
- The staging files survived that failure, and the next analyze cleared them (`Cleared 4 orphaned index-staging file(s)`). We had cloned them first, so we could salvage the vectors (below).

### Suggestions
- **Reuse the staged vectors.** When an interrupted checkpoint with a matching identity exists, harvest the orphaned staging DB's `CodeEmbedding` rows before sweeping it.
  - Index them by `nodeId`, with `contentHash` for freshness, like the published DB's rows.
  - Limit the harvest to nodes the checkpoint marks complete, because a node's chunk set can be partial inside the interrupted window.
  - The #2841 reclaim could likewise leave the staging DB for the next run to harvest once Phase 4 has started.
- **Keep the staged count out of `stats.embeddings`** until the swap publishes the index. A progress count could live in the checkpoint instead, for example `embeddingCheckpoint.stagedEmbeddings`.
- **Make the resume log match the work.** Today it promises 3,122 nodes and regenerates all 8,130.
- **Name `GITNEXUS_LBUG_MAX_DB_SIZE` in the max-size error.** With `GITNEXUS_LBUG_MAX_DB_SIZE=137438953472` (128 GiB, analyze only), the same repo (245k vectors) and another with 267k vectors both completed.

### Workaround we used
1. Clone (APFS `cp -c`) the orphaned `lbug.staging.<uuid>` base file, without its sidecars, before any retry.
2. Open the clone without WAL replay (its WAL was corrupt), and check its vector and graph counts.
3. Run `CREATE_VECTOR_INDEX` and `CHECKPOINT`.
4. Install it as the live `lbug`, keeping a backup.

The retry reused all 99,681 staged vectors and embedded only the rest. This worked for us after validating the counts; we are not proposing WAL-less opens as a general recovery procedure.

title: Default MCP vector cutoff (0.6) leaves hybrid search close to BM25-only with voyage-code-4
body:
**Version:** 1.6.12. On `main` at 668fac7, `DEFAULT_MCP_VECTOR_MAX_DISTANCE` is still `0.6`.
**Embedder:** HTTP, Voyage `voyage-code-4` (1024 dimensions).

#2332 (fixed by #2330) added `GITNEXUS_VECTOR_MAX_DISTANCE`, which makes the vector cutoff configurable. Raising it fixed search for us. This issue is a data point about the default.

At the default cutoff, hybrid `query` (the same backend path as the MCP tool) behaved almost like BM25 alone in our sample. For 28 of 40 queries, the first five `definitions` names were identical to a run with the vector leg returning nothing. We did not record raw distances. The way recall changes with the cutoff suggests that, for `voyage-code-4`, most query-to-code matches sit above 0.6.

**Probe**
- 8 repos. In each one, 4 non-test target symbols, each with a paraphrased query that shares no tokens with the symbol's name, plus 1 exact-name control.
- Every query ran through `gitnexus query --limit 10` with `GITNEXUS_VECTOR_MAX_DISTANCE` set to the values below.
- A target counts as found if it is in the top 10 of `definitions` or `process_symbols`.

| Search | Paraphrased targets found (of 32) | Queries whose first five `definitions` names equal BM25-only (of 40) |
|---|---|---|
| BM25 only (vector leg returning nothing) | 17 | – |
| Hybrid, cutoff 0.6 (default) | 20 | 28 |
| Hybrid, cutoff 0.8 | 25 | 2 |
| Hybrid, cutoff 1.0 | 28 | 0 |
| Hybrid, cutoff 2.0 | 28 | 0 |

Effects of the cutoff:
- The exact-name controls were found 8/8 at every cutoff.
- Going from 0.6 to 1.0 moved the target up for 20 of the 40 queries and down for 5. Four of those 5 dropped one place, two of them exact-name controls. One paraphrased target fell from 1st to 12th.
- So a higher cutoff is not free, but on balance it was much better here.

**Suggestions.** Any of these would have saved us the investigation:
- a model-aware default, or a looser one when an HTTP embedder is configured;
- fusing the top-k vector hits with no hard distance filter, or a much looser one;
- a line in the env-var docs saying the right value depends on the embedding model (`voyage-code-4` needed about 0.8–1.0 in this test).

**Caveats**
- Small sample (32 paraphrased queries, one model).
- The queries were written by agents that had read the code.
- Requests did not send Voyage's `input_type`.
- We recorded target positions and the first five names, not raw distances.

title: fix(group): join gin/echo route-group prefixes and accept method-value handlers in Go HTTP providers
body:
## Summary

The Go group-mode HTTP plugin (`http-patterns/go.ts`) now emits framework routes whose handler is a method value or package function (`h.List`, `handlers.List`), and prefixes each route with every enclosing `Group("/p")` bound in the same function.

Since #3417, group contracts read Go routes from the graph (Strategy A) and the source-scan plugin only supplements them (Strategy B). The unfixed plugin still ships Strategy B output with group-relative paths: those ids do not collide with the graph's correct ids, so they survive the merge as extra contracts with wrong paths (measured: 8 on a real gin backend). This PR makes Strategy B agree with Strategy A, and keeps it a correct standalone source for repos whose index has no Go `Route` nodes (indexes built before #3417, or routes the extractor declines).

## Motivation / context

Two gaps in `go-framework-route` broke the source-scan side of Go HTTP linking for idiomatic gin/echo code:

1. **Method-value handlers were dropped.** The handler capture only accepted `(identifier)` or `(func_literal)`. `admin.POST("/x", matchHandler.UnfinalizeRoundHandle)` is a `selector_expression`, so the route produced no provider at all. This is the most common gin shape: 245 of the 254 routes in the real project we measured use it.
2. **Route-group prefixes were ignored.** Only the literal at the call site was used, so `v1 := r.Group("/api/v1"); admin := v1.Group("/admin"); admin.POST("/seasons/:id/unfinalize", …)` became `/seasons/{param}/unfinalize`.

On a freshly analyzed repo, #3417 masks both gaps — the graph supplies correct, fully-prefixed ids. They are not fixed in the plugin, and Strategy B output still ships, where it does two kinds of harm today:

- **Wrong paths survive the merge.** Graph entries win only when the contract id collides. The unfixed plugin drops the `Group("/api/v1")` prefix, so `v1.GET("/health", …)` reaches `findMatchingKeys` as `http::GET::/health` — a different id from the graph's `http::GET::/api/v1/health`. Both are kept: a false contract that can exact-match a consumer legitimately calling `/health` elsewhere, and that contradicts the `Route` node for the same route.
- **Strategy B is the only source when the graph has no Go routes** — an index built by a GitNexus older than #3417, or a registration the ingestion extractor declines (fail-closed). There the unfixed plugin yields no usable links at all (measured below: 0).

Refs #1668. That issue covers the same `selector_expression` gap for `HandleFunc`. This PR fixes it for framework routes only; the `HandleFunc` operand and handler constraints are unchanged.

## Areas touched

- [x] `gitnexus/` (CLI / core / MCP server)
- [ ] `gitnexus-web/` (Vite / React UI)
- [ ] `.github/` (workflows, actions)
- [ ] `eval/` or other tooling
- [ ] Docs / agent config only

## Scope & constraints

**In scope**

- `go-framework-route` accepts `selector_expression` handlers. The handler name is the selector's field, because the group layer resolves providers by name only (file-scoped, then unique repo-wide), and the operand is usually a local variable (`matchHandler := NewMatchHandler(…)`), not the receiver type. The last-argument anchor is unchanged, so variadic gin middleware before the handler is still not taken for the handler.
- Group prefixes: the route receiver is followed back through `:=`, `=`, and `var` bindings to `x.Group("literal", mw...)` calls. This covers nested groups at any depth, `Group("")` middleware-only groups, `{ }` blocks, closures inside the function, and a `Group(...)` chained directly onto the route call. Lookup is lexical: the nearest binding that precedes the call site in the enclosing blocks, stopping at the function declaration and at closure parameters that shadow the name.
- echo's `e.Group("/p")` has the same shape and goes through the same code (covered by a test).

**Explicitly out of scope / not done here**

- **Groups passed to another function** (`registerAdmin(v1)`): inside the callee the group is a parameter and contributes no prefix. The route keeps the prefix that is visible in that function, which is its literal path when the receiver is the parameter itself. This is documented in the code. Cross-function propagation would need a call-site pass (`prepareRepo`) and has to handle callees invoked with several different groups.
- **Receivers not bound to a literal-prefix `Group(...)`** (constructor calls, `Group(prefixVar)`, struct fields): no prefix is guessed. Same behavior as today.
- **chi**: chi registers routes with `r.Get`/`r.Post` (mixed case), which this query never matched, so chi routes are not extracted today with or without this change. `r.Route("/p", func(r chi.Router){…})` would need its own receiver-to-closure-parameter binding. Left for a follow-up. (The old header comment claimed chi shares the gin shape. It doesn't, so the comment now lists gin and echo only.)
- **echo route-level middleware**: echo's signature is `GET(path, h, m...)`, so with trailing middleware the last-argument anchor binds a middleware. This bug predates this PR and is not changed here.
- **Ingestion-side Go routes** (`route_map`, `Route` nodes, `impact` `affected_routes`): landed as #3417 (closing #3402). This PR does not duplicate it — #3417 touches ingestion only and leaves `http-patterns/go.ts` unchanged; the two layers still do not share code.
- **`_test.go` registrations**: the 3 test-file provider contracts behave the same before and after this PR (neither layer traces the group they sit in). Not addressed here.
- Consumer-side gaps seen on the same project (below) are not addressed.

## Implementation notes

- All logic stays in the Go plugin, with no orchestrator, matcher or type changes. `scan()` keeps its unary shape, and there is no `prepareRepo`.
- The prefix walk runs per route over the enclosing blocks' preceding statements. It is bounded by the function body and a recursion cap (`MAX_GROUP_DEPTH`) against pathological chains. No extra parse is needed.
- Path join matches gin's `joinPaths` for the relevant cases: `Group("")` adds nothing, `GET("")` resolves to the group path, and duplicate slashes at the join are collapsed.
- A method value whose name is shared by several handler types (e.g. `Login` on two handlers) resolves to no symbol, because the unique-name rung declines to guess. The contract is still emitted, with the name and file-level fallback. That is the existing behavior for ambiguous names.
- After this PR, a plugin-emitted Go contract id collides with the graph's id for the same route, so the graph entry wins the merge (richer metadata) instead of both surviving.

## Testing & verification

- [x] Rebased on current `main` (incl. #3417): `test/unit/group/go-gin-route-groups.test.ts` + `test/unit/group/http-route-extractor.test.ts` → 224 passed; `tsc --noEmit` shows only pre-existing `main` errors in ingestion files this PR does not touch; `prettier --check` and `eslint` clean on the changed files. (Full-suite run not re-done on this machine; the pre-rebase full run failed only in 3 unrelated env-dependent files.)
- [x] New `test/unit/group/go-gin-route-groups.test.ts` (21 tests, written first; verified failing on the pre-change plugin, and the 2 that passed pin the unchanged literal-path fallbacks). Coverage:
  - the real gin `RegisterRoutes` shapes: selector / identifier / package-func / inline handlers, variadic middleware, 3-level nesting, `Group("")` with and without middleware, `{ }` blocks, and an engine-root route outside any group;
  - `=` and `var` bindings, a chained `Group().GET()`, sibling-block shadowing, reassignment order, closure capture;
  - the no-guess cases: parameter receiver, non-`Group` binding, a group bound in another function, and a non-literal prefix;
  - echo groups;
  - an end-to-end pairing through `HttpRouteExtractor` + `runExactMatch`: the grouped provider `POST /api/v1/admin/seasons/:seasonId/rounds/:roundId/unfinalize → UnfinalizeRoundHandle` links to ``fetch(`${API_BASE}/api/v1/admin/seasons/${seasonId}/rounds/${roundId}/unfinalize`, { method: 'POST' })``.

**Measured on a real gin + React/Vite project** (254 gin routes, all under `r.Group("/api/v1")`, 245 method-value handlers). Both halves were copied to scratch repos and indexed with the CLI built from each side; `group sync`, then `group contracts --json`.

Against current `main` including #3417 (2026-10-03):

| | `main` | this branch |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Go provider contracts | 265 | 257 |
| … with the correct full path | 254 | 254 |
| … with a wrong path (missing group prefix) | **8** | **0** |
| … from `_test.go` (unchanged) | 3 | 3 |
| consumer contracts (unchanged) | 142 | 142 |
| exact cross-links | 107 | 107 |

Cross-links are unchanged because #3417's `Route` nodes already carry correct ids for the merge. The 8 wrong-path contracts on `main` come from real routes — `v1.GET("/health", …)` emitted as `http::GET::/health`, `v1.POST("/upload/avatar", …)` as `http::POST::/upload/avatar`, and 6 more uploads — each disagreeing with its own `Route` node. After this PR they emit `/api/v1/…`, collide with the graph id, and the graph entry wins.

Same project before #3417, where Strategy A produced no Go routes at all and the plugin was the only source:

| | `main` | this branch |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Go provider contracts | 10 | 257 |
| … with the full `/api/v1` prefix | 0 | 254 |
| exact cross-links | **0** | **108** |

That second table is the fallback case this PR keeps working: an older index, or a route the ingestion extractor declines, still links.

## Risk & rollout

- Group-mode only. It changes which provider contracts `group sync` emits for `.go` files; ingestion and `route_map` are untouched. Re-run `gitnexus group sync <group>` to pick it up. No reindex is needed.
- On a freshly analyzed repo the visible change is the removal of the 8 wrong-path duplicate contracts (ids like `http::GET::/health`); correct ids already matched before, so no working link is lost. Where the graph has no Go routes, grouped routes move from group-relative ids (never matchable) to full ids, which is where the 0 → 108 links above come from.
- More providers means more candidates for exact matching on older indexes. A false provider needs `<x>.GET("literal", handler)` with an upper-case verb as the last-argument shape, which is the same bar as before, now also accepting a selector handler.
- Rollback: revert the commit.

## Checklist

- [x] PR body meets repo minimum length
- [ ] If `AGENTS.md` / overlays changed: n/a
- [x] No secrets, tokens, or machine-specific paths committed

title: feat(cypher): add schema hints to query errors
body:
## Summary

Add optional schema hints to Cypher binder errors while preserving the original error text. Suggestions use existing schema constants and DDL, conservative spelling matches, and the repository schema resource.

## Motivation / context

Misspelled labels/properties currently return only native binder errors. Another common mistake is using CALLS as a relationship table instead of CodeRelation {type: 'CALLS'}.

Focused upstream adaptation of https://github.com/articultur/GitNexus/commit/17f71ead18710164fcbb5b94517552454edadede, replacing fork-maintained candidate lists with upstream schema and real backend entrypoint tests.

## Areas touched

- gitnexus/ (CLI / core / MCP server)

## Scope & constraints

- Add hint only to recognized missing-table/property errors
- Retain read-only and WAL recovery priority
- Leave successful queries, empty results, parser errors, and unrelated failures unchanged
- No query rewrite/retry, index rebuild, new dependencies, schema or license changes

## Implementation notes

A helper reads canonical table/relation names and column names from existing DDL. Suggestions are omitted for distant, ambiguous, very short, or long inputs. Property hints explain that properties vary by table because native errors identify an alias, not its table. The call site is the final LocalBackend.cypher error branch shared by MCP and executeCypher; existing diagnostics run first.

## Testing & verification

- Native LadybugDB regression cycle: missing-hint cases failed before implementation and passed afterward
- Targeted local-backend-calltool, local-backend and mcp-wal-feedback files: 89 passed, zero skipped; rerun after rebasing onto a47cd17
- Build, tsc --noEmit and Prettier passed; changed-file ESLint had zero errors and existing warnings
- Full npm test is INCOMPLETE: cloud execution stopped over potential embedding-network egress before terminal aggregate counts. This is not a full-suite pass
- One observed unrelated failure reproduced on unmodified upstream d1971cf and patched code: lbug-delete-nodes-for-files.test.ts, catalog-read fallback test at line 471. Both had 9 passed, 1 failed. This environment lacks optional VECTOR, so ensureEmbeddingRowDmlSafe() returns false instead of expected true. That adapter and test are unchanged

Native tests cover table/property misspellings, relationship syntax, conservative fallback, both backend entrypoints, parameter aliases, successful empty results and case-insensitive names. Error injection preserves WAL and wrapped read-only precedence.

## Risk & rollout

Shared backend entrypoint has a broad caller graph; the change only adds a field to specific error responses. No migration or reindexing. Reverting helper import/call restores previous output.

## Checklist

- Focused scope and verification limits documented
- No secrets, tokens or machine-specific paths committed
- Existing PolyForm Noncommercial license preserved

## Summary

Interrupted staged analysis can now reuse completed paid embeddings on a plain retry or `--force --embeddings`, instead of deleting them and submitting the same content again.

This follow-up builds on #3461 by @azizur100389. His checkpoint-count implementation is retained: published counts change only after the replacement index is published. #3461 passed review and required CI, then merged with its original commit preserved. This branch includes that merge in its history.

## Motivation / context

Fixes #3456. #3461 handles metadata publication; this PR adds recovery of durable staged vectors so retries avoid paying again for completed work.

## Areas touched

- [x] `gitnexus/` (CLI / core / MCP server)
- [ ] `gitnexus-web/` (Vite / React UI)
- [ ] `.github/` (workflows, actions)
- [ ] `eval/` or other tooling
- [ ] Docs / agent config only

## Scope & constraints

**In scope**

- Retain the checkpoint-referenced staging generation and recover complete, unchanged embedding groups with matching model, dimensions, provider, and schema.
- Exclude the entire interrupted window and inherited incomplete groups, including nodes whose restore partly failed.
- Preserve the prior durable source until the replacement is checkpointed and its reference saved.
- Preserve explicit drop, model-change, manual-checkpoint opt-out, and storage-alias behavior.
- Add Windows staged/in-place count coverage and real final-close/rename failure tests around #3461.
- Fix review feedback: read recovery metadata through one verified file handle, and close the native database if connection construction fails.

**Explicitly out of scope**

- Salvaging legacy stages without provenance or guessing which orphan is safe.
- Changing the database size limit. Size failures mention the existing `GITNEXUS_LBUG_MAX_DB_SIZE` setting.

## Implementation notes

Recovery opens the referenced database in an isolated child with strict WAL replay. Failed or timed-out extraction imports nothing and leaves the source intact. Accepted vectors use the existing spill-backed cache; a node is reusable only when all its chunks pass validation.

Metadata is opened once, checked against its file identity, read through that descriptor, and closed on every path. A replaced file or symlink is rejected. Native extraction approves its output only after both connection and database close successfully.

With manual WAL checkpoints disabled, analysis still completes; it retains any prior durable source and does not advertise the new uncheckpointed stage as recoverable.

title: Dart pubspec discovery always fails on macOS: ENOTDIR on /dev/fd/N
body:
### Area

gitnexus (CLI / core / indexing / MCP server)

### Summary

On macOS, Dart pubspec discovery fails for every repo that has Dart files: `ENOTDIR` on `/dev/fd/N`.

### Context

`loadDartPackageConfig` throws `Dart pubspec discovery failed (read-directory): .` as soon as the walker lists its first directory, the repo root:

```
Error: ENOTDIR: not a directory, scandir '/dev/fd/13'
```

Discovery only runs when the repo has Dart files (`scope-resolution/pipeline/phase.ts`), so non-Dart repos are unaffected.

### Expected behavior

Discovery works on macOS, with the same no-follow guarantees the walker already gives child opens there (pinned parent chain re-checked before and after each lexical open).

### Actual behavior

`descriptorDirectoryPath` in `src/core/ingestion/languages/dart/package-config.ts` returns `/dev/fd/N` on darwin, and `listOpenedDirectory` calls `opendir` on it. macOS won't `opendir` a directory through `/dev/fd/N`. It's not a Node quirk, Python gets the same:

```
python3 -c "import os; fd=os.open('.', os.O_RDONLY); print(os.listdir(f'/dev/fd/{fd}'))"
# NotADirectoryError: [Errno 20] Not a directory: '/dev/fd/3'
```

Node has no `fdopendir`, so there is no descriptor-based listing on macOS at all. Linux is fine because `/proc/self/fd/N` resolves to the directory.

Came in with #3369. It wasn't caught because neither test file below is in `scripts/cross-platform-tests.ts`, so the macOS runners never run them.

### Steps to reproduce

On macOS, `main` at a47cd17f:

```
cd gitnexus
npx vitest run test/unit/dart-package-imports.test.ts
# 30 failed | 24 passed | 1 skipped
npx vitest run test/unit/incremental-orchestration.test.ts
# the four "Dart pubspec-only incremental persistence (#2963)" cases fail the same way
```

### Environment

- OS: macOS 26.7.1 (x86_64)
- Node: 26.10.0
- Commit: a47cd17f

I have a fix and will open a PR referencing this.

title: fix(dart): capture package metadata portably during repository scan
body:
## Summary

Fix Dart package discovery on macOS and Windows by capturing package metadata during the existing repository scan, then reusing it for parsing and scope resolution. Fixes #3464.

The previous Dart-specific walk failed on macOS when listing `/dev/fd/N` and returned no packages on Windows. Before/after directory timestamps cannot make enumeration atomic. This update replaces that walk with a portable acquisition boundary instead of adding another platform backend.

## Areas touched

- [x] `gitnexus/` CLI/core ingestion, Dart provider, regression tests and cross-platform test registration

## Implementation

- Add an optional provider capture hook. The shared scanner supplies discovered paths before ordinary stat/size filtering can discard required metadata. The resulting configuration is reused by both parsing and scope resolution.
- Open each pubspec before validating it, then validate and read through the same descriptor with a bounded buffer; preserve declared-name matching, exact `lib/` targets and conservative duplicate-name handling. Keep at most two deterministic ambiguity witnesses and check shared parent directories once per capture.
- Reject incomplete directory enumeration, unreadable Dart ignore controls, missing/unreadable candidate manifests, oversized files and observed file replacement/modification. Static symlinks and Windows junctions are excluded. POSIX no-follow/nonblocking flags remain in use where available.
- Keep strict repository-control validation inside the Dart provider. TypeScript and other scans preserve their existing support for linked ignore files; regression tests exercise both `.gitignore` and `.gitnexusignore`.
- Bound manifests to 20,000 and each document to the smaller of 1 MiB and the configured file-size limit. Remove the extra Dart tree traversal and directory-descriptor stack.
- Keep both the Dart acquisition suite and native Dart pipeline suite registered exactly once in the Windows/macOS CI subset. Remove the old platform-level discovery skip.

## Acquisition contract and scope

Acquisition assumes a stable, trusted workspace, as the existing source reader does. Resolution uses only the captured package map afterward. This is not an atomic filesystem snapshot or a sandbox against hostile concurrent mutation; source contents are still read by later pipeline phases.

This deliberately replaces Linux's separate descriptor-backed Dart walk as well as the macOS fallback. It changes the earlier review's Linux-unchanged constraint in order to provide one portable acquisition model. Ordinary scans without metadata capture retain their best-effort behavior; production metadata scans reject incomplete input rather than silently publishing a partial configuration.

Package semantics remain the existing source-only, in-repository pubspec identities. This does not add Pub dependency solving or claim full compiler resolution through generated `.dart_tool/package_config.json`. No native addon, dependency, schema or index-format change is introduced.

## Testing and verification

- 343 tests passed across 18 focused, Dart integration, shared pipeline and incremental-cache suites; one POSIX permission test skipped because the local container runs as root.
- Production build, production/test typechecks, formatting and ESLint passed (existing lint warnings remain).
- Real pipeline regression verifies one metadata capture and zero subsequent configuration reloads. Other regressions cover Windows discovery, junctions, missing/oversized manifests, duplicate names, same-size edits, descriptor acquisition races and reuse after repository-path replacement.
- A 10,000-source-path regression verifies only the two manifests are opened and their common parent is checked once.
- Independently injected `EACCES` before loading the scanner: ordinary scans retained best-effort behavior; metadata scans rejected before capture. The permanent regression covers the required-metadata failure path.
- Graph impact analysis covered the shared callers. The three-file follow-up maps to the expected functions. Full-PR mapping remains partial for anonymous test callbacks; the latest upstream merge also contains test/config edits without graph symbols. These diffs were inspected and the affected Dart/pipeline tests executed directly; no clean whole-graph coverage claim is made.
- CI Gate and all Linux/macOS/Windows tests passed at `b76605f`, preserving the latest main merge (`dd096e6`, including Vitest 5). The CodeQL follow-up at `b538f64` passed 228 tests across nine affected suites; its final Dart unit suite passed 64 tests with one root-permission skip. Both typechecks, formatting and lint passed. CI Gate, both CodeQL analyses, the CodeQL security-results check, and all Linux/macOS/Windows test shards passed at `b538f64`. The initial Linux shard 2 run failed an unchanged group-impact test; the focused retry passed unchanged with 7,499 tests passed and 19 skipped. The same test also passed isolated, repeated, and Node 22.23.3 coverage runs. The intermittent failure mechanism was not reproduced, and no speculative production change or weakened assertion was added. The new link fallback test uses a real POSIX symlink with O_NOFOLLOW removed; native Windows leaf-symlink coverage remains a limitation. The earlier local full-suite attempt was blocked by an unavailable VECTOR extension and then stalled; no green local full-suite claim is made.

## Review disposition

The duplicate CI registration and misleading Ubuntu-only explanation are corrected. The old lexical-listing implementation and its timestamp mitigation are removed. The remaining contract is stated above rather than claiming that path checks close every filesystem race. All functional review threads have replies and are resolved. The CodeQL follow-up removes the pre-open pathname check: acquisition now opens once before descriptor validation and reading. Regressions cover replacement during validation, replacement after open, and successful-open link exclusion with closure before reading. Both CodeQL language analyses and the security-results check passed at `b538f64`. No alert suppression or dismissal was added. The PR remains open for review; it is not merged.

title: fix(mcp): reject corrupt impact and context identities
body:
## Summary

MCP context and impact queries now fail with recovery guidance when returned identities are visibly corrupt, instead of producing results from malformed rows. Affected impact results report UNKNOWN risk and null counts; healthy query behavior remains unchanged.

## Motivation / context

Related: #3354 ([latest reproduction comment](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/issues/3354#issuecomment-5970252499)).

The reproduction describes NUL-containing paths, inconsistent process details, empty context entries, and different answers after restarting MCP. The private index is unavailable. A separate synthetic reproduction now establishes a native filtered-scan corruption class on LadybugDB 0.18.3; the same fixture is correct on 0.21.1. This does not establish the exact cause of the reporter's NUL-containing values.

## Areas touched

- [x] `gitnexus/` (CLI / core / MCP server)
- [ ] `gitnexus-web/` (Vite / React UI)
- [ ] `.github/` (workflows, actions)
- [ ] `eval/` or other tooling
- [ ] Docs / agent config only (`AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `.cursor/`, `llms.txt`, etc.)

## Scope & constraints

**In scope**

- Reject malformed required IDs and optional identity strings before filtering, caps, coercion, aggregation, or deduplication can hide them.
- Preserve zero-valued context process steps/counts.
- Verify exact native results across repeated, mixed, concurrent, and warm-backend reads after replacing the index at the same path.
- Pin the native upgrade's protection against mismatched long symbol strings after checkpointed multi-segment deletions.

**Explicitly out of scope / not done here**

- Changes to the native engine, dependencies, connection lifecycle, ingestion, or index publication.

## Implementation notes

Integrity errors propagate through the existing context/impact error boundaries, including PDG and AOP enrichment. Ordinary query failures retain their existing degraded behavior. Valid Unicode, optional null/empty identities, generated unresolved PDG markers, and NUL-containing source content remain supported.

## Native root-cause evidence

A 10,000-row fixture with three long STRING columns and an independent integer row identity is loaded in four COPY/CHECKPOINT batches. All rows match the source before deletion. After deleting 400 interior rows and checkpointing, filtered scans on **0.18.3** associate strings with the wrong integer rows. Primary-key lookups still return the correct source values, identifying a read/projection defect rather than evidence that those stored values were overwritten.

| Controlled probe | 0.18.3 | 0.21.1 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Four segments, no deletion; six reads | 10,000 exact rows | 10,000 exact rows |
| Delete 400 rows, close writer, reopen read-only; six reads | 3,632 of 9,600 rows have mismatched strings on every read | 9,600 exact, unique rows on every read |
| Reopen the old fixture in a fresh process; six reads | Same 3,632 mismatches per read | Not needed for the version control |
| Committed regression on the writer connection | Fails: 6,106 distinct IDs for 9,600 rows | Passes all exact-row checks |

[LadybugDB #737](https://github.com/LadybugDB/ladybug/pull/737), linked to [#678](https://github.com/LadybugDB/ladybug/issues/678), fixes the filtered STRING scan's bounds: result-vector positions were compared with segment-local offsets, allowing selected output slots across segments to be skipped. The observed failure is consistent with this mechanism. The 0.18.3-to-0.21.1 comparison establishes the upgrade boundary; it does not isolate every intervening engine fix.

**Prevention:** main already includes LadybugDB 0.21.1 through #3442. This PR adds an all-platform native regression that checks exact source identities, row counts, unique IDs, sorted and unsorted scans, surviving point lookups, and a deleted point lookup. It fails on the old engine and passes on the current engine; no redundant dependency change is needed.

**Recovery:** use a build containing the fixed engine, run that build's `gitnexus analyze --force`, and restart MCP readers. A rebuild is needed if earlier wrong reads affected derived analysis. The existing integrity errors provide rebuild guidance. Retrying or reopening the old engine does not repair this reproduced scan defect.

## Testing & verification

- [x] Affected unit/integration run: **702 tests passed across 12 files**, including the real LadybugDB identity and replacement regressions.
- [x] Broader MCP-related unit pass: **1,037 tests passed across 34 files**. These runs overlap.
- [x] `cd gitnexus && npm run build`
- [x] `cd gitnexus && npx tsc --noEmit`
- [x] `cd gitnexus && npx eslint src/ test/ --quiet`
- [x] Prettier checks for all changed files and the repository pre-commit hook.
- [x] Published-head CI at `e167653`: all checks passed; CI reported **24,386 passed, 0 failed, 87 skipped** across three platforms.
- [x] New native regression: current engine passes; substituting 0.18.3 fails at the distinct-identity assertion.
- [x] Incremental change: **190 focused tests passed across 2 files**, including **6 native integration tests**. Typecheck, ESLint, and Prettier passed.
- [ ] Local full `cd gitnexus && npm test`: attempted twice, without a passing result (the CI result above is authoritative for the published head).

Affected-test command:

```bash
cd gitnexus
npm test -- \
  test/unit/impact-context-integrity.test.ts \
  test/unit/symbol-identity-validation.test.ts \
  test/unit/mcp-context-route-chain.test.ts \
  test/unit/impact-pagination.test.ts \
  test/unit/impact-batching-grouping.test.ts \
  test/unit/impact-route-enrichment.test.ts \
  test/unit/calltool-dispatch.test.ts \
  test/unit/group/impact-by-uid.test.ts \
  test/unit/pdg-impact-engine.test.ts \
  test/integration/impact-context-integrity.test.ts \
  test/integration/local-backend-calltool.test.ts \
  test/integration/spring-aop-mcp.test.ts --maxWorkers=2
```

The first full run was disrupted when its dependency checkout disappeared. After restoring dependencies, `npm test -- --maxWorkers=4` exited 1 without a Vitest summary. Separately, five process-identity/file-lock failures reproduce on unchanged base code in this container. Build and type checks used a clean checkout containing only this PR's changes.

The same-path replacement test runs on POSIX and skips Windows. Browser testing is inapplicable to this backend-only change.

## Risk & rollout

These guards detect malformed identity values; they do not detect printable wrong rows or inflated counts. The native regression protects the fixed engine's exact row associations against the reproduced filtered-scan defect. The reporter's exact private-index cause remains unproven. This PR introduces no schema migration; rejected queries provide rebuild guidance.

title: Issue draft — `--name` / `.gitnexusrc` `name` is silently clobbered by the shared-store re-registration
body:
# Issue draft — `--name` / `.gitnexusrc` `name` is silently clobbered by the shared-store re-registration

> Draft for upstream. All repository names, paths, URLs, and log lines below are
> **fictional / sanitized** — no real repo, host, or credential is included.

---

**Title:**
`--name` (and `.gitnexusrc` `"name"`) is silently reverted to the remote-inferred name by the shared-store re-registration

**Labels (suggested):** `bug`, `storage`, `cli`, `shared-store`, `regression`

---

## Summary

On a repository whose index lives in a **shared store** (see below), setting the
registry name via `--name` or via `.gitnexusrc` `"name"` does not stick. `analyze`
reports success and even prints `Registry name changed: "OLD" -> "NEW".`, but the
final registry entry — and therefore `gitnexus list`, MCP, and `serve` — shows the
**remote-inferred** name instead. Every other `.gitnexusrc` key (`pdg`,
`embeddings`, `workerTimeout`, …) works correctly.

## Environment

- GitNexus `1.6.13-rc.57` (Docker image; `GITNEXUS_HOME=/data/gitnexus`)
- Reproduction still present in `v1.6.13-rc.73` (see "Affected versions")
- Index storage resolves to a shared store:
  `${GITNEXUS_HOME}/stores/<key>/checkouts/<slot>` (feature from #3352)
- No `GITNEXUS_STORAGE_ROOT` / `GITNEXUS_STORAGE_PATH` override is set
  (so shared-store is not disabled by an explicit storage env)
- A `.gitnexusrc` at the repo root, tracked in git and present at the indexed commit:

  ```json
  { "name": "demo-service", "pdg": true, "embeddings": 0, "workerTimeout": "300" }
  ```

## Reproduction

Scenario: a repo that ends up in a shared store — e.g. linked worktrees of one
repository, or sibling clones sharing one `origin` (both routes land in the same
store under `$GITNEXUS_HOME/stores/`).

```
/srv/work/acme-service        # main checkout  (indexed)
/srv/work/acme-service-wt     # linked worktree / sibling clone
origin = git@example.internal:team/acme-service.git
```

1. Put a `.gitnexusrc` with `{ "name": "demo-service" }` at the repo root and
   commit it.
2. Run analyze inside the container against the main checkout:

   ```sh
   docker exec -w /srv/work/acme-service <container> gitnexus analyze
   ```

   (Equivalently with an explicit flag: `gitnexus analyze --name demo-service`.)

3. Observe the run log:

   ```
   Registry name changed: "acme-service" -> "demo-service".
   Shared store: published commit graph <sha>.
   Repository indexed successfully
   ```

4. Check the registry:

   ```sh
   docker exec <container> cat "$GITNEXUS_HOME/registry.json"
   docker exec <container> gitnexus list
   ```

## Expected

The registry entry's `name` is `demo-service`.

## Actual

The registry entry's `name` is the remote-inferred value from the `origin` URL
(`acme-service`) — i.e. the value that `run-analyze` set was **reverted later in
the same run**.

```jsonc
[
  {
    "name": "acme-service",                 // ← expected "demo-service"
    "path": "/srv/work/acme-service",
    "storagePath": "/data/gitnexus/stores/acme-service-<hash>/checkouts/acme-service-<hash>",
    "lastCommit": "<sha>",
    "remoteUrl": "git@example.internal:team/acme-service.git"
  }
]
```

## Root cause

There are **two** `registerRepo` calls at the end of an analyze run:

| Call site | Forwards `name`? |
| --- | --- |
| `src/core/run-analyze.ts:4968` — `registerRepo(repoPath, meta, { name: options.registryName, onRename: …, allowDuplicateName: … })` | ✅ yes |
| `src/core/shared-store-analyze.ts:496` — `registerRepo(repoPath, meta, { storagePath: slot, dropBranches: moved })` | ❌ **no** |

The shared-store call runs **after** the shared graph is published
(`Shared store: published commit graph …`), which is **after** the run-analyze
call that printed `Registry name changed`. Because it omits `name`, `registerRepo`
re-derives the name through its normal precedence chain
(`src/storage/repo-manager.ts:1064`):

```
explicit opts.name > preserved alias > remote-inferred > path.basename
```

`opts.name` is undefined here, so it falls through. The "preserved alias" branch
is also skipped because of the basename exception in `hasCustomAlias`
(`src/storage/repo-manager.ts:944`):

```ts
const hasCustomAlias = (entry, inferredName) => {
  const resolved = path.resolve(entry.path);
  if (entry.name === path.basename(resolved)) return false;      // ← hits this
  if (entry.name === path.basename(resolveRepoIdentityRoot(resolved))) return false;
  if (inferredName && entry.name === inferredName) return false;
  return true;
};
```

When the desired alias happens to equal the checkout's directory basename
(`demo-service` under `.../acme-service`), the alias is deliberately treated as
**not** a custom alias and is not preserved. The name then falls through to the
remote inference (`acme-service` from `.../acme-service.git`), silently
overwriting the value the user just saw confirmed.

Two aggravating factors:

- The clobber is silent — the run still exits 0 and the log line still claims the
  rename succeeded.
- The final value depends on the **order** of the two registrations; the one that
  runs later is the one that never received the name.

## Affected versions

Verified by inspecting `src/core/shared-store-analyze.ts` at each tag — the
`registerRepo(repoPath, meta, { storagePath: slot, dropBranches: moved })` call is
**unchanged** in:

- `v1.6.13-rc.57` … `v1.6.13-rc.73`

(The shared store itself was introduced by #3352, so any release carrying that
feature is affected. Repositories not participating in a shared store — i.e. a
single non-shared checkout with its own repo-local `.gitnexus` — are **not**
affected, which makes this easy to miss.)

## Why only `name` is affected

`pdg`, `embeddings`, and `workerTimeout` are consumed **before** the analysis
completes (they decide whether the PDG layer is built, whether embeddings are
generated, and the worker timeout). They are already baked into the produced
index well before any registration runs.

`name` is the only option written to the **registry at the end of the run**, and
it has two write sites — the later one does not carry it.

## Suggested fix

Forward the name (and any other run-level registry fields) into the shared-store
registration:

```ts
// src/core/shared-store-analyze.ts (around line 496)
await registerRepo(repoPath, meta, {
  storagePath: slot,
  dropBranches: moved,
  name: options.registryName,          // ← forward the alias
  allowDuplicateName: options.allowDuplicateName,
});
```

or, alternatively, make the shared-store registration run **before** the
run-analyze registration so the named call wins.

Either way, please consider treating "a `--name` / `.gitnexusrc` name that equals
the checkout basename" as a value worth preserving across re-registration rather
than as a non-alias — the basename exception in `hasCustomAlias` is what turns a
missing-`name` oversight into a silent revert.

## Workaround

Use a registry name that is **not** equal to the checkout directory basename and
**not** equal to the remote-inferred name (e.g. `acme-service-app` for
`.../acme-service`), so `hasCustomAlias` returns true and the alias survives the
second registration. Renaming the directory also works, but it changes the store
key and triggers a full rebuild.

title: Add Visual Basic .NET (VB.NET) language support
body:
### Area

gitnexus (CLI / core / indexing / MCP server)

### Problem or opportunity

GitNexus currently does not support Visual Basic .NET (VB.NET) as a parsed language.

I maintain a large enterprise .NET codebase primarily written in VB.NET. I tested GitNexus 1.6.12 on the repository: indexing completed successfully, but the VB.NET source cannot benefit from the structural analysis that makes GitNexus particularly useful, such as symbols, method calls, inheritance, cross-file dependencies, impact analysis, and execution flows.

The repository contains thousands of files across multiple interconnected .NET projects, so GitNexus would be particularly valuable for understanding and safely modifying this kind of large enterprise/legacy .NET solution.

VB.NET is also commonly found alongside C# in existing .NET solutions, so supporting it would enable GitNexus to analyze mixed C#/VB.NET codebases more completely.

I would be happy to test experimental VB.NET support against a large real-world enterprise solution and provide feedback, examples, and parsing/resolution bug reports.

### Proposed solution

Add initial VB.NET language support to the GitNexus indexing pipeline.

For a first shippable phase, GitNexus should recognize `.vb` source files and extract the core structural information needed to build a useful knowledge graph:

- namespaces and imports
- classes, modules, structures, and interfaces
- methods, functions, constructors, properties, and events
- inheritance and interface implementation
- basic cross-file symbol resolution
- method/function call relationships

This initial support could then be expanded incrementally toward feature parity with C#, including more advanced type inference and framework-specific analysis.

### Alternatives considered

I considered relying on text search or generic repository indexing for VB.NET files, but this loses the main benefit of GitNexus: understanding structural relationships between symbols and files.

Converting or migrating the existing VB.NET codebase to C# is not a practical workaround for large production systems.

Supporting VB.NET directly in the language/indexing layer is therefore preferable.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `.vb` files are recognized and parsed during `gitnexus analyze`
- [ ] VB.NET namespaces and Imports statements are represented correctly
- [ ] Classes, Modules, Structures, and Interfaces are indexed as symbols
- [ ] Methods, Functions, Constructors, Properties, and Events are indexed
- [ ] `Inherits` and `Implements` relationships are represented in the graph
- [ ] Basic calls between VB.NET methods/functions are represented
- [ ] Cross-file references within a VB.NET project can be resolved
- [ ] `context` returns useful structural information for VB.NET symbols
- [ ] `impact` can identify basic upstream dependencies of a VB.NET symbol
- [ ] Existing supported languages are unaffected

### Constraints

VB.NET support should not regress parsing or indexing behavior for existing supported languages.

Initial support does not need to cover every VB.NET language feature or achieve immediate feature parity with C#. A smaller first implementation covering the core symbol and relationship graph would already make GitNexus useful for real-world VB.NET repositories.

Performance should remain suitable for large repositories containing thousands of source files and multiple projects.

### Contribution

- [ ] I am willing to open a PR for this (may need design discussion first).

title: Python: function reached through an aliased package import whose __init__.py re-exports it emits no CALLS edge (1.6.11)
body:
## Summary

On 1.6.11, a Python function reached through an **aliased import of a package** whose `__init__.py` re-exports the function gets no `CALLS` edge. Each half works alone: the `__init__.py` re-export resolves (1.6.10) and an aliased *module file* resolves (#2882). The combination does not, and `impact` then reports 0 callers with `epistemic: "exact"`.

## Reproduction (gitnexus 1.6.11, Python)

```
app/__init__.py              (empty)
app/services/__init__.py     (empty)
app/services/bp/gp.py
app/services/bp/__init__.py
app/combo.py
app/reex.py
```

`app/services/bp/gp.py`
```python
def pf():
    return 1
```

`app/services/bp/__init__.py`
```python
from .gp import (
    pf,
)

__all__ = ["pf"]
```

`app/combo.py` — aliased package, then attribute call (missed)
```python
from .services import bp as backplane

def combo_caller():
    return backplane.pf()
```

`app/reex.py` — same re-export, no alias (found)
```python
from .services.bp import pf

def reexport_pkg_caller():
    return pf()
```

```
git init && git add -A && git commit -m init
gitnexus analyze
gitnexus impact pf -d upstream --repo .
```

## Expected

Upstream callers: `combo_caller` and `reexport_pkg_caller`.

## Actual

Only `reexport_pkg_caller`. In a larger codebase with this shape, `impact` returns `impactedCount: 0`, `risk: "UNKNOWN"`, `epistemic: "exact"` for a function with several callers that all go through the alias.

## Neighbours

- #2882 (closed): `from <pkg> import <submodule>` as a namespace — fixed for a submodule **file**; here the aliased name is a **package**, and the call resolves through its `__init__.py`.
- #2826, #1659 (closed): other Python import spellings.

Environment: macOS arm64, Node 25.2.1, gitnexus 1.6.11 from npm.

title: fix(group): match Go framework imports exactly and follow bare-block group writes
body:
## Summary

Two small fixes to the Go group-mode HTTP plugin that were pushed to #3458 after it was merged, so they did not land:

1. Echo/gin imports are matched by **exact** import path, shared with ingestion, instead of a substring test.
2. An unconditional write inside a bare `{ … }` block is treated as the group binding, instead of declining the route.

## Motivation / context

Follow-up to #3458 (merged as 504bff71 at `f57056e5`). Both changes answer nexus-check findings raised on `f57056e5`:

- https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/pull/3458#discussion_r4177213551 — `readFrameworkImports` treated any path containing `labstack/echo` as echo, while ingestion (`go-gin-echo.ts`) uses `^github\.com/labstack/echo(/v\d+)?$`. A path such as `example.com/labstack/echo-wrapper` was classified as echo by the group layer only, which flips the handler-argument order (echo: first, gin: last), so a gin-style route with middleware recorded the middleware as its handler.
- https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/pull/3458#discussion_r4177213554 — `{ g = r.Group("/new") }` always runs, so `g.GET("/x", …)` after it is deterministically `/new/x`, but #3458 declined it as a conflicting binding.

My replies on those threads say "Fixed in 9e3be2c5". That commit was pushed after the merge; this PR carries it, rebased onto `main`.

## Areas touched

- [x] `gitnexus/` (CLI / core / MCP server)
- [ ] `gitnexus-web/` (Vite / React UI)
- [ ] `.github/` (workflows, actions)
- [ ] `eval/` or other tooling
- [ ] Docs / agent config only (`AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `.cursor/`, `llms.txt`, etc.)

## Scope & constraints

**In scope**

- `go-shared.ts` exports `isGinImportPath` (`github.com/gin-gonic/gin`) and `isEchoImportPath` (`^github\.com/labstack/echo(/v\d+)?$`). Ingestion's `readImports` switches to them with identical behavior, and the group plugin's `readFrameworkImports` replaces its substring checks. Both layers now classify imports from one definition.
- `lookupBinding`: when a statement before the use is a bare block, `bareBlockWrite` returns its last top-level `name = v`. Only statements before any `:=`/`var` redeclaration of the name inside the block count, because later writes target the inner variable. Nested bare blocks recurse. A write inside a branch, loop, or closure (including one nested in a bare block) still yields CONFLICT, and the route is declined as in #3458.

**Explicitly out of scope / not done here**

- Ingestion's own handling of bare-block writes. Ingestion may still decline these; the group layer now emits the deterministic path, and there is no graph contract to collide with.
- The ingestion-side miss for a leading comment before the route path (`r.GET(/* c */ "/users", h)`), noted in the #3458 review. It belongs to the #3417 extractor; happy to send it separately.

## Implementation notes

- `readImports` sits on the ingestion hot path (`parse-worker`). The change there replaces two inline checks with the shared functions, and the predicates are unchanged. GitNexus `detect_changes --scope compare --base-ref main` reports risk medium, driven by that call site. The Go ingestion and route-pipeline suites pass unchanged.

## Testing & verification

- [x] `cd gitnexus && npx tsc --noEmit`: 0 errors
- [x] `npx vitest run test/unit/group`: 62 files, 1320 passed
- [x] Go route ingestion + integration (`go-gin-route-pipeline`, `go-route-binding-identity`, `go-route-package-names`, `go-gin-echo` units, and the other Go/gin/echo-referencing suites): 20 files, 530 passed / 4 skipped
- [x] `eslint` and `prettier --check` clean on the changed files
- [x] New/updated tests in `test/unit/group/go-gin-route-groups.test.ts`, both failing without the source change:
  - "matches framework imports by exact path, as ingestion does": `example.com/labstack/echo-wrapper` keeps the last-argument handler; `github.com/labstack/echo/v4` is still echo.
  - "follows unconditional block writes and declines conditional ones": `{ g = r.Group("/new") }` → `/new/x`; `if cond { k = … }` and `{ if cond { n = … } }` declined; `{ m := …; m = …; }` leaves the outer `m` intact.
- [x] Real gin backend (209 Go files, 257 provider routes, scanned from a scratch copy): output identical before/after.
- [ ] Full `npm test` not re-run for this follow-up. The touched areas are covered by the suites above.

## Risk & rollout

- Behavior changes only for (a) Go files importing a module whose path merely contains `labstack/echo`/`gin-gonic/gin` but is not the framework, and (b) routes whose group is reassigned in a bare block. No schema change and no re-index required.

title: Issue draft — Shared-store copy-on-write re-embeds a cloned graph and aborts with a `CodeEmbedding` duplicate-primary-key error
body:
# Issue draft — Shared-store copy-on-write re-embeds a cloned graph and aborts with a `CodeEmbedding` duplicate-primary-key error

> Draft for upstream. All repository names, paths, URLs, commit hashes, and log
> lines below are **fictional / sanitized** — no real repo, host, or credential
> is included.

---

**Title:**
Shared-store copy-on-write re-embeds a cloned graph and aborts `analyze` with `Found duplicated primary key value` on `CodeEmbedding`

**Labels (suggested):** `bug`, `embeddings`, `storage`, `shared-store`, `regression`

---

## Summary

When a checkout's index lives in a **shared store**, `analyze` on a checkout
that has local changes takes a **copy-on-write copy of a sibling's graph**
(`Shared store: copied the shared graph for local changes …`). That copied graph
already contains `CodeEmbedding` rows for the same nodes. The embedding phase
then tries to re-embed those nodes and aborts the whole run:

```
Analysis failed: Batch execution failed for rows 1-4: Runtime exception:
Found duplicated primary key value :0, which violates the uniqueness constraint
of the primary key column.
```

The run exits non-zero and the index is left unusable (`atomic-incremental`
staging never commits).

This is a **regression**: #823 explicitly fixed "CodeEmbedding PK violations"
for exactly this situation ("A partial prior run left some embeddings in the DB
before a crash", "a concurrent analyze"), and the later AST-chunking change
(#889) reverted the fix in practice (details below).

## Environment

- GitNexus `1.6.13-rc.57` (Docker image; `GITNEXUS_HOME=/data/gitnexus`)
- Still present in `v1.6.13-rc.73` — `batchInsertEmbeddings` is still `CREATE` (verified against the tag)
- Index storage resolves to a shared store:
  `${GITNEXUS_HOME}/stores/<key>/checkouts/<slot>` (feature from #3352 / #3374)
- `GITNEXUS_SHARED_STORE` **not** set (sharing on by default), no `--share-with` / `--no-share`
- Two independent clones of the **same upstream repository** are registered in one GitNexus home
- Embeddings enabled (`"embeddings": 0` in `.gitnexusrc` = all nodes; remote HTTP embedding endpoint)

## Reproduction

Two "sibling" clones (different paths, **same normalized origin URL**) sharing one
`GITNEXUS_HOME`:

```
/workspace/acme-service            # clone A — already indexed, embeddings present
/workspace/acme-service-secondcopy # clone B — dirty working tree (one modified file)
origin = https://example.invalid/team/acme-service.git   # identical for A and B
```

1. Index clone A fully, with embeddings, so its store contains `CodeEmbedding` rows:

   ```sh
   docker exec -w /workspace/acme-service  <container> gitnexus analyze
   ```

2. Modify one tracked file in clone B so its tree is dirty, then analyze it:

   ```sh
   docker exec -w /workspace/acme-service-secondcopy <container> gitnexus analyze
   ```

Observed: clone B joins clone A's shared store (same origin URL), copies A's graph
for local changes, then aborts during embedding.

```
Shared store: copied the shared graph for local changes in 25287ms.
…
Embedding node-count cap disabled — generating embeddings for 1,938,567 nodes. …
Analysis failed: Batch execution failed for rows 1-4: Runtime exception:
Found duplicated primary key value :0, which violates the uniqueness constraint
of the primary key column.
    (CREATE (e:CodeEmbedding {id: $id, nodeId: $nodeId, chunkIndex: $chunkIndex,
             startLine: $startLine, endLine: $endLine, em)
```

Expected: the copied graph's existing `CodeEmbedding` rows are reused / replaced
idempotently; the run completes (matching the pre-#889 `MERGE` behaviour).

Workaround that avoids the path entirely: `GITNEXUS_SHARED_STORE=off` (each
checkout indexes into its own `<repo>/.gitnexus`).

## Root cause

The abort is in `batchInsertEmbeddings`
(`gitnexus/src/core/embeddings/embedding-pipeline.ts`):

```ts
await executeWithReusedStatement(
  `MATCH (e:${EMBEDDING_TABLE_NAME} {id: $id}) DELETE e`,   // DELETE by composite id
  paramsList.map(({ id }) => ({ id })),
);
const cypher = `CREATE (e:${EMBEDDING_TABLE_NAME} {id: $id, nodeId: $nodeId,
  chunkIndex: $chunkIndex, startLine: $startLine, endLine: $endLine,
  embedding: $embedding, contentHash: $contentHash})`;      // CREATE
await executeWithReusedStatement(cypher, paramsList);
```

`CodeEmbedding.id` is a composite `STRING` key, `${nodeId}:${chunkIndex}`
(introduced with AST chunking in #889). The per-batch `DELETE` is keyed the same
way, so it only clears rows this run itself wrote — it does **not** clear the
rows inherited from the shared-store copy, which carry the very same ids. The
subsequent `CREATE` therefore collides with an existing primary key.

The `DELETE`-before-`INSERT` pattern was sound when the table was keyed by
`nodeId` alone, on the assumption that every row's `id` was a *current* row that
the batch was about to replace. Copying an entire foreign graph into the slot
breaks that assumption: the rows are pre-existing, not "this batch's stale rows".

### Regression timeline (bisect)

| Date | Commit | Change |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 2026-04-14 | `8d38cc99` | "use MERGE instead of CREATE for CodeEmbedding inserts" — made the insert idempotent |
| 2026-04-15 | `c100577e` (#823) | "prevent batch errors from CodeEmbedding **PK violations**" — explicitly names concurrent analyze and partial prior runs |
| 2026-04-17 | `02739085` (#889) | AST-aware chunking: key becomes `nodeId:chunkIndex`; **`MERGE` replaced by `CREATE`** + per-batch `DELETE` |

#823's fix worked because `MERGE (e:CodeEmbedding {nodeId: $nodeId}) SET …`
matched existing rows regardless of how they got there. #889 changed the key and
the verb at once, and the new `DELETE` (by composite `id`) no longer covers rows
copied in from a shared store.

Note: the shared-store feature itself (`ad5c7364`, #3374) landed after #889 and
made a *pre-existing* latent idempotency gap reachable through a supported,
**default-on** code path.

## Impact

- `analyze` fails hard; the staged `atomic-incremental` write never publishes,
  so the checkout's index is left stale/unusable.
- Any user with two clones of the same repository in one `GITNEXUS_HOME` (and
  sharing on by default) can hit this — with no notice that their checkout is
  being attached to a sibling's store.
- Not fixable by upgrading today: `v1.6.13-rc.73` still has `CREATE`.

## Affected versions

- Confirmed on `1.6.13-rc.57`.
- `batchInsertEmbeddings` is unchanged in `v1.6.13-rc.73` (still `CREATE` +
  composite-id `DELETE`), so all rc builds with the shared store (≥ ~rc.36,
  when #3352/#3374 landed) are expected to be affected.

## Suggested fix (either)

1. Make the insert idempotent again: `MERGE (e:CodeEmbedding {id: $id}) SET e.nodeId = $nodeId, e.chunkIndex = $chunkIndex, e.startLine = $startLine, e.endLine = $endLine, e.embedding = $embedding, e.contentHash = $contentHash`.
2. Or, before the `CREATE`, delete any pre-existing row with the **same composite `id`** (not just this batch's stale set), e.g. widen the delete to the batch's `id` list unconditionally.

Either restores #823's guarantee that a half/cloned embedding table can be
rewritten without a PK abort.

---

## Minimal fixture (for a test)

No real code needed — the collision is purely on the embedding rows:

1. Index a repo with embeddings; snapshot a store slot containing `CodeEmbedding` rows.
2. Point a *second* checkout (same origin) at that store and give it a dirty tree
   so it takes the copy-on-write path.
3. Run `analyze` and assert it does not throw `duplicated primary key value`.

---

## Disclaimers

- All names, paths, URLs, and log lines above are fictional.
- The report is one bug (PK idempotency under a copied graph). Whether the
  shared store should auto-attach sibling clones by remote URL is a separate
  design question and is **not** part of this issue.

## Motivation / context

test(search): guard native lookup and Unicode FTS after COPY
body:
## Summary

CI now rejects the native failure patterns that made unchanged symbols disappear from context lookup and valid Unicode fail Property FTS after a small incremental write. The effective engine correction is already on main; this PR makes both symptoms reproducible and protects that correction.

## Motivation / context

A controlled build of LadybugDB 0.18.3 reproduced both failures. Applying only upstream [LadybugDB #737](https://github.com/LadybugDB/ladybug/pull/737) to the same source checkout removed both using identical CSV input and the same FTS extension. The native filtered string scan mixed output-vector positions with segment-local bounds.

GitNexus's core 0.21.1 upgrade in #3442 already includes that fix. #3475 remains a separate repair-hardening and public worktree-context change.

Related: #3421, #3423

## Areas touched

- [x] `gitnexus/` (CLI / core / MCP server)
- [ ] `gitnexus-web/` (Vite / React UI)
- [ ] `.github/` (workflows, actions)
- [ ] `eval/` or other tooling
- [ ] Docs / agent config only

## Scope & constraints

**In scope**

- Native regressions for retained name/UID lookup and Unicode Property FTS after DELETE/COPY, checkpoint, repair, and reopen.
- Complete tuple comparisons and real FTS search, including Windows/macOS test-list registration.
- The controlled causal evidence and the reason an FTS-only repair cannot correct bad string reads.

**Explicitly out of scope / not done here**

- Another production workaround, dependency change, schema migration, or package release.
- Replay of the overwritten private databases. The exact missing-index-only diagnostic from the original report remains unreproduced.

## Implementation notes

The context fixture needs multiple node tables and out-of-line names: a single-table primary-key lookup or a short inline name can hide the defect. The Property fixture uses valid, variable-length Unicode and indexes name, content, and description. It checks the entire source tuple set because the old engine sometimes returns blank strings without throwing.

| Controlled native check | 0.18.3 | 0.18.3 + the upstream patch only |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Retained label-free UID/name lookup | Missing | Correct |
| Labeled primary-key control | Correct | Correct |
| Property FTS build and `LOWER(content)` | Invalid UTF-8 | Success |
| Property FTS drop/recreate | Missing index / orphan table | Success |

The permanent fixtures also fail on published core 0.18.3 and pass on the pinned 0.21.1. This proves the synthetic mechanism; it does not establish physical byte loss in either historical database.
