title: `impact` rates a symbol HIGH/CRITICAL with `epistemic: exact` from file-level IMPORTS fan-out; non-exported types get importers as direct callers
body:
**Version:** gitnexus 1.6.12 (npm `latest` on 2026-10-15), Node v24.4.1, macOS arm64, `analyze --index-only`, default `impact` options (`--depth 3`).

### Repro 1: a module-scope call makes every importer a dependant

```bash
mkdir gn-repro && cd gn-repro && git init -q
mkdir -p src/lib src/app
cat > src/lib/auth.ts <<'EOF'
function makeAdapter() {
  return { kind: 'adapter' };
}

export const auth = { adapter: makeAdapter() };
EOF
for i in $(seq 1 120); do
  mkdir -p src/app/r$i
  printf "import { auth } from '../../lib/auth';\n\nexport function GET() {\n  return auth.adapter;\n}\n" > src/app/r$i/route.ts
done
echo '{"name":"gn-repro","private":true}' > package.json
echo '{"compilerOptions":{"strict":true,"module":"esnext","target":"es2020","moduleResolution":"bundler"}}' > tsconfig.json
git add -A && git -c user.name=t -c user.email=t@e.com commit -qm repro
gitnexus analyze --index-only
gitnexus impact makeAdapter --direction upstream --repo .
```

**Observed:** `risk: HIGH`, `impactedCount: 121`, `epistemic: exact`, `summary.direct: 1`, `processes_affected: 0`.
The only depth-1 node is `File:src/lib/auth.ts` (`CALLS`, 0.85, the module-scope call). All 120 depth-2 nodes are that file's importers (`IMPORTS`, 1.0).

**Expected:** the IMPORTS closure of the file that makes the call should not drive the risk tier the way CALLS do. At minimum it should be reported separately, or `epistemic` should not be `exact`.

**Real-world size:** in our Next.js app (≈108k nodes) the same shape gives `createMultiTenantAdapter` (one real call site, at module scope in `src/lib/auth/index.ts`) `risk: CRITICAL`, `impactedCount: 884`, `direct: 1`, `processes_affected: 0`, `epistemic: exact`. A whole-word text search finds 2 lines in 1 file. Because a route handler's import closure reaches most of the app, `impactedCount` and `risk` stop describing the blast radius on any route diff. `direct` and `affected_processes` stay usable.

### Repro 2: a non-exported interface gets the importers of its file as direct callers

Same repo, add:

```bash
cat > src/lib/svc.ts <<'EOF'
interface Entry {
  txid: string;
}

function parse(raw: unknown): Entry[] {
  return Array.isArray(raw) ? (raw as Entry[]) : [];
}

export function verify(raw: unknown): boolean {
  return parse(raw).length > 0;
}
EOF
for i in $(seq 1 8); do
  mkdir -p src/app/v$i
  printf "import { verify } from '../../lib/svc';\n\nexport function POST(body: unknown) {\n  return verify(body);\n}\n" > src/app/v$i/route.ts
done
git add -A && git -c user.name=t -c user.email=t@e.com commit -qm repro2
gitnexus analyze --index-only
gitnexus impact Entry --direction upstream --repo .
```

**Observed:** `risk: MEDIUM`, `impactedCount: 8`, `summary.direct: 8`, `epistemic: exact`. All 8 depth-1 nodes are `File:src/app/v*/route.ts` with `IMPORTS`, confidence 1.0. Each of those files imports only `verify`.

**Expected:** `Entry` is not exported, so no other file can reference it. Its only dependants are `parse` (and through it `verify`). Importers of the declaring file should not be listed as depth-1 dependants of a non-exported declaration, and certainly not at confidence 1.0 with `epistemic: exact`.

**History:** on an earlier version the same shape reached `CRITICAL` / `impactedCount: 2532` / `epistemic: exact`, with depth-1 "callers" that included a Markdown file (`IMPORTS`, 0.8) and an unrelated class (`IMPLEMENTS`, 0.85). Those were consistent with name-keyed resolution of short property names (`txid`, `value`, `ok`...). We did not record that version. 1.6.12 no longer shows the phantom callers and reports `epistemic: lower-bound` on our repo, so that part looks fixed. The importer-as-direct-caller part is what still reproduces.

### Also seen, no minimal repro yet

- **Stale index after a rebase:** every `impact` came back CRITICAL through a `route.ts` node with an empty `filePath`. `analyze --force` cleared it.
  We saw it again on 1.6.12 on 2026-10-16. An incremental `analyze --index-only` after two commits (which touched only a shell script, a `.mjs`, tests and docs) printed a disk/corruption hint and then reported "Already up to date" on re-run. After that, `impact materialiseCheckoutOrder` returned:
  - 42 path nodes with an empty `filePath`;
  - a direct caller `POST` attributed to `src/modules/sales/services/sales-agent.service.ts`;
  - `processes_affected: 93`, against 7 on a clean index.
  `analyze --force --index-only` restored the clean reading. There was 287 GiB free, so disk space was not the cause. A warning when a node in the walk has an empty `filePath` (or when `meta.json.lastCommit` is not an ancestor of HEAD) would have saved a review cycle.
- **`GET`/`POST` name collisions in `detect_changes`:** reviewers reported multi-route diffs scored HIGH/CRITICAL through same-named route handlers. On a fresh 1.6.12 index, a one-line edit to a single route's `GET` (both `export const GET = …` and `export async function GET`) scored `low` with 0 processes, so we cannot yet show it minimally. Bare `impact GET` correctly returns `status: ambiguous` (703 candidates).

### Suggestions

1. Resolve impact anchors by declaration site, and don't propagate a non-exported declaration past its own file.
2. Weight or separate `IMPORTS` from `CALLS` in the risk roll-up, or report an `imports_only` share next to `impactedCount`.
3. Don't report `epistemic: exact` when depth ≥ 2 is reached only through `IMPORTS` from a File node.
4. Flag nodes with an empty `filePath` in `impact`/`detect_changes` output as a stale-index signal.

title: fix(routes): resolve Express receivers and router mount paths
body:
## Summary

Express endpoints now use proven receivers and mounted paths in both ingestion and group HTTP contracts. A Router endpoint registered at `/users` and mounted at `/api` now appears at `/api/users`; unrelated object methods such as `storage.get('/not-http', 'fallback')` no longer create routes.

## Motivation / context

The earlier middleware-admission correction still left receiver guesses and missing Router mount prefixes, producing inaccurate endpoint graphs and cross-repository HTTP links.

Related: #3561

## Areas touched

- [x] `gitnexus/` (CLI / core / MCP server)
- [ ] `gitnexus-web/` (Vite / React UI)
- [ ] `.github/` (workflows, actions)
- [ ] `eval/` or other tooling
- [ ] Docs / agent config only (`AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `.cursor/`, `llms.txt`, etc.)

Route architecture documentation and the implementation plan are included.

## Scope & constraints

**In scope**

- Prove Express apps, Routers, aliases and builders through existing AST, ParsedFile lexical identities and configured import resolution.
- Compose static nested, repeated and array mounts before handler/source-priority selection.
- Share provenance and composition with source-only and graph-assisted group extraction; preserve consumers, Nest/data routes and direct Hono registrations.

**Explicitly out of scope / not done here**

- Executing application code, arbitrary factory evaluation, regex expansion, implicit HEAD/OPTIONS routes or Hono mount expansion.
- Changing graph schemas, dependencies, CI or public commands.

## Implementation notes

Two optional provider hooks carry opaque per-file facts through workers and the parse cache. Shared ingestion does not interpret framework details. JS/TS providers resolve those facts together before route winner selection; group extraction uses the same resolver over its existing parsed trees.

Standalone routers retain local paths. Known dynamic mounts suppress guessed root paths while independent static mounts remain valid. Ambiguous imports, lexical shadows and conflicting writes fail closed. Mutations through namespace aliases invalidate the underlying Router; uncertain mount parents cannot revive unprefixed child routes. Cycles terminate and expansion-limit exhaustion omits the affected component atomically.

The parse-cache version changes from 143 to 144. Mount, barrel and configuration edits recompute cross-file paths without caching derived prefixes in unchanged router files.

## Testing & verification

- Final reviewed tree: **444 tests passed across 10 focused suites**, covering receiver proof, mount composition, mutation invalidation, worker merge, parse-cache replay, ingestion integration and group extraction.
- Build, source/test typechecks, changed-file lint (zero errors), formatting and pre-commit hooks passed.
- Full core suite on the implementation before the two final review fixes: **26,326 passed, 46 failed, 98 skipped**. This run is **not green**. All 41 non-setup failures reproduce on unchanged base `6c0c75c`; they concern host process/PID and lock behavior, update checks, and an existing CPU-count expectation. The other five setup failures pass on both base and final code when inherited `CODEX_HOME` is removed from only the test subprocess environment.
- One full-run worker was killed while running `incremental-orchestration.test.ts`; all **39 tests passed** on the final code when rerun alone.
- GitNexus impact/change analysis ran. Graph coverage remains partial/UNKNOWN: new helper files are absent from the baseline index. Refresh attempts hit host resource limits and then an index lock whose process identity could not be verified in this environment. The lock was left intact; new-file callers and behavior were checked through source review and tests.
- Browser checks skipped: no product UI or served application route changed. Express fixture routes are parser input.
- Both actionable final-review findings were fixed and covered by regression tests.
- A subsequent simplification pass reused the existing export-write predicate and shared fixture writer. All **59 scoped tests**, core source/test typechecks, project-wide lint (zero errors; existing warnings), formatting and pre-commit hooks passed.
- **Fluent-chain efficiency fix:** member-call receivers are evaluated once, preserving depth, work-budget and factory-mutation guards. Real AST regressions now resolve every route in 13-call and 24-call chains. The 24-call fixture drops from 132,382 evaluator calls (12 routes resolved) to 305 (all 24 resolved). All **75 focused tests** across provenance, composition, ingestion and group extraction passed, along with source/test typechecks, scoped lint and pre-commit hooks. Scoped correctness, testing, performance and standards review found no further issues.

## Risk & rollout

Stricter provenance intentionally removes routes previously inferred only from receiver names or unresolved values. Re-run `gitnexus analyze` to rebuild affected route data; old parser-cache entries are invalidated automatically. No database-schema migration is required.

title: fix(eval): retain measurements across background completion turns

## Summary

Retain valid evaluation measurements when the pinned Claude CLI emits another result after a background task completes. Give both runtimes and arms a 60-minute session ceiling within the existing overall deadline and cleanup reserve.

## Motivation / context

The failed evaluation had one successful session rejected for emitting two results and two sessions that reached the previous 30-minute ceiling. EC2 cleanup succeeded.

Related: https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/actions/runs/38873262106

## Areas touched

- [x] `.github/` (workflows, actions)
- [x] `eval/` or other tooling

## Scope & constraints

**In scope**

- Validate background continuation evidence and account for the complete session.
- Run a pinned-CLI offline canary before paid sessions.
- Allow 3600 seconds per session while preserving the overall deadline and 5400-second evidence/cleanup reserve.

**Explicitly out of scope / not done here**

- No paid evaluation dispatch, release publication, or changes to task/model pins.
- No retroactive validation of the failed run or claim of MCP benefit.

## Implementation notes

Continuation results must share a session ID, have distinct result IDs, successful outcomes, complete usage, and a background notification followed by a fresh foreground turn. Tokens and turns are summed; cost uses the final cumulative value; elapsed time includes background wait. Malformed and replayed evidence remains excluded.

The real Claude CLI 2.1.214 canary performs an actual background Bash task against a loopback MockProvider. It verifies accounting across two result events, with external traffic blocked and no inherited host credentials.

## Testing & verification

- 228 targeted evaluation tests passed, 4 skipped.
- 71 evolution tests passed, 1 skipped.
- 1 real pinned-CLI background completion canary passed.

body:
Bumps [express](https://github.com/expressjs/express) from 5.2.1 to 5.3.0.
Release notes

Sourced from express's releases.

v5.3.0

Highlights

🐞 Bug fixes

  • Fixed HTTP header conflict between Content-Length and Transfer-Encoding in res.send - by @​YuryShkoda in #4893

    Fixed the behavior of res.send() to prevent conflicts between Content-Length and Transfer-Encoding HTTP headers in responses. The Content-Length header in res.send() is now only added when a Transfer-Encoding header is not present, complying with the HTTP specification that states both headers should not coexist in the same response. ETag generation is unaffected by the presence of a Transfer-Encoding header - by @​cuishuang in #7459

  • Upgrade qs to ^6.16.0, which fixes CVE-2026-2391 (GHSA-w7fw-mjwx-w883), CVE-2026-82417 (GHSA-4mjr-xmp4-gh2g) and CVE-2026-82562 (GHSA-x5fp-wj9c-mxmx): arrayLimit bypasses in comma parsing and a denial of service via an attacker-controlled isBuffer - by @​davetashner in #7057 and #7478, and @​cyphercodes in #7305

  • Upgrade proxy-addr to ^2.0.8, which fixes CVE-2026-90711 - by @​lazerg in #7474

🚀 Improvements

  • Allow conditional revalidation for QUERY requests. req.fresh previously only validated freshness for GET and HEAD requests, so QUERY responses never returned 304 despite a matching validator. Since QUERY is a safe, idempotent, and cacheable method that supports conditional requests, it is now included in the freshness check - by @​Cherry in #7366

    // QUERY /reports with If-None-Match: "12345"
app.query('/reports', (req, res) => {
  res.set('ETag', '"12345"');
  res.send(results); // now responds 304 Not Modified
});

  • Improve HTML structure in res.redirect() responses when HTML format is accepted by adding <!DOCTYPE html>, <title>, and <body> tags for better browser compatibility - by @​Bernice55231 in #5167

  • When calling app.render with options set to null, the locals object is handled correctly, preventing unexpected errors and making the method behave the same as when options is omitted or an empty object is passed - by AkaHarshit in #6903

    app.render('index', null, callback); // now works as expected

  • Upgrade content-type to ^2.0.0, bringing a faster parser (~1.5x quicker Content-Type parsing/formatting in res.send()) along with a behavior change: res.send() now keeps any existing parameters when adding the charset and no longer throws on a Content-Type that fails to parse. type-is is upgraded to ^2.1.0 as part of the same change - by @​blakeembrey in #7234

    res.set('Content-Type', 'text/plain; foo=bar').send('hey');
// -> Content-Type: text/plain; foo=bar; charset=utf-8

  • The default error handler now logs the full error object instead of only its stack trace, so nested details such as Error.cause and library-specific properties (e.g. Sequelize's parent/original) are no longer swallowed - by @​Nitin-Mohapatra in #6464

  • Upgrade content-disposition to ^2.0.1, which changes the Content-Disposition header emitted by res.download(), res.attachment(), and res.sendFile(): file names that are valid HTTP tokens are no longer wrapped in quotes. This is equivalent per RFC 6266, but applications asserting on the exact header bytes should update their expectations - by @​blakeembrey in #7233

    res.attachment('user.html');
// before -> Content-Disposition: attachment; filename="user.html"
// after  -> Content-Disposition: attachment; filename=user.html

title: feat(cache): derive parser and PDG cache identities automatically
body:
## Summary

Parser and PDG changes now invalidate cached facts automatically, so contributors no longer allocate or reconcile semantic version counters. Reuse is tied to the artifacts actually executed, including a compiled worker selected by a source-mode parent.

## Motivation / context

Manual counters can collide across branches or remain unchanged when grammar bytes or compiled workers change. This PR completes the approved automatic cache identity implementation, including paired-store reuse, shared graphs, recovery, installed-package coverage, and contributor guidance.

## Areas touched

- [x] `gitnexus/` (CLI / core / MCP server)
- [ ] `gitnexus-web/` (Vite / React UI)
- [ ] `.github/` (workflows, actions)
- [x] `eval/` or other tooling (cache benchmark)
- [x] Docs / agent config (contributor and shipped review guidance)

## Scope & constraints

**In scope**

- Automatic base and PDG identities for all supported providers, with compatible paired-cache reuse and isolated shared-store publication.
- Source execution, built packages, effective parser options, interruption recovery, and concurrent analyses.

**Explicitly out of scope / not done here**

- Bridge database and wire-format version changes, semantic code normalization, and per-language cache identities.

Publication retains the original three commits; later changes were transferred through GitHub browser upload commits because local git push credentials were unavailable. Validation commit IDs below identify the reviewed local reconstruction.

## Implementation notes

- Base and PDG identities remain separate from graph DDL and analyzer freshness. A CFG-only edit changes PDG keys; worker count does not.
- Conservative artifact boundaries hash raw bytes and are guarded by an import-coverage audit. Comments inside those boundaries can invalidate caches.
- Unknown identity disables persistent parser reuse and keeps the rebuilt graph private. Artifact changes during analysis reject publication.
- Slot-owned staging is reclaimed under its index lock, with unique children for late worker writes. Publication refreshes the compatible live cache index while retaining current repairs.
- Artifact guards reuse the regular file snapshot in direct and subprocess validation. Symlinks retain separate target and link checks.

## Simplification follow-up

Shared optional-grammar directive parsing and matching between runtime loading and cache identity, while retaining lazy runtime memoization. Identity frame sorting now serializes each UTF-8 sort key once. A regression test verifies that identity capture reads current options without changing the runtime loader's remembered selection.

- **Validation:** 155 focused tests passed (144 unit tests across seven files; 11 real-process/installed-package integration tests across three files). Production and test type checks, build, formatting, whitespace checks, and project ESLint passed. ESLint excluded the separate nested worktree and reported zero errors with 8,183 existing warnings. The full suite was not rerun for this follow-up.
- **Equivalence/performance:** 5,508 grammar-selection comparisons passed against the built shared helpers; 20,000 frame comparisons preserved the original stable UTF-8 order. Seven fresh-process cold distribution-identity samples had medians of 634.5 ms before and 624.9 ms after; this small difference is within shared-host variability and is not a general speedup claim.
- **Graph coverage:** refreshed the index and reran change mapping. It maps nine production symbols across the four changed files and 117 affected flows; the anonymous test callback remains unmapped and was inspected directly. Existing skipped-row/process-budget warnings remain. This is partial coverage, not a clean graph clearance. The maintainer approved the reported HIGH/CRITICAL impact before edits.
- **Publication:** remote head `4f93205ffef4ebd6160f18755f8d17a5e2992a78` and tested local commit `dd0f64f3f69f5e808cc904fec51826f6f45d5164` have the identical Git tree `bf3fc58711bea91c076b5fd09c9119a386124bd9`. The three browser commits contain exactly the tested four-file update.

## Testing & verification

- Initial publication verified after resolving the upstream merge: remote head `1dd095428d0ba52f2e1271948c32635277205fb5` and reviewed local head `b25b136f6959cdaf58be08d440ab10fdc0c5768b` have the identical Git tree `cde3514aca41f44f50bf8a324124abbd940b23a8`. The complete 80-file PR matches the validated reconstruction byte-for-byte.

- Full `npm test -- --maxWorkers=2` run: 26,305 passed, 88 failed, 98 skipped. All failures were investigated: 46 reproduce on pre-change `94f167a9`; 42 came from test fixtures updated by this PR. Those seven files now pass all 163 tests in targeted reruns. The full suite was not rerun after those corrections.
- `npm run test:integration -- --maxWorkers=2`: 6,779 passed, 12 failed, 41 skipped. Three failures are covered by the passing fixture reruns above; five reproduce on the baseline. Three Spring AOP cases pass with the normal native pool (12/12) after the suite's constrained 128 MiB pool exhausted. The remaining installed-package test passes in the main checkout (1/1); packing through the isolated worktree's dependency symlink had produced paths rejected by tar.
- Merged current `main` (`f8209df2`) and reran 216 focused tests across 10 files, including Express route provenance and cache lifecycle; all passed. The installed-package test also passed after the merge (1/1).
- Production and test type checks, build, Prettier, and whitespace checks passed. Scoped ESLint has zero errors and 189 warnings (174 preexisting, 15 guarded assertions).
- Real-process regressions cover unchanged commits with changed compiled workers, unknown provenance, same/different-identity overlap, interrupted staging, and installed packages. Warm replay tests assert cache metrics and graph facts.
- The final artifact-guard optimization passes 105 targeted tests across eight files, including symlinks, native artifact mutations, and both guard backends. The compiled-worker publication-rejection test and installed-package test pass again on the final build; independent review found no regression.

Independent full code review completed (run `20261016-194740-5ceacd2a`); all three findings were fixed with failing-then-passing regressions. All findings from that local review were fixed. Local validation uses Linux x64 / Node 24; Node 22 and Windows require CI. Baseline failures involve process-start probes, file locks, update notifications, local Codex setup, and CPU-count assumptions.

The graph was refreshed after the upstream merge and final guard optimization. Change mapping was rerun and remains partial (80 PR files, 428 mapped symbols, 132 affected processes); unmapped comments, module-level declarations, and test callbacks were inspected. Graph coverage also retains skipped-row and process-budget warnings, so this is not a clean graph clearance.

Final benchmark against `f8209df2`, using the exact code at `4f0322cd` (seven replay/CLI samples, 64 TypeScript files, one worker):

| Measurement | Main | Candidate |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Warm replay median | 1,849.6 ms | 1,626.8 ms (-12.0%) |
| Fresh-process unchanged CLI median | 1,566.4 ms | 2,111.9 ms (+34.8%, +545.5 ms) |
| Distribution identity warm p95 / cold | — | 26.3 ms / 626.5 ms |
| Source identity warm p95 / cold | — | 44.5 ms / 793.8 ms |

Both declared budgets pass: warm identity p95 below 50 ms and warm replay overhead below 5%. Every warm replay asserts 64 cache hits and zero reparsed files. Fresh CLI startup remains slower and is reported separately; it has no declared budget. Shared-host timings varied across runs, so the replay result is not a claim of a general speedup. Raw samples are committed in `gitnexus/bench/parse-cache-identity/baseline.json`; `candidateDirty` records the previous benchmark JSON as the sole uncommitted file during measurement.

## Risk & rollout

Existing numeric cache versions miss once. Source/distribution switches and parser artifact edits may also require a cold parse. Existing embedding preservation, graph schema checks, analyzer freshness, and explicit cache bypass remain in place.

## Post-Deploy Monitoring & Validation

During the first upgrade validation, the maintainer should analyze a representative repository, force a second analysis to verify matching parser-cache hits, then change a parser artifact and confirm a rebuild. Check that graph facts and embedding counts remain consistent with the intended change. Missing compatible cache hits after repeated runs, foreign graph facts, or repeated parser-stage growth warrant investigation; use `--no-parse-cache` while diagnosing cache reuse. The repository has no central deployment metrics or assigned rollout owner, so these are local CLI checks rather than an assumed monitoring service.

## Checklist

- [x] PR body meets repo minimum length.
- [x] No secrets, tokens, or machine-specific paths committed.

title: HTTP embedding: single-line structural node produces a 2×-content text that 400s and permanently drops its whole sub-batch
body:
## Summary

A single over-limit embedding text fails its entire sub-batch, permanently dropping every node in it. The over-limit text is generated for a long structural node whose stored `content` is a single line: `generateStructuralTypeText` emits both `declarationOnly` and the chunk body, and when the chunker cannot split the content the two are nearly the same content — doubling the text length past the endpoint's per-input limit.

## Environment

- gitnexus **1.6.12** (also checked 1.6.13-rc.115: `dist/core/embeddings/text-generator.js`, `chunker.js`, `character-chunk.js` are byte-identical to 1.6.12)
- Windows 11, Node v22.x
- HTTP embedding backend, OpenAI-compatible endpoint, `BAAI/bge-m3` (8192-token input limit), 1024 dims, `GITNEXUS_EMBEDDING_REQUEST_DIMS=omit`
- `GITNEXUS_FTS_CJK_SEGMENTATION=bigram` (CJK runs are space-segmented at write time, stretching stored `content`)

## Observed

One `Interface` node in a `.ts` file (stored `content` ≈ 6,470 chars, a **single line** after FTS normalization) yields a sub-batch of 8 texts:

```
chars: 338, 344, 577, 214, 14208, 7880, 7878, 7880  → HTTP 400
```

The endpoint rejects the whole request, so the pipeline logs `dropping 5 node(s)` — 4 of them are small (214–577 chars), and the three ~7.8K texts succeed on their own (a follow-up 2-text request with 7880 + 7749 returned 200).

`embedding-checkpoint-pending` then sticks forever: every subsequent `analyze` re-sends the same 8-text sub-batch, gets the same 400, and the 5 nodes stay without vectors. `gitnexus status` reports the index `stale` / incomplete indefinitely, and no run ever succeeds in clearing it.

## Threshold measured

Same endpoint, same model: 12,285 chars → 200, 14,208 chars → 400. The failing text sits just above the per-input limit.

## Root cause

1. The stored `content` of the node is a single line (FTS normalization + CJK segmentation collapse it to one line). The line-based chunker cannot split it, so the chunks it produces are ≈ the whole content.
2. `generateStructuralTypeText()` (`dist/core/embeddings/text-generator.js`) unconditionally pushes `declarationOnly`, then pushes `cleanedChunk` when `cleanedChunk !== cleanedContent`. For this node both parts ≈ the full content, so the first chunk text = header + `Container:` + declarationOnly + chunk ≈ **2× content ≈ 14.2K chars**.
3. Nothing caps the generated text by size or estimated tokens before it is sent.
4. One 400 fails the whole sub-batch (`embedding-pipeline.js` → `batchFailedNodeIds`), so the 4 healthy nodes lose their embeddings too.
5. The checkpoint design keeps retrying the identical doomed sub-batch, so recovery never happens by itself.

## Suggested fixes (any one would help)

- Cap the generated embedding text (chars or estimated tokens) before the HTTP call; split + merge when over budget.
- In `generateStructuralTypeText`, skip `cleanedChunk` when it is equal to / contained in `declarationOnly`.
- On a 4xx for a sub-batch, retry it one text at a time and drop only the offending text — collateral nodes keep their vectors.
- Give the checkpoint a terminal state for persistently-rejected nodes so the index can become "complete" instead of retrying forever.

## Repro sketch

Any large single-line structural node reproduces the shape: take an `interface` whose content survives FTS normalization as one line, run `analyze --embeddings` against an endpoint with a per-input limit, and watch the sub-batch fail as a whole while its healthy members succeed individually.

title: status reports a permanently stale index for repos containing a symlink to a directory (1.6.12)
body:
### Summary

On a repository containing a **symlink to a directory**, `gitnexus status` reports the index as permanently stale, even though the index was just built at the current HEAD and the next `gitnexus analyze` exits with `Already up to date`.

The drift report names the symlinked directory itself as an "added" file, so the warning can never be cleared.

### Environment

- GitNexus 1.6.12 (global npm install)
- macOS arm64, Node 24
- `git status` is clean; indexed commit == current commit

### Reproduction

```bash
R=/tmp/gx-symlink-repro
rm -rf "$R"; mkdir -p "$R/app" "$R/shared"
printf 'int shared(void){return 1;}\n' > "$R/shared/shared.c"
printf 'int main(void){return 0;}\n' > "$R/app/main.c"
ln -s ../shared "$R/app/shared"
cd "$R" && git init -q && git add -A
git -c user.email=a@b.c -c user.name=a commit -qm init

gitnexus analyze "$R" --index-only
cd "$R" && gitnexus status
gitnexus analyze "$R" --index-only
```

Actual (`status`):

```
Indexed commit: 89c23a1
Current commit: 89c23a1
Index content: 0 changed, 1 added, 0 deleted
  added: app/shared
Status: ⚠️ stale (re-run gitnexus analyze)
```

Second analyze:

```
GitNexus Analyzer (1.6.12)
Already up to date
```

Expected: `status` reports the index as current, or the symlinked directory is excluded consistently on both sides.

A real-world instance had 52 tracked directory symlinks (all pointing at sibling directories such as `../../shared/<name>/`), producing exactly 52 permanent "added" entries.

### Root cause (observed in the 1.6.12 dist build)

1. `core/ingestion/filesystem-walker.js` scans with `glob('**/*', { nodir: true })`, which returns a **symlink to a directory** as a file entry (e.g. `app/shared`).
2. `storage/file-hash.js` `computeFileHashesDetailed()` cannot read that path (the target is a directory, so reading fails), and reports it as unreadable. Only the successfully hashed map is persisted to `meta.fileHashes`, so the symlink path is **never recorded**.
3. `core/index-content-drift.js` re-scans with the same walker and diffs the result against `meta.fileHashes`. Since the recorded set can never contain the symlink path, it is always classified as `added`.

`analyze` cannot repair it either: its up-to-date decision is git-based and exits (`Already up to date`) before rewriting `fileHashes`, so re-running analyze does not converge.

This looks like the same class of unclearable-stale verdict that #3077 addressed for other walker/index mismatches; directory symlinks appear to be a remaining gap.

### Suggested fix

Either is sufficient:

- Make `walkRepositoryPaths` skip symlinked directories (e.g. an `lstat`-based regular-file check) so neither `analyze` nor the drift scan sees them; or
- Exclude paths that `analyze` cannot hash from the drift comparison (e.g. persist the scanned-but-unreadable set in coverage metadata and compare `added` against the union).

### Workaround

The index itself is correct; the warning is a false positive. Adding the symlinked paths to `.gitnexusignore` may hide them from the drift scan, but this is unverified.

> **Superseded by #3948 on 15 November 2026.** The new tracker is the active priority queue for 32 open issues (31 engineering items and one cleanup item). The six open direct sub-issues from this tracker have moved there; the 31 completed direct sub-issues remain here as history. Closing this tracker does not mark the unresolved work completed. The dated audits and evidence below are preserved; use the successor for current statuses and priorities.

---

## Purpose

This issue tracks the **32 engineering issues and one tracker-cleanup issue** from the 17 October 2026 triage. It also records later fixes, performance improvements and evaluation work.

The original 33 issues and the later additions have separate progress counts. Each entry explains what changed and what still needs to happen. Inclusion here is not a commitment to ship in 1.6.13.

The current audit comes first, followed by the dated progress updates, original issue checklist and duplicate review. The history and supporting evidence remain inline.

- **Merged:** the implementation is in the main branch.
- **Released:** the implementation has been checked against a specific published version. A release candidate (RC) is separate from the stable release.

Duplicate connections, `/mcps` behavior, and persistence under a live service remain upstream in [OpenCode #37844](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/37844); closure does not claim those behaviors or the reporter's original registry-race cause are resolved.

## Completed during this triage

Closed with verified fix/release comments: #3019, #3467, #3566, #1168, #1173, #95, #265, #749, #508, #2933. Closed #169 as not planned without duplicating its existing explanation. All eleven states and ten new comments were read back from GitHub.

Validation: passing build and test typecheck, 238 focused tests, and direct parser, ingestion, chunk-generation, and symlink-walker probes. This was not a full cross-platform or private-repository reproduction.

## Tracker cleanup and publication — original 17 October record

The publication attempt below is historical. Later progress/verification comments are linked in the current checklist; #713 is still open.

- [ ] #713 — **Cleanup** — Close promotional badge submission as **not planned**. No product engineering work is needed; this does not endorse its third-party security grade.
- [ ] Publish the prepared progress updates on the 32 engineering issues after checking for newer activity. Those comments were **not posted** during the triage pass.

The connector rejected writes with HTTP 403. The approved browser fallback completed eleven closures, then automatic browser security review blocked #713's closure. That issue remained open with no new comment; no workaround was attempted.

## Duplicate audit — 17 October 2026

**Result: no confirmed full-scope duplicate among these 33 that justifies closing a ticket now.** There are partial overlaps, historical recurrences, and two unresolved duplicate candidates. Keep all 33 direct sub-issues. This is an evidence-based disposition, not a guarantee that future reproductions will not establish a common cause.

Screened the current **244 open issues (including this tracker)** for candidates, compared relevant report bodies and available discussion, and searched closed reports across embeddings, rename, freshness, routes, taint, evaluation, plugins, process lifecycle, and multi-repository support. This was a duplicate/scope review, not a new reproduction or an exhaustive review of every closed issue. A shared error message, subsystem, or implementing PR is insufficient for duplicate closure.

### Scope ownership and decisions

| Tracked ticket | Closest overlap | Disposition and boundary |
| --- | --- | --- |

Do not close this newer reproducible path into an already-closed retry report. |

| #3529 | #3530, #3598; closed #3306 | Keep: transient native database address-space ceiling. EOF reads, V8 cached-vector OOM, and phase-resume requirements have different failure conditions. |
| #3530 | #3529, #3591 | Keep: native staging-file read failure during embedding DELETE. Investigation has not reproduced the natural EOF failure or proved a causal link to the publication race. |
| #3607 | #702; closed #2790, #2467 | Own final generated-text limits and isolation of permanently rejected inputs. Chunk configuration, malformed HTTP-200 retries, and partial-node resume are related but do not satisfy this acceptance case. |
| #702 | #3607 | Keep only remaining chunk configuration/strategy acceptance; refer final-text budgeting to #3607 so it is implemented once. |
| #628 | closed #695, #2385 | Keep embedded/in-process model selection. External Ollama/HTTP support and its misleading network diagnostics are separate. |
| #3608 | #1541, #3127; closed #3077, #2668 | Keep the directory-symlink walker/hash mismatch and convergence fixture. Older dirty-worktree checks, stale server metadata, and warning controls do not establish this fix. |

| #2858 | #3487, #3488; closed #1183, #701 | Keep original QwenPaw end-to-end prefix matching. #1183 explicitly directs residual work here; explicit gateway mappings in #701 are not the same as resolving an application's composed paths. Reuse shared extraction fixes. |

| #2973 | closed #3486, #2605, #3032 | Keep cross-call preview/apply binding and stale-plan rejection. Semantic edit accuracy and edit-count correctness do not ensure apply uses the exact previously approved plan. |
| #2193 | #1308; closed #77 | Keep broader workspace/system graph, infra/test/docs relationships and UI. Existing Groups and the older multi-repo vision overlap, but do not complete this scope. |
| #1308 | #2193 | Own multi-repo MCP selection/API decision and scale verification. Treat as a narrow capability contributing to the broader workspace request, not a second workspace implementation. |
| #264 | #663, #2510; closed #312 | Own global/shared skill installation and the documented no-duplication workflow. Plugin-specific defaults/on-demand indexing belong to #663; MCP initialization instructions belong to #2510. |
| #663 | #264, #1011, #2510; closed #52, #312 | Own the remaining plugin/default-generation/on-demand-indexing contract. Global storage and optional skip flags do not meet the request to change default behavior. #1011 is a related user report, not proof all plugin requirements are duplicates. |
| #3524 | #1496, #2456; closed #297, #3030 | Keep opt-in MCP refresh, discovery/call-time policy, and file-side-effect guarantees. An eval-server HTTP endpoint, CLI recovery contract, watch mode, or hot reload alone does not provide that tool. |

### Consolidation rule

When two tickets overlap, use the issue identified above to own the implementation, and link its PR and test evidence from the other ticket. Close a ticket as a duplicate only when the issue that remains open contains its reproduction and all unresolved acceptance criteria. For #3474/#3569 and #3527/#3564, first obtain the missing original-environment evidence; do not erase those verification requirements based on a similar synthetic failure. Historical closed reports remain references rather than reasons to close an unresolved recurrence.

No tickets were closed by this duplicate audit; priority counts remain unchanged.

## Completion

Close this tracker when each engineering item is resolved, explicitly descoped with a linked decision, or transferred to a separately accepted follow-up scope, and cleanup/publication is complete. Keep implementation discussion and repro details in the linked issues. Do not close unresolved child issues merely to complete this tracker.

title: fix(devcontainer): refresh Node and streamline development
body:
## Summary

The devcontainer uses a supported Node runtime, reuses unchanged dependency volumes, and verifies Husky on every setup. Native-workspace, UI and prebuilt-image profiles improve setup and daily development while retaining the existing host-checkout configuration.

## Motivation / context

The previous image ran Node 22.16.0, below the CLI and web dependency engine requirements. Setup also repeated dependency installs and ownership changes, while compilation and indexing could run over Docker Desktop's cross-host filesystem.

## Areas touched

- [ ] `gitnexus/` (CLI / core / MCP server)
- [ ] `gitnexus-web/` (Vite / React UI)
- [x] `.github/` (development image validation/publication)
- [x] Other tooling: `.devcontainer/` and generated-profile ignore rule
- [ ] Docs / agent config only

## Scope & constraints

Development tooling only. Application source, package manifests, lockfiles, agent instructions and vulnerability remediation are outside this change. Existing checkout-local indexes are not hidden behind new mounts. The native profile creates a separate remote checkout and preserves populated volumes.

## Implementation notes

- Pin the multi-architecture Node 22.23.3 image, enable container init, repair only incorrect owners/groups, reuse npm's cache, and exclude generated output/nested worktrees from VS Code watchers. Remove the global heap override so Node defaults and GitNexus's existing memory sizing apply.
- Cache successful dependency installations using manifests/lockfiles, local file-dependency manifests, Node/npm version, ABI/platform/architecture, tracked native build inputs, and the core optional-grammar setting. Changed inputs or missing direct dependencies run `npm ci`; failed installs invalidate their receipts. `GITNEXUS_FORCE_DEPS=1` repairs nested damage or inputs outside the fingerprint.
- Always run root Husky preparation and verification, including cached setup. Preserve tracked `.husky/pre-commit` while rebuilding its generated runtime cache. A temporary sentinel exercises the installed Husky helper and its startup configuration, rejecting disabled or skipped hooks without running the tracked formatter. Shared/CLI source builds remain independent of dependency reuse.
- Persist `GITNEXUS_HOME` in a native volume, retaining shared worktree stores and parse caches. Checkout-local `.gitnexus` remains in place. Native workspace profiles put the whole checkout on a native volume; bootstrap refuses a different origin or conflicting user files and never resets an existing checkout. Fresh branches track their remote, and `native --url` supports branches pushed to contributor forks.
- Generate native, UI, prebuilt and combined profiles from the main configuration using host Node without installing npm dependencies. UI images install OS dependencies for the locked Playwright version; runtime Chromium uses a persistent cache and private 1 GiB shared memory.
- Add setup timings, environment diagnostics and a development test runner with cgroup v2 CPU/memory-aware worker limits plus an explicit override. Keep ordinary package test commands available.
- Use native Codex installation with a package seed for reused config volumes. Enable pipefail, download retries and executable checks for the CLI installers.
- Keep 9p tuning enabled by default with SYS_ADMIN, exact-mount detection, a configurable 1 MiB target, a bounded non-interactive remount, and verification afterward. Failures never block startup. No actual 9p speedup is claimed.
- Validate default/UI builds in CI. A separate main-only workflow tests tooling and publishes amd64/arm64 core/UI toolchain images with registry caches, unique build tags and rolling aliases. Published metadata omits host mounts and project lifecycle hooks to avoid duplicate execution. PRs never publish images.

## Testing & verification

- [x] `node --test .devcontainer/*.test.cjs` — 90 passed. Covers grammar-setting cache invalidation, failed-install recovery, native input changes, cached real-Husky restoration, startup configuration disabling hooks, formatter/typecheck enforcement, default 9p behavior/failures/timeouts, profile flag validation, fork URLs, and native checkout conflict/retry/tracking behavior (including ignored user files), bundled-asset invalidation, local file-dependency manifest invalidation in all three dependency groups, Git ref validation, and UI generation with custom capabilities, custom-image Feature retention, short image names and uppercase tags.
- [x] Development runner: 57 CLI invocation tests and 15 web graph-load tests passed. Standard `npm test -- test/unit/resolve-invocation.test.ts --maxWorkers=2` also passed (57 tests).
- [x] Environment diagnostic command and read-only fingerprints exercised against the real workspace. Official Dev Container CLI resolved the combined native/UI configuration using a stub for Docker container discovery; this is configuration validation, not a container test.
- [x] ESLint for CJS helpers/tests, Prettier, the repository workflow-concurrency checker, and actionlint passed for the review fixes. Earlier shell/workflow syntax checks also passed (ShellCheck unavailable locally).
- [x] Earlier runtime validation: 109 focused core tests, CLI build/typecheck, strict-engine dependency dry-runs and ownership/lifecycle fixtures. Node 22.16.0 reproduces the engine mismatch; 22.23.3 passes both dependency trees.
- [x] Default/UI image builds and config tests passed [Devcontainer Smoke CI](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/actions/runs/39017077796) at `94b944042`, before the final review fixes. New head builds remain pending.
- [x] The previously failing import-target benchmark passed locally with its original threshold unchanged. Image profile fixes are in `3c72337e9`, and local devDependency receipt invalidation is fixed in `788f85c80`; fresh CI is pending for the latter.
- [ ] Current full image builds, real browser provisioning, multi-architecture publication and actual Docker Desktop remount performance require CI/container validation. Docker is unavailable locally.
- [ ] Full core suite previously did not complete because of repeated native worker readiness timeouts in this environment.
- [ ] Graph change analysis remains partial after retry: the new devcontainer CJS helpers/tests are not indexed. Direct references are confined to development lifecycle commands, profile generation, tests and workflows; this is not a clean graph-coverage result.

The earlier Linux ownership fixture measured 67.9 ms before versus 17.5 ms after over 10,000 correctly owned files (three-run medians). This measures ownership repair only. The dependency cache tests prove unchanged installs are skipped; no total startup speedup has been measured.

## Risk & rollout

Rebuild to apply the runtime, mounts and SYS_ADMIN capability. Broad mount privileges can weaken read-only bind protections; the README qualifies those guarantees and documents disabling tuning/removing the capability. A native volume is a separate authoritative checkout: push/export changes before deleting it. Export an existing shared store from an old container's writable layer before removing that container.

Prebuilt images become usable after merge and the first successful main-branch publication. New GHCR packages start private; a maintainer must enable public visibility for anonymous pulls, or users must authenticate. Local builds remain the default. Generated profiles must be regenerated when the main configuration changes.

## Checklist

- [x] PR body meets the repository minimum length.
- [x] AGENTS.md / overlays are unchanged.
- [x] No credentials or machine-specific environment values committed.

title: fix(taint): report inline and factory handler flows
body:
## Summary

`explain --pdg` reports cross-function taint from TypeScript/JavaScript inline callbacks and factory-returned handlers. Findings retain the handler's function identity, including same-line callbacks, and complete persisted source-to-sink paths.

Related: #3489, #3609

## Motivation / context

Named handlers worked, but bare callback and return expressions could have CFGs without graph Function definitions. A line-only summary join could also attribute callbacks to their enclosing function. Private expression names and generated display names needed distinct binding rules to avoid inventing call targets.

## Areas touched

- [x] `gitnexus/` (CLI / core / MCP server)
- [ ] `gitnexus-web/` (Vite / React UI)
- [x] `.github/` (workflows, actions)
- [ ] `eval/` or other tooling
- [ ] Docs / agent config only

## Scope & constraints

Covers callback arguments in bare expression statements and directly returned function expressions, including arrows, async callbacks, named/anonymous factory returns, same-line ownership, stable nested IDs, recursion, and lexical visibility. Array-result bindings retain their existing exclusion; arbitrary callback-context completeness is not claimed. Uses the existing graph and semantic layer; language behavior stays in providers. Captured closure-variable taint remains unsupported and the explain description says so. No compiler, LSP, or storage schema dependency is added.

## Implementation notes

Provider captures create the missing callable definitions. Shared orchestration separates source identity from generated display names, preserving existing anonymous-owner prefixes. Summary joining uses exact columns when available and conservative unique-line fallback otherwise. Private named expressions and anonymous display identities do not become guessed global call targets; authored bindings and named-expression self recursion remain valid. Generated names also comply with the existing persisted taint-path codec.

## Testing & verification

Current head: `8a8317ee7755bd78246ca17e25818ecf6bd7d6c7`. Merge commit `c35dc60c86845c6146f90b0d08ebd612091a51b9` includes `origin/main` at `30676685e03893f94081dc40e8c6b8c7fb9578df` after #3613–#3617 landed. The two conflicts were adjacent additions in CI benchmark steps and the native-test registry; both parents’ additions and both benchmark working directories are preserved. The merge tree matches the previously verified combined P1 checkout. The earlier `cb4a3b86e` follow-up changes only the persisted-explain assertion to reject all enclosing factory/container names, including `makeFilterHandler`. [Current source CI](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/actions/runs/39064312515) verifies the scheduling follow-up; the preceding run at `cb4a3b86e` timed out in coverage. The superseded merge-head run was canceled after preserving its artifacts; no full pass is claimed for that run.

CI timing diagnosis: the old estimator assigned nearly equal weights to sequential database suites despite observed runtimes from about one second to eight minutes. On `cb4a3b86e`, shard 1 received 1,037 seconds of sequential work; the other shards received 186–328 seconds. Tiny generated rename wrappers also defeated the file-size estimate. Commit `8a8317ee7` adds measured cost hints to the existing balancer and a replay regression, preserving the shard count, timeout, real integration tests and coverage thresholds. The regression fails on the prior code at 1,027 seconds versus a 600-second ceiling for the seven overlapping heavy suites. After the change, actual Vitest partitioning assigns all 1,272 files exactly once and the heaviest recorded sequential workload is 487 seconds. These are scheduling estimates from recorded timings, not a claim that indexing itself became faster. All 25 partition tests, test typecheck, lint and formatting pass; graph change analysis covers 15 symbols in two files at LOW risk without partial/truncated results. Fresh hosted verification is [running](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/actions/runs/39064312515). No full pass is claimed for the failed predecessor.

Previous-head `cb4a3b86e` evidence: both benchmark jobs and all 96 expected native cases passed on macOS/Windows, with no skips/errors. Full CI failed because coverage 1/8 exceeded its 25-minute job limit; completeness correctly rejected the missing report.

Local merge verification: **223/223 tests across 12 suites**, checked with the execution-report reconciler (zero failures/unverified), build, test typecheck, scoped formatting and lint all pass. Inline-taint and publication benchmark checks pass. All five new benchmark commands remain wired exactly once; all 159 parent native-test entries survive without duplicates, with peak estimated shard weight 989s below the unchanged 1,020s limit. Repeated graph change analysis maps 551 symbols across 84 incoming files and four flows, but remains partial/UNKNOWN for one test helper; that helper is byte-identical to main and its two real indexing tests pass. No implementation, threshold or timeout changed to resolve this merge. The separate review assertion follow-up passes 72 focused tests with zero failures, skips or execution errors, plus test typechecking and formatting. Its graph change analysis maps three test symbols in one file at LOW risk without partial/truncated coverage. The repeated array-callback review was checked again with real TS/JS worker ingestion; the actual callback retains its identity and result bindings remain excluded.

Pre-merge evidence at `2cc97b445853d91a2ede556162208a77f9fcdc5c`, containing then-main `2251adeeb`. The host-owned update changed only eval files; runtime and workflow implementation are unchanged from `089209292`. [Pre-merge source CI and its final conclusion](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/actions/runs/39040069255) are recorded in GitHub Checks. The completed-job receipts below verify all 82 native cases and the benchmark; they do not substitute for the overall CI gate.

| Native spec | Windows | macOS |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Interprocedural taint | [9/9 passed](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/actions/runs/39040069255/job/117422320268), 18.30s | [9/9 passed](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/actions/runs/39040069255/job/117422320284), 10.87s |
| Persisted explain | [21/21 passed](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/actions/runs/39040069255/job/117422320315), 10.30s | [21/21 passed](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/actions/runs/39040069255/job/117422320275), 5.94s |
| Function identity | [11/11 passed](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/actions/runs/39040069255/job/117422320269), 18.25s | [11/11 passed](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/actions/runs/39040069255/job/117422320265), 10.29s |

All 41 cases per OS passed without skips or execution errors. Windows enclosing shards took 684/388/718s; macOS 170/161/377s (interprocedural/explain/identity). Every shard stayed within existing headroom. No scheduler weights or watchdogs were relaxed.

The native regression command is:

```bash
cd gitnexus
npm test -- test/integration/cfg/interproc-taint.test.ts \
  test/integration/taint-explain.test.ts \
  test/integration/function-local-identity.test.ts --maxWorkers=2
```

The native execution audit compares every expected case name with the uploaded Vitest execution records, requires all cases to pass without skips, checks zero execution errors, and ties the reports to the exact head and actual runner jobs. Three changed native specs are explicitly registered for Windows/macOS; a failing-then-passing selection guard prevents silent omission. Their Windows scheduler weights remain documented estimates, not claimed measurements. Existing watchdogs and headroom checks are unchanged.

- Six focused files: 212 passing tests, including real worker ingestion, persistence, cold explain, named-handler controls, constant/capture negatives, exact anonymous callers, unchanged nested IDs, private-name refusals, and same-spelling collision controls. The coordinated P1 composition independently passes these assertions.
- Real CLI cold/incremental/repeated analysis: 11 findings, then 12 after an edit, then 12 again, all with complete expected source-to-sink paths. Existing Python CFG joining also passes with zero unresolved anchors or reaching-def gaps.
- Production/test typechecks, formatting, and ESLint pass with zero errors.
- [Pre-merge benchmark job](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/actions/runs/39040069255/job/117418220876) passed in 9m48s within its unchanged 25-minute budget. ## Summary

Budget the final generated embedding text, including headers and structural context, and isolate HTTP input rejections so one rejected input cannot permanently prevent healthy batch members from receiving vectors.

Related: #3607, #3609. Integrate identity validation (#3614) first when applying both changes.

## Changes

- Add `GITNEXUS_EMBEDDING_MAX_INPUT_CHARS` (default 4,096 UTF-16 units). Split final text without dropping content or splitting Unicode pairs; preserve contiguous chunk IDs and include the budget in the content fingerprint.

title: fix(rename): apply the exact reviewed edit plan
body:
## Summary

Rename apply executes exactly the edits approved in a successful preview. Changed source bytes, physical targets, graph identity, provider resolution semantics or supported source inventories invalidate that approval instead of causing apply to compute a different edit set.

## Motivation / context

Related: #2973, #3609. Builds on #3557's semantic spans and per-call snapshots; that merged change still replans between separate preview and apply calls. Published stable `1.6.12` and RC `1.6.13-rc.116` tarballs were verified against their SHA-512 metadata; neither has this token contract. The other storage, embedding, status and taint changes remain separate PRs.

## Areas touched

- [x] `gitnexus/` (CLI / core / MCP server)
- [ ] `gitnexus-web/` (Vite / React UI)
- [ ] `.github/` (workflows, actions)
- [ ] `eval/` or other tooling
- [ ] Docs / agent config only (`AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `.cursor/`, `llms.txt`, etc.)

## Scope & constraints

**In scope**

- Apply requires the successful preview's opaque `plan_token`, matching repository, symbol and destination.
- Preserve graph/provider planning, exact UTF-16 spans and tracked/untracked source evidence.
- Report landed, failed and unattempted files accurately; require a fresh reviewed preview after failure.
- Keep tool schemas, recovery hints, generated context and shipped instructions consistent.

**Explicitly out of scope / not done here**

- No compiler/LSP dependency, whole-workspace transaction, ignored/private-tree scan or raw configuration-byte binding.

## Implementation notes

Single-use capabilities expire after 15 minutes and survive neither eviction nor server restart. The process retains at most 16 plans within a 64 MiB estimate, including opaque provider configuration. Edited files retain full snapshots; unedited semantic and supported inventory sources retain canonical targets and SHA-256 evidence. Hashing uses bounded 64 KiB reads, including oversized unindexed files.

Approved edited targets survive the validation-to-execution handoff. Preview rejects an unedited source aliasing an edited destination. Apply validates source evidence before each replacement and configuration semantics at token consumption and after staging before the first installation. Provider-owned fresh loading bypasses workspace-package memoization without replacing the indexing memo. Configuration Maps/Sets and data-only classes compare correctly; the original Rust instance remains available to resolution. A small callback factory prevents retained configuration refreshes from retaining the planner's source/graph context.

Only edited source text remains retained. Stable symbol identity excludes optional context enrichment. Lazy provider loading preserves MCP startup. Tokens cannot move between processes, so read-only clients obtain a new reviewed preview from the writable server.

These paths are not mocked.

Final review fixtures pass 62/62: the approved cache destination is asserted before retarget refusal, apply-success routing includes its token, and missing-token routing requests a fresh preview. Mocked MCP routing tests supplement the real integration paths.
- [x] New preview-cache, executor and preview-plan integration suites are explicitly selected exactly once by the Mac/Windows shard planner. Combined six-PR partition guards pass with a 971-second peak below the unchanged 1,020-second limit. Actual final-head reports verify all 53 cases in the three newly registered filesystem suites on each OS, with success=true, zero execution errors and reason=passed. The seven real modes take 52.289 s on Mac and 115.141 s on Windows; the 175-second Windows scheduling hint remains conservative. No timeout or assertion gates changed.

title: analyze --no-stats has no effect: counts are still written to AGENTS.md / CLAUDE.md

### Area

gitnexus (CLI / core / indexing / MCP server)

### Summary

  What happens
  Running npx gitnexus analyze --no-stats . on a repo whose CLAUDE.md / AGENTS.md already has a <!-- gitnexus:start --> block regenerates the block with the counts still in it

### Context

  regenerates the block with the counts still in it:

  This project is indexed by GitNexus as **my-repo** (493905 symbols, 698316 relationships, 300 execution flows).

  Expected: the counts are left out, as the help text says: "Omit volatile file/symbol counts from AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md".

  Cause
  dist/cli/index.js:25 declares the flag with commander's negation syntax:

  .option('--no-stats', 'Omit volatile file/symbol counts from AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md')

  Commander turns --no-stats into options.stats === false (default true). It never sets options.noStats. But dist/cli/analyze.js
  reads options.noStats:

  // analyze.js:165
  noStats: options?.noStats,
  // analyze.js:219
  await generateAIContextFiles(repoPath, sp, result.repoName, {...}, skillResult.skills,
    { skipAgentsMd: options?.skipAgentsMd, noStats: options?.noStats });

  So noStats is always undefined, and generateGitNexusContent always writes the counts. Calling generateAIContextFiles(..., {
  noStats: true }) directly leaves them out correctly, so the generator is fine and only the flag wiring is broken.

  Suggested fix: either pass noStats: options?.stats === false, or rename the option to --omit-stats / .option('--no-stats') → read
  options.stats.

  Repro
  1. Create a repo with any source file and run npx gitnexus@1.6.3 analyze .. The counts appear in CLAUDE.md.
  2. Run npx gitnexus@1.6.3 analyze --no-stats .. The counts are still there.

body:
## What

Adds OpenCode v1 hooks alongside MCP and skills. Setup installs a self-contained plugin at `~/.config/opencode/plugins/gitnexus.js`; uninstall removes that file while preserving sibling plugins. title: feat(logger): public API to route the default logger into a host's sink (destination + mixin)
body:
### Area

gitnexus (CLI / MCP server) — `src/core/logger.ts`

### Problem or opportunity

A host that embeds GitNexus (for example, one that runs `gitnexus serve` or the MCP server as a long-lived service) usually has its own logging setup: one log file per service, request IDs carried across async calls, redaction before records reach disk. Today there is no supported way to send GitNexus's own records into that setup.

Every module logs through the `logger` singleton or `createLogger(name)`, and both write to stderr (`pino.destination({ dest: 2 })`, or `pino-pretty` on a TTY). The only way to redirect the singleton is `_captureLogger()`, which is test-only by name and contract. A host is left with two bad options: capture and re-parse stderr, or patch `logger.ts` and carry that patch through every upstream merge.

### Proposed solution

Promote the seam `_captureLogger()` already uses into a small public API, for example:

```ts
export interface LoggerSinkOptions {
  /** Where records go instead of stderr. */
  destination?: pino.DestinationStream;
  /** Base level; GITNEXUS_LOG_LEVEL still applies when unset. */
  level?: string;
  /** Extra fields merged into every record (pino `mixin`), e.g. a request ID from AsyncLocalStorage. */
  mixin?: () => Record<string, unknown>;
}

/** Route the default logger and every later createLogger() child through this sink. Returns a restore function. */
export function configureLoggerSink(opts: LoggerSinkOptions): () => void;
```

Behaviour:
- After the call, the `logger` singleton (already a Proxy, so modules that imported it earlier pick this up) and every later `createLogger(name)` child write to `destination`, with `mixin` fields on each record.
- `flushLoggerSync()` flushes the configured destination when it supports `flushSync`.
- Without a call, nothing changes: stderr, pretty on a TTY, the same levels.

### Alternatives considered

- **Capture stderr and re-parse it in the host.** This loses records when the process exits hard, mixes in any non-logger stderr writes, and can't add a request ID to the record at write time.
- **Use `_captureLogger()`.** It's underscore-prefixed, documented as test-only, and throws on a second call, so a host can't rely on it.
- **Patch `logger.ts` downstream.** It works, but every upstream merge has to re-apply it.

### Acceptance criteria

- With no `configureLoggerSink` call, output is byte-identical to today: same stderr records, same pretty mode, same levels.
- After `configureLoggerSink({ destination })`, records from the singleton and from `createLogger('x')` children reach `destination`, and none reach stderr.
- A `mixin` field appears on every record.
- The returned restore function brings back the stderr behaviour.
- `_captureLogger()` keeps working; it may be re-implemented on top of the new API.

### Constraints

- No new runtime dependency.
- The stdout/stderr split from #324 must not change: logs never go to stdout by default.
- Hot-path cost must not change when the API is unused.

title: feat(mcp): reduce response size and query overhead
body:
## Summary

Agents can request focused MCP evidence and retrieve keyword matches with fewer graph reads. Optional response filters retain symbol identity and diagnostics; ordinary requests keep their existing response format.

## Motivation / context

Large graph responses consume model context, while hydrating each matching file separately adds query latency. The maintainer-gated evaluation support is already merged; this PR contains the measured runtime and agent-guidance changes.

Related: #3622

## Areas touched

- [x] `eval/` or other tooling — cancellation-test synchronization

## Scope & constraints

**In scope**

- Single-repository MCP `query`/`context` response sections and context relationship filters.
- Bounded BM25 symbol hydration with existing ranking, ordering, identity checks and per-file fallback semantics.
- Focused exploration/debugging guidance in canonical and shipped skills.

**Explicitly out of scope / not done here**

- New defaults, ranking/traversal changes, embeddings, index migrations, and group-mode response filters.
- Retrieval pushdown: response filtering applies after existing bounded retrieval.

## Implementation notes

For callers only:

```js
context({
  uid: "<symbol id>",
  response_sections: ["incoming"],
  relationTypes: ["CALLS"]
})
```

`response_filter` identifies omissions; omitted evidence is not evidence of absence. Errors, ambiguity, staleness and completeness diagnostics remain. Existing byte-budget behavior is unchanged, and filter metadata can outweigh savings on small responses.

BM25 hydration reads up to 100 matching files per batch instead of issuing one graph read per file. Ordinary batch failures retry through the existing per-file path; corrupt identities still fail closed.

### Measured performance

Four tasks, three repetitions each, model `gpt-5.6-sol`, effort `xhigh`:

| MCP agent sessions | Solved | Total model cost | Mean session time |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: |
| Historical baseline | 12/12 | $58.6427 | 815.5 s |
| First PR candidate | 12/12 | $51.4229 | 903.2 s |
| Batched-hydration candidate | 12/12 | $50.2291 | 753.7 s |

The latest candidate used **14.3% less model spend** and **7.6% less mean session time** than the historical baseline. These are descriptive whole-agent measurements across 12 sessions, not guarantees for other workloads or an isolated causal estimate.

Evidence: [historical baseline](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/actions/runs/39039452570), [first comparison](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/actions/runs/39117852384), [latest comparison at `1385607bf`](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/actions/runs/39130467617). - Real native hydration coverage compares batched results with individual graph reads across files and node tables.
- The cancellation-test PID race was reproduced with delayed writes; atomic publication passed 20 delayed SIGINT/SIGTERM cases and the process-control suite (22 passed, two platform skips).

Filters are opt-in; clients should send the new options only when the server advertises them. body:
## Summary

CI now catches the LadybugDB string-scan defect behind the blank or duplicate `CodeEmbedding` keys and the unnecessary re-embedding. The new checks run on the embedding table itself, at the row counts where the defect appears. This PR changes tests only; the engine fix is already on main (0.21.1, #3442).

## Motivation / context

The two released builds in these reports both pin `@ladybugdb/core` **0.18.3**: 1.6.12 (#3569) and 1.6.13-rc.57 (#3474). Main has pinned 0.21.1 since rc.73. 0.18.3 has LadybugDB #737: `StringColumn::scanFiltered` reads string positions that belong to a later segment from the current segment. The stored bytes stay intact, but scans return blank or mispaired strings. This was already proven for `Method` rows after a selective DELETE/COPY (#3564).

New evidence:

| Experiment | 0.18.3 | 0.21.1 |
|---|---|---|
| Native `CodeEmbedding`: 8,192 rows, production schema and statements (exact-id DELETE + CREATE, then DELETE by `nodeId` + re-insert for 64 owners), then CHECKPOINT | **3,936 wrong tuples**; a retained row's `{nodeId}` lookup returns nothing | 0 wrong |
| Native `Method` selective DELETE/COPY: `WHERE n.id = ''` vs `WHERE trim(n.id) = ''` | 0 vs **3,936** (the scan misreads; no stored blank ids) | 0 vs 0 |
| `COPY` of two rows with `id = ""` | rejected | rejected |
| Released 1.6.12 CLI, Java fixture (4,480 methods), deterministic local embedding endpoint: one method edited, then `analyze --embeddings` | **exit 1**: `Found duplicated primary key value Meth…`; the next runs re-send 4,772 and then 974 inputs | (main CLI) exit 0; sends **1** input, then 0, then 0 on `--force` |
| Released rc.57, two same-origin clones, shared store: dirty copy-on-write run, then a repeat run with no changes | sends **391**, then **2,824** inputs; the copy-on-write slot reads 2,703 blank `nodeId`s while the sibling commit graph stays clean | (main CLI) sends **1**, then 0; both graphs clean |

The cached-hash map is keyed by misread `nodeId`s, so unchanged nodes look new and are re-embedded. Misread ids that collapse to the same value (blank gives `:0`) make the batch `CREATE` throw a duplicate-primary-key error.

The existing guards (#3614) and the 12-node shared-store test stay below the 2,048-row native vector size, so they cannot see this defect.

Related: #3569
Related: #3474

## Areas touched

- [x] `gitnexus/` (CLI / core / MCP server). Tests and the native bench harness only.
- [ ] `gitnexus-web/` (Vite / React UI)
- [ ] `.github/` (workflows, actions)
- [ ] `eval/` or other tooling
- [ ] Docs / agent config only (`AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `.cursor/`, `llms.txt`, etc.)

## Scope & constraints

**In scope**

- A new `embedding` scenario in `bench/incremental-write-integrity/reproduce-search.cjs`. It uses the production `CodeEmbedding` schema (`FLOAT[384]`, `chunkIndex INT32`, same column order) and the writeback's own statements, and checks complete tuples after the write, after a checkpoint and after a read-only reopen, plus the `{nodeId}` lookup.
- `lbug-incremental-search.test.ts` runs that scenario. Per-scenario expectations are now a data table instead of `if` branches.
- `incremental-method-integrity.test.ts` runs both analyses with embeddings against a loopback endpoint that returns a distinct vector per input. A cold reader then checks three things: (1) only the edited file's inputs are sent; (2) all 4,096+ other `CodeEmbedding` rows, vectors included, are identical; (3) every `Method` of the edited file has exactly one row with a unique key.

**Explicitly out of scope / not done here**

- No source change and no dependency change. The 0.21.1 → 0.21.2 bump for the separate duplicate-row defect stays in draft #3578, which is blocked on Windows FTS.
- No replay of the reporters' private Windows or Docker hosts. The defect is in engine scan code, not in a platform path.

## Testing & verification

Linux x64, Node 22.23, main `b961e695c`.

- [x] `npx vitest run --project lbug-db test/integration/lbug-incremental-search.test.ts test/integration/incremental-method-integrity.test.ts`: **5/5 pass** on 0.21.1.
- [x] **Fails before the fix:**
  - `LBUG_MODULE=<0.18.3 core> npx vitest run --project lbug-db test/integration/lbug-incremental-search.test.ts -t embedding` fails at the after-checkpoint and reopened stages.
  - With the 0.18.3 native packages swapped into `node_modules`, `incremental-method-integrity` fails with `Graph identity reconciliation failed (post-COPY/checkpoint, Method): unexpected or duplicate ID`.
- [x] `node bench/incremental-write-integrity/reproduce-search.cjs embedding`: about 17 s on both engines. It exits 1 on 0.18.3 and 0 on 0.21.1.
- [x] `npm run typecheck:tests`, prettier, eslint (no new warnings).
- [ ] Cross-platform shards: both files are already in `scripts/cross-platform-tests.ts`. I left the shard weights unchanged because I have no clean timing for them. On this host the **unmodified** `incremental-method-integrity` took 231 s under load, so local numbers don't say what the embedding addition costs. Windows CI timing will tell.

A review pass (`/code-review`) raised eight findings; the changes made for them are already in the commit:

- Baseline rows are loaded in one transaction (74 s → 17 s).
- The harness runs the production exact-id DELETE before CREATE, with the production column types and dims.
- The test asserts the full key set for the edited file.
- The endpoint returns text-derived vectors, and the test reads them back.
- The endpoint handler answers errors with a 500.
- The test timeout is 300 s (originally 180 s).
- CSVs are no longer written for the embedding scenario.

Tests only. `incremental-method-integrity` is now slower because it embeds about 4,900 nodes through the loopback endpoint.

title: test(lbug): guard max DB size accounting across repeated checkpoints
body:
## Summary

A new native regression test makes CI catch an engine pin that leaks `max_db_size` accounting on every CHECKPOINT. That leak is the mechanism behind the transient "Maximum database size … has been reached" failure that a retry heals. This PR changes tests only. The engine fix is already on main (0.21.1, #3442).

## Motivation / context

The report says `@ladybugdb/core` 0.21.x, but `v1.6.13-rc.57` pins **0.18.3**. On 0.18.3, `ShadowFile::reset()` orphaned the shadow `FileHandle` on every CHECKPOINT. Each new handle took fresh 4 MiB VMRegion frame groups that count against `max_db_size` and are released only when the database closes (LadybugDB #924, fixed by #925 on 6 Sep, before 0.21.1).

Measured here, Linux x64:

| Workload (native, under a fixed ceiling) | 0.18.3 | 0.21.1 |
|---|---|---|
| tiny write + CHECKPOINT, 64 MiB ceiling | fails after **7** checkpoints (file 136 KiB) | 200/200 pass |
| empty CHECKPOINT only, 64 MiB ceiling | fails after **7** | 200/200 pass |
| embedding-shaped writeback (DELETE by `nodeId` + CREATE `FLOAT[384]`), 512 MiB ceiling | 63 checkpoints (64 rows each), 56 checkpoints (512 rows each): about **8.1–9.1 MiB per checkpoint** | — |
| real `analyze --embeddings` (force + 6 incremental runs), `GITNEXUS_LBUG_MAX_DB_SIZE=256 MiB` | rc.57: every run exits 1 without logging an error (passes at 4 GiB) | main: 7/7 exit 0 |

Every trait in the report matches. The accounting is per `Database`, so a fresh process starts from zero ("retry heals"). It counts handles, not bytes on disk ("the file is only a few GB"). And it grows with every checkpoint: rc.57 checkpoints every 5 s through the WAL driver and again every 5,000 embedding nodes, so the longest phase (embedding writeback) is where the ceiling is reached.

Magnitude: the leak grows with the pages each checkpoint shadows. At 2,048 rows × `FLOAT[1024]` per checkpoint (1 GiB ceiling) it failed after 35 checkpoints with a 303 MiB file, which is about 20 MiB leaked per checkpoint, compared with about 9 MiB for small writes. That is roughly 2.5× the vector bytes written plus the ~9 MiB floor. So one long embedding writeback that rewrites tens of GiB reaches 2^38. This is an estimate from measured rates, not a replay of the reporter's run.

Related: #3529

## Areas touched

- [x] `gitnexus/` (CLI / core / MCP server). Tests and test registration only.
- [ ] `gitnexus-web/` (Vite / React UI)
- [ ] `.github/` (workflows, actions)
- [ ] `eval/` or other tooling
- [ ] Docs / agent config only (`AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `.cursor/`, `llms.txt`, etc.)

## Scope & constraints

**In scope**

- `test/integration/lbug-checkpoint-accounting.test.ts` opens a database through `initLbug`, with `GITNEXUS_LBUG_MAX_DB_SIZE` set to 256 MiB. It then runs 128 cycles of row write + `tryFlushWAL()`, which is the CHECKPOINT call each driver tick makes. Any leak of 2 MiB or more per checkpoint exceeds the ceiling.
- The test is registered in the `lbug-db` project (include and default-project exclude) and in the cross-platform native list.

**Explicitly out of scope / not done here**

- No source or dependency change.
- Two mechanisms reproduced in earlier rounds have no guard here: spill-handle charges from a COPY, and logical-size growth after *failed* checkpoints. They are separate, and neither reaches 2^38 at the measured rates.

## Testing & verification

- [x] `npx vitest run --project lbug-db test/integration/lbug-checkpoint-accounting.test.ts`: passes on 0.21.1 in about 4 s.
- [x] **Fails before the fix.** With the 0.18.3 native packages swapped into `node_modules`, it fails with `Buffer manager exception: Maximum database size of 268435456 bytes has been reached.`
