title: test(server): make the opaque repo id assertion deterministic
body:
## Summary

`test/unit/repo-projection.test.ts` no longer fails at random. A check on the opaque repo id failed in about 0.5% of runs, independent of the code under test. It now checks a property that cannot be broken by chance.

## Motivation / context

The id comes from `publicRepoId`: an HMAC under `KEY = randomBytes(32)`, drawn once per process (`src/server/public-repo-id.ts:16`), truncated to 22 base64url characters. So the id is effectively random on every run. The test asserted `expect(a.id).not.toContain('ws')` to show the id does not leak the path `/ws/a/api`. But a random 22-character base64url string contains `ws` with probability 21 × (1/64)² ≈ 0.51%. CI hit it on #3624 (coverage shard 6/8): `expected 'gt5f4oNtpcwsi6vep8lzQN' not to contain 'ws'`.

Diagnosis:

| Probe (real module, `vi.resetModules()` gives a fresh key each time) | Result |
|---|---|
| 20,000 fresh keys: id contains `ws` | 93 (0.47%); theory 0.51% |
| 1,000 calls under one key | 1 distinct id (fully stable within a process) |
| Old assertion across 20,000 fresh keys | **118 failures** |
| New assertion across 20,000 fresh keys | **0 failures** |

The new assertion checks the opaque shape `/^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{22}$/` and that the full path is absent. `/` is outside the base64url alphabet, so the path cannot appear by chance. The existing `toBe(publicRepoId('/ws/a/api'))` and `not.toBe(b.id)` checks are unchanged.

**The same pattern elsewhere.** `ops-snapshot.test.ts` makes negative substring checks on `JSON.stringify(view)`. These are safe:
- Views of failed jobs carry no `repoId` (`publicJobRepoId` returns one only for `complete` jobs).
- Job ids are UUIDs, which cannot spell the names being checked.
- The one complete-job check (`'alice'`) has a collision chance of about 1.7×10⁻⁸.

`server-sse-payload` and `analyze-api` check full paths, which contain `/`, so they cannot collide.

## Areas touched

- [x] `gitnexus/` (CLI / core / MCP server). One unit test.
- [ ] `gitnexus-web/` (Vite / React UI)
- [ ] `.github/` (workflows, actions)

- [ ] Docs / agent config only (`AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `.cursor/`, `llms.txt`, etc.)

## Scope & constraints

**In scope**

- One assertion in `repo-projection.test.ts`.

**Explicitly out of scope / not done here**

- No change to `publicRepoId`. The per-process key is intended: ids must not be persisted, and they must reveal nothing about the path.

## Testing & verification

title: fix(group): read Python prefixed literals and f-string URLs as paths
body:
## Summary

Python consumers whose URL is an f-string, or any string with a prefix (`r`, `b`, `u`, `rb`, `fr`, ...), now produce real contract ids and can pair with providers. Before this change, `requests.get(f"{BASE}/api/items")` became `http::GET::/f"{param}/api/items"`, which no provider can match.

## Motivation / context

f-strings are the normal way to build a URL with a path parameter in Python, so this affects the common case. `unquoteLiteral` only unwrapped text whose first character is a quote. For a prefixed literal the first character is the prefix letter, so the prefix and both quotes stayed in the path.

Stripping the prefix alone was not enough. `{BASE}` then became a `{param}` first segment (`/{param}/api/items`), which still never matches. JS templates already treat a leading `${base}` before `/` as a host binding (#3111), so f-strings now follow the same rule.

## Areas touched

- [x] `gitnexus/` (CLI / core / MCP server)
- [ ] `gitnexus-web/` (Vite / React UI)
- [ ] `.github/` (workflows, actions)
- [ ] `eval/` or other tooling
- [ ] Docs / agent config only (`AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `.cursor/`, `llms.txt`, etc.)

## Scope & constraints

**In scope**

- `unquoteLiteral` drops a Python prefix when a matching quote pair follows it.
- The Python HTTP plugin reads f/t-string URL arguments from the node and writes each interpolation as `${expr}`. The shared consumer normalizer then strips a leading binding followed by `/` and turns later ones into `{param}`.
- The uri-variable wrapper path (`uri = f"..."; obj.fetch(uri=uri)`) passes the raw value to the shared normalizer instead of pre-normalizing it into a `{param}` segment. Its root guard also skips a url that is only a host binding.

**Explicitly out of scope / not done here**

- Implicitly concatenated strings (`"a" f"/{x}"`) are still not captured, because the queries match `(string)` only. This gap existed before this PR.
- f-string provider paths (`@app.get(f"{PREFIX}/x")`) keep using `unquoteLiteral`, which matches what ingestion reads.

## Implementation notes

| Call | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `requests.get(f"{BASE}/api/items")` | `http::GET::/f"{param}/api/items"` | `http::GET::/api/items` |
| `requests.get(F"/api/items/{item_id:d}")` | `http::GET::/f"/api/items/{param}}"` | `http::GET::/api/items/{param}` |
| `requests.post(rf"/api/raw")` | `http::POST::/rf"/api/raw"` | `http::POST::/api/raw` |
| `requests.request("PATCH", f"https://svc.local/api/abs/{id!r}")` | `http::PATCH::/f"https:/svc.local/api/abs/{param}"` | `http::PATCH::/api/abs/{param}` |
| `requests.get(f"{BASE}api/relative")` | `http::GET::/f"{param}api/relative"` | dropped (not a routable path) |

Every other `unquoteLiteral` caller was checked by parsing real literals with each grammar: Java, Kotlin, JS/TS (including tagged templates), Go and the gRPC and topic extractors are unchanged, because their literal node text starts with a quote. PHP binary strings (`b"/api/x"`) are the only other change, and they improve: the full path is now read instead of only the first `string_content` run.

## Testing & verification

- [x] `cd gitnexus && npx vitest run test/unit/group/`: 1329 passed.
- [x] FastAPI and group integration tests (`fastapi-composed-route-constants`, `fastapi-prefix-pipeline`, `group/http-route-resolve-symbol`, `group/monorepo-sync`): 28 passed.
- [x] `cd gitnexus && npx tsc --noEmit`: clean.
- The new test in `http-route-extractor.test.ts` fails on `main`, where all of its contract ids carry the prefix or quotes, and passes on this branch. It also covers a relative uri variable, a root uri variable, and a brace-only interpolation.
- An independent review found no P0 to P2 defects. It found two P3s, both fixed here: an f-string root behind a uri variable, and an interpolation whose expression is only braces.

## Risk & rollout

Low. The change only alters text that starts with a Python prefix followed by a quote pair, and Python consumer URL arguments. Existing group contracts for affected Python repos change from unmatchable ids to real ones on the next `gitnexus group sync`. No index schema change.

- [x] PR body meets repo minimum length (workflow may label short descriptions)

- [x] No secrets, tokens, or machine-specific paths committed

title: fix(group): read net/http HandleFunc and Handle on proven routers as method-agnostic routes
body:
## Summary

Go services that register routes with `HandleFunc` or `Handle` on a local `ServeMux`, a gorilla router or a chi router now produce provider contracts. Those routes are method-agnostic unless the code names a method, so consumers of every verb can pair with them. Before this change only a literal `http.HandleFunc(...)` was read, and it was always recorded as `GET`.

## Motivation / context

- **#1668:** the provider query pinned the receiver to the identifier `http` and the handler to an identifier or inline function. `mux := http.NewServeMux(); mux.HandleFunc(...)`, gorilla and chi routers, `Handle(...)`, method-value handlers (`api.ListUsers`) and raw-string paths produced no provider. A Go service using any of these had no HTTP surface in the group graph.
- **#1670:** a ServeMux registration serves every HTTP method unless its pattern names one. The plugin hard-coded `GET`, so a `POST /api/users` consumer never paired with the route.

The closed PRs #1669 and #1671 proposed accepting any receiver and emitting one provider per common verb. The matcher already pairs a `*` provider with consumers of every verb (Django, Nest `@All` and Hono `.all` use it), so a single `*` provider is the convention-aligned choice.

## Areas touched

- [x] `gitnexus/` (CLI / core / MCP server)
- [ ] `gitnexus-web/` (Vite / React UI)
- [ ] `.github/` (workflows, actions)
- [ ] `eval/` or other tooling
- [ ] Docs / agent config only (`AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `.cursor/`, `llms.txt`, etc.)

## Scope & constraints

**In scope**

- `HandleFunc` and `Handle` with exactly a path and a handler (identifier, inline function or method value).
- Method `*` by default. A Go 1.22 pattern gives its method (`"POST /p"`), and the host and the `{$}` anchor are dropped (`"GET host/p/{id}"` → `GET /p/{id}`). A gorilla `.Methods(...)` on the route chain, including after `.Host(...)` or `.Schemes(...)`, gives its verbs.
- Gorilla `PathPrefix("/p").Subrouter()` and chi `Route("/p", func(r chi.Router))` prefixes are joined into the path.

**Explicitly out of scope / not done here**

- Struct-field routers (`s.router.HandleFunc(...)`) are declined, because the file cannot show where the router is mounted. Missing a route is preferred to recording a wrong URL.
- chi verb methods (`r.Get`, `r.Post`) and client-side gaps (`client.Get`, `NewRequestWithContext`, `http.MethodPost` constants) are separate gaps.
- gin/echo test files keep their current behavior. Only the new net/http loop skips `_test.go`.

## Implementation notes

`HandleFunc` and `Handle` are common names outside HTTP: telebot registers bot commands with `b.Handle("/start", fn)`. So the receiver must be a proven router:

- the net/http package itself (DefaultServeMux);
- a binding to `http.NewServeMux()`, gorilla `mux.NewRouter()` or chi `chi.NewRouter()` / `NewMux()`;
- a gorilla subrouter or a chi `Route` / `Group` callback parameter of a proven router;
- a parameter typed `*http.ServeMux`, `*mux.Router`, `chi.Router` or `*chi.Mux`. Like gin groups, it keeps its literal paths.

A router that the same file mounts under a stripped or prefixed path (`Mount`, `StripPrefix`, gorilla `.Handler`) is declined, either directly or through the function that builds it (`r.Mount("/api", apiRouter())`). Its registered paths are not its URLs. Routers in `_test.go` files are httptest mocks and are skipped.

The handler naming logic (qualified and strict resolution) moves into one helper shared with the gin/echo loop. The gin/echo output is unchanged.

## Testing & verification

- [x] `cd gitnexus && npx vitest run test/unit/group/`: 1359 passed, including the new `go-nethttp-providers.test.ts`.
- [x] `test/integration/http-inline-handler-symbol-roundtrip.test.ts` and `go-gin-route-pipeline.test.ts`: pass.
- [x] `cd gitnexus && npx tsc --noEmit`: clean.
- The new table test fails on `main` (it emits `GET`, or nothing for `mux.HandleFunc`). A pairing test runs the real extractor and `runExactMatch`: a ServeMux route pairs with both a `GET` and a `POST` `fetch()` consumer.
- An independent review found three P2 defects in the first version, all fixed and covered by tests:
  - telebot slash commands were accepted as routes;
  - `_test.go` mock servers published contracts;
  - gorilla subrouter and chi `Route` prefixes were dropped.

  It also found two P3s: patterns that are not valid, and `.Methods` after other route matchers. The 10 new cases for these fail against the first version and pass now.
- Existing `http.HandleFunc` fixtures gained `import "net/http"`, because the receiver proof needs the import that real Go code always has. Their contract ids change from `GET` to `*`.

## Risk & rollout

Medium. Group contracts for Go repos change: existing `http::GET::` HandleFunc providers become `http::*::`, and new providers appear for ServeMux, gorilla and chi routes. They take effect on the next `gitnexus group sync`. There is no ingestion counterpart for net/http routes, so there is no graph parity concern. No index schema change.

## Checklist

- [x] PR body meets repo minimum length (workflow may label short descriptions)
- [ ] If `AGENTS.md` / overlays changed: headers, scope block, and changelog updated per project conventions
- [x] No secrets, tokens, or machine-specific paths committed

Fixes #1668

title: fix(routes): link base-URL fetch calls made through wrapper chains
body:
## Summary

`api_impact`, `route_map` and `shape_check` now see consumers that call a backend through a base-URL template and a chain of fetch wrappers. On GitNexus's own repository, the web client gets 23 correct `FETCHES` edges to the server routes. Before this change it got 0, and all three endpoints in the report were rated `LOW`.

## Motivation / context

The web client calls ``fetchWithTimeout(`${_backendUrl}/api/repos`)``. `fetchWithTimeout` forwards the URL to `resilientFetch`, which calls a local alias of `globalThis.fetch`. Each of three causes dropped those calls on its own:

1. `normalizeFetchURL` returned null for any URL that did not start with `/`, so a leading `${base}` dropped the call. The group layer already strips such a binding (#3111). The single-repo routes phase, which builds the `FETCHES` edges, did not.
2. The wrapper call collector required a `/`-leading literal, so the template never became a wrapper candidate.
3. Wrapper detection only looked five AST levels deep for a call to an identifier named `fetch`. Arrow-const wrappers sit deeper than that, and neither `fetchWithTimeout` nor `resilientFetch` calls an identifier named `fetch`.

## Areas touched

- [x] `gitnexus/` (CLI / core / MCP server)
- [ ] `gitnexus-web/` (Vite / React UI)
- [ ] `.github/` (workflows, actions)
- [ ] `eval/` or other tooling
- [ ] Docs / agent config only (`AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `.cursor/`, `llms.txt`, etc.)

## Scope & constraints

**In scope**

- A leading `${...}` run followed by `/` is stripped as a base URL, with the same rules as the group layer. The helper moves to `route-path.ts` so both layers share it.
- Wrapper detection walks the whole function. It accepts `fetch`, `globalThis.fetch`, `window.fetch`, `self.fetch`, and local aliases whose value names one of those.
- A function that forwards its own first parameter to a URL-carrying wrapper is a wrapper too.
- When `[param]` matches several sibling routes, the fetch links to the best-fitting one.

**Explicitly out of scope / not done here**

- Response shapes are still read from the whole handler file, so every route in a multi-route Express file shares one key list (the report's lower-priority note). Per-route slicing needs handler end lines for inline handlers and a guard for handlers that delegate. It deserves its own change.
- `api_impact` does not yet report a lower bound when some fetch URLs could not be resolved.
- `FETCHES` still runs from the consumer file to the route. Importers of `fetchRepos` are not counted.

## Implementation notes

**URL normalization.**
- A path whose every segment is a param (`${base}/${id}`, `${base}/${id}.json`) is rejected, because it would match every route of that depth.
- Interpolations are collapsed brace-balanced before the query split, so ``${repo ? `?repo=${repo}` : ''}`` no longer ends the path. An interpolation glued to the last static segment counts as a query or suffix.

**Which functions count as wrappers.** Precision rules from review:
- Aliases are read from the AST (`??`, `||`, `?:`, parentheses, `as`). A function whose only "fetch" is a string such as `'Failed to fetch'` or a comment is not a wrapper. Text matching produced 6 false seeds on GitNexus itself.
- A function is followed through forwarding only when its first parameter actually reaches fetch's URL argument. `track(event)`, which posts an event to a fixed URL, lends nothing to `navigate(path) { track(path) }`.
- A callee declared in the caller's file, or imported from a relative module, must be a URL carrier in exactly that module. A package-imported name is followed only when every recorded function of that name carries a URL. So an unrelated IPC `request(channel)` in another package does not make its callers wrappers.

**Sibling routes.** `[param]` matches any segment, so `/api/analyze/${id}` used to link to the first sibling registered (`POST /api/analyze/upload`). It now prefers the route whose segments match by kind (`GET /api/analyze/:jobId`).

## Testing & verification

- [x] `cd gitnexus && npx vitest run` over the route, fetch and group suites (85 files): 1807 passed.
- [x] `cd gitnexus && npx tsc --noEmit`: clean.
- A new integration fixture models `backend-client.ts` and `resilientFetch`, plus negative files: guard bypass shapes, `track()`, an IPC name collision, and sibling routes. `main` yields 0 of its edges. This branch yields exactly the 7 expected edges and no others.
- An independent review reproduced 3 P2 and 2 P3 defects in the first version on its own fixtures, and all are fixed:
  - the guard bypass;
  - text-based alias matching;
  - forwarding through non-URL seeds and colliding names;
  - first-sibling matching;
  - a `?` inside an interpolation.

  On its fixtures: the guard case now gives 0 edges, the false-wrapper case gives no false edges, and the collision case keeps only the true edge.
- On the reviewer's subset of GitNexus's own sources (`gitnexus/src`, `gitnexus-web/src`, `gitnexus-shared/src`), every edge comes from `backend-client.ts` and points at the route it calls. The list includes `/api/repos`, `/api/file`, `POST /api/query` and the `:jobId` routes.

## Risk & rollout

Medium. More consumers get `FETCHES` edges, and every edge still requires a URL that matches a route. Wrapper matching stays name-based at the call site, as before. The parse-cache identity hashes the analyzer source, so cached wrapper facts are rebuilt automatically. Re-run `gitnexus analyze` to pick up the new edges. No index schema change.

## Checklist

- [x] PR body meets repo minimum length (workflow may label short descriptions)
- [ ] If `AGENTS.md` / overlays changed: headers, scope block, and changelog updated per project conventions
- [x] No secrets, tokens, or machine-specific paths committed

Related: #3488 (the consumer-linking defect is fixed here; the lower-bound risk rating, importer counting and per-route response shapes stay open)

title: fix(routes): resolve Express registrations made through helper parameters
body:
## Summary

Express routes registered inside a helper that receives the app, the path or the router as a parameter are indexed again. On GitNexus's own server that restores `* /api/mcp` and `GET /`, which disappeared from `route_map` after #3603. It also adds the two SSE progress routes that #3487 reported as never found.

## Motivation / context

#3603 made Express receivers provenance-proven, which removed the receiver-name false positives. It also dropped every registration on a function parameter, because a parameter has no binding value. No test caught it: every Express fixture allocates `express()` in the same file as its routes.

| Route on GitNexus's server | Registered via | origin/main | This PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| `* /api/mcp` | `mountMCPEndpoints(app, backend)` | missing | `server/mcp-http.ts:44` |
| `GET /` | `registerWebUI(app, staticDir)` | missing | `server/api.ts:319` |
| `GET /api/analyze/:jobId/progress` | `mountSSEProgress(app, '<path>', jobs)` | missing | `server/sse-progress.ts:78` |
| `GET /api/embed/:jobId/progress` | same helper | missing | `server/sse-progress.ts:78` |

Over all of `gitnexus/src`, the route set differs from `main` by exactly these four additions.

## Areas touched

- [x] `gitnexus/` (CLI / core / MCP server)
- [ ] `gitnexus-web/` (Vite / React UI)
- [ ] `.github/` (workflows, actions)
- [ ] `eval/` or other tooling
- [x] Docs / agent config only (`AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `.cursor/`, `llms.txt`, etc.) — one `ARCHITECTURE.md` paragraph

## Scope & constraints

**In scope**

- A registration whose receiver, literal path or mounted router is a parameter of a named function resolves through each call site of that function. It is emitted once per site and attributed to the helper's file.
- The group layer shares the resolver, so it emits the same providers.

**Explicitly out of scope / not done here**

- Forwarding is one hop. A site argument that is itself a parameter does not resolve.
- CommonJS `require('./routes')(app)` is not followed (the callee is a call, not a name).
- A forwarded parent that is later mutated (`app.locals.x = 1`) still keeps its child router's standalone paths, as `main` already does for that shape.
- The other open #3487 items are not changed here: test-only routes are still in the inventory, and regex routes stay a documented boundary.

## Implementation notes

**What the route facts record.**
- Named function values carry an identity and the binding id of each parameter. A TypeScript `this` parameter takes no position. A parameter written anywhere in the body, nested closures included, takes none either.
- Calls to plain functions and to namespace or default import members are recorded as invocations. Only arguments that can carry an allocation or a literal path are kept, and arguments after a spread have no position.

**Fail-closed rules.**
- A helper with no recorded call site is evaluated as written. So `function mountApi(prefix) { app.use(prefix, router) }` with an unknown prefix still suppresses the router's standalone paths instead of exposing them at the root.
- An unproven argument establishes nothing.

**Cost.**
- Only calls named like a function that registers on its parameters are evaluated. Resolution stays near `main`'s cost: a 25,000-call barrel resolves in 14 ms here against 8 ms on `main`.
- Route facts on `gitnexus/src` grow from 13.8 MB to 17.9 MB.
- A function value's invalidation key now includes its identity, so a property write on one function (`Button.displayName = ...`) no longer disables the others.

## Testing & verification

- [x] `cd gitnexus && npx vitest run` over the route, Express, group and pipeline suites (107 files): 2432 passed.
- [x] `cd gitnexus && npx tsc --noEmit`: clean.
- New integration fixture `express-forwarded-registrations` mirrors the server's three helpers, plus a never-called helper. `main` produces only `GET /api/info`; this branch produces all five expected routes, each in the right file.
- New unit cases cover:
  - cross-file helpers;
  - the decline cases: two hops, unproven arguments, reassigned and runtime parameters;
  - mount composition through helper parameters: literal, runtime and unproven paths, a forwarded router, a `this` parameter, a spread, closure reassignment, and an unrelated function's property write.
- An independent review found one P1 in the first version, now fixed: a path-only helper with no recorded site exposed its router at the root. It also found three P2s, all fixed: a resolver cost cliff of up to 69 s, facts growth of 74–101%, and one function-property write disabling all forwarding. Its three P3s are fixed too: the `this` parameter, spread arguments, and closure reassignment. Each repro now gives the expected result.

## Risk & rollout

Medium. Repositories whose Express routes live in helpers get those routes back, or for the first time. The path-forwarding cases also fix one shape where `main` invented a root path (a router passed into a helper's `use`). Re-run `gitnexus analyze` to pick up the routes. No index schema change.

## Checklist

- [x] PR body meets repo minimum length (workflow may label short descriptions)
- [ ] If `AGENTS.md` / overlays changed: headers, scope block, and changelog updated per project conventions
- [x] No secrets, tokens, or machine-specific paths committed

Related: #3487 (item a and the parameter-receiver regression are fixed here; test-route inventory policy stays open)

title: Fix TS/JS/Vue lexical binding ownership and make fetch-wrapper detection scope-aware
body:
Follow-up to #3628 (fetch-wrapper consumers) and #3629 (Express forwarded registrations). Both PRs approximate lexical scope with identifier text, and both stop short of it for one shared reason: the scope lookup can attribute a write to the wrong binding. This issue specs the fix and the move to binding identity as one separate PR on top of them.

## Problem

`lookupLexicalName` lets a scope own a name through a type fact alone (`gitnexus-shared/src/scope-resolution/name-claims.ts:272-280`). TS/JS scopes set `lookupPolicy.nameClaimsComplete`, but only `assignment-inferred` facts are exempt (`:274`). The rebind rule `u = new User()` (`languages/typescript/query.ts:1316-1319`) records a `constructor-inferred` fact on the innermost scope containing the write. So a closure that assigns an outer variable becomes its owner.

| Source | Write resolves to |
|---|---|
| `function f(a){ const g = () => { a = new Foo(); } }` | the arrow (should be `f`'s parameter) |
| same with `a = evil` and module `const evil = new Map()` (chained via `followChainedRef`) | the arrow |
| module `let app;` + `const swap = () => { app = new Map(); }` | the arrow (should be the module binding) |

Effects today:
- `main` emits a false `GET /let-closure` route: the closure write invalidates the wrong binding id.
- #3629 masks it for parameters with a text-based `written` set and `shadowedBetween` walk.
- An initialized `var` that redeclares a forwarded parameter is not treated as a write at all. Reproduced on `main` (TS and JS), through the route-provenance test harness:

  ```js
  import express from 'express';
  function mount(app) {
    var app = new Map();
    app.get('/not-http', () => {});
  }
  mount(express());
  ```

  This yields `GET /not-http`; the same happens with `mount(app, marker = 0)`. The `variable_declarator` branch records a binding value without invalidating anything (`framework-route-facts.ts:307`), and the resolver substitutes the caller's `express()` for the parameter (`framework-route-resolver.ts:309`, `:373-377`). An uninitialized `var app;` correctly keeps the route.
- TS rename carries a workaround for the same defect (`importedReceiverIsReassigned`, `rename.ts:335-350`).
- #3628's fetch-wrapper detection uses text heuristics for aliases, the URL parameter, platform `fetch`, nested-helper reachability and call-site module identity. They are fail-closed in most places but wrong in some: `platformFetch` accepts any identifier spelled `fetch` (`fetch-wrapper.ts:322-323`), and a wrapper call through a local parameter name-matches a repo wrapper of the same name (`extractFetchWrapperCalls`, `routes.ts` `isWrapperCall`).

The rest of the scope model holds up. Probes through the real TS and JS providers resolve parameters (plain, destructured, default, rest), `catch` names, `var` and function hoisting, named function expressions, local classes, imports, globals, `for-of`, nested parameter shadowing, self-referential defaults and names inside `static {}` blocks correctly.

## Core invariant

Scope of the claim: ECMAScript-aligned binding resolution for the supported cases, with documented analysis approximations. In ECMAScript an assignment resolves its target through the environment chain (`ResolveBinding` → `GetIdentifierReference`) and writes through that reference (`PutValue`): **an assignment does not declare a new local binding.** (An unresolvable assignment in non-strict code creates a global-object property and throws in strict code; neither creates an innermost lexical owner.)

> For TS/JS/Vue, an assignment-derived type fact must not establish lexical ownership of a name. The name resolves to its declared binding. The receiver-type information the assignment carries is preserved unless the owner has a stronger declared type.

The policy stays with the providers: `nameClaimsComplete` is their declaration that claims are the complete set of lexical declarations, and shared resolution honours it fully. No language names in shared code.

## Proposed changes

1. **Ownership (`name-claims.ts`).** Under `nameClaimsComplete`, an inferred fact never makes a claim-less scope the owner. No change for other providers.

   **Type facts after the ownership change** follow GitNexus's existing annotation-precedence policy: the JavaScript-family contract says writes to ordinary locals retain their declared type, and `typeBindingStrength` ranks `annotation` (3) and `parameter-annotation` (2) above `constructor-inferred` (1) (`scope-extractor.ts:1330-1348`; pinned by `typescript-inferred-field-receiver.test.ts`, "an annotated field beats its own initializer").

   > A carried assignment-derived constructor fact cannot replace a stronger declared type fact on the resolved owner. When the owner has no stronger fact, retain the nearest eligible carried inferred fact.

   - Return the selected owner fact's complete `TypeRef`, including `declaredAtScope`, `lookupPosition` and `lookupPurpose`. Annotations resolve in the type namespace and constructor facts in the value namespace (`scope-extractor.ts:1236-1239`); copying only a type name across would break that.
   - Otherwise keep today's inferred-fact behaviour. The extractor's within-scope "later equal-strength match wins" rule (`:1258-1263`) is not extended across scopes.
   - This is GitNexus policy, not a language requirement: annotations are erased, so ECMAScript cannot require an annotation to outrank a constructor fact, and TypeScript itself narrows annotated unions after assignment. Fuller assignment and control-flow narrowing stays deferred.
   - Worked example: `function f(a: Base) { const g = () => { a = new Foo(); return a.m(); }; return g(); }`.

     | Question | Answer |
     |---|---|
     | Which binding does the assignment update? | `f`'s parameter `a` |
     | Which type does GitNexus keep for static member lookup? | `Base` (annotation precedence) |
     | Which implementation runs? | `Foo.m()`; `f(new Base())` returns `"Foo"` at runtime |

     Today the same-scope form (`function f(a: Base) { a = new Foo(); a.m(); }`) already keeps `Base` and drops the constructor fact; only the closure form yields `Foo`, through the ownership defect. After the change both forms agree: `a.m()` gets `CALLS → Base.m`. GitNexus's dispatch index walks ancestors (`scope-resolution/graph-bridge/method-dispatch.ts`) and does not add `CALLS` to subclass overrides for a statically typed receiver; the possible `Foo.m` stays represented by the existing `METHOD_OVERRIDES` relationship, which must not change. The direct `CALLS → Foo.m` that the defect produces today disappears and is an explained difference in the comparison below. Adding the suppressed constructor fact as an extra possible target is part of the deferred narrowing work.

   Ownership, name resolution, route facts, taint global-root detection and rename may change. Receiver targets may change only where restoring the owner's declared type changes resolution (acceptance below).
2. **Rename.** Delete the walk-past loop in `importedReceiverIsReassigned`, gated on the existing rename coverage.
3. **Shared binding helper.** Move `ownership`/`bindingId`/`isGlobal` out of `framework-route-facts.ts` into `createLexicalBindings(parsedFile, lineOffset)`.
4. **Express route facts.** Delete `written` and `shadowedBetween`; reassignment is decided only by the resolver's `invalidBindings`. Before removing those guards, binding-based invalidation must cover an initialized `var` declarator whose binding is a parameter of the same function: it overwrites the forwarded value and counts as a write. An uninitialized `var app;` is not a write.
5. **Fetch-wrapper facts and call sites** on binding identity, with these contracts:

   **Platform fetch evidence.** A parameter's spelling is never evidence. A default makes the platform call possible, not guaranteed (callers can override it).

   | Case | Classification |
   |---|---|
   | `function load(url, fetch) { fetch(url); }` | no platform-fetch evidence |
   | `function load(url, fetch = globalThis.fetch) { fetch(url); }` | accepted when `globalThis` resolves to the platform global |
   | `function load(url, fetch = fetch) { fetch(url); }` | no evidence: the initializer reads the parameter being initialized |
   | `function load(url, globalThis, fetch = globalThis.fetch) { fetch(url); }` | no evidence: `globalThis` is the parameter |

   Configured `fetchWrappers` (`.gitnexusrc`) stays the explicit opt-in; see the configuration contract below.

   **Reachability.** Seed from the outer function's directly evaluated code, follow resolved references to nested callable values, and repeat until nothing new becomes reachable. Self-references and unrooted recursive cycles do not seed reachability; once a helper is reached from live code, its own references participate normally. Direct uses of anonymous function values (IIFEs, inline callbacks) count. Class evaluation is handled independently of name references: it includes heritage expressions, computed keys, static field initializers and static blocks; method bodies and instance field initializers are deferred. Where the provider supports decorators, their expressions, application and deferred initializers follow that dialect's execution rules (decorators are a TC39 proposal, not ECMA-262). The fixed-point marking is GitNexus's approximation of potential execution; ECMAScript does not prescribe it, and reading or returning a function does not execute its body. A referenced class makes its methods *potentially* reachable, a conservative policy, not a claim that every method runs.

   **Call-site identity (automatic detection).** Resolve the callee's binding and any available import target first, regardless of import syntax: a tsconfig path alias or workspace package (`import { request } from '@app/http'`) goes through the same project import resolver the route facts already use (`resolveRouteModuleTargets`, `pipeline-phases/parse-impl.ts:1579`), not a repository-wide name match. Classify the resolved target directly. A known local non-wrapper (parameter, nested local), a different resolved import, or ambiguity prevents automatic name fallback. When target resolution is unavailable and there is no contradictory binding evidence, fallback is permitted only when exactly one distinct same-named definition exists and it is a proven wrapper. This fallback is an analyzer recovery heuristic, not proven lexical identity (ECMAScript import bindings refer to a specific module binding). The same rule replaces the name branch of the forwarded-callee check (`carriesUrl`, which today accepts several same-named definitions if all carry).

   **Configuration contract (explicit override).** Automatic detection never lets a local parameter or shadowing binding inherit wrapper status through a name match. A name listed in `fetchWrappers` is the user's explicit assertion and keeps today's behaviour (`routes.ts` matches configured names before any module check): with `fetchWrappers: ["request"]`, `function load(request) { return request('/api/items'); }` is a wrapper call; without that configuration it is not. Both cases are tested separately.

6. **Missing scope model.** When a file has no `ParsedFile`, skip only the scope-dependent HTTP analysis (wrapper facts and call sites), as route facts already are, and count it through the existing `scopeExtractionFailures`. All other ingestion for the file continues.

7. **Resolution contract.** Update `docs/languages/local-import-scoping.md` in the same PR:
   - declaration ownership, separate from scoped type and value facts;
   - the owner's declared type taking precedence over carried constructor inference;
   - binding identity for route and wrapper provenance;
   - the remaining parameter-default environment limitation and exactly when inference fails closed;
   - its cache paragraph, which still describes the old numeric schema gate: align it with (or link to) MIGRATION.md "Automatic parser cache identities".

The parse cache needs no manual invalidation: parser caches use artifact-derived identities, and both the worker-result cache and the durable `ParsedFile` store validate the base identity (MIGRATION.md; `parse-cache-identity.ts` hashes `core/ingestion` and `gitnexus-shared` src/dist). Validation must run on rebuilt workers: cache invalidation does not rebuild compiled parser code.

## Acceptance

| Area | Evidence |
|---|---|
| Ownership | Assignment facts preserve the declared binding; genuine shadowing still resolves locally. |
| Call graph | Compare all `CALLS` edges before and after the change on the same corpus with pinned baseline and candidate builds: direct, constructor, receiver and callable-value-flow calls. Inspect additions, removals and changed targets at the call-site level, and explain every difference before updating any baseline. Edge counts alone are insufficient. |
| Receiver inference | `receiver-resolution --check` passes. Receiver-target changes are permitted where restoring the resolved owner's declared type changes resolution; each is explained and inspected, and existing polymorphic dispatch behaviour is preserved: `METHOD_OVERRIDES` edges and ancestor dispatch are unchanged, and the worked example resolves exactly like its same-scope form. An annotated variable identifies an expected cause, not an automatic exemption. |
| Non-`CALLS` consumers | Route/`FETCHES`, rename, import-ownership, inheritance and taint regression suites stay green alongside the comparison; the contract lists these as ownership consumers that a `CALLS` diff cannot cover. |
| Contract | `docs/languages/local-import-scoping.md` describes the new ownership, precedence, provenance and limitation behaviour, and its cache paragraph matches MIGRATION.md. |
| Rename | Real indexing and rename coverage passes after removing the workaround. |
| Platform fetch | Unknown injected `fetch` rejected; valid defaults and configuration accepted; shadowed globals and self-referential defaults rejected. |
| Reachability | Unrooted recursive helpers stay excluded; rooted helpers and anonymous callable uses participate; class evaluation handled independently of class-name references. |
| Wrapper identity | Import aliases and project-resolved specifiers resolve to their target; local shadowing, a different resolved import and same-named collisions cannot be overridden by name fallback; fallback needs exactly one distinct proven-wrapper definition. |
| Configuration | A configured `fetchWrappers` name used through a local parameter is a wrapper call; the same call without configuration is not. |
| Express reassignment | `mount(app) { var app = new Map(); app.get('/not-http', …) }` and the `mount(app, marker = 0)` variant produce no route; `var app;` without an initializer keeps the route. |
| Missing scope | The affected analysis is skipped and counted without suppressing unrelated file ingestion. |

Plus: no `/let-closure` false route, the `fetch-base-url-wrapper` FETCHES list unchanged, `tool-accuracy --check` green, and no text-based `written` / `shadowedBetween` / `conflicting` / `localNames` / `referenced` heuristics left.

## Known limitation (not fixed here)

`function example(x = 1, get = () => x) { var x = 2; return [get(), x]; }` must produce `[1, 2]`: when a function has parameter expressions, its body gets a separate variable environment. GitNexus resolves all three `x` to one function scope, so the binding key `${scopeId}\0${name}` merges the parameter with the body `var`.

Parameter-default environment separation remains unsupported and can affect route or wrapper classification when a default expression, or a closure created there, refers to a name declared in the function body. For example, with an unshadowed platform `fetch`:

```js
function load(url, send = () => fetch(url)) {
  var fetch = () => 0;
  return send();
}
```

`send` calls the platform `fetch`, but the collapsed scope attributes it to the body's `var fetch`. These shapes stay outside this PR's correctness guarantees. Where binding identity is known to be ambiguous, the affected inference must not claim proven HTTP provenance. Concretely: when the formals contain an expression (`ContainsExpression(formals)` in `FunctionDeclarationInstantiation`: a default value, including defaults inside destructuring patterns; a rest parameter alone does not count), a name that the body declares and that is also a parameter or is referenced inside a parameter expression is ambiguous, and wrapper facts and route forwarding through it decline. The guard prevents unsupported conclusions; it does not implement the missing environments. The full environment fix is deferred (below).

## Out of scope

- Fuller assignment and control-flow narrowing, including temporal applicability of assignment facts (only after the write) and propagation across function boundaries. An assignment inside a nested function must not, merely by being captured, establish an unconditional type fact for outer code.
- Carrying factory-call facts (`x = make()`) for receiver narrowing.
- Storing type facts by binding at capture time instead of on the writing scope.
- Extending the ownership policy to other providers. In Python an assigned name is a local of the whole function block, subject to `global`/`nonlocal`, so this rule does not apply there.
- Separate binding environments for parameter defaults (limitation above).
- SvelteKit `load({ fetch })`.

## Prior art

- Ownership from declarations: eslint-scope (`Scope.__resolve`, write references resolved upward with `from` ≠ `resolved.scope`), Babel `constantViolations`, the TypeScript binder (`FlowAssignment`, no symbol for an assignment), scope graphs (Néron et al. 2015), stack graphs, SCIP `WriteAccess`, rust-analyzer `type_of_binding`.
- Closure narrowing: [TypeScript 5.4](https://www.typescriptlang.org/docs/handbook/release-notes/typescript-5-4.html) / microsoft/TypeScript#56908 preserves outer narrowing in closures created after the last assignment, and an assignment inside a nested function prevents it; Pyright documents the same rule.
- Host semantics: the HTTP meaning of `fetch` comes from the host API (WHATWG Fetch Standard), not ECMA-262; wrapper classification and the configuration allowlist are GitNexus policy.
- Injected fetch: CodeQL `FetchUrlRequest` (`globalVarRef("fetch")`, global variables only), eslint-utils `ReferenceTracker` (global variable plus `AssignmentPattern` defaults).
- Reachability: Semgrep `Taint_lambdas.ml` (recursive self-uses are not uses), babel-minify dead-code elimination.
- Name fallback: CodeQL call-graph imprecision grading, Joern `NaiveCallLinker` (name link only when unique).
- Parameter environments: ECMAScript FunctionDeclarationInstantiation.
- Python block-local binding: Python language reference §4.2.

title: Share embeddings (and graph deltas) across branches of the same repository
body:
### Area

gitnexus (CLI / core / indexing / MCP server)

### Problem or opportunity

Indexing several long-lived branches of one repository duplicates almost all of the embedding work and storage.

Within a single branch index, embeddings are already incremental: `contentHashForNode` (`EMBEDDING_TEXT_VERSION` + embedding text) is stored on `CodeEmbedding`, and a later `analyze` of that same index only re-embeds nodes whose hash changed (`runEmbeddingPipeline` + `loadCachedEmbeddings` in `run-analyze.ts`).

Across branches that reuse stops. `--branch` places each branch in its own LadybugDB (`branches/<slug>/`, or the flat slot for the owning branch; #2106, `branch-index.ts`). Each database has its own `CodeEmbedding` table and HNSW index. The cache load only reads the database currently being written, so branch B re-embeds nodes whose text is identical to branch A.

The parse cache is already shared at the repo root (`RepoMeta.cacheKeys` is the union of every branch’s live chunks). The graph and the vectors are not. The shared store (#3352) dedupes an identical commit across worktrees and clones (`commits/<commit>-<featureKey>/`). Two branches at different commits still materialize two full graphs and two full vector tables, even when the diff is a handful of files.

For a repo with N indexed branches this is about N times the embedder time, N times the float storage, and N times the vector-index memory, while well over 90% of the embedding text is shared. We index `main`, release branches, and feature branches of the same origins and pay that cost on every new branch.

### Proposed solution

Phase 1 — cross-branch embedding reuse (the part we need first):

- Keep one branch-scoped index per branch, so search on branch B cannot return symbols that exist only on branch A.
- Add a repo-scoped embedding cache keyed by embedding identity plus the existing content hash. Identity includes model, dimensions, and `EMBEDDING_TEXT_VERSION`. Node id is the wrong key: the same text can have different ids on different branches.
- When `analyze --embeddings` runs for branch B, copy vectors whose hash is already present on a sibling index (flat slot, `branches/*`, or another commit graph of the same repo in the shared store) into B’s `CodeEmbedding` table and skip the model for those nodes. Changed and new texts still go through the embedder. Removed nodes are simply absent from B.
- Report reused vs newly embedded counts in the analyze log.

Phase 2 — incremental graph from a sibling branch:

- Pick a base index that is already built (primary branch, or the indexed commit closest to the merge-base). Copy that graph, then run the existing incremental writeback for the git diff between the base and the target branch.
- If the current escalation gate (`shouldEscalateIncrementalWrite`) says the delta is not a safe incremental, fall back to a full pipeline. Import and resolution changes can invalidate edges in files whose bytes did not change.
- The parse cache can stay as it is; this phase is about not re-resolving and not rewriting the whole graph for unchanged files.

### Alternatives considered

- One index per repository, with branch as a node property. Search would mix branches, which #2106 was opened to avoid.
- Rely on the shared store alone. It already dedupes identical commits. It does not help long-lived branches that have diverged.
- Content-address the vectors outside GitNexus. Every consumer would reimplement the hash identity, and the branch database would still need a copy of the rows for its own vector index.

### Acceptance criteria

- After branch A is indexed with embeddings, indexing branch B (same repo, small diff, same model and `EMBEDDING_TEXT_VERSION`) reuses vectors for unchanged embedding text. New embedder work and new vector rows scale with the diff.
- A changed file on B is re-embedded; a file deleted on B does not appear in B’s semantic search.
- A different model, dimension, or `EMBEDDING_TEXT_VERSION` does not reuse old vectors.
- Semantic search on B returns only B’s graph. Deleting B’s index leaves A’s embeddings intact.
- A single-branch repo keeps today’s flat `.gitnexus/` layout.
- Phase 2: B’s graph is produced from A’s graph plus the diff, unless the escalation gate forces a full rebuild.

### Constraints

- Branch-scoped query results stay branch-scoped.
- Copying rows into the target database is enough for phase 1. A shared vector table across databases is a larger schema change and not required for the first cut.
- This is separate from #3474. That bug is a duplicate-primary-key abort when copy-on-write re-embeds rows that are already in the cloned graph. The reuse path has to insert a copied row once into an index that does not already contain it, and skip both the embedder and the insert when the target row is already current.

### Contribution

- [ ] I am willing to open a PR for this (may need design discussion first).

title: fix(scope): preserve lexical bindings in HTTP wrapper detection
body:
## Summary

Fix lexical binding ownership and scope-aware fetch-wrapper detection for TS/JS/Vue.

Fixes #3630. Related predecessor work: #3628, #3629.

## Motivation and context

Inferred assignments could claim an enclosing binding, while HTTP wrapper detection could confuse unrelated functions with the same name or count unreachable nested fetch calls. That produced incorrect receiver targets and false HTTP edges.

## Areas changed

- Preserve lexical declaration ownership and explicit type annotations; keep rename lookup anchored to the original reference position.
- Share lexical binding identity between framework routes and fetch-wrapper analysis, including parameter/body scope and mutation handling.
- Classify wrappers through resolved binding/import targets with a reverse work queue and conservative unresolved-name fallback. Wrapper identity survives HOCs, CommonJS exports, object keys, overloads, declarator lists and barrel re-exports, including star exports that reach one declaration under two export names.
- Keep cached extraction facts independent of import configuration; resolve copied targets during aggregation and fail closed when scope extraction fails or an HTTP hook throws. A file without facts still records its function names, so name-only fallback elsewhere declines.
- Name-only fallback considers only definitions that can be the target: module-level exports for an unresolvable import, top-level functions for an undeclared global. Only possible wrappers and module-level functions are emitted.
- A rebound binding proves no wrapper across files; `(<T>x) = …` is a write; calls inside recovered syntax and instance-field initializers resolve; a local export makes a star-export conflict visible; an undeclared constructor write keeps its type for reads in the writing scope.
- Add regression tests, integration fixtures, semantic graph comparison, and a reproducible scaling benchmark.

## Scope and implementation notes

Existing configured wrappers, member-call behavior, and module-stem export behavior are preserved. This is potential-execution analysis, not a full JavaScript runtime or flow-sensitive analysis.

The position index avoids scanning completed sibling scopes. Wrapper evidence is collected in one tree-cursor walk that reads node types, fields and offsets from the cursor and only materializes the nodes its handlers inspect; it never asks the native layer for a parent. Lexical bindings only walk the formals and bodies of functions whose parameters contain an expression. Propagation uses an O(V + E) reverse work queue. None of the new traversals recurse.

No dependency or release changes. The cross-platform worker test list gains `fetch-wrapper-persistence.test.ts`.

## Testing completed

- Production build and test type checking pass. Lint reports no errors and no new warnings; formatting is clean.
- Focused ownership, route and wrapper suites: 235 files, 5019 tests pass, at `528ea1478` and again after the behavior-preserving simplification `3db8657ba`. HTTP integration: 4 files, 56 tests pass (at `528ea1478`).
- Review findings each have a regression: the export-alias diamond (unit and real-parser fixture pair), CommonJS assignment-captured wrappers (unit and fixture), name-only fallback twins, rebound exports, angle-bracket writes, recovered syntax, field initializers and non-callable star exports. Against the previous source, 33 of the new assertions fail. The head-against-main probes from review now match main or improve on it; the one intended loss is a helper that conditionally rebinds its parameter with `var`, which is documented.
- Full suite in CI at `61de364ff`, and all 73 checks again at `5c179994c`: 1269 files passed and 12 skipped; 27194 tests passed, 83 skipped, none failed. A local full run on a network-mounted checkout was stopped after four hours in the serial database lane, where its real-analysis tests hit their 60–180 s timeouts; the same files pass in CI in 16–490 s. It is not counted as a pass.
- CI at `c263c4f72`: 73 successful checks, three skips, one neutral result, and no failures.
- Receiver accuracy matches the pinned baseline; the new CommonJS fixture adds one dropped `module.exports` member write, recorded in `bench/receiver-resolution/BASELINE.md`. Tool accuracy matches it too: 29/32 answers, the same three known gaps, regression gate passes.
- Frozen 432-file corpus (`88be1faf…`) analyzed at `c263c4f72`: exactly one expected CALLS target change (the explicit `Base` annotation wins over the inferred `Foo`); the other 431 CALLS and all 11 METHOD_OVERRIDES edges are unchanged. The diff and both export fingerprints are committed under the benchmark results.

## Benchmark results

Baseline `565e50276` and candidate `c263c4f72` ran back to back on one pinned CPU. The protocol is duration-calibrated: a 500 ms iteration target, pilot confirmation, 5 warmups, 15 measured iterations, fresh inputs and recorded raw timings. It is a Node benchmark that borrows BenchmarkDotNet's measurement discipline, not BenchmarkDotNet itself. Normalized growth (the time ratio divided by the size ratio) must stay under 1.8 for both the minimum and the median at 2x and 4x input.

| Arm | Baseline 4x growth (min / median) | Candidate 4x growth (min / median) | Candidate time vs baseline, largest input |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `position-index` | 4.68 / 4.74 | 1.20 / 1.17 | 0.06x |
| `position-deep-completed` | 4.47 / 4.48 | 1.23 / 1.24 | 0.05x |
| `nested-helpers` | 3.69 / 4.64 | 1.20 / 1.16 | 0.03x |
| `nested-helper-chain` | 11.37 / 14.16 | 1.15 / 1.17 | <0.01x |
| `reverse-chain` | 4.30 / 4.31 | 1.21 / 1.22 | <0.01x |
| `name-collisions` | 2.94 / 3.07 | 1.08 / 1.08 | 0.16x |
| `spread-aliases` | 1.02 / 1.02 | 1.09 / 1.09 | 1.07x |
| `completed-scopes` | 1.05 / 1.04 | 1.13 / 1.12 | 1.00x |
| `wrapper-aliases` | 1.08 / 1.09 | 1.11 / 1.13 | 0.99x |

Every candidate check, at 2x and 4x, is below 1.25; the largest measured factor is 1.245 (rounded). The baseline fails six of nine arms. Workload fingerprints match except `name-collisions`, where the baseline's false positive is recorded as `known-baseline-failure` by design.

The last three arms already scaled linearly on main. On those the candidate median time at the largest input is 0.99–1.07x baseline in this run; earlier pairs measured between 1.01x and 1.24x. Run-to-run noise on this shared host is about 0.1x.

The runs shared the host with other work; the reports' environment note says so. The 1-minute load average, sampled every 30 s in a log that is not committed, had a median of 1.50 and peaked at 4.53 during the run.

See `gitnexus/bench/lexical-binding-provenance/README.md` for commands and `docs/plans/2026-10-18-2259-fix-lexical-binding-provenance-plan.md` for the implementation contract.

## Checklist

- [x] Finish calibrated candidate scaling run, inspect every arm, and commit comparable baseline/candidate reports.
- [x] Complete the full test suite; interrupted broad runs are not recorded as passes.
- [x] Complete final simplification and independent code review; resolve actionable findings.
- [x] Refresh semantic-result metadata and the plan checkpoint for the published revision.
- [x] Resolve CI findings and confirm the branch against current main.

## Risk

Shared scope lookup and native worker/cache integration have broad callers. Repository impact and detect-changes checks could not provide evidence because no usable repository index was available, so that result is unknown rather than clean; source caller tracing and the regression suites cover the gap. The public API of the changed modules is unchanged.

title: fix(mcp): report cross-function explain lines 1-based
body:
## What

`explain` now reports cross-function (`interprocedural: true`) findings with 1-based line numbers, like every other line in the response.

`source.line`, `sink.line` and each `hops[].line` were the endpoints' and hops' raw graph `startLine` (0-based, tree-sitter `startPosition.row`): one line above the function's declaration in an editor, and one line off from the intra-procedural findings of the same response, whose PDG statement lines are already 1-based. The three values now go through `toDisplayLine`, the response-boundary converter `context`, `query` and `impact` adopted in #2377 / #2380.

The response `note` also says what these lines are: for cross-function findings they are the declaration lines of the functions, not statement lines.

## Why

Fixes #3491. With a `--pdg` index of this repository, `explain` showed `callTool` at 2719 where it is declared on 2720, `query` at 2914 for 2915, and so on for every cross-function hop, while the intra-procedural finding in the same response matched the file exactly.

## How to verify

```bash
cd gitnexus && npm run build && npx vitest run test/integration/taint-explain.test.ts
```

The `taint-explain-interproc` block now asserts the exact lines against the fixture: `handle` is declared on line 7 of `source.ts` and `runIt` on line 6 of `sink.ts`; `source`, `sink` and the first and last hop report 7 and 6. Before the fix they read 6 and 5.

Also run: `npx tsc --noEmit`, `npm run typecheck:tests`.

## Risk / rollback

Output-only change on one branch of `explain`; storage, the path codec and `interproc-emit` are untouched. Consumers that compensated for the off-by-one on cross-function lines (none in this repository) would now read one line too far. Revert the single commit to go back.

Not in this PR: a cross-function finding has one `file` (the source function's), so a sink or hop in another file still comes without its file. That is the second point of #3491 and would need the path codec to carry a file per hop; happy to open it separately.

title: feat(web): resolve a root-relative GITNEXUS_BACKEND_URL against the page origin
body:
## Summary

`GITNEXUS_BACKEND_URL` accepts a root-relative path. With `/` (or `/prefix`), the web client calls the API on the origin that served the page, so one `gitnexus-web` deployment answers on every hostname a reverse proxy gives it. Absolute URLs keep working unchanged.

## Motivation / context

Closes #3593. The injected `backendUrl` is an absolute URL, so a UI exposed on two hostnames (an internal `*.localhost` name and a public one) can be same-origin for at most one of them; `.localhost` resolves to the user's own machine and a Compose service name is not reachable from the browser. A value that names no host avoids the problem: the browser fills in the hostname it used.

## Areas touched

- [ ] `gitnexus/` (CLI / core / MCP server)
- [x] `gitnexus-web/` (Vite / React UI) — `config/ui-constants.ts`, `vite-env.d.ts`
- [ ] `.github/` (workflows, actions)
- [x] `eval/` or other tooling — `docker-server.mjs` (the web container's server)
- [x] Docs / agent config only — README Docker section, `docker-compose.yaml` comment, `.env.example`

## Scope & constraints

**In scope**

- `docker-server.mjs`: a `GITNEXUS_BACKEND_URL` starting with `/` is injected as given, minus a trailing slash (`/gitnexus/` → `/gitnexus`). It is read before the URL validation, so no warning is logged. `//host` is protocol-relative, an origin change, and still goes through the URL check, which rejects it. Values with a query, fragment, whitespace or control characters are rejected too, since the value is a base for `${base}/api/...`.
- `ui-constants.ts`: `DEFAULT_BACKEND_URL` resolves a root-relative injected value with `new URL(value, window.location.origin)`, without its trailing slash. Everything downstream (`validateBackendUrl`, the circuit-breaker key, the settings panel) keeps seeing an absolute http(s) URL.
- README: a "Same-origin API behind a reverse proxy" section with the two ways to route `/api/*`: through the web container's own proxy (`GITNEXUS_UPSTREAM_URL` + token, which ends the browser origin so the server's CORS allowlist never sees the public hostnames — the right fit for several hostnames), or straight to `gitnexus serve`, which admits one public origin via `GITNEXUS_PUBLIC_ORIGIN`. A Traefik example for the first.

**Explicitly out of scope / not done here**

- Several public origins on `gitnexus serve` itself (`GITNEXUS_PUBLIC_ORIGIN` stays a single origin). Routing through the web proxy covers the multi-hostname case without it.
- No change to `RENDER_EXTERNAL_URL` handling or to the proxy.
- A user-saved server URL in `localStorage` still takes precedence over the injected default, as before.

## Implementation notes

The server could have resolved `/` itself, but it does not know which hostname the browser used; only the page does. So the server passes the path through and the client resolves it, which also keeps the config script free of any hostname.

## Testing & verification

- [x] `node --test docker-server.test.mjs` — 62 pass (3 new: `/` injected, `/gitnexus/` injected as `/gitnexus`, `//evil.example` not injected)
- [x] `cd gitnexus-web && npx vitest run test/unit/server-connection.test.ts` — 44 pass (4 new on `DEFAULT_BACKEND_URL`: `/` → page origin, `/gitnexus` → origin + prefix, `//evil.example` passed through, existing absolute and empty cases unchanged). The two resolution tests fail with the client resolution removed.
- [x] `cd gitnexus-web && npx tsc -b --noEmit`
- [x] Prettier and ESLint on the changed files
- [ ] Manual / Playwright E2E — not run; the change is in the injected default's resolution, covered by the unit tests above

## Risk & rollout

Opt-in: nothing changes unless `GITNEXUS_BACKEND_URL` starts with `/`. No index refresh, no migration. Release note: "`GITNEXUS_BACKEND_URL=/` makes the web UI call the API on its own origin."

## Checklist

- [x] PR body meets repo minimum length
- [x] No `AGENTS.md` / overlay changes
- [x] No secrets, tokens, or machine-specific paths committed

title: fix(routes): scope inline Express handlers and report api_impact lower bound
body:
Closes #3488. Covers what was left after #3632.

The consumer-matching part of #3488 is already on main: `backend-client.ts` is now listed as a consumer of `/api/repos`, `/api/file` and `/api/query`. This PR handles the other three items in the issue.

## Per-route response shapes and flows

An inline Express handler (`app.get('/x', (req, res) => …)`) never got a `handlerSymbolId`. It is a real Function node in the graph, named by position (`fn_<row>_<col>`), but the route facts only recorded a handler name for bare identifiers. That had two effects:

- response keys came from a scan of the whole file, so every route in the file got every handler's keys;
- `processes.ts` fell back to its per-file bucket, so every route got every flow that starts in the file.

The route facts now record that positional name for an inline handler, and the resolver accepts it the same way it accepts a lexical binding. When a file registers more than one route, response keys are read from the resolved handler's lines. Middleware detection still reads the whole file, and single-route files are unchanged.

Flows need no change. `processes.ts` already links exactly by `handlerSymbolId` once one is present.

Group HTTP contracts read the same route facts. They ignore the positional name, so an inline handler is still attributed to its enclosing registrar there, as before.

## Lower bound in `api_impact`

The routes phase already sees every call whose first argument is a `/…` URL, and keeps only those whose callee is a proven fetch wrapper. It now also counts, for each route, the files that pass that route's URL to a callee that is **not** proven. Two kinds of file are left out:

- files that are already proven consumers;
- the route's own handler file, so that `app.get('/x')` doesn't count itself.

The count is stored on the Route node as `unverifiedConsumers`. When it is non-zero, `api_impact` adds three fields to `impactSummary`: `epistemic: 'lower-bound'`, `unverifiedConsumers`, and a `boundaries` note. The field names follow `impact`'s #1858 convention. `riskLevel` still counts proven consumers only.

`api_impact` doesn't emit `epistemic: 'exact'`. A URL the analyzer couldn't resolve at all is invisible to it, so it can't claim the count is exact.

## Left for a follow-up

The issue also asks for files that call the request functions (for example, `App.tsx` calling `fetchRepos`). They never mention the URL, so this PR's count does not cover them. That is filed as #3644.

## Schema

The new Route column is `unverifiedConsumers INT64`, added to `schema.ts`, the CSV header and row, and the COPY column list. `fetchRoutesWithConsumers` retries without the column on an older index, and drops the runtime-evidence columns on a step further back. Previously there was only the runtime-evidence fallback.

## Tests

- `express-routes.test.ts`: a new fixture with two inline handlers and two consumer files.
  - Checks per-route keys, the exact `ENTRY_POINT_OF` set, and `unverifiedConsumers`.
  - The handler-file and proven-consumer exclusions are both pinned.
  - Written first; it failed on main with the unioned keys and the cross-linked flows.
- `api-impact-e2e.test.ts`: lower-bound fields present and absent.
- `route-runtime-evidence-roundtrip.test.ts`: the column survives CSV → COPY → query.
- `calltool-dispatch.test.ts`: both legacy-schema fallback steps.

Also ran the route, fetch-wrapper, group, shape-check and api-impact unit and integration suites locally, plus `tsc`.

## Bench baselines

- `emit-persistence`: `route.csv` gets the new header field. The synthetic graph has no Route rows, and stripping `,unverifiedConsumers` restores the prior fingerprint exactly. The note is in `baselines.json`.
- `receiver-resolution`: the new fixture reads `req.query.path` on an untyped inline-handler parameter, which adds one `receiver-unresolved` read (191 → 192). The note is in `BASELINE.md`.

title: api_impact: list callers of the function that sends the request (one level)
body:
Follow-up from #3488.

`api_impact` now lists the file that sends the request. For GitNexus's own web UI that is `gitnexus-web/src/services/backend-client.ts` for `/api/repos`, `/api/file` and `/api/query`. The files that call the request functions in that file are still missing. Examples are `fetchRepos` from `App.tsx`, `DropZone.tsx` and `Header.tsx`, and `readFile` from `CodeReferencesPanel.tsx` and `useAppState.tsx`. In the #3488 ground truth these are 6 of the 9 consumer files.

A `FETCHES` edge goes from the requesting file to the Route. Nothing follows the `CALLS` edges into the function that holds the request, so `directConsumers` and `riskLevel` count only the one requesting file.

Possible direction: start from the symbol that contains the fetch site, take its callers one level up, and report them as `indirectConsumers`, separate from `directConsumers`. At minimum they could be counted. The FETCHES edge is file-level today, so this first needs the enclosing symbol. The fetch-site capture from #2897 / #2899 may already have it.

#3643 adds `impactSummary.epistemic: 'lower-bound'` for files that pass the URL to an unproven function. These callers are a different gap: they never mention the URL, so that count does not include them.

title: fix: reduce MCP token overhead and correct cost comparisons
body:
## Summary

Reduce MCP response overhead without removing evidence, and make the default cost benchmark compare GitNexus with an agent that has no GitNexus access. A local six-response corpus uses 33.9–34.5% fewer tokens with compact JSON; total session cost and solve rate still need paired model runs.

## Motivation / context

The oracle and task-provenance fixes landed in #3503 and #3611. This completes the remaining benchmark-default and historical-claim corrections: `baseline` already has MCP, so it cannot measure GitNexus versus no GitNexus.

Fixes #3492.

## Areas touched

- [x] `gitnexus/` (CLI / core / MCP server)
- [ ] `gitnexus-web/` (Vite / React UI)
- [ ] `.github/` (workflows, actions)
- [x] `eval/` or other tooling
- [ ] Docs / agent config only (`AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `.cursor/`, `llms.txt`, etc.)

## Scope & constraints

**In scope**

- Preserve every decoded result value, source string, diagnostic, and next-step hint while removing JSON formatting whitespace.
- Make three repetitions and all four comparison arms the benchmark defaults; retain explicit one-run smoke checks.
- Provide a reproducible local measurement and qualify the historical unnamed-model, n=1 cost claims.

**Explicitly out of scope / not done here**

- Paid model runs, universal savings claims, and release-evaluation evidence. The authorized measurement budget was $0.

## Implementation notes

The measurement sends fixed synthetic payloads through the actual MCP server and SDK, checks decoded equality and unchanged hints, and counts tokens with pinned `tiktoken 0.12.0` encodings. Source and corpus hashes accompany the per-case results in `gitnexus/bench/mcp-serialization/results.json`.

| Complete response corpus | Before | After | Reduction |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| `o200k_base` tokens | 5,945 | 3,928 | 33.9% |
| `cl100k_base` tokens | 5,859 | 3,838 | 34.5% |
| UTF-8 bytes | 20,229 | 14,218 | 29.7% |

All six payloads round-trip exactly. Plain-text responses are unchanged. These results measure one input-cost component; they do not prove lower bills or better task accuracy.

## Testing & verification

- [x] [CI run 39424425128](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/actions/runs/39424425128) passed on `c226d6e7f93238f10aee5d2a8be7d89bd7bd4931`: 29,040 tests across Ubuntu, Windows, and macOS; coverage, evaluation, lint, and typecheck jobs passed.
- [x] 202 focused MCP tests passed: server serialization, output budgets, response filtering, HTTP transport, read-only mode, and repository policy.

title: fix(scope): follow namespace factory return types across languages and record untyped drops
body:
Fixes #3498. Covers what was left after #3595.

#3595 handled the conditional-expression and `or None` assignments. This PR covers the other two parts of the issue: factories called through a module object, and reporting the calls the analyzer cannot type.

## Factories through a module object

`import mod as rp; x = rp.make(); x.m()` lost the receiver type even when `make` is declared `-> C`. `x` was bound to the raw name `rp.make`, and nothing followed a dotted name to a function's return type.

- **Binding form** (`x = rp.make()`, `x = mod.make()`): the post-finalize chain follow in `imported-return-types.ts` now resolves `ns.f` when `ns` is a namespace import and the target module records a return annotation for `f`. That is the same fact `propagateImportedReturnTypes` already mirrors for `from mod import make`.
- **Inline form** (`rp.make().m()`): the compound receiver resolver read `ns.f()` only as a construction. It now tries `f`'s return annotation first and falls back to the construction.
- **Dart** (`import 'mod.dart' as rp; final x = rp.make()`): local call inference only accepted a bare callee, and the type normalizer stripped library prefixes. A local initialized by exactly `prefix.member(...)` (or `await prefix.member(...)`) now binds the dotted callee and keeps its prefix. Annotated `prefix.Type` spellings are unchanged.
- **Zig** gets the inline form from the shared change. The bound form (`const x = rp.make()`) keeps main's binding: the importing file can't tell a namespace module from a file-struct, and guessing from the filename's case lost edges on lowercase file-structs.

The lookup only answers when it can prove the fact, and fails closed otherwise:

- The return binding must be anchored on a module-level `Function` with that name. TS and Dart hoist method return annotations to the module under the method's name, and Go binds receiver methods at package scope, so a name-only read could pick `WidgetFactory.create(): Widget` for `m.create()`.
- The namespace must bind the module it targets. `import pkg.sub` binds `pkg` but targets `pkg/sub.py`, so it doesn't count.
- A dotted return (`-> models.Order`) is not followed further. The next step would read `models` in the caller's namespace map, not the producer's.
- The namespace-name set is built from the finalized import edges, never by walking `scopeTree.byId`, which throws after the out-of-core seal (`GITNEXUS_DISK_SCOPE_INDEX=1`).

Shadowing locals and class members (`rp.C()`) are left to the existing paths. On the full `lang-resolution` corpus, this branch emits exactly the same `CALLS`/`ACCESSES` edges as `origin/main` outside the new fixtures.

## Calls the analyzer cannot type

`impact` reported `epistemic: "exact"` for these sites, because the drop was never recorded. Two cases are now recorded as `receiver-unresolved`:

- **Untyped namespace call:** a plain receiver bound to a namespace function with no usable return type (`x = rp.untyped(); x.m()`). Each fail-closed case above lands here too. Plain `x = untyped()` was already recorded on main.
- **Shared start position:** sites are keyed by `file:line:col`, and an outer call starts where its inner receiver does. In `rp.untyped().m()` or `s.repo.Delete(id)`, a resolved inner site used to hide the outer site's drop. A site's identity is now `receiver.member`, so only a duplicate capture of the same site (or a call's own callee read) hides one, and `rp.untyped().untyped()` records its outer drop.

## Measurements

- **Receiver-resolution baseline:** call drops 128 → 153, reads 44 → 48. `BASELINE.md` lists every site. Each newly visible drop was checked against the corpus graph, and none has a `CALLS` edge to that member from its enclosing function. Ten shape-arm cells move from `INVISIBLE-GAP` to `VISIBLE-GAP` because of the same shared-position fix.
- **Tool-accuracy gate:** `python.factory-qualified` now passes, and its known-gap allowance is removed.
- **Timing:** a whole-repo A/B shows no slowdown (main 189.4 s / 161.4 s, this branch 183.0 s / 152.7 s). Two whole-repo runs give identical edges and drops.
- **Disk mode:** inline-only partitions (Python `rp.make().m()`, Go `pkg.New().Do()`, TS) analyze cleanly under `GITNEXUS_DISK_SCOPE_INDEX=1` and give the same edges as an in-memory run.

## Tests

- **Fixtures with data-driven blocks:**
  - `python-module-factory-return`: binding, module and inline forms resolve; the shadowed alias and untyped factories don't, and the drop list is pinned.
  - `dart-prefixed-factory-return`: same forms. An awaited `Future<C>` factory is pinned as a drop: no Dart path unwraps an awaited Future yet, named imports included.
  - `zig-namespace-factory-return`: the inline form resolves, the bound form is pinned at no edge, and file-struct controls resolve, including a genuinely lowercase file-struct (`config.zig`).
- **Temp-repo regression rows**, one per fail-closed case:
  - TypeScript: hoisted method, bound and inline.
  - Go: package method sharing a function's name.
  - Python: `import pkg.b` with same-named root and leaf factories, and a Django-style `-> models.Order`.
- **Unit:** data-driven cases for `recordSiteMember`.
- **Goldens:** the Python capture golden and the Dart scope-capture fingerprint move for the new fixtures only.

On main, the module-qualified cases had no edge, and neither untyped namespace case was recorded.

TypeScript and JavaScript (with JSDoc `@returns`) get the same result from the shared change alone. Go and Ruby already resolved the bound forms on main. Rust, PHP, Kotlin and C++ need their own provider work for qualified callees, which comes in separate PRs.

title: fix(ci): avoid RC tag collisions during npm processing
body:
## Summary

Keep RC publishing moving when npm accepts a package but has not yet exposed it in registry metadata. The next RC now advances past versions already reserved by Git tags as well as those visible in npm.

## Motivation / context

[Publish run 39472555350](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/actions/runs/39472555350) passed CI, then failed with `fatal: tag 'v1.6.13-rc.136' already exists`.

The preceding successful release had submitted `rc.136`; npm reported that the package was still being processed. Registry queries continued to return `rc.135`, so subsequent runs repeatedly chose the occupied version.

## Areas touched

- [x] `gitnexus/` (release workflow tests)
- [ ] `gitnexus-web/` (Vite / React UI)
- [x] `.github/` (workflows, actions)
- [ ] `eval/` or other tooling
- [x] Docs / agent config (`CONTRIBUTING.md` release policy)

## Scope & constraints

**In scope**

- Allocate the RC counter above both npm versions and Git release tags for the selected base.
- Exercise the actual workflow resolver with real local Git tags and controlled registry responses.

**Explicitly out of scope / not done here**

- npm's processing delay, credential changes, and manual release publication.

## Implementation notes

Checkout already fetches all tags, including tags on detached release commits. The resolver uses these as reservations. The existing npm existence check and atomic tag push continue to reject races. Tag suffixes must be numeric before contributing to the counter.

## Testing & verification

- [x] 27 release tests passed: `cd gitnexus && npm test -- --maxWorkers=2 test/unit/publish-rc-version.test.ts test/unit/publish-release-evidence.test.ts test/unit/release-docker-gate.test.ts`.

- [ ] Full `npm test`: attempted locally; worker-startup failures prevented a clean result. Full CI remains required.
