title: fix(go): type receivers through package-qualified declared types
body:
Go receivers lose their member calls whenever two packages declare a type with the same name. This came out of a triage of the receiver-resolution baseline (follow-up to #3498).

## Cause

`normalizeGoTypeName` cuts the package qualifier from every Go type binding except return types. So a field, parameter or local written `*models.User` is stored as plain `User`, and receiver typing looks up that bare name. Go namespace imports bind no member names, so the lookup falls through to the workspace-wide unique-name fallback, which only answers while the name is unique.

- **Missing edges:** with `models.User` and `api.User` in the same repo, every receiver typed through a cross-package field, parameter or local of that name loses its member calls.
- **Wrong edges:** a package that declares its own `User` is worse off. The scope chain binds `models.User` to the local type and emits an edge to the wrong method.

`TypeRef.declaredSpelling` still carries the qualifier.

## Fix

- A new optional `ScopeResolver.qualifiedTypeLookupSpelling(typeRef)` hook.
  - Go implements it by reducing `declaredSpelling` with `normalizeGoReturnType`, the same reduction return types already get, and returns `pkg.Type`.
- Receiver typing tries that spelling first, in both `classOfDeclaredType` (compound receivers) and the simple-binding case in `receiver-bound-calls`. Both go through one helper, `classOfQualifiedTypeSpelling`.
  - It resolves only through the qualifier's import targets, with the unique-name fallback switched off. So a hit always comes from the import, never from a guessed name.
  - Any miss falls back to today's bare lookup unchanged. That keeps a workspace-unique type reachable behind an import the resolver can't follow.
- The binding itself is not rewritten, because a dotted `rawName` reads as a member-alias path elsewhere.
- The qualifier is read from the file's imports, starting at the module scope, never from the binding's own scope. A field, parameter or local named after its package (`vault *vault.Vault`, a very common Go pattern) would otherwise find itself instead of the import. In Go, struct fields are never in lexical scope, a parameter's or local's type is resolved before its name enters scope, and there are no block-scoped imports.
- A chain step keeps the binding's own written spelling. `member models.User` is stored as `User`, and the extractor's chain-follow can land on another binding named `User` (a sibling field, a parameter, a package-level field in another file); the binding now keeps `models.User` rather than copying that binding's spelling. Go's hook also returns a spelling only when its last segment equals `rawName`, so a binding whose type a chain step replaced falls back to the bare lookup instead of borrowing a package.
- callable-value-flow types a method value's receiver (`f := p.Save`, `run(p.Save)`) through the same helper, so its CALLS edges agree with the ACCESSES edge.
- Shared code names no language. The hook is listed in the ARCHITECTURE.md hook table.

## Tests

`go-qualified-declared-types`: one `go.mod`, with `models.User` and `api.User` sharing method names. Its data-driven blocks in `go.test.ts` have 18 rows.

- **Positive rows (10):** value, pointer and aliased parameters, a declared local, a `&T{}` literal, value and pointer fields, a field chain, and a qualifier that names a different package from its namesake (`Forward`). All 10 failed before the fix. Three more rows cover the `vault *vault.Vault` shape (field, parameter and local, with a colliding `api.Vault` declaring the same method); they failed before the second commit.
- **Controls (5):** a bare same-package type, plus four cases behind an unresolved import. Two must still refuse an ambiguous bare name, and two must keep the unique-name fallback.

A temp-repo block covers the review shapes: a sibling field and a parameter named `User` beside `member models.User` (both resolve to `models.User`), a package-level `User *auth.Principal` in another file (fails closed instead of binding `auth.Principal`), and method values (`f := p.Save`, `run(p.Save)`). A unit table covers the Go hook, including `func() *models.User`, generics, arrays and a spelling that does not qualify `rawName`. The Go capture golden gains the fixture's entries; the change is additive only.

## Measurements

Full `lang-resolution` corpus A/B against main (`278863068`, after #3648 merged):

- **Edges:** none removed or retargeted outside the new fixture (re-checked after the second commit). Inside it, only `Forward` moves, from the wrong `api.User.Archive` to `models.User.Archive`. 19 previously missing edges appear:
  - the chains in `go-deep-field-chain`, `go-field-types` and `go-mixed-chain`;
  - `models.User` receivers in three other fixtures;
  - `PickService.StartSession → CartRepo.Get`.
- **Drops:** all 13 Go `receiver-unresolved` drops clear.
- **Receiver bench:** re-measured on top of #3648: call drops 153 → 148, reads 48 → 40, all kinds 221 → 208. The shape arm is unchanged.

## Verify

```bash
cd gitnexus && npm run build
npx vitest run test/integration/resolvers/go.test.ts test/unit/scope-resolution/go
npx tsx bench/receiver-resolution/measure.mjs --check
npx tsx bench/scope-capture/measure.mjs --check
```

## Rollback

Reverting the PR is self-contained: the hook is optional and only Go implements it, and the baselines and golden revert with it. #3654 is stacked on this branch and would need a rebase.

## Not in this PR

- Nested `go.mod` handling: the resolver reads only the root `go.mod` and suffix-matches imports across module boundaries. Separate PR.
- Bindings Go capture synthesizes without a written spelling: `new(models.User)`, `var w = &models.User{}`, multi-assign, an index into `[]*models.User` and `range` over it. Same root cause; follow-up.

title: fix(go): resolve imports within selected modules
body:
Go imports now resolve to exact package directories in the importer's own module or a module selected by its nearest `go.work`. Independent sibling modules remain unresolved. Receiver typing also stops when a written package-qualified type cannot resolve through its import, preventing a same-named type elsewhere in the repository from creating a false call edge.

Follows #3651 and addresses the module-visibility review on this PR.

## Behavior

- Discover every `go.mod` and `go.work` from the scan's file list, without a second directory walk. Module paths match at `/` boundaries; nested modules own their subtrees.
- Select the importer's own module, or a unique provider selected by the nearest `go.work`. A workspace that excludes the importing module cannot supply its siblings. A known but unselected module never falls through to suffix matching.
- Require exactly one selected module to contain the imported package. A shorter module path may supply it when a longer one has no Go files; two providers are ambiguous and remain unresolved.
- Preserve GOPATH-style suffix matching only outside module mode.
- Treat a failed qualified receiver lookup as a refusal in direct calls, field chains, and method values. This deliberately changes #3651's bare-name fallback after an unresolved qualified import. Languages without the qualified-type hook retain their existing behavior.
- Keep nearest-module and workspace lookups lazy and memoized per directory.

Manifest reads use one bounded `O_NOFOLLOW` handle. Read failures and standalone scan failures propagate; symlinked, oversized, non-regular, or vanished manifests are skipped. Reads run in batches of 32.

Local `replace` directives and `vendor/` remain unmodelled.

## Validation

- 314 focused Go tests pass, including positive workspace selection and negative independent-sibling, excluded-importer, and nearest-workspace cases. Each scenario checks exact import edges and direct, field-chain, and method-value call targets.
- Regression proof: 12 new visibility assertions failed on `85329b4de`; the import gate alone still left three false calls, which the receiver fix removes.
- The broader resolver suite passed at `255cf2345`: 7,263 tests across 256 files (4 tests and 1 file skipped). The subsequent ambiguity fix passes all 314 focused Go tests; its new ambiguous-provider assertion failed before the fix.
- Both TypeScript configurations pass. Core source/test ESLint reported no errors at `255cf2345`, and the follow-up changed-file lint passes.

title: fix(docker): verify bundled FTS artifacts
body:
## Summary

Docker builds now verify the packaged FTS extension instead of downloading a mutable CDN artifact. This restores ARM64 builds while keeping a mandatory native load check against the binary used by the runtime.

## Motivation / context

The ARM64 build failed with `undefined symbol: _ZN4lbug6common11ValueVector10setAllNullEv`. A fresh response from the versioned `v0.21.0/linux_arm64/fts` URL serves an October 20 rebuild that requires this symbol; the pinned core 0.21.1 does not export it. Cached responses still serve the older compatible binary, making identical builds depend on the CDN cache.

Related: #3654

## Areas touched

- [x] `gitnexus/` (extension verification script and tests)
- [x] Other tooling (`Dockerfile.cli`)

## Scope & constraints

**In scope**

- Load the packaged FTS artifact by the same path resolver used by `ExtensionManager`.
- Fail the build if that artifact is missing or cannot load; no network fallback.

**Explicitly out of scope / not done here**

- Changing the LadybugDB core pin or vendored binaries.

## Implementation notes

`--verify-bundled` is an explicit installer mode. Ordinary `INSTALL`, corruption-triggered `FORCE INSTALL`, and named `--verify-only` retain their behavior. The path resolver is reused without modification.

- ARM64 Node 22.23.3 under QEMU: reproduced the exact undefined-symbol error with the fresh CDN binary; the packaged binary passed `LOAD EXTENSION`, `CREATE_FTS_INDEX`, and a search returning the expected row.

title: chore(deps)(deps): bump i18next from 26.4.3 to 26.4.7 in /gitnexus-web
body:
Bumps [i18next](https://github.com/i18next/i18next) from 26.4.3 to 26.4.7.
Release notes

Sourced from i18next's releases.

v26.4.7

  • perf: cloneInstance() no longer inherits preload. loadResources() adds every preload language to each load, and clones copied preload from the parent, so a clone's init() and every changeLanguage() walked all preloaded languages × all namespaces through queueLoad() / hasResourceBundle(), although the parent had already loaded them into the shared store. With i18next-http-middleware (one clone + changeLanguage() per request), 25 preloaded languages and 20 namespaces, that was most of the per-request CPU: the reproduction from the issue went from ~90 µs to ~10 µs per request, the same as with a single language. A clone now only loads what it uses itself: its changeLanguage() no longer waits for parent preload languages that are still loading (the parent's own init() still does), and clone.loadNamespaces() loads the new namespace for the clone's language and fallbacks instead of every preloaded language. clone.loadLanguages() works as before, the parent instance is unchanged, and passing preload to cloneInstance() keeps the old behavior. Thanks @​theMostCuriousHomunculus for the detailed report (#2451).

v26.4.6

  • fix: a fallback language whose formatted code is already in the hierarchy is no longer added a second time. toResolveHierarchy() checked the raw fallbackLng value against the list, but the list holds formatted codes, so any fallback written differently from its formatted form slipped through: lng: 'de-CH' with fallbackLng: 'de-ch' gave languages ['de-CH', 'de', 'de-CH'], and the same happened with fallbackLng: 'EN' + cleanCode, lowerCaseLng, and Intl aliases (iw-IL → he-IL). Missing keys were looked up in the same language twice. Only exact duplicates are removed; the order is unchanged. Thanks @​lprnmns (#2450).

v26.4.5

  • fix: hasLoadedNamespace(ns, { lng }) no longer stays false forever when the passed in lng is loaded under another code, or not at all. It checked the load state of the raw lng, but loadLanguages() stores a language under its resolved code (de-ch → de-CH, de-CH → de with load: 'languageOnly') and skips a lng outside supportedLngs entirely (only the fallback gets loaded), so that state never got set. react-i18next's useTranslation(ns, { lng }) then never became ready: with useSuspense it kept throwing an already resolved promise and React retried forever (100% CPU, SSR never finished), without it the load effect re-rendered in a loop. It now checks the code the language is actually loaded under, and for a lng outside supportedLngs only waits for the fallback, which is also what t() resolves to. Calls without lng and the precheck (react-i18next's bindI18n: 'languageChanging') are unchanged (react-i18next#1934).

v26.4.4

  • fix(security): the nesting regexp no longer backtracks exponentially (ReDoS) on an unclosed $t(. Its repeated group had overlapping alternatives ([^()"']+ inside (?:...)*?, and inside parentheses [^()] also matched quotes), so a string containing $t( without a closing ) made the engine try every way to split the text: about 2x the runtime per extra character, and a ~25 character value hung t() for minutes. With the default config this was reachable through any interpolated value (t('greet', { name: '$t(aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa' })): escaping does not touch $, t or (, and the skipOnVariables check runs the regexp on the interpolated result, so nest: false did not help either. Every alternative now starts with a different character (plain char, ", ' or (), so there is only one way to match and the cost is linear. Quoted strings and one level of parentheses in nesting options keep working (#2336). The only difference: a lone " or ' inside unquoted parentheses within $t(...) is no longer matched. Affects 25.3.3 to 26.4.3. Thanks to Anisetti Chaitanya Eshwar Prasad for the responsible disclosure.
  • fix(security): nest() now resolves $t(...) in a single pass and no longer nests text that came out of a resolved value. Every nested lookup reset the shared nesting regexp, so the loop started over from the beginning of the string after each match. That had two effects. First, a $t(...) inside a variable that the nested lookup deliberately kept literal (default skipOnVariables: true) was resolved anyway by the outer loop: with outer: 'A $t(inner) B' and inner: 'Hi {{name}}', t('outer', { name: '$t(secret)' }) rendered the secret translation. body:
Bumps [jsdom](https://github.com/jsdom/jsdom) from 30.1.1 to 30.1.3.
Release notes

Sourced from jsdom's releases.

v30.1.3

  • Improved performance of getComputedStyle() and computed CSS property reads, including with stylesheets containing attribute selectors. (@​scttcper, @​asamuzaK)
  • Fixed slowdowns when focusing elements and running interaction tests, which regressed in v30.1.2. (@​scttcper)
  • Fixed XMLHttpRequest reusing credentials supplied to xhr.open() after cross-origin redirects, including in response to authentication challenges from the destination.
  • Fixed XMLHttpRequest incorrectly sending and accepting cookies after cross-origin redirects back to the document's origin when xhr.withCredentials is false.
  • Fixed exceptions from malformed CSS math functions, such as calc(0px - @submenu_space), while parsing documents, stylesheets, and style declarations. (@​rnavarro)
  • Fixed getComputedStyle() ignoring style rules nested inside multiple @media rules.
  • Fixed CSS shorthands overwriting longhands with higher priority or specificity during style computation, including declarations containing CSS variables.
  • Fixed getComputedStyle() returning unresolved or inconsistent shorthand values, including for 'background', 'border', 'flex', 'font', 'margin', and 'padding', and incorrect shorthand defaults and inheritance.
  • Fixed computed background positions to resolve font-relative lengths using the final font size and handle multiple image layers correctly.
  • Fixed computed 'color' values depending on property read order, including unresolved color-mix() results, which regressed in v29.0.2.
  • Fixed currentcolor border colors incorrectly becoming transparent when 'color' uses light-dark() or relative color syntax.
  • Fixed CSS calculations that reduce to a percentage incorrectly producing pixel values, which regressed in v30.0.0.
  • Fixed numeric font weights in the 'font' shorthand incorrectly setting 'line-height'.
  • Fixed selector matching involving XML namespaces, and selectors such as [data-a|=""] failing to match empty values and values beginning with -. (@​asamuzaK)

v30.1.2

  • Updated URLs to support Unicode v18.0.0 in internationalized domain names.
  • Reduced package size and memory use for CSS property definitions. (@​scttcper)
  • Fixed severe slowdowns when building large DOM trees, including SVG charts with D3, which regressed in v30.1.0. (@​cmdcolin)
  • Fixed exponentially slow reads of empty inherited CSS custom properties in deeply nested documents, and custom properties incorrectly inheriting past an initial reset. (@​scttcper)
  • Fixed getComputedStyle() returning stale results after editing stylesheet declarations, selectors, or media queries, including in imported stylesheets.
  • Fixed selector matching and computed styles after changes to form control checkedness, indeterminacy, selection, values, and validity, including during form resets and canceled clicks.
  • Fixed computed styles for :focus, :focus-visible, :focus-within, and selectors containing them after focus changes, including inside focus and blur listeners. (@​asamuzaK)
  • Fixed element.focus() incorrectly focusing elements hidden by 'display', including through shadow hosts and slots, and elements excluded by shadow DOM slot assignment. (@​asamuzaK)
  • Fixed getComputedStyle() throwing for elements without inline-style support, including XML and MathML elements.
  • Fixed a memory leak where stylesheet parsing retained the last parsed stylesheet's window after window.close().
  • Fixed memory growth from long-lived MutationObserver instances retaining bookkeeping for garbage-collected nodes. (@​scttcper)
  • Fixed retained select.selectedOptions collections becoming stale after selection changes and form resets.
  • Fixed rejection of negative CSS sizing values, including for 'min-width', 'min-height', 'max-width', and 'max-height', which regressed in v30.1.0.
  • Fixed handling of deeply nested color-mix() expressions, including exceptions during color resolution. (@​asamuzaK)

title: chore(deps)(deps): bump react-i18next from 17.0.16 to 17.0.21 in /gitnexus-web
body:
Bumps [react-i18next](https://github.com/i18next/react-i18next) from 17.0.16 to 17.0.21.
Changelog

Sourced from react-i18next's changelog.

17.0.21

  • fix(IcuTrans): explicit values now win over interpolation.defaultVariables, as they do in t(). IcuTrans merged them the other way round, so <IcuTrans values={{ user: 'John Doe' }} /> rendered the configured default variable user instead of John Doe. Trans had the same inverted merge and is fixed too. Compatibility note: only names that are set both in values and in defaultVariables render differently.
  • feat: new entry point react-i18next/IcuTransWithoutContext (with types) for React Server Components. Importing IcuTransWithoutContext from react-i18next in a Server Component could fail the build with createContext is not a function, because the main entry creates the React context when it is loaded. Like react-i18next/TransWithoutContext, the new entry point does not.
  • fix(build): the ESM build's dist/es/package.json now declares "sideEffects": false, like the root package.json already did. Bundlers use the nearest package.json, so the ESM build counted as having side effects and unused exports were kept: an app that only uses Trans still bundled IcuTrans with its HTML entity decoder, useTranslation and use-sync-external-store. With esbuild, a Trans-only bundle (React and i18next external) goes from 20.9 KB to 11.6 KB minified, 8.3 KB to 5.0 KB gzipped.
  • docs: the icu.macro Babel macro is now marked as deprecated in favour of using IcuTrans directly. It fails on Babel 8 (t.jSXIdentifier is not a function), <Plural count={count}> renders the raw ICU message, and a React key on <Plural>/<Select> becomes an ICU case. It keeps working on Babel 7 and is not removed. The IcuTrans docs page has a corrected example and props table and covers Server Components.

17.0.20

  • fix: useTranslation no longer suspends when a missing namespace is loaded by a synchronous backend. With useSuspense (the default), a namespace that wasn't in the store yet always made the component throw the loading promise, even when the backend had already delivered the resources while that promise was being created. React then showed the Suspense fallback and rendered again right away, which appears as a fallback flash (a white flash in React Native) and costs performance. The hook now starts the load first, checks the store again and only suspends if the namespace is still missing. This helps every backend that calls back synchronously, for example i18next-resources-to-backend with a static resources object or a loader that returns the data directly. Async backends, and an instance that isn't initialized yet, still suspend as before. Thanks @​oblador (#1937).

17.0.19

  • fix: useTranslation with an inline selector keyPrefix (useTranslation('ns', { keyPrefix: ($) => $.role })) returned a new t on every render, so every effect, useCallback and useMemo depending on t ran again each time. The cached t was compared against the keyPrefix function itself, and an inline arrow is a new function on every render. It is now compared against the key the selector resolves to (with the same options and namespace list getFixedT resolves it with), so t keeps its identity as long as the resolved prefix does, just like a string keyPrefix. A selector that resolves to a different key still gets a new t, and i18next still resolves the selector on each t call as before. Fixes #1936.
  • fix: useTranslation kept returning the previous t when only the namespace (useTranslation('a') → useTranslation('b')) or only the i18n instance (another instance with the same language, via props or I18nextProvider) changed on a mounted component. That t kept resolving against the old namespace or instance until something else (the language, the ready state, a bound i18n event) produced a new one. Both are now part of the check that decides whether the cached t can be reused.

17.0.18

  • fix(Trans): with shouldUnescape, the default unescape now turns   and &[#160](https://github.com/i18next/react-i18next/issues/160); into a no-break space (U+00A0) instead of a regular space (U+0020). The regular space dropped what the entity is for: u nás or 10 km could wrap across lines, and consecutive  s collapsed into one space. This also matches IcuTrans, whose entity decoder already mapped   to U+00A0. Compatibility note: only affects shouldUnescape; snapshots or exact textContent comparisons of such text now contain U+00A0 (Testing Library's default normalizer still matches it as a space). A custom react.unescape function can restore the old mapping for text nodes. Thanks @​lprnmns (#1935).

17.0.17

  • perf: useTranslation no longer unsubscribes and resubscribes its i18n listeners on every render. The subscribe callback handed to useSyncExternalStore depended on the merged options object, which is rebuilt whenever props is a new object: with no options (the {} default), with options passed inline (useTranslation('ns', { keyPrefix })), and through withTranslation and <Translation>. A new subscribe makes React resubscribe, so each render of each caller ran i18n.off and i18n.on in an extra effect. It now depends only on the instance and the bindI18n/bindI18nStore event names. No updates were ever missed, because React re-checks the snapshot after resubscribing; this only removes the churn, which adds up with many mounted components that re-render often. Reported via next-i18next#2349.

Bumps the codeql-action group with 3 updates in the / directory: [github/codeql-action/init](https://github.com/github/codeql-action), [github/codeql-action/analyze](https://github.com/github/codeql-action) and [github/codeql-action/upload-sarif](https://github.com/github/codeql-action). Updates `github/codeql-action/init` from 4.38.2 to 4.39.0
Release notes

Sourced from github/codeql-action/init's releases.

v4.39.0

  • Breaking change: Bump the minimum required CodeQL bundle version to 2.20.7. #4205
  • The codeql-action/analyze step now validates that a correct argument for the checkout_path input has been provided. The checkout_path input must be set to the path where the repository that is being analyzed is checked out at on the runner, if that path is something other than the workspace root. If the path does not point to a repository checkout or is different from the path that was used by codeql-action/init, then the CodeQL Action now produces a warning. #4148
  • Resolved an issue with third-party caching implementations that prevented caches from being restored correctly. #4206
  • The codeql-action/start-proxy step that is used in Code Scanning Default Setup now finds CodeQL releases using the same logic as codeql-action/init. This primarily benefits customers who are using GitHub instances other than github.com where the codeql-action/start-proxy step may previously have been unable to locate recent releases and ended up using outdated versions of the private registry authentication proxy as a result. #4198

v4.38.3

  • Upcoming breaking change: CodeQL version 2.21.2 and earlier were discontinued on 24 September 2026 alongside GitHub Enterprise Server 3.17, and will be unsupported by the next minor release of the CodeQL Action. Added a deprecation warning for customers using these versions of CodeQL. #4188
  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.27.2. #4203
  • Fixed a bug where the decision of whether to use a per-language bundle did not account for custom configurations that reference queries outside of compiled CodeQL packs. This issue was caught during internal testing and did not affect any customer repositories. We will resume the roll out of per-language bundles in the coming weeks. #4184

  • Resolved an issue with third-party caching implementations that prevented caches from being restored correctly. #4206
  • The codeql-action/start-proxy step that is used in Code Scanning Default Setup now finds CodeQL releases using the same logic as codeql-action/init. This primarily benefits customers who are using GitHub instances other than github.com where the codeql-action/start-proxy step may previously have been unable to locate recent releases and ended up using outdated versions of the private registry authentication proxy as a result. #4198

4.38.3 - 08 Oct 2026

  • Upcoming breaking change: CodeQL version 2.21.2 and earlier were discontinued on 24 September 2026 alongside GitHub Enterprise Server 3.17, and will be unsupported by the next minor release of the CodeQL Action. Added a deprecation warning for customers using these versions of CodeQL. #4188
  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.27.2. #4203
  • Fixed a bug where the decision of whether to use a per-language bundle did not account for custom configurations that reference queries outside of compiled CodeQL packs. This issue was caught during internal testing and did not affect any customer repositories. We will resume the roll out of per-language bundles in the coming weeks. #4184

  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.27.1. #4160

Per-language bundles support analysis for a single language and are therefore smaller than the combined bundles that allow analysis for all supported languages. As a result, per-language bundles take up less space on disk and are faster to download. We expect to roll this change out to everyone in the coming weeks. #4146

title: fix(web): guide Cypher label syntax and recovery
body:
## Summary

Nexus AI can generate Neo4j label predicates such as `WHERE n:Function OR n:Method` and `labels(n)[0]`. LadybugDB rejects these, and the existing generic error example does not explain how to correct them. Add consistent dialect guidance to the agent prompt, Cypher tool description, and error feedback.

## Areas touched

- [x] `gitnexus-web/` (AI agent and graph tools)

## Implementation

Use one shared guidance string documenting typed MATCH patterns, mixed-type filtering with `label(n) IN [...]`, and `label(n) AS kind`. Ask the agent to correct syntax and retry. The native error remains visible; queries are neither rewritten nor automatically re-executed by the tool. This complements the binder/schema hints proposed in #3459, which explicitly excludes parser errors and targets the MCP backend.

## Validation

- Regression cycle: the new tool tests failed before the change and pass afterward.
- Web test suite: 513 tests passed across 48 files.
- Web TypeScript check and production build passed.
- Changed-file Prettier passed; ESLint reported no errors. Existing warnings in the agent/tools files remain.
- Native LadybugDB check: an OR-of-label-predicates query fails with a parser error; the equivalent `label(n) IN [...]` query returns the expected definitions.
- Impact analysis and staged change analysis reported LOW risk.
- A fresh end-to-end model retest could not complete: the configured external provider returned HTTP 503 (model route unavailable) before any tools ran. This is not claimed as an end-to-end agent pass.

title: feat(web): support bounded line-range source reads
body:
## Summary

Nexus AI's `read` tool always returns the beginning of a file, truncated at 50,000 characters. Once search finds a handler beyond that cutoff, the agent cannot inspect it. Add optional, inclusive, 1-based `startLine` and `endLine` parameters so the agent can read the relevant section.

## Areas touched

- [x] `gitnexus-web/` (AI read tool)

## Implementation

Keep existing no-range reads and the 50,000-character output budget. Slice requested lines before applying that budget, report the selected range and total line count, validate positive integer bounds, clamp an end past EOF, and return actionable feedback for reversed or out-of-file ranges. Truncation feedback now suggests a narrower range. The backend interface is unchanged.

## Validation

- Regression cycle: 14 new assertions failed against the old behavior; all 16 read-tool tests pass with the change.
- Web test suite: 526 tests passed across 48 files.
- Web TypeScript check passed.
- Production build passed with this change and the independent Cypher-guidance change combined.
- Changed-file Prettier and ESLint checks passed with no errors; unrelated existing warnings remain.
- Tests cover a definition beyond the full-file cutoff, inclusive and partial ranges, null/omitted bounds, invalid bounds, output limits, and file-read failures.
- Impact analysis and staged change analysis reported LOW risk.
- Live source/API verification reads a late handler range using the changed tool. An end-to-end model retest was blocked by the external provider returning HTTP 503 (model route unavailable).

## Risk

Existing callers can continue passing only `filePath`. The range is applied to backend-returned content; this does not reduce the backend file transfer. No server endpoint, database schema, migration, or dependencies change. This is scoped to the current backend-based tool rather than the older browser-local implementation proposed in the unmerged #442.

title: --embedding-device dml (DirectML) returns vectors unrelated to CPU's (cosine ~0.37) for snowflake-arctic-embed-xs
body:
_Authorship disclosure: written by Claude (Anthropic's AI) working as the developer on the project that found this; the project's owner reviewed it and asked for it to be filed._

**Summary:** with `--embedding-device dml` (DirectML), the local ONNX embedder returns vectors that bear no relation to the CPU vectors for the same text. DirectML is deterministic run to run, but its output is wrong, and it is also slower.

**Environment:**
- gitnexus 1.6.12
- onnxruntime-node 1.30.0
- Snowflake/snowflake-arctic-embed-xs (fp32, 384-d)
- Windows x64, NVIDIA RTX 3050 Ti Laptop (4 GB), Node 24.19.0

**Repro:**
1. Load gitnexus's own `dist/core/embeddings/embedder.js`, the code path behind `--embedding-device`.
2. Call `initEmbedder(undefined, {}, 'dml')`, and separately `'cpu'`.
3. Call `embedBatch` on the same 64 real code texts, in batches of 16, after a 2-text warm-up.

**Measured:**

| Comparison | cosine min | mean | max |
|---|---|---|---|
| CPU vs CPU (2 runs) | 1.00000 | 1.00000 | 1.00000 |
| DML vs DML (3 runs) | 1.00000 | 1.00000 | 1.00000 |
| **CPU vs DML** | **0.306** | **0.366** | **0.434** |

- `getCurrentDevice()` reports `dml`.
- Both sides return 384 dimensions.
- Time for 64 texts: 9.6 s on DML vs 4.2 s on CPU.

An index built with `dml` would answer semantic queries with vectors in a different space from any CPU-built or query-time CPU vectors. Nothing reports it.

**Ask:** validate the device at init. Embed a fixed probe on the selected device and on CPU, and fall back to CPU with a warning if they disagree beyond a tolerance. Or keep `dml` out of the allowed set until it matches.

title: feat: add the test scenario map and a Vitest 5 mutation runner
body:
## Summary

Adds advisory test-quality tooling for the CLI package: a PR-time duplicate-test scan, a Stryker mutation runner validated under the repo's Vitest 5, and a Test Scenario Map report. Its primary verdict is the **scenario fingerprint**: two tests are duplicates when they run the same execution path on the same input data and check the same expectation. It needs no mutation run and covers every unit and integration test of `gitnexus/` (1,397 files); Layer 1 runs in 4 CI slices. Per-test mutation evidence stays as an optional deep check (manual dispatch, or the `scenario-map` label on a pull request). Everything reports only; nothing edits a test or blocks a merge.

This PR carries Phase 0 (runner and validation gates) and Phase 1 (the pure-JS report) of `docs/plans/2026-10-23-test-scenario-map-design.md`, with the fingerprint extended to every unit and integration test. Mutation evidence stays on the validated pure-JS category; Phase 2 (native-backed, fixture-reading and LadybugDB tests) and Phase 3 (integration tests) bring those into mutation scope later.

## Motivation / context

An audit of the suite (1,350 test files, ~22.7k cases, 42 bench dirs) found about 160 repeated cases, 22 redundant pipeline runs and bench `--check` gates no workflow runs. Text similarity cannot tell a real repeat from two distinct scenarios: look-alike tests often guard different behaviour. The reliable signal is mutation evidence ("does any fault catch one test but not the other?"), and Stryker's official `@stryker-mutator/vitest-runner` runs zero tests per mutant under Vitest 5. Plans: `docs/plans/2026-10-23-1823-feat-stryker-vitest5-runner-phase0-plan.md` (Phase 0), `docs/plans/2026-10-24-0902-feat-test-scenario-map-phase1-plan.md` (Phase 1).

## Areas touched

- [x] `gitnexus/` (CLI / core / MCP server): tooling only, under `gitnexus/tools/` (not published to npm); no `gitnexus/src` change
- [ ] `gitnexus-web/` (Vite / React UI)
- [x] `.github/` (workflows, actions): `test-dupes` job in `ci.yml`, a section in `ci-report.yml`, advisory `mutation-runner-validation.yml` (now with a path-gated `scenario-map-controls` job), new weekly `test-scenario-map.yml`
- [ ] `eval/` or other tooling
- [x] Docs / agent config only: `TESTING.md`, the design doc and plans under `docs/plans/`

## Scope & constraints

**In scope**

- `npm run test:dupes` (Layer 0, PR-time): five finding kinds, reported only on changed lines; `// dupe-ok: <reason>` silences an intentional repeat.
- A Stryker 10 test runner for Vitest 5 (`gitnexus/tools/mutation/`): task-id test selection (now also a dry-run `testIds` selection), per-test outcome classes from every attempt, hook-attributed coverage with a marker, a prepared copy that makes `as`-asserted code mutable. Validated on the pure-JS category by four gates, re-run after the Phase 1 runner extensions:

| Gate | What it shows | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 Fidelity | Unmutated runner run matches a normal Vitest 5 run | 251 files, 4,667 tests, 0 differences |
| 2 Conformance | Pinned runner behaviours on a fixture project, two profiles | 26/26 hold |
| 3 Oracle | An independent Vitest 5 oracle agrees with the runner | 3 scopes, 1,606 mutant classes and 20,455 sampled per-test outcomes, 0 differences |
| 4 Controls | Planted mutants killed by exactly the expected tests; two profiles give identical kill sets | Pass |

- `npm run test:scenario-map` (Phase 1), stages `plan`, `value-flow`, `shards`, `shard`, `merge`, `all`, `controls`:
  - Layer 1: per-test V8 block coverage retrieves candidate pairs (retrieval only, never a verdict).
  - Layer 2: per-instance checks, context and input facet, with the values the facet discards kept for the semantic check.
  - Layer 3: per-test kill sets (assertion failures only) per candidate group, two baselines, a full isolation pass, and a row-deletion operator for object/Set/Map tables.
  - Value-flow veto: Babel binding, the TypeScript 7 checker, a GitNexus PDG walk and a Vitest trace of value-sensitive built-ins. Any unknown sends the pair to Review.
  - Mutation verdict engine (Inconclusive > Out of scope > Weak > Repeat strong > Repeat weak > Row > Review > Distinct), a JSON and markdown report, and one tracking issue updated in place.
  - Scenario fingerprint (`verdict/fingerprint.ts`, the primary verdict): duplicate, possible duplicate (an unresolved input, fail-closed), table row (other input values), same scenario with different checks, distinct. `--mutation none|possible-duplicates|all` decides how much mutation evidence a run gathers; `possible-duplicates` mutates only the groups with a possible duplicate, trimmed to their tests and the files they executed.
- `test-scenario-map.yml`: the weekly fingerprint run (4 Layer 1 coverage slices, then plan, value flow and merge; no mutation shard) with the issue upsert; manual dispatch with a `mutation` input; the `scenario-map` label on a pull request starts a diff-scoped deep run: only pairs with a test of a changed test file; Layer 1 in the coverage slices over those files, the files sharing their checks-and-context keys and every file with a test of no static key; then mutation over the possible duplicates (no issue, no baseline; the report is an artifact and the job summary).

**Explicitly out of scope / not done here**

- Removing or folding any existing test; the tool never edits tests.
- Mutation evidence for native-backed, fixture-reading, LadybugDB, worker-backed and integration tests (Phases 2-3; the fingerprint already covers them); `gitnexus-web/` and Python tests.
- Any precision claim: the design's independent labelling and holdouts come later; the report says precision is not measured.
- Blocking merges: every job is `continue-on-error` and outside the CI Gate.

## Implementation notes

- **Fingerprint first, from evidence.** On the second full mutation run (40208819019), every pair with the same path, input and expectation, fully resolved and trace-clean (26 pairs), was either one of the run's 13 strong repeats or one mutation could not decide (13, real duplicates by title); none was Distinct or Row. The static scan catches 25 of the 26; the one it misses is a renamed copy (`method-props.test.ts` lines 47 and 185). So the fingerprint decides duplicates in minutes, and mutation is kept for the possible duplicates, weak tests and gaps.
- **Fail closed everywhere.** Missing, timed-out, retried, runtime-class or hook-attributed evidence, a skipped stage, an invalid trace run or a degraded value-flow run demotes a pair (Inconclusive, Review or weak). A committed controls fixture (`gitnexus/test/fixtures/mutation-scenario-map/`) holds one pair per adversarial case from the design (`Math.round` 2.4/2.5, regex alternatives, a numeric boundary, an expected-only difference, ...) plus positive controls; `expected.json` was written from the design, and the oracle fails on any unlisted repeat.
- **Value flow is stitched.** GitNexus PDG flows stay inside one function, so the check reads per-function REACHING_DEF and CALL_SUMMARY edges and follows calls through the TypeScript checker; truncation, ambiguity or depth over 4 is unknown.
- **Row deletion runs on plain Vitest 5.** Stryker applies only its own mutators, so the operator edits a throwaway prepared copy and reruns the pair with a fresh Vitest instance after a control run.
- **The CI budget comes from measurement.** Value flow runs before the shards and re-plans them so isolation is spent only on pairs that can still be strong; observations are stored compactly (a batch of 73 tests over 22k mutants needs 141k rows, not 1.6M). A full mutation run (scope `all`, dispatch only) measured about 4 h and 30 runner-hours over 9 shards; mutation verdict engines 2 and 3 (a kill witness decides a pair past unknown mutants; a test file that fails to import is recorded, not missing) took Inconclusive from 4,532 to 833 of 6,264 pairs.
- **Every unit and integration test, fingerprinted.** The fingerprint needs no Stryker run, so it is not bound to the mutation runner's validated category. Three things made the integration tests run in the prepared copy: the base config's `fileParallelism: false` projects (`lbug-db`, `cli-e2e`) run in a one-worker partition; the checkout's `vendor/` and `dist/` are copied in (the gate-3-hashed prepare step leaves them out, and integration tests load leiden, the parse worker and the built CLI); and Layer 1 runs as a `coverage` stage per slice, split like the CI test shards (`test/helpers/shard-balance.ts`), which `plan --coverage` merges. A test that did not pass makes its pairs Inconclusive (`not-passing`), and a slice that did not report leaves its files unrecorded.
- **Layer 1 skips what cannot produce a finding.** A duplicate, possible duplicate or table row needs equal (or unknown) checks-and-context keys, and the key is static, so Layer 1 runs only files with a shared or unknown key, plus every file the static view cannot vouch for (helper- or alias-registered tests, dynamic `it.each` counts, file snapshots). On the current checkout that skips 449 of 1,399 files, about a quarter of the weighted cost; on the last full unit run the static keys reproduce all 3,313 runtime keys, and runtime collection of the skipped files finds no unseen test. `--mutation all` and the controls still run every file.
- **A labelled pull request is diff-scoped, with full recall.** `--changed-since <ref>` keeps only candidate pairs with a test of a test file the diff added or modified. Layer 1 runs those files, their key partners and every file with a test of no static key (helper-registered, dynamic `it.each` counts, file snapshots), since such a test can pair with any changed test. That floor is 230 of 1,407 files (about 59% of the weighted Layer 1 cost), so a labelled run uses the coverage slices too; the slices record the changed files and the plan takes the scope from them.
- **Bounded locally.** `--concurrency` bounds both Stryker and every in-process Vitest run.

Session-settled decisions carried from planning: Vitest 5 only (user-directed, over a Vitest 4 harness); CLI package only (user-directed, over including `gitnexus-web/`); reports only with advisory CI (user-approved); Phase 1 on this PR (user-directed); similarity for retrieval only (user-approved); one artifact plus one tracking issue (user-approved); the pure-JS category only (user-approved); mutation through the Phase 0 runner (user-approved); a semantic value-flow check (user-directed, over a blanket rule). Proceeded under flagged conflicts: row deletion cannot go through the Phase 0 runner, so it runs plain Vitest 5 (KTD2); the PDG walk is stitched because PDG flows are intra-procedural (KTD11).

## Testing & verification

- [x] `cd gitnexus && npx vitest run test/unit/scenario-map test/unit/shard-balance.test.ts` (30 files, 1,049 tests), `test/unit/test-dupes.test.ts` and `test/unit/mutation`; `npm run typecheck:tests`; `eslint` and `prettier --check`
- [x] Gates 1-4 re-run after the runner extensions; gate 3 re-checked after the 2026-10-25 merges from main (results in the table above). The 2026-10-26 main merge left the three frozen manifests stale (see Risk & rollout)
- [x] `npm run test:scenario-map -- controls` (local): all 16 fixture pairs match `expected.json`, both the mutation verdict and rule and the fingerprint verdict and rule (the fingerprint expectations were written from its rules before any run)
- [x] Whole category, plan and value-flow stages: 4,667 tests, 6,280 candidate pairs in 611 groups, 1,374 facet-equal pairs, 321 with differing values (120 vetoed, 160 unknown, 41 clean)
- [x] Seeded slice of Layer 3 (16-20 groups, 263 evaluated pairs): Inconclusive 139 (runtime-class kills and unknown kills, as the strict kill rule requires), Distinct 85, Review 37, Row 1, Weak 1
- [x] Two full-category mutation runs on this PR through a temporary label-gated trigger (since removed): [40183982111](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/actions/runs/40183982111) and [40208819019](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/actions/runs/40208819019), both complete (9 of 9 shards); all 13 strong repeat candidates are real duplicates
- [x] Fingerprint-only run over all 4,632 eligible tests, locally: 8.2 min (plan 5.4, trace 2.6), 26 duplicates (the 26 the mutation evidence predicted), 109 possible duplicates in 17 groups, 945 table rows
- [x] Deep run over the possible duplicates via the `scenario-map` label ([40268120818](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/actions/runs/40268120818)): 5 min 42 s end to end, one shard of 5 groups and 844 mutants in 1.3 min. Re-merged locally (its merge missed the single shard artifact, fixed in `ac3dd186e`): of the 109 possible duplicates, 31 are Row (proven different), 1 Distinct, 3 weak-evidence repeats, 3 Inconclusive; 71 test `tools/mutation/` code outside the mutation scope
- [x] Integration sample, locally (shared host, concurrency 4): before the `vendor/`/`dist/` copy, 23 of 44 sampled integration files failed to load; after it, `resolvers/rust` (255 tests), `server-http-startup` and `typescript-async-generator-functions` pass in the prepared copy. the local timings are distorted by other suites on the shared host, so the 4 slices are sized from the test workflow, which runs the whole suite with coverage in three 7-8 minute shards (ci.yml run 30014110469); an instrumented run shows Layer 1's own overhead is small (coverage snapshots: 10.1 s of `resolvers/rust`'s ~190 s, whose work sits in `beforeAll`)
- [x] Code review (7 reviewers plus an independent cross-model pass); the six validated findings are fixed in this PR

## New concepts

**Per-test mutation kill sets.** Mutation testing makes small faults ("mutants") in production code, such as flipping a comparison or deleting a table entry, and reruns the tests. A test *kills* a mutant when it fails by an assertion. The set of mutants a test kills is evidence of what it actually protects.

- Why here: two tests that run the same code can still guard different scenarios. Identical non-empty kill sets mean no evaluated fault tells them apart, which is the strongest signal that one repeats the other. Coverage alone cannot show this.
- Example from this PR: in `type-extractors/shared.ts`, the mutant that changes `new Set(['Keys'])` to `new Set([])` is killed only by `methodToTypeArgPosition > returns first for Keys on Dictionary (C# key method)`.
- When not to use it: as proof of equivalence. Equivalent mutants and code outside mutation reach (native packages, workers) mean kill sets can only flag candidates for a human to review.

<details>
<summary>VitestDedup trial (22 October 2026)</summary>

**Recommendation: keep this PR's scanner and use VitestDedup only as an advisory companion.** The trial found useful candidates, but its context handling and coverage gaps do not support a blocking gate or automatic test removal.

Trialled `vitest-dedup@0.6.0` against this PR at `01b13dc3b3a011c8326036472272cfe4eb89ca4e`, using the existing Vitest configuration in the core `gitnexus/` package.

| Measure | Result |
| --- | ---: |
| Files reported analyzed | 1,288 |
| Tests extracted | 19,699 |
| Duplicate candidates | 31: 17 same-file, 14 cross-file |
| Parameterization suggestions | 1,215 |
| Other findings | 34 near-duplicates, 1 name collision |
| Initial full scan | 20.8 seconds, 79.1 MiB peak RSS |

**Coverage was incomplete:** 1,482 extracted tests were excluded because their context was unresolved; 51 files had every extracted test excluded, and 112 files were partially read. The test count is not a complete census. Application dependencies were not installed in the checkout, so some unresolved imports may be environment-dependent. Timings are individual observations, not a controlled benchmark.

Checks against the existing scanner fixtures and source exposed three important limits:

- **False positive:** identical test bodies under different describe-level assignments (`process.env.X = '1'` versus `'0'`) were labelled redundant with equivalent context and `incomplete: false`. This PR's scanner keeps that fixture distinct. Of seven negative `same-test` fixtures, VitestDedup distinguished five, misclassified this one, and extracted no tests from the wrapper-options fixture; the latter exited 2 and is not a successful check.
- **Missed coverage:** `test/unit/type-env.test.ts` exceeds VitestDedup's fixed raw syntax budget of 8,192 units and is skipped before parsing. That loses the 12 cross-file `stripNullable` duplicate candidates which this PR detects. This syntax limit is independent of dependency installation.
- **Intentional repetition:** both analyzers flag the later Python control in `function-local-import-chain.test.ts`, which is documented as checking for provider state leaking after the Rust cases. Retain that protection when reviewing the finding.

The 14 cross-file extractor findings are useful review candidates. The 1,215 parameterization suggestions propose retaining cases as table rows; they are not evidence that those cases can be deleted.

The existing scanner's `--all` run at this pinned head produced 114 findings in 7.1 seconds: 71 same-test, 20 fixture setups, 14 copied helpers, 3 assertion-subset findings and 6 orphan benchmark gates. It reads a different corpus and groups findings differently, so its totals and VitestDedup's are not directly comparable. This is separate from the earlier main-branch audit above.

**Validation:** all 17 existing scanner unit tests passed. The VitestDedup `--changed-since caacc3bac2d0c714f34fa4efd3abaa6ce3089ac6` run returned zero findings and exited 0, withholding all 1,281 unchanged-file findings; it still analyzed the full corpus and remained incomplete. Changed scope is by file, not by line.

A tested warning-only configuration retained just the 31 duplicate candidates and exited 0. Keep incomplete-analysis diagnostics visible alongside any report. The trial made no code or CI changes, and did not run the full application test suite.

<details>
<summary>Reproduce the advisory configuration</summary>

Save this configuration outside the checkout as `advisory-config.json`:

```json
{
  "rules": {
    "duplicate-test": "warning",
    "cross-file-duplicate": "warning",
    "duplicate-test-name": "off",
    "parameterization-candidate": "off",
    "near-duplicate-test": "off",
    "duplicate-suite": "off",
    "duplicate-each-row": "off",
    "redundant-hook": "off",
    "subsumed-test": "off"
  }
}
```

From `gitnexus/` at the pinned commit, with report paths outside the checkout:

```bash
npm install --prefix /path/to/trial-tools --ignore-scripts --no-audit --no-fund --save-exact vitest-dedup@0.6.0
/path/to/trial-tools/node_modules/.bin/vitest-dedup . \
  --config /path/to/advisory-config.json \
  --reporters json,html \
  --output /path/to/reports/advisory
```

For the default diagnostic run, omit `--config` and use `--reporters json,html,jsonl --emit-test-fingerprints`; preserve stdout and stderr. `--changed-since` requires full git history. The default run exits 1 on error-severity duplicate findings; the warning-only configuration changes that gate, not the completeness of the analysis.

</details>

</details>

## Risk & rollout

- Merges cannot be blocked: all new jobs are `continue-on-error` and outside the CI Gate.
- `ci-report.yml` and the scheduled workflow run from the default branch, so the duplicate-test section and the first weekly report appear only after this merges.
- **Before merge: remove the temporary test trigger.** `test-scenario-map.yml` carries a TEMPORARY `scenario-map-test` clause (coverage and plan job `if`s, the coverage step's diff-scope condition): that label, added by magyargergo on this PR only, runs the whole suite with mutation `possible-duplicates` to test every stage before the workflow can be dispatched. Delete the clause and the label.
- **After merge: re-freeze gate 3.** The frozen manifests in `gitnexus/test/fixtures/mutation-oracle/` hash their inputs, and main's changes (the `vitest.config.ts` include from #3725, shared closure files) left all three stale. Nothing on pull requests or in the scenario map reads them; gate 3 runs only on dispatch. Once `mutation-runner-validation.yml` is on the default branch, dispatch it with `oracle=refreeze`, `refreeze_scope=all` and a new seed (about 4.5 h for `shared`, 1 h for `middleware`, 45 min for `schema-constants`, one job each), then review and commit the uploaded manifests.
- Weekly cost: the fingerprint run over every unit and integration test, an estimated 1 to 1.5 runner-hours (4 coverage slices of roughly 10-15 minutes plus setup, then single-runner jobs); the first run measures it.
- Adding the `scenario-map` label (created 2026-10-26) to a pull request starts the diff-scoped deep run (4 coverage slices over at least the no-static-key floor, then plan, value flow, mutation shards over the possible duplicates and merge); any other label event leaves every job skipped.
- Permissions: only the `upsert-issue` job has `issues: write`, and it runs only for complete default-branch runs; the baseline comes only from this workflow's own default-branch runs of this repository.
- Phase 0 added `@stryker-mutator/core` and `@stryker-mutator/api` 10.0.0 (exact devDependencies); Phase 1 adds no dependency.

## Checklist

- [x] PR body meets repo minimum length (workflow may label short descriptions)
- [x] If `AGENTS.md` / overlays changed: headers, scope block, and changelog updated per project conventions (not changed)
- [x] No secrets, tokens, or machine-specific paths committed

title: lbugjs.node SIGSEGV in WALReplayer::replayFrozenWAL on 'gitnexus analyze --embeddings' - recurring WAL corruption crash loop
body: Environment: gitnexus 1.6.12 (npm), node 26.7.0, Arch Linux, systemd 261. Observed: on affected repositories, every 'gitnexus analyze --embeddings' run SIGSEGVs at store open; coredump stack: lbug::storage::NodeGroup::delete_ -> NodeTable::delete_ -> WALReplayer::replayNodeDeletionRecord -> WALReplayer::replayFrozenWAL (lbugjs.node). A 'lbug.shadow.dirty-recovery' marker file appears next to the store (alongside lbug, lbug.wal.checkpoint), so the DB is left needing recovery it cannot complete. The crash then repeats on every subsequent analyze, ~548 identical coredumps over 19 days on one host, ~34MB each. Two repos of seven on this host were affected simultaneously (large C++/TS monorepos); smaller repos never hit it. Recurrence: deleting .gitnexus (fresh store) fixes it temporarily - the same repo re-corrupted within 3 days (store replaced 2026-10-19, same crash signature back by 2026-10-22), so something during normal analyze/embedding writes leaves the WAL in a state replayFrozenWAL cannot survive. Suspect a crash or unclean close during a node-deletion-heavy phase leaves a bad WAL record. Workaround: rm -rf .gitnexus and re-index. Happy to provide a coredump or the poisoned store files if useful.

title: analyze rewrites the CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md section with LF, leaving mixed line endings in CRLF checkouts (Windows)
body:
**Environment**
- gitnexus 1.6.12 (`npm i -g`), Node 24, Windows 10
- Git with `core.autocrlf=true` and `* text=auto` in `.gitattributes`, so text files are checked out with CRLF

**Steps**
1. In such a checkout, with a `CLAUDE.md` that has hand-written content plus the `<!-- gitnexus:start -->` … `<!-- gitnexus:end -->` block, run `gitnexus analyze --no-stats --force`.
2. Run `git status` and `git ls-files --eol CLAUDE.md`.

**Observed**
- The file now has mixed line endings: the hand-written part stays CRLF (170 lines), and the regenerated block is written with LF (44 lines).
- `git ls-files --eol` reports `w/mixed`, and `git status` lists `CLAUDE.md` as modified, even though `git diff` is empty and `git add` stages nothing (the content is identical once normalized).
- So with `--no-stats` the content no longer churns, but the working tree still looks dirty after every reindex.
- `AGENTS.md`, which is entirely generated, comes out all-LF and is not affected.

**Expected**
When upserting the section into an existing file, keep the file's line endings: detect CRLF in the existing content and write the block with the same EOL.

**Workaround**
`.gitattributes`:
```
CLAUDE.md text eol=lf
AGENTS.md text eol=lf
```

Possibly related: #2838 (`detect_changes` flagging EOL-only diffs).

title: 1.6.13-rc.139: gitnexus query prints its result and never exits (the embedding sidecar keeps the process alive)
body:
_Authorship disclosure: written by Claude (Anthropic's AI) working as the developer on the project that found this; the project's owner reviewed it and asked for it to be filed._

**Summary:** on 1.6.13-rc.139, `gitnexus query <text>` prints its complete JSON result in about 2–3 s and then never exits. The local embedding sidecar it starts keeps the process alive. Any scripted caller that waits for the exit hangs.

**Environment:**
- gitnexus 1.6.13-rc.139, @ladybugdb/core 0.21.1
- Windows x64, Node 24.19.0
- Local ONNX embeddings (no `GITNEXUS_EMBEDDING_BASE_URL`); index built with `--embeddings 0`, 8,022 vectors

**Repro:**

```
gitnexus query resolve_storage > out.txt 2>&1
```

`out.txt` holds the full result (13,569 bytes: `processes`, `process_symbols`, `definitions`, `timing`, `staleness`). The process had not exited after 45 s on a clean slate. Earlier runs, for a known symbol and for an absent one, had not exited after 120 s. While a query is waiting, two processes are alive: `dist/cli/index.js query …` and its child `dist/core/embeddings/embedding-sidecar.js`. 1.6.12 exits normally.

**Cause, as far as we can read it:** `queryCommand` in `dist/cli/tool.js` calls `backend.callTool('query', …)`, writes the result with `output(result)`, and returns. It neither reaps the embedding sidecar (`disposeEmbedder` / `embedding-sidecar-reap`) nor exits. The lazy action wrapper (`dist/cli/lazy-action.js`) also just awaits and returns. The live sidecar child keeps the event loop alive.

**Impact:**
- `gitnexus query … && next-step` never proceeds.
- On Windows, a caller's own timeout that ends only the `.cmd` shim does not help either: the node process keeps the inherited pipe open. Our tooling waited 17 minutes before we found it.

**Checked against newer RCs:** the compare from rc.139 to rc.141 has 3 commits (#3669, #3654, release), none touching the CLI or the sidecar.

**Ask:** reap the sidecar and exit after one-shot CLI tool commands that may embed (`query` at least), or `unref()` the sidecar child so it cannot hold the process open.

title: On an index left dirty by an interrupted run, GitNexus exits 0xC0000005 instead of reporting (1.6.12 and 1.6.13-rc.139, Windows)
body:
_Authorship disclosure: written by Claude (Anthropic's AI) working as the developer on the project that found this; the project's owner reviewed it and asked for it to be filed._

**Summary:** on a store left behind by an interrupted run, GitNexus detects the condition and logs it, then dies with **0xC0000005 (ACCESS_VIOLATION)** instead of reporting. Seen on 1.6.12 (reads and analyze) and still on **1.6.13-rc.139** (analyze), on Windows.

**Environment:** Windows x64, Node 24.19.0, `analyze --pdg --index-only --skip-agents-md --skip-skills`, retention `symbol`.

**1.6.12 (2026-10-03 to 10-11):**
- An `analyze` died mid-write in `phase=load-graph`. It left `lbug` (17,100,771,328 bytes), `lbug.shadow.dirty-recovery` and `lbug.wal.checkpoint`, all frozen at the same second.
- From then on every `gitnexus context <symbol>`, including a symbol that cannot exist, exited -1073741819 after printing its banner. Meanwhile `analyze-last.log` already carried GitNexus's own diagnosis: *"Previous analyze run did not complete cleanly (incrementalInProgress flag set); last dirty state: phase=load-graph … forcing full rebuild to restore a known-good index."*
- One variable changed: the same binary, cwd and environment against a different registered repo returned clean JSON (`Symbol ... not found`, exit 1). The instrument was fine; one index was not.

**1.6.13-rc.139 / LadybugDB 0.21.1 (measured 2026-10-22, sandbox copies only):**

| Store | Result |
|---|---|
| Copy of an interrupted store written by 0.18.3 (`lbug` 16,671,494,144 bytes, `.shadow` + `.wal.checkpoint`), default 16 GiB ceiling | "Parked lbug.shadow.dirty-recovery …", "--force on a repo with 7834 existing embeddings …", then **0xC0000005 after 97 s** |
| Same store, fresh copy, `GITNEXUS_LBUG_MAX_DB_SIZE` = 64 GiB | **0xC0000005 after 51 s**, so the ceiling is not the cause |
| A store written by 0.21.1 and killed 51 s into an incremental write | Next run: "reclaimed quarantined WAL … from a prior crash", indexed in 17.5 s, **exit 0** |

So an interrupted write on the new engine recovered. We could not produce the exact `incrementalInProgress` state on 0.21.1, and we have not shown whether that state still crashes there.

**Ask:** when recovery of a dirty index fails, report it (non-zero exit plus the diagnosis already in `analyze-last.log`) rather than dying. If the forced rebuild cannot open the old file, say so and name the remedy (move the store aside and rebuild). A process that has already diagnosed its own fault should hand the caller the diagnosis, not a crash.

title: fix(cli): reap embedding sidecar after query

## Summary

Close the direct CLI query backend after every query, including failed queries, so a locally started embedding sidecar cannot keep the one-shot process alive after output is complete.

title: [Bug] scope-resolution thrashes into swap on a refactored Java branch: same repo runs 16 min on integration branch but >2h unfinished on refactor branch
body:
## Summary

On a 3.6 GB-RAM host, `gitnexus analyze --force` on the **same repository** behaves drastically differently depending on which Java branch is checked out — the refactor branch drives scope-resolution into swap-thrashing and never completes, while the integration branch finishes in 16 minutes.

## Environment

- GitNexus `1.6.13-rc.147` (npm install, standalone node_modules)
- Linux x86_64, 4 cores, **3.6 GB RAM + 8 GB swap (zram 6G + disk swap)**, low-memory host
- Repository: large outpatient HIS monorepo module, ~17,095 `.java` files
- Command: `analyze --force --workers 1`, `NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=8192`, `GITNEXUS_WORKER_POOL_SIZE=1`, `GITNEXUS_WORKER_READY_TIMEOUT_MS=30000`, `GITNEXUS_LBUG_BUFFER_POOL_SIZE=3221225472`, `GITNEXUS_FTS_CJK_SEGMENTATION=bigram`

## Reproduction (same repo, same engine, same flags)

| Branch | Character | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `branch-from/V6.0-20240815-it` (integration) | 17,095 java files | ✅ **958 s**, 344,859 nodes / 624,955 edges |
| `sr-rc` (refactor of the same system) | ~same file count | ❌ **>2 h 14 min, never finished** — killed |

For reference, 1.6.12 on the integration branch produced 171,326 nodes / 386,083 edges — so rc.147's receiver-inference fixes doubled graph completeness (+101% nodes), which is great; this report is only about the memory pathology.

## Observations on the failing branch

- VmSwap climbs to ~8.0 GB (swap saturated), VmRSS stays < 1.2 GB — classic thrash profile
- CPU decays from 116% → 38% over two hours (time going to page-in/page-out)
- The same shape we previously hit on a different branch of a related repo (25.8k java files), where 1.6.12 never finished either
- One file on the refactor branch is >512 KB (`ClinicalOrderQueryService.java`, skipped by the default large-file cap) — the refactor concentrates very large service classes

## Interpretation

The refactor branch has denser inheritance/interface structure (framework-style refactor), which appears to push the scope-resolution passes into a memory working set far beyond physical RAM. This looks related to the node-count growth we reported earlier (+81% nodes from expanded tree-sitter captures, 1.6.12 era) but now amplified by receiver-chain typing work in 1.6.13: more complete graphs require proportionally more resident working set during scope-res.

## Ask

1. Any knob to bound scope-resolution resident set (streaming/sharded passes), or is the working set inherently O(graph)?
2. Would a `--memory-budget`-style cap for scope-res be feasible (degrade edge completeness instead of thrashing)?
3. We can provide heap-probe traces (per-phase RSS timeline) for both branches if useful — the probes already exist in our 1.6.10/1.6.12 instrumentation setup.

Happy to test candidate fixes on these branches — the A/B branches make this a clean reproduction.

title: impact CLI: single upstream query allocates ~184 GB native heap (not buffer pool) on 66k-symbol index
body:
## Summary

A single `gitnexus impact` CLI call reaches a **184.5 GB physical footprint** (almost all of it swapped) on a 64 GB Mac. The memory is ordinary native heap allocations during query execution, **not** the LadybugDB buffer pool. Capping `bufferManagerSize` (the approach discussed in #2557) does not change it.

When a coding agent runs `impact` / `detect-changes` as part of its normal workflow, macOS reports "Your system has run out of application memory", and the host app (here the ChatGPT/Codex desktop app, which spawns the CLI) is shown at 86–186 GB.

## Environment

```text
OS: macOS 27.0.1, Apple Silicon, 64 GB RAM
Node: v26.5.1
gitnexus: 1.6.9 (global npm install)
@ladybugdb/core: 0.18.3
Repo: Python (FastAPI) + TypeScript (React) monorepo
Index: 65,833 symbols, 127,383 relationships, 300 processes; .gitnexus/lbug 209 MB
```

## Reproduction

```bash
gitnexus impact createLbugDatabase --direction upstream --limit 3
```

Any upstream `impact` on this index shows the same pattern. `detect-changes --scope staged` peaked at 11 GB in the same session.

## Measurements

`/usr/bin/time -l` on one run: **47.1 GB maximum resident set size**, 72 s wall time.

RSS sampled every 3 s on a second run. The RSS drops while pages are pushed to swap, so RSS alone understates the footprint:

```text
t=3s 34GB  t=6s 30GB  t=9s 12GB  t=15s 4GB  t=21s 2GB  t=27s 14GB  t=36s 12GB
```

`vmmap --summary` at t≈36 s, before the process was killed:

```text
Physical footprint:         184.5G
MALLOC ZONE   TOTAL   184.5G (virtual)   11.6G (resident)   172.8G (swapped)   48,071,900 allocations, 183.8G allocated
```

So ~48 million live malloc allocations totalling ~184 GB for an index that is 209 MB on disk.

## Buffer pool ruled out

As an experiment, `createLbugDatabase` in `dist/core/lbug/lbug-config.js` was patched locally to pass `bufferManagerSize = 4 GiB` instead of `0`. The run above was made **with that patch in place**: the footprint was still 184.5 GB, all in MALLOC. The patch has been reverted since. `--max-old-space-size=1024` (seen in agent-spawned invocations) also has no effect, as expected for native memory.

This suggests the upstream traversal query materialises an exploding intermediate result (variable-length path expansion?) rather than caching pages.

## Expected

- `impact` with `--limit 3` should stay within a bounded working set (a few GB at most) on an index of this size.
- Ideally a hard memory guard / query timeout in the CLI and MCP server, so one runaway query cannot take down the host.

## Related

- #2557 (closed): detect_changes via MCP ballooning to 80% of RAM. Its attribution to the buffer pool does not match what we see here.
- #3354 (closed): impact returning identical results for every target. Possibly related to how the upstream traversal is built.

Happy to run a build with query tracing (e.g. `GITNEXUS_POOL_RSS_TRACE`) or provide the generated Cypher if that helps.

title: fix(routes): link consumers to wrapper-composed URLs
body:
## Summary

HTTP consumers now link to the URL their proven wrappers construct. A caller of `request('/models')` whose wrapper fetches `'/api' + path` links to `/api/models`, instead of missing that route or linking an unrelated `/models` endpoint.

## Motivation / context

Provider mount-prefix extraction already landed; consumer matching still discarded URL composition inside wrappers. The original QwenPaw client passes paths through an imported `getApiUrl` helper before fetching them.

Fixes #2858
Related: #3609, #3408

## Areas touched

**In scope**

- Binding-proven string concatenations, templates, stable aliases, single unconditional synchronous URL-builder returns and wrapper forwarding.

**Explicitly out of scope / not done here**

- Inferring arbitrary runtime URL construction, `new URL`, reassigned normalization, imported prefix values, or URL transformations from member names alone.
- Expanding route matching heuristics or inferring additional providers.

URL facts describe a bounded set of string operations; source code is never evaluated. Returned helpers require an identified binding or resolved import. Unsupported automatic transformations remain unproven; explicit wrapper configuration retains its opaque-path fallback.

Only parameter-dependent HTTP flows reach callers. Fixed refresh or telemetry URLs remain attributed to their own fetch sites. Identity-only forwarding is collapsed iteratively, preserving a 5,000-hop chain without spending the transformation-depth budget. Direct-return facts come from the cursor walk, so deeply nested helpers meet the existing native AST-traversal bounds.

title: fix(eval): retain valid background completion measurements
body:
## Summary

Keep valid release-evaluation measurements when Claude Code announces a background completion before the foreground result. This prevents a successful session from making the stable report incomplete and failing the release gate.

## Motivation / context

The pinned Claude CLI 2.1.214 can emit `notification → result → init → reply → result`. The validator only searched between results, producing `additional result lacks a background completion turn` even though the process exited successfully and both task checks passed.

Related: [failed evaluation job](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/actions/runs/39948470804/job/120399273533), [prior continuation handling](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/pull/3604).

## Areas touched

- [ ] `gitnexus/` (CLI / core / MCP server)
- [ ] `gitnexus-web/` (Vite / React UI)
- [ ] `.github/` (workflows, actions)
- [x] `eval/` or other tooling
- [ ] Docs / agent config only

## Scope & constraints

**In scope**

- Preserve pending completion notifications across result boundaries and verify the real CLI event order.

**Explicitly out of scope / not done here**

- Paid evaluation reruns, release publication, and retroactive validation of the failed run.

## Implementation notes

Each pending notification can authorize one continuation. Session identity, distinct result IDs, success, usage, cumulative cost, and a fresh initialization/reply remain required.

## Testing & verification

The new unit regression and real CLI canary both failed with the exact CI error before the fix. The standalone CLI reproduction then passed with all usage retained.

- [x] 236 Python tests passed, 1 skipped, including both offline canaries using CLI 2.1.214:
  `uv run --locked --extra dev python -m pytest -q tests/test_workflow_bench_sessions.py tests/test_session_progress.py tests/test_release_report.py tests/test_release_gate.py tests/test_release_evidence.py tests/test_offline_session_integration.py`
  Set `CLAUDE_CANARY_BIN` to the pinned binary and `GITNEXUS_REQUIRE_CLAUDE_CANARY=1` to require the canaries.
- [x] 20 relevant core tests passed:
  `cd gitnexus && npm test -- test/unit/release-docker-gate.test.ts test/unit/publish-release-evidence.test.ts --maxWorkers 1`
- [x] `cd gitnexus && npx tsc --noEmit`
- [x] Ruff check and whitespace checks passed.
- [ ] Full core suite remains unverified: the earlier `npm test` run stayed at its startup banner for over three minutes and was interrupted.

## Risk & rollout

The main risk is accepting an unrelated continuation; the single-use notification check and existing result validation remain enforced. Revert this commit to restore the previous behavior. Graph change analysis returned an invalid empty symbol identity with unrelated execution flows, so its reported blast radius was not usable evidence; the two-file diff was reviewed directly.

- [x] PR body meets repo minimum length.
- [x] No secrets, tokens, or machine-specific paths committed.
