title: fix(taint): avoid false positives for guarded Git arguments
body:
## Summary

Validated Git data arguments can now pass through local and cross-function command construction without producing a command-injection finding. The original SHA guard followed by `git log -1 --format=%s <ref>` is covered, while unsafe alternatives retain findings.

## Motivation / context

Boolean validation previously left the taint summaries unchanged, so the solver could not distinguish guarded and unguarded callers. A regex match now supplies a bounded value restriction; the sink model decides whether that restriction is sufficient for the complete command.

Related: #3490

## Areas touched

- [x] `gitnexus/` (CLI / core / MCP server)
- [ ] `gitnexus-web/` (Vite / React UI)
- [ ] `.github/` (workflows, actions)
- [ ] `eval/` or other tooling
- [ ] Docs / agent config only (`AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `.cursor/`, `llms.txt`, etc.)

## Scope & constraints

**In scope**

- Immutable same-file or inline bounded ASCII regex predicates and strict literal guards over unchanged values.
- Imported `child_process.exec` / `execSync` with reviewed fixed Git log/show data positions, the default shell and literal encoding options.
- Shared local/summary semantics, conservative joins, bounded work and memory, worker/disk replay, and truthful explain limitations.

**Explicitly out of scope / not done here**

- Imported or wrapper validators, reassignment-aware proofs, arbitrary regexes, shell parsing, other sink contracts, and other language providers.

## Implementation notes

- A use must be dominated by the accepted guard edge. Bypass paths, mutation, exceptional regions and unsupported effects retain ordinary taint.
- Restrictions follow transitive const aliases through literal composition at the sink block, including across unrelated branches. A validated operand does not neutralize another input, an executable choice, or an interpreter argument.
- Destructured and rest formal parameters cannot inherit a whole-argument proof; their extraction effects retain conservative taint.
- Proof exhaustion restores conservative findings, including sinks considered clean before a later global budget failure. Refinement shares the existing worklist and file lifetime. Global memory-budget fallback is logged.
- Declared primitive-string types are analysis assumptions. Casts alone do not establish that contract, and known incompatible values cannot regain a proof through a join or later guard.
- CFG collection reuses completed scope tables, argument bindings and native AST reads. It preserves call-frame occurrences and error-recovered references without adding a new cache framework or wire format.
- The existing `wide-merge` and `fact-fanout` fingerprints change because argument facts are now serialized. Their performance and size budgets stay intact.

## Testing & verification

- [x] Full CLI suite in four shards: 1,338 files; 28,267 passed, 88 skipped, zero failures.
- [x] Corrected final source: 20,696 unit tests passed across 900 files (47 skipped), plus 141 CFG integration tests across 13 files. Includes real-worker guard-taint, cache replay and cross-function forwarding.
- [x] Regression controls preserve repeated arguments, capture limits, nested declaration scope and malformed-literal recovery. All 177 focused CFG/refinement tests pass; the two malformed-literal regressions failed before their fix.
- [x] Exact output equivalence: 1,140 fixture CFGs and 1,651 CFGs from 2,520 malformed-input mutations match the original PR implementation, including refinement facts.
- [x] CLI build, source and test typechecks; changed-file ESLint has zero errors (warning-level diagnostics remain).
- [x] All 15 CFG benchmark scenarios pass with existing time, payload, retained-heap and correctness budgets. Persisted tool accuracy remains 32/32; the oracle is unchanged.
- [x] The <=5% guard-free collection target is met in 15 paired samples per workload: argument-heavy -1.15%, transitive aliases +3.83%, direct calls -1.56% versus the pre-feature reference. Every five-pair block also passes. Against the original PR implementation, argument forwarding is 12.55% faster and the transitive holdout is 18.38% faster. See the [measurement report, raw samples and reproduction command](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/blob/cad7a2fd6b16e681bd92577315515297967020f4/docs/optimize/guard-taint-overhead-report.md).

The full-suite snapshot was frozen before the final malformed-literal correction; the corrected source was separately rebuilt and verified by the unit, integration, differential, performance, scaling and accuracy checks above. No proof rule, fallback or budget was weakened. Serialized proof data remains unchanged from the original PR (+27% on the representative argument workload versus pre-feature); the time result is specific to the measured workloads on this shared host.

## Risk & rollout

Shared CFG and taint paths changed; the planned HIGH/CRITICAL edits received maintainer sign-off. Re-run `gitnexus analyze --pdg` after upgrading to regenerate findings under the new model. Existing content identities invalidate affected parser/summary data; public finding shapes and the database schema stay compatible.

Graph change checks map the optimization follow-up to six files, 77 symbols and three observed execution flows (MEDIUM risk). The full PR against the current main merge base maps 42 files and 399 symbols across 16 observed flows (CRITICAL, within the approved shared-taint scope). Neither result carries a partial/truncated flag. Process counts remain bounded observations; the refreshed index does not include the PDG layer.

Review fixes include the unsafe whole-argument proof transfer to destructured formals and the alias/certificate mismatch reported in [the CFG review](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/pull/3703#issuecomment-6381095193). Both have positive/negative regression controls.

## Checklist

- [x] PR body meets repo minimum length
- [x] No agent-instruction files changed
- [x] No secrets, tokens, or machine-specific paths committed

title: wiki: parent and overview pages link to guessed page slugs, so cross-page links are broken
body:
### Area

gitnexus (CLI / core / indexing / MCP server)

### Summary

`gitnexus wiki` asks the model to link to other wiki pages by their file name, but never tells it what those file names are. The model has to guess each slug, and the guesses are wrong: in our run, **92 of the 92 cross-page links** in the parent pages and the overview pointed to pages that do not exist. In the generated `index.html`, every one of them opens "Page not found".

The prompts request links of the form:

- `PARENT_USER_PROMPT`: "Link to sub-module pages (e.g. `[Sub-module Name](sub-module-slug.md)`)"
- overview prompt: "Link to module pages (e.g. `[Module Name](module-slug.md)`)"

But the context given to the model only carries each module's display name:

- `generateParentPage`: `childDocs.push(\`#### ${child.name}\n${overview}\`)`
- `generateOverview`: `moduleSummaries.push(\`#### ${node.name}\n${overview}\`)`

`node.slug` is never passed, so the model reconstructs it from the name.

### Context

We generated an 80-page wiki for a Dart monorepo, using a `module_tree.json` we supplied ourselves (a two-level tree with kebab-case slugs, like the ones `slugify` produces; the generator reuses such a file as is). The model invents slugs in several consistent ways. Examples, with names anonymized:

| Module name given to the model | Actual page | Link written by the model |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `pkg_a — launch` | `pkg-a-launch.md` | `pkg_a-launch.md` (underscore kept) |
| `pkg_a — composition/database (2/2), composition/debug, composition/file` | `pkg-a-composition-database-2-2-composition-debug-composition-file.md` | `pkg_a-composition-database-2-2-debug-file.md` (repeated segments dropped) |
| `pkg_b — use_cases (1/4)` | `pkg-b-use-cases-1-4.md` | `use_cases-1.md` (package prefix and total dropped) |
| `pkg_c` | `pkg-c.md` | `pkg_c.md` (from the overview) |

This does not depend on the model: whatever the model, it cannot know a slug it is never shown.

### Expected behavior

Links between wiki pages point to pages that exist, so they work both in `index.html` and on GitHub.

### Actual behavior

All 92 links between pages were broken. We repaired them afterwards with a script that matches each guessed link against the slugs of `module_tree.json`.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Run `gitnexus wiki` on a repository whose module tree has parent nodes (any repository large enough to get grouped modules).
2. Open `index.html`, go to a parent page or to the overview, and click a link to a sub-module: "Page not found".
3. Or compare the link targets with the files that exist:

   ```bash
   cd .gitnexus/wiki
   grep -oh '](\([^)]*\.md\))' *.md | sed 's/^](//; s/)$//' | sort -u \
     | while read -r f; do [ -f "$f" ] || echo "missing: $f"; done
   ```

### Suggested fix

Give the model the slug next to the name, for example `#### ${child.name} (page: ${child.slug}.md)` in `generateParentPage`, and the same for `moduleSummaries` in `generateOverview`. A post-generation pass that checks every `](x.md)` target against the module tree, and reports or rewrites unknown ones, would also catch the remaining mistakes.

### Environment

- gitnexus 1.6.12 (current `latest`); the same code is on `main` (`gitnexus/src/core/wiki/generator.ts`, the `childDocs.push` and `moduleSummaries.push` lines, and `prompts.ts`)
- Node 22, macOS
- Model: `claude-opus-5-5`, through the `custom` OpenAI-compatible provider

title: wiki: Mermaid sanitizer breaks valid diagrams with '...' in a label or a dot in link text
body:
### Area

gitnexus (CLI / core / indexing / MCP server)

### Summary

The wiki's Mermaid sanitizer (`sanitizeMermaidDiagram`) turns some **valid** diagrams into invalid ones. Two patterns trigger it:

1. **`...` inside a quoted node label**, for example `A["value.when(...)"]`. `sanitizeMermaidLine` splits the whole line on `EDGE_RE`, and its `\.\.+` alternative matches any run of two or more dots, including inside the label. The rest of the label is then handled as a node reference and aliased.
2. **A dot in the text of a `-- text -->` link**, for example `N -- ref.invalidate --> A`. The text is taken as a node id containing an unsafe character, and rewritten as `ref_invalidate["ref.invalidate"]`.

`sanitizeMermaidMarkdown` runs both when a page is generated and when `index.html` is built (`generateHTMLViewer`). So a diagram fixed by hand in a page breaks again at the next viewer rebuild, unless the fix avoids these patterns.

### Context

In an 80-page wiki, 3 of the 133 diagrams were broken this way. All three were valid Mermaid before sanitizing.

### Expected behavior

A diagram that is already valid comes out of the sanitizer unchanged, or at least still valid.

### Actual behavior

Minimal reproduction with the installed package:

```js
import { sanitizeMermaidDiagram } from 'gitnexus/dist/core/wiki/mermaid-sanitizer.js';
console.log(sanitizeMermaidDiagram('flowchart TD\n    A["value.when(...)"] -->|data| B["data"]'));
console.log(sanitizeMermaidDiagram('flowchart TD\n    G["x = compute(...).result"] --> H["done"]'));
console.log(sanitizeMermaidDiagram('flowchart LR\n    N -- ref.invalidate --> A'));
```

| Input | Output |
| --- | --- |
| `A["value.when(...)"] -->\|data\| B["data"]` | `A["value.when(...node[")"]"] -->\|data\| B["data"]` |
| `G["x = compute(...).result"] --> H["done"]` | `G["x = compute(...result[").result"]"] --> H["done"]` |
| `N -- ref.invalidate --> A` | `N -- ref_invalidate["ref.invalidate"] --> A` |

Checked with `mermaid.parse` from mermaid 11, the version that `index.html` loads: the three inputs are valid, and the three outputs fail with "Parse error on line 2".

### Steps to reproduce

Run the snippet above, or generate a wiki where the model writes an ellipsis in a node label (common for call sites such as `foo(...)`) or a dotted name in the text of a link.

### Suggested fix

- Mask quoted strings and bracketed labels (`"…"`, `[...]`, `(...)`, `{...}`) before splitting a line into edges, and restore them afterwards.
- Treat dots as a link only in actual Mermaid link syntax (`-.-`, `-.->`), not as any `..` run.
- Leave the text of a `-- text -->` link alone: it is a label, not a node reference.

A regression test in `test/unit/wiki-mermaid-sanitizer.test.ts` with the three inputs above would pin it.

### Environment

- gitnexus 1.6.12 (current `latest`); `EDGE_RE` is unchanged on `main` (`gitnexus/src/core/wiki/mermaid-sanitizer.ts`)
- Node 22, macOS
- mermaid 11 (loaded by the generated `index.html`)

title: Windows: api_impact, route_map, shape_check and web UI node detail crash or hang on @ladybugdb/core 0.21.1 (OPTIONAL MATCH planner bug)
body:
On Windows, `main` (`@ladybugdb/core` 0.21.1) cannot run two gitnexus queries:

- `fetchRoutesWithConsumers` in `src/mcp/local/local-backend.ts`, used by `api_impact`, `route_map` and `shape_check`
- the node-detail query in `src/server/api.ts`, used by the web UI

`conn.prepare()` either spins on one core forever or crashes the process with 0xC0000005. In the MCP server, the hang shows as `Prepare timed out after 30000ms`, but the native prepare keeps running. One core stays busy, and later queries to the same repo in that server also time out. `test/integration/api-impact-e2e.test.ts` fails 21 of 21 on Windows. Windows CI does not run it, because it is not in `scripts/cross-platform-tests.ts`.

### Cause

LadybugDB 0.21.0 and 0.21.1 have a planner bug in `planOptionalMatch`. For an `OPTIONAL MATCH` whose pattern carries a property predicate, the planner iterates from `begin()` of one temporary to `end()` of another. Depending on heap layout, planning then loops forever or reads freed memory. LadybugDB fixed it in 0.21.2:
https://github.com/LadybugDB/ladybug/commit/37bf0dc8355cb4d0cf07265b60cc1523e910d4e6
The commit says the bug came from 58c10a424, which is in v0.21.0 and not in v0.20.4. Released gitnexus is not affected, because 1.6.12 ships 0.18.3.

### Repro with published packages only (Windows 11 x64, Node 24.19.0)

1. Create a git repo with two files: `server.ts` registers an Express route with `app.get('/api/users', listUsers)`, and `client.ts` calls `fetch('/api/users')`.
2. In an empty folder, install the package with `npm i gitnexus@1.6.13-rc.150`. Then run `gitnexus analyze --index-only <repo>`.
3. Run `gitnexus cypher "<query>" --repo <repo>` for each query below.

| Query | 1.6.12 (0.18.3) | 1.6.13-rc.150 (0.21.1) | rc.150 with `overrides: {"@ladybugdb/core": "0.21.2"}` |
|---|---|---|---|
| Route query (text of `fetchRoutesWithConsumers`) | 0.68 s | process exits 0xC0000005 | 0.69 s, returns the route and its consumer |
| Node-detail query from `server/api.ts` (literal id in place of `$nid`) | 0.70 s | process exits 0xC0000005 | 0.67 s |
| Control: `MATCH (consumer)-[r:CodeRelation]->(n:Route) WHERE r.type = 'FETCHES'` | 0.84 s | 0.65 s | 0.66 s |

To rule out gitnexus code, I created rc.150's `NODE_SCHEMA_QUERIES` and `REL_SCHEMA_QUERIES` (628 rel pairs) in a fresh database and inserted 3 nodes and 2 edges. Then I reopened it read-only with `createLbugDatabase` and timed `conn.prepare()` for 8 query shapes. On 0.21.1, the `OPTIONAL MATCH` shapes with a property predicate hung for more than 30 s or crashed, and the plain `MATCH` shapes prepared in about 0.1 s. On 0.18.3, 0.21.2 and 0.22.0-dev.20261020, all 8 shapes prepared in about 0.1 s.

### Relation to #3578

#3578 bumps the pin to 0.21.2, which would fix this too. It is blocked by the Windows FTS crash in LadybugDB/ladybug#1249, and I reproduced that crash here. With 0.21.2, `bench/incremental-write-integrity/reproduce-search.cjs property` crashes at `CREATE_FTS_INDEX` in 3 of 3 runs; with 0.21.1 it passes 3 of 3.

Until a matching FTS build exists, gitnexus could keep property predicates out of `OPTIONAL MATCH` in these two queries. For example, read the routes with one query and the FETCHES edges with a plain `MATCH`, then join them in code; that shape prepares fine on 0.21.1. Adding `api-impact-e2e.test.ts` to the Windows cross-platform list would catch a regression.

title: fix(wiki): keep valid Mermaid labels and link text through the sanitizer
body:
## Summary

Wiki diagrams retain their labels, node identity, and links when GitNexus sanitizes generated Markdown or rebuilds the viewer. The regression suite uses Mermaid's official tiny parser bundle without adding Mermaid to the CLI runtime.

Fixes #3705.

## Motivation / context

Valid labels such as `value.when(...)` and links such as `-- ref.invalidate -->` could be mistaken for node references. Rebuilding the viewer applied the same corruption again. Aliasing also needs to preserve references across the whole diagram without merging distinct nodes or replacing explicit labels.

## Areas touched

- [x] `gitnexus/` (CLI / core / MCP server)
- [ ] `gitnexus-web/` (Vite / React UI)
- [ ] `.github/` (workflows, actions)
- [ ] `eval/` or other tooling
- [ ] Docs / agent config only

## Scope & constraints

**In scope**

- Preserve quoted and multiline labels, node shapes, link text, classes, style references, frontmatter, and initialization directives in flowcharts.
- Repair unsafe identifiers consistently across standalone nodes, chained links, fan-out, and repeated references; reserve existing identifiers before allocating aliases.
- Validate parsed nodes, links, labels, shapes, and idempotence using `@mermaid-js/tiny`.

**Explicitly out of scope / not done here**

- Parsing or rewriting other diagram types; they pass through unchanged.
- Changing the web application's Mermaid renderer or the generated viewer's CDN.

## Implementation notes

Labels are protected before splitting diagram lines and links. A first pass collects existing identifiers and explicit labels; a second pass applies aliases consistently. Literal quotes in repaired labels use Mermaid entities.

`@mermaid-js/tiny` is pinned to 11.17.2 and loaded only by tests. Its unpacked package is about 2.6 MB, versus 84 MB for full Mermaid. `jsdom` 26.1.0 keeps these tests compatible with GitNexus's supported Node versions. Neither dependency is loaded by the CLI at runtime.

## Testing & verification

- [x] `cd gitnexus && npx vitest run test/unit/wiki-*.test.ts` — 234 tests passed.
- [x] Sanitizer and parser suites on Node 22.18.0 — 73 tests passed.
- [x] `cd gitnexus && npx tsc --noEmit && npm run typecheck:tests`
- [x] `cd gitnexus && npm run build`
- [x] Scoped ESLint, Prettier, and `git diff --check`.
- [x] Generated a wiki HTML viewer from sanitized Markdown, extracted its embedded page, and parsed the diagram again; node identity and both links survived the second sanitization.
- [x] A 10,000-link input remained idempotent and sanitized in about 117 ms locally.
- [ ] `cd gitnexus && npm test -- --maxWorkers=2` — stopped after repeated indexing-worker readiness failures; no clean full-suite result. The broader unit run encountered the same failure; a separate default-project run also failed an analyzer-runner setup test and did not complete. CI remains required.

## Risk & rollout

The behavior change is confined to wiki flowcharts. No migration or index refresh is required for users; rebuilding a wiki applies the fix. Parser assertions cover graph structure as well as successful parsing, since a diagram can parse while silently losing or duplicating nodes.

## Checklist

- [x] PR body meets repository requirements.
- [x] No secrets, tokens, or machine-specific paths committed.

title: fix(cli): write the AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md block in the file's own line ending
body:
## Summary

`gitnexus analyze` preserves the line endings in existing AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md files. It also repairs files left with mixed endings by earlier versions, then leaves them untouched on repeated runs. Fixes #3688.

## Motivation / context

On a checkout with `core.autocrlf=true` and `* text=auto`, the old writer inserted an LF block into CRLF prose. Git reported a modified file with `w/mixed` even when the normalized diff was empty. The count-only guard from #2907 also failed because the existing and generated blocks used different endings.

## Areas touched

- [x] `gitnexus/` (CLI / core / MCP server)
- [ ] `gitnexus-web/` (Vite / React UI)
- [ ] `.github/` (workflows, actions)
- [ ] `eval/` or other tooling
- [ ] Docs / agent config only (`AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `.cursor/`, `llms.txt`, etc.)

## Scope & constraints

**In scope**

- Preserve the first line break's ending when replacing or appending the managed section, including custom `gitnexus:keep` blocks.
- Repair mixed endings once without changing preserved text or committed counts. Report `updated` for a repair and `preserved` for a subsequent no-write run.
- Cover ordinary and `--no-stats` runs, custom blocks with and without a recognized stats line, and both context filenames.

**Explicitly out of scope / not done here**

- New files still use LF because there is no existing ending to follow.
- Skill-file generation and `refreshBaseRefLine` are unchanged.

## Implementation notes

Comparisons use LF-normalized content. Writes restore the detected ending. Before returning from a preservation path, the writer checks the original bytes for mixed endings; this repairs older files without regenerating custom blocks or refreshing volatile counts.

## Testing & verification

- [x] `cd gitnexus && npm test -- test/unit/ai-context.test.ts test/unit/ai-context-unknown-risk-policy.test.ts test/unit/ai-context-read-path-must.test.ts test/unit/analyze-no-stats-bridge.test.ts test/unit/analyze-gitnexusrc.test.ts test/unit/shipped-skills-sync.test.ts test/unit/analyze-self-commit-bridge.test.ts` — 196 passed across 7 files, including all 83 context tests.
- [x] `cd gitnexus && npm run build` and `npx tsc --noEmit`.
- [x] ESLint and Prettier on both changed files; zero lint errors, one existing non-null assertion warning outside the diff. `git diff --check` passes.
- [x] Real Git smoke test with `core.autocrlf=true` and `* text=auto`: both files change from `w/mixed` to `w/crlf`, staging has no content delta, and a repeated `--no-stats` run leaves tracked files clean.
- [x] Fixed old modification times prove repeat runs do not rewrite identical bytes; assertions also verify CLI status and exact custom text.
- [ ] Full local integration suite — not rerun for this context-writer change; full platform checks run in CI.

## Risk & rollout

Existing mixed files are normalized to the ending of their first line break. No dependency, schema, or index-format change is required.

## Checklist

- [x] PR body meets repo minimum length.
- [x] No secrets, tokens, or machine-specific paths committed.
- [x] Agent instruction files themselves are unchanged.

title: chore(deps): consolidate updates and vendor compatible VECTOR
body:
## Summary

Consolidates the three Dependabot updates from #3698, #3701, and #3702, and fixes the native VECTOR loading failure that blocked their combined CI run.

The lockfile installs `ip-address` 10.7.4, `zod` 4.6.7, `js-yaml` 5.5.0, and its `argparse` 3.0.3 dependency. VECTOR now loads a packaged binary built for the existing LadybugDB core pin before trying the home cache or a network install.

## Motivation / context

Ubuntu's strict VECTOR tests failed because the CDN download referenced a native symbol unavailable in `@ladybugdb/core` 0.21.1. Retrying reproduced the same failure. The official [LadybugDB v0.21.1 build](https://github.com/LadybugDB/ladybug/actions/runs/36647903773) retains matching artifacts for all five supported platforms; its Linux binary loads successfully with the pinned core.

## Areas touched

- [x] `gitnexus/` (CLI / core / MCP server)
- [ ] `gitnexus-web/` (Vite / React UI)
- [ ] `.github/` (workflows, actions)
- [ ] `eval/` or other tooling
- [ ] Docs / agent config only

## Scope & constraints

**In scope**

- The four lockfile records from the three Dependabot PRs, including their exact integrity hashes.
- Unmodified official VECTOR binaries for Linux x64/arm64, macOS x64/arm64, and Windows x64, with archive and binary checksums, source commits, and the upstream license.
- Packaged VECTOR loading through the existing extension manager, matching doctor diagnostics, and regression coverage.

**Explicitly out of scope / not done here**

- Core upgrades, FTS binary changes, CI-policy changes, and unrelated dependency updates.

## Implementation notes

The `@ladybugdb/core` pin stays at 0.21.1. Each artifact comes from upstream tag `v0.21.1`; its downloaded archive was verified against GitHub's SHA-256 digest before extracting the binary. `vendor/lbug-vector/manifest.json` records provenance and extracted-binary checksums.

The loader tries the packaged VECTOR binary first for both lowercase and uppercase extension names. Existing `never`, `load-only`, and bounded-install behavior remain intact. Missing or unloadable packaged artifacts retain the named-load fallback. Paths reuse the existing realpath containment check. Doctor probes the same packaged binary used by indexing and search.

## Testing & verification

- [x] Dependency consolidation baseline: clean `npm ci`, build, `npm ls --all`, source/test typechecks, and formatting.
- [x] Baseline full local suite: 28,193 passed, 88 skipped, seven environment-related failures. All seven passed unchanged after supplying the required local C++ runtime or moving auto-sync fixtures outside `/tmp`. This run preceded the native-loading repair.
- [x] New loader and doctor regressions fail before their fixes and pass afterward.
- [x] Native repair: 129 tests across nine selected loader, doctor, vector, pool, incremental-writeback, and FTS CLI suites passed via `npm test`.
- [x] Strict VECTOR availability: all 30 tests in incremental VECTOR ordering, vector-index integration, and pooled-query suites passed.
- [x] Pooled FTS loader tests and artifact checksum/core-pin checks passed.
- [x] Build, source/test typechecks, ESLint, Prettier, and `git diff --check` passed after the repair.
- [x] Packed npm archive contains all five verified binaries, provenance manifest, README, and upstream license.
- [x] All 12 required GitHub checks pass on the final commit; the [full CI workflow](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/actions/runs/40095079633) completed successfully.

## Risk & rollout

The shared extension manager serves indexing, embeddings, and search, so its graph impact is critical despite the small loader change. The repair uses the existing path-loading and policy behavior, with explicit regressions and real native tests. Cross-platform CI must validate the packaged binaries before merge. No migrations or configuration changes are required.

## Checklist

- [x] PR body meets repository minimum length.
- [x] No secrets, tokens, or machine-specific paths committed.

title: fix(wiki): pass real page slugs into parent and overview prompts
body:
When generating wiki parent module pages and overview summaries, prompts instruct the LLM to link to pages as `[Name](slug.md)`, but only module display names were provided in the prompt context. As a result, the model was forced to guess page slugs, producing broken cross-page links.

Pass each child module and top-level module's real `.md` file name (`${child.slug}.md` and `${node.slug}.md`) into `CHILDREN_DOCS` and `MODULE_SUMMARIES` contexts, and instruct the prompts to link using the exact file names given.

Added unit tests in `gitnexus/test/unit/wiki-generator-slugs.test.ts` driving `generateParentPage` and `generateOverview` with a mocked LLM and asserting the real slugs are present in prompt context.

Fixes #3704

title: perf: benchmark scope resolution and remove redundant allocation
body:
## Summary

Scope-resolution cost is now measured in required CI for all 18 supported languages, and two measured allocation bottlenecks are removed. Java import chains retain transitive factory resolution while avoiding repeated copies of dependency tables; four other language workloads that exhausted V8 heap now complete.

## Motivation / context

The Java hook copied return types from maps that earlier iterations had already expanded. Separately, shared import finalization built transitive re-export tables even when no lookup used them.

Related: #3695

## Areas touched

- [x] `gitnexus/` (CLI / core / MCP server)
- [ ] `gitnexus-web/` (Vite / React UI)
- [x] `.github/` (workflows, actions)
- [x] `eval/` or other tooling
- [ ] Docs / agent config only (`AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `.cursor/`, `llms.txt`, etc.)

## Scope & constraints

**In scope**

- Real worker parsing and production scope resolution at 100 and 1,000 entities, with 20 generated members or procedures per entity plus callers/helpers, and three fresh-process samples.
- CI reports phase times, endpoint heap, peak process RSS, binding counts, and graph fingerprints. Missing languages, graph changes, nondeterministic counts, or counts above measured baselines fail the required gate.
- Optimize redundant allocation without adding production heap, file-count, or propagation-depth limits.

**Explicitly out of scope / not done here**

- The reporter's private 17,095-file repository was unavailable; these synthetic results do not establish that its entire OOM problem is resolved.
- Go and PHP still show roughly 10 million module bindings at 1,000 entities. Their measured costs, package-sibling growth, source retention, and sharded indexing remain separate work.

## Implementation notes

Java keeps producer return facts once and searches imports only for missing names that a file uses. Ancestor returns and subclass overrides remain available; cycles terminate, and conflicting return types are rejected by class identity. Shared re-export tables are built on first use. Runtime and heap measurements have no machine-dependent pass/fail threshold; binding budgets come from the recorded measurements.

## Testing & verification

Same-host medians of three fresh processes. Java compares the original provider with the final provider while holding the shared finalization change fixed. Its stronger fixture includes transitive factories and repeated unreachable-name lookups.

| Workload / metric | Before | After |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Java, 1,001 files: resolution time | 21.12 s | 1.29 s |
| Java, 1,001 files: module type bindings | 10,510,001 | 42,977 |
| Java, 1,001 files: heap after resolution | 933.6 MiB | 284.0 MiB |
| C, C++, Dart, Ruby: 1,000-entity workloads | V8 heap OOM | All complete |

Heap values are endpoint samples, not retained or peak heap. All 36 final workloads completed across 108 samples; all 32 comparable before/after graph fingerprints match. Restoring the old Java provider fails the new binding checks at both sizes despite identical graph fingerprints.

- [x] 21 focused tests cover storage growth, traversal order, 12-file factories, cycles, inherited returns, overrides, and conflicting versus shared class identities. Worker regressions are registered for Windows/macOS CI as well as Ubuntu.
- [x] Build, core/benchmark/test typechecks, changed-code ESLint, Prettier, and workflow actionlint.
- [x] Full `npm test -- --maxWorkers=4` completed: 28,296 passed, 88 skipped, six environment-dependent failures. All four affected files then passed unchanged (71 tests): the packaged native module needed a compatible local `libstdc++`, and setup tests needed the host `CODEX_HOME` override removed. No test assertions or repository code were changed for those reruns.
- [x] Existing re-export performance gate and scope-resolution regression suite passed after the shared change.
- [x] 191 workflow tests passed, including all 125 combinations of the three required dependency results. The broader Python suite passed 1,262 tests with 24 skipped; its two oracle-toolchain failures passed unchanged using the pinned task dependencies required by CI.

Reproduce from `gitnexus/` after `npm run build`:

```sh
node --import tsx bench/scope-resolution/measure.mts --check --output /tmp/scope-resolution.json
```

## Risk & rollout

Graph impact is HIGH because shared finalization and the Java hook feed central indexing and semantic rename. Re-index to apply the corrected resolution behavior; no storage migration is required. Reverting the optimization commits restores the old behavior.

## Checklist

- [x] PR body meets repo minimum length
- [ ] If `AGENTS.md` / overlays changed: headers, scope block, and changelog updated (not applicable)
- [x] No secrets, tokens, or machine-specific paths committed

Release notes

Sourced from fast-uri's releases.

v3.1.9

Security

This security release fixes four URI parsing and normalization vulnerabilities in fast-uri 3.x. Applications that process untrusted URI input should upgrade to v3.1.9.

  • Medium — URI scheme spoofing through percent-encoded schemes (GHSA-w74x-v6f9-j3xg, CVE-2026-110306): percent-encoded scheme input is now rejected instead of being decoded into a live scheme.
  • Medium — Host confusion during domain-host canonicalization (GHSA-wjr9-j795-jxcr, CVE-2026-110180): malformed domain hosts containing ambiguous delimiters or stripped control characters are now rejected instead of being silently rewritten.
  • Low — Incorrect relative-reference normalization (GHSA-xhq7-xmqj-769h, CVE-2026-110095): dot-segment removal now preserves the resolution semantics of relative references.
  • Low — Scheme injection in suffix references (GHSA-333x-w4r6-6crp, CVE-2026-110725): first-segment colons in path-only suffix references are now escaped so the output is not reparsed as a scheme.

Upgrade with:

npm install fast-uri@3.1.9

title: fix(eval): keep candidate code out of agent comparisons
body:
## Summary

Release agent evaluations can now use MCP without reading the candidate implementation. The agent receives only a per-cell stdio socket; candidate code runs in a separately contained, read-only server.

## Motivation / context

The previous MCP arm could read compiled code containing fixes newer than the task checkout. That confounds a comparison intended to measure tool assistance. This correction prepares a trustworthy paired study after the recent tool fixes; the protected paid workflow must run the corrected harness from main after merge.

Related: #3500
Related: #3609

## Areas touched

- [ ] `gitnexus/` (CLI / core / MCP server)
- [ ] `gitnexus-web/` (Vite / React UI)
- [ ] `.github/` (workflows, actions)
- [x] `eval/` or other tooling
- [ ] Docs / agent config only (`AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `.cursor/`, `llms.txt`, etc.)

## Scope & constraints

**In scope**

- Isolated runtime access for the release baseline, including reconnects, per-cell ownership, and fail-closed cleanup.
- Host-generated exposure receipts required by release and PR evidence validation.
- Reproducible historical results with all 48 sanitized cells retained in [the dated report](eval/workflow_bench/measurement-2026-10-24.md).

**Explicitly out of scope / not done here**

- The fresh paid comparison: the protected workflow executes main's trusted harness even for PR previews. Keep the measurement issue open until the post-merge study is published.
- General product-benefit claims or a broader task corpus.

## Implementation notes

The transport reuses the existing process supervisor and Bubblewrap policy, passing a socket directly to server stdin/stdout without interpreting MCP messages. The server cannot access model credentials, networking, or writable agent state. A transport failure invalidates its cell.

No-MCP receives no endpoint. Workflow arms that intentionally expose the CLI retain an explicit `readable` receipt; historical artifacts remain readable but cannot satisfy the new isolated release gate.

## Testing & verification

- [x] Focused evaluation tests: **394 passed, 20 skipped**. Command: `cd eval && uv run --locked --extra dev pytest tests/test_proposer_sandbox.py tests/test_workflow_bench_sessions.py tests/test_release_report.py tests/test_release_gate.py tests/test_release_evidence.py tests/test_pr_evaluation.py`.
- [x] Full evaluation suite exercised: **1170 passed, 2 failed, 25 skipped** initially. Both oracle-control failures came from current dependencies applied to historical source; the pinned task dependency install passed those controls with the focused set (**419 passed, 19 skipped**).
- [x] Ruff on all changed Python paths; `cd gitnexus && npx tsc --noEmit`.
- [x] Tool-accuracy corpus **32/32**, no allowances; tool-score unit suite **18 passed**. Native checks used a compatible C++ runtime after the first parser load failed with `GLIBCXX_3.4.31`.
- [ ] `cd gitnexus && npm test`: supplemental run completed with **28,281 passed, 5 failed, 88 skipped**. The five failures are in unchanged Codex setup integration/environment cases. The preceding hosted run passed **28,375/28,375 core tests** and **516/516 web tests**; current-head CI is rerunning.
- [x] Native containment canaries: [Ubuntu containment passed on `d63b8e4c1`](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/actions/runs/40128102903/job/120973766627); Windows containment also passed. Tests cover runtime invisibility (including `/proc`), credentials, network/workspace restrictions, concurrent connections, cancellation, and server failure. Local Bubblewrap capability skips were not counted as proof.

- [x] Socket-readiness regression: both old tests reproduced `ConnectionRefusedError` with forced bind/listen ordering. Revised tests passed **100/100** stress checks; the exact Ubuntu CI selection passed **245 tests, 26 local capability skips**. Full inline `ce-code-review` ran before PR creation; a scoped follow-up review found no remaining issues in the test fix.

## Risk & rollout

This changes an evaluation trust boundary. Require native containment CI before merge. No new dependencies, workflow changes, or production index migration.

The [historical run](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/actions/runs/40015796596) solved 12/12 tasks in each candidate arm, with MCP cost **+21.6%** and agent time **−5.1%**. Runtime exposure and the small task set prevent an isolated or general benefit claim. The dated report records exact pins, exclusions, stable results, and the post-merge dispatch procedure.

## Checklist

- [x] PR body meets repo minimum length.
- [x] No `AGENTS.md` / overlay changes.
- [x] No secrets, tokens, or machine-specific paths committed.

title: [Bug] Runner selects unusable pnpm shim instead of working bunx with NVM for Windows
body:
### Area

gitnexus (CLI / core / indexing / MCP server)

### Summary

GitNexus selects a pnpm shim that cannot run under the active NVM for Windows Node.js version, preventing index refresh despite an available bunx fallback.

### Context

Bug report written by Sol 6.1 medium. My agents kept tripping up because pnpm isn't really installed.

NVM for Windows. AI agents refresh my repository’s index through the generated runner:
node .gitnexus/run.cjs analyze --index-only
The active environment has Node.js 26.10.0, npm 12.2.0, and working Bun/bunx 1.3.14. There is no global gitnexus command.
pnpm.exe is discoverable through NVM’s .nodejs directory, but pnpm is not installed for the active Node version. Agents repeatedly encounter this launcher failure and must find another invocation.
Relevant source: [resolve-analyze-cmd.cjs](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/blob/main/gitnexus/hooks/claude/resolve-analyze-cmd.cjs).

### Expected behavior

The runner should check whether pnpm can execute successfully before selecting it. When its version probe fails, it should continue to the working bunx fallback.
A successful probe with unparseable version output should remain distinguishable from a failed command.

### Actual behavior

The resolver treats the pnpm shim’s presence on PATH as sufficient availability and selects pnpm before checking bunx.
Running pnpm --version produces:
pnpm is not installed for this Node.js version.

Run:  corepack enable
      corepack prepare pnpm@stable --activate
error: CommandNotFound
Meanwhile, bunx --version succeeds and returns 1.3.14.
In the resolver source, direct runner selection relies on pnpm’s PATH presence. Command generation also falls back to PATH presence when the pnpm version probe fails, discarding the helper’s separate execution-success signal.

### Steps to reproduce

Use NVM for Windows with an active Node version that has npm 11 or newer.

Have an NVM-managed pnpm.exe shim on PATH, but no usable pnpm installation for that active Node version.

Confirm pnpm --version reports that pnpm is not installed for this Node version.

Install Bun and confirm bunx --version succeeds.

Ensure no global gitnexus command is available.

In a repository containing GitNexus’s generated runner, run:
node .gitnexus/run.cjs analyze --index-only

Observe that the runner selects the failing pnpm launcher instead of reaching bunx.

### Environment

Windows 11, latest NVM with latest NPM

### Logs / screenshots

Updates `filelock` from 3.25.2 to 4.2.1
Release notes

Sourced from filelock's releases.

4.2.1

  • On a singleton wrapper, close> and close> end only the holds that tasks acquired through that wrapper. A reader that arrives during close() gets the closed error instead of joining the ending hold. After synchronous code closes or force-releases the shared lock, the wrappers refuse to admit readers into the ended hold, and close() on such a wrapper returns. Closing one wrapper no longer ends a task's nested hold taken through another wrapper on the same path. #832
  • ReadWriteLock locks again after a release() that an exception from a signal handler interrupted. The async read-write wrappers stop admitting readers into such a level. The async read-write locks forget a hold whose backend release failed after the backend let go, and they free the memory of each acquire that times out or is canceled. AsyncFileLock returns from release() after a few hundred acquires gave up behind a waiting one. An exception from a signal handler delivered while an AsyncFileLock call joins its queue no longer blocks every later call on that lock. #833
  • Fix ReadWriteLock acting on -journal, -wal or -shm files another process puts beside its database: a write could land in another file, a reader could get in beside a writer, and an acquire could fail. SQLite now opens the database by name only in a directory no other account can write, and through a private hard link elsewhere. On Windows the directory's access control list decides. Where hard links are unavailable, keep the database in a directory other accounts cannot write, such as one under %LOCALAPPDATA%. The lock removes link directories through a checked descriptor rather than by name, reads a link directory's name only when the locking account owns it, and leaves alone a directory with other content renamed onto a link directory's name. A database whose schema takes more than a few kilobytes to load raises ValueError instead of running past the acquire timeout. #834
  • Fix five bugs in opening the lock file. UnixFileLock no longer truncates a file it did not create, such as one renamed to the lock path, and no longer applies mode to it. An on_acquired hook that writes holder metadata now truncates the file itself. A lease (Linux) or an oplock (Windows) on the lock file or a soft lock's marker no longer holds acquire() past its timeout or blocking=False, and an oplock no longer holds release(); ReadWriteLock on Windows waits for its timeout and raises Timeout. On Windows, a mode without group and other bits, such as 0o600, now creates the lock file with an owner-only permission list; the ReadWriteLock database gets the same. The soft locks' writability check no longer follows a symlink swapped in at the lock path. On a filesystem without flock, a contender from another account now waits on a marker it cannot write instead of raising PermissionError. #835
  • Fix SoftFileLock, MarkerSoftFileLock and SoftFileLease removing a live holder's marker in three cases: the holder and the contender run in Linux time namespaces with different boottime offsets; only one of them can read the boot id; a process other than the owner rewrote the marker. Soft markers no longer carry group or other write bits. A process name containing a carriage return or another line separator no longer makes the stale check raise ValueError. When /proc/self/ns/time exists but cannot be read, the stale check no longer compares start times and keeps the marker. #836
  • The async read-write locks record their hold under a task owner, so synchronous code on the executor thread that took the hold can no longer re-enter or release it. AsyncSoftReadWriteLock gives back one level on release, so synchronous readers of a shared singleton keep theirs. SoftReadWriteLock tracks read levels per thread: release() from a thread that holds none raises RuntimeError. After its heartbeat recorded a lost hold, it refuses new acquires until that hold is released. #838
  • StrictSoftFileLock creates <path>.filelock and its claims directory with the lock's mode and sets the sticky bit (a directory flag that lets only a file's owner remove it) on both. On the next acquisition it narrows a directory it owns that an earlier release created wider; it leaves a directory of another account as it is, so remove such leftovers by hand. It reaches claims through a descriptor opened without following symlinks; on Windows it holds both directories open and refuses a junction (a directory that points at another directory). Under a sticky parent such as /tmp it refuses a coordination directory of another account, as SoftReadWriteLock does for <path>.rw. One read grace now covers a whole claim scan, a failed claim cleanup no longer leaves the sentinel descriptor open, and a non-regular node at a sentinel private-record name raises SoftFileLockProtocolError. On Windows, contenders read claims without blocking their owner's unlink. #839

title: fix(ci): rebalance native tests and stabilize flaky gates
body:
## Summary

Keep native-test shards within their watchdog budget and reduce false CI failures from noisy measurements and failed artifact uploads. Performance limits and result fingerprints remain enforced, and missing execution evidence still fails the required checks.

## Motivation / context

Reviewed 40 main-branch Publish runs from October 20–25. The sample contained 20 successes, eight failures, ten cancellations and two active runs when collected. Several failed check names were downstream consequences of one failed benchmark or upload.

- [October 25 benchmark failure](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/actions/runs/40164065672/job/121091926631): callable-value-flow reported 1.973× widening overhead against 1.9×, with the expected fingerprint. The unchanged benchmark failed six of eight local repetitions under load.
- [October 25 macOS upload failure](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/actions/runs/40164065672/job/121091939321): 343 tests passed, then artifact creation failed with `ENOTFOUND`.
- [October 22 CJK timing failure](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/actions/runs/39872621700/job/120155888462): one 48.8ms measurement exceeded the 33.3ms limit in a coverage shard.
- [October 23 Windows watchdog failure](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/actions/runs/39934695864/job/120351841090): shard 10 spent 385s on Objective-C, 266s on C#, and 145s on incremental method integrity before reaching the watchdog with Kotlin still pending. Scheduling charged those suites 285s, 200s and zero measured seconds respectively.

The historical macOS stall after most tests completed remains unproven, and main's serialized Publish queue is unchanged. The older incompatible VECTOR extension failures were addressed by #3709.

## Areas touched

- [x] `gitnexus/` (benchmark harness, test sharding and tests)
- [ ] `gitnexus-web/`
- [x] `.github/` (workflows, actions)
- [x] `eval/` or other tooling
- [ ] Docs / agent config only

## Scope & constraints

**In scope**

- Recover transient test-artifact upload failures within three attempts; exhausted retries and missing files remain failures.
- Stabilize the two reproduced timing checks while preserving their input sizes and thresholds.
- Refresh six measured native-suite weights and spread the workload over eleven shards per platform.

**Explicitly out of scope / not done here**

- Production indexing changes, larger timeouts, release concurrency changes, or rerunning failed tests until green.

## Implementation notes

Callable-value-flow now interleaves all four workloads, discards complete warmup rounds, and compares paired window minima. The guard takes about 36 seconds longer. CJK timing runs through the existing serial benchmark discovery and execution audit, while its functional tests still run normally.

Corrected Windows timings exceed the existing 17-minute headroom rule with ten shards. Eleven shards preserve that rule and the 20-minute watchdog, at the cost of one additional Windows job and one macOS job. The Ubuntu shard count and required compatibility check names stay the same.

Upload retries replace a possibly incomplete artifact. A workflow contract rejects duplicate name templates and missing matrix dimensions to prevent one job replacing another job's evidence. The first upload remains eligible after cancellation; retries stop on cancellation.

## Testing & verification

- [x] Scoped `npm test`: CI, CJK and partition checks pass; the timing test is intentionally skipped outside benchmark mode. The final scheduling revision passes all 27 partition/completeness tests.
- [x] `GITNEXUS_BENCH=1` CJK run with execution reporter: 32 passed, no skips.
- [x] `uv run --frozen pytest tests/test_workflow_bench.py -q`: 192 passed.
- [x] `npx tsc --noEmit` and test-config typecheck.
- [x] ESLint: zero errors; existing warnings remain. Actionlint, Prettier and `git diff --check` passed.
- [x] Graph change analysis: complete, untruncated results; no affected production execution flows.
- [x] Independent review; artifact collision and cancellation findings addressed.
- [x] [Hosted CI attempt 2](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/actions/runs/40176744194): 61 successful jobs, one intentional E2E skip; execution audit reports 30,289 passing cases. The Windows write-integrity shard required one diagnostic retry; the original timeout is not claimed fixed.
- [x] Full local write-integrity file: all nine cases passed in 188 seconds.
- [ ] Full local `npm test -- --maxWorkers=2`: interrupted after 15 minutes without a completed file in the native-test phase. Full hosted CI remains required.

| Benchmark check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Revised sampling under load | Four probe runs and the final implementation passed with unchanged 1.6× / 1.9× limits |
| Slower name-match implementation | Rejected at 2.446× overhead; fingerprint unchanged |
| Deliberate scaling / overhead slowdowns | Both rejected |
| Changed result fingerprint | Rejected |
| Duplicate artifact name / omitted matrix axis | Both rejected by workflow contract |
| Conservative native workload replay | Old configuration fails at 1,394s; corrected weights plus eleven shards stay at or below 944s against the existing 1,020s headroom limit |

## Risk & rollout

No production behavior or index migration changes. Hosted CI must validate the composite action on Linux, Windows and macOS. Permanent artifact-service failures still fail CI after bounded retries. Reverting this PR restores the previous test harness and uploads.

## Checklist

- [x] PR body meets repo minimum length.
- [x] No agent instruction changes requiring header or changelog updates.
- [x] No secrets, tokens, or machine-specific paths committed.

title: feat(api_impact): list the callers of the requesting function as indirect consumers
body:
## Summary

`api_impact` reports the callers of the function that sends the request, one level up, as `indirectConsumers`, apart from the direct consumers and outside the risk level.

## Motivation / context

Closes #3644, the follow-up left from #3488. A `FETCHES` edge goes from the requesting file to the Route, so `api_impact` listed `backend-client.ts` and stopped there. `App.tsx`, `DropZone.tsx` and `Header.tsx` call `fetchRepos` from that file without ever mentioning the URL, so no edge of their own could reach the route; in the #3488 ground truth they are 6 of the 9 consumer files. Nothing followed the `CALLS` edges into the function that holds the request.

## Areas touched

- [x] `gitnexus/` (CLI / core / MCP server)
- [ ] `gitnexus-web/` (Vite / React UI)
- [ ] `.github/` (workflows, actions)
- [ ] `eval/` or other tooling
- [x] Docs / agent config only (`AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `.cursor/`, `llms.txt`, etc.) — `ARCHITECTURE.md` paragraph, `api_impact` tool description

## Scope & constraints

**In scope**

- Ingestion: the `FETCHES` reason names the callables whose spans contain the request sites, one `|via:<id>` field each (`fetch-url-match|keys:…|fetches:n|via:Function:src/client.ts:fetchRepos`). The containment rule is the one the R3-6 sink set already applies (innermost span wins, 0-based lines); it moves into `EnclosingCallableIndex` and `buildSinkFunctionSet` uses the same index, so the two attributions cannot drift apart. A site outside any callable adds no field, so a reason without attribution reads exactly as before. An id that contains `|` (a type tag can carry a union type) is left out rather than split.
- Several sites of one file for one route used to collide on the edge id, with the first one winning; they now share the edge and each contributes its callable. Edge order, confidence and the `keys:`/`fetches:` fields are unchanged.
- `api_impact`: one `CALLS` query for all the `via` ids of the report, then per route the callers whose file is neither a direct consumer file nor the handler file, as `indirectConsumers: [{ name, file, via }]` (sorted by file, name, via) and `impactSummary.indirectConsumers` (distinct files). `riskLevel` still counts direct consumers only, as the lower bound does. Both fields are absent when no consumer edge names a requesting function, so an index built before this change reads as today instead of claiming an empty result; they are also absent if the callers query fails (logged as degraded).
- Expo navigation sites carry their real line instead of `0`, so they attribute to the component that contains them rather than to whatever spans line 0 (this also corrects their R3-6 sink attribution).

**Explicitly out of scope / not done here**

- Deeper than one level, and counting indirect consumers in `riskLevel`: the issue asks for one level, reported separately.
- `route_map` and `shape_check` share the consumer query and ignore the new field; their output is unchanged.
- Template (`.html`, `.ejs`, …) sites keep `lineNumber: 0`; those files have no callable spans, so nothing is attributed.

## Implementation notes

Attribution uses the AST, not the line: the parser records the enclosing callable of every fetch site (`ExtractedFetchCall.enclosingId`, from the same `findEnclosingFunctionId` that gives call sites their `sourceId`) and, for wrapper calls, resolves it from the call's tree position carried on `FetchWrapperCall`. A helper defined on the line of the request (`const decode = (res) => res.json(); return fetch('/api/repos').then(decode);`) has the smaller span, so a line-only lookup named the helper and the callers of the requesting function disappeared from the report (review, magyargergo). The span lookup remains for sites found by text scan and for an id the graph does not hold, and the R3-6 sink set follows the same preference.


The reason field was chosen over a new relation column or a function-level `FETCHES` edge: it is the precedent for per-edge consumer facts (`keys:`, `fetches:`), needs no schema or DDL change, and a function-level edge would double-count the file in every label-agnostic consumer query. `indirectConsumersOf` is a pure function over the route's consumers and the callers map, so the exclusion rules are unit-testable without a database.

## Testing & verification

- [x] `cd gitnexus && npx vitest run test/integration/api-impact-indirect-consumers-e2e.test.ts` — a real `runFullAnalysis` of the fixture, then `api_impact` through `LocalBackend`: callers listed for the plain request, for a request sharing its line with a helper, and for a request made through a wrapper function.
- [x] `cd gitnexus && npx vitest run test/unit/fetch-consumer-attribution.test.ts test/unit/fetch-reason-parsing.test.ts test/unit/process-processor.test.ts test/unit/calltool-dispatch.test.ts` — 383 passed. New: 8 attribution cases (containment, innermost, Method/Constructor, one edge per file and route with every callable, keys/fetches ordering, other-file isolation, `|` guard, module scope unchanged), 2 reason-parsing cases, 1 dispatch case (direct consumer file and handler file excluded, `riskLevel` unchanged).
- [x] `npx vitest run test/integration/api-impact-e2e.test.ts test/integration/api-impact-method-e2e.test.ts` — 28 passed. Seed: `backend-client.ts` fetches `/api/secure` through `fetchSecure`; `App` and `Header` call it and are listed; `useMulti` calls it too but already fetches the route and stays direct only; `/api/grants` has no attribution and no field.
- [x] `npx vitest run test/integration/resolvers/fetch-consumer-attribution.test.ts test/integration/resolvers/express-routes.test.ts test/integration/resolvers/fetch-wrapper-consumers.test.ts test/integration/resolvers/api-deep-flow.test.ts` — 55 passed. The new fixture runs the real pipeline: the edge from `src/client.ts` reads `fetch-url-match|via:Function:src/client.ts:fetchRepos`, and `loadApp` / `refreshHeader` reach it through `CALLS`.
- [x] Mutation checks: outermost-wins instead of innermost, direct files no longer excluded, and `via` never written each fail their tests (2, 2 and 7 failures respectively; nothing else moves).
- [x] `cd gitnexus && npx tsc --noEmit` and `npm run typecheck:tests`
- [x] `npx eslint` on the changed files (0 errors) and `prettier --check`
- [x] `cd gitnexus && npm test` — 908 files: 20,788 passed, 49 skipped. `wiki-mermaid-sanitizer-parse.test.ts` fails to load in my environment on `main` as well (local `@mermaid-js/tiny` resolution), and 4 `incremental-orchestration` cases timed out while the suite shared the machine with an `analyze` run; alone on this branch the file passes 39/39.

## Receipt on this repository

Indexed this branch's build against the repository itself (`analyze --index-only`, isolated `GITNEXUS_HOME`, 102,278 nodes / 299,439 edges) and called `api_impact` through the MCP stdio server. Non-test entries of `indirectConsumers`, against the #3488 ground truth:

| Route | Direct (today) | Indirect now listed | Ground truth |
|---|---|---|---|
| `GET /api/repos` | `backend-client.ts` (+ e2e specs) | `App.tsx` (`AppContent`), `DropZone.tsx` (`handleAutoConnect`), `Header.tsx` (`Header`), via `fetchRepos` | `App.tsx`, `DropZone.tsx`, `Header.tsx` |
| `GET /api/file` | `backend-client.ts` | `CodeReferencesPanel.tsx`, `useAppState.tsx`, via `readFile` | `CodeReferencesPanel.tsx`, `useAppState.tsx` |
| `POST /api/query` | `backend-client.ts` (+ tests) | `useAppState.tsx` (`executeQuery`, `runQuery`), via `runQuery` | `useAppState.tsx` |

All six files the issue names are reached, none other than through the function the edge records. Test files that call the request functions (`backend-client-*.test.ts`, `server-connection.test.ts`) appear as well, as test files already do among the direct consumers; anonymous callbacks keep their positional names (`fn_238_12`). Sorting or collapsing test code there is left for a follow-up if wanted.

## Risk & rollout

Existing indexes keep working: the new fields appear only after `npx gitnexus analyze` rewrites the `FETCHES` edges. No schema change, no migration. Reason strings grow by one field per requesting callable on edges that have one.

## Checklist

- [x] PR body meets repo minimum length (workflow may label short descriptions)
- [ ] If `AGENTS.md` / overlays changed: headers, scope block, and changelog updated per project conventions — not changed
- [x] No secrets, tokens, or machine-specific paths committed

title: fix(cli): recover pnpm and Bun invocation paths

## Summary

GitNexus can fall back from an unusable pnpm shim and finish indexing when Bun skips the native install script. CI now exercises real npm, pnpm, and Bun installs of the PR tarball on Linux, macOS, and Windows.

## Motivation / context

Fixes #3717

A pnpm shim on PATH can exit with “pnpm is not installed for this Node.js version”; selecting it prevents fallback to bunx or npx. Separately, Bun's skipped lifecycle script leaves the LadybugDB binary unprepared, causing the analyzer to reject its own metadata with `Analyzer build or dependency runtime changed during analysis`.

## Areas touched

- [x] `gitnexus/` (CLI / core / MCP server)
- [ ] `gitnexus-web/` (Vite / React UI)
- [x] `.github/` (workflows, actions)
- [x] `eval/` or other tooling (mirrored runner hook)
- [ ] Docs / agent config only

## Scope & constraints

**In scope**

- Automatic runner fallback, recovery from skipped native install scripts, and package-manager installation coverage.

**Explicitly out of scope / not done here**

- Package publication and deployment.

## Implementation notes

A successful pnpm version probe still counts when its banner is not parseable. Forced runner choices keep their existing behavior.

The native binary copy now finishes before analyzer identity is captured. Native probing and analyzer imports remain after capture, preserving the identity check's trust boundary. The shared recovery helper and its diagnostics are unchanged.

## Testing & verification

- [x] Production and test TypeScript checks, build, and CLI ESLint (zero errors).
- [x] 202 targeted regression tests and 39 workflow/shard tests passed; one platform-specific test skipped. After merging current main, the build, test TypeScript check, and all 129 focused resolver/native/CI-wiring tests passed again.
- [x] Fresh PR-tarball installs with npm 10.9.9, pnpm 12.10.1, and Bun 1.3.14 each indexed a TypeScript repository on Linux with lifecycle scripts disabled.
- [x] Disabling the startup fix in a private installed copy reproduced the identity error; restoring it made indexing pass.
- [x] [Full CI on `996859f4`](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/actions/runs/40221582582): 62 jobs passed, zero failed. The execution audit verified 28,517 core tests, 516 web tests, and 1,302 evaluation tests passed, with zero unverified tests.
- [x] All nine native CI combinations passed on `996859f4`: npm 10.9.9, pnpm 12.10.1, and Bun 1.3.14 each installed and indexed the PR tarball on Linux x64, macOS ARM64, and Windows x64. All four packaging jobs, including Linux ARM64, passed.

## Risk & rollout

The startup change reuses native recovery code shared with other CLI paths. Regression tests verify preparation does not load native code or replace an existing binary. No schema migration or index refresh is required.

## Checklist

- [x] PR body meets repo minimum length.
- [x] No secrets, tokens, or machine-specific paths committed.

title: fix(eval): retain large session measurements
body:
## Summary

Long evaluation sessions now retain their final cost and token measurements when transcripts exceed 8 MiB. A 64 MiB limit provides headroom for verbose sessions while keeping capture bounded.

## Motivation / context

[Release evaluation 40181565589](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/actions/runs/40181565589/job/121136245675) discarded a completed 142-turn session because its parent-captured event stream exceeded 8,388,608 bytes. The process exited successfully, but truncation removed the final measurement event and made the candidate report incomplete.

Related: #3500, #3609

## Areas touched

- [x] `eval/` or other tooling

## Scope & constraints

**In scope**

- One limit shared by capture, redacted artifact persistence, evolution, and comparator reuse.
- Regression coverage for a 12 MiB stream and a deliberately constrained overflow case.

**Explicitly out of scope / not done here**

- Recovering the discarded transcript or changing the original evaluation's result.
- Changing quality thresholds, hidden oracles, agent isolation, or CI workflows.
- A new paid evaluation. The candidate's two parse-retry hidden-test failures remain separate from this harness defect.

## Testing & verification

- [x] Regression reproduced the original 8 MiB capture failure before the fix; both cases pass afterward.
- [x] `cd eval && uv run --python 3.13 --locked --extra dev pytest -q` with pinned task dependencies: **1,276 passed, 26 skipped**.
- [x] Four pinned parse-retry oracle controls: reference solutions pass and broken startup-only repairs fail.

The full core suite did not complete. A focused rerun reproduces the same native-load error; this test and its helper are unchanged from `main`.

The capture cap remains finite. Three concurrent paid cells may now retain up to 192 MiB of raw transcript data, plus parsing/redaction overhead. title: refactor(ingestion): share callable declaration extraction with scope resolution
body:
### Area

gitnexus (CLI / core / indexing / MCP server)

### Problem or opportunity

Method extraction and scope extraction currently build overlapping representations of the same callable declaration. Consolidate that work while preserving the metadata and identities that resolution depends on.

For example, a Java method's parameters are read through `javaMethodConfig.extractParameters` both when building `MethodInfo` for the structure graph and when computing arity metadata for scope definitions. TypeScript follows the same pattern. The language-specific parameter logic is shared, but extraction and metadata projection happen separately.

The worker already reuses the parsed syntax tree for scope extraction. This is repeated extraction from one AST, not evidence of a second tree-sitter parse.

### Performance motivation

Reducing duplicate extraction is an explicit objective alongside maintainability:
- **CPU:** both consumers walk callable parameters and derive overlapping signature facts. Sharing the extracted facts should remove repeated AST access and intermediate processing on parse-cache misses.
- **Allocations:** the paths construct separate parameter arrays and intermediate metadata. Reusing facts can reduce avoidable allocations; allocation volume and GC impact need measurement.
- **Scale:** quantify the cost on files with many methods, parameters, and overloads, and on a representative repository. The existing worker cache already reuses method metadata within a class, so count duplication across structure and scope consumers rather than assuming extraction repeats for every call site.

The duplicated work is confirmed by source inspection. Its share of indexing time, peak memory, and the achievable end-to-end improvement have not yet been measured. Consumer-specific projections may still be necessary; retain them where their semantics differ.

Method extractors remain necessary today:
- The parse worker uses their metadata for graph properties and overload-disambiguating node IDs.
- Scope resolution reads graph `isAbstract` and `isStatic` flags when selecting dispatch targets.
- Scope definitions and graph nodes have separate identities and are joined through the graph bridge.

Deleting `method-extractors/` without migrating these responsibilities would lose required behavior.

### Source evidence

Inspected at commit `e4b0efce0a1bf13a836429ea1d57ec4fb65521e4`:

- [MethodInfo extraction](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/blob/e4b0efce0a1bf13a836429ea1d57ec4fb65521e4/gitnexus/src/core/ingestion/method-extractors/generic.ts#L234-L273).
- [Worker metadata enrichment and overload identity](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/blob/e4b0efce0a1bf13a836429ea1d57ec4fb65521e4/gitnexus/src/core/ingestion/workers/parse-worker.ts#L2771-L2851).
- [Java scope arity extraction](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/blob/e4b0efce0a1bf13a836429ea1d57ec4fb65521e4/gitnexus/src/core/ingestion/languages/java/arity-metadata.ts#L13-L49) and [TypeScript equivalent](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/blob/e4b0efce0a1bf13a836429ea1d57ec4fb65521e4/gitnexus/src/core/ingestion/languages/typescript/arity-metadata.ts#L53-L97).
- [Dispatch consuming graph metadata](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/blob/e4b0efce0a1bf13a836429ea1d57ec4fb65521e4/gitnexus/src/core/ingestion/scope-resolution/passes/receiver-bound-calls.ts#L1041-L1097).
- [Existing AST reuse](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/blob/e4b0efce0a1bf13a836429ea1d57ec4fb65521e4/gitnexus/src/core/ingestion/workers/parse-worker.ts#L1707-L1730).

### Proposed solution

Extract callable declaration facts once per declaration during worker processing, then derive graph properties and scope-definition metadata from those facts.

Reuse the existing provider/config extraction logic and evolve the smallest suitable contract. Preserve raw signature facts separately from consumer-specific normalization: overload identity and call compatibility can legitimately require different representations.

Ship in stages:
1. Inventory consumers and define the shared facts, source identity, and lifetime. Account for synthesized members and owner-dependent semantics.
2. Migrate Java and TypeScript as initial examples; make both structure and scope consumers use the extracted result.
3. Migrate remaining affected providers, then remove redundant walks/adapters where both consumers have moved.
4. Document the extraction/resolution boundary and update obsolete migration comments in touched files.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Migrated structure and scope paths reuse one declaration extraction result; instrumented tests demonstrate that signature extraction is not repeated across those consumers.
- [ ] Graph node IDs, method properties, ownership edges, and resolved call targets remain equivalent on existing fixtures.
- [ ] Coverage preserves same-arity overloads, generic/raw parameter types, optional/variadic parameters, static/instance and abstract dispatch, and synthesized members sharing a source line with explicit declarations.
- [ ] Existing worker serialization, parse-cache replay, and scope extraction failure handling remain correct. Cached facts are bounded to the file/worker lifecycle and do not retain ASTs across files.
- [ ] Language-specific rules remain in provider hooks/configs; shared ingestion code gains no language-name branching.
- [ ] Targeted extraction/resolution tests, the core test suite (`cd gitnexus && npm test`), and typecheck (`cd gitnexus && npx tsc --noEmit`) pass.
- [ ] Record before/after extraction counts and phase timings, end-to-end indexing wall time, peak memory including workers, and allocation/GC evidence where practical. Include a declaration-heavy fixture and a representative repository.
- [ ] Measure cold parse-cache misses, warm cache replay, and changed-file reanalysis separately, using the same corpus, worker count, runtime, and repeated runs. Report variability and any time/memory tradeoff.
- [ ] Demonstrate reduced duplicate signature extraction on cache misses, preserve graph/resolution parity, and verify warm-cache behavior does not regress. Publish measured results before claiming an end-to-end speedup.

### Constraints and alternatives

Retain required method-extractor functionality until replacement consumers have parity. Limit the refactor to callable declaration metadata; broad field/class extraction redesign and changes to resolution policy are separate work. Preserve existing graph/API contracts.

Keeping the current split avoids migration work but retains repeated extraction and synchronization overhead. Removing the extractors immediately is unsafe because live consumers depend on them.

Related: #909 (scope-resolution architecture), #568 (MethodExtractor design), #880 (earlier extractor cleanup, closed; did not consolidate these two declaration paths).

title: Named JS/TS class expressions lose Class owners and drop member edges
fix(ingestion): retain named class-expression owners
body:
## Summary

Retain named JS/TS class expressions as Class nodes and keep their member-owner relationships consistent through workers, both persistent parse caches and native graph loading.

## Motivation / context

Closes #3724

A factory mock such as `ApiError: class ApiError extends Error { status = 500; messageForUser() {} }` emitted relationships to a missing Class node. COPY reported missing primary keys and skipped relationships. Related history: #1929 (F44/F86).

## Areas touched

- [x] `gitnexus/` (CLI / core / MCP server)
- [ ] `gitnexus-web/` (Vite / React UI)
- [ ] `.github/` (workflows, actions)
- [ ] `eval/` or other tooling
- [ ] Docs / agent config only

## Scope & constraints

**In scope**

- Named class-expression definitions, field/method metadata and matching scope declarations.
- Preserve existing method-local TypeAlias owner IDs and their member relationships.
- Owner/member IDs that distinguish same-named expressions in sibling factories or methods; internal class names stay inside their expression.
- Worker, nested-shadowing, JSX/Vue, cold/warm cache and native COPY regressions. Native tests are assigned to `lbug-db` and the cross-platform list.

**Explicitly out of scope / not done here**

- General anonymous-class support, expression alias/inheritance resolution, callback/process limits, COPY warning suppression, dependency/version changes or installed-package updates.
- The pre-existing evidence-provenance golden test's dependence on local Git commit signing.

## Implementation notes

JS/TS-specific behavior stays in provider, capture and extractor code; the shared parse worker is unchanged. Named expressions receive position-qualified IDs. Nested ordinary class-like declarations use their qualified type paths, with matching scope/member identities.

Object type aliases keep their existing simple TypeAlias IDs, including inside ordinary class methods and named expressions. The JS/TS qualifier fallback now uses the same owner name as the definition node, so their property/method relationships survive native COPY.

More frequent owner qualification exposed repeated top-level AST enumeration in the shared extractor. Skip that walk when `fileScopeSet` is empty; retain package/file-scope and ancestor qualification otherwise. A TS/Java/Ruby worker regression covers both branches.

On the same 446089-byte generated-interface fixture (1300 interfaces, 19500 fields), scope extraction improved from 11.742s to 1.075s and the real-worker parse/resolve pipeline from 22.047s to 8.232s. Capture and graph-fact SHA-256 values were identical before/after; no fields or member edges were dropped. These are comparative local measurements, not a general throughput guarantee.

## Testing & verification

- Initial real-worker RED: missing Class owners across `.ts`, `.tsx`, `.js`, `.mjs` and a TS constructor parameter property; an additional RED covered sibling expression ID collisions.
- `npm run build`, `npx tsc --noEmit`, `npm run typecheck:tests`: pass.
- Earlier broader ownership, qualified-name, cache-identity and C++/C#/Java/Ruby resolver suites: **1088 passed**. Current ownership/qualified-name follow-up: **33 passed**.
- Type-alias regression RED: all four new cases failed before the patch. TS/TSX/Vue workers now retain members inside ordinary classes and named expressions; a full-pipeline native regression reads back both exact alias-member relationships after COPY.
- The frozen full suite included **30/30** class-expression/type-alias owner tests and **3/3** qualified-class lookup tests passing.
- Cold parse uses the compiled worker; warm parse has 0 reparsed files and 4 cache hits, reusing both worker-result chunks and durable ParsedFile shards. Facts remain correct.
- Native COPY reports no warnings/skipped relationships for the fixture; SQL reads back the Class nodes and both member relationship groups.
- Changed-file ESLint, Prettier and `git diff --check`: pass.
- Full `npm test -- --maxWorkers=6 --reporter=default --reporter=json`: **28443 passed, 1 failed, 91 skipped; exit 1**. This is not a full-suite GREEN.

The sole failure is `test/unit/evidence-provenance-helper.test.ts`, “has one golden digest for every dirty state and identical planner/executor bytes”. An isolated checkout of the original base `ee7eff97f7f4eb7d68f7090cba448f7cc8285db2` reproduces the same digest mismatch with global SSH commit signing enabled (`commit.gpgsign=true`, `gpg.format=ssh`). Diagnostic runs with signing disabled only for that process pass on both base and working tree. Global Git configuration, assertions and golden values were not changed. The canonical full-suite failure is retained in this report. The latest full run reproduced the exact same failure message and the same set of 91 skipped cases; it completed in 4140.49 seconds.

The 91 recorded skips cover 35 conditional benchmarks, 47 platform-specific cases, 6 optional-Zig presence/suite gates, 2 unprovisioned Python workflow-preflight cases and 1 javac-dependent case. They remain unverified locally.

- [ ] Full `cd gitnexus && npm test` GREEN (baseline/environment failure documented above)
- [x] `cd gitnexus && npx tsc --noEmit`
- [x] `cd gitnexus && npm run typecheck:tests`
- [x] Integration coverage included in the full suite; not rerun separately

Independent Claude Opus 5.5 xhigh review and scoped re-review found the owner-qualification performance regression addressed, with no blocking findings. The additional scoped TypeAlias correction was also reviewed with Claude Opus 5.5 xhigh: code READY, no blocking findings. Repeated whole-PR comparison with merge base `f759753794fda8e399d670ef7f04b9d7473d6082` reports 18 changed files and 52 mapped symbols. Mapping remains PARTIAL/unknown because `vitest.config.ts` has no mapped symbol; the full diff and all 18 changed files were reviewed directly. The corrective two-file follow-up maps to five symbols with LOW risk and no partial or truncated result. No whole-PR graph all-clear is claimed.
