title: perf(ingestion): reduce indexing overhead and declaration memory
body:
## Summary

Reduce indexing overhead and retained callable metadata while preserving graph outputs. Structure extraction and scope resolution share immutable declaration facts and parameter-type arrays; overload lookups and Java export checks reuse prior results, and analyzer identity validation avoids unnecessary asynchronous filesystem overhead. The existing CI benchmark now guards time and memory growth across increasing workloads.

## Motivation / context

Both extraction consumers inspect the same parsed declarations. Method-extractors still provide structure metadata and overload identity, so they remain necessary; shared facts remove repeated work between the two paths.

Closes #3723.

## Areas touched

- [x] `gitnexus/` (CLI / core / MCP server)
- [ ] `gitnexus-web/` (Vite / React UI)
- [x] `.github/` (workflows, actions)
- [x] `eval/` or other tooling (benchmark harness and evidence)
- [ ] Docs / agent config only

## Scope & constraints

**In scope**

- Share pure declaration facts across Java, TypeScript/JavaScript, Kotlin, C#, Python, PHP, Swift, and Dart consumers.
- Reuse common parameter-type arrays, copying when provider normalization, positional unknowns, or variadic markers require a different result.
- Reuse each class method map's overload groups for definition and enclosing-callable IDs.
- Use a bounded storage sample to select synchronous or asynchronous reads inside the existing analyzer-identity subprocess.
- Cache Java parent modifier checks without retaining ASTs or changing export decisions.
- Guard spread/concentrated indexing and retained metadata across three sizes with the existing 1.5 normalized growth budget.
- Run the callable time and memory harness against committed `baseline.json` in the existing `benchmarks (GITNEXUS_BENCH)` job, alongside the unchanged scope-resolution measurements.

**Explicitly out of scope / not done here**

- Removing method-extractors, changing resolution policy, graph IDs, or persistent cache formats.

## Implementation notes

Declaration caches use tree ownership and native node IDs, including provider hooks for Python/Dart wrappers. Parameter-type projections use weak ownership of immutable parameter arrays and retain no AST references. File/owner-dependent callbacks remain outside that cache. Overload groups belong to complete per-file method maps.

The identity subprocess samples up to 16 distributed requests or 8 ms, then uses synchronous reads on fast storage or concurrent asynchronous batches on slower storage. Every validation guard and its ordering remain intact.

### Time and memory evidence

The earlier identity optimization reduced complete cold/warm/changed indexing totals by **4.16% / 8.52% versus the pre-refactor control**, and **5.78% / 5.87% versus the prior PR**, for repository / declaration workloads. The original [repository](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/actions/runs/40271406528) and [declaration](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/actions/runs/40272393865) CI runs contain the isolated evidence.

The memory follow-up compares against `e6744edca`, with three alternating full-indexing pairs per workload plus A/A calibration on isolated runners:

| Workload | Total time before → after | Peak RSS before → after |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Repository | 23.387 → 23.342 s (−0.19%) | 734.1 → 710.9 MiB (−3.16%) |
| Declarations | 14.909 → 14.775 s (−0.90%) | 649.3 → 657.9 MiB (+1.33%) |

These shifts do **not** establish an additional end-to-end speedup or general peak-RSS improvement. No cold/warm/changed median regresses beyond the declared 3% guardrail.

Ten fresh-process heap-probe pairs per language, each with 10,000 declarations, show **11.52% less retained JavaScript heap for Java and 11.54% less for TypeScript** after extraction. Emitted metadata retains about 21.6% less heap after releasing methods and trees. All trees collect; the savings include approximately 0.26 MiB of additional weak-cache capacity. Probe extraction time increases about 2–3%, while whole-index timing remains effectively unchanged. The instrumented declaration run verifies **97.6% fewer overload-group arrays: 110,210 → 2,626**.

The existing **benchmarks (GITNEXUS_BENCH)** job now runs `measure.mjs --check` against committed `baseline.json` and uploads `method-declaration-facts-benchmark`. It measures cold/warm/changed indexing time, heap, peak RSS, and retained declaration memory; provider fingerprints, shared-array counts, graph outputs, cache replay, and tree collection are checked. Numeric timing and memory deltas are reported as machine-dependent references. [Benchmark instructions](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/blob/refactor/shared-callable-extraction/gitnexus/bench/method-declaration-facts/README.md). The scope-resolution job remains unchanged. The one-off [memory experiment](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/actions/runs/40289711096) remains historical evidence; the `docs/optimize` Markdown/JSON reports have been removed.

### Scaling and the Java parsing hotspot

The new C#-style size matrix caught a concentrated cold-indexing failure: 4x declarations grew median time by 10.1x. A CPU profile attributed 30–33 seconds per worker attempt to Java export checks repeatedly scanning the same class body; a worker timeout then repeated the work. Weak parent-result caching preserves the existing decisions and removes those scans.

Three fresh-process samples per size, before and after the fix on the same local runtime:

| Concentrated workload | Cold time before → after | Peak RSS before → after |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| 2,560 generated methods | 8.078 → 8.088 s | 606.0 → 601.5 MiB |
| 10,240 generated methods | 81.539 → 19.038 s (−76.65%) | 875.3 → 806.7 MiB (−7.84%) |

The largest adjacent normalized time ratio fell from 2.524 to 0.588, below the 1.5 limit. All eight indexing/retained-metadata groups pass; the maximum normalized cost ratio across all groups is 1.015. These bounded workloads guard regressions rather than prove asymptotic complexity for every repository. All pre-fix graph and metadata fingerprints remain identical, and all 100 trees collect after exercising the new cache.

## Testing & verification

- [x] Build and production/test typechecks pass.
- [x] 441 focused tests pass, including Java parser/resolver coverage, sharing identity, normalization, variadics, both consumer orders, and 16 scaling-guard tests. Quadratic time or memory and invalid measurements fail the guard.
- [x] 72 uninstrumented isolated full analyses preserve graph hashes and cache counts; six additional instrumented analyses preserve the same graphs. Warm runs reparse zero files; changed runs reparse one.
- [x] 18 local full analyses cover declaration, repository, and all-eight-provider fixtures with graph parity.
- [x] Scoped ESLint has zero errors; Prettier passes.
- [x] Earlier full-PR graph change analysis mapped 61 symbols across 17 changed files to the expected parsing flow, with medium aggregate risk. The shared projection has CRITICAL upstream reach through all eight arity providers; sequential correctness, adversarial, reuse, and testing review found no actionable defects. No independent-model review is claimed.
- [x] Earlier full local `npm test` completed: 28,457 passed, 7 failed, 89 skipped. All seven failures passed unchanged in targeted reruns (78 tests) after unsetting inherited `CODEX_HOME`, selecting the compatible C++ runtime, and removing full-suite contention. No production code or test assertion was changed for those retries.
- [x] The heap probe explicitly reads retained methods after its live-heap sample; ten repeated local pairs preserve digests, tree collection, and roughly 11.5% retained-heap savings.
- [x] Baseline record passes with 63 full analyses, 18 retained-heap probes, and all eight providers. The original baseline fingerprints remain unchanged. The expanded matrix preserves the existing CI command and artifact.
- [x] Prior-head hosted callable baseline check at `a6dad8554` passed in 80 seconds. The [uploaded time/memory artifact](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/actions/runs/40304592369/artifacts/12642426767) was downloaded and verified: all eight providers, 18 full analyses, six heap probes, and baseline comparisons are present and pass.
- [x] The scaling follow-up passes fresh-index change analysis: seven files and 40 mapped symbols, no incomplete mapping. Java export detection has HIGH upstream reach; characterization, graph parity, and weak-tree lifetime checks pass. The original paired diagnostic mode passes 18 additional full analyses.
- [x] Exact local `--check` passes against the committed baseline: 63 full analyses, 18 heap probes, eight providers, 100 trees collected, and all eight scaling groups.
- [x] Hosted callable scaling check at `4ca807271` passed in 7m 20s. The [time/memory artifact](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/actions/runs/40320927312/artifacts/12649029110) was downloaded and verified: the complete matrix, exact baseline correctness, and all scaling groups pass (maximum normalized ratio 0.983 against the 1.5 budget).
- [x] The final pipeline execution artifact from the same run confirms 82/82 tests passed, but the overall benchmark job was cancelled at its 25-minute timeout as those tests finished. The callable size matrix adds roughly six minutes compared with the previous single-size check.
- [x] Increased only the benchmark job allowance to 30 minutes; workload sizes, repetitions, scaling limits, and per-test guards are unchanged. `actionlint` and all 16 scaling-guard tests pass.
- [ ] Hosted verification of the timeout-only follow-up at `2ef594070` is pending; the previous cancelled job is not a green whole-job result.

The preceding head `e6744edca` passed 28,541 core, 516 web, and 1,302 eval tests in [hosted CI](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/actions/runs/40273873811). That is prior-head evidence, not a result for this follow-up. Browser checks do not apply.

## Risk & rollout

Shared inputs, per-class method maps and ASTs must remain immutable during extraction. Tests preserve provider policies, wrappers, overloads, ownership, reparses, and resolved calls. Weak ownership prevents AST retention, but allocator/cache capacity can remain after collection. The measured heap reduction is specific to declaration metadata and is not a guarantee of lower whole-process peak memory. No migration is needed; ingestion implementation changes automatically invalidate parser-cache identity.

Session-settled decision: keep the measurements in the existing benchmark harness, CI job and artifact (user-directed).

## Checklist

- [x] PR body meets repo minimum length
- [x] Agent instructions unchanged; no header/changelog update needed
- [x] No secrets, tokens, or machine-specific paths committed

title: feat(taint): add AdonisJS request and Lucid models
body:
## Summary

GitNexus now understands AdonisJS. Values read from an AdonisJS request, such as `request.input()` or `ctx.request.qs()`, are taint sources, and Lucid's `rawQuery` is a SQL sink. A request value that gets concatenated into a raw query is reported as `sql-injection`, including when it travels through local variables or into another function.

## Motivation / context

Refs #2982. The built-in TypeScript/JavaScript model was written with Express in mind. It didn't know AdonisJS request methods or Lucid's raw-SQL entry point, so real source-to-sink flows in AdonisJS apps went unreported.

## Areas touched

- [x] `gitnexus/` (CLI / core / MCP server)
- Docs: `docs/mcp-reference.md`

## Scope & constraints

**In scope**

- Sources: results of `input`, `qs`, `header`, `param`, `cookie`, `all`, `body`, `params`, `headers`, `only`, `except` and `validateUsing`, called on the usual receivers `req`, `request` and `ctx.request`.
- Sink: the SQL text (argument 0) of `rawQuery` on `db`, `database` and `trx`, and on whatever name `@adonisjs/lucid/services/db` is imported under. Argument 1 holds value bindings and stays safe.
- The call-result matcher now accepts exact dotted receivers such as `ctx.request`. Existing single-name rules work as before.

**Explicitly out of scope / not done here**

- Source calls used inline or nested in concatenation, template interpolation, method chains, `??`/`||`, or wrappers like `String(...)`, even when the whole expression is assigned. The source call has to be the assigned or destructured value itself; `await`, parentheses and the supported TypeScript assertions around it are fine.
- Request receivers under other names, and loading custom taint models from the project (the second ask in #2982).

## Implementation notes

`validateUsing()` stays a source. A schema can accept strings that are unsafe in SQL, shell commands, paths or markup, so treating every validator as a sanitizer would hide real injections. Zero-argument `Model.query()` calls have no SQL argument and are unchanged.

The model digest changes on its own, which invalidates persisted taint findings. No schema or parser wire-format change is needed.

## Testing & verification

- [x] `cd gitnexus && npm run build`, `npx tsc --noEmit` and `npm run typecheck:tests`
- [x] New tests: 61 AdonisJS unit cases (`test/unit/taint/adonis-model-match.test.ts`), two real-worker TS/JS cases with a cold and a warm parse cache (`test/integration/cfg/adonis-taint.test.ts`), and a persisted LadybugDB → MCP `explain` case (`test/integration/taint-explain.test.ts`, 22/22 in that file). The controls include parameterized SQL, query builders, unrelated receivers and the coverage gaps listed above.
- [x] Windows/macOS: `adonis-taint.test.ts` is in the `WORKER_THREADS` cross-platform list. In run [40984437558](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/actions/runs/40984437558) it passed on windows-latest (shard 7/11) and macos-latest (shard 3/11).
- [x] Hosted CI on `0f049eb98`: all required checks are green, and the CI report shows 32,747 tests passed across 3 platforms, none failed or unverified.
- [x] Full local `cd gitnexus && npm test` on `0f049eb98`: 1,408 files and 30,753 tests passed, 13 files and 91 tests skipped.

The local failures listed in the earlier version of this description are gone. `evidence-provenance-helper.test.ts` failed only because my global git config signs commits, which changes its fixture commit IDs; with signing off for the fixture repositories, it passes. The `run-analyze-fts-repair` and `analyze-staged-embedding-recovery` failures did not recur.

## Risk & rollout

Other language models share the matcher, but matching stays exact and the existing single-name receiver rules are untouched. After upgrading, re-run `gitnexus analyze --pdg` to rebuild findings with the new model. Zero findings still don't mean the code is safe; `docs/mcp-reference.md` lists the known coverage gaps.

## Checklist

- [x] PR body meets the repository's description requirements
- [x] No secrets, tokens, or machine-specific paths committed

<!-- gitnexus-pr-summary:v1:start -->

---

title: fix(mcp): bound query previews and advertise repo defaults
body:
## Summary

Queries with `include_content: true` fetch bounded source previews after ranking and pagination. Large matches retain useful source instead of returning whole files. MCP tool schemas advertise the configured default repository so agents can use the existing binding without a discovery call.

## Motivation / context

[Run 40239809351](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/actions/runs/40239809351) contained two oversized query responses followed by 14 recovery shell calls, including a JSON parse failure caused by the prose trailer. All 12 candidate MCP sessions also initially used the wrong repository name. This addresses response cost separately from the indexing work in #3726.

## Areas touched

- [x] `gitnexus/` (CLI / core / MCP server)
- [ ] `gitnexus-web/` (Vite / React UI)
- [ ] `.github/` (workflows, actions)
- [x] `eval/` or other tooling
- [ ] Docs / agent config only

## Scope & constraints

**In scope**

- Query source retrieval and representation, MCP JSON guidance, and default-repository schema metadata.

**Explicitly out of scope / not done here**

- Indexing changes, the existing explicit `maxTokens` contract, and a paid agent evaluation.

## Implementation notes

- One 16,000-character source allowance is divided equally across unique symbols on the returned page. The database returns prefixes directly; content is fetched once per returned symbol. `content_truncated: true` identifies incomplete previews. Full source remains available through `context` or bounded `read_file` ranges.
- Ranking, match identities, ordering, retention restrictions, and completeness diagnostics remain intact. The shared backend serves CLI, HTTP, and MCP; group queries already request no source.
- MCP query guidance is a JSON `next` field. The serializer only serializes; it no longer budgets or removes source.
- The existing repository policy adds the resolved default path and name to tool schemas. Routing and authorization are unchanged. Benchmark task prompts remain unchanged.

## Measurements

Compared complete builds at base `34b873696b3766c3237700b5be23823c05d89374` and candidate `382b2693ad79532898da63c2e9e7992d9f3e46f0` through the real MCP stdio protocol, with the same dependencies and read-only index (102,388 nodes, 299,753 relationships; keyword search, no embeddings). The newer unrelated main ingestion change was excluded.

Eight fresh server pairs × five rounds produced **40 paired observations per warm workload**. Requests alternated between the two live servers, with one full warmup cycle. Intervals below use 10,000 paired bootstrap resamples clustered by server pair. The host was shared Linux x64, i9-12900K, Node 22.23.3, with identical four-CPU affinity. These are pointwise intervals, not guarantees for every workload or platform.

| Workload | Median milliseconds, base → candidate | Paired change (95% interval) |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| Eight-query workload total | 6273 → 5805 | -9.9% (-11.7% to -8.0%) |
| list_repos, source | 679 → 596 | -13.1% (-18.6% to -7.5%) |
| MCP repository discovery, source | 544 → 486 | -13.0% (-18.1% to -7.7%) |
| analyze command CLI, source | 645 → 546 | -11.7% (-16.8% to -6.9%) |
| query, higher limits + source | 1516 → 1204 | -19.5% (-22.0% to -16.9%) |
| Four concurrent discovery queries | 1548 → 1412 | -10.3% (-12.0% to -8.6%) |

All four source-query p95 latencies also improved (1,049 → 825; 858 → 721; 831 → 768; 1,798 → 1,524 ms). Concurrent-batch p95 improved from 1,806 to 1,620 ms. These tails are descriptive, with 40 samples.

Median concurrent throughput was **2.58 → 2.83 requests/sec**. Final server CPU time decreased **10.6%** (95% interval -11.5% to -9.7%); median CPU time per session was 101.11 → 88.95 seconds. Peak RSS was approximately unchanged: paired +0.5% (-1.6% to +3.0%), medians 1,049.6 → 1,061.3 MiB.

Source-response bytes decreased **43–88%**. The largest tested result decreased from **164,430 to 19,550 bytes**, retaining all 27 rows. Every measured pair checked match identities, order, and diagnostics; context retained full source. The tool-list schema grew by 862 bytes (68,366 → 69,228) to advertise the default repository.

### Remaining uncertainty

The predeclared material-regression threshold was more than 5% **and** more than 5 ms. No tested workload detected a regression beyond that threshold, but four main-run assessments were inconclusive. A separate, predeclared **12 fresh server pairs × four rounds** focused on those queries and repeated the same startup/first-query sequence:

| Follow-up workload | Median milliseconds, base → candidate | Paired change (95% interval) |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| Process startup | 661 → 646 | +1.5% (-14.1% to +24.6%) |
| Startup + first query | 2011 → 1969 | -4.8% (-13.4% to +5.2%) |
| list_repos, no source | 638 → 635 | -0.8% (-6.0% to +4.4%) |
| MCP repository discovery, no source | 524 → 509 | -4.4% (-14.0% to +4.9%) |
| No matches | 118 → 121 | +4.2% (-13.1% to +23.6%) |

The follow-up excludes a greater-than-5% slowdown for both ordinary no-source queries. **Startup and empty-result round trips remain inconclusive**; first-query timing also has a wider interval in the follow-up. This is evidence of a faster tested workload, not a blanket no-slowdown clearance.

All outliers were retained. One candidate empty-result request took 3,090 ms with 118.5 ms in the backend query timer; a baseline repository request took 3,847 ms with 522.9 ms in that timer. The identical-build control also showed a 1,273 ms gap. The delay lies outside the instrumented query phase; its cause is not established. No timeout or query-error logs were recorded. A quiet runner is needed to tighten startup and empty-result bounds.

The earlier five-pair 6–12% speed claim is **superseded**: a sequential-block identical-build control falsely appeared 7.9% faster. The revised interleaved control was +2.3% (-0.6% to +5.3%). Raw measurements, harnesses, configurations, and analysis are retained locally in `.context/mcp-performance/`; the two experiments are reported separately.

No model calls were made. Agent completion time and dollar savings remain unmeasured; smaller payloads alone do not establish those outcomes.

## Testing & verification

- [x] Query and MCP regression suites, native index-generation/query tests, HTTP/API compatibility, content retention, and repository-policy tests.
- [x] Native database tests cover oversized ASCII/Unicode source, unchanged matches and ranking, one preview per symbol, and full-source retrieval afterward.
- [x] 299 evaluation harness tests passed; 3 skipped.
- [x] `npm run build`, `npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.test.json`, web `npx tsc -b --noEmit`, scoped ESLint/Prettier, and `node --import tsx scripts/bench/mcp-serialization.ts`.
- [x] Fresh graph comparison against the merge base: 9 files, 38 changed symbols, 8 affected flows, high risk; complete, without partial/truncated results. The working-tree scan cannot map removed prototype symbols; comparison against main covers the final change, and a reference search confirms no removed-formatter callers remain.

## Risk & rollout

`include_content` now returns previews; callers needing complete source should use `context` or `read_file`. The allowance counts Unicode characters, not serialized bytes or tokens. Explicit/environment `maxTokens` retains the existing final text cap and can still truncate JSON. Clients must parse query JSON directly instead of removing a fixed prose-trailer length.

No index migration or rebuild is required. Compare model evaluations under the same harness revision before claiming dollar savings. CI will validate this revision across supported platforms.

## Checklist

- [x] Changes remain scoped to query responses, repository schema metadata, and their tests/docs.
- [x] No agent instruction files, dependencies, or workflow configuration changed.
- [x] No secrets or machine-specific paths committed.

title: feat(logger): let a host route GitNexus records into its own sink
body:
## Summary

`configureLoggerSink({ destination, level, mixin })` routes the default `logger` and every later `createLogger()` child into a host's own sink, and returns a function that restores the previous state. Without a call, nothing changes.

## Motivation / context

Closes #3620. A process that embeds GitNexus (its own service around `serve`, or the MCP server kept alive by a host) has its own logging: a file per service, a request id carried across async calls, redaction before disk. Today every record goes to stderr, and the only redirect is `_captureLogger()`, which is test-only by name and contract and throws on a second call. The host is left with re-parsing stderr or patching `logger.ts` through every merge.

## Areas touched

- [x] `gitnexus/` (CLI / core / MCP server)
- [ ] `gitnexus-web/` (Vite / React UI)
- [ ] `.github/` (workflows, actions)
- [ ] `eval/` or other tooling
- [ ] Docs / agent config only (`AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `.cursor/`, `llms.txt`, etc.)

## Scope & constraints

**In scope**

- `configureLoggerSink()` in `src/core/logger.ts`, with `LoggerSinkOptions` (`destination`: any writable stream, a pino destination included; `level`: base level, `GITNEXUS_LOG_LEVEL` applies when unset, a child's `debugEnvVar` still wins; `mixin`: pino's mixin, called once per record).
- The singleton is a Proxy, so modules that imported it before the call pick the sink up on their next record. A named child built before the call keeps the destination it was built with (three modules build one at import time: `update-check`, `bridge-db`, and lazily `receiver-drops`).
- The restore function permanently retires its sink. If it is active, the nearest earlier live sink becomes active again, or stderr if none remain. Retiring a displaced sink leaves the current destination alone and prevents later restores from resurrecting it.
- `flushLoggerSync()` also flushes a sink destination that has `flushSync`.
- Validation: a destination without `write()` throws `TypeError`, an unknown level `RangeError`, a non-function mixin `TypeError`.
- A record's own field wins over the mixin's (pino's default merge). A mixin that throws does not lose the record: it is written without the mixin's fields and the failure is reported on stderr once, the way a missing pino-pretty is, since the logger is what is failing.
- A test capture (`_captureLogger()`) keeps precedence over the sink while active; it is unchanged otherwise.

**Explicitly out of scope / not done here**

- Redirecting children created before the call: that would mean a per-record indirection on the hot path, which the issue rules out.
- A pretty transport or a `beforeExit` flush hook for the host sink: the destination belongs to the host.
- Reimplementing `_captureLogger()` on top of the new API: it works as is, and keeping it separate keeps the capture guard (throw on a double capture) untouched.

## Implementation notes

The default path changes by one `if (_sink)` at logger construction, nothing per record. `createLogger()` with an explicit `destination` (the test pattern) is untouched and still comes first. The sink branch builds `pino({ level, base: undefined, name, mixin }, destination)` the same way the explicit-destination branch does.

## Testing & verification

- [x] `cd gitnexus && npx vitest run test/unit/logger.test.ts` — 34 passed (19 existing, 15 new). New: singleton and a later child reach the sink with the mixin field while `pino.destination` is never built (fresh module instance, spy on `pino.destination`); sink level and `debugEnvVar` precedence; level case-insensitive and ahead of `GITNEXUS_LOG_LEVEL`; restore returns the singleton to the previous destination, through a two-sink chain too; a later sink replaces an earlier one and the earlier restore retires its sink without changing the active destination; capture precedence; a record's field over the mixin's; a throwing mixin keeps the record and warns once; `flushLoggerSync` reaches the sink's `flushSync`; the three validation errors.
- [x] Against the compiled package, as a host would use it (`dist/core/logger.js` imported from a separate Node process, sink = `fs.createWriteStream`, mixin `{ requestId, service }`, then a real GitNexus warning: `writeV8CacheFileSync` into a path under a regular file, plus a singleton and a child record):

  | mode | stderr | sink file |
  |---|---|---|
  | `configureLoggerSink` | 0 bytes | 3 records, each with `requestId: "req-42"` and `service: "host"`, the first being `v8 cache: write failed; treating as miss` from `gitnexus` |
  | no call | the same 3 records, same fields minus the mixin's | none |
- [x] Mutation checks: dropping the singleton rebuild on configure, and dropping the mixin, each fail their tests. Independent follow-up at `d2e9d3d3`: removing the child debug override from the host-sink branch fails only the new warn-level sink test; changing the retired-sink traversal from `while` to a single-hop `if` fails only the new four-sink test (33/34 pass for each mutation).
- [x] `npx vitest run test/unit/middleware-trust-proxy.test.ts test/unit/language-availability-skip.test.ts test/unit/repo-manager-registry-strict-read.test.ts` (the capture users) — 79 passed.
- [x] `cd gitnexus && npx tsc --noEmit` and `npm run typecheck:tests`
- [x] `npx eslint` and `prettier --check` on the two files

## Risk & rollout

title: test(mcp): track query performance in CI
body:
## Summary

CI now retains paired MCP performance measurements for each tested commit, so query latency, payload size, CPU, and memory changes can be inspected alongside correctness. The new job compares complete runtimes on the same runner and publishes both a summary and 30-day raw artifacts.

## Motivation / context

The query-preview optimization had local measurements, but no repeatable CI evidence. Tool runtime and agent cost need separate measurements: the supplied [release evaluation](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/actions/runs/40357855460) recorded faster candidate MCP sessions with higher mean cost than stable.

Related: #3728.

## Areas touched

- [x] `gitnexus/` (CLI / core / MCP server)
- [ ] `gitnexus-web/` (Vite / React UI)
- [x] `.github/` (workflows, actions)
- [x] `eval/` or other tooling
- [ ] Docs / agent config only

## Scope & constraints

**In scope**

- Real MCP stdio measurements for small/large source queries, metadata-only queries, empty results, context, tool listing, startup, and concurrency four.
- Pinned revisions, dependency and fixture fingerprints, every paired observation, server CPU/RSS, and diagnostic logs.

**Explicitly out of scope / not done here**

- Application behavior changes, model API calls, and dollar-cost or task-quality gates. Existing release evaluation owns the agent measurements.

## Implementation notes

The comparison uses the checked-out commit's first parent: the exact base for a PR merge commit, or preceding main revision in release CI. Both builds read one candidate-generated fixture index; incompatible index schemas fail explicitly. The fixture contains 32 short and 32 oversized TypeScript functions.

Eight fresh server pairs run five measured rounds each, alternating request order. Confidence intervals resample whole process pairs, preserving correlation between repeated requests. Timing fails only when the lower bounds exceed both 5% and 5 ms; inconclusive results remain labeled as such. Correctness, missing measurements, partial responses, and source-budget violations always fail.

The job summary includes latency, payload, CPU, and memory tables. The `mcp-query-performance` artifact retains JSON, Markdown, completed raw pairs, and fixture-only logs for 30 days, including on failures. The job uses read-only permissions and does not pass CI credentials to measured processes.

## Testing & verification

The [first CI measurement](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/actions/runs/40393026370/job/121818688736) passed in 2m 12s, excluding queue time. The [retained artifact](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/actions/runs/40393026370/artifacts/12684934503) contains all 40 paired rounds, eight process-resource pairs, and all six expected files. Recomputing the report from the downloaded raw samples reproduces every metric exactly.

All ten timing metrics are within threshold. Small-source query median: 77.1 → 77.6 ms; large-source query: 80.3 → 78.8 ms; four concurrent queries: 150.0 → 148.6 ms. Median server CPU: 7.09 → 7.07 seconds; peak RSS: 520.59 → 522.19 MiB. Response sizes are unchanged, and logs contain no request errors.

CI compared base `c417ccfc` with PR merge `86527e53`, whose parents are that base and reviewed head `b2c8d743`. This validates the measurement pipeline against unchanged application code; it does not establish a new application speedup or lower model cost.

- [x] `npm test -- --run test/unit/mcp-query-benchmark.test.ts test/unit/build-web-optin.test.ts test/unit/shard-balance.test.ts`: 42 passed.
- [x] Native smoke run through complete MCP runtimes.
- [x] Eight-session identical-build control: all 40 paired rounds completed with no detected timing regression.
- [x] Original pre-optimization runtime at `34b873696b` is rejected for exceeding the 16,000-character source allowance.
- [x] `npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.test.json`, scoped ESLint/Prettier, and actionlint.
- [x] Fresh graph change analysis: 5 files, 113 symbols, low risk; no partial/truncated result.

One earlier identical-build control stopped at 39/40 rounds after native FTS returned `Interrupted` during concurrent requests. That failed experiment is retained locally; the successful repeat does not erase it. Partial responses still fail the CI harness, and uploaded logs preserve their diagnostics.

## Risk & rollout

This adds one Linux CI job with a 20-minute timeout. Generated-fixture results do not establish performance for every repository, embedding search, platform, or agent task. Pointwise timing intervals and shared-runner variability can leave individual comparisons inconclusive. Native search failures need investigation rather than retries until green.

## Checklist

- [x] PR body meets repo minimum length.
- [x] No agent instruction files, application modules, or dependencies changed.
- [x] No secrets, tokens, or machine-specific paths committed.

body:
Bumps [jsdom](https://github.com/jsdom/jsdom) from 26.1.0 to 30.1.1.
Release notes

Sourced from jsdom's releases.

v30.1.1

  • Fixed spurious window blur and focusout events and incorrect event.relatedTarget values when focusing an element after removing the previously focused element, which regressed in v30.1.0. (@​asamuzaK)
  • Fixed focus and blur behavior across frames, and focusing the document's viewport through document.documentElement.focus(). (@​asamuzaK)
  • Fixed focus targets removed or disabled by blur listeners becoming active, and text selections made by focus and blur listeners being overwritten. (@​asamuzaK)
  • Fixed element.focus() incorrectly focusing disabled form controls and <input type="hidden"> elements with tabindex="". (@​scttcper)
  • Fixed invalid style.setProperty() calls changing existing !important priorities, serialized styles, or mutation records. (@​FedgeNo)
  • Fixed !important handling when updating CSS longhands after shorthands, using variables or CSS-wide keywords, and assigning style properties directly. (@​FedgeNo)
  • Fixed <noscript> parsing with includeNodeLocations: true or inside frames to honor the runScripts option.
  • Fixed the storageQuota option being ignored by frames.
  • Fixed encoding detection of HTML and XML byte input to honor XML encoding declarations and detect UTF-16 without a byte order mark.
  • Fixed exceptions caused by truncated charset parameters in <meta> elements, and encoding detection incorrectly using incomplete <meta> tags. (@​FedgeNo)
  • Fixed XML serialization errors for namespaces named constructor, toString, __proto__, or "null", and incorrect reuse of namespace prefixes declared on sibling elements.
  • Fixed element.innerHTML and element.outerHTML in XML documents to reject invalid characters in attribute values and avoid stack overflows on large strings.
  • Fixed selector matching for :lang(), :nth-child(... of ...) after mutations, and :has() with duplicate IDs or nested logical pseudo-classes. (@​asamuzaK)

v30.1.0

jsdom is feeling the AGI!

This release is dedicated to @​scttcper, who unleashed @​codex upon jsdom and found tons of performance improvements. Along the way, he found and fixed many correctness issues as well.

We really appreciate his thoughtful PRs, which did a great job following the project's contribution guidelines, and were clearly human-curated, with their PR descriptions edited to be brief and respectful of the maintainers' time.

Thanks to @​scttcper, as well as all the other contributors of this release (most of whom were AI-assisted).

  • Added named access to elements on document, such as document.myForm for <form name="myForm">. (@​vojtisprime11)
  • Added QuotaExceededError, including its use for storage quota errors and oversized crypto.getRandomValues() requests.
  • Added support for the relaxed DOM naming rules when creating elements, attributes, and document types.
  • Improved performance of DOM construction, tree mutations, range operations, and live collection access, especially on large documents. (@​scttcper, @​erezrokah)
  • Improved performance of getComputedStyle(), style changes, and CSS serialization. (@​scttcper, @​jhult)
  • Improved performance of event dispatch, form control and label lookups, and updates to <select> elements and radio button groups. (@​scttcper)
  • Reduced memory use when creating and working with DOM nodes, attributes, event listeners, and mutation observers. (@​scttcper)
  • Changed window.close() to preserve access to the document and its DOM through retained references.
  • Fixed element.querySelectorAll() returning no matches when the first part of the selector matches the element itself, which regressed in v30.0.0. (@​asamuzaK)
  • Fixed case sensitivity in CSS attribute selectors, including selectors matching data-state="", title="", and other case-sensitive values. (@​asamuzaK)
  • Fixed document.querySelector() failing to find a matching element when an earlier element has the same ID but does not match the rest of the selector. (@​vojtisprime11)
  • Fixed :focus matching in shadow trees. (@​asamuzaK)
  • Fixed DOM insertion and replacement, including valid document.replaceChildren() calls, invalid document element and doctype placements, and mutations during element.replaceWith().
  • Fixed the ordering of script execution, custom element callbacks, iframe loading, and mutation observer notifications during DOM insertion, including in shadow trees.
  • Fixed queued events and navigation continuing after window.close() or iframe removal, and prevented new scripts, resource loads, timers, and animation frames from starting in destroyed documents. (@​scttcper)
  • Fixed parent documents waiting indefinitely for loading to finish when a child iframe removes itself during loading.
  • Fixed request cancellation across redirects, during pending requestInterceptor() callbacks, and when reusing an XMLHttpRequest after aborting it.
  • Fixed resource loading and JSDOM.fromURL() potentially hanging when response handling throws and response stream cleanup does not finish.
  • Fixed successful cached resource loads being treated as aborted.
  • Fixed getComputedStyle() and document.styleSheets using the wrong stylesheet order after inserting or updating <style> elements.
  • Fixed getComputedStyle() ignoring nested @import and @media rules in imported stylesheets, and returning stale results after imports finish loading.
  • Fixed style invalidation, stylesheet removal, and frame source updates in shadow trees.
  • Fixed repeated getComputedStyle() calls changing case-sensitive background URLs, and inconsistent resolution of border shorthands containing system colors. (@​scttcper)
  • Fixed computed border widths, including borderless elements incorrectly reporting 16px, which regressed in v30.0.0. (@​Alberto-BaseNet)
  • Fixed getComputedStyle() to resolve 'font-weight' keywords to numeric values. (@​tianrking)
  • Fixed getComputedStyle() to convert lengths to pixels inside CSS math functions containing percentages, and to resolve percentages in 'font-size' math functions. (@​soroushm)

... (truncated)

title: Feature: opt-in to index dot-directories such as .github/ (CI scripts are invisible to the graph)
body:
### Problem

`.github/` (and any other dot-directory) is never indexed, so code that lives there — typically CI/automation scripts under `.github/scripts/` — has no symbols and no edges in the graph. `detect_changes` then reports `changed_symbols: 0` for edits there, which looks safe but is just a blind spot.

Two independent layers cause this (checked on `gitnexus@1.6.12` and `1.6.13-rc.162`; both unchanged):

1. `dist/config/ignore-service.js` — the default ignore list contains `'.github'` (`// GitHub config, not code`). Since #771 this layer can be lifted with `!.github/` in `.gitnexusignore`.
2. `dist/core/ingestion/filesystem-walker.js` — the walker calls `glob('**/*', { cwd, nodir: true, dot: false, ignore })`, so dot-directories are never even listed. No ignore-file rule can re-include them, which is why `!.github/` has no effect in practice.

### Why it matters

Repos that keep real code under `.github/scripts/` (workflow helpers, policy gates, JSON/YAML checkers) lose the call edges from those scripts into the rest of the code. Indexing `.github` as a separate repo works as a stopgap, but it splits the graph, so calls from `.github` scripts into `src/` are lost.

### Proposed solution

Mirror the existing opt-in env vars (`GITNEXUS_INDEX_TEST_DIRS`, `GITNEXUS_NO_GITIGNORE`):

```bash
GITNEXUS_INDEX_DOT_DIRS=.github gitnexus analyze
```

- Comma-separated allow-list of dot-directory names; default unchanged (byte-identical behaviour when unset).
- When set, the walker lists those directories (e.g. by adding them to the glob patterns instead of flipping `dot: true` globally), and the effective ignore check skips `.github` for them.
- Deliberately narrow: `.git`, `.gitnexus`, `node_modules` etc. stay ignored; only the named dot-directories are unlocked.

Alternative: make a `!`-negation of a dot-path in `.gitnexusignore` also add that path to the walk (so no new env var is needed).

### Workaround today

`gitnexus analyze .github --skip-git --index-only --name <repo>-github` (separate index; graph is split).

Happy to send a PR if either approach sounds acceptable.

title: fix(mcp): shut down when the stdio parent exits
body:
## Summary

Stdio MCP now shuts down when its immediate parent dies, including when another process keeps stdin open. Previously, the server remained alive indefinitely because neither EOF nor a termination signal reached it.

## Motivation / context

The lifecycle investigation found that EOF before and after the handshake already shuts down correctly. Killing a launcher while retaining a separate stdin writer reproduced an orphan on current main; the new subprocess regression failed after ten seconds before this change and passes afterward.

Related: #3515, #3609

- [ ] `gitnexus-web/` (Vite / React UI)
- [ ] `.github/` (workflows, actions)
- [ ] `eval/` or other tooling
- [ ] Docs / agent config only

## Scope & constraints

**In scope**

- Immediate-parent death after stdio server startup, with graceful backend cleanup.
- Existing EOF shutdown and independent MCP clients remain covered.

**Explicitly out of scope / not done here**

- The reported OpenCode service remains alive after the app exits. Its duplicate spawning and ancestor lifetime require an affected-host reproduction; the linked issue should remain open.
- HTTP server lifetime and registry writes are unchanged.

## Implementation notes

The unreferenced one-second check detects reparenting or a missing parent PID and enters the existing idempotent shutdown path. Permission failures are inconclusive and leave the server running. The check stops during shutdown; the existing five-second cleanup fallback remains in place.

title: fix(impact): avoid upstream file seeds for private types
body:
## Summary

Upstream `impact` no longer borrows every importer of a file for a Class or Interface that is confirmed private to that file. This addresses reproduction 2 of #3602 while retaining the owning-file fallback for exported and uncertain types.

The decision lives on the language provider. Swift and Zig can certify the stored visibility flag directly. TypeScript and JavaScript also inspect retained file text: their graph nodes can store `isExported: false` for export clauses, default exports, exported type aliases, CommonJS exports and ambient declarations or global augmentations. These cases keep the file seed. Missing source, scripts, parse errors, truncated text and line comments in newline-normalized file content also retain it. Vue retains its existing fallback.

Downstream queries keep the owning-file seed because private types can still depend on imports. Constructor and typed-property expansion are unchanged. The existing seed query returns the export flag and, only for a false flag, retained file text; no database round trip is added. Query labels are selected from the two literal supported tables, and symbol IDs remain parameterized.

## Scope and compatibility

- Core impact traversal, an optional provider capability, and focused regression coverage.
- No schema change, dependency change, CLI/MCP response change, or required re-index. Existing indexes fall back conservatively when evidence is unavailable.
- Java package-private and Kotlin internal types retain file importers. Other providers without the capability retain existing behavior.
- Issue #3602 reproduction 1 (IMPORTS fan-out driving risk scores) remains out of scope. This does not add missing type-reference edges or distinguish imported names for exported types.

## Validation

- Real parsing → LadybugDB persistence → impact tests cover separate/default exports, CommonJS, ambient declarations, global augmentations, normalized comments and private TS/JS controls. All 40 focused tests pass, including exported type aliases and a value-alias control.
- Seeded database tests cover private-interface callers, exported/unknown flags, Java/Kotlin visibility and downstream dependencies.
- Reinstating the original unconditional JS/TS suppression makes the four exported-type regressions fail while the private controls pass. The downstream, normalized-comment and global-augmentation regressions were independently observed failing before their fixes.
- Both database suites are registered in the serial native project and the Windows/macOS test list.
- On current head `477a0b2f`, all 275 tests across eight suites passed, including the 40 PR-specific regressions and 64 Mermaid parser tests for the dependency update from main. A fresh locked install/build and both production/test typechecks passed. Lint and formatting are covered by CI.
- Full CI passed on `477a0b2f`: all 65 jobs completed without failures and all 12 required checks passed. The execution audit verified 30,560/30,560 core tests, 516/516 web tests and 1,320/1,320 evaluation tests, with zero unverified cases or failures: [run 40645268434](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/actions/runs/40645268434).

Refs #3602. This PR does not close the broader issue.

title: fix(scope): reduce memory for terminal import misses
body:
## Summary

Reduce scope-finalization memory when a named import is missing from a module that cannot re-export it. That lookup previously built transitive export tables for unrelated files; it now returns the same unresolved result without those allocations.

## Motivation / context

The published rc.164 code places `sr-extract-start` before `sr-post-nodeLookup`, so the reporter's last heap marker points into finalization after extraction. A synthetic workload reproduces a large allocation from this terminal import miss, but the reporter's private repository has not been tested with this patch.

Related: #3695 ([rc.164 heap logs](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/issues/3695#issuecomment-6441912400), [shard/stub follow-up](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/issues/3695#issuecomment-6442312977)).

## Areas touched

Also changes the shared scope finalizer in `gitnexus-shared/`.

## Scope & constraints

**In scope**

- Avoid unrelated transitive export tables for terminal misses, including filtered wildcard lookups.
- Expose finalization phase boundaries through the existing heap-debug settings.

**Explicitly out of scope / not done here**

- Establishing that the reporter's whole-repository OOM is resolved.

## Implementation notes

The existing re-export predicate identifies eligible target files once, ignoring unresolved and external targets just as the closure builder does. A target without a contributing module-level edge has no transitive exports, so an empty lookup preserves its result. Real re-export requests retain the existing ambiguity, cycle, and precedence behavior; a terminal miss does not cache an empty global result.

Heap probes remain opt-in through `GITNEXUS_DEBUG_HEAP` / `GITNEXUS_HEAP_PROBE_FILE`. The shared algorithm receives an optional phase callback and does not import Node diagnostics.

title: feat(ingestion): opt-in indexing of named dot directories (GITNEXUS_INCLUDE_DOT_DIRS)
body:
## What

Adds `GITNEXUS_INCLUDE_DOT_DIRS`, a comma-separated list of dot-directory names to index besides the default non-hidden file set, e.g. `GITNEXUS_INCLUDE_DOT_DIRS=.github,.scallywag`.

- Each entry must be a single plain segment starting with `.` (`.github`, not `a/.b`, `.a*` or `{...}`); invalid entries are dropped with a one-time warning. `.git`, `.svn`, `.hg` and `.bzr` are always refused.
- A listed directory is indexed at any depth. Hidden files and other dot directories inside it stay excluded, and `.gitignore` / `.gitnexusignore` still apply.
- The active list is recorded in the index coverage policy, so `status` / content-drift replays the same file set the index was built with (same approach as `GITNEXUS_MAX_FILE_SIZE`).
- `IncludeExtractor.discoverIndexableFiles` uses the same glob patterns as the walker through one shared helper (`indexableGlobPatterns`), so group `File:<rel>` UIDs keep matching graph File nodes.
- Unset or empty means no change in behaviour.

## Why narrower than #2867

#2867 (`GITNEXUS_INDEX_HIDDEN`) turns on every hidden path. That pulls in `.env*`, `.npmrc`, editor and tool caches, which can hold secrets and noise. This change lets a repo name only the directories that hold real source, such as `.github/` workflows and scripts (#3736) or a project's own config-as-code directory, while `.env` and other hidden files stay out. Related: #2707 (this covers the hidden-directory half, not extensionless shebang scripts).

## Tests

- `test/unit/include-dot-dirs.test.ts`: parsing, validation, refusal, warn-once, pattern building.
- `test/integration/filesystem-walker.test.ts`: listed directory indexed at root and nested; unlisted dot dirs and hidden files inside a listed dir stay out; ignore rules still apply.

body:
Bumps the uv group with 2 updates in the /eval directory: [dnspython](https://github.com/rthalley/dnspython) and [litellm](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm). Updates `dnspython` from 2.8.0 to 2.9.0
Release notes

Sourced from dnspython's releases.

dnspython 2.9.0

This release fixes a potential excessive CPU consumption issue. Thanks to Evgenios Gkritsis, Constantinos Patsakis, and George Stergiopoulos, for discovering and reporting this issue.

See What's New for details.

The minimum supported version of Python is 3.11.

My thanks to the many people who have contributed to this release. Also thanks to my co-maintainers: Nicki Křížek, Petr Špaček, and Brian Wellington.

This release was published to PyPI using Trusted Publishing.

Changelog

Sourced from dnspython's changelog.

2.9.0

  • Decompression chain length is limited to 16. Prior to this change, a maliciously crafted DNS message could cause dns.name.from_wire_parser() to use excessive CPU for DNS name decompression. Applications which processed untrusted DNS wire form messages with dnspython could be degraded or DoS'd by the extra CPU use required.

    Thanks to Evgenios Gkritsis, Constantinos Patsakis, and George Stergiopoulos for finding and reporting this issue.

    See https://github.com/rthalley/dnspython/security/advisories/GHSA-45c3-73f7-pv4m

  • Httpx2 has replaced httpx for HTTPS TCP connections.

  • The minimum supported Python version is now 3.11.

  • DNSSEC now supports ML-DSA-44, a post-quantum signature algorithm.

  • The NSEC3 Next Hashed Owner Name in presentation format is now decoded as base32hex (RFC 5155 Section 1.3, RFC 4648 Extended Hex Alphabet). The letters W, X, Y, and Z are not in that alphabet; they used to be accepted and silently decoded to a different owner name, so to_text of the result did not match the input. They are now rejected.

  • The NID and L64 node/locator ids in presentation format are now rejected when a group contains anything other than hex digits. A sign or underscore, which int() silently accepts, produced a record whose text form did not parse back the same way (RFC 6742).

  • Rdata of a known type in the generic \# syntax, such as an NS record in a zone file, no longer fails to parse when it contains a name under the origin. Its names are relativized as in the type's own text form.

  • The SVCB and HTTPS ech parameter value must now be an ECHConfigList with a correct length prefix and at least 4 octets of content (RFC 9848, RFC 9849). The individual ECHConfig structures are not checked.

  • SVCB and HTTPS SvcParamKeys in presentation format, including those listed in mandatory, must now be spelled as RFC 9460 requires: 1-63 lowercase letters, digits, or hyphens. Uppercase keys such as ALPN and keys with underscores such as no_default_alpn are rejected.

  • SVCB and HTTPS presentation format parsing now follows the escaping rules of RFC 9460. SvcParamKeys may not contain escapes (e.g. \097lpn=h2), and in comma-separated values (alpn, docpath) only \, and \\ are valid escapes after character-string decoding (e.g. alpn="h2\\x" is rejected).

feat(ci): rebalance test shards from recorded timings
body:
## Summary

CI test shards now rebalance automatically from recorded runtimes using [vitest-shard-balancer](https://github.com/sidorovpavel/vitest-shard-balancer). Timing history stays in GitHub Actions storage, so rebalancing no longer requires commits to per-file weight tables.

## Motivation / context

Test costs change as the suite grows. Windows, macOS, and coverage runs now learn separate profiles, replacing the manually maintained native weights.

## Areas touched

- [x] `gitnexus/` (test infrastructure)
- [ ] `gitnexus-web/`
- [x] `.github/`
- [x] `eval/` or other tooling
- [ ] Docs / agent config only

## Scope & constraints

**In scope**

- Automatic duration-based assignment for the existing native and coverage matrices.
- One frozen timing snapshot per run, reused by every shard and retry.
- History promotion after complete successful test cohorts on `main`.

**Explicitly out of scope / not done here**

- Changing shard counts, watchdogs, native serialization, or completeness requirements.
- Removing scenario-map tooling's separate weighting helper.

## Implementation notes

The package handles partitioning and smoothing. Adapters preserve the native subset, reject incomplete merged reports, retain prior costs for skipped modules, and provide generic cold-start estimates. Cold estimates use a consistent scale so ordinary files spread across all coverage shards. Native blobs merge on their originating OS. The existing required `CI Gate` covers the new merge jobs.

Only the first attempt creates the timing snapshot. Retries must restore it; a failed download cannot replace it with newer history. If the artifact was never uploaded, deleted, or expired, trigger a fresh workflow run with a new commit. `TESTING.md` documents reproduction and recovery; the CLI reference lists `GITNEXUS_SHARD_PROFILE`.

## Testing & verification

- [x] 54 focused tests across seven suites, including real Vitest shards, JSON receipts, blob merging, rejection of a missing shard without changing history, and a cold-start load regression that failed before the fix.
- [x] 193 workflow-contract tests, including a regression that failed before the retry immutability fix.
- [x] Core build, source/test TypeScript checks, ESLint, changed-file formatting, actionlint, and `git diff --check`.
- [x] [Final hosted CI](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/actions/runs/40670511095): all eight coverage shards, all 22 Windows/macOS shards, timing merges, and execution completeness. All 12 required checks pass; the audit verifies 30,559 core, 516 web, and 1,321 evaluation cases with zero failures or unverified cases.

Local full-suite validation was interrupted after the packaged tree-sitter prebuild could not load because this container lacks `GLIBCXX_3.4.31`. The broader local evaluation run passed 1,292 tests and skipped 26; two historical-oracle cases failed on parser type definitions in their fixture checkout. Hosted CI completed successfully on this commit.

The seven-lane review covered complete partitions, retry immutability, timing promotion, native execution, permissions, and documentation. Confirmed allocation and documentation findings are fixed; the intermittent Windows test failure is recorded below. Graph comparison remains partial for the deleted allocator/test and comment-only Vitest config; pre-edit impacts and direct reference checks cover those paths.

## Risk & rollout

Hosted validation is complete; this PR remains unmerged. Timing-cache promotion runs only after a successful `main` test run and therefore cannot execute before merge. Cache expiry uses the cold-start estimate. The corrected cold-start run passed all eight coverage shards; its longest test step took 16.45 minutes under the unchanged 25-minute job limit. Learned profiles contain 1,401 coverage, 164 Windows, and 169 macOS entries. Steady-state speedup from learned history has not been measured. Reverting the PR restores the previous allocator; timing artifacts require no application-data migration.

One Windows case in `embedding-input-isolation.test.ts` [timed out at 120 seconds and its native worker crashed](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/actions/runs/40670511095/job/122755894612). One [diagnostic retry on the unchanged commit](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/actions/runs/40670511095/job/122770332599) passed the case in 61.3 seconds, with zero execution errors. An earlier [main-branch job](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/actions/runs/40644867372/job/122671376244) shows the same timeout/crash pattern in another native test. The underlying cause remains unresolved; this is a CI reliability follow-up, not a claimed fix. No timeout or assertion was weakened. The frozen input artifact retained its original creation and update timestamp during the retry.

## Checklist

- [x] PR body meets repo minimum length.
- [x] No agent instruction files changed; release-owned changelog untouched.
- [x] No secrets, tokens, or machine-specific paths committed.

title: fix(lbug): guard read queries against runaway native memory (#3696)
body:
## Summary

Mitigate runaway native allocations during pooled graph reads, following the 184 GB upstream-impact report in #3696. The underlying query explosion has not been reproduced; this PR adds containment and diagnostics and does not close that issue.

- Check process RSS at read start/end and every 200 ms during a read. On macOS, queries lasting at least one second also sample physical footprint, at most once per second without overlapping subprocesses. A late sample is ignored when every query present at sampling has ended.
- Exit with code 70 and a synchronous stderr diagnostic when the budget is exceeded. The default is max(8 GiB, 25% of effective RAM), capped at 75% of effective RAM; a reported runtime/container constraint lowers effective RAM. GITNEXUS_QUERY_MAX_RSS_MB overrides the budget in MiB; 0 disables it, and invalid or overflowing values use the default.
- Keep memory monitoring, cursors, and pool connections owned by native work until it settles, even after the caller's 30-second deadline. That deadline covers prepare, execution, and row materialization. Expired requests do not start the next native phase; timed-out connections cannot be reused by another query while still busy.
- Cap each impact BFS frontier at 100,000 relationship rows plus one sentinel. A capped walk stops and reports partial: true. Both risk and riskSharedAxes retain proven HIGH/CRITICAL scores; LOW/MEDIUM becomes UNKNOWN. Both directions are covered.
- GITNEXUS_QUERY_TRACE=1 reports duration, rows, and sampled memory on stderr. Bound parameters are omitted. Document configuration, recovery, and sampling limitations in the CLI reference and runbook.

- Fix the CI startup blocker inherited from main: fork approval counts as attempt 2 despite running zero jobs. Initialize the timing snapshot only after checking that the first attempt required approval and ran no jobs; real retries still require the frozen snapshot.

## Validation

- Five guard regression cases, three native-lifetime cases, and two capped shared-risk assertions failed before the fixes and pass afterward.
- 402 focused tests passed on the final commit across 11 files, including all eight timed-out connections remaining unavailable until native completion and skipped native phases after the deadline.
- The final native pool suite passed 22 tests, including a child process proving exit code 70, synchronous diagnostics, and omission of bound parameter values. Nine recovery tests also passed on both the PR and main.
- All 201 workflow-contract tests, Ruff, and actionlint passed. The approval bootstrap was also checked against the failed run’s actual GitHub API response.
- Production and test TypeScript checks, formatting, diff checks, and ESLint passed with zero lint errors. Existing lint warnings remain.
- A fresh 5,000-read benchmark on the final commit measured median 157 microseconds/read versus 149 on main for tiny parameterized reads, with overlapping trial ranges and identical results. The disabled guard fast path reduced its isolated overhead from about 6.9 to 3.6 microseconds/read.
- Graph change analysis against current main covered all 13 changed files and 194 symbols. The all-changes merge comparison separately reports known unmapped deletions/comment-only configuration from the main-branch update; it is not represented as a clean graph result.
- The long local run finished with 30,496 passes, six failures, and 89 skips. Two failures were the risk assertions fixed while that run was active; four others passed fresh isolated PR replays. The indexing and recovery cases also passed on main. This mixed-revision run is not a claimed clean final-commit pass.
- Exact-commit CI is running: https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/actions/runs/40694037926

## Compatibility and limits

No schema, dependency, reindex, or write-path change. Normal query results and uncapped impact results are preserved. The main-branch merge brings in the already-merged CI shard-balancing change.

The memory limit is process-wide: exit 70 interrupts all requests in that CLI/MCP/HTTP process. Sampling cannot guarantee a hard OS memory bound or prevent an allocation burst between samples. An unavailable macOS footprint command falls back to RSS, and the row cap does not bound database intermediate allocations. Query traces include query text and should be inspected before sharing.

One initial concurrent local microbenchmark attempt returned a native Interrupted error; subsequent 1,000- and 5,000-read runs passed. Its cause remains unlocalized. No timeout or assertion was weakened to obtain passing validation.

Refs #3696.

The impact is concentrated in the `Local` module, especially `LocalBackend`, `_runImpactBFS`, and `QUERY_CHAIN_BFS_CONCURRENCY`, alongside `executeParameterized` and `closeLbug` in `gitnexus/src/core/lbug/pool-adapter.ts` and `gitnexus/src/core/lbug/query-memory-guard.ts`. title: feat(go): index Gin and Echo routes through configured aliases
body:
Go services that register routes through an engine alias in an unvendored dependency could produce no Route nodes, and adapter-wrapped handlers could lose their HANDLES_ROUTE edges. This adds explicit `goRouterAliases` and `goHandlerWrappers` configuration, with `GITNEXUS_RC` for a configuration file outside the checkout.

The Go provider collects direct and alias registrations together through `extractRouteFacts`, sharing imports, lexical bindings, handler hints, and one memoized receiver-prefix walk per function. `resolveRouteFacts` uses the existing framework descriptors for handler position and provenance. Go owns alias validation, accepting Unicode type names while rejecting reserved words and the blank identifier. External-config diagnostics name the supplied file. CLI/watch, analysis, and provider hooks pass one internal `RouteHookConfig` object.

Workers collect configuration-free facts. The main thread applies configuration, so changing or removing aliases or wrappers rebuilds route evidence while allowing unchanged parser output to be reused. Tests preserve lexical shadowing, ambiguous-prefix rejection, and the existing configured-route winner when a direct registration has the same URL. Handler unwrapping remains in Go until another provider needs it.

Watch mode observes external-config edits, atomic replacement, and symlink target changes, and rereads configuration after watcher startup. The alias limit applies before deduplication.

## Performance guard

`gitnexus/bench/go-route-facts/measure.js` and its reviewed `baseline.json` replace the one-off comparison script. The existing `.github/workflows/ci-tests.yml` benchmark job runs the check and uploads the full JSON measurements.

Five workloads cover no routes, direct Gin routes, wrapped alias routes, mixed direct/alias routes, and a function whose unrelated parameter count grows together with its registrations. Each runs at 128, 512, and 2,048 inputs. The harness measures production fact collection and JSON-roundtripped fact replay, excluding parsing and serialization from timings. Eight warmups precede seven interleaved adaptive batches; comparisons use median per-call times.

Every adjacent 4× pair and the full 16× range must stay within 1.5× normalized linear time for collection and replay, and 1.15× for serialized bytes. Independent route assertions plus committed counts and SHA-256 fingerprints prevent missing or altered output from appearing as a speedup. This covers collector/replay scaling, not whole-repository ingestion or final handler-symbol resolution.

Three local check runs passed. Their worst normalized factors were 1.209 for collection, 1.133 for replay, and 1.004 for serialized bytes. Negative controls rejected malformed/incomplete baselines, a no-op collector, and injected quadratic collection work (5.774× normalized growth over the full range).

```sh
cd gitnexus
node --expose-gc --import tsx bench/go-route-facts/measure.js --check --output go-route-facts.json
```

## Validation

- Benchmark follow-up: 265 focused tests passed; source typecheck, JavaScript syntax, formatting, ESLint, and workflow concurrency checks passed. Baseline and benchmark negative controls passed as described above.
- 367 focused tests passed with an ambient external config set, on the combined head after retaining the incoming merge from `main`. Coverage includes real external-config watchers, the actual server launcher and forked worker, Go route/cache behavior, and namespace target caching.
- Broad core validation: 31,383 passed and 103 skipped across four shards. All nine initial failures passed targeted reruns: seven depended on temporary checkout/config paths; two encountered changing compiled artifacts and passed with isolated runtimes. The 40-case incremental orchestration file also completed; its final case was rerun separately to capture a result after the original runner was stopped. This broad run preceded the incoming `main` merge; the combined head received the focused checks above.
- All 230 Go fixture files matched the original build across 690 configuration cases in the earlier fixture-parity check.
- Build, source and test TypeScript checks, formatting, and ESLint passed (no lint errors). The duplicate-test scan found no new duplication.

Existing parser identity invalidation handles the changed fact shape. Run `gitnexus analyze` after upgrading. The public JSON configuration keys are unchanged.

title: chore(deps)(deps-dev): bump jsdom from 30.1.1 to 30.1.3 in /gitnexus
body:
Bumps [jsdom](https://github.com/jsdom/jsdom) from 30.1.1 to 30.1.3.
Release notes

Sourced from jsdom's releases.

v30.1.3

  • Improved performance of getComputedStyle() and computed CSS property reads, including with stylesheets containing attribute selectors. (@​scttcper, @​asamuzaK)
  • Fixed slowdowns when focusing elements and running interaction tests, which regressed in v30.1.2. (@​scttcper)
  • Fixed XMLHttpRequest reusing credentials supplied to xhr.open() after cross-origin redirects, including in response to authentication challenges from the destination.
  • Fixed XMLHttpRequest incorrectly sending and accepting cookies after cross-origin redirects back to the document's origin when xhr.withCredentials is false.
  • Fixed exceptions from malformed CSS math functions, such as calc(0px - @submenu_space), while parsing documents, stylesheets, and style declarations. (@​rnavarro)
  • Fixed getComputedStyle() ignoring style rules nested inside multiple @media rules.
  • Fixed CSS shorthands overwriting longhands with higher priority or specificity during style computation, including declarations containing CSS variables.
  • Fixed getComputedStyle() returning unresolved or inconsistent shorthand values, including for 'background', 'border', 'flex', 'font', 'margin', and 'padding', and incorrect shorthand defaults and inheritance.
  • Fixed computed background positions to resolve font-relative lengths using the final font size and handle multiple image layers correctly.
  • Fixed computed 'color' values depending on property read order, including unresolved color-mix() results, which regressed in v29.0.2.
  • Fixed currentcolor border colors incorrectly becoming transparent when 'color' uses light-dark() or relative color syntax.
  • Fixed CSS calculations that reduce to a percentage incorrectly producing pixel values, which regressed in v30.0.0.
  • Fixed numeric font weights in the 'font' shorthand incorrectly setting 'line-height'.
  • Fixed selector matching involving XML namespaces, and selectors such as [data-a|=""] failing to match empty values and values beginning with -. (@​asamuzaK)

v30.1.2

  • Updated URLs to support Unicode v18.0.0 in internationalized domain names.
  • Reduced package size and memory use for CSS property definitions. (@​scttcper)
  • Fixed severe slowdowns when building large DOM trees, including SVG charts with D3, which regressed in v30.1.0. (@​cmdcolin)
  • Fixed exponentially slow reads of empty inherited CSS custom properties in deeply nested documents, and custom properties incorrectly inheriting past an initial reset. (@​scttcper)
  • Fixed getComputedStyle() returning stale results after editing stylesheet declarations, selectors, or media queries, including in imported stylesheets.
  • Fixed selector matching and computed styles after changes to form control checkedness, indeterminacy, selection, values, and validity, including during form resets and canceled clicks.
  • Fixed computed styles for :focus, :focus-visible, :focus-within, and selectors containing them after focus changes, including inside focus and blur listeners. (@​asamuzaK)
  • Fixed element.focus() incorrectly focusing elements hidden by 'display', including through shadow hosts and slots, and elements excluded by shadow DOM slot assignment. (@​asamuzaK)
  • Fixed getComputedStyle() throwing for elements without inline-style support, including XML and MathML elements.
  • Fixed a memory leak where stylesheet parsing retained the last parsed stylesheet's window after window.close().
  • Fixed memory growth from long-lived MutationObserver instances retaining bookkeeping for garbage-collected nodes. (@​scttcper)
  • Fixed retained select.selectedOptions collections becoming stale after selection changes and form resets.
  • Fixed rejection of negative CSS sizing values, including for 'min-width', 'min-height', 'max-width', and 'max-height', which regressed in v30.1.0.
  • Fixed handling of deeply nested color-mix() expressions, including exceptions during color resolution. (@​asamuzaK)

  • a3ee786 Cascade computed style properties on demand

With the ELK layout, an edge from a node that a subgraph feeds back into that subgraph is now routed downstream instead of around the subgraph. This changes the layout of existing ELK diagrams that contain such edges; set elk.orientFeedbackEdges: false to keep the previous routing.

  • #8250 fd4f5f2 Thanks @​kartben! - feat: add a bitOrder option to packet diagrams. It defaults to ascending, which is the current behaviour, and descending mirrors every row so it reads from that row's highest bit down to its lowest. title: feat(eval): add opt-in baseline_cli arm to measure MCP catalog cost
body:
## Summary

Adds an opt-in `baseline_cli` arm to `eval/workflow_bench`. It gives the agent the same read-only GitNexus tools as `baseline` through a `gitnexus` shell command instead of MCP, so no tool catalog enters the model context. The point is to measure how much of the MCP arm's extra cost the catalog accounts for. The Release evaluation workflow runs the arm only when it is dispatched with `cli_arm: true`.

## Motivation / context

All six successful Release evaluations from Oct 10–26 show the same pattern: MCP `baseline` solves exactly as many tasks as `baseline_nomcp` (paired delta +0) and costs **+22% to +43%** more. In the token breakdown, output tokens are flat across arms. Nearly all of the extra is **cache-read input**, about +35% (~3.4M → ~4.5M per cell at xhigh). That is the context being re-sent each turn, so cost scales with context size × turns.

The tool catalog is the one thing the MCP arm adds to the context on every turn, whether or not a tool is called. It was about 84 KB before #3739 and about 70 KB after. Over ~70 turns, a catalog of that size is roughly the size of the whole gap. Large tool results and extra verification turns also contribute. This arm separates those causes:

- `baseline_cli` vs `baseline`: the catalog's share. Tool output is byte-identical, because it is the same server.
- `baseline_cli` vs `baseline_nomcp`: what remains (payload size, extra turns).

## Scope & constraints

**In scope**

Each invocation opens one MCP session on the cell's isolated socket (`/run/gitnexus-mcp.sock`) and makes one `tools/call`. title: perf(scope): reduce post-resolution memory overhead
body:
Large repositories retain avoidable call-site data after `sr-post-resolve`: the deferred-call collector builds a signature object and position key for every ordinary call even when there are no indirect invokes, and subsequent emit passes copy the whole handled-site set twice.

Collect signatures only for argument facts that the indirect-call solver consumes, skip the solver when it has no canonical invokes, and extend one handled-site set after its earlier readers finish. Preserve overload evidence for direct calls that feed callbacks in other files. Add opt-in `sr-emit-*` heap/timing checkpoints to distinguish receiver resolution, replay, reference/property emission, callable flow and provider hooks.

The existing `scope-resolution-benchmark` CI job runs the two new probes once alongside its all-language checks. `--check` rejects unused ordinary-call signatures and dense Java graph changes. Their measurements join the existing artifact; setup, runner, artifact upload and required-check gate are reused. Heap and timing remain reported measurements, without absolute thresholds.

Measurements on Node 22.23.3, Linux:

| Check | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 500,000 ordinary calls: median retained collector overhead, 3 fresh processes | 90.29 MiB | 0.08 MiB |
| Same input, 160 MiB old-space limit | OOM, exit 134 | Completes |
| Dense Java: 300 files, 60,000 receiver calls | 66,300 nodes / 126,600 relationships | Identical full graph fingerprint |
| Existing benchmark: 18 languages, 100 and 1,000 entities, 3 trials each | Committed baselines | All 36 workloads match; binding counts within budget |

Reproduction commands and limits are in `gitnexus/bench/scope-resolution/README.md`. The dense Java probe uses the in-memory test graph, so it does not measure the CLI streaming sink. These synthetic probes establish a concrete allocation defect; they do not reproduce the reporter's complete private workload or guarantee that it fits in 3.6 GB RAM. Keep #3695 open for the next RC retest.

Local validation:

Eleven initial environment-only failures were resolved by rerunning setup fixtures without inherited `CODEX_HOME` and running clone-root tests outside `/tmp`; all 112 tests in those four files pass. No tests were omitted or duplicated in the audit.

- Both new probe checks pass. Negative checks reject the pre-fix collector's 500,000 retained signatures and an incorrect dense Java graph baseline.
