title: fix(ingestion): drop member edges to owners the file never emitted
body:
## Summary

Repair `HAS_METHOD` / `HAS_PROPERTY` edges whose same-file owner was never emitted by the parser. The worker removes the invalid edge and attaches its emitted member to the File with a deduplicated `DEFINES` edge. This prevents the native COPY failures and silent edge loss reported in #3747.

Closes #3747

## Motivation / context

Owner IDs come from syntax, while node labels come from query captures. The issue's chained `z.object(...).refine(...)` declaration emits a Function but names a Const owner; an ambient TypeScript module names a Trait owner that no capture emits. Both produced invalid foreign-key references.

The guard operates on each file's appended node/relationship slice. It settles at the next file boundary and in `processFileGroup`'s `finally`, including when a provider throws and `processBatch` returns partial results. Cross-file owners, node IDs, symbol owner IDs, schema, and resolution contracts are preserved. Parser-cache identity automatically includes the new helper.

## Areas touched

- [x] `gitnexus/` (CLI/core ingestion, tests, benchmark)
- [ ] `gitnexus-web/`
- [ ] `.github/`
- [ ] `eval/`

## Review follow-up

- Register the native COPY regression in the serialized `lbug-db` project and the Windows/macOS test subset.
- Add a real worker/provider exception regression. It verifies that the remaining file is skipped and the partially parsed member still receives `DEFINES`.
- Add deterministic tests against rescanning earlier files and a standalone scaling benchmark.
- Independent correctness, adversarial, reliability, standards, testing, security, and simplicity reviews found no remaining production-code defect. The implementation was retained after the simplicity review.

Two late automated findings were checked against the production repair path and classified as false positives:

- [Benchmark expected edge](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/pull/3767#discussion_r4429343357): each dangling fixture emits its target node. The guard creates a File → member `DEFINES` edge when removing its invalid owner edge, so expecting that fallback edge is correct. All 84 benchmark cases and seven prefix cases already verify exact output relationships.
- [Unit-test cardinality](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/pull/3767#discussion_r4429343367): four members retain existing definitions and the other four receive fallback definitions; duplicate owner edges are discarded. The correct count is eight definitions per file plus the prefix edge. All three scaling tests passed again on the unchanged candidate.

Neither finding requires a code change.

## Scaling evidence

Run from `gitnexus/`:

```bash
node --expose-gc --import tsx scripts/owner-edge-guard-scaling.ts > owner-edge-scaling.json
```

Measured on Node 22.23.3, Linux x64, Intel i9-12900K. The harness covers six shapes, one-file and many-file distributions, seven sizes from 1,024 to 65,536 members, and a separate growing-prefix sweep. Each timing case uses three warmups and eleven fresh-fixture samples. Fixture construction, assertions, instrumentation, and explicit GC are outside the timed region; each result is checked.

| Shape | Many-file log-log slope | Median at 65,536 members |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| No member edges | 1.090 | 4.42 ms |
| Valid owners | 1.026 | 18.06 ms |
| Dangling owners | 1.058 | 39.05 ms |
| Existing DEFINES | 1.010 | 35.79 ms |
| Duplicate dangling edges | 1.085 | 50.69 ms |
| Owner emitted last | 1.020 | 19.49 ms |

Every case satisfied at most N node reads, 3E relationship reads, and E compaction writes, with zero indexed accesses to previous file slices. With 16 active members and previous rows growing from 2,048 to 131,072, work stayed at 64 reads / 16 writes; median time was 25.9–32.6 microseconds.

This establishes O(F + N + E) row work for fixed identifier lengths and average Set costs, with live scratch space bounded by the largest active file (delayed garbage collection is separate). Multi-file timings are consistent with near-linear scaling. Giant single-file timings are less uniform: slopes ranged 0.797–1.178, and the duplicate-heavy case grew 133x in time for 64x rows (0.532–70.860 ms). These are guard measurements, not an end-to-end indexing throughput claim. Whole-harness maxRSS was 348 MiB and includes fixtures and assertions.

The existing [CI scope-resolution benchmark](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/actions/runs/41143519191/job/124363138541) also measured 100 → 1,000 entities across 18 languages (three repetitions), matching all 36 graph/binding baselines. Its Go and PHP resolver times grew approximately 59x and 49x for 10x entities; their 99.02x module-binding-count growth matches the unchanged main baseline. Matching graph/binding baselines establishes semantic consistency, not unchanged runtime versus main. The linear-work claim here is specific to the owner-edge guard; whole-index linearity remains unestablished.

## Testing & verification

From `gitnexus/`:

```bash
npm run build
npx tsc --noEmit
npm run typecheck:tests
npx vitest run test/unit/owner-edge-guard.test.ts test/unit/owner-edge-guard-scaling.test.ts test/integration/dangling-owner-edges.test.ts test/unit/parse-cache-identity.test.ts test/unit/parse-cache-input-coverage.test.ts
npm test -- --shard=1/4 --maxWorkers=2
# Repeat for shards 2/4, 3/4, and 4/4.
npm run test:dupes -- --base origin/main
```

- Build and production/test typechecks pass; changed files pass formatting and ESLint (existing parser warnings remain).
- Real worker/provider failure test passes. Removing only the production `finally` settlement makes it fail with the original dangling `HAS_METHOD` edge; the compiled worker was restored afterward.
- Cold-to-warm analysis of both repro shapes: 2 reparsed / 0 hits → 0 reparsed / 2 hits. Both runs persist identical 7-node / 5-edge graphs, including both fallback edges; both durable ParsedFile shard keys and parser identity match, with no incomplete reasons.
- All 84 scaling cases and seven prefix cases pass correctness and operation-bound checks, including 1,274 warmup/measured invocations.
- Full local suite completed against the exact committed tree: 31,048 tests across 1,431 disjoint files; 30,946 passed, 91 skipped, and 11 environment-dependent assertions initially failed. All 109 tests in the four affected files pass on corrected-environment reruns; no candidate-specific failure remains.
- All 12 required GitHub checks pass for `1a73c1bda19674f18e705f6ac0ee4eb11ac0e4df`, including CI Gate, coverage aggregation, and the every-test-executed gate. All eight Linux coverage shards and all eleven Windows and eleven macOS platform shards passed. [Final-head CI run](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/actions/runs/41143519191).

Local environment exceptions, independently checked against unchanged main sources:

- Setup-skills (2 assertions) and setup unit tests (2): inherited `CODEX_HOME` overrode temporary HOME. Both entire suites pass with `env -u CODEX_HOME` (6 + 56 tests).
- Server analysis (1 assertion): the test assumes the configured home contains `.gitnexus`; all 5 tests pass with a fresh isolated home using that conventional basename.

The raw suite failures are retained in the validation accounting; no tests or production code were changed to hide them.

feat(eval): paired DeepSWE runs, baseline vs GitNexus CLI, with Claude Code on a dedicated EC2
body:
## Summary

Adds `eval/deepswe/`, a paired **baseline vs GitNexus CLI** comparison on [DeepSWE](https://deepswe.datacurve.ai/) (113 long-horizon tasks, 91 repos, 5 languages). It runs with the benchmark's own harness ([pier](https://github.com/datacurve-ai/pier)) and Claude Code, on a dedicated EC2 instance separate from the release-evaluation runner.

## Motivation / context

The release-evaluation tasks are small, single-repo changes. On those, GitNexus adds steps without replacing exploration (Discussion #3493; the `baseline_cli` arm from #3762). DeepSWE solutions need about 5.5x more code than SWE-bench Pro. It is a fairer test of whether the graph pays off on multi-file work.

## Areas touched

- [ ] `gitnexus/` (CLI / core / MCP server)
- [ ] `gitnexus-web/` (Vite / React UI)
- [ ] `.github/` (workflows, actions)
- [x] `eval/` or other tooling
- [ ] Docs / agent config only (`AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `.cursor/`, `llms.txt`, etc.)

## Scope & constraints

**In scope**

- `prepare.py` copies one seeded subset per arm.
  - `baseline` is the unchanged task.
  - `gitnexus` builds `FROM` the task's prebuilt image, then:
    - adds a checksum-verified Node 22.18 in `/opt`;
    - installs the gitnexus tarball built from this checkout;
    - adds a `/usr/local/bin/gitnexus` wrapper, leaving PATH alone so a task's own `node`/`npm` stay first;
    - runs `gitnexus analyze --index-only`.
  - The build fails if indexing changed `git status`, which would leak into the graded patch.
  - Tasks are renamed `-gitnexus` so pier's per-task image tag never reuses a baseline image.
  - The instruction gets the CLI form of GitNexus's shipped agent rules (`--guidance product`, the default). `--guidance optional` gives a plain command list for an ablation.
- `report.py` pairs pier trials by task id and attempt.
  - Deltas use only pairs graded in both arms with the metric measured in both.
  - Ungraded trials (including the grader's `-1` crash sentinel), interrupted sweeps, unbilled trials and agent errors are listed as problems.
  - A trial that hit the cost cap is still graded on its patch, so expensive failures are not dropped.
- `run.sh` does the following:
  - Pins `deep-swe@0b9fabbb`, `pier 0.3.1` and Claude Code `2.1.214` (the release evaluation's CLI).
  - Builds the package with the CI pack job's steps.
  - Runs both arms.
  - Writes `deepswe-comparison.{md,json}`.
- **Claude Code toolset:**
  - Only `Read`/`Edit`/`Write`/`Bash`, matching the release evaluation's single-agent toolset.
  - pier's forced background-task env is switched off.
- **Model access:**
  - `gpt-5.6-sol` (default) goes through a LiteLLM gateway container, routed like `workflow_bench.model_gateway`: Anthropic Messages to OpenAI Responses, with LiteLLM pinned to `eval/uv.lock`.
  - The gateway listens on host port 80, because pier's egress proxy only allows 80 and 443. Trials reach it as `host.docker.internal` or the EC2 private DNS name.
  - `anthropic/` models use `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` directly.
  - `--agent mini-swe-agent`, the leaderboard's agent, also works.
- `ec2/launch.sh` + `ec2/bootstrap.sh`:
  - Start Ubuntu 24.04 on an `m7i.4xlarge` with 400 GB gp3, tagged `purpose=gitnexus-deepswe`.
  - Open SSH to the caller's IP only and use IMDSv2.
  - Stop the instance after `--max-hours`.
  - Never put a model key in user-data.

**Explicitly out of scope / not done here**

- No change to `gitnexus/`, the release gate, `workflow_bench`, or any workflow. This is run by hand, not from CI.
- No MCP arm and no grep-augmentation arm (pier's Claude Code supports MCP servers; that is a follow-up).
- Only a 5-task pilot so far (below). A larger sample, with repeated attempts, is the next run.

## Implementation notes

Two problems turned up in smoke testing and are fixed here:

1. **Runaway background agents.** pier forces `ENABLE_BACKGROUND_TASKS=1` / `FORCE_AUTO_BACKGROUND_TASKS=1` for Claude Code. The first baseline trial fanned out into 237 background agents. Its main session stopped at the $3 `--max-budget-usd` cap, but the background work kept going, to $40.82 by Claude Code's own accounting, while pier reported $3.04. Disallowing the agent and task tools and overriding that env fixed it: each session now has one result, and its `modelUsage` cost equals the reported cost.
2. **Guidance.** With a note that only listed the commands as optional, the GitNexus agent never called `gitnexus`. With the product rules it ran `query` ×2, `impact` ×2 and `detect-changes` ×1.

Costs come from Claude Code's per-session `total_cost_usd`. Through the gateway that is Claude Code's price table applied to a non-Claude model: consistent across arms, but not the provider's invoice.

## Testing & verification

- [x] `cd eval && uv run --locked --extra dev python -m pytest tests/test_deepswe.py`: 11 passed on Windows and in Ubuntu 24.04 (Python 3.12).
- [x] `ruff check deepswe tests/test_deepswe.py`, plus `shellcheck -S warning` on `run.sh` and `ec2/*.sh`.
- [x] Derived image built for `abs-module-cache-flags` in 148 s (the index took 17 s). Inside it, with `docker run --network none`, `gitnexus query`, `impact` and `detect-changes` answer in 0.3–0.6 s. The task's own `node` stays first on PATH, and the git tree stays clean.
- [x] **End to end with pier 0.3.1** in an Ubuntu 24.04 container driving Docker: Claude Code 2.1.214 with `gpt-5.6-sol` via the gateway, effort low, $3 cap, one task:

  | Arm | Resolved | Cost | Input tokens | Steps | Agent time | GitNexus calls |
  | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
  | baseline | 1/1 | $0.517 | 427,064 | 26 | 161 s | — |
  | gitnexus | 1/1 | $0.508 | 379,538 | 17 | 132 s | 5 |

  One task proves the pipeline works, not that either arm is better.
- [x] `ec2/bootstrap.sh` (as filled by `launch.sh`) run in a fresh `ubuntu:24.04` container with `shutdown` and `systemctl` stubbed: pier 0.3.1, Node v22.18.0, Docker and Compose all present, the checkout at the requested ref, and the auto-stop scheduled.
- [x] **EC2 pilot.** `ec2/launch.sh --ref eval/deepswe-bench --max-hours 6` started an `m7i.4xlarge` in us-east-1. Bootstrap finished in about a minute, at the requested commit, with the auto-stop scheduled. On the instance I ran `run.sh --n-tasks 5 --concurrency 4 --cost-limit 3` (seed 0, Claude Code 2.1.214, `gpt-5.6-sol` via the gateway, effort low). It built the package from the checkout, prepared both arms, ran 10 trials and wrote the report, all in 31 minutes. The instance was then terminated, after 37 minutes in total.
  - Every trial was graded and the report listed no problems. Each session had only `Bash`/`Edit`/`Read`/`Write`, ran as one Claude Code session, and no trial hit an exception.
  - The model key went over SSH stdin into a mode-600 file and was shredded before termination. A scan of the downloaded results found no copy of it.

  | Arm | Resolved | Target tests passed (F2P) | Mean cost | Mean input tokens | Mean steps | Mean agent time | GitNexus calls/trial |
  | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
  | baseline | 1/5 | 117/177 | $1.813 | 2,423,779 | 57.2 | 365 s | — |
  | gitnexus | 0/5 | 146/177 | $1.604 | 1,905,921 | 41.4 | 318 s | 7.8 |

  Paired deltas (5/5 pairs): cost −11.5%, input tokens −21.4%, steps −27.6%, agent time −12.9%, output tokens +11.6%. GitNexus calls: `impact` 21, `detect-changes` 9, `query` 7, `context` 2.

  | Task | baseline F2P | gitnexus F2P |
  | --- | --- | --- |
  | anko-default-function-arguments | 2/2 ✅ | 1/2 |
  | kea-atomic-signal-selectors | 2/12 | 9/12 |
  | koota-composite-trait-aspects | 29/51 | 47/51 |
  | testem-bail-on-test-failure | 76/90 | 81/90 |
  | wasmi-trap-coredumps | 8/22 | 8/22 |

  Five tasks with one attempt each is too few to rank the arms. Binary resolution went 1–0 to baseline, while GitNexus passed more target tests on three tasks and was cheaper on average. All existing (P2P) tests passed in every trial. The pilot shows the EC2 path works end to end.- [ ] GitNexus `detect_changes`: there is no local index of this checkout.

## Risk & rollout

Tooling only, opt-in, run by hand. The gateway's port 80 must stay closed to the outside; `launch.sh`'s security group opens only SSH. `launch.sh` prints the `terminate-instances` command, and the instance stops itself after `--max-hours` (default 12).

## Checklist

- [x] PR body meets repo minimum length (workflow may label short descriptions)
- [ ] If `AGENTS.md` / overlays changed: headers, scope block, and changelog updated per project conventions
- [x] No secrets, tokens, or machine-specific paths committed

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

<!-- gitnexus-pr-summary:v1:start -->

---

### 📝 Summary by GitNexus

## Summary

*This appears to be a focused evaluation harness change, with low risk and no graph-traced dependents.*

**🟢 LOW blast radius. An evaluation tooling change for paired DeepSWE runs comparing baseline and GitNexus CLI with Claude Code on a dedicated EC2, contained in the `eval/` tree.**

The change centers on the evaluation documentation in `eval/README.md` and `eval/deepswe/README.md`, alongside Python and shell scripts for preparation, reporting, running, and EC2 setup. The graph found no affected execution flows or cross-repo consumers.

Review the run and setup paths first: `eval/deepswe/run.sh`, `eval/deepswe/prepare.py`, `eval/deepswe/report.py`, `eval/deepswe/ec2/bootstrap.sh`, and `eval/deepswe/ec2/launch.sh`. `eval/tests/test_deepswe.py` is the corresponding test file.

title: feat: Oracle PL/SQL language support (standalone ANTLR4-based provider)
body:
### Area

gitnexus (CLI / core / indexing / MCP server)

### Problem or opportunity

A lot of enterprise software — banking, insurance, telecom, government — keeps its core business logic in Oracle PL/SQL packages, procedures and triggers. These systems are often the hardest code to onboard into: logic is spread across hundreds of packages, call chains cross package boundaries, and "which procedures write this table?" is usually answered by grep and tribal knowledge. Today GitNexus has no SQL-family language, so none of this is visible to `query`, `context`, `impact` or `wiki`.

Related issues are blocked on the parser choice:
- #1373 (generic SQL): `tree-sitter-sql` ships WASM only, with no native binding for the Node tree-sitter runtime.
- #1868 (PL/pgSQL): parser choice open for maintainer input.

This issue proposes Oracle PL/SQL specifically, with a parser approach that needs no native binding.

### Proposed solution

Add `PlSql` as an **experimental, standalone provider following the COBOL precedent**:
- `parseStrategy: 'standalone'`, `treeSitterQueries: ''`
- a dedicated pipeline phase (deps `structure`, consumed by `parse`) that writes nodes and edges
- `scopeResolutionEdgeMode: 'callable-flow-only'` in its scope resolver

**Parser:** the [grammars-v4 PlSql grammar](https://github.com/antlr/grammars-v4/tree/master/sql/plsql) (Apache-2.0, actively maintained, already ships an `Antlr4ng` target), generated with antlr-ng and run on [antlr4ng](https://www.npmjs.com/package/antlr4ng) (BSD-3). It is pure JS: no native binding, no per-platform builds, no grammar vendoring. `antlr4ng` would be registered in `PARSE_CACHE_PACKAGE_INPUTS`.

**Files:** `.pks .pkb .pck .pls .plb .prc .fnc .trg .tps .tpb .typ`. `.sql` only when `classifyFileContent` detects Oracle PL/SQL units (`CREATE [OR REPLACE] PACKAGE|PROCEDURE|FUNCTION|TRIGGER|TYPE … IS|AS`, `/` terminators, `%TYPE`/`%ROWTYPE`). I'm happy to coordinate `.sql` ownership with #1373 / #1868.

**Graph mapping, phase 1 (existing labels only, no schema change):**

| PL/SQL | Graph |
|---|---|
| package (spec + body merged) | `Module` |
| procedure / function / nested subprogram / trigger | `Function`, `CONTAINS` from its owner |
| call (local, package-qualified, schema-qualified; overloads by arity / named args) | `CALLS` |
| table / view | `Record` (placeholder when referenced but not defined in the repo) |
| SELECT / INSERT / UPDATE / DELETE / MERGE | `ACCESSES` with `reason: plsql-<op>` (mirrors COBOL's `sql-<op>`) |
| `EXECUTE IMMEDIATE` | best-effort, low confidence, reported as ambiguity |

Dedicated `Table` nodes and `READS`/`WRITES` edges could come later as a separate schema discussion.

**Robustness:**
- a line-preserving pre-pass that blanks SQL*Plus client commands (`SET`, `DEFINE`, `@@`, `-` continuations, `&` substitution) and resolves conditional compilation (`$IF … $END`)
- split files into compilation units
- SLL first, falling back to LL
- per-unit timeout
- a regex fallback for unparsable or `WRAPPED` units, at low confidence

### Spike results

I ran a spike before opening this: 801 files / 245k lines from 5 open-source PL/SQL projects (utPLSQL, OraOpenSource Logger, Alexandria PL/SQL utils, OOS-Utils, Oracle db-sample-schemas), Node 25, single thread.

| Metric | Result |
|---|---|
| Package / procedure / function / trigger files with zero syntax errors | **97.6%** (332/340) |
| All files incl. SQL*Plus install scripts and object types | 85.6% |
| Throughput, cold | ~650 ms/kLOC |
| Throughput, warm ATN/DFA cache (second pass, same process) | **~175 ms/kLOC**, p95 191 ms/file, max 4.2 s |
| Generated parser bundle | 6.8 MB minified (1.4 MB gzip). For scale: the gitnexus 1.6.12 package unpacks to ~230 MB |

A ~170-line listener prototype extracts these correctly on a realistic package-body fixture:
- definitions with arity
- local, package-qualified and schema-qualified calls
- table access: SELECT incl. subqueries, INSERT, UPDATE, MERGE target vs. USING source, INSERT…SELECT write vs. read, cursors, trigger target table
- `EXECUTE IMMEDIATE` sites

Findings that shape the design:
- **Error recovery is uneven.** On files that do have syntax errors, recovery sometimes keeps every definition and sometimes loses most of a package body. So unit splitting plus the regex fallback is required, not optional.
- **The remaining failures are grammar gaps:** nested `$IF`, newer keywords not usable as identifiers (`annotations`, `XDB`), `TREAT(x AS t).method()`, some object-type member syntax. I plan to send fixes upstream to grammars-v4.

An implementation is ready on a branch. It covers everything above plus rename, and passes the new-language CI gates: https://github.com/Asyncronize/GitNexus/tree/feat/plsql-provider (draft PR to follow). The PR description lists test results and known gaps.

### Alternatives considered

- **tree-sitter PL/SQL grammar.** The available ones are early-stage, and this reopens the native-binding / vendoring problem from #1373.
- **Regex-only, like COBOL.** This can't reliably handle nested blocks, overloads, quoted identifiers or DML target-vs-source, so here it is used only as a fallback.
- **The Oracle data dictionary (`DBA_DEPENDENCIES`).** It needs a live database, has no table read/write distinction or line numbers, and doesn't fit GitNexus's file-based indexing. It could be an optional import later.

### Acceptance criteria

- `gitnexus analyze` on a PL/SQL repo creates package / procedure / function / trigger nodes. `context` and `impact` work on them, including cross-package calls.
- "Which procedures write table X?" is answerable via `ACCESSES` edges with `plsql-insert|update|delete|merge` reasons.
- Ambiguous resolution (overloads, dynamic SQL, regex-fallback units) is reported as ambiguity, never as exact.
- It passes the inventory gates for a new registered language:
  - `docs/languages/plsql-ingestion-gaps.md` and a row in `docs/languages/README.md`
  - resolver integration tests and `lang-resolution` fixtures
  - rename provider matrix, CFG worker roundtrip (`collectSourceCfgs`)
  - parse-cache input coverage
- A bench under `gitnexus/bench/` for parse throughput.

### Constraints

- No native dependencies; no change to the shared graph schema in phase 1.
- Shared ingestion code stays language-agnostic (per DoD). All PL/SQL specifics stay in the provider and its phase.
- Starts as `experimental` in `language-classification.ts`.

**Questions for maintainers:**
1. Is an ANTLR-based standalone provider acceptable? Should the generated parser be committed, or generated in `prepare`?
2. Is it OK to start with `Module` / `Function` / `Record` + `CALLS` / `ACCESSES`, and discuss dedicated `Table` / `READS` / `WRITES` later?
3. Proposed PR split:
   - (1) provider skeleton + definitions + `CALLS` + required gates
   - (2) table access
   - (3) dynamic SQL, synonyms, CFG and rename refinements

   Does that work for you?

### Contribution

- [x] I am willing to open a PR for this (may need design discussion first). The draft PR is linked above.

title: feat(plsql): add Oracle PL/SQL language support (standalone ANTLR4 provider)
body:
Closes #3771. Related: #1373, #1868.

## Summary

This adds `SupportedLanguages.PlSql` as an **experimental, standalone provider** that follows the COBOL precedent. PL/SQL packages, procedures, functions and triggers become graph nodes. Calls, table reads/writes and SQL*Plus script includes become edges. That makes `context`, `impact`, `query` and `rename` work on Oracle code, where many enterprise systems keep their core business logic.

The parser is the [grammars-v4 PlSql grammar](https://github.com/antlr/grammars-v4/tree/master/sql/plsql) (Apache-2.0), generated with antlr-ng for **antlr4ng** (BSD-3). It is pure JS: no native binding and no per-platform build, so it avoids the blocker in #1373.

## What it models

| PL/SQL | Graph |
|---|---|
| package (spec + body, merged) | `Module`, anchored at the spec; `CONTAINS` from each defining file |
| procedure / function / nested subprogram / trigger | `Function`. For package members, `isExported` is true when the spec declares them |
| local, nested, `pkg.proc`, `schema.pkg.proc` calls | `CALLS` (`plsql-call`). Overloads are narrowed by arity (defaults count) and named arguments; when they can't be narrowed, `plsql-call-ambiguous` at 0.5 |
| `SELECT` / `INSERT` / `UPDATE` / `DELETE` / `MERGE` / `LOCK`, trigger target | `Record` per table; `ACCESSES` with `reason: plsql-<op>` (mirrors COBOL's `sql-<op>`) |
| SQL*Plus `@@script` / `@script` / `START script` | `IMPORTS` File → File, exact paths only. `@@` is resolved against the calling script's directory; `@` / `START` against the repository root, then the caller's directory |

The graph schema is unchanged.

Deliberately no edge:
- built-ins and anything that doesn't resolve to a definition in the repo;
- database-link calls;
- CTE names and `DUAL`;
- scripts outside the repo.

`.sql` files are claimed through `classifyFileContent` only when they contain an Oracle unit or SQL*Plus includes. A PL/pgSQL decoy in the fixture stays unclaimed.

## Design notes

- **Phase.** `plsql` runs after `structure` and before `parse`, like `cobol`. The scope resolver uses `callable-flow-only`, so `plsql-processor.ts` owns all structural edges. Shared ingestion code stays language-agnostic. The only shared edits are the registration tables, the phase list and `parse.deps`.
- **One resolver for edges and rename.** `plsql/resolve.ts` holds the name resolution: innermost-first, package-qualified, schema-qualified, with overload narrowing. The processor uses it for `CALLS`; the scope resolver uses it in `emitPostResolutionEdges` → `recordSourceBinding`. So rename and the graph always agree.
- **Position-based ownership.** Calls and accesses are owned by the innermost enclosing definition by position, so overloads keep their own edges.
- **Repository-aware identity.** Each package spec pairs with its nearest body. Ties between same-named definitions in different folders (release copies, fixtures) are broken by path proximity, and rename families stay within one package instance.
- **Robust parsing:**
  - A line- and column-preserving pre-pass handles SQL*Plus commands (recognized only between statements, so `EXECUTE IMMEDIATE` inside a block is untouched), `&` substitution variables and nested conditional compilation.
  - Each file is split into `/`-terminated segments. Each segment is parsed SLL first, falling back to LL, with a deadline that scales with segment size (10 s floor, 15 ms/line, overridable via `GITNEXUS_PLSQL_SEGMENT_DEADLINE_MS`).
  - When a segment has syntax errors, a regex fallback recovers the definitions the error-recovered tree lost. These are marked low confidence, and rename is refused on them.
- **Conservative rename.** It covers:
  - spec declaration + body as one family;
  - `END <label>`;
  - package qualifiers;
  - cross-file call sites.

  Identifiers in expression positions that aren't recorded calls are left unproven, so a same-named variable makes rename refuse instead of guess. Rename also refuses when the name appears in dynamic-SQL text, in a SQL*Plus client command such as `EXEC pkg.proc`, or in a file with unparsed segments.
- **Imports.** `resolveImportTarget` resolves SQL*Plus includes against the calling script's directory, then the repo root (appending `.sql` when there is no extension). It never does a suffix search, so it satisfies `external-import-conformance` and `import-target-index-reuse` without a `KNOWN_GAPS` entry.
- **Parser loads lazily.** The generated parser is about 14 MB of JS (about 120 MB resident), so no module reachable from the provider registry, parse workers or scope resolver imports it. `plsql/facts-store.ts` loads the parser and extractor on demand: the `plsql` phase does so only after it finds PL/SQL files, rename awaits it, and other synchronous callers fall back to `require(esm)`. On a repo without PL/SQL the registry loads as before: 426 ms / 104 MB, against 568 ms / 241 MB when the parser was imported statically. `test/unit/plsql-lazy-parser.test.ts` fails if a value import of the parser, `antlr4ng` or the extractor slips into those modules.
- **Generated code.** The grammar is vendored under `plsql/grammar/`, and the generated lexer/parser under `plsql/generated/`. `scripts/generate-plsql-parser.mjs` regenerates them (verified byte-identical). Provenance and the grammar commit are in `plsql/generated/README.md`. Lint and Prettier skip the generated directory.

## Tests

| Suite | Result |
|---|---|
| `test/integration/resolvers/plsql.test.ts`: exact node/edge lists, overload source/target lines, negatives | 11/11 |
| `test/unit/plsql-preprocess.test.ts`, `plsql-extract.test.ts`, `plsql-processor.test.ts`: pre-pass, classification, extraction/fallback, overload ownership and named-argument binding, forward declarations, folder copies and schemas, include semantics, comment/string-aware splitting, schema-qualified calls, deadline, facts store | 39/39 |
| `rename-integration/plsql/`: cross-file success, plus refusals for dynamic SQL and SQL*Plus `EXEC` | 3/3 |
| Registration gates: external-import-conformance, import-target-index-reuse, pipeline-phase-registry, callable-value-flow, parse-cache-input-coverage, framework-detection, cfg worker-roundtrip, callable-capture-options | 254/254 |
| rename-provider-matrix | 20/20 |
| Full `test/unit` | 23,105 passed. The remaining failures also fail on unmodified `main` in this environment: macOS `/var`↔`/private/var` paths, a missing CLI, FTS artifacts, and timing-sensitive `hooks.test.ts` ps-guard cases, which fail on `main` too. |
| Neighbouring resolver suites: COBOL, Java, JavaScript, Python | 528/528 |
| `test/unit/plsql-lazy-parser.test.ts`: structural guard on lazy parser loading (value imports, side-effect imports, re-exports) | 17/17 |
| Full `test/integration` | 431 files passed, 12 skipped, 0 failed (7,643 tests) |
| CI bench guards run locally (`bench/*/measure.mjs --check`, all 28 scripts in `ci-tests.yml`). `import-target` gained a `plsql` arm and baseline, as its inventory check requires. | 28/28 pass |
| `tsc --noEmit`, Prettier, ESLint (0 errors) | clean |

**CLI end-to-end.** Running `gitnexus analyze` on the fixture indexes 41 nodes and 87 edges and detects 3 clusters and 5 processes, with no write warnings. `impact SETTLE_ONE --direction upstream` reports `RUN_BATCH → PRC_ARCHIVE` across 4 processes.

**Corpus run.** I ran the processor on utPLSQL, Logger, Alexandria, OOS-Utils and Oracle sample schemas: 618 claimed files, 121k lines, about 60 s cold on a single thread. It produced 184 packages, 3,864 subprograms and 44.6k call edges. No segment hit the parse deadline, and 10 definitions came from the regex fallback. Measured in an earlier spike, 97.6% of package/procedure/function/trigger files parse with zero syntax errors.

## Impact analysis (`detect_changes` / `impact`)

- `detect_changes --scope all` maps the tracked diff to registration tables only: `EXTENSION_MAP`, `SYNTAX_MAP`, `LanguageClassifications`, `providers`, `SCOPE_RESOLVERS`, `LANGUAGE_QUERIES`, `PARSE_CACHE_PACKAGE_INPUTS`, `buildPhaseList`, `parsePhase.deps`, the gate-test tables, and doc sections. Affected processes: 0.
- The result is PARTIAL because three edits have no symbol to map to: one ESLint ignore line, one enum member, and one re-export.
- **`buildPhaseList` is HIGH** (`runPipelineFromRepo → runFullAnalysisInner → runFullAnalysis`). This is inherent to adding a phase: every analyze runs it.
  - With no PL/SQL in a repo, the phase does one extension filter over `scannedFiles` and returns.
  - `.sql` files are read once to classify their dialect.
  - Verification: the full unit suite, neighbouring resolver suites, and a cold self-index of this repo all pass. The self-index produced 116,380 nodes / 348,827 edges and had the same single pre-existing COPY warning as `main`.
  - Flagging this for your sign-off.

## Known gaps (tracked in `docs/languages/plsql-ingestion-gaps.md`)

- Parsing runs on the main thread, about 60 s cold for 121k lines. Facts are shared with scope extraction within a run but not persisted across runs (PLSQL-07: workers plus parse-cache persistence; the cache contract is shaped around worker chunks, so I'd like your view first).
- Overloads that differ only by parameter type fan out to every candidate (PLSQL-09, type-based narrowing).
- No edges from dynamic SQL yet (PLSQL-04).
- Object types are out of scope (PLSQL-05).
- No CFGs yet (PLSQL-08).

- Rename does not yet consult Java/XML callers that invoke procedures by string (PLSQL-11).
- A `.sql` file that holds only SQL*Plus `EXEC` lines, with no Oracle unit or include, is not claimed: `EXEC` is also T-SQL. Rename cannot see such a caller.
- Incremental writeback behaviour of the multi-file table/package nodes is untested (PLSQL-12).

## Questions for maintainers

1. Is committing the generated parser (about 12.8 MB of TS; about 6.8 MB minified) acceptable, or would you prefer generating it in `prepare`?
2. Is reusing `Module` / `Function` / `Record` with `ACCESSES` OK for now, with dedicated `Table` / `READS` / `WRITES` discussed separately?

Reports separate measurement cohorts and retain failures. Incomplete token totals stay unknown. Public session diagnostics exclude prompts, arguments, source, result text, and argument hashes. Markdown labels are escaped.

title: wiki: allow configuring max_completion_tokens
body:
`gitnexus wiki` always sends `max_completion_tokens: 16384`. The wiki command has no flag for it, `~/.gitnexus/config.json` has no field for it, and there is no environment variable for it either.

### Proposed solution

Add three ways to set the limit, in the same order as the other LLM settings:

1. `gitnexus wiki --max-completion-tokens <n>`
2. `GITNEXUS_MAX_COMPLETION_TOKENS`
3. optional `maxCompletionTokens` in `~/.gitnexus/config.json`

The flag overrides the environment variable. The environment variable overrides the config file. If none of them is set, keep sending 16384.

title: fix(wiki): configure limits and retry truncated pages
body:
## Summary

Combine #3776 with the configurable completion limit from #3775. Wiki generation now rejects responses cut off at the token limit, records failed modules for retry, and returns a failure exit code when pages are incomplete.

Fixes #3774. Includes commit 34fe4138ae6c5b4c6c88fccc595954e39d31e8db from #3776 through a merge commit.

## Behavior

- Set the limit with `--max-completion-tokens`, `GITNEXUS_MAX_COMPLETION_TOKENS`, or `maxCompletionTokens` in the config file, in that order. The default remains 16384. Values must be positive safe integers.
- Reject `finish_reason: "length"` for streaming and non-streaming HTTP responses, including responses where reasoning used the budget before any visible answer arrived. The error names the configured limit.
- Persist failed module names so a normal rerun retries them at the same repository commit. Successful pages are retained, and parent pages wait for failed children to recover.
- Remove the old completion metadata when starting forced regeneration, so a truncated overview cannot leave the wiki falsely marked up to date.
- Report incomplete runs with exit code 1 in normal and review mode, and skip Gist publication for incomplete results.

title: fix(wiki): reject LLM responses cut off at the completion token limit
body:
## Summary

`callLLM` now throws when the provider reports `finish_reason: "length"`, streamed or not. A wiki page cut off at the completion token limit is no longer written as if it were finished. The module fails, is listed under "Failed modules", and is regenerated on the next run.

## Motivation / context

Refs #3774. That issue has two parts. The first is the hardcoded 16384 limit, which #3775 makes configurable. The second is this one: `readSSEStream` only fails the call on `content_filter`, and the non-streaming path does not read `finish_reason` at all. A page cut off at the limit is saved and the command reports success. A reasoning model can spend the whole limit before the answer starts, and a raised limit can still be reached. #3775 does not touch this path, and this PR does not touch the limit, so the two are independent.

## Areas touched

- [x] `gitnexus/` (CLI / core / MCP server)
- [ ] `gitnexus-web/` (Vite / React UI)
- [ ] `.github/` (workflows, actions)
- [ ] `eval/` or other tooling
- [ ] Docs / agent config only (`AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `.cursor/`, `llms.txt`, etc.)

## Scope & constraints

**In scope**

- `callLLM` (`gitnexus/src/core/wiki/llm-client.ts`), both paths. The error names the limit: `LLM response stopped at the completion token limit (16384, finish_reason "length") and is incomplete.` When the limit is spent before any answer arrives, this message replaces "LLM returned empty response", since the limit is the cause.
- Nothing changes in the generator. It already catches a failed leaf or parent page, skips the write, and lists the module.

**Explicitly out of scope / not done here**

- The configurable limit (#3775).
- The `cursor`, `claude`, `codex`, `opencode` and `grok` providers, which do not go through `callLLM`.
- Retrying with a higher limit.

## Implementation notes

Every wiki LLM call goes through this function, so two outcomes change beyond page writes:

- A cut-off overview page now fails the run. It used to be written truncated.
- A cut-off answer to the single grouping request now fails the run. It used to fail JSON parsing and fall back to directory grouping without saying why. Batched grouping still falls back on any error, this one included.

I kept both as errors rather than special-casing them, because a silent fallback hides the cause. If you would rather the grouping step keep falling back, it is a `try`/`catch` around the single grouping call in `buildModuleTree`.

## Testing & verification

- [x] `test/unit/wiki-llm-truncation.test.ts` (4), in its own file so it does not conflict with #3775's changes to `wiki-llm-client.test.ts`:
  - a non-streaming answer with `finish_reason: "length"` is rejected;
  - an empty answer with `finish_reason: "length"` is rejected with the limit message, not "empty response";
  - a streamed answer whose last chunk carries `finish_reason: "length"` is rejected;
  - answers ending with `"stop"`, streamed and not, still resolve.
- [x] Mutations: removing the non-streaming check fails 2 of these tests, removing the streaming check fails 1.
- [x] Built CLI against a local OpenAI-compatible stub that answers the grouping and overview requests normally and cuts every module page off at the limit (`gitnexus wiki --provider custom --base-url http://127.0.0.1:…/v1 --allow-insecure-connection 127.0.0.1`, two-module repository):
  - `main`: "Pages: 3", and `billing.md` ends mid-table (`| --- | -`);
  - this branch: "Pages: 1" (the overview), and "Failed modules (2): Billing, Shipping". Neither page is written.
- [x] `npx vitest run --project default test/unit`: 23,013 passed, 50 skipped. The wiki tests (`test/unit/wiki-*`, 10 files, 253 tests) pass.
- [x] `cd gitnexus && npx tsc --noEmit`: no errors. eslint: no new warnings. prettier and the pre-commit hook are clean.
- [x] `detect_changes --scope all`: `callLLM` and `readSSEStream`, risk low. `impact` on `readSSEStream` is HIGH because all wiki generation goes through it. That is the behaviour change described above.

## Risk & rollout

A run that used to save cut-off pages now reports them as failed modules. No change to the request, the config, or the index.

- [ ] If `AGENTS.md` / overlays changed: headers, scope block, and changelog updated per project conventions (not changed)

title: fix(storage): preserve fresh registrations during pruning
body:
## Summary

Prevent registry validation from deleting a repository that was successfully re-registered after the validator's initial storage inspection. Recheck deletion candidates under the registry lock before persisting removals, including when the new registration has identical metadata.

## Motivation / context

A validator can observe missing storage, pause while another process rebuilds and registers the same storage slot, then remove that valid registration using its stale inspection. The database remains readable but disappears from registry-based discovery.

Refs #3515; related tracker #3609. This fixes a reproduced registry race; the original macOS/OpenCode incident has not been reproduced, so this PR does not establish that this race caused it.

## Areas touched

- [x] `gitnexus/` (CLI / core / MCP server)

## Scope & constraints

**In scope**

- Revalidate candidate removals against current storage while holding the registry lock.
- Preserve registrations on transient inspection failures and avoid rewriting a missing or corrupt registry.
- Add deterministic regressions for concurrent registration, pruning, and registry read failures.

**Explicitly out of scope / not done here**

- MCP parent-process lifecycle changes and replay of the original macOS/OpenCode environment.

## Implementation notes

Healthy listings retain the existing lock-free path. When pruning is needed, read the registry strictly under the lock, inspect only matching deletion candidates with bounded concurrency, and remove only candidates still safe to prune. Preserve the existing return snapshot and best-effort cleanup behavior.

## Testing & verification

title: feat(eval): add capped two-cell diagnostic trial

## Summary

Add a manual `diagnostic_trial` mode to the release evaluation workflow. It runs one no-graph cell and one eager-MCP cell serially, with a $5 CLI budget stop per cell, and publishes their measurements in the GitHub Actions summary.

## Motivation / context

#3773 added session diagnostics and offline experiment preparation. The protected workflow still only exposed the full release sweep or an unpaid runner probe, so it could not launch the prepared two-cell trial within its spend scope.

## Areas touched

- [x] `.github/` (workflows, actions)
- [x] `eval/` or other tooling

## Scope & constraints

**In scope**

- One `trivial-status-json-alias` task per arm, `gpt-5.6-sol`, `xhigh`, seed 3762, one worker, and a 900-second session timeout.
- Reject additional experiment flags, other models/efforts, non-SHA candidates, and rerun attempts. Validate both cells before starting either, and refuse reused or interrupted plans.
- Retain failed-cell measurements and publish sanitized JSON/Markdown. Missing result rows, session diagnostics, or provider ledgers fail the trial.

**Explicitly out of scope / not done here**

- No paid trial has been dispatched during implementation.
- Trial output cannot approve a release or establish a statistically reliable cost difference.

## Implementation notes

The executor accepts only the fixed two-cell plan produced by the existing planner. It runs each cell through the existing evaluation runner and records an exclusive execution receipt before launching any paid work.

The workflow preserves the protected main-only environment, candidate ancestry checks, shared EC2 lock, sandbox preflight, stop deadline, evidence reserve, and verified shutdown. The trial skips the stable runtime and full release sweep. Public artifacts contain sanitized diagnostics; raw provider ledgers stay private on the runner.

## Testing & verification

- [x] Ruff; Actionlint with ShellCheck enabled; Prettier; `git diff --check`.
- [x] GitNexus change analysis — 5 files, 30 symbols; no partial or truncated result. Workflow control flow was reviewed directly because it is not represented in the code graph.
- [x] Sequential Compound Engineering review of correctness, standards, testing, security, reliability, and failure scenarios. No blocking findings remain; no independent model review was run as part of that review.

## Risk & rollout

The planned $10 uses CLI accounting. It is not a provider invoice cap: in-flight requests and provider accounting can exceed it.

title: chore(deps)(deps): bump glob from 13.0.6 to 14.0.2 in /gitnexus
body:
Bumps [glob](https://github.com/isaacs/node-glob) from 13.0.6 to 14.0.2.
Changelog

Sourced from glob's changelog.

changeglob

14

  • Use minimatch 11. Each portion of a pattern with magic is now matched with a Matcher from @isaacs/nonrecursive-glob-match in place of a RegExp, so patterns can no longer cause ReDoS. Matching follows the minimatch 11 changes, which are closer to Bash in some edge cases.
  • Pattern#pattern() returns a Matcher for a portion with magic. The MMPattern type is now minimatch's ParseReturnFiltered, and the new MMMatcher type is the Matcher part of it.
  • Rename Pattern#isRegExp() to isMatcher(), and Processor#testRegExp() to testMatcher().
  • Remove the debug option, which minimatch no longer has.
  • Add the normalize option, to normalize unicode in the pattern and in the file names that it is matched against.
  • GlobWalker#walk() and walkSync() return arrays in place of sets, and MatchRecord#entries() is removed.
  • ignore patterns that start with / now start at the same place as other patterns that start with /: the root option if set, or else the root of the cwd, such as C:\ on Windows.
  • ignore patterns follow the windowsPathsNoEscape option, the same as other patterns.
  • On Windows, patterns that start with a long UNC root like //?/UNC/host/share/ walk that share, the same as //host/share/.
  • Faster ignore patterns (about 1.2 to 3 times faster), and less work for each entry in a walk (about 10% faster sync, and 15% to 30% faster async, for large trees).
  • Allow const string[] or readonly string[] as ignore option or pattern argument.
  • When the signal aborts an async walk, the walk stops. Before, it rejected, but continued to read directories.

13

  • Move the CLI program out to a separate package, glob-bin. Install that if you'd like to continue using glob from the command line.

12

  • Remove the unsafe --shell option. The --shell option is now ONLY supported on known shells where the behavior can be implemented safely.

11.1

... (truncated)

Commits
  • 93957bf 14.0.2
  • 4682e8c fix: do not continue walking after signal abort
  • 668a669 14.0.1
  • 6ff2314 allow const/readonly string[] for ignore, patterns
  • bbe1e5d 14.0.0
  • d9586ad use actual published deps, not symlinks
  • 8b16637 handle long unc forms
  • 5bcdc65 extglobs cannot contain /
  • d8b40c2 handle root in platform-independent way, for ignores and patterns
  • 7d1c45a add native fs glob test (todo on failure)

Remove 12 redundant assignment-chain integration cases: two each for C#, Go, Java, Kotlin, PHP, and Python. In each language, the existing `each alias resolves to its own class/struct, not the other` test already performs both removed checks and verifies that the targets differ.

Also give the native recovery cases a Windows-only 240-second timeout after two CI attempts exhausted their 120-second budget in different cases. Their assertions and other platforms’ timeouts are preserved.

## Motivation / context

The [full scenario-map collection](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/actions/runs/41129111922) identified these pairs as consolidation opportunities. Manual review confirmed identical fixture inputs and suite setup within each pair, matching observed execution paths, and complete containment of each removed callback's statements in the retained callback. This implements the assignment-chain batch from the audit tracked in #3785.

## Areas touched

- [x] `gitnexus/` integration and unit tests

## Scope & constraints

**In scope**

- Remove the separate positive User and Repo alias-resolution cases in the six assignment-chain propagation suites.
- Preserve the broader combined test, the existing edge-count checks, and class/struct/method inventory checks in every language.

- Allow the multi-analysis recovery cases in `incremental-write-integrity.test.ts` enough time to finish on Windows.

**Explicitly out of scope / not done here**

- Production code, fixtures, shared helpers, detector logic, recall manifests, and CI configuration.
- Other audit candidates and a fresh full-repository duplicate collection.

## Implementation notes

Each suite uses one shared `beforeAll` pipeline result. These deletions remove repeated assertions and test reporting overhead; they do not remove ingestion runs. Fixtures remain separate for each language.

An AST comparison against base `1f08ca38f8faabe4242c352e22b0e941fabd9dcd` verified all 12 containment pairs and unchanged callbacks and setup hooks for all 1,440 surviving static test sites. Runtime collection confirms exactly 12 removals:

| Resolver file | Before | After, all passed |

<!-- assignment-containment-proof:start -->
## Containment re-audit

The precise classification is **12 fully subsumed tests, zero identical whole-test pairs**. Each removed callback has one assertion; its retained callback repeats both removed checks and adds a target-file inequality assertion. For the same pipeline result, retained-pass implies both removed tests pass. The reverse is not true.

An independent source audit confirmed the same top-level suite and beforeAll hook, no per-test hooks, unchanged fixture bytes across 21 files, and every removed statement preserved in dependency order. The original callbacks passed on fresh real ingestion results in both test orders without mutating the result, including frozen graph snapshots.

## Summary

Resolve supported Java overloads using JLS strict, loose and variable-arity invocation phases, followed by most-specific selection. Restore the caller counts in #3789 and preserve explicit uncertainty when an overload family cannot be resolved, so context/impact results do not imply complete coverage from missing call edges.

## Motivation / context

Closes #3789.

The original fixture now resolves the exact targets and caller counts below in both resolver and persisted impact tests:

| Overload | Callers |
| --- | ---: |
| `find(Collection<Long>)` | 3 |
| `find(Long)` | 1 |
| `resolve(String)` | 1 |
| `resolve(Long)` | 1 |
| `count(Req)` | 2 |
| `count(Long, Req)` | 1 |

Selection follows [JLS 15.12.2](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/specs/jls/se21/html/jls-15.html#jls-15.12.2) for supported inputs and is checked against executed javac oracles.

## Areas touched

- [x] `gitnexus/` (CLI / core / MCP server)
- [x] Architecture documentation

## Scope & constraints

**In scope**

- Preserve lexical argument types, declared receivers, inherited/static-import overload families, accessibility and supported generic/array/null/primitive distinctions.
- Keep ambiguous, inapplicable and unsupported families terminal; preserve selected compile-time return types separately from runtime dispatch.
- Persist bounded omission receipts with candidate, owner and caller identities; expose matching uncertainty through context/impact.
- Cover cold/warm caches, backend reopen, source correction/deletion, synthetic members and bounded inheritance traversal.

**Explicitly out of scope**

- Arbitrary generic inference, wildcard/unchecked conversion, general method-call argument inference outside the modeled collection factories, and unavailable external classpaths; unsupported selection remains unknown.
- Pre-existing named-construction binding through external `Runnable` and private-only legacy fallback.
- Dependency, graph-DDL or release changes.

## Implementation notes

Java behavior stays in the Java provider; shared ingestion hooks remain language-neutral. Complete overload families participate before shared pruning. Selected returns propagate through a producer/consumer queue, while runtime dispatch retains receiver bounds and excludes static/private primaries.

Omission summaries replace previous analysis metadata, including complete-empty results after correction or deletion. Missing, malformed, legacy and capped receipts cannot establish exact-zero coverage. Parser cache identity remains automatically derived from source/artifact inputs.

Memoized field, inventory and subtype traversal avoids exponential interface-diamond work. Counted probes reduced inventory reads from 4,194,303 to 43 at depth 20 and subtype reads from 262,144 to 36 at depth 16, preserving selected targets and conservative depth/cycle behavior.

## Testing & verification

- [x] Deterministic tool accuracy: **32/32 controls pass**. Its metadata fixture now persists actual overload outcomes, matching the production writer; the expected answers and missing-receipt safeguards are unchanged.
- [x] Repository-wide ESLint: **0 errors, 8,522 warnings**. Changed-file Prettier and `git diff --check` pass.
- [x] Dedicated Java/JLS adversarial, shared-resolution correctness and completeness/API reviews: no open introduced findings.

Focused reproduction commands include:

```bash
cd gitnexus
npm test -- test/integration/resolvers/java-overload-jls.test.ts test/integration/resolvers/java-javac-overloads.test.ts test/integration/java-overload-impact-persistence.test.ts
```

The persistence regression exercises separate-process cold analysis, durable warm reuse, backend reopen, unknown-source insertion, correction and deletion. Environment-only failures were rerun unchanged with supported storage/workspace paths and without inherited `CODEX_HOME`. Windows/macOS execution remains for CI.

## Risk & rollout

Shared resolution and completeness paths have broad reach. Upstream review covered 102 changed production functions and 179 direct dependents outside the diff. Graph verification at implementation snapshot `62d6168d855b185f2563a5419feb1be7614ed47b` used matching schema-4 analyzer identity and reported no incomplete-index reasons. No changed production path is unmapped, no query failed, and the symbol list is not truncated. Native/compiler/persistence tests and direct configuration review supplement those six gaps. Execution-flow enumeration also retains its configured limits.

## Java scaling benchmark follow-up

Commit `3322fca29` adds `gitnexus/bench/java-overload-resolution/measure.js`, a measured `baseline.json`, and reproduction instructions. It removes repeated declaration, lexical-binding and callable-position scans, repeated native child-array materialization, and Java export detection scans across sibling methods. Deterministic work-count tests preserve the existing resolution and ambiguity behavior.

The benchmark uses 128, 512 and 2,048 units, two corpus shapes, and cold/warm/edited analyses. Each recording and check runs three fresh-process samples per size/shape, with real parser workers and database writes. Exact call targets, method counts, cache reuse and extraction/process completeness are mandatory. Workload limits explicitly include the entire generated corpus.

- Recording and an independent `--check` both passed. Worst normalized time/memory growth was **1.281** when recording and **1.379** when checking, against a **1.5** budget.
- For **16× input**, recorded median total analysis time grew **2.15–5.39×** and scope-resolution time grew **9.96–15.72×**. These are bounded measurements with fixed overload-family width and inheritance depth, not an asymptotic claim for arbitrary Java programs.
- Source and test typechecks passed; changed-file ESLint reported zero errors; formatting and diff checks passed. An isolated build was verified against all 1,131 ingestion/shared source files. The recorded built-runtime digest matched the independent check.
- The persistence failure reported by the earlier focused run was traced to exhaustion of the test’s 128 MiB database buffer pool during repeated impact traversals. The test now uses 512 MiB and asserts that every result is complete before checking callers. The full cold/warm/reopen/edit/correction/deletion lifecycle passes in the current validation below.

Reproduce from `gitnexus/` after building:

```sh
node bench/java-overload-resolution/measure.js --check --output /tmp/java-overload-check.json
```

### Simplification validation (`8c813a78a`)

Local bindings are no longer duplicated in the field index. Diagnostic candidate lookup builds one lazy map, preserving scope-definition precedence and the first supplied definition for duplicate IDs. A redundant private-helper comment was removed. Three added tests cover precedence and bounded lookup work; existing tests remain intact.

- The work-count probe uses exactly four identity reads per candidate across 256, 512, 1,024 and 2,048 candidates. The two regression cases fail against the preceding implementation.
- A fresh benchmark `--check` passed all 54 cold/warm/edited analyses. Worst normalized growth was **1.429**, below **1.5**, with unchanged corpus/call/cache fingerprints and fixed overload-family width/depth. The committed baseline remains the reference measurement.
- The simplification run’s persistence failure is resolved by the test buffer-pool fix described above. Current validation supersedes that run; source/test typechecks, ESLint, formatting and diff checks pass.
- The investigation into `UNKNOWN` impact results found a cached LadybugDB **0.18.3** reader opening a **0.22.0** index. The matching runtime finds all three symbols; the stored identities are intact. The index was refreshed at `8c813a78a` with the matching runtime. Impact resolves both edited helpers (critical shared reach: 18 and 14 affected symbols). Change detection maps 13 symbols across four files and remains explicitly partial only for the standalone comment deletion before `setCallResultBinding`; that non-executable region was inspected. Its zero directly affected process count is not an upstream blast-radius estimate.

## Current CI fixes and validation

Replay cleanup now compacts diagnostics in one linear pass and retains one receiver-unresolved receipt per full call-site identity, preserving the latest metadata. The fixture comparison removes 51 duplicate receipts while all 2,506 CALLS relationships remain identical. A regression covers distinct and nested unresolved calls.

The capture fingerprints and receiver diagnostic baseline now reflect the added Java facts and fixtures. Existing capture differences were attributed to return types and `var` initializers; receiver call drops are 141 after deduplication. Timing and memory budgets remain unchanged.

The existing scope-resolution CI job now runs the Java overload/ingestion benchmark and uploads its measurement artifact.

- **7,936 passed, 14 skipped, zero failed** across scope-resolution unit tests, all resolver integrations, persisted Java overload impact, and impact completeness tests.
- The full Java benchmark passes all **54 cold/warm/edited analyses**. Worst normalized time/memory growth is **1.320**, below the unchanged **1.5** budget, with exact target, corpus and cache checks.

- The duplicate-test scanner reports no findings; one unrelated existing test file is unparseable. Source duplicate scanning found no duplicated JLS selection algorithm. Small repeated AST-range and receiver-deferral blocks remain; larger matching receiver-dispatch blocks predate this PR.

The follow-up in `ca6bffe55` separates the known Java accessibility result from unsupported method-call argument capture. An executed javac oracle selects the public `Object` overload for the exact nested-call example; typed `Object` and `String` resolver controls select the same overload. Replaying the preceding CI reports with only those five labels corrected reconciles **31,332 core tests and 516 web tests**, all passed; this replay is not a new CI run. title: fix(impact): smaller agent output, token-budget trimming, old-index walks
body:
## Summary

Make `impact` cheaper for coding agents to read, and stop it reporting nothing on older indexes. On the impact calls agents actually made in a DeepSWE trial repo, output drops from 225 KB to 57 KB (−75%) with the same answers. A new `maxTokens` / `--max-tokens` trims whole records so the result stays valid JSON.

## Motivation / context

**Token cost.** Agents keep every tool output in context and re-read it on every later turn, so a large impact result is paid for many times over. In a paired DeepSWE pilot (Claude Code, gpt-6.1-sol, 5 tasks × 2 GitNexus arms), `impact` was the largest GitNexus output: 35 calls and 194 KB, with single calls up to 22 KB. Weighted by the turns that re-read them, that is roughly 2.1M input tokens across 10 trials, about 40% of the GitNexus arm's extra input over the no-GitNexus baseline. None of those calls set `--limit`, and only 3 used `--summary-only`.

Breaking down 44 impact results from those trials:

| Where the bytes went | Share |
| --- | --- |
| Per-symbol `processes` arrays inside `byDepth` | 56% of `byDepth`; every symbol repeats each flow it is in, which `affected_processes` already lists once |
| CLI indentation (`JSON.stringify(…, null, 2)`) | Pretty output was 45% larger than compact output |
| `byDepth` length | Small on these repos (1–6 symbols per depth), but hub symbols reach 40–60 per depth |

**Large and hub-symbol results.** The MCP schema advertised `limit` with `default: 100` and the CLI help said "default: 100", but an omitted limit was actually unlimited. A hub symbol therefore returned its whole list. On anko, `funcExpr` returned 72 KB, `invokeExpr` 62 KB and `makeCallArgs` 58 KB. The existing `maxTokens` budget cut the serialized text at a byte offset, which leaves the agent a broken JSON document.

**Older indexes.** The frontier query reads `r.staticGated`. An index built before edges carried that property fails every level with `Binder exception: Cannot find property staticGated for r.`. The walk logs a degraded query and reports no dependants at all, which looks exactly like an unused symbol.

## Areas touched

- [x] `gitnexus/` (CLI / core / MCP server)
- [ ] `gitnexus-web/` (Vite / React UI)
- [ ] `.github/` (workflows, actions)
- [ ] `eval/` or other tooling
- [ ] Docs / agent config only

## Scope & constraints

**In scope**

- **CLI:** JSON is indented only when stdout is a terminal; piped and agent output is compact. This applies to every direct tool command, since they share `output()`.
- **Agent boundary (MCP server and `gitnexus impact` only),** in the new `src/mcp/impact-agent-output.ts`:
  - Each affected symbol lists at most 3 processes, with `processCount` carrying the full count.
  - A default page of **30 symbols per depth** applies when the caller sets none of `limit`, `offset` or `summaryOnly`. `byDepthCounts`, `impactedCount` and `summary` stay complete. `GITNEXUS_IMPACT_DEFAULT_LIMIT=0` restores the unpaged result.
  - Group (`@name`) and PDG requests pass through unchanged, because they ignore pagination.
- **`maxTokens` for impact:** whole symbols are dropped from the deepest levels first (a binary search over the kept prefix), so direct dependants survive longest and the JSON stays valid. What was shown is reported in `pagination.trimmedForBudget`. The byte cap still runs afterwards as a backstop for anything that cannot fit.
- **CLI `--max-tokens <n>`,** with English and Chinese help text.
- **Old-index fallback:** on that binder error the frontier query is retried once with `NULL AS staticGated`, and the result is remembered for the rest of the walk.
- **Accurate descriptions:** the tool schema and CLI help now state the real default.

**Explicitly out of scope / not done here**

- Resumable or checkpointed impact (`continuationToken` / `analysisId`, saved summary/module/process views). That needs an extracted impact engine and per-query deadlines, so it is a possible follow-up.
- A wall-clock budget for single-repo impact. The per-level row cap and memory guard from #3696 already bound a walk; a time limit is a separate change.
- Changing backend results for internal callers (group fan-out, the web UI, other tools). Only the two agent-facing paths are shaped.
- Changing the agent rules that make agents call `impact` before every edit.

## Implementation notes

- The shaping runs after the backend and before serialization, so the backend contract is unchanged and the web UI still gets full results.
- The default page is applied by adding `limit` to the backend arguments. That reuses the backend's existing per-depth pagination and `pagination.truncated` flag rather than slicing a second time.
- Process lists keep backend order; the cap only bounds per-symbol detail.
- The token estimate is the existing conservative 4 bytes per token from `output-budget.ts`, and bytes reserved for the next-step hint are subtracted from the budget.

## Testing & verification

- [x] `cd gitnexus && npx tsc --noEmit` passes, after building `gitnexus-shared`.
- [x] Targeted unit run: 66 files covering impact, MCP server, tools, CLI and help; **1,740 passed, 57 skipped, 0 failed.**
- [x] New `test/unit/impact-agent-output.test.ts` covers the default-page rules, the env override, the process cap, budget trimming (deepest level first, valid JSON, counts kept, room reserved for the hint), and the `staticGated` error and query rewrite.
- [x] New server test: an over-budget impact result through `CallTool` with `maxTokens: 800` stays within 3,200 bytes and has no truncation marker. It parses as JSON, keeps both direct dependants, and trims depth 2.
- [x] Updated tests: three CLI assertions now expect compact JSON (stdout is not a TTY under Vitest), and the depth-alias server test now expects the default `limit: 30`.
- [x] `skip-git-cli.test.ts` and `wiki-llm-client.test.ts` fail identically on unmodified `main` in this environment (8 cases), so they are unrelated.
- [ ] Full `npm test` and `npm run test:integration`: not run.
- [ ] ESLint: not run. The repo root's lint dependencies aren't installed in this worktree. Prettier was run with the repo settings.

**Before/after on a real index:** `mattn/anko` (94 Go files; 1,227 nodes, 6,184 edges), using the impact calls agents made on it in the pilot, with output piped as it is for an agent. Base is `main` built from source; new is this branch.

| Call (upstream) | main | this PR | this PR, `--max-tokens 1000` |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| `funcExpr` | 71,813 | 14,027 | 3,963 |
| `invokeExpr` | 62,141 | 15,194 | 3,798 |
| `makeCallArgs` | 58,385 | 12,708 | 3,605 |
| `Run` | 12,311 | 3,285 | 3,286 |
| `FuncExpr` | 7,967 | 3,408 | 3,408 |
| 7 smaller calls | 12,912 | 8,372 | 8,372 |
| **Total bytes** | **225,529** | **56,994 (−75%)** | **26,432 (−88%)** |

Cumulative contribution on the three hub symbols (bytes):

| Symbol | main | Compact JSON | + process cap | + 30/depth page |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| `funcExpr` | 71,812 | 47,964 | 16,678 | 14,027 |
| `makeCallArgs` | 58,384 | 39,018 | 15,804 | 12,708 |
| `invokeExpr` | 62,140 | 41,484 | 17,814 | 15,194 |

**Old index:** on an index whose edges predate `staticGated`, `impact resolveSymbolCandidates --direction upstream` on `main` logs the binder error and returns no dependants. This branch returns 10 affected symbols (depths 1/2/3: 2/2/6, risk LOW) with no errors.

## Risk & rollout

- **Agent-visible shape changes**, all additive or opt-out:
  - `processes` holds at most 3 entries per symbol, and `processCount` appears only when more existed.
  - `byDepth` is paged to 30 per depth by default, with `pagination.truncated` set. `byDepthCounts` is unchanged.
  - Piped CLI JSON is compact. Scripts that parse it are unaffected; scripts that grep for `"key": value` with a space are affected.
- **Opt-outs:** `GITNEXUS_IMPACT_DEFAULT_LIMIT=0` for the full list; an explicit `--limit` / `limit` for a different page.
- **No index or schema change;** no reindex needed.

## Checklist

- [x] PR body meets repo minimum length
- [ ] If `AGENTS.md` / overlays changed: n/a
- [x] No secrets, tokens, or machine-specific paths committed

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

The implementation centers on `gitnexus/src/mcp/impact-agent-output.ts`, `gitnexus/src/mcp/local/local-backend.ts`, and `gitnexus/src/mcp/server.ts`, alongside CLI handling in `gitnexus/src/cli/tool.ts`. title: Python: attribute reads never produce ACCESSES edges, yet context/impact report epistemic "exact" (1.6.12)
body:
### Summary

In GitNexus 1.6.12, a Python attribute read (`obj.field`) never becomes an `ACCESSES` edge. The repro below tries three shapes: a dataclass field read through a variable assigned from a function annotated `-> Result`, the same field read through a variable assigned from `Result()`, and a plain-class attribute read through a parameter annotated `p: Plain`. None is linked. The equivalent TypeScript read (`readBox(b: Box) → b.size`) is linked.

`context` on the Python field then lists only the owning class (`has_property`) and reports `epistemic: "exact"`, with no boundary or cause. An agent reading it concludes the field is unused. `impact` with the default relation types answers `risk: "UNKNOWN"`, which is the right hedge, but its `riskNote` names other reference classes and `epistemic` is still `"exact"`.

Two smaller observations from the same repro:

1. A plain class's `self.value = 1` in `__init__` produces no `Property` node; only the dataclass field does.
2. When a TypeScript file reads a field that is defined only in Python, `analyze` prints the "declined to link" warning and `context` carries `unresolved` and `anchorLanguages`. `impact` on the same symbol carries neither, and both tools report `epistemic: "exact"`.

### Environment

- GitNexus 1.6.12 (npm, global install), CLI. Node 24.14.0, Windows 10 x64, Git Bash.
- Index built with `gitnexus analyze --force --index-only`.
- Not checked on `1.6.13-rc.*`.

### Reproduction

Create these files in an empty directory. `pkg/__init__.py` is empty.

`pkg/model.py`:

```python
from dataclasses import dataclass, field


@dataclass
class Result:
    failures: dict[str, str] = field(default_factory=dict)


class Plain:
    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self.value = 1


def check() -> Result:
    return Result()
```

`pkg/use.py`:

```python
from pkg.model import Plain, Result, check


def read_from_annotated_return() -> dict[str, str]:
    r = check()
    return r.failures


def read_from_constructor() -> dict[str, str]:
    r = Result()
    return r.failures


def read_from_annotated_param(p: Plain) -> int:
    return p.value
```

`ts/box.ts` (control):

```ts
export class Box {
  size = 1;
}

export function readBox(b: Box): number {
  return b.size;
}
```

Then:

```sh
git init -q && git add -A && git commit -qm repro
gitnexus analyze --force --index-only
gitnexus cypher "MATCH (a)-[r]->(p) WHERE r.type = 'ACCESSES' RETURN a.name AS reader, p.name AS field, p.filePath AS file"
gitnexus cypher "MATCH (p:Property) RETURN p.name AS name, p.filePath AS file"
gitnexus context failures
gitnexus impact failures --direction upstream
```

### Actual

`ACCESSES` edges: only the TypeScript one.

```
| reader | field | file |
| --- | --- | --- |
| readBox | size | ts/box.ts |
```

`Property` nodes: no `value` for `Plain`.

```
| name | file |
| --- | --- |
| failures | pkg/model.py |
| size | ts/box.ts |
```

`context failures`:

```json
{
  "status": "found",
  "symbol": { "uid": "Property:pkg/model.py:Result.failures", "name": "failures", "filePath": "pkg/model.py", "startLine": 6, "endLine": 6 },
  "epistemic": "exact",
  "incoming": { "has_property": [ { "uid": "Class:pkg/model.py:Result", "name": "Result", "filePath": "pkg/model.py" } ] },
  "outgoing": {},
  "processes": []
}
```

`impact failures --direction upstream`:

```json
"impactedCount": 0,
"risk": "UNKNOWN",
"riskNote": "No callers resolved. Absence of edges is not evidence the symbol is unused: a caller reaching it through a reference class this index does not record — plain-object property access, a bare-identifier read of a module-scope const — produces no edge to find. Confirm with a text search before treating the change as safe.",
"epistemic": "exact"
```

### Expected

- `ACCESSES` edges `read_from_annotated_return → Result.failures` and `read_from_constructor → Result.failures`, as TypeScript gets `readBox → Box.size`. Likewise `read_from_annotated_param → Plain.value`, if attributes assigned in `__init__` are meant to be `Property` nodes.
- Until Python attribute reads are modelled, `context` and `impact` on a Python `Property` should return `epistemic: "lower-bound"`, with a boundary saying Python attribute reads are not tracked, instead of `"exact"`.

### Cross-language variant

Add `ts/reader.ts` and re-run `analyze`, `context` and `impact`:

```ts
export function readFailures(r: { failures?: Record<string, string> }) {
  return r.failures ?? {};
}
```

`analyze` warns: `1 property read/write site(s) name a field that IS defined in this workspace, but only in another language, so per-language inference declined to link them. ... Affected: failures (python)`. `context failures` now carries `"unresolved": "property reads of this name were NOT linked: every definition of it is python, and name inference does not cross languages. ..."` and still `"epistemic": "exact"`. `impact failures` is unchanged from above: no `unresolved` note, `"epistemic": "exact"`.

Not linking across languages makes sense. The suggestion is only that `impact` carry the same `unresolved` note as `context`, and that both tools report `"lower-bound"` when they know reads were declined.

### Why it matters

In a repo where Python jobs write data that TypeScript code reads, for example through a database JSON column, renaming a Python dataclass field shows no readers in either language. Python's own readers are missing because of the gap above, and the TypeScript readers are missing by design. The `"exact"` label hides both.

title: perf(analyze): skip unchanged dirty snapshots
body:
## Summary

Repeated `analyze` calls against an already-indexed dirty checkout now verify its covered paths and content hashes, then return already up to date without parsing or rewriting the database. Real edits and uncertain snapshots continue through analysis.

Freshness hashes are captured before parsing. This fixes a reproduced race where a file edited after parsing received a new hash beside an older graph, allowing a later repeat to preserve stale results.

## Motivation

Three runs per variant on the same pinned main corpus and LadybugDB 0.22.0:

| Unchanged dirty checkout | Main | Hardened candidate |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Median analysis time | 127.837s | 1.960s |

The ratio of medians is **65.21×**. All candidate repeats preserved the complete database bytes, native FTS and graph counts. These are shared-host measurements around `runFullAnalysis`, excluding import/startup/shutdown.

A separate real-edit control produced matching filtered graph hashes and persisted function, call-edge and FTS results. Main took 121.055s and candidate 140.828s in that single pair; no real-edit speedup is claimed. Full method, raw samples and limitations: [analyze phase breakdown](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/blob/04a47af3d9b7b36420a4cb97ade7b1a66c6198c7/gitnexus/bench/analyze-phase-breakdown.md#production-hardening--2026-11-01).

## Areas touched

- Shared analysis runner used by CLI, watch and refresh callers.
- A dedicated native integration suite, the existing linked-worktree context test, and their test registration.
- Performance measurements and hardening notes.

## Scope and implementation

The shortcut stays behind existing runner/schema/configuration, recovery and embedding-checkpoint gates. It requires an existing graph, a complete indexing receipt, matching scan policy, matching covered paths and matching readable hashes. It catches hidden Git edits and falls back on scan errors. Deleted or unindexed dirty paths conservatively retain the normal analysis path.

No dependency, native-linking, public flag or storage-schema change. The new content-hash timing adds a path-only scan, not another full-content hashing pass. Analysis still reads a live working tree; it is not an atomic filesystem snapshot.

## Testing

The 11 environment-related failures in four setup/auto-sync/server files passed reruns with the expected home variables and checkout location; those test sources were not changed.

- [x] ESLint, formatting, pre-commit hooks and duplicate-test scan passed for the hardening change. The duplicate scan reported no findings and one unrelated existing unparseable file.

- [x] Integrated upstream and indexing regression selection on `815b06b`: **166 passed across 8 files, no skips**, including the dedicated dirty-snapshot suite, linked-worktree context, analyzer identity, MCP server and impact/CLI tests.
- [x] Windows exposed a fixture assumption about LF versus CRLF checkout bytes. Reproduced the failure locally with `core.autocrlf=true`; the fixture now captures the actual checkout bytes before indexing and verifies exact preservation afterward. Both LF and CRLF native reruns pass with required FTS, and the test-only fix is `6e9bbdc`. Typechecking, formatting, pre-commit hooks and graph change mapping pass for that fix.

title: fix(cursor): keep cold npx hooks within host deadlines
body:
Cursor's old 10-second hook deadline could kill a cold `npx -y gitnexus` install before augmentation completed. This change gives the shipped hook a 60-second host window and derives the npx allowance from the active manifest and elapsed hook time, capped at 45 seconds with time reserved for cleanup and output.

- Read the installed `.cursor/hooks.json` and select the GitNexus command entry; retain adjacent-manifest support for source-tree execution.
- Skip npx when too little time remains. Bound Unix guard discovery to three seconds, kill unresponsive probes, and recalculate the child budget after discovery.
- Validate timeout overrides and Homebrew `gtimeout` candidates before adoption. Use the Unix guard for the npx process tree where supported.
- Keep live hook slots valid for 60 seconds across the four adapters sharing `.hook-locks`, so longer cold starts cannot bypass the concurrency cap.
- Cover installed manifests, live lock owners, real unresponsive probes, spawn deadlines, relative overrides, and the Windows fallback.
