The sidecar child inherits the environment, so it loads that model. `resolveEmbeddingIdentity` already reported `resolveEmbeddingConfig().modelId` for local mode, so checkpoints and staged recovery now see a model change.
- **Width.** In local mode `getEmbeddingDimensions()` returned 384 unconditionally. For a custom model it now returns `GITNEXUS_EMBEDDING_DIMS`, the same value `schema.ts` creates the vector column with, so analyze, the identity and the MCP query width agree. The default model keeps 384 whatever `GITNEXUS_EMBEDDING_DIMS` says, as before.
- **Re-embedding on switch.** The content hash did not include the model, so an embedding pass after switching between two models of the same width (arctic-embed-xs and bge-small are both 384) would have kept the old vectors next to new ones. A non-default `modelId` now joins the hash. Default-model hashes are byte-identical (the existing "fingerprints the template…" test pins the formula), so no existing index is re-embedded.
- **Wrong width.** A custom model whose vectors differ from `GITNEXUS_EMBEDDING_DIMS` throws `LocalEmbeddingDimensionError` with the value to set, the way the HTTP client handles the same mismatch. The pipeline treats it as configuration and stops on the first sub-batch instead of dropping nodes until the consecutive-failure ceiling: every later batch would fail the same way. The CLI prints it as one line, without a stack dump (`embedding-dims-invalid` hint).
- **Docs.** README "Local Embedding Model" section, the environment-variable reference, and `analyze --help` text in `en` and `zh-CN`. Model switches require `analyze --force --embeddings`; restart query servers with the matching model and dimensions. The docs include rollback, the embedding cap, mean pooling, and the lack of automatic model-mismatch detection at query time.

**Explicitly out of scope / not done here**

- A CLI flag. `--embedding-model` already names the HTTP model; adding a second model flag felt like a separate decision.
- Recording the model in `meta.json`. As with an HTTP model today, a query server started without the same variables embeds queries with the default model; when the widths differ, the existing `FLOAT[768]` vs `FLOAT[384]` warning tells the operator, and the README says to set both variables wherever the index is queried.
- Per-model pooling or query prefixes. The pipeline keeps mean pooling + normalization for every model.
- Putting the HTTP model into the content hash. It has the same gap, but changing it would re-embed every HTTP index once.

## Implementation notes

- `resolveLocalEmbeddingModelId()` reads only the environment, so the width check in `embedBatch`/`embedText` does not resolve the whole config per batch.
- The width check is skipped for the default model. That keeps the default path identical, and it is why `embedding-sidecar-client.test.ts` (whose fake child returns 3-element vectors) passes unchanged.
- `impact` upstream: `resolveEmbeddingConfig` CRITICAL (16 impacted: analyze, doctor, sidecar, semantic search), `getEmbeddingDimensions` CRITICAL (8: identity, MCP query width, embeddings sync), `contentHashForNode` HIGH. Every one of those paths is unchanged while the variable is unset; the receipts below cover them with it set. `detect_changes --scope all` reports high, from the new branch in `analyzeCommandImpl`'s error handler.

## Testing & verification

- [x] `test/unit/local-embedding-model.test.ts` (6): default model stays at 384 even with `GITNEXUS_EMBEDDING_DIMS=1024`; a custom model takes its width from the variable and rejects a malformed one; the identity records the custom model and width; a mismatching vector is rejected from `embedBatch` and `embedText`, a matching one returned; the content hash changes for a custom model only, and differs between two custom models.
- [x] `test/unit/embedding-config.test.ts` (+2): env over explicit config, trimmed; unset or blank keeps the explicit or default id.
- [x] `test/unit/embedding-pipeline.test.ts` (+1): a width mismatch aborts after one sub-batch, cleans up the touched node, writes no rows.
- [x] `test/unit/analyze-local-embedding-error.test.ts` (+1): the CLI prints the mismatch with the `embedding-dims-invalid` hint and no "Analysis failed" dump.
- [x] Mutations on the final commit, each run against the four test files: env ignored in `resolveEmbeddingConfig` (3 failed), custom width always 384 (3), no width check (1), model left out of the hash (1), no fail-fast in the pipeline (1: 5 sub-batches instead of 1), no CLI branch (1).
- [x] 86 related unit files (embeddings, i18n, doctor, analyze-*, mcp-*, local-backend, semantic): 1,429 passed. Full unit suite (`npm run test:unit`): 1,009 files, 23,744 passed, 50 skipped, 0 failed.
- [x] `cd gitnexus && npx tsc --noEmit`, `npm run typecheck:tests`, eslint on touched files (no new warnings), prettier, pre-commit hook.
- [x] Real runs, built CLI, local runtime, on a two-file TypeScript repo:
  - default model: 5 embeddings, `embeddingDims: 384`;
  - `GITNEXUS_EMBEDDING_MODEL_ID=Xenova/bge-small-en-v1.5` (also 384) with `--force`: all 5 vectors replaced (first component of each changed), nothing reused from the previous model;
  - `Xenova/bge-base-en-v1.5` without `GITNEXUS_EMBEDDING_DIMS`: exit 1, single line `Embedding dimension mismatch: local model Xenova/bge-base-en-v1.5 returned 768d vectors, but expected 384d. Set GITNEXUS_EMBEDDING_DIMS=768 to match your model output.`;
  - the same with `GITNEXUS_EMBEDDING_DIMS=768`: 5 embeddings, `embeddingDims: 768`;
  - `gitnexus query` with both variables: semantic results with no warning; without them: the existing width warning (`FLOAT[768]` vs `FLOAT[384]`).

Additional production-readiness verification:

- Real `runFullAnalysis` + LadybugDB regression covers default → custom A → custom B → default at the same width, persisted vector replacement, stable node identities, and reuse on repeated runs. Only inference/runtime availability are mocked.
- Clean-checkout reproduction confirms that an unforced `--embeddings` run can return "Already up to date" after changing models; the README now documents the working forced path.
- Full local run covered all 1,464 discovered files: 31,548 passed, 14 initially failed, and 103 skipped. All 14 failures passed on targeted reruns (11 environment assumptions; three recovery/process cases passed in isolation). The first full run was not clean.
- Focused tests: 102 unit tests and 24 database integration tests passed. Build, source/test type checks, lint (existing warnings only), repository formatting checks, and graph change analysis passed.

- After synchronizing with `main`: 163 tests across the embedding, Kotlin grammar, CLI, and structural schema suites passed; build and source/test type checks passed.

## Risk & rollout

Opt-in. With `GITNEXUS_EMBEDDING_MODEL_ID` unset, model, width, hashes and errors are the same as on `main`. When switching models, run `gitnexus analyze . --force --embeddings` (use `--embeddings 0` above the default 50,000-node cap). A plain `analyze`, even with `--embeddings`, can return "Already up to date" on unchanged source; changed-source runs without embedding generation only preserve old vectors. To roll back, unset both `GITNEXUS_EMBEDDING_MODEL_ID` and `GITNEXUS_EMBEDDING_DIMS`, repeat the forced embedding pass, and restart query servers with the same settings.

title: feat(lbug): report every undeclared relation pair in one failure
body:
## Summary

An edge whose FROM→TO label pair is missing from the relation DDL no longer stops the emit on the spot. Each emit path records the pair, skips the edge, keeps going, and fails once at close/finalize with every undeclared pair it met. The run still fails and nothing partial is published; it just takes one round trip instead of one per pair.

## Motivation / context

Closes #2797. #2793 needed four reproduction repos for four pairs that were live at the same time, because `analyze` died at the first one.

While wiring this I found that the `--pdg` path did not fail at all. `PdgEmitSink.addRelationship` threw from inside the per-file `try/catch` of the PDG emit loop (`scope-resolution/pipeline/run.ts`), which only warns. An undeclared PDG pair cost that file's CFG and the run exited 0 with "Repository indexed successfully". Since the sink now records instead of throwing, `finalize` fails the run as the other two paths do.

## Areas touched

- [x] `gitnexus/` (CLI / core / MCP server)
- [ ] `gitnexus-web/` (Vite / React UI)
- [ ] `.github/` (workflows, actions)
- [ ] `eval/` or other tooling
- [ ] Docs / agent config only (`AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `.cursor/`, `llms.txt`, etc.)

## Scope & constraints

**In scope**

- `assertDeclaredPair` → `checkDeclaredPair(pairKey, declaredPairs, undeclared, relationType, fromId, toId): boolean`. Declared: `has` + `return true`, still allocation-free with positional arguments. Undeclared: recorded in an `UndeclaredPairCollector`, the caller skips the edge.
- `UndeclaredPairCollector` keeps the first edge of each pair as its example and counts the others. `throwIfAny()` throws one `UndeclaredRelationPairError`.
- `UndeclaredRelationPairError` gains `pairs` (every pair with its first edge and edge count). The top-level `pairKey` / `relationType` / `fromId` / `toId` / `sourceFile` stay those of the first pair. With one pair the message is unchanged; with several it lists each pair with its example edge and count, and the two suggestions go plural. It is still the only rendering, so `serve` users get the full list through `err.message`.
- `RelPairRouter.close()`, `GraphEmitSink.finalize()` and `PdgEmitSink.finalize()` throw it after their existing stream/IO checks. `close()` on the sinks (error path) stays quiet, as before. Undeclared edges are not counted in the router's `skipped`, which stays the invalid-label counter.
- CLI: the existing branch prints the message unchanged and adds `labelPairs` (every pair key) to the `cliError` fields; `labelPair` keeps the first.
- Docblock: the reason the run fails rather than degrades is now stated as graph completeness (a dropped `CALLS` edge makes `impact` wrong), and that the argument is relation-type-scoped, so a future relaxation would split by relation type. The weaker COPY-only argument is gone from the module header.

**Explicitly out of scope / not done here**

- One report across all three paths. Each path reports everything it met. In a `--pdg` run the PDG sink finalizes inside scope resolution, the structural sink at the end of the pipeline, and the router during `loadGraphToLbug`, so a run with undeclared pairs on two different paths still reports them in two rounds. Collecting across paths would mean letting the run continue through the remaining phases after a known failure; I left that alone.
- Skip-and-warn for some relation types. Not decided here; the docblock records where the split would go.
- In `GraphEmitSink`, an undeclared edge is skipped before the id dedup, so the per-pair edge count can include a repeated id. It only affects the count in the message.

## Implementation notes

- `impact` upstream: `GraphEmitSink.addRelationship` and `PdgEmitSink.addRelationship` CRITICAL (99, every emitter through `KnowledgeGraph`), `UndeclaredRelationPairError` CRITICAL (132, its importers), `GraphEmitSink.finalize` HIGH (3), `RelPairRouter.route` / `close` LOW (4), `PdgEmitSink.finalize` LOW (1). For declared edges the emitters see the same thing as before; the one behaviour change is that an undeclared edge no longer throws out of `addRelationship`, which is what lets the per-file PDG catch stop swallowing it.
- `checkDeclaredPair` is a rename because the old name described the old behaviour. The other references (schema.ts, node-lookup.ts, test comments) are renamed with it.
- `detect_changes --scope all` stays `partial` after a reindex: the only hunks in `schema.ts`, `node-lookup.ts` and `schema-pair-coverage.test.ts` are that rename inside docblocks, outside any symbol's range. Mapped: 47 symbols, 39 processes, through the emit sinks and `analyzeCommandImpl`.

## Testing & verification

- [x] `test/unit/rel-pair-routing.test.ts`: the guard passes a declared pair and records an undeclared one without throwing; the single-pair error keeps every field and message string #2789 pinned; four edges over three pairs give one error with the pairs in order, `[2, 1, 1]` edge counts, the plural message, and the second edge of a pair counted but not listed; the router skips two undeclared pairs, still writes the declared edge, keeps `skipped` at 0, ends every stream and rejects at `close()` with both.
- [x] `test/unit/lbug/graph-emit-sink.test.ts`: two undeclared pairs do not throw from `addRelationship`, the declared edge is still streamed, no CSV is opened for the undeclared pair, and `finalize` throws with both.
- [x] `test/unit/lbug/pdg-emit-sink.test.ts`: `addRelationship` no longer throws; `finalize` does.
- [x] `test/unit/analyze-undeclared-pair-error.test.ts`: a two-pair error wrapped in a phase `cause` prints both pairs and reports `labelPairs`.
- [x] Mutations, each run against those four files: throw at the first pair (6 failed), router `close` never throws (1), either sink's `finalize` never throws (1 each), keep only the first pair (4), no edge count (2), CLI without `labelPairs` (1), router writes the undeclared edge anyway (1).
- [x] 93 related unit files (pair, emit, csv, schema, lbug, sink, pdg, cfg, analyze-*, pipeline): 1,515 passed. Integration: `structural-pair-coverage`, `csv-pipeline`, `graph-emit-streaming-roundtrip` (40 passed) and the 14 PDG/CFG/taint files (207 passed). Full unit suite (`npm run test:unit`): 1,008 files, 23,736 passed, 50 skipped, 0 failed.
- [x] `npx tsc --noEmit`, `npm run typecheck:tests`, eslint (the same 4 pre-existing warnings as `main`), prettier.
- [x] Real `analyze` with the built CLI on a one-file TypeScript repo, with two pairs removed from `DECLARED_RELATION_PAIRS` through a local, uncommitted env hook (the DDL itself unchanged):
  - `Function|Function` + `Method|Function`: `main` stops at `Function → Function` and says nothing about the other; this branch exits 1 once with `2 relationship label pairs are not declared…`, both pairs, their edges and files.
  - `BasicBlock|BasicBlock` with `--pdg`: `main` exits 0 with "Repository indexed successfully" and only a `[cfg] … CFG emission failed` warning in the log; this branch exits 1 naming the pair.

## Risk & rollout

No schema or index change. A run that would have failed still fails, with a longer list; a `--pdg` run with an undeclared PDG pair now fails instead of silently dropping that file's CFG.

## Checklist

- [x] PR body meets repo minimum length (workflow may label short descriptions)
- [ ] If `AGENTS.md` / overlays changed: headers, scope block, and changelog updated per project conventions
- [x] No secrets, tokens, or machine-specific paths committed

title: perf: reduce lookup allocations and stream identity checks
body:
## Summary

Reduce allocation overhead in lexical lookup and stream persisted node identities during incremental verification. Both post-COPY and pre-publication identity checks remain mandatory; corrupt identities and read/cleanup errors still prevent freshness publication.

- Reuse frozen empty results, avoid empty filtering/concatenation, and return carried types without a temporary object while preserving lookup snapshots and provider-hook order.
- Read identities one row at a time, holding the connection lock through cursor cleanup and yielding every 1,024 rows. TypeScript rejects asynchronous visitors.
- Run differential checks and all three paired edits in both fresh and persistent CI processes. Pin the baseline to the PR event SHA, with a verified parent fallback.
- Remove the PR-specific optimization reports. Benchmark scripts, regression tests, and CI measurement artifacts remain available.

## Performance evidence

Measured baseline `6aeeace8` → streaming candidate `b5cea365`, using an 862-file sparse corpus, Node 22.23.3, LadybugDB 0.22.0, two workers, a 4 GiB heap, and FTS:

| Mode | Baseline median | Candidate median | Reduction |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Fresh processes, 9 pairs | 19.164s | 17.435s | 9.02% |
| Persistent processes, 9 pairs | 18.826s | 16.805s | 10.73% |

All 18 pairs matched semantic graph digests and persisted call targets. These shared-host measurements isolate the identity-reader follow-up; they do not establish a full-repository or watch-mode speedup. Earlier full-repository lexical measurements improved fresh median time by 8.95% but regressed the first persistent edit by 12.68%.

At 1,048,576 nodes, matched 12-read peak RSS fell from 1972.1 to 1926.7 MiB. A 40-read streaming soak completed, with retained heap after GC returning from 433.2 to 432.6 MiB. Three fresh processes per size supported approximately linear RSS over 16,384–1,048,576 fixed-width nodes; the held-out largest-size median was 1.14% below the fit. This is finite workload evidence, not a universal native-memory bound. JavaScript verifier memory grows with expected nodes, normalized identity bytes, and the largest row; the original graph remains resident.

[Timing reproduction](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/blob/bf7bf0f7947b843db6dce16f2a539006b3393d65/gitnexus/bench/analyze-phase-breakdown.md) · [Memory reproduction](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/blob/bf7bf0f7947b843db6dce16f2a539006b3393d65/gitnexus/bench/incremental-write-integrity/README.md#memory-scaling)

## Validation

- Shared-first build, CLI and web source typechecks, and test typecheck passed.
- **3,503 core tests across 178 files and 516 web tests passed** after simplification, covering scope resolution, identity-reader contracts, reconciliation, benchmark inputs/lifecycles, and native connection serialization. The earlier 141-test verification also covered corruption recovery and freshness-marker behavior.
- **72,000 differential comparisons** against the preceding head passed; explicit carried-type exit checks preserved values, property order, and type identity.
- Repository lint completed with zero errors (warnings remain); formatting, whitespace, and graph change checks passed without partial/truncated results.
- [Full CI for final head `eca9c1319`](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/actions/runs/41807907129) passed, including all 12 required checks, cross-platform tests, coverage, both lexical benchmark lifecycles, and the test-execution audit.

## Risk and rollback

The shared lookup has broad upstream reach; identity verification controls freshness publication. The implementation preserves both verification gates, connection ownership, and failure propagation. No public CLI/API contract, dependency, graph schema, or migration changes. Reverting the PR is the rollback path.

Web UI behavior and release/version changes are outside this PR. Performance results remain bounded to the workloads above.

title: test(schema): pin the Impl and Template pairs the emitters actually produce
body:
## Summary

Adds the Rust `impl` and C++ template emitters to `NON_BRIDGE_CORPUS`, with the three `Impl` / `Template` pairs they actually produce as sentinels. The other rows from #2799 have no emitter on `main`, so no fixture can pin them; the test now records why.

## Motivation / context

Refs #2799. The issue counts 17 hand-declared `Impl|*` / `Template|*` member rows with no fixture behind them. Before writing new fixtures I ran the real pipeline (`runPipelineFromRepo` with the dist worker, as this suite does) over all 206 `rust-*` and `cpp-*` fixtures and collected every pair with `Impl` or `Template` on either side. Three come out, and nothing else:

| Pair | Edge | Fixtures emitting it |
|------|------|------|
| `File\|Impl` | DEFINES | 53 (Rust) |
| `Impl\|Function` | HAS_METHOD | 53 (Rust) |
| `File\|Template` | DEFINES | 15 (C++) |

I also wrote shapes no fixture has (`impl` with an associated `const`, an `impl` nested in a function, a trait impl, `impl<T> Wrap<T>`; a C++ class template with a constructor, destructor, nested struct/enum/alias, member templates and a static member, a function template calling a function, a method, a macro and a constructor, a class template deriving from a class). Same three pairs.

The reasons are structural:

- **`Impl`** comes only from Rust inherent `impl` blocks (`@definition.impl` is `!trait`). An `impl` body cannot hold a struct, trait or nested impl, Rust has no constructors or fields there, and its methods are `Function` nodes. `Impl|{Method, Constructor, Property, Struct, Trait, Impl}` cannot be produced by the current extractor.
- **`Template`**: a C++ template is captured twice, once as `Template` and once as the `Class` / `Function` it declares. Every member, call and heritage edge lands on the second (`Class:box.hpp:Box -HAS_METHOD-> Method:box.hpp:Box.get`, `Function:t.hpp:callAll -CALLS-> …`). The `Template` node is a leaf its file DEFINES, so none of the ten `Template|*` rows fires.
- The reverse rows (`{Function, Class, Method, Constructor}|{Impl, Template}`) are in the same state.

## Areas touched

- [x] `gitnexus/` (CLI / core / MCP server)
- [ ] `gitnexus-web/` (Vite / React UI)
- [ ] `.github/` (workflows, actions)
- [ ] `eval/` or other tooling
- [ ] Docs / agent config only (`AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `.cursor/`, `llms.txt`, etc.)

## Scope & constraints

**In scope**

- `test/integration/structural-pair-coverage.test.ts`, test-only:
  - `rust-member-calls` with sentinels `File|Impl`, `Impl|Function`;
  - `cpp-template-partial-order-pointer` with sentinel `File|Template`;
  - a NOTE below the corpus explaining the rows no emitter reaches;
  - the corpus docblock's "two of them … the other nine" count, already stale since `Constructor|CodeElement`, now lists the six hand-declared sentinels.
- Both fixtures already exist, so neither trap from the issue applies: the `bench/scope-capture` fingerprint and the Python captures golden do not move.

**Explicitly out of scope / not done here**

- The DDL is unchanged. The 16 unreached member rows (and the 8 reverse ones) stay declared: an unemitted declared pair costs DDL width, an emitted undeclared one aborts `analyze`. Dropping them would take `STRUCTURAL_PAIR_DDL` down by 24 lines, which matters for the `bench/schema-pairs` budget the schema docblock discusses, but it is a call about future emitters, so I left it to you. Happy to do it here or in a follow-up if you want them gone.

body:
Bumps [onnxruntime-common](https://github.com/Microsoft/onnxruntime) from 1.30.0 to 1.31.1.
Release notes

Sourced from onnxruntime-common's releases.

ONNX Runtime v1.31.1

ONNX Runtime 1.31.1 is a patch release that fixes an OpenVINO-enabled Python build regression and corrects WASM Debug external-data tests. These notes cover changes since ONNX Runtime 1.31.0.

Highlights

  • Fixed a provider-info namespace mismatch that caused compilation failures when building with both OpenVINO and Python enabled (#33327).
  • Fixed WASM Debug test failures by skipping file-backed external-data cases unsupported by the WASM test module, while retaining compile-output checks, buffer-destination coverage, and native test coverage. This is a test-only change and does not change runtime behavior (#33226).

Contributors

Thanks to our 3 human contributors for this release!

@​eserscor, @​mustjab, @​tianleiwu

Full Changelog: rel-1.31.0...rel-1.31.1

Release highlights were prepared with AI assistance.

ONNX Runtime v1.31.0

ONNX Runtime 1.31.0 stabilizes model-package and EPContext data APIs, improves CPU model loading and quantized MoE inference, expands device-based execution-provider selection, and strengthens model-loading and runtime reliability. These notes cover changes since ONNX Runtime 1.30.0. CUDA and WebGPU kernel updates are summarized here; detailed provider notes are covered by their separate plugin EP releases.

Highlights

  • Promoted the model-package API and EPContext data callbacks to stable C and C++ APIs, with EPContext callback support added across language bindings (#33166, #32265).
  • Reduced CPU session-initialization overhead by parallelizing eligible weight prepacking, and accelerated block-wise INT4/INT8 QMoE experts with MLAS QNBit kernels and grouped expert dispatch (#31691, #32644, #32668).
  • Added x86 FP16 LayerNorm/RMSNorm acceleration, Arm KleidiAI SVE2.1 FP16 GEMM support, and additional RISC-V vector kernels (#32715, #32670, #32710).
  • Enabled CoreML participation in device-based EP selection, including Apple Neural Engine selection through PREFER_NPU (#31975).
  • Added workspace-memory accounting and verification for constrained-memory graph partitioning, alongside broader model, graph, and tensor validation (#31962, #32189).

Announcements & Compatibility

  • CUDA Plugin EP v0.3.0 and WebGPU Plugin EP v0.5.0 are matched with ONNX Runtime 1.31.0. For contrib-op compatibility, core and the plugin must use the same contributed-operator schemas; building both from the same ONNX Runtime revision is recommended. Schema mismatches can cause incorrect execution or crashes and may not be detected during plugin registration.
  • GatherBlockQuantized behavior change: out-of-range indices now produce zero output slices across CPU, CUDA, and WebGPU for both integer and floating-point quantized formats. This deliberately differs from ONNX Gather error semantics (#32480).
  • Experimental API migration: model-package consumers should use OrtApi::GetModelPackageApi and the stable OrtModelPackageApi table. EPContext callback registration now uses stable APIs; the corresponding experimental lookup entries were removed. The stable native callback contract carries callback/state pointers, with payload limits enforced by application callbacks, bindings, or EPs rather than a native read-options policy (#33166, #32265).
  • ACL EP is deprecated and will be removed in a future release. Source builds using --use_acl now receive a deprecation warning (#32564).
  • The ONNX dependency remains at 1.22.0. The initial ONNX 1.23 integration was reverted pending upstream fixes; this release does not ship that integration's new opset or FLOAT6 support (#33073).
  • Supported native builds now default to 1DS telemetry. Windows TraceLogging remains selectable with --use_windows_telemetry or onnxruntime_USE_WINDOWS_TELEMETRY=ON; telemetry can be disabled with --no_telemetry (#32384).

New Features

Core APIs & Runtime

  • Stabilized the model-package C and C++ APIs for loading packages, selecting compatible model variants, and creating sessions (#33166).
  • Stabilized named EPContext data read/write callbacks for application-managed storage. Added EP support negotiation so registered callbacks do not silently fall back to filesystem I/O (#32265).
  • Extended the Compile API to write external initializers and EP context data to buffers, enabling in-memory compilation workflows for models larger than 2 GB (#31347).
  • Added workspace-memory accounting, source reporting, and post-partition reservation verification. Set session.strict_workspace_verification=1 to fail initialization on workspace declaration overruns or nonzero orphaned reservations; strict verification is not supported for ORT-format model loads (#31962, #32189).
  • Added the opt-in source-build option onnxruntime_DISABLE_DEVICE_DISCOVERY=ON to skip platform accelerator probing and report only the CPU device (#32592).

body:
## Summary

Adds an `anthropic` provider to `gitnexus wiki` that calls the Anthropic Messages API directly: `x-api-key` auth, a top-level `system` prompt, `max_tokens`, and the Messages streaming events. A user with only an `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` (no Claude Code install, no OpenRouter account) can now generate a wiki.

## Motivation / context

Closes #3413.

#1404 added the same provider in May and was closed after one review request: consolidate the second SSE reader with the existing one, through "an abstraction where you tell the function how you want the streaming to progress". This PR is built around that. There is one `readSSEStream`; it takes a `StreamProtocol` that says what each `data:` payload contributes (text, or a stop reason that makes the answer unusable) and how the provider names a stop at the token limit. Chat completions and Messages are two small protocol objects.

## Areas touched

- [x] `gitnexus/` (CLI / core / MCP server)
- [ ] `gitnexus-web/` (Vite / React UI)
- [ ] `.github/` (workflows, actions)
- [ ] `eval/` or other tooling
- [x] Docs / agent config only (`AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `.cursor/`, `llms.txt`, etc.)

## Scope & constraints

**In scope**

- `llm-client.ts`
  - `LLMProvider` gains `anthropic`; `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` (`https://api.anthropic.com/v1`), `ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_MODEL` (`claude-opus-5-5`) and `ANTHROPIC_API_VERSION` (`2023-06-01`).
  - `resolveLLMConfig`: for `anthropic`, key from `--api-key`, then `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, then `GITNEXUS_API_KEY`. `OPENAI_API_KEY` is never sent to Anthropic. `GITNEXUS_LLM_BASE_URL` / `--base-url` still override the endpoint (proxies), with the same `validateLLMBaseUrl` rules.
  - `callLLM` builds the request per provider (`buildChatCompletionsRequest`, which is the previous code moved as is, and `buildAnthropicRequest`), then shares the fetch, retry, timeout and error handling.
  - Messages request: `model`, `max_tokens` (the existing `--max-completion-tokens` / `GITNEXUS_MAX_COMPLETION_TOKENS` limit), `system`, one user message, `stream` when streaming. No `temperature`: current Claude models reject sampling parameters, and the wiki's `temperature: 0` is a chat-completions default, not a user setting.
  - Responses: only `text` blocks become the page; thinking content is skipped. `max_tokens`, `refusal`, and `model_context_window_exceeded` stop reasons fail instead of saving partial pages. Streaming requires `message_stop`; premature EOF and mid-stream errors fail. Readers are cancelled and unlocked on completion or failure, including when the server keeps its connection open.
  - Anthropic requests reject redirects so `x-api-key` and source-containing request bodies cannot be forwarded to another endpoint. The shared reader accepts SSE `data:` lines with or without the optional space.
  - Image parts (data URL or https URL) become Messages `image` blocks; video parts are refused with a clear error.
- `cli/wiki.ts`: `--provider anthropic` fills in the endpoint and default model like `--provider minimax` does; the interactive setup gets `[7] Anthropic (api.anthropic.com)`; the no-key message lists `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`.
- `CLIConfig.provider`, the `--provider` help (en, zh-CN), the README and the three `gitnexus-cli` skill copies.

**Explicitly out of scope / not done here**

- The web UI's own LLM settings (`gitnexus-web`), which are separate from the CLI wiki.
- Prompt caching, effort or thinking settings, and refusal fallbacks. The request stays minimal; any of these can be a follow-up.
- `anthropic-version: 2026-10-21`. The request sends nothing that version changes, and `2023-06-01` is the value proxies and gateways accept today. Moving is a one-constant change.

## Implementation notes

- `impact` upstream: `callLLM` HIGH (9, every HTTP wiki call through `WikiGenerator.invokeLLM`), `readSSEStream` HIGH (7), `buildRequestUrl` HIGH (7, unchanged), `resolveLLMConfig` LOW (2), `wikiCommandImpl` LOW (1). For every provider other than `anthropic`, the request is built by the same code as before, and the stream reader keeps the same rules: a `content_filter` chunk's delta is dropped, a `length` chunk's delta is kept and then the response is rejected, malformed `data:` lines are skipped. The existing chat-completions tests (`wiki-llm-client`, `wiki-llm-truncation`) pass unchanged.
- The interactive menu: Anthropic takes `[7]`, so detected local CLIs start at `[8]` instead of `[7]`.
- Graph checks after merging main (`450702e`): the pre-commit all-changes check completed (26 files, 237 symbols, 15 processes, HIGH risk; includes changes merged from main). The full PR comparison reports 13 files, 149 symbols, and 10 processes. That comparison remains `partial` for the one provider-help string in `cli/index.ts`, outside an indexed symbol range; re-analysis/retry confirmed the gap, and the exact hunk plus built `--help` output were checked manually.

## Testing & verification

- [x] New `test/unit/wiki-llm-anthropic.test.ts` (20 tests): config defaults and key precedence (`ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `GITNEXUS_API_KEY`, never `OPENAI_API_KEY`); the exact request (URL, `x-api-key`, `anthropic-version`, no `Authorization`, body with `system` and `max_tokens`, no `temperature`); a base URL override with a trailing slash; text-only content when thinking blocks are present, with usage mapped; `max_tokens` and `refusal` rejected, non-streaming and streaming; thinking deltas skipped and `onChunk` progress over a stream split mid-event; a mid-stream `error` event; image conversion and video refusal.
- [x] `test/unit/wiki-flags.test.ts`: switching to `--provider anthropic` saves the Anthropic endpoint and default model.
- [x] Mutations, each red on its test: thinking deltas kept as text, no version header, `temperature` sent, `OPENAI_API_KEY` accepted for `anthropic`, a streamed `max_tokens` stop ignored, the CLI default endpoint dropped.
- [x] End to end with the built CLI against a local fake Messages API that checks every request (path, headers, body fields) and streams a thinking block before the text: `gitnexus wiki . --provider anthropic --api-key … --base-url http://127.0.0.1:<port>/v1 --force` on a two-file TypeScript repo made 3 streaming requests with no check failing, wrote `authentication.md` and `overview.md` without the thinking text, and saved `provider: anthropic`, `model: claude-opus-5-5` to the config.
- [x] Added redirect, incomplete-stream, context-window, compact-SSE, and reader-cleanup regressions. Seven new cases failed against the original PR before the fixes. Two generator recovery cases verify that incomplete pages remain absent, failed modules retry at the same commit, and successful sibling pages stay unchanged.
- [x] Focused wiki and skill-sync validation: 12 files, 362 tests passed. Build, source and test typechecks, formatting, and ESLint passed (three pre-existing warnings).
- [x] Full core suite, four shards with the exact lockfile dependencies: 31,615 passed, 103 skipped, six initial runner-related failures. All six passed on isolated reruns: four setup cases with inherited `CODEX_HOME` omitted, one Vue rename case after a concurrent generated-file rebuild, and one server clone-path case with the expected `.gitnexus` directory name. No code changes were needed for those six failures.
- [x] [GitHub Actions for `f4080b86a`](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/actions/runs/41822494640): CI Gate passed; 33,891 tests passed, zero failed or unverified. Linux, macOS, Windows, benchmarks, coverage completeness, formatting, typechecks, CodeQL, dependency review, and secret scanning passed.
- [x] The hosted GitNexus review found no issues in 13 changed files. Its CRITICAL blast-radius warning is retained in the review summary below.
- [ ] Vercel's deployment check still requires NexusCore team authorization for the contributor.
- [ ] Not run against the real Anthropic API (no key here).

## Risk & rollout

Existing providers retain their request formats. The shared stream reader now accepts compact SSE lines and releases readers on errors and completion. Anthropic proxies must use their final Messages endpoint URL because redirects are rejected. Users selecting a local CLI by number in interactive setup see it one higher.

## Checklist

- [x] PR body meets repo minimum length (workflow may label short descriptions)
- [ ] If `AGENTS.md` / overlays changed: headers, scope block, and changelog updated per project conventions
- [x] No secrets, tokens, or machine-specific paths committed

<!-- gitnexus-pr-summary:v1:start -->

---

### 📝 Summary by GitNexus

## Summary

*This appears to be a wiki-generation provider and API change, with impact spanning core wiki, CLI, and storage code. The blast level is critical, while the file risk classification is low.*

**🔴 CRITICAL blast radius. A wiki-generation change adding a native Anthropic Messages API provider reaches 52 graph dependents.**

The main implementation focus is `gitnexus/src/core/wiki/llm-client.ts`, with related changes in `gitnexus/src/cli/wiki.ts` and `gitnexus/src/storage/repo-manager.ts`. The graph impact spans `Local`, `Wiki`, `Storage`, `Cli`, `Integration`, `Server`, `Mcp`, `Unit`, and `Augmentation`.

Review the provider implementation alongside `gitnexus/test/unit/wiki-llm-anthropic.test.ts` and `gitnexus/test/unit/wiki-flags.test.ts`. The change also updates CLI documentation and English and Chinese translations; there are no HIGH or CRITICAL risk files and no cross-repo consumers.

title: feat(embeddings): preserve AST chunk coverage
body:
## Summary

Preserve complete source coverage for large callable embeddings and use AST boundaries inside oversized statements, arrays, and argument lists. Adapt cAST's split/merge algorithm to the existing tree-sitter parsers, with MIT attribution and no new dependencies.

- Keep fitting child nodes whole, preserve source offsets and delimiters, and use bounded character splitting for oversized leaves.
- Project classes into declarations, fields and structural names while excluding implementation bodies.
- Read eligible full source only after verifying indexed fingerprints and contained real paths; bound the source cache to 64 files / 16 MiB.
- Refresh affected AST-layout fingerprints, including hydrated source larger than a custom chunk budget. Preserve short callable and fixed-window fingerprints, model invalidation, checkpoint recovery and reuse of unchanged prepared inputs.

Replace repeated native sibling walks with verified offset lookups when splitting oversized AST nodes. Preserve exact chunk layouts, text, offsets and overlap; add regressions for sparse-array gaps and overlap-tail progress.

Fixes #702.

## Performance

`gitnexus/bench/embedding-chunking/measure.mjs` runs directly in `.github/workflows/ci-tests.yml`. `baseline.json` records 25 cohorts / 400 measured pairs against base `3c068dd11`, with three warmup pairs and 16 alternating measured pairs per cohort. Each revision uses its own process and independent dependencies. Measurements use Snowflake/snowflake-arctic-embed-xs on CPU with two threads; each inference sample embeds four nodes.

| Fixture | Median inference, base → candidate | Inputs per node |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| short | 12.21 → 12.31 ms | 1 → 1 |
| flat | 773.47 → 709.83 ms | 3 → 3 |
| nested | 1616.68 → 1219.44 ms | 6 → 5 |
| large | 1402.06 → 2053.97 ms | 5 → 8 |
| medium | 304.52 → 201.01 ms | 5 → 8 |
| array | 1848.34 → 1320.04 ms | 6 → 5 |
| literal | 67.28 → 133.53 ms | 5 → 11 |
| class | 1550.66 → 39.20 ms | 5 → 1 |

These are synthetic diagnostic measurements, not timing gates or whole-repository performance claims. Large functions and long literals recover source omitted by the capped baseline and therefore do more work. Preparation, hashing, p95s and individual samples are included in the JSON. Memory observations are per revision at sample completion, not peak measurements. The recorded source and runner digests identify the measured implementation.

A separate C++/Node-API prototype passed 48 boundary-parity cases. Including AST packing, it was 2.4–5.1× slower than the JavaScript reference on flat/nested/array/Unicode fixtures; including parsing, 1.2–1.6× slower. The long-literal fixture was an exception. Native packaging remains outside this PR.

The final JavaScript-only optimization reduces normalized chunking time by **7.36% on the selection set and 4.95% on the held-out set**, compared with the preceding `c15f48f0e` implementation. Both results use five fresh paired runs; chunk outputs remain identical. The held-out result narrowly misses the original 5% automatic acceptance threshold and was explicitly accepted by the user. This is a chunking measurement, not an end-to-end indexing speedup. The separate `jsOptimization` evidence is recorded in `gitnexus/bench/embedding-chunking/baseline.json`.

## Validation

- **151 focused tests and the execution audit passed**, with zero unhandled errors or unverified tests. Three new real-parser expression regressions failed before the splitter change; the source-backed fingerprint regression failed before its fix.
- **48 frozen exact-output configurations and 568 supplemental comparisons** (168 stress, 400 deterministic malformed inputs) match the preceding implementation's complete chunk JSON. The two new real-parser regressions fail when their respective native-lookup or overlap safeguard is removed.
- **96 stress cases** verified exact source slices, full non-whitespace coverage, hard size bounds and bounded overlap, including deep nesting, long leaves, Unicode and CRLF.
- The final paired benchmark completed all 25 cohorts, then both native processes exited successfully before writing the result.
- Build, source/test typechecks, formatting and scoped ESLint passed (existing warnings remain). The earlier broader implementation review passed 299 targeted tests across 12 files, including two native lifecycle tests, and checked the workflow with actionlint/ShellCheck and Zizmor.
- Deep and simplification follow-up reviewed correctness, cache invalidation, boundary coverage, performance, native lifetime constraints, standards and prior feedback. All 11 review threads remain resolved. The follow-up graph change analysis is LOW; the full PR remains CRITICAL across the broader source/embedding paths. Graph flow discovery is bounded.
- Earlier full-suite local results remain a limitation: 31,678 passed, 21 failed, 103 skipped and a native worker SIGSEGV. Ten failures reproduced on unchanged base; the remaining eleven passed follow-up runs. The full suite was not repeated for this follow-up.
- Optimization commit `1c6b34b65` is pushed; merge readiness depends on its required CI checks. The preceding `ea171625d` run passed the embedding benchmark and execution audit after the CI fixes. [Current PR checks](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/pull/3817/checks)

## Risk and rollout

Changed chunk layouts and class projections regenerate affected vectors on the next embedding-enabled analyze/sync. Short unchanged default-model inputs keep their hashes. A checkout that no longer matches the indexed snapshot fails source verification; reindex before retrying. Legacy indexes without source fingerprints also require reanalysis.

More complete source coverage can produce more vectors and take longer. `GITNEXUS_EMBEDDING_CHUNK_STRATEGY=fixed` selects fixed callable splitting while retaining source recovery and class projection. Rollback requires reverting the change and regenerating affected embeddings.

<!-- gitnexus-pr-summary:v1:start -->

---

### 📝 Summary by GitNexus

## Summary

*This is a broad change to GitNexus’s embeddings pipeline, touching core processing alongside tests, documentation, and CI. Its critical blast radius warrants close review of the pipeline and the CI workflow.*

**🔴 CRITICAL blast radius: an AST-based embeddings change spanning chunking, configuration, sync, and analysis, with 22 dependents.**

Impact is concentrated in `Embeddings`, with additional impact in `Server`, `Lbug`, `Cli`, and `Integration`. Start with `gitnexus/src/core/embeddings/embedding-pipeline.ts`, then review the AST chunking logic in `gitnexus/src/core/embeddings/chunker.ts` and `gitnexus/src/core/embeddings/ast-utils.ts`, including `chunkNode`, `astChunk`, and `buildChunk`. The sync path also changes `embeddingsSyncCommand` and checkpoint handlers in `gitnexus/src/cli/embeddings-sync.ts`.

`.github/workflows/ci-tests.yml` is the HIGH risk file, so review its changes alongside the embedding tests and CI configuration.

_Added by GitNexus for PR #3817. Edit freely — this block is replaced on the next review, everything above it is left untouched._

title: 1.6.12 (latest) still pins @ladybugdb/core 0.18.3 - the #3564/#3569 blank-id defect is live on Windows for Function nodes, and it self-propagates through the incremental write set
body:
## Summary

The defect diagnosed and closed in #3564 / #3569 is **still live in the published `latest`**, because `gitnexus@1.6.12` pins `"@ladybugdb/core": "0.18.3"` — the exact engine the fix bisected as broken (LadybugDB #737, `StringColumn::scanFiltered`).

This report adds three things the earlier threads do not have:

1. **Windows x64 confirmation** (the earlier reproductions were macOS and Linux), and the victim node type is `Function`, not `Method` — so it is not Python/`unittest`-specific.
2. **The damage self-propagates**, which is why it looks permanent and why "just re-run analyze" makes it worse. Measured chain below.
3. Measurements that **exclude** the parse cache, the CSV emitter and leftover staging, so the remaining explanation is the native engine.

## Environment

- `gitnexus@1.6.12` (`npm dist-tags latest`, still current as of 2026-11-03), `dist` build, Node v24.19.0
- Windows 11 x64, npm global install
- Repo: 779 indexed files, 10,062 nodes, 27,759 edges, 2,340 `Function` nodes, mixed PHP/TS/TSX/JS/PY/MJS
- `.gitnexus/meta.json`: `contentRetention: "full"`, 6,847 embeddings

## Symptom

Plain `analyze --index-only` exits 0 and prints `Repository indexed successfully`. A read-back then shows:

```
MATCH (n:Function) RETURN count(n) AS total,
  sum(CASE WHEN coalesce(size(n.id),0)=0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS empty_id
--> 2340 | 2212
```

`name`, `filePath`, `startLine` survive; `id` and `content` are both empty, 1:1. Only `Function` is hit — `File`/`Method`/`Variable`/`Class`/`Const` are clean (0 of 779 / 962 / 306 / 67 / 436).

Consequence: `embeddings sync` aborts with `duplicated primary key value :0` (the embedding key is `nodeId + ":" + chunk`), and everything that joins on node id returns wrong answers.

## Reproduction (10 controlled runs, clean rebuild before each)

```
analyze --index-only --no-parse-cache        # clean start
MATCH (n:Function) ...                        --> 0 blank ids

# then ONE commit-like change, plain incremental analyze:
changed=4, added=0, deleted=0 (3 markdown + 1 .ps1)
  + "+9 importer(s) added to writable set (BFS depth <= 4)"
MATCH (n:Function) ...                        --> 2212 blank ids, 239 distinct files
```

**2 of the ~10 runs corrupted; 8 stayed clean with the same inputs.** That intermittency is what sent us down the wrong paths for a long time, and it is consistent with a segment-boundary read defect rather than a deterministic planner bug.

## Finding 1 — the write set is not the input, it is the damage

A **4-file** change (none of them source code) rewrote `Function` rows for **239 files**. The write set was `toWrite` + importer-BFS(<=4) + `computeEffectiveWriteSet` (1 hop over every file-owned edge).

That only makes sense if the *previous* state already had unusable ids: `computeEffectiveWriteSet` builds its map with `indexNodeFilePaths`, i.e. **keyed on `n.id`**. With 2,212 rows sharing `id = ''` that map collapses, the 1-hop walk resolves to the wrong files, the write set balloons, and the run rewrites far more than it should — re-collapsing more ids. **One lost id therefore turns into a repo-wide, self-sustaining loss.** It also explains why the 128 surviving `Function` nodes are exactly the ones outside the write set (`_standalone/*/lib/shims/*`, `store/db-store.ts`, `auth.ts`).

Note the escalation valve (#2409) does **not** save you here: 239/779 = 30.7% < `INCREMENTAL_MAX_WRITE_FRACTION`, so the surgical path runs and spreads the damage instead of doing a clean full write.

## Finding 2 — what it is NOT (all measured)

| Candidate | Measurement | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| Parse cache replay | 243 shards read back with `loadParseCacheChunk`: **10,397 nodes, 0 blank `id`** | clean |
| CSV row emission | captured `function.csv` from two runs: **369 and 582 rows, 0 blank `id`** | clean |
| Leftover staging (fixed-name `.gitnexus/csv`) | deleted before the corrupting run; it then found **0** leftovers and still corrupted | excluded |
| `contentRetention` | `full` | n/a |
| Language | .php / .tsx / .ts / .js / .py / .mjs all affected | n/a |

So the rows leave the emitter correct and come back wrong — which is the native filtered-scan signature from #3564.

## Another repository on the same machine

A second, unrelated index on the same box (`openreel-video`) reads **8,920 of 10,062** `Function` nodes blank. Same CLI, same engine, no shared storage.

## Impact

- `embeddings sync` is unusable until a full rebuild: `duplicated primary key value :0`.
- `detect_changes` / `impact` / `context` return misleading results once ids collapse (they still exit 0 — nothing fails loudly).
- The only repair is `analyze --no-parse-cache` (measured **531 s** on this repo); the next incremental can re-break it.

## Ask

Please cut a release that ships a LadybugDB with #737 fixed. `1.6.13-rc.201` already pins `@ladybugdb/core: 0.22.0`, which looks like the right vehicle — the remaining question is Windows:

- #3706 reports Windows breakage on 0.21.1 for `fetchRoutesWithConsumers` / node-detail (`OPTIONAL MATCH` planner). It does **not** touch `analyze`, so it may already be fine on 0.22.0 — but Windows CI does not run those tests, so it is currently unverified.

Until then, every Windows user on `latest` is stuck between a 0.18.3 defect that silently corrupts the index and an RC that is untested on Windows for part of the query surface.

## Workaround for other users on 1.6.12

```
# detect
MATCH (n:Function) RETURN count(n), sum(CASE WHEN coalesce(size(n.id),0)=0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)
# if blank ids > 0: DO NOT run another incremental analyze (it spreads),
# repair first:
gitnexus analyze --index-only --no-parse-cache
gitnexus embeddings sync
```

title: perf(analyze): batch Git checkout metadata reads
body:
## Summary

Read the current commit and branch in one Git process per checkout snapshot. Analyze still takes a fresh snapshot after acquiring the index lock, reducing the normal metadata-read path from four Git processes to two per analysis.

## Motivation / context

Follow-up to #3805. Spawning Git becomes more expensive in a long-lived analyzer process with a larger resident memory footprint.

On the 862-file ingestion corpus, three alternating baseline/candidate edit pairs per lifecycle produced these median metadata-read times:

| Lifecycle | Before | After |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Fresh process | 16.3 ms | 8.0 ms |
| Persistent process | 175.7 ms | 93.5 ms |

Measured with Node 22.23.3, two parser workers, a 4096 MiB heap limit, FTS enabled, and the existing edit benchmark's pre-sample GC. Seeds were excluded. The baseline is #3805's merged source tree (`450702e10`), equivalent to its tested head `eca9c1319`.

Observed total-edit medians were 21.46 → 20.92 seconds (fresh) and 20.79 → 19.90 seconds (persistent). Three pairs on a shared host cannot attribute those larger differences to this small change; the direct metadata timings and process counts are the performance evidence.

## Areas touched

- [x] `gitnexus/` (CLI / core / MCP server)

## Scope & constraints

**In scope**

- Combine commit/branch reads at each existing checkout-snapshot boundary.
- Preserve fallback behavior and cover branch changes, detached HEAD, linked worktrees, unborn branches, ambiguous refs, non-Git directories, and unavailable Git.

**Explicitly out of scope / not done here**

- Native compilation, semantic-resolution changes, FTS changes, and persistent metadata caches.

## Implementation notes

`getCurrentCheckout` uses `git rev-parse HEAD --abbrev-ref HEAD` through `execFileSync`. Failed or incomplete combined reads fall back to the existing independent helpers. Branch validation and the under-lock reread remain in place. Tests retain coverage for a commit landing during lock acquisition and for lock release on failure.

## Testing & verification

- 263 focused tests passed across Git utilities, analyze, FTS repair, lock concurrency, and multi-branch analysis using `npm test -- <test paths> --maxWorkers=2`; the full suite was not run locally.
- `cd gitnexus && npm run build`
- `cd gitnexus && npx tsc --noEmit`
- `cd gitnexus && npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.test.json`
- Prettier and ESLint on all four changed files: passed; ESLint reported no errors.
- Six real-edit benchmark pairs: identical semantic node/edge digests, incremental writes, and correct persisted call targets after every edit.

## Risk & rollout

The existing independent reads remain the error fallback. No persistent cache, schema change, or migration is introduced. Memory samples are not a proof of whole-indexer linear scaling. Reverting this commit restores the prior metadata-read path.

## Checklist

- [x] PR body meets repo minimum length.
- [x] No secrets, tokens, or machine-specific paths committed.

title: perf(storage): skip redundant cache interning work
body:
## Summary

Speed up V8 cache string interning while preserving graph values, aliases, cycles, collection order, and cross-shard string pooling. Plain-object fields skip redundant recursive calls and identity writes; per-call visit tracking uses a Set. All visited objects remain reachable from the deserialized graph during traversal, and visit state is discarded after each call.

The new CI check measures actual built runtimes on identical source corpora and fails on a slowdown above 5% in either the overall median or median paired ratio, for wall and process CPU time. It also verifies semantic graph equality, persisted call targets, and real-shard interning equivalence.

## Motivation / context

Follow-up to #3819. The earlier version reported a fresh-process regression despite a faster interner. This revision adds repeatable checks to `.github/workflows/ci-tests.yml` and improves the interner further. It does not claim a proven whole-indexer speedup: fresh-process overall wall median is 2.9% higher locally, while its paired median improves.

## Areas touched

- [x] `gitnexus/` (storage, tests, benchmarks)
- [x] `.github/` (CI performance gate)

## Scope & constraints

In scope: cache interning, paired performance measurements, and CI enforcement. No cache-format, parser semantics, dependency, or schema changes. String interning remains enabled.

## Implementation notes

The existing indexing benchmark supplies fresh and persistent process runs. Each records a seed plus nine real call edits; seed and first edit are excluded, leaving eight measured pairs with alternating order. Timers stop before graph verification. The interner comparison loads all real baseline cache shards, verifies graph/serialized-byte/string-pool equivalence, then excludes two warm-ups and measures eight alternating rounds. Missing, duplicate, screened, cold-cache, nonfinite, or semantically inconsistent evidence cannot pass.

CI publishes a job summary and retains raw measurements and diagnostics as `lexical-lookup-performance` for 30 days, including failure paths. The 5% budget is an operational regression limit, not statistical significance or a guarantee across all hardware and repositories. Persistent samples share processes.

## Testing & verification

Baseline `3c068dd11d53c1c8f373957d0c144da0acbfbc17`, Node v22.23.3, two parser workers, 4096 MiB main heap, identical 862-file source corpus. Of 1,136 compiled JavaScript files, only `storage/v8-sidecar.js` differs. Candidate measurements use the final working-tree implementation; its built module SHA-256 is `0f65d8e4bbb857e0331f288ce0d7f068823703ece65566bc9a0e73fd19ecdd40`.

### Hosted performance

[Final-head benchmark](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/actions/runs/41995692831/job/127141522295) passed on PR head `1862ac49b0fb8b8085cbba906d6973eb3de40edf` (merge `ea000e01bec2f64c6ea5a9c2941425fc42149f56`). Its production module hash matches the implementation above. Raw evidence is retained in [lexical-lookup-performance](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/actions/runs/41995692831/artifacts/13403827116).

Warm-up samples excluded; execution order alternates. Times in ms.

| Measurement | Base median | Candidate median | Median change | Median paired change | Result |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |
| fresh/ms | 25215.5 | 25022.0 | -0.8% | -0.7% | within-budget |
| fresh/cpuMs | 37140.3 | 36971.0 | -0.5% | -0.6% | within-budget |
| persistent/ms | 24604.3 | 24323.1 | -1.1% | -1.4% | within-budget |

    A tool that throws GraphDrained, for example one whose inner graph run is drained with RunControl.requestDrain(), now stops the agent run with that error, as an interrupt already did, instead of coming back as an error ToolMessage that lets the agent go on as if the tool had failed.

  • #11877 2f4d891 Thanks @​byhow! - feat(agents): add opt-in interruptMode: "per_call" to humanInTheLoopMiddleware. Each gated tool call raises its own interrupt (type: "tool_approval", with a typed responseSchema built from the tool's allowed decisions), answered by interrupt ID. respond is supported. Edits are pinned to the called tool and checked against the input side of its Zod v4 schema, so its transforms run once, when the tool does. An invalid answer throws without being saved. Also adds Interrupt.response_schema. In both modes, interruptOn: { tool: true } now allows every decision, respond included, as in Python; batched mode is otherwise unchanged.

langchain@1.5.16

Patch Changes

  • #11880 22ea038 Thanks @​eliornl! - fix(langchain): createAgent with middleware now passes a Command built by a different copy of @langchain/langgraph to the graph as-is, instead of merging it into the input state as a plain object.

langchain@1.5.15

Patch Changes

title: feat(analyze): make indexing resource-bounded and resumable
body:
Publish the verified graph and keyword index before generating embeddings. Provider failures leave the graph usable; another analyze resumes durable vector work without repeating completed provider requests. Closes #3598.

- Separate graph and vector publication with ownership receipts, crash recovery, complete-vector receipts and compatible legacy reuse.
- Preserve automatic heap sizing and independent parser-worker limits. `--resource-budget` adds an aggregate phase ceiling; reservations are not OS-enforced RSS limits.
- Route CLI, watch, auto-sync, HTTP, MCP queries and status through published generations. Pending semantic work reports degradation and preserves keyword fallback. Permanently rejected inputs stop after three attempts while retaining healthy vectors.
- Stream fixed and AST chunks with source ranges, class projections, notebook ranges, overlap and input fingerprints preserved. Batch vector writes and source-aware hash completion within bounded recovery units.
- Retain paid artifacts when ownership is ambiguous. Reclaim orphan attempt metadata, retained-copy preparations and obsolete generations only when recovery and native ownership permit it. Explicit dropping removes validated vector artifacts and their owners so subsequent embedding runs regenerate them. Cancellation holds reservations until native resources or child processes exit; terminal worker messages clear the analysis deadline while still awaiting exit.
- Defer unused parser/provider imports and analyzer receipts. Skip redundant Git identity probes for inferred names and ordinary checkout roots; worktrees, symlinks and Git overrides retain their resolution. Use native automatic transactions for standalone vector writes while preserving multi-query transactions, durable WAL commits and final publication checkpoints.

`MIGRATION.md` covers upgraded CLI/MCP clients and hooks, complete-index backup and rollback. Legacy retirement receipts include ctime; earlier preview receipts without it are retained but cannot certify reuse. No PR-added files remain under `docs/plans`.

Validation: build, production/test typechecks, formatting and lint pass (existing lint warnings remain). The latest resource, preflight, progress and native vector suite passes 288 correctness tests, including a cache-pressure case that completes all work within its admitted byte budget. Earlier cache-path, cleanup, hook and legacy regressions passed 274 cases; real CLI phase/lifecycle and adoption checks also pass. The native crash-window test requires the VECTOR extension. Graph impact and change analysis ran before commits; unmapped anonymous test callbacks and comment-only changes were reviewed directly after refreshing and repeating graph analysis.

[CI run 42361296439](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/actions/runs/42361296439) passed every native test shard but failed the fresh-HTTP performance comparison in both profiles: default 1.0152× baseline (95% interval 1.0067–1.0237×), explicit 1.0252× (1.0036–1.0474×). The other five scenarios passed. Its execution audit also rejected four parameterized publication tests with duplicate titles; those assertions themselves passed.

`dd45978cd` removes redundant per-unit physical vector checkpoints. Acknowledgements follow verified transactions whose WAL is already durable in the pinned LadybugDB version. Automatic checkpoints bound WAL growth, and sealing still checkpoints before read-only publication. Real-process crash tests require a nonempty WAL before recovery and verify completed inputs are not replayed. All 117 vector, journal and restart tests pass with VECTOR required. The 43 publication tests also pass with unique parameterized titles, and the execution auditor recognizes all 43 cases. Build, typechecks, formatting and lint pass. No local benchmarks were run.

Both performance profiles passed in [CI run 42364018083](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/actions/runs/42364018083) on `dd45978cd`. All six scenarios in each profile have seven measured pairs, no detected regression and no inconclusive result. Equal-work and no-paid-input-replay checks passed. Ratios below are candidate/baseline (lower is faster):

| Scenario | Default | Explicit resource budget |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Graph only | 0.919× | 0.892× |
| No-op | 0.597× | 0.576× |
| Incremental | 0.878× | 0.861× |
| Fresh HTTP | 0.966× | 0.974× |
| Cached HTTP | 0.608× | 0.583× |
| Resumed HTTP | 0.259× | 0.289× |

Fresh-HTTP 95% intervals are 0.960–0.973× (default) and 0.962–0.986× (explicit). The complete CI workflow and CI Gate pass: 70 successful jobs and two skipped. The execution audit verifies 32,531 CLI/core tests, 516 web tests and 1,650 eval cases, with zero unverified cases or failures. CodeQL and Docker also pass on this commit. These synthetic fixtures do not establish universal performance equivalence.

The completed feedback batch has 33 verified, resolved threads: 23 fixes and ten evidence-backed rebuttals. Ten later findings have verified acknowledgments and remain open for the bounded follow-up decision required by the feedback workflow: directory-sync retry paths, legacy-checkpoint routing/capabilities, per-query embedding-width diagnostics, chunker documentation, non-Linux PID reuse, and three claims with code-backed rebuttals (worker draining, indexed-input validation and automatic memory policy). No further feedback fix cycle has started.

`.github/workflows/ci-tests.yml` is the only benchmark entry point. Both automatic and explicit resource profiles compare base and candidate on the same runner: one warmup and seven alternating pairs for six scenarios. Equal-work and no-paid-input-replay checks precede timing comparisons. The 95% interval encloses paired bootstrap and Student-t estimates; a lower bound above 1.0 fails, while an interval crossing 1 remains inconclusive. Thresholds and sample counts are unchanged.

`gitnexus/bench/analyze-resume/` contains only `measure.mjs`, `baseline.json` and `README.md`. Historical baseline samples provide provenance; CI remeasures the current base. Benchmarks stay outside unit and integration suites. These fixtures do not establish universal performance equivalence, local-model throughput or concurrent query latency.

The separate GitNexus review check still reports a blocking unreachable-module finding for the benchmark entry point. CI invokes the script directly; both current performance jobs prove execution. title: perf(ingestion): reduce import emission memory
body:
## Summary

Large import graphs retain a global deduplication entry for every distinct file pair until emission finishes. Collect and emit consecutive source files individually to reduce that overlap, while preserving relationship order and import-reason precedence. Add progress checkpoints inside the import-emission phase and a CI benchmark check against a reviewed baseline.

## Motivation / context

Refs #3695. The reporter's last checkpoint was `sr-emit-callable-flow-end`; import emission runs before the next checkpoint. This addresses a measured allocation source in that window. The reporter's private-repository OOM has not been reproduced.

## Areas touched

- [x] `gitnexus/` (CLI / core / MCP server)
- [x] `.github/` (benchmark step and artifact in `ci-tests.yml`)

## Scope & constraints

- Read each scope once and retain its source path, including disk-backed scopes.
- Merge all consecutive scopes for a file before emitting its pairs. Preserve initializing > deferred > type-only precedence and first-seen order.
- Keep the global collector for interleaved source files and paths containing the legacy `->` delimiter, preserving existing collision behavior.
- Add bounded heap-probe checkpoints, nine emitter regression tests, and a reproducible benchmark using the production streaming sink.
- Follow the benchmark convention with a colocated `bench/import-emission/` runner (`measure.mjs`), fresh-process helper (`probe.mts`), README, checked-in `baseline.json`, and generated `measure.json`. CI checks three fresh processes for identical output hashes and at most 16 MiB of first-emission heap growth; it retains samples and failure diagnostics in the scope-resolution artifact.

## Performance evidence

Three paired fresh-process runs on Node 22.23.3/Linux, comparing the emitter at `3c068dd11d53c1c8f373957d0c144da0acbfbc17` against this change with 547,040 synthetic import pairs:

| Heap after GC | Baseline | This change |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| First emitted edge | 137.96 MiB | 51.01 MiB |
| Last emitted edge | 345.84 MiB | 258.19 MiB |

The last-edge checkpoint is about 25% lower. All six runs produced identical ordered-edge and CSV hashes. With a 288 MiB old-space limit, the baseline exhausted the heap and this change completed with the same hashes. These are synthetic memory measurements, not an end-to-end speed claim.

Reproduce from `gitnexus/`:

```sh

```

After consolidating the probe and README, **23 focused tests** and production/test/probe typechecks passed; the relocated runner again passed all three fresh-process samples.
- [x] Real CI-style benchmark: **3/3 candidate samples passed**. The previous emitter was rejected with 85–87 MiB first-emission heap growth despite identical hashes. A failed child process also failed the check and retained diagnostics in `measure.json`.

title: fix(devcontainer): move workspace and snapshots to Linux volumes
body:
## Summary

The devcontainer now runs the workspace and selected host configuration from persistent Linux Docker volumes instead of host bind mounts. The host stages a one-time copy of the checkout, Git state, local work and configuration. Container creation commits it once, so later rebuilds keep container edits and logins.

## Motivation / context

Host bind mounts keep every file access on the host filesystem, which is slow on Windows (9P) and needed `SYS_ADMIN` for tuning. Native volumes remove that runtime dependency. Existing dependency, configuration, cache and session volume names are unchanged.

## Areas touched

- [ ] `gitnexus/` (CLI / core / MCP server)
- [ ] `gitnexus-web/` (Vite / React UI)
- [x] `.github/` (workflows, actions) — `ci-devcontainer.yml` gains a macOS/Windows host-importer job
- [x] `eval/` or other tooling — `.devcontainer/` setup and tests
- [ ] Docs / agent config only

## Scope & constraints

**In scope**

- One-time import of the host checkout (including nested worktrees), Git metadata, local changes and selected configuration.
- Persistent source, staging and read-only snapshot volumes for the default and generated runtime profiles.
- Migration, backup, snapshot refresh and recovery instructions in `.devcontainer/README.md`.

**Explicitly out of scope / not done here**

- Continuous synchronization between host and container.
- Worktrees outside the checkout: they are not copied, and their registrations are not rewritten.
- Codespaces, and a full Docker Desktop rebuild of an existing workspace (see Testing).

## Implementation notes

**Stage on the host, commit once in the container.** `initializeCommand` also runs whenever an existing container is reopened. So the host only streams into a staging volume (`gitnexus-seed-<id>`), with a completion marker written last. `onCreateCommand` runs once per container creation: it commits a complete stage into the empty source volume, normalizes Git, empties the stage and repairs ownership.

- Reopening a pre-volume container after pulling this change only refreshes the stage, so the eventual rebuild imports current work.
- The commit script is copied from the host into the seed volume on every start, so it matches `devcontainer.json` with any image.

**Staging and snapshot copies are best-effort.** A busy host (indexer, agent, claude-mem writer) must not lock out a reopen. A failed copy clears its target, warns and retries on the next start. A creation without a complete stage stops at `onCreateCommand` with `No complete staged checkout`. A partial snapshot is replaced, and the seeding markers in `post-create.sh` are written only from a complete snapshot, so a later rebuild still seeds.

**Node writes the tar stream** (ustar plus PAX records for long and UTF-8 names), so the host needs only Node and Docker. Host tar is avoided for three reasons:

- Windows `tar.exe` reads file lists in the ANSI code page, so any non-ASCII path failed.
- macOS tar adds AppleDouble `._*` files.
- Both pad or truncate a file that changes while it is read. A size or mtime change now discards that copy instead.

**Git and links in the copy.**
- Nested worktrees created on a Windows or other host path are relinked to their copied location, and an absolute `core.worktree` is removed from the root and nested configs.
- Filesystem flags (`ignorecase`, `filemode`, `symlinks`) are probed on the destination, while staged and unstaged bytes are preserved.
- Selected snapshot roots that are symlinks (`~/.config/gh`, `~/.claude.json`) are followed like the bind mounts they replace. Dangling ones are kept as links. Every other symlink is restored verbatim inside the destination.

**Ownership.** Snapshots belong to the container's `node` user. A root host user maps to UID 1000, matching the Dev Containers CLI.

## Testing & verification

- [x] `node --test .devcontainer/*.test.cjs` — 122/122 pass on Linux, and also under `umask 077`.
- [x] macOS and Windows CI: the new `host-importer` job runs `initialize-volumes.test.cjs` on both and passes.
  - Tests replace the Docker CLI with a Node adapter through `GITNEXUS_IMPORT_DOCKER`.
  - Container-only code (`seedWorkspace`, snapshot ownership repair) is gated to Linux.
  - Symlink tests check for the symlink privilege before running.
  - UTF-8 names are verified with Python's `tarfile`, because Windows `tar.exe` cannot extract them. Docker's extractor can.
- [x] Full CI on `a36e92e76` (tests, typecheck, lint, packaged installs, devcontainer image builds): green.
- [x] Real Windows/Docker check before the redesign: reproduced `Cannot stat: Invalid argument` from WSL-created symlinks with host tar, and confirmed the Node-enumerated import on isolated fixtures.
- [ ] Full VS Code rebuild of an existing workspace — not performed. The staged commit flow is covered by the adapter tests only.
- [ ] GitNexus `detect-changes` — not applicable: `.devcontainer/` is not in the graph index.

## Risk & rollout

After the first rebuild, host and container files diverge. Before rebuilding:

1. Stop writers on the host: agents, Git operations, indexers and claude-mem.
2. Preserve the old container's writable layer and the existing volumes.
3. Keep the host folder and config path stable, so `${devcontainerId}` keeps selecting the same volumes.

A failed `onCreateCommand` is not retried in the same container; run **Rebuild Container** (or `devcontainer up --remove-existing-container`). The stage uses disk equal to the checkout until the container commits it. Host credential rotation does not refresh existing snapshots. A rollback must export container-only work before returning to a host-bound workspace.

## Checklist

- [x] PR body meets repo minimum length.
- [x] No secret or token values are included in the changes.
- [x] Scope is limited to `.devcontainer/` and its CI workflow.
