title: [bug] detect_changes forwards git CRLF/LF conversion warnings to the process stderr (MCP hosts / CLI logs)
body:
### Area

gitnexus (CLI / core / indexing / MCP server)

### Summary

`detect_changes` runs `git diff` through `execFileSync` without a `stdio` option, so git's CRLF/LF conversion warnings are inherited into GitNexus's own stderr — one line per modified file — and in MCP mode that reaches the host's console/log even though the call succeeds.

### Context

Running GitNexus 1.6.9 as a stdio MCP server inside a local MCP host on Windows. The target repo is a normal Windows checkout with `core.autocrlf=true` (system + user config) and **no `.gitattributes`**; tracked blobs are LF, and the working tree has modified files written as LF.

Calling the `detect_changes` tool (`{"repo":"<repo>","scope":"unstaged"}`) printed 24 lines like the following into the **host console**, not into the tool result:

```
warning: in the working copy of 'MANIFEST.md', LF will be replaced by CRLF the next time Git touches it
... (24 lines, one per modified file)
```

The tool itself returned success (`summary.changed_count`, `changed_files`, `risk_level`, exit code 0). `gitnexus detect-changes -r <repo>` on the CLI reproduces the same stderr flood.

Searched for duplicates before filing: `in the working copy of`, `LF will be replaced`, `autocrlf`, `stderr`, `execFileSync`, `detect_changes stderr`, plus open/closed issues and PRs. #2838 (EOL-only diff → false changed symbols, closed) and #3688 (`analyze` writes LF in a CRLF checkout, closed) are adjacent EOL issues but do not cover this stderr-forwarding behavior; #1172 fixed the same class of leak for `getCurrentCommit` only.

### Expected behavior

`detect_changes` keeps stdout as its only payload and writes nothing to stderr when git only emits informational warnings (git exits 0). MCP hosts' consoles/logs stay clean; scripted `2>&1` consumers keep getting parseable output.

### Actual behavior

Git's stderr is inherited by GitNexus and forwarded to the MCP host. Host log/console receives one line per modified LF file on every `detect_changes` call, which looks like a failure to users, floods logs, and breaks `gitnexus detect-changes 2>&1 | jq`-style pipelines.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Create a repo that mirrors the common Windows checkout:

```bash
git init demo && cd demo
git config core.autocrlf true
printf 'const a=1\nconst b=2\n' > a.js
git -c core.autocrlf=false add a.js
git -c user.email=t@t -c user.name=t commit -m seed
printf 'const a=1\nconst b=3\n' > a.js   # keep LF while modifying
```

2. Minimal proof of the forwarding behavior the call site relies on (no index required):

```js
// demo.mjs
import { execFileSync } from 'node:child_process'
const out = execFileSync('git', ['diff', '--numstat'], { cwd: process.argv[2], encoding: 'utf-8' })
process.stdout.write(JSON.stringify(out))
```

```bash
node demo.mjs . 1>out.txt 2>err.txt
# out.txt: "1\t1\ta.js\n"      (clean stdout)
# err.txt: warning: in the working copy of 'a.js', LF will be replaced by CRLF the next time Git touches it
```

3. End-to-end in an **indexed** repo with the same git config:

```bash
gitnexus detect-changes -r . 1>out.txt 2>err.txt
```

`out.txt` holds the normal JSON result; `err.txt` holds one `LF will be replaced by CRLF` line per modified file (24 in my repo).

4. Via MCP: call `detect_changes` from any stdio MCP host → the host console/log receives those stderr lines.

Control: with `core.autocrlf=false` (or a repo `.gitattributes` containing `* text=auto eol=lf`) the stderr output is empty and results are identical — confirming the lines are git-side informational warnings, not errors.

### Environment

- OS: Windows 11 (10.0.26200)
- Node: v22.23.2
- Git: 2.54.0.windows.1
- Git config: `core.autocrlf=true` (system `.../Git/etc/gitconfig` + user `~/.gitconfig`); repo has no `.gitattributes`
- GitNexus: 1.6.9, installed via `npm i -g gitnexus`; also verified on `main` (see Root cause)
- MCP host: stdio transport, `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk` 1.29.0 (server stderr defaults to `inherit`)

### Logs / screenshots

CLI reproduction (paths redacted):

```
$ gitnexus detect-changes -r <repo> 1>out.json 2>err.txt
$ echo $?          # 0
$ wc -l <err.txt   # 24
$ head -2 err.txt
warning: in the working copy of 'MANIFEST.md', LF will be replaced by CRLF the next time Git touches it
warning: in the working copy of 'README.md', LF will be replaced by CRLF the next time Git touches it
$ head -c 120 out.json
{"summary":{"changed_count":184,"affected_count":3,"changed_files":25,"risk_level":"medium"},...
```

### Root cause

- `gitnexus/src/mcp/local/local-backend.ts:6922` on `main` (installed 1.6.9: `dist/mcp/local/local-backend.js:3275`):

```ts
// maxBuffer raised from Node's 1MB default to 256MB to avoid ENOBUFS on
// repos with large unstaged/untracked diffs (e.g. unignored build folders).
diffOutput = execFileSync('git', diffArgs, {
  cwd: diffCwd,
  encoding: 'utf-8',
  maxBuffer: 256 * 1024 * 1024,
  windowsHide: true,
});
```

There is no `stdio` option, so Node forwards the git child's stderr to GitNexus's stderr (documented `execFileSync` behavior). GitNexus already fixed exactly this class of leak for `getCurrentCommit` in `storage/git.js` (comment: *"without an explicit stdio option, Node's execSync forwards the child's stderr to the parent process … #1172"*, using `stdio: ['ignore', 'pipe', 'ignore']`), but the `detect_changes` call site still lacks it.

### Impact

- Every stdio MCP host (and any tool wrapping the CLI) receives N warning lines per `detect_changes` call; logs grow and real errors get buried.
- Scripted consumers that merge streams (`2>&1`) lose parseable JSON.
- No data loss and no exit-code change; detection results are correct.

### Suggested fix

Give the call explicit stdio and keep stdout piped:

```ts
diffOutput = execFileSync('git', diffArgs, {
  cwd: diffCwd,
  encoding: 'utf-8',
  maxBuffer: 256 * 1024 * 1024,
  windowsHide: true,
  // git's informational warnings (e.g. CRLF/LF conversion under core.autocrlf=true)
  // must not leak into the CLI's/MCP server's stderr.
  stdio: ['ignore', 'pipe', 'ignore'],
});
```

If stderr diagnostics are wanted for real failures, capture it and append it to the `Git diff failed: …` message only on a non-zero exit code.

### Acceptance criteria

1. On a repo with `core.autocrlf=true` and modified LF files, `gitnexus detect-changes -r <repo> 2>err.txt` leaves `err.txt` empty while stdout JSON is unchanged.
2. A stdio MCP host that inherits the server's stderr receives no git warning lines from `detect_changes`.
3. Detection results and exit code are unchanged (control run with `core.autocrlf=false` yields the same summary).

title: docs(eval): retain isolated agent comparison
body:
## Summary

The evaluation docs still described the isolated rerun as pending, while its results existed only in #3500 and an expiring Actions artifact. Retain the 1 November comparison in the repository and link it from the root, SWE-bench and workflow READMEs. Record the fresh 7 November comparison against main `4ab9e8a48849daab417ccaab7268c946f62ca644`: [run 42377890515](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/actions/runs/42377890515), using `gpt-6.1-terra` at `xhigh`, with workflow outcome `success` and a retained evidence record. The earlier `gpt-5.6-sol/xhigh` run 42373957594 was force-cancelled at the user's request; shutdown was verified and its partial evidence is excluded from the Terra comparison.

On 7 November, `gpt-6.1-terra/xhigh` solved 12/12 repetitions without GitNexus, 10/12 with candidate MCP, and 8/12 with stable MCP. Candidate MCP reported model cost was 7.1% higher and mean agent time was 23.9% lower than its no-GitNexus arm; mean total cell time was 15.6% lower. The original oracle marked two candidate repetitions of `inv-feature-list-repos-filter` as failures (1/3 versus 3/3); the boundary mismatch below qualifies that result. The release gate passed because it checks per-task solve counts against stable MCP; it does not require parity with no GitNexus or cost savings. title: fix(detect-changes): stop autocrlf warnings leaking to stderr
body:
## Summary

`detect_changes` was letting git's autocrlf warnings spill onto GitNexus stderr. The diff result was already correct; the noise was not. `git diff` now captures stderr, so a clean exit stays quiet, and a real git failure still shows up in `Git diff failed:`.

Fixes #3837

## Motivation / context

On a `core.autocrlf=true` checkout, `git diff` exits 0 and still prints one `warning: in the working copy of '…', LF will be replaced by CRLF the next time Git touches it` line per modified file. `execFileSync` was called without `stdio`, so Node forwarded that stream into the MCP host log and into `gitnexus detect-changes`. Same class of leak as #1172 (`getCurrentCommit`), which already pipes stderr. Sibling git calls on this path (`getGitRoot`, `getCanonicalRepoRoot`) already do too, and they do not emit this warning.

## Areas touched

- [x] `gitnexus/` (CLI / core / MCP server)
- [ ] `gitnexus-web/` (Vite / React UI)
- [ ] `.github/` (workflows, actions)
- [ ] `eval/` or other tooling
- [ ] Docs / agent config only (`AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `.cursor/`, `llms.txt`, etc.)

## Scope & constraints

**In scope**

- The `git diff` call inside `detectChanges` (`gitnexus/src/mcp/local/local-backend.ts`). MCP and `gitnexus detect-changes` both go through it.
- A child-process regression test: temp repo with `core.autocrlf=true` and an LF edit, assert stderr is empty while the parsed change is unchanged, and assert a bad `compare` ref still returns git's message on the tool error.

**Explicitly out of scope / not done here**

- Other git subprocesses. The ones `detect_changes` already uses for worktree detection suppress stderr and do not print this warning.
- Changing how EOL-only diffs are classified (#2838 / #3688).

## Implementation notes

`stdio: ['ignore', 'pipe', 'pipe']` keeps stdout as the diff text. On a non-zero exit Node still puts the captured stderr on `error.message`, which is what `Git diff failed:` returns. Dropping stderr with `'ignore'` would have swallowed `fatal: unknown revision`.

## Testing & verification

- [x] `cd gitnexus && npx vitest run test/unit/detect-changes-stderr.test.ts` (and the other `detect-changes` unit files)
- [x] `cd gitnexus && npm run test:unit` — the new tests pass with the suite. Two unrelated files fail in this sandbox: `auto-sync` refuses clone roots under `/tmp` (this checkout lives there), and `wiki-llm-client` sees an ambient provider key in the environment.
- [x] `cd gitnexus && npx tsc --noEmit` and `npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.test.json`
- [x] eslint on the touched files (no new errors) and prettier
- [ ] `cd gitnexus && npm run test:integration` *(not run; this does not change indexing)*
- [ ] `cd gitnexus-web && npm test` *(web unchanged)*
- [ ] `cd gitnexus-web && npx tsc -b --noEmit` *(web unchanged)*
- [ ] Manual / Playwright E2E

Before the fix, the new test failed with the CRLF warning (and, for a bad ref, `fatal:`) on the child process stderr while the JSON payload was already right. After the fix that stderr is empty.

## Risk & rollout

No index migration and no change to the tool's success payload. Rollback is reverting the `stdio` option. The only behavior change on failure is that git's diagnostic stays inside the returned error instead of also being printed.

## Checklist

- [x] PR body meets repo minimum length (workflow may label short descriptions)
- [ ] If `AGENTS.md` / overlays changed: headers, scope block, and changelog updated per project conventions
- [x] No secrets, tokens, or machine-specific paths committed

title: fix(analyze): harden recovery, vector readiness, and RAM admission
body:
## Summary

Analysis retries and recovery now honor durability, vector-readiness, and memory-admission guarantees. This follow-up covers the ten later review outcomes from the merged resumable-analysis implementation, including explicit, tested dispositions for the two disputed behavior claims.

## Motivation / context

The original implementation merged while these later review conversations remained open. Closing the tracking issue recorded the merged scope; it did not settle those conversations.

Related: #3598, #3829

## Areas touched

- [x] `gitnexus/` (CLI / core / MCP server)

- [ ] `eval/` or other tooling
- [ ] Docs / agent config only (`AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `.cursor/`, `llms.txt`, etc.)

## Scope & constraints

**In scope**

| Review thread | Outcome and evidence |
| --- | --- |
| [Worker draining](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/pull/3829#discussion_r4501142288) | Preserve existing behavior. Real-worker tests hold active rounds during cancellation and graph-drain failure, proving shutdown waits for completion. |
| [Non-Linux PID reuse](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/pull/3829#discussion_r4501142291) | Add tagged process-birth evidence for Linux/macOS/Windows; unknown identity remains conservative. Receipt and real-platform probe tests cover the new contract. |
| [Indexed-input validation](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/pull/3829#discussion_r4501142295) | Preserve indexed-snapshot reuse. Native-store tests distinguish unindexed live edits from changed indexed fingerprints and verify source/provider calls. |
| [Retained-artifact retry](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/pull/3829#discussion_r4501142298) | Retry parent sync before existing hard-link or validated-copy success; repeated failure stays an error. |
| [Legacy checkpoint routing](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/pull/3829#discussion_r4501142299) | Gate unfinished vectors before legacy fallbacks; count-only markers retain runtime validation and live COUNT checks. Query metadata retains bounded checkpoint information. |
| [Chunker documentation](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/pull/3829#discussion_r4501142301) | Describe incremental yields accurately, including retained source/class-projection text. |
| [Concurrent query width](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/pull/3829#discussion_r4501218589) | Give each query its own produced-width diagnostic; overlapping-query tests prevent cross-query interference. |
| [Automatic memory admission](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/pull/3829#discussion_r4501218592) | Keep aggregate reservations within a fixed effective-RAM share and propagate admitted heaps through launchers. |
| [Existing-directory retry](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/pull/3829#discussion_r4501218593) | Validate the child and sync its parent after both mkdir and EEXIST; inject repeated failures in tests. |
| [Checkpoint capabilities](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/pull/3829#discussion_r4501218596) | Keep pending and unverified-count capability receipts unavailable; runtime readers can independently verify count-only recovery. Graph and keyword access remain available. |

**Explicitly out of scope / not done here**

- Shared index-lock protocol changes, worker-draining rewrites, live-source rereads for verified indexed-snapshot reuse, and package release.

## Implementation notes

- Automatic admission fixes the family ceiling at 75% of effective process/container RAM, divided among concurrent analyses. Native graph opens obey the admitted ceiling for automatic and explicit budgets. Each parser worker reserves at least the main-heap allocation because Node’s process heap flag overrides per-worker limits. Automatic main sizing yields to fitting explicit worker reservations; concurrency shrinks or admission fails when required allocations cannot fit.
- Smaller hosts may reject local-model embeddings. `embeddings sync` and server embedding jobs reserve their running process's actual heap before locking or creating work. An infeasible server request returns an error immediately. Remedies include resuming with `analyze` or restarting sync/serve with a smaller Node heap.
- New writer-birth fields are optional in v2 receipts. Old receipts, failed probes, and equal coarse timestamps retain conservative recovery behavior. Windows probes have a five-second startup budget; recovery uses the same bound for receipts with birth evidence. Other platforms and legacy receipts retain their prior deadlines.
- Pending-work checkpoints disable the vector lane. Count-only recovery permits existing runtime checks (including live COUNT before model initialization) while capability receipts remain unavailable with `embedding-count-unverified`. Graph and keyword queries remain available; dirty-graph precedence is unchanged.

Session-settled decisions carried from planning: bounded automatic admission within RAM (user-directed) and all ten outcomes in one follow-up PR (user-directed).

## Testing & verification

- [CI at `f3e687a55`](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/actions/runs/42407491190) passes after one targeted performance retry: **34,761 tests passed, zero failed, zero unverified**. Vercel preview deployment separately requires NexusCore team authorization.
- Full `npm test`: 32,465 passed, 103 skipped, six failures across four files (94m55s). All four files pass on targeted reruns: the API budget expectation was corrected with actual-server-heap admission; four setup failures disappear when the subprocess does not inherit `CODEX_HOME` (62/62 on both base and this branch); the native orchestration failure was the analyzer identity guard detecting source/build changes during analysis (40/40 on stable base and changed-branch reruns).
- Focused recovery, checkpoint routing, query concurrency, process identity, worker-drain and admission regressions pass. The final API/sync/admission batch passes 105/105; API compatibility checks pass 68/68; the real HTTP outage/resume flow passes after the final build.
- `npm run build`, `npx tsc --noEmit`, ESLint (no errors), Prettier and `git diff --check` pass.
- Initial implementation graph analysis covered 39 files, 78 symbols and 41 flows. Subsequent fixes received scoped graph checks; the CLI fixture correction covers 14 files and 17 symbols; the later package-smoke correction covers one file and two symbols. Both report no affected processes and complete traversal.
- Follow-up review validation: 95 focused tests pass, including count-only legacy search, failed/empty COUNT gating, capability receipts, generation preservation and the RAM admission matrix. Typecheck, ESLint, formatting and diff checks pass.
- Latest memory-enforcement review fixes: 228 tests across 11 files pass, including the real worker factory under CLI heap flags and `NODE_OPTIONS`, automatic native pool limits, launchers, watch, sync and server admission. Build, typecheck, lint (no errors), formatting, diff and staged graph checks pass.
- CI’s separate test-typecheck exposed three fixture-shape errors, corrected in `57b995191`. `npm run typecheck:tests`, the production typecheck, and all 36 affected checkpoint tests now pass locally; production behavior is unchanged.
- Native macOS CI exposed obsolete fixture heap pins and inherited manual-memory mode. `7878d2942` moves nine real CLI fixtures to automatic admission and gives three unit fixtures consistent heap inputs. Under a simulated 7 GiB host, 190 distinct tests across 14 suites pass; the failing skills case also passes through the TypeScript source entry, confirming loader-preserving re-execution. Both typechecks, lint (no errors), formatting, diff and staged graph checks pass.
- The package-manager smoke fixture also forced manual-memory mode. `07f9a47db` restores automatic sizing. The original npm failure reproduces before the fix and passes afterward at simulated 7 GiB; 26 related unit tests pass. Clean CI at that commit passed all four package smoke jobs, including actual npm, pnpm and Bun installation/indexing on macOS. Local pnpm validation had stopped at a tarball-path rejection caused by linked worktree dependencies; the clean CI result supplies the missing verification.
- Native process-birth probes pass on Linux locally and on [macOS](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/actions/runs/42407491190/job/128508808476) and [Windows](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/actions/runs/42407491190/job/128508808465) at `f3e687a55`. Windows initially returned unknown after about 1.56 seconds with the 1.5-second timeout, and a skills-fixture cleanup failed with EBUSY. The shared five-second Windows capture/recovery budget and existing Windows-aware cleanup helper fix those failures. The unchanged native probe and full Windows shard pass (343 tests, 7 skipped); all 125 targeted local tests, build, both typechecks, lint, formatting and graph checks also pass.
- The first explicit-resource performance run at `f3e687a55` flagged fresh HTTP embeddings (paired geometric ratio 1.088; 95% interval 1.006–1.176). The initial implementation received sequential `ce-code-review` lenses and an independent Claude review. Its OOM-guidance finding is fixed and regression-tested. Later feedback and CI fixes received focused local validation; the independent review predates those fixes.

## Risk & rollout

Automatic heaps are smaller than the previous independent caps. Large repositories may need explicit heap/family settings within available RAM, reduced concurrency, a supported HTTP embedding provider, or more RAM. These are admission reservations, not an OS-enforced RSS limit. Publication keeps artifacts when identity is uncertain; no receipt migration is required.

body:
Bumps the uv group with 1 update in the /eval directory: [oauthlib](https://github.com/oauthlib/oauthlib). Updates `oauthlib` from 4.0.0 to 4.0.1
Release notes

Sourced from oauthlib's releases.

4.0.1

Security

  • CVE-2026-49272 / GHSA-3jp2-3mrg-2vxc: The device code flow token endpoint did not validate the device_code parameter. A request with a known client_id and a bogus device_code could obtain a bearer token. DeviceCodeGrant.validate_token_request now calls DeviceCodeGrant.validate_device_code(), which rejects missing or unknown device codes (invalid_request / invalid_grant) and delegates the code's authorization status to the new RequestValidator.validate_device_code() hook, per RFC 8628 Section 3.5. (cherry-picked from #954)

Upgrade note for device flow integrators

Custom RequestValidator implementations using the device flow must now implement validate_device_code(client_id, code, request). Return one of the DeviceCodeGrant.DEVICE_CODE_* statuses for known codes, or None for an unknown code. When returning AUTHORIZED, the validator must also populate request.user and request.scopes from the stored authorization.

Sourced from oauthlib's changelog.

4.0.1 (2026-11-04):

## Summary

The repository-filtering oracle called `LocalBackend.callTool` directly, bypassing the MCP policy wrapper. ## Motivation / context

title: fix(graph): validate reference sites and dedupe context
body:
## Summary

Repeated call-site edges could consume context's 30-row limits and hide other callers. Context now selects distinct relationship types and symbols in the graph query before sorting and limiting. Ingestion separately validates reference identities and source bounds before writers discard the provenance, and MCP reports what was checked.

Refs #3500 and its [ingestion acceptance criteria](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/issues/3500#issuecomment-6718915892). The merged recovery/vector/RAM fix in #3842 does not implement these changes.

## Behavior

- Source hashes come from the exact worker/cache input. If validation reads changed or unavailable source after parsing, it records unverified provenance instead of aborting analysis or certifying newer source. Invalid graph identities still fail.
- Streamed identity lookup uses bounded numeric-tail probes; multiple-arrow IDs remain opaque. Transient MCP generation/metadata uncertainty recommends retrying the tool.
- All seven context reference windows keep `DISTINCT` before `LIMIT 30`. Six use an allowlisted resolved node label to avoid scanning every node table; absent or unrecognized labels retain the untyped fallback. The typed-property bridge has no symbol anchor and is unchanged.
- Complete spans preserve nested calls such as `service.ping().ping()` that share a start position. Different sites, dispatch targets, relationship types and access kinds remain distinct.
- Both graph writers reject contradictory identities, including across retained/streamed partitions. For source-backed point/span identities, they also validate endpoints, available coordinate ordering and source-buffer bounds against the parsed input before writing; opaque and collapsed provenance remains unverified. Exact repeated submissions remain idempotent; confidence/reason differences retain first-writer-wins behavior. A rejected record prevents a clean receipt even when an emitting pass catches the error.
- Versioned `graph_integrity` receipts report repository-wide ingestion checks, separately from query completeness. Legacy, collapsed, point-only, extracted and partially mapped provenance remains unverified. Notebook recognition is case-insensitive; partially mapped notebook columns cannot be certified against the original JSON.
- Successful single-repository MCP graph object results carry the receipt. Empty/non-tabular Cypher results retain their raw array contract; an absent receipt means unverified. Missing/malformed receipts and mixed database generations cannot acquire verified status.
- Structured stderr logs provide an ingestion summary, at most one debug example per unverified reason, and rejected identities/endpoints/source files/emission reasons/stacks. Error messages escape control characters; source buffers are not logged, but diagnostic fields can contain source-derived names or literals. RUNBOOK.md documents debugging and reindexing.

## Benchmark correctness and performance

The benchmark updates account for the intended representation change without removing correctness or performance gates:

- Across 21 declaration workloads (cold/warm/changed), node and relationship content is unchanged apart from adding end coordinates to reference IDs. Only those 21 correctness hashes changed; historical timing references were retained. The declaration correctness/scaling check passed.

The candidate has 65,317 edges: 64 additional edges recover source spans from four formerly collapsed point identities. Node hashes and projected edge hashes match. Historical target resolution accuracy is not certified by this migration proof.

The `f80540070` default-resource benchmark failed once on fresh HTTP analysis, then passed on an unchanged-commit rerun. Both runs used seven measured pairs with matching workload and dependency receipts; the runner CPUs differed.

title: fix(deps): resolve minimatch, glob and zod audit advisories
body:
## Summary

This PR clears three advisories from the root, `gitnexus` and `gitnexus-web` lockfiles:

- **GHSA-g3hv-75wg-m249** (minimatch)
- **GHSA-3g3m-2fjr-6pw4** (glob)
- **GHSA-mrhx-c7xc-m3w5** (zod, high)

Refs #3804

### Why overrides instead of `npm audit fix --force`

minimatch's fix exists only in **11.0.1+**, and no upstream release has moved to it yet:

| Consumer | Requires | Latest upstream |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `@typescript-eslint/typescript-estree` (root lint) | `minimatch ^10.2.2` | 8.72.1, still `^10.2.2` |
| `@stryker-mutator/core` (gitnexus, dev) | `minimatch ^10` | |
| `@vercel/nft` 1.10.0 (pinned exactly by `@vercel/node`) | `glob ^13` → `minimatch ^10` | 1.11.1, still `glob ^13` |

`npm audit fix --force` would **downgrade** `@typescript-eslint/parser` to 6.15.0 and Stryker to 6.4.1. Instead, this PR adds parent-scoped overrides, in the same style as the existing `gitnexus-web` entries:

- root: `@typescript-eslint/typescript-estree` → `minimatch ^11.0.1`
- `gitnexus`: `@stryker-mutator/core` → `minimatch ^11.0.1`
- `gitnexus-web`: `@vercel/nft` → `glob ^14.0.2` (glob 14 brings minimatch 11)

Because the overrides are scoped to those parents, eslint's own `minimatch@3` copies stay as they are; they fall outside the advisory range (`>=7 <11.0.1`).

**API compatibility.** minimatch 11 removes `makeRe` and `AST`. The overridden consumers use only `minimatch()`, `Minimatch#match`/`negate`/`hasMagic`, and `glob()`, all of which are unchanged. I checked this against the published `dist/` of each consumer.

**zod** moves from 4.3.6 to 4.6.7 inside `eslint-plugin-react-hooks`' existing `^3.25 || ^4` range. That is a lockfile-only change and needs no override.

### Relation to #3804

On `main`, the `gitnexus` **production** tree already resolves `glob@14.0.3` and `minimatch@11.0.3`, so `npm audit --omit=dev` reports **0**. The remaining minimatch finding in `gitnexus` came from the dev-only Stryker path, which this PR fixes. The release that #3804 asks for is still needed to get a clean audit for consumers of the stable dist-tag.

### Lockfile hygiene

- I regenerated the lockfiles with **npm 11**. npm 10 strips the `libc` platform fields and produced about 60 lines of unrelated churn.
- The tree-sitter `0.25.1` peer pins (CONTRIBUTING § Native tree-sitter) are unchanged.

- **nft:** `nodeFileTrace` on a wildcard `require("./locales/" + n + ".js")` (the code path that calls `glob`) produced the **same** file list under glob 14.0.4 and 13.0.6.

title: feat(mcp): query multiple repositories in one call
body:
## Summary

Allow MCP `query` and its legacy `search` alias to search up to ten indexed repositories in one call. For example, `query({repo: ["frontend", "backend"], search_query: "authentication"})` returns merged results with each row's repository and native symbol ID.

Closes #1308.

## Behavior

- Validate and authorize the entire selection before searching; deduplicate checkout aliases and resolve every requested branch first.
- Run at most four member searches concurrently and release each database lease after its search.
- Merge local ranks under global result and source-preview budgets. Preserve per-repository errors, warnings, timing, retention, and staleness.

title: fix(cli): honor --no-stats on the already-up-to-date analyze fast path
body:
## Summary

`gitnexus analyze --no-stats .` silently ignored the flag whenever the index was already up to date: the committed `AGENTS.md`/`CLAUDE.md` GitNexus block kept its `(N symbols, N relationships, N execution flows)` parenthetical. This restores the flag's contract on that path.

## Motivation - context

Fixes #3618.

Reported against 1.6.3, and the reporter's diagnosis is half right: the pipeline path and the `--skills` re-generation already bridge the negated Commander flag as `noStats: options.stats === false` (#1477, #1478), and `.gitnexusrc` maps `noStats` → `stats` too. What never got the bridge is the `alreadyUpToDate` fast path in `analyze.ts`: it returned before `generateAIContextFiles`, so an already-indexed repo could not drop the counts no matter how often the flag was passed. Users hitting this are exactly the ones running `analyze --no-stats` repeatedly on a committed repo, i.e. the flag's main audience.

## Areas touched

- [x] `gitnexus` (core engine, CLI, MCP)
- [ ] `gitnexus-web` (UI/frontend)
- [ ] `.github` / CI workflows
- [ ] `eval` or other tooling
- [ ] Docs or agent config only (no product code)

## Scope & constraints

**In scope:** the `alreadyUpToDate` fast path in `gitnexus/src/cli/analyze.ts`; a new best-effort `refreshStatsLine` helper in `gitnexus/src/cli/ai-context.ts`; unit tests for both.

**Explicitly out of scope:** regenerating the whole context block on an up-to-date run (would churn `--skills` community rows), per-skill count restoration (the fast path has no per-skill numbers — flagged with a `shortcut:` comment), and the `--branch` sub-index gate, which already skips context refresh.

## Implementation notes

- `refreshStatsLine(repoPath, stats, { noStats, skipAgentsMd })` mirrors `refreshBaseRefLine`: it edits only the block between the `gitnexus:start`/`gitnexus:end` markers and writes only when the line actually changes, so routine up-to-date runs stay silent.
- With `--no-stats` it removes the parenthetical (and the `(N symbols)` cells of an existing skills table). Without the flag it restores the parenthetical **only if absent** — an existing figure is never rewritten, since the fast path cannot improve it (#2907) and stale churn would show up in every diff.
- `analyze.ts` calls it beside `refreshBaseRefLine` inside the existing try/catch, gated on `result.isPrimaryBranch !== false` like the base_ref refresh, and prints `Omitted`/`Restored volatile counts in AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md` when a file changed.
- Both phrasings the keep path accepts are handled: the template's sentence and a trimmed block's `Indexed as **name**` line.

## Testing & verification

- [x] `cd gitnexus && npm test` (targeted: `npx vitest run test/unit/ai-context.test.ts test/unit/analyze-no-stats-bridge.test.ts test/unit/analyze-gitnexusrc.test.ts` → 112 passed; broader affected set incl. `analyze-config`, `analyze-finalize-failure-exits`, `analyze-self-commit-bridge`, `analyze-phase-handoff`, `watch-paths` → 244 passed)
- [ ] `npm run test:integration` — not run (offline environment, native index building unavailable)
- [x] `npx tsc --noEmit` and `npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.test.json`
- [ ] `gitnexus-web` build/test — not applicable
- [ ] Manual/Playwright — not applicable

Regression test is real: reverting `analyze.ts` makes `applies --no-stats to an already up-to-date index (#3618)` fail with `expected "vi.fn()" to be called 1 times, but got 0 times`. End-to-end on a throwaway repo: first `analyze .` writes `(4 symbols, 5 relationships, 0 execution flows)`; `analyze . --no-stats` then prints `Already up to date` + `Omitted volatile counts in AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md` and both files drop the parenthetical; a third run without the flag restores it; a plain third run leaves the files byte-identical.

## Risk & rollout

Low. The helper is best-effort: a missing file, missing/blank block or unmatched header line leaves the file untouched, and nothing is written unless the line changes. A repo whose index predates captured `stats` keeps its count-free block rather than restoring zeros. No behaviour change on fresh pipelines, `--branch` sub-indexes, or `--skip-agents-md`.

title: perf: per-file parse-result reuse (content-hash keyed) instead of chunk-level parse cache
body:
## Summary

Reuse each unchanged file's parse result across runs, keyed by **path + content hash**, instead of the chunk-level parse cache from #1479.

## Why

We ran the existing parse cache (`parseCache.storagePath`) in our hosted deployment on a ~4,300-file TypeScript repo, and it was a net loss:

- scope resolution streams parsed files back from disk JSON: **28.7 s → 96 s**, pipeline 75 s → 142 s;
- the store was 816 MB;
- keys are per chunk, so one edited file invalidates its whole chunk.

## What we built and measured

- **Store:** each worker result is `v8.serialize`d + zstd-3 (gzip fallback), kept in a pack file + JSON index beside the graph.
- **Key:** path + sha256 of content, under an identity that covers the analyzer build, parse-cache version, worker options and `GITNEXUS_*` env.
- **Workers:** in this mode they return each file's result encoded. The main thread decodes reused and fresh results alike and merges them in file order, so a reuse run merges exactly the inputs a full parse merges. This relies on worker output being batch-independent, which we verified: one file per sub-batch gave the same graph digest as normal batching.
- **Periodic full parse:** a reuse counter forces one after N runs.

Same machine, same commit:

| Run | Parse | Pipeline | Peak RSS |
|---|---|---|---|
| Full parse | 42–57 s | 75–106 s | 6.7–7.0 GB |
| First run, writing the store | about the same | about the same | |
| All files reused | **9–12 s** | **43–64 s** | 2.3 GB |
| 2-file edit, reusing the rest | 15 s | 67 s | 2.5 GB |

- Store size: 68 MB.
- The graph digest (every node and edge) was identical to a full parse in all cases.
- Scope resolution is unchanged; that's #1841.

## Known gap

When only a few files change, parse still pays for starting the full worker pool. A 20-file push took noticeably longer than a 0-miss run. Sizing the pool by miss count is a likely follow-up.

Happy to contribute a PR if this direction fits.

title: perf: cache compiled tree-sitter queries per parse worker
body:
## Summary

`parse-worker` compiles each language's tree-sitter `Query` once per sub-batch. The TypeScript query costs ~125 ms to compile. Caching the compiled `Parser.Query` per worker, keyed by grammar and query text, removes that repeated cost. Queries are only read (`query.matches`), so sharing them is safe.

## Why it matters

- With many small sub-batches (for example `GITNEXUS_WORKER_SUB_BATCH_MAX_BYTES` set low, or a per-file mode), the compile cost dominates. One-file sub-batches took cold parse from 52 s to 88 s on a ~4,300-file repo.
- Normal runs also recompile once per sub-batch per language, on every worker.

## Change

A small module-level `Map<grammar, Map<queryText, Query>>` in the worker. It is used where `processFileGroup` compiles the query today. We measured identical graph output.

title: perf: member-derived stable community/process ids to stop per-run renumbering churn
body:
## Summary

Community and process ids come from discovery order (`comm_${idx}`, `proc_${idx}_…`). A small edit renumbers them, so every run churns thousands of rows that didn't really change.

## Data

On a ~4,300-file repo, real PRs that changed rows in only ~20 files caused ~24k `MEMBER_OF` rewrites plus ~3k Community/Process node changes, all from renumbering.

With member-derived ids, membership changes per PR dropped to 129–334, a >99% cut:

- `comm_` + sha1(smallest member id)[0:12]
- `proc_` + sha1(entry \0 terminal)[0:12] + `_name`

## Why it matters for OSS

- Incremental writeback currently has to delete and reinsert all communities and processes.
- Stable ids would let it write only real changes.
- They also give consumers stable references across runs (web UI colours, saved links).

Note for whoever picks it up: the CLI incremental path calls `deleteAllCommunitiesAndProcesses`; with stable ids that call could later be narrowed.

title: LadybugDB: in-place delta writes inflate the database 1.6-2.1x and slow queries; bulk reload stays compact
body:
## Summary

Writing small deltas into an existing LadybugDB database inflates the file 1.6–2.1× and slows queries. A fresh bulk load (COPY) of the full graph stays compact and is fast. This affects incremental writeback, which edits rows in place.

## Measurements

Real graph, 236 MB after a bulk load:

- **One-off edits:**
  - one `DETACH DELETE`: +48 MB;
  - one edge insert: +18 MB;
  - `SET` of one `content` value: +16 MB;
  - one file's rows (36 nodes / 94 edges): +92 MB.
- **Twelve sequential one-file deltas:** 236 → 391 → 456 MB, then a plateau. Free pages are only ~26 MB; the rest looks like CSR slack, because the first change after a bulk load rewrites whole CSR regions (forward and backward) and large string columns.

Grown vs compact, same graph:

| Measure | Compact | Grown |
|---|---|---|
| Open | baseline | +40% |
| Type-filtered relationship scan | baseline | 2–3× slower |
| `context` / `impact` | baseline | +10–20% |
| Query-process RSS | 690 MB | 915 MB |

Point operations also cost ~4–7 ms per row. For example, 2,000 `MEMBER_OF` rewrites took 24 s, while a full COPY load of the same graph is ~10–15 s.

## Suggestion

- Compute the delta (useful for FTS and other derived indexes), but write the database as a fresh bulk load when the delta is non-trivial; or
- compact periodically.

`CALL fsm_info()` and `storage_info('<table>')` show the growth.

title: fix: compact incremental graphs adaptively
body:
## Summary

Keep small edits selective and periodically compact the graph with a fresh bulk load. This bounds the storage growth reproduced in #3852 while retaining the fast update path for both large repositories and independent small repositories.

Closes #3852.

## Motivation / context

The committed native reduction reproduces 1.69× physical growth after row updates with unchanged node/edge tuples; fresh COPY restores compact storage. It identifies the native write pattern without claiming a particular C++ allocator defect. Always copying the full graph regressed the larger CI corpus, so this implementation chooses between both write paths.

## Areas touched

- [x] Analysis, incremental storage, shared stores and search
- [x] Tests, benchmark tooling and operational guidance

## Scope & constraints

Small edits, deletions and renames retain selective writes and existing atomic-incremental controls. Compaction occurs after 16 successful incremental writes, growth beyond the larger of 50% or 16 MiB, a source-file mutation reaching the larger of 2,000 graph rows or 5% of the graph, or an existing extension/file-fraction safety gate. Older indexes establish a compact baseline once. Due compaction runs before the unchanged-snapshot fast return.

The mutation estimate includes capped reads of old nodes and incident edges, covering files that shrink or disappear. It uses the larger old/new source-file footprint; it is not a count of every DELETE/INSERT operation or graph-wide derived-layer rewrite. Write-count and storage-growth triggers cover every incremental run.

## Implementation notes

Compaction state belongs to each physical index and advances only after durable, verified publication. Reused shared graphs carry their own state, including during vector-only publication; a healthy private graph is retained through edit/revert cycles when the immutable shared copy needs compaction. Physical state does not change graph compatibility.

Compatible legacy vectors survive compaction, including underreported vectors. Unexpected probe/read failures stop destructive compaction. Missing graphs skip legacy cache reads; force recovery from a corrupt or incompatible graph retains its original bytes before rebuilding. Read-only recovery preserves native memory/thread limits.

FTS construction and search skip only tables proven empty by fresh, one-row presence probes. Missing or malformed evidence skips nothing; populated tables still require valid indexes.

title: fix(ingestion): stabilize community and process IDs
body:
## Summary

Stop unrelated graph changes from renumbering existing communities and processes. Community IDs derive from a stable member anchor, process IDs derive from their endpoints, and the web UI preserves opaque IDs for grouping and deterministic colors.

Parent #3856 has merged into `main`; this PR targets `main`. No `docs/plans` or generated benchmark artifacts are included.

**Historical performance measurements:** the earlier measurements against the adaptive-compaction parent show roughly flat CLI performance: cold time -0.4%, one-file update time -0.9%, and cold peak process RSS +1.0% (median paired changes). Historical focused measurements show faster web conversion and lower retained heap. Improvement in every metric is not established.

## Motivation / context

Closes #3851.

Adding an unrelated disconnected component previously changed 16 existing records in the reproduction: 2 communities, 6 memberships, 2 processes, and 6 steps. All 16 retain their identities after the fix.

Performance investigation also found that the graph integrity lookup retained the pipeline's lexical scope. Retaining the returned graph could therefore retain completed phase results and progress state. Isolating that lookup and releasing the completed deferred callback makes the temporary state collectible.

## Areas touched

- Remove redundant whole-graph maps and temporary entry tuples; reuse partition lookups for cohesion. Web traversal uses insertion-ordered Set iteration to avoid repeated `queue.shift()` calls, and hoists repeated type-set allocation.
- Give the graph integrity lookup its own closure scope. Release the completed deferred callback before native database loading. Add eager/deferred lifetime regressions and verify callback release in the analysis owner.

PDG coverage is limited for the oversized outer analysis function, so source inspection and executable regressions supplement it.

The earlier full core suite reported **32,689 passed, 33 failed, 121 skipped**. ## Performance validation — previous stack

Focused tests compare 48663b8a9 (PR before the allocation follow-up) with de0c6a0a0; these three measured modules are identical in final head. Each variant runs in three fresh processes, with one excluded warm-up and three timed repetitions per process. The real fixture has 34,592 nodes and 96,988 edges. The synthetic fixture has 100,000 symbols plus 10,001 file/folder nodes and 280,000 input edges. Both fixtures produced exactly equal community/process results and seeded UI node/edge data before and after. UI timing measures graph conversion, not browser rendering. Operation heap deltas and process high-water RSS are diagnostics, not exact allocation counts; RSS also includes fixture setup.

| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |

The historical original-main comparison exposed the previous parent's persistence tradeoff: one-file updates bulk-loaded a fresh physical database, which was smaller but took longer and used more peak RSS on this corpus. title: fix(cache): reuse unchanged files across chunk boundaries
body:
## Summary

Cache parser facts and scopes per file while retaining batched worker jobs and compressed pack storage. Editing one file no longer reparses unchanged files that happened to share its cache chunk.

Originally stacked on [#3854](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/pull/3854), which is now merged. This PR targets `main`. Removing the obsolete stacked-branch CI trigger remains pending maintainer sign-off.

## Motivation / context

Closes #3849.

The real-worker reproduction places four files in the same old cache bucket. Before this change, editing one file reparses all four; afterward, it reparses one and reuses three. Unchanged runs containing only reusable parser results start no parser workers. Files that yield no parse output, such as template-only Vue files, still dispatch on warm runs, matching the previous behavior.

## Areas touched

- [x] `gitnexus/` (CLI / core / MCP server)
- Architecture documentation, a reproducible benchmark, and `.github/workflows/ci.yml` / `.github/workflows/ci-tests.yml`

## Scope & constraints

- Apply per-file reuse to the default analysis path.
- Preserve complete graph output, bounded worker dispatch, native-safe shutdown, scope loading, and publication/recovery behavior.
- Whole-repository scope resolution still runs; fewer reparsed files do not imply proportional end-to-end speedups.

## Implementation notes

- Bind each result to its path, content, parser identity, and effective extraction options.
- Store independently validated facts and scopes in bounded compressed packs; pin selected scope packs for the analysis run.
- Preserve deterministic merge order, staged-repair precedence, sibling cache entries, and supervisor recovery receipts. Incomplete or sanitized results are not reusable.
- Add coverage for edit/add/delete/rename/repacking, graph equality with PDG on/off across languages, corruption, quarantine, failed writes, concurrent publication, and recovery.
- Retain immutable published packs while at least half their bytes remain live; compact sparser packs. No-op publication preserves pack names and active readers.
- Restore packed results with bounded 64 KiB read-ahead, restricted to requested neighbours during publication and observed adjacency during scope replay. Authenticate and bind each envelope once before deserialization, and size decompression buffers from the declared output length within a 64 KiB cap.

On the 1,126-file real-source fixture, a one-file edit reparses **1 file instead of 14**, two edits reparse **2 instead of 24**, and repacking reparses **0 instead of 1,126**. Cold parser-cache storage falls from **285.96 MiB to 28.82 MiB**. All corresponding complete graph digests match.

Historical observations and reproduction commands remain in [the benchmark report](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/blob/fix/3849-per-file-parse-reuse-pr/gitnexus/bench/file-result-reuse/README.md). Historical paired measurements are below. They predate the review fixes. The current CI run passes the synthetic performance gate; real-source speed, graph equality, exact reuse, and disk-size checks pass, while each seven-pair run has inconclusive memory-improvement evidence.

## Testing & verification

CI follow-up in [9fa640bc0](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/commit/9fa640bc0d7ad46ee972c9f848d00763503aabea): build, production/test typechecks, lint, all 18 Java benchmark samples, and ten Objective-C benchmark repetitions pass. The full local run recorded 32,880 passed, 5 failed, and 103 skipped tests. The failures were one unchanged Swift timing tripwire and four setup checks affected by inherited `CODEX_HOME`. Fresh runs of all three failing files pass all 64 tests on both the PR and base, with that variable unset for the setup test processes. The local seven-pair cold-CLI comparison remains inconclusive (candidate/base 0.988; 95% interval 0.928–1.052). [The first CI attempt](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/actions/runs/42769412027/attempts/1) and [one unchanged rerun](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/actions/runs/42769412027/job/129695363885) passed speed, graph equality, exact reuse, and disk-size checks, but both failed the real-source memory improvement gate. Their paired 95% RSS intervals are 0.939–1.009 and 0.953–1.006, respectively: each seven-pair result is inconclusive. A diagnostic combination of all 14 measured pairs from the two runner hosts gives 0.957–0.996; both warmups are excluded and no measured pair is discarded. This does not override the failed hosted checks. The sampling-change proposal was superseded by implementation optimization; CI retains seven pairs and all existing thresholds.

Memory follow-up in [9b4a5acd2](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/commit/9b4a5acd2e438cb93de7915fe5634e16b00380ea) shares repeated paths, IDs, and labels while decoding fresh and cached facts. Each string table belongs to one batch; no table survives between analyses. Failed optional interning falls back to ordinary decoding, preserving graph output and cache hits. The 68 focused tests, build, production/test typechecks, formatting, and lint pass (zero lint errors). The unchanged hosted seven-pair gates now pass on both [real source](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/actions/runs/42789779595/job/129739962491) and [synthetic](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/actions/runs/42789779595/job/129739962597). Real-source median peak RSS fell from 2,127.5 to 1,884.8 MiB; the paired geometric ratio is 0.903 with a 95% interval of 0.862–0.945. Repeated analyses including repacking fell from 138.426s to 69.197s (interval 0.492–0.522). Every phase, disk-size, graph-equality, and exact-reuse check passes. The [real-source artifact](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/actions/runs/42789779595/artifacts/13752559957) and [synthetic artifact](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/actions/runs/42789779595/artifacts/13750644662) retain every trial. An independent local seven-pair real-source run also passes every gate, with RSS interval 0.863–0.948. These compare the full PR against base `612136cad`; the heap diagnostic attributes about 79 MiB of retained-heap savings to the additional string sharing.

Linux, Windows, macOS, and CodeQL checks pass. One unrelated import-resolution timing guard failed its initial CI attempt (Vue depth ratio 2.335, limit 2.3); its benchmark and language-provider sources are unchanged from the base. The complete import-target benchmark passes locally on both revisions (Vue ratios 2.175 and 2.172). The [single diagnostic retry](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/actions/runs/42789779595/job/129762344751) passed every benchmark guard and all 82 pipeline benchmark tests; no benchmark threshold or sampling rule was changed.

After stacking, the combined cache, publication, FTS, and atomic-swap suites passed **332 tests (2 skipped)**. Another **54 CI-related tests** passed. The build, production/test typechecks, actionlint, workflow concurrency checks, and workflow formatting also passed. No `docs/plans` files are included.

Run from `gitnexus/`:

- `npm run build`
- `npx tsc --noEmit`
- `npm run typecheck:tests`
- `node --import tsx bench/parse-dispatch-rounds/measure.mjs --check`
- Full suite for the initial cache implementation in four shards: `npm test -- --shard=1/4 --maxWorkers=2 --reporter=verbose`, repeated for `2/4`, `3/4`, and `4/4`.
- Focused cache, worker, publication, corruption, and graph-equivalence suites; formatting and lint checks.

The initial implementation’s full run recorded four setup failures caused by inherited `CODEX_HOME`, plus one native worker SIGSEGV in `mcp-multi-repo-query.test.ts`. Both setup files passed with that variable removed (62 tests), and the multi-repository file passed separately (3 tests). No implementation changes were needed for those reruns.

GitNexus impact/change analysis and the sequential review cover the storage, worker, ingestion, and publication paths.

## Historical CI performance acceptance

Both parse-cache performance jobs passed on the stacked PR: [synthetic](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/actions/runs/42626797564/job/129192837395) and [real source](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/actions/runs/42626797564/job/129192837739). CI compared parent `2ec20f32d` with merge commit `f8c01db0` (the same tree as PR head `80608363a`), using Node 22.23.4 on Linux x64, two parser workers, and a 4 GiB heap. Each corpus used one excluded warmup pair and seven alternating fresh-process pairs.

The test workflow calls `bench/file-result-reuse/measure.mjs --check` against a separately built PR base and writes `measure.json`. The [synthetic artifact](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/actions/runs/42626797564/artifacts/13679541798) and [real-source artifact](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/actions/runs/42626797564/artifacts/13681218685) contain the JSON report, Markdown summary, and every trial log.

Medians below include cache publication. Ratio intervals are candidate/base; lower is better.

| Metric | Synthetic base → PR | Paired 95% ratio | Real source base → PR | Paired 95% ratio |
| --- | ---: | --- | ---: | --- |
| Repeated analyses, including repacking | 24.667s → 14.872s | 0.588–0.605 | 140.925s → 71.678s | 0.499–0.524 |
| Ordinary repeats, excluding repacking | 11.146s → 11.465s | 1.001–1.059 | 55.622s → 53.482s | 0.942–0.991 |
| Peak process RSS | 1,023.2 → 854.9 MiB | 0.809–0.877 | 2,077.3 → 2,018.6 MiB | 0.954–0.980 |
| Cold | 12.734s → 13.041s | 1.003–1.050 | 56.929s → 56.832s | 0.981–1.018 |
| Warm | 2.874s → 3.102s | 1.032–1.100 | 15.918s → 16.141s | 0.994–1.048 |
| One-file edit | 4.109s → 4.231s | 0.980–1.070 | 20.091s → 19.380s | 0.946–0.990 |
| Two-file edit | 4.061s → 4.132s | 0.980–1.040 | 19.539s → 18.013s | 0.893–0.950 |
| Repacking | 13.867s → 3.443s | 0.243–0.254 | 85.453s → 18.196s | 0.209–0.222 |
| Cold cache storage | 79.33 → 6.64 MiB | 0.084–0.084 | 285.64 → 28.79 MiB | 0.101–0.101 |

Most aggregate time savings come from repacking. The ordinary-repeat row is an additional calculation from the same seven pairs using the same interval method, not a separate CI gate: it sums warm, one-edit, and two-edit runs. Ordinary repeats are about 2.9% slower on the synthetic fixture and 3.8% faster on real source. Real one-file and two-file edits improve by 3.5% and 7.8%; their intervals support those improvements. Cold and warm are not broadly faster.

The existing gates are unchanged: against chunk caching, the paired 95% upper bounds must establish at least 5% faster repeated analyses (including repacking) and strictly lower peak process RSS; each phase has a 15% regression limit; cache bytes must fall by at least 50%. Once the base has per-file reuse, each metric has a 5% regression budget. Inconclusive intervals fail the parse-cache gate. Complete graph equality and exact per-file reuse passed in both corpora.

The fixture sizes were 1,024 synthetic and 1,126 real TypeScript files. CI candidate compiled-tree SHA-256: `1e18299b89167332b8886f2dfb85a0c785a59cbbf39ed65f129c60aab8f0de68`; baseline: `dee110ac3f1d37000c9626b29a149743d6d4879392912d38b98e607d8c689f96`.

A separate local seven-pair synthetic run also established lower aggregate time and RSS, but retained a **failed** verdict: edit/two-edit upper bounds of 1.187 and 1.252 exceeded the 1.15 phase budget. The local real-source smoke run passed graph/reuse validation; its single measured pair is not acceptance evidence.

The separate end-to-end analyze benchmarks passed their regression checks with explicit and default resources. Most timing intervals crossed parity and their acceptance remained incomplete, so these results do not establish a general CLI speedup. Parse-cache measurements exclude graph database publication, embeddings, and CLI startup; disk-cache size is separate from process RSS.

## Risk & rollout

Three review decisions remain open under the repository guardrails: the receipt limit near 125k cold-file keys, the 128 MiB index writer/reader mismatch, and CI trigger/platform-suite configuration. The index file-read race is addressed by the bounded reader that checks and reads the same open handle.

The cache format/identity change causes one cold parse. Subsequent analyses reuse compatible per-file records automatically. Publication is the highest-risk area; regression coverage includes interrupted writes, missing staged repairs, sibling publication, and recovery after writer exit. Reverting the change also invalidates incompatible cache entries and rebuilds them.

## Checklist

- [x] Description includes behavior, evidence, verification, and rollout implications.
- [x] Documentation reflects the new cache layout.
- [x] No secrets, tokens, or machine-specific paths added.

## Summary

Pins the edge accounting for interface dispatch through a field receiver outside Go: which targets a `this.repo.save(u)` call reaches through the subtype closure, and how many CALLS edges it emits per collapse class. Test only, no source change.

## Motivation / context

Closes #2834.

`generic-field-receiver-matrix.test.ts` already covers the first half of the issue (an interface-typed field emits the primary edge plus the fan-out, since #2855). What it can't see is the count and the closure, because each control has one implementor and one call site and compares targets as a set. This follows the plan in https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/issues/2834#issuecomment-6765660562.

## Areas touched

## Scope & constraints

**In scope**

- New `test/integration/resolvers/field-receiver-dispatch-counts.test.ts`, one inline fixture (`writeFixtureRepo`) per language: Java, C#, TypeScript, Kotlin. The collapse flag is set per provider, so each language needs its own.
- Each fixture: one interface, two direct implementors, one implementor through a sub-interface, one through an abstract base, every type in its own file. A `Service` with an interface-typed field calls `this.repo.save(u)` twice in `runField`, and `runParam` makes the same two calls on a parameter `r.save(u)`.
- Assertions on the raw target list per caller, with multiplicity, named by target file:
  - Java, C#: 5 edges (declaration + `UserRepo`, `MockRepo`, `SubImpl`, `BaseImpl`, one each).
  - TypeScript, Kotlin: 10 edges (the same five targets, two each).

- The receiver is spelled `this.repo` in all four languages, so the field caller is certain to take Case 0. Kotlin's matrix control uses bare `plain.save(u)`.
- The abstract base declares `save` as abstract in C# and TypeScript and declares nothing in Java and Kotlin. In both shapes the abstract declaration is not a target and the concrete `BaseImpl.save` is.

title: test(hooks): pin the helpers both Claude hook trees ship
body:
## Summary

Pins the helpers that `gitnexus/hooks/claude/` and `gitnexus-claude-plugin/hooks/` both ship: every shared helper must be byte-identical, and a helper added to one tree only fails CI. Adds a Windows-only test that runs `win-rm-list-json.ps1` the way the probe does, so a broken edit made to both copies is caught too. Tests only.

## Motivation / context

Closes #1591.

Most twins already had a per-file parity test (`hook-db-lock-probe.cjs`, `hook-lock`, `registry-query.cjs`, `resolve-analyze-cmd.cjs`). `win-rm-list-json.ps1`, the file from the #1493 incident, did not: the Factory plugin test compares the Factory copy with the plugin copy, but nothing compared the plugin copy with `gitnexus/hooks/claude/`. On `main`, editing only the canonical `.ps1` fails no test in `hooks`, `factory-plugin`, `cursor-hook` or `setup-antigravity`. With this PR it fails one, which names the file.

This takes option 1 from the issue (a CI parity check). It keeps both copies in the repo, so nothing changes in `setup`, the plugin package or the release.

## Areas touched

- [x] `gitnexus/` (CLI / core / MCP server)
- [ ] `gitnexus-web/` (Vite / React UI)
- [ ] `.github/` (workflows, actions)
- [ ] `eval/` or other tooling
- [ ] Docs / agent config only (`AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `.cursor/`, `llms.txt`, etc.)

## Scope & constraints

**In scope**

- `test/unit/hooks.test.ts`, `Claude hook trees ship identical helpers (#1591)`:
  - Names the twin pairs explicitly (`hook-db-lock-probe.cjs`, `hook-lock.cjs` / `hook-lock.js`, `registry-query.cjs`, `resolve-analyze-cmd.cjs`, `win-rm-list-json.ps1`).
  - Pins each tree's full file listing: the twins, the adapter, and the files each tree keeps to itself (`pre-tool-use.sh` and `session-start.sh` in the canonical tree, `hooks.json` in the plugin). Any new file in either tree fails here, including a second spelling of an existing helper, until it's listed.
  - Requires each shared helper to be byte-identical. `.gitattributes` pins `eol=lf`, so this holds on the Windows lane.
- `test/unit/hooks.test.ts`, `win-rm-list-json.ps1 runs on Windows (#1591)` (`describe.runIf(win32)`): builds the encoded command exactly as `getWindowsRmListEncodedCommand()` does, runs Windows PowerShell with the probe's arguments against a temp file nobody holds, and expects exit 0 and `[]`.

**Explicitly out of scope / not done here**

- The adapters (`gitnexus-hook.cjs` / `gitnexus-hook.js`) differ on purpose and keep their function-level parity tests.
- Option 2 (one source plus a generated copy) would change how the plugin is packaged; this PR doesn't touch that.

## Implementation notes

Why the Windows test is needed: parity can't catch a broken edit applied to both copies, and `hasGitNexusServerOwnerWindows` treats any PowerShell failure as "no owner", so a script that stopped compiling would silently turn off the Windows DB-owner check. `Add-Type` compiles the embedded C# before Restart Manager is called, so a compile error fails the run before any output.

I couldn't run Windows PowerShell here, so I checked that assumption with PowerShell 7.4 in Docker on Linux:

- The current script compiles and gets as far as `RmStartSession` (line 45), which fails only because Linux has no `rstrtmgr.dll`.
- A copy with the #1493 defect (`RM_UNIQUE_PROCESS` declared twice in the same body) fails at `Add-Type` (line 7), before any output.

On Windows, the first exits 0 with `[]`: for a file nobody holds, `RmGetList` returns 0 rather than `ERROR_MORE_DATA`, and the script prints `[]`. The Windows lane is the first real run of this test.

## Testing & verification

- [x] `npx vitest run test/unit/hooks.test.ts -t 1591`: 6 passed on Linux (the pin test and 5 byte comparisons); the Windows test is skipped there.
- [x] Mutations, each restored afterwards:
  - one byte added to the plugin `.ps1`: the `.ps1` comparison fails;
  - `Pack = 4` changed to `Pack = 8` in the canonical `.ps1` only: the `.ps1` comparison fails, and it's the only failure across `hooks`, `factory-plugin`, `cursor-hook` and `setup-antigravity` (1 failed, 408 passed);
  - a new helper added to the canonical tree only, or to both trees without being listed: the listing test fails;
  - `hook-lock.cjs` added next to `hook-lock.js` in the plugin (the case nexus-check raised): the listing test fails. The first version of this PR passed it.
- [x] `hooks`, `factory-plugin`, `cursor-hook`: 399 passed, 41 skipped.
- [x] `npm run typecheck:tests`, prettier, eslint (no new warnings), pre-commit hook.

## Risk & rollout

Tests only. A future helper that belongs in both trees has to be added to the list in the pin test, which is the point. If the Windows lane shows PowerShell needing more than the probe's 6 s on a cold runner, the test already allows 60 s.

title: Embedding write path is ~20x more native round-trips per node after #3829 (rc.211+), making large-repo embedding runs ~10x slower
body:
## Summary

On a large repository (~516k embeddable nodes) with an external HTTP embedding endpoint, the embedding phase of `analyze` now proceeds at roughly **11–17 nodes/second**, i.e. **~9–13 hours** for the full node set. The same repository finished the embedding phase much faster on `1.6.13-rc.181`.

The process is **not** stalled and **not** waiting on the endpoint:

- container CPU is pinned at `~100%` (single core), while `NET I/O` grows only slowly;
- inside the process, **one thread owns ~87% of all CPU time** and a second thread (a `libuv` worker) owns most of the rest;
- `load average` stays below 1, confirming one or two runnable threads rather than a saturated machine.

The cost profile matches the durable-embedding-journal layer introduced in #3829 (`cc6225d2c`): the vector write path went from *one batched insert per 16 nodes* to *one 64-node "unit" that performs `beginNodes` + per-8-row transactions + a full `verify()` re-read + a `checkpointUnit()` re-read + three `fsync`s*. At ~516k nodes that is on the order of **200k+ embedded-native queries and ~23k fsyncs**, versus roughly 30k queries before, all on the Node main thread.

## Environment

- GitNexus `1.6.13-rc.216` (Docker), compared against `1.6.13-rc.181`
- `@ladybugdb/core` (pinned by the release)
- Host: 64 GB RAM, 64 GB container limit; the analyze child runs with a 12 GB V8 heap (`--memory-budget 12288`)
- `--skip-fts` (the FTS phase is disabled for this run — the slowdown is entirely inside the embedding phase)
- External HTTP embedding endpoint, 8 texts per provider request (default `subBatchSize`)
- `contentRetention: full` (the index default), so original source hydration is active

## Reproduction

A full rebuild on a large repository:

```bash
gitnexus analyze --force --skip-fts --memory-budget 12288
```

The run reaches the graph phases at the expected speed, then enters the embedding phase:

```
  90% | Embedding 3776/515973 (3m 45s)
  90% | Embedding 3968/515973 (1m 55s)
```

Progress and throughput observations:

- `3776 → 3968` nodes advanced in a few minutes despite the low reported rate — note the elapsed counter resets, so per-interval rates are noisy;
- cumulative throughput across observations is **11–17 nodes/s**;
- after several hours the counter is still in the low thousands, i.e. a few percent of the corpus;
- the run does complete units and the journal advances — it is simply slow.

Thread-level CPU on the running `analyze` process (`top -H`), after ~77 minutes of embedding work:

```
   PID USER      PR  NI    VIRT    RES  SHR S  %CPU  %MEM     TIME+
  7422 root      20   0 1046.9g   2.2g 49864 S  99.9   3.5  76:59.46  node          <- main thread
  7437 root      20   0 1046.9g   2.2g 49864 R  99.9   3.5  11:33.30  libuv-worker  <- fs calls
  7423 root      20   0 1046.9g   2.2g 49864 S   0.0   3.5   0:00.00  DelayedTask
  7424 root      20   0 1046.9g   2.2g 49864 S   0.0   3.5   1:16.69  node
  7425 root      20   0 1046.9g   2.2g 49864 S   0.0   3.5   1:16.41  node
  7426 root      20   0 1046.9g   2.2g 49864 S   0.0   3.5   1:16.98  node
  7427 root      20   0 1046.9g   2.2g 49864 S   0.0   3.5   1:16.82  node
```

`docker stats` for the same container:

```
CONTAINER ID   NAME              CPU %     MEM USAGE / LIMIT     NET I/O          BLOCK I/O
<id>           <name>            100.65%   9.029GiB / 62.74GiB   1.05GB / 475MB   48.4MB / 31.3GB
```

Roughly 1 GB of network traffic against 31 GB of block I/O over the same window supports "the main thread is doing native work, the endpoint is not the constraint."

The embedding phase also reads as a near-stationary `90%` for the first half of the run by construction (`percent = 90 + 8 * completed / totalNodes`), so the progress bar hides the throughput — worth fixing in the same place.

## Analysis

### What was added in #3829 (`cc6225d2c`)

`git log -S` shows both re-verification functions first appear in that commit — neither exists in the parent tree:

- `VectorStore.verify()` (`gitnexus/src/core/lbug/vector-store.ts`)
- `VectorStore.checkpointUnit()` (`gitnexus/src/core/lbug/vector-store.ts`)

Per 64-node work unit (`UNIT_NODES = 64` in `gitnexus/src/core/embeddings/embedding-work-manifest.ts`), the runner now performs:

1. `store.beginNodes()` — `receipts()` PK read, mark incomplete, delete every previous chunk row, insert new receipts;
2. `store.appendBatch()` once per ≤8 rows — each in its own `BEGIN`/`COMMIT` transaction (`vector-store.ts`, `appendBatch`);
3. `store.finishNodes()` — `receipts()` PK read, then `verify()` re-reading **every chunk** of the unit by primary key, then `SET complete=true`;
4. `store.checkpointUnit()` — `receipts()` PK read **again** over the same nodes that step 3 just wrote in this process;
5. `journal.acknowledge()` — `fs.remove()` + directory `fsync`, and the journal `mutate()` path rewrites `job.json` through `writeEmbeddingJobRecord()` (temp file `fsync` → `rename` → **directory `fsync`**), which is three durability barriers per unit.

Observed against the pre-#3829 pipeline, which wrote a whole 16-node batch with a single `UNWIND ... CREATE` statement in one transaction and checkpointed every 5,000 nodes.

### Why this is expensive here

- LadybugDB is embedded; every one of those queries and transactions is a synchronous native call on the **Node main thread**. There is no worker offload for the vector write path.
- `STEP 3` already verifies the unit's chunk coverage in-process. `STEP 4` re-reads the same rows and compares the same `complete` / `contentHash` / `chunks` fields — the same facts, one round-trip later, with no new information about durability.
- The chunk count itself grew with #3817 (`a0586d967`, "preserve AST chunk coverage"), which indexes long callable tails; more chunks means more rows, more `verify()` re-reads, and more provider calls for the same node count.
- `blkid`/`BLOCK I/O` growth indicates the fsync chain is a real cost on this storage, not a no-op.

### Suggested directions

Not prescriptive — flagging the shapes that look removable:

1. **Drop or fold `checkpointUnit()`.** `finishNodes()` has just verified the same unit in the same process; the journal acknowledgement needs a durability signal, not a second PK sweep. If it must stay, it could read only the unit's receipt rows rather than each chunk.
2. **Make the verification granularity configurable.** A per-unit `verify()` is what buys exact resume. Verifying every N units (or behind a flag) would keep crash-resume usable while restoring most of the throughput.
3. **Batch `appendBatch` transactions per unit.** One `BEGIN`/`COMMIT` per 8 rows is the smallest possible transaction; per unit (64 nodes, ≤ dozens of rows) would cut commit count by an order of magnitude.
4. **Add a throughput signal.** The phase reports node counts but never nodes/second or an ETA, so a 10x slowdown is invisible until the elapsed counter is read manually.

## Additional observation (possibly separate issue)

`httpEmbed()` in `gitnexus/src/core/embeddings/http-client.ts` is a plain sequential `for ... await` over `chunk(texts, 64)` — there is no concurrency knob anywhere in the HTTP path, and `GITNEXUS_EMBEDDING_THREADS` only sizes local ONNX `intraOpNumThreads`. At the default `subBatchSize: 8`, a ~516k-node corpus becomes ~64k strictly serial round-trips. On a multi-core endpoint this leaves most of the server idle; on a slow endpoint it multiplies latency by the corpus size.

## Impact

Large repositories (500k+ embeddable nodes) become impractical to index in one pass: a run that used to finish in roughly an hour now needs most of a day, with no config knob that recovers it. The only current workarounds are reducing the corpus (`--embeddings <n>`) or pinning an older release.

Raised as a performance regression rather than a correctness bug — the run is resumable and produces correct vectors; it is just far slower than the release the user migrated from.

title: fix(ruby): bind YARD @param types to the declaring method (RUBY-01)
body:
## What

Gap RUBY-01 from `docs/languages/ruby-ingestion-gaps.md`: a YARD `@param user [User]` on one method leaked onto the class scope, so an untyped sibling `def other(user); user.save; end` resolved to `User#save`, a wrong call edge.

Root cause: the YARD pass anchors the synthesized `@type-binding.parameter` capture on the method node, which is also the method's own `@scope.function`, so the shared scope-extractor's auto-hoist (anchor range equals innermost scope range) lifted the binding to the enclosing Class/Module scope. `rubyBindingScopeFor` returned null for that tag, so the hoisted scope won.

Fix: one provider-hook branch in `languages/ruby/simple-hooks.ts` pins `@type-binding.parameter` to the declaring method. No shared-code change, no capture or golden change (`captures.ts` and the Ruby captures golden are byte-identical to `main`).

## What is deliberately not in this PR

Field typing from typed parameters (`@user = user` → type the field, so `holder.user.save` via `attr_reader` resolves). It was prototyped and reviewed three times; it cannot be made sound at per-file capture level (class reopening across files, mixins, `attr_accessor`/`attr_writer` writes, writes inside blocks and multiple assignment, `Array<User>` collapsing to its element). Those cases are documented in the gaps doc as a parked design with the full hazard list. Missing edges beat wrong edges.

## Proof

- New integration test (temp-dir fixture, exact owner IDs from `HAS_METHOD`, decoy `AuditLog#save` must never be chosen): 39 cases in three suites: the 7 pin cases (both declaration orders, class and Module scope), 7 boundary cases, 25 review-corpus cases asserting exact edge sets including "no edge".
- Fail-first: with the hook branch commented out and dist rebuilt, exactly the three untyped siblings fail with `Method:models.rb:User.save#0`, plus the 8 corpus cases that are leak probes by construction; restored: 39/39.
- Receiver-resolution bench (fresh dist, both arms): all 16 language rows cell-by-cell identical to `main` (93 RESOLVES / 15 VISIBLE-GAP / 1 INVISIBLE-GAP / 1 WRONG-TARGET / 58 N/A); count arm identical (141 call drops / 175 total); `--check` OK.
- Targeted suites (resolvers, scope-resolution, Ruby tripwire, call-routing, CFG visitor, rename providers): 285 files, 8,155 tests, 0 failures. `tsc --noEmit` clean; prettier clean.
- `detect-changes --scope compare --base-ref main` on a fresh index: 5 files, 36 symbols, 0 processes, risk low.

Reviews: cubic (0 issues on the pin) and three codex adversarial passes; every finding targeted the withdrawn field-typing commits, none the pin.

Note: the bench's count arm loads the parse worker from `gitnexus/dist`; rebuild dist before `--check`.

## Behaviour summary (for the release changelog; `CHANGELOG.md` is not edited in this PR per DoD.md 4.5)

**Ruby** — YARD `@param` types bind to the declaring method instead of the enclosing class or module, so a typed method no longer lends its parameter type to an untyped sibling with the same parameter name; the untyped call stays unresolved rather than gaining a wrong edge. The tag types only a formal parameter the body never REBINDS (plain/multiple/splat assignment, `||=`/`+=`, `for`, `rescue =>`, a block/lambda/nested-def parameter or block local, a `case … in` / rightward pattern including the hash shorthand `{user:}`); a write INTO the parameter (`user.name = x`, `user[0] = 1`, `user.count += 1`, `user.a, user.b = …`), a block-parameter default or pinned `^user` / `^(user)` read, and reads inside nested blocks/lambdas keep it. A declined tag resolves like the untagged method, so `user = AuditLog.new; user.save` keeps `AuditLog#save`. Edges main resolved that are now missing by design: the `attr_reader :user` reads `holder.user.save`, and in-class `user.save` / `self.user.save`, after `# @param user [User] def initialize(user)` (they resolved only through the leaked class binding); a tag on a name the body rebinds anywhere, including a block `|user|` or nested `def` that merely shadows it. Not guarded (documented gaps): regex named captures, `binding.local_variable_set`, `eval`. The inert `@type [T]` synthesis, which bound an empty name, was removed (RUBY-01, #3871).
