title: perf(embeddings): remove quadratic vector-store scans and speed up the embedding phase
body:
## Summary

Removes a quadratic cost from the embedding write path and makes the rest of the embedding phase faster: primary-key lookups instead of table scans in the vector store, cheaper vector row inserts, a multi-threaded vector index build, cheaper Class nodes, and bounded concurrent requests to HTTP embedding providers.

## Motivation / context

Refs #3870 (large-repo embedding runs became impractically slow after `rc.181`).

Investigation against the released `1.6.13-rc.216` build with a fake OpenAI-compatible endpoint showed:

- Throughput decays as the vector tables grow (331 → 153 inputs/s over 192k chunks) while the main thread is 84% idle. The cause is the query plan, not the journal: statements keyed by `{pk:$ids[i]}` plan as `SCAN_NODE_TABLE → CROSS_PRODUCT → FILTER`, and `MERGE` always hash-joins a full table scan. Every 64-node unit scanned the whole receipt and chunk tables.
- After fixing that, the remaining time on a 31k-node fixture (108 s) was: vector index build 44 s, vector row inserts 24 s, commits 8 s, journal fsync 7 s, provider 7.5 s.
- Class nodes are main-thread bound since source hydration: `extractFieldNames → buildTypeEnv` took 52% of main-thread time on a class-heavy Java fixture.

This PR does not claim to explain everything in the issue. The reporter's thread table shows the main thread pinned at ~100%, which the scans (they run on libuv workers) do not produce. A CPU profile from the reporter is still needed, so this references the issue rather than closing it.

## Areas touched

- [x] `gitnexus/` (CLI / core / MCP server)
- [ ] `gitnexus-web/` (Vite / React UI)
- [ ] `.github/` (workflows, actions)
- [ ] `eval/` or other tooling
- [ ] Docs / agent config only (`AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `.cursor/`, `llms.txt`, etc.)

## Scope & constraints

**In scope**

- `vector-store.ts`: bind list-indexed keys through `WITH $ids[i] AS id` so LadybugDB plans `QUERY_PRIMARY_KEY_LOOKUP`; replace `MERGE` in `beginNodes` and `markSelected` with a keyed update plus `CREATE` inside one transaction.
- `vector-store.ts`: pass each vector as one float32 string and `CAST` it natively, instead of a numeric list that the Node binding converts element by element on the main thread.
- `seal()`: build the vector index with the whole CPU allowance (`budget.embedding.indexThreads`) instead of the model thread cap.
- `structural-extractor.ts`: use an empty type environment for field names. Only field types consulted it, and embedding text keeps the names alone.
- `embedInputRanges` / durable runner: keep a bounded window of provider requests in flight per unit, results in input order. New `GITNEXUS_EMBEDDING_CONCURRENCY` (1-64, default 4, `1` = serial), HTTP providers only.

**Explicitly out of scope / not done here**

- Per-unit durability cost (about 8 fsyncs per 64-node unit across WAL commits and the journal) and the unit size. Reducing these means changing the journal protocol.
- Progress/ETA reporting for the embedding phase.
- The `rc.181` comparison in the issue title: on the same 31k-node fixture `rc.181` took ~230 s and `rc.216` ~80 s, so the regression is scale dependent, not a constant factor.

## Implementation notes

- **Why `WITH`:** `UNWIND $ids AS id MATCH (n {pk:id})` already used the primary-key index. Only the `UNWIND range(...) AS i ... {pk:$ids[i]}` form did not. `MERGE` keeps a scan even with a bound key, hence the explicit update/create split. The transaction keeps each unit all-or-nothing, as the single `MERGE` statement was.
- **Float32 exactness:** values are rounded to float32 first (`Float32Array`), then printed. 200k random float32 bit patterns plus denormals, extremes and exponent forms round-trip exactly on `@ladybugdb/core` 0.21.1 and 0.22.0. The only difference from the numeric path is that the sign of a negative zero is not kept. Casting raw doubles is *not* exact on exact float midpoints, which is why the rounding happens first.
- **Concurrency is not part of `EmbeddingConfig`**, so it cannot change the embedding identity hash or invalidate existing vectors. Pacing (`GITNEXUS_EMBEDDING_MIN_INTERVAL_MS`), retries and the circuit breaker still apply per request. Each queued row holds its byte reservation until its response is written, so a tight budget shrinks the window instead of exceeding it. Local models stay serial.
- **Default of 4 is a judgment call.** It changes the request pattern for every HTTP provider user. An endpoint that enforces strict rate limits may see more 429s; `GITNEXUS_EMBEDDING_CONCURRENCY=1` restores the old behaviour. Happy to flip the default to 1 if reviewers prefer opt-in.
- **Generated inputs are unchanged:** the fake provider recorded the same input count and the same order-independent digest of all input texts before and after. A differential run of `extractStructuralNames` over 3,491 source files (568 with fields, 16 languages) showed zero differences.

## Testing & verification

Measurements: released `rc.216` with only the changed compiled files swapped in, fake endpoint, 1024 dimensions, 24 cores. The `rc.216` column was measured with the CPU profiler attached, so its gap is slightly overstated.

| Fixture | `rc.216` | This PR |
|---|---|---|

title: fix(java): bind on-demand import edges to AST scopes
body:
## Summary

```text
Java AST → distinct unbound names → visible import targets → persisted IMPORTS
Java edit → re-resolve group → compare per-file graph rows → rewrite changed rows
```

Java package wildcard imports now persist `IMPORTS` edges for types selected by AST-bound name lookup. For example, `import models.*; class Main { User value; }` depends on `User.java`; an `Order` mention in a comment or a local type named `User` does not create a wildcard dependency.

Refs #3695. The reported 24,736-file Java repository produced 3,742,494 `IMPORTS` edges, 81% of its graph, and ran out of heap while writing them. Expanding every package wildcard into persisted edges makes the graph grow with importers × package size.

## Scope and implementation

- Capture simple-name uses from the existing Java AST, including field/parameter types, generic arguments, annotations, casts, `instanceof`, `throws`, class literals and receiver qualifiers. Declaration names, qualified member tails, comments and strings are excluded.
- Bind value and type shadows in one top-down AST traversal carrying lexical scopes. Constructor bodies, varargs parameters, annotation types and member-type visibility remain local to their declaring scope. Package annotations and constructor references remain type uses. Resolve the remaining names against explicit imports, same-directory package declarations and wildcard packages. Ambiguous wildcard candidates are retained.
- Persist versioned, distinct unbound names in the ParsedFile side channel so worker and warm-cache paths need no source rescan or reparse. The new `ScopeResolver.onDemandImportTargets` hook supplies target files to the language-neutral emitter and works after scopes are sealed to disk.
- Share each package's declaration index across importers. Same-package lookup does not depend on the capped receiver-inference sibling injection. A namesake outside the importer's directory cannot prove a wildcard dependency unused, so test source sets, other build modules and sample directories retain that dependency conservatively.
- Keep finalized import visibility intact for chained calls and inheritance. Only persisted File→File edges are narrowed; unused explicit imports still produce edges.

The rules follow [JLS 6.3](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/specs/jls/se25/html/jls-6.html#jls-6.3), [6.5.5.1](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/specs/jls/se25/html/jls-6.html#jls-6.5.5.1), and [7.5.2](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/specs/jls/se25/html/jls-7.html#jls-7.5.2).

## Conservative cases and incremental correctness

Static/member-type wildcard imports retain their concrete owner-file dependency, including inherited static members; narrowing those needs a complete member inventory under JLS 7.5.4. Pattern-flow shadowing that is not proven can retain extra dependencies.

Tree-sitter does not perform [Java's Unicode-escape translation](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/specs/jls/se25/html/jls-3.html#jls-3.3), and the current scope keys do not normalize identifier-ignorable characters. Raw Unicode-escape markers (including escapes inside comments), parser errors, those identifiers, missing AST facts, and unavailable target evidence retain dependencies conservatively. Old cache entries therefore remain safe. `sr-emit-imports-*` probes report `unused` edges and distinct `incomplete_files`.

A call chain can depend on a type the importer never names. Java uses the workspace resolution-group hook so a Java change/addition/deletion refreshes Java resolution across directories. Per-file graph-row digests restrict writes to candidates whose resolved rows changed; missing digests require a conservative rewrite. The native regression compares incremental CALLS and IMPORTS with fresh full rebuilds after reparenting an unmentioned intermediate base, adding and deleting a shadowing type, and editing a method body.

## Performance

The following comparison measured the earlier lexical and AST implementations within this PR, before the review follow-up replaced ancestor walks with a cursor traversal. It is not a base-versus-final-head measurement.

A synthetic workload with 1,000 package types and 100 importers, each using one type and mentioning 25 others only in a comment, scans 100,000 wildcard pairs:

| Measurement | Lexical scan | AST and scope lookup |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Persisted import pairs | 2,600 | 100 |
| Warm emission median | 7.0 ms | 6.0 ms |
| Capture median, 1,100 files | 268 ms | 232 ms |

These are local microbenchmarks, with a counting graph sink and shared package indexes warmed. They show improved precision and a modest emission speedup; capture medians varied from 232 to 275 ms across local runs, so there is no clear capture-time improvement. They do not establish end-to-end speed on the reported repository.

Finalize still materializes the wildcard visibility objects. Removing that remaining importer × package-size allocation is separate work. Other languages do not opt into this hook.

## Evidence

Validation of the published follow-up (`2ad8a39bf`):

- `npm test -- --maxWorkers=8`: 33,054 passed, 101 skipped, five failed across 1,553 files. Four Codex setup failures reproduce on the original PR commit `a3021aca8`. The fifth was the parse-cache input-coverage guard finding obsolete June/September build artifacts with no current source; after moving those generated leftovers out of `dist/`, all 21 tests in that file pass. The full suite was not rerun after this build-output cleanup; no source changed.
- The five focused Java/import/incremental regression files pass all 105 tests, including native CALLS/IMPORTS parity.
- Build, source and test typechecks pass. Changed-file ESLint, formatting checks, and commit hooks pass.
- Scope-capture baseline check passes all 17 cases, including the new deep-expression workload.
- The 300-file explicit-import reproduction rewrites only the edited file and no dependents.
- GitNexus change analysis completed without partial/truncated results. The whole PR reaches nine flows (HIGH); the final follow-up reports LOW.

Earlier validation of `d1e80e37`:

- Full suite, before the final Unicode-comment and annotated-type-parameter guards: `npm test -- --maxWorkers=8` — 32,965 passed, 101 skipped, 10 failed across three setup/auto-sync files. All 10 failure identities reproduce on the original PR commit `a3021aca8` (94 passed, 10 failed in the three-file baseline run). The auto-sync cases reject the validation checkout's `/tmp` location; the setup cases concern Codex configuration handling. These failures are outside this change.
- Final source: 33 Java and related regression files — 800 passed, 13 skipped (31 files passed, 2 skipped), including native incremental/full parity and Java rename coverage. The focused scope/import/group tests separately pass all 61 cases.
- Final build and test typecheck passed. ESLint passed for the final capture helper and regression file; the earlier combined lint check had no errors.
- Scope-capture baseline check passed for all 16 language cases and the final fixture corpus.
- GitNexus change analysis: 18 files, 42 symbols, 4 affected flows; no partial/truncated result. `git diff --cached --check` passed.

Regression coverage includes shadowing, declaration order and scope boundaries, explicit-only imports, ambiguous packages, type-only uses, source-free cached facts, old-cache fallback, Unicode/parser limitations, interleaved emission and incremental/full parity. The Java capture baseline is remeasured for the final fixture corpus.

## Areas touched

- [x] `gitnexus/` CLI/core and tests
- [ ] `gitnexus-web/`
- [ ] `.github/`
- [ ] `eval/`

## Merge Danger

**Door:** Two-way. Reverting and re-analyzing restores the previous graph behavior.

**Blast Radius:** High. Graph change analysis against the fetched main merge base reaches nine flows, including Java import resolution and analysis writeback.

A re-analysis produces fewer Java File→File import dependencies, which changes file-level impact and cycle results. Unknown evidence remains conservative. Java resolution is still workspace-wide; row digests keep unchanged candidates out of incremental writes. The reported external repository has not been remeasured, so #3695 remains open for confirmation.

title: fix(dart): resolve a parenthesized awaited receiver through its owner (DART-04)
body:
## What

Gap DART-04 from `docs/languages/dart-ingestion-gaps.md`: `(await svc.getUserAsync()).save()` resolved to `Address.save`, a wrong call edge. The receiver-resolution bench recorded the cell as WRONG-TARGET.

Root cause: the Dart emitter only names a receiver when the head is an identifier, `this` or `super`. A parenthesized head produced a call with no receiver at all, which fell into the free-call tier, where a wildcard import had materialised every method name from `models.dart` and the first `save` declared (`Address.save`) won. The type was never the problem.

## Commits (each builds and typechecks on its own; six in total)

1. `feat(scope-resolution): let a provider answer the await step of a receiver chain` — language-free: `ElementAccessRoute` gains `{ kind: 'await' }`; the compound-receiver fold asks the provider's route at an await step (identity when the position already names a class or the provider answers undefined).
2. `feat(scope-resolution): carry an awaited marker on call-result bindings and unwrap it on chain follow` — language-free: `TypeRef.awaited?: true` (gitnexus-shared) set from a generic `@type-binding.awaited` sub-tag; `followedStep` in `utils/type-ref-chain.ts` is the single unwrap point for both chain follows; providers without the route are unchanged. Unit test with a stub provider.
3. `fix(dart): resolve a parenthesized awaited receiver through its owner (DART-04)` — Dart emitter mints receiver text and a structural chain for parenthesized heads (index, non-null assert, cast, arithmetic, `(make())`, deep chains → recorded `receiver-unresolved` drops, never a guess); `Future`/`FutureOr` signature return re-join (tree-sitter-dart splits `type_arguments`), kept whole so the un-awaited Future types nothing; Dart answers only the await route (`List`/`Set`/`Iterable`/`Stream` deliberately not unwrapped); awaited initializers carry the marker.
4. `fix(dart): guard the awaited call-result inference (DART-04 review)` — the awaited direct call must be the entire awaited operand (no trailing `.then(...)`); qualified types keep their qualifier; a local written anywhere else in the function refuses the inference.
5. `fix(dart): read a qualified awaited yield in the producer's scope; treat pattern writes as writes (DART-04 review 2)` — `AwaitedFollow { yields, resolveQualified? }`: a `.`-qualified yield is resolved in the producer's module through its own namespace imports (one hop, exactly one module, class-like member) or declined; an unanswered hop leaves the binding untouched; every identifier inside any `*_pattern` counts as a write.

## Effect on edges

- Bench (fresh dists, both arms): exactly one of 168 shape cells moved, `dart.awaitParen` WRONG-TARGET → RESOLVES (`User.save`); count arm `callDrops 141 → 140` because `dart-prefixed-factory-return/lib/callers.dart:22` (`final x = await rp.makeAsync(); x.m()`) now carries the exact `C.m` edge instead of a recorded drop; every other cell and bucket identical; `--check` OK (baseline.json updated for that one cell).
- `dart.test.ts` `awaitedCall` expectation moved from unresolved to the exact `C.m` edge.
- Precision cases asserted to produce no edge: un-awaited `svc.getUserAsync().save()`, `await make().then(...)`, reassigned locals (plain, record/list patterns, `??=`, closure write, `late` re-init, if-case shadow), six refusal shapes; decoys (`Address.save`, same-file `User`, cross-file reused-prefix `decoy.dart:User`) never chosen.
6. `docs(dart): record the two awaited-inference recall boundaries from review 3` — docs only.

- Filed, not fixed: DART-07 (un-awaited `var x = Foo().bar()` keeps a first-call binding), a shared silent drop for typed-but-classless bare receivers, `Future<models.User<T>>` (missing edge, never a decoy).

## Proof

- DART-04 test: 35 cases. Fail-first per guard (edit-revert, dist rebuilt each time): paren branch → 20/23 fail with the original `Address.save` edge; binding unwrapped at binding time → the non-await guard fails; await route disabled → awaited cases lose their edge; marker not emitted → the awaited-variable edge silently disappears; followedStep unwrap disabled → stub-provider unit cases fail; F1/F2/F3 and F2b/F3b guards each disabled → exactly their cases gain the wrong edge.
- Targeted suites (resolvers, scope-resolution, dart units, receiver-chain codec/fold, call-form, parsedfile-store): 289 files, 8,283 tests, 0 failures. `tsc --noEmit` clean in gitnexus and gitnexus-shared; prettier clean.
- `detect-changes --scope all` on a fresh index: 8 files, 52 symbols, 0 processes, risk low.
- Three codex adversarial reviews; every finding addressed in commits 4 and 5; the third verdict is approve, with two low recall boundaries documented in commit 6 (a prefix bound to two modules declines even when the member is unambiguous; a pattern field label spelled like the local counts as a write).

## Behaviour summary (for the release changelog; `CHANGELOG.md` is not edited in this PR per DoD.md 4.5)

- **Dart** — a member call on a parenthesized receiver, `(await svc.getUserAsync()).save()`, resolves through its receiver instead of as a receiver-less call: it reaches the declared `Future<User>` result's `User.save` rather than the first same-named method the imported library declares (`Address.save`); a parenthesized head the resolver cannot type is a recorded drop, never a name guess (member-call selectors; a cascade `..save()` on such a head is still a free-call name guess, recorded as DART-08). A `Future<T>` / `FutureOr<T>` return binding is carried whole, so a member called on the un-awaited Future is not typed as a member of `T`, and an awaitable spelling never binds to a workspace class of the wrapper's name (DART-09). A call-result local (`final x = await f()`, and the un-awaited `final x = f()`) is inferred only when the call is the whole initializer and the name has exactly one binder in its outermost function body and is assigned nowhere in it — closure/catch/local-function parameters, sibling closures and `if`/`else` branches reusing a name get no inferred binding from either declaration. A qualified `Future<models.User>` is resolved through the producer's own import or declined, never through the consumer's prefix map. Recall boundaries of the inference are documented in docs/languages/dart-ingestion-gaps.md (DART-04, DART-06, DART-07).
- **Scope resolution** — a receiver chain's `await` step asks the language's `elementTypeOf` route (`{ kind: 'await' }`) before any class found for the position; a declared spelling that route can unwrap is an awaitable wrapper and names no owner in any receiver lookup; providers without the route keep the identity behaviour (pinned for every non-Dart provider and resolver).
- **Scope resolution** — an awaited call-result binding (`@type-binding.awaited`, kept as `TypeRef.awaited`) takes what the followed return type yields under `await` at both chain follows, through the same route; a language without the route is unchanged. Dart's `final x = await rp.makeAsync(); x.m()` now reaches the exact `C.m` instead of recording a drop.

## Review round 2 (head `349d747eb`)

Every reproduced finding of the maintainer review is fixed precision-first and pinned; see the thread replies and the round summary comment for the mutation receipts.

title: fix(php): bind a PHPDoc @param to the declaring method, only for an unrebound formal (PHP-04)
body:
## What

PHP-04. A PHPDoc `@param User $user` on a **bodyless** method (an abstract method, or one in a trait) was anchored on the method node. Its binding range therefore equalled the Function scope, the shared auto-hoist lifted it to the Class scope, and a sibling method's untyped `$user` borrowed it:

```php
abstract class Base {
    /** @param User $user */
    abstract public function typed($user);
    public function plain($user) { $user->save(); }   // resolved to User::save: wrong
}
```

Pinning the tag to its own callable exposed a second problem. In a bodied method, the tag outranked a local's constructor-inferred type, so `@param AuditLog $user` beside `$user = new User()` typed the call as `AuditLog::save`. And `@param X $this` retyped `$this`.

## Behaviour after `d1e06d947` (PHP provider only; no shared code)

1. **Pin.** `phpBindingScopeFor` (`php/simple-hooks.ts`) pins `@type-binding.parameter` to the declaring callable. This closes the bodyless-sibling leak in both declaration orders.
2. **Formal-name check.** A tag binds only a name that is one of the callable's formal parameters, including a promoted by-reference `public &$x`. It never binds `$this`. A tag on any other name (doc drift) types nothing and shadows nothing.
3. **Decline guard.** A tag is declined when the body rebinds the formal or when the body has opaque writes.
   - Rebindings: assignment and destructuring, `.=`/`??=`, `=&` on either side, `foreach … as` (including `&$x`), `catch`, a nested closure/arrow/function parameter, `use (&$x)`, a reference taken in the body, `static`/`global`/`unset($x)`.
   - Opaque writes: `$$x`, `${'x'}`, `"${$x}"`/`"${expr}"`, `extract()`, `eval()`, and the opaque forms of `parse_str()` (bare, upper-cased or `\`-qualified). An opaque write declines every tag of that callable.
   - Writes into the variable (`$x->p = …`, `$x[0] = …`, `unset($x->p)`) do not decline.
4. **A declined tag shadows its name.** The callable's scope masks every declined formal. The capture `@receiver-owner.declined-doc-params` rides the callable's own `@scope.function` match and is read through `scopeOwnsReceivers` (`phpScopeOwnsReceivers`, the same `Scope.ownsReceivers` contract the Dart shadowed-fields mask uses). The site is then suppressed before lookup with `receiver-owned-but-unbound`, and the lexical walk stops at that scope. Two PHP-provider changes make the mask hold:
   - The local inference bindings for a declined formal inside its own callable are dropped: `$x = new A()`, `$x = $y`, `$x = f()`, `$x = $o->m()`, and a foreach element type. `isReceiverOwnedButUnbound` reads `typeBindings` before the mask, so these bindings would otherwise win. A native type hint is not dropped and still wins, as before.
   - The unresolved-receiver fallback (`phpEmitUnresolvedReceiverEdges`) checks the mask itself, so the single-owner name fallback does not depend on the receiver pass having marked the site handled.
5. **One decision per callable.** The parameter binding, the foreach element type, the mask and the drop all read one memoised `PhpDocParamDecision`, built from one descendant scan of the body. Callables without a `@param` tag do no scan.

### The four routes from the review (before → after)

The fixture has `format`, `where` and `get` each with exactly one owner, a top-level `$user = new AuditLog();` in another file, and a call before the rebinding.

| Route | `d1e0075ce` | `d1e06d947` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 rebind after use (`before_then_rebind`) | `AuditLog::save` | no edge; `suppressed: receiver-owned-but-unbound` |
| 2 single-owner name fallback (`render_date_default`) | `AuditLog::format` | no edge; `suppressed: receiver-owned-but-unbound` |
| 3 module-scope climb (`lib_reassign`) | `AuditLog::save` | no edge; `suppressed: receiver-owned-but-unbound` |
| 4 call-result alias (`$query = $query->where(); $query->get();`) | `Report::where`, `Report::get` | no edges; both sites suppressed |

The untagged twins still reach the decoy on every build. That is pre-existing and outside this guard. They are pinned as controls so the fixture keeps exercising the routes.

**Recall cost (documented):** `$x = new User(); $x->save();` on a documented formal that is rebound (`ra`) gives no edge. The engine keeps one binding per name per scope, so it cannot tell that order from route 1. Missing beats wrong.

### Review round 1 inline items

- A by-value `use ($x)` is no longer a rebinding; `use (&$x)` still is, through `by_ref`.
- `"${name}"` / heredoc `${name}` interpolation is a read, while `"${$x}"` and `"${expr}"` still decline.
- `\Foo\extract()` is not the builtin: any named `prefix` child names another namespace.
- A promoted by-reference formal `public &$user` counts as a formal.

The docs now say that a variable passed to a callee's by-reference parameter (`preg_match($re, $s, $m)`, a user `fill(&$out)`) is not seen as a write.

## Proof

- `test/integration/resolvers/php-docblock-param-scope.test.ts` has 82 cases. Negatives assert an empty edge list plus the exact suppression reason at the site, and each block ends with an exact edge list.
- **Fail-first:** 47 of the 82 fail on the review-round sources (`d1e0075ce`, dist rebuilt), including the four wrong edges in the table.
- **16 mutations.** Each was applied alone with dist rebuilt, and `captures.ts` was restored byte-identical afterwards. Every one fails its targeted cases:
  - mask emission off; local-binding drop off; both off;
  - the `static`, `global`, `unset`, `eval`, one-argument `parse_str` and call-time `&` arms;
  - the `extract` text pre-filter; the alternate `@param $name Type` parse;
  - `use` restored as a rebinding; the interpolation exemption off, or accepting any child;
  - the old first-prefix-child test; no `by_ref` unwrap.
- **Fallback check, shown on its own:** I temporarily removed the receiver pass's `handledSites.add` (restored afterwards). With the PHP check, every route test passes. Without it, route 2 gives `AuditLog::format` and route 4 gives `Report::where/get`.
- **Suites:**
  - every `*php*.test.ts` plus `test/unit/scope-resolution/php`: 17 files passed, 1 env-gated skip, 697 tests;
  - shared `test/unit/scope-resolution`: 178 files, 3,524 tests.
- **Checks:** `npm run build` OK. `tsc --noEmit` and `tsc -p tsconfig.test.json` are clean. Prettier, `git diff --check` and the bidi scan are clean.
- **Benches:**

## Summary

Route setup-installed Claude/Codex hooks and the Claude plugin through the package-owned `gitnexus-hook` entrypoint. Hook behavior and helpers have one implementation, with no runtime copies to synchronize.

## Motivation / context

## Areas touched

title: fix(ruby): a bare identifier that names a parameter or local is a read, not a call (RUBY-04)

## Summary

Remove false Ruby CALLS edges when a captured bare identifier reads a parameter or an already-bound local.

```diff
 class Host
   def target; end
   def run(target)
     target
   end
 end
- run → Host#target
+ no CALLS edge for the parameter read
```

The guard lives in the Ruby scope-capture provider and follows lexical scopes and parse order. It handles parameters and defaults, local assignments, binding patterns, scope headers, and BEGIN/END bodies. Heredoc bodies belong to their opener's scope even when that scope closes on the opener line; their bindings are visible to reads parsed later on that line.

Only bare-identifier statement captures are filtered. Call-shaped captures continue through the existing resolver. The [Ruby ingestion notes](docs/languages/ruby-ingestion-gaps.md#bare-identifier-reads-ruby-04-fixed) document supported forms and remaining gaps, including the pre-existing explicit-call/parameter collision and uncaptured branch-body reads.

title: fix(group): match a manifest link's consumer only in the repo it names
body:
## Summary

A `links:` entry in group.yaml now only matches providers in the repo it names. Until now, the consumer contract the link creates went through the exact and wildcard passes, which matched it on the contract id alone, so a route that another repo in the group also serves gained an extra cross-link nobody declared.

## Motivation / context

Closes #1188.

This is fix B from the issue: the matcher respects what the link says. Fix A (provider routes losing their controller prefix) is a separate problem and isn't touched here.

What the issue describes, reproduced with `gitnexus group sync` on three indexed repos: `learning` and `user-service` both serve `POST /import`, `gen-question` has no HTTP call the extractors can see, and group.yaml declares a single link, `backend/gen-question → backend/learning POST::/import`.

| cross-link in contracts.json | `main` | this PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `manifest` gen-question → learning | yes | yes |
| `exact` gen-question → learning (`importLessons`) | yes | yes |
| `exact` gen-question → user-service (`importUsers`) | **yes** | no |

## Areas touched

- [x] `gitnexus/` (CLI / core / MCP server)
- [ ] `gitnexus-web/` (Vite / React UI)
- [ ] `.github/` (workflows, actions)
- [ ] `eval/` or other tooling
- [ ] Docs / agent config only (`AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `.cursor/`, `llms.txt`, etc.)

## Scope & constraints

**In scope**

- `extractors/manifest-extractor.ts`: the consumer contract a link creates carries `meta.providerRepo`, the repo the link names. The provider contract is unchanged.
- `matching.ts`:
  - `runExactMatch` skips providers outside that repo for such a consumer.
  - `runWildcardMatch` does the same. It filters before the bare-name thrift ambiguity check, so a same-named service in a repo the link doesn't point to no longer blocks the declared one.
- `sync.ts`: `withoutDeclaredProvider` drops the field from `contracts` and `unmatched` once matching is done. `contracts.json` and the bridge keep their current shape.
- `PIPELINE.md`: one paragraph under Manifest extraction.

**Explicitly out of scope / not done here**

- Consumers the extractors find in source still match across the whole group. Only a link states where a call goes.
- The exact pass's bare-name thrift method lookup (`findMatchingKeys`) still requires a group-wide unique match. For a link consumer, a same-named method elsewhere means no `exact` link, which is the conservative outcome; the `manifest` link is still there.

## Implementation notes

- Why the field is dropped after matching rather than kept. `sync-partial-extraction.test.ts` requires that the registry never names a repo the run couldn't read. A link consumer whose provider is unreadable would name it through `providerRepo`.
- Why it can't be dropped earlier. Removing it before matching would make that same consumer match the whole group again. The new unreadable-provider test fails in that case.
- Callers: `syncGroup` is the only production caller of the changed functions, so `group sync`, auto-sync and the MCP `group_sync` tool all go through it. `impact` rates all three HIGH for that reason. `detect_changes` lists the 7 `group sync` flows through `syncGroup`. `buildProviderIndex` and two `sync.ts` properties appear only because lines moved.

## Testing & verification

- [x] 9 new tests:
  - `matching.test.ts`, 6 tests:
    - a link consumer ignores a same-id provider in another repo;
    - it stays unmatched when the declared repo serves nothing;
    - an extracted consumer still matches every repo;
    - a link consumer without the field keeps the group-wide match;
    - a gRPC service wildcard matches only the declared repo;
    - a bare thrift wildcard isn't made ambiguous by an undeclared repo.
  - `sync.test.ts`: the issue's scenario through `syncGroup`, and the persisted consumer has no `providerRepo`.
  - `sync-partial-extraction.test.ts`: with the declared provider unreadable, a third repo serving the same method gets no cross-link.
  - `manifest-extractor.test.ts`: the field is set on the consumer for both `role` values and absent on the provider.
- [x] Mutations, each restored afterwards:

  | mutation | new tests failing |
  | --- | --- |
  | all three source files at `main` | 7 |
  | no tag in the extractor | 3 |
  | no filter in the exact pass | 3 |
  | wildcard filter removed | 2 |
  | wildcard ambiguity counted over all repos | 1 |
  | field not dropped before writing (also fails the existing `sync-partial-extraction.test.ts:481`) | 2 |

- [x] `test/unit/group` + `test/integration/group`: 1453 passed. The other `syncGroup` callers (`repo-manager-registry-strict-read`, `group-service-not-found`, `auto-sync-runner`): 85 passed.
- [x] Full unit suite: 24,925 passed and 50 skipped. The 2 failures were the SIGTERM / IPC handoff cases in `analyze-phase-handoff.test.ts`, under full-suite load. That file passed 25/25 on each of two runs on its own, and it doesn't touch group code.
- [x] `npx tsc --noEmit`, `npm run typecheck:tests`, prettier, eslint (no new warnings), pre-commit hook.
- [x] The `group sync` run in the table above, with the CLI built from `main` and from this branch, in an isolated `GITNEXUS_HOME`.

## Risk & rollout

Groups that declare `links:` can lose `exact` / `wildcard` cross-links. Only the links to repos other than the declared one go: those are the false positives this PR removes. No schema or registry format change.

## Checklist

- [x] PR body meets repo minimum length (workflow may label short descriptions)
- [ ] If `AGENTS.md` / overlays changed: headers, scope block, and changelog updated per project conventions
- [x] No secrets, tokens, or machine-specific paths committed

## Correction (maintainer, 2026-11-15)

- "Explicitly out of scope", second bullet. For a link consumer, the bare-name thrift lookup in `findMatchingKeys` is not reached while the declared repo is readable. The link also creates a provider contract with the same id in that repo, and `findMatchingKeys` returns on that exact key first (`matching.ts:151`). So a bare `Service/Method` link gets no `exact` link to a package-qualified handler, whether or not another repo has that method. This was the same before this PR. The `/*` form of the link does match the declared repo's handlers.
- Added in 92419bc85: both passes track matched consumers as records. A link consumer that matched nothing is now counted in `unmatched` even when another consumer with the same repo and contract id matched. The commit also adds tests for the wildcard pass through `syncGroup`, the strip on `unmatched`, the contracts handed to the bridge write, and other contract types.
- Added in 6080b83f8: `bench/group-link-matching/measure.mjs`, run with `--check` in the benchmarks job. It fingerprints every cross-link and unmatched contract of the matching stage at 8,000 links and checks that the cost stays linear in the number of links (ratio 1.04 to 1.19 between 2,000 and 8,000 links, budget 1.8). The matcher from before this PR measures the same slope, so the fix adds no scaling cost.

title: fix(dart): capture `import … deferred as p` as a namespace import
body:
## What

The Dart scope query's import pattern only matches the grammar's first `import_specification` branch, `(configurable_uri) @import.source (identifier)? @import.alias`. In the vendored tree-sitter-dart, the deferred form is a separate branch with a **bare `(uri)`** child (no `configurable_uri` wrapper), the anonymous `deferred` / `as` tokens, and the alias `(identifier)` — verified by printing the S-expressions:

```
import 'x.dart' deferred as p;   (import_specification (uri (string_literal)) (identifier))
import 'x.dart' as p;            (import_specification (configurable_uri (uri (string_literal))) (identifier))
import 'x.dart' as p show A;     (import_specification (configurable_uri (uri (string_literal))) (identifier) (combinator (identifier)))
import 'x.dart';                 (import_specification (configurable_uri (uri (string_literal))))
```

This PR adds a second pattern for that branch:

```scheme
(import_or_export
  (library_import
    (import_specification
      (uri) @import.source
      "deferred" @import.deferred
      (identifier) @import.alias))) @import.statement
```

`interpretDartImport` already turns `@import.alias` into a `kind: 'namespace'` import, so the deferred prefix resolves like the non-deferred `as p` form (combinators such as `show`/`hide` are tolerated by both patterns), **with one exception the language defines**: a deferred prefix carries an implicit `Future<void> loadLibrary()`, and the load imports the library with `hide loadLibrary`, so `p.loadLibrary` never names a declaration of the imported library. `@import.deferred` marks the prefix, and the Dart capture emitter drops every `<deferredPrefix>.loadLibrary` reference: the call, the tear-off read, the call-result seed (`final f = p.loadLibrary();`) and members called on its result (`p.loadLibrary().timeout(d)`). Without that, a library that declares its own top-level `loadLibrary` (legal when the import hides it) received CALLS/ACCESSES edges from those sites, and its return annotation typed the Future (review finding 1).

## Architecture

Two Dart-only source files change. Nothing in the shared pipeline, the Dart `ScopeResolver`, `interpretDartImport`, or `resolveDartImportTarget` changes.

- `languages/dart/query.ts` — the second import pattern, with the `deferred` token captured as `@import.deferred`. The two patterns are disjoint (one requires `configurable_uri`, the other a bare `uri` plus the `deferred` token), so no statement is captured twice.
- `languages/dart/captures.ts` — Pass A records the alias of each import match that carries `@import.deferred` (per file, in the emitter that already walks that file). After the passes, a file with at least one deferred prefix filters out the matches that name `<prefix>.loadLibrary`. A file without a deferred import returns its captures untouched; its only added cost is one property check per query match.

The shared `isNamespaceMemberVisible` hook was not used: it sees only the member, not which prefix reached it, and the return-type path (`imported-return-types.ts`) does not consult it.

## Effect on edges / the review bot

- A Dart file whose only path to a library is a deferred import now gets its `IMPORTS` edge; before, the file had none and the library looked unreferenced from it.
- Qualified calls through the prefix (`p.make()`) bind their result type, so `final x = p.make(); x.m()` resolves `m` to the right class; constructors (`p.C()`) and static members (`p.C.sm()`, `p.C.sf`) resolve too — the same as `import … as p`. Before, those sites were dropped as `receiver-unresolved` or reached only by a prefix-blind unique-class-name match.
- `p.loadLibrary` through a deferred prefix produces no edge and types nothing, even when the library declares a top-level `loadLibrary`.
- For the review bot this closes a false "unused / no callers" hole for Flutter code that uses deferred (lazy) library loading, without inventing callers of a library's own `loadLibrary`.
- Non-deferred imports, exports, and every other language: unchanged (receiver-resolution bench rows byte-identical; scope-capture fingerprints byte-identical for every language except Dart — see below).

## Known limits (inherited from prefixed imports; follow-ups)

These behave the same for `import … as p` on base and head; deferred files now share them.

- **A deferred import of a re-exporting library resolves nothing through the prefix, the same as `as p`** (review finding 2). `lookupNamespaceMember` (`scope-resolution/passes/receiver-bound-calls.ts`) reads only the target file's own declarations and does not follow `export`, so with `import 'facade.dart' deferred as p;` where `facade.dart` only has `export 'impl.dart';`, the file gets its IMPORTS edge and `p.C.sm()` / `p.C.sf` resolve nothing. Making Dart namespace-member lookup follow `export` directives is a follow-up. (Not pinned by a fixture here: with a second `C` in the workspace, base and head both give only the IMPORTS edge, so such a test could not fail on either side of this change.)
- Closure parameters, for-in / pattern variables and `late` locals named like a prefix do not shadow it (`xs.forEach((p) => p.run())` binds `run` through the prefix).
- A parameter named like the prefix loses the `x.m()` edge after `final x = p.make();`.
- A missing relative deferred target binds to a same-suffix file elsewhere (`dart/import-target.ts`).
- `p.C.named()` (a named constructor through a prefix) is recorded as `receiver-unresolved` for both `as p` and `deferred as p`.
- The `loadLibrary` filter matches the spelling `<prefix>.loadLibrary`: a local or parameter that shadows a deferred prefix and has its own `loadLibrary` member loses that call (a missed edge, never a wrong one).
- Conditional URIs never resolve (the first pattern captures the whole `configurable_uri`), with or without `deferred`.

## How tested

Fail-first — every new test fails with its fix removed:

- `test/unit/dart-import-resolver.test.ts` — `keeps deferred prefixed imports as namespace handles`: `import 'x.dart' deferred as p;` and `import 'y.dart' deferred as q show A;` through real grammar captures must yield `{ kind: 'namespace', localName: 'p' … }` / `q`. title: chore(deps)(deps-dev): bump jscpd from 5.4.2 to 5.4.3 in /gitnexus
body:
Bumps [jscpd](https://github.com/kucherenko/jscpd/tree/HEAD/rust/jscpd) from 5.4.2 to 5.4.3.
Release notes

Sourced from jscpd's releases.

Release v5.4.3

New Features

  • runJscpd() runs the jscpd binary from Node.js. require("jscpd") and import { runJscpd } from "jscpd" now export runJscpd(args, options). It finds the platform binary the way the jscpd command does and returns the result of spawnSync, so a script no longer starts a second Node.js process to run the command, and tools such as knip see that the script uses jscpd. Where the command prints an error and exits, the function throws an Error with the same message. The types are in index.d.ts. Detection still runs only in the Rust binary, and nothing parses or returns clones in JavaScript. By @​abrahamguo. (#1238)

  • The HTML report shows both fragments of a clone and highlights the code. "Show code" used to open only the first fragment. Now it opens both side by side, or one above the other on a narrow screen, each under its file with line numbers in a gutter, and a long line scrolls inside its pane. The report highlights the code with Prism 1.30.0 again, as the v4 report did, and inlines only the languages it shows. A block inside another file, such as guide.md:typescript, keeps the lines that detection gives it. (#1263, #1265)

Bug Fixes

  • The GitHub Action installed the newest jscpd, whatever ref you pinned. The version input defaulted to latest, so kucherenko/jscpd@v5.4.1 installed 5.4.2 once it came out. Now an empty version installs the release that the action's own ref belongs to, so pinning the action pins jscpd, and a Dependabot bump of the action updates both. version: latest still installs the newest release. This works from v5.4.3 on: older tags still install the newest jscpd. Reported by @​dannystaple, fixed by @​sarankumar1325. (#1240, #1249)

  • A /* or // inside a JS or TS string ended a jscpd:ignore region. The tokenizer looked for the markers with a byte scan that took every /* and // for a comment, so 'a /* b' inside a marked region opened a comment that ran to the end marker, and the code after the string came back as clones. The markers are now found by their text, as in the other languages, so a region runs from jscpd:ignore-start to the next jscpd:ignore-end. Markers inside template literals, such as the CSS of a styled component, keep working. Reported by @​bauchdj, fixed by @​sarankumar1325. (#1257, #1258)

  • "Ignore this clone" in the language server broke JSX. It wrote // jscpd:ignore-start among JSX children, where the page shows it as text, and could put a marker inside a tag, such as < /* jscpd:ignore-end *//ul>, which TypeScript can't parse. Now it writes {/* jscpd:ignore-start */} among children and never puts a marker inside a tag. The start goes before the tag and the end after it, so the region still covers the clone. Each copy of a --cross-formats clone gets the comment of its own format, JSX in the <script lang="tsx"> of a Vue, Svelte or Astro component gets the JSX markers, and a marker after / gets a space so it doesn't turn into a line comment. (#1260, #1264)

  • --dead-code reported a file loaded with import(`./x`) or import('$lib/x') as unused. import() read only quoted specifiers and turned away any specifier with a $ in it, so a backtick import() with nothing interpolated and SvelteKit's $lib alias were never followed. The importing file also lost 30 points of confidence on every finding. jscpd dropped import.meta.glob(`./pages/*.ts`) the same way. Now only ${ inside backticks counts as interpolation. On six repositories nothing new was reported. Reported with the cause by @​abrahamguo. (#1239, #1251)

  • --dead-code reported constructors and dunder methods as unused members. constructor in JavaScript and __init__ or __repr__ in Python are called by the runtime, not by name, and the unused-member check didn't skip them. It does now. Reported by @​abrahamguo, fixed by @​sarankumar1325. (#1253, #1254)

  • --dead-code reported knip's knip.ts and knip.js as unused files. They are knip's config, but no rule knew them. The new knip framework entry keeps them as entry points, and knip shows up in the console's Frameworks: line. Reported with the fix by @​abrahamguo. (#1255, #1256)

  • The Linux binaries accepted certificates from the leaked emSign intermediate CAs. rustls-webpki moved to 0.103.16 and webpki-roots and webpki-root-certs to 1.0.10, so they reject them. This matters for --semantic-url with a remote API on Linux. Model downloads are pinned by SHA-256, and macOS and Windows use the system TLS stack. (RUSTSEC-2026-0381, 0382, 0383, #1236)

  • nix run github:kucherenko/jscpd didn't build. The flake built the dependencies without the workspace's paste shim and left out files that the crates include at compile time. It takes the whole rust/ folder now, and a new Nix workflow builds and runs the package on Linux and macOS. (#1272)

Other

  • The release pipeline asks npmmirror to sync every npm package after a release, because the mirror never copied jscpd-linux-x64-gnu@5.4.2, and pnpm installs from it lost the Linux binary without a warning. Reported by @​icret. (#1261, #1262)
  • The release pipeline waits up to 30 minutes for npm to serve a new version, and the release tag now points at the release commit. (#1232, #1250)
  • The Super Linter section of docs/ci-and-hooks.md shows where the config file goes and how to gate on new clones only, with Super Linter v9.0.0 or later. (#994)
  • The README's "Who Uses jscpd" lists 28 projects and the file in each one that runs jscpd. (#1287)

Dependencies

  • candle moved to 0.11.1 and zip to 9.3.0, which fixes RUSTSEC-2026-0429 and the three zip advisories that were ignored until now (#1278, #1279)
  • askama builds without its config feature, so the unmaintained basic-toml leaves the build (RUSTSEC-2026-0374, #1230)
  • oxc, ruff, tree-sitter 0.27.1, tree-sitter-scala 0.26.4, serde-saphyr 2.0.0, ureq 3.5.1, ignore 0.4.34, memmap2 0.9.12 and log 0.4.35 moved to newer releases

Thank You ❤️

  • @​abrahamguo for runJscpd() and for three dead-code reports that came with the cause and the fix (#1238, #1239, #1253, #1255)
  • @​sarankumar1325 for the Action version pin, the ignore markers and the dead-code member fix (#1249, #1254, #1258)
  • @​dannystaple, @​bauchdj, @​crystalfp and @​icret for the reports (#1240, #1257, #1263, #1261)

Published Packages

  • basta@0.3.3 on crates.io
  • cpd-core@0.1.23 on crates.io
  • cpd-finder@0.1.22 on crates.io
  • cpd-reporter@0.1.24 on crates.io

... (truncated)

Commits
  • b82d841 release: cpd-v5.4.3
  • 2dd58e0 test(npm): cover the launcher and runJscpd, give the no-binary error a code
  • 0daacf0 feat(npm): runJscpd runs the jscpd binary from Node.js

body:
Bumps [i18next-browser-languagedetector](https://github.com/i18next/i18next-browser-languageDetector) from 8.2.1 to 8.3.0.
Changelog

Sourced from i18next-browser-languagedetector's changelog.

8.3.0

  • security: a detected language must now have the shape i18next 26.7 accepts for a language code from outside (its isSafeLanguageCode): letters, digits, -, _, @ and . (no ..), at most 128 characters. It replaces the list of XSS patterns, which missed values like <b>x</b> or " onmouseover="x() from the query string, a cookie or storage, which then became the language; apps put it into <html lang="...">. Compatibility note: a value with other characters (spaces, slashes, quotes) is now skipped and the next detector is used; codes like en_US, zh_Hant_TW or sr@latin still pass, and i18next 27 refuses such codes from outside as well.

8.2.4

  • fix: lookupFromSubdomainIndex counts hostname labels again, so with 1, dev.en.example.com is detected as en. Since 6.1.5 the index picked a regex group instead, and any index other than 0 returned a part of the domain (en.exampl, example.com). Index 0 (the default) works as before. Thanks @​lprnmns 329

8.2.3

  • fix: the subdomain detector now detects language tags with script and region subtags, so pt-BR.site.com, zh-Hans-CN.site.com, es-419.site.com and sr-Latn.site.com are detected as pt-BR, zh-Hans-CN, es-419 and sr-Latn. The pattern only accepted 2 to 5 word characters, without hyphens. Release notes

Sourced from github/codeql-action/init's releases.

v4.39.3

  • Fixed diff-informed alert filtering incorrectly removing alerts in changed files whose paths contain spaces, special characters, or non-ASCII characters. #4283

v4.39.2

  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.27.4. #4284
  • Upcoming breaking change: CodeQL version 2.22.3 and earlier were discontinued on 16 October 2026 alongside GitHub Enterprise Server 3.18, and will be unsupported by the next minor release of the CodeQL Action. Added a deprecation warning for customers using these versions of CodeQL. #4266
  • Starting with macOS 27 and Xcode 27, traced analyses are unsupported. See this blog post for more information. The CodeQL Action will now try to identify if a workflow is about to perform a traced analysis on version 27 or above of macOS or Xcode.   • The undocumented TRAP cache cleanup feature that could be enabled using the CODEQL_ACTION_CLEANUP_TRAP_CACHES environment variable has been removed, as announced in the release notes for CodeQL Action 4.35.2. If you used TRAP cache cleanup to limit Actions cache usage, we recommend disabling TRAP caching by passing the trap-caching: false input to the init Action. #4243

  • Upcoming breaking change: CodeQL version 2.22.3 and earlier were discontinued on 16 October 2026 alongside GitHub Enterprise Server 3.18, and will be unsupported by the next minor release of the CodeQL Action. Added a deprecation warning for customers using these versions of CodeQL. #4266
  • Starting with macOS 27 and Xcode 27, traced analyses are unsupported. See this blog post for more information. The CodeQL Action will now try to identify if a workflow is about to perform a traced analysis on version 27 or above of macOS or Xcode.   • The undocumented TRAP cache cleanup feature that could be enabled using the CODEQL_ACTION_CLEANUP_TRAP_CACHES environment variable has been removed, as announced in the release notes for CodeQL Action 4.35.2. The analyze Action now warns if this environment variable is set. If you used TRAP cache cleanup to limit Actions cache usage, we recommend disabling TRAP caching by passing the trap-caching: false input to the init Action. #4243

4.39.1 - 21 Oct 2026

  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.27.3. #4256

4.39.0 - 15 Oct 2026

  • Breaking change: Bump the minimum required CodeQL bundle version to 2.20.7. #4205
  • The codeql-action/analyze step now validates that a correct argument for the checkout_path input has been provided. The checkout_path input must be set to the path where the repository that is being analyzed is checked out at on the runner, if that path is something other than the workspace root. If the path does not point to a repository checkout or is different from the path that was used by codeql-action/init, then the CodeQL Action now produces a warning. #4148
  • Resolved an issue with third-party caching implementations that prevented caches from being restored correctly. #4206

This primarily benefits customers who are using GitHub instances other than github.com where the codeql-action/start-proxy step may previously have been unable to locate recent releases and ended up using outdated versions of the private registry authentication proxy as a result. #4198

4.38.3 - 08 Oct 2026

  • Upcoming breaking change: CodeQL version 2.21.2 and earlier were discontinued on 24 September 2026 alongside GitHub Enterprise Server 3.17, and will be unsupported by the next minor release of the CodeQL Action. Added a deprecation warning for customers using these versions of CodeQL. #4188
  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.27.2. #4203
  • Fixed a bug where the decision of whether to use a per-language bundle did not account for custom configurations that reference queries outside of compiled CodeQL packs. 4.38.2 - 24 Sept 2026

  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.27.1. #4160

4.38.1 - 18 Sept 2026

  • The CodeQL Action now has experimental support for CodeQL releases for which per-language bundles are available. 4.38.0 - 09 Sept 2026

  • On GitHub-hosted runners, the CodeQL Action now deletes unused CodeQL bundles from the toolcache before downloading a different bundle, which frees up disk space for the analysis. We expect to roll this change out to everyone in September. #4124
  • The CodeQL Action now supports CodeQL releases that are compatible with Linux Arm64 and downloads the native linux-arm64 CodeQL bundle when available. #4072
  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.27.0. #4129

title: chore(deps)(deps): bump tailwindcss from 4.3.3 to 4.3.5 in /gitnexus-web
body:
Bumps [tailwindcss](https://github.com/tailwindlabs/tailwindcss/tree/HEAD/packages/tailwindcss) from 4.3.3 to 4.3.5.
Release notes

Sourced from tailwindcss's releases.

v4.3.5

Fixed

  • Canonicalization: improve performance in projects with many functional variant values (e.g. a matchVariant plugin with thousands of values) (#20663)
  • Don't crash or create a fallback with the wrong color for a color-mix(…) without a color interpolation method (e.g. color-mix(var(--color-red-500)) or color-mix(currentcolor 50%, transparent)) (#20658, #20666)
  • Ensure @tailwindcss/oxide-wasm32-wasi loads instead of hanging forever (e.g. with NAPI_RS_FORCE_WASI=error or in WebContainers) (#20667)
  • Remove as: '*.css' from the @tailwindcss/turbopack setup in its README, because it breaks CSS modules (#20660)
  • Ignore <!-- and --> between top-level rules in CSS instead of throwing or swallowing the next rule (e.g. a { color: red } --> b { color: blue }) (#20665)
  • Ensure @tailwindcss/oxide-wasm32-wasi detects changed and new source files after the first scan (e.g. in WebContainers) (#20487)
  • Prevent type errors with skipLibCheck: false caused by imports of unshipped modules in the @tailwindcss/node type declarations (#20632)

v4.3.4

Added

  • Add @tailwindcss/turbopack, a Turbopack loader for using Tailwind CSS with Next.js (#20367)

Fixed

  • Ensure watch mode detects changes to symlinked @source files whose real paths aren't otherwise scanned (#20356)
  • Ensure variants using @scope wrap generated utilities instead of nesting inside them (#20369)
  • Ensure nested @scope rules preserve their scoping semantics when flattened (#20369)
  • Preserve declarations directly inside @scope by wrapping them in :where(:scope) (#20369)
  • Ensure generated utilities include a space in empty var() fallbacks (e.g. var(--tw-blur,) → var(--tw-blur, )) (#20373)
  • Canonicalization: convert arbitrary breakpoint and container query variants to named equivalents (e.g. max-[64rem]:flex → max-lg:flex) (#20380)
  • Prevent @tailwindcss/vite from crashing on every edit under Vite's experimental bundledDev mode (#20379)
  • Ensure @tailwindcss/oxide falls back to WASM on platforms without native bindings (@tailwindcss/oxide-wasm32-wasi now installs on all platforms, but only loads when no native binding is available) (#20383)

title: fix(setup): quote the Windows codex command line
body:
## Summary

On Windows, `gitnexus setup` registered a broken Codex MCP server when the global `gitnexus.cmd` lives under a path with a space. This builds the `codex` command line with `composeWin32Command`, the same quoting the npm spawns in `update` and `runtime-install` already use.

## Motivation / context

`setupCodex` called `execFile('codex', [...args], { shell: true })` on Windows. With `shell: true`, Node only joins the args with spaces, so `C:\Program Files\nodejs\gitnexus.cmd` reached codex as `C:\Program` and `Files\nodejs\gitnexus.cmd`. Setup still printed "+ Codex", but the server could not start. Recorded with a stand-in `codex.cmd` in a folder named `fake bin`:

```
before: ["mcp","add","gitnexus","--","C:\\...\\fake","bin\\gitnexus.cmd","mcp"]
after:  ["mcp","add","gitnexus","--","C:\\...\\fake bin\\gitnexus.cmd","mcp"]
```

The same pattern made Node 24 print `DEP0190` on every `npx gitnexus analyze` on Windows (from the `npm --version` probe), and in `codex mcp remove`. Those two now pass a single command string as well.

## Areas touched

- [x] `gitnexus/` (CLI / core / MCP server)

## Scope & constraints

**In scope**
- `setup.ts` codex add, `uninstall.ts` codex remove, `resolve-invocation.ts` npm probe (Windows only; POSIX calls are unchanged).

**Explicitly out of scope / not done here**
- `hooks/claude/resolve-analyze-cmd.cjs` (probe and the `run.cjs` runner) has the same shell + args pattern, so a spaced argument like `--repo "C:\Users\Jane Doe\proj"` is split there too. Left alone because #3879 rewrites that file.

## Testing & verification

- [x] `npx vitest run test/unit/setup-codex.test.ts test/unit/resolve-invocation.test.ts test/unit/uninstall.test.ts`: the new and updated tests fail on `main` (6 failed) and pass here (119 passed, 1 skipped)
- [x] `cd gitnexus && npx tsc --noEmit`

Windows-only change to how three child processes are spawned. No index refresh needed.

title: fix(bench): isolate parse-cache benchmark phases
body:
## Summary

The linked [PR job](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/actions/runs/43099166675/job/131040212546?pr=3871) and [main job](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/actions/runs/43026424335/job/130552016981) failed the parse-cache RSS gate. Graph verification retained large serialized source copies, and later measurements remained unstable even between identical compiled runtimes.

Only repository files and the disk cache persist between phases. Timing covers ingestion and cache publication; peak RSS is the largest phase-process high-water mark, including parser workers.

├── benchmark.js    # measurement, graph checks, paired comparison
└── baseline.json   # reviewed limits and historical measurements

title: Claude hook: registry lookup prefers the main checkout's index over a registered linked worktree when the main path is longer
body:
## Summary

`findRegisteredRepo` in `gitnexus/hooks/claude/registry-query.cjs` picks the matching registry entry with the **longest registered path**. For a linked worktree, `registryPathsForCwd` also adds the main checkout (the parent of `--git-common-dir`) to `repoPaths`. When both the worktree and the main checkout are registered, the main checkout wins whenever its absolute path is longer than the worktree's. The hook then augments searches from the worktree with the main checkout's index, which may be on a different branch.

## Where

`gitnexus/hooks/claude/registry-query.cjs` on `main` (lines 404–431), and the same code in the 1.6.12 release:

```js
if (registeredPath.length > bestLen) {
  bestLen = registeredPath.length;
  best = { ... };
}
```

`repoPaths` is built as: ancestors of cwd up to `--show-toplevel`, then the worktree root, then (for linked worktrees) the common-dir parent.

## Reproduce

1. Register a repo at a long path, for example `/home/me/src/projects/some-repo`, and analyze it.
2. `git worktree add /tmp/wt feature-x`, then analyze and register `/tmp/wt`.
3. From `/tmp/wt`, run a hook-augmented search.

Expected: the `/tmp/wt` index is used.
Actual: `/home/me/src/projects/some-repo` is used, because it is the longer of the two matching paths.

The order is correct only when the worktree happens to sit under a longer path, such as a worktree nested inside the main checkout.

## Suggested fix

Rank candidates by their position in `repoPaths`, which is already ordered from nearest to furthest, rather than by string length. Keep longest-match only among the in-worktree ancestors, where it is used to support `--skip-git` subdirectory indexes. The common-dir parent should be used only when nothing inside the worktree matched.

Found by code review of the vendored 1.6.12 hook. I have not run the reproduction end to end.

title: evidence-provenance.mjs rejects valid branch names (e.g. `feature/c++`, `fix/@scope`) as "Invalid symbolic HEAD ref"
body:
## Summary

`captureHeadGuards` in `evidence-provenance.mjs` (used by the `gitnexus-plan` and `gitnexus-work` skills) checks the symbolic HEAD ref against a character whitelist:

```js
if (!/^refs\/[A-Za-z0-9._\/-]+$/.test(ref) || ref.includes('..')) {
  throw new Error(`Invalid symbolic HEAD ref: ${ref}`);
}
```

Git allows many more characters in ref names than this whitelist does, including `+`, `@` (except in `@{`), `#`, `,`, `=` and non-ASCII letters. On a branch such as `feature/c++`, the script throws and evidence capture fails, even though the branch is valid and has already been resolved by `git symbolic-ref`.

## Where

On `main` this is line 958 in all six copies:

- `gitnexus/skills/gitnexus-{plan,work}/scripts/evidence-provenance.mjs`
- `.claude/skills/gitnexus-{plan,work}/scripts/evidence-provenance.mjs`
- `gitnexus-claude-plugin/skills/gitnexus-{plan,work}/scripts/evidence-provenance.mjs`

## Reproduce

```sh
git switch -c 'feature/c++'
# any evidence-provenance.mjs run that reaches captureHeadGuards
```

Expected from reading the code: `Error: Invalid symbolic HEAD ref: refs/heads/feature/c++`.

## Suggested fix

The check is there to keep `ref` from escaping the git dir when it is joined into an administrative path. That containment is a path concern, not a character-set concern. Two options:

- Validate with `git check-ref-format "$ref"`, which applies Git's own rules and already rejects `..`, a leading `/`, control characters and so on. Keep the explicit `..` check as a second layer.
- Or keep a deny-list (`..`, `\0`, a leading `/`, backslash, any segment equal to `.` or `..`) and rely on `resolveAdministrativePath` to confirm that the resolved path stays under the git dir.

Found by code review of the vendored 1.6.12 skills. The six copies are byte-identical to `main` today.

title: Claude/Antigravity PostToolUse stale-index hint misses git commands with global options (`git -c … commit`, `git -C dir commit`)
body:
## Summary

The PostToolUse handler decides whether a Bash command mutated the repo with this regex:

```js
/\bgit\s+(commit|merge|rebase|cherry-pick|pull)(\s|$)/
```

It requires the subcommand to come right after `git`. Commands with global options do not match, so no stale-index hint is shown after them. Examples:

- `git -c user.name=x commit -m msg`
- `git -C ../other commit -am msg`
- `git --no-pager pull`

Agents use `git -c` and `git -C` often, for example to set an identity per commit or to work in a worktree without `cd`.

## Where

On `main`:

- `gitnexus/hooks/claude/claude-hook-runtime.cjs:429`
- `gitnexus/hooks/antigravity/gitnexus-antigravity-hook.cjs:299`

The OpenCode adapter already gets this right. `isGitMutationCommand` in `gitnexus/hooks/opencode/gitnexus-plugin.js` tokenizes the command, skips `GIT_SWITCHES` and `GIT_OPTIONS_WITH_VALUES` (including `-C`/`-c`), and checks the first real subcommand. It also splits compound commands (`a && git commit`).

## Suggested fix

Move `isGitMutationCommand` (with `splitShellCommands` and `tokenizeArgv`) into a shared helper and use it in the Claude and Antigravity adapters as well, so all three adapters agree.

Found while testing the vendored 1.6.12 hook: a `git -c … commit` did not trigger the hint, and a plain `git commit` did.

title: 1.6.13-rc.219: analyze hangs forever in COPY phase — LadybugDB 0.22.0 PrimaryKeyIndex deadlock (NodeBatchInsert, all workers wait on shared_mutex)
body:
## Summary

On `1.6.13-rc.219`, `gitnexus analyze --force` on a large mixed Swift/Objective-C iOS repo hangs forever during the DB write (COPY) phase. The process stays alive at 0% CPU and nothing progresses. It reproduced 2/2 runs at the same point.

The good news first: the parse/graph phase now finishes in about 2 minutes under a ~6 GB heap. On 1.6.12 the same repo OOMs at 28 GB (#3355), so #3387 does fix the memory blow-up. The rc can't produce an index for this repo, though, because of the hang below.

## Environment

- gitnexus `1.6.13-rc.219` (npm `rc` tag), bundled `@ladybugdb/core` **0.22.0** (1.6.12 ships 0.18.3)
- macOS 26.6.2, arm64 (10 cores, 32 GB), Node v25.9.0
- Repo: private iOS app, ~12.5k tracked files (~2.6k `.swift`, ~0.9k `.m/.h/.mm`), Xcode project without SPM targets. It has a `.gitnexusignore`.

## Command

```
GITNEXUS_STORAGE_ROOT=<tmp>/idx GITNEXUS_LBUG_BUFFER_POOL_SIZE=8589934592 \
  gitnexus analyze --force --index-only --skip-git <repo>
```

## What happens

1. Parse and resolution complete. `graph_reference_integrity` logs `checkedSites: 96993, unverifiedEdges: 22401`.
2. COPY starts. There are a few non-fatal `Copy exception: Unable to find primary key value Class:objc:class:UIImage` / `File:<vendored header>.h` warnings (21 in total), and the fallback path continues.
3. After the last logged copy (`COPY CodeRelation FROM ".../graph-csv/rel_File_File.csv"`), the log stops. 15+ minutes later the process is still alive at 0% CPU, `graph-csv/` is empty, and the `lbug.staging.*` file (~420 MB) is no longer modified.

## Where it is stuck (macOS `sample`)

All 9 LadybugDB TaskScheduler worker threads are blocked on the same shared mutex inside the primary-key hash index during `NodeBatchInsert`:

```
lbug::common::TaskScheduler::runWorkerThread()
 lbug::processor::ProcessorTask::run()
  lbug::processor::NodeBatchInsert::executeInternal(ExecutionContext*)
   ...IndexBuilderGlobalQueues::maybeConsumeIndex(...)
    lbug::storage::PrimaryKeyIndex::appendWithIndexPosNoLock<std::string>(...)
     lbug::storage::HashIndex<string_t>::lookupInternal(...)
      lbug::storage::HashIndexLocalStorage<string_t>::lookup(...)
       std::__shared_mutex_base::lock_shared()
        std::condition_variable::wait(...)
```

Other threads are in `IndexBuilder::finishedProducing(...)` or idle in libuv. Nothing holds CPU, so it looks like a lock-order deadlock between `finishedProducing` and `lookup` on the local hash-index storage, not slow I/O.

An analyze child that outlived Ctrl+C on the parent also stayed in this state indefinitely.

## Notes

- This looks new with the `@ladybugdb/core` 0.18.3 → 0.22.0 bump. 1.6.12 never reaches this point on this repo because it OOMs first, so I can't A/B the same graph on 0.18.3.
- I'm happy to provide the full `sample` output or run a debug build or env flag. The repo is private, so I can't share the source.

title: Claude Code hook runs a graph query when grep is only a filter in a Bash command
body:
## What happens

The Claude Code PreToolUse hook (`gitnexus-hook.cjs`) runs a graph query when `grep` is used only as a filter inside a longer Bash command. The query uses an unrelated word as the search pattern, and the hook then adds unrelated symbols to Claude's context.

Example command:

```sh
sed -i '' 's/old text/new text/' notes.md && grep -c 'direct `tool' notes.md
```

The hook took `direct` as the pattern and returned three unrelated C# test methods as "related symbols". The command was a file edit with a match count afterwards, not a code search.

## Cause

In `extractPattern()`, the Bash branch:

1. matches `/\brg\b|\bgrep\b/` anywhere in the command, and
2. takes the first non-flag token after the first `grep`/`rg` token.

So `grep` after `&&`, `;` or `|` is treated as a code search, and so is `grep` that reads stdin.

## Cost

These are Claude Code transcript timings for this hook (`PreToolUse:Bash`) across 50 sessions: 25 recorded runs, median 1826 ms, max 8277 ms. Each run blocks the Bash call it is attached to.

## Suggested fix

Extract a pattern only when `grep`/`rg` is the first command of the line. Alternatively, skip any `grep`/`rg` that comes after `|`, because it reads stdin and is not a search of the repository.

## Environment

- gitnexus 1.6.12 (global npm install), hook installed by the gitnexus setup
- Claude Code 2.1.322, macOS
- Hook matcher `Grep|Glob|Bash`

title: fix(ci): stabilize release validation
body:
## Summary

Restore release validation by fixing a fan-out timeout race, pinning the host inputs of mocked CLI tests, and isolating benchmark samples with deterministic V8 scheduling.

```text
CLI test admission → explicit hardware fixture → real admission policy
neighbor timeout → latch timeout → no further graph fan-out
benchmark arm → fresh process → local warmups → timed work → unchanged gates
```

## Motivation / context

[Main CI](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/actions/runs/43242377740) rejected mocked CLI tests before their intended behavior ran because live heap/RSS readings exceeded the admission budget. The [PR run](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/actions/runs/43272053307) then exposed a real timeout race and rejected byte-identical runtime builds in both performance comparisons.

## Areas touched

- [x] `gitnexus/` — group impact, tests, benchmark tooling.

## Scope & constraints

The timeout fix treats a fired neighbor timer as final, even when the wall clock has not reached the deadline. Manifest-only crossings retain their existing behavior. A controlled-clock test reproduces the extra neighbor call on the old code and asserts the exact call list after the fix.

Mocked CLI tests receive explicit hardware readings; the production resource policy still runs. The real analyzer-identity child gets a bounded heap. Positive and negative admission tests prove the fixture cannot bypass the policy.

Both benchmark arms use fresh processes and `--predictable` alongside the existing GC profile. This controls background GC/JIT scheduling and seeds; collection and compilation during the operation remain timed. Matching parse-cache phases run consecutively, with the first arm alternating between pairs, so measurements are no longer separated by a whole trial. Parse-cache report schema 5 records and validates the execution flags and actual phase order. Historical reference timings are not rewritten. End-to-end indexing still runs its existing fresh/persistent process profiles.

No thresholds, confidence bounds, measured sample counts, coverage floors, CI gates, or existing assertions are removed or relaxed. All assertions introduced by this PR use exact outcomes or values; no greater-than/less-than matchers were added.

## Evidence

| Check | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| CI-sized host preload | 76 CLI failures | 434 tests pass in 31 files |
| Clock trails a fired neighbor timer | Incorrectly calls the second neighbor | Exact one-neighbor call list |
| Same code, 720 MB cache, six samples | Wall-time coefficient of variation 9.0% | 2.4% with deterministic scheduling |
| Same code, 250 MB real cache, full interning harness | Hosted gate rejected identical modules | All three gates pass; paired changes +0.6%, +0.6%, +0.4% |

## Testing & verification

- Earlier group validation: 1,372 tests pass across 66 files.
- 65 focused benchmark, timeout and group integration tests pass across seven files.
- Earlier focused CLI coverage: 489 tests pass across 33 files; analyzer-identity and interning tests: 39 pass across four files.
- Full local suite at `40926cadb` completed: 33,011 passed, four setup failures, 104 existing skips. The four failures came from inherited `CODEX_HOME`; both affected files pass all 73 tests with that variable removed from the test process. A completely green full local run is not claimed.
- `npx tsc --noEmit` and `npm run typecheck:tests` pass.
- ESLint, Prettier and `git diff --check` checked before commit.
- Hosted CI and the seven-pair real-source parse-cache comparison are pending for `eb42aa5ed`. The intermediate whole-trial A/A run was stopped after two measured pairs still showed substantial variation; it is not passing evidence for the final harness.

Focused command:
`env -u CODEX_HOME npm test -- test/unit/cache-interning-isolation.test.ts test/unit/cache-interning-benchmark.test.ts test/unit/cache-interning-corpus.test.ts test/unit/parse-cache-benchmark-gates.test.ts test/unit/group/cross-impact-fanout-cap.test.ts test/integration/group/group-impact.test.ts test/integration/group/manifest-synthetic-impact-lbug.test.ts --maxWorkers=2`

Graph analysis was refreshed and rerun. Its incomplete caller mapping and unmapped test edits remain **partial / unknown**, so direct caller searches and diff review supplement it; this PR does not claim a clean graph-analysis result.

## Risk & rollout

**Door:** two-way; revert these commits to roll back.

**Blast radius:** cross-repository impact timeout handling, test inputs and benchmark measurement. The benchmark execution profile changes, so timings are comparable only between arms measured under the same profile. Production admission policy and release workflows are unchanged. title: fix(scope-resolution): stop the receiver type walk at the nearest lexical binder, typed or not (DART-11)
body:
## What

DART-11 from `docs/languages/dart-ingestion-gaps.md`: a closure or local function that rebinds a name climbed to the enclosing binding of that name, and emitted a CALLS edge for a call the source never makes.

```dart
void f(Address cs, List<dynamic> items) {
  items.forEach((cs) {   // the closure's own, untyped `cs`
    cs.save();           // main: f -> Address.save   (WRONG)
  });
  cs.save();             // f -> Address.save          (right)
}
```

The rule: the receiver type walk stops at the NEAREST scope that binds the receiver name, typed or not. A typed binder answers with its type, an untyped one stops the walk with no type, and the namespace and workspace fallbacks are skipped.

The shared half of that rule was already on main: `lookupLexicalName` (`gitnexus-shared/src/scope-resolution/name-claims.ts`) treats `Scope.lexicalNames` as ownership. Both receiver walks read it: `findReceiverTypeBinding` and the registry twin `lookupReceiverType` go through it. Dart never fed it. Inline closures and local functions had no scope at all, so their body sat in the enclosing function's scope, and no Dart Function scope published the names it binds.

## Commits

1. `fix(scope-resolution): record why a receiver walk stopped at an untyped binder; PHP name fallback respects the stop` (language-free, plus PHP)
   - `findUntypedReceiverBinder` (walkers) names the scope that stopped the walk only because it lists the name in `lexicalNames` with no type fact. That excludes a value binding, an import, and names decided by name claims.
   - `emitReceiverBoundCalls`: a bare receiver that falls through every case at such a binder records `suppressed` / `receiver-type-unresolved` with `declineDetail: 'untyped-binder'` and `binderScopeId`. This is diagnostic only. `summarizeUnresolvedReceivers` does not count it, so the persisted unresolved-receiver artifact is unchanged.
   - `phpEmitUnresolvedReceiverEdges` no longer turns "no type" into a 0.6 unique-method guess when the walk stopped at an untyped binder. After the merge it checks both #3877's owner mask and this stop, in that order. PHP publishes no lexical names today, so no PHP edge moves; a unit test drives the emitter with a hand-built scope that does.
2. `fix(dart): closures and local functions own their binders; the receiver walk stops at them (DART-11)`
   - Every Dart Function scope carries `@scope.lexical-names`: parameters, locals, catch, loop and pattern variables, with the binder forms taken from `visitDartBinderName`. Nested closures are not descended into.
   - Inline closures (`function_expression`) and local functions (`local_function_declaration > lambda_expression`) get a Function scope of their own. It owns no definition, so calls inside it stay attributed to the enclosing callable.
   - Typed parameters of closures (inline or bound to a name) and of local functions bind inside that scope, so `(Other cs) { cs.save(); }` reaches `Other.save`. On main it reached `Address.save`.
3. Merge of main (#3871, #3876, #3877). Conflicts and the two semantic follow-ups are listed in the merge commit; see "Merge with main" below.
4. `bench(scope-capture): re-measure the Dart fingerprint on the merged tree`.
5. `perf(dart): collect lexical names in Pass B's one walk; emit no scope for a closure that binds nothing`.
   - Pass B's tree walk carries the body that owns each node, so filing a binder is a map lookup. A closure or local function that binds nothing (`setState(() { … })`) gets no scope, the same filter the JS/TS block scopes use.
   - `DART_BINDER_NODE_TYPES` gates `visitDartBinderName`, so the binder list stays one list for the field mask, the inference census, and lexical names.
   - Captures are byte-identical to commit 2 on 56 sources: every Dart fixture, the bench synthetic unit, a closure-heavy synthetic, and the pin fixtures.
6. `fix(dart): only declarations become lexical names; statements, closures and catch bodies scope their own binders (DART-11 review)`. See "Review round 1" below.
7. `bench(scope-capture): re-measure the Dart fingerprint after the DART-11 review fixes`.
