## Recall note

- A name belongs to the nearest scope that declares it: a closure or local function, a nested block, a `for`, a switch case, an if-case, or the body a catch clause guards. A loop, catch or block-local variable therefore stops reads only inside its statement.
- Only declarations count. Matching constants, field labels and pattern assignments declare nothing, and `_` declares nothing.
- Remaining over-approximation:
  - Within one scope the walk is position-insensitive.
  - A function's parameters share its top-level body scope, so a local function or top-level local named like a typed parameter of the same function does not hide it.
  - Collection `for` elements bind into the enclosing scope.
- A binder with no type fact stops the walk with no type. That covers `dynamic` and a container type Dart drops (`List<dynamic> items`).
- Measured cost on the full fixture corpus: zero edges (A/B below and in "Review round 1"). The review's shapes are pinned both ways.

title: fix(dart): accessors and comment-separated signatures open their own Function scope; withhold accessor return bindings (DART-10)
body:
**Stacked on #3903 (DART-11).** This branch merges `fix/receiver-walk-stops-at-untyped-binder` at `cf0a24666` (merge commit `5f36a6cd6`). Merge #3903 first; this diff then reduces to the DART-10 changes.

## What

Gap DART-10 in `docs/languages/dart-ingestion-gaps.md`. Dart's `function_signature` and `function_body` are siblings, so the emitter builds a Function scope from the pair. Two shapes never got one:

- **Getters and setters.** A top-level `getter_signature` / `setter_signature` was not captured at all, and a member accessor went through the field path. Their parameters bound nothing. Their locals landed in the enclosing Module / Class scope, so `User get topGetter { final v = User(); … }` typed `void reader() { v.save(); }` as `User.save` beside an untyped `var v;`: a wrong edge.
- **A comment between a signature and its body.** tree-sitter keeps a comment (`comment` or `documentation_comment`) as a named sibling, so `findFunctionBody` stopped one node early and `void commented(User v) /* note */ { v.save(); }` opened no scope.

## Shapes

1. **Accessor scopes.** `query.ts` gives top-level and member getters / setters a private `@dart.accessor` capture.
   - `captures.ts` routes it through the function-scope path: `@scope.function`, the `this` and parameter bindings, and DART-11's lexical names.
   - The declaration stays a Property, and its **name** still binds on the enclosing Class / Module scope (`dartBindingScopeFor` hoists it). A bare `cs` read in a sibling member therefore stops at `this.cs`.
   - A field never carries the capture, and a static accessor binds no `this`.
2. **Comment skip.** Three walks skip both comment kinds and nothing else:
   - `findFunctionBody` (forward), so a bodiless signature followed by a comment never takes the next member's body;
   - DART-11's parameter-owner walk (`nextDartNonCommentSibling`), so a `///`-separated signature's parameters still belong to its body;
   - `signatureBefore` (backward), used by the binder census and the field-shadow set.

   The census also reads a top-level setter's parameter.
3. **Accessor return bindings are withheld.** `dartBindingScopeFor` hoists every return binding to the Module scope. Before this change accessors published nothing, so withholding is parity with `main`. Publishing them on the Class scope is now feasible behind DART-11 and is a follow-up for recall.
4. **A parameter is withheld only when its own scope redeclares it** (`dartParameterRedeclared`).
   - Parameter bindings are published after Pass B, once each scope's declarations are counted with DART-11's declaration reader.
   - A binder in a closure, local function, nested block, loop, case or catch body belongs to that scope and leaves the annotation alone.
   - Pattern field labels, a function-typed parameter's own parameters, pattern assignments and plain assignments declare nothing.
   - A withheld name stays the scope's untyped lexical binder, so the receiver walk stops there (`receiver-type-unresolved`) instead of reaching a same-named binding further out.
   - In valid Dart the same-scope case is a collection `for` element.
5. **Field-shadow mask behind a comment.** `collectDartBodyShadows` reads the signature through `signatureBefore`.

All changes are in `languages/dart/`, plus one #3903 unit-test expectation (below); shared ingestion code is untouched. The pins are `dart-scope-openers.test.ts` (14 tests) and `test/fixtures/lang-resolution/dart-scope-openers/`, which holds `main`, `models`, `getters`, `shadow`, `nested_rebinding`, `accessor_names` and `declares_nothing` (all valid Dart).

## Review round 1 — final status on the stacked tree

| Finding | Status |
| --- | --- |
| H1 (P1): a withheld annotation re-pointed the edge | **Fixed, recall restored.** Withholding is per scope now. Your trigger gives `f -> Address.save` again and the closure's own `cs` stops at the closure. `nested_rebinding.dart` keeps `Address.save` for the for-in, catch and enum-method shapes beside `Other ds()`, `Depot.es()` and `Kind.depot`. The one same-scope case (a collection `for`) ends as `receiver-type-unresolved` at both sites, never `Other.save` and never a wrong `Address.save`. |
| H1b: the census counted non-binders | **Fixed.** Counts come from DART-11's declaration reader. `declares_nothing.dart` keeps `Address.save` for a function-typed parameter, an object label, a record label and a pattern assignment beside `Maker.x()`. |
| H2 (P1): an accessor name bound in its own scope | **Fixed** by the `dartBindingScopeFor` hoist (`accessor_names.dart`). |
| The `main.dart:26` guard could not fail | **Fixed.** `Factory.cs()` is the adversary; `moduleVarRebound -> Address.save` is the pinned outcome. |
| `documentation_comment` | **Fixed** in all three walks. |
| Gap doc | **Updated** for the stacked model, with two recall boundaries. |
| Fixture validity | **Fixed**; the remaining recall gaps are labelled. |

One DART-11 pin moved: `a closure carries its own this only where no enclosing scope binds it`. An accessor body now binds `this` itself, so the case is pinned under an operator, which still opens no scope, and the getter variant asserts the getter's own binding.

## Effect on edges (post-merge A/B)

Each arm used its own `dist` and this branch's corpus, with 0 pipeline errors. Every CALLS / ACCESSES edge, every suppressed outcome and every per-directory node / relationship count was compared.

title: fix(ruby): a block parameter stops the receiver type walk — it no longer takes a same-named outer local's type (RUBY-03)
body:
## Summary

Ruby parameter scopes now stop type lookup at the parameter that owns the name. An untyped block, lambda/proc, or method parameter no longer inherits an unrelated outer type. YARD types remain available beside those scopes.

```ruby
# @param user [User]
def run(user, target)
  ->(user, x = user.save) {} # lambda parameter: unresolved
  user.save                 # outer parameter: User#save
  items.each do |target|
    target                  # local read
    target(1)               # Host#target, arity preserved
  end
end
```

The Ruby provider emits lexical names for parameter scopes and separate scopes for lambda defaults, respecting declaration order. Explicit calls that cross a parameter claim dispatch through `self`; callable-local forms `.call` and `.()` keep their invocation facts. Cached parameter sets avoid repeated linear name scans, and each default scope lists only the parameter names its expression references.

Regression tests require exact owners and call sites, including decoy owners, lambda/proc forms, earlier/later/current parameters, destructuring, splats, keywords, and an unshadowed outer read. The Ruby ingestion gap documentation reflects the corrected behavior.

## Evidence

- **Before the review fixes:** the lambda-default probe emitted no outer YARD binding or default lexical stop, and the three explicit calls emitted no self-call captures.
  **After:** one outer binding, one default stop, and all three self-call captures.
- Resolver and scope suites: **8,604 passed, 16 skipped**. Final focused Ruby suite: **165 passed**.
- The full run finished with 33,696 passed, 104 skipped, and 26 initial failures. Final Ruby, logger, and setup validation passed all 272 tests. Targeted reruns cleared the build-overlap, log-level, and inherited CODEX_HOME failures; the identical auto-sync suite passed outside /tmp. The external clone-engine version check still fails on the untouched PR baseline: installed jscpd 5.4.2 versus expected 5.4.3.

- The updated Ruby parameter benchmark passed, including its 16× sibling-block gate and fixed-width nested inputs. All 17 language capture fingerprints matched. Ruby capture scaling was **1.173**; a Go timing check failed under concurrent load and passed its isolated rerun at **1.032**.

The new [scaling benchmark](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/blob/ff4a22bfb306d39242ee24f14d0c0bc692fd509b/gitnexus/bench/ruby-block-param-stop/README.md) passed twice. Release notes

Sourced from @​hono/node-server's releases.

v2.1.8

What's Changed

  • fix(request): forward duplex to the native request in honojs/node-server#409
  • fix(utils): do not chain a promise per chunk while streaming a response in honojs/node-server#417
  • fix(listener): cancel the response body when the client has already disconnected in honojs/node-server#412
  • fix(utils): cancel late HTTP/2 response bodies in honojs/node-server#419
  • fix(listener): do not send a complete response when the body fails during the early read in honojs/node-server#420

Full Changelog: https://github.com/honojs/node-server/compare/v2.1.7...v2.1.8

v2.1.7

Security fixes

This release includes a fix for the following security issue:

serveStatic with allowPercentInPath still allows the double-decode middleware bypass

Affects: serveStatic with allowPercentInPath: true. The fix for GHSA-rmxm-3fg6-px4f rejects a path containing %, but the allowPercentInPath option skipped that check entirely. A malformed percent sequence such as /static/%%36%31dmin/secret.txt was routed as /static/%61dmin/secret.txt, so middleware on /static/admin/* did not run, and serveStatic then decoded %61 to a and served static/admin/secret.txt. The default configuration was already fixed in 2.1.3. GHSA-fj57-4f93-cfw6

serveStatic now accepts the second decode only when its result equals the routed path with %25 replaced by %. File names containing a literal %, requested as %25, are served as before.

The same fix ships in hono v4.13.18 (GHSA-74fm-fwc7-3fwp).

Full Changelog: https://github.com/honojs/node-server/compare/v2.1.6...v2.1.7

v2.1.6

Security fixes

This release includes fixes for the following security issues:

Backslash in the request path is parsed as a path separator, bypassing path-based access control at a reverse proxy

Affects: all requests. The raw request-target was passed to the WHATWG URL parser, which treats a backslash in the path as / and resolves .. segments, so /admin\secret reached the application as /admin/secret. A reverse proxy that forwards the backslash unchanged applied its path-based rules to the original path. GHSA-jpvv-r467-5p4w

A request whose path contains a raw backslash is now rejected with 400 Bad Request, for HTTP/1.1, HTTP/2 and WebSocket upgrades. A percent-encoded backslash (%5C) and a backslash in the query string are still accepted.

WebSocket upgrade request-target starting with // replaces the host in c.req.url, bypassing Origin checks

Affects: upgradeWebSocket. The URL of an upgrade request was built by resolving the request-target against the Host header, so a request-target such as //attacker.example/ws set the host of c.req.url to a client-chosen value while routing still saw /ws. An application that compared Origin with the origin of c.req.url could be bypassed by a page on another site. GHSA-7v5p-43qr-wch5

The host of upgrade requests now comes from the Host header, as for ordinary requests.

Unhandled ECONNRESET on the socket during an asynchronous WebSocket upgrade crashes the process

Affects: upgradeWebSocket. While the application handled an upgrade request, the socket had no error listener. A client that reset the connection during asynchronous middleware caused an unhandled 'error' event and terminated the process. GHSA-qv5m-9pm6-hqp3

Error and close events on the socket are now handled while the application runs, and a pending upgrade is released when the socket closes.

title: test(analyze): pin host RAM in analyzeCommand unit tests
body:
## What

The `analyzeCommand` unit tests now pass or fail the same way on any host, whatever RAM it reports. Only test files change. The admission check itself is not touched.

## Why: CI runners with 15700 MiB refuse the mocked analysis

Since #3829 (cc6225d2c), `analyzeCommand` calls `resolveHostAnalysisResources` before it reaches `runFullAnalysis`. That admission check reads the real host:

- effective RAM: `os.totalmem()`, or a smaller cgroup limit;
- the main heap. `vitest.config.ts` sets `GITNEXUS_MEMORY=off`, so analyze treats the heap as manual and charges the test fork's own V8 heap limit;
- the supervisor reservation, which is the fork's RSS.

A GitHub runner that reports 15700 MiB gets a budget of 11775 MiB. The check needs 11787 MiB, so it refuses by 12 MiB:

```
Resource budget 11775 MiB cannot admit parser/model work; requires at least 11787 MiB for these allocations.
```

Analyze then exits 1 before the mocked pipeline runs. Every test that expects `runFullAnalysis` to be called, or expects an error routed out of it, fails. Which file fails depends on which coverage shard lands on such a runner:

| run | PR | job | failing `analyzeCommand` files |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [43242448204](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/actions/runs/43242448204) | #3877 | coverage 7/8 | `analyze-worker-timeout` |
| [43294464967](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/actions/runs/43294464967) (attempt 1) | #3882 | coverage 8/8 | `analyze-lbug-checkpoint-threshold`, `analyze-phase-handoff`, `analyze-undeclared-pair-error`, `analyze-wipe-error` |
| [43338834204](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/actions/runs/43338834204) | #3906 | coverage 6/8 | `analyze-gitnexusrc`, `analyze-local-embedding-error`, `analyze-self-commit-bridge` |
| [43360437693](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/actions/runs/43360437693) | #3882 | coverage 2/8 | `analyze-http-endpoint-error`, `analyze-self-commit-bridge` |
| [43360657466](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/actions/runs/43360657466) | #3903 | coverage 8/8 | `analyze-embeddings-limit` |

That is five runs on four PRs since 2026-11-12, found by searching every failed coverage job of every CI run since that date, earlier attempts included. Each of these job logs prints the same `11775` / `11787` line. None of these PRs touched analyze.

## How

`test/helpers/admitted-host-memory.ts` is a `vi.mock` factory for `src/core/ingestion/utils/effective-ram.js`. It keeps the real module and pins only `effectiveRamBytes()` to 64 GiB. Each affected test file adds one hoisted mock:

```ts
vi.mock('../../src/core/ingestion/utils/effective-ram.js', async (importOriginal) =>
  (await import('../helpers/admitted-host-memory.js')).withAdmittedHostMemory(importOriginal),
);
```

- **The real admission policy still runs.** It reads the fork's real heap limit and RSS. Only the RAM figure is fixed. The same seam already exists in `analyze-worker-pool-size.test.ts`, which pins 32 GiB inline.
- **The heap re-exec cap is unchanged.** `HEAP_MB` in `cli/analyze.ts` reads `os.totalmem()` directly, not through this module.

A `--require` preload makes `os.totalmem()` return a fixed size:

```js

const mib = Number(process.env.FAKE_TOTALMEM_MIB);
if (mib > 0) os.totalmem = () => mib * 1024 * 1024;
```

The fork heap is pinned with `--max-old-space-size=3952`, which gives a `heap_size_limit` of 4144 MiB, the runner's value. Command:


For "without this change", the test edits were stashed, the replay was run, and the stash was restored. A checksum of the diff confirmed the restore was byte-identical.

title: refactor(scope-resolution): put import visibility behind one interface
body:
## What this changes

`ScopeResolutionIndexes.imports` was a public map of edge arrays, so every reader depended on finalize storing one edge per imported file. It is now an `ImportVisibility`: the only way to ask what a scope imports, with one operation per question a reader has.

| Operation | Question |
| --- | --- |
| `edgesAt(scope)` | Which imports can I select here by name, definition or kind? |
| `reaches(scope, file)` / `reachesDirectory(scope, dir)` | Does this scope import that file, or any file of that directory? |
| `membership(scope)` | The same question, asked many times at one scope |
| `forEachTarget(scope, visit)` | Every imported file in statement order, with the edge describing how it is imported |
| `scopes()` | Every scope finalize recorded |

`createEagerImportVisibility` implements it over the edge map finalize already produces. Storage is unchanged in this PR.

This is the prerequisite for the import-group memory work in #3695. It carries no memory optimization itself.

## Why

Finalize creates one import edge per (importing file, package file) for Java `import pkg.*;`. The follow-up stores that relationship once per statement and once per package. Before changing storage, readers have to stop depending on it, and no reader should be able to hold a collection that silently omits part of what a scope reaches.

`edgesAt` is deliberately not "all imports". It is complete for anything a reader can select by a non-empty local name, a non-empty exported name, a linked definition, or a kind other than a nameless wildcard (`isSelectableImport`). The one thing an implementation may leave out is a nameless wildcard target, which carries nothing but a file, and those still answer `reaches`, `membership` and `forEachTarget`.

## Reader migration

The compiler enumerated the readers: with the field's type changed, 26 statements failed to compile. Each moved to the operation it needs.

| Reader | Operation |
| --- | --- |
| `isClassFileImportGrounded` | `reaches`, plus `edgesAt` for the definition and exported-name checks |
| `resolveAmbiguousInheritanceBaseViaImports` | `reaches`, `reachesDirectory` |
| unique-name property narrowing | a cached `membership` per importing scope, asked only for files that reach the import tier, instead of a set of imported files built for every file up front |
| `emitImportEdges` | `scopes`, `forEachTarget` |
| Java on-demand fallback | `forEachTarget`, matching the statement by `atRange` |
| name lookup, namespace targets, imported return types, receiver namespace chains, JVM package siblings, rename | `edgesAt` (they select by name or `kind === 'namespace'`) |
| C++, Go, Kotlin, PHP, Rust, TypeScript, Vue provider code | `edgesAt` over their own language's edges |

An earlier inventory, taken by making three import-list types opaque at once, listed 33 diagnostics. They reconcile with these 26: two were second diagnostics on the same two statements, three were sites that only construct pre-finalize scope lists, and two were inside the shared package (finalize's own output and the name lookup's parameter).

Test fixtures that build an index by hand now wrap their edge map with the eager implementation. No expected result changed.

## Commits

1. `test(java)`: fourteen `import pkg.*;` scenarios from JLS SE 21 (7.5.2, 6.4.1, 6.5.5.1, 6.5.4.2, 6.6.1), each pinned to the exact `CALLS` / `EXTENDS` / `IMPORTS` edges emitted today. Nine agree with the JLS; five are labelled known semantic gaps. They are pinned so a change of import representation cannot move them by accident, not endorsed.
2. `refactor(scope-resolution)`: the interface, the eager implementation, the reader migration and the fixture updates.
3. `test(scope-resolution)`: a contract suite checked against a description of each import relation rather than any implementation's storage, and a graph-identity helper.

## Evidence

| Evidence | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Baseline | `09665c5a9` (`main`) |
| Candidate | `52d92c381` (this branch) |
| Clean-candidate tests | 183 files, 3,707 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped (`test/unit/scope-resolution`, `test/unit/graph-identity.test.ts`, `test/integration/resolvers/java-on-demand-jls.test.ts`) |
| Baseline fixture completion | 820 expected fixture IDs, all completed |
| Candidate fixture completion | the same 820 IDs, all completed |
| Graph comparison | zero semantic differences: 820 of 820 identical, 13,846 nodes and 20,610 relationships |
| Acceptance command | exit 0, checker `sha256:8bccebd4fcb61278777f38ad0a7bf4f07b46647f804a832ef22b66cee567bcf6` |
| Build isolation | each commit exported with `git archive` into its own directory and built from scratch; each run recorded the resolved path of `gitnexus-shared`, and the interface export is present only on the candidate |
| Prerequisite isolation | the grouped implementation is absent from the candidate checkout |
| Interface validation | 71 shared contract cases pass for the eager implementation here, and for the grouped implementation on the follow-up branch |

The head has since moved to `3816d6a59`, a review follow-up that changes three test files only (one coverage assertion and two comments). `git diff 52d92c381 3816d6a59` touches nothing outside `gitnexus/test`, and the comparison above was not re-run for it.

The 820 fixtures are every directory under `test/fixtures/lang-resolution`, all languages. The graph identity compared is node id, label and every property; relationship id, type, both endpoints and every property. Only storage order and property-key order are normalized.

Also run on the working tree before the clean comparison: all 107 resolver test files (4,743 tests, every language) passed; the full unit suite passed in 1,082 of 1,083 files. The two failures in the remaining file (`incremental-write-integrity.test.ts`, "Parser build changed during analysis") occurred during a run in which the shared package was rebuilt, and both passed when the file was run alone. The import-emission benchmark `--check` passes with an identical output hash.

A first comparison attempt was discarded and is not part of the evidence above: the checkouts had been exported without the rest of the monorepo, the build failed, and 817 of 820 fixtures errored identically on both sides. The acceptance check exists because of that run; it rejects a fixture that failed on either side even when both sides agree.

GitNexus change analysis rates the refactor commit critical (56 files, 66 symbols), which is expected for the boundary every language reads through and is why the comparison covers every language's fixtures.

## What this PR does not claim

- No memory or time improvement. Storage is the same.
- Nothing about the grouped representation end to end. Its pipeline integration, cache and incremental behaviour, and measured savings belong to the follow-up PR.
- No change to Java resolution. The five known gaps in the JLS scenarios stay as they are.

The debug-only `sr-emit-imports-*` probe now counts visited targets rather than visited edges in `scanned=`, so unresolved imports are no longer counted there.

Refs #3695

<details>
<summary>Reproducing the comparison</summary>

For each commit: `git archive <sha> | tar -x -C <dir>`, provide dependencies, run `node scripts/build.js` in `<dir>/gitnexus`, then from that directory:

```sh
W=$PWD node --import tsx graph-dump.mts <out.json>
```

then `python3 accept.py <baseline.json> <candidate.json> <inventory.txt>`, where the inventory is the list of directory names under the baseline's `test/fixtures/lang-resolution`.

`graph-dump.mts`

```ts
// Dump a canonical graph hash per lang-resolution fixture. Usage: W=<gitnexus dir> node --import tsx graph-dump.mts <out.json> [prefix-filter]
import { createHash } from 'node:crypto';
import { readdirSync, statSync, writeFileSync } from 'node:fs';
import path from 'node:path';
const W = process.env.W!;
const { runPipelineFromRepo } = await import(`${W}/src/core/ingestion/pipeline.js`);
const stable = (value: unknown): string =>
  JSON.stringify(value, (_k, inner: unknown) =>
    inner !== null && typeof inner === 'object' && !Array.isArray(inner)
      ? Object.fromEntries(Object.entries(inner as Record<string, unknown>).sort(([a], [b]) => (a < b ? -1 : 1)))
      : inner);
const { realpathSync } = await import('node:fs');
const { createRequire } = await import('node:module');
const shared = await import(`${W}/node_modules/gitnexus-shared/dist/index.js`);
const meta = {
  label: process.env.LABEL ?? '',
  gitnexus: realpathSync(W),
  shared: realpathSync(createRequire(`${W}/x.js`).resolve('gitnexus-shared')),
  hasImportVisibility: typeof shared.createEagerImportVisibility === 'function',
  pipeline: realpathSync(`${W}/src/core/ingestion/pipeline.ts`),
};
console.log('META', JSON.stringify(meta));
const root = process.env.FIXTURES ?? path.join(W, 'test/fixtures/lang-resolution');
const filter = process.argv[3];
const out: Record<string, { nodes: number; rels: number; hash: string } | { error: string }> = {};
const dirs = readdirSync(root).filter((d) => statSync(path.join(root, d)).isDirectory() && (filter === undefined || d.startsWith(filter))).sort();
let done = 0;
for (const dir of dirs) {
  try {
    const result = await runPipelineFromRepo(path.join(root, dir), () => {});
    const nodes = [...result.graph.iterNodes()].map(stable).sort();
    const rels = [...result.graph.iterRelationships()].map(stable).sort();
    out[dir] = { nodes: nodes.length, rels: rels.length, hash: createHash('sha256').update(nodes.join('\n')).update('\n--\n').update(rels.join('\n')).digest('hex') };
  } catch (error) {
    out[dir] = { error: String(error).slice(0, 200) };
  }
  if (++done % 100 === 0) process.stderr.write(`${done}/${dirs.length}\n`);
}
writeFileSync(process.argv[2]!, JSON.stringify({ __meta: meta, fixtures: out }, null, 1));
console.log(`fixtures=${dirs.length} errors=${Object.values(out).filter((v) => 'error' in v).length}`);
process.exit(0);
```

`accept.py`

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Acceptance check for a two-commit fixture graph comparison.

Exit 0 only when the comparison is VALID and shows zero semantic graph
differences. Anything that makes the comparison meaningless is a failure, even
when both sides agree: a fixture that failed on both sides proves nothing.

usage: accept.py <baseline.json> <candidate.json> <expected-inventory.txt>
"""
import json
import sys


def load(path):
    """Parse a dump, refusing a fixture ID that appears twice."""
    duplicates = []

    def pairs(items):
        seen = {}
        for key, value in items:
            if key in seen:
                duplicates.append(key)
            seen[key] = value
        return seen

    with open(path, encoding='utf-8') as handle:
        data = json.load(handle, object_pairs_hook=pairs)
    return data.get('__meta', {}), data.get('fixtures', {}), duplicates


def check(baseline_path, candidate_path, inventory_path):
    problems = []
    with open(inventory_path, encoding='utf-8') as handle:
        expected_list = [line.strip() for line in handle if line.strip()]
    expected = set(expected_list)
    if len(expected) != len(expected_list):
        problems.append('expected inventory lists a fixture ID twice')
    if not expected:
        problems.append('expected inventory is empty')

    sides = {}
    for name, path in (('baseline', baseline_path), ('candidate', candidate_path)):
        meta, fixtures, duplicates = load(path)
        sides[name] = (meta, fixtures)
        if duplicates:
            problems.append(f'{name}: duplicate fixture IDs {sorted(set(duplicates))[:5]}')
        missing = sorted(expected - set(fixtures))
        extra = sorted(set(fixtures) - expected)
        if missing:
            problems.append(f'{name}: {len(missing)} expected fixtures not executed, e.g. {missing[:5]}')
        if extra:
            problems.append(f'{name}: {len(extra)} fixtures outside the expected inventory, e.g. {extra[:5]}')
        failed = sorted(k for k, v in fixtures.items() if 'error' in v or 'hash' not in v)
        if failed:
            first = fixtures[failed[0]].get('error', 'no graph recorded')[:120]
            problems.append(f'{name}: {len(failed)} fixtures did not complete, e.g. {failed[:3]}: {first}')

    (bmeta, base), (cmeta, cand) = sides['baseline'], sides['candidate']
    if bmeta.get('shared') and bmeta.get('shared') == cmeta.get('shared'):
        problems.append('both sides loaded the same gitnexus-shared build')
    if bmeta.get('gitnexus') and bmeta.get('gitnexus') == cmeta.get('gitnexus'):
        problems.append('both sides ran from the same checkout')

    comparable = sorted(k for k in expected if 'hash' in base.get(k, {}) and 'hash' in cand.get(k, {}))
    different = [k for k in comparable if base[k]['hash'] != cand[k]['hash']]
    if different:
        problems.append(f'{len(different)} fixtures have a semantic graph difference, e.g. {different[:5]}')

    summary = {
        'expected': len(expected),
        'baseline_completed': sum('hash' in v for v in base.values()),
        'candidate_completed': sum('hash' in v for v in cand.values()),
        'compared': len(comparable),
        'identical': len(comparable) - len(different),
        'different': len(different),
        'empty_graphs': sum(1 for k in comparable if base[k].get('nodes') == 0),
        'nodes': sum(base[k].get('nodes', 0) for k in comparable),
        'relationships': sum(base[k].get('rels', 0) for k in comparable),
    }
    return problems, summary, different


def main(argv):
    if len(argv) != 4:
        print(__doc__)
        return 2
    problems, summary, _ = check(argv[1], argv[2], argv[3])
    print(json.dumps(summary))
    for problem in problems:
        print('INVALID:', problem)
    print('ACCEPTED' if not problems else 'REJECTED')
    return 0 if not problems else 1


if __name__ == '__main__':
    sys.exit(main(sys.argv))
```

title: perf(java): store an on-demand import once per statement and per package
body:
> Replaced by upstream-owned draft PR [#3934](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/pull/3934). The same commit and target branch are preserved; review history remains here.

## Summary

```diff
Java import pkg.*
- one retained ImportEdge per importer × package file
+ one group per statement pointing to the shared package file list
```

Stacked on #3920 at `7869c68f6aa66726e98ff17272802fd2e16faa09`. **Merge #3920 first.** This PR targets `abhigyanpatwari:perf/callable-flow-linear-depth` from `magyargergo:perf/3695-java-import-groups`. Java opts into grouping through the provider contract; other languages retain expanded imports. Selectable imports, bindings, traversal order, cycles, statistics and graph identity remain covered by equivalence tests.

The optional scope-graph emitter includes grouped targets. The two receiver-test fixture fixes from closed #3927 are inherited from #3920. Trailing-group sentinel reads have explicit bounds guards, and the diagnostic switch is documented with a forced rebuild.

## Evidence

The full-suite and equivalence results below were recorded at the previous #3909 head, `baadf926f`, before this rebase. Validation of the combined head is listed separately.

- **Before:** the scope-emission regression produced one scope import edge instead of seven. **After:** all seven edges are present and the complete graph matches expanded storage.
- **Before:** the 700-importer × 700-file synthetic benchmark retained about 54.5 MiB and 490,000 wildcard edges. **After:** about 4.3 MiB and zero per-file wildcard edges, with all 490,000 targets reachable and the same graph fingerprint (92% less retained heap). The gate passes with grouping and rejects forced expanded storage.
- All 822 language-resolution fixtures produce identical graphs with grouping enabled and disabled on the candidate, comparing every node and relationship property.
- Core validation covers all 1,580 configured files: 34,001 tests pass and 104 are skipped after documented full-file reruns. The two migrated receiver fixtures pass all nine existing tests. A final 403-test affected-path recheck passes with installed dependencies matching the lockfile.
- All 525 web tests pass. Build, core/test/web typechecks, formatting and pre-commit checks pass.

Validation of the rebased runtime:

- Build, production/test typechecks, and **5,208 tests across 225 files pass**, with 13 skipped.
- The Java import-storage gate passes: 4,509,216 retained bytes, all 490,000 targets reachable, zero per-file wildcard edges, and the same graph fingerprint.
- The 27-shape Dart gate passes on repeat and the seven-shape Ruby gate passes. The first Dart run exceeded one timing budget (1.522 versus 1.5); unchanged #3920 passed at 1.454 and the combined-head repeat passed at 1.349. Correctness, fingerprints and deterministic-work checks passed throughout. No thresholds changed.
- These checks ran at `03a5d886f`. The final rebase to `6967ed6b5` adds only #3920's CI timeout change (30 to 45 minutes); runtime and test sources are identical. Range comparison preserves all Java changes and drops only the two duplicate fixture fixes already in #3920. The final tree exactly matches a merge of the prior #3909 head and the pinned #3920 head.

title: test(bench): gate Dart deferred-import resolution and its scaling
body:
## Summary

Add a correctness and performance regression gate for the Dart deferred-import path introduced in #3882, plus a reproducible sweep that shows which dimensions scale approximately linearly. CI runs `measure.mjs --check` in the `benchmarks (GITNEXUS_BENCH)` job.

```text
deferred imports / ordinary prefixed imports
  → grow prefixes or uses: 16, 32, 64, 128, 256
  → real capture and scope resolution, exact graph checks
  → retained timing samples → estimates and linear-reference plot
```

The normal `measure.mjs --check` command preserves the fast CI profile: six validated graphs at 8×16, 32×16 and 8×64; four timed workloads; five samples after one warmup. `--full --check` times all six and records fresh-process peak RSS. The optional `sweep.mjs` command records all samples over 16–256 and three fresh-process rounds; `plot.py` renders the evidence. That larger sweep takes about 24 minutes and is not added to CI.

## Evidence

The repository contains a five-size sweep, raw measurements, graph fingerprints, plotting code, and [reproduction instructions](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/blob/fcd3c005c26b907ab089b2019b9a572e23e4cbf3/gitnexus/bench/dart-deferred-imports/README.md).

![Dart capture and resolution against linear growth](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/fcd3c005c26b907ab089b2019b9a572e23e4cbf3/gitnexus/bench/dart-deferred-imports/results/2026-11-13-linux/scaling.png)

Measured on Linux x64 / Node 22.23.3 at source commit `4290f5c`, with 60 fresh processes, two warmups and five measured passes per cell: 300 measured passes per phase. Each fitted exponent is the median of three round-specific log–log slopes; **1.00 is linear**.

| Input grows | Phase | Deferred exponent | Ordinary prefixed exponent | Deferred time growth for 16× input |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Prefixes, 16 uses each | Capture | 1.06 | 1.08 | 19.25× |
| Uses, 16 prefixes | Capture | 1.06 | 1.02 | 18.39× |
| Prefixes, 16 uses each | Resolution | **1.50** | **1.54** | **64.97×** |
| Uses, 16 prefixes | Resolution | 0.98 | 0.94 | 14.81× |

Capture and resolution with increasing uses are approximately linear over this range. **Resolution with increasing prefixes is superlinear for both forms.** The existing namespace cache collects imports per function scope, contributing `P² × U` work for `P` prefixes and `U` functions per prefix. This PR measures that cost; it does not optimize the resolver.

Minimum timings give the same conclusion. The chart bands are observed round ranges, not confidence intervals, and finite measurements do not prove asymptotic complexity. [Raw samples](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/blob/fcd3c005c26b907ab089b2019b9a572e23e4cbf3/gitnexus/bench/dart-deferred-imports/results/2026-11-13-linux/sweep.json) and the exact measured harness patch are retained alongside the chart.

Every timed resolution matched its validated graph, and all 30 deferred/control pairs had identical fingerprints. The benchmark also checks expected edges, prefix ownership, absence of `loadLibrary` edges, and exact workload counts. The prefix-resolution budget of 2.2 permits 8.8× time for 4× input; the documentation now states that passing it does not establish linearity. The previously documented `captures × prefixes` negative control remains below the small CI gate's sensitivity.

Validation:

- `npm run build` and `npx tsc --noEmit` passed.
- `npm test -- dart --maxWorkers=2`: 346 tests passed across 11 files.
- `node --import tsx bench/dart-deferred-imports/measure.mjs --check` and `--full --check` both passed.
- The full 60-cell sweep passed all correctness checks; a 12-cell smoke sweep passed after integration with the smaller CI profile and verifies revision metadata.
- The checked-in raw data regenerates the retained estimates and chart.
- Formatting, ESLint and `git diff --check` passed. The full repository test matrix is left to CI.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** Two-way. Revert the benchmark and its CI invocation to roll back.

**Blast Radius:** Benchmarks. No production resolver, parser, dependency, or timing-budget changes. The added sweep is opt-in; CI keeps the existing small gate.

title: test(bench): gate Dart closure-binder resolution and its scaling (#3903)
body:
## What

This adds `gitnexus/bench/dart-closure-binders/` (`measure.mjs` + `baseline.json`) and runs it with `--check` in the `benchmarks (GITNEXUS_BENCH)` job. It benchmarks the closure-binder path of #3903 (DART-11) for linear scaling, in the format of `bench/ruby-gem-resolution` and #3910.

**Stacked on #3903.** This branch starts at #3903's head `82c585d89`, so the diff below includes #3903's commits. Only the last commit (`9c3f7a537`) is new: the bench, its baseline and one CI step. The numbers were measured at `82c585d89`. #3903 is being revised, so the bench will be re-run on the revised head before this merges.

**Result.**
- **Linear:** both capture and resolution scale linearly in the number of functions and in closures per function, on main and on #3903.
- **Super-linear, partly new:** capture grows faster than linear with closure nesting depth. Main already does this; #3903 makes it steeper. From depth 3 to 24 the fitted exponent is 1.63 (1.49–1.76) on #3903 against 1.46 (1.32–1.61) on main. At depth 24 × 256 functions that is 6,609 ms against 4,506 ms. The cause and a fix direction are below.

## Architecture

- **Workload.** `lib/types.dart` declares `Address` and `Other`, each with `save()` and `run()`, so a name-only guess cannot pick the owner. Each `f<i>(Address cs, List<int> items)` in `lib/main.dart` holds K closures that rotate three kinds:
  - `(cs) { cs.save(); }` declines with `untyped-binder`.
  - `(Other cs) { cs.save(); }` resolves to `Other.save`.
  - `(x) { cs.run(); }` resolves through the nearest `cs`.

  The `sibling` form puts the closures side by side; the `nested` form nests them K deep.
- **Accuracy gate.** Each function's CALLS edges must equal the expected multiset exactly. The expected edges are computed from the binder rule, not read back from the graph. The cells also cover capture groups, relationships, declines by reason/detail, and a sha256 over every relationship and decline. On main the gate fails, with missing and mis-targeted edges (for example 64 missing and 128 wrong at 64 × 3).
- **Timing.** `capture_ms` is `emitDartScopeCaptures`. `resolve_ms` is `runScopeResolution` over worker-extracted files, replayed through `mergeChunkResults` outside the timer. It needs `dist/`.
- **Shapes.** small is 128 functions × 3 closures; large is 512 × 3 (functions 4×); dense is 128 × 12 (closures per function 4×, and nesting depth 4× in `nested`).
- **Profiles.**
  - `--check` (CI) runs one process with one parse worker, timing every workload at min of 5 after 1 warmup, interleaved. It takes 23.6–25.0 s locally.
  - `--full` times at min of 15 after 2 warmups and starts a fresh process per shape for peak RSS.

## Effect

There is no source change. The new CI step `Dart closure-binder correctness + scaling guards (#3903)` sits after `Receiver-resolution drop guards` with `if: ${{ !cancelled() }}`. It fails on any of these:
- a missing or extra edge;
- count or fingerprint drift;
- a ratio over its budget.

**Updated after review (`3589cebbc`, as merged).** The table that budgeted the depth ratios at 2.2 is gone.

How the gate works now:
- Every axis grows 16×: 32 → 512 functions, and 3 → 48 closures per function or nesting levels.
- Nested closures use fixed-width indentation.
- Each ratio is divided by the larger of the input-byte, capture-group and relationship growth.
- Every gated ratio's budget is 1.5.
- An operation count allows at most one enclosing-type ancestor step per Function scope.
- Resolution over nesting depth is reported, not gated (#3921). Its term is the shared `lookupLexicalName`, tracked in #3915.

On main the gate fails on capture over depth (11.2–11.6), and the operation counter lands with #3917.

Nesting-depth sweep: 64 functions, fixed width, a fresh process per cell, 3 rounds, arms rotated. Exponents are against input bytes, with 95% intervals:

| depth | phase | main | #3917 | #3917 + #3920 | #3917 + #3920 + #3922 |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 3→24 | capture | 1.84 (1.63–2.06) | 1.33 (1.16–1.50) | 1.17 (1.06–1.27) | 1.26 (1.10–1.42) |
| 3→48 | capture | 2.01 (1.85–2.17) | 1.54 (1.38–1.71) | 1.29 (1.18–1.41) | 1.27 (1.15–1.39) |
| 3→48 | resolve | 1.35 (1.19–1.51) | 1.29 (1.10–1.48) | 1.39 (1.23–1.55) | 1.39 (1.26–1.51) |

- **Median capture at depth 48:** 9,014 → 2,943 → 1,402 → 935 ms.
- **Median wall time per cell at depth 48,** parse worker included: 71.6 → 50.2 → 36.0 → 11.7 s.

What each PR does:
- **#3917:** the Dart climbs (the enclosing type, the callable-flow owner, and the callee and static sibling reads).
- **#3920:** the shared operand search of every closure argument.
- **#3922:** the parse worker's enclosing-function climbs, which caused the depth-48 quarantine.

## Doubling sweep: main `5d6e5c4f4` vs #3903 `82c585d89`

Each cell ran in a fresh process with `--shape … --reps 3 --warmup 1`, for 3 rounds, with arm order rotated per cell. The exponent is the least-squares slope of log time over log size, with its 95% interval.

| input grows | form | phase | main | #3903 |
| --- | --- | --- | ---: | ---: |
| functions 256→4096 | sibling | capture | 1.13 (1.04–1.22) | 1.12 (1.05–1.20) |
| functions 256→4096 | sibling | resolve | 1.02 (0.95–1.09) | 0.99 (0.89–1.08) |
| closures 3→48 | sibling | capture | 0.98 (0.88–1.08) | 1.00 (0.89–1.10) |
| closures 3→48 | sibling | resolve | 0.86 (0.76–0.97) | 0.87 (0.73–1.00) |
| depth 3→24 | nested | capture | 1.46 (1.32–1.61) | **1.63 (1.49–1.76)** |
| depth 3→24 | nested | resolve | 0.78 (0.61–0.94) | 1.12 (0.95–1.28) |

Per-doubling ratios for capture along depth, in ms at 3 → 24:

| arm | 3→6 | 6→12 | 12→24 | ms |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| main | 2.58 | 3.07 | 2.86 | 199 → 4506 |
| #3903 | 2.61 | 3.18 | 3.49 | 228 → 6609 |

Peak RSS was within noise of main on every axis, for example 317 → 920 MiB against 323 → 880 MiB over 256 → 4096 functions.

## The depth term

`attachDartLexicalNames` calls `synthesizeDartReceiverBinding` for every closure scope that no enclosing scope binds `this` for. That is every closure under a top-level function. `synthesizeDartReceiverBinding` then calls `findEnclosingTypeDeclaration`, which walks `.parent` up to the root. So each closure costs O(depth), and each nest costs O(depth²). In a profile at depth 48, this path took 9.1 s of 16.6 s capture time. Carrying the enclosing type, or its absence, down the scope chain would remove the climb.

Separately, and the same on main: at depth 48 × 256 functions, neither build produces Function nodes for the file. The sweep therefore stops at 24.

## How tested

- `--check` passes on this branch in 23.6 s.
- **Fail-first:** main misses or mis-targets the expected edges at every size of the sweep.
- **Negative controls**, as temporary edits of `languages/dart/captures.ts`:
  - A root climb per binder in `recordDartLexicalName` fails `nested_capture_closure_scaling_ratio` at 2.324 > 2.2 under the CI profile, with fingerprints unchanged. It also gave 2.729 and 2.66 under the full protocol.
  - A per-binder scan of every scope is O(binders × scopes). It adds about 300 ms at 1024 × 3 but moves no ratio past its budget, which is below what the gate resolves at these sizes.
- Fingerprints are identical at `ecd25da87` and `82c585d89`.
- prettier and eslint are clean, and the pre-commit typecheck passed.

**Environment:** macOS arm64, Node 24.16.0, on a shared host with load average 7–40.

title: Taint: validating-predicate barrier guards are not modelled (clean-on-patched regressions)
body:
## Problem

Taint is neutralised only when a sanitizer **transforms** the value (`escape(x)`, `parseInt(x)`, `path.basename(x)`). A path that is reached only because a predicate **vouched** for the value is not a barrier, so a sink that is guarded by a validating check is still reported.

Measured on the OpenSSF CVE benchmark (85 shared CVEs, engine v5 vs CodeQL): we are clean-on-patched on 42/85 while detecting 30/85; CodeQL is clean on 50/85 while detecting 50/85. Five of seven clean-on-patched regressions are CVEs whose fixes are guards, not transformations:

- `dns-sync`: validates with `isValidHostName(hostname)` and still calls `shell.exec(cmd)` on the next line;
- `reduce-object`: returns early on a config flag before the write;
- `set-value`: filters keys with `.filter(isValidKey)` where `isValidKey` is a separate top-level function holding the `__proto__` check.

CodeQL calls these **barrier guards**. Reporting a finding on code that was already fixed is the failure users punish hardest.

## Where the pieces are

- The CDG (control dependence, true/false sense) and REACHING_DEF layers are already emitted (`gitnexus/src/core/ingestion/cfg/emit.ts`), so the predicate dominating a sink is available.
- Taint transfer (`gitnexus/src/core/ingestion/taint/propagate.ts`) accepts CFG/def-use and sanitizer calls; its "guard" set is a recursion-cycle set, not a safety predicate. There is no barrier relation.

## Proposal (language-agnostic, via the existing hooks)

1. Control-dependence-aware barriers: a dominating call to an `isX` / `validX` / `test`-shaped predicate on the tainted binding, on the branch sense that reaches the sink, kills taint for the kinds that predicate guards. Unknown or non-dominating predicates must not kill taint.
2. For prototype pollution specifically, accept a `__proto__` guard literal in a function the writer CALLS (fixes `set-value`, keeps `node.extend`'s `setProperty`).
3. Pin each shape as a fail-first test; add a bench in the `bench/` shape (`measure.mjs` + `baseline.json`, `--check` ≤60 s in CI) over guarded vs unguarded corpora so the barrier cost scales linearly.

Happy to open the PR if the direction is agreed.

title: Graph fact: resource / listener lifetime (acquire, owner scope, cleanup) is not represented
body:
## Problem

The graph has provider-dependency relations (`INJECTS`, `CONDITIONAL_ON`, `DECLARES`) but no relation that says **how long a resource lives and who disposes it**. A reviewer that sees `session.add_listener(fn)` registered inside a request-scoped function cannot tell from the graph that the session dies with the request, so it reports "listeners accumulate" even though the owner scope cleans up.

Concrete case from a reviewed Python/FastAPI change: `database.py` creates a request-scoped async session via a dependency factory; `live_studies.py` registers transaction-end listeners on it; the finding "launch acknowledgment hooks accumulate on the session" was false because the session is disposed per request.

## Where the pieces are

- `INJECTS` and the DI pipeline phase (`gitnexus/src/core/ingestion/pipeline-phases/di.ts`) know the provider; they do not know acquisition/ownership/cleanup.
- `gitnexus-shared/src/graph/types.ts` has no lifetime/owned-by-scope relation.

## Proposal (language-agnostic, via `LanguageProvider` / `ScopeResolver` hooks)

Providers extract three facts where the language or framework makes them explicit: **acquired-in** (the scope that creates the resource), **owned-by** (the scope whose exit disposes it: request handler, context manager / `with` / `using` / `try-with-resources`, test fixture), and **cleanup-at** (the explicit dispose call, if any). Everything else is `unknown`, never "leaks". Shared code consumes typed facts without naming languages.

Pin the FastAPI dependency case, a `with`/`using` case and an explicit `close()` case fail-first; add a `bench/` entry so lifetime extraction scales linearly.

title: Indexer: track super-linear ingestion costs and remaining fixes
body:
Updated 2026-11-15. **Keep this issue open.** #3920 and #3934 merged on 2026-11-14 and are present on `main`. The consolidated fixes have passing final-head CI, but four performance workstreams below still need fixes or fresh measurements. Source status checked at [`8973bd0bc`](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/commit/8973bd0bc05016f91314664162aebfb475877f61); no new timing or memory measurements were run for this update.

## Current PR status

| PR | Status and role |
| --- | --- |
| #3920 | Merged 2026-11-14 as [`ee81970bc`](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/commit/ee81970bcd5962e0db8869834a13bda16f9ad591). Consolidates capture, lexical-lookup and worker improvements. Final head: `f01048de0`. |
| #3917, #3918, #3922 | Closed, unmerged, and superseded by #3920. Their fixes and follow-up review changes are included there. |
| #3921 | Closed, unmerged. Its proposal to report rather than gate Dart depth resolution is not the current #3920 policy. |
| #3934 | Merged 2026-11-14 as [`b714fd1e7`](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/commit/b714fd1e782144eac862276fccd4c260cca1c8f3), present on `main`. Stores Java on-demand imports once per statement and shares package file lists. Replaces #3909. |
| #3909, #3927 | Closed. #3934 replaces the fork-based #3909; #3927's two fixture fixes are already included in #3920. |

Both stack changes are now on `main`. Java wildcard-import storage in #3934 is separate from the Dart per-Function namespace-snapshot cost tracked below. #3928 also merged: it removes repeated registry-bucket scans in `reconcileOwnership`; it does not establish that the Dart/Ruby crowded-file class-binding costs are resolved.

## Merged fixes from #3920

| Tracked cost | Merged fix and coverage |
| --- | --- |
| Dart closure root/enclosing-type climbs and repeated callable-flow subtree searches | Per-file ownership/type answers, memoized operand searches and explicit-stack traversal. Includes the remaining #3917 changes and a deep-closure worker regression. |
| Ruby per-read method climbs, nested argument-list searches and heredoc opener pairing | One classification walk per file, arguments taken from the call's own argument field, and indexed heredoc pairing. Consolidates #3918. |
| Repeated shared lexical lookup through empty scopes | Read-only navigation caches with import, policy, ownership and namespace barriers. Passes with source-binding or selected-call callbacks remain uncached. The tested Dart/Ruby depth cases are gated; this is not a claim that every lookup is linear. |
| Worker ancestor climbs | #3922 and its review fixes are incorporated. Per-file memos retain negative answers; parent indexing is lazy. Unused worker call/assignment records are no longer built, while their wire fields remain empty and live request ownership is retained. The final #3920 implementation leaves the unused type-environment lookup as a plain loop because it has no production caller. |

## Completion checklist

- [x] **Namespace snapshot per Function scope.** `collectNamespaceTargets` through `createNamespaceTargetCache(...).at()` visits file imports for each Function scope. The original CPU and retained-memory term remains tracked; no fix is established by #3920 or #3934. Measure with `bench/dart-deferred-imports` from merged #3910. The proposed direction remains a shared per-file namespace-target table. Current [`namespace-target-cache.ts`](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/blob/8973bd0bc05016f91314664162aebfb475877f61/gitnexus/src/core/ingestion/scope-resolution/scope/namespace-target-cache.ts#L81-L114) still stores snapshots by scope and invokes `collectNamespaceTargets` for each uncached scope/activation bucket.
- [x] **Many classes in one file.** Retain the Dart `materializeBindings` → `dartMergeBindings` / `findClassBindingInScope` term, and the Ruby `merge-bindings.ts` / class-binding term. Re-measure after #3920 before declaring either resolved. The Dart `bench/dart-accessor-scopes --shape crowded` sweep from merged #3919 exposes this case; its one-class-per-file gate does not establish the crowded-file result. The [current baseline](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/blob/8973bd0bc05016f91314664162aebfb475877f61/gitnexus/bench/dart-accessor-scopes/baseline.json#L103) still records the crowded-file term as ungated.
- [x] **Ruby surviving bare/free calls.** `rubyBareCallNeedsSelfReceiver` still has the separately tracked climb from a surviving bare call to its class. #3920 explicitly leaves this outside its fixes; the [parent walk remains on current main](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/blob/8973bd0bc05016f91314664162aebfb475877f61/gitnexus/src/core/ingestion/languages/ruby/captures.ts#L1763-L1784).
- [x] **Dart typed initializers in nested closures.** `outermostBody` climbs once per initializer. The [recorded probe](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/issues/3915#issuecomment-6862665217) found 192 calls / 19,968 steps at depth 24 and 768 / 301,056 at depth 96, with about 4 seconds of capture at depth 96. #3920 explicitly leaves this term open; [`outermostBody` still walks to the root on current main](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/blob/8973bd0bc05016f91314664162aebfb475877f61/gitnexus/src/core/ingestion/languages/dart/captures.ts#L1449-L1457), including after #3925.
- [x] **Merge and verify the consolidated fixes.** #3920 is merged. Its [final-head CI run](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/actions/runs/43598695572) passed, including CI Gate, every-test-executed, benchmarks, scope-resolution time/memory, lexical lookup/cache interning, and production/web typechecks. The tested head `f01048de0` and merge commit `ee81970bc` have the identical Git tree `ad8e005af0896cdce6c97e3ce23d37d30a0ab672`, so the tested correctness/work guards are present in the merged revision. This verifies existing CI evidence; it is not a new local test run. Other class/definition parent walks remain outside its whole-worker claims.

The [earlier audit comment](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/issues/3915#issuecomment-6859497508) retains the original crowded-file measurements and profiles.

## Evidence and corrections

- **The depth-48 missing Function nodes were caused by worker idle-timeout quarantine, not a parser limit.** The earlier 1.6 MB stress fixture also requires raising the default 512 KB ingestion cap; it should not be presented as a default ingestion workload. See #3922 and the current #3920 measurements.
- At `9e2b080ce`, **#3920 reports** median worker time **36.54 s → 2.84 s** across three alternating before/after pairs for 64 Dart functions with 48 argument closures each, below the default file-size cap. All 64 functions and remaining worker data match. These are worker timings, not full `analyze` timings.
- #3920 reports output parity across **2,355 language-resolution fixture files**, excluding only the intentionally emptied legacy arrays, plus **5,742 passing tests and 14 skipped**. Build and production/test typechecks pass. Those local counts are targeted-suite evidence; the final PR-head CI subsequently completed successfully as linked above.
- The current #3920 benchmark baselines cover **27 Dart shapes and seven Ruby shapes**. Dart timing budgets are **1.5** and deterministic-work budgets **1.1**; Ruby capture and resolution budgets are **1.5**, including depth 4–64. Both depth-resolution gates are present. The older “reported, not gated” and blanket 2.2-budget statements below describe earlier revisions.
- #3920 documents the Dart normalization change explicitly: it includes CALLS growth alongside input/output structure and still prints the original formula. One recorded nested-resolution comparison is **1.73 under the original formula versus 1.29 under the CALLS formula**. Normalized CI growth ratios and the fitted exponents in the original report are different metrics.
- Capture/resolution gates exclude worker preparation and persistence. The separate worker measurements exclude persistence and full `analyze`; they do not establish whole-worker linearity for every program. The serial CI job allowance is now 45 minutes, while individual benchmark budgets remain enforced.

<details>
<summary>Original report — 2026-11-13 measurements and hypotheses</summary>

The text below preserves the original evidence. The parser-limit hypothesis and benchmark-policy statements are superseded by the corrections above.

The scaling benches added on 2026-11-13 (`bench/dart-deferred-imports`, `bench/dart-closure-binders` in #3912, `bench/ruby-bare-reads` on #3880, `bench/ruby-block-param-stop` on #3905) are green for the PRs they gate, but they measure three **pre-existing** super-linear terms that none of those PRs introduce. Recording them here so the exponents have an owner. All numbers are fitted time-vs-size exponents (1.0 = linear, 95% intervals, 3 rounds, fresh process per cell).

1. **Dart resolution vs number of prefixed imports: 1.41 (1.28–1.54)** on head, 1.45 for plain `import 'a.dart' as a` on main before #3882. A CPU profile at 256 prefixes × 16 uses puts 4.0 s of 6.0 s in `collectNamespaceTargets` via `createNamespaceTargetCache(...).at()`: one snapshot per Function scope, each visiting every import of the file, so cost ∝ function scopes × prefixed imports. Fix shape: build the per-file namespace target table once and share it across scopes.
2. **Dart capture vs closure nesting depth: 1.63 (1.49–1.76)** on #3903's head vs 1.46 (1.32–1.61) on main: `attachDartLexicalNames` → `synthesizeDartReceiverBinding` → `findEnclosingTypeDeclaration` climbs to the root for every closure. Fix shape: memoise the enclosing type per scope during the single walk. Separately, at depth 48 neither main nor head produces Function nodes for the file (a parser limit worth its own look).
3. **Ruby capture vs block depth: 1.50 (1.35–1.66)** on #3880 vs 1.18 on main: each bare read climbs to its method, so a nest where every level reads the parameter is O(depth²) (3.8–3.9× per doubling from depth 16). Also pre-existing and not gated: Ruby resolution vs classes in one file, 1.60 on main and head alike, in `merge-bindings.ts` / `findClassBindingInScope`.

The benches' budgets are 1.5 on linear axes and 2.2 on the axes above, so these terms are tracked rather than hidden; the `--full` protocol and `--shape` sweeps reproduce each number.

</details>

title: chore(deps)(deps): bump hono from 4.13.13 to 4.13.18 in /gitnexus
body:
Bumps [hono](https://github.com/honojs/hono) from 4.13.13 to 4.13.18.
Release notes

Sourced from hono's releases.

v4.13.18

Security fixes

This release includes fixes for the following security issues:

validator() skips validation for requests whose Content-Type parameters are formatted differently

Affects: validator('json') and validator('form') in hono/validator. A Content-Type with whitespace before ;, a trailing ;, or an unusual parameter name was not recognized, so the validator saw an empty object while the handler could read all fields. This completes the fix for GHSA-4h7h-rv7c-7m2v. The validator now decides by the media type alone, as c.req.parseBody() does. GHSA-92p4-j3wq-jmqx

bodyLimit() keeps every transfer chunk of a request body in memory

Affects: bodyLimit() in hono/body-limit. A body sent in very small transfer chunks was retained as one object per chunk, so a request within the configured limit could exhaust memory. The body is now buffered in one array bounded by maxSize. GHSA-39q9-qp46-w8xg

mount() and app.mount() forward a wrong path when a custom getPath adds a prefix

Affects: mount() in hono/mount and app.mount() on 4.13.16 and 4.13.17. With a getPath that prepends a prefix such as the host name, one segment too many was removed from the forwarded path, so middleware scoped inside the mount prefix could be skipped. The prefix is removed from the routed path again. Paths that would change meaning when forwarded now get 400, and an optional regular expression parameter in a mount path throws. GHSA-h25j-2p75-qj33

serveStatic() serves a path that was decoded twice when allowPercentInPath is enabled

Affects: serveStatic() in hono/serve-static and the runtime adapters, only with allowPercentInPath: true. A malformed percent escape in the request path was decoded a second time, so a path that middleware registered on the encoded form did not see could still reach a static file. The file path must now be the same as the routed path, and otherwise the response is 404. GHSA-74fm-fwc7-3fwp

Users who rely on validator(), bodyLimit(), mount() with a custom getPath, or serveStatic() with allowPercentInPath are strongly encouraged to upgrade to this version.
