title: perf(dart): carry the enclosing type down the capture walk, not a climb per closure
body:
> **Superseded by #3920.** Its branch now includes the remaining enclosing-type/static-check fixes and the deep-closure worker regression from this PR. The callable-owner and callee caches were already covered there. Continue review and merge in #3920.

## What

This fixes the repeated work that the #3912 review found in the Dart closure-binder capture path (P1). A closure that no enclosing scope binds `this` for synthesizes its own receiver binding. Under a top-level function every closure is in that position, and each one called `findEnclosingTypeDeclaration`, which walked `.parent` to the root. That is O(depth) per closure and O(depth²) per nest. At depth 24 × 256 functions it took 4.5 s of 12.9 s capture time (`node --cpu-prof`, main `e2b7cdbd0`).

The enclosing type, including the known absence of one, now travels down the tree with the walk. This PR does not make capture linear in nesting depth. A second, older term remains in shared code, measured below and left for a separate change.

## Architecture

- **Pass B (the tree walk).** `walkDartTree` already carries the owner of the current scope down the tree. It now also carries the nearest enclosing type declaration: `null` above or outside any class, mixin, extension, extension type or enum. Each closure scope stores it when it registers. `attachDartLexicalNames` passes it to `synthesizeDartReceiverBindingWithin`, so a closure's receiver binding never reads `.parent`.
- **Pass A (declared members).** The query loop runs before the walk. It still looks the type up, but through a per-file memo keyed by node id. A climb stops at the first ancestor whose answer is already known and records its answer, `null` included, for every node it passed. A closure bound to a local inside another closure therefore stops where the outer lookup stopped, instead of climbing to the root again.
- **Test hook.** `getDartEnclosingTypeStats()` / `resetDartEnclosingTypeStats()` in `languages/dart/receiver-binding.ts` count the ancestors the search steps onto.

No shared pipeline code changes. Everything is in `languages/dart/`.

## Effect

The output is identical. The Dart scope-capture fingerprint is unchanged at `2049dd91…` (`capture_groups_fp` 1702, `fixture_count` 57, synthetic 8261/26411).

### Nesting-depth sweep: main `e2b7cdbd0` vs this PR `09db678c6`

**Protocol.** This uses #3912's `measure.mjs --shape nested 64 <depth> --reps 3 --warmup 1` with #3912's fixed-width indentation, so input bytes grow linearly with depth. It runs depths 3, 6, 12, 24 and 48 for 3 rounds. Every cell runs in a fresh process, and the arm order rotates per cell.

**Exponent.** This is the least-squares slope of log time over log input bytes, with its 95% interval (12 points for 3→24, 15 for 3→48). `GITNEXUS_WORKER_SUB_BATCH_TIMEOUT_MS=300000` keeps the parse worker from quarantining the depth-48 file in either arm, so every cell resolved all its expected edges.

| depth | phase | main | this PR |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: |
| 3→24 | capture | 1.76 (1.68–1.84) | **1.58 (1.51–1.65)** |
| 3→48 | capture | 1.94 (1.83–2.05) | **1.65 (1.60–1.71)** |
| 3→24 | resolve | 1.22 (1.10–1.34) | 1.29 (1.19–1.39) |
| 3→48 | resolve | 1.35 (1.25–1.45) | 1.34 (1.28–1.41) |

Against depth instead of bytes, capture from 3 to 48 is 1.74 (1.60–1.88) on main and 1.49 (1.41–1.56) here.

Median ms per cell. Peak RSS is the largest of the 3 rounds:

| depth | input bytes | capture groups | relationships | capture main → PR | resolve main → PR | peak RSS MiB main → PR |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 3 | 10,800 | 1,043 | 199 | 74 → 73 | 8.0 → 8.2 | 337 → 265 |
| 6 | 18,736 | 1,683 | 327 | 177 → 159 | 14.0 → 14.5 | 308 → 309 |
| 12 | 34,608 | 2,963 | 583 | 532 → 447 | 33.0 → 32.5 | 337 → 340 |
| 24 | 66,352 | 5,523 | 1,095 | 1,909 → 1,240 | 74.7 → 81.6 | 469 → 457 |
| 48 | 129,840 | 10,643 | 2,119 | 9,728 → 4,310 | 248.8 → 233.6 | 509 → 546 |

Resolution does not touch this code, and its numbers stay within noise. Peak RSS also moves within noise.

**Environment:** macOS arm64, Node 24.16.0, shared host with load average 24–75 on 15 cores during the runs.

### What is still super-linear, and why it is not in this PR

Capture is still above 1 in depth. A CPU profile of this PR at depth 48 attributes 12.5 s of 14.5 s capture time to `synthesizeCallableFlowCaptures` in the shared `utils/callable-flow-captures.ts`. That code was already on main and is unchanged here.

- **`emitCallFacts` → `operandSyntax`** runs on every call argument. Dart wraps a closure argument in an `argument` node, so `terminalIdentifier` (reverse DFS) and `hasMultipleIdentifierLeaves` search the closure's whole subtree. The result is then discarded, because a closure argument is not a direct designator. That costs O(depth) per closure.
- **`isVisibleValueBinding`** follows the anchor chain from each call site to the root. That also costs O(depth) per call.

The climb this PR removes was 4.5 s of 12.9 s at depth 24 × 256 functions. `attachDartLexicalNames` now costs 0.5 s at depth 48 × 64 functions.

Making depth linear needs a language-neutral change to callable-flow that keeps every language's capture output identical. It should be its own PR with all 17 scope-capture fingerprints pinned.

### The missing Function nodes at depth 48

At depth 48 × 256 functions, #3912 found no Function nodes on main or on its own head. This is neither a tree-sitter limit nor a recursion cap: the nest parses with no `ERROR` or missing node, and `emitDartScopeCaptures` opens all 12,544 Function scopes in process. The cause is the worker pool's idle timeout in our code. The single 1.6 MB file took longer than 30 s in the parse worker, then longer than 60 s on its split retry. The next retry would exceed the 150 s cumulative cap, so the pool quarantined `lib/main.dart`:

```
Worker 0 parse job idle timeout. Splitting into 1/1 item jobs.            (timeoutSec 30, nextTimeoutSec 60)
Worker 0 parse job exhausted cumulative timeout budget. Surfacing in-flight file(s).   (cumulativeMs 90000, nextCumulativeMs 210000, maxCumulativeMs 150000)
Worker quarantine: 1 new file(s) skipped this chunk
```

The worker spends that time on the same super-linear capture work, plus the legacy `type-env` `findEnclosingScopeKey`, which climbs past every anonymous closure to the named function on each lookup. The timeout policy is deliberate, so this PR does not change it. The new resolver test pins one function nested 48 deep through the real worker: its Function node and exact CALLS edges are present.

## How tested

- **New unit test** `test/unit/scope-resolution/dart-enclosing-type-cost.test.ts` counts ancestor steps through the hook:
  - inline closures nested 64 deep under a top-level function: at most one step per Function scope, and the same count as at depth 8;
  - nested under an operator: the outermost closure still binds `this: Svc`, and the closures inside inherit it;
  - closures bound to locals, nested: each added level costs the same.
- **Fail-first.** I ran the test against main's `findEnclosingTypeDeclaration` with only the counter added. Two tests failed:
  ```
  × inline closures nested under a top-level function: at most one ancestor step per scope, flat in depth
    AssertionError: expected 16641 to be less than or equal to 65
  × closures bound to locals, nested: the memoised member lookup stops where the outer one did
    AssertionError: expected 9720 to be less than or equal to 3000
  ```
  The operator test passes on both, because there `this` was already inherited after the first closure.
- **New resolver test** `test/integration/resolvers/dart-deep-closure-nest.test.ts` (depth 48, fixed-width indentation). It passes on main too: it pins that the depth itself is fine.
- `vitest run test/integration/resolvers test/unit/scope-resolution` plus every Dart suite: 303 files, 8,754 passed, 3 skipped.
- `bench/scope-capture --check`: the Dart cell matches its baseline exactly and its scaling is 1.077. The full gate failed twice on this host on other languages' timing ratios, swift and javascript in one run and java in the next. Those languages are untouched here, and the host load average was 35–75, so CI is the run that counts for them.
- `bench/receiver-resolution --check`: OK.
- `npx tsc --noEmit`, `npm run typecheck:tests`, prettier and eslint are clean. eslint reports only the existing non-null-assertion warnings in `captures.ts`.

## Update: second commit `6ac3b803e`, the callable-flow owner hook

The shared callable-flow pass asks Dart's `lexicalFunctionOwner` hook for the owning function of every call, argument and binding it checks. The hook climbed `parent`. In node-tree-sitter, every `parent` or sibling read re-descends from the root, about 150 ns per AST level: 4 µs at AST depth 54 and 224 µs at 1,542. Each lookup therefore cost its depth, and at closure depth 96 the hook took 2.6 s of 11.5 s capture time.

The walk now carries the hook's answer down the tree. The previous named sibling is simply the child the loop just visited. The answer is recorded per node id, and the shared pass reads it, falling back to the climb only for a node the walk did not see. The walk also hands each node its parent's type, which replaces a `parent` read per assignable selector. All 17 scope-capture fingerprints match. A new test asserts that the hook takes zero `parent` steps for nests 64 deep. With the old hook it fails with `expected 511 to be +0`.

**Four-arm sweep.** The protocol is the one above: 64 functions, fixed width, a fresh process per cell, 3 rounds, arms rotated. Exponents are against input bytes. The third arm adds #3920, the shared callable-flow fix. The fourth also adds #3922, the parse-worker climbs.

| depth | phase | main | this PR `545eb3412` | + #3920 | + #3920 + #3922 |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 3→24 | capture | 1.84 (1.63–2.06) | 1.33 (1.16–1.50) | 1.17 (1.06–1.27) | 1.26 (1.10–1.42) |
| 3→48 | capture | 2.01 (1.85–2.17) | 1.54 (1.38–1.71) | 1.29 (1.18–1.41) | 1.27 (1.15–1.39) |
| 3→48 | resolve | 1.35 (1.19–1.51) | 1.29 (1.10–1.48) | 1.39 (1.23–1.55) | 1.39 (1.26–1.51) |

- **Median capture at depth 48:** 9,014 → 2,943 → 1,402 → 935 ms. The fourth arm changes no capture code, so its difference from the third is noise.
- **Median wall time per cell at depth 48,** which includes the parse worker: 71.6 → 50.2 → 36.0 → 11.7 s.
- Peak RSS stays within 488–573 MiB.
- Resolution is not changed by any of these PRs. Its depth term (`lookupLexicalName`) is reported, not gated, in #3921 and tracked in #3915.

**What remains.** The third commit, `545eb3412`, removes the two sibling reads that were left. The callee hook read `previousNamedSibling` once per call; it now reads the sibling the walk already passed. The closure static check read `previousSibling` once per closure; it now gets the answer from one forward pass over the parent's children. All 17 fingerprints match. The new test asserts zero sibling reads, and on the previous head it fails with `expected 320 to be +0`.

At depth 96 with #3920, capture fell from 3.6 s to 2.5 s. What is left there is mostly `extractSingleParam`'s `previousSibling` per parameter (0.28 s) and scattered `parent` reads (0.29 s).

@magyargergo, this is the P1 fix from the #3912 review. The depth term that remains is measured above, and so is what removing it would take.

title: perf(ruby): bare reads, call arguments and heredoc pairing in O(file); gate block depth over 4 → 64 (RUBY-04 follow-up)
body:
> Superseded by #3920, which includes all feature commits from this PR and the subsequent benchmark cleanup. Continue review and merge in #3920.

The #3912 review set a bar for our scaling benches: no budget above 1.5, a negative control that fails, and generators that grow input linearly. `bench/ruby-bare-reads` (#3880) missed all three:

- Block depth was gated only over 4 → 16. Over that range the O(depth²) per-read climb, which is the shipped code, passed at 1.222.
- The generator indented each level two spaces deeper, so input grew 47× over 4 → 64.
- Pairing heredoc bodies with their openers was O(H²) per line. At 4× that was not visible.

This PR fixes the three terms in the Ruby capture pass and tightens the bench.

## Changes

1. **`perf(ruby)`: classify every bare read of a file in one walk.**
   - `rubyBareNameIsLocalRead` used to climb from each read through every enclosing block to its method.
   - The first call for a file now walks the tree once (`rubyBoundReadIds`). For each name it keeps a stack of the earliest position at which the open scope chain binds it, and a closed scope starts a new chain. Each read is then one peek.
   - Closed-scope headers are visited in the enclosing chain, and heredoc bodies at their opener, so verdicts do not change.
2. **`fix(ruby)`: a call's callable-flow arguments are its own argument list.**
   - Ruby now supplies `extractCallArguments`. A call without an `arguments` field passes no arguments.
   - Before this, the shared fallback searched the call's whole subtree, including its block, and took the first nested call's list. `run_with do helper(cb) end` recorded `cb` as `run_with`'s argument 0, and `[1].each do … helper(cb) end` recorded it as `each`'s.
   - That search was also O(block size) per call. With (1) in place it was most of the remaining capture time at depth 64.
3. **`perf(ruby)`: pair heredoc bodies with their openers in one pass.**
   - Runs of sibling bodies are built in one pass, and each run finds its openers by binary search over the openers on its line.
   - The pairing rule is unchanged.
4. **`test(bench)`: tighten `bench/ruby-bare-reads`.**
   - Fixed-width indentation.
   - `input_bytes` pinned per shape, next to capture groups and relationships.
   - Capture depth gated at **1.5 over the full 4 → 64**. Each ratio divides by its shape's own growth.
   - Negative controls recorded.
   - Resolution along depth is reported, not gated. The reasons are below.

The Ruby fingerprint in `bench/scope-capture` is unchanged (`4843d3f3…`), and so is every Ruby pin.

## Before / after

Doubling sweep with fresh processes and this PR's fixed-width runner, at 128 methods. Each cell is the min of 3 after 1 warmup, 3 rounds, with trees interleaved. Exponents are pooled log-log OLS fits with 95% intervals. main is e2b7cdbd0; "PR" is 65553d6aa (the blocks workload has no heredocs, so the heredoc commit does not apply).

| axis | phase | main | this PR | ms at largest, median (main → PR) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| depth 4 → 64 | capture | **1.51 (1.36–1.65)** | **0.73 (0.68–0.77)** | 8908 → 925 |
| depth 4 → 64 | resolve | 1.07 (0.95–1.18) | 0.93 (0.76–1.09) | 371 → 296 |
| methods 128 → 1024 | capture | 1.01 (0.95–1.07) | 1.01 (0.90–1.11) | 1006 → 974 |
| methods 128 → 1024 | resolve | 1.05 (0.99–1.12) | 1.08 (0.93–1.24) | 179 → 177 |

- **Input bytes exponent:** 0.84 along depth and 1.00 along methods. Capture groups go 3328 → 18688 and relationships stay at 768, both identical on main and this PR.
- **Peak RSS at depth 64**, worker thread included: 552–584 MiB on main, 581–586 MiB with this PR.
- **`--full` peak RSS per shape:**

  | shape | peak RSS (MiB) |
  |---|---|
  | blocks small | 298 |
  | blocks methods | 389 |
  | blocks depth | 494 |
  | heredocs | 300–346 |

## Operation counts (fail on main, pass here)

`test/unit/scope-resolution/ruby/ruby-bare-read-cost.test.ts` counts SyntaxNode navigation steps. Each navigation call counts one step, plus one per node an array-returning call materialises. Linear work grows 4×; the test allows up to 5×.

| case | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| classify every bare read, depth 16 → 64 (same name; a distinct unbound name per level) | 623 → 7079 (×11.36) | 484 → 1876 (×3.88) |
| whole capture pass, depth 16 → 64 | 4522 → 50194 (×11.10) | 1871 → 7295 (×3.90) |
| whole capture pass, 32 → 128 heredocs on one line | 12126 → 72702 (×6.00) | 10046 → 39806 (×3.96) |

Failures on main, quoted:

```
AssertionError: tree steps 623 at depth 16 -> 7079 at depth 64 (x11.36): expected 11.362760834670947 to be less than or equal to 5
AssertionError: capture-pass tree steps 4522 at depth 16 -> 50194 at depth 64 (x11.10): expected 11.099955771782398 to be less than or equal to 5
AssertionError: capture-pass tree steps 12126 at 32 heredocs -> 72702 at 128 (x6.00): expected 5.995546759030183 to be less than or equal to 5
AssertionError: expected [ 'helper(0)=cb', 'run_with(0)=cb' ] to deeply equal [ 'helper(0)=cb' ]
AssertionError: expected [ 'each(0)=cb', 'helper(0)=cb' ] to deeply equal [ 'helper(0)=cb' ]
```

## Negative controls

Each control is a temporary edit, run with `--check` in the CI profile. Fingerprints are unchanged in every case.

| edit | result |
|---|---|
| restore the per-read method climb (main's `rubyBareNameIsLocalRead`) | `blocks_capture_depth_scaling_ratio: 3.872 > 1.5` (fail) |
| restore the callable-flow subtree search (drop Ruby's `extractCallArguments`) | `blocks_capture_depth_scaling_ratio: 1.792 > 1.5` (fail) |
| restore the per-body heredoc opener search | passes every timing ratio, even at 32 heredocs per line (0.565); the operation-count test above is its guard |
| main's bench on main (depth 4 → 16, old indentation) | the O(depth²) climb passes at 1.222, which is the defect |

## Resolution along depth is reported, not gated

Resolution code is unchanged, and the captures it consumes are identical. The fresh-process sweep fits 1.07 on main and 0.93 here. The in-process CI ratio over 4 → 64, however, ranged from 0.94 to 1.54 across seven runs, for two reasons:

- the depth-4 denominator is about 16 ms;
- the shared lexical lookup (`lookupLexicalName` via `lookupNameClaim`, mostly from receiver-bound calls) still climbs from each reference to its binder, which is O(depth) per reference.

A 1.5 gate on this ratio would flake. The old 4 → 16 gate (0.78) measured mostly per-file overhead. `baseline.json` `_depth_note` records all of this.

## Checks

| check | result |
|---|---|
| Ruby suites (15 files outside unit/scope-resolution) | 539 passed, 1 skipped |
| `test/unit/scope-resolution` | 3705 passed |
| `test/integration/resolvers` | 4874 passed, 3 skipped |
| `bench/scope-capture --check` | every fingerprint matches; Ruby `4843d3f3…` unchanged, Ruby ratio 0.97–1.21 over three runs. Each of the two full `--check` runs failed timing ratios in languages this PR does not touch, a different one each time (java 1.516 and javascript 1.543; then swift 1.633), at load average 55–100. |
| `bench/receiver-resolution --check` | OK |
| `tsc`, `typecheck:tests`, prettier | clean |
| eslint | no new warnings |

`bench/ruby-bare-reads --check` took 24–44 s wall on this shared host at load average 25–80. main's bench took 25 s under the same conditions.

## Not in this PR

- **Pre-existing:** the shared lexical-lookup term above.
- **Pre-existing:** the parse worker's `findEnclosingFunctionId` climbs `parent` for each call, which is O(depth²). It took about 6 s of the worker's 11 s at depth 64, and no bench times it.
- **RUBY-03 (#3905):** `rubyBareCallNeedsSelfReceiver` climbs from each surviving bare call to its class. It can reuse the walk added here once both PRs have landed.

@magyargergo this is the follow-up for #3880 that applies the bar you set on #3912.

title: test(bench): gate Dart accessor scopes and parameter redeclaration scaling (#3904)
body:
This PR adds the scaling bench for #3904 (DART-10, merged as 0b59f5325): Dart accessor scopes and parameter redeclaration. It brings the bench up to the bar set on #3912:
- every budget is 1.5;
- a negative control fails on each gated term;
- input grows linearly, and `input_bytes` is pinned per shape.

The branch also carries a plain merge of main. The only diff against main is three files: the bench runner, `baseline.json`, and its CI step.

## What it gates

The bench pins the getter, setter and redeclared-parameter CALLS edges exactly: no missing edge and no extra one. A runner built on #3903's head fails: it misses every setter edge and gains a wrong `reader → Address.save` per class.

| shape | `accessors` (one class per file) | `params` (one file) |
|---|---|---|
| small | 64 classes × 4 accessors | 64 functions × 4 params |
| large (4×) | 256 × 4 | 256 × 4 |
| dense (4×) | 64 × 16 | 64 × 16 |

`--shape crowded` is the `accessors` workload with every class in `lib/main.dart`. It is for sweeps only and is not gated.

## Why one class per file

An earlier draft gated resolution × classes at 2.2 because every class sat in one file. That term predates #3904.

The sweep below runs a fresh process per cell, min of 3 after 1 warmup, over 3 rounds. Exponents come from a pooled log-log fit, with 95% intervals. Workloads have 64 → 1024 classes with 4 accessors each, and input bytes grow with exponent 1.00 in every form.

| tree / form | resolution | capture |
|---|---|---|
| before #3904 (700443c9a), one file | **1.34 (1.27–1.42)** | 1.09 (1.04–1.15) |
| main with #3904, one file | **1.24 (1.16–1.33)** | 1.09 (1.05–1.14) |
| main with #3904, one file (`--shape crowded`, separate sweep) | 1.27 (1.21–1.33) | 1.12 (1.05–1.19) |
| main with #3904, **one class per file** (gated) | **0.98 (0.87–1.09)** | **1.00 (0.91–1.08)** |

At 1024 classes, resolution takes 219 ms with one class per file and 352 ms with every class in one file (medians). Peak RSS is 655 MiB and 688 MiB respectively, worker thread included.

A CPU profile at 256 vs 1024 classes in one file puts the growth in finalize:
- `materializeBindings` → `dartMergeBindings` (`languages/dart/merge-bindings.ts`): **×14.8** for 4× classes;
- `findClassBindingInScope` / `lookupMatchingNameClaim` (`scope-resolution/scope/walkers.ts`): **×9**.

DART-10 does not add this term; with #3904 the exponent is lower. The one-file term is recorded in `_one_file_note` and tracked in #3915.

The other gated axes, from the same audit and pooled over 3 rounds:

| axis | capture | resolution |
|---|---|---|
| accessors per class, 4 → 64 | 1.03 | 0.83 |
| functions, 64 → 1024 | 1.11 | 0.98 |
| parameters per function, 4 → 64 | 1.09 | 0.86 |

## Negative controls

Each control is a temporary edit, run with `--check` in the CI profile. Fingerprints were unchanged in every run.

| edit | result |
|---|---|
| rebuild the workspace MRO once per parsed file (`buildMro` hook in `languages/dart/scope-resolver.ts`, O(files × classes)) | `AssertionError [ERR_ASSERTION]: accessors_resolve_unit_scaling_ratio: 1.9014287611838079 > 1.5` (a second run gave 1.829). The 2.2 budget would have passed it. |
| re-walk the scope body for every parameter binding in `dartParameterRedeclared` (O(parameters × body)) | `params_capture_per_unit_scaling_ratio: 1.672 > 1.5` |

## Measured

The CI profile was run 3 times, all passing. The highest ratio per metric:

| ratio | capture | resolution |
|---|---|---|
| accessors, units | 0.999 | 1.220 |
| accessors, per unit | 0.821 | 0.880 |
| params, units | 1.152 | 1.260 |
| params, per unit | 1.135 | 1.253 |

Wall times were 15–17 s, with one 57 s run at load average ~80. A `--full` run peaked at 309–416 MiB per shape. Everything is in `baseline.json`.

The `accessors` fingerprints changed from the one-file runner because the file paths changed; the `params` fingerprints did not.

@magyargergo, this is the bench for #3904. It was held until #3904 merged, because the bench branch conflicted with main before then.

title: perf(ingestion): remove unused worker records and repeated AST walks
body:
## Summary

Nested closures made capture, name resolution and worker preparation repeatedly search the same syntax trees and scopes. This PR removes that repeated work and stops building unused worker call/assignment records. On the measured deep Dart fixture, median worker time falls from **36.54 s to 2.84 s** across three alternating before/after pairs.

```diff
 ingest a file
-  rescan nested operands, ancestors and sibling closures
-  build legacy call/assignment records without a production consumer
+  memoize operand searches and read-only scope navigation
+  reuse per-file ownership and ancestor answers; index parents only when needed
+  resolve calls from ParsedFile.referenceSites
+  verify exact output and traversal counts across increasing closure depth
```

- **Shared capture and resolution:** use an explicit stack for operand searches, reuse lexical parent maps, and skip absent value names. Navigation caches preserve import, policy, ownership and namespace barriers; passes with source-binding or selected-call callbacks stay uncached.
- **Language capture:** index Dart tree links, callable owners and enclosing types per file; index Ruby bound reads and heredoc pairing once per file; use native filtered Java/Kotlin searches while preserving nested declarations and source order. Java member reads find assignment write targets in one native search instead of one native parent read per member; this brings the `scope-capture` `java-deep-chain` gate from 1.42 to 1.58 (budget 1.5, red on `main`) to 0.97, with all 17 capture fingerprints unchanged.
- **Ruby behaviour change:** a call without its own argument list (`run_with do helper(cb) end`, a receiver chain, an invoke) no longer takes a nested call's arguments or arity. This removes wrong CALLS edges such as `run_with -> target`. The repository fixtures do not contain this shape, so the fixture parity below is unaffected.
- **Worker preparation:** retain empty `calls`/`assignments` wire fields and live request ownership. Required per-file ancestor memos cache negative answers. Short walks use native parents; a parent index is built after 32 ancestors in one climb, or when 256 accumulated native reads land on a node at least 32 levels deep, so flat files keep native parents. The type-environment lookup keeps its plain loop because it has no production caller.
- **Regression guards:** check exact traversal counts, output parity and capture fingerprints, with 27 Dart shapes and seven Ruby shapes. New and revised assertions use only `toBe`.
- **CI:** extend the serial benchmark job from 30 to 45 minutes so all guards can finish and write their execution receipt; its commands and budgets remain unchanged.

Supersedes #3917, #3918 and #3922. All #3922 commits and review fixes are included here; #3922 is closed.

**Stack:** `main → #3920 → #3934`. #3934 targets this PR's `perf/callable-flow-linear-depth` branch. #3927 remains closed because its two fixture fixes are included here. #3936 and #3937 (the analyze admission fix) are folded into this PR; see "CI unblock" below.

## CI unblock (folded from #3937)

Two commits that make `tests / MCP query performance` independent of the runner:

- **`fix(analyze)`:** with `GITNEXUS_MEMORY=off` and no `--max-old-space-size`, analyze passed V8's default heap limit (about 4144 MiB) to admission as an explicit main heap, reserved once for the main process and again for a worker. The default command then needed about 11,800 MiB against a budget of 75% of RAM and refused every host below about 15.8 GiB. An unpinned default limit is now a ceiling (`mainHeapLimitMb`); a pinned heap is still rejected when it does not fit.
- **`test(mcp)`:** `bench/mcp-query/measure.mjs` passes `--memory-budget 1024` when each runtime indexes the 64-file fixture. The job builds its baseline from the PR base, so the runtime fix alone cannot help a PR whose base lacks it. Indexing is outside the timing window; the measured requests are unchanged.

From the job's `report.json`: every failing run was on an Intel Xeon 6975P-C runner reporting 15,701.6 MiB; runs with the same baseline on runners reporting 15,983 MiB passed. After the change the job passed on that 15,701.6 MiB hardware with all 40 rounds. With an unfixed `main` build as baseline, the index command fails on a simulated 15,700 MiB host without the flag and succeeds with it, and the full `--check` run passes locally.

## Evidence

- **Worker before/after:** for 64 Dart functions with 48 argument closures each, three alternating pairs measured median worker time **36.54 s → 2.84 s** (about **12.9× faster**). All 64 functions and the remaining worker data match. This fixture is below the default 512 KB ingestion cap; these are worker measurements, not full `analyze` timings.
- **Sparse lookup:** for a 220 KB TypeScript array plus one call, the lazy index keeps the lookup at native cost (**0.21 ms** median, excluding parsing); an eager whole-tree index measured **44.2 ms**. This compares two designs of the index, not the merge base. The regressions assert exactly three native parent reads and zero indexed nodes, and zero indexed nodes for 300 shallow climbs in a flat file.
- Worker output matches on **2,355 language-resolution fixture files** after excluding only the intentionally emptied legacy arrays. Fetch owners, nodes, relationships, symbols and parsed-file facts remain in the comparison. The fixtures contain no Lombok source; the Lombok search rewrite is covered by `lombok-synthesizer.test.ts`.
- New and revised tests use only `toBe`. Exact ancestor counts are 65 / 129 / 513 at depths 8 / 16 / 64; negative-answer reuse takes 386 steps. An independent native-parent oracle covers default parameters, bodies, different named functions and file scope. Controls losing the answering ancestor, ignoring cached `null`, eagerly indexing the tree, indexing on shallow reads, and never indexing on accumulated deep reads all fail.
- **Before:** the recursive operand wrapper failed at 500 nested Dart argument closures; a source-binding recorder could leave cached lookups pointing to an outer binding.
  **After:** the depth-500 regression passes. Removing the source-binding cache guard fails a regression in each pass: the receiver pass emits an extra wrong CALLS edge, and the reference pass keeps a stale outer binding.
- All nine reviewed lookup-barrier mutants fail assertions. All four native descendant-search controls exceed the bound that protects the Ruby implementation. Work guards reject zero measurements.
- All 17 capture fingerprints match. The original 18 Dart benchmark shapes and all seven Ruby shapes retain their exact fingerprints.
- The 27-shape Dart gate passes with zero missing or unexpected edges (worst timing growth 1.4613 < 1.5; worst work ratio 0.9993 < 1.1). Bound-depth capture is 1.1254 and resolution 1.4270. Native parent reads stay at 112 across 3–48 closures.
- Ruby's seven-shape gate passes; normalized depth-resolution growth is **0.4644 < 1.5**.
- Dart timing normalization includes CALLS to account for growing call work alongside fixed file/function structure. The report also prints the original formula. For the previously committed nested-resolve endpoints, the original formula yields **1.73 (fails 1.5)** and the CALLS formula **1.29 (passes)**. The baseline makes this gate change explicit; in its recorded review measurement the bound closure sweep also depends on the CALLS term (1.534 original, 1.427 gated). A timing-only failure is measured a second time before the gate fails, with the same budgets and workloads. Deterministic work gates use the varied input dimension, and native sibling reads must stay flat across the closure sweep, like parent reads.
- Final validation: **5,742 tests pass, 14 skip**, across 229 passing and two skipped files on the final base. Build, production/test typechecks, formatting and lint pass (zero lint errors). The full callable-declaration benchmark guard passes. Review follow-up `1f843caf7`: typechecks, lint, 6,079 targeted tests (scope-resolution, type-env, worker and resolver suites) and both scaling gates pass.
- Graph change analysis: all eight local files / 58 symbols and the full 37-file PR / 386 symbols are mapped, without partial or truncated results. Formatting and production/test typechecks were run explicitly.

Capture/resolution gates exclude worker preparation and persistence. The separate worker measurements above include preparation but exclude persistence and full `analyze`. The gains apply to the tested shapes. Other native-parent walks in class and definition processing remain; this PR does not establish whole-worker linearity for every program. Preexisting Ruby free-call and Dart typed-initializer climbs remain tracked in [#3915](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/issues/3915). The preexisting Kotlin/Swift trailing-lambda fallback is outside this change. There is no clean full-repository test-suite result for this combined head; earlier attempts encountered resource and unrelated fixture failures.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way — code and tests; no schema or dependency changes.

**Blast Radius:** critical

Shared lookup, caller attribution and operand capture serve multiple languages. Capture fingerprints, resolver tests and mutation controls guard output compatibility. Graph provenance and capped process coverage make impact counts lower bounds.

title: test(bench): report Dart closure resolution over nesting depth, do not gate it
body:
## What

This is a follow-up to #3912, which merged at `3589cebbc`. It moves one ratio, `nested_resolve_closure_scaling_ratio`, from gated to reported. That is how `bench/ruby-bare-reads` (#3918) treats the same lookup. Capture over nesting depth stays gated at 1.5.

## Why

- On main, resolution over depth 3 → 48 measured 3.26 and 3.11 in two runs.
- Resolution code is unchanged by the capture fixes. #3917 and #3920 change capture only, and the captures they produce are byte-identical, so this ratio moves with neither.
- The term is the shared lexical lookup. `lookupLexicalName`, reached through `lookupNameClaim` mostly from `emitReceiverBoundCalls`, climbs the scope chain from each reference to its binder: O(depth) per reference.
- That term is shared, not Dart's, and is tracked in #3915. A 1.5 gate on it would fail on every tree until that lookup changes.

## Effect

- `budgets` no longer lists `nested_resolve_closure_scaling_ratio`. The ratio is still computed and printed, and `_resolve_depth_note` records its value and cause. `_depth_note` now lists the capture terms and the PRs that remove them.
- `--check` on main still fails, as intended:
  - the capture depth ratio exceeds 1.5 (11.2–11.6);
  - the enclosing-type operation counter is unavailable until #3917 lands.
- Both failures need #3917 and #3920. Until then the merged gate fails the `benchmarks (GITNEXUS_BENCH)` job on main.

## How tested

- prettier and eslint are clean.
- On main (`e2b7cdbd0`, Dart sources unchanged since), the shape cells and fingerprints match `baseline.json`, and the failure list is the two items above.

@magyargergo, this follows up your review on #3912.

title: perf(worker): climb to the enclosing function once per ancestor, with parents from an index
body:
**Superseded by #3920.** [9e2b080ce](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/commit/9e2b080ce7857dadf856c4e91cdf9acf9a8910a2) includes this PR's head commit and its review fixes. Current validation and measurements are in #3920. All six inline review threads here have verified replies and are resolved.

The 1.6 MB stress fixture in the original measurements below requires increasing the default 512 KB ingestion cap. The current #3920 worker measurements use a smaller fixture within that cap.

---

## What

Two climbs in the parse worker go from every call or reference to its enclosing named function, passing every anonymous closure on the way:
- `findEnclosingFunctionId` in `workers/parse-worker.ts` runs once per call;
- `findEnclosingScopeKey` in `type-env.ts` runs once per receiver lookup.

Each step read `parent`. In node-tree-sitter that read re-descends from the root and costs the node's depth, about 150 ns per AST level (4 µs at AST depth 54, 224 µs at 1,542). A lookup k levels deep therefore cost k steps of depth each.

**Why it matters.** In a file of closures nested 48 deep, these two climbs took 8.1 s each of the worker's 17.9 s at 64 functions. At 256 functions (1.6 MB) the worker exceeded the pool's idle timeout: 30 s, then 60 s on the split retry, with the 150 s cumulative cap next. The pool quarantined `lib/main.dart`. A quarantined file contributes no nodes and no edges, so every consumer of the graph is missing its context. That is the "no Function nodes at depth 48" that #3912's review found.

**Relation to other PRs.** This is based on main `c9fb37481` and stacked on nothing. `git merge-tree` is clean against #3917 `b1782e1d6`, #3918 `30b60bb44`, #3920 `7cdb97cfc`, #3921 `988c9f56b`, and #3905 / #3912, both merged. #3917 and #3920 make Dart capture linear in depth; this PR does the same for the worker's legacy climbs.

## Architecture

- **`utils/ancestor-climb.ts`** (new):
  - `indexedParent` answers from one downward pass over a tree's named nodes. The pass runs the first time a climb on that tree asks, and the index lives in a `WeakMap` keyed by the tree.
  - `climbAncestors(start, memo, examine, absent)` records the answer at every ancestor a climb examined, keyed by node id. The answer at an ancestor depends only on that ancestor and the ones above it, so the next climb that reaches it stops there.
- **`findEnclosingFunctionId`.** Its per-ancestor rules are unchanged. The loop body moved into `enclosingFunctionIdAt`, which re-indents it, so view the diff with whitespace hidden. The memo `functionIdAtAncestor` is cleared with the worker's other per-file caches. The existing `functionIdCache` was keyed by node object, and node-tree-sitter hands out a fresh wrapper on every read, so it hit only for the exact node it was filled for.
- **`findEnclosingScopeKey`.** Its rules are unchanged, and it has one memo per `buildTypeEnv`, i.e. per file.
- **Test hook.** `getAncestorClimbStats()` / `resetAncestorClimbStats()` count climb steps and native `parent` reads.

**Impact before editing.** I re-indexed this worktree first (`analyze --index-only`: 126,203 nodes). Upstream impact:
- `findEnclosingFunctionId`: LOW, lower-bound. Callers are `processFileGroupFiles` and `requestEnclosingId`, then `processFileGroup`.
- `findEnclosingScopeKey`: LOW, lower-bound. Callers are `lookupInEnv`, then `lookup`.

The graph has few static callers, but both climbs run on every file of every language in the worker. That is why output identity is pinned through the worker as well as through the 17 capture fingerprints.

## Effect

**Depth-48 worker probe.** This is the 1.6 MB file from #3912's review: 256 functions × 48 nested closures, old indentation. It goes through the real parse worker from `dist/`:

| tree | default timeout (30 s idle, 60 s retry) | uncapped worker time | `lib/main.dart` Function nodes |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: |
| main `e2b7cdbd0` | quarantined after 92.1 s | 97.1 s | 0 |
| this PR | finishes in 64.5 s, on the 60 s retry | 33.0 s | 256 |
| this PR + #3917 + #3920 | finishes in **12.0 s** | 13.2 s | 256 |

- **Does `lib/main.dart` now finish inside the 30 s timeout?** With this PR alone: no. It needs 33 s, misses the first 30 s window, and completes on the pool's 60 s retry, so it is no longer quarantined. With #3917 and #3920 as well: yes, in 12 s.
- **Host load.** The first four runs were at load average 5–9. The two #3917 + #3920 + this PR runs were at 51–71, so their times are if anything high.
- **What dropped.** At 64 functions × 48, a worker profile on #3917 + #3920 put 8.1 s each of 17.9 s in these two climbs. The fourth arm below shows the result.

**Dart closure-binder depth sweep.** 64 functions, fixed width, a fresh process per cell, 3 rounds, arms rotated. Median wall time per cell, parse worker included:

| depth | main | #3917 | #3917 + #3920 | + this PR |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 24 | 16.4 s | 10.0 s | 7.4 s | 6.0 s |
| 48 | 71.6 s | 50.2 s | 36.0 s | 11.7 s |

Capture and resolve timings are unaffected by this PR, which changes worker-only code. In the same sweep, the capture exponent against bytes over depth 3→48 is 1.29 (1.18–1.41) with #3917 + #3920 and 1.27 (1.15–1.39) with this PR added.

## How tested

- **New test** `test/unit/ancestor-climb.test.ts`:
  - type-env's lookups through `buildTypeEnv(...).lookup` over TypeScript nests of 8, 16 and 64 arrow functions, each passed as an argument to the call around it;
  - the parse-worker stop-rule shape through `climbAncestors`;
  - a check that a memoised answer equals a fresh climb for every call.

  `parse-worker.ts` posts to `parentPort` on import, so a test cannot load it (see `callable-id.ts`). With the helper set back to main's behaviour (native `parent` reads, no memo), both depth tests fail:
  ```
  × type-env: every receiver lookup reuses the scope an enclosing lookup found
    AssertionError: expected 19488 to be less than or equal to 6048
  × parse-worker shape: a call climbs only as far as the first ancestor already answered
    AssertionError: expected 19488 to be less than or equal to 6048
  ```
- **Output identity:**
  - All 17 `bench/scope-capture` fingerprints match.
  - Through the real worker, `bench/dart-closure-binders` shape cells and fingerprints match `baseline.json`. Its `--check` fails only on the capture depth ratio and the missing operation counter, both of which belong to #3917 and #3920.
  - `bench/receiver-resolution --check`: OK.
- **`scope-capture --check`:** PASS (17 languages, fingerprints and every scaling ratio; load average 50–70 at the time).
- **`vitest run test/integration/resolvers test/unit`:** 30,135 passed and 39 failed, in 18 files. None is a resolver, scope-resolution or language suite.
  - They are the same git, hooks, shared-store, vendored-extension, scenario-map and release-gate files that fail on main in this environment.
  - Two more files failed here: `repro-3291-staleness-indexed-ref` (an ENOTEMPTY temp-directory cleanup) and `wiki-truncation-recovery`, which passes on re-run.
- **Clean:** `npx tsc --noEmit` and `npm run typecheck:tests`; prettier; eslint (no new warnings: type-env 9 and parse-worker 12, the same as main).

@magyargergo, this is the worker-side follow-up for the depth-48 quarantine from #3912's review.

<!-- gitnexus-pr-summary:v1:start -->

title: proposal(scope-resolution): cap property-dispatch CALLS per key (changes output; maintainer decision)
body:
## Proposal: a per-key edge cap for property dispatch (changes output — maintainer decision)

`emitPropertyDispatchCalls` (`scope-resolution/passes/property-dispatch.ts`) synthesizes CALLS from every member-call site named `k` to every function registered under the object-literal key `k`. Today the only bound is `MAX_PROPERTY_DISPATCH_FANOUT` (default 32, `GITNEXUS_MAX_PROPERTY_DISPATCH_FANOUT`): a key with more than 32 **registrations** is dropped whole. The **call-site** factor is unbounded.

### What goes wrong

A common method name that is also an object-literal key somewhere — `get`, `now`, `parse`, `getState`, `filter` — links every `map.get()` / `Date.now()` in the language to every registration of that key. Measured on a private ~14k-file TypeScript tree: property dispatch alone synthesized about 750k CALLS for a handful of such keys while the whole rest of the graph was about 730k edges, and the process ran out of heap. These edges are not the hook tables the pass was written for (#2437); they are the same promiscuous-name failure the fan-out cap already names, measured in edges instead of registrations.

### The proposal

Count each surviving key's member-call sites before emitting anything, and drop a key whole (never truncate part-way) when `sites × registrations` exceeds a per-key edge budget; report the dropped keys and the pair count the same way `skippedKeyNames` does, so the gap is visible in the stats and the log. A default of 8192 keeps this repository's own heaviest key (`filter`, about 3.3k sites × 2 registrations) under the cap; the hook tables #2437 targets are tens of edges. Override via `GITNEXUS_MAX_PROPERTY_DISPATCH_EDGES_PER_KEY`.

### Why this is an issue and not a PR

It changes the graph. On a private ~4k-file TypeScript monorepo the cap took property-dispatch CALLS from about 109k to about 11.6k; every removed edge was a 0.7-confidence edge on a key called from thousands of sites, but it is still a removal, and the maintainers decide what the default graph contains. The alternatives are:

1. ship the cap with the default above and the stats/log contract (my recommendation: these edges make impact walks lie by fan-out, and "no edge" is better than ten thousand wrong ones);
2. ship it off by default (cap = ∞) so only operators who hit the heap wall opt in;
3. leave it out and let the fan-out cap stand alone.

If 1 or 2 is wanted I will open the PR with a fail-first test on the drop-whole rule, the stats contract, and a before/after edge table on `gitnexus/test/fixtures` and on this repository.

cc @magyargergo

title: fix(dart): scope collection-element binders and every `_` declaration (DART-12)
body:
## What

I re-checked the six review findings on the DART-11 lexical-binder stop (#3903) on main `ef126ea20`, after #3903 and #3904 merged. For each finding I used the quoted snippet and every secondary shape the finding named beside it.

All six snippets are already correct on main: #3903's review round fixed them, and `receiver-walk-untyped-binder.test.ts` pins each one. Two findings still reproduced in forms the review named or implied but no test covered. This PR fixes those two forms and pins the remaining secondary forms as regressions.

- **5, a binder's cost on free and implicit-`this` calls (collection elements).** A collection `for` or `if` element put its variable in the enclosing scope:
  - `[for (final tick in xs) tick]; tick();` lost `Tk.listFor -> Tk.tick` with no recorded outcome. `{for (…) tick: 1}` and `[if (o case int tick) tick]` behaved the same.
  - A parameter that an element rebinds lost its annotation (DART-10 recall boundary 1), so `collect`'s outer `fs.save()` lost `Address.save`.
  - Fix: `for_element` and `if_element` open a Block scope when they declare a name, as the `for` and `if` statements already do.
- **6, typed wildcard `_` (signature parameters and locals).** #3903 skips `_` only for closure and local-function parameters.
  - A typed `_` parameter of a method, function or constructor still typed `_`. So did a local `final Other _ = Other()`. As a result, `_.save()` beside a field named `_` reached `Other.save`.
  - Fix: `_` gets no type binding as a signature parameter or as a local declarator.

## Why

Item 5 lost correct edges and recorded no outcome. Item 6 produced wrong edges. From Dart 3.7, a parameter or local named `_` declares nothing, so `_` in the body reads an enclosing `_`.

The `_` rule is the one closures already follow, and it is not version-gated. Cost: a pre-3.7 source that calls a method on a `_` parameter loses that edge. That is a missing edge, never a wrong one.

## Results

Edges are measured on each finding's snippet and, where the snippet was already fixed, on its secondary forms. Base is main `ef126ea20`; head is this branch.

| # | Finding | Status | Before → after |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | P1, names that declare nothing | Already fixed on main (#3903 review round); regression pins added | `handle`: `Address.save`, `Address.parse`, `Other.parse` on both. Unpinned forms (pattern assignment in a local function; if-case, switch-expression and logical-or constants) are correct on both. |
| 2 | P2, `this` in a closure under a getter, setter, operator or `late` initializer | Already fixed on main; regression pins added | `Svc -> Address.save @8:16` on both. Setter, operator and `late` forms and the `this.addr.city` `ACCESSES` edge are correct on both. |
| 3 | P2, comment between a local function's signature and body | Already fixed on main; regression pins added | `k1 -> Address.save @8:5` and `k1 -> Other.run @6:7` on both. `/* */`, `///` and closure-comment forms are correct on both. |
| 4 | P2, block-local redeclaration typed by the parameter | Already fixed on main; regression pins added | `b1`/`b2`: no edge, `untyped-binder` at the Block, on both. `if`/`while`/`try`/case forms are the same on both. |
| 5 | P2, a binder's cost on free and implicit-`this` calls | Statements already fixed; **collection elements fixed here** | Statement forms keep `Tk.m3 -> Tk.tick`, `g4`, `h5` on both. Elements: `Tk.listFor`/`mapFor`/`listIfCase -> Tk.tick` and `topFor -> helper` go from none to the edge. `collect -> Address.save @26:5` goes from none to the edge. The inner site's binder moves from the Function scope to the element's Block. |
| 6 | P3, typed wildcard `_` | Closures already fixed; **signature parameters and locals fixed here** | Closure forms: no edge on both. `Holder.param`, `Holder.arrowParam`, `Holder(Other _)` and `Holder.local` go from `Other.save`/`Other.run` (wrong) to no edge (`receiver-owned-but-unbound`). `topParam(Other _)` goes from `Other.save` to no edge. |

## Testing

**Fail-first on main `ef126ea20`.** `dart-lexical-binder-gaps.test.ts` has 11 tests. The 6 regression pins pass on main. The 5 fail-first pins fail with the reproduced edges:

```
after the literal, an implicit-`this` or free call reaches the name ...
  expected [] to deeply equal
  [ topFor -> helper, Tk.listFor -> Tk.tick, Tk.listIfCase -> Tk.tick, Tk.mapFor -> Tk.tick ]
a parameter an element rebinds keeps its annotation outside the element
  expected [] to deeply equal [ collect -> Address.save#0 @26:5 ]
inside the element, the element's own variable still stops the walk
  received binder scope:elements.dart#24:0-27:1:Function at 25:52 and at 26:5 (the outer site)
`_` in a method, constructor or local is the field, never an `Other`
  + Holder.Holder#1 -> Other.run @6:6, topParam -> Other.save @19:4,
  + Holder.arrowParam#1 -> Other.run @11:32, Holder.local#0 -> Other.save @14:6,
  + Holder.param#1 -> Other.save @9:6
a top-level function with a typed `_` parameter binds no `Other`
  + topParam -> Other.save @19:4
```

**Each fix reverted alone** (`git apply -R` of its hunk, `dist/` rebuilt, the patch restored byte-identical afterwards). Each revert turns only its own pins red:

| reverted | red |
| --- | --- |
| `for_element` / `if_element` in `DART_BLOCK_SCOPE_TYPES` | 5: the 3 element pins, plus the 2 `dart-scope-openers` pins updated here |
| `_` guard in `synthesizeDartSignatureBindings` | 2: `Holder(Other _)`, `param`, `arrowParam` and `topParam` regain `Other` |
| `_` guard in `emitVarTypeBinding` | 1: `Holder.local -> Other.save @14:6` returns |

**Local probe A/B, main versus this branch.** The probe is not committed. It has 8 files and about 75 call sites covering every finding's snippet and the variants each finding named. Only the intended sites move:
- 4 correct edges added: `Tk.m3k`, `Tk2.e1`, `Tk2.e2` → `tick`/`tock`, and `Tk2.e3 -> Address.save`.
- 5 wrong `_` edges removed: `param`, `arrowParam`, `localVar`, `topParam`, `topLocal`.
- `e3`'s inner binder moves from the Function scope to the element's Block scope.

Every other line of edges and outcomes is identical.

**Updated pins.** In `dart-scope-openers.test.ts`, the two pins that described the collection-`for` limit now assert the regained annotation and the edge `collect -> Address.save`. The `nested_rebinding.dart` header comment is reworded with the same line count.

**Suites.** I ran `test/integration/resolvers` + `test/unit/scope-resolution` (299 files): 8716 passed, 3 skipped, 8 failed.
- All 8 failures are in `untyped-receiver-binder.test.ts` and `php-unresolved-receiver-fallback.test.ts`.
- They fail identically on main `ef126ea20` with `TypeError: scopes.imports?.edgesAt is not a function`. Those tests hand-build scopes with an `imports` value that #3908's interface no longer accepts.
- This PR does not touch them.

The Dart resolver files alone: 7 files, 238 passed. `tsc --noEmit` and `tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.test.json` both exit 0. Prettier is clean. ESLint shows 0 errors; the 9 non-null warnings in `captures.ts` are also on main.

**Benches** (shared host, load average 12-31):
- `dart-accessor-scopes`, `dart-deferred-imports`, `receiver-resolution`: `--check` PASS.
- `scope-capture`: Dart is rebaselined; the note is in `baselines.json`.
  - Running main's emitter and this one over the same 56 Dart fixtures, one file differs, `dart-scope-openers/nested_rebinding.dart`. It gains two groups: the element's Block scope and `collect`'s restored `fs: Address` binding.
  - `capture_groups_fp` goes 1702 → 1704. The synthetic counts stay 8261/26411. Dart scaling is 0.999, then 0.746.
  - All 17 fingerprints match.
  - The scaling gate failed for one untouched language per run: rust 1.741, then c 2.619. Each passed in the other run (rust 1.08, c 1.184).
- `dart-closure-binders`: `--check` fails on main and on this branch, on the same pre-existing gates.
  - The failing gates are the nested-depth closure ratios (main 13.5 / 3.9; this branch 11.0 / 2.7) and the six "unavailable until #3917" counters.
  - All six shape fingerprints are identical to main, with 0 missing and 0 unexpected edges.
  - The change adds no per-closure work: two set entries and two string compares.

**Not verified here:** CI's own timing runs.

**Seen but out of scope.** A cascade on a nested function's parameter, `Other inner(Other cs) => cs..run();`, reaches `Address.run`. It does so with or without a comment, because the cascade is captured as a free call. That is DART-08, already recorded.

## Overlap with #3920

Functions and constants touched:

- `gitnexus/src/core/ingestion/languages/dart/captures.ts`:
  - `DART_BLOCK_SCOPE_TYPES`: two set entries and its doc comment.
  - `emitVarTypeBinding`: one guard.
- `gitnexus/src/core/ingestion/languages/dart/signature-bindings.ts`:
  - `synthesizeDartSignatureBindings`: one guard.

#3920 edits none of these. It touches `walkDartTree`, `recordDartLexicalName`, `attachDartLexicalNames`, `emitDartNestedFunctionScope` and `DartLexicalScope` in the same file, but not the lines changed here.

title: fix(ingestion): merge each parse chunk in one canonical order
body:
## What

`mergeChunkResults` (`gitnexus/src/core/ingestion/parsing-processor.ts`) now merges each parse chunk in one canonical order, whatever shape the chunk's results arrived in:

- **Graph nodes** in source order (path, line, id) across all of the chunk's results. This is the existing `nodesInSourceOrder`, applied to the chunk's concatenated nodes instead of to each result.
- **Symbols and every per-file list** stably by file path, so a file's own items keep the order its parse produced. The lists are routes, fetch calls, fetch-wrapper defs/calls/re-exports, decorator routes, route facts, router includes/imports/constructor prefixes/module aliases, module constants, Spring types, tool defs, ORM queries, file-scope bindings, parsed files and scope-extraction failures.
- **Exported-type accumulation** goes through files in path order. Within a file, nodes keep their parse order, as before, so the later export of a name still wins.
- **`routeFacts[].routePosition`** is recomputed against the reordered `decoratorRoutes` (details below).
- Input that is already in order costs one linear check and no copy. The caller's arrays, which the parse cache may persist, are never sorted in place.

## Why

A chunk reaches the merge in one of two shapes:

- **Batched worker results.** These are contiguous job slices of the chunk, and the worker groups each job's files by detected language. This shape is used with `--no-parse-cache` and on the one-shot `processParsing` path, and the slicing depends on the worker count.
- **One result per file, in path order.** This shape is used whenever the parse cache is on, both for files reparsed in this run and for files replayed from the cache.

Graph node ids (`graph.addNode`), the symbol table and the routes phase's write-once registry are all first-wins. Merging result by result in arrival order meant the arrival shape, not the files, decided which file owns an id that two files declare.

**Tie rule after this change:** within a chunk, the file first in path order wins. Across chunks nothing changes, because chunks are still merged in chunk order.

**Route positions.** `routePosition` is an index into the chunk's merged `decoratorRoutes`. The worker records it before extracting a file's decorator routes, so it marks where that file's own routes begin. Reordering the routes moves those starts, so each position is recomputed by binary search over the reordered list: the start of the file's decorator routes, or where they would start if the file has none.
- For a file with decorator routes, the new position points at the same route object the arriving position pointed at. The test checks object identity.
- For a file with facts but no decorator routes, the slot no longer depends on which file happened to follow it in the batch. The only consumer is the route-fact insertion in `parse-impl.ts`. It offsets each chunk's positions by the routes already collected, which still holds because positions stay chunk-local.

## Results

**Parity check.** `gitnexus/test/fixtures` (3,459 parseable files) was analyzed with the CLI (`--skip-git --index-only --skip-fts`) using a build of `main` (ef126ea20) and a build of this branch. Every node row (label, id, all properties except embeddings) and every `CodeRelation` row (type, endpoints, all properties) was dumped and sorted, and the dumps were compared byte for byte.

| Comparison | Nodes (20,809) | Relationships (33,034) |
|---|---|---|
| main vs branch, parse cache on, default workers | identical | identical |
| main vs branch, `--no-parse-cache`, default workers | identical | identical |
| main vs branch, `--no-parse-cache --workers 1` | identical | identical |
| main vs branch, `--no-parse-cache --workers 4` | identical | identical |
| branch: parse cache on vs `--no-parse-cache` | identical | identical |
| branch: full parse vs replayed cache (3,420 files reused) | identical | identical |
| branch: default vs 1 vs 4 workers | identical | identical |

All 12 node dumps share one SHA-256, and so do all 12 relationship dumps (`8b1c6332…` and `fa8b7181…`). **No row differs, including all 150 `Route` nodes and their owning files.**

**Why nothing changes on the fixtures.** On this revision, chunks are packed per filename language and kept in path order, and worker jobs are contiguous slices. A batched result therefore leaves path order only when content detection splits a pack, which today means headers classified as Objective-C inside a C/C++ pack. On the fixtures that happens in 15 of 1,552 chunks. Only one of them would reorder anything when batched as one job (2 files), and those files share no first-wins id. This change pins the merge contract so that, if batching or packing changes, ownership of a shared id cannot change with it.

## Testing

**New tests** in `gitnexus/test/unit/merge-chunk-order.test.ts` (5 tests):
1. Batched (language-grouped), two-batch, per-file and reversed per-file arrivals merge identically. The comparison covers graph node order, the recorded `symbolTable.add` sequence, callable lookup order, symbol file order, exported types, every per-file list, decorator routes and route facts.
2. An id that two files declare goes to the file first in path order in every arrival shape.
3. Files come out in path order and each file keeps its own order (nodes in source order, exported types in parse order).
4. After reordering, every route position points at its file's slot. A file with routes keeps the same route object; a file with no routes lands between files.
5. The caller's arrays are neither reordered nor rewritten.

**Fail-first proof.**
- With the source diff reverted (`git apply -R`), tests 1–4 fail.
- Test 5 is a guard, and it passes on the old code by design. It fails when the copy in the path-order helper is replaced by an in-place sort.
- Test 4 also fails when the routes are reordered but the positions are not recomputed.
- Test 3 also fails when exported types are accumulated in source order instead of parse order.

**Checks run:**
- `npx tsc --noEmit` and `tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.test.json`: clean.
- eslint and prettier on both changed files: clean.
- Targeted vitest run: 32 files, 516 tests passed. It covered `test/unit/merge-chunk-order`, `test/unit/ingestion`, `test/integration/pipeline*` (including `pipeline-graph-golden`), `test/integration/file-results-{reuse,worker}`, `test/integration/cfg/*`, `test/integration/cli-e2e`, `test/unit/incremental-parse-cache`, `test/unit/result-merge`, `test/unit/scope-resolution/node-lookup-determinism` and the Go/C#/PHP capture goldens.
- **Full `test/unit`** (1,091 files, 25,395 tests): 1,072 files pass and 19 files fail (40 tests). None of the failures is caused by this change:
  - Rerunning the 19 files, 15 fail and every one of them also fails with the fix reverted.
  - Two of the 15 are scope-resolution tests (`untyped-receiver-binder`, `php/php-unresolved-receiver-fallback`), which fail identically on both builds with `scopes.imports?.edgesAt is not a function`.
  - The other 13 are git, filesystem, hook and registry tests. Their failing cases change from run to run on both builds in this environment.
  - The remaining 4 files failed only under full-suite load and pass on reruns of both builds.

## Impact

- **Upstream callers** (`impact mergeChunkResults --direction upstream`, read on an index a few commits behind): `processParsing`, plus `finalizeWorkerChunk` and `drainRound` in `runChunkedParseAndResolve`. They are reached through `closeRound` and `parsePhase.execute`. The graph rates this LOW, but every analysis merges through this function.
- `detect-changes`: 1 file and 20 symbols changed, no affected processes.
- No schema, cache-format or public API change. Parse-cache entries are untouched.
- **Cost:** a multi-result chunk now concatenates its node and symbol arrays once. A sort runs only when the input is out of order. Performance was not benchmarked. Single analyze runs on the fixtures showed no consistent direction (main/branch: 36/32 s, 23/19 s, 33/42 s, 25/28 s, 27/29 s).

cc @magyargergo

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

## Correction (maintainer, 2026-11-15)

"Why nothing changes on the fixtures" above, and the caveat in the first comment, understate what this change does. The tie is reachable today in a run without a parse cache:

- A worker job parses its `.ts` files before its `.tsx` files (`workers/parse-worker.ts`: the TypeScript group is processed one grammar at a time). With one worker a chunk is one job, so a chunk holding a `.tsx` that sorts before a `.ts` reaches the merge out of path order. With one file per job it arrives in path order.
- Before this PR, when two such files declare the same route, the `.ts` file owned the `Route` node and its `HANDLES_ROUTE` edges at 1 worker, and the `.tsx` file owned them with one file per job. With this PR the file first in path order owns them in both runs. So this fixes a worker-count dependence that exists on `main`, and route ownership can change for such repositories when they are analyzed without a parse cache at one worker.
- The parity table above still holds: on the fixtures no row differs.

Added in 251be0588:

- `test/integration/parse-chunk-merge-order.test.ts` runs that shape through the real pipeline and worker at 1 worker and at 2. With the merge from before this PR, 3 of its 4 cases fail.
- Graph relationships are merged in the same canonical order as the rest of the chunk. On `gitnexus/test/fixtures` without a parse cache, the graph at 1 worker and at 4 workers is identical, including relationship insertion order.

title: test(scope-resolution): build hand-made scopes with the import-visibility interface
body:
## What

Two unit tests hand-build a `ScopeResolutionIndexes`. Their `imports` field is now built with `createEagerImportVisibility(new Map())` instead of a bare `Map`. Every other hand-built index in `test/unit/scope-resolution` already does it this way. Test-only change: no source file changes.

## Why

#3908 made `ScopeResolutionIndexes.imports` the `ImportVisibility` interface, and `lookupNameClaim` in `scope/walkers.ts` now calls `scopes.imports?.edgesAt(...)`. These two fixtures still passed the old `Map` shape, so `main` fails 8 unit tests with `TypeError: scopes.imports?.edgesAt is not a function`:

- `untyped-receiver-binder.test.ts`: `imports: new Map()` in `indexes()` (line 53 before this change). 6 of its 7 tests failed.
- `php/php-unresolved-receiver-fallback.test.ts`: `imports: new Map()` in `run()` (line 119 before this change). Both of its 2 tests failed.

The `imports: []` entries on the hand-built `Scope` objects are unchanged, because `Scope.imports` is still `readonly ImportEdge[]`.

#3909 and #3920 already carry this same change in their larger diffs, and it is byte-identical, so either one merges cleanly on top of this. This PR is just the fix, so every open PR's CI can go green without waiting for them.

## Testing

title: perf(scope-resolution): reconcile ownership in O(defs)
body:
## What

One change to the scope-resolution pipeline, plus a gate for it. The graph does not change.

1. **`reconcileOwnership` runs in O(defs).** Before registering a field-kind or nested-type def, the pass checks whether its node id is already registered under its `(owner, name)`. It used to answer that by scanning the registry bucket for every def (`lookupAllByOwner(...).some(...)`). It now keeps a `Set` of node ids per `(owner, name)`. A key's set is read from the registry the first time the key is asked for, and the loop keeps it current as it registers. Nothing else writes these registries during the pass, and `register` always appends, so the set and the bucket contain the same ids. The sets are keyed by owner and then name, like the registries, so an ownerless key is its own bucket. The `methods` branch keeps its scan: ownerless callables `continue` before reaching it, so its bucket holds one owner's overloads, and it also matches a deleted def by signature, which a node-id set can't answer.
2. **`bench/ownership-reconcile/`**: a correctness and scaling gate for (1), wired into the `benchmarks` job next to the Dart closure-binder gate.

## Why

Defs without an owner share one registry bucket per name across the whole repository. In TypeScript that covers module-level values, top-level types, and locals of free functions. Scanning that bucket for every def made the duplicate check quadratic in the number of same-named ownerless declarations.

On this repository's own 3611 TypeScript files (extracted the way `runScopeResolution`'s first phase does it, then one `reconcileOwnership` pass into a fresh model, min of 5):

| | largest ownerless bucket | `reconcileOwnership` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| bucket scan | `result`: 4732 defs (then `calls` 1578, `i` 1466, `tree` 1115) | 498.7 ms |
| per-key sets | same | 69.6 ms |

## Results

### `bench/ownership-reconcile --check` (small = 250 files, large = 1000 files; CI profile, min of 25 after 3 warmups)

Each file declares `logger`, `router` and `config` at module level and a top-level `interface Options { level: number }`. The timed workload registers into a fresh model, then reconciles the same files again and must register nothing.

| | time ratio (budget 1.5) | registry-entries-read ratio (budget 1.1) | small / large ms | entries read small / large |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| this branch, run 1 | 1.131 | 1.0 | 0.471 / 2.131 | 1250 / 5000 |
| this branch, run 2 | 1.072 | 1.0 | 0.454 / 1.947 | 1250 / 5000 |
| sets reverted (`git apply -R`) | **4.194** | **4.002** | 4.366 / 73.23 | 374750 / 5999000 |

Both runs on this branch print `[ownership-reconcile --check] PASS`. Negative control, with only the `reconcile-ownership.ts` change reverted. It passes the exact shape/fingerprint comparison and then fails both gates:

```
AssertionError [ERR_ASSERTION]: reconcile_files_scaling_ratio: 4.193624253622248 > 1.5
registry_entries_read_files_scaling_ratio: 4.002001334222816 > 1.1
```

The shapes and fingerprints pin every `(registry, owner, name)` key and its node ids in registry order. They are identical with and without the sets.

Two departures from the parse-worker gates, both explained in `baseline.json`:
- **Smaller shapes.** A pass costs well under a microsecond per def, mostly hash probes into tables that grow with the file count. At 1000 vs 4000 files, a plain loop doing the same probes read 1.5–1.8 on a loaded host, and the linear pass read 1.3–1.6. At 250 vs 1000 both cells stay in the same cache regime, and the bucket scan still reads about 4.
- **More samples (25).** A sample takes milliseconds, so extra samples cost nothing and keep the minimum stable. With 5 samples, the linear pass ranged 1.06–1.62 at load averages above 100.

`analyze --index-only` of this repository gives the same node, edge, cluster and flow counts with and without (1): 126,427 nodes, 393,593 edges, 3597 clusters, 817 flows.

A clear of the resolved-reference index before property dispatch was tried and dropped: peak RSS did not move beyond run-to-run noise (median 2620 vs 2847 MiB, spread 600–700 MiB).

## Testing

All commands run from `gitnexus/`. The two suite runs below were taken on the first commit, which also carried the reference-index clear. The second commit reverts that, so `run.ts` is now identical to `main`. After the revert, `npx tsc --noEmit` is clean, `reconcile-ownership.test.ts` passes 20/20, and `node --import tsx bench/ownership-reconcile/measure.mjs --check` passes (time ratio 1.280, registry-entries-read ratio 1).

- `npx tsc --noEmit`: clean.
- `npx vitest run test/unit/scope-resolution` plus every other test file that imports `pipeline/run` or `pipeline/reconcile-ownership` (`scope-resolution-phase-failures`, `cfg/emit-guard`, `cfg/source-provider`, `taint/disk-scope`, and the integration files `commonjs-extraction-parity`, `go-build-variant-owners`, `go-cross-file-struct-owner`, `java-imported-return-types`): 193 files, 3823 tests, **3815 passed, 8 failed**. The 8 failures are in `untyped-receiver-binder.test.ts` (6) and `php/php-unresolved-receiver-fallback.test.ts` (2). They fail the same way on `main` ef126ea20 with this change reverted, with `TypeError: scopes.imports?.edgesAt is not a function`: those fixtures build the import index by hand in the shape it had before #3908 introduced `ImportVisibility`. This PR does not touch them.
- `npx vitest run test/integration/resolvers`: 112 files, **4938 passed, 3 skipped**.
- `reconcile-ownership.test.ts`: 20 passed, 2 of them new.
  - *Parity pin* (labelled in the test as one; it passes with and without the sets). Same-named ownerless values and top-level types from different files are both registered. A def already in the registry before the pass is skipped. The same def appears twice in one pass. A second pass registers nothing. Exact `ReconcileStats` and bucket contents, in order.
  - *Read count* (fails without the sets). A wrapper records the length of each bucket the pass reads. Each shared bucket must be read once per pass. With only the `reconcile-ownership.ts` change reverted:
    ```
    AssertionError: expected { calls: 50, entries: 1225 } to deeply equal { calls: 1, entries: +0 }
    ```
    With the first-pass read assertions removed, the second-pass block also fails on its own:
    ```
    AssertionError: expected { calls: 100, entries: 3725 } to deeply equal { calls: 2, entries: 50 }
    ```
- `prettier --check` on every changed file: clean. `eslint` on the changed source, test and bench files: 0 errors.

## Impact

`gitnexus impact --direction upstream`, read-only against an index of `main` 7 commits behind ef126ea20:

- `reconcileOwnership`: risk **HIGH**, 7 impacted. Direct: `runScopeResolution`. Depth 2: `scopeResolutionPhase.execute`, `resolveSources` (rename), the scope-resolution bench. Depth 3: `planGraphRename`. A text search finds no other caller.
It sits on every language's indexing path, which is why it rates HIGH. The mitigation is that the change does not alter output: the exact bench fingerprints, the unit pins, the integration resolver suite, and identical graph counts on this repository with and without it.

title: perf(group): load route handler symbols for many files in one query
body:
## What

The HTTP route extractor resolves symbols through `CONTAINING_QUERY`, which returns the Function/Method/CodeElement rows of **one** file (`WHERE sym.filePath = $filePath`). It issued that query once for every file it resolved a symbol in. `filePath` has no index, so each of those queries scans the three node tables.

This PR loads many files in one query:

- **`CONTAINING_FILES_QUERY`**: the same three-label `UNION ALL` with `sym.filePath IN $filePaths`, at most 500 files per query.
- **Expected files.** The per-file symbol cache now takes a list of files it will be asked for:
  - before the graph provider loop, every file whose `HANDLES_ROUTE` row carries a `handlerSymbolId`;
  - after `collectProjectDetections`, every file with project-scan detections.

  On the first cache miss, those files and the file asked for load in one query, grouped by file.
- **Edge cases.**
  - A file with no rows caches `[]`, exactly what its own query returns.
  - A batch whose query fails caches nothing, so each of its files falls back to its own `CONTAINING_QUERY`.
  - A file that was never named still gets its own `CONTAINING_QUERY`, as before.
- `CONTAINING_QUERY` and `CONTAINING_FILES_QUERY` are exported so an integration test can run both against a real LadybugDB.

**Ordering.** The batch has no `ORDER BY`, because `CONTAINING_QUERY` has none. Rows are grouped by file in arrival order, so each file keeps the row order its own query gives: Function, then Method, then CodeElement rows, each label in scan order. `resolveSymbolByName` (first name match) and `resolveContainingSymbol` (first of two equal spans) depend on that order, so this PR leaves it unchanged.

## Why

On a large graph every per-file lookup pays for a scan of three node tables. A routes build that resolves symbols in many files issues one such scan per file.

## Results

All measurements below were taken on a busy machine (load average around 60 on 15 cores), so treat the wall times as indicative.

**Route fixtures.** 18 route fixtures from `gitnexus/test/fixtures`, each analyzed once. The extractor from origin/main and from this branch ran alternately: one warm-up, then 3 runs each. Both builds were given the same `HANDLES_ROUTE` / `FETCHES` rows, so they saw the same input order.

| | origin/main | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| Output (87 HTTP contracts) | byte-identical in all 6 runs, for every repository | same |
| Symbol queries | 41 per-file | 11 batched + 7 per-file |
| Median extract time, summed over 18 repos | 217.8 ms | 169.4 ms |
| of which time in symbol queries | 85.4 ms | 39.5 ms |

`gitnexus group sync` over a group of the 18 repositories (3 runs per build):
- Every run gives 108 contracts and 8 cross-links, and the sorted `contracts.json` is identical across all 6 runs.
- The unsorted file is not a usable comparison: it differs between two runs of origin/main as well, because `HANDLES_ROUTE_QUERY` and `FETCHES_QUERY` have no `ORDER BY`.

**This repository's graph** (indexed at 5c7da84f: 3,565 files, 124,815 nodes, 118 HTTP contracts):

| | origin/main | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| Symbol queries | 22 per-file | 2 batched (8 files) + 14 per-file |
| Rows returned | 681 for the same 22 files | 681 for the same 22 files |
| Replaying each build's recorded symbol queries (7 alternating runs, median) | 197.3 ms | 145.7 ms |

- **End-to-end output.** Two rounds of 3 runs per build were made. In one round all 6 outputs were byte-identical. In the other, 2 distinct outputs appeared among the 6 runs, while run 1 of each build matched.
- **Why outputs can vary.** On this graph `CONTAINING_QUERY` itself returns the same rows in different orders from call to call. `gitnexus/src/server/api.ts` came back in 2 orders over 3 calls, and so did one test file. That happens on origin/main too, and this PR does not change it.
- **Wall time.** End-to-end extract time on this graph is dominated by the source scan (140–320 s per run on the loaded machine), so it is not a usable comparison here.
- **Remaining queries.** The 14 per-file queries left are files reached only through `FETCHES` rows, which are not named in advance.

## Testing

- **Unit tests** (`http-route-extractor.test.ts`), with a fake executor that records every query:
  - the handler files load in one batch with no per-file queries;
  - a file never named gets its own query;
  - a failing batch falls back to one query per file and gives identical contracts;
  - a file the batch has no rows for caches `[]` and is not queried again;
  - batched and per-file runs resolve the same `symbolUid` / `symbolName`, including an equal-span tie that only row order decides.
- **Mutation check.** Sorting a file's batched rows by uid makes the parity test fail.
- **Existing tests.** Express stubs that matched on `$filePath` now also answer `$filePaths`. The failed-lookup test in `http-route-graph-method.test.ts` now expects the failing batch followed by one per-file query, still with no retry per route.
- **Integration test** (`http-route-symbol-batch.test.ts`), using the real pipeline and LadybugDB:
  - for every file, the batch returns exactly that file's `CONTAINING_QUERY` rows in the same order;
  - the extractor gives the same contracts with and without the batch, in fewer queries (here: 1 batched + 1 per-file vs 6 per-file);
  - passed 10 of 10 repeated runs.
- **Fail-first.** With the source change reverted (`git apply -R`), 8 of these tests fail. The new ones fail on the missing batch (e.g. `expected [] to deeply equal [ [ …(3) ] ]`).
- **Checks run:**
  - `npx tsc --noEmit` and `tsc -p tsconfig.test.json`: clean.
  - `npx vitest run test/unit/group test/integration/group` plus the route integration tests: 83 files, 1462 tests passed (82 files / 1455 tests before this change).
  - eslint and prettier: clean on the changed files.

## Impact

- **Callers.** Only `HttpRouteExtractor.extract` changes, and it is reached from `syncGroup` (`gitnexus group sync`, auto-sync, and the MCP `group_sync` tool).
- **Behaviour.** No change to contracts. With a database that rejects the batch query, every file falls back to the old per-file query.
- **Follow-up.** Naming the files of `FETCHES` rows before the graph consumer pass would also batch the remaining per-file lookups.
