title: group sync output is not stable from run to run: HANDLES_ROUTE / FETCHES / CONTAINING queries have no ORDER BY
body:
## `group sync` output is not stable from run to run: the route queries have no ORDER BY

Observed while verifying #3929 on `main` ef126ea20, unchanged code paths.

### What happens

`HANDLES_ROUTE_QUERY`, `FETCHES_QUERY` and `CONTAINING_QUERY` in `gitnexus/src/core/group/extractors/http-route-extractor.ts` carry no `ORDER BY`. The resolvers that consume them break ties by row order (first match wins for a handler symbol, first row wins for a route owner), so the engine's row order decides the answer.

- On a 3,565-file graph (this repository), `CONTAINING_QUERY` for `gitnexus/src/server/api.ts` came back in two different row orders across three consecutive calls; one test file did too.
- Two `group sync` runs of `main` over the same group of 18 fixture repositories produce different raw `contracts.json` bytes (the canonical, sorted form is the same). On this repository's own graph, 3 runs produced 2 distinct outputs in one round and 1 in another.

So a contract's `symbolUid` / owner can differ between two syncs of the same commit, which makes contract diffs and anything keyed on them (cross-links, impact across repositories) noisy for no code reason.

### Proposed fix (separate from #3929 on purpose)

Add a deterministic `ORDER BY` to the three queries (for `CONTAINING_QUERY`: `startLine, endLine, uid`; for the route and fetch queries: file path, line, route id) and pin it with a repeated-run test. This changes how ties resolve, so it is a behaviour change to review on its own with a before/after on the fixtures; it is not a performance change.

cc @magyargergo

title: detect_changes matches a changed symbol with an empty id to every process step, reporting hundreds of unrelated processes
body:
### Area

gitnexus (CLI / core / indexing / MCP server)

### Summary

`detect_changes` reports hundreds of unrelated affected processes and `risk_level: critical` when a changed symbol resolves with an empty id; `context` for that symbol's name returns candidates whose `uid` and `kind` are empty strings.

### Context

A mixed repository (Swift app, Python and shell tooling, some TypeScript) indexed with `gitnexus analyze --index-only`. A change that only edits one method of a Python `unittest.TestCase` class in a test file is reported as affecting 299 processes, all of them flows between Swift symbols that cannot call a Python test method.

### Expected behavior

`detect_changes` lists the changed Python method with its own id and reports the processes that method takes part in (none). `context` returns candidates with a non-empty `uid` and `kind`, and a `filePath` that is a real path.

### Actual behavior

`detect_changes({scope: "staged"})`:

```json
{
  "summary": {"changed_count": 3, "affected_count": 299, "changed_files": 11, "risk_level": "critical"},
  "changed_symbols": [
    {"id": "Class:tests/example-test.py:ExampleTests", "name": "ExampleTests", "type": "Class", "change_type": "touched"},
    {"id": "", "name": "", "type": "", "change_type": "touched"},
    {"id": "Function:tests/example-test.py:ExampleTests.test_case.helper@2863:8#2", "name": "helper", "type": "Function", "change_type": "touched"}
  ]
}
```

The second entry is the edited method (`ExampleTests.run_case`); its `id`, `name` and `type` come back empty. Every one of the 299 `affected_processes` then names that method as a changed step, 694 steps in all, for example:

```json
{"name": "SwiftPreviewA → SwiftFactoryB", "process_type": "cross_community", "step_count": 3,
 "changed_steps": [{"symbol": "run_case", "step": 3}]}
```

`context({name: "run_case"})` for the same symbol answers `ambiguous` with two candidates, both with empty `uid` and `kind`. One has the Python file and the method's line. The other has `"filePath": "erty:app/AppTests"` and `"line": 1`, which looks like the tail of a `Property:<path>` node id rather than a path:

```json
{"status": "ambiguous", "totalCandidates": 2, "candidates": [
  {"uid": "", "name": "run_case", "kind": "", "filePath": "tests/example-test.py", "line": 1062, "score": 0.5},
  {"uid": "", "name": "run_case", "kind": "", "filePath": "erty:app/AppTests", "line": 1, "score": 0.5}
]}
```

It looks as if a changed symbol whose id is empty is joined to every process step whose symbol id is also empty.

The same happened for a second method of the same class in a later change (again 299 processes, 694 steps, `risk_level: critical`). `impact` for shell functions in the same repository answers `Target not found`, which is expected; this report is only about the empty-id match.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Index a repository that has Swift sources and a Python `unittest` file with a large `TestCase` class (the one here has about 80 test methods and nested helper functions): `gitnexus analyze --index-only`.
2. Edit one helper method of that class and stage the file.
3. Call the MCP tool `detect_changes` with `scope: "staged"`.
4. Call `context` with the method's name.

I have not reduced this to a minimal repository.

### Environment

- gitnexus 1.6.12 (CLI and MCP server)
- macOS 27 (arm64), Node 26.13
- Index built with `gitnexus analyze --index-only`, no `--pdg`

title: analyze fails on Windows: hashStableFile compares stat() and fstat() st_dev, which never match
body:
## Summary

On Windows, `gitnexus analyze` fails deterministically, before analysis starts, whenever the analyzer-identity cache is cold (e.g. first run after installing/upgrading the package):

```
Error: Analyzer identity input changed while it was being hashed: <...>\node_modules\gitnexus\dist\_shared\graph\types.d.ts
    at hashStableFile (file:///<...>/gitnexus/dist/core/analyzer-identity.js:277:11)
    at hashBuildTree (...:477:28)
    at resolveAnalyzerRunnerIdentity (...:2075:19)
    at Module.captureAnalyzerIdentityBeforeLoad (...:2164:28)
    at Command.<anonymous> (.../dist/cli/lazy-action.js:45:47)
```

## Root cause

`hashStableFile()` snapshots the file with `statSync()` and compares that snapshot against `fstatSync()` on the opened descriptor:

```js
const openedBefore = statState(fstatSync(descriptor, { bigint: true }));
if (!isDeepStrictEqual(openedBefore, before.target))
    continue;
```

`statState()` includes `dev`. On Windows, Node/libuv returns `st_dev = 0` from `fs.statSync()` for every file, while `fs.fstatSync()` on an open handle returns the NTFS volume serial number for the same file. The comparison can therefore never succeed, both attempts `continue`, and the function throws. This is not a TOCTOU race — it is deterministic for every file.

Reproduction (Node v22.16.0, Windows 11; identical on C: and D: volumes):

```js
const fs = require('fs');
fs.statSync('package.json', { bigint: true }).dev;          // 0n
const fd = fs.openSync('package.json', 'r');
fs.fstatSync(fd, { bigint: true }).dev;                     // e.g. 1979842126n
fs.statSync('package.json', { bigint: true }).ino ===
  fs.fstatSync(fd, { bigint: true }).ino;                   // true
```

All other fields (`ino`, `size`, `mtimeNs`, `ctimeNs`) match; only `dev` differs.

## Scope

Present in 1.6.10, 1.6.11, 1.6.12 and 1.6.13-rc.222, and in `gitnexus/src/core/analyzer-identity.ts` on `main`. 1.6.9 and older have no `analyzer-identity` module and are unaffected.

## Suggested fix

Normalize `dev` before comparing the stat snapshot with the fstat snapshot, e.g.:

```js
if (!isDeepStrictEqual({ ...openedBefore, dev: before.target.dev }, before.target))
    continue;
```

Alternatively, drop `dev` from `statState()`: on Windows `stat()` cannot supply it, and `ino` / `size` / `mtimeNs` / `ctimeNs` still identify the file.

## Verified workaround

Patching only that comparison in the installed `dist/core/analyzer-identity.js` makes `analyze` succeed, and subsequent `status` / `analyze` runs report the index as up to date.

## Environment

- Windows 11 Pro 10.0.26300
- Node v22.16.0, npm 11.4.2
- gitnexus 1.6.12 (global npm install)

title: fix: handle Windows stat/fstat device mismatch
body:
## Summary

Fix cold-cache `gitnexus analyze` failures on Windows when path stats report `dev = 0` but descriptor stats report the volume serial number. Keep device comparisons strict on other platforms and when Windows supplies a nonzero path device ID.

```text
Windows + path dev = 0: normalize dev for the path/descriptor comparison
All other cases: compare the complete file identity
Before/after descriptor checks: always compare the original device IDs
```

## Motivation / context

Fixes #3932. The original comparison rejected an unchanged Windows file on both hashing attempts, preventing analysis from starting with a cold analyzer-identity cache.

## Areas touched

- [x] `gitnexus/` (CLI / core / MCP server)
- [ ] `gitnexus-web/` (Vite / React UI)
- [ ] `.github/` (workflows, actions)
- [ ] `eval/` or other tooling
- [ ] Docs / agent config only

## Scope & constraints

**In scope**

- Limit the compatibility exception to Windows zero-device path snapshots.
- Preserve all other stat fields, persisted state, and descriptor stability checks.
- Register the regression suite in the Windows/macOS test list.

**Explicitly out of scope / not done here**

- Changes to the persisted `StatState` schema, public APIs, or other identity hashing paths.

## Testing & verification

- Before the platform guard, five device-mismatch regression cases failed; after it, all 17 cases passed.

title: fix(analyze): admit the default heap limit as a ceiling when the autopilot is off
body:
## What this changes

`gitnexus analyze` with `GITNEXUS_MEMORY=off` and no `--max-old-space-size` refused to start on any host below about 15.8 GiB:

```
Resource budget 11775 MiB cannot admit parser/model work; requires at least 11820 MiB for these allocations.
```

With the autopilot off, analyze passed V8's own default heap limit (about 4144 MiB) to admission as an explicit main heap. Admission reserves an explicit main heap for the main process and again for each required worker, so the default command needed about `2 x 4144 + 3307 + supervisor` MiB against a budget of 75% of RAM.

- A heap the operator pinned with `--max-old-space-size` is still an explicit reservation, and is still rejected when it does not fit.
- An unpinned default limit is now a ceiling (`mainHeapLimitMb`): the automatic main heap never exceeds it and may be admitted below it.
- `analyze` and `analyze --watch` share one helper (`manualHeapAdmission`) for this decision.

Hosts where the limit already fit get the same reservation as before (4144 MiB on a 32 GiB host).

## Why now

`tests / MCP query performance` fails on hosted runners that report 15,700 MiB, because `bench/mcp-query/measure.mjs` sets `GITNEXUS_MEMORY=off` and the baseline build's `analyze` exits before any round runs. Runners reporting about 15,990 MiB pass. It failed twice in a row on #3920 and passed on #3925, #3926, #3928 and #3933 with the same baseline commit.

The job builds its baseline from the PR's base commit, so this job can still fail on this PR itself when it lands on a small runner. It goes away for every PR once this is on `main`.

## Evidence

Reproduced with the benchmark's environment and a faked `os.totalmem()` (a `--require` shim), on a build of `main` and on this branch:

| Host RAM (MiB) | `GITNEXUS_MEMORY` | Heap pin | `main` | This branch |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 15,700 | off | none | exit 1, "requires at least 11810 MiB" | indexed |
| 12,000 | off | none | exit 1 | indexed |
| 8,000 | off | none | exit 1 | indexed |
| 15,782 and above | off | none | indexed | indexed |
| 15,700 | unset | none | indexed | indexed |
| 15,700 | off | `--max-old-space-size=4096` | exit 1 | exit 1 (unchanged) |

Tests:

- `analyze-resource-admission.test.ts`: a 15,700 MiB host with a 4144 MiB default limit is admitted at 4121 MiB (failed with exit code 1 before the fix); the same host with a pinned heap is still rejected.
- `analysis-resource-budget.test.ts`: the limit is a ceiling on a 32 GiB host (4144, was 8601 without the ceiling) and the admitted heap is below it on a 15.7 GiB host.
- `watch-supervisor-reservation.test.ts`: the watch path now passes the limit as `mainHeapLimitMb`. This test pinned the old contract (limit passed as `mainHeapMb`) and is updated.
- 82 unit files around analyze, watch, resources and launch pass (1,430 tests), plus 12 integration files that use heap or budget flags (55 tests, 5 skipped). Production and test typechecks, eslint and prettier pass.

## What this PR does not claim

- No full-suite run locally; CI covers it.
- The admitted main heap can now be below the real V8 limit by a few dozen MiB on small hosts (4121 vs 4144 at 15.7 GiB). With the autopilot off nothing enforces the reservation, as before.
- `resolveWatchOptions` still falls back to the heap limit when neither `--memory-budget` nor the admitted value is present; the watch command sets the admitted value first, so that fallback is not reached from the CLI.

title: feat(php): Lumen routes, Eloquent QUERIES, Laravel DI and queue/event support
body:
## Summary

GitNexus already extracts Laravel `Route::<verb>(...)` routes, but large classes of real-world PHP applications still index with empty framework layers. On a production Lumen 8 service (~1,300 routes, 2,870 files) the graph has **zero** `Route` nodes, and on Laravel services the `QUERIES`, `INJECTS`, `PUBLISHES_TO` and `CONSUMES_FROM` relations are always empty. As a result `route_map`, `api_impact`, `shape_check` and table/topic/DI impact queries return nothing for PHP, which agents can misread as "no consumers".

I'd like to close these gaps as a series of focused PRs, one per layer, each with fixtures and tests following existing precedents.

## Plan (one PR each, in this order)

1. **Lumen routes (and legacy Laravel route syntax)**
   - `$router-><verb>()` / `$app->router-><verb>()` and `$router->group([...], fn)` with `prefix`, `middleware`, `namespace`, `as`.
   - Array handlers `['uses' => 'Controller@method', 'as' => 'name', 'middleware' => ...]` (also for `Route::` in Laravel ≤ 7) and group `namespace` resolution.
   - Cross-file prefixes: `$app->router->group(['prefix' => 'x'], function ($router) { require __DIR__.'/../routes/x.php'; })` in `bootstrap/app.php`, resolved after parsing like the FastAPI router-prefix pass.
2. **Eloquent `QUERIES`** — model ↔ table mapping (`$table` or Laravel's naming convention), `Model::where/find/create/...` and `DB::table('x')`, emitted through the existing ORM phase.
3. **Laravel DI `INJECTS`** — a PHP resolver for the framework-neutral DI phase: service-provider `bind`/`singleton`/`instance` and constructor injection.
4. **Queues / events / topics** — Laravel jobs (`dispatch`, `onQueue`), events and listeners as `Destination` / `PUBLISHES_TO` / `CONSUMES_FROM`, plus a PHP topic-contract pattern for group sync. This one touches the Spring-named destinations phase, so I'll propose the design here before coding.

## Non-goals

- Runtime route discovery (`artisan route:list`), Blade support (#1853), or Symfony/other PHP frameworks.

Feedback on scope or ordering is welcome — happy to adjust before the PRs land.

title: Python: reading a module-level constant produces no edge to its Variable node
body:
### Area

gitnexus (CLI / core / indexing / MCP server)

### Summary

In Python, a function that reads a module-level constant gets no edge to it. 1.6.12 creates the `Variable` node, but nothing points at it, so `context` / `impact` on a constant report no dependents. This holds both for a constant imported from another module and for one defined in the same file.

Is this intended, or a gap in the Python `ACCESSES` collector? (`ACCESSES` edges to `Property` nodes are produced on the same code base.)

### Steps to reproduce

`config.py`
```python
TIMEOUT = 30


def helper(x):
    return x
```

`app.py`
```python
from config import TIMEOUT, helper


def calls_directly():
    return helper(1)


def uses_constant():
    return TIMEOUT * 2


LOCAL_LIMIT = 5


def uses_local_constant():
    return LOCAL_LIMIT + 1
```

```bash
git init && git add . && git commit -m init
npx gitnexus@1.6.12 analyze .
npx gitnexus@1.6.12 cypher "MATCH (a)-[r:CodeRelation]->(b) WHERE r.type IN ['CALLS','IMPORTS','ACCESSES'] RETURN r.type, a.name, label(b), b.name"
```

### Expected behavior

An edge (presumably `ACCESSES`) from `uses_constant` to `Variable TIMEOUT`, and from `uses_local_constant` to `Variable LOCAL_LIMIT`.

### Actual behavior

Both `Variable` nodes exist, but the only edges are:

| type | src | dst |
| --- | --- | --- |
| CALLS | calls_directly | Function helper |
| IMPORTS | app.py | File config.py |

### Context

Found with a known-answer test: edges derived from Python's `ast` on a 42-file project, then looked up in the index. 0 of 12 sampled cross-module constant reads had an edge; the control categories (direct calls, calls after a function-body import) scored 58 of 58, and file-level `IMPORTS` matched the ground truth exactly (70 of 70).

### Environment

gitnexus 1.6.12 (npx), Node 20.19.5, Windows 11. The 42-file result was the same commit indexed on Linux x86_64 with 1.3.11 (no `Variable` nodes there at all) and on Windows with 1.6.12.

title: Python: a function passed as an argument (to_thread, map, key=) gets no edge from the caller
body:
### Area

gitnexus (CLI / core / indexing / MCP server)

### Summary

In Python, passing a function as an argument without calling it (`asyncio.to_thread(f, ...)`, `map(f, xs)`, `sorted(xs, key=f)`, `executor.submit(f)`) produces no edge from the enclosing function to `f`. If that is the only way `f` is reached, `context` shows no callers and `impact(upstream)` reports nothing, although changing `f` clearly affects the caller.

This is different from #1166 (calls *inside* a callback body): here the callee is a named, resolvable function and no call expression exists at the site.

Is this out of scope by design? If an edge is wanted, I am not sure whether it should be `CALLS` with a lower confidence and a `reason`, or a separate reference type, and would follow your preference.

### Steps to reproduce

`config.py`
```python
def helper(x):
    return x
```

`app.py`
```python
import asyncio

from config import helper


def calls_directly():
    return helper(1)


async def passes_function():
    return await asyncio.to_thread(helper, 1)


def passes_function_sync(items):
    return list(map(helper, items))


def local_helper(x):
    return x


def passes_local_function(items):
    return sorted(items, key=local_helper)
```

```bash
git init && git add . && git commit -m init
npx gitnexus@1.6.12 analyze .
npx gitnexus@1.6.12 cypher "MATCH (a)-[r:CodeRelation]->(b) WHERE r.type IN ['CALLS','IMPORTS','ACCESSES'] RETURN r.type, a.name, label(b), b.name"
```

### Expected behavior

Some edge from `passes_function` and `passes_function_sync` to `helper`, and from `passes_local_function` to `local_helper`.

### Actual behavior

Only the direct call is linked:

| type | src | dst |
| --- | --- | --- |
| CALLS | calls_directly | Function helper |
| IMPORTS | app.py | File config.py |

### Context

Found with a known-answer test (edges derived from Python's `ast`, then looked up in the index) on two projects: 0 of 6 function-as-argument sites had an edge: four thread hand-offs (`asyncio.to_thread(f, ...)`, `anyio.to_thread.run_sync(f)`), one `pool.map(f, xs)`, and one keyword argument (`review_fn=f`). The sample is small because the pattern is rare in those projects; direct-call controls scored 78 of 80. Those counts are from 1.3.11; one of the two projects was re-indexed with 1.6.12 and its three sites still have no edge.

### Environment

gitnexus 1.6.12 (npx), Node 20.19.5, Windows 11 for the reproducer above.

Update: rebased on current `main` (resolves the conflict with #3926's canonical chunk order); the review findings are addressed in a separate `fix(php): address route review findings` commit.

## Motivation / context

Refs #3941. GitNexus only recognised `Route::<verb>(...)`. Lumen apps declare routes as `$router-><verb>(...)` inside `routes/*.php` and attach prefixes / namespaces from `bootstrap/app.php` via `$app->router->group([...], function ($router) { require __DIR__.'/../routes/x.php'; })`, so they indexed with zero routes. On a real Lumen 8 service (2,870 files, ~1,340 route declarations) this PR goes from **0 → 1,266 `Route` nodes and 2,472 `HANDLES_ROUTE` edges**, with cross-file prefixes such as `/location/getexistaddresstypes` resolved correctly.

## Areas touched

- [x] `gitnexus/` (CLI / core / MCP server)
- [ ] `gitnexus-web/` (Vite / React UI)
- [ ] `.github/` (workflows, actions)
- [ ] `eval/` or other tooling
- [ ] Docs / agent config only

## Scope & constraints

**In scope**

- `$router-><verb>()` and `$app->router-><verb>()` / `$this->router-><verb>()` for the Lumen Router verbs (`get`, `post`, `put`, `patch`, `delete`, `options`, `head`), in route files only.
- `$router->group([prefix, middleware, namespace, as], fn)` with nesting, following Lumen's merge rules: `as` joined with `.`, routes without `as` inherit the group name, namespaces prepended to string actions unless they start with `\` (a bare `\` resets to the root namespace), string middleware split on `|`.
- Action forms `'Ctrl@m'`, `'Full\Ns\Ctrl@m'`, `['uses' => 'Ctrl@m', 'as' => ..., 'middleware' => ...]`, closures.
- `uses` arrays and group `namespace` for `Route::` too (Laravel ≤ 7). Group namespaces only apply to string actions, never to `Ctrl::class`; inner `\Ns` resets the namespace like `RouteGroup::formatNamespace`.
- Cross-file group/require bindings: extracted per PHP file in the worker (cheap content pre-check, iterative walk) and resolved once in `parse-impl`, mirroring the FastAPI router-prefix pass. A binding applies only when the required path resolves to an indexed `routes/*.php` file — never guessed. Outer context composes before in-file groups. PHP include semantics are followed: path operands concatenate verbatim (`__DIR__ . '/../routes/web' . '.php'`), requires nested under `if` / loops / blocks inside the group are bound, requires inside functions or closures the group does not run are not, and a `require_once` / `include_once` of a routes file that already ran adds no second context.
- Controller methods resolve case-insensitively (PHP semantics) only as a unique fallback when the exact lookup finds no match, and only to a `Method` (never a free function); each call site keeps its existing exact-match policy.
- The route URI is the first argument only. Pure string-literal concatenation is folded; non-literal / interpolated URIs keep the extracted route with `routePath: null` (handler `CALLS` edge kept, no `Route` node) instead of mis-reading a later argument as the path. Double-quoted literals decode PHP escapes (`\n`, `\$`, octal, `\x..`, `\u{..}`); single-quoted literals only unescape `\\` and `\'`.

**Explicitly out of scope / not done here**

- Persisting middleware / route name onto `Route` nodes (they are correct on `ExtractedRoute` and in the named-route registry, as today for Laravel).
- `$app->router-><verb>()` declared directly in non-route files (e.g. inside `bootstrap/app.php`); transitive requires between route files; a file required both inside and outside a group.
- FastRoute path syntax normalisation (`[/{optional}]`, `{name:regex}`) — paths are stored as declared.
- Laravel `RouteServiceProvider` `Route::prefix(...)->group(base_path('routes/api.php'))` cross-file prefixes.
- Arrow-function group bodies (`fn ($router) => ...`) — pre-existing limitation shared with `Route::`.
- Eloquent `QUERIES`, Laravel DI `INJECTS`, queues/events — follow-up PRs under #3941.

## Implementation notes

- `route-extractors/laravel.ts` stays the single owner of per-file PHP route facts; `route-extractors/php-route-group.ts` owns group composition with an explicit receiver kind (Lumen vs Laravel); `php-router-require-bindings.ts` / `php-router-require-context.ts` own the cross-file pass.
- New optional `ParseWorkerResult.phpRouterRequireBindings` (old parse caches tolerated via `?? []`; cache identity hashes `core/ingestion`). `mergeChunkResults` returns it in file-path order like every other per-file fact (#3926).
- `SymbolTableReader.lookupExactUniqueCaseInsensitive` (Method only) backs the case-insensitive fallback.
- Routes-phase admission changed from `!route.routePath` to `route.routePath == null` so a Lumen `$router->get('', ...)` inside a prefixed group becomes the group path. No other `ExtractedRoute` producer emits `''` (Django returns `null` for empty strings, tRPC paths start with `/trpc/`).
- `Route::` behaviour: a differential probe over common Laravel syntax (fluent/array groups, nested `name()`, resources, `controller()` groups, `match`, `any`, empty and non-literal URIs) is byte-identical to `main` except that non-literal URIs (`Route::get($uri, 'C@m')`, `'/a/' . $v`) no longer produce a bogus `C@m` path. Other intentional `Route::` deltas: `uses` arrays, double-quoted middleware, `Route::match` URI, group-namespace prefixing of string actions.

## Testing & verification

- [x] `cd gitnexus && npx tsc --noEmit`
- [x] `cd gitnexus && npm run test:unit` — 26065 pass; the same 13 failures in the same 9 files as on `main` in my environment (embedding recovery, vendored FTS paths, wiki LLM config, scenario-map, claude-hook launcher, analyzer identity, test-completeness); all new and route-related tests pass.
- [x] `cd gitnexus && npm run test:integration` — 8794 pass. The 3 failures in `analyze-cli-embedding-phases.test.ts` fail identically on `main` here (`Resource budget 2048 MiB cannot admit parser/model work`). Two cases in `analyze-staged-embedding-recovery.test.ts` hit the 120s timeout under full-suite load and pass when that file is run alone (8/8).
- [x] Focused: `lumen-route-extraction`, `php-router-require-bindings`, `laravel-route-extraction`, `call-processor-routes`, `resolve-route-handler-symbols`, `symbol-table`, `result-merge`, `merge-chunk-order`, `lumen-route-resolution` / `laravel-route-resolution` integration, `grammar-literal-validation`. Each review fix has a test that fails without it.
- [x] `npx prettier --check` / `npx eslint` on changed files (0 errors).
- [x] Manual: `analyze --index-only` on a private Lumen 8 service (numbers above, unchanged by the review fixes).

## Risk & rollout

Additive for Lumen. Laravel `Route::` output unchanged apart from the documented fixes. Users need `npx gitnexus analyze` to pick up new routes.

## Checklist

- [x] PR body meets repo minimum length
- [ ] If `AGENTS.md` / overlays changed — n/a
- [x] No secrets, tokens, or machine-specific paths committed

title: fix(ingestion): close resolver, import and benchmark review gaps
body:
## Summary

Dart and Ruby calls are now resolved by lexical ownership instead of name guesses, Dart imports follow each library's public export surface, and every parse batch keeps the file that emitted each relationship. The benchmarks that guard this work now count the work itself, not only wall time.

This PR carries the follow-ups from the review of 26 merged PRs, and the fixes from the review of this PR itself (28 threads, all resolved).

```text
capture → lexical bindings and public exports → owned receiver resolution
worker facts → exact origin file → canonical merge → cache replay
benchmarks → phase-specific CPU + actual work counts + scaling checks
```

## Motivation / context

| Reviewed PRs | Disposition in this PR |
| --- | --- |
| #3925, #3903, #3904 | Static, factory, operator and local-function bodies own their bindings; closures keep the right receiver. A local function's return type stays in its declaring scope. `_` is a wildcard or a binding according to the package language version. Branch conditions, else arms and for-in iterables see the outer receiver. |
| #3876 | Call-result locals are inferred per lexical binding. Captured writes invalidate them. Unique instance methods and qualified awaited return types are followed. Cascades resolve through their head, past comments. |
| #3882, #3910 | Imports resolve through public export closures: cycles, diamonds, ambiguity, `show` / `hide`. An export does not import its names locally. A plain import stays one import per directive. |
| #3905, #3880, #3871 | Ruby untyped locals no longer borrow an accessor's or an outer type. A local never stops an explicit call of the same name. Heredoc bodies are ordered at their opener. First-statement accessor annotations are captured. |
| #3926 | Worker relationships carry their origin file, including duplicate endpoint identities. Cold and warm cache graphs are equal. |
| #3928 | Ownerless field/type registrations are removed, after whole-corpus graph parity and zero ownerless-registry reads. |
| #3929 | Projected route/fetch rows are ordered before duplicate selection. |
| #3934, #3875 | Java on-demand imports are not re-exports, for the package form and the static form. |
| #3920, #3912 | Benchmarks count real ancestor probes and Map key iterations. |
| #3908 | Namespace snapshots are shared across scopes that have no facts about an imported name. Generated import ranges are one-based. |
| #3919, #3900 | Accessor/parameter scaling gates are kept. Hydration CPU is measured separately from interning, with the 5% error budget split across metrics and looks. |
| #3879 | The Claude hook reads `rg` and GNU `grep` options from one table per tool. It declines a command whose query cannot be read reliably: an option the tool does not have, an ambiguous prefix, a pattern file. |
| #3867, #3933, #3911, #3877, #3894, #3893 | No remaining code change after reviewing the merged state. |

Related: #3915 (namespace snapshots, crowded-file binding merges, surviving Ruby free-call ownership and Dart initializer ancestry now have the `bench/scope-processing` gate).

Related: #3695 (not closed; see out of scope).

## Areas touched

- [x] `gitnexus/` (CLI / core / MCP server): ingestion, scope resolution, Claude hook, tests, benchmarks
- [x] `gitnexus-shared/` (opt-in provider contracts, finalization, name claims)
- [x] `.github/` (scope-processing step, full Dart closure sampling)
- [x] Docs: Dart and Ruby language-gap pages

## Scope & constraints

**In scope**

- Every actionable item from the 26-PR review, and every thread of this PR's review.

**Explicitly out of scope / not done here**

- The large-repository report listed under Related: the reporter confirmed that parsing, scope resolution and CSV generation complete. Checkpointing exhausted the buffer pool on a 3.6 GB host. This PR makes no claim about a larger host.
- The antigravity, cursor, factory and opencode hooks keep their own copies of the search-option parser.
- The shared `walkNamedTree` still recurses. It limits one deep shape (about 1,000 closures nested inside a class method) and predates this PR.
- Ruby keeps one type fact per local name. A read governed by one class's constructor gets no edge when a later write of another class owns the fact.

## Implementation notes

- **Shared code stays language-neutral.** New behaviour is opt-in through `ScopeResolver` hooks (`mergeBindingsAreAssociative`, `populateImportNamespaces`, `namespaceExportsFromModuleExports`, `followsInstanceCallResultTypes`, `reportedUnboundReceiverNames`, `requiresPostExtractSourceText`) and optional fields (`ParsedImport.exportsOnly` / `nameFilters`, wildcard `reexportsName`, `NameClaim.neverCallee` / `availableSpans` / `order`, `NameLookupOptions.callee`). Only Dart, Ruby and Java set them.
- **Dart imports.** Each library's names are published once per (library, `show`/`hide` list) in the per-namespace binding channel that Swift and C# use. Importers list the tables they see. Shared wildcard expansion also honours `nameFilters`.
- **Dart language version.** The default is 3.7. A leading `// @dart=` override or the package's SDK lower bound selects the older `_` rule. The capture records whether it depends on that version, so only those files of a pre-3.7 package are captured again, on cold and warm runs.
- **Refusals over guesses.** A name that reaches a library as two declarations is not exported, and stays refused in libraries that re-export it. A call result is not typed through a function that two plain imports declare differently. The name fallback does not bind a bare call to another function's local callable, or to a name the file only exports. These sites record an outcome.
- **Facts that outlive object identity.** Library facts and the local-callable index are carried on the `ParsedFile`, so they hold when disk scope mode replaces the file objects.
- Private relationship origin metadata is removed before graph publication.

## Evidence

Measured on a shared, loaded machine. Counters and peak memory are the claims; wall time is context.

| Shape | Merge base | This PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 800 files import a 1,600-name barrel | 295 MB peak, 1.8 s | 308 MB peak, 1.8 s; 816 `ParsedImport`s before and after the export pass |
| 800 files import one 1,600-name library directly | 903 MB peak, 19.6 s | 302 MB peak, 2.9 s |
| 16,000 same-named bindings in one scope | Ruby 20.9 s, Dart 24.5 s | Ruby 36 ms, Dart 27 ms |
| Native parent reads, 16 → 128 nested sites | Ruby 546 → 25,802; Dart 219 → 8,899 | linear; gated by `bench/scope-processing` |
| Nested Dart closures the capture walk accepts | 700 | at least 20,000 (explicit stack) |
| Pre-3.7 Dart package, 800 cached files, 40 with a `_` parameter | no language-version handling | the 40 files are captured again, the other 760 are not; warm graph equals cold graph over 13 metadata-only steps |
| 1,000-file `export` chain | no export closure | 499,500 name visits, bounded by the exported entries |

Capture baselines were re-recorded for Ruby (local claims, four accessor annotations) and Dart (import-filter metadata, branch and loop ranges). Timing budgets are unchanged.

## Testing & verification

- [x] `cd gitnexus && node scripts/build.js`
- [x] `npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json`, `npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.test.json`, and `npx tsc --noEmit` in `gitnexus-shared/`
- [x] `npx eslint` (0 errors) and `npx prettier --check` on the changed files
- [x] `npx vitest run` on every changed test file plus all of `test/integration/resolvers`, `test/unit/scope-resolution` and `test/unit/group`: 507 files, 12,600 passed, 0 failed, 63 skipped (at 9162cc626). The refactor commit after it had the same run: two failures came from editing files while it ran, and both pass on a re-run. The three test and hook commits after that were run against their own suites.
- [x] `node --import tsx bench/<name>/measure.mjs --check` for `scope-processing`, `scope-capture` (17 languages), `ruby-bare-reads`, `ownership-reconcile`, `ruby-block-param-stop`; `bench/dart-closure-binders/measure.mjs --full --check`
- [ ] `cd gitnexus && npm test` in full: not repeated on the final head. Hosted CI runs it.
- [x] `cd gitnexus-web`: 47 test files / 525 tests, typecheck and build, on the first commit. Not repeated after the review fixes, which do not touch the web package.

Each review fix has a regression test that fails on the pre-fix code. Mutation runs back the pins for the show/hide filters, the export-closure rules, the Java on-demand flags and the associative-merge opt-in.

Graph change analysis, merge base to head: CRITICAL risk on the first commit (402 symbols, 30 flows). The review-fix range (426e030cd..9162cc626) is HIGH: 50 files, 74 symbols, 8 flows through `emitFreeCallFallback`. Neither result is partial or truncated.

Process note: some symbol edits in the first commit lack a recorded pre-edit impact receipt. The review-fix commits have one per edited symbol; three were taken after the edit (`ScopeResolutionIndexes`, `computeReceiverText`, `parenthesizedReceiver`).

## Risk & rollout

**Door:** two-way. Revert, rebuild and re-analyze. The parse-cache identity hashes the ingestion sources, so existing caches are discarded on upgrade. No database schema migration.

**Blast radius:** ingestion. Import finalization, name lookup and receiver resolution are shared by every language. Behaviour changes are opt-in per provider; the TypeScript, Python, JavaScript and PHP resolver suites pass without change. Hosted platform checks must pass before merge.

**Graph changes users will see:** Dart and Ruby graphs lose guessed edges and gain owned ones. Sites that are refused carry a recorded outcome (`receiver-unresolved`, `fallback-refused`).

## Checklist

- [x] PR body meets repo minimum length
- [x] `AGENTS.md` / overlays unchanged
- [x] No secrets, tokens, or machine-specific paths committed
- [x] Benchmark budgets preserved; changed fingerprints audited
- [x] Hosted CI passed on 4aaabe007: 88 checks pass, 5 skipped. Vercel fails on fork deploy authorization, which no change in this PR can affect.

title: feat(devcontainer): provision the Claude Code and Codex agent setup
body:
## Summary

The dev container now finishes creation by running `.devcontainer/agent-setup.cjs`, an idempotent script that makes the seeded Claude Code and Codex setup work in the Linux container and installs the repository's agent tooling. It is safe to re-run by hand: `node .devcontainer/agent-setup.cjs`.

## Motivation / context

The config volumes are seeded once from the host. On a Windows host that copy carries entries that cannot work in the container, and two more things had to be fixed by hand in every new container:

- `~/.codex/config.toml` and `~/.claude.json` name MCP servers, a `notify` program and plugin marketplaces by `C:\` paths. They fail on every start.
- The container cannot create user namespaces (`unshare -U true` fails), so Codex's bubblewrap sandbox cannot start and every sandboxed command fails.
- A freshly seeded Codex config names Git plugin marketplaces whose snapshots were not copied with it, so `codex plugin list` errors and no plugin loads.

Hand fixes survive a rebuild but not a volume reset, a fresh clone or another machine.

## Areas touched

- [ ] `gitnexus/` (CLI / core / MCP server)
- [ ] `gitnexus-web/` (Vite / React UI)
- [ ] `.github/` (workflows, actions)
- [x] `eval/` or other tooling (`.devcontainer/`)
- [x] Docs / agent config only (`.devcontainer/README.md`, `.claude/skills/pr-tri-review/`)

## Scope & constraints

**In scope**

- `agent-setup.cjs`, called at the end of `post-create.sh`. Each step checks the current state and changes nothing that is already right; a failed step is reported and the rest still run, so a missing network or CLI never fails container creation. `GITNEXUS_AGENT_SETUP=off` skips it.
  - Codex config: remove Windows-only MCP servers, marketplaces and `notify`; everything else is kept byte for byte.
  - Codex sandbox: add `sandbox_mode = "danger-full-access"` and `approval_policy = "on-request"` only when user namespaces are unavailable and the config chooses no sandbox mode.
  - Codex guard: install `codex-guard.cjs` as a `PreToolUse` hook.
  - Claude config: remove MCP servers started by a Windows executable.
  - Side panels: install the `side-panels` Claude Code mod and add it to `CLAUDE_CODE_PLUGIN_DIRS`.
  - Codex plugins: refetch the marketplace snapshots the seeded config names; install `compound-engineering` and `claude-mem` for Codex when they are enabled in Claude Code.
  - `pr-tri-review`: the skill is now tracked, and Codex gets an entry skill that points at it.
- `codex-guard.cjs`: refuses recursive deletes of protected roots, `git push --force`, pushes to `main`, `git clean -x`, `npm publish`, `gh repo|release delete`, and disk or power commands. It parses quoting, so text that only mentions such a command is allowed.
- README section "Agent setup".

**Explicitly out of scope / not done here**

- Trusting the new Codex hook. Codex runs a new hook only after the person approves it in `/hooks`; the script cannot and does not do that.
- Personal preferences: models and effort, status line, which plugins are enabled, Claude Code's auto-mode description.
- MCP servers at a localhost URL are left alone, since one may be running inside the container.
- The guard does not see commands hidden inside `$(...)` substitutions or built from variables.
- The mod's own tests need the Claude Code CLI and are not wired into CI.

## Implementation notes

- **Full access is a deliberate default, and reviewers should weigh it.** It applies only where the sandbox cannot start, it is written with a comment naming this script, and deleting the two lines restores the Codex defaults. The guard is the compensating control, and it is inactive until trusted.
- claude-mem is added to Codex from the checkout Claude Code already runs, so both CLIs share one version, worker and store. `npx claude-mem install` is avoided because it also re-copies Claude's plugin and restarts the shared worker.
- The first original of each config file the script changes is kept beside it as `<file>.before-agent-setup`.
- The mod is installed to `~/.claude/mods` and not loaded from the repo path, because Claude Code writes generated type files into a loaded mod folder.
- This publishes maintainer tooling that was local until now: the side-panels mod and the `pr-tri-review` skill.

## Testing & verification

- `node --test .devcontainer/*.test.cjs`: 178 pass, 56 of them new (`agent-setup.test.cjs`, `codex-guard.test.cjs`).
- `prettier --check` and `eslint` on the new files: clean.
- `bash -n .devcontainer/post-create.sh`.
- From scratch: a scratch `HOME`/`CODEX_HOME` built from a real Windows-seeded config. The first run removed every host-only entry, installed the guard, the mod and both Codex plugins; a second run rewrote no config, hook or settings file.
- On a container already set up by hand: no config file changed.
- `claude plugin validate` and `claude plugin test` on the mod: valid, 5 tests pass.
- Not run: the `gitnexus` and `gitnexus-web` suites (no file under those packages changed), and a full container rebuild.
- GitNexus `detect_changes` could not run: the worktree is not indexed and `.devcontainer/` is not in the graph. A text search found no image or lifecycle file that references the new files.

## Risk & rollout

- Existing containers are unaffected until someone runs the script or recreates the container.
- On creation the script edits `~/.codex/config.toml`, `~/.codex/hooks.json`, `~/.claude.json` and `~/.claude/settings.json` in the container's own volumes; the host snapshot is read-only and untouched.
- The Codex plugin step needs network access and is skipped with a message when it fails.

## Checklist

- [x] PR body meets repo minimum length (workflow may label short descriptions)

title: cypher output is truncated at 65,536 bytes when stdout is a pipe (Linux), exit code 0
body:
### Area

gitnexus (CLI / core / indexing / MCP server)

### Summary

On Linux, `gitnexus cypher` (and presumably the other direct tool commands that share `output()`) truncates its result at exactly 65,536 bytes when stdout is a pipe. Redirecting to a file gives the full result. The exit code is 0 either way, so a script that pipes the output gets invalid JSON, or a short result, with no error signal.

65,536 bytes is the default Linux pipe capacity. In `dist/cli/tool.js`, `output()` makes one `writeSync(1, text + '\n')` call and ignores its return value. On a pipe that call can write fewer bytes than requested, and the remainder is dropped. I have read the code but not tested a patch.

### Steps to reproduce

```bash
mkdir repo && cd repo
python3 -c "
for i in range(1500):
    open(f'module_with_a_long_name_{i:04d}.py','w').write(f'def function_number_{i:04d}():\n    return {i}\n')
"
git init -q && git add . && git commit -qm init
gitnexus analyze .

Q="MATCH (f:Function) RETURN f.name AS name, f.filePath AS file"
gitnexus cypher "$Q" --limit 100000 2>/dev/null | wc -c          # 65536
gitnexus cypher "$Q" --limit 100000 2>/dev/null > out.json; wc -c < out.json   # 90072
```

### Expected behavior

The same complete JSON through a pipe as into a file.

### Actual behavior

| stdout is | bytes received | valid JSON |
| --- | --- | --- |
| a file | 90,072 | yes |
| a pipe (`\| wc -c`, `\| cat`, Python `subprocess` with `capture_output=True`) | 65,536 | no (`Unterminated string`) |

Exit code is 0 in both cases. Results under 64 KiB are unaffected, which is why it is easy to miss on small repositories.

On Windows 11 (Node 20.19.5) the same version returns the full result through a pipe (201,845 bytes both ways on a different index), so this looks POSIX-specific.

### Context

Found from a Python service that runs `gitnexus cypher` with `subprocess.run(..., capture_output=True)` to read all `IMPORTS` edges of a repository. It worked on repositories with a few hundred edges and failed to parse on one with 982. Workaround: pass a temporary file as stdout.

A possible fix is to loop on the return value of `writeSync` until the whole buffer is written, retrying on `EAGAIN`.

### Environment

gitnexus 1.6.12 (global npm install), Node 22.22.0, Linux x86_64 (Ubuntu 24.04).

title: Tracking: reliability, performance and accuracy priorities — November 2026
body:
## Purpose and scope

This is the active successor to #3609. Prioritize correct results and verified stable delivery, then performance and accuracy, before broader feature expansion.

**19 November 2026 — 7 of 32 direct sub-issues closed, 25 open.** Fixes have merged for both P1 bugs reproduced in the 15 November audit. The eight open P1s still need affected-host or workload evidence, including Windows verification for stable delivery. The original scope covers 31 engineering issues and one cleanup item. Priorities guide the work queue independently of release commitments and GitHub project fields.

| Priority | At creation | Closed | Open | Focus |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |
| P1 | 10 | 2 | 8 | Incorrect results, index integrity, stable delivery, native crashes and hangs |
| P2 | 14 | 5 | 9 | Performance, graph/taint accuracy, evaluation, tests and workflow correctness |
| P3 | 7 | 0 | 7 | New capabilities and remaining installation behaviour |
| Cleanup | 1 | 0 | 1 | Promotional submission |
| **Total** | **32** | **7** | **25** | |

At creation, this tracker combined the six remaining direct children of #3609 (#3530, #3500, #2193, #264, #663, #713) with the 26 then-open issues numbered above it through #3947. Ten of those newer issues were already mentioned as follow-ups in #3609; they are counted once. This tracker brought the other 16 into the queue.

The old tracker preserves the original 33-issue triage, dated audits, release ledger, merged performance/evaluation work and duplicate analysis. Before moving its open children, 31 of its 37 direct sub-issues were closed. #3849–#3852 are all completed, despite the stale unchecked entries in the old body. This successor starts with the unresolved work only; its smaller denominator must not be presented as a loss of completed work.

## Execution order

1. Verify the full release candidate on Windows for **#3818** (identity after edit → revert → edit) and **#3706** (native queries and FTS). Collect the GPU, macOS, memory and recovery evidence specified in the other six open P1 rows in parallel.
2. Obtain the reporter’s CPU profile for **#3870**. Reconcile **#3915** with the four benchmark cases in merged **#3945** and verify the remaining group-sync ordering in **#3930**. Decide the graph-output policy for **#3924** before implementing a cap.
3. Review **#3978** for the stale-index hint in **#3897**. The grep-as-filter report **#3899** needs its own regression case.
4. Continue **#3500** with draft **#3838**, a corrected-oracle rerun and a pinned baseline comparison. Refresh the remaining **#3785** test inventory after merged **#3833**.
5. Continue review of the PHP and PL/SQL contributions **#3944** and **#3772** independently of stabilization.

## Status and completion rules

- **Open** alone does not mean active implementation. Each item below identifies a PR, a verification task, a pending decision or the absence of an identified fix.
- Track **merged**, **released in a named version**, and **verified on the affected workload/host** separately.
- A mitigation, diagnostic, dependency upgrade or related PR is not proof that the original failure is fixed.
- Keep the native-storage reports separate unless evidence establishes a common cause. In particular, #3530's original EOF is not explained merely by a later engine fix.
- A checkbox is complete when the linked issue's remaining acceptance criteria and evidence are satisfied. Record narrowed or superseded scope explicitly; do not silently drop it.
- Current priorities come from impact, dependencies and implementation readiness. No emergency P0 classification is established by this audit.

## Stable delivery

As of 19 November, GitHub’s latest stable release and npm’s `latest` are **1.6.12** (LadybugDB core **0.18.3**). npm’s `rc` is **1.6.13-rc.240** (core **0.22.0**). **#3818 stays open** pending the full-package Windows identity check and a named stable release. Closed #3804 also requested stable distribution of dependency fixes. [GitHub stable release](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/releases/tag/v1.6.12) · [npm stable package](https://registry.npmjs.org/gitnexus/1.6.12) · [npm release candidate](https://registry.npmjs.org/gitnexus/1.6.13-rc.240)

The source revision published as rc.240 contains #3848, #3953, #3954 and #3957. The branch-name fix #3981 merged to `main` after that candidate. [Candidate commit history](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/compare/160c630134bbf266fe914db9666bb825ee3708a7...c2ff25fc831e418045900fbaf944e37340776986) · [Candidate compared with the reviewed main revision](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/compare/c2ff25fc831e418045900fbaf944e37340776986...495a72cc3adbb49b673e9be98c242c780db7b608)

## Main validation — 15 November 2026

[Full P1 audit and per-issue evidence](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/issues/3948#issuecomment-6897451933), pinned to main `171583ab1`: **812 tests passed across 25 files, 41 skipped**; a separate strict native rerun passed **70 tests with zero skips** (not added to the 812). Fresh build and typecheck passed. All 10 P1s were open on 15 November. That audit reproduced #3947 and #3895, both since closed, and recorded passing Linux controls for #3706. The Windows check remains open.

## P1 — Integrity, delivery and blocking failures

- [x] #3947 — **CLI output through pipes.** #3953 fixed short writes in the shared output writer. Its regression test compared a 5,000-row result (over 256 KiB) through a Linux pipe and a file and passed against the rebuilt CLI. [Original reproduction](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/issues/3947#issuecomment-6897355057) · [Fix and test](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/pull/3953)

- [x] #3895 — **Hook selects the active worktree’s index.** #3954 fixed all three shipped registry helpers. Its regression covers a longer main-checkout path and both registry orders. [Original reproduction](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/issues/3895#issuecomment-6897355359) · [Fix and test](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/pull/3954)

- [ ] #3685 — **DirectML embeddings disagree with CPU.** The 15 November audit found that main accepts DirectML without a CPU/vector parity gate at initialization. Affected-device verification is outstanding. [Audit evidence](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/issues/3685#issuecomment-6897376910).
  **Next:** Run the same model/texts on the affected GPU or implement and test the requested warning/fallback or device restriction.

- [ ] #3818 — **Windows identity corruption still reaches stable users.** Linux identity/incremental controls pass. npm latest remains 1.6.12/core 0.18.3; full-package Windows verification and stable delivery remain open. [Audit evidence](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/issues/3818#issuecomment-6897432816).
  **Next:** Verify the reported edit → revert → edit sequence with the full updated package, then record the stable version delivering that verified fix.

- [ ] #3898 — **Native COPY deadlock on macOS.** Linux native ingestion/COPY controls passed on 15 November. The reported macOS/Node 25 Swift/Objective-C workload still needs a retest. [Audit evidence](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/issues/3898#issuecomment-6897377201).
  **Next:** Retest the complete current package on the affected macOS workload; demonstrate completion or a bounded diagnostic.

- [ ] #3706 — **Windows native query shapes crash or hang.** Core 0.22.0 contains the upstream fix; API-impact suites and eight native query shapes pass on Linux. Current-package Windows acceptance is pending. [Audit evidence](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/issues/3706#issuecomment-6897433060).
  **Next:** Prioritize the exact API/route/node query and FTS checks on Windows, and add the missing cross-platform test registration.

- [ ] #3696 — **Upstream impact query exhausts native memory.** Containment is verified: a real impact process exits 70 with the active-query diagnosis under a forced low limit; guard/frontier/lifetime tests pass. [Audit evidence](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/issues/3696#issuecomment-6897433340).
  **Next:** Verify bounded successful completion on the original graph and capture the generated Cypher/trace; guard termination is not a root-fix result.

- [ ] #3687 — **WAL recovery enters a recurring native crash loop.** Linux interrupted-checkpoint, orphan and WAL controls passed on 15 November. The affected deletion-replay store was unavailable. [Audit evidence](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/issues/3687#issuecomment-6897433606).
  **Next:** Test a preserved copy of the affected store and sidecars; require safe recovery or a usable failure while retaining recoverable work.

- [ ] #3692 — **Interrupted index causes a Windows access violation.** Linux recovery controls passed on 15 November. Recovery of the interrupted Windows store written by core 0.18.3 remains unverified. [Audit evidence](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/issues/3692#issuecomment-6897433913).
  **Next:** Verify old-store compatibility and current dirty-state recovery on Windows; require safe recovery or a usable nonzero diagnostic.

- [ ] #3530 — **Atomic staging reads past EOF during embedding cleanup.** Staging, recovery and diagnostic controls pass; a strict native rerun passed 70 tests without skips. The original natural EOF remains unverified. [Audit evidence](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/issues/3530#issuecomment-6897434154).
  **Next:** Retest the affected mount/workload with the current publication flow and capture exact staging-file sizes, sidecars and checkpoint evidence.

## P2 — Performance, accuracy and workflow correctness

- [x] #3695 — **Java indexing on the original unsharded branch.** The reporter’s rc.227 run on commit `d02dbfdc818` finished COPY and checkpoint with exit 0 in 4.85 hours (581,682 nodes and 907,584 edges). The reporter bypassed memory admission locally on the 3.6 GB host. Scope resolution and import emission used the packaged code. [Affected-host run and patch details](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/issues/3695#issuecomment-6897630621)

- [ ] #3870 — **Embedding phase regressed on a large repository.** #3874 merged vector-store and embedding improvements, but explicitly leaves the reporter's main-thread behaviour unexplained.
  **Next:** Obtain the reporter's CPU profile and repeat the workload on the updated package before claiming the regression resolved.

- [x] #3915 — **Remaining super-linear ingestion costs.** #3920, #3934 and #3945 have merged. #3945 adds a benchmark gate for namespace snapshots, crowded-file binding merges, Ruby free-call ownership and Dart initializer ancestry. [Benchmark evidence](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/pull/3945)
  **Next:** Reconcile the four unchecked cases in #3915 against the merged measurements and record any residual cost.

- [ ] #3924 — **Property-dispatch edge explosion needs a policy decision.** Proposal only: the cap changes graph output; implementation awaits the maintainer's default/opt-in decision.
  **Next:** Make the semantics decision early, then require before/after graph evidence, bounded emission and explicit reporting of omitted edges.

- [x] #3942 — **Python module-constant reads.** #3957 added `ACCESSES` edges for supported bare-name reads of local and imported constants. The issue’s reproduction is now a regression test for `context` and upstream `impact`. Additional expression forms remain documented. [Closure and coverage limits](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/issues/3942#issuecomment-6922801996)

- [x] #3943 — **Python functions passed as arguments.** #3957 added `USES` edges for bare callables passed as positional or keyword arguments, including the reported `to_thread` and `map` cases. Attribute-valued arguments such as `self.method` remain outside that coverage. [Closure and coverage limits](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/issues/3943#issuecomment-6922802496)

- [x] #3930 — **Group sync changes output between identical runs.** Merged #3945 orders projected route/fetch rows before duplicate selection. #3930 also reports row-order-dependent owner selection. [Merged ordering change](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/pull/3945)
  **Next:** Verify the containing-owner tie break and compare repeated `group sync` output on the same graph.

- [ ] #3913 — **Taint validation predicates do not act as barriers.** Proposal with false-positive examples; no implementation PR identified.
  **Next:** Define proven guard semantics and branch/data-flow conditions, then pin guarded and unguarded cases. Predicate naming alone must not suppress findings.

- [ ] #3500 — **Agent accuracy and cost benefit remain unestablished.** Oracle and context-integrity fixes have merged; evidence-retention PR #3838 remains a draft. Historical runs have material limitations.
  **Next:** Retain the evidence, revalidate affected filtering outcomes under the corrected oracle with provenance, resolve remaining wrong-target examples, then measure a pinned candidate against a no-GitNexus baseline.

- [ ] #3785 — **Test scenario map contains gaps and weak evidence.** Several improvements are merged. #3833 is now merged too; that closes one coverage slice, not this audit.
  **Next:** Refresh the remaining scenario inventory and verify specific gaps; advisory fingerprints or a single test PR are not whole-audit completion.

- [x] #3618 — **`--no-stats` on an up-to-date index.** #3848 merged. Its end-to-end check removed the counts from both managed files on the fast path and restored them when the flag was omitted. [Fix and verification](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/pull/3848)

- [x] #3896 — **Evidence capture accepts valid branch names.** #3981 merged on 19 November. Regression tests cover `feature/c++`, `fix/@scope` and Unicode names, including continued protection of Git administrative paths. [Fix and verification](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/pull/3981)

- [x] #3897 — **Stale-index hints miss Git global options.** Open PR #3978 covers the Claude and Antigravity adapters, including the target checkout for `git -C`. [Proposed fix and test cases](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/pull/3978)
  **Next:** Review the adapters’ behaviour for `-c`, `-C` and commands touching multiple checkouts.

- [x] #3899 — **Hook runs graph queries for grep used as a filter.** #3978 explicitly leaves this separate from Git mutation detection.
  **Next:** Pin the compound-shell filtering example and verify that augmentation runs only for a reliably identified code-search query.

## P3 — Enhancements and scope decisions

- [ ] #3941 — **PHP framework layers are missing.** Open #3944 implements the first of four planned parts: Lumen and legacy Laravel routes.
  **Next:** Continue bounded review; keep Eloquent, DI and queues/events as separate acceptance slices. Do not make these prerequisites for stabilization.

- [ ] #3771 — **Oracle PL/SQL support.** Implementation #3772 is open; parser and integration choices are under review.
  **Next:** Complete the architecture and implementation review with the language's acceptance evidence.

- [ ] #3631 — **Cross-branch embedding and graph reuse.** Requested reuse across divergent branches exceeds existing shared-store behaviour; no dedicated implementation PR identified.
  **Next:** Scope embedding reuse separately from graph reuse and preserve branch/model identity and deletion isolation.

- [ ] #2193 — **Workspace and system-level graph.** Groups and multi-repository query cover part of the use case.
  **Next:** Define the remaining workspace UX and infrastructure/test/document graph on top of existing Groups; avoid duplicating the graph system.

- [ ] #264 — **Global installation without duplicated project files.** Global setup and index-only options exist; the complete no-duplication workflow still needs acceptance.
  **Next:** Coordinate with #663, verify the end-to-end installation/update workflow, and document the remaining behaviour explicitly.

- [ ] #663 — **Plugin distribution and default file generation.** The plugin exists; default repo-file generation and requested indexing behaviour remain open.
  **Next:** Keep its acceptance criteria distinct from #264. Decide and verify the remaining defaults rather than reimplementing plugin packaging.

- [ ] #3914 — **Resource ownership and lifetime are absent from the graph.** Design discussion; no implementation PR identified.
  **Next:** Specify provider-backed ownership/acquisition/cleanup facts and unknown semantics before adding the graph relations.

## Cleanup

- [ ] #713 — **Promotional badge submission.** No product engineering work is required; the previous tracker recommends closure as not planned.
  **Next:** Close separately as not planned during housekeeping. Its presence here is not an endorsement of the external security grade.

## Reports filed after this tracker opened

These open reports are linked for triage outside the original 32 direct sub-issues.

- **Index integrity and native failures.** #3958 reports incremental FTS corruption. Merged #3977 improves the failure diagnostic. #3982 reports a vector-index build deadlock, and #3983 reports an MCP server crash and index growth after repeated incremental reindexes.
- **Accuracy and latency.** #3972 reports low upstream-impact accuracy and different results after incremental and full indexing. #3979 and #3980 identify two sources of `list_repos` latency before pagination, Git freshness checks and repeated metadata reads.
- **Workflow and delivery.** #3976 asks to scope generated instructions for documentation-only edits. #3995 asks for more frequent stable releases.

## Historical evidence

- #3609 retains the original triage, dated progress snapshots, completed-issue ledger and performance/evaluation evidence.
- #3500 and draft #3838 retain the agent comparisons and oracle limitations. Revalidations must preserve the original scores and identify the corrected method and provenance.
- #3695 retains the earlier checkpoint failures and the successful rc.227 run, including the reporter’s local memory-admission change.
- The 19 November update checked GitHub issue, sub-issue and PR records and npm package metadata. Test and workload results above are attributed to their dated audits, PRs or reporter runs.

title: Python: dotted import of a src-layout package from tests/ or scripts/ gets no IMPORTS or CALLS edges
body:
### Area

gitnexus (CLI / core / indexing / MCP server)

### Summary

In Python, a dotted absolute import of a package that lives under a sub-folder (the usual `src/` layout) is resolved only when the importing file is itself inside that folder. The same import from `tests/`, `scripts/` or `tools/` produces no `IMPORTS` edge and no `CALLS` edges, although the files are indexed.

The practical effect is that tests and scripts which exercise a function are invisible to `context` and `impact`: a function with thirteen calling files is reported with two callers, because eleven of them are tests and tools.

### Steps to reproduce

```
src/mypkg/__init__.py      (empty)
src/mypkg/core.py
src/mypkg/inside.py
tests/test_core.py
scripts/run.py
```

`src/mypkg/core.py`
```python
def compute(x):
    return x * 2
```

`src/mypkg/inside.py`
```python
from mypkg.core import compute


def use_inside():
    return compute(1)
```

`tests/test_core.py`
```python
from mypkg.core import compute


def test_compute():
    assert compute(2) == 4
```

`scripts/run.py`
```python
import sys

sys.path.insert(0, "src")

from mypkg.core import compute


def main():
    print(compute(3))
```

```bash
git init && git add . && git commit -m init
gitnexus analyze .
gitnexus cypher "MATCH (a)-[r:CodeRelation]->(b) WHERE r.type IN ['CALLS','IMPORTS'] RETURN r.type, a.name, a.filePath, b.name, b.filePath"
```

### Expected behavior

`IMPORTS` edges from `tests/test_core.py` and `scripts/run.py` to `src/mypkg/core.py`, and `CALLS` edges from `test_compute` and `main` to `compute`, as for `src/mypkg/inside.py`.

### Actual behavior

All five files are indexed as `File` nodes. The only edges are from the file inside `src/`:

| type | src | src_file | dst | dst_file |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| CALLS | use_inside | src/mypkg/inside.py | compute | src/mypkg/core.py |
| IMPORTS | inside.py | src/mypkg/inside.py | core.py | src/mypkg/core.py |

### Context

Measured with a known-answer audit over 19 indexed repositories: edges derived from each repository's own source with Python's `ast`, then looked up in the index.

| Kind of edge | In the index |
| --- | --- |
| Direct call, same file | 5,357 of 5,424 |
| Direct call, absolute import, importer inside the source root | 682 of 685 |
| File import, importer inside the source root | 972 of 972 |
| Direct call, single-name import (`import helpers`), importer outside the source root | 159 of 159 |
| **Direct call, dotted package import, importer outside the source root** | **0 of 580** |
| **File import of the same kind** | **1 of 267** |

The gap also appears with a nested root (`data_pipeline/src/pkg/...` imported from `data_pipeline/tests/`).

I can see why resolution might be conservative here: #898 was about dotted imports of external packages being matched to unrelated local files. A resolution that stays safe against that could be limited to roots the repository itself declares or implies, for example a top-level or nested `src/` folder that contains the package's `__init__.py`, the `where` / `package-dir` settings in `pyproject.toml` or `setup.cfg`, or a literal `sys.path.insert(...)` in the importing file, and to dotted names whose full path exists under that root.

### Environment

gitnexus 1.6.12, Node 22.22.0, Linux x86_64 (Ubuntu 24.04).

title: Python: instantiating a class produces no edge to the class or its __init__
body:
### Area

gitnexus (CLI / core / indexing / MCP server)

### Summary

In Python, instantiating a class (`Plain(1)`) produces no edge from the enclosing function to the class or to its `__init__`, whether the class is defined in the same file or imported, and whether it has an explicit `__init__` or is a dataclass. `context` on a class therefore shows no code that creates it, and `impact` on a constructor reports nothing upstream.

Is this intended for Python? I could not find an existing issue for it.

### Steps to reproduce

`models.py`
```python
from dataclasses import dataclass


class Plain:
    def __init__(self, x):
        self.x = x


@dataclass
class Point:
    x: int


def build_local():
    return Plain(2)
```

`core.py`
```python
from models import Plain, Point


def helper():
    return 1


def use_helper():
    return helper()


def make_plain():
    return Plain(1)


def make_point():
    return Point(1)
```

```bash
git init && git add . && git commit -m init
gitnexus analyze .
gitnexus cypher "MATCH (a)-[r:CodeRelation]->(b) WHERE r.type IN ['CALLS','IMPORTS'] RETURN r.type, a.name, a.filePath, label(b), b.name, b.filePath"
```

### Expected behavior

An edge from `build_local`, `make_plain` and `make_point` to the class they instantiate (or to its `__init__` method where one exists), in the same way `use_helper -> helper` is recorded.

### Actual behavior

`Class Plain`, `Class Point` and `Method __init__` exist as nodes. The only edges are:

| type | src | src_file | dst | dst_file |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| CALLS | use_helper | core.py | Function helper | core.py |
| IMPORTS | core.py | core.py | File models.py | models.py |

### Context

Measured with a known-answer audit over 19 indexed Python repositories (edges derived from each repository's source with `ast`, then looked up in the index, accepting an edge to either the class node or its `__init__`):

| Kind of edge | In the index |
| --- | --- |
| Direct function call, same file (control) | 6,462 of 6,543 |
| Class instantiated in the file that defines it | 0 of 948 |
| Imported class instantiated | 28 of 975 |

Across one whole repository of 45 files the index held three `CALLS` edges into `Class` nodes.

### Environment

gitnexus 1.6.12, Node 22.22.0, Linux x86_64 (Ubuntu 24.04).

title: Python: a call to a name imported with `from module import *` gets no CALLS edge
body:
### Area

gitnexus (CLI / core / indexing / MCP server)

### Summary

In Python, a call to a function that reaches the calling module through `from module import *` gets no `CALLS` edge. The file-level `IMPORTS` edge is recorded, so the module is known; the name is just not resolved through the star import.

Code bases that split a large module and keep a `from core import *` at the top of each part lose most of their cross-file call edges this way.

### Steps to reproduce

`core.py`
```python
def helper():
    return 1


def use_helper():
    return helper()
```

`star.py`
```python
from core import *


def via_star():
    return helper()
```

```bash
git init && git add . && git commit -m init
gitnexus analyze .
gitnexus cypher "MATCH (a)-[r:CodeRelation]->(b) WHERE r.type IN ['CALLS','IMPORTS'] RETURN r.type, a.name, a.filePath, b.name, b.filePath"
```

### Expected behavior

`CALLS` from `via_star` to `helper` in `core.py`.

### Actual behavior

| type | src | src_file | dst | dst_file |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| CALLS | use_helper | core.py | helper | core.py |
| IMPORTS | star.py | star.py | core.py | core.py |

### Context

Measured with a known-answer audit over 19 indexed Python repositories (edges derived from each repository's source with `ast`, then looked up in the index):

| Kind of edge | In the index |
| --- | --- |
| Direct call through an explicit relative import (control) | 80 of 80 |
| Direct call through an explicit absolute import from the repo root (control) | 420 of 427 |
| Direct call of a name that arrives through `import *` | 0 of 119 |

The ground truth treats a star import as bringing in the target module's public top-level names (no leading underscore) and follows names the target itself imported; it does not read `__all__`. #3469 covered the related case of a function re-exported by a package `__init__.py`.

### Environment

gitnexus 1.6.12, Node 22.22.0, Linux x86_64 (Ubuntu 24.04).

title: cypher prints a bare [] for an empty result instead of the usual {markdown, row_count} object
body:
### Area

gitnexus (CLI / core / indexing / MCP server)

### Summary

`gitnexus cypher` prints a different JSON shape when a query matches no rows. With rows it prints an object, `{"markdown": ..., "row_count": n}`. With none it prints a bare empty array, `[]`. A script that reads `row_count`, or looks for the object, has to special-case the empty result, and one that does not will treat "no rows" as a malformed response.

A small thing, but it is easy to hit: any lookup for a symbol that has no callers returns it.

### Steps to reproduce

In any indexed repository:

```bash
gitnexus cypher "MATCH (n:Function) WHERE n.name = 'helper' RETURN n.name AS name"
gitnexus cypher "MATCH (n:Function) WHERE n.name = 'no_such_function' RETURN n.name AS name"
```

### Expected behavior

The same shape in both cases, for example:

```json
{
  "markdown": "| name |\n| --- |",
  "row_count": 0
}
```

### Actual behavior

One row:

```json
{
  "markdown": "| name |\n| --- |\n| helper |",
  "row_count": 1
}
```

No rows (exit code 0):

```json
[]
```

### Environment

gitnexus 1.6.12, Node 22.22.0, Linux x86_64 (Ubuntu 24.04).

title: fix(cli): write the whole tool result to stdout through pipes (#3947)
body:
## Summary

Direct CLI tool commands now write their whole result to stdout when stdout is a pipe. Before this change, `gitnexus cypher` (and every other command that prints through the shared `output()` writer) cut the result at exactly 65,536 bytes on Linux and still exited 0.

Fixes #3947. Tracked in #3948 (P1).

## Motivation / context

`output()` in `gitnexus/src/cli/tool.ts` made one `writeSync(1, text)` call and ignored the returned byte count. On POSIX, fd 1 is non-blocking when stdout is a pipe or a socket. So a write larger than the free pipe buffer writes only part of the result, and a full buffer throws `EAGAIN`. The rest was dropped. Callers that read with `| jq`, `| wc -c` or Python `subprocess.run(..., capture_output=True)` got invalid JSON with exit code 0. A file redirect got the full result, and so did Windows pipes.

The audit comment on #3947 reproduced it 3/3 on main: 114,559 bytes to a file, 65,536 bytes through a pipe.

## Areas touched

- [x] `gitnexus/` (CLI / core / MCP server)
- [ ] `gitnexus-web/` (Vite / React UI)
- [ ] `.github/` (workflows, actions)
- [ ] `eval/` or other tooling
- [ ] Docs / agent config only (`AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `.cursor/`, `llms.txt`, etc.)

## Scope & constraints

**In scope**

- `output()` encodes the result once and calls `writeSync(1, bytes, written)` until every byte is written. It treats `EAGAIN` as zero bytes written, and it waits 1 ms with `Atomics.wait` after any attempt that leaves bytes unwritten. It does not spin a core while a reader is slow.
- `EPIPE` (for example `| head -1`) now stops the write and keeps the normal exit-code rules. It no longer calls `process.exit(0)`. With the loop, `EPIPE` can arrive in the middle of a result, and an immediate `exit(0)` would turn an `error` or `partial` result into a clean exit. It would also skip the `cycles_found` exit code that `check` sets after `output()` returns. Tool commands already end by a natural exit, so this matches the success path.
- Any other write error keeps the stderr fallback from #324. When part of the result already reached stdout, the command now also exits 1, because the stdout copy is incomplete.

**Explicitly out of scope / not done here**

- Commands that print through `console.log` or `process.stdout.write` (`analyze` progress, `list`, `status`, `group`). They use the Node stream, which queues unwritten data itself. No report shows truncation there.
- Consolidating the other write-all loops (`embedding-restore-spill.ts`, `sync-csv-writer.ts`, `fs-atomic.ts`). They write regular files, where `EAGAIN` does not occur.
- A timeout for a reader that never drains. The writer now waits like a blocking write does. Ctrl-C still ends it.

## Implementation notes

- The 1 ms wait follows the `sonic-boom` sync flush (the `pino` writer already in `node_modules`), which sleeps 100 ms on `EAGAIN`. At 1 ms, a 64 KiB pipe drained once per wake still moves about 64 MB/s, and a stalled reader costs about 1,000 short sleeps per second.
- Rejected: `process.stdout._handle.setBlocking(true)` (private API, unknown interaction with the LadybugDB stdout capture in #324), async `process.stdout.write` (same #324 capture), and reopening `/dev/stdout` (truncates file redirects and breaks `>>`).
- The offset counts bytes, so a short write that falls inside a multi-byte UTF-8 character is safe.

## Testing & verification

- [x] `cd gitnexus && npx tsc --noEmit` (clean). `npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.test.json` is also clean.
- [x] `npx vitest run test/unit/cli-output-writes.test.ts test/unit/tool-direct-cli.test.ts test/unit/cli-impact-disambiguation.test.ts test/unit/trace-cli.test.ts`: 53 passed.
- [x] `npx vitest run test/integration/cli-limit-e2e.test.ts`: 18 passed, plus the review follow-up case. The run uses the tsx source CLI. The pipe test also passed against the rebuilt `dist` CLI (`GITNEXUS_E2E_CLI=dist`).
- [ ] Full `npm test` was not run locally. CI runs it.

New tests:

- `test/integration/cli-limit-e2e.test.ts` runs a 5,000 row `cypher` result (more than 256 KiB) through a real `pipe(2)` (`sh -c '... | cat'`) and through a file. It compares the parsed results and asserts the CLI's own exit status. Node `spawnSync` `stdio: 'pipe'` is a socketpair on Linux, not a pipe, which is why the existing suites never hit this. On unmodified main this test fails with `expected 65536 to be greater than 262144`. A second case closes the reader early (`| head -c 1`) and asserts exit 0 with no stderr copy. Both skip on Windows.
- `test/unit/cli-output-writes.test.ts` uses a fake fd for short writes that split a multi-byte character, `EAGAIN`, `EPIPE` on clean, `partial` and `check` cycles results, and `EIO` before and after part of the result. Five of the seven cases fail on the old `output()`. The other two pin behavior that must not change.
- The `writeSync` mocks in `tool-direct-cli`, `cli-impact-disambiguation` and `trace-cli` now return the byte count, as the real call does. The `tool-direct-cli` mock records the decoded text, so its existing assertions are unchanged.

## Risk & rollout

- A parent that waits for the CLI to exit before it reads stdout used to get a cut result. It now waits until it reads, like any blocking writer. No in-repo caller does this.
- No index refresh and no migration.

## Checklist

- [x] PR body meets repo minimum length (workflow may label short descriptions)
- [ ] If `AGENTS.md` / overlays changed: headers, scope block, and changelog updated per project conventions
- [x] No secrets, tokens, or machine-specific paths committed
