title: fix(hooks): prefer the active worktree index over the main checkout
body:
## Summary

Hooks now select a registered linked worktree’s own index even when the main checkout has a longer absolute path. This prevents a fresh worktree index from producing a false stale warning after a commit.

## Motivation / context

Fixes #3895.

The issue’s [follow-up reproduction](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/issues/3895#issuecomment-6897355359) confirmed the mismatch using distinct commits and two real indexes.

## Areas touched

- [x] `gitnexus/` (CLI / core / MCP server)
- [ ] `gitnexus-web/` (Vite / React UI)
- [ ] `.github/` (workflows, actions)
- [x] `eval/` or other tooling — shipped Cursor and Factory hooks
- [ ] Docs / agent config only

## Scope & constraints

**In scope**

- Registered worktree and subdirectory precedence in all three shipped registry helpers, independent of registry order.

**Explicitly out of scope / not done here**

- Changing registry-versus-local fallback, storage ownership checks, or CLI query resolution.

## Implementation notes

Use the existing nearest-ancestor search order, which places the main checkout last as a linked-worktree fallback. A matching owned entry remains authoritative when its graph is invalid; damaged worktree storage must not silently select the main graph.

## Testing & verification

- [x] `cd gitnexus && npm test -- test/unit/hooks.test.ts test/unit/hooks-shared-store.test.ts test/unit/cursor-hook.test.ts test/unit/factory-plugin.test.ts --maxWorkers=2` — 416 passed, 41 platform skips.
- [x] `cd gitnexus && npm test -- --maxWorkers=2` — 34,637 passed and 104 skipped; the initial run had eight failures and one native-worker abort. All four affected files then passed unchanged on isolated reruns (96 tests): setup tests with inherited `CODEX_HOME` removed, and native tests after host memory pressure cleared.
- [x] `cd gitnexus && npx tsc --noEmit`
- [x] `cd gitnexus && npm run typecheck:tests`
- [x] `env -u CODEX_HOME npm test -- test/unit/setup.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` (70 passed); the same command for `test/integration/analysis-publication-flow.test.ts` (14 passed), then `test/unit/incremental-index-extension-dml-gate.test.ts test/integration/setup-skills.test.ts` (12 passed).
- [x] `npx eslint .` — no errors; existing warnings remain.
- [x] Regression: 10 failures before the fix; all 16 cases pass after it. Covers both registry orders, all three helpers, nested indexes, main fallback, and fresh versus genuinely stale hook output.
- [x] Manual Linux check with two real CLI-built indexes at distinct commits: all three helpers selected the worktree in both registry orders, and PostToolUse emitted no false stale warning.
- [x] Graph change analysis: four files, low risk. Focused correctness and independent adversarial review found no actionable defects.

## Risk & rollout

Low scope: candidate ranking changes; no schema migration or index refresh is required. A valid nearer registered index now consistently takes priority over the main checkout.

title: fix(java): preserve receiver and generated dependency ownership
body:
Java receiver ingestion loses array shape and lexical ownership in several declaration and alias forms. Generated Lombok members can also survive after workspace annotation evidence changes. This change keeps those identities through Java-local captures and resolution, preferring an unresolved receipt when ownership cannot be proven.

### Changes

- Preserve array dimensions, per-declarator/trailing dimensions and varargs; peel one dimension only at an array index. Retain array/container negative controls and selected-call overload/accessibility checks.
- Replace file-global alias rewriting with lexical, source-position-aware claims and complete field expressions. Preserve factory-result identity without rebinding copied aliases after reassignment.
- Capture qualified/annotated types and correctly bounded resource declarations. Give lambda parameters their own lexical scope, including unknown-type shadow barriers; infer supported callbacks only from proven JDK container identities.
- Add proven Lombok `@Value` accessors and conservative generated-constructor Spring dependency facts. Count explicit/generated constructors together and refuse uncertain qualifier/property-annotation copying. Reconcile workspace annotation proof, remove stale synthetic members, and preserve cold-worker, durable-cache and incremental parity.
- Add a deterministic P1–P4 corpus, `measure.mjs`, reviewed `baseline.json`, portable evaluation data and `npm run bench:java-ingestion`. No schema, CI or dependency changes. The scaling fixes below also touch shared scope-resolution code and the shared JVM package-sibling pass; Kotlin behaviour is unchanged.

### Measured evaluation

The same frozen corpus runs against original commit `26636d7a058d32c165999ab5f28a8a2540f50df5` and the changed build. Exact case results improve from **205/405 → 405/405**, **805/1581 → 1581/1581**, and **1029/2029 → 2029/2029**. These are 4,015 evaluations across nested synthetic workloads, with reused cases across shapes.

Cold-pipeline time rises **6.7%, 16.7% and 19.4%**; capture time rises approximately **37–44%**. All normalized growth budgets pass. A trigger-only optimization removed eight redundant file re-extractions while retaining identical capture, target and full-graph fingerprints. Separate full-profile record and check runs pass.

See [measured results](gitnexus/bench/java-ingestion/RESULTS.md), [protocol and limitations](gitnexus/bench/java-ingestion/README.md) and [portable evaluation](gitnexus/bench/java-ingestion/evaluation.json).

The existing receiver benchmark passes both arms after a measured baseline update: Java array indexing now resolves; non-Java entries stay unchanged. Java call-drop receipts increase by 13: nine existing JDK calls had no edge in either build and now report unresolved receivers; four foreach sites refuse duplicate imported FQNs in the invalid combined workspace. Both builds preserve all four exact targets when the fixtures are indexed separately. [All 13 sites and target identities](gitnexus/bench/java-ingestion/receiver-delta.json) are retained.

### Scaling

Java resolution is held to linear growth on concentrated shapes. This is measured as exact V8 block executions with inlining off, one pipeline run per size at N = 250/500/1000/2000; growth is the worst adjacent doubling divided by 2. Twelve generated shapes were measured, including N nested same-named member types, N wildcard-imported siblings in one package and N inherited fields. The worst shape fell from **1.79 to 1.025**, and every other shape is at or below 0.999. Graph fingerprints stay identical across all 822 lang-resolution fixtures and the shape corpus, except for the intended recall gain below.

- Shared: finalized binding buckets are returned without copying (name claims, walkers); imported return-type chain following is memoized per type and stop scope; the unique-name property index dedupes with one id set; the call processor finds exported definitions through an incremental id index.
- Java: opts into the associative batch merge; first-containing fact search is a cached binary search; SAM method facts are indexed by name; cross-file return-type mirrors are deduped; qualified simple-name keys are cached.
- Java no longer copies every package sibling's type bindings into each file. That copy cost K x N per package and was skipped above 500 files. Fields inherited from a same-package superclass in another file now resolve through the superclass chain instead, following JLS 8.3: private fields are never inherited, package-access fields only along a same-package chain, and a class's own field hides an inherited one. Large packages therefore keep inherited-field calls they previously dropped. Kotlin keeps the copy.

### Validation

- Build, source typecheck, test typecheck and changed-test duplication check pass.
- Scaling push: full unit suite 26,238 pass (one local-only jscpd 5.4.3 version pin) and full integration suite 9,289 pass.
- Focused Java regressions, exact forbidden-target controls, worker/cache parity, persisted incremental Lombok shadow add/remove, and independent adversarial review pass.
- New full-profile benchmark record/check, existing receiver-resolution both-arm check, Java Lombok synthesis check and Java overload-resolution check pass.
- Fresh GitNexus MCP staged analysis covers all 53 files and 490 changed symbols with no partial/truncated flag. Its HIGH risk is in the reviewed Java capture/Lombok reconciliation paths.

**The whole suite is not green on this host.** Six shards execute all **1,638 files exactly once**: **34,713 passed, 78 failed, 95 skipped**. No Java semantic regression failed. Failures were investigated rather than changing unrelated code or weakening expectations:

- 42 fixture cleanup `ENOTEMPTY`, 12 assertions affected by preserved local instruction/skill files, seven macOS canonical-path assertions, five installed Linux ARM64 prebuild headers, three CLI memory-admission failures, and two jscpd span assertions.
- Five existing baseline assertions covering evidence/runner identity, release/install subprocesses and a missing combined report; one copied Homebrew Node executable missing its adjacent dylib; one packed-artifact outer timeout.
- The unchanged packed-artifact test subsequently passes in isolation in **75.5 seconds**, including packed-runtime cold/warm cache checks. Baseline comparisons reproduce the applicable non-Java failure families.

Fully indexed multidimensional arrays, generic return substitution, compiler-complete classpath behavior and broader real-repository accuracy evaluation remain deferred. Unsupported/raw/wildcard/custom callback cases retain shadow ownership while inference refuses.

## Summary

`context` and upstream `impact` now find Python functions that read module constants or pass a function as a call argument. Previously, these dependencies were absent for expressions such as `return TIMEOUT`, `map(helper, xs)` and `sorted(xs, key=helper)`.

## Motivation / context

Closes #3942. Closes #3943.

The Python query previously captured calls and attribute accesses but missed these bare identifiers. Passing a callable now records a value reference without claiming a direct invocation.

## Areas touched

- [x] `gitnexus/` (Python ingestion, MCP descriptions, regression tests and capture baselines)
- [x] `gitnexus-shared/` (optional scope lookup policy)
- [x] Python coverage documentation

## Scope & constraints

**In scope**

Covered reads include operator operands, returns, assignment values, call arguments and parameter defaults. Callable references cover bare positional and keyword arguments. Shadowing, annotation filtering, evaluation-scope ownership and FastAPI `Depends` behavior remain covered by regression tests.

**Explicitly out of scope / not done here**

Broader expression shapes and attribute-valued callable arguments remain follow-up work. The Python gaps document records those boundaries and two remaining fail-closed lookup cases.

## Implementation notes

- Python disables implicit receiver lookup through an optional generic scope policy. This prevents a class attribute or sibling-method local from winning over a module/import binding. Explicit receivers still resolve, and other providers retain their default behavior.
- New read and value-reference captures share the existing language-neutral resolution paths. No language names were added to shared code.
- Capture snapshots and the benchmark fingerprint changed only for the two new capture kinds; all 233 corpus cases retain their prior captures after those additions are excluded. Scope metadata also records Python's new lookup policy.

title: Incremental analyze fails with "FTS index file_fts is inconsistent: document for node offset N is missing during delete" and needs clean -f to recover
body:
## Summary

`gitnexus analyze` (incremental path) aborts on a locally indexed repo with an FTS writeback failure, and the index stays unusable until a full wipe:

```
Analysis failed: COPY failed for File: Runtime exception: FTS index 'file_fts' is inconsistent:
document for node offset 969 is missing during delete. Drop and recreate the FTS index.
Error: COPY failed for File: ... FTS index 'file_fts' is inconsistent: document for node offset 969 is missing during delete.
    at lbug-adapter.js:806:19  (copyCsvWithRetry)
    at lbug-adapter.js:786:9
    at async copyNodeCSVs (lbug-adapter.js:804:9)
    at async loadGraphToLbug (lbug-adapter.js:941:9)
    at async runFullAnalysis (run-analyze.js:909:13)
    at async analyzeCommandImpl (cli/analyze.js:943:24)
```

Two things look wrong at once:

1. The reported row is `File` but the inconsistent index is `file_fts` — the File node writeback deletes through the FTS doc table, and a doc for node offset 969 is not there.
2. The error surfaces as a raw native exception with no recovery hint, and after it fires the next `analyze` fails identically, so incremental mode is not self-healing.

## Environment

- gitnexus **1.6.12** (global install resolved from `D:/dev/caches/npm_global/node_modules/gitnexus`)
- Windows 11, Node **v24.9.0**
- Repo: ~446 code files, ~12k symbols, ~24k edges, 300 flows
- Prior state: index built by an earlier successful `analyze` (12,013 nodes)
- The failing run reported: `Incremental: changed=61, added=77, deleted=0 (skipping wipe + 616 unchanged file rows preserved)` and `+54 importer(s) added to writable set (BFS depth ≤ 4)`

## Reproduction

1. Build an index: `gitnexus analyze` (succeeds, ~23s, 12k nodes)
2. Change and add ~130 files, leaving the index in place
3. `gitnexus analyze` again → the incremental path fails with the error above
4. Retry `gitnexus analyze` → fails identically; the index is now unusable for MCP/query too

## Recovery that worked

```
gitnexus clean -f      # "Deleted: <repo>/.gitnexus"
gitnexus analyze       # full rebuild: "Repository indexed successfully (22.8s)"
```

So recovery requires exactly the full wipe the incremental path exists to avoid.

## Expected

- The incremental path repairs the drift itself, or
- it fails with an actionable hint (`run gitnexus clean`) instead of a raw native exception, or
- a targeted `file_fts` reindex / `--repair-fts` recovers without dropping the whole index (see #3421, where the repair path itself could not recover).

## Suggested investigation

`copyNodeCSVs` → `loadGraphToLbug` (lbug-adapter.js:786-806): the delete resolves an FTS doc by node offset. If a File node can be written without its `file_fts` doc — e.g. the `deleted=0 ... 616 unchanged file rows preserved` shortcut, a partial writeback, or a failed earlier run leaving the pair half applied — then every later delete is short by N documents and the write can never succeed. Worth checking whether the File node CSV and the `file_fts` doc rows are written in the same transaction, and whether the "preserved rows" path re-emits FTS docs for preserved nodes.

## Related

title: fix(ingestion): bind TS/JS default imports to their default export
body:
## Summary

`impact` and `context` now report the real callers of default-exported TypeScript, TSX and JavaScript functions, classes and components. Before this change every default import (`import Child from './Child'`) stayed unlinked, so these symbols showed zero callers and risk `UNKNOWN`. Named imports were not affected.

The PR also removes a quadratic in framework route resolution that wide `export *` barrels triggered. Route resolution now scales linearly: on 13.4k files it takes 0.2 s, against 61 s on `main`.

Fixes #3956

## Motivation / context

A default import asks the target module for its `default` export, but the TS/JS export surface only published declarations under their own names. Nothing was ever published as `default`, so the import never bound. Default exports are very common in React and Next.js code, so every default-exported component had no callers in the graph.

## Areas touched

- [x] `gitnexus/` (CLI / core / MCP server)
- [ ] `gitnexus-web/` (Vite / React UI)
- [ ] `.github/` (workflows, actions)
- [ ] `eval/` or other tooling
- [ ] Docs / agent config only (`AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `.cursor/`, `llms.txt`, etc.)

## Scope & constraints

**In scope**

- Default exports written as `export default function F` / `class C` / `abstract class C` (overloads included), `export default X`, `export { X as default }`, and the existing synthesized HOC default (`export default hoc(() => ...)`).
- Every default import form: `import X from`, `import { default as X } from`, `import X, { Y } from`, with any local name.
- Barrels that re-export a default by name: `export { default } from` and `export { default as Btn } from`.
- `export * from` no longer forwards a default export, as ECMA-262 requires. Without this, a barrel with `export * from './c'` and `export default makeClient()` would bind `import client from './lib'` to the wrong declaration.

**Explicitly out of scope / not done here**

- Pass-through defaults: `import X from './x'; export default X` (or `export { X as default }`). These stay unlinked, as before.
- Wrapped and expression defaults: `export default memo(Child)`, `export default (X)`, `X satisfies T`, `export default makeClient()`, and anonymous defaults.
- CommonJS default interop, TS `export = X` (its meaning for `import X from` depends on `esModuleInterop`), `import X = require(...)`, identifier defaults in mixed CommonJS/ESM files, `.d.ts` defaults, and Vue SFC default imports.
- The data-route handler default path in `call-processor.ts` can use the new marker in a follow-up.

## Implementation notes

- **Provenance comes from the language layer.** The TS and JS capture emitters mark the declaration a module default-exports (`SymbolDefinition.isDefaultExport`). `typescriptModuleExports` (shared by TS, JS and Vue) publishes it under `default`, choosing the same callable winner a named import of that name gets. The issue's name-based fallback was not used, because it misses imports whose local name and file name both differ from the declared name.
- **`export *` exclusion is a language-neutral hook.** `ScopeResolver.wildcardReexportExcludedNames` is forwarded to `FinalizeHooks` and keeps those names out of re-export closures. TS, JS and Vue set it to `default`. Shared finalize code names no language and no `default` literal. `filterWildcardNames` was not reused, because it also drives phase-4 wildcard expansion and would start creating barrel-scope bindings for TS `export *`.
- **Scope-capture baseline.** The new presence-only `@declaration.is-default-export` tag moves the TypeScript fingerprint by exactly one tag, on the existing HOC fixture. Dropping only that tag restores the prior fingerprint byte for byte. JavaScript is unchanged.

- **Star-export index in the framework route resolver.** `exportValue` walked every `export *` source of a barrel on each lookup, so N consumers of one wide barrel cost O(N²). Each file now gets a lazily built index from export name to the star sources that can publish it.
  - Sources that may publish anything are always walked: unresolved targets, chains deeper than `MAX_RESOLUTION_DEPTH`, and files on an `export *` cycle.
  - Candidates stay in source order.
  - Resolved routes are byte-identical to `main` below the resolver's step and depth bounds. Above them, a route that the old walk dropped only because unrelated sources used up the budget now resolves, because the index proves those sources cannot publish the name.

Session-settled decisions carried from planning: default-export provenance from the TS/JS language layer (user-directed, over the issue's local-name / file-basename fallback heuristic).

## Testing & verification

- Issue repro through the built CLI (`analyze`, then `impact` / `context`):
  - `Child` and `plainFn` now report `impactedCount: 1` (`Parent`), risk `LOW`, epistemic `exact`, and `context` lists `Parent` as a caller. Before: 0 callers, risk `UNKNOWN`.
  - `Named` is unchanged.
- `npx tsc --noEmit`, `npm run typecheck:tests`, eslint (0 errors) and prettier: clean.
- Unit tests (`esm-export-marker`, `finalize-algorithm`, `scope-resolution/typescript/`): 478 passed.
  - New cases cover the marker, the `default` key winner, and the `export *` exclusion, including inherited closures.
  - Each new case failed before the change.
- Integration suites in `resolvers/typescript.test.ts` and `resolvers/javascript.test.ts` cover:
  - JSX and plain-call default imports;
  - a local name that differs from both the declared name and the file stem;
  - `{ default as X }`, `export { f as default }`, and a `const` arrow default;
  - both barrel forms and the HOC default;
  - two negatives: `export *` forwards no default, and no default is invented for a module without one.

  All pass. On a `dist` built from `main`, the positive cases fail.
- New rename fixture `default-import-locals`: renaming a default-exported function rewrites only the declaration and leaves importer locals untouched. Passes.
- `bench/scope-capture/measure.mjs --check`: the TypeScript drift is attributed and rebaselined. A 1.5 scaling reading on `typescript-deep-chain` was timing noise; a re-time gave 1.167.
- Scaling, measured on a synthetic corpus of default exports, `export *` barrels, and default-importing consumers:

  | Route resolution | 3.4k files | 6.7k files | 13.4k files | Per doubling |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | `main` | 1.3 s | 9.3 s | 60.9 s | ×6.5 |
  | this PR | 0.04 s | 0.09 s | 0.21 s | ×2.2 |

  End to end, the pipeline on the same corpus grows ×1.68 from 3.4k to 6.7k files (×3.03 on `main`), and takes 9.6 s instead of 18.9 s at 6.7k files. Resolved routes are byte-identical to `main` at every size measured.
- Route suites (10 files): 380 passed.
  - New: a router behind a 10,500-source star barrel resolves (this fails on `main`, which exhausts its step budget), and a 5,000-file `export *` chain no longer recurses without bound.
  - The repeated-diamond bound test now gives every level a real export, so it still reaches the step budget.
- Not run locally: the full `npm test` / `test:integration` suites and some neighbouring suites (`impact-private-type-source`, `fetch-wrapper-consumers`, `data-route-table-pipeline`, `rename-provider-javascript`, `vue*`). The host ran out of memory and that run was stopped before any test finished. CI covers these suites.

## Risk & rollout

- Graphs gain CALLS edges for default imports after re-analysis, so caller counts, `impact` results, and process detection change for affected repos. The analyzer build digest changes, so the next `npx gitnexus analyze` rebuilds on its own.
- A declaration that is both a type and a value under one name (`interface W {}` plus `const W = ...; export default W`) binds `default` to the same winner a named import of `W` already gets.
- No schema or storage change.

title: fix(python): link src-layout imports, class calls and literal __all__
body:
## Summary

The Python call graph now records three edge kinds it used to drop. These are imports of a `src/`-layout package from `tests/`, `scripts/` or a sibling service directory, calls that instantiate a class (`Plain(1)`), and calls to names that a `from m import *` brings in when `m` defines a literal `__all__`. `context` and `impact` on the target now list these callers.

Fixes #3949
Fixes #3950
Fixes #3951

## Motivation / context

The three issues come from a known-answer audit over 19 Python repositories:

| Audit row | Before |
| --- | --- |
| Direct call, dotted package import, importer outside the source root (#3949) | 0 of 580 |
| Class instantiated in its own file / imported class instantiated (#3950) | 0 of 948 / 28 of 975 |
| Call to a name that arrives through `import *` (#3951) | 0 of 119 |

The audit ran on v1.6.12. Its #3951 repro (bare `helper()` through `from core import *`) already resolves on `main` through #3504. That fix shipped after 1.6.12, and nothing pinned it with a test. On `main`, any module that binds `__all__` still contributes no names to a star import. Python's import statement binds exactly the names in `__all__` when a module defines it. In the CPython 3.13 stdlib, 27 of the 31 in-tree star-import targets define it.

## Areas touched

- [x] `gitnexus/` (CLI / core / MCP server)
- [ ] `gitnexus-web/` (Vite / React UI)
- [ ] `.github/` (workflows, actions)
- [ ] `eval/` or other tooling
- [ ] Docs / agent config only (`AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `.cursor/`, `llms.txt`, etc.)

## Scope & constraints

**In scope**

- #3949: a dotted absolute import resolves into `<dir>/src/<path>` when `<dir>` is the repository root or an ancestor of the importer. The closest root wins. Only an exact file matches, so external imports such as `django.apps` stay unresolved (#898). A `src/` that has its own `__init__.py` is a package, not an import root, and is skipped.
- #3950: a bare call whose name binds to exactly one class, and to nothing else, gets a CALLS edge to the Class node. This holds for same-file, imported, aliased, dataclass, inherited-`__init__`, nested and exception classes. A function of the same name still wins. An ambiguous name, a builtin, `cls()`, and a value of the same name from another star import emit nothing.
- #3951: a star import of a module whose `__all__` is a module-level `=` or `+=` of string literals binds exactly the listed names that module defines or imports, underscore names included. Every other `__all__` form keeps today's decline. The issue's bare-call shape is now pinned by a test.

**Explicitly out of scope / not done here**

- No edge to `__init__`. Python has no Constructor node, and `models.Plain()` already targeted the Class. `impact` on the class lists the creators. `impact` on `__init__` itself does not yet walk them.
- No reading of `pyproject.toml` / `setup.cfg` `package-dir` / `where`, or of `sys.path.insert(...)` roots.
- Single-segment imports keep their existing tiers. The src tier applies to dotted targets only.
- Two pre-existing gaps were found during research and left as they are. A single-segment external import such as `import requests` can still bind to a vendored `vendor/requests/`. Since #3504, `from m import f` no longer resolves when `f` is defined in both branches of an `if`/`else`.

## Implementation notes

- **Src tier.** It is a Python-only step in `import-target.ts`. It runs after the existing root and ancestor tiers and before the suffix fallback. It also runs when the external-import gate rejects a target, and then only exact files count. A new `srcChildDirNames` index set makes the miss path a single lookup, so the per-import cost stays O(depth). The probe-count rows and the import-target fingerprint are unchanged.
- **Class calls.** They are gated on the existing `constructionSyntax.bare` provider flag, which only Python declares. The new branch in the shared `emitFreeCallFallback` links through the existing constructor-target choice. It keeps the `construction` source-binding basis. The contract comment now says the flag links the call as well as typing the receiver. No shared code names a language.
- **Scaling.** Each new path was measured at doubling sizes. The figure below is `t(2N) / (2·t(N))`: about 1.0 means linear, about 2.0 means quadratic.
  - Src tier over N packages: about 1.0.
  - Literal `__all__` capture by list size or by `+=` count: about 1.0.
  - End-to-end scope resolution with class calls and star imports: 0.9 to 1.0.
  - Importer depth: 0.5 to 0.8, after a fix in this PR. Both the existing `hasRepoCandidate` ancestor walk and the new src tier hashed a fresh `${ancestor}/${segment}/` key per step, which made a non-matching walk O(depth²). The index now maps a directory name to its parent directories, and each step looks up the memoized ancestor string. At depth 64, 1000 imports took 23.2 ms before and 1.7 ms after. Resolution results did not change: the import-target fingerprint (14,027 cases) is the same.
- **`__all__`.** The capture step records the literal names on the Python capture side channel, and `ParsedFile.captureSideChannel` persists them unchanged. Star-import expansion reads them only from a `python-capture` snapshot that holds a string array. The parse-cache identity already hashes `core/ingestion/**`, so no manual cache bump is needed.

## Testing & verification

- [x] `cd gitnexus && npx tsc --noEmit` and `npm run typecheck:tests`
- [x] `npx vitest run test/unit/scope-resolution`: 201 files, 4164 tests
- [x] `npx vitest run test/integration/resolvers`: 123 files pass after the class-call change, with no change outside the Python suites. The later review fixes touch only the Python-gated branch, and the Python suites were run again after them.
- [x] Python resolver, namespace-semantics, module-accessor and worker-parity suites: 488 passed, 1 skipped
- [x] `bench/scope-resolution/measure.mts --check`, `bench/receiver-resolution/measure.mjs --check`, `bench/python-scope/measure.mjs --check`, `bench/python-scope/import-target-fingerprint.mjs --check`

Every behavior test was written first and seen failing. The exception is the #3951 bare-call pin, which records behavior that already works on `main`. The three issue repros were run with the built CLI, and each now returns its "Expected behavior" table:

- #3949: `tests/test_core.py` and `scripts/run.py` IMPORT `src/mypkg/core.py`. `test_compute` and `main` CALL `compute`.
- #3950: `build_local` and `make_plain` CALL `Class Plain`, and `make_point` CALLS `Class Point`.
- #3951: `via_star` CALLS `helper`. A module with `__all__ = ["pub_fn"]` now binds `pub_fn`.

## Risk & rollout

- `bench/scope-resolution/baselines.json` re-records `python/100/20` and `python/1000/20`. The generated corpus calls `C{p}()` in every file, so each file gains one cross-file CALLS edge: edges go 2397 to 2496, and cross-file calls go 99 to 198. Nodes and type bindings are unchanged.
- Python graphs gain Class edges, and processes gain Class leaf steps, as TypeScript, Java and PHP graphs already have. A class used as a decorator also gets an edge, because CPython calls it.
- Six existing assertions in three Python test files now include the new Class edge. They were updated, not loosened.
- Re-analyze Python repositories (`npx gitnexus analyze`) to pick up the new edges.

- [x] PR body meets repo minimum length (workflow may label short descriptions)

- [x] No secrets, tokens, or machine-specific paths committed

title: perf(python): keep exported-name lookups linear
body:
## Summary

Python named imports inspect each exported definition at most once per resolution pass, preserving early-match behavior and package/submodule resolution. This removes the only superlinear JavaScript work left in Python value-reference resolution on the committed benchmark corpus.

## Motivation / context

The previous lookup rescanned a file's definitions for every imported name: 2N² + N definition visits for N imported names. Companion PR #3964 removes a separate quadratic loop in capture (lexical import-claim reconciliation). The two PRs touch different files and merge cleanly in either order.

Related: #3957, #3964.

## Areas touched

- [x] `gitnexus/` (Python ingestion, regression tests, benchmark identity metadata)

## Scope & constraints

**In scope:** exported-name lookup, deterministic work-count tests, and scaling evidence for the resolution arm.

**Out of scope:** capture-side lexical claim reconciliation (#3964). Wall-time growth caused by GC and memory pressure is also out of scope; see verification.

## Implementation notes

The export index remembers the prefix of definitions it has already inspected. A first-name hit still reads one definition; later hits and misses reuse the scanned prefix. The index belongs to the resolution pass, so a new pass rebuilds it even when it receives the same parsed-file or definition-array objects. Each `ParsedFile.localDefs` array keeps its identity for the whole pass. `resolveImportBinding` copies a `ParsedFile` with a spread, which keeps the same `localDefs` reference, and no pass replaces or appends definitions after extraction.

For D definitions and I lookups, definition inspections are bounded by D, with expected O(D + I) collection operations and O(D) stored names. Qualified-name suffix matching and first-file precedence for duplicate paths are unchanged.

## Testing & verification

**Exact work counts.** Measured with V8 precise coverage: one resolution run per size, N = 128…2048 on the committed `bench/python-scope` corpus. Inlining is disabled for the counting process so every call is counted.

| | main (`9b77866c8`) | this PR |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Block-execution growth, worst doubling (1.0 = linear) | 1.157 | **0.9996** |
| Function-call growth, worst doubling | 1.335 | **0.9989** |
| Blocks growing faster than input | 1 (export-scan callback: 2,098,176 → 8,390,656 = 2N² + N) | **0** |

Running the counter twice on identical code gives results within 3.4 ppm, and on main it flags the known quadratic exactly. The unit tests in `python-import-export-scaling.test.ts` pin the same bound: for 2,048 definitions and 6,144 hit/miss queries, definition reads fall from 8,390,656 to 2,048. These tests fail on the previous implementation.

**Wall time.** Head and main on the same corpus at N = 250…2000, min of 15 calibrated batches:
- Graph facts are identical at every size.
- Resolution at N = 2000 takes 863 ms vs 1044 ms on main (−17%).
- Every doubling factor is 2.07–2.35 (2.0 = linear).

Wall-time growth still sits above linear. Two runs of identical head code measured 1.14 and 1.53 normalized across the full span. A CPU profile attributes that excess to GC (×6.0 for ×4 input) and cache pressure on O(1) map lookups, not to extra JavaScript work.

**Checks**

- 532 tests passed across 23 Python and shared regression files. Production and test typechecks passed, and the CLI build passed.
- CI: all checks pass.

## Risk & rollout

`impact` on `pythonFileExportsName` is CRITICAL: 23 upstream symbols, all reached through `resolvePythonImportTarget`. The complete graph fingerprints and semantic tests guard that path, and output is unchanged at every measured size. No schema or dependency change.

title: perf(python): remove quadratic import-claim reconciliation and deep-syntax hazards
body:
## Summary

Six fixes remove superlinear work, stack overflows and heap exhaustion from the Python capture route and the shared helpers it uses:

- Import reconciliation groups claims by name and checks import identity with a set, removing repeated full-claim scans.
- The lexical walk (`visit`, `bind`, `pattern`) uses an explicit stack instead of recursion.
- Annotation membership and attribute access kinds come from one tree-sitter query pass per tree instead of `.parent` climbs.
- The shared `walkNamedTree` and `bindingIdentifier` helpers walk with explicit stacks, for every language that uses them.
- The Python scope query ends each match at the node it finishes on and runs with a start-depth limit. The shared callable-flow helper memoizes four per-file lookups.
- A tree parsed through the chunked input callback (sources over 16K characters) reads node text from the source string.

This is the second independent change removing quadratic work from Python value-reference ingestion.

## Motivation / context

Distinct imported names previously scanned and copied the whole environment's claim list repeatedly. Repeated imports under one name also used a nested identity scan. The companion PR, #3963, handles exported-name lookup; these PRs can be reviewed and merged independently.

Syntax depth is input-controlled. Generated code can chain thousands of operators, and several paths on the same capture route crashed, ran out of memory or went cubic on such files (see Deep-syntax hazards).

Related: #3957.

## Areas touched

- [x] `gitnexus/` (Python ingestion, shared ingestion helpers, the safe-parse helper, regression tests, benchmark identity metadata, one docs pointer)

## Scope & constraints

**In scope:** lexical import-conflict reconciliation, iterative lexical and named-tree walks, linear annotation and attribute-access classification, a linear Python scope query, linear callable-flow captures, node text reads after a chunked parse, and deterministic scaling and depth coverage.

**Explicitly out of scope / not done here:**

- Exported-name lookup (#3963, now merged into this branch from main).
- Three scope-query shapes are still quadratic in `matches()`: nested calls, parenthesized comparisons and nested `as` patterns. Each needs brackets nested more than 200 deep, which CPython refuses to compile, and the exact fix costs 42-58% more `matches()` time on every file.
- tree-sitter keeps a match's start depth in 16 bits, so matches that start below depth 65,535 are lost, before and after this change. The only valid Python that deep is an `and`/`or` with more than 65,534 operands.
- Other languages' scope queries still run without the start-depth limit.

Wall-time growth is not the linearity gate: it carries GC and cache-pressure noise (see #3963), so exact block counts decide it.

## Deep-syntax hazards

| Input | Before | After |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| `x = a + a + … + a`, 1,000 terms | 10,071 ms | 41 ms |
| same, 2,000 terms | `RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded` | 73 ms |
| 2,000 nested list literals | `RangeError` | 37 ms |
| 2,000-deep class pattern or nested tuple target | `RangeError` | binding claimed |
| `.parent` reads, 1,000-term chain | 504,506 | 3 |
| `.parent` reads, 1,000-link member chain or call chain | 3,003 | 3 |
| `walkNamedTree`, 20,000 nested lists | `RangeError` | walks all 20,000 |
| 16,000-deep nested tuple target | `RangeError` | binding claimed |
| scope query `matches()`, 4,000-link call chain | 1,100.6 ms | 8.8 ms |
| capture pass, 6,000-link call chain | `RangeError` | completes |
| capture pass, nested walrus, 600 levels | 12,180 ms | 37 ms |
| capture pass, `a = b = …`, 600 targets | 2,560 ms | 49 ms |
| capture pass, `a()()…`, 2,000 calls | 10,219 ms | 52 ms |
| attribute context query, `x = f() or f() or …`, 90,000 operands | 35.7 s | 0.28 s |
| capture pass, 16,000-target assignment chain | 3,588 ms, 1,668 MB | 1,490 ms, 184 MB |
| one call with 40,000 arguments | out of memory (4 GB heap) | 60 MB retained |
| `x = o.v or o.v or …`, 40,000 operands | out of memory (4 GB heap) | 49 MB retained |

- **Recursive lexical walk.** `visit`, `bind` and `pattern` in `lexical-bindings.ts` recursed per syntax level and overflowed V8's stack near depth 2,000, dropping the whole file's scope extraction. They now use an explicit stack. Steps the recursive walk ran between child visits (parameter and comprehension-target binding) run as deferred tasks, so events, environments and range marks keep their pre-order.
- **Cubic annotation check, quadratic attribute classification.** `isPythonTypeAnnotation` climbed `.parent` from every bare read and attribute, and `pythonAttributeAccessKinds` read `.parent` three times per attribute to find its target context. tree-sitter nodes keep no parent pointer, so each `.parent` re-walks from the root. Both answers now come from one query pass per tree, memoized per tree like `javaTypeIdentityMemo`:
  - the `(type)` pattern marks every identifier and attribute under an outermost `type` node;
  - nine context patterns (call callee, decorator, `del`, `as` alias, assignment target, annotation-only target, augmented assignment, `for` and comprehension targets) record the access kinds of attributes in target position, descending through tuple, list and parenthesized wrappers.

  Each check is one map lookup by `node.id`, and the file reads no `.parent`. Every context pattern ends at its capture. A two-step pattern such as `(assignment left: (_) @write right: (_))` keeps its match open across the target, so tree-sitter buffers every capture inside it: quadratic, and past 65,535 buffered captures its 16-bit capture ids wrap and the process segfaults. A 70,000-argument regression test pins this.
- **Recursive shared helpers.** `walkNamedTree` (29 call sites) recursed per level and overflowed near depth 8,000 for every language that uses it. It now keeps a frame per node with the index of its next named child, so it makes the same `namedChild(i)` reads in the same order as the recursion; the Dart and Ruby navigation-count tests are unchanged. `bindingIdentifier` in `callable-flow-captures.ts` searches its field steps lazily from an explicit stack and skips a subtree that already failed.
- **Open matches in the scope query.** tree-sitter revisits every in-progress match at every node it enters or leaves. Eight rules (member call, member read, `binary_operator` and `boolean_operator` operands, four call-argument rules) were rooted at a parent whose later child they needed, so they stayed open across the earlier child, and that child can hold the same rule again: about six open matches per link of a call chain. Each rule is now anchored at the node it ends on with tree-sitter's wildcard-root form, and `expandPythonScopeMatches()` rebuilds the original capture lists in the same order. A chain holds at most 11 open matches at any length.
- **Start-depth limit.** The scope query and the attribute context query run with `maxStartDepth: 0xffff`. Past depth 65,535 the previous code kept wrapped matches open and took 893 s on a 70,000-link chain; it now drops the same deeper matches (one match fewer) in 0.4 s.
- **Callable-flow lookups.** `nearestFunctionOwner`, `nearestLexicalRegion`, `terminalIdentifier` and `hasMultipleIdentifierLeaves` are memoized per file by `node.id`, and a call's text is read once for all of its arguments. The helper is shared by 15 languages.
- **Node text after a chunked parse.** For sources over 16K characters, node-tree-sitter rebuilt `node.text` from the input callback on every read, copying the node's source each time. The tree now reads from the source string, as node-tree-sitter already does for a string parse.

## Implementation notes

Each claim enters a name bucket once. Reconciliation checks only the relevant bucket and builds one identity set for its imports. Work is bounded by the total number of claims and import records, assuming ordinary hash-collection costs; memory is O(claims + import records).

Claim order, redirected claims, definite declarations, compatible package imports, and conflicting runtime stores retain their previous behavior. Unchanged claims keep their identity, and input claims are not mutated.

## Testing & verification

| Deterministic stress case | Previous algorithm | This change |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| 2,048 repeated imports under one name | 2,098,176 import-claim reads | 2,048 import-claim reads, at most 4,096 identity reads |
| 2,048 distinct imported names | Repeated full-claim scans | At most 4,096 claim-name reads |

- All eight scaling cases failed against the previous reconciliation algorithm and pass with the grouped implementation. The repeated-import cases count `claim` and `identity` reads separately; re-running the identity compatibility check per claim fails them too. Sizes are 32, 128, 512 and 2,048, covering both distinct names and repeated identical imports.
- Full unit suite: 26,148 tests in 1,117 files pass. Integration resolvers: 5,156 tests in 124 files pass.
- Production and test typechecks pass; the CLI build passes. ESLint on the changed files: 0 errors.
- Full benchmark results: all eight committed fingerprints and existing 1.8 full-span / 1.5 adjacent budgets passed across 120 measured batches (500 ms calibration, 5 warmups, 15 batches per size). Strict all-pair growth over minimum and median times is 1.142 for capture and 1.444 for resolution, above the requested 1.0. This single matrix is not a paired speedup or stability confirmation. Reproduce with `node --import tsx bench/python-scope/value-references.mjs --check`. The benchmark identity now also hashes `attribute-references.ts` and its built `.js`.
- Head vs merge base, same host, two interleaved rounds, minimum batch time, sizes 250/500/1,000/2,000 on the benchmark's single-file corpus. This was measured against `9b77866c8` (#3960), the merge base before main was merged in; the merge base is now `85e7d8403`. Graph fingerprints are identical between builds at every size. Every doubling stays below 2.6× (2.0× is linear). Capture 1,000→2,000: head 2.24× / 1.95×, base 2.42× / 2.37×. At 2,000 entities the minimum capture batch is 5,498 / 5,440 ms on head vs 6,535 / 6,766 ms on base. Resolution is within noise of base (head 2.18× / 2.47×, base 2.49× / 2.47×).
- Deep-syntax commits: captures are byte-identical to the merge base over 340 repository `.py` fixtures plus synthetic cases (nested generic annotations, `type` aliases, match patterns, walrus in comprehensions, lambda defaults, `global`/`nonlocal`, chains and nested literals up to depth 1,000). The only difference is a 1,000-level annotation that the base walk could not process. `python-deep-syntax.test.ts` fails on the old walk (`RangeError`) and on the old annotation check (32,381 and 504,506 parent reads against a bound of 16).
- Attribute classification:
  - A node-level oracle compared the old and new functions on every attribute and identifier of 87,282 sources: the stdlib, a 2,000-file third-party sample, and 84,684 generated and mutated sources (75,000 with parse errors). That is 723,697 attributes and 2,443,869 identifiers, with 0 differences.
  - The six new member-read, member-chain and call-chain parent-bound rows fail on the previous head (753 and 3,003 reads) and read 3 parents here.
  - The 70,000-argument test segfaults the test worker with the two-step pattern and passes in about 0.4 s here.
- Shared helpers, scope query and parse text:
  - Emission-order captures are identical to the previous head `97b03b769` over 340 repository fixtures, 598 CPython 3.13 stdlib files, 9 deep-shape files and 23,464 generated files.
  - A raw-match oracle compared the old and new scope queries on 113,221 trees, 89,131 of them with syntax errors: 0 differences. The 15 languages that share the callable-flow helper show 0 differences over 7,995 files.
  - 17 mutants of the new query and memos: 12 are caught, and the other 5 are equivalent.
  - The new tests fail on the previous code: the anchored-query tests, the callable-flow depth-cost rows, the start-depth spy test and the safe-parse text test. The Dart navigation-count rows now expect 2 more map reads per level, from the memo lookups; parent and child navigation counts are unchanged.
  - Peak RSS of `analyze` with and without the parse-text change, three alternating runs each, with identical node and edge counts: median max RSS 2,124,660 KB with it vs 2,116,568 KB without on the stdlib, and 2,543,096 KB vs 2,553,068 KB on `gitnexus/src`.
- `bench/python-scope/measure.mjs`, `import-target-fingerprint.mjs`, `value-references.mjs` and `bench/scope-capture/measure.mjs` all pass `--check`.
- Exact V8 block-execution counts (the approved linearity gate from #3963; inlining off, one run per size, N = 128…2048) on the final head: capture growth **0.9990** and resolution growth **0.9996** per doubling (gate ≤ 1.0), with no superlinear blocks. At N = 2,048 resolution runs 22,406,078 blocks, the same count as the previous head `97b03b769`.
- Graph change analysis on the refreshed index: 9 files, 42 symbols, 3 affected flows, medium risk. Impact on the changed functions is critical (`emitPythonScopeCaptures` 57 dependents, `synthesizeCallableFlowCaptures` 61, `parseSourceSafe` 164); the capture identity checks across all 15 languages that share the helpers, and the full suites, cover them.

## Risk & rollout

Python capture processing, the shared named-tree walk, callable-flow captures and the safe-parse helper all have a critical graph blast radius. Complete capture and graph fingerprints guard the serialized scope metadata and resulting edges. No schema or dependency change is required.

## Checklist

- [x] Regression and deterministic work-count coverage included
- [x] No secrets, tokens, or machine-specific paths committed
- [x] No graph-output change: fingerprints match the merge base at every measured size
- [x] No stack overflow on 3,000-level operator chains or nested literals, 2,000-level match patterns and tuple targets, or 20,000-level named-tree walks
- [x] Linear by exact block counts on the final head: capture 0.9990, resolution 0.9996 per doubling
- [x] Attribute classification reads no `.parent`; member and call chains are linear
- [x] The Python scope query holds a bounded number of open matches on any chain
- [x] A call with 40,000 arguments, or an expression with 40,000 `or` operands, stays within the default heap

title: impact analysis less accurate than text search, results differ between incremental and full index, risk labels saturate (v1.6.12)
body:
### Area

gitnexus (CLI / core / indexing / MCP server)

### Summary

On a mid-sized Python repository, `impact --direction upstream --depth 1` found the files that call a function less accurately than a plain `rg` search: precision 0.26 and recall 0.29, against 0.71 and 1.00. Results also changed between an incremental and a full index, and the risk labels marked almost every widely used function HIGH or CRITICAL. On one real signature-breakage bug, `impact` listed the broken caller among 7 files, while `detect-changes` gave no usable signal.

Other problems found along the way: the default buffer pool is too small for this repo, the AGENTS.md / CLAUDE.md block is not refreshed, and the plugin hooks are noisy.

### Context

I wanted to know whether `impact` and `detect-changes` could replace text search when deciding what a change to a Python function or class might break. Two checks:
- **Caller accuracy:** compare `impact` against an exact ground truth and against `rg`, for 30 top-level functions and classes taken from recent commits.
- **Real bug:** run both commands on a known signature-breakage bug (a class constructor dropped a keyword argument, but one caller still passed it, so the program crashed at start-up).

### Expected behavior

- `impact --direction upstream` lists the files that call the symbol, including same-file callers and `from pkg.mod import name` / `import x as m` callers, with at least the accuracy of `rg`.
- The same query gives the same answer after an incremental `analyze` and a full `analyze`.
- A risk label reflects the size of the change and its direct callers, so it can drive a decision.
- `detect-changes` over a range points at the changes that matter, such as a callable whose callers no longer bind.
- `analyze` completes on a repo of this size with default settings.
- The AGENTS.md / CLAUDE.md block is refreshed on re-index, and the two files can be skipped separately.
- Hooks only add relevant context, and the stale-index nudge does not fire after docs-only commits.


### Actual behavior

### Test 1: upstream callers against an exact ground truth
| | impact (depth 1) | rg |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Precision | 0.26 | 0.71 |
| Recall | 0.29 | 1.00 |
| Cross-file callers only (8 symbols) | 0.09 / 0.50 | 0.88 / 1.00 |
| Exactly right | 6 / 30 | 17 / 30 |
| Time per query | ~1.9 s | ~0.01 s |
| `risk: UNKNOWN` (no callers resolved) | 19 / 30 | n/a |

### Test 2: a real signature-breakage bug
- **`impact` on the class:** listed the broken caller's file among 7 files. `rg 'ClassName\('` listed 9 files, including 2 genuine callers that `impact` missed.
- **`detect-changes --scope compare --base-ref <commit>` over that range:** `Changes: 1687 files, 2254 symbols … Risk level: critical`. The listing started with Markdown "Section" nodes from docs files, and nothing pointed at the broken call.

### Issues
1. **Low precision and recall for upstream callers (Python).**
   - **Same-file callers:** almost never reported, even for private helpers called only there.
   - **Missed imports:** module-level functions imported with `from pkg.mod import name` and called as `name(...)` are sometimes missed, even with `--file`.
   - **UNKNOWN:** 19 of 30 symbols returned `risk: UNKNOWN` although each has real callers.
2. **The same query gives different answers after incremental and full analysis.** `impact <fn>` without `--file`, with no change to the function between runs, returned 5 direct callers (HIGH) after an incremental `analyze` and 106 (CRITICAL) after a full `analyze`. The full-index list included vendored minified JS files and scripts that never reference the function.
3. **Risk labels saturate.** They seem driven by transitive counts at depth 2–3, so almost any widely imported utility is HIGH or CRITICAL whatever the change. That makes them unusable as a decision signal.
4. **`detect-changes` over a range is dominated by Markdown sections** and has no signature-compatibility signal. The one real broken call in the range did not stand out among 2,254 "changed symbols".
5. **The default buffer pool is too small for a mid-sized repo.** `analyze` failed with the error quoted under Logs. It worked with `GITNEXUS_LBUG_BUFFER_POOL_SIZE=4294967296`.
6. **The AGENTS.md / CLAUDE.md block isn't refreshed, and the two can't be skipped separately.**
   - **Not refreshed:** neither an incremental `analyze` nor `analyze --force` updated the stats line (`N symbols, N relationships, N execution flows`) inside an existing block.
   - **Coupled flags:** `--skip-agents-md` skips both files, so the CLAUDE.md block can't be kept without generating AGENTS.md.
7. **Plugin hook noise.**
   - **Unrelated "related symbols":** the PreToolUse hook adds "N related symbols found" to shell commands, chosen apparently by keyword and mostly unrelated to the command.
   - **"Index stale" after docs-only commits:** the PostToolUse hook prints "index is stale, run analyze" after every commit, including commits that change only Markdown.

### Verdict
On this repository, `rg` plus an explicit test of call signatures caught more, faster, than `impact` / `detect-changes`.

### Suggestions
- Report same-file callers in `impact`.
- When `--file` is given, resolve Python `from x import y` / `import x as m` bindings exactly, since that alone would fix most of the misses in test 1.
- Make full and incremental indexes give the same `impact` result. If a fallback name match is used, flag it as such and keep it out of `byDepth`.
- Separate the transitive dependant count from the risk verdict, or base risk on direct callers only.
- In `detect-changes`, exclude docs sections by default, and add a signature-compatibility check for changed callables (callers whose arguments no longer bind).
- Size the default buffer pool from available RAM, or retry with a larger pool on this error.
- Refresh the stats line on every re-index, and split `--skip-agents-md` from the CLAUDE.md update.
- Skip the stale-index nudge when only non-code files changed.


### Steps to reproduce

**Test 1: upstream callers**
1. Index a mostly-Python repository (about 1,570 files, 17k symbols, 44k edges) with a fresh `analyze`, setting `GITNEXUS_LBUG_BUFFER_POOL_SIZE=4294967296` (see issue 5).
2. Pick 30 top-level functions and classes from recent commits.
3. Build a file-level ground truth with Python's `ast` module. A file is a caller when it:
   - imports the symbol and uses it;
   - uses `module_alias.symbol`;
   - or is the defining module and uses the symbol by name inside another function.
4. Run `impact <name> --direction upstream --file <defining file> --depth 1 --limit 1000` and score the file paths in `byDepth["1"]`.
5. Run the baseline `rg -l '\b<name>\b'` and score it the same way.

**Test 2: signature-breakage bug**
1. Index the repository at the commit that introduced the bug (a class constructor dropped a keyword argument, one caller still passed it).
2. Run `impact` on the class and compare with `rg 'ClassName\('`.
3. Run `detect-changes --scope compare --base-ref <commit>` over that range.

**Issue 2 (incremental vs full)**
1. Run an incremental `analyze`, then `impact <fn>` without `--file`.
2. Without changing the function, run a full `analyze`, then the same `impact <fn>`.
3. Compare the direct-caller counts (5 vs 106).

**Issues 6 and 7**
- Re-run `analyze` and `analyze --force` on a repo that already has an AGENTS.md / CLAUDE.md block, and check the stats line. Try `--skip-agents-md`.
- With the Claude Code plugin hooks enabled, run shell commands and commit a Markdown-only change.

I can share the ground-truth scoring approach in more detail if that helps reproduce the problems on another Python repo.

### Environment

| Item | Value |
| --- | --- |
| GitNexus | 1.6.12, CLI through `.gitnexus/run.cjs` and the Claude Code plugin (with its hooks) |
| Node | v18.19.1 |
| OS | Linux x64 |
| Repository | Mostly Python; about 1,570 indexed files, 17k symbols, 44k edges; a few vendored minified JS files |
| Index | Fresh `analyze` before each test, with `GITNEXUS_LBUG_BUFFER_POOL_SIZE=4294967296` (see issue 5) |

### Logs / screenshots

No full logs were kept. Output captured:

`analyze` with the default buffer pool (issue 5):
```
COPY failed for Function: Buffer manager exception: Unable to allocate memory! The buffer pool is full … The LadybugDB buffer pool (256 MiB) was exhausted during the bulk COPY.
```

`detect-changes --scope compare --base-ref <commit>` (test 2):
```
Changes: 1687 files, 2254 symbols … Risk level: critical
```

title: ci: drop persisted checkout token from claude and ci-report workflows
body:
## What

Sets `persist-credentials: false` on the last two checkouts that still persist the `GITHUB_TOKEN`: `.github/workflows/claude.yml` (the PR-aware repository checkout) and `.github/workflows/ci-report.yml` (the sparse checkout of `gitnexus/vitest.config.ts`). Every other workflow already does this, including the artipacked-gated ones.

## Why

`actions/checkout` writes the scoped `GITHUB_TOKEN` into `.git/config` by default, where any later step can read it. Neither job pushes with the checkout token — `claude.yml` hands an explicit `github_token` to the Claude action, and `ci-report.yml` only reads a config file and posts via the sticky-comment action — so persisting it buys nothing and widens the blast radius of a compromised step.

## Scope

Two files, two lines. No behavior change expected; jobs that do push (e.g. the release-candidate PAT checkout) are untouched and intentionally keep persistence.

<!-- gitnexus-pr-summary:v1:start -->

---

### 📝 Summary by GitNexus

body:
Bumps the uv group with 1 update in the /eval directory: [dnspython](https://github.com/rthalley/dnspython). Updates `dnspython` from 2.9.0 to 2.9.2
Release notes

Sourced from dnspython's releases.

dnspython 2.9.2

A malicious WKS record in text format can consume excessive memory and CPU when parsed, possibly causing the process to exit due to memory exhaustion. Thanks to Jace (GitHub @​manus-use) for discovering and reporting this issue.

See What's New for details.

The minimum supported version of Python is 3.11.

My thanks to the many people who have contributed to this release. Also thanks to my co-maintainers: Nicki Křížek, Petr Špaček, and Brian Wellington.

This release was published to PyPI using Trusted Publishing.

dnspython 2.9.1

See What's New for details.

The minimum supported version of Python is 3.11.

My thanks to the many people who have contributed to this release. Also thanks to my co-maintainers: Nicki Křížek, Petr Špaček, and Brian Wellington.

This release was published to PyPI using Trusted Publishing.

Changelog

Sourced from dnspython's changelog.

2.9.2

  • A maliciously crafted zone file could use a WKS record to consume excessive memory and CPU, possibly causing the process to exit due to memory exhaustion. Thanks to Jace (GitHub @​manus-use) for discovering and reporting this issue.

2.9.1

  • LOC text parsing now converts the altitude, size, horizontal precision, and vertical precision fields to centimeters exactly, and requires them to be decimal numbers of meters with at most two fractional digits, as RFC 1876 section 3 specifies. They were converted with float(), so 9.29m became 928 cm rather than 929 cm and the text and wire forms of the record disagreed, forms such as 1e3m, 1_000m, +10m, nanm, and infm were accepted, extra fractional digits were silently dropped, and an altitude outside the representable range was accepted and then failed in to_wire() with a non-DNS exception. dns.exception.SyntaxError is now raised for all of these.

  • The resolver now assigns a new random query id to every query.

  • For transports that require a 0 query id, set it in a way that does not break TSIG.

  • dns.message.QueryMessage.resolve_chaining() now caps the minimum TTL of a negative response with no SOA record at 300 seconds (dns.message.NEGATIVE_TTL_WITHOUT_SOA). Previously the TTL was left at its initial value of 2^32 - 1, so a single NXDOMAIN or NODATA response with no SOA, e.g. a spoofed one, stayed in the resolver cache for the life of the process.

  • DNSSEC validation now rejects an RRSIG whose type covered or class does not match the RRset, as RFC 4035 section 5.3.1 requires. This was not checked, so a revoked DNSKEY, which may only validate the DNSKEY RRset, still validated any RRset signed with its private key if the RRSIG claimed to cover DNSKEY.

  • dns.tokenizer.Tokenizer now ends a line at a carriage return, or at a carriage return followed by a line feed, unless the carriage return is in a quoted string. The carriage return of CRLF line ends used to stay in the last token of each line and in the text of a comment, so e.g. dns.zone.from_text() rejected a zone with CRLF line ends.

  • DNSSEC validation no longer uses a DNSKEY with the REVOKE flag set to validate anything other than the DNSKEY RRset. RFC 5011 section 2.1 says a revoked key must not be used for any other purpose, but it was a candidate key like any other, so as long as the revoked key was still published, data signed with its private key, e.g. by whoever compromised it, validated.

... (truncated)

Commits
  • 854bedd bump README.md version
  • 388db14 Constrain WKS bitmap size.
  • 7e1832f version bump
  • dddd69c black lint
  • 185cc38 release prep
  • cf22838 Randomize the id of every message the resolver sends. (#1395)
  • e0fce7f use a short negative TTL for a negative answer with no SOA in resolve_chainin...
  • ad0803c check the RRSIG type covered and class against the RRset (#1388)
  • 8c38a04 Strictly apply RFC 3597 compression rules when decompressing. (#1383)
  • ab5ade8 end a line at a carriage return in the tokenizer (#1387)
  • Additional commits viewable in compare view

title: Generated AGENTS.md block: MUST rules have no scoping for documentation-only edits
body:
## Problem

The `<!-- gitnexus:start -->` block that `analyze` injects into AGENTS.md carries unconditional MUST rules:

- "MUST run impact before editing"
- "MUST analyze graph changes before committing"
- "NEVER edit a function, class, or method before MCP/CLI impact analysis"

These make sense for code changes, but they also bind documentation-only edits (a typo in Markdown, a test description change), where impact analysis is pure tooling overhead.

## Why it is hard to fix locally

The block is regenerated on every `analyze` (it is bounded by the `gitnexus:start` / `gitnexus:end` markers), so a scoping sentence hand-added inside the block is silently lost on the next run. A note placed outside the block works, but it sits in tension with the generated MUST wording and is easy to miss.

## Suggestion

One of:

1. Make the generated rule text scoping-aware, e.g. "MUST run impact before editing code, config, or tests; documentation-only changes need only the detect-changes check before committing."
2. Or offer a per-repo setting (e.g. in `.gitnexus/gitnexus.json`) to customize or append to the generated rule text, so users can state their scoping in a stable place that survives re-analysis.

## Environment

- gitnexus 1.6.12
- macOS arm64
- analyzed repo: mixed Markdown + JS orchestration repository

title: fix(lbug): make FTS COPY failures actionable
body:
## Summary

When COPY reports an inconsistent FTS index, analysis now stops with the complete native error and an actionable `gitnexus analyze --force` recovery command. It preserves the original cause and avoids retrying an index-integrity failure as a malformed CSV row.

## Motivation / context

The existing retry could discard the cause and truncate the recovery diagnosis. A full graph/FTS rebuild is appropriate after interrupted graph writes because FTS-only repair cannot restore missing graph rows; it also avoids recommending deletion of the entire index directory and its reusable artifacts.

Related: #3958

The native reproducer fails with the exact missing-document error on LadybugDB 0.18.3 and passes with the already bundled 0.22.0 engine. This matches [the upstream duplicate-COPY defect](https://github.com/LadybugDB/extensions/issues/118) and [its fix](https://github.com/LadybugDB/extensions/pull/123). The reporter's reason for reaching COPY with a live `file_fts`, despite the existing drop-before-DML guard, remains unproved.

## Areas touched

- [x] `gitnexus/` (CLI / core / MCP server)
- [ ] `gitnexus-web/` (Vite / React UI)
- [ ] `.github/` (workflows, actions)
- [ ] `eval/` or other tooling
- [ ] Docs / agent config only (`AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `.cursor/`, `llms.txt`, etc.)

## Scope & constraints

**In scope**

- First-COPY, retry, and retained-warning handling for the native FTS inconsistency signature.
- Native regression coverage for rejected duplicate rows, search contents, deletion, checkpoint/reopen, and index rebuild.

**Explicitly out of scope / not done here**

## Implementation notes

The classifier matches the native exception prefix so ordinary conversion warnings containing FTS-like source text remain recoverable. The native reproducer throws this error directly with no retained warnings; the injected warning test is defensive coverage for the same diagnostic if retained by COPY.

## Testing & verification

title: fix(hooks): show the stale-index hint after git commands with global options
body:
## Summary

The stale-index hint now shows after git commands that put global options before the subcommand, such as `git -c user.name=x commit`, `git -C ../other commit` and `git --no-pager pull`. The Claude-schema and Antigravity adapters each tested the command with a regex that wanted the subcommand right after `git`.

After `git -C <dir> …` the index that is checked is the one of the repository in `<dir>`, and the hint names that checkout when the agent works in another one. Every git call of a command is read, so one command can give a hint for each stale repository it touched.

## Motivation / context

Closes #3897.

Through each adapter, with an index that is behind HEAD:

| command | `main` | this PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `git commit -m x` | hint | same hint |
| `git -c user.name=x commit -m msg` | nothing | hint |
| `git --no-pager pull` | nothing | hint |
| `git pull;` | nothing | hint |
| `git -C . commit -am msg` | nothing | hint |
| `git -C ../other commit -am msg`, `../other` indexed and behind | nothing | hint that names `../other` |
| `git -C ../other commit -am msg`, `../other` up to date or not indexed | nothing | nothing |
| `git -C "$WT" commit -m a && git commit -m b` | hint | same hint |
| `git -C ../other pull && git commit -am x`, both behind | hint for cwd | one hint for each |
| `cd ../x && git -C ../other commit -am m` | nothing | nothing |
| `git -C commit status` | nothing | nothing |

## Areas touched

- [x] `gitnexus/` (CLI / core / MCP server)
- [ ] `gitnexus-web/` (Vite / React UI)
- [ ] `.github/` (workflows, actions)
- [ ] `eval/` or other tooling
- [ ] Docs / agent config only (`AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `.cursor/`, `llms.txt`, etc.)

## Scope & constraints

**In scope**

- `hooks/claude/git-mutation-command.cjs` (new):
  - `gitMutationDirectories(command, cwd, shell)` returns the directories in which the git mutations of a command run, in the order of the command and without repeats: `cwd`, or the directory `-C` names. At most four besides `cwd`, and `cwd` always has a place.
  - Before it reads the subcommand it skips git's global options together with their values: `-C <path>`, `-c <name>=<value>`, `--git-dir`, `--work-tree`, `--namespace`, `--config-env`, `--attr-source` (as `--opt value` or `--opt=value`), `--exec-path=<path>`, `-p`, `-P`, `--no-pager` and the other switches.
  - `-C` is read like git reads it: a relative `-C` applies to the one before it, and the path is walked through the filesystem, so `link/..` is the parent of the link's target.
  - `shell` is `bash`, `powershell`, or `either` when the caller knows it is one of the two but not which. The word rule and the decoder are built from it.
  - `readHead(directory, cwd)` returns HEAD of the checkout git reaches from `directory`, and the root of that checkout when `cwd` is in another one.
- `claude-hook-runtime.cjs` and `gitnexus-antigravity-hook.cjs` call the helper in place of their own regex, check each directory, and send one hint per stale repository. The hint ends with `in <checkout>` only when git ran in a checkout the agent is not working in. The Antigravity adapter resolves `tool_input.dir_path` first.
- `registry-query.cjs` (three identical copies): `resolveHookRepo(cwd, spawnCwd = cwd)` and the functions under it. Git starts in `spawnCwd` and reaches `cwd` through `-C`. Cursor and Factory pass one argument and behave as before.
- `setup.ts`: the helper joins `HOOK_HELPERS`, and the helpers are copied before the Antigravity adapter is written.
- Docs: the sentence that said Antigravity has no stale-index hint, in `docs/editor-setup.md` and `gitnexus/README.md`, and one line on `-C`.

**A git call is left out when its repository cannot be read from the command**

- the shell computes the path: `-C "$DIR"`, `` -C `pwd` ``, `-C ~/x`;
- `--git-dir` or `--work-tree` point git at another repository;
- the first `-C` is relative and a `cd`, `pushd` or `popd` word comes before the call;
- the shell is `either` and bash and PowerShell read the path differently: a bare backslash, an escape inside double quotes, a doubled quote (`'Bob''s Project'`);
- on Windows, the path starts with `\\` or `//`.

The other git calls of the command are still read. A check of a repository the command did not touch would be worse than no check.

**Explicitly out of scope / not done here**

- The OpenCode plugin keeps its own recognizer (see the notes).
- Text inside quotes still matches (`echo 'git commit -m x'`), as on `main`.
- #3899 touches the same two adapters and is a separate change.

## Implementation notes

- Why the helper is not OpenCode's `isGitMutationCommand`, which the issue suggests sharing. The plugin has to stay one self-contained file (its header explains why), so the code could only be copied. And its recognizer reads the first word of each simple command, which is stricter than what these two adapters accept today. Run on forms the current regex matches, it misses:
  - `GIT_EDITOR=true git rebase --continue` and `HUSKY=0 git commit -m x`;
  - `timeout 60 git pull` and `sudo git pull`;
  - `(git commit -m x)`;
  - `git commit -F - <<EOF …`.

  That strictness suits OpenCode, where a match costs a `gitnexus status` call. Here a match costs a few `git rev-parse` calls, and the hint is shown only when HEAD differs from the indexed commit. So the adapters stay permissive: with no global option the new expression matches what the old one matched.
- Which shell. Claude Code runs the Bash tool in bash on every platform. Codex goes through the same runtime, matches shell commands as `Bash`, and can run natively in PowerShell on Windows. So on win32 the runtime passes `either`: the command is read with the bash grammar, and a `-C` path is placed only when PowerShell reads it the same way. `git -C "C:\src\app" commit` is placed, `git -C src\app commit` is not. Antigravity passes `powershell` on Windows and `bash` elsewhere.
- The decoder ends on every input. An unbalanced quote or a trailing backslash returns null.
- Where the hint points. For a `-C` target the hook asks git (`git -C <dir> rev-parse --show-toplevel HEAD`) and names that root only when it is not the top level of the session cwd. A linked worktree or a nested clone is named for itself. A plain commit keeps one `git rev-parse HEAD` and the text it had on `main`.
- Where git starts. Always in the session cwd, never in a directory that was only named in a command: Windows looks for `git.exe` in the working directory of the child before PATH. The exit code is read before the command.
- Cost bounds. The run of options is bounded to 32, and a command above 16 KB is matched with `main`'s expression only. The slow shape (`'git -c ' + "\\''git -c ".repeat(n)`) takes under 30 ms at 16 KB; without the cap it takes about 400 ms at 64 KB.
- Only a commit id from the index metadata is echoed in the hint: another string prints `unknown`, and a value that is not a string counts as never indexed.
- Callers: `impact` rates every edited function that exists on `main` LOW (the `registry-query.cjs` functions have one candidate per copy, at most 8 impacted). The helper's functions are new, and their only callers are the two adapters. `detect_changes` against the merge base reports 16 files, no affected flow, low risk.
- Existing Antigravity installs get the change at the next `gitnexus setup`. The helpers go in before the adapter, so an adapter never sits next to an older set of helpers. If a required helper cannot be copied, the installed adapter is left as it was and the hook is not registered again.

## Testing & verification

- [x] `test/unit/git-mutation-command.test.ts` (new), 130 cases on Linux:
  - the five subcommands, alone, after `cd src &&`, and ending at `;`, `&&`, `|` or `)`;
  - commands with global options that leave the directory alone;
  - commands with `-C`: relative, absolute, quoted, escaped, several in a row, and a path that crosses a symlink, checked against what `git -C link/.. rev-parse --show-toplevel` answers;
  - the same paths read as `bash`, `powershell` and `either`: bare backslashes, a backslash before a quote, doubled quotes, unbalanced quotes;
  - commands whose repository cannot be read, alone and followed by a git call that can be;
  - several git calls in one command, the cap of four directories, and `cwd` kept when the cap is reached;
  - a relative and an absolute `-C` after `cd`;
  - forms the previous regex matched (environment prefix, `timeout`, subshell, heredoc);
  - commands that must not match, such as `git -C commit status`, `git -C/tmp commit`, `git -cuser.name=x commit`, `git log -c commit` and `git --help commit`;
  - 32 and 33 options, the two 400 KB shapes, non-string input;
  - `readHead`: same checkout, linked worktree, nested clone, a directory that is not a repository.
- [x] Through the adapters:
  - `test/integration/hooks-e2e.test.ts`, through the Claude launcher and the plugin launcher: the commands of the table above; a linked worktree (plain commit inside it, `-C` into it from the main checkout, `-C` into the main checkout from it); a nested clone; an unindexed `git init` repository; a logging `git` first on PATH that records the directory each spawn starts in, and that a failed command starts none; what is echoed for a `lastCommit` that is not a commit id.
  - `test/unit/setup-antigravity.test.ts`: the same through a staged Antigravity adapter, plus `dir_path`, an up-to-date and an unindexed `-C` target, and the order of the copies at setup.
  - `test/unit/hooks.test.ts`: both adapters call the helper and keep no list of subcommands; the runtime reads the exit code before the command; `resolveHookRepo` finds the same repository when git starts elsewhere; the #1224 worktree test checks where the hint points.
- [x] Mutations, each restored afterwards. Every one fails at least one test:

  | mutation | tests failing |
  | --- | --- |
  | `either` decodes a bare backslash like bash | 5 |
  | `either` decodes an escape inside double quotes like bash | 1 |
  | a doubled quote is read as in bash in every shell | 4 |
  | the checkout is always named after `-C` | 3 |
  | the checkout is never named | 17 |
  | `readHead` starts git in the `-C` directory | 3 |
  | the repository lookup starts git in the `-C` directory | 3 |
  | the Claude runtime looks the repository up without the session cwd | 2 |
  | only the first git call is read | 6 |
  | a `cd` before a relative `-C` is ignored | 4 |
  | attached `-C<path>` accepted | 1 |
  | attached `-c<name>` accepted | 1 |
