title: list_repos performs full-registry Git freshness checks before pagination, causing high latency and HTTP timeouts
body:
## Description

With 944 registered repositories, MCP `list_repos` takes approximately 60–106 seconds when successful. Repeated calls have also resulted in transport errors and HTTP 504 responses.

Reducing the page size from 100 to 10 does not materially improve latency. During the degraded state, even direct requests to the server’s `/api/health` endpoint time out.

Repository discovery should remain lightweight and responsive, independently of Git freshness checks.

## Environment

- GitNexus: reproduced on `1.6.13-rc.238` and `1.6.13-rc.240`
- Linux, Node.js `v24.22.2`
- 944 registered repositories
- 32 GiB RAM
- MCP over HTTP behind Nginx

## Reproduction

Call `list_repos` sequentially:

```json
{"limit": 100, "offset": 100}
{"limit": 100, "offset": 400}
{"limit": 100, "offset": 600}
```

Repeat with `limit: 10`. Each request still incurs substantial latency.

## Measurements

One successful round on `rc.240`:

| Offset | Limit | Duration |
|---|---:|---:|
| 100 | 100 | 75.447 s |
| 400 | 100 | 75.340 s |
| 600 | 100 | 75.526 s |

A later round on the same version:

| Offset | Limit | Duration | Result |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| 100 | 100 | 120.020 s | HTTP 504 |
| 400 | 100 | 120.012 s | HTTP 504 |
| 600 | 100 | 120.014 s | HTTP 504 |

The 120-second failures match Nginx’s configured upstream read timeout. However, direct localhost health requests also time out, so the degradation is not limited to the reverse proxy.

## Additional observations

During investigation:

- Up to 943 exited, unreaped Git child processes were observed under the GitNexus server process.
- The Node.js main thread was observed in `pipe_read`.
- Host CPU was approximately 93% idle, with approximately 27 GiB available memory and no significant I/O wait.
- In a separate Node.js process running as the service user, the same freshness checks for 10 sampled repositories completed successfully in approximately 79 ms.

These observations suggest a problem with the full-registry subprocess fan-out and request handling, rather than individual Git checks or insufficient host resources. A controlled comparison with listing freshness checks disabled has not yet been performed.

## Relevant code

`listRepos()` checks all registered repositories concurrently:

```javascript
const listing = await Promise.all(handles.map(async (h) => {
    const [stale, meta] = await Promise.all([
        checkStalenessAsync(h.repoPath, h.lastCommit),
        loadMeta(h.storagePath).catch(() => null),
    ]);
    // ...
}));
```

Pagination occurs afterwards:

```javascript
const all = await this.listRepos();
all.sort(/* ... */);
const repositories = all.slice(offset, offset + limit);
```

The MCP `repository-policy.js` pagination path also obtains the full listing before slicing.

Although `checkStalenessAsync()` uses asynchronous subprocesses, the listing still starts checks across the entire registry and waits for them to finish. Its name and asynchronous implementation do not remove this work from the request’s critical path.

## Requested behavior

Please decouple Git freshness checking from `list_repos`. Listing repositories should not start or wait for a full-registry Git scan.

Possible approaches include:

- A setting to disable freshness checks for repository listings.
- Background freshness refresh with bounded concurrency and cached results.
- An explicit freshness check for a selected repository.

If cached freshness information is unavailable, returning `staleness.status: "unknown"` would be preferable to delaying the listing.

A configurable opt-out would also be useful as an immediate mitigation if background refresh requires a larger change.

## Acceptance criteria

- `list_repos` returns without starting or awaiting Git freshness checks.
- Slow freshness checks do not delay repository discovery or unrelated endpoints.
- Repeated listing requests do not trigger duplicate full-registry scans.
- Any background checking has bounded concurrency.
- Missing or expired freshness information is distinguishable from a confirmed `current` status.

title: list_repos repeatedly parses full-registry index metadata before pagination, limiting throughput even without Git freshness checks
body:
## Summary

`list_repos` still takes approximately 10 seconds for a page of 10 or 100 repositories **after bypassing the full-registry Git freshness checks** described in #3979.

Profiling the installed implementation shows another expensive path: every listing validates storage for all registered repositories and then reads their full index metadata again before pagination. These metadata files contain large analysis fields that repository discovery does not need. Synchronous JSON parsing adds substantial main-thread work, and concurrent requests repeat the same work rather than sharing a listing snapshot.

This is a separate bottleneck from #3979: the measurements below were collected with the `checkStalenessAsync` invocation inside `listRepos()` locally bypassed. Other freshness checks were left unchanged, and listing freshness was reported as `unknown`.

## Environment

- GitNexus `1.6.13-rc.240`
- Linux, Node.js `v24.22.2`, 32 GiB RAM
- 944 registered repositories
- Their 944 primary metadata files total approximately **404.26 MiB**
- MCP over HTTP

## Reproduction

1. Use a registry with many indexed repositories and substantial index metadata.
2. For isolation, bypass only the `checkStalenessAsync` invocation in `listRepos()` and return unknown freshness. This is a diagnostic local patch, not an existing configuration option.
3. Call MCP `list_repos` sequentially with `limit: 10` and offsets `10`, `40`, and `60`. Repeat with `limit: 100` and offsets `100`, `400`, and `600`.
4. Issue multiple concurrent paginated requests against the same registry.

## Measurements after bypassing listing Git checks

Sequential MCP calls:

| Page size | Offsets | Individual durations | Mean |
|---|---|---|---|
| 10 | 10, 40, 60 | 10.183 s, 10.118 s, 9.873 s | 10.058 s |
| 100 | 100, 400, 600 | 11.056 s, 10.696 s, 8.819 s | 10.190 s |

Concurrent MCP calls used the same 15 requests, with page sizes between 50 and 100 and contiguous offsets covering all 944 repositories exactly once:

| Concurrency | Requests | Success | Batch wall time | Mean request latency | Requests/min |
|---|---:|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 3 | 15 | 15/15 | 138.247 s | 27.034 s | 6.51 |
| 8 | 15 | 15/15 | 143.603 s | 69.028 s | 6.27 |

Higher concurrency increased latency without improving throughput in these two batches. These are end-to-end MCP timings, not server-only timings, and the sample size is limited.

## Isolated backend profiling

In a separate Node.js process running as the service user, using the same installation and registry, I instrumented filesystem reads and `JSON.parse` and invoked the exported storage functions and the real patched `LocalBackend.listReposPage()`.

| Operation | Wall time |
|---|---:|
| `readRegistry()` | 13.15 ms |
| `listRegisteredRepos({ validate: true })` — separate measurement | 8,082.82 ms |
| `refreshRepos()` inside the measured listing | 5,844.59 ms |
| Complete patched `listReposPage({ limit: 10, offset: 10 })` | **10,751.22 ms** |

Counters for the complete listing call:

- **1,889 asynchronous file reads**, totaling **848,524,011 bytes (~809 MiB)**.
- **463 additional synchronous file reads**; their bytes are not included in the total above.
- **2,352 `JSON.parse` calls**, taking **5,453.86 ms** cumulatively.
- 5,664 `realpathSync.native` calls, taking approximately 189 ms cumulatively.

The separate validation measurement is not additive with the complete listing measurement. Graph-path metadata caching also makes cold and warm read counts differ. Instrumentation adds some overhead; nevertheless, the backend wall time closely matches the roughly 10-second MCP measurements.

Some individual metadata files exceed 3 MiB. Their largest fields include `unresolvedOverloads`, `fileHashes`, and `cacheKeys`, none of which need to be parsed merely to return a repository page.

## Relevant call chain

```text
listReposPage()
  -> listRepos()
     -> refreshRepos()
        -> listRegisteredRepos({ validate: true })
           -> mapPool(all entries, inspectRegisteredStorage, 8)
              -> inspectStoragePath()
                 -> readOwnershipMetadata() -> readFile + JSON.parse
                 -> inspectCodeIndexDB() -> resolveGraphPath()
                    -> readRecordedGraphPath() -> possible readFileSync + JSON.parse
     -> loadMeta() for every repository -> readFile + JSON.parse again
  -> sort and slice the requested page
```

The MCP `repository-policy.js` pagination path similarly obtains the full listing before slicing.

Relevant installed files:

- `dist/mcp/local/local-backend.js`: `refreshRepos`, `listRepos`, `listReposPage`
- `dist/mcp/repository-policy.js`: `listAllowedRepos`, `listReposPage`
- `dist/storage/repo-manager.js`: `listRegisteredRepos`
- `dist/storage/storage-resolver.js`: `inspectStoragePath`, `readOwnershipMetadata`, `inspectCodeIndexDB`
- `dist/storage/shared-store.js`: `resolveGraphPath`, `readRecordedGraphPath`
- `dist/storage/repo-meta.js`: `loadMeta`

## Requested improvement

Make paginated repository discovery independent of full index-metadata parsing where possible:

- Return lightweight listing fields from a registry or compact metadata projection rather than loading full analysis metadata for every repository.
- Reuse an already-loaded metadata snapshot across storage validation, graph-path resolution, and source-availability projection.
- Cache and deduplicate concurrent listing/validation refreshes, with appropriate invalidation when an index or registration changes.
- Perform expensive per-repository enrichment only for the requested page where semantics permit.

Storage ownership and validity checks are important. The request is to avoid repeatedly paying their full parsing cost on each listing, not to remove those protections.

## Expected result

- Small pages do not require repeated parsing of hundreds of MiB of unrelated metadata.
- Concurrent requests can reuse a consistent registry/validation snapshot rather than multiplying identical work.
- Index publication, registration changes, and source-retention changes invalidate any cached projection correctly.
- Improving this path does not incorrectly mark unavailable source or foreign/invalid storage as usable.

Related: #3979.

title: fix(skills): accept every UTF-8 branch name Git accepts in evidence capture
body:
## Summary

Evidence capture no longer fails on a branch whose name holds a character outside letters, digits and `._/-`, such as `feature/c++` or `fix/@scope`. `captureHeadGuards` now asks Git whether the symbolic HEAD ref is a valid name instead of matching it against a list of allowed characters.

## Motivation / context

Closes #3896.

Reproduced with `snapshotEvidence` on a fresh repository, one commit, then `git switch -c 'feature/c++'`:

| | result |
| --- | --- |
| `main` | `Invalid symbolic HEAD ref: refs/heads/feature/c++` |
| this PR | the receipt, `schema_version` 2 |

## Areas touched

- [x] `gitnexus/` (CLI / core / MCP server)
- [ ] `gitnexus-web/` (Vite / React UI)
- [ ] `.github/` (workflows, actions)
- [ ] `eval/` or other tooling
- [ ] Docs / agent config only (`AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `.cursor/`, `llms.txt`, etc.)

## Scope & constraints

**In scope**

- `captureHeadGuards` in the six copies of `evidence-provenance.mjs` (`gitnexus/skills`, `.claude/skills` and `gitnexus-claude-plugin/skills`, for `gitnexus-plan` and `gitnexus-work`). They stay byte-identical. The ref must now:
  - start with `refs/`;
  - hold no `..`;
  - pass `git check-ref-format`.
- Tests in `evidence-provenance-helper.test.ts`.

**Explicitly out of scope / not done here**

- Nothing else in the script changes: the same five control files are captured, through the same no-follow path.

## Implementation notes

- This is the first option from the issue. The ref is turned into a path by `git rev-parse --git-path`, and `resolveAdministrativePath` does not check that the result stays under the Git directory. Git's naming rules do that job: no `..`, no backslash, no control character, no `:`, no component that starts with a dot. Using them means there is no second list to keep in step with Git.
- The check is also stricter in two places. The old list accepted `refs/heads/.hidden` and `refs/heads/a.lock`, which Git refuses.
- The `refs/` prefix stays explicit because `git check-ref-format heads/main` succeeds.
- The `..` check stays as a second layer, as the issue suggests. `check-ref-format` already refuses it, so removing that line fails no test.
- Git never reports such a name for HEAD. With a hand-written `ref: refs/heads/../../x`, `git symbolic-ref` fails, and with a HEAD outside `refs/` Git stops treating the directory as a repository. So the refusal tests put a stand-in `git` first on `PATH`: it answers `symbolic-ref` and passes every other command to the real one.
- Cost: one more `git` process per snapshot.
- Callers: `impact` rates `captureHeadGuards` LOW in each copy, with `snapshotEvidence` as its only caller. `detect_changes` against the merge base reports 7 files and no affected flow.

## Testing & verification

- [x] 12 new tests in `test/unit/evidence-provenance-helper.test.ts`:
  - `snapshotEvidence` returns its receipt on `feature/c++`, `fix/@scope`, `user/a,b=c#1` and `café`, through both the plan and the work copy;
  - on `feature/c++` with reflogs removed, moving the branch and moving it back during the snapshot fails with `Git refs/heads/feature/c++ changed while evidence was materialized`, so the ref file of such a branch is guarded and not only tolerated;
  - seven names are refused with `Invalid symbolic HEAD ref`: `refs/heads/../../config`, `refs/heads/a\b`, `refs/heads/.hidden`, `refs/heads/a b`, `refs/heads/a:b`, `refs/heads/a.lock` and `heads/main`.
- [x] Mutations, each restored afterwards:

  | mutation | new tests failing |
  | --- | --- |
  | the previous list of characters | 7 |
  | no `check-ref-format` | 5 |
  | no `refs/` prefix | 1 |
  | no `..` check | 0 |
- [x] The four files the skill-sync workflow runs (`shipped-skills-sync`, `skills-steering`, `engineering-skills-contract`, `evidence-provenance-helper`): 178 passed.
- [x] `cd gitnexus && npx tsc --noEmit`, `npm run typecheck:tests`, eslint and prettier on the changed files.
- [ ] `cd gitnexus && npm test` in full: left to CI.

The new tests sit in the existing describe that is skipped on Windows, like the other real-git fixtures of this file. Each one passes on Linux.

## Risk & rollout

Evidence capture now works on every branch name Git accepts. It refuses two kinds of name it used to accept, a component that starts with a dot and a `.lock` suffix, which Git cannot create.

## Checklist

- [x] PR body meets repo minimum length (workflow may label short descriptions)
- [ ] If `AGENTS.md` / overlays changed: headers, scope block, and changelog updated per project conventions
- [x] No secrets, tokens, or machine-specific paths committed

title: analyze --embeddings deadlocks in CREATE_VECTOR_INDEX when the adaptive buffer pool is too small (spillToDisk → pthread_mutex_lock)
body:
### Summary

On one of our repositories, `gitnexus analyze --embeddings` intermittently never finishes. The log stops right after "Rebuilt the graph and FTS". The process then sits at 0 % CPU until our external timeout kills it. Other runs of the same repository end with SIGSEGV (rc 139), with `pthread_mutex_lock.c: Assertion ... failed` (SIGABRT), or with the warning `Vector index creation failed ... Owner died` and an index without a VECTOR index.

A gdb backtrace of a hung run shows a LadybugDB worker thread blocked in `InMemChunkedNodeGroup::spillToDisk` while `CREATE_VECTOR_INDEX` scans the embedding column under buffer-pool pressure. Raising `GITNEXUS_LBUG_BUFFER_POOL_SIZE` to 4 GiB makes the problem go away: 2 of 2 runs succeeded, compared with 4 of 6 failures on the default.

### Environment

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| gitnexus | 1.6.11 (also reproduced with 1.6.12) |
| @ladybugdb/core | 0.19.1 (1.6.12: 0.18.3) |
| Node | v20.20.2, linux x64, glibc 2.36 (node:20-slim) |
| Host | Docker on Ubuntu, kernel 6.8, 12 cores, 31 GiB RAM |
| Embeddings | OpenAI-compatible endpoint, text-embedding-3-small (1536 dims) |
| Command | `gitnexus analyze <repo> --force --name <name> --embeddings --skip-git --skip-agents-md` |
| NODE_OPTIONS | `--max-old-space-size=16384` |

### Repository shape

- 1581 indexed files: 773 Java, 529 TS/TSX.
- 18540 nodes, 49915 edges, 1014 flows.
- 14434 embeddings.

### Backtrace of the blocked thread (gdb, 1.6.11 / Ladybug 0.19.1)

```
#0  ?? () from libc.so.6
#1  pthread_mutex_lock () from libc.so.6
#2  lbug::storage::InMemChunkedNodeGroup::spillToDisk()
#3  lbug::storage::BufferManager::reserve(unsigned long)
#4  lbug::storage::BufferManager::claimAFrame(...)
#5  lbug::storage::BufferManager::pin(...)
#6  lbug::storage::BufferManager::optimisticRead(...)
#7  lbug::storage::(anonymous namespace)::FloatColumnReadWriter<float>::readCompressedValuesToVector(...)
#8  lbug::storage::Column::scanSegment(...) const
#9  lbug::storage::ListColumn::scanSegment(...) const
#11 lbug::storage::Column::scan(...) const
#12 lbug::storage::ColumnChunk::scan(...) const
#13 lbug::storage::ChunkedNodeGroup::scan(...) const
#14 lbug::storage::NodeGroup::scan(...) const
#15 lbug::storage::NodeTableScanState::scanNext(...)
#16 lbug::function::tableFunc(...)
#17 lbug::processor::TableFunctionCall::getNextTuplesInternal(...)
#20 lbug::processor::ProcessorTask::run()
#21 lbug::common::TaskScheduler::runWorkerThread()
```

All other threads are idle:
- 12 in `TaskScheduler::runWorkerThread` / `pthread_cond_wait`.
- The rest are node/libuv pool threads.

Over 10 s the process used 0 CPU ticks. There was no open TCP connection, so it was not waiting on the embedding endpoint.

### What we tried

| Variant | Runs | Result |
|---|---|---|
| default (adaptive pool) | 6 | 4 failed: 3 hangs, 1 SIGSEGV; 1 ok; 1 ok with "Owner died" / no VECTOR index |
| `--drop-embeddings`, no `--embeddings` | 1 | ok in 51 s |
| connection `setMaxNumThreadForExec(1)` and `(4)` via preload | 2 | both hung, same stack |
| gitnexus 1.6.12 (Ladybug 0.18.3) | 1 | hung |
| `GITNEXUS_LBUG_BUFFER_POOL_SIZE=4294967296` | 2 | both ok (551 s, 519 s), VECTOR index built |

A second repository shows the same class with a clean error. Every run fails after about 20 s with `The LadybugDB buffer pool (256 MiB) was exhausted during the bulk COPY`. With 1 GiB it succeeds.

### Two suggestions

1. **gitnexus:** `estimateBufferPool` sizes the analyze pool from node and relationship counts only. Embedding rows (n × dims × 4 bytes) and the HNSW build are not part of the estimate. Including them, or raising the floor when `--embeddings` is set, would avoid the pressure.
2. **LadybugDB:** Under the same pressure, the bulk-COPY path throws "buffer pool is full". The vector-index path instead deadlocks in `spillToDisk`, or crashes. A thrown error there would let gitnexus fall back cleanly.

title: MCP server segfaults (BufferManager::optimisticRead) after repeated incremental reindexes under a running server; incremental analyze bloats the index
body:
## Summary

The `gitnexus mcp` server segfaults inside LadybugDB (`lbugjs.node`, `BufferManager::optimisticRead`) when it has been running while other processes incrementally reindex `.gitnexus/lbug` underneath it. The MCP client (Claude Code) does not restart a crashed stdio server, so the graph tools vanish for the rest of the session.

It looks tied to index bloat from repeated incremental reindexes: incremental `analyze --index-only` seems to add edges without removing the old ones. One index grew to **708 MB / ~287,000 edges**; `analyze --index-only --force` on the same commit gave **155 MB / ~37,000 edges**.

## Environment

- gitnexus 1.6.12 (global npm install; also reproduced from the npx cache, same version)
- `@ladybugdb/core` 0.18.3
- Node v24.21.0, macOS 15.7.2, arm64
- Kotlin/Gradle monorepo, ~1,100 files

## What happens

An automated coding run committed ~16 times over several hours. Each commit triggered two incremental reindexes (one in the foreground before the commit, one from a post-commit hook in the background), about 32 in total, all under a single long-lived `gitnexus mcp` process. The server died mid-call with:

```
EXC_BAD_ACCESS (SIGSEGV) KERN_INVALID_ADDRESS at 0x0000000000001ec0
lbugjs.node  lbug::storage::BufferManager::optimisticRead(FileHandle&, unsigned int, std::function<void (unsigned char*)> const&)
lbugjs.node  lbug::storage::(anonymous)::DefaultColumnReadWriter::readCompressedValues<unsigned char*>(...)
lbugjs.node  lbug::storage::Column::scanSegment(...)
lbugjs.node  lbug::storage::DictionaryColumn::scan(...)
lbugjs.node  lbug::storage::StringColumn::scanUnfiltered(...)
lbugjs.node  lbug::storage::Column::scan(...)
lbugjs.node  lbug::storage::ColumnChunk::scan(...)
lbugjs.node  lbug::storage::ChunkedNodeGroup::scan(...)
lbugjs.node  lbug::storage::CSRNodeGroup::scanCommittedPersistentWithoutCache(...)
lbugjs.node  lbug::storage::CSRNodeGroup::scan(...)
lbugjs.node  lbug::storage::RelTableScanState::scanNext(...)
lbugjs.node  lbug::processor::RelTableCollectionScanner::scan(...)
lbugjs.node  lbug::processor::ScanMultiRelTable::getNextTuplesInternal(...)
```

macOS crash reports from four separate days have the same stack, so this keeps recurring and isn't a one-off.

## Repro

The script below keeps one `gitnexus mcp` server up, runs `analyze --index-only` N times underneath it (touching one source file each time), and sends `context` calls after each reindex.

- On the bloated index: the server crashed with the stack above within three reindexes.
- After `analyze --index-only --force`: the same test survived.

That is one run each, so it suggests rather than proves the bloat is the trigger. What it did **not** reproduce: a single bad query on its own, or a query concurrent with a single write on its own.

<details><summary>repro_longlived_server.py</summary>

```python
"""Keep one `gitnexus mcp` server running across several incremental reindexes, querying it after each.

Usage:
  python3 repro_longlived_server.py <repo dir> <registered repo name> <source file to touch> <symbol> [<symbol> ...]

Each round appends comment lines to <source file> (restored at the end), runs
`node .gitnexus/run.cjs analyze --index-only` while the server stays up, then sends `context`
calls for the symbols, three at a time. On an index that has been incrementally reindexed many times
the server died with SIGSEGV in lbug::storage::BufferManager::optimisticRead; on the same repo right after
`analyze --index-only --force` it survived the same rounds.

GITNEXUS_BIN overrides the server binary (default: `gitnexus` on PATH). ROUNDS sets the reindex count (default 3).
"""
import json, os, pathlib, shutil, subprocess, sys, threading

if len(sys.argv) < 5:
    sys.exit(__doc__)
repo_dir, repo_name, touched, *symbols = sys.argv[1:]
rounds = int(os.environ.get("ROUNDS", "3"))
binary = os.environ.get("GITNEXUS_BIN") or shutil.which("gitnexus") or sys.exit("gitnexus not on PATH")
src = pathlib.Path(repo_dir, touched)
original = src.read_text()

srv = subprocess.Popen([binary, "mcp"], cwd=repo_dir, stdin=subprocess.PIPE, stdout=subprocess.PIPE,
                       stderr=subprocess.PIPE, text=True, bufsize=1)
stderr = []
threading.Thread(target=lambda: stderr.extend(srv.stderr), daemon=True).start()


def send(msg):
    srv.stdin.write(json.dumps(msg) + "\n")
    srv.stdin.flush()


def recv():
    line = srv.stdout.readline()
    return json.loads(line) if line else None


send({"jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": 0, "method": "initialize", "params": {
    "protocolVersion": "2025-06-18", "capabilities": {}, "clientInfo": {"name": "repro", "version": "0"}}})
recv()
send({"jsonrpc": "2.0", "method": "notifications/initialized"})
next_id = 1


def burst(tag, repeats=5):
    global next_id
    for _ in range(repeats):
        batch = symbols[:3]
        for name in batch:
            send({"jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": next_id, "method": "tools/call",
                  "params": {"name": "context", "arguments": {"name": name, "repo": repo_name}}})
            next_id += 1
        try:
            replies = [recv() for _ in batch]
        except (BrokenPipeError, json.JSONDecodeError):
            replies = [None]
        if any(r is None for r in replies) or srv.poll() is not None:
            print(f"SERVER DIED during '{tag}', exit={srv.wait()}")
            print("".join(stderr)[-2000:])
            return False
    print(f"{tag}: OK")
    return True


try:
    alive = burst("before any reindex")
    for n in range(rounds):
        if not alive:
            break
        src.write_text(original + "".join(f"// repro {i}\n" for i in range(n + 1)))
        subprocess.run(["node", ".gitnexus/run.cjs", "analyze", "--index-only"], cwd=repo_dir, capture_output=True)
        alive = burst(f"after reindex {n + 1}")
finally:
    src.write_text(original)
    srv.kill()
sys.exit(0 if alive else 1)
```
</details>

```
python3 repro_longlived_server.py <repo dir> <registered repo name> <source file> <symbol> [<symbol> ...]
```

## Related oddity

On the bloated index, a plain `analyze` printed "Already up to date" while `status` reported the index stale.

## Expected

- Incremental reindexes don't grow the edge count unboundedly (old edges are removed when a file is reindexed), and
- a running `mcp` server survives the index being rewritten under it: it reopens the database, or fails the call with an error instead of segfaulting.

## Workaround

`analyze --index-only --force` periodically, keep it to one reindex per commit, then reconnect the MCP server.

  • Ignore <!-- and --> between top-level rules in CSS instead of throwing or swallowing the next rule (e.g. a { color: red } --> b { color: blue }) (#20665)
  • Ensure @tailwindcss/oxide-wasm32-wasi detects changed and new source files after the first scan (e.g. in WebContainers) (#20487)
  • Prevent type errors with skipLibCheck: false caused by imports of unshipped modules in the @tailwindcss/node type declarations (#20632)

Added

  • Canonicalization: preserve & when moving a pseudo-element into * or ** (e.g. [&_::before]:flex → **:[&::before]:flex) (#20550)
  • Ensure the Set.prototype.intersection polyfill in canonicalizeCandidates(…) returns the intersection instead of the first set on Node.js < 22 (#20562)
  • Canonicalization: ensure inline theme(…) alphas with more than 2 decimals migrate to a percentage modifier with the same opacity (e.g. theme(colors.red.500/.12345) → text-red-500/[12.345%], not text-red-500/[12.345]) (#20563)
  • Canonicalization: preserve inline theme(…) alphas as an arbitrary percentage when a custom --opacity-* theme value would change the opacity (e.g. theme(colors.red.500/50%) → text-red-500/[50%] with --opacity-50: 10%) (#20563)
  • Ensure the @property fallback isn't applied in Safari versions that no longer support margin-trim: inline (#20569)
  • Treat viewport units like dvmin and svi and font-relative units like cap and rex as lengths in arbitrary values (e.g. text-[10dvmin] generates font-size instead of color) (#20516)
  • Write plugin logs to stderr in tailwindcss canonicalize so they don't end up in the results on stdout (#20561)
  • Extract class shorthands on later lines when Pug text, comments, or quoted attribute values contain unbalanced brackets, or a quote that doesn't start a string (e.g. input(pattern=/"/.source)) (#20547, #20572)

title: fix(mcp): avoid Git scans and repeated metadata parsing during discovery
body:
## Summary

MCP `list_repos` now returns a page without starting Git or repeatedly parsing every index manifest. It reports `staleness.status` as `unknown`. Clients can read `gitnexus://repo/{name}/context` for measured freshness on a selected repository.

Fixes #3979
Fixes #3980

## Motivation and scope

The reported registry had 944 repositories and about 404 MiB of index metadata. A ten-row page could start a Git process for every repository and read each manifest twice. Concurrent pages multiplied that cost and delayed unrelated requests.

Every listing still reads the current registry and validates storage ownership, permissions and graph presence. Pages share only the compact fields parsed from the same opened file version. This lets a later request see an index publication or a retention change while an earlier request is still running. An inconclusive inspection keeps source unavailable and preserves an existing graph connection for the same checkout and slot.

The allowlist applies before sorting and pagination. Visible clones on other pages still appear as siblings. Checkout availability is checked only for returned rows that retain full source.

## Testing and verification

The measurements below use the real MCP HTTP endpoint, ten-row pages and synthetic manifests on local Linux storage. Git probes were bypassed by empty indexed commits in both versions to isolate metadata costs. A separate four-repository regression with nonempty commits verifies that discovery starts zero freshness checks.

| 160 repositories, 128 KiB per manifest | Before | After |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| First page, full manifest parses | 320 | 160 |
| Next page, full manifest parses | 320 | 0 |
| Eight concurrent warm pages, bytes parsed | 320.6 MiB | 0 |
| Eight concurrent warm pages, wall time | 1.32 s | 0.32 s |
| Slowest concurrent health response | 297 ms | 15 ms |

On a 944-repository fixture with 404 MiB of metadata, the first page took 1.04 s and the next page took 0.27 s. Eight concurrent warm pages finished in 1.47 s with zero full manifest parses. The slowest of 113 health responses during that batch took 20 ms. These timings are single-run observations, and each page still performs filesystem checks across the registry. Server startup has its own validation pass.

Regression tests cover overlapping cold reads, warm reuse, atomic replacement, out-of-order refreshes, transient graph access, directory permissions, restricted pagination, and visible off-page siblings. The CLI builds, typechecks, and passes its focused storage, backend and MCP integration tests. Hosted checks and their logs are attached to the PR.

## Risk and rollout

The wire-level change for clients is explicit unknown freshness during discovery. The cache is per backend and in memory. Installing the fix requires no registry migration or reindex.

title: fix(hooks): scope graph context to leading rg and grep searches
body:
## Summary

Cursor, Factory and Antigravity now add graph context only when the first shell command invokes `rg` or `grep`, matching the rule in Claude Code, Codex and OpenCode. For example, `git log | grep UserService` filters the log and skips the graph lookup. With `rg UserService src | head`, the hook looks up `UserService`.

Claude Code, Codex and Antigravity also share a parser for Bash and PowerShell. It handles leading blank lines, Bash assignment prefixes such as `NO_COLOR=1 rg …`, and PowerShell’s `&` call operator when the shell is known. When the shell is ambiguous on Windows, the hook uses a query only if both readings agree.

For searches with multiple patterns, such as `rg -e LoginService -e TokenStore src`, these three adapters pass up to three patterns to `gitnexus augment`. It looks up each pattern and combines the matching symbols into one result. Cursor and Factory each keep a single-pattern parser in their own hook file. Both adapters ship with their own support files and run without the shared Claude search parser. Broader option handling for these two adapters is outside this PR.

The npm package also includes `hooks/claude/pre-tool-use.sh`, which still matches `rg` or `grep` anywhere in a command. No supported installer or editor manifest registers or invokes that script.

## Motivation / context

Closes #3899.

`extractPattern` on each adapter:

| command | Claude on `main` | Antigravity on `main` | Cursor, Factory on `main` | this PR, every adapter |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ``sed -i '' 's/old text/new text/' notes.md && grep -c 'direct `tool' notes.md`` (the issue) | none | `direct` | ``direct `tool`` | none |
| `git log --oneline \| grep UserService` | none | `UserService` | `UserService` | none |
| `cd src && rg UserService` | none | `UserService` | `UserService` | none |
| `grep -rn UserService src \| head` | `UserService` | `UserService` | `UserService` | `UserService` |
| `rg 'user service' src` | `user service` | `user` | `user service` | `user service` |
| `rg --max-count 100 UserService src` | `UserService` | `100` | `UserService` | `UserService` |

The last two rows come from the Antigravity parser, which split the line on whitespace and knew twelve options. They are fixed because the adapter now uses the Claude runtime's parser.

## Areas touched

- [x] `gitnexus/` (CLI / core / MCP server)
- [ ] `gitnexus-web/` (Vite / React UI)
- [ ] `.github/` (workflows, actions)
- [ ] `eval/` or other tooling
- [ ] Docs / agent config only (`AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `.cursor/`, `llms.txt`, etc.)

## Scope & constraints

**In scope**

- `hooks/claude/search-command-pattern.cjs` (new): `searchCommandPattern(command, shell = 'bash')`. The tokenizer, the option tables and `extractSearchCommandPattern` move here from `claude-hook-runtime.cjs` unchanged, apart from the shell parameter below.
- `shell` is `bash`, `powershell`, or `either` when the caller cannot tell, as in `git-mutation-command.cjs`:
  - In PowerShell a backslash is an ordinary character, and a doubled quote inside quotes is one literal quote.
  - A bare comma, parenthesis, brace or leading `@` in PowerShell builds a value the shell computes, so the command has no query.
  - With `either`, the query is used only when the two readings give the same words.
- In bash, variable assignments before the command belong to it: `NO_COLOR=1 rg UserService src` is read as `rg UserService src`. A quoted word or a word after a newline is not an assignment, and PowerShell has no such prefix.
- `claude-hook-runtime.cjs` passes `BASH_TOOL_SHELL` (`either` on win32, for Codex). `gitnexus-antigravity-hook.cjs` passes its `SHELL` (`powershell` on win32) and drops its own parser.
- `parseRgGrepPattern` in the Cursor and Factory adapters, still identical: a line whose first command is not `rg` or `grep` (after the wrappers it already knew, such as `npx`, `sudo`, `env X=1` or `git grep`) has no query.
- `setup.ts`: the helper joins `HOOK_HELPERS`, so setup copies it next to the Antigravity adapter.
- `docs/editor-setup.md`: the first-command rule was written for OpenCode only. It now applies to every editor.

## Implementation notes

- Behavior change in Cursor and Factory: `cd grep && rg LongPattern src/` was a listed case that returned `LongPattern` (#2938). It returns nothing now, like Claude and OpenCode, and the case moves to the no-pattern list. After a `cd` the search runs in another directory, and the editor docs already said such a search gets no augmentation.
- The Claude runtime behaves as before on Linux and macOS. On win32 a Codex command whose words bash and PowerShell read differently, such as `rg C:\Users src` (`C:Users` in bash), no longer gets a query.
- Callers: `impact` rates `extractPattern` (each adapter), `parseRgGrepPattern` (both copies) and `extractSearchCommandPattern` LOW. Their only callers are the adapters' tool handlers. `detect_changes` reports 15 files, no affected flow, low risk.
- Existing Antigravity installs get the change at the next `gitnexus setup`, which copies the helpers before it writes the adapter.

## Testing & verification

- [x] `test/unit/search-command-pattern.test.ts` (new):
  - a search that starts the line, in `bash`, `powershell` and `either`;
  - no query after `&&`, `;`, `||` or `|`, including the command from the issue, in all three shells;

title: docs(taint): say the call join matches callee names, not identities
body:
## Summary

The taint skill and two solver comments said the callee identity of the interprocedural join is exact. `solveInterprocTaint` matches a summary's call-arg edge to the caller's `CALLS` edges by the callee's declared name (`callsByCallerName`, `resolveCallees`). As a result:

- when a caller has two distinct callees with the same name, the solver considers both when propagating taint;
- a call-arg edge with no callee name matches every outgoing call of its caller.

The skill already lists the first case under its known limits ("a flow into one over-attributes to both"). The "Name-based call join" bullet contradicted it. Now both say the same thing.

## Motivation / context

Closes #2977.

The issue asked for two things. The second, routing model edits to the right language file, was done by #2809: the skill's "Adding a source / sink / sanitizer" section names `typescript-model.ts`, `python-model.ts` and `java-model.ts`. `taintModelVersion` is a digest of every built-in model, so a model edit needs no manual version bump. This PR covers what was left, the "identity is exact" wording.

## Areas touched

- [x] `gitnexus/` (CLI / core / MCP server)
- [ ] `gitnexus-web/` (Vite / React UI)
- [ ] `.github/` (workflows, actions)
- [ ] `eval/` or other tooling
- [ ] Docs / agent config only (`AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `.cursor/`, `llms.txt`, etc.)

## Scope & constraints

**In scope**

- `gitnexus-taint-analysis` skill, in its three identical copies (`gitnexus/skills/`, `.claude/skills/gitnexus/`, `gitnexus-claude-plugin/skills/`): the "Name-based call join" bullet.
- `interproc-solver.ts`:
  - the `InterprocCallEdge` comment, same correction, with the `tatints` typo fixed;
  - the `unmatchedCallSites` comment, which described a call-site line match. It counts failed lookups of a matching outgoing `CALLS` edge. Repeated failures for the same summary edge count separately.
- `summary-model.ts`: the `ParamToCallArg` and `SourceToCallArg` comments. They also called `callLine` a tie-breaker among same-named callees. The solver never reads it for the join. It is shown in the hop chain, and it is part of the entry's key, so two calls on different lines stay two entries.
- Two solver tests for the two behaviors above.

**Explicitly out of scope / not done here**

- No change to the join itself. Telling same-named callees apart would need a resolved symbol id on the summary's call-arg edge, which the CFG harvest does not have today.

## Testing & verification

- [x] `test/unit/taint/interproc-solver.test.ts`, two new cases:
  - one caller, two callees named `process`, one tainted call: a finding for each callee;
  - a call-arg edge without `calleeName`: a finding for each outgoing call.
  - An unmatched name already has its test (`counts an unmatched call site`).
- [x] Mutations in `resolveCallees`, each restored afterwards. Each fails a test:
  - only the first same-named edge kept;
  - an edge with no name matching nothing;
  - an unmatched name not counted.
- [x] `npx vitest run test/unit/taint/`: 363 passed. `test/unit/shipped-skills-sync.test.ts` passes with the three copies identical.
- [x] Typecheck, eslint and prettier on the changed TypeScript (pre-commit hook). The skill file's existing prettier warning is unchanged: it is there on `main` too, and the file is not reformatted.
- [x] `detect_changes`: 6 files, no affected flow, low risk.

## Risk & rollout

Comments, skill text and tests only. No runtime change.

body:
Bumps [chokidar](https://github.com/paulmillr/chokidar) from 5.0.0 to 6.0.0.
Release notes

Sourced from chokidar's releases.

6.0.0

High-level changes

  • Rewrote the watcher around a single observation pipeline. Backend callbacks are treated as invalidations and confirmed with lstat, stat, or readdir before any event is emitted, so the final state after a burst of changes matches the filesystem.
  • Added native recursive watching through fs.watch({ recursive: true }). The default auto backend uses it on macOS and Windows and per-directory watching elsewhere.
  • Shared native handles across watchers and opened them per directory only: files no longer own handles. This fixes EBADF errors when watching many files on macOS (#1385, #1452).
  • Replaced fs.watchFile with Chokidar-owned stat polling. Poll loops are shared across watchers at the fastest requested interval.
  • Required Node.js 22.22 or later.

API changes

  • Added the backend option: 'auto' (default), 'native', 'native-recursive', or 'polling'.
    • usePolling: true remains as a deprecated alias for backend: 'polling'.
  • Renamed interval and binaryInterval to pollingInterval and pollingBinaryInterval.
    • The old names remain as deprecated aliases; the new names win when both are given.
  • Changed the atomic default to false with polling. An explicit value is preserved.
  • Made close() terminal: add() now throws once closing has started. Construct a new watcher instead.
  • Validated options in the constructor: invalid backend, atomic, depth, awaitWriteFinish, and polling intervals throw TypeError.
  • Emitted errors from add() as error events instead of unhandled rejections (#1378).
  • Made getWatched() return a null-prototype object, so a watched directory named __proto__ is listed (#1493). Use Object.hasOwn() instead of hasOwnProperty() on the result.
  • Stopped applying ignored to directories above a path passed to watch() or add(), so a missing path is still watched through its parent (#1374). Other entries in those directories are still filtered.

Fixes

  • Fixed a 100% CPU loop when the process working directory containing a relatively watched file was deleted (#1474).
  • Fixed watching a filesystem root, which emitted unlink and unlinkDir for every entry (#1184, #452).
  • Fixed UNKNOWN errors from fs.watch on macOS sockets, which prevented watching /var/run (#1391).
  • Fixed a symlink whose target passes through a regular file (ENOTDIR) disabling watching of its directory and preventing ready (#1476).
  • Fixed files created in a newly added directory between its scan and watch registration being missed (#1471).
  • Fixed watching a missing nested path stopping its parent directory's subtree from being watched (#1470).
  • Fixed false change events on Windows when many sibling files are written (#1466).
  • Fixed duplicate add events for unchanged files under directory activity (#1465).
  • Fixed replacing a watched directory with a file of the same name hanging the process (#1464).
  • Fixed persistent watching stopping after a watched directory was removed (#1463).
  • Fixed a deleted watched path not being reported when recreated: previously only a deleted file that was the sole watched path was watched for its return. Any path passed to watch() or add() is now awaited from its nearest existing parent.
  • Fixed event throttling discarding updates; the newest differing change is now replayed when the window closes (#1455).
  • Fixed relative ignored paths; relative strings now resolve against cwd or the process working directory (#1436).
  • Fixed files not being detected when their directory did not exist before watching (#1422).

  • Fixed changes not being detected after the second save (#1399).

  • Fixed re-watching a path not honoring ignoreInitial (#1386).
  • Fixed EISDIR errors during the initial scan of network drives (#1376).
  • Fixed watching an array of absolute file paths (#1366).

  • Documented that unwatched paths stay ignored until they are added again (#1439).

title: chore(deps)(deps): bump react-i18next from 17.0.21 to 17.1.13 in /gitnexus-web
body:
Bumps [react-i18next](https://github.com/i18next/react-i18next) from 17.0.21 to 17.1.13.
Changelog

Sourced from react-i18next's changelog.

17.1.13

  • fix(types): the react init options keep their types with i18next 27. i18next 27 declares ReactOptions (the type of i18next.init({ react })) as an empty interface and leaves its shape to react-i18next, so with react-i18next 17 the react options were no longer checked and getDefaults().useSuspense did not compile. react-i18next now declares them itself, with exactly the types i18next 26 has: TypeScript accepts the repeated declaration on i18next 26, and on i18next 27 it fills in the empty interface. Nothing changes with i18next 26.

17.1.12

  • fix(types): type-checking a <Trans> is fast again with large resources. Since 17.0.2 the return type of the key was a type parameter of Trans, so TypeScript also computed it for every key of the namespace: with 50 namespaces of 200 keys, one <Trans> cost about 1.3 million more type instantiations than in 17.0.1, with or without a values prop. The return type is computed inside the values prop again, as in 17.0.1, and values still only needs the variables of the given i18nKey (#1913). The exported TransProps type loses the Ret parameter added in 17.0.2, so its 6th parameter is the element props E again, as before 17.0.2. Thanks @​leshaduduk (#1947), fixes #1946.

17.1.11

  • fix(Trans): with i18next 26.7.0 or later and debug: true, the variables of object children are no longer logged as missing. When Trans interpolates before parsing (with count, values, tOptions or interpolation.defaultVariables), its t() call leaves the placeholders of object children like {{ name }} for after parsing, and i18next 26.7 logs each of them as missed to pass in variable name, although the output is right: <Trans count={n}>Hello <b>{{ name }}</b>, you have {{ count }} messages.</Trans> logged it for name. Trans now passes a missingInterpolationHandler to that call that does what i18next does without one (it keeps the placeholder, and a variable passed as undefined becomes empty), so the output is unchanged. It does not with skipOnVariables: false, a missingInterpolationHandler of your own, an i18nFormat plugin, or an escape function that would change the placeholders of the children.

17.1.10

  • fix(Trans): markup inside an interpolated value is no longer parsed as translation markup. Trans interpolates values (and count, values in tOptions, or the whole string when there are no children) before it parses the string. With interpolation.escapeValue: false, or with an i18nFormat plugin (i18next-icu, i18next-mf2, i18next-fluent), which inserts values without escaping whatever escapeValue says, a value like <0 href="https://example.com">x</0> was rendered as component 0 with that href, overriding the props of the component, and <strong>x</strong> in a value became a real <strong>. Trans now escapes the values for this t() call (with a plugin, the string values in values) and decodes the entities after parsing, so such a value renders as text, and a " in a value no longer closes an attribute like <Item title="{{name}}" />. {{- var}} stays the explicit way for a translator to insert a value unescaped. As with shouldUnescape, entities written in these translations (for example &) are now decoded instead of shown literally. Output with escapeValue: true and no plugin, with i18next-icu escapeVariables: true, and with children and no values or count is unchanged.
  • fix(IcuTrans): the same for IcuTrans with escapeValue: false or an i18nFormat plugin: a value like <0>x</0> no longer becomes the first component, and a value containing an entity like & is no longer decoded a second time.

17.1.9

  • fix(useTranslation): namespaces added to or removed from the ns array are now picked up. The hook used the array itself as the useMemo dependency list, and React only compares the entries both lists have in common when its length changes, so going from useTranslation(['nsA']) to useTranslation(['nsA', 'nsB']) kept returning ['nsA']: React warned that the dependency array changed size, nsB was never loaded, and with nsMode: 'fallback' keys only in nsB rendered as the key. Removing a namespace kept the old list the same way. The namespaces are now compared by content, so a growing list loads the new namespace (suspending until it is loaded, as switching from 'nsA' to 'nsB' already does) and t uses it. Lists that keep their length behave as before. Thanks @​lprnmns (#1945).

17.1.8

  • fix(Trans): an interpolation variable named format is no longer dropped. Trans reads format in an interpolation object as the formatter name ({{ value, format }}), so with {{ format }} as the only key nothing was left: <Trans>Export as {{ format }}</Trans> warned TRANS_INVALID_OBJ and used the default string Export as instead of Export as {{format}}. When format is the object's only key it is now treated as the variable. {{ value, format }} works as before. Without an i18nKey, the key derived from the children changes accordingly, from Export as to Export as {{format}}. i18next-cli serializes Trans children with react-i18next, so extracting with this version produces the same key. Thanks @​Pharex38 (#1944).

17.1.7

  • fix(IcuTrans): each HTML entity in a translation is now decoded exactly once. Named, decimal and hexadecimal entities were decoded in three passes, and each pass decoded the output of the previous one, so an escaped numeric entity was decoded twice: "Write &[#169](https://github.com/i18next/react-i18next/issues/169); to get &[#169](https://github.com/i18next/react-i18next/issues/169);" rendered Write © to get © instead of Write &[#169](https://github.com/i18next/react-i18next/issues/169); to get ©, and &[#60](https://github.com/i18next/react-i18next/issues/60); rendered < instead of &[#60](https://github.com/i18next/react-i18next/issues/60);. This also hit interpolated values with escapeValue: true, where a value containing &[#60](https://github.com/i18next/react-i18next/issues/60); is escaped to &[#60](https://github.com/i18next/react-i18next/issues/60);. Escaped named entities like &lt; already stayed <, as browsers and Trans decode them. Unknown named entities and entities above U+10FFFF still stay as written. Thanks @​Pharex38 (#1943).

17.1.6

  • fix(Trans): a count passed in tOptions is now used. Trans spread tOptions and then set its own count prop, so a count only in tOptions was overwritten with undefined: <Trans i18nKey="items" tOptions={{ count: 5 }} /> rendered the key items instead of 5 items, and with children Trans could pick the wrong plural form. Like context, Trans now falls back to tOptions.count, handled the same way as the count prop. A count prop, a count in the children or values.count still take precedence, and tOptions is not modified. Thanks @​nk-batman21 (#1942).

17.1.5

  • fix(Trans): with an array of keys and no children, Trans now falls back to the last key when none of them has a translation, as t() does. It used the array itself as defaultValue, which i18next handles as an object, so <Trans i18nKey={['notifications.crm_item_created', 'crm_item_created']} components={[<strong />]} /> rendered key 'crm_item_created (en)' returned an object instead of string. instead of crm_item_created. An array of selectors falls back to the key of the last selector. The first key that has a translation still wins, and children, defaults and tOptions.defaultValue are used as before. With saveMissing, these calls now report the missing key, like a single i18nKey does. Thanks @​nk-batman21 (#1941).

17.1.4

  • fix(types): without allowObjectInHTMLChildren, the children of HTML elements now use React's own type (DOMAttributes<T>['children']) instead of the ReactI18NextChildren | Iterable<ReactI18NextChildren> union. Both accept the same children, so nothing compiles differently. For default installs the global HTMLAttributes augmentation now repeats whatever @types/react declares, so changes in React's types flow through instead of meeting a copy, and type errors on element children no longer list an extra Iterable<...>. With allowObjectInHTMLChildren: true nothing changes. First step of #1928.

17.1.3

  • fix(IcuTrans): numeric HTML entities above U+FFFF, like emoji, now decode to the right character. "Hello 👋 <0>friend</0> &[#127881](https://github.com/i18next/react-i18next/issues/127881);" rendered U+F44B and U+F389, private-use glyphs that usually show as a box, instead of 👋 and 🎉: the decoder used String.fromCharCode, which keeps only the low 16 bits of the code point. This shows up with translations that a TMS or CMS exports HTML-encoded. Entities above U+10FFFF, which are no valid code points, now stay as written instead of becoming U+0000. Entities below U+10000, including surrogate pairs written as two entities, decode as before. Thanks @​nk-batman21 (#1940).

17.1.2

  • fix(Trans): when the only child is a string, a tag whose index the children don't have now renders its own text. <Trans i18nKey="welcome">Welcome</Trans> with "Welcome <1>friend</1>" rendered Welcome e, and defaults="Hi <1>there</1>" with the child Hi rendered Hi i. The fallback for a single object of components ({{ 1: <strong /> }}) looked the tag up on the string and rendered one of its characters. It now applies only when that child is an object, so {{ 1: <strong /> }} renders as before, and the tag falls back to its inner text, as it already did with several children or with a number or an element as the only child. This also stops a single-entry array child holding null ({[null]}, e.g. from a .map that returned null) from throwing Cannot read properties of null. Thanks @​Cayan (#1939).

17.1.1

... (truncated)

title: feat(embeddings): share embeddings across branches of the same repository
body:
## Summary

Analyzing a second branch of a repository no longer re-embeds the world. Sibling branch indexes donate their embeddings by content hash, gated on embedding identity, on both analyze paths:

- the **inline embedding pipeline** (`runEmbeddingPipeline`) harvests sibling `CodeEmbedding` rows (flat slot, `branches/*` slots, shared-store checkout slots) into a demand-driven, repo-scoped cache keyed by content hash, and copies rows for hash hits instead of calling the embedder;
- the **staged publication job** (`runPublishedEmbeddingJob` — the path shipped entry points actually take under `graphPublication: 'auto'`) takes sibling slots as donors whose sealed artifact matches the job's exact space, joining the job's existing provenance-checking reuse and line rebasing.

The analyze log reports the reused-vs-fresh split on both paths.

## Motivation / context

Refs #3631. Per-branch LadybugDBs (#2106) mean two branches differing by one file each paid the full embedding cost. The issue's Phase 1 asks for a repo-scoped embedding cache keyed by content hash + model identity (not node id), copying sibling vectors into the new branch's `CodeEmbedding` table during `analyze --embeddings`, skipping the embedder for hits, and reporting reused vs newly embedded counts. Phase 2 (building the graph incrementally from a sibling via `shouldEscalateIncrementalWrite`) is a separate step and is not attempted here.

Acceptance criteria from the issue, as covered:

- ✅ Second branch reuses vectors for unchanged text; new embedding work scales with the diff (integration test: 1 of 3 files re-embedded).
- ✅ Changed file is re-embedded under its new hash.
- ✅ Deleted file is absent from the new branch's index (reuse only ever targets live graph nodes).
- ✅ Different model / dimensions / `EMBEDDING_TEXT_VERSION` ⇒ no reuse (identity gate; tested via a model change).
- ✅ Search on branch B only ever sees B's graph — rows are copied *into* B's own database; no shared vector table, no cross-DB reads at query time.
- ✅ Deleting B's index leaves A's embeddings intact (asserted in the integration test).
- ✅ Single-branch repos keep the flat `.gitnexus/` layout and unchanged behavior (no siblings ⇒ no harvest, no log line, own-cache path untouched).
- ✅ Reuse runs under the shipped entry-point shape (`graphPublication: 'auto'`), covered by an integration test in that shape.

## Areas touched

- [x] `gitnexus/` (CLI / core / MCP server)
- [ ] `gitnexus-web/` (Vite / React UI)
- [ ] `.github/` (workflows, actions)
- [ ] `eval/` or other tooling
- [ ] Docs / agent config only (`AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `.cursor/`, `llms.txt`, etc.)

## Scope & constraints

**In scope**

- Repo-scoped sibling embedding reuse for both analyze paths: the inline pipeline (`runEmbeddingPipeline`, the path #3631 names) and the staged publication job (`runPublishedEmbeddingJob`), with the same identity gate and content-hash keying.
- Sibling sources: the flat slot, every `branches/<slug>/` slot, and — for shared-store checkouts (#3352) — every other checkout slot of the store (including its `branches/*`), whose recorded graph pointer is resolved with the existing `resolveGraphPath`.
- A persisted provenance stamp for inline-pipeline runs (`RepoMeta.embeddingIdentity`), so slots written by the inline path can serve as siblings; published runs record the same digests in `vectorGeneration`, and published slots donate through their sealed artifacts in the publication job.
- Tests: unit coverage for the identity recipes, cache keying, claims and slot enumeration; a composite reuse-source unit test; real-database integration tests running two full branch analyzes on both paths, including the `graphPublication: 'auto'` shape.

**Explicitly out of scope / not done here**

- Phase 2 of #3631: incremental graph construction from a sibling index (`shouldEscalateIncrementalWrite`) — untouched.
- Cross-mode reuse between a local `.gitnexus` and a shared store for the same repo (each mode enumerates only its own slot family).
- Bug #3474 (duplicate-PK abort on copy-on-write re-embed) — not fixed; the copy path is constructed to never trigger it (see Implementation notes).
- Persisting a per-node expected chunk count in sibling indexes (raised in review as the deeper completeness fix): nothing in the sibling DB records one today, and adding it is a schema/write-path change across every embedding writer; the completion-state markers are used as the count anchor instead (see Round 2 notes).

## Implementation notes

- **Where the cache lives:** `src/core/embeddings/sibling-embedding-cache.ts`. `findSiblingSlotDirs` enumerates sibling slots; the cache is demand-driven — creation reads sibling metas only, a sibling's row metadata (never the vector column) is scanned lazily on the first lookup that reaches it, and vectors are fetched per claimed node. Eligibility is gated on the sibling's persisted embedding identity (below); a missing, locked, legacy-shaped, or identity-mismatched sibling is skipped and the run embeds fresh.
- **Key composition:** `contentHash` (the existing `contentHashForNode` value) → the complete chunk-row set for that hash, claimed **per node**: a hash is offered only when one sibling node holds its full chunk set (chunkIndex 0..n−1 under one stored hash), verified against the sibling's completion state (siblings mid-incremental-write are skipped; nodes in an interrupted checkpoint's `pendingNodeIds` or a recovery's `unsafeNodeIds` are excluded), and fetched rows are re-verified before copying. Claims are indexed under the stored hash and, for full-form (`hash:inputsDigest`) rows, under the bare prefix; copies write the full stored hash. Node ids are never used as keys; copied rows are rewritten to the target node id at insert time.
- **Identity gate:** for the inline path, the sibling's metadata must carry `embeddingIdentity` (inline run) whose `vectorIdentity` **and** `inputIdentity` equal the consuming run's; slots carrying `vectorGeneration`/`embeddingJob` are skipped there (their vectors live in the published artifact). The digests are factored out of `embeddingJobIdentity` into exported `embeddingVectorIdentity` / `embeddingInputIdentity` helpers (single recipe, unit-tested for equality with the job identity). The gate is load-bearing, not redundant: `contentHashForNode` folds in the model id only for non-default models, so the hash alone cannot prove two indexes share a vector space. Harvested rows are additionally width-checked against the run's dimensions.
- **Where reuse hooks in (inline):** `run-analyze` Phase 4 computes the run's digests, builds the sibling cache (excluding the target's own read/write graph paths), and passes it via `EmbeddingPipelineOptions.siblingCache`. In the pipeline's incremental filter, a node whose current hash has a claimed row set is planned for copy — unless it is in `forceReembedNodeIds`, which always wins. Copies are applied per batch: stale own rows for that batch are deleted immediately before its inserts via `batchInsertEmbeddings` — so a copied row lands exactly once and a planned node is filtered out of the embed loop (#3474-safe by construction).
- **Counts:** the pipeline result gains `reusedNodes` / `reusedChunks` (optional fields; the pipeline always sets them). `nodesProcessed` keeps its existing meaning (nodes the embedder produced), mirroring how same-index cache hits are already excluded. `run-analyze` logs: `Reused N node embeddings (C chunks) from sibling branch indexes; embedded M nodes fresh.`
- **Provenance stamp:** Phase 5's meta gains `embeddingIdentity` on the inline path only — set when the pipeline ran, carried forward when a run produced no embeddings, cleared by `--drop-embeddings`. The stamp is only written when it honestly describes the retained rows: if the prior stamp's `vectorIdentity` differs from the run's and retained rows exist, those rows are force-re-embedded instead; with no prior stamp, retained rows of unknown provenance get no stamp. The field is optional and additive: older binaries ignore it, and its absence means "no evidence", so the sibling gate simply skips such slots (backward-compatible persisted-data change; no DB schema change, no migration).
- **Line provenance (inline):** a copied row keeps the start/end lines of the index it came from — the same provenance the existing same-index restore already accepts when a file is edited above an unchanged node. (The publication path rebases lines by delta; the inline path never has, and this change matches the inline path it extends.)
- Lazy-embeddings convention (#2370) is preserved: all new runtime imports in `run-analyze` are dynamic, inside the Phase 4 block; the top-level import is type-only.

## Round 2 notes (tri-review follow-up)

Round 1 wired only the inline pipeline; the tri-review showed that path never runs for shipped entry points, which all pass `graphPublication: 'auto'`. Round 2 therefore wires sibling reuse into the staged publication job, following the review's suggested route:

- Donors are sibling slots whose **sealed artifact** matches the job's exact space — the space key is the identity gate (vector + input identity, dimensions, schema). Each donor's owner is validated against the sibling's own work manifest and its vectors file must pass `assertOwnedVectorGeneration`. A new `readEmbeddingArtifactSpaceReadOnly` (storage/embedding-artifact.ts) reads foreign space records without reconciling or writing the foreign slot; a pending rebase intent reads as absent.
- Donors open as read-mode `VectorStore`s and join the job's existing provenance-checking reuse through a new `CompositeEmbeddingReuseSource` (own fallback/legacy first, then siblings; chunk reads routed to the receipt's origin), so the runner's receipt verification and line rebasing (embedding-job-runner.ts) apply unchanged. The reader half of the pool reservation is subdivided across all open readers (8 MiB floor per reader, max 4 sibling donors).
- The review's other findings are addressed in the inline path as well: hash keying for full-form rows, the stamp-provenance rule, the gate reading only the artifact each path actually consumes, completion-state-anchored chunk completeness, demand-driven harvest, `--drop-embeddings` suppressing sibling reuse on both paths, bounded-batch copy deletes, and per-node claims for duplicate hashes. The reply comment on this PR has the point-by-point disposition.

## Testing & verification

New/updated tests:

- `test/unit/sibling-embedding-cache.test.ts` — **17 passed**: identity helpers equal `embeddingJobIdentity`'s persisted digests and separate on model/dimensions/text-version; per-node claims (complete chunk sets by hash, dual key forms, duplicate-hash nodes judged independently, unsafe/incomplete nodes excluded); slot enumeration for local and shared-store layouts.
- `test/unit/embedding-reuse-composite.test.ts` — **4 passed**: ordering (own source first), per-source attribution, chunk reads routed to the receipt's origin.
- `test/integration/cross-branch-embedding-reuse.test.ts` — **7 passed**: two real git branches analyzed end-to-end (only the embedder is faked) — inline reuse with identical hash and vector for unchanged files, changed file re-embedded, deleted file absent, sibling index intact after deleting the new branch's index; the `graphPublication: 'auto'` publication-job shape (second run submits only the changed file's texts, logs the reused/fresh split, artifact holds reused hashes verbatim); same-width HTTP model switch force-re-embeds retained rows and updates the stamp; `--drop-embeddings` suppresses reuse; an interrupted sibling donates nothing for its pending node.

Commands run (Node v24.22.1):

- [x] `cd gitnexus && npx tsc --noEmit` — pass, no errors (also `npm run typecheck:tests` — pass)
- [x] `cd gitnexus && npm run test:unit` — 1,206 files, 28,228 tests: **28,106 passed, 63 skipped, 59 failed**. All 59 failures are confined to 7 environment-sensitive files unrelated to embeddings (git-clone, review-agent-workflow, auto-sync, asyncapi-document, cli-index-help, parse-cache-benchmark-pairing, r-replacement-scaling) and reproduce **identically on a pristine worktree of unmodified HEAD**; the per-test sets differ only by two timing flakes flipping in opposite directions. Zero regressions attributable to this PR.
- [x] Embedding-adjacent integration batch (14 files: analysis-embedding-flow, embedding-job-controller/restart, shared-store-embedding-reuse, legacy vector source/controller, embedding-identity-integrity, load-cached-embeddings-spill, embedding-chunking-lifecycle, analyze-cli/HTTP embedding phases, analyze-embedding-flags-e2e, embedding-vector-store, legacy-vector-reuse-index) — **160/160 passed**.
- [x] `cd gitnexus && npm run test:dupes` — 0 findings
- [x] Prettier — applied to all changed files with the repo `.prettierrc` settings (the Tailwind plugin is absent from this sandbox's node_modules; it only affects Tailwind CSS files, of which this PR has none)

- [ ] ESLint — cannot execute in this sandbox (`@typescript-eslint/eslint-plugin` absent from node_modules, pre-existing); CI will run it.
- [ ] `gitnexus-web` checks — not applicable (no web changes)

## Risk & rollout

- **Behavior change:** second-and-later branch analyzes with embeddings get faster on both analyze paths and print the reuse split. No CLI flags, env vars, MCP tools, or query paths change; semantic search reads only the target DB, as before.
- **Persisted data:** one new optional metadata field (`embeddingIdentity`). Indexes written before this change simply never serve as inline siblings until re-analyzed; indexes written by it are readable by older binaries (unknown field ignored). No reindex is required; `--drop-embeddings` clears the stamp.
- **Failure mode:** every reuse failure degrades to today's behavior (embed fresh). Sibling DBs and artifacts are opened read-only and are never written.
- **Rollback:** revert is safe — the only residue is the ignored metadata field and any copied rows, which are ordinary `CodeEmbedding` rows indistinguishable from embedded ones.
- **Residual risk:** copied rows on the inline path carry the source index's line numbers (see Implementation notes); a function moved without content changes reports the sibling's offsets until its content changes or a forced re-embed. This matches the existing same-index restore semantics; the publication path rebases.

title: fix: improve Python caller accuracy and flag incompatible calls
body:
## Summary

Python upstream impact now reports callers of a class without counting every file that imports its module. When a Python function or constructor drops an explicit keyword parameter, `detect-changes` points to the caller that still passes it.

## Motivation / context

On the 1,570-file Python fixture for #3972, the index found all 1,584 expected caller-file pairs across 30 symbols, but also reported 777 unrelated pairs. With this change the same fixture returns all 1,584 expected pairs and zero extras. The reporter’s original repository was unavailable.

## Areas touched

- [x] `gitnexus/` (CLI, core, MCP server, hooks)
- [x] `gitnexus-shared/` (impact risk scoring)
- [x] `gitnexus-web/` (incomplete traversal handling and risk regressions)

## Scope & constraints

- The Python compatibility check covers explicit keywords on statically resolved calls, including new staged callers. It lists call sites and reports incomplete coverage for bounded scans, unavailable source or unresolved dynamic behavior.
- Mixed code and Markdown diffs count documentation sections separately. Docs-only diffs still list changed headings.
- Issue #3972 item 6 requested count refresh on explicit `analyze`. This includes the up-to-date and `--self-commit` paths: a count-only change to a tracked instruction file can now produce a diff after an explicit run (#2907). Use `--instruction-file AGENTS.md` or `--instruction-file CLAUDE.md` to select one file. The stale-index hook checks for code changes across the entire unindexed commit range. Related-symbol hints use the whole search phrase.
- Incremental indexing recomputes calls inferred from a unique name when another file adds or removes a competing definition. CLI, MCP and web impact count omitted name-only calls and report the retained caller count as a lower bound. An incomplete walk that would otherwise rate LOW or MEDIUM reports UNKNOWN. Raw graph queries expose them with `reason = 'global-name-fallback'`.
- The analyzer sizes its LadybugDB writer pool for retained text as well as graph elements. It reserves additional space when building keyword indexes and respects the configured resource ceiling and explicit pool setting.

## Implementation notes

The MCP dispatches call-compatibility and type-import checks through provider capabilities. The Python provider owns its syntax and keyword semantics. The query registry loads syntax parsers only when a check needs them. CI checks all MCP, CLI, HTTP, core analysis and web Graph-RAG modules for language-specific routing and compares other changed shared runtime code with the merge base.

Upstream risk follows the number of direct dependants. A target with one caller on 20 execution flows now reports `LOW` and still lists all 20 flows. The thresholds for `MEDIUM`, `HIGH`, and `CRITICAL` are 5, 15, and 200 direct dependants, respectively.

## Testing & verification

- Caller parity (#3972 item 2). In a mixed-language fixture, removing a competing JavaScript definition reproduced five callers after incremental indexing and 106 after a forced rebuild. Both now return the same five caller IDs. Raw graph queries returned 101 name-only calls with a unique definition and zero with the competing definition restored, in both index modes.
- Default import (#3972 item 5). A 1,570-file Python fixture with long docstrings exhausted the old 260 MiB pool during bulk COPY. The default `gitnexus analyze` published 20,630 nodes and 45,960 edges. A live full-text query returned an indexed function without a pool override.

- [x] CLI build and test typechecks passed. The earlier 33-suite run passed 1,682 tests. After review, the execution reporter verified all 651 affected core cases and the two native database suites passed all 84 tests. The CI architecture job runs the merge-base check with an explicit base. To rerun the Python and impact regressions from `gitnexus/`, use `npx vitest run test/unit/python-signature-changes.test.ts test/unit/impact-risk.test.ts test/integration/impact-private-type-source.test.ts`.
- [x] All 533 web tests passed with `npm test` in `gitnexus-web/`. The web typecheck passed with `npx tsc -b --noEmit`.
- [x] On the constructor fixture, `detect-changes --scope compare` reported `use_invoice.py:3`, named the removed `legacy` keyword, and rated the change high.
- [ ] The full CLI suite has not been verified locally. See the sharded CI jobs for the remaining suites.

On real Git fixtures, 1,600 candidate callers yielded the same eight broken calls in a median 321 ms. Comparing 512 edited definitions fell from 3,249 ms to 314 ms and preserved the reported call site. Cold checks on a TypeScript diff took 215 ms versus 219 ms on the pre-refactor commit (b1bafdf37) (three runs each).

On the GitNexus worktree index (about 330,000 relationships), five alternating warm runs measured a median of 55 ms for the two previous relationship counts and 26 ms for the combined count, including name-only calls. These timings cover the read before incremental deletion.

## Risk & rollout

Automation that gates on upstream `HIGH` or `CRITICAL` may now warn less often. Consumers that use execution-flow breadth can still read the process and module counts. Existing indexes can use these changes without a migration.

title: perf(indexing): avoid repeated lookups during call resolution
body:
## Summary

Call resolution now skips scopes that cannot bind the requested name and reuses receiver-type lookups within a pass. Looking up a name from 384 nested scopes with unrelated declarations took 769 scope reads, down from 74,688.

## Motivation / context

On a one-file edit, the parser reused 867 files, but the analyzer still resolved calls across the language group before selecting graph rows to write. Scope resolution took a median 14.2 seconds out of roughly 29 seconds on the CI corpus.

The CI job that prompted this investigation failed three cache-interning timing checks. Both revisions ran the same compiled interner on the same TypeScript and JavaScript corpus. Fresh and persistent indexing passed the job’s budget. [Original CI measurements](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/actions/runs/44575398963/job/135752736338)

## Areas touched

- [x] `gitnexus/` (CLI / core)
- [x] `gitnexus-shared/` (scope lookup)

## Scope & constraints

**In scope.** Shared lexical lookup and receiver-call resolution across language providers.

**Explicitly out of scope / not done here.** Reusing resolved calls across indexing runs. A new method can change a call in an untouched file, even when that call previously had no target. The analyzer still resolves the language group on each edit.

## Implementation notes

The navigation cache checks declarations and imports for the requested spelling. It considers both the lexical imports and the finalized imports, and leaves source-position and namespace decisions to the resolver. Receiver resolution skips preparation for files without receiver sites and reuses stable declared owners within one pass. Callbacks that can change bindings force a fresh owner lookup.

## Testing & verification

- [x] `cd gitnexus && npx tsc --noEmit` and `npm run build`. All 65 tests in the four changed regression files passed.
- Ran `cd gitnexus && npm test` in groups. All reported failures passed on isolated reruns. The full suite did not produce a single clean run.
- Compared baseline and candidate code-graph fingerprints across seven single-file edits and the initial seed. All matched, including a missing method becoming available and a new implementation changing dispatch in an untouched caller. The compact fixtures also matched a fresh index after each edit.

Seven paired warm edits on the pinned CI corpus produced the following end-to-end measurements. Each build ran once per edit, in a fresh process, including graph and full-text index writes.

| Metric | Baseline median | PR median | Median paired change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Wall time | 29.05 s | 28.81 s | −0.49% |
| CPU time | 35.40 s | 36.60 s | +2.31% |
| Peak resident memory | 1,720 MiB | 1,753 MiB | +1.62% |

These measurements do not establish an end-to-end speedup.

## Risk & rollout

Semantic rename consumes these same call targets. Regression coverage exercises shadowing, imports, source positions and binding changes during a pass. An existing index can incur a one-time parser-cache rebuild when it first uses the changed analyzer. Reverting this commit restores the previous lookup behavior.

- [x] No secrets, tokens, or machine-specific paths committed.
