title: chore(deps)(deps): bump i18next from 26.4.7 to 26.7.2 in /gitnexus-web
body:
Bumps [i18next](https://github.com/i18next/i18next) from 26.4.7 to 26.7.2.
Release notes

Sourced from i18next's releases.

v26.7.2

  • fix: the debug-mode deprecation warning for a language code without a region no longer says that v27 replaces aliases. 26.7.0 and 26.7.1 warned that v27 turns 'iw' into 'he' or 'tl' into 'fil' and asked you to rename them. v27 only gives such codes their canonical casing ('EN' becomes 'en', 'IW' becomes 'iw'), so iw, tl, eng and similar codes stay as they are. If you renamed them because of that warning, you can keep or restore the old codes. The warning now only appears when the casing changes.

v26.7.1

  • fix: reloadResources() retries the bundles that failed to load. The load queue skipped them also when reloading, so a language whose first load failed (a backend or network outage at startup) stayed missing. i18next-http-backend 4.0.8, i18next-chained-backend 5.0.7 and i18next-locize-backend 10.0.5 reload through reloadResources() with i18next 26.7, so their reloadInterval no longer recovered from such a failure, as their own reload did before.
  • fix: reloadResources() without languages reloads the current languages and every language the backend loaded or tried to load, for the instance and its clones, as the API docs describe ("pass languages and namespaces if you don't want to reload all"). It reloaded only the current languages, so on a server (one clone per request with i18next-http-middleware) a backend's reloadInterval never refreshed the languages loaded for requests. It never requests cimode. With languages given, nothing changes.

v26.7.0

The last 26.x minor before v27, which follows in about a week. It adds the APIs v27 builds on, and with debug: true it warns wherever a setup relies on something v27 changes. Most of the v27 defaults are existing options, so you can try them now:

i18next.init({
  debug: true, // prints the warnings below
  fallbackLng: 'en', // v27: fallbackLng defaults to false, set your source language (no implicit 'dev')
  returnEmptyString: false, // v27 default: an empty string falls back like a missing key
  cleanCode: true, // close to v27, which canonicalizes codes without a region ('EN' becomes 'en')
});

declare module 'i18next' {
  interface CustomTypeOptions {
    strictInterpolationChecks: true; // v27 default
    returnEmptyString: false; // v27 default
  }
}

The other v27 changes (/ no longer escaped in values, a logger and post-processors per instance, the key instead of a sentence for an object hit, the dotted-language store calls and *Escaped options removed) have no switch; the debug warnings below show where they apply.

  • feat: with the default skipOnVariables: true, a missing interpolation variable is now logged in debug mode, once per string and variable: missed to pass in variable name for interpolating Hello {{name}}. The raw {{name}} reached the UI without any log line, even with debug: true, because the warning only ran with skipOnVariables: false. A variable passed as undefined and a missingInterpolationHandler still log nothing.
  • feat: i18next.hydrate(resources, lng) puts resources rendered on the server into the store and changes to the server's language, each only the first time. It does what react-i18next's useSSR did by writing resourceStore.data, options.ns, isInitialized, initializedStoreOnce and initializedLanguageOnce directly, and sets the same flags, so integrations can switch to it and stay compatible with code that still reads or writes them. On a clone it does nothing, as useSSR does: a clone shares its parent's store (one clone per request with i18next-http-middleware). Called before init(), it logs a warning and changes nothing.
  • feat: services.utils.reloadResources() lets a backend reload its bundles through i18next (as i18next.reloadResources(), with retries and the loaded event), instead of calling backendConnector.read() and loaded() itself as the reloadInterval of i18next-http-backend and i18next-chained-backend does. Without languages (no lng, no detector, the default fallbackLng), reloadResources() reloads nothing instead of throwing Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'forEach'); a backend that also reloads preload passes its languages.
  • feat: backends and async language detectors can declare their calling convention with callbackApi (an instance or static property). true: read(language, namespace, callback), create(languages, namespace, key, fallbackValue, callback, options) and detect(callback); false: they return a promise or a value, and create gets the options as its fifth argument. Without it, i18next keeps guessing from the number of parameters (Function.length), which default and rest parameters change: i18next-chained-backend's create(..., clb = () => {}, opts = {}) has length 4 and never got its options (isUpdate), and i18next-http-backend's callback form of create has length 5, the length reserved for the callback-less form. Guessing is deprecated: in debug mode an unmarked backend or async detector logs a deprecation warning, once per init().
  • feat: isSafeLanguageCode(code) is exported for plugins that take a language from a request, a URL or storage: letters, digits, -, _, @ and . (no ..), at most 128 characters, not a prototype key. It is not a BCP 47 check, so en_US, zh_Hant_TW, sr@latin and de_DE.UTF-8 pass; markup, slashes and spaces do not. The language detector, i18next-http-middleware and i18next-http-backend each have their own rule today.
  • feat: use() logs a warning in debug mode when a second backend, language detector, i18nFormat or formatter replaces the first one; only one of each is used per instance, and losing an ICU setup this way was silent. As use() usually runs before init(), the warning is printed once init() has set up the logger.
  • feat(types): ParseKeysWithoutVariables<Ns, KPrefix>, the keys t() takes without options: their string has no variables, and a plural key is left out when its forms take count. A wrapper typed with it, like (key: ParseKeysWithoutVariables<'common'>) => t(key), compiles with strictInterpolationChecks without a cast.
  • feat(types): defaultVariables in CustomTypeOptions declares the variables interpolation.defaultVariables fills in at runtime (defaultVariables: { appName: string }). They become optional in the t() options, also with strictInterpolationChecks; passed, they keep their type.
  • feat(types): interpolationFormatSeparator in CustomTypeOptions for a custom interpolation.formatSeparator: the types split {{price, currency}} at a hard-coded ,, so with formatSeparator: ';' the format was not recognized. The per-call skipInterpolation option is typed, and returnedObjectHandler may return a value (what it returns is what t() returns; it was typed as returning void).
  • feat(types): SelectorFn, ApplyTarget, ConstrainTarget and GetSource are exported on purpose, under their current names. react-i18next imports them for Trans; they were importable only because every declaration in the type files counts as exported.
  • fix(types): with nsSeparator: false in CustomTypeOptions, the key union no longer contains nsfalsekey-style keys for the other namespaces, and a key that contains the text false (isfalsey) is no longer split at it, which typed its t() result as never.
  • fix: with clones (i18next-http-middleware makes one per request), saveMissing now checks that the namespace is loaded for the instance that misses the key. Each cloneInstance() pointed the parent's services.utils.hasLoadedNamespace at the new clone, and the backend connector, which all clones share, used that one: a key missing in one request was not saved (did not save key ... as the namespace ... was not yet loaded) while a newer request was still loading its language, and the parent's services.utils answered for the newest clone. A clone's services.utils is now bound to the clone, and the parent keeps its own. A direct services.backendConnector.saveMissing() call, like the missing keys route of i18next-http-middleware, still checks the newest clone (follow-up to #1413).
  • fix: dir() without a language (before init(), or with no language resolved) returns 'ltr' instead of 'rtl' ([discussion #2135](https://github.com/i18next/i18next/discussions/2135)).
  • fix: t() before init() returns an empty string, as typed (with a warning when debug logging is already on); it returned undefined.
  • fix: off('a b', listener) removes the listener from both events, as on('a b', listener) adds it to both. It looked for an event named 'a b', so once('a b', listener) never removed its listener and ran it on every event.
  • deprecate: dotted languages in the resource store calls (getResource('en.translation.key'), addResource('en.translation.key', value), addResourceBundle('en.translation', resources)) log a deprecation warning in debug mode; they are removed in v27. Pass language, namespace and key as separate arguments.
  • deprecate: interpolation.prefixEscaped, suffixEscaped, nestingPrefixEscaped and nestingSuffixEscaped (inserted into the RegExp unescaped) log a deprecation warning in debug mode and are marked @deprecated; they are removed in v27. Pass the literal delimiters as prefix, suffix, nestingPrefix and nestingSuffix.
  • deprecate: compatibilityJSON is marked @deprecated (it has no effect since v24) and removed from the types in v27.
  • deprecate: a language code without a region that v27 canonicalizes differently logs a deprecation warning in debug mode: 'EN' stays 'EN' today and becomes 'en' in v27, 'iw' becomes 'he'. cleanCode: true already lower-cases them.
  • deprecate: when fallbackLng is not set, the first request for the default fallback language dev (loading it, or saving missing keys to it) logs a notice in debug mode: v27 defaults to fallbackLng: false and no longer requests dev. Set fallbackLng to your source language, or to 'dev' to keep the current behavior.

  • fix: off('a b', listener) removes the listener from both events, as on('a b', listener) adds it to both. It looked for an event named 'a b', so once('a b', listener) never removed its listener and ran it on every event.
  • deprecate: dotted languages in the resource store calls (getResource('en.translation.key'), addResource('en.translation.key', value), addResourceBundle('en.translation', resources)) log a deprecation warning in debug mode; they are removed in v27. Full Changelog: https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code-action/compare/v1.0.272...v1.0.273

⚠️ Upgrade notes: new security defaults

This release tightens what a Claude session can do, especially on content from people without write access. Workflows on @v1 get these changes automatically. Most keep working as they are, but check the items below if yours runs tests on outside pull requests, uses later steps after the action, or relies on --allowedTools as a strict list.

Sessions start in auto mode

A safety review now decides tool calls that no allow rule covers. Calls that used to be denied can run if the review passes, so --allowedTools is no longer a strict list. Workflows with a prompt can also edit workspace files without an allow rule.

Opt out: set the earlier mode in claude_args: --permission-mode acceptEdits for @claude mentions, or --permission-mode default for workflows with a prompt.

Sessions keep the earlier defaults if you set allowed_non_write_users, allowed_bots, a custom ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL or path_to_claude_code_executable. The same applies if your settings input is a file path, or sets a base URL or another permission mode.

Code-running commands are denied on outside pull requests

If a pull request's author doesn't have write access, common commands such as npm test and bun install are denied, even if claude_args allows them. The run still succeeds, so check the log for a warning.

Opt out: restrict_untrusted_prs: false. This lets code from that pull request run in a job that holds your workflow's tokens.

title: Antigravity hook: `npx rg`, `sudo grep` and `git grep` lost graph context in #4002
body:
## What happens

Since #4002, the Antigravity hook adds no graph context to a shell search that starts with a wrapper such as `npx`, `sudo`, `env` or `git grep`. Before #4002 it did.

| command | Antigravity before #4002 (3354b5075) | `main` (1da37eb46), bash | `main`, PowerShell |
|---|---|---|---|
| `npx rg UserService src` | `UserService` | none | none |
| `sudo grep -rn UserService src` | `UserService` | none | none |
| `git grep UserService` | `UserService` | none | none |
| `env NO_COLOR=1 rg UserService src` | `UserService` | none | none |
| `rg UserService src` | `UserService` | `UserService` | `UserService` |

The Claude Code and Codex hooks use the same parser and never read these forms. The Cursor and Factory hooks do read them, so the five editors disagree on the same command.

## Cause

#4002 moved Antigravity to the parser shared with the Claude runtime, `gitnexus/hooks/claude/search-command-pattern.cjs`. That parser reads a search only when `rg` or `grep` is the first word, after any bash `NAME=value` assignments. It has no list of wrappers. The Cursor and Factory parsers keep one (`wrappers` in `gitnexus-cursor-integration/hooks/gitnexus-hook.cjs`). The old Antigravity parser took the first word ending in `rg` or `grep` anywhere in the line, which covered wrappers too.

The helper header and `docs/editor-setup.md` already note the difference. The loss for Antigravity was also mentioned in the #4002 review.

## Suggested fix

Let the shared parser read past a small set of wrappers that run the next word with its own arguments, and decline when it cannot be sure:

- `npx`, `bunx` and `sudo` in both shells;
- in bash only: `env`, `command`, `exec`, `time`, `nice` and `xargs`, which are not PowerShell commands;
- `git grep`, read with the grep option table: a `git grep` option that GNU grep lacks (`--cached`, `--and`, `-p`, …) declines, as an unknown option does today.

A wrapper followed by one of its own options (`sudo -u bob rg …`, `command -v rg`, `nice -n 5 rg …`) would give no query, since some of those options take a value or run no search. `NAME=value` after `env` or `sudo` would be read as an assignment.

On Windows the Claude Code and Codex hooks read the line in both shells and keep a query only when both agree. So `env X=1 rg …` would get none there, while `npx rg …` and `git grep …` would.

title: fix(hooks): read a shell search past npx, sudo and git grep
body:
## Summary

Since #4002 the Antigravity adapter reads shell searches through `gitnexus/hooks/claude/search-command-pattern.cjs`, the helper it shares with the Claude runtime. The helper had no wrappers, so `npx rg x`, `sudo grep x` and `git grep x` lost the graph context the old Antigravity parser gave them. The Claude runtime never read them.

The helper now reads past wrappers that run the next word with its own arguments.

| command | Antigravity before #4002 | `main` | this PR, bash | this PR, PowerShell | this PR, `either` |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `npx rg UserService src` | `UserService` | none | `UserService` | `UserService` | `UserService` |
| `sudo grep -rn UserService src` | `UserService` | none | `UserService` | `UserService` | `UserService` |
| `git grep -n UserService` | `UserService` | none | `UserService` | `UserService` | `UserService` |
| `env NO_COLOR=1 rg UserService src` | `UserService` | none | `UserService` | none | none |
| `sudo -u bob rg UserService src` | `UserService` | none | none | none | none |
| `git grep --cached UserService` | `UserService` | none | none | none | none |
| `cd src && npx rg UserService` | `UserService` | none | none | none | none |

## Motivation / context

Closes #4023. The loss was also noted in the #4002 review.

## Areas touched

- [x] `gitnexus/` (CLI / core / MCP server)
- [ ] `gitnexus-web/` (Vite / React UI)

- [ ] `eval/` or other tooling
- [ ] Docs / agent config only (`AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `.cursor/`, `llms.txt`, etc.)

## Scope & constraints

**In scope**

- `search-command-pattern.cjs`:
  - `searchCommandStart` finds the word the wrappers run, and `extractSearchCommandPatterns` reads the search from there.
  - Wrappers in both shells: `npx`, `bunx` and `sudo`.
  - Wrappers in bash only: `env`, `time`, `nice`, `command`, `exec` and `xargs`. PowerShell has none of them.
  - `git` counts only before `grep`, with `--no-pager` as the one global option read past. `git -C dir grep x` gets no query.
  - git grep options are read with the grep table. An option git grep has and GNU grep lacks (`--cached`, `--and`, `-p`) is unknown there and declines the line. I checked git 2.55's `git grep -h` against the table: every shared option has the same kind in both tools.
  - A wrapper's own option (`sudo -u bob`, `nice -n 5`, `command -v rg`, `npx --yes`) is read as the command, so the line gets no query.
  - In bash, `NAME=value` words after `env` or `sudo` are read as assignments. One with a parenthesis gives no query, since bash rejects it unquoted and the quotes are gone at that point. After any other wrapper, `NAME=value` is the command and gives no query (`npx NO_COLOR=1 rg x`).

**Explicitly out of scope / not done here**

- The OpenCode plugin keeps its own parser and reads no wrapper.
- Package-manager subcommands (`pnpm exec rg`, `npm exec -- rg`, `yarn rg`) are not read. npm parses its own options anywhere before `--`, so the line alone does not say which words reach rg.

  - 20 lines that give no query: a wrapper option, `git -C`, `git log --grep`, `git rg`, git grep options GNU grep lacks, a wrapper with no search after it, `env A=(x)`, `npx NO_COLOR=1 rg`, and a wrapper after `&&`.
- [x] `test/unit/claude-hook-runtime.test.ts`: `npx rg` and `git grep` rows through the runtime.
- [x] `test/integration/antigravity-hook-e2e.test.ts`: `npx rg`, `sudo grep` and `git grep` through the adapter that `gitnexus setup` installs, with a fake `gitnexus` that records its arguments. All three fail with `main`'s helper.

title: perf(ingestion): deferred indirect resolution is single-threaded and dominates analyze wall-time on large repos
body:
## Summary

On a large Go monorepo (~48.8k files), `gitnexus analyze` spends most of its wall time in the deferred indirect-resolution pass running on a single core. The parse phase uses the worker pool efficiently; the deferred pass then leaves every other core idle for tens of minutes while memory keeps growing.

## Environment

- GitNexus 1.6.12 (container image), Node v22
- Repo: Go, 48,853 files, SDK-style with a dense cross-file symbol network (~12 edges per symbol)
- Container limits: 48 CPU / 48 GiB

## Measurements (from GITNEXUS heap-probe log lines)

- Parse phase: 8-worker pool, sustained ~57–82 files/s
- `sr-extract-end`: used_mb=8094, rss_mb=10598
- Deferred resolution phase right after: process sits at ~1 core (0.9% of 4800% total), RSS climbs 10.5 → 15+ GiB across the phase, no heap-probe milestones until it finishes
- Full analyze of this repo: 4357 s; the single-threaded middle is the largest contiguous chunk of that
- `GITNEXUS_RESOLVE_DEF_GRAPH_ID_MEMO` already defaults to on, so there is no user-facing knob left for this phase
- CPU quota is irrelevant during the phase (single-threaded); only per-core clock matters

## Problem

`src/core/ingestion/scope-resolution/pipeline/run.ts` walks `deferredIndirectSites` in a plain serial `for` loop, with shared mutable memo tables (`graph-bridge/ids.js` keys defs by immutable identity strings). From outside, the work items look largely independent per receiver/namespace key.

#4013 ("avoid repeated lookups during call resolution") improves the constant factors — thanks — but the pass remains serial.

## Suggestions

- Shard `deferredIndirectSites` by receiver/namespace bucket into N independent partitions, resolve them on the existing worker pool, and merge the (deterministic) edge output afterwards
- Alternatively: precompute the defGraphId map once (single pass under a lock) so workers only read it
- Or expose an experimental opt-in `GITNEXUS_DEFERRED_CONCURRENCY` knob

Happy to share the full heap-probe logs if useful.

title: fix(ingestion): spill lexical scopes under heap pressure for all PDG languages
body:
## Release preflight failure

During PDG indexing, rc.247 held the lexical scopes for 2,213 TypeScript files in memory while building call and dependence edges. The first sanitized task exhausted its V8 heap before the evaluation could run. Stable passed all four preflight checks. [Failed candidate job](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/actions/runs/44815932529/job/136570359504) · [Tracking issue #3500](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/issues/3500)

## Change

At 70% V8 heap use, a PDG build with a backing store can release its resident scopes before emitting edges. This applies to every provider with a syntax-tree CFG visitor or a source CFG builder, including COBOL. Emitters can look up scopes by ID, iterate scopes in insertion order and read one file's scopes at a time. Call-result type inference survives shard eviction.

Automatic spills use temporary directories. If a write fails, indexing logs a warning and continues in memory. Full-scope debug output and resolved-file callbacks keep scopes resident in automatic mode. `GITNEXUS_DISK_SCOPE_INDEX=0` selects resident scopes and `1` forces disk storage.

## Verification

| Cold rc.247 build on the sanitized task source | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Original candidate, 6 GiB | V8 heap exhausted during TypeScript call resolution |
| Original candidate, 10 GiB | 373,373 nodes and 835,148 relationships |
| Candidate with the runtime changes from `38a776602`, 6 GiB | Identical graph in 9m19s |

The cold runs used one worker, PDG enabled and a 512 KiB maximum file size. The TypeScript spill reduced used heap from 1,546 to 1,221 MiB. Every table and relationship type matched the reference by SHA-256, including properties and endpoints. The evaluation harness verified the PDG metadata and found zero benchmark markers. The graph manifest digest was `91b684ce60c1a52122b49609970afabfbf814d053bfc3adf829063fffb63c986`.

All 19 PDG providers produced identical nodes and edges with resident and spilled scopes. Each fixture built real basic blocks and CFG edges and verified that its scope tree switched to disk. A separate mixed-language fixture exercised cross-file resolution with 67 TypeScript shards, JavaScript and a one-shard cache. The CLI build and TypeScript typecheck passed.

The final build passed all 122 targeted tests across 11 suites, including incremental graph-write integrity and callback access to disk-backed files. The full local suite initially stopped when the parser build changed during a test. That entire test file passed on the fixed build. PR CI tracks the full suite.

title: fix(wiki): split large modules by package and leave IntelliJ and Gradle files out
body:
## Summary

On a Gradle project, `gitnexus wiki` gave IntelliJ files pages of their own and put a whole Maven `src/main` tree on one page. This PR changes two things:

1. `.iml`, `.ipr` and `.iws` files and `*.lockfile` files are no longer indexed, like `.idea/` and the other lockfiles already are, so the wiki never sees them.
2. A module over the page budget is now split by directory, below the directory its files share. `src/main/java/com/linkedin/metadata/{entity,graph,…}` becomes `src — main/entity`, `src — main/graph`, and so on.
   - Files sitting directly in a directory share pages up to the budget, instead of a page each. That removes the page per root file and the `metadata-io-api — metadata-io-api` duplicate.
   - A directory still over budget is split again.
   - Small neighbouring directories share a page, up to the budget.
   - Only a single file larger than the budget makes a page over it.

I measured the first version of this PR on a copy of the issue's layout, running the real CLI (`analyze`, then `wiki` against a local stand-in model). The changes made after review only touch pages that were still over budget; I did not run the CLI measurement again.

| | `main` | this branch |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Pages | 24 | 14 |
| Requests to the model (grouping, pages, overview) | 25 | 15 |
| `.iml` and `.lockfile` File nodes | 12 | 0 |
| Share of the module source sent to the model | 61% | 98% |

## Motivation / context

Closes #1060.

The two causes, on `main`:

- `shouldIgnorePath` (`config/ignore-service.ts`) keeps `.iml` files and `gradle.lockfile`, although it ignores `.idea/`, `yarn.lock`, `Cargo.lock`, `go.sum` and `poetry.lock`. `analyze` therefore indexes them as File nodes. `fullGeneration` then documents every File node that `shouldIgnorePath` lets through.
- `splitBySubdirectory` grouped files by the first two segments of their path from the repository root (`parts.length > 2 ? parts.slice(0, 2).join('/') : parts[0]`), whatever the module. This had three effects:
  - each file at the root became a page of its own: `root-metadata-io-iml.md`, `root-build-gradle.md`, `root-readme-md.md`;
  - the files sitting directly in a module directory got a page named after that directory, `metadata-io-api — metadata-io-api`;
  - everything under `src/main/java/…` fell into a single `src — main` page. That page was then truncated to the 30,000-token budget, so most of the classes never reached the model.

## Areas touched

- [x] `gitnexus/` (CLI / core / MCP server)
- [ ] `gitnexus-web/` (Vite / React UI)
- [ ] `.github/` (workflows, actions)
- [ ] `eval/` or other tooling
- [x] Docs: one paragraph in `docs/wiki-generation.md`

## Scope & constraints

**In scope**

- `config/ignore-service.ts`: `.iml`, `.ipr` and `.iws` are IntelliJ's module, project and workspace files. `.lockfile` covers Gradle's `gradle.lockfile`, `buildscript-gradle.lockfile` and any custom `lockFile` name that ends in `.lockfile`. All four go into `IGNORED_EXTENSIONS`. A `!*.iml` line in `.gitnexusignore` indexes them again.
- `core/wiki/module-split.ts` (new): `splitModuleByDirectory(files, tokensOf, budget)`, a pure function.
- `core/wiki/generator.ts`:
  - `buildModuleTree` calls the new function instead of `splitBySubdirectory`, which is removed.
  - `estimateFileTokens` replaces `estimateModuleTokens` and returns an estimate per file. Each estimate includes the `--- path ---` line the file is quoted under, and a file that cannot be read counts as the `(file not readable)` placeholder its page quotes, so a page sized to the budget is not truncated.
  - A page whose slug is already taken gets a number. This happens with `api-v1` and `api_v1`, with a directory page that would land on another module's page, or with a directory named `overview`. To fit the number into the slug, the module name loses words and the directory label stays. Every node still satisfies `slug === slugify(name)`, which incremental updates rely on.
- `docs/wiki-generation.md`: how a large module is split, and that IntelliJ files and Gradle lockfiles get no page.

**Explicitly out of scope / not done here**

- The tree keeps two levels, a module and its pages. A deeper split is flattened into the module's pages, because `flattenModuleTree`, `countModules` and `extractModuleFiles` read one level of children.
- Grouping by graph communities, the issue's third suggestion, and the text of the overview page, which comes from the model.
- Wikis already generated keep their saved tree. Every run writes `module_tree.json`, and the next run reads it back first. #4035 makes `--force` group the files again, so with it merged first, `--force` gives an existing wiki the new pages.
- The incremental update that regenerates a split module's parent page instead of the sub-module page holding the changed file. That `break` predates this PR, and #4034 removes it; it should land before or with this one.

## Implementation notes

- Files are grouped by the next directory below the directory they share. The files sitting directly in that directory form one page.
- A directory over budget is divided the same way. Files that sit in one directory and exceed the budget are packed in name order into pages of at most the budget, so only a single file larger than the budget is cut.
- A module of three files or fewer stays on one page, as on `main`. That minimum applies to the module only, not to the directories the split goes through.
- Neighbouring directories under budget share a page, in name order, up to the budget. The number of pages therefore follows the size of the source: 50 one-file migration directories give 5 pages, not 50.
- Page labels:
  - the directories taken below the module's directory, for example `main/entity`;
  - `a, b` or `a … z` for a page that several directories share;
  - `top-level files` for the files sitting directly in the module's own directory;
  - `(1 of 2)` after the label when files sharing a directory fill several pages, so these read differently from the numbers that make a taken slug unique.
- Directories are ordered by name, so the pages do not depend on the order in which the model listed the files.

## Testing & verification

- [x] `test/unit/wiki-module-split.test.ts`, new, 22 tests.
  - The function on its own:
    - the Maven split;
    - files at the root, packed into complete pages;
    - the `top-level files` page;
    - shared pages (50 directories give 5 pages; `a, b`);
    - files in one directory packed in name order; a small directory over budget divided anyway; a page over budget only for a single file larger than the budget;
    - the four-file minimum: three files stay on one page, four are divided;
    - a module exactly at the budget, which stays on one page;
    - Windows paths;
    - an empty list.
  - 300 random directory trees, each checked for four properties:
    - every file is on exactly one page;
    - labels are unique;
    - no page is over budget unless it holds one file or the module has fewer than four;
    - reversing the input gives the same pages.
  - Through `WikiGenerator.run()`, with real files on disk and the graph and model mocked:
    - the grouping prompt and the tree contain no `.iml` or `.lockfile` path;
    - the issue's layout gives exactly the expected pages;
    - every node satisfies `slug === slugify(name)` and is found by `findNodeBySlug`.
  - A full run: no page prompt says `source truncated`.
  - Slugs that are already taken get numbers, and a directory named `overview` does not take the overview's page.
  - Ten unreadable files push their directory onto its own page, which is not truncated.
  - `uniqueModuleName` keeps its number inside the 60-character slug and keeps the directory label, shortening the module name instead.
  - On `main`, the four tests that go through the generator fail.
    - The grouping prompt lists the `.iml` files.
    - With only the ignore list fixed, `metadata-io-api` still gets 2 pages, one of them the duplicate.
- [x] `test/unit/ignore-service.test.ts`, 15 new cases.
  - The ignored names, at the root and nested.
  - Source files whose names contain `iml` or `lockfile`, which stay indexed.
  - The `!*.iml` negation.
  - The 8 cases about ignoring or re-including fail on `main`.
- [x] Mutations: 27 mutations on the first version, each restored afterwards. 26 fail a test. The one that passes changes `directory.tokens > budget` to `>=`, which gives the same result: a directory exactly at the budget is returned whole either way. 14 more on the review changes: 13 fail a test; the 14th showed that reserving the empty slug changed nothing, so that line is gone.
- [x] The 41 test files that touch the wiki, the ignore rules, the filesystem walker or the workspace extractors: 1,382 tests pass and 41 are skipped.
- [x] `npx vitest run test/unit`: 1,211 files, 28,517 tests pass and 54 are skipped.
- [x] Integration: the 6 integration files among those 41 pass (`filesystem-walker`, `ignore-and-skip-e2e`, `analyze-dirty-snapshot`, `analyze-directory-symlinks`, `parse-impl-quarantine-cache-skip`, `wiki-graph-queries-engine`). I did not run the whole integration suite, because no tracked fixture contains an `.iml`, `.ipr`, `.iws` or `.lockfile` file.
- [x] `npx tsc --noEmit` and `typecheck:tests` pass. eslint reports no new warning, and prettier is clean.
- [x] With #4034 and #4035 merged on top of this branch, the 15 wiki test files pass (337 tests), with #4035's sub-module fixture sized for either split.
- [x] The real CLI, built from `main` and from this branch, on a fixture shaped like the issue.
  - Fixture: DataHub `metadata-io` with 10 `.iml` files, `gradle.lockfile`, two SQL scripts at the root, `metadata-io-api`, and a Maven `src/main` holding packages of different sizes.
  - Commands: `analyze --index-only`, then `wiki --provider custom` against a local stand-in model, with a throwaway `HOME`.
  - `main` reproduces the issue's file list:
    - ten `root-*-iml.md` pages;
    - `root-gradle-lockfile.md`;
    - `metadata-io-api-metadata-io-api.md`;
    - `src-main.md` with 37 files, of which 31% of the source is sent.
  - This branch gives 14 pages:
    - `root`, `metadata-io-api-top-level-files`, `metadata-io-api-src-api`, `metadata-io-api-src-spi`;
    - `src-main-aspect`, `src-main-entity`, `src-main-entity-ebean`, `src-main-graph`, `src-main-graph-elastic-neo4j`, `src-main-search-timeline`, `src-test-testfixtures`;
    - the two parent pages and `overview`.
  - The only page still truncated in that run was `root`, whose two large SQL scripts sit in the same directory. Since the review changes, files sharing a directory are packed into pages of at most the budget, so such a page is only cut when one file alone exceeds it or the module has fewer than four files.
  - The same split happens when the model groups all of `src/main` into one module.
  - Running `analyze` again without `--force`, with this branch, on an index built by `main` removes the 12 metadata File nodes.
- [x] `impact`:
  - `buildModuleTree`, `splitBySubdirectory` and `estimateModuleTokens`: LOW, with one caller, `fullGeneration`.
  - `shouldIgnorePath`: MEDIUM, 24 symbols: the `analyze` walk, the workspace extractors and the wiki.
  - A text search finds no code that reads `.iml` or `.lockfile` files.
- [x] `detect_changes`, with the index refreshed at the branch head and compared with `main`: risk HIGH, with 13 flows. All of them are wiki generation going through `buildModuleTree` (`FullGeneration → …`, `BuildModuleTree → …`). The changed source symbols are `IGNORED_EXTENSIONS`, `buildModuleTree`, `readSourceFiles`, `estimateFileTokens`, `slugify`, `uniqueModuleName`, `sourceSection`, `MAX_SLUG_LENGTH` and the new `module-split.ts`. After the review changes, `impact` on `splitModuleByDirectory` and `estimateFileTokens`: LOW, through `buildModuleTree` and `fullGeneration`.

## Risk & rollout

- Index: a project with `.iml` or Gradle lockfile files loses those File nodes, which hold no symbols, at its next `analyze`. A `!*.iml` line in `.gitnexusignore` keeps them.
- Wiki: new wikis only, because existing ones keep their saved tree. The pages of a split module are named after their directories, for example `src — main/entity` instead of `src — main`.

## Checklist

- [x] PR body meets repo minimum length (workflow may label short descriptions)

- [x] No secrets, tokens, or machine-specific paths committed

title: test(go): benchmark ownership and deferred callable-flow scaling
body:
## Summary

Add a standalone Go benchmark for ownership reconciliation and deferred callable flow. The serial benchmark job runs `measure.cjs --check` against `baseline.json` and uploads the JSON report, including individual timings and failures.

Each package contributes two Go files with repeated declaration names and a cross-file callback. Every run checks that the package registers its method and field and that `Apply` calls its own package's `Step`. The sweep doubles from 1,024 to 8,192 files, uses a fresh graph per run, and takes five timed samples at each size.

## Scaling check

The baseline caps owner lookups and returned entries at one per file and solver iterations at three per file. It also caps the growth in median time per file at 1.75× for each pass across every pair of sizes. Linear timing gives a ratio of 1×. Quadratic timing gives 8× over the full sweep.

| Median pass time on the PR branch | 1,024 files | 2,048 files | 4,096 files | 8,192 files | Growth in time per file, first to last |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Ownership reconciliation | 2.25 ms | 5.72 ms | 10.42 ms | 20.63 ms | 1.15× |
| Deferred callable flow | 76.10 ms | 172.48 ms | 359.70 ms | 759.66 ms | 1.25× |

At each size the PR made one ownership lookup per file, returned zero prior entries and used three solver iterations per file. The v1.6.12 negative control returned 8,386,560 prior entries at 8,192 files and failed both ownership gates. Measurements used Node 22.23.3 on Linux x64. The fixture has fixed fan-out. The 48,853-file repository in #4027 is private.

## Reproduction

From `gitnexus/` with dependencies installed, run

```sh
npm run build
node --experimental-test-module-mocks bench/go-resolution-scaling/measure.cjs --check --output go-resolution-scaling.json
```

Local checks passed for the build, core TypeScript, lint, and 93 focused ownership and callable-resolution tests. Replaying quadratic timings for either pass independently failed the timing check with linear work counts. Removing a size also failed. The check also passed locally on GitHub’s test merge `4a176f67` against `main`. Across the eightfold increase in files, time per file grew 1.07× for ownership and 1.16× for callable flow.

title: fix(wiki): regenerate the sub-module page of a changed file on incremental runs
body:
## Summary

When a file inside a sub-module changed, an incremental `gitnexus wiki` run regenerated the parent page but not the sub-module page that documents the file. The sub-module page kept describing the old code, and the parent page was rewritten from that stale page. This PR regenerates both: the sub-module page first, then the parent page from the new one.

I checked it with the real CLI, built from `main` and from this branch. The fixture is the Gradle layout from #1060, where the large `src` module is split into 3 sub-modules. Steps: `analyze`, `wiki`, edit one file under `src/main`, commit, `analyze`, `wiki` again, against a local stand-in model that writes a run number into every page.

| Second `wiki` run | `main` | this branch |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Pages requested | `src` (parent), overview | `src — main` (sub-module), `src` (parent), overview |
| `src-main.md`, which documents the edited file | still from the first run | regenerated |
| `src.md` | regenerated from the old `src-main.md` | regenerated from the new `src-main.md` |

## Motivation / context

I found this while testing #4031, and there is no issue for it yet. #2937, open since August, drops the same `break` as part of its document profiles; this PR is that fix on its own, with tests.

The cause, on `main`:

- `extractModuleFiles` lists a sub-module's files twice: under the parent (the files of all its sub-modules) and under the sub-module itself, parent first.
- `incrementalUpdate` looks each changed file up in that map and stops at the first module that lists it. For a file in a sub-module, that is always the parent.
- So only the parent page was regenerated, and `generateParentPage` builds it from the sub-module pages already on disk. Incremental runs never refreshed a sub-module page; only a full generation did.

## Areas touched

- [x] `gitnexus/` (CLI / core / MCP server)
- [ ] `gitnexus-web/` (Vite / React UI)
- [ ] `.github/` (workflows, actions)
- [ ] `eval/` or other tooling
- [ ] Docs / agent config only (`AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `.cursor/`, `llms.txt`, etc.)

## Scope & constraints

**In scope**

- `core/wiki/generator.ts`, `incrementalUpdate`: every module that lists a changed file is marked, not only the first one. The rest already handles both pages:
  - sub-module pages are regenerated before parent pages;
  - a parent whose sub-module page fails is held back, and both are retried on the next run.
- A parent page is removed just before the parent is regenerated rather than up front, so a held-back parent keeps its last page until the retry succeeds.
- `removeFailedPages`: the two incremental runs that fall back to a full generation (diverged branch, more than five new files) first remove the pages of the modules the last run could not write. A full generation keeps the pages it finds, so a held-back parent would otherwise stay as it was and lose its retry.

**Explicitly out of scope / not done here**

- Changed files that no module lists, which are new files. Up to five are recorded under `Other` in `meta.json`, but `generateLeafPage` writes a page from the tree node's files, so they are not documented either. More than five trigger a full generation, which reads the saved `module_tree.json` back instead of grouping again, and then skips every page already on disk; #4035 handles that path. Both paths are unchanged here.

## Implementation notes

- The cost is one more model request per changed sub-module: the parent page was already being regenerated. The measured run makes 3 requests instead of 2.
- Saved files keep their format, and existing wikis need nothing. Their next incremental run that touches a sub-module refreshes its page.

## Testing & verification

- [x] `test/unit/wiki-incremental-update.test.ts`, new, 7 tests. They use a real git repository, the graph mocked, and a stand-in model that writes a run number into every page:
  - A file in a sub-module changes:
    - the sub-module page is regenerated first, with the edited source in its prompt;
    - the parent page is then regenerated, and its prompt contains the new sub-module page;
    - the other pages are untouched;
    - the file is not counted as new.
  - Files of two sub-modules change: both sub-module pages are regenerated, then the parent once.
  - A file in a module without sub-modules changes: only that page and the overview are regenerated, as on `main`.
  - A sub-module page stops at the completion-token limit:
    - the parent waits, and both are listed as failed;
    - the failed page is removed, and the parent keeps its last page;
    - the next run regenerates the sub-module, then the parent.
  - A parent page stops at the limit: its page is removed, and the next run regenerates it.
  - A failed run followed by a diverged branch, then by six new files: the held-back parent is written again, not kept from before the failure. The second test only checks that the old page does not survive, because #4035 groups the files again on that path.
  - The repository turns commit signing off, so a `commit.gpgsign` setting cannot fail the setup.
  - On `main`, 3 of the first 4 fail. The module without sub-modules passes, as expected.
- [x] Mutations: 6, each restored afterwards, and each one fails a test:
  - stopping at the first module again;
  - no longer marking the file as known;
  - regenerating parents together with sub-modules;
  - skipping parents;
  - letting a parent run after its sub-module failed;
  - marking every module that has files.
  - After review, 6 more on the new code, each failing a test: removing a parent page up front again, not removing it before it is regenerated, dropping either fallback's `removeFailedPages`, restoring the `break`, removing the hold-back.
- [x] The 13 test files that touch the wiki: 473 tests pass. After review, the wiki test files pass (303 tests), and with `commit.gpgsign=true` and no usable key the incremental test file passes 7 of 7.
- [x] `npx vitest run test/unit`: 1,212 files, 28,498 tests pass and 54 are skipped.

title: fix(wiki): group files again on --force and when many new files arrive
body:
## Summary

`gitnexus wiki --force` is meant to group the files into modules again, and so is a run that finds more than five new files since the last generation. Neither did: both reused the previous generation's module tree. The second case also skipped every page already on disk, so it only regenerated the overview. The new files, and the files changed in the same commits, got no documentation.

This PR:

1. Groups the files again on those runs, unless `module_tree.json` was edited since the last generation or the user has just approved it on `--review`.
2. On the new-files path, rewrites only the pages of modules whose files or shape changed, and deletes the pages of modules that are gone. Other pages, and `.md` files the wiki did not write, are kept.
3. Makes that path safe to stop. Before it deletes anything, `meta.json` records the regrouping; the next run at the same commit completes it, and a run at another commit takes back what it wrote.
4. Counts as new only files the graph indexes, at paths that did not exist at the last generation.

I checked it with the real CLI, run from `main` and from this branch, against a local stand-in model and with a throwaway `HOME`. The repository has `api/` and `core/` with two files each, and the first `wiki` run groups them by directory.

| Second run | `main` | this branch |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `wiki --force`, the model now answering one `Everything` module | no grouping request; the tree stays `Api`, `Core` | grouped again: `Everything` |
| six new files under `jobs/` and an edit to `core/db.ts`, then `wiki` | only `overview` is regenerated; no page covers `jobs/`, and `core.md` still describes the old `core/db.ts` | grouped again: `Api` kept, `Core` rewritten, `Jobs` written |
| `wiki --review --force` in a terminal, answering `edit` | the review shows the previous tree | the review shows the new grouping, and the pages follow the tree as edited |
| `wiki --review --force` without a terminal | previous tree | grouped again |

The cases raised in review, against the previous head of this branch (`2d42b87c8`):

| Run | previous head | this head |
| --- | --- | --- |
| six new files, the overview cut off at the token limit; then `wiki` again, the model now answering `Services` | grouped again into `Services` | completed: only the overview is requested, the tree stays `Api`, `Core`, `Jobs` |
| six new files grouped into `Api`, the overview cut off; then `git checkout HEAD~1`, `analyze`, `wiki` | "Wiki is already up to date", `module_tree.json` missing, `api.md` still documents `jobs/` | `Api` and the overview written again; `module_tree.json` is `Api`, `Core` |
| six new files, `wiki --review` in a terminal, `edit` removing `Jobs`, which gives back the previous tree | two grouping requests; the unreviewed `Services` is generated | one grouping request; `Api`, `Core` as approved |
| six `.changeset/*.md` files committed, then `wiki` | grouped again into `Services` | no request |

## Motivation / context

I found this while testing #4031, and there is no issue for it yet. #2937, open since August, also deletes `module_tree.json` on `--force`, as part of its document profiles. Here a tree edited since the last generation is kept, and the new-files path is fixed as well.

The cause, on `main`:

- `buildModuleTree` reads `module_tree.json` first, as the tree a user edited during `--review`. That check came with `--review`, in #381. But every completed generation also writes `module_tree.json`, for the HTML viewer.
- `--force` and the "Significant new files" path delete only `first_module_tree.json`, "to force re-grouping" as their comments say. Since #381, the next `buildModuleTree` finds `module_tree.json` and returns the previous tree.
- On the new-files path, `fullGeneration` then skips every page already on disk, which is what lets an interrupted run resume. So only the overview is written.

## Areas touched

- [x] `gitnexus/` (CLI / core / MCP server)
- [ ] `gitnexus-web/` (Vite / React UI)
- [ ] `.github/` (workflows, actions)
- [ ] `eval/` or other tooling
- [x] Docs: one paragraph in `docs/wiki-generation.md`, and the `--force` row of the three `gitnexus-cli` skill copies

## Scope & constraints

**In scope**

- `core/wiki/generator.ts`:
  - `keepsSavedTree(meta)`: a run that groups again still uses `module_tree.json` when it differs from the tree `meta.json` records (an edit; key order and indentation do not count), or when `useSavedTree` is set.
    - `--force` (`discardSavedGrouping`) deletes `first_module_tree.json`, and `module_tree.json` unless it is kept.
    - The new-files path deletes neither: `buildModuleTree(files, groupAgain)` skips them in memory, and the final `saveModuleTree` replaces `module_tree.json`.
  - `WikiOptions.useSavedTree`, set by `cli/wiki.ts` for the run that follows a review: the approved tree is generated as it is, even when it equals the previous one.
  - New files, in `incrementalUpdate`: a changed path no module lists is new when the graph indexes it (`getAllFiles()`, queried only when something was added) and `git diff --no-renames --diff-filter=A` lists it. So a moved file's new path counts, and an edit or an unindexed path does not. The full changed set still decides which pages are rewritten.
  - `fullGeneration(commit, regroup)` and `removeStalePages` on the new-files path, after the `--review` stop:
    - `keptPages` keeps a page when the previous `meta.moduleTree` has a node with the same slug, name, files and sub-module slugs, none of whose files changed; a parent page also needs every sub-module page kept;
    - `meta.json` first gets `regrouping: { commit, tree, keptPages, staleRemoved }`, while the rest of it still describes the previous wiki;
    - the pages of both trees that are not kept are deleted, `staleRemoved` is set, and the generation writes the missing pages as usual. Its final `saveWikiMeta` drops the record.
  - A recorded regrouping is never up to date:
    - the next run at its commit completes it from the recorded tree, deleting first if `staleRemoved` is false;
    - a run at another commit, or the run that follows a review, takes it back. It deletes the pages of both trees that are not kept, lists the previous modules whose pages are gone as failed, and goes on from the previous `meta.json`.
  - `getChangedFiles` reads `git diff -z`, so non-ASCII paths are not C-quoted and match the graph.
  - A review-only run leaves `index.html` alone.
- `cli/wiki.ts`: the continuation after a review sets `useSavedTree`.
- `test/unit/wiki-truncation-recovery.test.ts`: two tests now answer the grouping request that a forced run makes first. They relied on `--force` reusing the tree, so their first mocked answer used to go to a page.
- `docs/wiki-generation.md` and the skill rows: what `--force` and the new-files path do with the grouping.

**Explicitly out of scope / not done here**

- Runs with five new files or fewer. They record the new files under `Other` in `meta.json`, but `generateLeafPage` writes from the tree node's files, so these files are not documented either. Unindexed and edited paths are no longer added to `Other`.
- Incremental runs that change a file inside a sub-module: #4034 fixes them.
- The branch-diverged path, where `getChangedFiles` returns `null`. It runs a full generation that still reuses the saved tree, as on `main`.

## Implementation notes

- `module_tree.json` and `meta.moduleTree` are written from the same tree at the end of a generation, and incremental runs rewrite neither. A user edit or a `--review` run makes them differ. A wiki whose `meta.json` has no `moduleTree` keeps its `module_tree.json`, as on `main`.
- An edit is used for the next generation only. Once a generation records it in `meta.json`, the next `--force` or new-files run groups again. The docs say so.
- After `n` at the review prompt, the next `gitnexus wiki` generates the saved proposal, as it already does after a first-run review. Until then, the viewer keeps showing the last wiki.
- Cost: the new-files path makes one grouping request and one request per new or changed module. Completing an interrupted run makes no grouping request. On `main`, the path made one request, for the overview, and left the rest undocumented.

## Testing & verification

- [x] `test/unit/wiki-regroup.test.ts`, new, 36 tests. They use a real git repository, the graph mocked, and a stand-in model that answers a grouping chosen by the test and writes a run number into every page.
  - `--force`: groups again after a completed generation, and after a tool only reordered the saved tree's keys. It keeps a tree edited since the last generation, and a tree written before any generation. With `--review`, it groups again, then generates the tree as edited. A failed run resumes from its new grouping.
  - More than five new files:
    - Grouping: groups again and writes the new module's page only. A module whose file changed in the same commits is rewritten. So is a module that gained or lost files, and so are two modules of the same size that swapped files. The page of a module that is gone is deleted.
    - Edge cases: a module named `constructor`; an invalid `module_tree.json`; a page an older wiki left under a new module's name, which is written again; `runbook.md`, which stays.
    - What counts as new: files moved to new paths group again, and six `.changeset/*.md` files the graph does not index do not.
    - `--review`: pages and `index.html` are untouched while it waits; the edited tree is generated; an approved tree equal to the previous one is generated as it is.
  - Interrupted runs:
    - a rerun at the same commit completes the run, whatever the model would answer now;
    - back at the documented commit, the run is not up to date and writes again what the failed run wrote;
    - a later commit groups again and writes those pages again;
    - a run that stops while deleting pages is taken back;
    - a failed grouping request keeps the tree, the pages and the viewer;
    - `--review` after a failed run generates the approved tree.
  - Edits to files a curated tree left out, with one new file, do not group again. An `Other` page that gained files on a small run is rewritten on a regrouping. A file with a non-ASCII name is matched.
  - With sub-modules (a small `maxTokensPerModule` splits a module):
    - a parent page is kept when its sub-module pages are, and rewritten after a changed sub-module page;
    - on `--review`, it is also rewritten when the user renames a sub-module, changes only its slug, removes it, or turns the parent into a module without sub-modules;
    - a rename that keeps the slug rewrites the page.
  - On `main`, 32 of the 36 fail. On the previous head of this branch, 16 fail. The 20 that pass there are the earlier tests, plus tests that pin behaviour the new code must keep, such as the swapped files, the moved files and the invalid saved tree. The 4 that pass on `main` check an edited tree, a tree written before any generation, an invalid saved tree, and an approved tree equal to the previous one, the last because `main` always reuses the saved tree.
- [x] `wiki-truncation-recovery.test.ts`: the two updated tests fail on `main`, because a forced run there makes no grouping request.
- [x] Mutations, each restored afterwards and each failing a test:
  - First round, 15: keeping or always deleting `module_tree.json`; an inverted `meta` guard; keeping the snapshot; calling `discardSavedGrouping` without `meta`; skipping `removeStalePages`; ignoring changed files, lost files or sub-modules; never keeping sub-module pages or the overview; deleting files other than pages; comparing slugs with the extension; deleting pages before the `--review` stop.
  - After review, 24 more. They cover:
    - ignoring `useSavedTree`, or resuming despite it;
    - an up-to-date check that ignores the record, or a review-only run rebuilding the viewer;
    - never resuming, or grouping again on resume;
    - a takeback that keeps pages, marks nothing, or keeps the record;
    - no record before the deletion, or ignoring `staleRemoved`;
    - dropping the name, child-slug, file-membership, changed-file or sub-module check;
    - deleting only the previous tree's pages;
    - dropping `--diff-filter=A`, `--no-renames`, `-z`, the indexed check or the added check;
    - never grouping again, or always treating the saved tree as an edit.
- [x] The 13 wiki test files: 343 tests pass, and with `commit.gpgsign=true` and no usable key the regroup file passes 36 of 36.
- [x] `npx vitest run test/unit`: 1,214 files, 28,599 tests pass and 54 are skipped.
- [x] `npx tsc --noEmit` and `typecheck:tests` pass. eslint reports no new warning, prettier is clean, and `npm run test:dupes` reports nothing.
- [x] The real CLI: see both tables. In the terminal cases, `script` provides the terminal, the prompt is answered `edit`, and a script standing in for `$EDITOR` changes the tree.
- [x] Together with #4034, now that #4031 is merged: no conflict, and the 14 wiki test files pass, 354 tests.
- [x] `detect_changes`, with the index refreshed at the branch: risk HIGH, from the `WikiGenerator` class and 14 flows inside `gitnexus wiki`; the ten it prints start at `wikiCommandImpl`. `impact` on `incrementalUpdate`, `fullGeneration`, `buildModuleTree` and `getChangedFiles` is LOW.

## Risk & rollout

- `--force` now asks the model to group again, one request as in a first generation, so module names can change on a forced run.
- Runs that bring more than five new indexed files now group again and rewrite the changed modules' pages. That takes more requests than on `main`, where those runs documented nothing new.
- `meta.json` gains an optional `regrouping` field while such a run is in progress; older versions ignore it. No migration: the saved tree of an existing wiki is compared with its `meta.json`.

## Checklist

- [x] No secrets, tokens, or machine-specific paths committed

## Summary

Two jobs failed on the same Publish run. Locked pytest rejected the optional SonarQube LCOV upload added in #4033, and a PHP HTTP extraction test in coverage shard 3/8 lost a file-scope assignment after garbage collection. [Locked pytest job](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/actions/runs/44911747794/job/136918900935) · [Coverage shard](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/actions/runs/44911747794/job/136918903705)

title: fix(wiki): regenerate the page of a module renamed on --review
body:
## Summary

Once a module is renamed on `--review`, incremental `gitnexus wiki` runs never regenerate its page again. `meta.json` records modules by name, and both lookups in `incrementalUpdate` find the node by slugifying that name, but a renamed module keeps its old page name. This PR finds a module by its name first, sub-modules included, then by the page its name gives.

It answers the nexus-check warning on #4034 ([thread](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/pull/4034#discussion_r4658139271)). The fix was ready, but #4034 was merged before I pushed it.

I checked it with the real CLI, run from the sources of `main` and of this branch. The fixture has `api/orders.ts`, `api/users.ts`, `core/cache.ts` and `core/db.ts`, which a local stand-in model groups into `Api` and `Core`; it writes a run number into every page. `gitnexus wiki --review` runs in a terminal, and `edit` at the prompt opens an `EDITOR` script that renames `Api` to `HTTP API` and leaves `"slug": "api"`. Then `api/orders.ts` is edited and committed, followed by `analyze` and `wiki`.

| | `main` | this branch |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--review` run | `HTTP API`, `Core` and the overview written, `HTTP API` on `api.md` | the same |
| Next run, pages requested | none | `HTTP API`, overview |
| Next run, CLI output | `Wiki generated successfully`, `Pages: 0` | `Pages: 2` |
| `api.md` | still from the `--review` run | regenerated |

On both, `meta.json` then records the new commit, so on `main` later runs do not come back to that change.

## Motivation / context

`--review` prints "You can edit this file to remove/rename modules." A rename changes `name` and leaves `slug`. `meta.json` names modules by `name` (the `moduleFiles` keys and `failedModules`), while pages are named by `slug`, and `buildModuleTree` reads an edited `module_tree.json` as it is. So after a rename, the slug is no longer the slugified name. Both lookups in `incrementalUpdate` used `findNodeBySlug(tree, slugify(name))`:

- The modules of the changed files, a lookup older than #4034. A file of the renamed module finds no node; when nothing else changed, the run writes nothing.
- `removeFailedPages`, added by #4034. The page of a failed module with a page name of its own is not removed, so the full generation of the diverged-branch or new-files fallback keeps the page instead of retrying the module. This is the bot's warning.

## Areas touched

- [x] `gitnexus/` (CLI / core / MCP server)
- [ ] `gitnexus-web/` (Vite / React UI)
- [ ] `.github/` (workflows, actions)
- [ ] `eval/` or other tooling
- [ ] Docs / agent config only (`AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `.cursor/`, `llms.txt`, etc.)

## Scope & constraints

**In scope**

- `findModule(tree, name)` in `core/wiki/generator.ts`: the node with that name, sub-modules included, or else the node `findNodeBySlug(tree, slugify(name))` returns. Both lookups use it.
- The page-name match stays for a name no node has. New files are recorded under `Other`, and when the catch-all module is renamed (`Misc`, keeping `other.md`), they still reach it.

**Explicitly out of scope / not done here**

- The other `slugify` calls build new trees, where the page name comes from the module name. They are unchanged.
- Changes that a renamed module missed before this fix stay missed: its page is regenerated the next time one of its files changes, or with `--force`.

## Implementation notes

- The name is tried first because it is what `meta.json` stores. Once modules are renamed, a name can also give the page of another module: one test renames `Shipping` to `Notes` and `Notes` to `Journal`, and trying the page name first regenerates `notes.md` for a change to `shipping.ts`.
- `moduleFiles` is keyed by name, so it cannot tell apart two modules with the same name. `findModule` returns the first in tree order, as `findNodeBySlug` does for page names.
- Saved files keep their format, and existing wikis need nothing.
- The six-new-files test now lists the new files in the mocked graph, as `analyze` would. It passes either way on `main`. #4035 counts only indexed files as new, so the test keeps passing once both are in.

## Testing & verification

- [x] `test/unit/wiki-incremental-update.test.ts`: 4 new tests, 11 in all, on trees edited as `--review` allows:
  - A parent and a sub-module have page names of their own (`Commerce` on `shop.md`, `Billing` on `payments.md`): a change to `billing.ts` regenerates both.
  - `Shipping` is renamed `Notes` and `Notes` is renamed `Journal`, both keeping their pages: a change to `shipping.ts` regenerates the module named `Notes`, on `shipping.md`.
  - A held-back parent on a page of its own is retried through the diverged-branch fallback.
  - The catch-all module is renamed `Misc` and keeps `other.md`: it still gets a new file listed as `Other`.
  - On `main`, the first three fail. The fourth passes there, since it covers the page-name match `main` already has.
- [x] Mutations: 5, each restored afterwards, and each one fails a test:
  - either lookup back to the slug alone;
  - no page-name match;

title: fix(ingestion): resolve TypeScript receivers and ECMAScript exports
body:
## Summary

Resolve TypeScript Map entries and guarded receivers to the declarations they actually name. Follow ECMAScript re-exports to their defining modules in both TypeScript and JavaScript, and make ambiguous or erased paths visible without assigning them a runtime call target.

## Motivation

Wrong receiver and module edges send impact analysis and PR review to the wrong declarations. The fixtures use same-named methods and exports so that choosing the wrong owner cannot pass simply because a call edge exists.

## Implementation

- Preserve Map tuple positions through holes, nested patterns, defaults, and `for await`. Distinguish general iterables from Maps.
- Attach an `instanceof` fact to member uses in the proven branch. Check lexical ownership, writes, and closure boundaries before emitting it.
- Resolve named and star re-exports to the terminal declaration or module object. Honor explicit exports, coalesce paths to the same owner, and report conflicting candidates. Keep file dependencies, type-only exports, and local bindings distinct. Preserve local, default, and quoted export aliases and exact import-token targets for rename.
- Add an exact-target ingestion benchmark and a separate property-dispatch benchmark for the output-size question in #3924. Related to the reliability and accuracy work in #3948.

title: perf(core): speed up HTTP embedding resume by reusing verified file hashes
body:
## Summary

Resuming interrupted HTTP embeddings took 13.0% less time with a 2 GiB heap and two workers, and 11.2% less time with default resources. On the explicit-resource fixture the median fell from 2,900 ms to 2,605 ms. Both builds finished the same 688 pending inputs in 43 provider requests.

## Motivation / context

A Publish job flagged a 0.93% slowdown. Two local repeats were inconclusive about that commit. Profiling the timed resume invocation identified a reproducible cost on both revisions. The parser reread 495 MB across 830 dependency files whose contents the analyzer had already verified. [Original CI job](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/actions/runs/45024292484/job/137218786923)

## Areas touched

- [x] Performance report and contributor guidance

The comparison uses the existing six CI scenarios, both resource profiles, and the existing acceptance thresholds. Performance estimates come from local Linux runs on those fixtures. ## Implementation notes

The analyzer caches a regular file’s raw content hash and applies the existing framing when constructing its public dependency digest. The parser can reuse the hash after checking the live file state and readability. The existing byte budget and final inventory checks still apply. Parser reads fell from 509 MB to 14 MB. [How to profile the measured resume process](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/blob/2d7aede9241666787931a09edb79b528d8cea6fc/docs/solutions/performance-issues/profiling-http-resume-identity-reads.md)

title: fix(wiki): use the repository that contains a given folder or file
body:
## Summary

`gitnexus wiki <path>` took the path as the repository root. A folder inside an indexed repository failed with "No GitNexus index found at <folder>/.gitnexus", and a file with "Not a git repository", which is the error in #493. Running `gitnexus wiki` with no path from that same folder worked, since that path goes up to the Git root.

With this PR, a file stands for its folder, and a folder without an index of its own uses the index of the repository that contains it. The CLI says so with one line: `Using the index of <repository>`.

I checked it with the real CLI, run from the sources of `main` (302969291) and of this branch. The repository has `api/orders.ts` and `core/db.ts`, it was indexed with `analyze`, and the wiki ran against a local stand-in model.

| `gitnexus wiki …` | `main` | this branch |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `repo` | wiki generated | the same |
| `repo/api` | `Error: No GitNexus index found at repo/api/.gitnexus` | `Using the index of …/repo`, wiki generated |
| `repo/api/orders.ts` | `Error: Not a git repository` | `Using the index of …/repo`, wiki generated |

The review follow-ups, checked the same way against the first commit of this PR (31ddba6f9):

| case | 31ddba6f9 | this branch |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `GIT_DIR` and `GIT_WORK_TREE` exported for another indexed repository, `wiki repo/api` | `Using the index of …/other` | `Error: No GitNexus index found at repo/api/.gitnexus`, as on `main` |
| `GITNEXUS_STORAGE_PATH` set for `analyze` and `wiki`, `wiki repo2/api` or `repo2/api/orders.ts` | `Error: Storage path is in state "foreign"` | `Using the index of …/repo2` |
| a path under a folder at mode 000, or a 300-character name | uncaught `EACCES` / `ENAMETOOLONG` stack trace | `Error: Not a git repository`, as on `main` |
| `wiki link/api`, with `link` a symlink to the repository | `Using the index of …/repo` | the same |
| `wiki repo/api` after `analyze repo/api --skip-git` | the folder's own index | the same |

## Motivation / context

Fixes #493. It was reported on 1.4.8, and the v1.6.5 triage left it open; it is still reproducible on `main`. The reporter wanted a wiki per feature folder. The wiki still documents the whole repository; this PR makes the path inside it work instead of failing with a wrong error.

## Areas touched

- [x] `gitnexus/` (CLI / core / MCP server)
- [ ] `gitnexus-web/` (Vite / React UI)
- [ ] `.github/` (workflows, actions)
- [ ] `eval/` or other tooling
- [x] Docs / agent config only (`AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `.cursor/`, `llms.txt`, etc.): one example line in `docs/wiki-generation.md`

## Scope & constraints

**In scope**

- `cli/wiki.ts`, path resolution: a path to a file becomes the folder that holds it. A path that cannot be read is left to the git check, which reports it as before.
- `findIndex`: the index of the given folder, or else the index of the Git root that contains it, when:
  - the folder has no index of its own: `missing`, `empty`, or no code index, but not a slot that could not be read (`isTransientStorageInspection`);
  - or the folder resolved to the repository's own storage, as it does with `GITNEXUS_STORAGE_PATH`;
  - and the root contains the folder once symlinks are resolved, so an exported `GIT_DIR` / `GIT_WORK_TREE` cannot point it at another checkout.
- A folder analyzed on its own (`analyze <folder> --skip-git`) keeps its own index, as it does today. Its wiki is still written to `<folder>/.gitnexus/wiki`.
- Any other storage state of the folder (`foreign`, `unowned`, `invalid_storage`) is reported as before; the command does not move to the repository on it. When the repository's own storage cannot be used, the error says which repository it is.

**Explicitly out of scope / not done here**

- A wiki for one folder only. The wiki keeps documenting the whole repository.
- The nearest indexed ancestor: the fallback goes to the Git root, as `gitnexus wiki` with no path does.
- `gitnexus wiki` with no path, and a path outside any repository: unchanged.
- `analyze <path>` still takes the path as the root; that is how a folder gets an index of its own.

## Implementation notes

- The fallback uses `getGitRoot`, the same helper the no-path case already uses, so a folder inside a submodule or a linked worktree resolves to that checkout.
- The containment check compares the real paths of the root and the folder, so a folder reached through a symlink to the repository still falls back.

## Testing & verification

- [x] `test/unit/wiki-repo-path.test.ts`, new, 19 tests. Git runs for real on temporary repositories, with `GIT_CEILING_DIRECTORIES` set above them. The first block mocks the index lookup; the second runs the real `requireStoragePath` with `GITNEXUS_STORAGE_PATH` and a temporary `GITNEXUS_HOME`. The tests check the repository, the storage path and the graph path the generator receives.
  - the repository itself is documented, as before;
  - a folder and a file inside it use the repository's index and print `Using the index of`;
  - a folder whose storage is `empty`, or `owned` without a code index, uses the repository's index;
  - a folder with an index of its own keeps it;
  - a folder whose slot could not be read, or whose storage is `foreign`, `unowned` or `invalid_storage`, is reported;
  - when neither the folder nor the repository is indexed, the error names the repository's `.gitnexus`; when the repository's storage cannot be used, the error names the repository;
  - a folder reached through a symlink uses the repository's index;
  - with `GIT_DIR` and `GIT_WORK_TREE` exported for another indexed repository, its index is not used;
  - a path outside any repository, and a path that cannot be read, are refused with `Not a git repository`;
  - with `GITNEXUS_STORAGE_PATH`, the repository, a folder and a file all use the repository's index.
  - On `main`, 9 of the 19 fail. On 31ddba6f9, the first commit of this PR, 6 fail: the review follow-ups.
- [x] Mutations: 10 on the follow-ups and 7 on the first commit, each restored afterwards, and each one fails a test. A storage path replaced with `/nonexistent` in `getStoragePaths` fails 5 tests.
- [x] `test/unit/wiki-flags.test.ts` passes unchanged (89 tests), and the 15 wiki test files pass (373 tests).
- [x] `npx vitest run test/unit`: 1,216 files, 28,630 tests pass and 54 are skipped.
- [x] `npx tsc --noEmit` and `npm run typecheck:tests` pass. prettier is clean, `npm run test:dupes` reports nothing, and eslint reports no new warning.
- [x] The real CLI: see the tables above.
- [x] `detect_changes`, with the index refreshed at the branch: four changed symbols in `wiki.ts` (`isWithin`, `hasNoIndexOfItsOwn`, `findIndex`, `wikiCommandImpl`) and the tests. Its risk level is high because the change reaches the 10 flows of the wiki command, all entered through `wikiCommandImpl`; the change is in the path lookup that runs before them. `impact` on `wikiCommandImpl` is LOW: its only caller is `wikiCommand`.

## Risk & rollout

Low. Only `gitnexus wiki <path>` changes, and only for a path that failed before: a file, a folder without an index of its own, or a folder under `GITNEXUS_STORAGE_PATH`. No migration is needed.

## Checklist

- [x] PR body meets repo minimum length (workflow may label short descriptions)
- [x] If `AGENTS.md` / overlays changed: headers, scope block, and changelog updated per project conventions (not changed)
- [x] No secrets, tokens, or machine-specific paths committed
