title: fix(group): stop group sync from holding every parsed tree-sitter tree in memory
body:
## Summary

`gitnexus group sync` kept a tree-sitter tree alive for every file the contract extractors parsed, and passed the trees of a whole language family to the project scan at once. Tree memory is native, and the binding frees it only from a deferred N-API finalizer, so even dropped trees stayed resident until the scan ended. This PR bounds that memory: each tree lives only while its own file is processed, the parse loops yield so finalizers can run, and V8 is nudged to collect the dropped wrappers. On a synthetic 6.3k-file Java/Kotlin/TypeScript repo, peak RSS of `group sync` drops from 5.8–6.6 GB to about 1.0 GB. The extracted contracts are identical.

## Motivation / context

On a large Kotlin/Android monorepo with no HTTP routes in its graph, `group sync` grew past the default 8 GiB query memory budget (#3696, #3749), and the guard stopped the process with exit 70. `GITNEXUS_QUERY_TRACE=1` showed RSS growing by several GB between two zero-row graph queries, with no query in flight: the HTTP extractor's source scan was the consumer, not a query.

Three things combined:

1. `HttpRouteExtractor.extract()` cached `{ plugin, input: { filePath, tree }, repoContext }` for every parsed file in `cachedInputs` until it returned. Nothing evicted it.
2. The first file of a plugin family with `scanProject` (Java, Kotlin, JS/TS) parsed every file of that family and passed all the trees to `scanProject(inputs)` at once. Dropping the cache afterwards would not have lowered that peak.
3. node-tree-sitter frees a tree in the `Tree` wrapper's N-API finalizer. Node runs those finalizers from a `setImmediate` after the GC that found the wrapper dead, and the binding never reports the native size to V8. A synchronous parse loop never reaches that phase, and V8 sees only small wrappers, so it rarely runs the major GC that would free promoted ones. Measured on 4,000 Kotlin files: 4.4 GB peak with every tree dropped and no yield, 0.13 GB when the loop yields every 16 parses.

The topic, gRPC, Thrift and include extractors and the HTTP plugins' `prepareRepo` passes have the same synchronous parse loops, so the fix covers them too.

## Areas touched

- [x] `gitnexus/` (CLI / core / MCP server)
- [ ] `gitnexus-web/` (Vite / React UI)
- [ ] `.github/` (workflows, actions)
- [ ] `eval/` or other tooling
- [ ] Docs / agent config only (`AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `.cursor/`, `llms.txt`, etc.)

## Scope & constraints

**In scope**

- `src/core/tree-sitter/native-tree-release.ts` (new): a tree releaser that parse loops await once per parse. Every 16 parses it yields one macrotask so pending finalizers run. When RSS has grown by 32 MB over the lowest RSS since the last nudge, and in any case at least every 8 yields, it nudges V8: it replaces one held, never-written 64 MB buffer, which V8 counts as external memory that only a major GC can release. The buffer is above glibc's largest mmap threshold and is not zero-filled, so it adds no resident memory (checked on macOS and on Linux with glibc). The nudge is best effort: an allocation failure is swallowed. Under `--zero-fill-buffers` the buffer is allocated with `new ArrayBuffer`, because `allocUnsafeSlow` aborts the process on failure in that mode. Detection errs to the safe side: any mention of the flag (either spelling) in `execArgv` or `NODE_OPTIONS`, or of a Node config-file flag, counts as on, so a mistake can only cost residency (about 130 MB on macOS), never an abort. Overlapping scans share one buffer. A group sync holds it between extractors. After the last group hold and standalone scan end, V8 can reclaim it.
- HTTP plugin contract (`http-patterns/types.ts`): `scanProject(inputs)` is replaced by `projectScan: { collect(input, ctx), resolve(facts, ctx) }`. `collect` reduces one parsed file to plain data while its tree is alive; `resolve` runs the cross-file pass over the facts. Java, Kotlin and the shared JS/TS family are ported. `prepareRepo` may now return a Promise.
- `HttpRouteExtractor.extract()`: caches detections and facts, never trees. Each file is still parsed at most once: its own `scan()` and its `collect()` run in the same pass. Detections and facts go through `structuredClone`, which throws if a plugin leaks a tree or node into them and drops sliced-string references to the file source; the `prepareRepo` contexts copy the strings they keep for the same reason. One releaser is shared by the extraction and the `prepareRepo` passes, and failed parses count toward its cadence. A throw from `scan`, `collect`, `resolve` or a clone is rethrown naming the plugin (and file) with `{ cause }`.
- Java, Kotlin, Python and JS/TS `prepareRepo` loops, and the topic, gRPC, Thrift and include scans, await the releaser.
- `group/sync.ts`: each repo's pool entry is leased (`pinRepo`) while its contracts are extracted. The new yields would otherwise let the pool's idle sweep or an LRU eviction from a concurrent caller close the repo mid-extraction, after which every graph query failed silently into empty results. If the repo is closed and reopened, a disposer from the earlier pool entry leaves the reopened entry’s leases intact.
- `CHANGELOG.md` is release-owned and not edited. Suggested release note: **Group sync no longer keeps every parsed source tree in memory** — the HTTP contract scan holds one tree-sitter tree at a time instead of every tree of a project family, and the `prepareRepo` pre-passes and the topic, gRPC, Thrift and include scans release tree memory as they parse, so tree memory no longer grows with repository size. Each repository's graph handle stays leased while its contracts are extracted. For HTTP language plugins, `scanProject` is replaced by `projectScan { collect, resolve }`, and `prepareRepo` may return a Promise and accept a shared tree releaser.

**Explicitly out of scope / not done here**

- The per-file facts and detections still sit in the JS heap until the cross-file pass ends, as on `main`, and grow with the number of files. The JS/TS facts no longer carry a `ParsedFile` (heap retained at the JS/TS `resolve`: 92.9 → 19.4 MB at 150 TS files, 182.9 → 36.0 MB at 300), so the remaining growth is mostly Spring type facts; collecting fewer of them, for example skipping non-controller classes, is a possible follow-up.
- Parse loops in `graphql-extractor.ts` and `python-workspace-extractor.ts`, and the ingestion parse workers, are not changed.
- On Windows, a graph `filePath` spelled differently from the scanned path still re-parses that file, as before.
- The query guard's attribution message (it blamed a zero-row query here) is fixed separately in #4071.

## Implementation notes

- The orchestrator stays language-agnostic: project families are pooled by `projectScan` object identity, as they were by `scanProject` function identity.
- Why a nudge is needed in addition to yielding: without it, a wrapper that survives two scavenges while its file is scanned is promoted, and only a major GC frees it. On the synthetic repo, yielding alone left about 6,700 of 7,200 dropped trees uncollected for most of the scan, and peak RSS varied between 0.5 and 3.7 GB from run to run.
- Why the trigger is "growth over the minimum RSS, capped at 8 yields": six variants were measured on the synthetic repo at 1× and 4× size (no trigger, RSS growth over the last nudge, over the minimum, fixed cadence, minimum plus cap, a parsed-bytes budget). Growth over the last nudge ratchets: each nudge raises the bar to that cycle's peak, so tree memory grew with repo size (2.8 GB off-heap at 4×). Minimum-plus-cap kept tree memory at 0.18–0.35 GB at both sizes, on macOS and Linux, with no wall-time change on a multi-core host.
- The extra major GCs cost about 5–8 % more user CPU; on a single-CPU container wall time is about 8 % higher than with the trigger alone.
- `runProjectScan` (the one-shot `resolve(inputs.map(collect))`) lives in a test helper; production code always collects per file.

## Testing & verification

Synthetic repo: 3,005 `.kt`, 3,004 `.java` and 302 `.ts` files (78 MB) with Spring and Kotlin controllers (including interface-inherited ones, the cross-file case), a constant-folded Kotlin route, RestTemplate consumers, an Express router and fetch/axios consumers. `group sync` with `GITNEXUS_QUERY_MAX_RSS_MB=0`, macOS arm64, Node 22, three interleaved rounds each:

| group | build | peak RSS (MiB) | wall (s, mean) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| HTTP only | `main` | 5786–5909 | 70.3 |
| HTTP only | this PR | 1011–1052 | 67.3 |
| all extractors | `main` | 6460–6627 | 93.8 |
| all extractors | this PR | 1021–1055 | 91.9 |

- Contracts are identical to `main` in every run once sorted. Byte order varies between runs on `main` as well, because the source file glob is not ordered.
- HTTP extractor alone, no graph, at 1× / 2× / 4× size: `main` peaks at 2.5 / 5.2 GB (4× not run); this PR at 0.45 / 0.79 / 0.93 GB, with RSS above the JS heap at 0.2–0.3 GB at every size.
- Linux (node:22-bookworm container), extract-only: tree memory 0.23–0.34 GB at 1× and 4×; the nudge buffer adds 0 MB resident.

New tests (each fails on the commit before its fix):

title: fix(lbug): say when memory was already in use before the query the guard blames
body:
## Summary

When the read-query memory guard (#3696, #3749) stops the process, its message now shows the RSS each running query started at, the net change in process RSS since then on RSS breaches, and how long the query ran. When every listed query started with more than half of the breaching RSS already in use, the headline reports the lowest starting RSS and points operators to both earlier work and the running queries. A breach measured on the macOS physical footprint is named as such and is not compared with RSS.

## Motivation / context

The guard samples **process** memory while any query is in flight and names the queries active at the breach. If other work in the same process has already pushed RSS close to the budget, the first query that starts takes the blame.

We hit this on a large Kotlin/Android monorepo during `gitnexus group sync`. The guard stopped the process at the 8 GiB default and named a `FETCHES` query that returns 0 rows. `GITNEXUS_QUERY_TRACE=1` showed RSS growing by several GB between two zero-row queries, with no query in flight. The memory came from source parsing in the HTTP contract extractor, which #4070 addresses. The message sent us looking for a runaway query that did not exist.

`ActiveQuery.startBytes` was already recorded for the trace line but was not part of the breach report.

## Areas touched

- [x] `gitnexus/` (CLI / core / MCP server)
- [ ] `gitnexus-web/` (Vite / React UI)
- [ ] `.github/` (workflows, actions)
- [ ] `eval/` or other tooling
- [x] Docs / agent config only — `RUNBOOK.md` § Query memory limit

## Scope & constraints

**In scope**

- `QueryMemoryBreach`: `rssBytes` / `activeLabels` → `memoryBytes`, `measurement: 'rss' | 'footprint'`, `activeQueries: { label, startBytes, runningMs }[]` (oldest first). The only producer is `observe` in `createQueryMemoryGuard`; the only consumer is `formatBreachMessage` via the default `onBreach`.
- Breach message wording, plus the `RUNBOOK.md` symptom and a paragraph on reading the new headline.

**Explicitly out of scope / not done here**

- Exit code 70, `GITNEXUS_QUERY_MAX_RSS_MB`, `GITNEXUS_QUERY_TRACE`, budget resolution and the sampling cadence are unchanged.
- On macOS, the optional query trace's `memPeakMB` can include physical-footprint samples. The same accumulator is present on the base branch. This PR changes the exit diagnostic. [Base implementation](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/blob/ab02dac758564c0f9de819ebd3d8c42e6d8a914e/gitnexus/src/core/lbug/query-memory-guard.ts#L124-L152), [review discussion](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/pull/4071#discussion_r4687594883).
- The memory consumer from the motivating case (HTTP extractor tree retention) is fixed separately in #4070.

## Implementation notes

The guard compares growth and the pre-existing share only in one unit. `startBytes` is RSS. On macOS a breach can come from `phys_footprint`, which counts compressed and swapped pages that RSS does not. Subtracting the two would charge compressed pre-existing memory to the query, so a footprint breach reports start RSS and run time only, and says why.

The headline uses the lowest starting RSS over the active queries. RSS can fall and rise during a query, so these samples establish the process total at each start time. They cannot attribute the memory present at the breach. The comparison is strict `>` half of the breach value (`PREEXISTING_MEMORY_SHARE = 0.5`, a constant, not a setting). The floor is printed rounded down, so "X GB or more" stays true.

Example messages (budget 16 GB, breach 16.5 GB):

```text
GitNexus stopped: process memory (RSS) reached 16.5 GB, over the 16.0 GB limit, while running a graph query. The database cannot cancel a running query, so the process is exiting to protect the host.
Running queries:
  - MATCH (a)-[r]->(b) RETURN a, b (RSS at start 1.0 GB, +15.5 GB since start, running 42.0 s)
```

```text
GitNexus stopped: process memory (RSS) reached 16.5 GB, over the 16.0 GB limit. RSS was already 12.0 GB or more when each query listed below started. Check earlier work such as source parsing as well as the running queries. The database cannot cancel a running query, so the process is exiting to protect the host.
Running queries:
  - MATCH (a) RETURN a (RSS at start 12.0 GB, +4.5 GB since start, running 4.0 s)
  - MATCH (b) RETURN b (RSS at start 13.0 GB, +3.5 GB since start, running 1.0 s)
```

```text
GitNexus stopped: physical footprint reached 16.5 GB, over the 16.0 GB limit, while running a graph query. Start memory below is RSS, which excludes compressed and swapped pages, so it cannot show how much of the footprint was in use before these queries started. ...
```

All three keep the `Set GITNEXUS_QUERY_MAX_RSS_MB=<MiB> …` hint and the pointer to #3696.

## Testing & verification

- [x] All eight Ubuntu CLI coverage shards and all 22 macOS and Windows platform test shards passed on `06c2c3861`. [GitHub Actions run](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/actions/runs/45504514475).
- The full-suite result above comes from CI. The local full run was interrupted. I reran the local failures separately, using an ordinary checkout path, isolated settings, and freshly installed locked dependencies. All of those cases passed on rerun.
- [x] `cd gitnexus && npx vitest run test/unit/query-memory-guard.test.ts test/unit/lbug-pool-query-lifetime.test.ts test/integration/lbug-pool.test.ts` — 3 files, 65 tests pass, including negative RSS deltas and the pooled-read exit diagnostic
- [x] `cd gitnexus && npx tsc --noEmit` — clean
- [x] Differential: each commit's new tests fail against the previous source (5 / 12 / 3 failures) and pass on head. The follow-up regression also failed on the previous message when RSS went from 900 to 100 to 1,100 MiB during a query. New cases cover the 50% boundary, the lowest-start floor when the oldest query started high, two real guard queries with different start time and RSS, a footprint breach, a backwards clock step and an empty query list.
- [x] Prettier leaves the changed `.ts` files unchanged; ESLint reports 0 errors.

## Risk & rollout

Low. Message text changes; anything that greps stderr for `GitNexus stopped: process memory reached` must now match `process memory (RSS) reached` or `physical footprint reached`. The repo had two such consumers (an integration test and `RUNBOOK.md`); both are updated. No index refresh needed.

doctor: FTS/VECTOR probes fail on constrained mmap environments (8 TiB reservation)
body:
## Summary

`gitnexus doctor` reports `Full-text search: unavailable` and `VECTOR extension: unavailable` in constrained environments, with:

```
Buffer manager exception: Mmap for size 8796093022208 failed.
```

The extension probes themselves are fine — the failure happens while creating the throwaway probe database, before `LOAD EXTENSION` runs.

## Root cause

`probeExtensionLoad()` in `gitnexus/src/core/lbug/native-check.ts` opens:

```ts
const db = new lbug.Database(':memory:');
```

`@ladybugdb/core`'s `Database` constructor takes `maxDBSize` as its 5th argument, and `0` (the default) means *reserve the platform's full mmap address space* — typically 8 TiB on 64-bit Linux. Constrained environments reject that reservation, so the probe never reaches the extension load.

`analyze` / `query` are unaffected because those database opens pass a bounded `maxDBSize` (for example `LBUG_MAX_DB_SIZE` in `lbug-config.ts`).

## Environment

- GitNexus 1.6.13-rc.96 (reproducible on 1.6.12 as well)
- `@ladybugdb/core` 0.21.1
- Linux arm64 (Android proot), glibc 2.39, Node v22.23.5, 14 GB RAM

## Reproduction

1. `gitnexus doctor` → FTS/VECTOR unavailable plus the mmap error above.
2. Opening the same in-memory database with an explicit cap works, and the extension loads:

```js
const db = new libug.Database(':memory:', 0, false, false, 1024 * 1024 * 1024);
await conn.query('LOAD EXTENSION fts');   // OK
await conn.query('LOAD EXTENSION vector'); // OK
```

3. `gitnexus analyze` / `gitnexus query` succeed because they already pin a bounded size.

## Proposed fix

Pass a small bounded `maxDBSize` (1 GiB is enough for a throwaway probe database) when constructing the probe DB. Keep the constant local to `native-check.ts`: importing `lbug-config` there is explicitly avoided so `doctor` still runs when the native addon is missing. Both FTS and VECTOR probes share `probeExtensionLoad`, so one change covers both lines.

## Verification

With the one-line change + local constant applied to a local build, `gitnexus doctor` now prints:

```
Graph store:      available
Full-text search: available
VECTOR extension: available
Semantic support: vector-index capable (repository index not checked)
```

`analyze` and `query` results are unchanged.

title: fix(lbug): pin doctor probe DB max size to avoid 8 TiB mmap reservation
body:
## What changed

Both extension checks in `gitnexus doctor` now open their temporary in-memory database with a 64 MiB buffer pool and a 64 MiB maximum database size. The limit lives in `native-check.ts` so doctor can still start when the native addon is missing.

## Why

Fixes #4074.

LadybugDB's default database mapping can reserve 8 TiB of virtual address space. On the reporter's Android proot installation this failed before either extension could load. Capping only the database mapping still left a second reservation sized from host RAM. On a 32 GiB Linux host with a 16 GiB process limit, that pool requested 25 GiB and both probes failed.

- The reporter verified that capping the database mapping allowed FTS and VECTOR to load on Linux arm64 with LadybugDB 0.21.1.

title: fix(analyze): print progress lines when stderr is not a terminal
body:
## Summary

When neither stdout nor stderr is a terminal (Docker without `-t`, CI, or both streams redirected), `gitnexus analyze` printed no progress until it finished. It now prints a plain progress line every 10 seconds there, and log lines no longer carry the bar's cursor controls as raw bytes. A terminal behaves as before.

## Motivation / context

Fixes #1194. The reporter runs analyze from a script in a compose service, on a plain Node image, and sees nothing until it ends. Any CI log of `gitnexus analyze` has the same gap: on a 1,199-file repository with output piped, `main` printed its header and then nothing for 92 seconds.

The cause is cli-progress itself: it does not render when its stream is not a TTY and `noTTYOutput` is off. A log line written during the run also went out as `\x1b[2K\r` plus the text, so logs got raw escape bytes.

## Areas touched

- [x] `gitnexus/` (CLI / core / MCP server)
- [ ] `gitnexus-web/` (Vite / React UI)
- [ ] `.github/` (workflows, actions)
- [ ] `eval/` or other tooling
- [ ] Docs / agent config only (`AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `.cursor/`, `llms.txt`, etc.)

## Scope & constraints

**In scope**

- `src/cli/analyze.ts`:
  - `PLAIN_PROGRESS_INTERVAL_MS` (10 s).
  - The progress setup names the two existing cases, `bridgesParentTty` and `redrawsInPlace`. When the bar is not redrawn in place, it turns on cli-progress' non-TTY mode with that schedule and a format without bar characters.
  - `barLog` clears the line only where the bar is redrawn.
  - `toProgressLabel` takes control characters and line breaks out of a label before it reaches the bar, and the plain mode sets `clearOnComplete` so the log does not end on a blank line.
- `test/unit/analyze-respawn-progress-terminal.test.ts`: six tests next to the bridge tests, reusing their mocks.
- `test/integration/cli-e2e.test.ts`: the #1169 test, which already runs the real CLI with piped stdio on a fresh repository, also checks the progress output.
- `docs/cli-reference.md`: one sentence under the analyze flags on what analyze prints when no terminal is involved.

**Explicitly out of scope / not done here**

- Phase messages and how often the pipeline reports them are unchanged.
- No new flag or environment variable; the interval is a constant.
- The bar on a terminal and the ANSI bridge for the respawned child (#1751) are unchanged.
- Other commands with progress output, such as `wiki`, are not touched.
- Two behaviours that predate this change stay as they are. From an interactive shell, `analyze 2> file` still writes the redrawn bar to the file, because the parent bridges its terminal to the respawned child when either stream is a terminal (#1751). And `analyze > file` with stderr on a terminal still puts `\x1b[2K\r` in front of log lines in the file.

## Implementation notes

- **Why a schedule, not one line per message.** Phase messages carry per-file and per-chunk text, such as `Scanning repository... (f5.ts)` and `Parsing chunk 3/5 (cache)...`. One line per message would flood a log on a large repository. The schedule prints the latest state, and the elapsed time analyze already appends to a long phase (`Creating search indexes... (14s)`) shows the run is alive.
- **When the plain mode applies.** It applies when stderr is not a TTY and the process is not a respawned child bridging to its parent's terminal (`GITNEXUS_RESPAWN_PROGRESS_TTY`). That is exactly the case where cli-progress used to print nothing. A respawned child under a non-TTY parent gets the plain mode, and the parent's tee forwards its lines live.
- **Lifecycle.** In non-TTY mode, cli-progress renders on a timer that `bar.stop()` clears. Every exit path of analyze already stops the bar: up to date, FTS repair only, graph phase handed to the continuation process, success, and failure or cancellation. The bar on a terminal re-arms the same kind of timer every 100 ms. cli-progress' `gracefulExit` stays off, so no signal listener is added.
- **Who reads this output.** Nothing in the repository parses the CLI's analyze output. The Docker image runs `serve`, the server analyzes through its forked worker, and the hooks only print the command.

## Testing & verification

title: feat(cli): add --json to gitnexus list
body:
## Summary

`gitnexus list --json` prints the indexed repositories as one line of JSON on stdout, so a script can map a checkout path to its registry name without scraping the human output.

## Motivation / context

Closes #1533. A host service that runs `gitnexus analyze` on clones it creates needs the registry name of each clone, for example to pass `--repo`. The name is not always the directory's basename: `HelixDB__helix-db` is registered as `helix-db`. `gitnexus list` already shows the mapping, but only as formatted text. `status --json` exists for one repository; nothing listed them all in a machine-readable form.

## Areas touched

- [x] `gitnexus/` (CLI / core / MCP server)
- [ ] `gitnexus-web/` (Vite / React UI)
- [ ] `.github/` (workflows, actions)
- [ ] `eval/` or other tooling
- [ ] Docs / agent config only (`AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `.cursor/`, `llms.txt`, etc.)

## Scope & constraints

**In scope**

- `src/cli/list.ts`: `listCommand(options)` takes `{ json?: boolean }`. With `json`, it prints `{"schemaVersion":1,"repositories":[...]}` and returns. An empty registry prints an empty list instead of the "run analyze" hint.
- `src/cli/index.ts`: `--json` on `list`, described like `check --json`.
- `src/cli/help-i18n.ts`: `list|--json` uses the existing `help.option.json` key, as `check` and the `group` commands do, so zh-CN help is translated with no new string.

**Explicitly out of scope / not done here**

- No staleness or source-availability fields. `list_repos` computes those per repository; the registry rows are what `list` already reads.

## Implementation notes

Each row has the field names of the MCP `list_repos` tool: `name`, `path`, `storagePath`, `indexedAt`, `lastCommit`, `remoteUrl`, `stats`, `branch`, `branches` (`branch`, `indexedAt`, `lastCommit`). Optional fields are omitted when absent, as in `list_repos`. The rows are built field by field, so internal registry fields such as `shareOptOut` stay out of the contract. `schemaVersion: 1` matches `status --json`. title: fix(eval): stabilize containment and explain failed preflight checks
body:
## Summary

Linux can keep an exited helper in its process group until its new parent reaps it. GitNexus treated a successful signal to that group as proof that a live descendant had needed killing. In the native proposal canary, a zombie `socat` caused a successful model session to be discarded after 8 of the expected 12 provider requests.

```text
managed leader exits
  residual Linux group → SIGSTOP → wait up to the existing termination grace
    group disappears → preserve the leader's exit status
    group persists   → SIGKILL and record a forced kill
```

The canary now checks report completeness first, so pytest identifies the failed arm, run and error category if a sweep ends early. It still requires six sessions, twelve provider requests, the expected usage and costs, and both positive and negative grading results.

Mohammed Faisal Parvez (@faisalhacks) contributed the offline preflight diagnostics and regression tests in #4082. The preflight now names each failed check, so a successful tool count can be distinguished from a CLI session failure, missing tool, incorrect patch, or wrong repository. The merge preserves the original commit and credits Faisal as a co-author. [Original contribution](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/pull/4082) · [Reported preflight failure](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/issues/4046)

## Combined revision

The focused proposal and process-control suites passed 29 tests locally with six platform-dependent skips. Ruff passed for all four changed files. GitHub is running the checks for the combined revision. [Combined CI](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/actions/runs/45691313007)

## Evidence for the process-group fix

- The linked Ubuntu 24.04 job stopped at eight requests. The hosted reproduction recorded the same count, a successful CLI exit and its full cost, and a single `socat` process in state `Z` when cleanup marked the session as a forced kill. [Original job](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/actions/runs/45671209079/job/139406910611) · [Instrumented reproduction](https://github.com/magyargergo/GitNexus/actions/runs/45680110111/job/139438079780)
- A deterministic Linux regression holds an exited process waitable until the group is signaled. It failed on the previous code and passes with the fix. Existing quiet and inherited-pipe descendant tests also pass.
- All 144 hosted canaries passed under concurrent Docker load, 48 each on Ubuntu 22.04, 24.04 and 26.04. The logs captured three more zombie `socat` helpers, all followed by successful sessions. [Hosted stress run](https://github.com/magyargergo/GitNexus/actions/runs/45682508023)
- The PR's containment matrix passed on Ubuntu 22.04, 24.04, 26.04 and Windows. The Ubuntu 24.04 job passed 286 tests with 30 capability-dependent skips. Its JUnit report confirms that the native paired proposal canary, pinned proposal graders and the new regression all executed. [Ubuntu 24.04 containment](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/actions/runs/45682482101/job/139446785647)
- The local containment selection passed 272 tests with 44 platform-dependent skips. Ruff and `git diff --check` passed.

## Merge risk

The shared evaluator process supervisor changes its Linux cleanup after a leader exits with a residual group. Live descendants are stopped immediately. A persistent group can add up to the configured termination grace before escalation to SIGKILL, five seconds by default. A successful result requires the kernel to confirm that the group has gone. The change can be reverted independently of the assertion improvement.

title: fix(swift): resolve cross-file extension owners by declared type
body:
## Summary

Resolve Swift calls to helpers declared in separate files when a top-level type and a nested type share a short name. This covers calls from the original type body and calls from another extension of that type.

Refs #3426.

## Reproduction

The six-file fixture defines `Handler` and `Container.Handler`, places their helpers in separate files, and adds an unrelated same-name method and a function local to a different caller. On `main` at `50228e1`, five of the seven assertions fail. On that baseline, `runFromExtension` links to a helper local to another method in `ExtensionCallers.swift`. The extension-contained caller also fails against the first revision of this PR.

| Call site | Verified target with the fix |
| --- | --- |
| `Handler.run()` | `HandlerExtension.swift` |
| `Container.Handler.runNested()` | `NestedHandlerExtension.swift` |
| `Container.Handler.runFromExtension()` | `NestedHandlerExtension.swift` |
| `Container.Handler.runInstanceMethod()` | `OtherNestedExtension.swift` |

## Implementation

- Reuse the Swift extension-header reader to reconcile the full declared owner inside its Swift target.
- Implement the workspace-owner hook directly on the typed Swift resolver. Its required context parameter is inferred from the [shared hook declaration](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/blob/f37840b71005846f2db1cc5a6f3b3b8196594b3a/gitnexus/src/core/ingestion/scope-resolution/contract/scope-resolver.ts#L799-L805).
- Use the enclosing member’s reconciled owner for a bare call from an extension body. Respect nearer lexical bindings and use the recorded `self` binding to distinguish type and instance methods.
- Record ambiguity when several compatible same-owner overloads survive and emit no guessed `CALLS` edge.

## Verification

- `npm test -- test/integration/resolvers/swift.test.ts -t 'Swift cross-file extension ownership'` exercises ownership, the extension caller, type and instance methods, local shadowing, and ambiguity.
- **412 tests passed across 18 files** covering Swift resolution, local shadowing, rename, parse-cache identity, and language-boundary checks.
- A cold CLI run and a forced rebuild that reused all six files both resolved `runFromExtension` to `Function:NestedHandlerExtension.swift:Container.Handler.makeValue#1` with current index freshness.
- `npm run build`, `tsc --noEmit`, `npm run typecheck:tests`, `npm run test:dupes`, and `git diff --check` passed.

The earlier automated review flagged the nested graph ID. The CLI outputs the fully qualified persisted ID above. The regression now checks the exact target file for each named callee and requires a single matching edge.

title: fix(impact): exclude IMPORTS-only nodes from risk tier calculation
body:
## Summary

Prevents IMPORTS-only BFS nodes from inflating risk tier in impact analysis. Nodes reached exclusively via file-level IMPORTS edges are excluded from the `directCount`/`impactedCount` fed to `scoreImpactRisk`, while `impactedCount` in the response retains its total-walk meaning for backward compatibility.

## Motivation / context

Fixes #3602 (Repro 1). An exported Interface declared in a module with 120 importers but only 1 real consumer (USES edge) reported `risk: HIGH, impactedCount: 121, epistemic: exact`. The 120 IMPORTS edges represent file-level module imports — "file X imports the module" — which is not evidence of direct usage of the target symbol. The `impactedCount >= 100` threshold in `score()` falsely elevated the risk tier.

This implements Option 2 from the [design discussion](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/issues/3602): smallest diff, no new required response fields, `impactedCount` keeps its current meaning, and the exclusion is transparent via `summary.imports_only` and `riskNote`.

## Areas touched

- [x] `gitnexus/` (CLI / core / MCP server)

## Scope & constraints

**In scope**

- Exclude IMPORTS-only nodes from `directCount`/`impactedCount` passed to `scoreImpactRisk` for symbol targets (Class, Interface)
- File target exemption: `isFileTarget` gates the exclusion so File impact queries retain their current behavior — IMPORTS edges ARE the correct evidence for "who imports this file?"
- Add `summary.imports_only` (optional, only present when > 0) for transparency
- Add `riskNote` explaining the exclusion when it affects the risk verdict
- Regression test reproducing the exact #3602 Repro 1 scenario (1 USES edge + 120 IMPORTS edges)

**Explicitly out of scope / not done here**

- Option 1 (separate `importers` field replacing `impactedCount` semantics) — can follow if preferred
- Downstream direction changes — downstream scoring is unaffected

## Implementation notes

The `compareImpactEdgeStrength` argmax sorts by `relType ASC`. Since `'CALLS' < 'IMPORTS'` lexicographically, a node reachable by both CALLS and IMPORTS is stamped CALLS. Therefore `relationType === 'IMPORTS'` on a BFS node truly identifies nodes reached *exclusively* via IMPORTS edges — no false positives.

The fix is applied between the BFS result grouping and the `scoreImpactRisk` call: two new counts (`importsOnlyCount`, `importsOnlyDirectCount`) are computed from the `impacted` array, gated by `isFileTarget`, and subtracted from the values passed to `scoreImpactRisk`. The response-level `impactedCount` and `summary.direct` are unchanged.

The `riskNote` chain already has a priority structure: `omittedNameOnlyCalls > 0` → `risk === 'UNKNOWN'` → (new) `tierImportsOnlyCount > 0`. The IMPORTS note fires only when neither higher-priority condition applies.

## Testing & verification

- [x] `cd gitnexus && npx vitest run test/integration/impact-imports-only-risk.test.ts` — 5/5 new tests pass
- [x] `cd gitnexus && npx vitest run test/integration/impact-file-risk-scale.test.ts` — File target exemption verified (risk='MEDIUM' preserved)
- [x] `cd gitnexus && npx vitest run test/integration/impact-private-type-file-seed.test.ts` — Repro 2 fix preserved (8/8 pass)
- [x] `cd gitnexus && npx vitest run test/integration/impact-zero-caller-risk.test.ts` — Zero-caller UNKNOWN preserved (9/9 pass)
- [x] `cd gitnexus && npx vitest run test/integration/impact-` — All 22 impact integration files pass (318 tests, 0 failures)
- [x] `cd gitnexus && npx vitest run test/unit/impact-risk.test.ts` — All 20 unit tests pass
- [x] `cd gitnexus && npx tsc --noEmit` — Clean typecheck
- [x] `npx prettier --check gitnexus/src/mcp/local/local-backend.ts gitnexus/test/integration/impact-imports-only-risk.test.ts` — Formatted
- [x] `npx eslint gitnexus/src/mcp/local/local-backend.ts gitnexus/test/integration/impact-imports-only-risk.test.ts` — 0 errors (warnings are pre-existing `no-explicit-any`)

**Regression test seed graph:**

```
Interface:AdapterConfig <--[USES, 0.85]-- Function:initAuth
File:adapter.ts <--[IMPORTS, 1.0]-- File:route-0..route-119.ts
File:adapter.ts --[DEFINES]--> Interface:AdapterConfig
```

Before fix: `impactedCount=121, risk=HIGH` (121 >= 100 threshold)
After fix: scoring receives `impactedCount=1, directCount=1` → `risk=LOW`; response still shows `impactedCount=121, summary.imports_only=120`

## Risk & rollout

Risk is **LOW**: the response shape is additive only. Consumers of `impactedCount` see no change. `summary.imports_only` and the IMPORTS-related `riskNote` are both optional new fields. Risk tier becomes more accurate — no false HIGH verdicts from IMPORTS fan-out. No index refresh needed.

title: fix(csharp): capture array_type parameters to resolve indexElement calls (CSHARP-01)
body:
### Area

core / ingestion / scope-resolution / csharp

### Summary

C# array parameters typed as T[] fail to emit @type-binding.parameter captures, leaving array receivers untyped and causing indexed element calls like repos[0].Save() to drop as an unresolved receiver.

### Context

Auditing the C# receiver resolution matrix tracked in docs/languages/csharp-ingestion-gaps.md (CSHARP-01) and gitnexus/bench/receiver-resolution/BASELINE.md.

In the benchmark matrix (measure.mjs), C# resolves 8 of 10 shape cells, with indexElement (repos[0].Save();) remaining as the sole VISIBLE-GAP.

Tracing the pipeline indicates:

gitnexus/src/core/ingestion/utils/call-analysis.ts (SUBSCRIPT_NODE_TYPES) correctly identifies C#'s element_access_expression.
csharpScopeResolver.elementTypeOf (unwrapCsharpElementType in accessor-unwrap.ts) correctly delegates index unwrap to extractElementTypeFromString(containerType), which already handles T[] → T.
However, in gitnexus/src/core/ingestion/languages/csharp/query.ts (lines 153–171), the tree-sitter @type-binding.parameter query matches (identifier), (generic_name), (qualified_name), (nullable_type), and (predefined_type), but lacks a pattern for (array_type). Consequently, parameters like User[] repos never emit a type binding in the scope graph.

### Expected behavior

Given a method parameter with an array type annotation:

csharp
void Process(User[] repos) {
    repos[0].Save();
}

Tree-sitter captures @type-binding.parameter with type User[] (or equivalent array type node) for parameter repos. The compound receiver / scope resolution pass unwraps the element type to User via csharpScopeResolver.elementTypeOf and links repos[0].Save() to Method:...:User.Save#0 with zero decoy edges.

### Actual behavior

repos receives no type binding capture from csharp/query.ts. The receiver remains untyped during compound receiver walk, and repos[0].Save() drops as an unresolved receiver (VISIBLE-GAP), emitting no call edge to User.Save.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Inspect the C# receiver shape in gitnexus/bench/receiver-resolution/measure.mjs (lines 970–1035):
csharp
class Cap_indexElement {
    async Task indexElement(Service svc, User[] repos) {
        repos[0].Save();
    }
}

2. Run the receiver resolution benchmark check from gitnexus/:
sh
npm run build
node --import tsx bench/receiver-resolution/measure.mjs --check

3. Observe csharp.shapes.indexElement recorded as VISIBLE-GAP in baseline.json.

### Environment

OS: Windows / Linux (all platforms affected)
Node version: v22.x
Commit SHA: 50228e11a (main)
Component: gitnexus/src/core/ingestion/languages/csharp/query.ts

### Logs / screenshots

From docs/languages/csharp-ingestion-gaps.md:
| ID        | Evidence     | Gap or boundary                                      | Next planning step and acceptance                                                                                                       |
| --------- | ------------ | ---------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| CSHARP-01 | Measured gap | `indexElement` remains VISIBLE-GAP for a typed array. | Locate the lost array/type-owner evidence, then assert the exact User.Save target with a same-name decoy and an untyped/unsupported negative. |

Missing AST match in gitnexus/src/core/ingestion/languages/csharp/query.ts:

scheme
;; Current captures:
(parameter type: (identifier) @type-binding.type name: (identifier) @type-binding.name) @type-binding.parameter
(parameter type: (generic_name) @type-binding.type name: (identifier) @type-binding.name) @type-binding.parameter
(parameter type: (qualified_name) @type-binding.type name: (identifier) @type-binding.name) @type-binding.parameter
(parameter type: (nullable_type) @type-binding.type name: (identifier) @type-binding.name) @type-binding.parameter
(parameter type: (predefined_type) @type-binding.type name: (identifier) @type-binding.name) @type-binding.parameter
;; Missing:
(parameter type: (array_type) @type-binding.type name: (identifier) @type-binding.name) @type-binding.parameter

title: fix(csharp): capture array_type parameters to resolve indexElement calls
body:
## Summary

C# parameters typed `T[]` now produce a `@type-binding.parameter` capture, so element calls such as `repos[0].Save()` and `repos?[0].Save()` on a `User[] repos` parameter resolve to `User.Save` instead of being dropped as unresolved receivers.

Closes #4098

## Motivation / context

`gitnexus/src/core/ingestion/languages/csharp/query.ts` had parameter type-binding patterns for `identifier`, `generic_name`, `qualified_name`, `nullable_type` and `predefined_type`, but none for `array_type`. An array parameter therefore got no binding, and the compound-receiver pass had no container type to peel on the index step.

The rest of the path already existed:
- `unwrapCsharpElementType` answers the `index` route with `extractElementTypeFromString`, which maps `User[]` to `User`.
- `User[]?` was already bound (through the `nullable_type` pattern + `stripNullable`) as `User[]`, so the `User[]` spelling is already a binding that production code handles.

Java already captures `(array_type)` in `formal_parameter` (#3955), so this brings C# in line.

## Areas touched

- [x] `gitnexus/` (CLI / core / MCP server)
- [ ] `gitnexus-web/` (Vite / React UI)
- [ ] `.github/` (workflows, actions)
- [ ] `eval/` or other tooling
- [ ] Docs / agent config only

## Scope & constraints

**In scope**

- One new tree-sitter pattern in the C# query: `(parameter type: (array_type) ...) @type-binding.parameter`.
- `receiver-chain-walker-spellings.test.ts`: the C# `OptionalElement` row (`repos?[0].Save()`) was pinned as a KNOWN GAP; it now expects `User.Save`. Added an `IndexElement` row for the plain `repos[0].Save()` from the issue.
- Regenerated `csharp-captures-golden/expected-captures.json` (`UPDATE_GOLDEN=1`). Exactly two capture groups are added, both the `string[] args` parameter of `Main` in `csharp-async-binding/Program.cs` and `csharp-hello/Hello.cs`.
- Rebaselined `bench/receiver-resolution`: `shapeArm.csharp.indexElement` VISIBLE-GAP -> RESOLVES; count arm unchanged. Entry added to `BASELINE.md`.

**Explicitly out of scope / not done here**

- `params User[] items`: tree-sitter-c-sharp parses it as `type`/`name` fields directly on `parameter_list`, not as a `parameter` node, so it needs a separate pattern. Left for a follow-up to keep this change small.
- Shapes the existing element peel does not recognize stay unresolved (no edge, same as before): jagged `User[][]`, multi-dimensional `User[,]`, `User?[]`, `List<User>[]`. I checked these return `undefined` from `unwrapCsharpElementType(…, { kind: 'index' })`, so the new binding cannot produce a wrong target for them.
- Local variables and fields typed `T[]` (`User[] xs = …;`) — the local/field annotation patterns have the same gap; not changed here.

## Implementation notes

The binding keeps the `[]` spelling (`interpretCsharpTypeBinding` strips nullable/generic/qualifier, so `Ns.User[]` becomes `User[]`), and the index step peels it. A direct member call on the array itself (`repos.Save()`) looks up a type named `User[]`, which does not exist, so it does not resolve to `User`.

## Testing & verification

- [x] `cd gitnexus && npx vitest run test/integration/resolvers/receiver-chain-walker-spellings.test.ts` — the two C# rows fail before the change, 16/16 pass after (note: the pipeline parses through `dist/`, so `npm run build` first)
- [x] `cd gitnexus && npx vitest run test/unit/scope-resolution/csharp test/integration/resolvers/csharp.test.ts test/integration/resolvers/csharp-1924.test.ts` — 404/404
- [x] `cd gitnexus && node --import tsx bench/receiver-resolution/measure.mjs --check` — OK against the updated baseline
- [x] `cd gitnexus && npx tsc --noEmit`
- [x] `cd gitnexus && npm run typecheck:tests`
- [ ] `cd gitnexus && npm test`

## Risk & rollout

Low. The change only adds bindings for C# array parameters; every new binding is either peeled to its element type on an index step or unmatched. Users get the new CALLS edges on their next `npx gitnexus analyze` (parser cache identity is derived from the query bytes, so no manual cache bump).

## Checklist

- [x] PR body meets repo minimum length
- [ ] If `AGENTS.md` / overlays changed — n/a
- [x] No secrets, tokens, or machine-specific paths committed

title: feat(cli): add --json output to gitnexus list
body:
## Summary

Adds a `--json` flag to `gitnexus list` that prints the global registry as one machine-readable JSON document on stdout.

Closes #1533

## Motivation / context

As described in #1533, a host service that drives `gitnexus analyze` needs to map its own clone directory (e.g. `/app/data/repos/HelixDB__helix-db`) to the GitNexus registry name (`helix-db`). `gitnexus list` already has that mapping in its `Path:` line, but only as human-formatted text, so consumers have to scrape it or guess from the directory basename, and the basename does not always match the name.

## Areas touched

- [x] `gitnexus/` (CLI / core / MCP server)
- [ ] `gitnexus-web/` (Vite / React UI)
- [ ] `.github/` (workflows, actions)
- [ ] `eval/` or other tooling
- [ ] Docs / agent config only (`AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `.cursor/`, `llms.txt`, etc.)

## Scope & constraints

**In scope**

- `gitnexus list --json` → `{"schemaVersion":1,"repositories":[...]}`. Each row has `name`, `path`, `storagePath`, `indexedAt`, `lastCommit`, `branch`, `remoteUrl`, `stats` and `branches` (per-branch indexes from #2106).
- Every key is always present: optional values become `null` / `[]` / `{}`, so consumers do not need existence checks.
- An empty registry prints `{"schemaVersion":1,"repositories":[]}` instead of the human "not indexed" hint.
- Help text for the new option in `en` and `zh-CN` (needed by the `cli-index-help` localization test), plus a line in the `gitnexus/README.md` CLI reference.

**Explicitly out of scope / not done here**

- The default human-readable `gitnexus list` output is unchanged.
- No `gitnexus resolve --path` command. The issue named it as an alternative; `list --json` covers the use case.

## Implementation notes

- Output fields are picked explicitly (`toJsonRow`) rather than serializing the registry entry. Internal bookkeeping such as `discovery` evidence and `shareOptOut` therefore stays out of the public contract, and future registry fields don't silently become API.
- `remoteUrl` is already credential-stripped on registry read (#2914), so it is safe to emit.
- The envelope (`schemaVersion` + payload, compact single line) mirrors `gitnexus status --json`. The CLI banner goes to stderr, so stdout parses directly (`gitnexus list --json | jq`).
- No new `GITNEXUS_*` environment variables.

## Testing & verification

- [x] `cd gitnexus && npx tsc --noEmit`: clean
- [x] Targeted unit tests (142 passed across 9 files): `list-status-branch`, `cli-index-help`, `cli-i18n`, `cli-entry`, `cli-command-banner`, `cli-message`, `status-content-drift`, `clean-stale`, `doctor-format`
- [x] Three new tests in `test/unit/list-status-branch.test.ts`: full row shape including branch indexes and exclusion of internal fields, stable defaults for absent optional fields, and the empty-registry output
- [x] Manual check on Windows (Node 24.12) against a real registry: `gitnexus list --json` parses cleanly, `GITNEXUS_LANG=zh-CN gitnexus list --help` shows the localized option, and plain `gitnexus list` output is unchanged
- [ ] Full `npm test`: not completed locally. The whole unit suite stalled on this Windows machine, so I am relying on CI for the full matrix.
- [x] `detect-changes --scope all`: only the `ListCommand → *` flows are affected. It reported a partial result because the one-line `.option('--json', …)` addition in `src/cli/index.ts` sits in top-level commander wiring with no enclosing symbol.

## Risk & rollout

Additive and opt-in. Without `--json`, behavior is identical. No index refresh is needed and nothing breaks.

## Checklist

- [x] PR body meets repo minimum length
- [x] If `AGENTS.md` / overlays changed: n/a, not changed
- [x] No secrets, tokens, or machine-specific paths committed

title: feat(web): add startLine/endLine line ranges to the agent read tool
body:
## Summary

The web UI agent's `read` tool now accepts optional `startLine` / `endLine` (1-indexed, inclusive), so the agent can read just the lines it needs instead of a whole file.

Closes #439

## Motivation / context

As described in #439, `read` always returned the whole file. That wastes tokens on large files, and the agent can't follow its own `[[src/auth.ts:45-60]]`-style citations to a specific range. Separately, the 50,000-character cutoff meant the agent could **never** see anything past that point in a large file. A range now reaches content beyond the cutoff.

## Areas touched

- [ ] `gitnexus/` (CLI / core / MCP server)
- [x] `gitnexus-web/` (Vite / React UI)
- [ ] `.github/` (workflows, actions)
- [ ] `eval/` or other tooling
- [ ] Docs / agent config only (`AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `.cursor/`, `llms.txt`, etc.)

## Scope & constraints

**In scope**

- `read({ filePath, startLine?, endLine? })`. Either bound may be omitted or `null`: `startLine` alone reads to the end of the file, `endLine` alone reads from line 1.
- The output header names the window: `File: src/a.ts (lines 3-5 of 10)`.
- An `endLine` past the end of the file is clamped. A `startLine` past the end, a `startLine < 1`, or an `endLine < startLine` returns an explanatory message instead of an empty slice. The agent gets told what went wrong and can retry.
- An oversized range is still capped at 50k characters, with a hint to narrow the range. A truncated whole-file read now hints at `startLine`/`endLine`.
- One line in `BASE_SYSTEM_PROMPT` mentions the range parameters.

**Explicitly out of scope / not done here**

- Whole-file reads without a range are byte-for-byte unchanged.
- No change to the `GraphRAGBackend` interface, the `useAppState` wiring, or the server.

## Implementation notes

- **Slicing happens in the tool.** `/api/file` already supports `startLine`/`endLine`, but 0-indexed. Using it would mean widening `GraphRAGBackend.readFile` (string → `ReadFileResult`) and updating its other caller, the impact tool's snippet path, plus test stubs. Slicing in the tool keeps this PR to one source file and a test. Moving the range to the server, to save transferring large files, is an easy follow-up if you'd prefer it.
- **Schema uses plain `z.number().optional().nullable()`**, matching the other tools in this file. Range validation (integer, ≥ 1, ordered) happens in code rather than with `.int().positive()`, because some providers' function-calling schema converters reject `exclusiveMinimum`.

title: feat(group): add Swift HTTP consumer plugin
body:
## Summary

Closes #1677.

`group/extractors/http-patterns/` had no Swift plugin, and `.swift` was not in `HTTP_SCAN_GLOB`, so no consumer contracts were ever emitted for iOS, macOS or Swift-on-server clients. Backend provider contracts in the same group could never cross-link to them.

This adds `http-patterns/swift.ts` (consumers only) and registers it for `.swift`. Like `kotlin.ts`, it exports `null` when the vendored `tree-sitter-swift` binding is unavailable, so a missing grammar means no detections, never a crash.

## What it detects

| Shape | Example | Method |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Verb-named wrapper, labeled path | `RelayClient.get(path: "/api/customers")` | from method name |
| Verb-named wrapper, positional / `url:` | `client.put("/api/users/me", body: d)`, `client.delete(id: 3, url: "https://…/v1/items")` | from method name |
| `request` (Alamofire or wrapper) | `AF.request("/v1/items", method: .post)`, `client.request(method: "POST", path: "/api/users")` | `method:` arg (`.post`, `HTTPMethod.post`, `"POST"`); none → `GET` on `AF` (Alamofire default), `*` on other receivers; variable → `*` |

- Verbs: `get`, `post`, `put`, `patch`, `delete`. A receiver is required (`x.get(...)`, not bare `get(...)`).
- Swift interpolation `\(expr)` is emitted as a `${…}` placeholder, so the existing consumer normalizer folds it to `{param}` and strips a leading `\(baseURL)` prefix. `"/api/customers/\(id)"` becomes `http::GET::/api/customers/{param}`.
- Only literals that look like a URL path are emitted: they start with `/` (not protocol-relative `//host`), `http(s)://`, or an interpolated base followed by a single `/`. This keeps out `cache.get("authToken")`, `defaults.post("didLogin")` and similar.

Compared with the earlier attempt in #1678: this version handles interpolated paths (it doesn't truncate at the first `\(`), adds the `url:` label and Alamofire `request`/`method:`, and adds the path-shape guard against non-HTTP `get`/`post` methods.

**Out of scope** (these need data flow the source scan doesn't have): `URLRequest` + `request.httpMethod = "POST"`, bare `URLSession.shared.data(from: URL(string:))`, and paths held in variables or constants.

## Tests

New file: `test/unit/group/swift-http-consumers.test.ts`, 11 tests, including both shapes from the 1.6.12 comment on the issue (`client.request(method: "POST", path: "/api/users")`, `client.get("/api/users")`).
- Plugin level: labeled, positional and `url:` paths; interpolation; Alamofire default, `.post`, `HTTPMethod.delete` and variable verbs; negative cases (non-path literals, non-literal path, non-first positional, bare call, non-verb method); line reporting.
- End to end: `HttpRouteExtractor.extract` on a temp repo with a `.swift` file emits `http::GET::/api/customers/{param}` and `http::POST::/api/devices/register`.
- Verified that the registration and end-to-end tests fail without the `index.ts` change.

## How to verify

```bash
cd gitnexus
npx vitest run test/unit/group/swift-http-consumers.test.ts
npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json && npm run typecheck:tests
cd .. && npx prettier --check gitnexus/src/core/group/extractors/http-patterns gitnexus/test/unit/group/swift-http-consumers.test.ts
npx eslint gitnexus/src/core/group/extractors/http-patterns/swift.ts gitnexus/test/unit/group/swift-http-consumers.test.ts
```

`test/unit/group` as a whole: same pass and fail set as `main`, plus 11 new passing tests. The pre-existing local failures are LadybugDB `dlopen` (`libssl.3.dylib`) in the sync/service suites and are unrelated.

## Risk

The change is additive. The only shared edit is the `.swift` registry entry and the glob extension in `http-patterns/index.ts`. Swift files now get a tree-sitter parse during `group sync` source scanning. Confidence is 0.7, the same as the other source-scan consumers.

title: feat(nexus-ai): add max iterations, token tracking, and budget controls
body:
## Summary

Implements configurable iteration limits, real-time token usage tracking, approximate USD cost estimation, and per-question token budget guardrails for the Nexus AI web agent in `gitnexus-web`. Fixes #438.

## Motivation / context

Previously, `streamAgentResponse` in `gitnexus-web/src/core/llm/agent.ts` hardcoded `recursionLimit: 50` with no user-configurable iteration cap, no token accounting across streamed turns, no USD cost visibility, and no per-question token budget cutoff in `SettingsPanel` or `RightPanel`. Links to feature request #438.

## Areas touched

- [x] `gitnexus-web/` (Vite / React UI)
- Not touched: `gitnexus/`, `.github/`, `eval/`, or docs/agent config

## Scope & constraints

**In scope**

- Configurable `maxIterations` (default `8`, clamped `[1, 50]`, mapped to LangGraph `recursionLimit = 2 * maxIterations + 1`) and `tokenBudget` (default `0` = unlimited) stored in `AgentConfig` (`LLMSettings.agent`) via `settings-service.ts`.
- Deduplicated cumulative token tracking (`inputTokens`, `outputTokens`, `totalTokens`) across LangChain `'messages'` chunks and `'values'` snapshots, plus `GRAPH_RECURSION_LIMIT` detection in `streamAgentResponse`.
- Per-question `tokenBudget` enforcement via a linked `AbortController` that stops execution cleanly without overriding user Stop cancellations (`options.signal`).
- Provider/model approximate USD pricing lookup (`gitnexus-web/src/core/llm/pricing.ts`), rendering `Local (free)` for Ollama and omitting fabricated dollar estimates for unrecognized/unsplit cloud models.
- UI controls in `SettingsPanel.tsx` (supporting exponent-form inputs and temporary blank editing), conversation + per-message token/cost indicators in `RightPanel.tsx`, localized limit notices in `useAppState.tsx`, matching `en` / `zh-CN` translations, and Vitest unit tests.

**Explicitly out of scope / not done here**

- CLI / MCP / `gitnexus-shared` changes (this PR is isolated to `gitnexus-web/`).
- Live provider-billed invoice reconciliation or dynamic remote pricing fetches (uses a static published rate table in `pricing.ts`).
- Full browser-driven Playwright E2E run against a live LLM API key (checked existing `gitnexus-web/e2e/` selectors statically — no conflicts found).

## Implementation notes

- **Zero double-counting:** Token usage is keyed per AI message ID (or `anon-ai-<index>` fallback) using `Math.max` across `'messages'` deltas and finalized `'values'` snapshots.
- **Signal identity preserved:** When `tokenBudget === 0` (unlimited), `options.signal` is passed straight through to `agent.stream` without wrapping, preserving strict signal-reference equality and existing abort behavior.
- **Honest cost reporting:** `estimateCostUsd` checks strict numeric/latest version suffixes (`VERSION_SUFFIX_RE`) so distinct variants like `gemini-2.0-flash-lite` are not silently billed at base rates, returns `null` if a paid cloud model reports `totalTokens > 0` without input/output breakdown, and `RightPanel` omits conversation cost pills whenever any turn has unknown cost.

title: C#: global-name fallback links `new Color(...)` to an unrelated in-repo type from a namespace the caller never imports
body:
## Summary

When a C# file constructs a type that is not in the repo (e.g. `UnityEngine.Color`), the free-call
fallback picks any in-repo type with the same simple name and emits a CALLS edge
(`reason: global-name-fallback`, confidence 0.5). Namespace visibility is not checked. C# has no
`isGlobalNameFallbackPlausible` hook (Go, Rust, Dart, Swift, Ruby and JS have one).

## Repro (gitnexus 1.6.12 and `main` @ 50228e1)

`Lib/Color.cs`
```csharp
namespace Vendor.Proto { public sealed class Color { public Color() { } } }
```

`App/Painter.cs` (only `using UnityEngine;`)
```csharp
using UnityEngine;
namespace MyGame {
    public class Painter { public void Run() { var c = new Color(1f, 0.5f, 0f); } }
}
```

`App/Painter2.cs`
```csharp
using Vendor.Proto;
namespace MyGame {
    public class Painter2 { public void Run() { var c = new Color(); } }
}
```

```
gitnexus analyze --index-only .
gitnexus cypher "MATCH (a)-[r:CodeRelation {type:'CALLS'}]->(b) RETURN a.filePath, b.filePath, r.reason"
```

| src | target | reason |
|---|---|---|
| App/Painter.cs | Lib/Color.cs | global-name-fallback ❌ (C# can't bind this) |
| App/Painter2.cs | Lib/Color.cs | import-resolved ✅ |

## Real-world impact

This is common in Unity projects that vendor a protobuf-based plugin (e.g. MediaPipe-style packages
that generate `Rect`, `Color` and so on). On one Unity 6 project (830 `.cs` files), about 30
`new Color(...)` / `new Rect(...)` calls in plain `using UnityEngine;` files were linked to the
vendored protobuf constructors. `impact` on the vendored `Color` then reports unrelated UI scripts
as dependents.

## Expected

No edge when the type's namespace is not visible from the caller. Visible means one of: the caller
is in the same or an enclosing namespace, the file has a `using` for it, there is a project-wide
`global using` or MSBuild `<Using Include>`, or the call is qualified.

## Related (separate, not in this fix)

In a file that has `using TrackerPro;`, an explicitly qualified `new UnityEngine.Rect(0, 0, 1, 1)`
still resolves to `TrackerPro.Rect` (`import-resolved`). The written qualifier `UnityEngine` doesn't
match the candidate's namespace. I can file this separately if useful.

title: fix(csharp): refuse global-name fallback into namespaces the caller cannot see
body:
## What

Adds a C# `isGlobalNameFallbackPlausible` hook (`languages/csharp/name-fallback-visibility.ts`). A
bare-name guess to a type is refused only when its namespace is provably not visible from the
caller. It is allowed when any of these hold:

- the caller is declared in the type's namespace or a nested one;
- the caller's file has a `using`, `using static` or alias reaching it (relative `using` inside a
  namespace block is matched by suffix);
- the namespace is imported project-wide, via `global using` in any `.cs` file or MSBuild
  `<Using Include>` in a `.csproj` / `Directory.Build.props` / `Directory.Build.targets`;
- the namespace is under `System` or `Microsoft` (SDK `ImplicitUsings`);
- the call is qualified, the candidate has no recorded namespace, or the workspace scan was
  truncated or unavailable. In these cases the hook fails open, per the hook contract
  ("only answer false when the call is impossible").

To know about `global using`, the existing C# workspace scan (`scanCSharpProject`, which already
reads every `.cs` file for namespaces) now also collects `global using` targets through the line
scanner, and reads MSBuild `<Using Include>` items. They are exposed as
`CSharpNamespaceEvidence.globalUsings`. An unreadable project file marks the scan truncated, so it
fails open.

## Why

title: fix(resolution): carry a nested container through receiver index steps (JAVA-03)
body:
## Summary

JAVA-03. `repos[0][0].save()` on a `User[][]` parameter or local emitted no `CALLS` edge. The receiver fold now lets an index step whose element is still a container hand that container on to the next index step, so the call reaches `User.save`.

## Motivation / context

Listed as a gap in `docs/languages/java-ingestion-gaps.md` ("Gap on both builds"). A single `User[]` already resolved (JAVA-01), and so did `grid()[0][0].save()` with a `User[][]` producer. Only a **variable** base with two or more index steps failed. That covered parameters, locals, trailing-dimension declarations (`User[] users[]`) and `User[][][]`.

Root cause: `foldReceiverChainState` (`scope-resolution/passes/compound-receiver.ts`). Each `index` step peels one level through `elementTypeOf` and then requires the element to name a class. `User[]` names none, so the fold returned `undefined` before the second step could peel it. A call-result base takes `elementAfterTrailingIndexSteps` in `receiver-bound-calls.ts`, which peels every trailing index step, which is why the producer form worked.

**In scope**

When an index step's element names no class but the provider's `elementTypeOf(element, { kind: 'index' })` still answers (it is itself a container), the step carries `{ def: undefined, declaredType: element }`. title: fix(eval): classify preflight SandboxError failure causes accurately (#4046)
body:
## Summary

Disentangle the compound preflight failure check in `_probe_servers()` so that each condition (session errors, tool registration mismatches, patch persistence/content errors, and output validations) emits a specific, accurate `SandboxError`.

## Motivation / context

Fixes #4046.

In `eval/workflow_bench/proposal_evaluation.py`, `_probe_servers()` grouped all six preflight validation checks into a single compound `if` block:
```python
if (
    not result["ok"]
    or not required <= names <= permitted
    or len(outputs) != len(tools)
    or not patch.is_file()
    or patch.read_bytes() != b"offline probe"
    or (augmented and "benchmark-target" not in str(outputs.get("toolu_mock_1", {}).get("content")))
):
    arm = "with GitNexus" if augmented else "without GitNexus"
    raise SandboxError(
        f"offline CLI preflight {arm} failed: {len(outputs)}/{len(tools)} successful tool results"
    )
```

When all tool executions completed successfully (`len(outputs) == len(tools) == 2`), but a subsequent check failed (e.g. `patch` missing/corrupted, session non-zero exit, or missing target content in `list_repos`), it threw:
`SandboxError: offline CLI preflight with GitNexus failed: 2/2 successful tool results`

This contradictory error obscured the real failure reason and falsely implied tool result count failure.

## Areas touched

- [ ] `gitnexus/` (CLI / core / MCP server)
- [ ] `gitnexus-web/` (Vite / React UI)
- [ ] `.github/` (workflows, actions)
- [x] `eval/` or other tooling
- [ ] Docs / agent config only (`AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `.cursor/`, `llms.txt`, etc.)

## Scope & constraints

**In scope**

- Classify preflight failure conditions into distinct checks with specific diagnostic messages:
  - Session execution failure (`not result["ok"]`), reporting exit code and stderr/diagnostics when available.
  - Missing required tools (`required - names`).
  - Declared unpermitted tools (`names - permitted`).
  - Incomplete tool execution (`len(outputs) != len(tools)`).
  - Missing `change.patch` file (`not patch.is_file()`).
  - Patch content mismatch (`patch.read_bytes() != b"offline probe"`).
  - Target repository missing in `list_repos` tool output.
- Unit tests covering each failure branch and verifying that successful 2/2 tool runs do not emit the contradictory message when subsequent validation fails.

**Explicitly out of scope / not done here**

- Changes to evaluation runner session logic or Claude CLI sandbox invocation behavior.

## Implementation notes

The check for `len(outputs) != len(tools)` is retained for actual tool count mismatches so existing expected diagnostic patterns remain consistent when a tool genuinely fails to execute.

title: fix(routes): fold Express route paths written through module constants
body:
## Summary

Express routes whose path is written through a module constant produced no `Route` node and no provider contract. Only a string literal, or an array of literals, was read as a path, so every shape below was dropped without a trace:

```ts
const API = '/api/v1';
const ROUTES = { HEALTH: '/api/health' } as const;

app.get(ROUTES.HEALTH, health);   // dropped
app.get(`${API}/users`, list);    // dropped
app.post(API + '/users', create); // dropped
app.get('/api/literal', list);    // only this one was found
```

The consumer side already folds these exact shapes with `resolveJsPathExpression` in `js-const-resolver.ts`, and Spring, Kotlin and Python providers fold constants too.

## What changed

`framework-route-facts.ts` now tries a constant fold when a path argument isn't a literal. That covers route calls, builders (`router.route(...)`), mounts (`app.use(PREFIX, router)`), and a path forwarded through one helper call. The fold is the same consumer-side `resolveJsPathExpression`, so a provider and its caller read a constant the same way.

The fold only runs when all of the following hold:

- **Every identifier** in the expression resolves, at the use site, to a top-level `const` of the same file. A shadowing local or parameter, a `let` or `var`, an import, a subscript or any call leaves the path unknown. That is today's behavior: no route.
- **Every referenced const folds on its own** to a string. A const bound to a non-string leaves the path unknown instead of producing a `${…}` placeholder. A string const whose value contains `${` keeps its text, exactly as the same literal would.
- **Object tables haven't escaped.** A table (a const bound to an object literal) is trusted only while every reference to it in the file reads a string leaf (`T.A`, `T.N.A`) and none writes one. It is untrusted if it is aliased, passed to a call, put in a shorthand property, read by subscript, read as a sub-table, or exported in any form (`export const`, `export { T }`, `export default T`, `module.exports`). `as const` is only a type, so an importer could write an exported table before routes register. String consts are immutable and fold whether exported or not. `typeof T` in a type position is not an escape.

**Cost:** the top-level const scan is cheap and runs first. The whole-file escape scan and the module facts are built at most once per file, and only for a path whose identifiers are all module consts. Files whose paths are literals, or that call helpers with locals, pay nothing extra.

## Verification

```sh
cd gitnexus
npx vitest run test/unit/framework-route-provenance.test.ts test/unit/framework-route-paths.test.ts test/unit/group/http-route-extractor.test.ts test/unit/express-route-provenance-pipeline.test.ts test/unit/route-lexical-bindings.test.ts test/unit/cross-file-routes.test.ts
npx tsc --noEmit
```

- **Positive tests:** identifier, table member, nested member, `+`, template, a const built from a const, builders, mounts, one helper hop, leaf reads in other calls, `typeof` in types, and a string const containing `${`.
- **Negative tests:** 24 cases covering shadowing, mutability, imports, calls and subscripts, every way a table can escape (including all four export forms), and a non-string const in a template.
- **Mutation checks:** I removed each guard in turn, and each removal fails its own tests. Dropping the identifier guard fails 6 tests. Dropping the escape scan fails 6. Dropping the exported-table seed fails the `export const` case. Dropping the per-reference fold fails the non-string case. Restoring the old `${` text filter fails the literal-parity case.
- **End to end:** I built the CLI and ran `analyze --index-only`, then `MATCH (r:Route) …`, on the snippet above plus a function-local `const API = '/shadowed'` and an exported table. `main` gives 1 route. This branch gives 4, and the shadowed and exported-table routes are correctly absent.

## Review rounds

- **Round 1:** the bot found that a table written through an alias was still folded. I fixed it in 83df11f8 by replacing write tracking with the escape rule above.
- **Round 2:** the bot found that exported tables were still folded, and that the `${` text filter dropped legitimate values. I fixed both in ec4c72b5.

## Out of scope

- **Constants imported from another file** (`import { ROUTES } from './routes'`) are still unknown. Route facts are extracted per file in the worker. Folding an import needs the repo-wide constant map at resolve time, and the exporting file's escapes would also need checking. I'm happy to do that as a follow-up if this approach looks right.
- **Table members whose value is an expression** (`{ USERS: \`${BASE}/users\` }`) don't fold. This matches the consumer side, where `flattenObjectLiteral` keeps literal members only.

## Risk

Low. The change only adds routes where the path was previously `null`, and every unresolvable or untrusted case falls back to `null`.

title: fix(rust): resolve calls written inside macro arguments
body:
## Summary

A Rust call written inside a macro's arguments (`println!("{}", helper())`, `vec![make()]`, `assert!(ready())`) produced no `CALLS` edge. This parses those arguments as Rust expressions and sends the calls through the normal capture path.

Fixes #1388

## Motivation / context

tree-sitter-rust leaves the inside of a macro invocation as a flat `token_tree`, so there is no `call_expression` for the scope query to match. In the repository from #1388 ([identity](https://gitlab.gnome.org/YaLTeR/identity) at `72150680`), `handle_local_options` calls `gettext_f` inside `g_printerr!(…)`:

| `impact` on that repo | `main` (`50228e11a`) | this branch |
| --- | --- | --- |
| upstream of `freplace`, d=2 | `resolution` | `resolution`, `handle_local_options` |
| downstream of `handle_local_options` | nothing (one name-only call omitted) | `gettext_f`, then `freplace` |

`DisplayMode::from_str`, the other callee named in the issue, is already in the graph as a name-only (`global-name-fallback`) edge, so `impact` still omits it by default. This PR doesn't change that.

It also unblocks `rename`: on `main`, renaming a function that is called inside a macro is rejected with `incomplete_semantics` / `Uncovered occurrence`. With these references the rename plans and applies.

## Areas touched

- [x] `gitnexus/` (CLI / core / MCP server)
- [x] Docs / agent config only (one row in `docs/languages/rust-ingestion-gaps.md`)

## Scope & constraints

**In scope**

- Free, path, method and struct-literal calls in `( … )` and `[ … ]` macro arguments, including nested macros (bounded at 8 levels).
- Third-party macros as well as `std` ones. An allowlist would not cover the reported `g_printerr!`.

**Explicitly out of scope / not done here** (each errs toward a missing edge)

- Brace invocations (`items! { … }`), which usually hold items or a DSL.
- Argument lists with any syntax error, e.g. `log::info!(target: "net", …)` or `tracing`'s `?field` sigils.
- `stringify!`, `cfg!`, `quote!` / `parse_quote!` family: arguments are not evaluated.
- `matches!` / `assert_matches!`: only the first argument is read, so a call in a guard is not captured.
- A call that depends on a name bound inside the arguments (`|row| row.save()`), since no scope is created for it.
- Field reads/writes inside macros, macro expansion, and CFG/PDG call sites (comment in `rust-harvest.ts` updated).

A custom macro whose argument is type or pattern syntax that happens to parse as a call (`my_macro!(Wrapper(u32))`) will be read as a call. `Variant(_)` and `Variant(..)` are filtered; other spellings are not.

## Implementation notes

- New `languages/rust/macro-argument-calls.ts`; `captures.ts` calls it for each `macro_invocation` and reuses the existing arity and receiver-chain code. Nothing changes outside the Rust provider.
- Only an error-free parse counts. Arguments with no nested delimiter, such as `("{}", total)`, are not re-parsed.
- Capture ranges are shifted back to file coordinates; tests compare them against the source text, including across lines and after non-ASCII characters.

## Measured effect

Each repo was analyzed three times per side with `--force --no-parse-cache`, swapping only `captures.js`.

| Repo | distinct `CALLS` pairs | added | removed | median `analyze` |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| identity `72150680` | 139 → 144 | 5 | 0 | 8.50 s → 8.63 s |
| ripgrep `3e85c6c` | 2246 → 2585 | 339 | 0 | 17.35 s → 16.95 s |
| just `62784c2` | 1708 → 1817 | 109 | 0 | 15.66 s → 15.24 s |

**Precision.** An automated qualifier check plus manual sampling (not an exhaustive review) found at least 21 wrong edges among the 453 added. They come from existing resolver behaviour that now sees more call sites:

- an external type's method bound to a same-named local one (`File::open` → `MmapChoice.open`, `Seq::infinite()` and `seq.len()` → the test wrapper `TSeq`, `Hir::look` → a test helper `look`);
- a path call bound by its last segment to a nearby item (`fn or()` calling `List::or()` becomes a self-loop; `Comparison::new` → `Test.new`);
- `recipe.doc()` resolved to the field `Justfile.doc`.

I checked each pattern on `main` with the call written outside a macro (on these repos or a reduced fixture), and it happens there too. I left the resolver alone to keep this PR to extraction; happy to file them separately.

## Testing & verification

Local run: macOS arm64, Node 22.23.1.

- [x] `npx tsc --noEmit`, `npm run typecheck:tests`, `.husky/pre-commit`, Prettier; ESLint reports 0 errors.
- [x] `npx vitest run test/unit` (1196 files): 27,867 passed, 58 skipped, 15 failed. 11 of those also fail on a clean `main` checkout (`analyzer-identity`, `embedding-recovery`, `fts-availability-resolve`, `vendored-extension-path`, `test-completeness`, `scenario-map/*`); the other 4 (three timeouts, plus one assertion following a timeout in the same file) pass when rerun without file parallelism.
- [x] Integration, resolvers + `rust-*` + Rust rename and rename matrix + PDG + incremental + parse-cache (197 files): 5,895 passed, 4 skipped, 1 timeout. `parse-cache-identity-package` also exceeds its 240 s limit on `main` here; on this branch it passes (292 s) with the limit raised locally.
- [x] Integration, 23 further files picked mainly for mentioning Rust: 586 passed, 2 skipped, 2 failed on a subprocess timeout (`skills-e2e`, C++), which pass on rerun.
- [ ] The remaining integration files were not run to completion locally; leaving those to CI.
- [x] `bench/scope-capture --check` (after the rebaseline below), `bench/receiver-resolution --check`, `bench/rust-cargo-targets --check`.
- [x] GitNexus self-check: upstream `impact` on `emitRustScopeCaptures` is LOW (reported as a lower bound, 2 direct callers). `detect_changes` maps source symbols to the two Rust capture files only; it reports partial because comment-only and test files have no mapped symbols.

New coverage: exact capture positions and skipped spellings (unit), exact `CALLS` edges including negatives (pipeline), and a rename preview/apply fixture.

## Risk & rollout

- Rust graphs gain edges, so `impact`, processes and communities can change after re-indexing. No schema or ID change.
- Parser cache identity is derived from the artifacts, so existing caches invalidate on their own. Checked a cold then warm run on identity: 13 files reused, identical `CALLS` pairs.
- Golden capture snapshot and `bench/scope-capture` Rust fingerprint are rebaselined: +4 capture groups, all from two `rust-for-call-expr` files containing `vec![T { name: "..".into() }]`.
- Rollback: revert and re-index.
