title: feat(cli): add --stale-policy to the index-reading tool commands
body:
## Summary

Adds `--stale-policy warn|ignore|error` to the index-reading tool commands (`query`, `context`, `impact`, `trace`, `cypher`, `detect-changes`, `check`), so scripts and CI can choose what a stale index means: keep the warning (default, unchanged), drop it, or fail.

Closes #3127

## Motivation / context

#3127 asks for a CLI-level switch for stale-index handling. An interactive user wants the warning, while an automated workflow may want it gone or wants the run to fail. The signal already exists: hot read tools carry a `staleness` field (#2655) that names the index ref it describes (#3291). This PR only decides what the CLI does with that field. It never re-indexes.

## Areas touched

- [x] `gitnexus/` (CLI / core / MCP server)
- [ ] `gitnexus-web/` (Vite / React UI)
- [ ] `.github/` (workflows, actions)
- [ ] `eval/` or other tooling
- [ ] Docs / agent config only (`AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `.cursor/`, `llms.txt`, etc.)

## Scope & constraints

**In scope**

- `--stale-policy <policy>` on the seven commands above, validated with Commander `.choices()` (default `warn`).
- `warn`: output byte-for-byte unchanged. The policy code returns the same object, and nothing extra is spawned.
- `ignore`: on a stale payload (`behind` / `diverged`), drop `staleness.hint` but keep `status`, `commitsBehind` and the ref fields (`branch`, `lastCommit`, `indexedAt`, `measuredAgainst`).
- `error`: print the result unchanged, then write one line to stderr (`Index is 1 commit(s) behind HEAD`, or `Index is not at HEAD (diverged)`) and set exit code 1. This matches how `output()` fails on `error` / `partial` payloads.
- `unknown` freshness (e.g. a `--skip-git` index, or a git probe that failed) and `current` pass under every policy (fail-open).
- en and zh-CN strings for the help text and the error. One README line.

**Explicitly out of scope / not done here**

- No re-indexing, and no index, pipeline or analyze changes.
- MCP tools are unchanged: the policy lives in the CLI layer only, and the MCP payloads are the same as before.
- No new dependencies.
- No env var or `.gitnexusrc` setting for the policy. The issue prefers a flag, and one can be added later.

## Implementation notes

- **Where it applies:** in `src/cli/tool.ts`, right after `callTool`, before `--limit` slicing and printing. The stderr reason and the exit code come after printing, so `check`'s prose mode and `detect-changes`' formatter are covered and unchanged.
- **Module split:** the choices live in the dependency-free `src/cli/stale-policy-choices.ts`, so `index.ts` builds the option without loading the logger at startup. The logic lives in `src/cli/stale-policy.ts`, which `tool.ts` loads lazily.
- **Results with no `staleness` field:** the backend attaches `staleness` only to query/context/impact/cypher. `check`, `detect_changes`, `trace` and raw-row `cypher` results never carry it. Under `error` only, for such a result, the CLI resolves the repo the same way `callTool` did (`selectToolRepository(repo, branch, { allowCwdDefault: true })`). It then runs the same `checkStalenessAsync` the backend uses and maps the answer through `stalenessPayload`. Nothing is added to the printed result. If the lookup fails, the probe is `unknown`, or the index records no commit, the command passes (fail-open). `warn` and `ignore` never spawn git. Without this probe, `--stale-policy error` would have silently passed a stale index on three of the seven commands. I confirmed that live before adding it.
- **Plain stderr write:** the reason is written with `process.stderr.write`, not `cliError`. `cliError` also tees a pino record onto stderr, which would turn the one-line reason into two lines.
- **Plurals:** the English message uses `commit(s)` rather than `_one`/`_other` keys, to keep the line exactly as proposed in the issue.

## Testing & verification

- [x] `cd gitnexus && npx tsc --noEmit`: clean
- [x] `cd gitnexus && npm run typecheck:tests`: clean
- [x] `cd gitnexus && npm run test:unit`: 27,869 passed, 58 skipped, 13 failed. The same 13 tests in 9 files fail identically on an untouched `upstream/main` checkout on this machine, so they are environmental (vendored FTS/vector artifacts, the release/review/CI workflow contracts, and the pinned clone engine) and not caused by this change. Every other file passes, including the three CLI test files touched here.
- [x] New `test/unit/cli-stale-policy.test.ts`: each policy on `behind`, `diverged`, `current`, `unknown`, no field and non-object results; the stderr line in en and zh-CN; no stderr or exit code without a failure.
- [x] `test/unit/tool-direct-cli.test.ts`, new cases:
  - `warn` prints exactly what no flag prints;
  - `ignore` keeps status and the ref;
  - `error` prints the result, writes exactly one stderr line and exits 1;
  - `error` passes on `current`/`unknown`;
  - `error` on `impact` diverged;
  - `error` on `check` prose mode, `detect-changes`, `trace` and raw-row `cypher` through the probe;
  - `warn`/`ignore` never probe;
  - a result that states its freshness is not re-probed;
  - the probe is fail-open on unknown, an empty commit and a lookup failure.
- [x] `test/unit/cli-index-help.test.ts`: the zh-CN `query` help column is wider (`--stale-policy <policy>` is the longest flag). There are new cases that all seven commands show the option with its choices, and that `--stale-policy bogus` exits 1 with Commander's "Allowed choices are warn, ignore, error."
- [x] Manual, against the built CLI (`node dist/cli/index.js`) with an isolated `GITNEXUS_HOME`. I indexed a two-function git repo, then made one more commit:
  - `query`: no flag and `warn` print the same JSON, apart from the per-run `timing` numbers, which also differ between two runs with no flag. `ignore` drops only `hint`. `error` exits 1 with `Index is 1 commit(s) behind HEAD`.
  - `check --cycles` (prose and `--json`), `detect-changes`, `trace`, `cypher`, `context` and `impact` with `error` all exit 1 with the same line. `trace … --stale-policy ignore` exits 0.
  - A `--skip-git` index with `error` (`query`, `check`) exits 0. After re-running `analyze`, `error` exits 0.

## Risk & rollout

Low. The default (`warn`) leaves output and exit codes unchanged and spawns nothing new. `ignore` and `error` are opt-in, and `error` fails open whenever freshness cannot be established. No index refresh, migration or MCP change.

## Checklist

title: docs(impact): replace WILL BREAK wording and pin the risk table to the scorer

## Summary

The impact skill labelled depth-1 dependents **WILL BREAK**. This changes the label to **DIRECT — REVIEW FIRST**, says why a graph edge is a lead rather than proof, and adds a test that checks every threshold in the skill's risk table against `scoreImpactRisk`.

Closes #2975

## Motivation / context

#2975 raised two problems: the thresholds in the skill did not match the scorer, and d=1 was presented as certain breakage. The thresholds were brought in line by #3082 (for #3075): the Risk Assessment table now matches `gitnexus-shared/src/impact-risk.ts`. Two things were still open:

- **Wording.** A d=1 edge is a strong reason to review a caller, not proof that it fails. The listing is also a lower bound when the result is `partial` or truncated, or when callers go through dynamic dispatch, DI or cross-language calls. "WILL BREAK" tells an agent the opposite on both counts.
- **Drift.** Nothing tied the table to the scorer, so the next threshold change could silently make the skill wrong again. The issue's acceptance test asks for exactly this check.

## Areas touched

- [x] `gitnexus/` (CLI / core / MCP server): new unit test, plus the shipped skill copy `gitnexus/skills/gitnexus-impact-analysis.md`
- [ ] `gitnexus-web/` (Vite / React UI)

## Scope & constraints

**In scope**

**Explicitly out of scope / not done here**

Changing them changes eval-server output and the prompts behind the eval baselines, so I left that decision to you. Happy to follow up if you want the wording aligned there too.

## Implementation notes

The test reads the Risk Assessment table from the canonical skill file. For every documented threshold, upstream and each downstream axis (direct, processes, modules, total), it builds one case at the bound and one just below it. The expected level comes from the table and the actual level from `scoreImpactRisk`. That gives 26 `it.each` cases, each with a single `toBe`. Inputs are kept realistic: total reach is never below the direct count. Three more tests pin the LOW and UNKNOWN rows and the absence of "WILL BREAK".

Because the expected values are read from the table rather than hard-coded, a threshold edited on only one side fails with a name that says which, for example `upstream 5 direct scores LOW` or `downstream 2 processes (HIGH row) scores HIGH`.

These include the guards `skill-sync.yml` runs.

title: feat(cli): add --stale-policy option
body:
## What

Adds `--stale-policy <warn|ignore|error>` (default `warn`) to `query`, `context`, `impact`, `cypher`, `check`, and `trace`.

- `warn` — unchanged behavior; `.staleness` stays in the result, exit code untouched.
- `ignore` — strips `.staleness` from the result.
- `error` — exits non-zero when the index isn't confirmed `current`, including when `.staleness` is missing entirely (the freshness probe itself failed — see fix below), except on a result that never carries it by design (a raw-array cypher row) or that `output()` already fails for an unrelated, already-explained reason (`partial: true`).

Default is backward compatible — confirmed by diffing output (same index, same command) between this branch and upstream `main` via `git stash`; identical apart from the new field.

Closes #3127.

## `error` also fails on `status: unknown` — and on a missing `.staleness` key entirely

The staleness probe is fail-open by design: a git failure (missing binary, shallow clone, broken worktree) collapses to `status: unknown`, not `isStale: true`. But `--stale-policy error` is opt-in specifically to gate on trustworthy freshness, so treating `unknown` as "fine" would exit 0 on exactly the case it exists to catch. `error` fails on `behind`, `diverged`, and `unknown`; only `current` passes. Reproduced `unknown` for real by moving `.git` out of a live indexed repo mid-test.

A review bot caught a second layer of the same hole: `LocalBackend.attachToolStaleness` attaches nothing at all when the freshness probe's promise rejects, so a result can reach the CLI with no `.staleness` key, not even `status: 'unknown'`. `error` now treats that the same way. Verified by reading the exact code path and reproducing it directly (a mocked rejection resolves to a result with zero `.staleness` key); couldn't trigger it through live CLI usage, since the probe is self-catching for every failure mode reachable that way (moved `.git`, git removed from `PATH` both resolve cleanly to `unknown`, never reject) — locked in with mocked unit tests instead.

## Scope: 6 of 7 candidate commands

`query`/`context`/`impact`/`cypher` already computed `.staleness` via `LocalBackend.withToolStaleness`. `check` and `trace` didn't — both are now wired into the same dispatch wrapper, so the flag has something to act on. This also means **`check`/`trace` results now carry `.staleness` over MCP** (`gitnexus mcp`), verified live against a running MCP stdio server. (Neither has an HTTP route in `serve`'s `api.ts`, so there's no HTTP-path claim here.)

`detect_changes` is deliberately excluded: it already explicitly diffs two commits via `scope`/`base_ref` rather than implicitly trusting the index matches HEAD, so the generic wrapper would give "stale" a second, confusing meaning there. Left as a follow-up, not bolted on.

## Test evidence

- Every test touching `check`/`trace`/`withToolStaleness`/dispatch located and run as a pre-change baseline: 9 files / 547 tests, green.
- One genuine contract break, expected: a named "drift guard" test asserting *only 4 tools* route through the freshness check correctly failed once `check`/`trace` were added; updated to assert the new 6-tool set by name. 5 more `check`-result exact-equality assertions needed the new `.staleness` field added.
- New `warn`/`ignore`/`error` × `current`/`behind`/`diverged`/`unknown`/missing-entirely matrix for all six commands, matching the existing pattern.
- Live CLI verification against a real indexed repo (fresh/stale/unknown, all 6 commands) plus the `git stash` upstream comparison above.
- Final state: 11 files / 608 tests, all green; `tsc` (src + tests), `eslint` (`npm run lint`), `prettier --check` clean; pre-commit hook (lint-staged + typecheck) passed on both commits.

## Known gaps

- `cypher`'s row-to-markdown conversion has an unreachable-looking branch that would return a raw array for a non-object first row, excluded from staleness attachment by design — distinct from the missing-key fix above, which covers object-shaped results. Tried 4 query shapes against the real binding and couldn't reproduce a non-object row; not fixed, flagging only.
- Full `npm test`/`npm run test:unit` stalled 30–40+ min with near-zero CPU progress on the native `lbug-db` project in this sandbox, consistent with open native-deadlock issues (#3898, #3982) rather than something this PR introduced. Verified instead via every test file this change touches, run in isolation — CI's full run is the first real confirmation of the rest of the suite.

## How to verify

```bash
cd gitnexus
npx tsc --noEmit && npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.test.json
cd .. && npm run lint
cd gitnexus
npx vitest run test/unit/calltool-dispatch.test.ts test/unit/trace-bfs.test.ts \
  test/unit/trace-cli.test.ts test/unit/tool-direct-cli.test.ts test/unit/tools.test.ts \
  test/unit/mcp-read-only.test.ts test/unit/mcp-tool-arguments.test.ts \
```

title: fix(swift): type indexed elements of array-sugar receivers (SWIFT-01)
body:
## Summary

SWIFT-01. `repos[0].save()` with `repos: [User]` emitted no `CALLS` edge because the Swift scope resolver had no `elementTypeOf` hook. `swiftElementType` now reads the element out of array sugar, so the call reaches `User.save`.

## Motivation / context

`docs/languages/swift-ingestion-gaps.md` lists it as a measured gap, and the receiver bench records it as the `indexElement` VISIBLE-GAP cell. The walker already builds the `2|repos|i` chain. The fold's index step asks the provider for the element of the written spelling and, with no hook, declined.

## Areas touched

- [x] `gitnexus/` (CLI / core / MCP server)
- [ ] `gitnexus-web/` (Vite / React UI)
- [ ] `.github/` (workflows, actions)
- [x] `eval/` or other tooling: receiver bench baseline + BASELINE.md entry
- [x] Docs: `docs/languages/swift-ingestion-gaps.md`

## Scope & constraints

**In scope**

- Provider-owned only. `swiftElementType` sits in `swift/interpret.ts` next to the existing `stripOptional` / `stripArraySugar` helpers and reuses them. It is wired as `elementTypeOf` in `swift/scope-resolver.ts`. There are no shared-code changes.
- `[User]` yields `User`, including `[User]?` / `[User]!` indexed through `?[` / `![`.
- A dictionary `[K: V]` declines, because it is keyed and yields `V?`. Every other spelling declines too. The `await` and `accessor` routes decline.

**Explicitly out of scope / not done here** (both recorded as new rows in the gap doc, and still asserted as KNOWN GAP rows in the walker spellings test)

- SWIFT-04: `repos: Array<User>`. Parameter capture keeps only `Array`, so no element reaches the hook. Answering `Array<T>` in the hook would be dead code until capture preserves the generic spelling.
- SWIFT-05: `holder.users[0].save()` on a `[User]` field. The fold's field step hands the index step no written spelling, which is a shared-fold change.

## Implementation notes

- The index step carries no argument, so a range subscript (`repos[0..<2]`, an `ArraySlice`) also reads as the element. A member it names must still exist on `User` to resolve, and the doc comment notes this.
- `stripArraySugar` refuses any spelling containing `:`, so `[[String: User]]` also declines. That is conservative and was already the capture layer's rule.

## Testing & verification

Rows in `test/integration/resolvers/receiver-chain-walker-spellings.test.ts` (Swift case). The two former KNOWN GAP rows are updated and six new callers are appended, so existing line numbers are unchanged:

| Caller | Receiver | Expected |
|---|---|---|
| `indexElement` | `[User]` | `User.save` (was KNOWN GAP) |
| `optionalIndexElement` | `[User]?`, `repos?[0]` | `User.save` |
| `forcedIndexElement` | `[User]!`, `repos![0]` | `User.save` |
| `decoyIndexElement` | `[Address]` | `Address.save` |
| `dictionaryValue` | `[String: User]`, `byName["a"]?` | no target, drop recorded |
| `partialIndexElement` | `[[User]]`, one index | no target, drop recorded |
| `genericIndexElement` | `Array<User>` | KNOWN GAP (SWIFT-04) |
| `fieldIndexElement` | `holder.users[0]` | KNOWN GAP (SWIFT-05), reason updated |

- Before the fix, the 4 positive rows failed and the 2 negatives already passed. After it, 21/21 pass.
- `npx vitest run test/integration/resolvers test/unit/scope-resolution`: 10152 passed, 3 skipped.
- `node --import tsx bench/receiver-resolution/measure.mjs --check`: the only drift was `swift.indexElement` VISIBLE-GAP -> RESOLVES. The count arm is identical. Baseline regenerated with `--update-baseline` and a BASELINE.md section added.

title: feat(embeddings): reuse vectors across branches
body:
## Summary
Reuse completed embeddings from compatible sibling branch indexes during analysis, so unchanged code chunks do not need another model inference pass.

## Motivation / context
Resolves the Phase 1 opportunity described in #3631: analyzing several branches of one repository currently repeats embedding work for content already indexed elsewhere. This reduces analysis time and embedding-provider cost while keeping each branch's graph and vector index isolated.

## Areas touched
- [x] `gitnexus/` (CLI / core / MCP server)

## Scope & constraints
**In scope**
- Persist a versioned receipt of the vector/input identity and completed embedding snapshot in branch metadata.
- Discover compatible sibling branch indexes and shared-store checkout slots; read their databases read-only.
- Reuse vectors only when embedding identity, content hash, dimensions, and the complete contiguous chunk group match; embed cache misses normally.
- Defer loading the local embedder until actual misses remain.
- Add unit and integration coverage, including verification that source branch rows remain unchanged.

**Explicitly out of scope / not done here**
- Shared physical vector storage or graph-delta reuse (follow-up Phase 2).
- Cross-repository reuse or reuse across incompatible embedding models/configurations.

## Implementation notes
Cache sources are treated as optional: stale, incomplete, or incompatible receipts become misses. Source graph databases are opened read-only and closed after analysis. The target branch still receives its own vectors, preserving branch-local search behavior. This reduces inference work; it does not reduce per-branch vector disk usage.

title: trace CLI requires positional names even when both endpoint UIDs are supplied
body:
### Area
gitnexus (CLI / core / indexing / MCP server)

### Summary
`gitnexus trace` fails with `missing required argument 'from'` when both endpoints are supplied as UIDs. The CLI parser requires two names even though the trace handler accepts a UID in place of each name.

### Expected behavior
With both exact UIDs, trace should resolve the two symbols and run. If an endpoint has neither a name nor a UID, it should still fail with usage.

### Actual behavior
Commander exits 1 before the trace handler runs. Passing the same UIDs alongside positional names works.

### Steps to reproduce
1. In a temporary Git repo, commit a file named `route.ts` with the following code and run `gitnexus analyze`.


`detect-changes` should report the same edited symbols regardless of how a developer likes to read Git diffs. title: Persist the analyzer identity cache on Windows
body:
### Area

gitnexus (CLI / core / indexing / MCP server)

### Problem or opportunity

I noticed `status` and `analyze` can be made faster on Windows than it already is. From what I can tell, GitNexus fingerprints its own install on every single run, and on Mac/Linux it saves that fingerprint so later runs are quick. On Windows it doesn't save it, because there's no `getuid` to prove the folder is private ([here](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/blob/50228e11/gitnexus/src/core/analyzer-identity.ts#L2046-L2050)). I get that this is on purpose as a security consideration, but it means every run starts from scratch:

| | now | with the cache saved |
|---|---|---|
| `status` | 9.3s | 1.7s |
| `analyze` (nothing changed) | 20.2s | 5.8s |

### Proposed solution

Maybe Windows could save it in `%USERPROFILE%\.gitnexus\analyzer-identity`, but only after making sure the folder is private:

- When creating the folder, lock it with Windows' `icacls` so only the user, SYSTEM and Administrators can access it.
- Each run, check that lock (by account ID, so it works in any language) before using the cache.
- If the folder isn't locked properly, wipe it and start fresh.
- If anything goes wrong, just skip the cache like today.

For Mac/Linux, nothing will change

### Alternatives considered

- PowerShell can check permissions too, but it took ~0.5s per run, while icacls took ~12ms.
- If implementing the stuff above isn't feasible, least that can be done is just document `GITNEXUS_ANALYZER_IDENTITY_CACHE_DIR` in the README. It already works, but people won't know it exists.

### Acceptance criteria

_No response_

### Constraints

- It shouldn't be any less safe than today: if it can't confirm the folder is private, no cache.
- Each cache file is about 8MB and old ones aren't cleaned up, so they could pile up over updates. Happy to add cleanup if that's wanted.

### Contribution

- [x] I am willing to open a PR for this (may need design discussion first).

title: fix(group): migrate thrift extractor to canonical ignore filter
body:
## Summary

Replaces two hardcoded five-entry ignore arrays in the thrift extractor with calls to `createIgnoreFilter`, matching the pattern established by the grpc, graphql, http-route, topic, and include extractors in #1185. This is the last extractor with the hand-rolled list.

## Motivation / context

Resolves `TODO(#1156-followup)` at `thrift-extractor.ts:222` and `:299`. Both glob calls — the `.thrift` IDL discovery in `buildThriftContext` and the source-scan discovery in `extract` — used a hardcoded array:

```typescript
ignore: ['**/node_modules/**', '**/.git/**', '**/vendor/**', '**/dist/**', '**/build/**']
```

This bypassed `createIgnoreFilter` from `src/config/ignore-service.ts`, so patterns added to `DEFAULT_IGNORE_LIST` (e.g. `third_party`, `3rdparty` added in commit a9936a9b) or to `.gitnexusignore`/`.gitignore` silently did not apply during Thrift contract extraction.

## Areas touched

- [x] `gitnexus/` (CLI / core / MCP server)

## Scope & constraints

**In scope**
- Replace both hardcoded ignore arrays with `createIgnoreFilter(repoPath)` calls
- Add import for `createIgnoreFilter` from `../../../config/ignore-service.js`
- Remove both `TODO(#1156-followup)` comment blocks
- Add regression tests for `.gitnexusignore` filtering in both `extract()` and `buildThriftContext()`

**Explicitly out of scope / not done here**
- Changes to ignore-service itself
- Other extractor changes — all other extractors were migrated in #1185

## Implementation notes

The pattern is identical to what `grpc-extractor.ts` does at lines 270 and 464:

```typescript
const ignoreFilter = await createIgnoreFilter(repoPath);
const files = await glob('**/*.thrift', {
  cwd: repoPath,
  ignore: ignoreFilter,
  ...
});
```

`createIgnoreFilter` returns an object with `ignored(p)` and `childrenIgnored(p)` methods, which is the shape `glob`'s `ignore` option accepts. Both `buildThriftContext` and `extract` are already async, so no signature changes needed.

The hardcoded array was a strict subset of `DEFAULT_IGNORE_LIST`, so all previously-ignored paths continue to be ignored. The behavioral change is that additional patterns from the central list and `.gitnexusignore`/`.gitignore` rules now also apply — which is exactly the fix.

## Testing & verification

- [x] `cd gitnexus && npx vitest run test/unit/group/thrift-extractor.test.ts` — 16/16 tests pass (14 existing + 2 new)
- [x] `cd gitnexus && npx tsc --noEmit` — Clean typecheck

- [x] `npx eslint gitnexus/src/core/group/extractors/thrift-extractor.ts gitnexus/test/unit/group/thrift-extractor.test.ts` — 0 errors

**New test cases:**
1. `ThriftExtractor > respects .gitnexusignore > thrift IDL glob skips files matched by .gitnexusignore` — Places a valid `.thrift` under a non-ignored path and another under `mentor_env/`, writes `.gitnexusignore` with `mentor_env/`, verifies only the control file produces contracts.

title: perf(identity): persist the analyzer identity cache on Windows
body:
## Summary

Lets the analyzer identity cache work on Windows by keeping it in a folder that only the current user can open. `gitnexus status` and up-to-date `analyze` runs stop re-hashing the whole install every time.

Closes #4128

## Motivation / context

Right now Windows skips cache. On my machine that was most of the wait:

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `gitnexus status` | ~9.3s | ~1.7s |
| `analyze` (nothing changed) | ~20.2s | ~5.8s |

I tried to keep the same safety idea as Linux/macOS: only use cache if no one else can mess with it.

## Areas touched

- [x] `gitnexus/` (CLI / core / MCP server)
- [ ] `gitnexus-web/` (Vite / React UI)
- [ ] `.github/` (workflows, actions)

- [ ] Docs / agent config only

**In scope**

- Windows only. The cache lives in `~\.gitnexus\analyzer-identity`

title: detect_changes maps hunks onto the post-image, so after a line shift it reports the wrong symbols and never reports a deleted function
body:
### Area

gitnexus (CLI / core / indexing / MCP server)

### Summary

`detect_changes` reads every modified file's hunks in the post-image line space (the `+` side of `@@ -a,b +c,d @@`), but the graph's `startLine`/`endLine` are from the bytes `analyze` read. in the AGENTS.md flow (analyze, edit, then `detect_changes` before commit) the graph holds the **pre**-image. so once an edit adds or removes lines, every later hunk lands on the wrong symbols:

- an edit below inserted lines reports the functions above it and misses the edited one
- a deleted function is never reported. its post-image range is empty, so the hunk anchors on the neighbour

the risk level is computed from those wrong symbols, so the pre-commit gate can say `low` for a change that deleted a function with callers.

### Context

the code already knows the graph can lag the diff, just not for modified files:

- deleted files map with the old-side range: "Its indexed symbols still use the pre-delete file" ([git.ts#L1084-L1086](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/blob/50228e11abc2491e6391943288696671dd62c1d5/gitnexus/src/storage/git.ts#L1084-L1086))
- renames map back to the old path: "The graph may still use the pre-rename path" ([local-backend.ts#L7108-L7109](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/blob/50228e11abc2491e6391943288696671dd62c1d5/gitnexus/src/mcp/local/local-backend.ts#L7108-L7109))
- for every other file the parser takes the `+` range ([git.ts#L1123-L1130](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/blob/50228e11abc2491e6391943288696671dd62c1d5/gitnexus/src/storage/git.ts#L1123-L1130)), and those ranges get overlapped with the indexed lines ([local-backend.ts#L7312](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/blob/50228e11abc2491e6391943288696671dd62c1d5/gitnexus/src/mcp/local/local-backend.ts#L7312))

`meta.fileHashes` already records the SHA-256 of the exact bytes `analyze` indexed per file, so which image the graph holds is checkable.

### Minimal case

`util.ts`, committed and analyzed:

```ts
export function first() { return 0; }
export function helper() { return 1; }
export function second() { return 2; }
export function third() { return helper(3); }
export function fourth() { return 4; }
```

### Expected behavior

| edit (no re-analyze) | diff | expected |
|---|---|---|
| prepend 3 comment lines, change `helper(3)` to `helper(33)` | `@@ -0,0 +1,3 @@`, `@@ -4 +7 @@` | `third` |
| delete the `helper` line | `@@ -2 +1,0 @@` | `helper` |
| delete the `fourth` line | `@@ -5 +4,0 @@` | `fourth` |

### Actual behavior

on main `50228e11`:

| edit | reported |
|---|---|
| prepend + edit `third` | `first`, `helper`, `second` (medium) |
| delete `helper` | `first` (low) |
| delete `fourth` | `third` |

same result for `--scope staged` and for a path with a space and non-ASCII characters. on windows with `core.autocrlf=true` it's the same, since the hunks come from the same `+` side.

### Steps to reproduce

```sh
# GNX = node <main checkout>/gitnexus/dist/cli/index.js
mkdir dc && cd dc && git init -q
# write util.ts as above
git add -A && git commit -qm init
$GNX analyze --index-only
printf '// a\n// b\n// c\n' | cat - util.ts > t && mv t util.ts
sed -i 's/helper(3)/helper(33)/' util.ts
$GNX detect-changes --scope unstaged
```

### Environment

- OS: Windows 11 x64 (the logic is platform-independent)
- Node: 26.3.0
- Commit / version: main `50228e11`, dist build, `@ladybugdb/core` 0.22.0

### Logs / screenshots

i have a fix: pick the image per file whose bytes hash to `fileHashes[path]`, using the `-` range when it's the pre-image (`--full-index` blob ids plus `git cat-file --batch --filters`, so autocrlf and smudge filters match), and mark the result `partial` when neither image matches. legacy indexes without `fileHashes` keep today's behaviour. PR coming with an integration test (8 of 10 cases fail on main).

title: fix(doctor): bound the extension probe's mmap reservations (#4074)
body:
Closes #4074

## Summary

`gitnexus doctor` reported `Full-text search: unavailable` / `VECTOR extension: unavailable` on constrained hosts (e.g. Android proot, containers with restricted address space) because the extension probe's throwaway database reserved the platform's full mmap address space (~8 TiB on 64-bit) before `LOAD EXTENSION` ever ran.

## Root cause

`probeExtensionLoad()` in `gitnexus/src/core/lbug/native-check.ts` constructed:

```ts
new lbug.Database(':memory:')
```

With defaults, `@ladybugdb/core` interprets `maxDBSize = 0` as "reserve the full mmap address space". Constrained kernels reject that reservation (`Mmap for size 8796093022208 failed`), so the probe threw before loading the extension — even though the extension itself was perfectly loadable.

## Fix

Construct the probe database with the same bounds `analyze`/`query` use:

- `bufferPoolSize` = 64 MiB — the `BUFFER_POOL_FLOOR` constant already used by `lbug-config.ts` for small/capped allocations.
- `maxDBSize` = 1 GiB — generous headroom for a throwaway probe that loads `fts`/`vector` and touches no real data.

The constants stay local to `native-check.ts`: the module must remain free of heavier imports so `doctor` can probe the native module in isolation.

## Changes

- `src/core/lbug/native-check.ts`: pass bounded `bufferPoolSize`/`maxDBSize` to the probe `Database`.
- `test/unit/native-check-probe.test.ts`: record constructor args on the harness mock and assert the probe passes bounded reservations (regression coverage against a future default-args construction).

## Test plan

- [x] `npx vitest run test/unit/native-check-probe.test.ts` — pass
- [x] `node dist/cli/index.js doctor` — FTS + VECTOR probes report `available` against the real native module
- [x] `npx tsc --noEmit` — clean
- [x] `npx eslint` / `npx prettier --check` on touched files — clean
- [x] Full unit suite — green

## Notes

`analyze`/`query` DB opens already pass a bounded `maxDBSize`, so no other call site is affected.

title: fix(cli): let trace run on --from-uid/--to-uid without positional names (#4124)
body:
Closes #4124

## Summary

`gitnexus trace --from-uid <uid> --to-uid <uid>` failed at argument parsing with `missing required argument 'from'`, even though the trace handler accepts UIDs in place of names. Positional names were required by commander before the handler ever ran.

## Root cause

`src/cli/index.ts` registered the command as `trace <from> <to>` — two mandatory positionals — while `traceCommand` in `src/cli/tool.ts` already treats `from`/`fromUid` and `to`/`toUid` as interchangeable endpoint inputs and validates that at least one of each is present.

## Fix

Register the positionals as optional — `trace [from] [to]` — so commander hands control to `traceCommand`, which owns endpoint validation:

- UID-only invocations now reach the backend and resolve.
- Positional invocations are unchanged.
- A genuinely missing endpoint (neither name nor UID) still exits 1 with the handler's existing usage error — no validation moved, just un-shadowed.

## Changes

- `src/cli/index.ts`: `trace <from> <to>` → `trace [from] [to]`; help/description strings updated to match.
- `src/cli/i18n/en.ts`, `src/cli/i18n/zh-CN.ts`: localized usage/description strings updated.
- `test/unit/trace-cli.test.ts`: new dispatcher-level coverage — UID-only invocation reaches the trace backend, and a missing endpoint exits 1 through the real CLI path.

## Test plan

title: fix(ingestion): preserve enclosing scope in C++ and Ruby member node IDs
body:
## Summary

Preserve full enclosing scope (namespaces, modules, outer classes, and normalized compact paths) in C++ and Ruby `Method`, `Constructor`, and `Property` node IDs instead of collapsing to the unqualified tail class name.

Fixes #2874

## Motivation / context

Although `cppClassConfig` and `rubyClassConfig` set `qualifiedNodeId: true` so containers and `HAS_METHOD` / `HAS_PROPERTY` edges already use qualified IDs (such as `Struct:...:N.Box~bool` and `Class:...:N.Box`), member node ID construction in `parse-worker.ts` still used `enclosingClassInfo.className` (the simple tail name), `callableOwnQualifiedName` / `enclosingFunctionIdAt` omitted `getQualifiedOwnerName` while sharing the same `WeakMap` cache, C++ out-of-line methods (`void N::Box::save() {}`) had no detached owner resolver, and C++ anonymous namespaces encoded shifting byte offsets (`@anon${node.startIndex}`). As a result, `N::Box<bool>::save` and `::Box<bool>::save` in one translation unit collapsed onto the same node ID.

## Areas touched

- [x] `gitnexus/` (CLI / core / MCP server)
- [ ] `gitnexus-web/` (Vite / React UI)
- [ ] `.github/` (workflows, actions)
- [ ] `eval/` or other tooling
- [ ] Docs / agent config only (`AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `.cursor/`, `llms.txt`, etc.)

## Scope & constraints

**In scope**

- Populate `EnclosingClassInfo.qualifiedClassName` (preserving template specializations such as `N.Box<bool>` and normalizing Ruby `class N::Box` to `N.Box`) and prefer `qualifiedClassName ?? className` across definition, routed-property (`attr_accessor`), and caller-ID resolution sites in `parse-worker.ts`.
- Unify `getQualifiedOwnerNameForProvider(provider)` inside `cachedFindEnclosingClassInfo` so caller and definition lookups cannot populate inconsistent cache entries.
- Add `resolveCppDetachedOwnerName` on `cppProvider` (combining enclosing namespaces, honoring leading `::` global anchoring, and avoiding duplicate `namespace N { void N::Box::save() {} }` prefixes) and match qualified owner paths in `findClassNodeByQualifiedName`.
- Replace C++ anonymous-namespace byte offsets (`@anon${node.startIndex}`) with deterministic per-parent sibling ordinals (`@anon1`, `@anon2`, ...) via `cppAnonymousNamespaceSegment`.
- Register `cpp.member-scope-identity` and `ruby.member-scope-identity` in `ANALYSIS_FEATURES`.
- Add integration tests in `gitnexus/test/integration/cpp-ruby-member-scope-id.test.ts`, add feature coverage in `gitnexus/test/unit/analysis-features.test.ts`, and update existing C++ integration test assertions that previously encoded unnamespaced `Method:` IDs.

- Non-C++/Ruby languages without `qualifiedNodeId: true` keep their existing member ID behavior unchanged.

## Implementation notes

title: feat(thrift): add support for annotation-based client detection
body:
## Summary

Add detection for `@ThriftClient` and `@RpcClient` annotated fields in Java thrift consumers. Extracts service names from interface naming patterns like `ISimpleServiceClient`, `OrderServiceClient`, and similar conventions, then binds them to the existing variable resolution flow for method call detection.

## Motivation / context

Fixes #2629. GitNexus's Java thrift scanner only recognized standard type-naming patterns (`*Service`, `*Management`, `*Iface`, `*Client` via the type itself). This missed annotation-based thrift client declarations commonly used in Spring-based internal frameworks:

```java
@XxxThriftClient(remote = "some-service-name")
private ISimpleClient simpleClient;

public void callService() {
  simpleClient.callSomeMethod(); // Was never detected as thrift consumer
}
```

Method calls on such fields resulted in empty `cross: []` in group impact analysis even when provider and consumer repos were both indexed, because the scanner never emitted a detection for the annotated field declaration.

## Areas touched

- [x] `gitnexus/` (thrift extractor patterns)

## Scope & constraints

**In scope**
- Add `ANNOTATED_CLIENT_PATTERNS` tree-sitter query for `@ThriftClient` / `@RpcClient` annotations
- Add `serviceFromAnnotatedClient()` helper to extract service name from client interface types
- Integrate annotated bindings into existing variable resolution flow
- Add 7 unit tests for service name extraction patterns

**Explicitly out of scope / not done here**
- Changes to IDL parsing
- Changes to provider detection
- Support for other annotation types (focus on ThriftClient/RpcClient only)
- Conformance tests (would require Java fixtures; unit tests cover the core logic)

## Implementation notes

**Pattern matching rules (from most specific to least):**
1. `I{Service}Client` → `{Service}` (e.g., `ISimpleServiceClient` → `SimpleService`)
2. `{Service}ServiceClient` → `{Service}Service` (e.g., `UserServiceServiceClient` → `UserServiceService`)
3. `{Service}Client` → `{Service}` (e.g., `OrderClient` → `Order`)

**Integration with existing scanner:**
- New `ANNOTATED_CLIENT_PATTERNS` queries capture field declarations with `@marker_annotation` or `@annotation` nodes
- Filter annotations by name: only process if annotation contains "ThriftClient" or "RpcClient"
- Extract service name via `serviceFromAnnotatedClient()` helper
- Add binding to `bindings: VariableBinding[]` array with `usesGeneratedServiceMember: true`
- Existing `CALL_PATTERNS` scan already detects method calls on these variables and emits consumer detections

**Confidence scores:**
- Uses weak-consumer path: `confidenceWithIdl: 0.75`, `confidenceWithoutIdl: 0.45`
- Same as standard type-based detection, since the annotation + Client suffix provides equivalent signal

## Testing & verification

- [x] `npx vitest run test/unit/group/thrift-extractor.test.ts` — 21/21 tests pass (14 existing + 7 new)
- [x] `npx tsc --noEmit` — Clean typecheck
- [x] `npx prettier --check` — Formatted
- [x] `npx eslint` — 0 errors

**New test cases:**
1. `ISimpleServiceClient` with `@SimpleThriftClient` → `SimpleService`
2. `OrderServiceClient` with `@OrderRpcClient` → `OrderService`
3. `IUserClient` with `@UserThriftClient` → `User`
4. Qualified type names (`com.example.service.IOrderServiceClient`)
5. Non-thrift annotations (`@Autowired`) return null
6. Non-Client type patterns return null
7. `UserServiceServiceClient` → `UserServiceService` (edge case)

## Risk & rollout

Risk is **LOW**: This is an additive feature that runs in parallel with existing type-based detection. The weak-consumer confidence path already exists and is well-tested. No changes to IDL parsing, provider detection, or cross-repo matching logic.

The annotation filter (`contains('ThriftClient')` or `contains('RpcClient')`) is intentionally conservative to avoid false positives from generic Spring annotations.

title: refactor(web): replace scattered console.log with a dev-only debug logger (#437)
body:
Closes #437

## What changed

- **New `gitnexus-web/src/lib/debug.ts`**: `debugLog(category, ...args)` logs through `console.debug` with a `[gitnexus:<category>]` prefix, only when `import.meta.env.DEV` is true. Categories: `llm`, `agent`, `stream`, `impact`.
- **Replaced all seven DEV-guarded `console.log` calls** in the web app (the issue listed three; the same pattern also appeared in `tools.ts` and `useAppState.tsx`):
  - `core/llm/agent.ts`: OpenRouter config, system prompt, per-event stream trace, stream completion
  - `core/llm/tools.ts`: impact target resolution, d=1 query
  - `hooks/useAppState.tsx`: agent initialized
- Emoji removed from the messages.
- The per-event stream trace keeps its `import.meta.env.DEV` guard, so production builds don't do the per-event field reads used to build the message.

## Why

The logging was spread across three files with ad-hoc formatting and emoji. One helper gives a single place to change the behavior, and a consistent prefix to filter on in devtools.

On the bundle-size point in the issue: Vite already replaced `import.meta.env.DEV` statically, so the old blocks weren't actually shipping. The production build check below confirms this is still the case after the change.

## Behavior note

The helper uses `console.debug` rather than `console.log`, so in Chromium devtools these messages show under the **Verbose** level. That suits a debug logger, but it is a visible change for anyone used to seeing them by default. Switching to `console.log` is a one-word change if reviewers prefer it.

## How to verify

```sh
cd gitnexus-web
npx vitest run                          # 48 files / 535 tests pass (includes new src/lib/debug.test.ts)
npx tsc -b --noEmit                     # clean
npx vite build && grep -l "gitnexus:stream\|system prompt:\|yielding done\|d=1 query" dist/assets/*.js | wc -l   # 0
```

Dev-only logging; no production behavior change. Revert the single commit to roll back.

title: fix(detect-changes): map hunks with the side of the diff the index holds
body:
## Summary `detect_changes` now maps each modified file's hunks with the side of the diff the index actually holds. After the documented analyze → edit → `detect_changes` flow that is the pre-image, so edits below inserted or removed lines and deleted functions are reported on the right symbols. Closes #4136. ## Motivation / context The parser always took the `+` side of `@@ -a,b +c,d @@`, while the graph's `startLine`/`endLine` come from the bytes `analyze` read. Deleted files and renames already account for the graph lagging the diff; modified files did not. The pre-commit gate could rank a change `low` because it attached the hunks to the wrong functions. ## Areas touched - [x] `gitnexus/` (CLI / core / MCP server) ## Scope & constraints **In scope** - `parseDiffWithPreImage` (in `storage/git.ts`): the existing parse, plus each file's old-side hunks and the blob ids from the `index` header. `parseDiffHunks` / `parseDiffHunksResult` keep their exact output. - `storage/indexed-image.ts`: per modified file, compare `meta.fileHashes` against a hash of the diff's new side (the working tree, or the index blob for `--scope staged`) and of its old side (`git cat-file --filters --path=

`, so CRLF/smudge bytes match what `analyze` read). Old-side ranges are used only when the recorded hash matches the old side and not the new one. - `coalesceHunks`: a pure insertion on the old side is the empty range `{g+1, g}` ("between old lines g and g+1"). It overlaps exactly the symbols spanning the gap, and merging never widens it into a neighbouring one-line symbol. **Explicitly out of scope / not done here** - Indexes whose hashes match neither side, or that have no `fileHashes`: unchanged (post-image mapping, as today). - The call-compatibility check still receives the post-image hunks it was written for. - `git cat-file --batch --filters` was not used: on git 2.39 its header reports the unfiltered size, so the stream cannot be framed. Each blob is one `cat-file` call, and only for files whose working copy does not match the index. ## Testing & verification - `test/integration/detect-changes-pre-image.test.ts` (real engine + real git, in the `lbug-db` project): the three cases from #4136, `--scope staged`, and an insertion between two symbols. Fails on `main`: - prepend + edit `third`: `expected [ 'first', 'helper', 'second' ] to deeply equal [ 'third' ]` - delete `helper`: `expected [ 'first' ] to deeply equal [ 'helper' ]` - delete `fourth`: `expected [ 'third' ] to deeply equal [ 'fourth' ]` Passes with this change. - `test/unit/indexed-image.test.ts`: old side picked for a pre-image index; new side kept for a post-image index, an unknown image, or no hash; staged scope compares the index blob; `core.autocrlf=true`. - `test/unit/parse-diff-hunks.test.ts`: old-side ranges and blob ids, and `files` identical to `parseDiffHunks`. - `test/unit/detect-changes-hunk-scale.test.ts`: brute-force check that `coalesceHunks` + `hunksOverlapRange` answer every `[s, e]` exactly like the raw ranges when empty gaps are mixed in. - End to end with the built CLI and the exact steps from the issue (`analyze --index-only`, edit, `detect-changes --scope unstaged`): reports `third`, `helper`, `fourth`. - `npx tsc --noEmit` clean; Prettier and ESLint clean on the touched files (no new warnings). - Full `test/unit` on macOS arm64: the remaining failures also fail on `main` on this machine or depend on the environment (`pnpm` probing in `resolve-invocation`, a 30s timeout in `r-replacement-scaling`). None touch `detect_changes`. ## Risk & rollout - Adds one `gitnexus.json` read per `detect_changes` call, plus one `git cat-file` per modified file whose working copy differs from the indexed bytes. - No index refresh needed. Any failure along the new path falls back to today's post-image mapping. ## Checklist - [x] PR body meets repo minimum length - [x] No secrets, tokens, or machine-specific paths committed --- Built with Claude Code; I reviewed and verified every step above. --- ### 📝 Summary by GitNexus ## Summary *This appears to be a TypeScript change centered on Git diff parsing and local change detection, with broad graph reach despite low file-level risk.* **🔴 CRITICAL blast radius. A TypeScript change to Git diff hunk parsing and local change detection reaches 24 dependents.** The change is concentrated in `gitnexus/src/storage/git.ts` and `gitnexus/src/mcp/local/local-backend.ts`, including `parseDiffHunks`, `parseDiffHunksResult`, and `detectChanges`. Its impact spans `Cli`, `Storage`, `Local`, `Integration`, `Scenario-map`, `Server`, and `Mcp`, and passes through 35 affected flows. Review the diff parsing and hunk coalescing behavior first, then check how `detectChanges` uses the parsed hunks alongside `gitnexus/src/storage/indexed-image.ts`. The unit and integration tests cover these areas in `gitnexus/test/unit/parse-diff-hunks.test.ts`, `gitnexus/test/unit/detect-changes-hunk-scale.test.ts`, `gitnexus/test/unit/indexed-image.test.ts`, and `gitnexus/test/integration/detect-changes-pre-image.test.ts`. File risk is LOW, with no HIGH or CRITICAL risk files. title: fix(resolution): drop the self-loop from interface dispatch out of a decorator (#2836)
body:
## Summary

Interface dispatch no longer emits a CALLS edge from a method to itself. A decorator that implements an interface and calls its delegate through a field of that interface type used to get `loggingRepo.DeleteItem -> loggingRepo.DeleteItem` (`interface-dispatch`). Dispatch to every other implementation is unchanged.

## Motivation / context

Fixes #2836, which asks for this to be decided and pinned with a fixture. The issue lists three options. This PR takes option 2: exclude the enclosing caller from the fan-out.

The self edge is only real when a decorator wraps another instance of itself. Emitted for every decorator, which is one of the most common Go shapes, it makes `check --cycles` report a cycle that no concrete execution has, shows the method as its own caller in `impact()`, and feeds a cycle into clustering and process truncation. Dropping it loses the nested decorator case. A genuine direct recursive call is still resolved by the ordinary receiver path, because only the `interface-dispatch` fan-out is filtered.

## Areas touched

- [x] `gitnexus/` (CLI / core / MCP server)
- [ ] `gitnexus-web/` (Vite / React UI)
- [ ] `.github/` (workflows, actions)
- [ ] `eval/` or other tooling
- [ ] Docs / agent config only (`AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `.cursor/`, `llms.txt`, etc.)

## Scope & constraints

**In scope**

- `emitInterfaceDispatchFor` drops the dispatch target whose graph id is the call site's enclosing caller. It does this before the fan-out cap, so the dropped target does not use up the budget.
- A Go fixture that pins the decorator shape and three controls.

**Explicitly out of scope / not done here**

- Options 1 and 3 from the issue (document the self edge, or keep it with a distinguishing marker).
- Other edge reasons. Only the `interface-dispatch` fan-out is filtered.

## Implementation notes

- The check compares graph ids, so it is language neutral and covers the same shape in Java, C#, Kotlin and TypeScript.
- The caller id is resolved once per site, and only when there is at least one dispatch target.

## Testing & verification

- [x] `cd gitnexus && npx vitest run test/integration/resolvers/go.test.ts -t "decorator"` (the self-loop case fails on main, all 4 pass here)
- [x] Resolver suites for go, csharp, kotlin, typescript, dart and python, plus generic-interface-dispatch, generic-field-receiver-matrix and the parse-cache identity and coverage guards: 1687 passed. One parse-cache-identity timing test fails identically on main on my Windows machine.
- [x] `cd gitnexus && npx tsc --noEmit` and `npm run typecheck:tests`
- [ ] `cd gitnexus && npm test` (left to CI)
- [x] Manual: `analyze --force` on the issue's snippet. The self-loop is gone, and `loggingRepo.DeleteItem -> SqlRepo.DeleteItem` and the `Repository.DeleteItem` edge remain.

The fixture checks four things:

- There is no self-loop CALLS edge.
- The decorator still dispatches to `SqlRepo`.
- The decorator still dispatches to its own other method (`loggingRepo.DeleteItem -> loggingRepo.Count`).
- A non-implementing caller (`Service.Run`) keeps the full fan-out.

## Risk & rollout

This changes graph output only where a self-loop was emitted. Parse-cache identity covers `core/ingestion` automatically, so existing caches are invalidated by the source change and no manual step is needed. Users see the change after their next `npx gitnexus analyze`.

## Checklist

- [x] PR body meets repo minimum length (workflow may label short descriptions)
- [ ] If `AGENTS.md` / overlays changed: headers, scope block, and changelog updated per project conventions
- [x] No secrets, tokens, or machine-specific paths committed

title: fix(ingestion): bind default imports of components exported through a wrapper
body:
## Summary

`impact` and `context` now report the JSX consumers of components exported through a wrapper call: `export default memo(Card)`, `forwardRef(Card)`, `memo(forwardRef(Card))`, `connect(mapState)(Card)`, `React.memo(Card, areEqual)`. Before this change the default import of such a module never bound, so these components showed 0 callers and risk `UNKNOWN`.

## Motivation / context

Refs #323. The 2026-07-25 comment there shows a Next.js app where components rendered as `<InspectorPanel />` have no incoming edges while another app's components do. After #3960, default imports bind for `export default function F`, `export default X` and `export { X as default }`, and plain default exports link. The remaining gap is the wrapper form the comment calls out (`export default memo(Foo)`), which is very common in React code.

Root cause: `collectEsmExportEvidence` (`ts-js-export-marker.ts`) only records a default local when `export default` is followed by a bare identifier. For `export default memo(Card)` the child is a `call_expression`. So `Card` was neither exported nor default, `typescriptModuleExports` published no `default`, and `import Card from './Card'` stayed unbound.

## Areas touched

- [x] `gitnexus/` (CLI / core / MCP server)
- [ ] `gitnexus-web/` (Vite / React UI)
- [ ] `.github/` (workflows, actions)
- [ ] `eval/` or other tooling
- [ ] Docs / agent config only (`AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `.cursor/`, `llms.txt`, etc.)

## Scope & constraints

**In scope**

- A default-exported call to a component wrapper publishes the top-level function or class it wraps. Component wrappers are `memo` / `forwardRef` / `observer` (bare or as a member, e.g. `React.memo`), `withX` HOCs, and the HOC returned by a known factory (`connect` / `compose` / `inject`, or a `withX` name: `connect(mapState)(Card)`, `withStyles(s)(Card)`). The wrapped value is the first argument, followed through nested wrappers and through TS `as` / `satisfies` / parentheses / `!`. A local "function" means one declared directly, or bound to a function/class expression either bare or inside those same component wrappers (`const Field = forwardRef((p, r) => …)`, `memo(forwardRef(…))`).
- `memo(Card, (a, b) => …)`: the inline comparator is no longer declared as the file-named default. On `main` it was, so `<Card />` linked to the comparator. The existing synthesized HOC default is unchanged when the first argument is inline (`export default memo(() => …)`) or is not a local function (`hoc(importedOpts, () => …)`).
- `Card` is published only as the default, not under its own name. A type with the same name (`interface Card` next to `function Card`) stays private.
- One change in the shared TS/JS export evidence, so TS, TSX, JS and JSX all pick it up.

**Explicitly out of scope / not done here**

- Angular/Vue template usage, mentioned at the end of #323. That is template parsing, not export binding, so this is `Refs`, not `Fixes`.
- Calls that build a value from the component instead of wrapping it (`React.createElement(Card)`, `h(Card)`, `createApp(App)`, `createApp(config)(App)`, `make()(Card)`), and wrapped values that are not a top-level function or class (`make(config)`, `const store = createStore(() => …)`, imports, destructured bindings). These stay unbound, which is the fail-safe direction.
- Known limit: a project-specific HOC that isn't named `withX` and isn't curried (e.g. `export default enhance(Card)`) doesn't link. It could be added to the wrapper set later if needed.

## Implementation notes

- `ts-js-hoc-utils.ts`: `wrappedDefaultLocal(call, root)` and its helpers live next to the existing HOC rules, so the export marker and `isBlockedDefaultExportHoc` share one definition. Each wrapper level must pass `isComponentWrapperCallee` (callee names decoded, so `React.\u006demo` matches). The same `unwrapComponentWrappers` walk decides whether a `const` initializer is a component. Comment arguments are skipped.
- `ts-js-export-marker.ts`: the wrapped local is added to `defaultLocals`, so the existing "two different defaults publish none" rule still applies. It gets its own `wrappedDefaultLocal` field instead of joining `namedLocals`, and that field is set only when it is the single resolved default. So only the runtime declaration of that name is marked exported, and conflicting defaults export nothing.
- No new capture, resolver hook or env var. Parse-cache identity is derived automatically. The scope-capture fingerprints are unchanged (`measure.mjs --check` passes), so no golden update was needed.

## Testing & verification

- [x] `cd gitnexus && npm test`: all resolver integration suites pass (`npx vitest run test/integration/resolvers`, 5591 passed). `npx vitest run test/unit` has 24 failures in 13 files on my machine (macOS, Node 25.1). None are in ingestion: 12 of the files fail the same way on `main` (process-spawning hook tests, pnpm/bunx probes, vendored FTS paths, shallow-clone release/scenario tests), and `parse-cache-benchmark-pairing` timed out under full-suite load but passes on its own.
- [ ] `cd gitnexus && npm run test:integration`: resolver suites only (above). I didn't run the full LadybugDB integration set locally.
- [x] `cd gitnexus && npx tsc --noEmit`, plus `npm run typecheck:tests`
- [x] Also run: prettier, eslint on the touched files, `GITNEXUS_LANGUAGE_BOUNDARY_BASE=origin/main npx vitest run test/unit/shared-tool-language-boundary.test.ts test/unit/parse-cache-identity.test.ts test/unit/parse-cache-input-coverage.test.ts` (81 passed), `node --import tsx bench/scope-capture/measure.mjs --check` (PASS, 17 languages). I ran `npm run build` before validating the parser facts.

New tests (each fails on `main`, verified by restoring the two source files from `main` and rebuilding: 6 fail, then all 14 pass):

- `esm-export-marker.test.ts`, both emitters: wrapped defaults (`memo`, `React.memo(X, eq)`, nested, curried, class, const arrow, `const F = forwardRef(…)` and `memo(forwardRef(…))`, `withStyles(s)(X)`, `compose(…)(X)`, comment argument, escaped callee names), TS assertions/parentheses, the comparator case, type + value with the same name, and conflicting wrapped defaults. Negative cases: value-building calls (`React.createElement`, `h`, `createApp`, `createStore`, an unknown `wrap`), curried calls through unknown factories (`make()(X)`, `createApp(config)(X)`), `const` values from callback-taking calls (`createStore(() => …)`, `debounce(() => …)`, `xs.map(…)`), object argument, import, `setTimeout(f)`, `make(1, f)`, `f.bind`, `xs.map(f)`, `p.then(f)`, an inline function next to a non-local argument.
- `typescript.test.ts` / `javascript.test.ts`: real CALLS edges from `<Card />`, `<Input />` (`memo(Field) as typeof Field` over `forwardRef`) and `<Line />` (`React.memo(Row, cmp)`). A guard checks that a named import `{ Card }` does not resolve.

Real run with the built CLI on a small React app: one `Studio.tsx` rendering components exported eight different ways. I ran `gitnexus analyze --index-only --force`, then `gitnexus impact <Component> --direction upstream`:

```
main (50228e1)
impact MemoDefault       -> impactedCount=0 risk=UNKNOWN callers=[]
impact ForwardRefDefault -> impactedCount=0 risk=UNKNOWN callers=[]
impact RefField          -> impactedCount=0 risk=UNKNOWN callers=[]
impact ComparedRow       -> impactedCount=1 risk=LOW callers=['Studio']   # edge lands on the comparator, declared as default "ComparedRow"
impact PlainDefault      -> impactedCount=1 risk=LOW callers=['Studio']
CALLS into components: 5

this branch
impact MemoDefault       -> impactedCount=1 risk=LOW callers=['Studio']
impact ForwardRefDefault -> impactedCount=1 risk=LOW callers=['Studio']
impact RefField          -> impactedCount=1 risk=LOW callers=['Studio']
impact ComparedRow       -> impactedCount=1 risk=LOW callers=['Studio']   # now the component itself

CALLS into components: 8
```

I also ran a property check over the whole class rather than single examples. It covers 30 call shapes × 20 ways of declaring the argument, in both emitters: 1093 cases. The property is "a wrapped default is marked only when the argument is a top-level function/class, and never alongside a second default". On `main` there are 181 violations, all missing bindings, with 0 false positives. On this branch there are 0. Each new rule was also mutated (wrapper set, `withX`, curried factories, `withX` factories, member callees, name decoding, conflicting defaults, wrapped `const` initializers, comparator block, callable gate, HOC-wrapped const, erased-type guard, unwrapping, comment filter), and a unit test catches every mutation.

## Risk & rollout

Those components gain the incoming CALLS edges they were missing, and the comparator case moves its edge from the comparator to the component. Existing indexes pick this up on the next `npx gitnexus analyze`. Parse-cache identity covers the changed files automatically. Not breaking.

title: feat(web): restore chat history across page reloads (#432)
body:
Closes #432

## What changed

- **New `gitnexus-web/src/core/llm/chat-history-store.ts`**: `loadChatHistory(repoKey)` / `saveChatHistory(repoKey, messages)`, storing the newest 50 messages per repository.
  - A stored history always starts at a user message, so a trimmed transcript never opens with an assistant reply or tool result whose question was cut away.
  - If a write is refused (quota), the oldest half is dropped and the write retried until it fits; if nothing fits, the entry is removed.
  - Unreadable JSON, unexpected shapes and blocked storage all fall back to in-memory chat, exactly as before.
- **`useAppState.tsx`**
  - `restoreChatHistory(repoKey)` sets the chat's storage key and the restored messages in the same update, so the save effect can never write one repo's messages under another repo's key.
  - A `useEffect` saves once each turn settles (skipped while a reply streams, so a long answer is written once rather than per token). `clearChat` empties the list, which removes the stored copy; the existing "Clear chat" button needed no change.
  - `switchRepo` restores the new repo's history instead of always clearing.
- **`App.tsx`**: `handleServerConnect` (also the path a page reload takes) restores the repo's history.
- The key is the repo path, falling back to the display name only when the server reports no path, so same-named repos (#2419) keep separate histories. Both connect paths compute it the same way, so a reload after a repo switch finds the same history.

## Design decisions for review

1. **sessionStorage, not localStorage.** The issue proposed localStorage, but this app already moved provider API keys (`settings-service.ts`) and the deploy token (`AUTH_TOKEN_STORAGE_KEY`) to sessionStorage. Chat history holds code excerpts, so I matched that: a reload restores the conversation, but closing the tab doesn't leave it on disk. It also keeps the history's lifetime in step with the API key the agent needs to continue it. If you'd rather keep history across tab closes, it's a one-line change in `getStorage()`.
2. **Repo switch now restores that repo's earlier conversation** from the same session, rather than always starting empty. The agent is still re-created for the new repo; it picks up the restored messages as history on the next turn, the same way it does after a reload.

## How to verify

```sh
cd gitnexus-web
npx vitest run src/core/llm/chat-history-store.test.ts test/unit/chat-history-persistence.test.tsx
npx vitest run          # 49 files / 547 tests pass
npx tsc -b --noEmit     # clean
```

- `chat-history-store.test.ts` (10): round-trip through sessionStorage (and not localStorage), per-repo isolation, 50-message cap starting at a user turn, clear removes the entry, quota back-off, quota exhaustion, unreadable data, blocked storage.
- `chat-history-persistence.test.tsx` (4) against the real `AppStateProvider`: restore after a fresh mount (reload), switching between same-named repos without cross-writes, empty history for an unused repo, `clearChat` removing only the current repo's copy. Disabling the save in the effect makes the `clearChat` case fail, so the wiring is covered.
- `update-banner.test.tsx`: its mocked app state gained `restoreChatHistory`, which `handleServerConnect` now calls.

Manual: connect a repo, ask a question, reload — the conversation is back; Clear chat, reload — it stays empty. I have not run this against a live server and LLM.

## GitNexus checks

- `impact --direction upstream` before editing: `switchRepo`, `clearChat` and `handleServerConnect` are LOW (2–3 callers each). The `AppState.*` property entries return UNKNOWN because components read them off the context object; a text search confirms the readers (`RightPanel` for `clearChat`).
- `detect-changes --scope all`: 3 tracked files, 9 symbols (exactly the edited ones), 0 affected processes, risk **low**.

## Risk / rollback

Web UI only; no server or CLI changes. Storage failures degrade to the current in-memory behavior. Revert the single commit to roll back; stored entries are namespaced under `gitnexus-chat-history:v1:` and expire with the tab.

title: fix(detect-changes): map hunks in the line space of the image the index holds
body:
## Summary
`detect_changes` now maps each modified file's hunks using whichever side of the diff the index actually holds, so edits that add or remove lines no longer report the wrong symbols and deleted functions are reported.

## Problem
Hunks were always read from the post-image (`+c,d`), but graph `startLine`/`endLine` come from the bytes `analyze` read — the pre-image in the documented analyze → edit → detect_changes flow. After an edit that shifts lines, later hunks hit neighbouring symbols, a deleted function was never reported, and the risk level was computed from the wrong symbols.

## Root cause
Only deleted files used the old-side range (`git.ts` `parseDiffHunksResult`); every other file was overlapped with indexed lines in post-image coordinates.

## Solution
- Parse the old side of each hunk and full blob ids (`--full-index`) on request.
- Per modified file, hash both images and compare with `meta.fileHashes`: work-tree side from disk; blob side by stored bytes, falling back to `git cat-file --filters --path` so `core.autocrlf`/filter drivers match what `analyze` read. (`cat-file --batch --filters` prints the unfiltered size in its header, so filtered reads are per blob, bounded at 8 concurrent.)
- Pre-image → old-side ranges; a pure insertion touches only a symbol that encloses the insertion point.
- Neither image matches → `partial: true`, `risk_level: unknown`, new `unverified_line_files` field and CLI note.
- Legacy indexes without `fileHashes` keep today's behaviour.

## Key changes
- `src/storage/git.ts`: opt-in `withPreImage` parsing, `insertionGapsOf`, `hunksStraddleGap`
- `src/storage/diff-image-match.ts` (new): image classification
- `src/mcp/local/local-backend.ts`: per-file side selection, `--full-index`
- `src/cli/detect-changes-format.ts`, i18n (en, zh-CN), `src/mcp/tools.ts`: surface `unverified_line_files`

## Testing
- New integration test `detect-changes-indexed-image.test.ts` (real engine): 9 cases; 7 fail on main, all pass with the fix.
- New unit tests: `diff-image-match.test.ts` (autocrlf=true, staged, spaced/non-ASCII path, subdirectory cwd), pre-image parser cases.
- Manual CLI repro of the issue's cases: before → first/helper/second, first, third; after → third, helper, fourth (also `--scope staged`, `core.autocrlf=true`, path with space + non-ASCII).
- `tsc --noEmit`, `typecheck:tests`, prettier, eslint (no new warnings).

title: fix(ingestion): qualify C++ and Ruby member ids by enclosing scope
body:
## What

C++ and Ruby member node ids used only the immediate class name, so two members that differ only by enclosing namespace or module collapsed onto one id. `N::Box<bool>::save` and `::Box<bool>::save` became one node, and `CALLS` edges and impact reports mixed them up.

This qualifies member ids with the same enclosing namespace, module, and nested-type path the class node already has. Other languages are unchanged.

## Why

A collapse is worse than a miss: callers of one member can be attributed to the other. Issue #2874 documented a prior attempt that was measured and then reverted for three shape defects. This change handles those cases:

1. Out-of-line C++ definitions (`void N::Box::save() {}`) resolve back to the class instead of prepending a namespace the declarator already names, so ids do not become `N::N::Box.save`.
2. Ruby `class A::B` normalizes to the same `A.B` path as `module A; class B`.
3. Anonymous namespaces use a sibling ordinal (`@anon1`) instead of a byte offset, so an edit above the namespace does not rename every member inside it.

`ANALYSIS_FEATURES` entries `cpp.member-scope-identity` and `ruby.member-scope-identity` trigger a one-time rebuild for indexed C++ and Ruby repositories so a warm index does not mix old and new id shapes.

## How to verify

```bash
cd gitnexus
npm run build
npx tsc --noEmit
npm run typecheck:tests
npx prettier --check .
npx eslint
npm test
```

New coverage is in `test/integration/cpp-ruby-member-scope-id.test.ts` and `test/unit/cpp-member-owner.test.ts`. Existing tests that pinned the old unqualified ids were updated.

Full suite on this branch: 37,111 passed, 138 skipped. One network flake failed on the first run and passed when run alone. `test/unit/evidence-provenance-helper.test.ts` ("has one golden digest for every dirty state...") fails identically on clean `main`, so it is not caused by this change.

## Risk and rollback

- Member ids change for namespaced C++ and Ruby symbols. Previously indexed C++ and Ruby repos rebuild once on upgrade via the new analysis features.
- Methods defined in a `.cpp` whose class lives only in a header still get a separate id, because ids include the file path, as they did before.
- A few rare template and nested-namespace edge cases fall back to the path as written.
- Rollback is reverting the commit.

#4141 is also open for this issue. This branch additionally splits `::` inside template arguments and covers extensionless Ruby files such as `Rakefile` and `Gemfile`.

Fixes #2874

title: fix(mcp): return the tool-usage policy in initialize instructions
body:
## What

The Always Do / Never Do tool-usage policy now lives in one module. `createMCPServer` returns it as MCP `initialize` instructions, so any host that honors server instructions gets the policy when the server connects. `analyze` still writes the same bytes into `AGENTS.md` and `CLAUDE.md`. ## Why

MCP already has a first-class channel for tool-usage policy (`instructions` on initialize), and GitNexus was not using it. The policy had to be injected into project instruction files, which are shared with other tools and go stale when the server changes. Serving the policy from the server lets it travel with the tool and stay in sync with the server version. This change does not remove or shrink the file block, so non-MCP workflows keep working as before.

No overlap with #4080 or #4122.

## How to verify

```bash
cd gitnexus
npm run build
npm test
```

New coverage is in `test/unit/mcp-server-instructions.test.ts` and `test/unit/tool-usage-policy.test.ts`, plus a golden fixture for the file block.

Full suite on this branch: 37,128 passed. The 1 failure is `test/unit/evidence-provenance-helper.test.ts` ("has one golden digest for every dirty state..."). It fails identically on clean upstream `main`.

## Risk and rollback

- The server copy uses `node .gitnexus/run.cjs` and target branch `main`, and omits the per-index PDG and Spring Actuator lines. Repos that need those lines still get them from the file block.
- Read-only mode still shows the rename `dry_run:false` sentence, which the server rejects.
- Hosts that ignore `instructions` keep using the file block.
- Rollback is reverting the commit.
